units.la: EPistolarum omnium Apostolicarum Expositioni huicce a Clarissimo viro, Domino Davide Dicsono conscriptæ, studiosis Theologiæ utilissimæ, Authore simul ac lectore dignissimæ: utpote quæ spiritus scopum, verborum sensum, doctrinarum medullam, argumentorum aciem, optimè attingit, eruit, extrahit, extruit: in officium, potiùs quàm suffragium, hoc quantulumcunq; sit calculi, adijcere gestit
units.tr: To this Analytical Exposition of all the Apostolic Epistles, written by the most distinguished Mr David Dickson, most useful to students of theology and most worthy of both author and reader, since it grasps the aim of the Spirit, the sense of the words, the marrow of the doctrines and the edge of the arguments, and brings them out, draws them forth and builds them up, I am eager to add my name, as a duty rather than a vote, however small this pebble of a ballot may be.

units.la: ANalyticam Expositionem Epistolarum Apostolicarum a Cl: viro Domino Davide Dicsono concinnatam, legi avidus; gustatâ antea suavissimâ necnon ut ilissimâ ejus commentatione Anglico jdiomate, in Epistolam ad Hebræos, conscriptâ; De utrâq; dicam quod sentio, jmo quod res est, Satis multum in jis reperturum, qui non expectat nimis. Nec quicquam me vidisse in tanta brevitate, tantum porrigens, et sensus genuini sacri textus et fructus jnde colligendi. Gratulor itaq; Jnsulanis nostris præsertim studiosæ juventuti, tam egregia Doctrinæ, quæ est secundum pietatem, adminicula. Multum a R. Authore efflagitans, tam ut utramque curet (quod de postremâ hâc videtur promittere) & doctis & Jdiotis communicarj; quam ut denuò se accingat ad enarrandas, ijsdem methodo & modo, cæteras S. Scripturæ partes. Quo in opere ut diu eum sospitet Cœlestis Pater, duplicetq; in eum spiritum sapientiæ & Revelationis, precibus haud dubio contendent multi, inter quos, me non omnino nullum, dignißimo viro ignotus licet, Spondeo.
units.tr: I have read eagerly the Analytical Exposition of the Apostolic Epistles, composed by the distinguished Mr David Dickson, having earlier tasted his most sweet and useful commentary on the Epistle to the Hebrews, written in English. Of both I will say what I think, and what is the truth: they will contain quite a lot for those who do not expect too much. Nor have I seen anything that in such brevity reaches so far, both in bringing out the genuine sense of the sacred text and the fruit to be gathered from it. I therefore congratulate our islanders, and especially our studious youth, on such excellent aids to that doctrine which is according to godliness. I earnestly ask much of the reverend Author: that he see to it that both of these works (the latter of which he seems to promise) are communicated to the learned and the unlearned alike, and that he prepare himself again to expound, by the same method and manner, the remaining parts of Holy Scripture. In which work may the Heavenly Father keep him safe for many years, and double in him the spirit of wisdom and of revelation. Many will undoubtedly contend in prayer to this end, and among them I, not altogether the least, though unknown to so worthy a man, promise to be.

units.la: [Q]Uemadmodum Satan Spiritus ille tenebrarum & humani generis hostis infensissimus, nec non vaferrimi ipsius satellites id omnibus viribus moliuntur, ut si non ex orbe terrarum divinæ scripturæ tollantur, saltem pro verbo Dei somnia & commenta hominum, atque istius verbi glossemata vel spuria & impia, vel vana & inutilia Ecclesijs Christi obtrudantur; ita fideles ovilis Christi pastores nihil prius in votis habent, nihil impensius nituntur, quàm ut sacrarum literarum rivuli è throno Dei & agni scaturientes, civitatem Jehovæ abundè reficiant, & sacra Scriptura à fucatis omnium pseudoprophetarum interpretamentis purgata, & à vermiculato cujuscunq; generis Mangonio vindicata, in genuino suo nitore pura perpetuò conservetur.
units.tr: Just as Satan, that spirit of darkness and most bitter enemy of the human race, and his most crafty henchmen, strive with all their might that, if the divine Scriptures are not removed from the earth, then at least the dreams and inventions of men, and glosses upon that Word, either spurious and impious or vain and useless, be foisted upon the Churches of Christ; so the faithful ministers of the flock of Christ have nothing more at heart and strive for nothing more eagerly than that the streams of sacred letters, springing from the throne of God and of the Lamb, abundantly refresh the city of Jehovah, and that Holy Scripture, purged of the painted interpretations of all false prophets and vindicated from the worm-eaten wares of every kind of peddler, be kept pure and unchanging in its genuine lustre.

units.la: Quandoquidem autem jam tertia pars fontium & fluviorum casu stellæ, cui nomen est absinthium, miserè intoxicata sit, & nimis quàm multa sidera, quæ non ita pridem in Ecclesiæ firmamento collucere videbantur, ictu caudæ Draconis cœlo exciderint: adeo ut agrum dominicum Zizanijs hæreseon, & putidarum commentationum lolijs luxuriantem & silvescentem omnis verè pius, cui causa Dei cordi est, magno cum animi dolore conspicere cogatur: idcirco stellas Jesu Christi dexterâ suffultas, virosDei, quos princeps Ecclesiæ dono & facultate aperiendi scripturas instruxit, omnibus officijs & honore prosequi par est.
units.tr: Since now a third part of the fountains and rivers has been wretchedly poisoned by the falling of the star called Wormwood, and very many stars, which not long ago seemed to shine in the firmament of the Church, have fallen from heaven by the blow of the dragon's tail, so that every truly pious man, to whom the cause of God is dear, is compelled to behold with great grief of mind the Lord's field luxuriating and growing into a forest with the tares of heresies and the darnel of foul commentaries: it is therefore fitting to honour and attend with every service and respect the stars that are upheld by the right hand of Jesus Christ, that is, the men of God whom the Prince of the Church has equipped with the gift and ability to open the Scriptures.

units.la: Uerum enim vero, inter illos, quos divina misericordia Ecclesiæ nostræ Scoticanæ à multis retrò annis indulsit, Censemus nos virum clarissimū D. Davidem Dicksonum S. Theologiæ in Academia Glasguensi professorem, neminj secundum; Nostro quidem testimonio tanti viri lucubrationibus nihil accedere posse, & opus hoc nostrâ hederâ minimè indigere lubenter agnoscimus. Margarita {x}excellentissima gemmarij encomium nequaquam desiderat, suo enim insito fulgore vel noctu resplendet; Attamen absque adulationis fuco Authorem esse Jehovæ nuntium, interpretem unum e mille, sagittam politam & tersam, in umbrâ manus Dej absconditam, non possumus non profiteri & testari.
units.tr: Indeed, among those whom divine mercy has for many years granted to our Scottish Church, we judge the most distinguished man Mr David Dickson, professor of Holy Theology in the University of Glasgow, to be second to none. By our testimony we gladly acknowledge that nothing can be added to the labours of so great a man, and that this work has little need of our ivy. The most excellent pearl does not at all require a jeweller's praise, for it shines even by night with its own inborn lustre; yet, without the varnish of flattery, we cannot but profess and testify that the Author is a messenger of Jehovah, one interpreter out of a thousand, a polished and burnished arrow hidden in the shadow of the hand of God.

units.la: Commentarius hic in omnes Apostolorum Pauli, Jacobi, Petri, Joannis & Judæ Epistolas, in quo brevitas cum perspicuitate & cum utrâque utilitas concertare videtur, brevi viâ longum iter conficit; In eo sensus spiritus Sancti solidè detegitur, series argumentorum elaboratè enodatur, semina doctrinarum & fontes controversiarum dilucidè aperiuntur. Cum autem Commentariorum in sacram Scripturam mole & copiâ, ingenia S. Theologiæ candidatorum tantùm non obruantur, & lectores Scripturientis hujus sæculi voluminum fastidio magis nauseam contrahant, quam delectatione capiantur, hic liber nobis unus est pro multis. Authorem itaq; rogamus, obsecramus, obtestamur, ut in itinere hoc tam feliciter suscepto progrediatur: Comprecantes D. Jesum Christum leonem illum de tribu Judæ ut curâ & industriâ talium Dei organorum librum obsignatum indies aperire, pro immensâ suâ misericordiâ, non dedignetur.
units.tr: This commentary on all the Epistles of the Apostles Paul, James, Peter, John and Jude, in which brevity seems to vie with clarity and both with usefulness, accomplishes a long journey by a short road. In it the sense of the Holy Spirit is solidly laid open, the sequence of arguments is laboriously unfolded, and the seeds of doctrines and the sources of controversies are clearly set forth. But since the minds of candidates in Theology are all but overwhelmed by the bulk and abundance of commentaries on Holy Scripture, and the readers of this scribbling age are made more nauseated by the weariness of volumes than delighted, this one book is for us as many. We therefore ask, beseech and entreat the Author to proceed on this journey so happily begun, praying that the Lord Jesus Christ, that lion of the tribe of Judah, in his immense mercy, will not disdain, by the care and diligence of such instruments of God, to open day by day the book that has been sealed.

units.la: ILLUSTRISSIMO ARGATHELIÆ MARCHIONI, Comiti Kinteræ, Domino Cambello, Domino Lornæ, &c. Summo Architriclino Regio, Et summo Quæstori Rerum Capitalium per Æbudas Insulas, Sanctioris Concilii Senatori integerrimo:
units.tr: TO THE MOST ILLUSTRIOUS MARQUIS OF ARGYLL, Earl of Kintyre, Lord Campbell, Lord of Lorne, &c., Chief Steward of the Royal Household, and Chief Justiciar over the Western Isles, most upright Senator of the Privy Council:

units.la: Necnon, GENEROSISSIMO DOMINO, D. ARCHIBALDO CAMBELLO, Domino Lornæ, Ejus Filio natu Maximo, Et Hæredi, Dominis suis Nobilissimis, omnigenam Felicitatem precatur DA. DICSONUS.
units.tr: And to the most noble gentleman, LORD ARCHIBALD CAMPBELL, Lord of Lorne, eldest son and heir of the same, his noble lords, DA. DICKSON wishes every kind of happiness.

units.la: Peciosum ubique locorum semper fuit, Marchio illustrissime, Felicitatis & Sapientiæ nomen; & apud omnes laudi datum est, utriusque studiosum esse: Sed Pauci res ipsas probè intellectas habuerunt; Nam qui felicitatem in ulla re, præterquam in unius DEI consortio & fruitione posuerunt, illi etiam in Sapientiæ negotio hallucinati sunt: Siquidem illa demum vera est Sapientia, per quam ad solidam, æternamque felicitatem, rectâ certoque ducimur. Tristissimum est spectaculum, lum, sed prudenter observantibus non inutile, conjunctam cum amentia, Miseriam in humano Genere, contemplari. Exulant homines à Coelo palantes vagantur in Terra, miseriae stimulis, & caeco quodam beatitudinis appetitu agitati, ad quaerendum remedium feruntur. Sed quum in Coelo requirerent, in coeno & fordibus scrutantur Felicitatem, nec usquam inveniunt: Pro summo Bono, bonorum infima, & vanitatis Umbras fallaces amplectuntur: Conceptae Spei frequenti frustratione subinde admonentur erroris: irrequietique Animi oestro perpetuo punguntur, ut Patriam Coelestem, & Paternam Domum repetant: Sed errant ab utero, & fine fine, novasque sibi attrahunt & multiplicant, quas fugiebant Miserias.
units.tr: The name of happiness and of wisdom has always been held in high esteem everywhere, most illustrious Marquis, and everyone has agreed that it is praiseworthy to pursue both. Yet few have rightly understood the things themselves. For those who have placed happiness in anything other than fellowship with and enjoyment of the one God have also gone astray in the matter of wisdom. Indeed, that alone is true wisdom through which we are led straight and surely to a solid and eternal happiness. It is a most sorrowful spectacle, though not useless to those who observe it prudently, to contemplate the misery of the human race joined with madness. Men, wandering far from heaven, roam the earth, driven by the goads of misery and by a certain blind desire for blessedness, and they press on in search of a remedy. But while they should seek it in heaven, they grope for happiness in mire and filth, and nowhere find it. In place of the highest Good, they embrace the lowest of goods and the deceptive shadows of vanity. Repeated frustration of their hopes from time to time warns them of their error, and they are constantly stung by the restless gadfly of the soul, so that they might seek again the heavenly homeland and the Father's house. Yet they wander from the womb onward and without end, and they draw to themselves and multiply new miseries, the very ones they were trying to flee.

units.la: Auget spectaculi tristitiam, Divinae Bonitatis cum insanâ Hominum Pervicaciâ conflictantis, contemplatio. Prodit è Coelo Felicitatis Fons (Decore & Majestate indutus, & Luce amictus ut panno) tenebrionibus è longinquo manifestat invisibilia sua, aeternam nempe Potentiam,& Divinitatem suam in operibus Creationis splendentem, ut invitet rebelles ad redeundum in gratiam. Illi vero vel non respiciunt Deum, vel respicientes non agnoscunt, vel aliqua ex parte agnitum non glorificant ut Deum, sed evanescunt in cogitationibus suis, & proni in Terram pergunt clamitare, Quis ostendet nobis Bonum? Nulli serio orant, Attolle super nos lucem Faciei tuae.
units.tr: The contemplation of the Divine Goodness struggling with the mad obstinacy of men adds to the sadness of the spectacle. The Fountain of happiness comes forth from heaven, clothed in majesty and decked in light as in a garment, and from afar he reveals his invisible things to those in darkness, namely his eternal power and his divinity, shining forth in the works of creation, so as to invite rebels to return into favour. But they either do not regard God, or regarding him they do not acknowledge him, or, though they acknowledge him in some measure, they do not glorify him as God, but vanish away in their own thoughts. Bent low, they go on crying out to the earth: "Who will show us any good?" No one prays earnestly: "Lift up over us the light of your face."

units.la: Accedit Deus propius, in operibus Providentiae; utque se experitem esse Testimonii non sinat, Bona tribuit indignis, Pluvias dat coelitus, & ferendis fructibus Tempora praestituta; Corda ingratissimorum Hostium suorum cibo & delectatione implens, ut palpando reperiant Dominum quem dereliquerunt, & per Divitias Benignitatis & Tolerantiae ipsius, ad resipiscentiam deducantur. Accipiunt Beneficia, gulae & abdomini sacrificant accepta; Et quaecunque Benignitas Divina concessit, una cum membris suis omnibus, in arma iniquitatis Θεομαχοι convertunt.
units.tr: God draws nearer in the works of providence. Lest he leave himself without witness, he bestows good things on the unworthy, gives rains from heaven and fruitful seasons at their appointed times, and fills the hearts of his most ungrateful enemies with food and gladness, so that by groping they might find the Lord whom they have forsaken, and by the riches of his goodness and forbearance be led to repentance. They receive his benefits and sacrifice what they have received to their belly and their gullet; and whatever gifts the Divine Goodness has granted, together with all their members, they turn into weapons of iniquity, as theomachi [θεομάχοι, fighters against God].

units.la: Sed
units.tr: But

units.la: Dedicatoria.
units.tr: Dedicatory.

units.la: Sed neque hic gradum sistit φιλανθρωπια Dei ; accedit quàm proximè, extendit manum, pulsat uniuscujusque pectus: profert legendum singulis inscriptum cordibus Legis opus; Conscientias concutit, Cogitationes excitat quæ trahant fugitivos Hostes ad Tribunal Justitiæ, accusent Reos, convincant ingratitudinis odiosæ, excusationemque omnem auferant Convictis, ut resipiscant, veniamque deprecentur: Illi vero convicti iniquitatis, insurgunt Contumaces, oblatrant conscientiæ suæ, manusque ei ut taceat, injiciunt violentas; veritatem illam Dei, cordibus inscriptam invadunt, suppressamque in carcerem conjiciunt, & detinent in injustitia. Quid mirum si Deus αυτοκατακριτος tam perdite pervicaces sinat incedere in viis suis, Diaboloque & suis affectibus tradat pro meritis tractandos, Proh dolor! pereunt myriades, & perire volunt.
units.tr: But neither does the philanthropy of God stop here; it draws as near as possible, stretches out its hand, and knocks at the breast of each one. It sets before each person the work of the Law, written upon their hearts; it shakes their consciences and stirs up thoughts which drag fugitive enemies before the tribunal of Justice, accuse the guilty, convict them of hateful ingratitude, and strip the convicted of every excuse, so that they may repent and beg for pardon. But those who are convicted of wickedness rise up in obstinacy, bark at their own conscience, and lay violent hands on it to silence it; they assail that truth of God written in their hearts, cast it down, shut it up in prison, and keep it held in injustice. What wonder, then, if God, self-condemned, permits such utterly stubborn men to walk in their own ways and, as they deserve, hands them over to the Devil and their own passions to be dealt with? Alas! Myriads perish, and they are willing to perish.

units.la: Verùm quanto hoc spectaculum est lamentabilius, tanto est Dei conspecta bonitas amabilior, quæ non patitur ut Divina Gratia repulsam patiatur, ab iis quos Dei beneplacitum voluit esse suos, ad sanam mentem redire, & esse salvos. Lætum dicas illud spectaculum quod in æternum beatos reddere poterit Spectatores. Mittitur ex sinu Patris in mundum, æterna Sapientia, Filius Paternæ dilectionis, Angelorum deliciæ, lux vera Mundi, & vita Hominum, Sol ille Justitiæ, sub cujus alis est Sanitas & Salus, Dominus noster Iesus Christus; Ille persoluto pretio Redemptionis, & debellatis hostibus, Currum triumphalem ascendit, perequitat omnes regiones ubicunque locorum degunt ab ipso redempti; in eorum gratiam tollit vexillum Amoris sui; Emittit vocem Sapientiæ salutiferæ in Euangelio Pacis: per cujus Ministerium miseriarum Fontem ipsis aperit altius, arguit peccati, & dolorem secundum Deum creat: ostentat iram venturam & terrefacit, demonstrat ipsis propriam insipientiam, indignitatem & impotentiam ad eluctandum ex malis, & efficit ut humiliati suas ipsorum Vires & Consilia abnegent: offert fert se Mediatorem ad amicitiae cum Deo redintegrationem, & accendit vitae & justitiae oblatae sitim; offert liberationem à foedere operum, & novi etiam foederis plane gratuiti percussionem, facitque ut consentiant; persuadet ipsis ut Christum, magnum illud donum Dei, amplectantur, ipsique se totos credant: Exhibet iis peccatorum remissionem, & facit ut eam apprehendant ad justitiam: Praecipit justificatis, veteris hominis mortificationem, & accendit non minus serium sincerumque sanctificationis, quam adipiscendae salutis, studium: Requirit fructus fidei in nova Legis divinae obedientia, & facit ut fugant ex vite, vitalem succum, haustumque emittant in fructus dignos Euangelio; jubet ut tollant crucem quisque suam, in via ad Coelum obviam, efficitque ut imperata faciant, & pone Dominum gloriae, portantes ejus opprobrium, per prospera & adversa pergant ad vitam aeternam.
units.tr: Yet the more lamentable this spectacle is, the more lovable is the goodness of God seen in it, which does not suffer the Divine Grace to be rejected by those whom God's good pleasure willed to be his own, so that they might return to a sound mind and be saved. You may call that spectacle joyful, one which can make its spectators blessed for ever. From the bosom of the Father into the world is sent the eternal Wisdom, the Son of the Father's love, the delight of the Angels, the true light of the World and the life of Men, that Sun of Righteousness under whose wings is health and salvation, our Lord Jesus Christ. He, having paid the price of Redemption and overcome the enemies, mounts the triumphal chariot and rides through all regions wherever those redeemed by him dwell; for their sake he raises the banner of his love. He sends forth the voice of saving Wisdom in the Gospel of Peace; through its ministry he opens for them a deeper fountain of miseries, convicts them of sin, and creates godly sorrow; he displays the coming wrath and terrifies them, shows them their own folly, unworthiness and inability to struggle out of evils, and brings it about that, humbled, they renounce their own strength and counsels. He offers himself as Mediator for the restoration of friendship with God, and kindles a thirst for the life and righteousness offered; he offers deliverance from the covenant of works and the embrace of the new covenant, wholly gratuitous, and brings it about that they consent; he persuades them to embrace Christ, the great gift of God, and to entrust themselves wholly to him. He presents to them the remission of sins and causes them to lay hold of it for righteousness; he commands the justified to mortify the old man, and kindles no less a zeal for sanctification than for obtaining salvation, sincere and earnest; he requires the fruits of faith in the new obedience to the divine Law, and brings it about that they draw the living sap from the vine and send forth fruits worthy of the Gospel; he bids each one take up his own cross on the way that leads to heaven, and makes them do what is commanded, and, bearing his reproach, follow the Lord of glory through prosperity and adversity to eternal life.

units.la: Haec est sapientia illa salutaris quae neminem decipit, sed filios suos omnes justificat & beat, viciissimque ab omnibus suis filiis justificatur, asseritur, defenditur. Haec est illa supernè descendens sapientia, quae per sacrarum Scripturarum codicem sparsim diffusa, in ter septem Apostolicis Epistolis plusquam viginti in compendium contracta, ad usum praesentem filiorum lucis accomodatur.
units.tr: This is that saving wisdom which deceives no one, but justifies and blesses all its sons, and in turn is justified, asserted and defended by all its sons. This is that wisdom descending from above, which, poured out sparsely through the codex of the holy Scriptures, has been gathered into a compendium in the seven Apostolic Epistles, more than twenty in number, and is adapted to the present use of the sons of light.

units.la: Harum Epistolarum explicationem in publicum prodire jussi sub nomine tuo, Heros inclyte, ut cum aliis meis Symmistis qui labores suos Honori tuo dedicarunt, persolverem aliquam portiunculam gratitudinis, quam olim debebat illustrissimae tuae Familiae Reformata Ecclesia Scoticana, & etiamnum amplius debet propter te, qui non tantum Stemmatis tui illustrissimi avitam in purgandae religionis studio gloriam renovasti, sed etiam totis septem annis proximè elapsis, cum vitae fortunarumque omnium multiplici periculo, eos labores, qui mediocrium
units.tr: I have been ordered to bring out to the public, under your name, illustrious hero, an exposition of these Epistles, so that, along with my other fellow-ministers who have dedicated their labours to your honour, I might pay some small portion of the gratitude which the Reformed Church of Scotland once owed to your most illustrious family, and still owes more, on account of you, who have not only renewed the ancestral glory of your illustrious lineage in the zeal for purging religion, but also, throughout the seven years just past, amid the manifold danger to life and all fortunes, those labours which the moderate...

units.la: Dedicatoria.
units.tr: Dedicatory.

units.la: crium virorum vires & animos penitus confregissent, exantlando, magnopere auxisti.
units.tr: ...who had utterly broken the strength and spirits of ordinary men by their toil, you have greatly increased.

units.la: Debet tibi hunc Honorem Academia Glasguensis, cui educandos filios tuos generosissimos credidisti, eamque in augendo professorum Theologiæ numero, cum primis Synodi Nationalis Delegatis, Præsentiâ, Consilio, & Authoritate tuâ, semel atque iterum adjuvisti.
units.tr: The Academy of Glasgow owes you this honour, to whose care you entrusted your most noble sons, and whom you have twice helped, by your presence, counsel and authority, especially among the delegates of the National Synod, in increasing the number of professors of Theology.

units.la: Et hic quia Res mea agebatur, nomen meum profiteri parest, quod tu in Tabulas tuas referre poteris, ut debitum exigas à me, quem evectum ad hanc professionis Theologiæ cathedram, tua Authoritas inter præcipuos Synodi Delegatos præscripto penso ad scopum Scripturæ difficilioris studiosis aperiendum, oneravit dicam an honoravit. Quapropter post unum alterumque autumnum, æquum est ut sementis, quam in Academia fecisti, Fructum aliquem ab eâ, & à me, nominatim, recipias.
units.tr: And here, since my own affair is being dealt with, I may declare my name, which you can record in your ledgers, so that you may demand a debt from me, whom your authority, among the chief delegates of the Synod, raised to this chair of Theology and burdened (shall I say honoured?) with the assigned task of opening up the more difficult scope of Scripture to students. Therefore, after one or two autumns, it is fitting that you receive some fruit from the seed you sowed in the Academy, and from me in particular.

units.la: Sed exigua sunt hæc munuscula nostra ad Merita tua, cujus spectata in Pace & in Bello Virtus, probata in utraque Fortuna Fides & quadrata Constantia (quæ nullis tentationibus à dextra vel sinistra in hunc usque diem à Republica Civili & Ecclesiastica promovenda potuit unquam dimoveri) effecerunt ut in omnibus Delegationibus tam Ecclesiasticis quam Politicis Marchionis Argathelia Nomen, Ordinibus Regni & Synodis Nationalibus semper esset, & gratissimum & auspicatissimum: Neque poterit unquam Invidia vel Obloquium sive apertorum hostium, sive parum fidorum amicorum Ecclesiæ & Reipublicæ (qui unà cum asseclis suis & imperitis rerum æstimatoribus, nullis nisi de Republica utraque optimè meritis oblatrare solent) Honorem illum quem meruit Virtus, tribuerunt Comitia Regni & Synodi nationales, vel auferre, vel apud æquos Judices obfuscare.
units.tr: But these little gifts of ours are slight compared with your merits, whose virtue, tested in peace and in war, whose faith proven in both fortunes, and whose steadfast constancy (which no temptations from right or left have been able to move from promoting the civil and ecclesiastical commonwealth to this day) have ensured that in all delegations, both ecclesiastical and political, the name of the Marquis of Argyll was always most welcome and most auspicious to the orders of the kingdom and the National Synods. Nor will envy or detraction, whether from open enemies or from friends of the Church and commonwealth of little trust (who, together with their followers and inexperienced judges of affairs, are wont to bark against those who have deserved well of both commonwealths), ever be able either to take away that honour which virtue has earned from the assemblies of the kingdom and the national synods, or to obscure it before fair judges.

units.la: Epistola Dedicatoria.
units.tr: Dedicatory Epistle.

units.la: TUI vero etiam Nominis facta hic est Mentio, Illustrissima Patris nobilissimi, & optimæ spei Soboles, quia æquum est ut Paternæ Hæreditatis, sic etiam & Honoris te esse Participem. Accedit quod Apostolicæ Doctrinæ præfixum tuum Nomen argumento & incitamento tibi esse poterit, ut Christi Sapientiam & Virtutem, arctius indies amplectaris; Viamque compendiosam quæ in hac ipsius Doctrina tibi præscribitur ad unum illud Necessarium, solidam Felicitatem, patrissans prosequaris: Denique, ut hæc Nominum vestrorum Conjunctio Paternæ & Avitæ Virtutis æmulum te reddat, secundum eam Spem, quam Ingenii tui (qui nondum ex ephebis excessisti) supra ætatem maturitas, genuit in nobis omnibus, qui surgentem ad magna Indolem tuam observamus, votisque, eam prosequimur; ut Familiæ vestræ antiqua Gloria in Te continuetur, & augeatur.
units.tr: Your name is also mentioned here, most illustrious son of a most noble father and of excellent promise, since it is fitting that you share in the honour as well as in the paternal inheritance. Moreover, your name prefixed to this apostolic doctrine may serve as an argument and an incentive to you, that you embrace more closely each day the wisdom and virtue of Christ, and that you pursue, with a father's zeal, the short way prescribed to you in this doctrine toward the one thing necessary, solid happiness. Finally, may this conjunction of your names make you a rival of your father's and grandfather's virtue, in accordance with that hope which the maturity of your mind, rising above your years (you have not yet passed out of boyhood), has begotten in all of us who observe your talent rising toward great things and who follow it with our prayers; so that the ancient glory of your family may be continued and increased in you.

units.la: LECTORI
units.tr: To the Reader

units.la: LECTORI S.
units.tr: To the Reader

units.la: HAbent omnes Disciplinæ suas Isagogas, & Rudimenta faciliora, quibus discentium Ingenia ad penitiorem rerum Cognitionem præparentur: Habent omnes Familiæ Nobiliores suos Janitores, & Servos Atrienses, qui Hospites excipiant, & in Palatiorum penetralia humaniter deducant: Vt habeat etiam Scripturarum explicatio suam Introductionem, & Commentatorum Nobilis Familia suos Ostiarios, & Servos Atrienses, æquum esse juxta mecum judicabis spero, Lector æquanime: Huic familiæ ut inservirem, & simul introducendis sacri Ministerii Candidatis, ad opulentiores in DEI Familia peni Procuratores, operam meam collocarem, in domus Dei limine mihi sedem elegi.
units.tr: All disciplines have their introductions and easier rudiments, by which the minds of learners are prepared for a deeper knowledge of the subject. All noble families have their gatekeepers and servants of the entrance hall, who receive guests and courteously lead them into the inner recesses of the palace. So also the explanation of the Scriptures should have its introduction, and a noble family of commentators its doorkeepers and servants of the entrance hall. I hope, calm reader, that you will judge it fair that I, in order to serve this family and at the same time to bring candidates for the sacred ministry to the richer stewards of the household of God, have chosen for myself a place on the threshold of the house of God.

units.la: Vulgò notum est in Scholis Theologicis, quantulo tempore, quot & quanta Volumina perlegenda; quot & quæ exercitia parasceuastica adolescentibus Theologiæ studiosis absolvenda sint; & in distributione sive dierum sive horarum, ad singula studia, quantillum temporis Scripturis Divinis cedat perlustrandis, in quibus intelligendis maximè laborandum esset omnibus, præsertim verò iis qui Dominum ipsum loquentem audire vellent ut credant, & ut quæ crediderunt,
units.tr: It is commonly known in the theological schools how little time is given to reading through so many and such great volumes, how many and what preparatory exercises young students of theology must complete, and how little time, in the distribution of days or hours among the individual studies, is left for going through the divine Scriptures, which all should labour most to understand, and especially those who wish to hear the Lord himself speaking, so that they may believe, and so that what they have believed...

units.la: Epistola
units.tr: Epistle

units.la: tanquam eloquia DEI, pro concione proferunt. Huiusmodi nobilibus Beroensibus, Scripturarum discipulis quicunque operam dabit promovendis, ne ille opera sua pretium non perdet.
units.tr: as the very words of God, they set them forth in preaching. To such noble Bereans, disciples of the Scriptures, whoever takes pains to advance, may his labour not go unrewarded.

units.la: In eorum gratiam qui apud nos Student Theologiae, ex authoritate Delegatorum Synodi nationalis, duobus proxime praeteritis annis, publice praelegi omnium Apostolicarum Epistolarum analyticam expositionem, & praelecta licet rudiora, ut novorum hospitum, in iis describendis labori parcerem, typis commisi: consilii que mei rationes candide tibi, ut aequicrem te experiar, statui explicare.
units.tr: For the sake of those among us who study theology, by the authority of the Delegates of the National Synod, I committed to print, for the two years just past, the analytical exposition of all the Apostolic Epistles, which I had lectured on publicly. I did this so that new students might be spared the labour of copying out the lectures, though they are rather rough. I have also resolved to explain candidly the reasons for my plan, so that I may try to be fair to you.

units.la: Studiosis Adolescentibus quibus lectio Scripturarum est necessaria, Commentariorum vero pleniorum lectio impossibilis est, paranda erat ex officio meo aliqua ad pleniores Commentarios postea legendos cum per otium liceret, introductio. In qua requirebatur explicatio Scopi, & Verborum Textus obscuriorum, & sententiarum difficiliorum, & connexionis earum inter se, & cum scopo principali. Et hic opus erat analysi, scholiis & expositione vel paraphrasi aliqua, quae expositionis vicem supleret. Ad institutam introductionem & explicationem, adeo essentialis erat brevitas, ut non omnino suscep tam esse, quam non esse brevem expediret; nam nisi brevitatis spes fuisset, ea non omnino fuisset. Cum brevitate explicationis, necessaria erat perspicuitas, ne multarum rerum in pauciora verba concisa contractio Lectorem implicaret.
units.tr: Young students who need to read Scripture, but cannot manage to read the fuller commentaries, needed from me, as part of my office, some introduction to be read afterwards in fuller commentaries when there was leisure. In it, an explanation was required of the scope, of the obscure words of the text and the more difficult sentences, and of how these connect with one another and with the main scope. Here there was need of analysis, scholia, and some exposition or paraphrase to take the place of a full exposition. For the introduction and explanation I had in mind, brevity was so essential that it was worth attempting, since without the hope of brevity the work would not have been undertaken at all. Along with brevity, clarity was necessary, so that the compression of many matters into fewer words would not entangle the reader.

units.la: Analysin igitur, & Scholia, & expositionem, vel paraphrasin expositionis loco positam (quae seorsim singula sine prolixitate disponi non poterant) in unum quasi compegi, ut finem mihi propositum assequerer. Verum an aliqua saltem ex parte assequutus sim, penes te judicium esto, postquam comparata cum textu explicatione, quae quibus respondeant, perspexeris. Tantum istud scito, quod multo minori labore hanc explicationem tibi dedisses longiorem, quam dedi brevem. Analysin Logicam non sum ulterius prosequutus, quam necesse erat ad scopum textus demonstrandum: membratim enim & minutatim singulas sententias, deartuare prolixioris est commentarii. Logica Technologemata, quae dicuntur, non nisi parcissime adhibui, quia si adhibuissem, statim videbam creari litem mihi, & laborem tibi, qui facilius rem ipsam intelligeres, quam an termini artis recte a me assignati essent examinares; & mecum de re ipsa consentires potius, quam in Logicis notionibus assignandis subscriberes. Sua enim unicuique diversa est analysios ratio, ita ut difficulter reperias duos scriptores, qui vel in unius quidem capitis resolutione, in terminis Logicis omnibus consentiant, etiam cum inter ipsos de ipsa
units.tr: So I have pulled together, as it were into one piece, the analysis, the scholia, and the exposition or paraphrase put in place of exposition (which could not be arranged separately, item by item, without prolixity), so that I might reach the aim I had set myself. Whether I have reached it, at least in some part, is for you to judge, once you have compared the explanation with the text and seen which parts correspond to which. Know only this: you would have spent much less labour on a longer explanation than I have on this brief one. I have not pursued the logical analysis further than was needed to demonstrate the scope of the text. To go through each sentence piece by piece and limb by limb belongs to a longer commentary. I have used the so-called logical technicalities only very sparingly, because had I used them, I saw at once that a quarrel would arise for me, and labour for you, since you would rather understand the matter itself than examine whether I had assigned the technical terms correctly, and would agree with me about the thing itself rather than subscribe to my assignment of logical notions. For each person's method of analysis is different, so that you would find it hard to find two writers who agree on all the logical terms, even in the resolution of a single chapter, and this even when they are in dispute among themselves about the very

units.la: { } — none
units.tr: { } — none

units.la: Lectori.
units.tr: To the Reader.

units.la: de sensu maximè conveniret. Nam pro vario argumenti respectu ad subjectum & attributum propositionis probandæ, mutantur, & salvo loci sensu mutari debent notiones Logicæ. Præcepta & hortationes quæ in modo imperativo, vel alio aliquo modo Rhetorico emphatice proponuntur, in modum indicativum, secundum præcepta Logicæ converti, ut thesis confirmanda clarius perspiceretur. Emphasin & prudentiam Spiritus, plenioribus commentariis & concionibus explicandam reliqui. Singulorum capitum partes, memoriæ tuæ juvandæ causa, & theses præcipuas in singulis partibus, quantum pati potuit rei veritas, paucissimas feci. Argumenta ad confirmationem propositionis illius quæ scopum exprimit, prout ad perspicuitatem faciebat, numeravi plura aut pauciora: argumentorum plurium vim, nunc in unum contrahens, nunc sigillatim explicans.
units.tr: ...would most fittingly agree with the sense. For, according to the varying relation of the subject to the predicate of the proposition to be proved, the logical terms must change, and they ought to change while the meaning of the passage is preserved. Precepts and exhortations that are stated emphatically in the imperative, or in some other rhetorical mode, I have converted into the indicative according to the rules of logic, so that the thesis to be confirmed might be seen more clearly. I have left the emphasis and the wisdom of the Spirit to be explained in fuller commentaries and sermons. To help your memory, I have made the parts of each chapter, and the principal theses in each part, as few as the truth of the matter allowed. I have numbered more or fewer arguments for the confirmation of the proposition that expresses the scope, as clarity required: sometimes condensing the force of several arguments into one, sometimes explaining them one by one.

units.la: Argumenta quæ & ad scopum præcipuum, & ad proximè præcedens argumentum confirmandum faciunt, ad utrumque retuli. Omnia verò enthymematicè, brevitatis & perspicuitatis causa disposui. Si sæpius quam opus erat scopus, seu conclusio repeti videatur, ignosces mihi spero hunc laborem, ubi consultò suppressam à me conclusionem perspexeris facilius legi quam ex superioribus repeti potuisse. Licet prima facie coincidere videantur argumenta: statim observabis tamen novam aliquam vim ab Apostolo additam, facere discrimen. Nec te offendat quod argumenta quæ ego ad confirmationem alicujus propositionis retuli, adhibeantur à Doctis ad alias conclusiones probandas: Idem enim medium pluribus conclusionibus confirmandis commodè potuit inservire. Ubi obvius est versiculorum sensus, & connexio plana, hac mea opella (quæ in obscurioribus potissimum usum habet) non opus erat: sed ne hiatus esset ullus, opus pertexi, & homogeneum esse opportuit. Qui hoc concisum scribendi genus non probat, ne alios à legendo deterreat quæso. Si ostiolum Studiosis Theologiæ aperuerit ad pleniores commentarios, introductio hæc nostra, habeo quod quæro. Clavis quo minoris fuerit molis tanto majoris solet æstimari. In tanta scriptorum varietate, & copia, Reip. consultum it, qui vel necessaria bene, vel breviter saltem tractat, ut Lector operâ & olei, quam fieri potest, minimum perdat.
units.tr: Arguments that serve to confirm both the main scope and the argument immediately preceding, I have referred to both. I have arranged all of them in enthymematic form, for the sake of brevity and clarity. If the scope, or conclusion, seems to be repeated more often than necessary, I hope you will forgive this labour; when you notice that I have deliberately left out a conclusion, you will find it easier to read than it would have been to repeat it from what went before. Although the arguments may at first sight seem to coincide, you will at once observe that some new force added by the Apostle makes the difference. Nor should it trouble you that arguments which I have cited for the confirmation of one proposition are used by learned men to prove other conclusions: the same middle term can well serve to confirm many conclusions. Where the sense of the verses is plain and the connection obvious, this little work of mine (which is chiefly useful for the more obscure passages) was not needed; but so that there might be no gap, I had to carry the work through, and it was fitting that it should be uniform. I beg those who do not approve of this concise manner of writing not to be deterred from reading the rest on that account. If this introduction of ours opens a little door for students of theology to the fuller commentaries, I have what I sought. The smaller a key is in bulk, the more it is usually valued in proportion to its use. Amid such a variety and abundance of writings, the republic of letters is well served by the author who treats what is necessary either well or at least briefly, so that the reader loses as little labour and midnight oil as possible.

units.la: Si Tibi gratus fuerit hic labor meus, non ingrata mihi erit admonitio tui, si quid emendatum vis. Et si quid consilii mihi suggerere visum fuerit prudentiæ tuæ: Dabo operam, juvante Deo, ut in versione Anglicana ad quam hortantur amici nonnulli, si id operæ pretium futurum comperietur, ut tibi satisfiat. Interim Patrem luminum supplex oro, ut in hanc messem emittat doctiores
units.tr: If this labour of mine is pleasing to you, your correction will not be unwelcome to me, should you wish anything to be amended. And if you think fit to suggest any counsel to me in your wisdom, I will take care, God helping, to make it satisfactory to you in the English version that some friends urge me to produce, should it be found worthwhile. Meanwhile I humbly pray the Father of lights to send more learned men into this harvest...

units.la: Epistola Lectori.
units.tr: To the Reader.

units.la: doctiores, & magis idoneos servos suos, qui quod à me præstari nequit, in hoc genere scribendi præstetur. Spes enim est fore ut permulti, qui nunc sola prolixitate commentariorum deterriti, vel nihil vel pauca, & exiguo cum fructu legunt, Scripturas legerent avidius, si breviculi aliquid ad scopum sensumque aperiendum ipsis offerretur. Valę.
units.tr: more learned and more fitting servants of his own, who may accomplish in this kind of writing what I cannot. For there is hope that very many, who now, deterred by the sheer length of commentaries, read little or nothing, and with little profit, would read the Scriptures more eagerly, if some small summary were offered them to open up the aim and sense. Farewell.

units.la: Tuæ Ædificationis & Salutis in CHRISTO Studiosus Da. Dicsonus.
units.tr: Yours, eager for your edification and salvation in Christ, D. Dickson.

units.la: EXPOSITIO
units.tr: EXPOSITION

units.la: EXPOSITIO ANALYTICA EPISTOLAE PAULI AD ROMANOS; Summarium.
units.tr: EXPOSITIO ANALYTICA EPISTOLAE PAULI AD ROMANOS; Summarium.

units.la: STatuebat Apostolus Romanos invisere, ut viva voce ipsos in fide confirmaret. Interim dum netti sibi longiores moras indies observat, à Spiritu Domini excitatus, celeberrimam bancad eos scribit Epistolam.
units.tr: The Apostle intended to visit the Romans, so that he might confirm them in the faith by the living voice. Meanwhile, while he observed from day to day that longer delays were being imposed on him, roused by the Spirit of the Lord, he wrote to them this most celebrated letter.

units.la: Partes Epistolae, praeter exordium & conclusionem, statui possunt duae. Prima docet divinam & unicam rationem justificandi peccatores, per fidem in Iesum Christum: ad caput duodecimum.
units.tr: The parts of the Epistle, apart from the introduction and conclusion, may be set out as two. The first teaches the divine and only way of justifying sinners through faith in Jesus Christ; it runs to the twelfth chapter.

units.la: Altera praecipit de vita justificatorum sanctè instituenda ad finem.
units.tr: The second instructs how those who are justified should lead a holy life, to the end.

units.la: Quod ad primam attinet. Statim post epistolae exordium, probandum sibi suscipit Apostolus; Neminem ex operibus seu inhaerente justitia justificari posse, sed ex justitia Christi solâ, per fidem solam à nobis apprehensâ, & gratis ex gratia nobis credentibus à Deo imputata.
units.tr: As for the first part: immediately after the introduction to the Epistle, the Apostle undertakes to prove that no one can be justified by works, that is, by inherent righteousness, but only by the righteousness of Christ, apprehended by us through faith alone, and imputed by God freely, out of grace, to us who believe.

units.la: Hanc Thesin probat argumentis decem plus minus: Quorum duo priora habentur Capite primo; Tertium Capite secundo, septem reliqui Capite tertio.
units.tr: He proves this thesis by about ten arguments: of these, the first two are found in the first chapter; the third in the second chapter; the remaining seven in the third chapter.

units.la: Ad haec argumenta altius infigenda, subnexit hujus suae doctrinae sextuplicem confirmationem.
units.tr: To fix these arguments more deeply, he adds a sixfold confirmation of this doctrine of his.

units.la: Prima est, Quod Abraham sola fide justificatus sit, Capite quarto.
units.tr: The first is that Abraham was justified by faith alone; chapter four.

units.la: Secunda est, quod haec justificandi ratio sola consolationem praestet adversus justam Dei iram, & peccati originalis, ab Adamo in nos derivati venenum. Capite quinto.
units.tr: The second is that this manner of justification alone brings consolation against the just wrath of God and against the poison of original sin, derived into us from Adam; chapter five.

units.la: Tertia est, quod haec justificationis ratio ad promovendam in justificatis sanctimoniam maximè conducat, Capite Sexto.
units.tr: The third is that this manner of justification contributes most of all to promoting holiness in those who are justified; chapter six.

units.la: Quarta est, quod haec justificandi ratio sola consolationem praebeat justificatorum conscientiis afflictis propter imperfectam suam obedientiam & peccati inhabitantis in se reliquias, capite septimo,
units.tr: The fourth is that this manner of justifying alone offers consolation to the afflicted consciences of the justified, on account of their imperfect obedience and the remnants of indwelling sin in them; chapter seven.

units.la: Summarium.
units.tr: Summary.

units.la: Quinta est, quod hæc justificandi ratio justificatos sanctitati studentes, non solum muniat adversus condemnationem, sed malum omne post hanc vitam metuendum; sed etiam adversus omnes molestias, quibus obnoxii sunt Dei filii in hac vita solidè confirmet & consoletur, Capite octavo.
units.tr: The fifth reason is that this method of justification not only fortifies the justified who strive after holiness against condemnation and every evil to be feared after this life, but also firmly confirms and comforts them against all the troubles to which the sons of God are subject in this life, chapter eight.

units.la: Sexta confirmatio est, quod experientia compertum sit Judæos quærentes justitiam ex operibus, justificationem minimè consequutos fuisse; Gentes verò omni specie inhærentis justitiæ destitutas, per fidem in Iesum Christum, veram & salutiferam justitiam obtinuisse, Capite nono: ubi ex occasione repudiationis Judæorum de Electione & Reprobatione agitur.
units.tr: The sixth confirmation is that experience has shown that the Jews, seeking righteousness from works, did not attain justification, whereas the Gentes, destitute of every kind of inherent righteousness, obtained through faith in Jesus Christ a true and saving righteousness: chapter nine, where, on the occasion of the rejection of the Jews, election and reprobation are discussed.

units.la: Quorum Judæorum rejectionem apertam & apud omnes Ecclesias jam manifestam propter ipsorum factam incredulitatem & pertinaciam, justam esse probat, Capite decimo.
units.tr: He proves that the open rejection of that people, now manifest among all the Churches because of their own unbelief and obstinacy, is just: chapter ten.

units.la: Non tamen propterea desperiendos esse omnes Judæos, eò quod Gentis illius repudiatio ad tempus tantùm duratura sit, ostendit, Capite undecimo.
units.tr: He shows that nevertheless not all Jews are to be despaired of, since the rejection of that nation will last only for a time: chapter eleven.

units.la: Altera Epistolæ parte, quæ præcipit de Justificatorum vita sanctè instituenda. Primo, post obtestationem seriam, ut omnes justificati totos se Deo consecrent, & omnes Ecclesiæ Ministri pacem inter se colentes, pro suo quisque munere & dono, sanctificationem & salutem fidelium promoveant; Præcepta dat generalia de sanctimonia Capite duodecimo.
units.tr: The second part of the Epistle, which teaches how the life of the justified is to be rightly ordered. First, after a earnest entreaty that all the justified devote themselves wholly to God, and that all the ministers of the Church, cultivating peace among themselves, each in his own office and gift, promote the sanctification and salvation of the faithful, he gives general precepts concerning holiness: chapter twelve.

units.la: Secundo descendit specialius ad officia fidelium erga magistratum, & omnis ordinis proximos, secundum legem charitatis præstanda, Capite decimotertio.
units.tr: Second, he descends more particularly to the duties which the faithful owe to the magistrate and to neighbours of every rank, to be performed according to the law of charity: chapter thirteen.

units.la: Tertio agit de Fidelium officiis mutuis, ad prudentem usum Christianæ Libertatis spectantibus, Capite decimoquarto, & priori parte Capitis decimiquinti.
units.tr: Third, he treats of the mutual duties of the faithful, which pertain to the prudent use of Christian liberty: chapter fourteen, and the first part of chapter fifteen.

units.la: Denique, confirmata sua in Romanos benevolentia & autoritate reliqua parte capitis decimiquinti, cum Sanctorum salutationibus, concludit epistolam, Capite decimosexto.
units.tr: Finally, having confirmed his goodwill and authority toward the Romans, he concludes the epistle with the rest of chapter fifteen, together with the greetings of the saints: chapter sixteen.

units.la: Caput primum.
units.tr: Chapter 1.

units.la: Vjus Capitis duæ sunt partes: Prima continet totius Epistolæ exordium, ad versum decimumseptimum: Altera est inchoata probatio principalis propositionis per totam epistolam confirmandæ, nempe quod justificemur per fidem in Iesum Christum, & non ex operibus.
units.tr: The chapter has two parts. The first contains the exordium of the whole Epistle, up to verse 17. The second is the beginning of the main proof, to be confirmed throughout the Epistle, namely that we are justified through faith in Jesus Christ, and not by works.

units.la: Exordium constat Epistolæ inscriptione ad versum octavum, & proœmiali sermone, ad versum decimumseptimum; totumque comparatum est ad præparationem fidelium Romanorum, ut cum omni animi submissione & benevolentia, doctrinam subsequentem subsequentem recipiant. Qui scopus hoc vel simili aliquo, in eundem sensum, axiomate comprehendi potest. Debetis vos Romani cum omni animi submissione & benevolentia subsequentem doctrinam recipere. Argumenta in hunc finem insinuat octodecem, quorum aliqui in Epistolae inscriptione, reliqua in prooemiali sermone continentur.
units.tr: The exordium consists of the inscription of the Epistle, to verse 8, and a introductory discourse, to verse 17. The whole is designed to prepare the faithful Romans to receive the following doctrine with all submission of mind and goodwill. This aim can be summed up in this or a similar maxim to the same effect: You Romans ought to receive the doctrine that follows with all submission of mind and goodwill. He suggests eighteen arguments to this end, some of which are contained in the inscription of the Epistle and the rest in the introductory discourse.

units.la: Versus primus.
units.tr: Verse 1.

units.la: Paulus servus Iesu Christi, ex vocatione Apostolus, separatus ad praedicandum Euangelium Dei.
units.tr: Paul, a servant of Jesus Christ, called to be an apostle, set apart to preach the gospel of God.

units.la: IN Epistolae inscriptione descriptio est Scriptoris ad versum septimum & eorum ad quos scribitur, versu septimo.
units.tr: In the inscription of the Epistle there is a description of the writer, in verse 1, and of those to whom he writes, in verse 7.

units.la: Argumentum primum, Ego Paulus scriptor hujus ad vos Epistolae, servus sum Iesu Christi, id est, non meam, sed Domini nostri Iesu Christi tem ago sincere, ipsique servitii mei reddituros sum rationem; Idcirco debetis vos Romani quae scribo in hac Epistola cum omni animi submissione, & benevolentia recipere.
units.tr: The first argument: I, Paul, the writer of this Epistle to you, am a servant of Jesus Christ, that is, I do the work sincerely, not for myself but for our Lord Jesus Christ, and I shall render an account of my service to him. Therefore you Romans ought to receive what I write in this Epistle with all submission and goodwill.

units.la: Secundum argumentum, Vocatione sum Apostolus, id est, servus extra ordinem, qui tanquam legatus, cum mandatis missus sum a Christo ad praedicandum Euangelium, accepta potestate ad fundandas & regendas Ecclesias, quod munus non ipse invasi, sed immediate a Deo vocatus suscepi. Idcirco debetis cum omni animi submissione admittere quae scripsi ad vos.
units.tr: The second argument: I am an apostle by calling, that is, a servant outside the ordinary order, who, as an envoy sent with commissions by Christ to preach the gospel, have received authority to found and govern churches. I did not seize this office myself, but took it up as one called directly by God. Therefore you ought with all submission to admit what I have written to you.

units.la: Tertium argumentum, Separatus sum ad Euangelium Dei, id est, ex Dei consilio destinatus, ut huic uni officio totus incumberem, ab utero sanctificatus, Galat. 1. 15. speciali Christi auctoritate designatus, & oraculo Spiritus (ut est, Act. 13. verf. 2.) separatus, & ablegatus ad praedicandum vobis Gentibus laetum nuncium de redemptione hominum per Christum. Idcirco debetis cum omni reverentia & benevolentia recipere quae scripsi ad vos.
units.tr: The third argument: I am set apart for the gospel of God, that is, appointed by God's counsel to devote myself wholly to this one office, sanctified from the womb (Gal. 1:15), designated by the special authority of Christ, and set apart and sent out to preach to you Gentiles the joyful news of the redemption of men through Christ, by the oracle of the Spirit (as in Acts 13:2). Therefore you ought to receive with reverence and goodwill what I have written to you.

units.la: Verf. 2. (Quod ante promiserat per Prophetas suos in Scripturis sanctis.)
units.tr: Verse 2. (which he had promised beforehand through his prophets in the holy Scriptures.)

units.la: Quartum argumentum, Euangelium quod ego praedico, non est novum, non commentitium, sed antiquissimum illud Dei verbum, quod porro revelandum Deus promisit jam olim per Prophetas suos, sicut in sacra Scriptura veteris Testamenti legendum proponitur. Idcirco debetis cum omni animi submissione amplecti subsequentem doctrinam.
units.tr: The fourth argument: the gospel which I preach is not new, not invented, but that most ancient word of God, which God promised long ago through his prophets to reveal further, as is set forth to be read in the sacred Scripture of the Old Testament. Therefore you ought with all submission to embrace the following doctrine.

units.la: Verf. 3. De Filio suo, (facto ex semine Davidis, secundum carnem.
units.tr: Verse 3. Concerning his Son, (made of the seed of David according to the flesh.

units.la: Verf. 4. Declarato Filio Dei potenter secundum Spiritum sanctitatis, per resurrectionem a mortuis) nempe Iesu Christo Domino nostro.
units.tr: Verse 4. Declared to be the Son of God with power according to the Spirit of holiness, by the resurrection from the dead) namely, Jesus Christ our Lord.

units.la: Quintum argumentum, Materia Euangelii quod ego praedico, non est res aliqua vilis seu vulgaris, sed ipse Dei Filius IESUS CHRISTUS Dominus noster, homo-Deus, in unitate personae simul vere homo, conceptus a Spiritu sancto, ex substantia Virginis Mariae, a Davide Rege oriundae secundum carnem, seu humanam ipsius naturam: simul vere Deus, ut per alia multa signa, sic per resurrectionem a mortuis potissimum declaratus definite Filius Dei potentissimus, secundum divinam ipsius naturam, quae Spiritus dicitur summe sanctus, 1 Tim. 3. 16. & 1 Pet. 3. 18. Ideo debetis cum reverentia & benevolentia doctrinam subsequentem recipere.
units.tr: The fifth argument: the subject matter of the gospel which I preach is not some cheap or common thing, but the Son of God himself, Jesus Christ our Lord, God-man, who in the unity of person is at once truly man, conceived by the Holy Spirit of the substance of the Virgin Mary, descended from King David according to the flesh, that is, his human nature; and at the same time truly God, who, as declared by many other signs, was above all declared by the resurrection from the dead to be the Son of God with power, according to his divine nature, which is called the Spirit of supreme holiness (1 Tim. 3:16; 1 Pet. 3:18). Therefore you ought to receive the following doctrine with reverence and goodwill.

units.la: Verf. 5. (Per quem accepimus gratiam & apostolatum ad obedientiam fidei, inter omnes gentes, pro ipsius nomine.)
units.tr: Verse 5. (Through whom we have received grace and apostleship, to bring about obedience of faith among all nations, for the sake of his name.)

units.la: Sextum argumentum, Eo ipso fine, a CHRISTO gloriosum munus apostolatus gratuito concessum est aliis apostolis & mihi, ut pro auctoritate, quam CHRISTUS habet & nobis fecit, procuraremus inter omnes gentes, salutarem illam obedientiam, quae fidei doctrinae debetur: Idcirco debetis cum omni animi submissione Euangelii doctrinam hanc admittere.
units.tr: The sixth argument: for this very end, the glorious office of apostleship has been freely granted by Christ to the other apostles and to me, so that by the authority which Christ has and has given to us, we might bring about among all nations that saving obedience which is owed to the doctrine of faith. Therefore you ought with all submission of mind to admit this doctrine of the gospel.

units.la: Verf. 6. Inter quas estis etiam vos vocati a Iesu Christo:)
units.tr: Verse 6. Among whom you also are called by Jesus Christ:)

units.la: Septimum argumentum. Inter has gentes ad quas ego missus sum, vos fideles Romani primas tenetis, quippe qui jam efficaciter ab ipso Christo vocati, ipsique in obedientiam fidei jam mancipati estis. Idcirco debetis cum omni animi submissione Euangelii doctrinam hanc admittere.
units.tr: The seventh argument: among these nations to which I have been sent, you faithful Romans hold the first place, since you have already been effectually called by Christ himself and have already been bound over to the obedience of faith. Therefore you ought with all submission of mind to admit this doctrine of the gospel.

units.la: Verf. 7. Omnibus qui Romae estis, dilecti Dei, ex Dei vocatione sanctis: Gratia sit vobis & pax a Deo Patre nostro, & Domino Iesu Christo.
units.tr: Verse 7. To all who are in Rome, beloved of God, called to be saints: Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.

units.la: Restat in Epistolae inscriptione descriptio & salutatio eorum ad quos scribit, in quibus continetur argumentum octavum, in hunc sensum.
units.tr: There remains in the inscription of the Epistle the description and greeting of those to whom he writes, in which the eighth argument is contained, to this effect.

units.la: Vos dilecti estis a Deo, efficaciter vocati, & ex parte sanctificati, & haeredes gratiae & pacis: ita ut liceat mihi Dei nomine Euangelii benedictionem
units.tr: You are beloved of God, effectually called, and in part sanctified, and heirs of grace and peace; so that it is permitted to me, in the name of God, to pronounce the blessing of the gospel

units.la: Caput primum.
units.tr: Chapter 1.

units.la: [?]ationem vobis applicare, & vobis comprecari Gratiam (id est, omnia bona quae per modum sanctificationis à Dei favore speciali proveniunt) & Pacem (id est, omnia, quae ad felicitatem sive in hac, sive in futura vita faciunt) à Deo per Christi mediationem in vos derivanda. Idcirco debetis cum omni benevolentia doctrinae meae auscultare.
units.tr: to bestow on you the blessing, and to wish for you, Grace (that is, all the good things that come to us through sanctification from God's special favour) and Peace (that is, all the things that contribute to happiness, both in this life and in the life to come), to be derived from God through Christ's mediation. Therefore you ought to listen to my teaching with all goodwill.

units.la: Verf. 8. Trimum quidem gratias ago Deo meo per Iesum Christum super omnibus vobis, quod fides vestra annuntiatur in toto mundo.
units.tr: Verse 8. First, I thank my God through Jesus Christ for you all, because your faith is proclaimed throughout the whole world.

units.la: Reliquis exordii versibus habetur sermo proœmialis in eundem scopum.
units.tr: The remaining verses of the opening contain a introductory discourse aimed at the same purpose.

units.la: Nonum argumentum, Toto terrarum orbe celebratur fama fidei vestrae, quam Euangelio adhibetis, de quo equidem gaudeo, & Deo per Mediatorem pro vobis omnibus gratias ago. Idcirco debetis cum omni benevolentia Euangelio meo attendere.
units.tr: Ninth argument: The fame of your faith, which you hold in the Gospel, is celebrated throughout the whole world. I rejoice at this, and through the Mediator I give thanks to God for all of you. Therefore you ought to attend to my Gospel with all goodwill.

units.la: Verf. 9. Testis enim mihi est Deus, quem colo spiritu meo in Euangelio Filii ipsius, me sine intermissione mentionem facere vestri.
units.tr: Verse 9. For God is my witness, whom I serve in my spirit in the Gospel of his Son, that I make mention of you without ceasing.

units.la: Argumentum decimum, Cura quam gero vestrae salutis, studiumque quo feror in bonum vestrum, nunquam finit me vestri immemorem esse in precibus meis: quod quia aliter vobis probari nequit, testem invoco Deum, qui quam sincero corde in ministerio Euangelii Filii sui ipsi serviam, ipse optime novit. Idcirco debetis scribenti mihi ad vos, vicem reddere.
units.tr: Tenth argument: The care I take for your salvation and the zeal with which I am carried toward your good never let me forget you in my prayers. Since this cannot be proved to you in any other way, I call God to witness, who knows best how sincerely I serve him with my whole heart in the ministry of the Gospel of his Son. Therefore you ought to repay me in kind, as I write to you.

units.la: Verf. 10. Semper in orationibus meis rogantem, si quomodo tandem aliquando prosperum itur mihi detur ex voluntate Dei, ut veniam ad vos.
units.tr: Verse 10. always in my prayers making request, if by any means now at length I might have a prosperous journey by the will of God to come unto you.

units.la: Argumentum undecimum, Ut vobis prosim non tantum proficiscendi ad vos laborem non refugio, sed etiam precibus enixe à Deo flagito, ut prosperum tandem mihi faciat iter ad vos, cum ipsi visum fuerit. Idcirco debetis cum benevolentia auscultare.
units.tr: Eleventh argument: That I may be of use to you, I not only do not shy from the labour of travelling to you, but also earnestly beg God in my prayers to make my journey to you prosperous at last, when it seems good to him. Therefore you ought to listen with goodwill.

units.la: Verf. 11. Expeto enim videre vos, ut aliquod impertiar vobis donum spirituale, ut vos stabiliamini.
units.tr: Verse 11. For I long to see you, that I may impart unto you some spiritual gift, to the end ye may be established.

units.la: Argumentum duodecimum, Summo desiderio teneor vos invisendi, non ut participem de facultatibus vestris, sed ut communicem vobis pleniorem cognitionem mysterii Euangelii, tanquam donum spirituale, quo in fide contra omnes tentationes stabiliamini. Idcirco debetis cum benevolentia hanc doctrinam admittere.
units.tr: Twelfth argument: I am held by the greatest desire to visit you, not to share in your resources, but to communicate to you a fuller knowledge of the mystery of the Gospel, as a spiritual gift by which you may be established in faith against all temptations. Therefore you ought to receive this teaching with goodwill.

units.la: Epist. ad Romanos;
units.tr: Epistle to the Romans;

units.la: Verf. 12. Hoc est, ad communem exhortationem percipiendam apud vos, per mutuam fidem, vestram simul & meam.
units.tr: Verse 12. That is, that I may be comforted together with you by the mutual faith both of you and me.

units.la: Hoc argumentum explicat, ne arroganter dictum videretur, modeste significans se non minus paratum esse consolationem & ædificationem ex eorum fide capere, quam ex sua, ipsis præbere.
units.tr: He explains this argument so that it might not seem said arrogantly, modestly indicating that he is no less ready to receive comfort and edification from their faith than to offer his own to them.

units.la: Verf. 13. Nolim autem vos ignorare fratres, me sæpe proposuisse venire ad vos, sed prohibitus fui usque adhuc, ut fructum aliquem haberem inter vos quoque, sic ut inter reliquos Gentes.
units.tr: Verse 13. Now I would not have you ignorant, brethren, that I often purposed to come unto you, (but was let hitherto,) that I might have some fruit among you also, even as among other Gentiles.

units.la: Argumentum decimumtertium, Licet hactenus impeditus sim ne ad vos venirem, sæpe tamen post objecta impedimenta, propositum ad vos veniendi denuo suscepi, ut prædicatione Euangelii non tantum vos confirmarem in fide & obedientia Euangelii, sed etiam aliquos inter vos converterem ad fidem, sicut inter alias gentes DEO aliquos lucratus sum. Idcirco debetis doctrinæ meæ auscultare.
units.tr: Thirteenth argument: Although I have hitherto been hindered from coming to you, nevertheless, after the obstacles were put in the way, I have often again taken up the purpose of coming to you, so that by preaching the Gospel I might not only confirm you in faith and in obedience to the Gospel, but also convert some of you to the faith, just as I have won some to God among the other nations. Therefore you ought to listen to my teaching.

units.la: Verf. 14. Et Græcis & barbaris tum sapientibus tum insipientibus debitor sum.
units.tr: Verse 14. I am debtor both to the Greeks, and to the Barbarians; both to the wise, and to the unwise.

units.la: Decimumquartum argumentum, Ex officio apostolatus, & speciali mandato CHRISTI teneor omnis generis hominibus, tanquam debitor Euangelium annunciare. Idcirco debetis doctrinæ meæ auscultare.
units.tr: Fourteenth argument: By the duty of my apostleship and by the special command of Christ, I am bound, as a debtor, to proclaim the Gospel to men of every kind. Therefore you ought to listen to my teaching.

units.la: Verf. 15. Itaque quicquid in me situm est, promptum est ad vos etiam qui Romæ estis, euangelizandum.
units.tr: Verse 15. So, as much as in me is, I am ready to preach the gospel to you that are at Rome also.

units.la: Argumentum decimumquintum, Propensa in vos Romanos voluntate feror, & pro facultate mihi divinitus concessa, quantum ad meas partes attinet, non minus vobis cum aliis Euangelium prædicare, ad salutem vestram paratus sum. Idcirco debetis doctrinæ meæ auscultare.
units.tr: Fifteenth argument: I am carried by a favourable will toward you Romans, and, as far as my part goes, with the ability granted me by God, I am ready to preach the Gospel to you for your salvation no less than to others. Therefore you ought to listen to my teaching.

units.la: Verf. 16. Non enim me pudet Euangelij Christi: potentia siquidem est Dei ad salutem cuivis credenti, Judæo primùm, tum etiam Græco.
units.tr: Verse 16. For I am not ashamed of the gospel of Christ: for it is the power of God unto salvation to every one that believeth; to the Jew first, and also to the Greek.

units.la: Decimumsextum argumentum, Etiamsi Euangelium quod ego prædico vulgò contemnatur, & cum cruce conjungatur, quoniam tamen non meum, sed CHRISTI est Euangelium, gratiam quæ per eum nobis facta
units.tr: Sixteenth argument: Even if the Gospel which I preach is commonly despised and is joined with the cross, nevertheless, since the Gospel is not mine but Christ's, explaining the grace which has been made ours through him, it is honourable and glorious, and I am by no means ashamed of it.

units.la: {y} Pudet] Decimumsextum argumentum. facta est explicans, honorificum & gloriosum est, cujus me minime pudet. Idcirco debetis doctrinæ meæ auscultare.
units.tr: {y} Ashamed] Sixteenth argument. Therefore you ought to listen to my teaching.

units.la: Argumentum decimumseptimum, confirmans etiam superius, Euangelium quod ego prædico, est potens & efficax instrumentum Dei ad salutem conferendam cuivis credenti, sine exceptione nationis, sive ex Judæis, sive ex Gentibus, servata tamen prærogativa Judæorum, quibus Euangelium omnium primo annunciari debuit, propter fœdus inter Deum & Judæos jam olim ictum. Idcirco debetis, &c.
units.tr: Seventeenth argument, also confirming what was said above: The Gospel which I preach is a powerful and effective instrument of God for bringing salvation to every believer, without distinction of nation, whether from the Jews or from the Gentiles, yet with the privilege of the Jews preserved, to whom the Gospel ought to have been announced first of all, on account of the covenant struck long ago between God and the Jews. Therefore you ought, etc.

units.la: Verf. 17. Justitia enim Dei per illud retegitur ex fide in fidem, sicut scriptum est, Qui vero ex fide justus est, vivet.
units.tr: Verse 17. For therein is the righteousness of God revealed from faith to faith: as it is written, The just shall live by faith.

units.la: Argumentum decimumoctavum confirmans superius, In Euangelio quod ego prædico, retegitur, & in apertum producitur prius abscondita, & involucris ceremoniarum tecta justitia illa Dei ex fide in fidem, id est, illa justificandi peccatores ratio, quam ipse Deus excogitavit, quâ solâ coram Deo consistere possumus, & in qua solâ Deus acquiescit; nempe illa Christi Dei nostri justitia, quæ nostra fit ex fide in fidem, i. ex fide gradatim augescente à minore ad majorem mensuram, seu ex fide mera, sola, & non ex operibus, seu inhærente justitia nostra. Idcirco debetis cum omni animi submissione & benevolentia quæ ad vos scribo, recipere.
units.tr: Eighteenth argument, confirming what was said above: In the Gospel which I preach, that righteousness of God is uncovered and brought into the open, which was previously hidden and concealed under the veils of ceremonies. That is, it is the way of justifying sinners which God himself devised, by which alone we can stand before God and in which alone God is satisfied; namely, that righteousness of Christ our God, which becomes ours from faith to faith, that is, from faith gradually increasing from a lesser to a greater measure, or from faith alone, bare and not from works, nor from our inherent righteousness. Therefore you ought to receive what I write to you with all humility of mind and goodwill.

units.la: Secunda pars.
units.tr: Second part.

units.la: HIC transitur ad secundam partem Capitis, in qua statuitur propositio per reliquam epistolam confirmanda, quæ hæc est, Justitia quæ in Euangelio retegitur, est justitia illa Dei seu Christi, nobis ex Dei gratia imputata, & per solam fidem apprehensa, non vero justitia illa hominibus inhærens, quæ est ex operibus; seu quæ sensu eadem est, justificamur ex fide in Christum, & non ex operibus.
units.tr: Here the author passes to the second part of the chapter, in which he lays down the proposition to be confirmed through the rest of the epistle: The righteousness revealed in the Gospel is that righteousness of God or of Christ, imputed to us by the grace of God and apprehended through faith alone, and not that righteousness inhering in men, which is from works; or, in sense, the same thing: we are justified by faith in Christ, and not by works.

units.la: Argumenta ad probandam hanc thesin affert decem, quorum duo hoc capite, unum secundo, reliqua vero capite tertio continentur: quibus omnibus præsternenda est hæc immediat adisiunctio; Aut justificamur fide seu gratis imputata justitia, aut operibus, seu inhærente justitia.
units.tr: He brings ten arguments to prove this thesis, of which two are contained in this chapter, one in the second, and the rest in the third chapter. Before all of them must be placed this immediate disjunction: either we are justified by faith, that is, by righteousness imputed freely, or by works, that is, by inherent righteousness.

units.la: Argumentum primum, Per solam justitiam fidei vitam consequimur; Idcirco per solam justitiam fidei justificamur: individuo enim nexu junguntur justitia & salus, & utriusque eadem est ratio. Hoc argumentum confirmat testimonio Hab. 2. 4. qui confidentes in seipsis, vel suis operibus; tanquam hypocritas rejicit à vita, justos vero ex fide, solos pronunciat vitæ hæredes.
units.tr: The first argument: We obtain life through the righteousness of faith alone; therefore we are justified through the righteousness of faith alone, for righteousness and salvation are joined by an indivisible bond, and the reason of both is the same. He confirms this argument by the testimony of Hab. 2. 4., where he rejects from life those who trust in themselves or in their own works as hypocrites, and pronounces only the just who live by faith to be heirs of life.

units.la: Verf. 18. Tatet enim ira Dei è cælo adversus omnem impietatem & injustitiam hominum, ut qui veritatem injuste detineant.
units.tr: Verse 18. For the wrath of God is revealed from heaven against all the ungodliness and unrighteousness of men, who hold the truth in unrighteousness.

units.la: Argumentum secundum, Quia tantùm abest ut justificemur ex operibus, ut ira Dei palam prosequatur impia & injusta opera omnium hominum, Gentium, & Judæorum, scilicet extra Christum constitutorum. Idcirco justificamur per solam justitiam fidei, seu per justitiam Christi fide apprehensam, & ex gratia nobis imputatam.
units.tr: The second argument: Justification by works is so far from being the case that the wrath of God openly pursues the ungodly and unrighteous works of all men, both Gentiles and Jews, that is, those who are outside Christ. Therefore we are justified through the righteousness of faith alone, that is, through the righteousness of Christ apprehended by faith and imputed to us by grace.

units.la: Veritatem ] Hoc argumentum confirmat per partes, & primo impietatem & injustitiam hominum in exemplo Gentium demonstrat, ad verf. 24. deinde iram Dei in impios effusam, & ipsorum injustitiam amplius ostendit, ad finem capitis. Probat impietatem & injustitiam Gentium, ex eo quod etiam hominum sapientissimi (Gentium scilicet Gubernatores & Philosophi) veritatem Dei injustè incarceratam detineant, id est, veram quam de Deo assequuti sunt notitiam, per injustitiam, seu pravitatem suæ voluntatis supprimant, ac veluti captivam intra se detineant, dum vel non communicant eam aliis, vel non ostendunt per opera pietatis: Ergo Impii & Injusti sunt omnes. Valet hoc argumentum ad propositum; nam si verum est hoc de flore generis humani extra Christum, i. de sapientissimis inter gentes legislatoribus & philosophis, de reliquis erit verum multo magis; nam si flos correptus sit, quid de fæce sentiamus?
units.tr: Truth] He confirms this argument part by part. First he demonstrates the ungodliness and unrighteousness of men in the example of the Gentiles, down to verse 24; then he sets forth the wrath of God poured out on the ungodly and shows their unrighteousness more fully, to the end of the chapter. He proves the ungodliness and unrighteousness of the Gentiles from the fact that even the wisest men among them (namely the Gentile rulers and philosophers) hold down the truth of God unjustly, that is, they suppress through the unrighteousness or perversity of their will the true knowledge of God which they had attained, and keep it captive within themselves, while they either do not share it with others or do not show it by works of piety. Therefore all are ungodly and unrighteous. This argument serves the purpose; for if this is true of the flower of the human race outside Christ, that is, of the wisest lawgivers and philosophers among the nations, it will be much more true of the rest; for if the flower is corrupt, what shall we think of the dregs?

units.la: Verf. 19. Quoniam id quod de Deo cognosci potest, manifestum est intra ipsos: Deus enim eis manifestum fecit.
units.tr: Verse 19. Because that which may be known of God is manifest in them; for God hath shewed it unto them.

units.la: Verf. 20. Ipsius enim invisibilia, jam inde a creatione mundi ex iis quæ fecit animadversa, pervidentur, æterna videlicet ejus tum potentia tum divinitas: ad hoc ut sint ipsi inexcusabiles.
units.tr: Verse 20. For the invisible things of him from the creation of the world are clearly seen, being understood by the things that are made, even his eternal power and Godhead; so that they are without excuse.

units.la: Hoc argumentum explanat duobus modis, primo ostendendo, quod veritatem seu reliquias luminis naturæ de Deo colendo aliquas, habuerint Gentes, quia quod naturali luce de Deo cognoscibile est, ipsis fuit cognitum, nempe Dei æternitas, potentia & divinitas, seu reliqua attributa Dei, quæ naturali notione Dei comprehenduntur, jam inde à condito mundo per res creatas, tanquam in speculo propositá ipsis manifestabantur adeo perspicuè, ut excusationem ignorantiæ prætexere non potuerint.
units.tr: He explains this argument in two ways. First, by showing that the Gentiles had some truth or remnants of the light of nature concerning the worship of God, because what can be known of God by natural light was known to them, namely the eternity, power and divinity of God, or the other attributes of God which are comprehended by the natural notion of God.
