From the created world these were made manifest to them, set forth as in a mirror, so clearly that they could not pretend the excuse of ignorance.

units.la: Verf. 21 Propterea quod quum Deum cognoverint, tamen ut Deum non glorificaverunt, neque gratias ei egerunt: sed vani facti sunt in ratiocinationibus suis, & obtenebratum est desipiens cor eorum.
units.tr: Verse 21. Because that, when they knew God, they glorified him not as God, neither were thankful; but became vain in their imaginations, and their foolish heart was darkened.

units.la: Vers. 22. Quum se dicitent sapientes, stulti facti sunt.
units.tr: Verse 22. Professing themselves to be wise, they became fools.

units.la: Vers. 23. Mutarunt enim gloriam incorruptibilis Dei in simulacrum imaginis corruptibilis hominis, & volucrum & quadrupedum, & reptilium.
units.tr: Verse 23. And changed the glory of the uncorruptible God into an image made like to corruptible man, and to birds, and fourfooted beasts, and creeping things.

units.la: Secundo explanat superius argumentum, ostendendo Gentes incarceratam detinuisse cognitam veritatem, partim quia gloriam attributorum & divinorum operum, & pro beneficiis divinis gratias, quas naturale lumen rationis Deo dandas dictabat, Deo non tribuerunt: partim quia digressi à veris principiis de Deo, per falsas ratiocinationes suas, fallum de Deo, ejusque cultu assumentes & concludentes, in speculationibus suis evanescebant, seque ipsos decipiebant, & excaecabant, atque ita infatuabantur, etiam tum cum videri volebant sapere maximè. Partim denique quia ingratitudinem & stultitiam suam opere aperte prodentes, fingebant imagines hominum & brutorum animalium, quibus Deum, seu Dei proprietates, sibi ad oculum representarent, atque ita gloriam Dei, comparatione tam vili foedatam, commutarunt in abominandas illas imagines, quantum in ipsis fuit.
units.tr: Second, he explains the preceding argument by showing that the Gentiles held the known truth captive, partly because they did not ascribe to God the glory of his attributes and works, nor the thanks for divine benefits which the natural light of reason dictated should be given to God; partly because, having departed from the true principles concerning God, they assumed and drew false conclusions by their false reasonings about God and his worship, and in their speculations grew vain, deceived and blinded themselves, and so became foolish, even when they most wished to seem wise. And lastly, because by their deeds they openly showed their ingratitude and folly, they fashioned images of men and brute animals by which they might represent God, or God's properties, to their eyes; and so, as far as lay in them, they exchanged the glory of God, debased by so base a comparison, for those abominable images.

units.la: Vers. 24. Quamobrem etiam tradidit eos Deus cupiditatibus cordium ipsorum, ad impuritatem, ut foedarent corpora sua in semetipsis.
units.tr: Verse 24. Wherefore God also gave them up to uncleanness through the lusts of their own hearts, to dishonour their own bodies between themselves.

units.la: Vers. 25. Ut qui Dei veritatem transmutarint in falsitatem & venerati sint & coluerint res conditas, praeterito Creatore qui est benedictus in saecula, AMEN.
units.tr: Verse 25. Who changed the truth of God into a lie, and worshipped and served the creature more than the Creator, who is blessed for ever. Amen.

units.la: Ostensa impietate & injustitia hominum contra Deum in exemplo Gentium, in eodem exemplo ostendit iram Dei in impios effusam, & iniquitatem ipsorum ampliorem demonstrat. Quod in poenam foedae idololatriae Deus justissimè desertos, judicialiter tradiderit regendos à cupiditatibus suis: ut qui Deum gloria debita fraudaverant, ipsi ex adverso turpissimam in seipsis & à seipsis ignominiam paterentur, & ut qui commutaverant Dei gloriosa attributa in mendaces imagines, quae nihil minus sunt quam id quod dicuntur, se etiam in bestias, per effrenes suas libidines commutarent. Dicuntur coluisse ac serviisse rebus creatis; praeterito Creatore, quia licet idololatrae Deum falso repraesentatum, in cultu quem imagini à se confictae exhibent, honorari velint & intendant, Deus tamen cultum
units.tr: Having shown the ungodliness and unrighteousness of men against God in the example of the Gentiles, in the same example he shows the wrath of God poured out on the ungodly and demonstrates their greater iniquity. God, most justly, in punishment for their foul idolatry, judicially gave them up, deserted, to be ruled by their own lusts, so that those who had defrauded God of the glory due to him might themselves suffer the most shameful disgrace in and from themselves; and those who had exchanged the glorious attributes of God for lying images, which are in no way what they are called, might themselves be changed into beasts by their unbridled lusts. They are said to have worshipped and served created things, passing over the Creator, because although the idolaters wish and intend God, falsely represented, to be honoured in the worship which they offer to an image fashioned by themselves, God nevertheless utterly rejects that worship, and leaves the whole of it to the image or creature, with which he will in no way share his worship.

units.la: B tum illum omnino rejicit, totumque relinquit imagini seu creaturae cum qua cultum suum non vult ullo modo partiri.
units.tr: Then he utterly rejects it, and leaves the whole of it to the image or creature, with which he is unwilling in any way to share his worship.

units.la: Dicitur Deus benedictus in secula hoc loco, ut sciamus nihil detractum Dei felicitati per Idololatrarum injurias, sed constare Deo suam gloriam & beatitudinem in aeternum, cui applaudere debemus omnes cum Apostolo, dicentes, AMEN.
units.tr: God is called blessed for ever in this place, so that we may know that nothing is taken from the happiness of God by the injuries of idolaters, but that God's glory and blessedness remain for ever. In this we should all join with the Apostle, saying, Amen.

units.la: Vers. 26. Propterea, inquam, tradidit eos Deus foedis affectibus: nam & foeminae illorum transmutarunt naturalem usum in eum qui est praeter naturam.
units.tr: Verse 26. For this cause God gave them up unto vile affections: for even their women did change the natural use into that which is against nature.

units.la: Vers. 27. Similiter etiam masculi relicto naturali usu foeminae exarserunt sua libidine, alius in alium; masculi in masculos foeda perpetrantes, & compensationem quam opportuit, erroris sui in semetipsos recipientes.
units.tr: Verse 27. And likewise also the men, leaving the natural use of the woman, burned in their lust one toward another; men with men working that which is unseemly, and receiving in themselves that recompence of their error which was meet.

units.la: Ulterior injustitiae humanae & irae divinae in impios demonstratio in exemplo Gentium. Quod scilicet Deus indulgentes suis pravis affectibus in religionis negotio, in potestatem libidinis suae, & impurorum spirituum judicialiter tradiderit, ut praeter naturam Sodomitica & nefanda foeditate viri pariter & foeminae, se infra bestias, sua non naturali libidine, quasi per compensationem abjicerent, qui in idololatria sua Dei gloriam ad similitudinem rerum creatarum, per sua figmenta deprimerent.
units.tr: A further demonstration of human unrighteousness and divine wrath against the ungodly in the example of the Gentiles. God, namely, judicially gave up to the power of their lust, and of unclean spirits, those who indulged their evil affections in matters of religion, so that men and women alike, beyond nature, by Sodomitic and unspeakable foulness, and by their unnatural lust, cast themselves, as it were in recompense, below the beasts; they who in their idolatry had degraded the glory of God, by their fabrications, to the likeness of created things.

units.la: Vers. 28. Et sicut non visum est eis Deum in agnitione retinere, ita tradidit eos Deus in mentem omnis judicii expertem, ut facerent quae minime conveniebat.
units.tr: Verse 28. And even as they did not like to retain God in their knowledge, God gave them over to a reprobate mind, to do those things which are not convenient.

units.la: Vers. 29. Oppleti omni injustitia, malitia, fornicatione, improbitate; avaritia: pleni invidia, caede, contentione, dolo, malignitate:
units.tr: Verse 29. Being filled with all unrighteousness, fornication, wickedness, covetousness, maliciousness; full of envy, murder, debate, deceit, malignity;

units.la: Vers. 30. Susurrones, obloquutores. Dei osores, injuriosi, superbi, gloriosi, inventores malorum, parentibus inobedientes,
units.tr: Verse 30. Whisperers, backbiters, haters of God, despiteful, proud, boasters, inventors of evil things, disobedient to parents.

units.la: Vers. 31. Intelligentia carentes, foedifragi, charitatis expertes, implacabiles, immisericordes:
units.tr: Ver. 31. Without understanding, faithless, without natural affection, implacable, unmerciful:

units.la: Pergit in Gentium exemplo hominum injustitiam & Dei iram porro ostendere. Quod scilicet Deus repudiantes cognitionem sui, & non diguantes Dei notitiam, naturae luce in operibus creationis omnibus conspicuam spiciam, in animis suis retinere & fovere, justissime tradiderit in mentem reprobam, ut communis judicii usu & fructu privati, quasi brutescerent, & amentes in omnia maleficia contra jura Gentium & naturæ, sine omni rationis prætextu ruerent.
units.tr: He goes on, using the example of the Gentiles, to show further the injustice of men and the wrath of God. Because they rejected the knowledge of him and did not deign to acknowledge God, which is plainly visible in all the works of creation by the light of nature, God most justly gave them over to a reprobate mind. Deprived of the use and fruit of sound judgment, they were as it were made brutish, and, madmen, they rushed into every kind of wickedness against the laws of the nations and of nature, with no pretext of reason.

units.la: Oppleti ] Ne putemus uni vitio obnoxios, recitat Apostolus catalogum vitiorum circiter vigintitrium, quibus oppletos nobis proponit homines sibi relictos.
units.tr: Filled with] Lest we think them guilty of only one vice, the Apostle recites a list of about twenty-three vices, with which he presents men left to themselves as filled.

units.la: Omni injustitia ] Id est, omni genere injustitiæ contra proximum.
units.tr: With all unrighteousness] That is, with every kind of injustice against one's neighbour.

units.la: Scortatione ] Hoc nomine comprehendit omnem illicitum concubitum viri cum fœmina.
units.tr: Fornication] By this word he includes every unlawful intercourse of a man with a woman.

units.la: Malitia ] Id est, nocendi studio cum fraude & labore conjuncto.
units.tr: Malice] That is, a desire to harm, joined with deceit and effort.

units.la: Improbitate ] Id est, animi perversitate palam se prodente.
units.tr: Wickedness] That is, a perversity of mind openly revealed.

units.la: Malignitate ] Id est, morum asperitate & difficultate.
units.tr: Maliciousness] That is, harshness and difficulty of manners.

units.la: Susurrones ] Quales sunt qui proximos occulte mordent, eo fine ut solvant amicitiam.
units.tr: Whisperers] Such are those who secretly bite their neighbours, with the aim of breaking up friendship.

units.la: Obloquutores ] Quales sunt qui aliorum famam apud quosvis lacerant.
units.tr: Backbiters] Such are those who tear to pieces the reputation of others before anyone at all.

units.la: Dei osores ] Quales sunt qui (ex mala conscientia) non sustinent quicquam de Deo audire.
units.tr: Haters of God] Such are those who (from an evil conscience) cannot bear to hear anything about God.

units.la: Contumeliosi ] Quales sunt feroces, qui alios per vim opprimunt.
units.tr: Despiteful] Such are the fierce, who oppress others by force.

units.la: Gloriosi ] Quales sunt jactabundi.
units.tr: Boasters] Such are the braggarts.

units.la: Inventores malorum ] Quales sunt qui nova peccandi genera excogitant.
units.tr: Inventors of evil things] Such are those who devise new kinds of sinning.

units.la: Desipientes ] Quales sunt qui sine prætextu rationis ut bruta feruntur, quo libido alia atque alia trahit.
units.tr: Senseless] Such are those who, with no pretext of reason, are carried along like beasts, wherever lust drags them, now this way, now that.

units.la: Vers. 32. Qui Dei jure agnito, (nempe eos qui talia faciunt, dignos esse morte) tamen non solum ea faciunt, sed etiam cum iis qui ea faciunt consentiunt.
units.tr: Ver. 32. Who, though they know the righteous judgment of God (namely, that those who do such things are worthy of death), not only do the same, but also give their approval to those who do them.

units.la: Ultima injustitiæ hominum, in ira Dei sibi juste derelictorum demonstratio, & exaggeratio triplex; Prima est, Quod sceleribus prædictis operam dederint contra conscientiæ dictamen; Sciebant ea Hagitia Deo displicere. Secunda est, Quod contra agnitum Dei judicium, & notum peccatorum meritum, peccarint: Sciebant morte dignos esse, qui talia patrarunt. Tertia est, Quod non solum ea, & talia ipsi fecerint, sed etiam talia patrantes non silentio solùm, sed & suo consensu, adulatione, & auctoritate confirmarint, iisque patrocinati sint. Hæc est sapientissimorum hominum extra Christum conditio, qui tantum absunt à justitia operum, ut nihil possint nisi principiis justitiæ cognitis abuti, iram Dei in se provocare, sequi omni genere pollutionum, ad perditionem extremam magis magisque contaminare.
units.tr: The final injustice of men, and the demonstration of their being justly abandoned by God to his wrath, is set out in a threefold amplification. The first is that they laboured at the aforesaid crimes against the dictate of their conscience; they knew that these abominations displease God. The second is that they sinned against the recognised judgment of God and the known desert of sins; they knew that those who committed such things were worthy of death. The third is that they not only did these things, and such things, themselves, but also, by their silence, and even by their own consent, flattery and authority, confirmed those who committed such things and defended them. This is the condition of the wisest of men outside Christ, who are so far from the righteousness of works that they can do nothing but misuse the known principles of righteousness, provoke the wrath of God upon themselves, follow every kind of pollution, and defile themselves more and more to utter destruction.

units.la: Caput secundum.
units.tr: Chapter 2.

units.la: HOC Capite affertur tertium argumentum ad thesin probandam, de justitia non per opera, sed per fidem: quod proponitur versu primo & secundo, reliquo vero capite sublatis è medio objectionibus, confirmatur.
units.tr: In this chapter the third argument is brought forward to prove the thesis, that justification comes not by works but by faith. This is set out in verses 1 and 2, and the rest of the chapter confirms it by removing the objections.

units.la: Vers. 1. QUapropter inexcusabilis es O homo quisquis alterum damnas: nam hoc ipso quod damnas alterum, teipsum condemnas: eadem enim magis tu qui alium damnas.
units.tr: Verse 1. Therefore you are inexcusable, O man, whoever you are who condemn another; for in the very act of condemning another you condemn yourself, since you who judge do the same things.

units.la: Vers. 2 Scimus vero judicium Dei esse secundum veritatem adversus eos qui talia agunt.
units.tr: Verse 2. But we know that the judgment of God is according to truth against those who commit such things.

units.la: Tertium argumentum contra justificationem ex operibus, ab omnium hominum αὐτοκαταχρίσει, deductum ex superioris Capitis versu novissimo. Omnis homo (damnando alios, & eadem faciendo quæ ipse damnat) suopte judicio sine excusatione condemnatur. Ergo tantum abest ut nullus ex operibus justificetur, ut contra ex eis, omnis homo condemnetur.
units.tr: This is the third argument against justification by works, drawn from the self-condemnation [αὐτοκαταχρίσει] of all men, and taken from the last verse of the previous chapter. Every man, by condemning others while doing the same things he condemns, is condemned without excuse by his own judgment. Therefore it is not only that no one is justified by works; on the contrary, every man is condemned by them.

units.la: Additur versu secundo ratio antecedentis, quia Dei judicium justum est, & secundum facti meritum condemnat omnem peccatorem, judicantem pariter & judicatum. Ergo qui secundum Dei judicium damnat alium mortis ob peccatum, damnat etiam seipsum talia agentem.
units.tr: Verse 2 adds the reason for the preceding statement: God's judgment is just, and it condemns every sinner according to the merit of his deed, whether he judges or is judged. So whoever condemns another for sin, according to God's judgment, condemns himself too, since he does such things.

units.la: Vers. 3. Cogitas autem hoc, O homo, qui damnas eos qui talia faciunt, & facis ea, fore ut tu effugias judicium Dei?
units.tr: Verse 3. But do you think this, O man, who condemn those who do such things and do them yourself, that you will escape the judgment of God?

units.la: Hoc argumentum reliquo capite confirmatur, sublatis quatuor objectis pratextibus, quibus possent homines vim argumenti eludere.
units.tr: This argument is confirmed in the rest of the chapter, where four pretexts are removed by which men might try to evade its force.

units.la: Prima objectio, est judicii Divini contemptoris securi, qui alios peccatores judicat, & sibiipsi impunitatem pollicetur, quia hactenus ipsi Deus pepercit & benefecit; Non metuo mihi inquit a Dei judicio. Refutat Apostolus objectionem, & rejiciendam probat hanc sententiam rationibus sex.
units.tr: The first objection belongs to the secure despiser of God's judgment, who judges other sinners but promises himself impunity, because God has so far spared and blessed him. "I do not fear God's judgment," he says. The Apostle answers the objection and shows by six reasons that this opinion must be rejected.

units.la: Prima ratio, Quod istiusmodi cogitatio sit inanis & stolida, nam putasne &c. idem valet quod, frustra putas fore ut effugias judicium Dei.
units.tr: The first reason is that such a thought is empty and foolish. The phrase do you think means the same as you vainly think that you will escape the judgment of God.

units.la: Verf. 4. An divitias benignitatis ejus & tolerantiae ac lenitatis contemnis, ignorans te benignitate Dei ad resipiscentiam deduci?
units.tr: Verse 4. Or do you despise the riches of his goodness and forbearance and long-suffering, not knowing that the goodness of God leads you to repentance?

units.la: Ratio 2. Quod haec cogitatio prodat contemptum & abusum divitis benignitatis, tolerantiae, & lenitatis Dei, cum quis, quia Deus hactenus ipsi pepercit, pergit in peccato, & spem impunitatis concipit.
units.tr: The second reason is that this thought shows contempt for and abuse of the rich goodness, forbearance and long-suffering of God, when someone, because God has so far spared him, persists in sin and conceives hope of impunity.

units.la: Ratio 3. Quod Dei benignitas invitare & movere debeat ad resipiscentiam, non ad pergendum in peccato, ex spe impunitatis.
units.tr: The third reason is that God's goodness ought to invite and move a man to repentance, not to persist in sin on the strength of a hope of impunity.

units.la: Verf. 5. Sed pro duritia tua & corde quod resipiscere nescit, thesaurizas tibi ipsi iram in diem irae & patefactionis justi judicii Dei:
units.tr: Verse 5. But because of your hardness and your impenitent heart, you are storing up for yourself wrath on the day of wrath and of the revelation of the righteous judgment of God.

units.la: Ratio 4. Quod istiusmodi cogitatio sit proprij cordis obduratio in peccatis, & obfirmatio ne possit resipiscere.
units.tr: The fourth reason is that such a thought hardens one's own heart in sins and makes it fixed, so that it cannot repent.

units.la: Ratio 5. Quod securus judicij contemptor accumulet sibi quendam poenarum thesaurum, apud justitiam Dei, in tempus illud ultimi terribilis judicij, quo thesaurus ille poenarum universus super ipsum in Dei ira justissima aperte effundetur.
units.tr: The fifth reason is that the secure despiser of judgment piles up for himself a store of punishments with the justice of God, against that time of the final and terrible judgment, when that whole store of punishments will be poured out openly upon him in the most just wrath of God.

units.la: Verf. 6 Qui reddet unicuique secundum opera ipsius:
units.tr: Verse 6. Who will render to each one according to his works:

units.la: Verf. 7. Iis quidem qui secundum patientem expectationem quaerunt boni operis gloriam & honorem & immortalitatem, vitam aeternam:
units.tr: Verse 7. To those who by patient continuance in well-doing seek for glory and honour and immortality, eternal life;

units.la: Verf. 8. Litigiosis vero, & veritati quidem non obedientibus, obedientibus autem injustitiae erit excandescentia & ira:
units.tr: Verse 8. But to those who are contentious and do not obey the truth, but obey unrighteousness, there will be indignation and wrath.

units.la: Verf. 9. Afflictio inquam erit & angustia adversus omnem animam hominis perpetrantis malum, tum Judaei in primis, tum etiam Graeci:
units.tr: Verse 9. Tribulation and anguish, I say, will come upon every soul of man who does evil, both of the Jew first and also of the Greek;

units.la: Verf. 10. Gloria vero & honor & pax erit cuivis operanti bonum, tum Judaeo in primis, tum & Graeco.
units.tr: Verse 10. But glory and honour and peace to everyone who does good, both to the Jew first and also to the Greek.

units.la: Quod Deus unicuique redditurus sit in die judicij secundum opera ipsius bona vel mala, praemia ex gratia, vel poenas ex justitia; nempe vitam aeternam perseverantibus spe praemij in veritatis obedientia, versu 6. 7. Et præter iræ signa in hac vita, etiam mortem æternam post hanc vitam, sicut iratum Deum infligere æquum est veræ doctrinæ, seu veritatatis adversariis, & injustitiæ mancipiis, versu 8. Confirmat hanc rationem, quod Deus in infligendis pœnis, nullam nationis, vel adjunctorum externorum, rationem sit habiturus, sed impio Judæo, qui primas habebat in Dei beneficiis, primas etiam sit tributurus in pœnis: & impio etiam Ethnico, seu Gentili, meritas animæ & corporis pœnas inflicturus, versu 9. Similiter in remuneratione, quod sine discrimine nationum, sit glorificaturus (id est, donis omnibus quæ hominem ab externo perficiant, qualia sunt gloria & honor, & ab interno (quæ pace significantur) cumulaturus Judæum pium & probum, secundum omnia privilegia quæ Genti illi secerat, & Gentilem seu Ethnicum pium & probum, suo quoque loco, vita æterna coronaturus, versu 10. Unde sequitur falli eum, qui spem impunitatis fovet, quia hactenus Deus ipsi pepercit.
units.tr: God will render to each one on the day of judgment according to his works, whether good or evil: rewards by grace, or punishments by justice. To those who persevere in obedience to the truth, with hope of reward, he gives eternal life (verses 6 and 7). Besides the signs of his wrath in this life, he also inflicts eternal death after this life, as it is right for an angry God to do to the adversaries of true doctrine, or of the truth, and to the slaves of injustice (verse 8). He confirms this reasoning: in inflicting punishments God will take no account of nation or external circumstances, but he will assign the first place in punishment to the wicked Jew, who had the first place among God's benefits, and he will inflict the punishments due to body and soul on the wicked Gentile as well (verse 9). Likewise in the reward: without distinction of nations he will glorify the pious and upright Jew, that is, load him with all those gifts which perfect a man from outside, such as glory and honour, and from within (signified by peace), according to all the privileges granted to that people; and he will crown the pious and upright Gentile with eternal life in his own place (verse 10). Hence it follows that he is mistaken who cherishes hope of impunity because God has so far spared him.

units.la: Vers. 11 Non enim est personarum respectus apud Deum.
units.tr: Verse 11. For there is no respect of persons with God.

units.la: Confirmat superiorem rationem à Dei æquitate seu ἀπροσωπολημψία; simul etiam occurrit secundæ objectioni, contra districtum Dei judicium in peccatores, versu secundo propositum. Objiceret aliquis; At in executione judicii ratio habenda est cum Ethnici qui extra Ecclesiam degit, sine legis seu doctrinæ Dei cognitione; tum etiam Judæi, qui discipulus est Dei, & auditor legis, absit ut vel ille, vel hic pereat; nam injustum esse videtur utrumque, etiam si peccatores sint. Refutat objectionem, & perire æquum esse probat quemvis peccatorem, quinque rationibus.
units.tr: He confirms the preceding reasoning from the justice of God, or impartiality [ἀπροσωπολημψία]. At the same time he meets the second objection, which was raised against the strict judgment of God on sinners, stated in verse 2. Someone might object: in carrying out judgment account must be taken of the Gentile who lives outside the Church without knowledge of God's law or teaching, and also of the Jew, who is a disciple of God and a hearer of the law; far be it that either of them should perish, for both seem unjust, even if they are sinners. He answers the objection and shows that it is right for any sinner to perish, by five reasons.

units.la: Prima ratio. Quia apud Deum non est personarum acceptio, ut perseverantes in peccato, sive Gentiles sive Judæos, eximat à perditione propter rationem aliquam, quæ personam, non causam attingit. Et hic observandum quod peccatorem Judæum & Gentilem extra Christum æquet Deus, non in pœnarum gradibus, sed in mortis æternæ reatu tantum, quo pariter tenentur omnes peccatores, licet non in pari gradu.
units.tr: The first reason: because there is no partiality with God, so that he would not exempt from destruction, for any reason touching the person rather than the cause, those who persist in sin, whether Gentiles or Jews. Here it must be observed that God treats the Jewish and Gentile sinner outside Christ alike, not in degrees of punishment but in the guilt of eternal death, under which all sinners are equally held, though not in equal degree.

units.la: Vers. 12 Quicunque enim absque Lege peccaverunt, absque Lege quoque peribunt: & quicunque cum Lege peccaverunt, per Legem damnabuntur.
units.tr: Verse 12. For as many as have sinned without the law shall also perish without the law; and as many as have sinned in the law shall be judged by the law.

units.la: Ratio 2. confirmans & explicans priorem, quia quicunque sine lege (scripta scilicet) peccarunt, adversus legem, cordi per naturam inscriptam, etiam per eandem legem innatam, sine lege scripta peribunt, ex justitiæ dictato. Et quicunque in lege, seu in legis scriptæ notitia peccaverunt; per sententiam etiam legis scriptæ damnabuntur. Idcirco sine personarum acceptione æquum est ut pereant quivis peccatores.
units.tr: The second reason confirms and explains the first: whoever has sinned without the written law, against the law inscribed in the heart by nature, will perish without the written law, by the same law which is innate, under the dictate of justice. And whoever has sinned in the law, or with knowledge of the written law, will be condemned by the sentence of the written law as well. Therefore it is right, without respect of persons, that every sinner should perish.

units.la: Verf. 13. Non enim qui audiunt Legem, justi sunt apud Deum, sed qui Legem præstant, justificabuntur.
units.tr: Verse 13. For not the hearers of the law are just before God, but the doers of the law will be justified.

units.la: Ratio. 3. Potissimum militans adversus judæos, Quia secundum justitiæ regulam, non possunt pro juštis haberi apud Deum, qui auditores sunt legis, nisi etiam legem perfectè præstiterint; quod quia neque Judæi neque Gentes præstare possunt, neque eximi per consequens à merita perditione possunt, sed contra Judæi potissimum, qui auditores sunt legis, & eam non præstant, digni sunt perditione maximè.
units.tr: The third reason, aimed chiefly against the Jews: according to the rule of justice, those who are hearers of the law cannot be held righteous before God unless they have also fulfilled the law perfectly. Since neither Jews nor Gentiles can do this, neither can they consequently be exempted from merited destruction; but on the contrary the Jews, who are hearers of the law and do not fulfil it, deserve destruction most of all.

units.la: Verf. 14. Nam quum Gentes, quæ Legem non habent, naturaliter quæ Legis sunt faciant, isti Legem non habentes, sibi ipsis sunt Lex.
units.tr: Verse 14. For when the Gentiles, who do not have the law, by nature do the things of the law, these, not having the law, are a law to themselves.

units.la: Verf. 15. Ut qui ostendant opus Legis scriptum in cordibus suis, una testimonium reddente ipsorum conscientia, & cogitationibus se-se mutuò accusantibus, aut etiam excusantibus)
units.tr: Verse 15. Who show the work of the law written in their hearts, their conscience bearing witness with them, and their thoughts accusing or else excusing one another.

units.la: Ratio 4. Militans adversus Gentes potissimum; quia Gentes etiam si non habeant legem scriptam, habent tamen legem innatam, & natura faciunt aliqua externa opera legis, licet non habeant scriptam legem, ipsis tamen innata lux, lex est, & ea quidem reipsa & opere in cordibus ipsorum scripta, sicut testatur in ipsis conscientia, accusans in malefactis, & excusans in recte factis. Idcirco nihil habent quod obtendant quominus meritam damnationem subeant, cum peccant, multò minus Judæi.
units.tr: The fourth reason is aimed chiefly against the Gentiles: although the Gentiles do not have the written law, they do have the innate law, and by nature they do some external works of the law. The inner light is law even without the written law, and it is indeed written in their hearts in fact and in deed, as their conscience bears witness, accusing them in wrongdoing and excusing them in right doing. Therefore they have nothing to plead why they should not undergo the damnation they deserve when they sin, much less the Jews.

units.la: Verf. 16. In die quo judicabit Dominus de occultis hominum, ex Euangelio meo, per Iesum Christum.
units.tr: Verse 16. In the day when God shall judge the secrets of men, according to my gospel, by Jesus Christ.

units.la: Ratio 5. Quia in die judicii, Dominus occulta cordium proferet, & secundum hanc meam in Euangelio doctrinam, justam esse perditionem peccantium pronunciabit, sive ij ex Gentibus sint, sive ex Judæis. Idcirco non possunt excusari qui peccant, quin merito suo jure pereant.
units.tr: Reason 5. Because on the day of judgment the Lord will bring the hidden things of hearts to light, and according to this my doctrine in the gospel he will pronounce that the destruction of sinners is just, whether they are of the Gentiles or of the Jews. Therefore those who sin cannot make excuse, but perish deservedly and rightly.

units.la: Verf. 17. Ecce, tu cognominaris Judæus, & acquiescis in Lege, & gloriaris in Deo. Verf. 18 Et nosti ejus voluntatem, & exploras quæ discrepant, instītutus ex Lege.
units.tr: Verse 17. Behold, thou art called a Jew, and restest in the law, and makest thy boast of God. Verse 18. And knowest his will, and approvest the things that are more excellent, being instructed out of the law.

units.la: Verf. 19. Confidisque teductem esse cæcorum, lucem eorum qui sunt in tenebris,
units.tr: Verse 19. And art confident that thou thyself art a guide of the blind, a light of them which are in darkness,

units.la: Verf. 20. Eruditorem insipientium, magistrum infantium, quod habeas informationem cognitionis ac veritatis in Lege.
units.tr: Verse 20. An instructor of the foolish, a teacher of babes, which hast the form of knowledge and of the truth in the law.

units.la: Tertia objectio. At aliquid dandum saltem Judæorum privilegiis, & prosessioni, ne in condemnationem veniant pariter cum Gentibus; Et hic cum justitiæ operum patrono aliquo, legis videlicet doctore Coryphæo congreditur, producitque in medium septem fulcra inanis ipsius fiduciæ, per concessionem illi largiens omnia. Primum quod ei concedit est externus honor Dei cultoris, & confessoris. Tu cognominarū Judæus, quod nomen erat non nationis tantum, sed & religionis veræ, confessoris. Secundum est, submissio animi erga doctrinam Legis, Tu acquiescis in lege, & applaudis seu gratularis tibi de ea, tanquam insigni beneficio. Tertium est, gloriatio in Deo, quod scilicet esset de populo Electo præ omni alia natione, & cum Deo fœderato. versu. 17. Quartum, Est notitia voluntatis Dei ex lege accepta, Quintum, Est judicium boni & mali, & rerum discrepantium ac controversiarum beneficio Ejusdem legis. versu. 18. Sextum. Est confidentia de scientiæ tanta copia, & certitudine, ut possit alios docere. Septimum est, quod habeat idæam formatam & exemplar expressum, in unum collectum, omnis illius cognitionis & veritatis quæ sparsim in lege seu doctrina sacra continetur, ita ut omnes alii præ Rabbi hoc nostro, infantes & insipientes sint, versu. 19. 20.
units.tr: Third objection. But at least something must be granted to the privileges and profession of the Jews, lest they come into condemnation together with the Gentiles. Here he engages with a certain defender of the works of righteousness, namely a doctor of the law, the leader of them all, and he brings forward seven props of his empty confidence, granting him everything by concession. First, what he concedes to him is the external honour of a worshipper and confessor of God: Thou art called a Jew. This name was not only the name of a nation but also of the true religion, a confessor. Second, is submission of mind to the doctrine of the law: Thou restest in the law, and you applaud yourself and congratulate yourself on it as a remarkable benefit. Third, is glorying in God, namely that he is of the chosen people above every other nation and in covenant with God (v. 17). Fourth, is knowledge of the will of God received from the law. Fifth, is the judgment of good and evil, and of differing things and controversies, by the benefit of the same law (v. 18). Sixth, is confidence in so great an abundance and certainty of knowledge that he can teach others. Seventh, is that he has a formed idea and an expressed exemplar, gathered into one, of all that knowledge and truth which is scattered through the law or sacred doctrine, so that all others, compared with this our Rabbi, are infants and fools (vv. 19, 20).

units.la: Verf. 21. Qui igitur doces alium, teipsum non doces; qui prædicas non furandum, furaris?
units.tr: Verse 21. Thou therefore which teachest another, teachest thou not thyself? thou that preachest a man should not steal, dost thou steal?

units.la: Verf. 22. Qui dicis non mœchandum, mœcharis; qui abominaris idola, sacrilegium admittis?
units.tr: Verse 22. Thou that sayest a man should not commit adultery, dost thou commit adultery? thou that abhorrest idols, dost thou commit sacrilege?

units.la: Verf. 23. Qui de Lege gloriaris, per Legis transgressionem Deum dedecoras?
units.tr: Verse 23. Thou that makest thy boast of the law, through breaking the law dishonourest thou God?

units.la: Respondet Apostolus ad objectionem, & his omnibus concessis non sufficere ista ad justitiam ostendit, duabus rationibus. Prima ratio, Quia te ipsum inquit non doces, id est, doctrinam tuam facto non ostendis, doctrinæ vim factis tuis non imprimis, sed vel te polluis iisdem vitiis quæ vetas vel tas,vel similibus. Idcirco non sufficiunt ista ut eximaris ē condemnatione.
units.tr: The Apostle answers the objection and, with all these things granted, shows that they are not sufficient for righteousness, on two grounds. The first ground: because, he says, you do not teach yourself; that is, you do not show your doctrine by your deeds, you do not impress the force of your doctrine on your actions, but you either defile yourself with the same vices which you forbid, or with similar ones. Therefore these things do not suffice to free you from condemnation.

units.la: Verf. 24. Nam dei nomen propter vos blasphematur in Gentes, sicut scriptum est.
units.tr: Verse 24. For the name of God is blasphemed among the Gentiles through you, as it is written.

units.la: Ratio 2. confirmans superiorem, Quia vestra culpa Gentes male de Deo loquuntur, quasi vitiosos cultores habeat, vel ferat. Nihil ergo recitata privilegia ad justitiam faciunt.
units.tr: Reason 2, confirming the previous one: because through your fault the Gentiles speak evil of God, as if he had, or tolerated, vicious worshippers. Therefore the privileges recited do nothing for righteousness.

units.la: Hanc rationem confirmat testimonio Ezekielis, 36. 22. qui de sui temporis hypocritis in iisdem privilegiis gloriantibus conqueritur.
units.tr: He confirms this reason by the testimony of Ezekiel 36:22, who complains of the hypocrites of his own time, who gloried in those same privileges.

units.la: Verf. 25. Nam circumcisio quidem prodest si Legem observes, quod si transgressor Legis fueris, circumcisio tua facta est praeputium.
units.tr: Verse 25. For circumcision verily profiteth, if thou keep the law; but if thou be a breaker of the law, thy circumcision is made uncircumcision.

units.la: Quarta objectio. At propter foedus Dei cujus sigillum est circumcisio, non peribo ego, qui circumcisus sum, inquit Judaeus externae ceremoniae confidens.
units.tr: Fourth objection. But because of the covenant of God, of which circumcision is the seal, I shall not perish, I who am circumcised, says the Jew, trusting in an external ceremony.

units.la: Respondet Apostolus, & probat circumcisionem non eximere ē condemnatione, vel morte, 4. rationibus:
units.tr: The Apostle answers and proves that circumcision does not free from condemnation or death, by four reasons:

units.la: Prima ratio, Quia circumcisio si jungatur cum perfecta obedientia omnium mandatorum reliquorum, si fieri posset, prodesset quidem ut pars obedientiae ad justificationem per opera, pro qua decertabat Judaeus; sed si inveniatur in circumciso transgressio legis, perinde se habebit ad justitiam operum circumcisio & praeputium. Idcirco non eximit circumcisio ē damnatione.
units.tr: First reason: because circumcision, if it were joined with perfect obedience to all the remaining commandments (if that could be done), would indeed profit as a part of obedience towards justification by works, for which the Jew was contending. But if transgression of the law is found in the circumcised man, circumcision and uncircumcision stand in the same relation to the righteousness of works. Therefore circumcision does not free from damnation.

units.la: Verf. 26. Itaque si praeputium jura Legis observet, nonne praeputium illius pro circumcisione reputabitur?
units.tr: Verse 26. Therefore if the uncircumcision keep the righteousness of the law, shall not his uncircumcision be counted for circumcision?

units.la: Ratio secunda, Quia Gentilis praeputium conjunctum cum Legis persecta obedientia, si fieri posset, pari loco habebitur, ac Judaei circumcisio; siquidem ad justificationem per opera nihil requirit Deus praeter moralis Legis perfectam observationem. Idcirco non eximit circumcisio ē condemnatione.
units.tr: Second reason: because the Gentile's uncircumcision, joined with perfect obedience to the law, if that could be, would be held in the same place as the Jew's circumcision; for God requires nothing for justification by works except perfect observance of the moral law. Therefore circumcision does not free from condemnation.

units.la: Verf. 27. Et quod est ex natura praeputium, si Legem servet, damnabit te, qui per literam & circumcisionem transgressor legis?
units.tr: Verse 27. And shall not uncircumcision which is by nature, if it fulfil the law, judge thee, who by the letter and circumcision dost transgress the law?

units.la: Ratio 3. Quia Gentilis natura & genere praeputium habens, si possibile esset ut Legem moralem servaret, tecum qui circumcisus es externè, & es transfes transgressor Legis, in judicio comparatus, teipso judice, argueret te condemnatione dignum. Idcirco non eximit circuncisio è condemnatione.
units.tr: Third reason: because the Gentile, having uncircumcision by nature and by birth, if it were possible for him to keep the moral law, would be set beside you, who are circumcised outwardly and are a transgressor of the law, and would, as judge of himself, prove you worthy of condemnation in judgment. Therefore circumcision does not free from condemnation.

units.la: Verf. 28. Non enim qui est in propatulo Judæus, Judæus est: nec ea quæ est in propatulo circuncisio, id est, in carne, circuncisio est.
units.tr: Verse 28. For he is not a Jew, which is one outwardly; neither is that circumcision which is outward in the flesh.

units.la: Verf. 29. Sed qui in occulto Judæus est & circuncisio cordis, id est, in spiritu, non littera: cujus Judæi laus non est ex hominibus, sed ex Deo.
units.tr: Verse 29. But he is a Jew, which is one inwardly; and circumcision is that of the heart, in the spirit, and not in the letter; whose praise is not of men, but of God.

units.la: Ratio 4. Quia neque externa professio veræ religionis, inter Judæos olim per Deum erectæ, pro vera professione religionis verae, neque circuncisio carnis externa, pro vera circumcisione est habenda, versu 28. Sed ille est verae religionis verus professor, qui in spiritu est talis: Et illa est vera circuncisio quae est cordis, quae est spiritualis in interiori anima, & non quae est in externo corpore, quæque in litera externa, seu titulo communi appellatur circumcisio. Qui verus Judæus, seu quae vera circumcisio spiritualis, laudem & commendationem habet, non apud homines, qui non vident nisi quae foris sunt conspicua, sed apud Deum, qui cor intus intuetur. Idcirco non perficit externa circumcisio justitiam, nec eximit è condemnatione quaenquam, versu 29.
units.tr: Fourth reason: because neither the external profession of the true religion, once established among the Jews by God, is to be counted as the true profession of the true religion, nor is outward bodily circumcision to be counted as true circumcision (v. 28). But he is a true professor of the true religion who is such in spirit, and that is true circumcision which is of the heart, which is spiritual in the inner soul, and not that which is in the outward body and is called circumcision by the outward letter or common title. The true Jew, or true spiritual circumcision, has praise and commendation not from men, who see only what is conspicuous outwardly, but from God, who looks into the heart within. Therefore external circumcision does not perfect righteousness, nor frees anyone from condemnation (v. 29).

units.la: Caput tertium.
units.tr: Chapter 3.

units.la: Apitis duae sunt partes: In prima solvit quinque objectiones adversus praecedentem doctrinam, ad versum 9. In secunda pergit in probanda Thesi, de justificatione non per opera, sed per fidem.
units.tr: The chapter has two parts. In the first, it answers five objections against the preceding doctrine, up to verse 9. In the second, it proceeds to prove the thesis that justification is not by works but by faith.

units.la: Verf. 1. Quae est igitur prestantia Judæi; aut quae utilitas circuncisionis?
units.tr: Verse 1. What then is the advantage of the Jew, or what is the use of circumcision?

units.la: Verf. 2. Multa per omnem modum, Primarium enim illud est quod eis credita sunt eloquia Dei.
units.tr: Verse 2. Much, in every way. For first of all, the oracles of God were entrusted to them.

units.la: Prima objectio est, Ex hac doctrina diceret aliquis nulla est Judæi praerogativa præ Gentili, nulla circumcisionis utilitas, versu 1. Respondet versu 2. hoc imprimis, & præcipuè esse Judæis privilegium, Quod foedere icto. isto cum Judæis, huic genti custodia Scripturarum sacrarum, id est, tabularum fœderis à Deo concredita sit, & judæi depositarii constituti, quod erat singulare beneficium & eximius honor.
units.tr: The first objection is this: from this doctrine someone might say that the Jew has no preeminence over the Gentile and circumcision has no use, verse 1. He answers in verse 2 that this is the chief and special privilege of the Jews: that the custody of the holy Scriptures, that is, the tables of the covenant, was entrusted by God to this nation, and the Jews were made its depositaries. This was a unique benefit and a distinguished honor.

units.la: Verf. 3. Quid tum enim si infidi fuerunt quidam; num ipsorum infidelitas, fidem Dei cassam reddet?
units.tr: Verse 3. What then if some were unfaithful? Will their unfaithfulness make the faithfulness of God void?

units.la: Secunda objectio, At per te exciderunt illo honore, quia non crediderunt eloquiis Dei, & sic fides Dei illis data in fœdere irrita reddita est. Respondet quatuor modis,
units.tr: The second objection: But through you they have fallen from that honor, because they did not believe the oracles of God, and so the faith of God given to them in the covenant has been made void. He answers in four ways.

units.la: Primo, Non sequi fideles Dei promissiones factas huic genti, inanes esse, quia aliqui ex iis increduli erant.
units.tr: First, it does not follow that the promises of God made to this nation are empty, because some of them were unbelieving.

units.la: Verf. 4. Absit: imo esto Deus verax, omnis autem homo mendax: sicut scriptum est, Ut justificeris in sermonibus tuis, & vincas quando tu judicas.
units.tr: Verse 4. Far from it. Rather, let God be true, and every man a liar; as it is written, That you may be justified in your words, and may prevail when you are judged.

units.la: Secundo, Respondet abominando objectionem, Quia absurdum est singere Deum posse fidem fallere.
units.tr: Second, he answers by abhorring the objection, because it is absurd to imagine that God can deceive faith.

units.la: Tertio, Respondet posita verissima sententia in contrarium, Quod nimirum tenendum sit Deum semper esse veracem, omnem autem hominem natura sua mendacem esse.
units.tr: Third, he answers by setting against it the most true opinion, namely that it must be held that God is always truthful, but every man by his nature is a liar.

units.la: Quarto, Respondet hominum peccata & mendacia à Deo non impedire, quin Deus præstet promissa, ut potius illustriorem faciant ejus veritatem, misericordiam & justitiam, Quia quanto plura & graviora sunt hominum peccata, tanto illustrior Dei justitia cum punit, & misericordia & veritas cum parcit. Quod confirmat ex Psal 51. verf. 4. ubi David in confessione peccatorum suorum commendat Dei veritatem, docetque Deum semper victorem in causa pronunciandum, quoties quisquam de ejus factis vel dictis disputationem contra ipsum suscipit.
units.tr: Fourth, he answers that the sins and lies of men do not prevent God from performing his promises, but rather make his truth, mercy and justice more illustrious. For the more numerous and grievous the sins of men, the more illustrious God's justice is when he punishes, and his mercy and truth when he pardons. He confirms this from Psalm 51:4, where David, in confessing his sins, commends the truth of God and teaches that God is always to be pronounced the victor in the cause whenever anyone takes up dispute against his deeds or words.

units.la: Verf. 5. Quod si injustitia nostra Dei justitiam commendat, quid dicemus; num injustus Deus, qui inferat pœnam (humano more loquor.)
units.tr: Verse 5. But if our unrighteousness commends the righteousness of God, what shall we say? Is God unjust who inflicts wrath? (I speak after the manner of men.)

units.la: Objectio 3. Ex verbis Psalmi in blasphemiam detortis, Si nostra peccata illustrant Dei justitiam, tum injustus videtur Deus, qui vindicat peccata, quibus ipse glorificatur. Hæc objicit Apostolus in persona hominis Deum ignorantis.
units.tr: Objection 3, drawn from the words of the Psalm twisted into blasphemy: if our sins illustrate the righteousness of God, then God seems unjust who punishes the sins by which he himself is glorified. The Apostle raises this objection in the person of a man ignorant of God.

units.la: Verf. 6. Absit. alioquin quo modo judex erit Deus mundi?
units.tr: Verse 6. Far from it; otherwise how will God judge the world?

units.la: Respondet primo, rejiciendo objectionem tanquam blasphemiam. Absit, inquit.
units.tr: He answers first by rejecting the objection as blasphemy. Far from it, he says.

units.la: Secundo respondet, rationem reddendo rejiciendi objectionem, Quia impossibile est Deum, qui est mundi judex, esse injustum.
units.tr: Second, he answers by giving the reason for rejecting the objection: it is impossible that God, who is the judge of the world, should be unjust.

units.la: Verf. 7 Etenim si veritas Dei per meum mendacium redundavit in gloriam ipsius, cur amplius ego ut peccator condemnor?
units.tr: Verse 7. For if the truth of God has abounded through my lie to his glory, why am I still condemned as a sinner?

units.la: Verf. 8 Ac non (sicut de nobis male loquuntur, & sicut quidam aiunt nos dicere) faciamus mala ut veniant bona? quorum damnatio justa est.
units.tr: Verse 8. And why not do evil that good may come, as we are slandered, and as some report us to say? Their condemnation is just.

units.la: Objectio 4. urgens superiorem, Si per meum peccatum, verbi gratia, mendacium, Dei veritas magis glorificatur, non tantum non condemnandus sum peccati, sed etiam studendum peccato, ut gloria Deo major cedat. Pro responsione ostendit primo, calumniatores affirmare, sed falso, hanc esse apostolorum doctrinam, ut faciamus mala, eo fine ut eveniat bonum.
units.tr: Objection 4, pressing the previous one: if through my sin, for example lying, the truth of God is more glorified, then I am not only not to be condemned for sin, but ought even to pursue sin, so that greater glory may accrue to God. In reply, he shows first that slanderers assert, but falsely, that this is the doctrine of the apostles, that we should do evil so that good may come.

units.la: Secundo Respondet & calumniatores istiusmodi, & eos qui docent vel sequuntur hanc doctrinam, facientes malum, ut eveniat bonum, juste damnari a Deo.
units.tr: Second, he answers that such slanderers, and those who teach or follow this doctrine of doing evil that good may come, are justly condemned by God.

units.la: Verf. 9. Quid igitur praecellimus? nullo modo: nam ante criminati sumus & Judaeos & Graecos omnes esse sub peccato.
units.tr: Verse 9. What then? Are we better? In no way. For we have already charged both Jews and Greeks, that all are under sin.

units.la: Objectio 5. At per te non adhuc praecellimus nos Judaei Gentilibus, scilicet in negotio justificationis per opera, quae principalis est quaestio.
units.tr: Objection 5. But by your reasoning we Jews are not yet better than the Gentiles, namely in the matter of justification by works, which is the principal question.

units.la: Respondet hoc respectu, nullo modo praecellere Judaeum Gentili, & rationem reddit, Quia hactenus probavimus, inquit, & Judaeos & Graecos esse sub peccato.
units.tr: He answers that in this respect the Jew in no way excels the Gentile, and he gives the reason: because, he says, we have so far proved that both Jews and Greeks are under sin.

units.la: Secunda Pars.
units.tr: The Second Part.

units.la: Secunda pars Capitis in qua redit ad disputationem prosequendam de justificatione non per opera, sed per fidem.
units.tr: The second part of the chapter, in which he returns to pursue the argument concerning justification not by works but by faith.

units.la: Verf. 10. Sicut scriptum est, Non est justus, ne unus quidem:
units.tr: Verse 10. As it is written, There is none righteous, no, not one.

units.la: Verf. 11. Non est qui intelligat, non est qui exquirat Deum.
units.tr: Verse 11. There is none who understands, there is none who seeks after God.

units.la: Verf. 12. Omnes declinaverunt, simul inutiles facti sunt: non est qui faciat quod bonum est, non est usque ad unum
units.tr: Verse 12. They have all turned aside, they have together become unprofitable; there is none who does good, no, not one.

units.la: Arg. 4. de justificatione non per opera sed per fidem. Scriptura te-stratur omnes homines esse sub peccato & obnoxios condemnationi,ad ver-sum 20. Ergo nullus ex operibus legis justificatur, versu. 20.
units.tr: Arg. 4 on justification not by works but by faith. Scripture testifies that all men are under sin and liable to condemnation, verse 20. Therefore no one is justified by the works of the law, verse 20.

units.la: Scripturæ testimonia sunt Sex. Primum ex Psal. 14. versu. 1, 2, 3. & Psal. 53. versu. 1, 2, 3. ubi Propheta loquens de irregenitis sui temporis, & omnibus quoad statum naturalem extra Christum, pronunciat: Primo. Neminem esse justum, versu 10. Secundo, Omnes esse cæcos & ignaros rerum, quæ ad salutem faciunt Tertio, Nullos esse qui Deum cognoscendi, Deum colendi, aut habendæ cum ipso communionis desiderio tangantur, versu 11. Quarto, Omnes tenaces esse apostasiæ originalis à Deo, & a cognita ejus voluntate: Quinto. Omnes inutiles, putridos,& abominabiles factos esse ob fæditatem scelerum: Sexto, Nullum esse ex hominibus irregenitis scilicet, qui ullum faciat bonum, & per consequens, nullum esse qui quantum quantum facit, non faciat malum & malum tantum; nam etiam cum opus mandatum facit, non mandanti Deo, sed sibi servit, & suis idolis sacrificat irregenitus.
units.tr: There are six testimonies of Scripture. The first is from Psal. 14, verse 1, 2, 3, and Psal. 53, verse 1, 2, 3, where the Prophet, speaking of the unregenerate of his own time and of all who are in their natural state apart from Christ, declares: First, that no one is righteous, verse 10; second, that all are blind and ignorant of the things that make for salvation; third, that none is moved by a desire to know God, to worship God, or to have communion with him, verse 11; fourth, that all are tenacious of original apostasy from God and from his known will; fifth, that all have become useless, putrid and abominable because of the foulness of their sins; sixth, that there is no one among the unregenerate who does any good, and consequently no one who, however much he does, does not do evil, and only evil. For even when the unregenerate man does what is commanded, he does not serve the commanding God but himself, and sacrifices to his own idols.

units.la: Verf. 13. Sepulchrum apertum guttur eorum: linguis suis ad dolum usi sunt; venenum aspidum sub labiis eorum;
units.tr: Verse 13. Their throat is an open sepulchre; they have used their tongues for deceit; the venom of asps is under their lips.

units.la: Secundum testimonium est ex Psal. 5. 9. In quo David, in typo inimicorum suorum; omnes irregenitos, seu Deo non reconciliatos, damnat cordis corruptissimi, unde nihil nisi fætidum & Deo abominabile prodeat, adeo ut guttur uniuscujusque sit instar sepulchri recens aperti, tetrum ac pestiferum fætorem pravarum cogitationum exhalantis, ex quorum ore nihil nisi pestilentes, noxii & dolosi sermones exeant.
units.tr: The second testimony is from Psal. 5:9. In it David, in the type of his enemies, condemns all the unregenerate, or those not reconciled to God, whose hearts are so corrupt that nothing but what is foul and abominable to God comes forth from them. So each one's throat is like a freshly opened sepulchre, breathing out the foul and deadly stench of depraved thoughts, and from whose mouth issue nothing but pestilent, harmful and deceitful words.

units.la: Venenum Tertium testimonium ex Psal. 140. 3. In quo idem confirmatur de Davidis inimicis, qui typi erant non reconciliatorum Deo per Christum, seu irregenitorum hominum, Quod scilicet semper parati sint, venenata dicta, non minus nocentia quam virus aspidum ex ore pharetra depromere.
units.tr: The third testimony is from Psal. 140:3. In it the same thing is confirmed concerning David's enemies, who were types of men not reconciled to God through Christ, that is, of the unregenerate: namely, that they are always ready to bring forth from their mouths venomous words, no less harmful than the poison of asps drawn from a quiver.

units.la: Verf. 14. Quorum os diris & amaritudine plenum est:
units.tr: Verse 14. Whose mouth is full of cursing and bitterness.

units.la: Quartum testimonium ex Psal. 10. 7. in eundem sensum, in quo Psaltes de homine naturali conqueritur, Quod os plenum execrationibus, & calumniis refertum habeat, quibus & Dei gloria, & proximorum fama, lædatur.
units.tr: The fourth testimony is from Psalm 10:7, to the same effect, where the Psalmist complains of the natural man, that his mouth is full of curses and slanders, by which both the glory of God and the good name of neighbours are harmed.

units.la: Verf. 15. Veloces pedes eorum ad effundendum sanguinem.
units.tr: Verse 15. Their feet are swift to shed blood.

units.la: Verf. 16. Contritio & calamitas in viis eorum.
units.tr: Verse 16. Destruction and misery are in their ways.

units.la: Verf. 17. Et viam pacis non cognoverunt.
units.tr: Verse 17. And the way of peace they have not known.

units.la: Quintum testimonium ex Psal. 59. 7, 8. In quo irregeniti pronunciantur rei saevitiae, violentiae, oppressionis & homicidii, qui nihil aliud quam miseriam, & perditionem, sibi aliisque, in toto vitae suae curriculo procreant, quique a ratione, vel pacem, vel boni quidvis procurandi sibi vel aliis, alienissimi sunt.
units.tr: The fifth testimony is from Psalm 59:7, 8. In it the unregenerate are declared guilty of cruelty, violence, oppression and murder. Throughout the whole course of their lives they produce nothing but misery and ruin for themselves and others, and they are utterly estranged from reason, whether from peace or from the pursuit of any good for themselves or others.

units.la: Verf. 18. Non est timor Dei coram oculis eorum.
units.tr: Verse 18. There is no fear of God before their eyes.

units.la: Sextum testimonium ex Psal. 36. 2. in quo ex factis damnantur omnes irregeniti profanitatis & contemptus Dei, nam cum vacui sint timore Dei, nihil est quod prohibeat quominus in omnia scelera praecipites ruant.
units.tr: The sixth testimony is from Psalm 36:2, in which all the unregenerate are condemned by their deeds of profanity and contempt of God. Since they are empty of the fear of God, nothing prevents them from rushing headlong into every kind of wickedness.

units.la: Verf. 19. Scimus autem, quaecunque Lex dicit, iis qui in Lege sunt dicere: ut omne os obturetur, & obnoxius fiat totus mundus condemnationi Dei.
units.tr: Verse 19. Now we know that whatever the Law says, it says to those who are under the Law, so that every mouth may be stopped, and the whole world may become subject to the condemnation of God.

units.la: Occurrit objectioni, & ne quis elideret ictum testimoniorum allatorum, quasi pertinerent ad paucos aliquos, & certos impios, qui temporibus Davidis aut Isaiae vivebant, ostendit taxari hic commune ingenium omnium, qui sub lege seu foedere operum vivunt, & non sub gratia, proinde que legis sententias has prolatas, ad omnes homines in corruptae naturae statu constitutos, maxime vero ad Judaeos dirigi; unde infertur triplex Conclusio, Prima, Hinc omne os obturatur, ne quis in se glorietur, aut se excusef in Dei judicio.
units.tr: He meets the objection. Lest anyone should evade the force of the testimonies cited, as if they pertained only to a few particular impious men who lived in the time of David or Isaiah, he shows that the common disposition of all who live under the law or covenant of works, and not under grace, is censured here. Therefore these sentences of the law apply to all men placed in the state of corrupted nature, and most of all to the Jews. From this a threefold conclusion is drawn. First: hence every mouth is stopped, so that no one may glory in himself or excuse himself in God's judgment.

units.la: Altera conclusio, Hinc totus mundus obnoxius redditur condemnationi, & obstrictus ad poenam.
units.tr: Second conclusion: hence the whole world is made liable to condemnation and bound over to punishment.

units.la: Verf. 20. Propterea ex operibus Legis nulla caro justificabitur in conspectu ejus, per Legem enim agnitio peccati.
units.tr: Verse 20. Therefore by the works of the Law no flesh shall be justified in his sight, for through the Law comes the knowledge of sin.

units.la: Tertia conclusio & principalis ex testimoniis citatis illata, Ergo ex operibus Legis nulla caro justificabitur in conspectu Dei: nam quin aliqui justificentur coram hominibus ex operibus, nihil obstat.
units.tr: The third conclusion, and the principal one drawn from the testimonies cited: therefore by the works of the Law no flesh shall be justified in the sight of God. That some may be justified before men by works is no obstacle.

units.la: Per Legem enim Arg. 5. Ad idem probandum serviens, Omnes homines per legem peccati convincuntur & damnantur; nam per legem est agnitio peccati uniuscujusque, non acquisitio justitiæ cuiquam; Ergo nullus ex operibus legis justificatur.
units.tr: For through the Law: Argument 5, serving to prove the same point. All men are convicted and condemned through the law of sin, for through the law comes the knowledge of each one's sin, not the acquisition of righteousness for anyone. Therefore no one is justified by the works of the law.

units.la: Verf. 21. Nunc vero absque Lege justitia Dei patefacta est, comprobata testimonio Legis ac Prophetarum.
units.tr: Verse 21. But now, apart from the Law, the righteousness of God has been revealed, attested by the Law and the Prophets.

units.la: Verf. 22. Justitia, inquam, Dei per fidem Iesu Christi in omnes & super omnes qui credunt: non enim est distinctio.
units.tr: Verse 22. The righteousness, I say, of God through faith in Jesus Christ, unto all and upon all who believe, for there is no distinction.

units.la: Arg. 6. Ad partem thesis affirmativam faciens. Nunc in Euangelio patefacta est justitia Dei sine legis operibus, comprobata testimonio scripturarum, ea scilicet justitia Dei quæ omnibus credentibus datur & imputatur per fidem apprehendentibus oblatam justitiam Iesu Christi, sine discrimine nationum aut personarum. Ergo per solam hanc justitiam Dei, quæ est per fidem in Christum, justificamur. Valet argumentum, nam si per legis opera non possumus justificari, & tamen alia inveniutur ratio nos justificandi, nempe ea quam in Lege & Prophetis Deus nobis commendat, ut, E. g. cum dixit in lege, In semine Abrahami benedicentur omnes Gentes: & in Prophetis; Justus ex fide vivet, æquum est ut per hanc posteriorem rationem solam justificari nos credamus.
units.tr: Argument 6, supporting the affirmative side of the thesis. Now in the Gospel the righteousness of God has been revealed apart from the works of the law, attested by the testimony of the Scriptures. This is the righteousness of God that is given and imputed to all believers, who by faith lay hold of the righteousness of Jesus Christ offered to them, without distinction of nations or persons. Therefore we are justified by this righteousness of God alone, which is through faith in Christ. The argument holds. For if we cannot be justified by the works of the law, and yet another way of justifying us is found, namely the one that God commends to us in the Law and the Prophets, as when he said in the law, In your seed shall all the nations be blessed, and in the Prophets, The just shall live by faith, then it is right that we believe we are justified by this latter way alone.

units.la: Deinde, cum justitia duplex tantum concipi possit, una quæ vocatur legis, seu operum, seu inhærens, seu propria hominis operantis justitia: alia quæ vocatur Euangelii, seu fidei, seu aliena imputata, seu Christi, & Dei donantis justitia qua Deus ex pacto judicali, transfert justitiam Christi obedientia comparatam, in omnes credentes; polt exclusam primam illam justitiam, seu justificandi rationem, quia illa jam est impossibilis, necessario admittenda est altera, quæ commendatur nobis in scriptura veteri, revelatur nunc in Euangelio, seu Novo Testamento, & sola est possibilis, sola Deo accepta, & sola Dei justitia dici meretur.
units.tr: Next, since only two kinds of righteousness can be conceived: one, called the righteousness of the law, or of works, or inherent, or the proper righteousness of the man who works; the other, called the righteousness of the Gospel, or of faith, or alien and imputed, or of Christ, and of God who bestows it, by which God, from the judicial covenant, transfers to all believers the righteousness obtained by Christ's obedience. After the first kind of righteousness, or way of justifying, has been excluded because it is now impossible, the other must necessarily be admitted. It is commended to us in the Old Scripture, is revealed now in the Gospel, or New Testament, and alone is possible, alone acceptable to God, and alone deserves to be called the righteousness of God.

units.la: Verf. 23. Omnes enim peccaverunt, ac deficiuntur gloria Dei.
units.tr: Verse 23. For all have sinned, and come short of the glory of God.

units.la: Verf. 24. Ut qui justificentur gratis, id est, ejus gratia, per redemptionem factam in Iesu Christo:
units.tr: Verse 24. Being justified freely by his grace, through the redemption that is in Jesus Christ.

units.la: Arg. 7. Quo ostenditur communis morbus omnium hominum, sic etiam communis remedii necessitas: Omnes homines sine exceptione peccarunt, & jure excluduntur a gloria Dei, seu vita æterna. Ergo omnes non aliter justificantur quam gratis, seu divina gratia per redemptionem factam in Christo, hoc est, non aliter justificari possunt, quam per fidem in CHRISTUM Redemptorem, qui sanguine suo justitiam, & salutem emit nobis, & tanto pretio emptam, nostram facit gratis, ex gratia.
units.tr: Argument 7. By this is shown that sin is the common disease of all men, and so also the need of a common remedy: all men without exception have sinned, and are rightly excluded from the glory of God, that is, from eternal life. Therefore all are justified in no other way than freely, that is, by divine grace through the redemption made in Christ. In other words, they can be justified only through faith in Christ the Redeemer, who by his own blood bought righteousness and salvation for us, and, having bought them at so great a price, makes them ours freely, by grace.

units.la: Verf. 25. Quem proposuit Deus placamentum per fidem in fanguine ipsius, ad demonstrationem justitiæ suæ, prætereundo peccata quæ antecesserunt, in illa Dei tolerantia.
units.tr: Verse 25. Whom God has set forth to be a propitiation through faith in his blood, to declare his righteousness, for the remission of sins that are past, through the forbearance of God.

units.la: Verf. 26, Ad demonstrationem justitiæ suæ præsenti tempore, ut sit ipse justus, & justificans eum qui est ex fide Iesu.
units.tr: Verse 26. To declare, I say, his righteousness at this present time, that he might be just, and the justifier of him who believes in Jesus.

units.la: 8. Arg. Proposuit Deus CHRISTUM, ut esset placamentum, seu sacrificium propitiatorium quo placatur ira Dei, in omnes qui per fidem ipsum apprehendunt. Ergo non nisi per fidem in CHRISTUM offerentem hoc placamentum, & sanguinantem, possibile est hominem justificari, nisi rationem sui placandi mutaret Deus.
units.tr: Argument 8. God has set forth Christ to be a propitiation, that is, a propitiatory sacrifice by which the wrath of God is appeased, for all who lay hold of him by faith. Therefore a man can be justified only by faith in Christ, who offers this propitiation and shed his blood, unless God were to change the manner in which he is appeased.

units.la: Ad demonstrationem ] Arg. 9. Deus præsenti hoc tempore Euangelii proposuit CHRISTUM placamentum iræ suæ, per fidem ipsum amplectentibus, ut in hac justificandi ratione manifestaretur justitia ipsius in tempore præterito, in tolerantia & remissione peccatorum præteritorum, quæ ab initio mundi toleravit & remisit! Quod scilicet Deus suorum peccata nec toleraverit, nec remiserit unquam, nisi propter futurum propitiatorium sacrificium CHRISTI, Ideoque sine justitiæ suæ violatione. Ergo hæc justificandi ratio non minus tenenda quam justitiæ Dei gloria manifestanda est: Res patet. Nam si justificatio per fidem in sanguine CHRISTI ostendit Deum nunquam remisisse peccata, nisi ob satisfactionem factam iuxtæ justitiæ per CHRISTI sanguinem; Certè celatam vellet Dei justitiam, qui aliam justificandi rationem quam per fidem statuit.
units.tr: To declare: Argument 9. God, in this present time of the Gospel, has set forth Christ as a propitiation for his wrath to those who embrace him by faith, so that in this way of justifying the righteousness of God might be made manifest in past time, in his forbearance and remission of past sins, which he has forborne and remitted from the beginning of the world. For God never forbore or remitted the sins of his people, except on account of the future propitiatory sacrifice of Christ, and so without violation of his righteousness. Therefore this way of justifying must be held no less firmly than the glory of God's righteousness must be made manifest. The matter is plain. For if justification by faith in the blood of Christ shows that God never remitted sins except on account of satisfaction made according to justice through the blood of Christ, then surely he would wish his righteousness to be hidden who has established another way of justifying than by faith.

units.la: Vt ipse sit justus ] Hoc argumentum confirmat, quod Deus propofuerit CHRISTUM, ut esset placamentum per fidem in sanguine ipsius, non solum ut declararet se esse justum in promissò Messia mittendo, propter quem gratis simul & juste peccata remitteret, sed etiam ut se veræ justitiæ autorem esse & largitorem, nobis omni justitia propria destitutis & credentibus in IESUM CHRISTUM, ostenderet. Ergo hæc justificandi ratio per fidem, non minus tenenda est, quam justitiæ, fidelitatis, & bonitatis Dei gloria in justificandis fidelibus declaranda est.
units.tr: That he might be just: This argument confirms that God set forth Christ to be a propitiation through faith in his blood, not only so that he might declare himself just in sending the promised Messiah, on account of whom he would remit sins freely and yet justly, but also so that he might show himself to be the author and giver of true righteousness to us, who have lost all our own righteousness and believe in Jesus Christ. Therefore this way of justifying by faith must be held no less firmly than the glory of God's righteousness, faithfulness and goodness must be declared in justifying believers.

units.la: Verf. 27. Ubi igitur gloriatio? exclusa est: Per quam legem? operum? Non: sed per legem fidei. Verf. 28.
units.tr: Verse 27. Where is boasting then? It is excluded. By what law? Of works? Nay: but by the law of faith. Verse 28.

units.la: Verf. 28. Colligimus igitur fide justificari hominem absque operibus Legis.
units.tr: Verse 28. Therefore we conclude that a man is justified by faith without the deeds of the law.

units.la: Arg. 10. Quia per legem fidei, seu fædus gratiæ, quod fidem requirit ad justificationem per justitiam alienam; excluditur gloriatio hominum in se, & non per legem operum, seu fædus operum, quod operum perfectionem exigit, & gloriandi materiam in justitia inhærente hominibus suppeditat. Idcirco concludimus (inquit) fide justificari hominem absque operibus legis. Valet argumentum, Quia si homines justificarentur per opera sua, & inhærentem justitiam, possent gloriari causam meritoriam justificationis suæ esse in seipsis; sed qui justificantur fide, coguntur suæ justitiæ inhærenti renunciare, & totam fiduciam suam in Christi unius justitiæ imputatione, & Dei gratia sola collocare.
units.tr: Argument 10. Because it is by the law of faith, that is, the covenant of grace, which requires faith for justification by an alien righteousness, that the boasting of men in themselves is excluded; and not by the law of works, that is, the covenant of works, which demands perfect works and supplies men with matter for boasting in an inherent righteousness. Hence, he says, we conclude that a man is justified by faith without the deeds of the law. The argument holds. For if men were justified by their own works and an inherent righteousness, they could boast that the meritorious cause of their justification lay in themselves; but those who are justified by faith are compelled to renounce their inherent righteousness and to place all their trust in the imputation of the one righteousness of Christ and in the grace of God alone.

units.la: Verf. 29. An Deus Judæorum solum? annon & Gentium certè & Gentium.
units.tr: Verse 29. "Is God the God of the Jews only? Is he not also, surely, of the Gentiles? Yes, of the Gentiles also."

units.la: Verf. 30. Quandoquidem Deus unus est qui justificabit circumcisionem ex fide, & præputium per fidem.
units.tr: Verse 30. "Since God is one, who will justify the circumcision by faith, and the uncircumcision through faith."

units.la: Claudit hanc disputationem solutione duarum quæstionum, quarum solutio doctrinæ præsenti lucem affert: Prima quæstio est, Sitne hæc justificandi ratio per fidem, communis & Judæis & Gentibus? Cui respondet, Quod communis sit utriusque, cujus rationem addit, quia Deus justificatorum est unus, Idcirco unam oportet esse rationem justificationis omnium, scilicet ex fide, seu per fidem. Nam si una ratione justificaret Judæos, alia ratione vero Gentes, videretur Deus à se dissidere in negotio justitiæ & salutis communicandæ peccatoribus, Judæis & Gentibus, quod absurdum est.
units.tr: He closes this disputation by resolving two questions, and the solution of these sheds light on the present doctrine. The first question is: is this way of justifying through faith common to both Jews and Gentiles? To this he answers that it is common to both, and he gives the reason: because God is one of those who are justified, so there ought to be one way of justification for all, namely from faith, or through faith. For if God justified the Jews by one way and the Gentiles by another, God would seem to be at odds with himself in the matter of righteousness and of communicating salvation to sinners, both Jews and Gentiles, and this is absurd.

units.la: Verf. 31. Legem igitur cassam reddimus per fidem? Absit: imò Legem stabilimus.
units.tr: Verse 31. "Do we then make void the law through faith? God forbid: yea, we establish the law."

units.la: Altera quæstio est, An doctrina fidei seu justificationis per fidem, reddat legem inanem seu otiosam, & frustra datam, dum negat justificari homines per legem? Respondet Legem minimè inanem reddi, sed stabiliri potius per fidei doctrinam. Nam fides, seu fidei doctrina stabilit Legem tribus modis; Primò, respectu comminationum, ostendendo Christum mortuum esse ex Legis sententia, ut Legi satisfaceret, & nos morti esse obnoxios, nisi liberemur per CHRISTUM à morte. Secundo, Respectu præceptorum, quia Legis obedientiam perfectam demonstrat jam præstitam, in CHRISTI justitia. Tertio, Fides Legem stabilit, respectu Fidelium, quia fide justificati, virtute CHRISTI novam obedientiam inchoant, qui ante justificationem per fidem, nihil nisi peccare poterant.
units.tr: The second question is: does the doctrine of faith, or of justification through faith, make the law empty or idle, and given in vain, since it denies that men are justified by the law? He answers that the law is by no means made empty, but rather is established by the doctrine of faith. For faith, or the doctrine of faith, establishes the law in three ways. First, with respect to its threats, by showing that Christ died under the sentence of the law, so as to satisfy the law, and that we were liable to death unless we were freed from death through Christ. Second, with respect to its precepts, because it demonstrates that the perfect obedience of the law has already been rendered in the righteousness of Christ. Third, faith establishes the law with respect to believers, because those justified by faith, by the power of Christ, begin a new obedience, whereas before justification through faith they could do nothing but sin.

units.la: Caput quartum.
units.tr: Chapter 4.

units.la: AD Caput usque duodecimum Apostolus hanc divinam justificationis rationem per fidem, absque operibus illustrat, commendat, & porro plurimis argumentis confirmat. Nos facilioris Methodi causa confirmationem hujus doctrinæ facimus sextuplicem.
units.tr: Up to the twelfth chapter the Apostle illustrates, commends and further confirms with many arguments this divine manner of justification through faith, apart from works. For the sake of an easier method, we make the confirmation of this doctrine sixfold.

units.la: Prima Confirmatio Justificationis per fidem, quæ hoc Capite continetur, est ab exemplo Abrahæ potissimum, cujus justificandi ratio communis est, & Judæis & Gentibus, & cujus fides nobis omnibus in exemplar à Deo proposita est.
units.tr: The first confirmation of justification through faith, which is contained in this chapter, is taken chiefly from the example of Abraham, whose manner of justification is common to both Jews and Gentiles, and whose faith God has set before all of us as a pattern.

units.la: Capitis partes tres sunt: In prima, exemplum justificationis Abrahæ proponitur, ad versum 9. In secunda, Justificationis rationem hanc probat communem esse Judæis, & Gentibus, ad versum 18. In tertia, Fides Abrahæ commendatur, in usum Credentium, ad finem.
units.tr: The chapter has three parts. In the first, the example of Abraham's justification is set forth, to verse 9. In the second, he proves that this manner of justification is common to Jews and Gentiles, to verse 18. In the third, the faith of Abraham is commended for the use of believers, to the end.

units.la: Vers. 1. Quid igitur dicemus Abrahamum patrem illum nostrum nactum esse secundum carnem?
units.tr: Verse 1. What then shall we say that Abraham, our father, has obtained according to the flesh?

units.la: Quod ad exemplum attinet justificationis Abrahæ, sub forma interrogationis, negat Abrahamum consecutum fuisse justificationem per carnem, seu opera legis, seu per inhærentem justitiam, quæ caro dicitur, Galat. 3. versu 3. respectu spiritualis justitiæ CHRISTI. Unde sequitur neminem justificari operibus.
units.tr: As to the example of Abraham's justification, in the form of a question he denies that Abraham obtained justification through the flesh, that is, through the works of the law or through inherent righteousness, which is called flesh, Galatians 3:3, in comparison with the spiritual righteousness of Christ. Hence it follows that no one is justified by works.

units.la: Vers. 2. Nam si Abrahamus ex operibus justificatus fuit, habet de quo glorietur, at non apud Deum.
units.tr: Verse 2. For if Abraham was justified by works, he has something to boast of, but not before God.

units.la: Hanc Thesin de Abrahamo confirmat quinque rationibus: Prima ratio, Si Abraham ex operibus justificatus fuit, habet quod glorietur, at non apud Deum, supple habet quod glorietur.
