units.tr: Verse 14. For as many as are led by the Spirit of God, they are the sons of God.

units.la: Arg. 4. Confirmans superius, Omnes qui sequuntur mandata, & ductum Spiritus sancti, testantur se esse filios Dei, virtute Spiritus regenitos: Ergo ut probetis vos esse Dei filios, Spiritui Dei obtemperantes, sanctitati studete.
units.tr: Fourth argument. Confirming what was said above: all who follow the commands and leading of the Holy Spirit testify that they are sons of God, regenerated by the power of the Spirit. Therefore, that you may prove yourselves sons of God by obeying the Spirit of God, devote yourselves to holiness.

units.la: Verf. 15. Non enim accepistis Spiritum servitutis rursus ad metum, sed accepistis spiritum adoptionis per quem clamamus, Abba, id est, Pater.
units.tr: Verse 15. For you have not received the spirit of bondage again to fear, but you have received the spirit of adoption, by which we cry, Abba, that is, Father.

units.la: Simul etiam, Confirmans eos esse Dei filios, Quia postquam confugerunt ad Christum, & foedus gratiae amplexi fuerunt, liberati sunt per fidem, à servili metu condemnationis, (quem incutit Spiritus, omnibus, qui ex foedere legali, seu operibus quaerunt vitam) & donati sunt Spiritu adoptionis. Hinc argumentum; Postquam foedus gratiae, per fidem in Christum, amplexi estis, non datur vobis amplius, secundum Evangelij tenorem, servilis metus condemnationis, sed Spiritus adoptionis, ut possitis Deum familiariter, cum Dei populo, sua quisque lingua, Patrem invocare. Ergo & filii Dei estis, & ut filios Dei in sanctitatis studio, vos gerere tenemini.
units.tr: At the same time, confirming that they are sons of God: since they have fled to Christ and embraced the covenant of grace, they have been freed through faith from the servile fear of condemnation (which the Spirit inspires in all who seek life from the legal covenant, or by works), and they have been given the Spirit of adoption. Hence the argument: since you have embraced the covenant of grace through faith in Christ, the servile fear of condemnation is no longer given to you, according to the tenor of the Gospel, but the Spirit of adoption, so that each of you may call upon God as Father familiarly, in his own tongue, together with God's people. Therefore you both are sons of God, and you are bound to conduct yourselves as sons of God in the pursuit of holiness.

units.la: Verf. 16. Et ille ipse Spiritus testatur una cum spiritu nostro, nos esse filios Dei.
units.tr: Verse 16. The same Spirit also bears witness with our spirit that we are the children of God.

units.la: Spiritus Dei, obsignat in cordibus nostris, & una testatur cum Spiritu nostro, seu conscientiis nostris, nos esse Dei filios: Tenemur ergo sicut decet Dei filios, in sanctitatis studio nos gerere.
units.tr: The Spirit of God seals in our hearts and, together with our spirit, that is, our consciences, bears witness that we are the sons of God. We are therefore bound, as becomes the sons of God, to conduct ourselves in the pursuit of holiness.

units.la: Secunda Pars.
units.tr: Second Part.

units.la: Quod si filij, etiam haeredes: haeredes quidem Dei, coheredes autem Christi, si modo cum eo patimur, ut cum eo etiam glorificemur.
units.tr: If children, then heirs also: heirs indeed of God, and fellow-heirs with Christ, if so be that we suffer with him, that we may also be glorified together with him.

units.la: Secunda pars capitis, continens consolationes justificatorum per fidem, adversus afflictionum, in hac vita, acerbitatem.
units.tr: The second part of the chapter, containing the consolations of those justified by faith against the bitterness of afflictions in this life.

units.la: Praemittit autem consectarium, ex superioribus deductum, in quo probat fideles, seu justificatos per fidem, non solum haeredes esse Dei, & jus habere ad omnia ejus bona, sed etiam coheredes esse Christi, & ascitos per adoptionem, ad communionem cum unigenito filio, & in societatem haereditatis cum ipso, propterea quod sint filii Dei. Hoc jus est justificatorum ad haereditatem, cujus haereditatis possessionem, ut adeant, annectit conditionem afflictionum, cum Christo perferendarum. Consolationis autem argumenta affert Tredecim.
units.tr: He first sets down a corollary, drawn from what has gone before, in which he proves that the faithful, that is, those justified by faith, are not only heirs of God and have a right to all his good things, but are also fellow-heirs with Christ, adopted into fellowship with the only-begotten Son and into partnership in the inheritance with him, because they are sons of God. This is the right of the justified to the inheritance. To take possession of that inheritance, he attaches the condition of afflictions to be endured with Christ. He brings forward thirteen arguments of consolation.

units.la: Primum argumentum consolationis, Communionem cum Christo in afflictionibus, sequetur communio cum Christo in regno caelesti, & in possessione gloriosae haereditatis. Ergo in afflictionibus nosmet consolemur.
units.tr: First argument of consolation: if we share with Christ in his afflictions, we shall also share with him in the heavenly kingdom and in possession of the glorious inheritance. Therefore let us console ourselves in afflictions.

units.la: Verf. 18 Reor enim minime pares esse præsentis temporis perpessiones gloriæ in nobis revelandæ.
units.tr: Verse 18. For I reckon that the sufferings of this present time are not worthy to be compared with the glory which shall be revealed in us.

units.la: Arg. 2. Non est hæc dura conditio; Quia subductis calculis, comperi- tio, quæcunque in hac vita perpetimur, justitiæ causa, indigna esse ut ullo modo, æquiparentur gloriæ revelandæ, & in nos tandem conferendæ; sive rerum qualitatem, sive temporis durationem spectemus: Ergo in afflictionibus nosmet consolemur.
units.tr: Argument 2. This condition is not harsh. When we make the reckoning, we find that whatever we suffer in this life for the sake of righteousness is unworthy of being set beside the glory that is to be revealed and finally conferred upon us, whether we look at the quality of the things or the length of the time. Therefore let us console ourselves in afflictions.

units.la: Verf. 19. Etenim mundus hic conditus; exerto capite, observans expectat dum revelentur filij Dei.
units.tr: Verse 19. For the earnest expectation of the creature waiteth for the manifestation of the sons of God.

units.la: Arg. 3. Figuratè propositum; tota mundi machina, suo modo nobiscum patiens, sustinet se ipse revelandæ filiorum Dei gloriæ in die judicii, & solicitè quasi exerto capite, tempus illud optatum expectat; Ergo & nos, hac etiam spe, cum consolatione, nosmet sustinere debemus.
units.tr: Argument 3. This is put figuratively: the whole machinery of the world, suffering with us in its own way, sustains itself in the hope of the revelation of the glory of the sons of God on the day of judgment, and waits anxiously for that longed-for time, as it were with head stretched out. Therefore we too ought to sustain ourselves with this hope, and take comfort in it.

units.la: Verf. 20. Nam vanitati mundus hic conditus, subjectus est, non sua sponte, sed propter eum qui subjecit eum isti vanitati.
units.tr: Verse 20. For the creature was made subject to vanity, not willingly, but by reason of him who hath subjected it to that vanity.

units.la: Explicat hoc argumentum; Ostendendo primo, res creatas, subjectas esse vanitati, id est, conditioni corruptibili, & abusui vanissimorum hominum, qui creaturâ abutuntur, ad omne genus peccati, eamque sibi servire cogunt, ad libidines suas vanissimas explendas: Secundo creatnram, non subjici huic servituti, sua sponte, seu naturali sua propensione, seu secundum usum naturalem, ad quem à Deo condita est, sed propter voluntatem, seu judicium Dei, qui huic maledictioni subjecit creaturam, unà cum homine peccatore, cujus causa creata est mundi machina. Hinc, Arg. 4. Creaturæ subjacent vanitati, & miseriæ, non sua sed nostra culpa, & patienter eam sustinent: Ergo multo magis nos, qui miseriis nostra culpa subjacemus, sub spe liberationis, patienter afflictiones tolerare decet.
units.tr: He explains this argument. First, he shows that created things are subject to vanity, that is, to a corruptible condition and to the abuse of the most vain men, who misuse creatures for every kind of sin and force them to serve their most vain lusts. Second, he shows that the creature is not subjected to this servitude of its own will, or by its natural inclination, or according to the natural use for which God made it, but by the will or judgment of God, who subjected the creature to this curse together with sinful man, for whose sake the machinery of the world was created. Hence, Argument 4. The creatures are subject to vanity and misery, not by their own fault but by ours, and they bear it patiently. Therefore much more should we, who are subject to miseries through our own fault, bear afflictions patiently under the hope of deliverance.

units.la: Verf. 21. Sub spe quòd & ipse liberabitur ex servitute corruptionis in libertatem gloriæ filiorum Dei.
units.tr: Verse 21. Because the creature itself also shall be delivered from the bondage of corruption into the glorious liberty of the children of God.

units.la: Arg. 5. Spes est de creaturis, fore ut vindicentur ex servitute corruptionis, in statum, convenientem futuræ gloriosæ conditioni filiorum Dei. Ergo, multo magis, ipsis Dei filiis speranda est liberatio.
units.tr: Argument 5. There is hope concerning the creatures, that they will be set free from the bondage of corruption into a state fitting the future glorious condition of the sons of God. Therefore much more is deliverance to be hoped for by the sons of God themselves.

units.la: Verf. 22. Scimus enim totum mundum creatum una suspirare, & una parturire ad hoc usque tempus.
units.tr: Verse 22. For we know that the whole creation groaneth and travaileth in pain together until now.

units.la: Arg. 6. Scimus, mundi machinam totam, ab eo tempore quo peccatum introiit in mundum, ad hoc usque tempus, una ingemiscere, & una parturire, ut ab onere peccatorum hominum, liberata, in lucem aeternam edat maturum partum, omnium Dei Filiorum: Ergo nisi vanum, hunc naturae instinctum, diceremus; tempore a Deo constituto, speranda est plena liberatio, Filiorum Dei.
units.tr: Argument 6. We know that the whole machinery of the world, from the time when sin entered into the world until now, groans together and travails together, that, freed from the burden of men's sins, it may bring forth in eternal light the ripe fruit of all the sons of God. Therefore, unless we were to call this natural instinct vain, we must expect full deliverance of the sons of God at the time appointed by God.

units.la: Verf. 23. Neque vero ille solum, sed & ipsi qui primitias Spiritus habemus, nosipsi, inquam apud nos ipsos suspiramus, adoptionem expectantes, id est redemptionem corporis nostri.
units.tr: Verse 23. And not only they, but ourselves also, which have the firstfruits of the Spirit, even we ourselves groan within ourselves, waiting for the adoption, to wit, the redemption of our body.

units.la: Arg. 7. Non tantum res creatae, sed etiam nosipsi, qui primitias Spiritus, pacem & gaudium pignora & initia vitae aeternae accepimus, suspiramus, expectantes plenam, adoptionis nostrae manifestationem, in resurrectione corporum, vi redemptionis a Christo factae, a malis omnibus liberandorum. Ergo nisi, & primitias meliis aeternae vitae, & Spiritus desideria, pro nihilo ducamus, ex liberationis certitudine consolationem capere debemus.
units.tr: Argument 7. Not only the created things but we ourselves, who have received the firstfruits of the Spirit, peace and joy, the pledges and beginnings of eternal life, groan, waiting for the full manifestation of our adoption in the resurrection of the bodies, which are to be freed from all evils by the power of the redemption made by Christ. Therefore, unless we count the firstfruits of the better eternal life and the desires of the Spirit as nothing, we ought to draw consolation from the certainty of deliverance.

units.la: Verf. 24. Nam quae servati sumus, spes autem si videatur, non est spes, quod enim quis videt, cur speret?
units.tr: Verse 24. For we are saved by hope: but hope that is seen is not hope: for what a man seeth, why doth he yet hope for?

units.la: Verf. 25. Si vero quod non videmus speramus, nempe per toleran-tiam expectamus.
units.tr: Verse 25. But if we hope for that we see not, then do we with patience wait for it.

units.la: Arg. 8. A natura spei, quae dicitur servare, quia promissionum Dei complementum, expectat ad salutem. Datur nobis spes salvifica, quae non est visibilium, & praesentium, sed futurorum bonorum certa & patiens expectatio: Ergo nisi spei salvificae renunciemus in afflictionibus, consolatio non deerit nobis expectantibus liberationem promissam ex omnibus molestiis.
units.tr: Argument 8. From the nature of hope, which is said to save, because it waits for the fulfilment of God's promises for salvation. We are given a saving hope, which is not of things visible and present but a certain and patient expectation of future good things. Therefore, unless we renounce saving hope in afflictions, consolation will not fail us as we wait for the deliverance promised from all troubles.

units.la: Verf. 26. Itidem autem & Spiritus una sublevat infirmitates nostras, quid enim oremus ut oportet, non novimus: sed ipse Spiritus intercedit pro nobis suspiriis ineffabilibus.
units.tr: Verse 26. Likewise the Spirit also helpeth our infirmities: for we know not what we should pray for as we ought: but the Spirit itself maketh intercession for us with groanings which cannot be uttered.

units.la: Arg. 9. In afflictionibus soli non sumus, sed auxiliarem habemus Spiritum sanctum consolatorem, qui nos laborantes & infirmos sustinet, & ad precandum ignaros instruit, ita ut ipse excitans in nobis suspiritus inenarrabilis, quasi advocatum agat, pro nobis, apud Patrem. Ergo in afflictionibus consolationem capere debemus.
units.tr: Argument 9. In afflictions we are not alone, but we have the Holy Spirit as a helper and comforter, who sustains us when we labour and are weak, and teaches us when we are ignorant how to pray, so that by stirring up in us unutterable groanings he acts as an advocate for us before the Father. Therefore we ought to draw consolation in afflictions.

units.la: Versf. 27. Qui vero scrutatur corda, novit quid sapiat Spiritus: quia secundum Deum intercedit pro Sanctis.
units.tr: Verse 27. And he that searcheth the hearts knoweth what is the mind of the Spirit, because he maketh intercession for the saints according to the will of God.

units.la: Arg. 10. Cum occupatione objectionis; Diceret aliquis, Nos ipsi confusorum, & indiligentiorum suspiriorum, sensum, non discernimus. Responsio suppeditat argumentum consolationis: Deus qui scrutatur corda, Spiritus sui suspiria in nobis excitantis, sensum probè novit, & ut voluntati suae congruentem, acceptat. Quia, ut secundum Dei voluntatem precentur Sancti efficit, & ipse etiam, suo modo, interpellat: Ergo certi de exauditione precum, in afflictionibus nostris consolationem capere debemus.
units.tr: Argument 10. With an answer to an objection. Someone might say: we ourselves do not discern the meaning of our confused and careless groanings. The answer supplies an argument of consolation: God, who searches the hearts, knows well the meaning of the groanings that his Spirit stirs up in us, and accepts them as agreeing with his will. For he makes the saints pray according to God's will, and he himself also intercedes in his own way. Therefore, being certain that our prayers will be heard, we ought to draw consolation in our afflictions.

units.la: Verf. 28. Novimus autem, iis qui diligunt Deum, omnia simul adjumento esse ad bonum, iis videlicet qui ex proposito ipsius vocati sunt.
units.tr: Verse 28. And we know that all things work together for good to them that love God, to them who are the called according to his purpose.

units.la: Arg. 11. Ut res omnes, sic etiam afflictiones, cooperantur in bonum Justificatorum, seu Fidelium: Ergo consolationem capere possunt in rebus adversissimis. Pro Justificatis, seu Fidelibus, ponit ipsorum descriptionem; Primò, quod diligant Deum, utpote qui misericordiam, & benevolentiam Dei in Christo, per fidem amplexi sunt, & non possunt Deum non diligere ex animo: Secundò, quod efficaciter vocati sint, utpote quos Spiritus Dei, per verbum suum efficaciter movit, ut coelesti vocationi, peccatores ad Christum invitanti, obtemperarent. Tertiò, quod vocati sint ex proposito, siquidem electi à Deo, ex mero beneplacito, ante tempora, sine ullo respectu ad ipsorum merita, vel dignitatem, & eo ipso consilio in tempore vocati sint, ut perducerentur ad vitam æternam; ad quam praedestinati sunt.
units.tr: Argument 11. As all things, so also afflictions work together for the good of the justified, or faithful. Therefore they can take consolation even in the most adverse circumstances. For the justified, or faithful, he gives a description of them. First, that they love God, as those who have embraced by faith the mercy and goodwill of God in Christ, and cannot but love God from the heart. Second, that they are effectually called, as those whom the Spirit of God, through his Word, has effectually moved to obey the heavenly call that invites sinners to Christ. Third, that they are called according to purpose, since they were chosen by God from his mere good pleasure, before time, without any regard to their merits or worth, and for this very purpose are called in time, that they may be brought to eternal life, for which they were predestined.

units.la: Verf. 29. Nam quos praescivit, etiam praedestinavit conformandos imagini Filii sui: ut is sit primogenitus inter multos fratres.
units.tr: Verse 29. For whom he did foreknow, he also did predestinate to be conformed to the image of his Son, that he might be the firstborn among many brethren.

units.la: Arg. 12. Confirmans superius, Indissolubili catena conjunxit Deus, in decreto electionis & praedestinationis, conformitatem Justificatorum, seu efficaciter vocatorum, cum Christo, in omnimoda similitudine; nempe crucis, sanctitatis, & felicitatis, eo ipso fine, ut Christi gloria magis apparēat, dum Ille sicut decet primogenitum Antesignanus, inter electos fratres comperitur, sicut in afflictionibus sancte & fortiter ferendis, sic in gloriæ corona, post afflictiones reportanda: Ergo debent Justificati, in afflictionibus suis consolationem capere, cum videant eas, & in bonum suum, & in Christi gloriam tendere.
units.tr: Argument 12. Confirming what was said above: God, by an indissoluble chain in the decree of election and predestination, joined the conformity of the justified, or effectually called, with Christ in every likeness, namely of cross, holiness and blessedness, to this very end, that the glory of Christ might appear the more, while he, as the firstborn should be, is found to be the leader of the chosen brethren, as in bearing afflictions holily and bravely, so in the crown of glory to be won after afflictions. Therefore the justified ought to draw consolation in their afflictions, since they see that these tend both to their own good and to the glory of Christ.

units.la: Verf. 30. Quos vero prædestinavit, eos etiam vocavit: & quos vocavit, eos etiam justificavit: quos autem justificavit, eos etiam glorificavit:
units.tr: Verf. 30. Moreover, whom he predestinated, them he also called; and whom he called, them he also justified; and whom he justified, them he also glorified.

units.la: Arg. 13. Vocatio efficax, & justificatio, quæ in hac vita fidelibus datur, ut beneficia à Deo; tanquam annuli catenæ indissolubilis, adeo firmiter connectuntur cum electione & prædestinatione ante tempora, & cum glorificatione post tempora sæcularia, ut qui efficaciter vocatus est, & justificatus, certus esse possit, de prædestinatione sui, ad vitam ab æterno, & certus etiam de glorificatione sui futura apud Deum, in æternum; Nam quos prædestinavit, eos vocavit, &c. Ergo justificati, solidam habent consolationem quantumvis afflicti in hac vita.
units.tr: Arg. 13. The effectual calling and the justification that is given to believers in this life, as benefits from God, are so firmly linked, like the links of an unbreakable chain, with election and predestination before time and with glorification after the ages of this world, that whoever is effectually called and justified can be certain of his predestination to eternal life and certain also of his future glorification with God for ever. For "whom he predestinated, them he called," etc. Therefore the justified, however afflicted they may be in this life, have a solid consolation.

units.la: Tertia Pars.
units.tr: Third Part.

units.la: Verf. 31. Quid igitur dicemus ad hæc; si Deus pro nobis, quis contra nos?
units.tr: Verse 31. What then shall we say to these things? If God is for us, who is against us?

units.la: Tertia pars capitis, continens justificatorum per fidem in Christum, sextuplicem triumphum, de salutis suæ hostibus.
units.tr: The third part of the chapter, containing the sixfold triumph of those justified through faith in Christ over the enemies of their salvation.

units.la: Huic autem gloriationi in Deo præmittit interrogationem, ad indubitatam veritatem doctrinæ totius præcedentis ostendendam, cui contradicere nemo jure poterit; Quid igitur dicemus ad hæc? Sequitur pro responsione triumphus omnium justificatorum per fidem in Christum, quibus se accenset Apostolus, & quorum nomine, nonnunquam, ut primipilus aliquis, in singulari numero loquitur. Primus triumphus est, de omnibus hostibus in cumulo, propter justificatorum cum Deo conjunctionem: Si Deus pro nobis sit, quis contra nos? id est, quum Deus sit pro nobis, impleturus in nobis, æternum suum propositum sanctificationis, & glorificationis nostræ, quis vel hominum, vel dæmonum, contra nos insurgat, ut salutem nostram impediat?
units.tr: Before this boasting in God, he sets a question, to show the indubitable truth of the whole preceding doctrine, which no one can rightly contradict: What then shall we say to these things? The answer that follows is the triumph of all those justified through faith in Christ, among whom the Apostle counts himself, and in whose name he sometimes speaks in the singular number, like a leader of the front rank. The first triumph is over all enemies together, on account of the union of the justified with God: If God is for us, who is against us? That is: since God is for us, about to accomplish in us his eternal purpose of our sanctification and glorification, who, whether men or demons, could rise up against us to hinder our salvation?

units.la: Verf. 32. Is quidem qui proprio Filio non pepercit, sed pro nobis omnia bù omnibus tradidit eum, quomodo non etiam cum eo illa nobis omnia gratificabitur?
units.tr: Verse 32. He who did not spare his own Son, but delivered him up for us all, how shall he not also with him freely give us all things?

units.la: Secundus Triumphus, est de defectibus boni cujusvis ad salutem necaffarii, nitens Dei dilectione tanta erga nos, ut dederit pro nobis, Filium suum in mortem; In hunc sensum, Deus qui Filio suo, (quo nihil habet charius) non pepercit, sed pro salute noltra, impendit eum & tradidit pro nobis Electis omnibus, in mortem, non potest non dare nobis Filium suum, & cum illo caetera omnia dona, ad salutem necessaria, & denique falutem ipsam & gloriam. Quid igitur ad salutem necessarium deesse nobis potest?
units.tr: The second triumph concerns the lack of any good necessary to salvation, and rests on God's love towards us, so great that he gave his Son for us to death. To this effect: God, who did not spare his own Son (than whom he has nothing dearer), but gave him up and delivered him for our salvation, for us all who are elect, to death, cannot fail to give us his Son, and with him all other gifts necessary to salvation, and finally salvation itself and glory. What then can be lacking to us that is necessary to salvation?

units.la: Verf. 33. Quis intentabit crimina adversus electos Dei? Deus is est qui justificat.
units.tr: Verse 33. Who shall bring any charge against God's elect? It is God who justifies.

units.la: Tertius triumphus est de omni accusatore, Diabolo, Mundo, & propria conscientia, nitens Dei justificantis sententia absolutoria: Quis accusationem instituet, objectis criminibus adversus eos, quos Deus elegit, id est, nullus id fecerit, nisi frustra: Deus est qui justificat, id est a peccatis, & ab intentata cujusvis adversarij actione, electos suos absolvit. Triumphamus igitur de omnibus in Christo.
units.tr: The third triumph is over every accuser, the Devil, the World, and our own conscience, and rests on God's sentence of justification, which acquits. Who will bring an accusation, laying crimes against those whom God has chosen? That is, no one can do so, except in vain: it is God who justifies, that is, he absolves his elect from sins and from any action brought against them by any adversary. Therefore we triumph over all in Christ.

units.la: Verf. 34. Quis est qui condemnet? Christus is est qui mortuus est: imo vero qui etiam suscitatus est: qui etiam est ad dextram Dei, qui etiam intercedit pro nobis.
units.tr: Verse 34. Who is it that condemns? It is Christ who died; yes, rather, who was also raised; who is also at the right hand of God, who also makes intercession for us.

units.la: Quartus triumphus est, de omni judice, seu judicis partes sibi affumente & sententiam condemnationis, adversus justificatos ferente: Quum Deus justificaverit nos, quis est alius, qui audet nos condemnare? Quum Christus, pro nobis mortuus fit, imo vero, & de morte, victor resurrexerit, & ascenderit in coelum, & ibi in gloria jam nunc interpellet pro nobis, non est metuenda nobis ulla condemnatio, nisi frustra esse Christi mortem, resurrectionem, ascensionem, sessionem in gloria, & intercessionem, diceremus, quod est blasphemum. Triumphamus igitur in Christo.
units.tr: The fourth triumph is over every judge, or anyone who assumes the role of judge and pronounces a sentence of condemnation against the justified. Since God has justified us, who else dares to condemn us? Since Christ died for us, yes, rather, having conquered death, rose again, ascended into heaven, and there now in glory intercedes for us, no condemnation is to be feared by us, unless we were to say that the death, resurrection, ascension, sitting in glory and intercession of Christ are in vain, which is blasphemy. Therefore we triumph in Christ.

units.la: Verf. 35 Quis nos separabit a charitate Christi? num afflictio, num angustia, num persequutio, num fames, num nuditas, num periculum, num gladius?
units.tr: Verse 35. Who shall separate us from the love of Christ? Shall affliction, or distress, or persecution, or famine, or nakedness, or peril, or the sword?

units.la: Quintus triumphus, de afflictionibus externis, quarum sex species enumerat, quibus comprehendit omnes res adversas, quibus Christiani, ullo modo, ab ingrato mundo, urgeri solent propter justitiam; de omnibus negans, quod ullus hostis, per haec mala impedire poterit, quominus effectum plenissimum,& sensum suavissimum divinae erga nos charitatis, tandem percipiamus.
units.tr: The fifth triumph is over external afflictions, six kinds of which he enumerates, by which he comprehends all adversities with which Christians are wont in any way to be pressed by the ungrateful world on account of righteousness. He denies that any enemy can by these evils hinder us from finally perceiving the fullest effect and the sweetest sense of God's love towards us.

units.la: Verf. 36. (Sicut scriptum est, Tui causa occidimur totum diem: reputati sumus velut oves destinata mactationi.)
units.tr: Verse 36. (As it is written: For your sake we are killed all the day long; we are accounted as sheep appointed for slaughter.)

units.la: Ne de hoste ficto, triumphare videretur, probat ex Psalmo 44. versu 22, omnes veros DEI servos, eosque qui tunc temporis in vivis agebant, omnibus istis miseriis esse obnoxios, ita ut possent Psalmi verba sibi accommodare, dicentes, nos quotidie tua causa, O Deus, occidimur, & perinde tractamur ac si oves essemus, mactationi destinatae.
units.tr: Lest it seem he triumphs over an imaginary enemy, he proves from Psalm 44, verse 22, that all the true servants of God, and those who were then living, were exposed to all these miseries, so that they could apply the words of the Psalm to themselves, saying: for your sake, O God, we are killed every day, and are treated as if we were sheep destined for slaughter.

units.la: Verf. 37. Imo in his omnibus amplius quam victores sumus, per eum qui dilexit nos.
units.tr: Verse 37. Nay, in all these things we are more than conquerors, through him who loved us.

units.la: Prosequitur triumphum, excellentiam victoriae praedicans, quam de his malis, reportabant suo tempore Christiani, per virtutem CHRISTI: a pugna enim semper redibant plus quam victores, nempe nec vulnerati, nec defatigati, nec jacturam ullius boni passi, sed saniores, robustiores, sanctiores, gratia omni auctiores, etiam tum cum mundo victi videri possent maxime, cujus triumphi gloriam, in solidum totam CHRISTI dilectioni, ascribit.
units.tr: He continues the triumph, proclaiming the excellence of the victory which Christians in his time won over these evils through the power of Christ. For from the battle they always returned more than conquerors: indeed neither wounded nor exhausted, nor having suffered the loss of any good, but healthier, stronger, holier, and richer in grace, even when they might seem most of all to be vanquished by the world. The glory of this triumph he ascribes wholly to the love of Christ.

units.la: Verf. 38. Nam mihi persuasum est, neque mortem, neque vitam, neque Angelos, neque principatus, neque potestates, neque praesentia, neque futura. Verf. 39. Neque sublimitatem, neque profunditatem, neque ullam rem aliam creatam posse nos separare a charitate Dei, quae est in Christo Iesu Domino nostro.
units.tr: Verse 38. For I am persuaded that neither death, nor life, nor angels, nor principalities, nor powers, nor things present, nor things to come, Verse 39. nor height, nor depth, nor any other created thing, shall be able to separate us from the love of God, which is in Christ Jesus our Lord.

units.la: Sextus, & ultimus triumphus, de ipsa incredulitate,& de dubitationibus omnibus, quae ex quavis creatura, vel quavis causa praesenti, vel futura, oriri possent. Per vitam & mortem intelligit, omnia extrema, secunda & adversa, quibus allici, vel terreri possemus. Per Angelos intelligit bonos & malos Spiritus, si possibile esset, ut concurrerent, ad nos a CHRIsto separandos; Per Principatus & Potestates intelligit potentiam Regum, Imperatorum, Gubernatorum, Tyrannorum, in universo Mundo. Per instantia & futura intelligit, omnes eventus intermedios, qui jam evenerunt, vel ante mortem accidere possunt. Per profunditatem & sublimitatem intelligit creaturas, supra vel infra nos constitutas. Per ullam aliam creaturam, intelligit universaliter, rem quamvis creatam, in toto universo, seu quicquid praeter Deum est, quod posset videri terribile. De his omnibus, plena fidei persuasione triumphat, propter potentem, & efficacem, certam, & immutabilem Dei dilectionem, qua nos ad salutem vult provehere, a cujus dilectionis amplexu, affectu, sensu salutari, & fruitione, nihil unquam, justificatos per fidem in Christum divellet: Cujus rationem reddit, quia gratuitae dilectionis Dei ad nos derivandae efficacia, fundata est in Christi merito infinito, & omnipotente ipsius virtute, qua custodimur per fidem, ad salutem.
units.tr: The sixth and last triumph is over unbelief itself and over all doubts which could arise from any creature or from any present or future cause. By life and death he understands every extreme, prosperous and adverse condition, by which we might be enticed or terrified. By angels he understands good and evil spirits, if it were possible for them to combine to separate us from Christ. By principalities and powers he understands the power of kings, emperors, governors and tyrants throughout the whole world. By things present and things to come he understands all intervening events, which have already happened or may occur before death. By height and depth he understands creatures placed above or below us. By any other created thing he understands universally any created thing whatever in the whole universe, or whatever is besides God, which could seem terrible. Over all these he triumphs, with full assurance of faith, on account of the powerful, effective, certain and unchangeable love of God, by which he wills to bring us to salvation; from the embrace, affection, saving sense and enjoyment of which love nothing will ever tear those justified through faith in Christ. The reason for this he gives: because the efficacy of God's free love flowing down to us is founded on the infinite merit of Christ and on his almighty power, by which we are kept through faith unto salvation.

units.la: Caput nonum.
units.tr: Chapter 9.

units.la: Estat sexta, & ultima confirmatio, gratuitae justificationis per fidem in Christum, & non ex operibus, ab experientia, Partim rejectitiorum Israelitarum, qui justitiam ex operibus quaerentes, justitiam non sunt assequuti, seu non sunt omnino justificati: partim Gentilium fidelium, qui operibus destituti, justificati sunt per fidem in Christum, absque operibus legis: unde sequitur justificationem per fidem in Christum, absque operibus legis, solam esse veram, & solidam.
units.tr: This is the sixth and last confirmation of the free justification by faith in Christ, and not by works, drawn from experience: partly from the rejection of the Israelites, who, seeking justification by works, did not attain justification, that is, were not fully justified; partly from the experience of the faithful Gentiles, who, though lacking works, were justified by faith in Christ without the works of the law. Whence it follows that justification by faith in Christ, without the works of the law, alone is true and solid.

units.la: Hoc argumentum, quia videbat, variis cavillationibus obnoxium, hinc atque hinc studiose munit, & explicat tribus proximè sequentibus Capitibus.
units.tr: Since he saw that this argument was open to various cavils, he carefully fortifies it on both sides and explains it in the three following chapters.

units.la: Capitis tres sunt partes: In prima, praeoccupantur quatuor objectiones, adversus sententiam Apostoli, de rejectione Judaeorum: In quarum solutione, accurate tractat, doctrinam praedestinationis, ad versum 24. In secunda, probat ex Scripturis, Judaeorum rejectionem & vocationem Electorum, ex Judaeis, & Gentibus, ad versum 30. In tertia, ad confirmandam doctrinam, de justificatione per fidem absque operibus, in medium affert experientiam Judaeorum, qui quaerentes justificationem ex operibus, non sunt justificati: Et experientiam credentium, inter um, inter Gentes, qui destituti operum pretextu, per fidem in Christum, justificati sunt.
units.tr: The chapter has three parts. In the first, four objections against the Apostle's teaching on the rejection of the Jews are anticipated; in answering them he treats carefully the doctrine of predestination, to verse 24. In the second, he proves from the Scriptures the rejection of the Jews and the calling of the elect from Jews and Gentiles, to verse 30. In the third, to confirm the doctrine of justification by faith without works, he brings forward the experience of the Jews, who seeking justification by works were not justified, and the experience of believers, among the Gentiles, who, lacking works, were justified by faith in Christ.

units.la: Verf. 1. Veritatem dico per Christum, non mentior, (attestante mihi simul conscientia mea per Spiritum sanctum.)
units.tr: Verse 1. I speak the truth in Christ, I do not lie, my conscience also bearing me witness in the Holy Spirit.

units.la: Prima pars Capitis, in qua tollit objectiones, quae de repudio Judaeorum, moveri possent: Prima objectio, Diceret aliquis, quaecunque prolaturus es, Paule, de rejectione Judaeorum, odio gentis tuae, quam infensam habes, dicere videberis. Hanc objectionem praeoccupat, & suspicionem a se amolitur, septem rationibus.
units.tr: The first part of the chapter, in which he removes the objections that could be raised concerning the rejection of the Jews. First objection: someone might say, "Whatever you are about to say, Paul, about the rejection of the Jews, you seem to say out of hatred for your nation, which you regard with hostility." He anticipates this objection and removes the suspicion by seven reasons.

units.la: Prima ratio, juramento me purgo, quod absque odio, vel praejudicio, sincere veritatem dicam, sicut decet virum, qui in Christo est, & per Spiritum sanctum agitur & afflatur in loquendo; quos duos, testes veritatis a me proferendae, una cum conscientia mea, advoco.
units.tr: First reason: I clear myself by an oath, that without hatred or prejudice I will speak the truth sincerely, as becomes a man who is in Christ and is moved and inspired by the Holy Spirit in speaking. These two witnesses of the truth I call upon, together with my conscience.

units.la: Verf. 2. Magnam mihi tristitiam esse, & cruciatum sine intermissione cordi meo.
units.tr: Verse 2. That I have great sorrow and unceasing anguish in my heart.

units.la: Ratio 2. Quia testis est mihi juranti conscientia, & Christi Spiritus, qui scrutatur corda, quam tristis sim, & quanto dolore crucier, de repudio gentis meae.
units.tr: Reason 2. Because my conscience is witness to me as I swear, and the Spirit of Christ, who searches the hearts, how sad I am and how greatly I am tormented with grief at the rejection of my nation.

units.la: Verf. 3. Optarim enim ego ipse anathema esse separatum a Christo, pro fratribus meis, cognatis inquam meis secundum carnem.
units.tr: Verse 3. For I could wish that I myself were accursed, cut off from Christ, for my brethren, my kinsmen according to the flesh.

units.la: Ratio 3. Quia tantus est meus erga Judaeos amor, ut si fieri posset, ipsorum exitium, propriae meae salutis jactura redimerem, & velut piaculum quoddam execrabile, separari a Christo, prae studio salutis ipsorum & gloriae Dei, optarem equidem, si eo modo servari possent Judaei, qui jam separantur a Christo. Tanto zelo, ad gloriam Dei, & salutem tot millium animarum ferebatur, ut non comparandam censuerit salutem sui unius, cum salute tot myriadum.
units.tr: Reason 3. Because my love for the Jews is so great that, if it could be done, I would redeem their destruction at the cost of my own salvation, and, as a kind of detestable expiation, I would indeed wish to be separated from Christ, out of zeal for their salvation and the glory of God, if in that way the Jews, who are now separated from Christ, could be saved. He was carried by such zeal for the glory of God and the salvation of so many thousands of souls that he judged his own salvation not comparable with the salvation of so many myriads.

units.la: Cognatus ] Ratio 4. Quia teneor eos ut cognatos meos, & fratres secundum carnem diligere, quod & ex animo facio.
units.tr: Kinsmen: Reason 4. Because I am bound to love them as my kinsmen and brethren according to the flesh, which I also do from my heart.

units.la: Verf. 4. Qui sunt Israelitae, quorum est adoptio, & gloria, & pacta, & Legis constitutio, & cultus, & promissiones: Ratio 5 Quia populum Judaeorum honorare teneor, propter privilegia quibus Deus eos honoravit: qualia enumerat septem, quorum Primum est, quod Israelitae sint participes honoris, quem secum tulit, nominis Israel, divinitus impositi patriarchae Jacob, appellatio. Secundum est, adoptio in populum Dei, prae aliis gentibus. Tertium est, praesentia gloriae Dei in arca, & aliis symbolis. Quartum est, quod Deus, pacta seu foedera, cum ipsis inierit. Quintum est, Quod lex illis specialiter fit data. Sextum est, Quod cultus Dei, inter ipsos sit erectus; Septimum est, Quod ipsis, factae sunt specialiter promissiones.
units.tr: Verse 4. Who are Israelites, to whom belong the adoption, and the glory, and the covenants, and the giving of the law, and the worship, and the promises. Reason 5: because I am bound to honour the Jewish people on account of the privileges with which God has honoured them. He lists seven of these. The first is that the Israelites share the honour which the name Israel carries, the appellation divinely given to the patriarch Jacob. The second is adoption into the people of God above other nations. The third is the presence of the glory of God in the ark and other symbols. The fourth is that God made covenants with them. The fifth is that the law was given to them specially. The sixth is that the worship of God was established among them. The seventh is that the promises were made to them specially.

units.la: Verf. 5. Quorum sunt Patres illi, & ex quibus est Christus quod ad carnem attinet, qui est supra omnes Deus benedictus in secula. Amen.
units.tr: Verse 5. Of whom are the fathers, and from whom is Christ according to the flesh, who is over all, God blessed for ever. Amen.

units.la: Ratio 6. Quia propter ipsorum progenitores, Abraham, Isaac, & Jacob, aequum censeo ut eos magnifacerem.
units.tr: Reason 6. Because on account of their forefathers, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, I think it right to hold them in high regard.

units.la: Ratio 7. Quia ex hoc populo, oriundus est Christus, secundum carnem suam, qui in unitate personae, verus homo, & verus Deus est, super omnia benedictus, & in aeternum celebrandus; cui omnes accinamus Amen. Quem Dominum, & Deum nostrum qui honorat, populum unde ille secundum carnem oriundus est, non potest malitiose dehonestare: Ergo non est quod quisquam, me suspectum habeat, in iis quae de populi mei rejectione dico, vel dicturus sum.
units.tr: Reason 7. Because from this people Christ is descended according to his flesh, who in unity of person is true man and true God, blessed above all and to be celebrated for ever, to whom we all say Amen. Whoever honours this Lord and God cannot maliciously dishonour the people from whom he came according to the flesh. Therefore there is no reason why anyone should suspect me, in what I say, or shall say, about the rejection of my people.

units.la: Verf. 6. Fieri vero non potest, ut exciderit sermo Dei. Non enim omnes qui sunt ex patre Israele, sunt Israel:
units.tr: Verse 6. But it is not possible that the word of God has failed. For they are not all Israel, which are of Israel.

units.la: Objectio secunda; diceret aliquis, At si Judaei sint anathema a Christo, ut tu doces, excidit Dei sermo, & irrita est promissio gratiae facta Israelitis, cum dixit Deus Abrahamo, Ero Deus tuus, & seminis tui.
units.tr: Second objection: someone might say, "But if the Jews are accursed from Christ, as you teach, the word of God has failed, and the promise of grace made to the Israelites is void, since God said to Abraham, 'I will be your God and the God of your seed.'"

units.la: Respondet, Etiamsi Judaeorum Gens, maxima ex parte repudiata sit, fieri tamen non posse, ut Dei sermo exciderit, vel promissio irrita facta fuerit. Rationes responsionis sunt sex.
units.tr: He answers that even if the nation of the Jews has been for the most part rejected, nevertheless the word of God cannot have failed or the promise been made void. There are six reasons for the answer.

units.la: Prima ratio. Non omnes, qui ex Israele Patriacha secundum carnem orti sunt, illi veri & electi sunt Israelitae, seu electus populus Israel, cui promissio communionis cum Deo facta est: Ergo etiamsi multi, ex Israele Patre oriundi, repudiati sint, non sequitur sermonem Dei, vel promissionem Dei excidisse, nempe, quia completur in Electis.
units.tr: First reason. Not all who are born of Israel the patriarch according to the flesh are the true and elect Israelites, that is, the chosen people of Israel, to whom the promise of communion with God was made. Therefore, even if many born of Israel the father are rejected, it does not follow that the word or promise of God has failed, namely because it is fulfilled in the elect.

units.la: Verf. 7. Neque quia sunt femen Abrahami ideo, omnes func filii, sed in Isaaco vocabitur tibi semen.
units.tr: Verse 7. Neither, because they are the seed of Abraham, are they all children; but in Isaac shall thy seed be called.

units.la: Ratio 2. Neque sequitur, quia Judæi sunt semen Abrahæ, secundum carnem, ideo omnes eos esse filios, in sensu Scripturæ, seu semen illud promissum. Nam sic, etiam Ismaelitæ, censerentur in semine Abrahæ, contra Scripturam, quæ jus filiorum restrinxit ad Isaacum, & ejus familiam, dicendo, In Isaac vocabitur tibi semen. Ergo etiamsi Judæi, maxima ex parte rejiciantur, non sequitur promissionem Dei excidisse.
units.tr: Reason 2. Nor does it follow that, because the Jews are the seed of Abraham according to the flesh, they are for that reason all children in the sense of Scripture, or that promised seed. For so the Ishmaelites too would be counted in the seed of Abraham, contrary to Scripture, which restricted the right of children to Isaac and his family, saying, "In Isaac shall thy seed be called." Therefore, even if the Jews are for the most part rejected, it does not follow that the promise of God has failed.

units.la: Verf. 8. Hoc est non qui filii carnis, ij filii Dei: sed qui sunt filii promissionis, reputantur in semine.
units.tr: Verse 8. That is, those who are the children of the flesh are not the children of God, but the children of the promise are counted for the seed.

units.la: Ratio 3. Distinguendi sunt filii carnis, à Filiis Dei electis: Nam hoc voluit Deus, cum seclusò Ismaele, Isaacum vocavit semen Abrahæ, nempe filios carnis Abrahæ, non esse omnes electos Filios Dei, sed solos Filios promissionis, (seu quos Deus ex gratia statuebat filios fidei Abrahami efficere cum Isaaco) esse Filios Dei, & semen illud cui promissio facta est: Ergo etiamsi repudientur Judæi, qui jam vivunt, maxima ex parte, non sequitur promissionem Dei excidisse.
units.tr: Reason 3. The children of the flesh must be distinguished from the elect children of God. For God willed this, when, Ishmael being set aside, he called Isaac the seed of Abraham: that not all the fleshly children of Abraham are the elect children of God, but only the children of the promise (that is, those whom God, out of grace, determined to make children of Abraham's faith along with Isaac) are the children of God and that seed to whom the promise was made. Therefore, even if the Jews now living are for the most part rejected, it does not follow that the promise of God has failed.

units.la: Verf. 9. Promissionis enim sermo hic est, Hoc ipso præstituto tempore veniam, & erit Sara filius.
units.tr: Verse 9. For this is the word of promise: At this time I will come, and Sarah shall have a son.

units.la: Ratio 4. confirmans priorem, Promissionis sermo, (qui hic est, Hoc eodem tempore, post annum revolutum, quando reversus, veniam ad te, Sara conjunx tua, quamvis sterilis & vetula, filium habebit) promissionis sermo inquam, indicans Isaacum, non vi carnis, sed virtute divinæ promissionis prognatum, probat non semini carnali, sed semini electo, gratuito excitato, benedictionem dari. Ergo, etiamsi repudientur Judæi, maxima ex parte, non sequitur promissionem Dei excidisse, quia supersunt electi, qui hæredes sunt promissionis.
units.tr: Reason 4, confirming the former: the word of promise (which here is, "At this same time, after a year has come round, when I return, I will come to you, and Sarah your wife, though barren and old, shall have a son"), the word of promise, I say, indicating that Isaac was born not by the power of the flesh but by the power of the divine promise, proves that the blessing is given not to the carnal seed but to the chosen seed, raised up by grace. Therefore, even if the Jews are for the most part rejected, it does not follow that the promise of God has failed, because the elect remain, who are the heirs of the promise.

units.la: Verf. 10. Neque hic solum, sed & Rebecca, quum ex uno concepisset, nempe ex Isaaco patre nostro, hæc experta est.
units.tr: Verse 10. Nor is this the only case: Rebecca too, when she had conceived by one man, namely our father Isaac, experienced this.

units.la: Ratio 5. in hunc sensum; Non solum superiora exempla, ostendunt non omnes filios esse verum semen, cui promissio facta est, sed etiam & multò luculentius, exemplum Rebeccæ, quæ gemellos concepit, ex eodem Patre nostro Isaaco, nempe Esavum & Iacobum, quorum alter tantùm verè Filius fuit, cui promissa benedictio data est. Ergo sequitur aliquod semen Abrahæ repudiari posse, & promissionem Dei non excidere, sed firmam manere, & compleri in semine electo.
units.tr: Reason 5 in this sense: not only do the earlier examples show that not all children are the true seed to whom the promise was made, but also, and much more clearly, the example of Rebecca, who conceived twins from the same Father, our Isaac, namely Esau and Jacob, of whom only one was truly the son and the one to whom the promised blessing was given. Therefore it follows that some seed of Abraham can be rejected, and God's promise does not fail but remains firm and is fulfilled in the elect seed.

units.la: Vers. 11. Nondum enim natis pueris, quum nihil fecissent boni vel mali, ut præstitum illud Dei quod est secundum ipsius electionem, id est, non ex operibus, sed ex vocante, firmum maneret. Vers. 12. Dictum est ei, Major serviet minori.
units.tr: Vers. 11. For before the boys were born, when they had done nothing good or evil, so that God's purpose according to election, that is, not by works but by him who calls, might stand firm. Vers. 12. It was said to her, The elder shall serve the younger.

units.la: Hoc discrimen feminis, seu electionis filiorum aliquorum, & rejectionis aliorum, explicat à suis causis, nempe quod pendeat non ex operibus, seu ulla re bona, vel mala, in creatura, sed à mera voluntate Dei vocantis: Cum enim nondum nati essent pueri, vel quicquam fecissent boni vel mali, ut ostenderet Deus propositum suum, quod est secundum electionem, seu electionis rationem gratuitam, firmum & stabile manere, non ex operibus, seu ex hominum meritis, sed ex vocante Deo, seu ex vocantis Dei solo arbitrio; Responsum est Rebeccæ, de gemellis, omni ratione jam æqualibus fore, ut benedictio, sub primogenituræ, seu Dominii typo, cederet minori natu, maledictio verò, sub servitutis typo, majori natu. Hinc,
units.tr: This distinction between the children, the election of some and the rejection of others, is explained from its causes: namely, that it depends not on works, or on any good or evil thing in the creature, but on the mere will of God who calls. For when the boys were not yet born, and had done nothing good or evil, in order that God might show that his purpose, which is according to election, that is, the free ground of election, remains firm and stable, not by works, or by the merits of men, but by God who calls, that is, by the sole decision of the God who calls; it was answered to Rebecca concerning the twins that, by every reckoning, they would already be equal, so that the blessing, under the type of the firstborn or lordship, would pass to the younger by birth, and the curse, under the type of servitude, to the elder by birth. Hence,

units.la: Ratio 6. Propositum quo Deus secundum electionis decretum, de unoquoque homine statuit, firmum manet, dependens non ab ullis hominum operibus sed à mera Dei vocantis quos vult voluntate liberrima, sicut ex responso Rebeccæ dato, constat, de gemellis nondum natis: Ergo repudiatis his, vel illis Judæis, firma manere poterit Dei promissio in aliis.
units.tr: Argument 6. The purpose by which God, according to the decree of election, determines concerning each man stands firm. It depends not on any works of men but on the most free will of God, who calls whom he wills, as is clear from the answer given to Rebecca about the twins not yet born. Therefore, with these or those Jews rejected, God's promise can remain firm in others.

units.la: Vers. 13. Sicut scriptum est, Iacobum dilexi, Esavum autem odio habui.
units.tr: Verse 13. As it is written: Jacob I have loved, but Esau I have hated.

units.la: Ratio 7. confirmans & explicans priorem; Deus ex iis qui omni ratione pares sunt, aliquos ab æterno amat, & in tempore se amare ostendit, aliquos verò odit & in tempore se odisse ostendit, ut ex Malachia Prophetæ, cap. 1, vers. 2. in exemplo Iacobi & Esavi constat: Ergo, repudiatis his vel illis Judæis, firma manere poterit Dei promissio in aliis.
units.tr: Argument 7, confirming and explaining the former: God, among those who are equal in every respect, loves some from eternity and shows in time that he loves them, and hates others and shows in time that he hates them, as is clear from the prophet Malachi, ch. 1, verse 2, in the example of Jacob and Esau. Therefore, with these or those Jews rejected, God's promise can remain firm in others.

units.la: Vers. 14. Quid igitur dicemus? num injustitia est apud Deum? Absit.
units.tr: Verse 14. What then shall we say? Is there injustice with God? By no means.

units.la: Hinc critur obječtio tertia, Si ex omni ratione paribus, Deus aliquos diligit & eligit, alios vero odit & reprobat, Quid dicemus? nonne videtur in Deo injustitia esse, quia de æqualibus non æqualiter disponit? Respondet Apostolus cum abominatione, Absit.
units.tr: Hence arises a third objection: if God, among those who are equal in every respect, loves and elects some, and hates and reprobates others, what shall we say? Does it not seem that there is injustice in God, because he does not dispose equally toward equals? The Apostle replies with abhorrence: By no means.

units.la: Versf. 15. Nam Mosi dicit, Miserebor cujus misertus fuero: & commiserabor quem commiseratus fuero.
units.tr: Verse 15. For he says to Moses: I will have mercy on whom I have mercy, and I will show compassion to whom I have shown compassion.

units.la: Rationem reddit negationis, Primum in electione, deinde in reprobatione: Ex quibus rationibus datis consectaria deducit. Ratio cur in electione non sit injustitia, hæc est, Quia misericordiæ exercendæ causa, sola & suprema est Dei liberrima voluntas; liberam habet potestatem agendi de suo quod vult, ut patet ex Domini dicto ad Mosen, Exod. 33. 19. Ergo nulla injustitia est in Deo, cum in electione exercet misericordiam sicut vult.
units.tr: He gives the reason for his denial, first concerning election, then concerning reprobation, and from these given reasons he draws consequences. The reason why there is no injustice in election is this: the sole and supreme cause of exercising mercy is God's most free will. He has free power to act with what is his as he wishes, as appears from the Lord's word to Moses, Exod. 33. 19. Therefore there is no injustice in God, since in election he exercises mercy as he wills.

units.la: Versf. 16. Nempe igitur electio non est ejus qui velit, neque ejus qui currat, sed ejus qui miseretur, nempe Dei.
units.tr: Verse 16. So then election is not of him who wills, nor of him who runs, but of him who shows mercy, namely God.

units.la: Hinc deducit consectarium, in hunc sensum, Si divinæ misericordiæ exerendæ, seu exertæ causa sola, sit liberrima Dei voluntas, tum ejus causa non est in hominis voluntate, seu arbitrio, neque in hominis actionibus, seu bonis operibus, sed in solo Deo. Non est volentis, inquit, Ergo non est ab hominis libero arbitrio. Non est currentis, inquit, Ergo non est ab humanis conatibus & actionibus, quod quisquam diligitur, eligitur, seu misericordiam, & benedictionem consequitur; & per consequens a solo Deo miserente pendet.
units.tr: From this he draws a consequence to this effect: if the sole cause of exercising divine mercy is God's most free will, then its cause is not in the will or choice of man, nor in man's actions or good works, but in God alone. "It is not of him who wills," he says; therefore it is not from man's free choice. "It is not of him who runs," he says; therefore it is not from human efforts and actions that anyone is loved, elected, or obtains mercy and blessing, and consequently it depends on God alone, who shows mercy.

units.la: Versf. 17. Dicit enim Scriptura Pharaoni, ad hoc ipsum excitavite, ut ostendam in te potentiam meam, & ut annuncietur nomen meum in tota terra.
units.tr: Verse 17. For the Scripture says to Pharaoh: I raised you up for this very purpose, that I might show my power in you and that my name might be proclaimed in all the earth.

units.la: Secundo loco rationem reddit de reprobatione, cur non sit in ea injustitia sanctissimo reprobationis fine; Quia ad illustrandam Dei gloriam facit Reprobatio, ut patet ex Scriptura loquente de Pharaone; quem Deus excitavit in eum finem, ut in eo glorificaret nomen suum: Ergo non est in Deo, reprobante quos vult, injustitia.
units.tr: Secondly, he gives the reason for reprobation, why there is no injustice in it: reprobation serves the most holy end of illustrating God's glory, as appears from Scripture speaking of Pharaoh, whom God raised up for this end, that he might glorify his name in him. Therefore there is no injustice in God, who reprobates whom he wills.

units.la: Versf. 18. Itaque cujus vult miseretur, quem autem vult indurat.
units.tr: Verse 18. So then he has mercy on whom he wills, and whom he wills he hardens.

units.la: Hinc deducit consectarium, commune electioni & reprobationi; Quod causa reprobationis, pariter & electionis quaerenda sit, in sola liberrima & sanctissima voluntate DEI, qui liberrimè, & sine injustitia miseretur quorum vult, & liberrimè sine injustitia, sanctissimis modis indurat quos vult.
units.tr: From this he draws a consequence common to election and reprobation: the cause of reprobation, as well as of election, is to be sought in the sole most free and most holy will of God, who most freely and without injustice shows mercy on whom he wills, and most freely, without injustice, by most holy means hardens whom he wills.

units.la: Vers. 19. Dices ergo mihi, Quid adhuc succenset? nam voluntati illius quis obstitit?
units.tr: Verse 19. You will say to me then: Why does he still find fault? For who has resisted his will?

units.la: Objectio quarta, ex superioribus orta, Si Deus indurat quos vult, tum induratos in peccato immeritò reprehendit, & per consequens immeritò punit, quia nemo poterit ejus efficaci voluntati resistere.
units.tr: Fourth objection, arising from the above: if God hardens whom he wills, then he blames the hardened for sin undeservedly, and consequently punishes them undeservedly, since no one can resist his effectual will.

units.la: Vers. 20. Imo vero, O homo, tu quis es qui ex adverso respondes Deo? Num dicet figmentum fictori, Cur me tale fecisti?
units.tr: Verse 20. But indeed, O man, who are you who answer back against God? Will the thing formed say to the one who formed it, Why have you made me thus?

units.la: Ad hanc objectionem Apostolus quadruplicem responsionem reponit, quia in talibus disputationibus ratio carnalis, & corrupta, sibi perplacet. Responsio prima est ad personam objicientis; Imo vero, O homo, tu quis es qui ex adverso respondes Deo? Quibus verbis ostendit duo: Primum, quod haec objectio proponatur ab homine corrupto, qui natura mendax est, & inclinatione naturali, nec non libera sua voluntate peccator, cui conscientia debeat os obturare, ne Deo obloquatur, Quis tu es, O homo?
units.tr: To this objection the Apostle gives a fourfold reply, because in such disputes carnal and corrupt reason is pleased with itself. The first reply concerns the person of the objector: "But indeed, O man, who are you who answer back against God?" By these words he shows two things. First, that this objection is put forward by a corrupt man, who is a liar by nature, a sinner by natural inclination and by his own free will, and whose conscience ought to stop his mouth lest he speak against God: "Who are you, O man?"

units.la: Secundum est, quod is adversus quem objectio intenditur, est Deus, cujus viae nobis sunt impervestigabiles, semper tamen sanctae, etiam tum cum rationes consilii ejus, nobis brevissimae capacitatis homuncionibus, minimè patent, Quis tu es qui respondes DEO?
units.tr: Second, the one against whom the objection is aimed is God, whose ways are unsearchable to us, yet always holy, even when the reasons of his counsel are by no means evident to us, poor little men of very short capacity: "Who are you who answer God?"

units.la: Secunda responsio, est ab autoritate Dei absolutâ in creaturas suas, verbis Esaiae, cap. 45. verf. 9. propositia; Væ contendenti cum plasmatore suo, testa cum testis terrae, nunquid dicet lutum fictori suo, quid facis, seu cur me talem fecisti? Quâ responsione ostendit Apostolus hanc objectionem, & Scripturae, & rationi sanae repugnare, (quia impingit in absolutum, & illimitatum Dei jus in creaturas) & propterea maledictionem, seu væ disputanti hunc in modum adversus Deum, incumbere.
units.tr: The second reply is drawn from God's absolute authority over his creatures, put forward in the words of Isaiah, ch. 45, verse 9: Woe to him who strives with his Maker, a potsherd with the potsherds of the earth! Shall the clay say to its potter, "What are you making?" or "Why have you made me thus?" By this reply the Apostle shows that this objection contradicts both Scripture and sound reason, since it strikes against God's absolute and unlimited right over his creatures; and therefore woe, that is, a curse, rests on one who disputes in this way against God.

units.la: Vers. 21. Annon habet jus figulus in lutum, ut ex eadem massa faciat aliud quidem vas ad decus, aliud vero ad dedecus?
units.tr: Verse 21. Does not the potter have a right over the clay, to make from the same lump one vessel for honour and another for dishonour?

units.la: Tertia responsio, propositia per comparationem potestatis Dei in homines, cum potestate hominis in creaturas alias, in hunc sensum, Quantum licet homini, in aliquam ex Dei creaturis, tantum licet Deo in hominem quem creavit: At homini licet ex eadem luti massa, aliud vas ad honorem, aliud ad dedecus, pro arbitrio suo formare. Ergo Deo licet, de massa humani generis, alios formare ad honorem, alios ad dedecus, pro ipsius arbitrio: Et per consequens, non objicienda est Deo injustitia, in electionis & reprobationis negotio.
units.tr: The third reply is put forward by comparing God's power over men with a man's power over other creatures, to this effect: as far as a man may act with any one of God's creatures, so far may God act with the man he has created. But a man may, at his own discretion, form from the same lump of clay one vessel for honour and another for dishonour. Therefore God may, from the mass of mankind, form some for honour and others for dishonour, according to his own pleasure; and consequently no injustice is to be charged against God in the matter of election and reprobation.

units.la: Verf. 22. Quid si vero volens ostendere Iram, & notam facere potentiam suam, pertulit multa lenitate vasa irae compacta ad interitum:
units.tr: Verse 22. But what if God, wishing to show His wrath and make His power known, endured with great patience the vessels of wrath fitted for destruction,

units.la: Quarta responsio, non modo liberans Deum ab omni injustitia, in hac sua liberrima electione aliquorum, & reprobatione reliquorum, sed etiam ostendens summam Dei aequitatem, & sapientiam, in toto hoc negotio ut nec reprobi conqueri possint de injustitia, nec electi de suis meritis gloriari. Vis autem responsionis per modum quaestionis, ad conscientias hominum acrius pungendas, urgetur in hunc sensum. Quid si vero Deus volens ostendere iram suam seu justitiam vindicativam, & volens potentiam suam notam facere in executione justitiae vindicativae (quod justissima sit scilicet) pertulit multa lenitate vasa irae, sua pravitate congmentata ad interitum, priusquam executioni mandari voluerit meritam ipsorum condemnationem? Quid inquam est hic, quod vel communis ratio Deo obloquatur? quid est hic, quod quivis non laudet in hoc consilio? Ita vero se res habuit, in rejectione Judaeorum, quos Deus non nisi post repudiatam gratiam Christi, & multae lenitatis abusum, ab Euangelii gratia repudiavit. Quae justitia, in executione decreti, liberat Deum ab omni injustitia in decernendo; siquidem non aliter exequitur, quam decrevit exequi.
units.tr: Fourth response, which not only frees God from all injustice in this free choice of some and rejection of others, but also shows God's supreme fairness and wisdom in the whole matter, so that the reprobate cannot complain of injustice nor the elect boast of their merits. The force of this response, put as a question so as to prick men's consciences more sharply, is urged in this sense: What if God, wishing to show His wrath, that is, His avenging justice, and wishing to make His power known in carrying out avenging justice (which is most just), endured with great patience the vessels of wrath, made complete in their wickedness, for destruction, before He chose to execute their deserved condemnation? What, I ask, is there here that even common reason could find fault with? What is there here that anyone would not praise in this plan? Indeed, this is how it stood in the rejection of the Jews, whom God rejected from the grace of the Gospel only after they had rejected the grace of Christ and abused His long patience. This justice, in the execution of the decree, frees God from all injustice in decreeing, since He carries out only what He decreed to carry out.

units.la: Verf. 23. Et ut notas faceret divitias gloriae suae, erga vasa misericordiae, quae praeparavit ad gloriam?
units.tr: Verse 23. And that He might make known the riches of His glory toward the vessels of mercy, which He prepared for glory?

units.la: Pendet adhuc quaestio, ideoque repetendum est, Quid si Deus, etiam ut notas faceret, & illustriores redderet, divitias gloriosae gratiae suae, erga vasa misericordiae quae praeparavit ad gloriam, iram & potentiam suam manifestari vult, in reproborum seu vasorum irae justa perditione? Quid est, quod in hoc decreto culpet quisquam, in cujus executione tanta justitia, & sapientia, & bonitas manifestatur.
units.tr: The question is still pending, and so it must be put again: What if God, also wishing to make known and render more conspicuous the riches of His glorious grace toward the vessels of mercy which He prepared for glory, wills that His wrath and power be manifested in the just destruction of the reprobate, or vessels of wrath? What is there in this decree that anyone could blame, when in its execution such justice, wisdom and goodness are displayed?

units.la: Secunda Pars.
units.tr: Second Part.

units.la: Verf. 24. Quos etiam vocavit, nimirum nos non solum ex Judaeis, verum etiam ex Gentibus.
units.tr: Verse 24. Whom He also called, namely us, not only from among the Jews, but also from among the Gentiles.

units.la: Secunda pars Capitis, in qua, ut de vocatione Gentium, & rejectione Judaeorum omnibus satisfaciat, & fidem Romanorum muniat, ne suspicione reprobationis laederetur: Primo doctrinam electionis applicat Christianis Judaeis & Gentibus, quorum electionem & futuram glorificationem, per efficacem vocationem ad fidem, manifestam fecerat Deus.
units.tr: The second part of the chapter, in which, in order to satisfy everyone about the calling of the Gentiles and the rejection of the Jews, and to strengthen the faith of the Romans lest it be harmed by suspicion of reprobation, the Apostle: first, applies the doctrine of election to Christian Jews and Gentiles, whose election and future glorification God had made manifest through effectual calling to faith.

units.la: Verf. 25. Ut etiam apud Osee dicit, Vocabo populum meum non erat: populum meum? & eam quae dilecta non erat, dilectam.
units.tr: Verse 25. As He also says in Hosea: I will call that which was not My people, My people; and her who was not beloved, beloved.

units.la: Verf. 26. Et erit in loco ubi dictum fuerat eis, Non populus meus vos, illic vocabuntur filij viventis Dei.
units.tr: Verse 26. And it shall come to pass that in the place where it was said to them, You are not My people, there they shall be called sons of the living God.

units.la: Secundo probat praedictam esse vocationem Gentium, testimonio Hosee, cap. 2. verf. 23. in hunc sensum; Eos, qui non erant populus meus, efficaciter vocabo, seu efficiam populum meum, & qui gratiae, seu dilectionis donis affecti non erant a me, dilectionis seu gratiae donis afficientur: & cap. 1. verf 10. in hunc sensum; In Graecia, Italia, caeterisque locis, inter Gentes (ubi tum degebant alieni a foedere Dei) praedicabitur Evangelium, & efficaciter vocabuntur Filii Dei viventis, seu convertentur Dei Electi, ad verum Dei cultum.
units.tr: Second, he proves that the calling of the Gentiles was foretold by the testimony of Hosea, chapter 2, verse 23, in this sense: I will effectually call those who were not my people, or I will make them my people, and those who were not favoured by me with the gifts of love will be favoured with the gifts of love and grace; and chapter 1, verse 10, in this sense: in Greece, Italy and other places, among the Gentiles (where they then lived, estranged from God's covenant), the Gospel will be preached, and those who are effectually called will be the sons of the living God, that is, God's elect will be converted to the true worship of God.

units.la: Verf. 27. Esaias autem clamat super Israel, Etiam si fuerit numerus filiorum Israel ut arena maris, reliquiae servabuntur.
units.tr: Verse 27. But Isaiah cries out concerning Israel: Though the number of the sons of Israel be as the sand of the sea, only a remnant will be saved.

units.la: Verf. 28. Rem enim conficiet & concidet cum justitia: quoniam rem concisam peraget Dominus in terra.
units.tr: Verse 28. For the Lord will finish the work and cut it short in righteousness, for the Lord will make a short work upon the earth.

units.la: Verf. 29. Et sicut prius dixit Esaias, Nisi Dominus Sabbaoth reliquisset nobis semen, facti fuissemus ut Sodoma, & Gomorrhae simile facti fuissemus.
units.tr: Verse 29. And as Isaiah said before: Unless the Lord of Sabaoth had left us a seed, we would have become like Sodom, and we would have been made like Gomorrah.

units.la: Tertio probat, praedictam esse Judaeorum rejectionem, Testimonio Isaiae, cap. 10. versu 22. In hunc sensum clamantis; etsi populus secundum carnem ex Israele genitus, juxta promissionem Dei, usque adeo multiplicetur, ut comparari poterit cum arena, quae est in littore maris, solae tamen It tamen reliquiæ seruabuntur, id est, paucissimi salvi erunt, multitudo vero rejicietur, & peribit, versu 27. Nam Deus post multam lenitatis suæ abusum, breviter finiet controversiam suam cum populo illo, districtam sequens justitiam: quoniam Deo statutum est, severitatem suam cito exequi, & perficere in populi rejectione. Et Cap. 1. versu 9. idem Isaias prædixit, nisi Deus exercituum reliquisset populo Judaico, saltem exiguum semen, in quo, velut reliquiis promissæ benedictiones implerentur, penitus effemus consumpti, & perditi, sicut Sodomæi & Gomorrhæi.
units.tr: Third, he proves that the rejection of the Jews was foretold by the testimony of Isaiah, chapter 10, verse 22, where he cries out in this sense: although the people born of Israel according to the flesh, in accordance with God's promise, should multiply so greatly that they could be compared with the sand which is on the seashore, yet only a remnant will be saved; that is, very few will be saved, but the multitude will be rejected and will perish (verse 27). For God, after the long abuse of His patience, will briefly bring His dispute with that people to an end, following strict justice, since it has been decreed by God that He will quickly carry out and complete His severity in the rejection of the people. And in chapter 1, verse 9, the same Isaiah foretold that unless the God of hosts had left the Jewish people at least a small seed, in which the promised blessings would be fulfilled as in a remnant, we would have been utterly consumed and destroyed, like the people of Sodom and Gomorrah.

units.la: Tertia Pars.
units.tr: Third Part.

units.la: Verf. 30. Quid igitur dicemus? nempe Gentes quæ non sectantur justitiam, apprehendisse justitiam, justitiam autem eam quæ est ex fide.
units.tr: Verse 30. What shall we say then? That the Gentiles, who did not pursue righteousness, have attained righteousness, namely the righteousness which is of faith.

units.la: Tertia pars capitis, In qua Apostolus scopum suum in præcedentibus exponit hunc esse, ut experientia credentium inter Gentes, & justitiariorum inter Judæos, præcedentem suam confirmet doctrinam de justificatione per fidem, & non ex operibus. Prima experientiæ pars de Gentibus, Gentes (inquit) quæ non sectabantur justitiam operum, apprehenderunt veram justitiam, illam nempe justitiam, quæ est ex fide: Ergo justificandi ratio illa sola, quæ non est ex operibus sed ex fide, obtinet.
units.tr: The third part of the chapter. In it the Apostle sets out his aim in what precedes: to confirm his doctrine of justification by faith, and not by works, by the experience of believers among the Gentiles and of the self-righteous among the Jews. The first part of this experience concerns the Gentiles. The Gentiles (he says), who did not pursue the righteousness of works, have attained the true righteousness, namely that righteousness which is of faith. Therefore that way of being justified alone, which is not by works but by faith, prevails.

units.la: Verf. 31. Israelem vero consectando Legem justitiæ, ad Legem justitiæ non pervenisse.
units.tr: Verse 31. But Israel, pursuing the law of righteousness, has not attained to the law of righteousness.

units.la: Altera experientiæ pars, de Judæis incredulis; Israelitæ (inquit) sectabantur legem justitiæ, ut secundum eam justificarentur ex operibus, & illam justitiam quæ ex operibus est, non sunt assequuti; quia per legem, justitia est impossibilis: Ergo justificatio non est ex operibus, seu secundum legem justitiæ, sed ex fide.
units.tr: The second part of the experience concerns the unbelieving Jews. Israel (he says) pursued the law of righteousness, so that they might be justified by works through it, and they have not obtained that righteousness which is by works, because by the law righteousness is impossible. Therefore justification is not by works, or according to the law of righteousness, but by faith.

units.la: Verf. 32. Quare? Quia non ex fide, sed velut ex operibus legis, nempe offenderunt ad lapidem ad quem impingitur.
units.tr: Verse 32. Why? Because it was not by faith, but as it were by the works of the law; namely, they stumbled at the stone over which one strikes.

units.la: Ut hanc experientiam, amplius in usum suum trahat, quærit causam, cur Judæi legis sectatores, non sint assequuti justitiam: Et respondens, causam affert triplicem: Prima est, quia non ex fide quærebant justitiam, quæ sola est recta ratio justificationis. Altera causa, quia quaerebant justitiam quasi per opera, quae ratio est impossibilis; non tantum quia nemo perfecte observare poterit legem, sed etiam quia bona opera, quae justitiae legalis absque fide, sectatores faciunt, non sunt digna operum bonorum nomine, larvam enim habent operum tantum, & qui affectant per ea justificari, affectant justificari quasi per opera, vel per larvam bonorum operum. Tertia causa, Quia Christum in quem crederent, ut justificarentur, propter ejus humilitatem & carnis infirmitatem, non agnoverunt, sed despexerunt, & in suam perniciem se illi opposuerunt, impingentes in eum, ut in lapidem offensionis.
units.tr: To draw this experience further into his own use, he asks the reason why the Jews who pursued the law did not attain righteousness. Answering, he gives a threefold cause. The first is that they did not seek righteousness by faith, which alone is the right way of justification. The second cause is that they sought righteousness as if by works, which way is impossible: not only because no one can observe the law perfectly, but also because the good works which the adherents of legal righteousness perform without faith do not deserve the name of good works. For they have only the mask of works, and those who aim to be justified by them aim to be justified as if by works, or by the mask of good works. The third cause is that they did not recognise Christ, in whom they ought to believe in order to be justified, on account of his humility and the weakness of his flesh, but despised him, and in their own ruin set themselves against him, stumbling upon him as upon a stone of offence.

units.la: Verf. 33. Quemadmodum scriptum est, Ecce, statuo in Sion lapidem ad quem impingetur, & petram offendiculi; & quisquis credit in eum, non pudefiet.
units.tr: Verse 33. As it is written: Behold, I lay in Sion a stone to stumble over, and a rock of offence; and whoever believes in him will not be put to shame.

units.la: Utramque hanc experientiae partem, confirmat ex Prophetae praedictione, Is. 8. 14. & 28. versu 16. In hunc sensum; Ecce ponam, inquit Deus, Christum in Ecclesia, cujus initium est ex Sion, lapidem probatum, & lapidem probationis seu offendiculi, (sicut Judaei increduli experti sunt) & quicunque crediderit in Eum, expectatione sua, id est, justitia & vita aeterna, non frustrabitur, sicut credentes ex Gentibus experti sunt: atque ita confirmavit Apostolus justitiam per fidem.
units.tr: He confirms both parts of this experience from the prophet's prediction, Isa. 8.14 and 28.16. In this sense: Behold, I lay, says God, Christ in the Church, whose beginning is from Sion, a tried stone, and a stone of trial or offence (as the unbelieving Jews have found), and whoever believes in him that is, will not be disappointed in his expectation, namely righteousness and eternal life, as the believers from the Gentiles have found. And so the Apostle confirmed justification by faith.

units.la: Caput decimum.
units.tr: Chapter 10.

units.la: Prosequitur argumentum, de temporali rejectione Judaeorum; Causam rejectionis ostendens fuisse, quod Judaei insipienter, & pertinaciter, rejecerint justitiam Dei in Christo.
units.tr: He pursues the argument concerning the temporary rejection of the Jews, showing that the cause of the rejection was that the Jews foolishly and obstinately rejected the righteousness of God in Christ.

units.la: Partes capitis sunt duae: In priori, ostendit Judaeorum insipientiam, ad versum 14. In altera ipsorum pertinaciam, ad finem.
units.tr: The chapter has two parts. In the first, he shows the foolishness of the Jews, up to verse 14. In the second, their obstinacy, to the end.

units.la: Verf. 1. Fratres, propensa quidem voluntas cordis mei, & deprecatio ad Deum super Israel, est ad salutem.
units.tr: Verse 1. Brethren, the good will of my heart and my prayer to God for Israel is for their salvation.

units.la: Justas causas rejectionis Judaeorum ostensurus Apostolus, praefatur ut supra, de suo erga eos benevolo affectu, ne ex odio quicquam ab eo dictum putaretur.
units.tr: Intending to set out the just causes of the rejection of the Jews, the Apostle first speaks, as above, of his well-disposed affection towards them, so that nothing he said might be thought to arise from hatred.
