units.la: Verf. 2. Testor enim de ipsis, eos zelum Dei habere, sed non ex notitia.
units.tr: Verse 2. For I bear them witness that they have a zeal for God, but not according to knowledge.

units.la: Hujus sui affectus causam, praeter supra dictas causas, affert ipsorum zelum pro Deo, licet praepostcrum: qui zelus, humana quidem commiseratione dignus fuerat, licet laudabilis non fuerit, quia non ex notitia, sed ex ignorantia ortum habebat, & idcirco zelus caecus, zelus insipientium erat.
units.tr: Besides the reasons already mentioned, he gives as a reason for this his affection their zeal for God, though it is misdirected. This zeal deserved human pity, though it was not praiseworthy, because it did not arise from knowledge but from ignorance; and for this reason it was a blind zeal, the zeal of the foolish.

units.la: Verf. 3. Nam ignorantes Dei justitiam, & propriam justitiam statuentes constituere, justitiae Dei non fuerunt subjecti.
units.tr: Verse 3. For, being ignorant of the righteousness of God, and seeking to establish their own righteousness, they did not submit themselves to the righteousness of God.

units.la: Insipientiam Judaeorum probat sex argumentis. Argumentum primum, Ex ignorantia justitiae DEI per fidem in CHRISTUM nobis imputatae, affectabant operum suorum inhaerentem justitiam, & oblatam justitiam CHRISTI, superbe rejiciebant. Insipientiam suam igitur prodebant.
units.tr: He proves the foolishness of the Jews by six arguments. First argument: from their ignorance of the righteousness of God, which is imputed to us through faith in Christ. They proudly rejected the inherent righteousness of their own works and the righteousness of Christ offered to them. By this they revealed their foolishness.

units.la: Verf. 4 Nam finis Legis est Christus, ad justitiam cuivis credenti.
units.tr: Verse 4. For Christ is the end of the Law, for righteousness to everyone who believes.

units.la: Arg 2. CHRISTUS est finis Legis, ad justitiam, cuivis credenti, id est, tota Lex ideo traditur, ut homines ex agnitione peccatorum suorum per legem manifestorum, confugerent ad CHRISTUM, & justitiam per fidem consequerentur. Ergo insipienter agebant Judaei, qui prae se ferentes studium Legis, CHRISTUM, qui finis est Legis, non agnoscebant.
units.tr: Argument 2. Christ is the end of the Law, for righteousness to everyone who believes; that is, the whole Law was given so that men, recognising their sins made manifest by the Law, might flee to Christ and obtain righteousness through faith. Therefore the Jews acted foolishly, for, while professing zeal for the Law, they did not acknowledge Christ, who is the end of the Law.

units.la: Verf. 5. Moses enim describit justitiam quae est ex Lege, dicens, Qui praestiterit ea, vivet per illa.
units.tr: Verse 5. For Moses describes the righteousness which is from the Law, that the man who does those things shall live by them.

units.la: Arg. 3. Justitia legis seu operum, sicut testatur Moses, non affert vitam ulli, nisi perfecte praestiterit omnia quae in lege praecipiuntur, quod impossibile est. Ergo Judaei insipienter ejusmodi justitiam affectabant.
units.tr: Argument 3. The righteousness of the Law, or of works, as Moses testifies, brings life to no one unless he has perfectly performed everything commanded in the Law, which is impossible. Therefore the Jews foolishly pursued such righteousness.

units.la: Verf. 6. At quae ex fide est justitia, ita dicit, Ne dixeris in corde tuo, Quis ascendet in coelum; hoc est, Christum ex alto deducere.
units.tr: Verse 6. But the righteousness which is of faith says this: Do not say in your heart, Who will ascend into heaven? that is, to bring Christ down from above.

units.la: Verf. 7. Aut, quis descendet in abyssum? hoc est, Christum ex mortuis reducere.
units.tr: Verse 7. Or, who will descend into the abyss? that is, to bring Christ up from the dead.

units.la: Arg. 4. Justitia fidei, (sicut idem Moses testatur) prohibet ne credentes in DEUM, corde turbentur propter ea, quae homini tam sunt difficilia, aut impossibilia, quam ascendere in Coelum, aut descendere in abyssum, quia quum Christus illas difficultates jam superaverit, descendendo ex Coelo, & ex mortuis resurgendo, amplius turbari, quomodo justitiam, quomodo vitam aeternam, & liberationem à morte consequamur, nihil aliud est quam fundamenta Christianae religionis convellere, & inquirere, quomodo possibile sit Christum descendisse de Coelo, aut ex mortuis resurrexisse. Ergo insipientes se produnt Judaei qui hanc justitiam fidei repudiarunt.
units.tr: Argument 4. The righteousness of faith (as the same Moses testifies) forbids believers in God to be troubled in heart about things that are as difficult or impossible for a man as to ascend into heaven or descend into the abyss. For since Christ has already overcome those difficulties, by descending from heaven and rising from the dead, to be further troubled as to how we may obtain righteousness, how we may obtain eternal life and deliverance from death, is nothing other than to overthrow the foundations of the Christian religion and to inquire how it is possible that Christ came down from heaven or rose from the dead. Therefore the Jews who rejected this righteousness of faith reveal themselves as foolish.

units.la: Versf. 8. Sed quid dicit? Prope te verbum est in ore tuo & in corde tuo. Hoc est verbum illud fidei quod praedicamus.
units.tr: Verse 8. But what does it say? The word is near you, in your mouth and in your heart. This is the word of faith which we preach.

units.la: Justitia fidei, sicut securos reddit credentes, de difficultatibus in via salutis, sic etiam viam ad justitiam, & salutem facilem proponit: Verbum enim Dei, seu verbum Evangelii, idem scilicet quod Apostoli praedicarunt, prope nos stat, ut corde illud recipientes, in eo acquiescamus, & ejus veritatem ore confiteamur; quasi nobis diceret, Ne turbemini, tantum conjectis in Deum loquentem, omnibus difficultatibus Evangelio fidem habete, fidemque factis ostendite. Ergo Judaei facilem hanc rationem justitiae propositam rejicientes, insipientes sunt.
units.tr: The righteousness of faith, as it makes believers secure about the difficulties on the way of salvation, so also sets out a way to righteousness and salvation that is easy. For the word of God, or the word of the Gospel, namely the very thing the Apostles preached, is near us, so that receiving it in our heart we may rest in it and confess its truth with our mouth; as if he were saying, Do not be troubled; only cast yourselves upon God speaking, believe the Gospel in all difficulties, and show your faith by deeds. Therefore the Jews, who rejected this easy way of righteousness set before them, are foolish.

units.la: Versf. 9. Nempe si professus fueris ore tuo Dominum Iesum, & credideris in corde tuo, quod Deus eum suscitavit ex mortuis, salvaberis.
units.tr: Verse 9. Indeed, if you confess with your mouth the Lord Jesus, and believe in your heart that God raised him from the dead, you will be saved.

units.la: Explicans & confirmans superius: Evangelii summa, suavissima hac conditione proponitur, nempe, Si redemptionem per Christum partam, & ipsius resurrectione per potentiam Dei manifestatam, sincero cordis affectu, tibi ipsi applicueris, Christumque sincera confessione glorificare studueris, salutem proculdubio consequeris. Ergo Judaei repudiantes hanc conditionem Justificationis & Salutis, insipientiam suam produnt.
units.tr: Explaining and confirming what was said above: the sum of the Gospel is set forth under this most sweet condition, namely, that if you apply to yourself, with a sincere affection of heart, the redemption obtained through Christ and his resurrection, made manifest by the power of God, and if you strive to glorify Christ by sincere confession, you will undoubtedly obtain salvation. Therefore the Jews, who reject this condition of justification and salvation, reveal their foolishness.

units.la: Versf. 10. Nam corde creditur ad justitiam, fit autem ore prosessio ad salutem.
units.tr: Verse 10. For with the heart one believes unto righteousness, and with the mouth confession is made unto salvation.

units.la: Confirmat hujus connexi partes copulatas, & connexas, quinque rationibus: Prima ratio est, à connexionis fidei cordis, & confessionis oris ordine, per Deum constituto; qui est, ut per fidem, ex corde in Christum stum, justitiam seu justificationem consequeremur; & ut justificati per fidem, pergeremus ad salutis possessionem, per oris, seu externorum operum confessionem, Christum glorificantes. Ergo conjungi debent fides Christi in corde & confessio Christi in ore, seu conjungi debet interna fides, cum fructibus externis.
units.tr: He confirms the joined and connected parts of this connection by five reasons. The first reason is from the order, appointed by God, of the connection between faith of the heart and confession of the mouth: namely, that through faith, from the heart, in Christ we obtain righteousness or justification; and that, being justified through faith, we proceed to the possession of salvation, by confessing Christ with the mouth, that is, by external works, glorifying Christ. Therefore faith in Christ in the heart and confession of Christ in the mouth must be joined; that is, inward faith must be joined with outward fruits.

units.la: Verf. 11. Dicit enim Scriptura, Quisquis credit in eum, non pudefiet.
units.tr: Verse 11. For the Scripture says, Whoever believes in him will not be put to shame.

units.la: Ratio 2. Confirmans connexionem verae fidei & salutis, à testimonio Isaiæ, cap 28, verf. 16. cui pronunciat, non festinandos ipse suâ, seu salute sperată, qui cunque credunt in Christum. Ergo firma est connexio fidei, & salutis.
units.tr: Reason 2. Confirming the connection between true faith and salvation, from the testimony of Isaiah, chapter 28, verse 16, where it is declared that those who believe in Christ shall not be hasty in their own salvation, or in the hope of it. Therefore the connection of faith and salvation is firm.

units.la: Verf. 12. Non enim est distinctio vel Judæi vel Græci: nam idem est Dominus omnium, dives in quosvis à quibus invocatur.
units.tr: Verse 12. For there is no distinction between Jew and Greek; for the same Lord is Lord of all, rich toward all who call upon him.

units.la: Ratio 3. Confirmans generalitatem connexionis inter fidem & salutem; Non est distinctio nationum Judæorum vel Gentium, nec exceptio cujusquam credentis apud Deum. Ergo omnis, qui fidem habet, sine exceptione servabitur, Judæus pariter & Græcus.
units.tr: Reason 3. Confirming the universality of the connection between faith and salvation: there is no distinction of nations, Jews or Gentiles, nor any exception of any believer before God. Therefore everyone who has faith, without exception, will be saved, Jew and Greek alike.

units.la: Idem Ratio 4. Confirmans connexionis universalitatem, inter fidem & oris confessionem, seu veram Dei invocationem & salutem. Dominus Iesus Christus est idem, suique in omnibus similis, & in gratia sua dives in quosvis, qui ipsum invocant. Ergo omnes credentes, & Christum ex fide invocantes, seu ore eum confitentes, servabuntur.
units.tr: The same. Reason 4. Confirming the universality of the connection between faith and the confession of the mouth, or true invocation of God, and salvation. The Lord Jesus Christ is the same and like himself toward all, and rich in his grace toward all who call upon him. Therefore all believers, who call upon Christ from faith, or confess him with the mouth, will be saved.

units.la: Verf. 13. Quisquis enim invocaverit nomen Domini, servabitur.
units.tr: Verse 13. For whoever calls upon the name of the Lord will be saved.

units.la: Ratio 5. Confirmans connexionem, inter oris confessionem veram, seu invocationem Christi ex fide, & salutem, à testimonio Joelis 2. 32, qui pronunciat omnes vere invocantes nomen Domini, salvandos esse.
units.tr: Argument 5. Confirming the connection between a true confession of the mouth, or the invocation of Christ from faith, and salvation, from the testimony of Joel 2. 32, who declares that all who truly call upon the name of the Lord are to be saved.

units.la: Secunda Pars.
units.tr: Second Part.

units.la: Verf. 14. Quomodo igitur invocabunt eum in quem non crediderint? quomodo autem credent ei de quo non audierint? quomodo autem audient absque prædicante?
units.tr: Verse 14. How then shall they call upon him in whom they have not believed? And how shall they believe him of whom they have not heard? And how shall they hear without a preacher?

units.la: Verf. 15. Quomodo autem prædicabunt, nisi missi fuerint? sicut scriptum est, Quàm speciosi pedes evangelizantium pacem, evangelizantium bona.
units.tr: Verse 15. And how shall they preach, unless they be sent? As it is written, How beautiful are the feet of those who preach peace, who bring good things.

units.la: Secunda pars Capitis, in qua pertinaciam Judæorum ostendit, ex solutione objectionum, quæ ad ipsorum excusationem facere potuissent.
units.tr: Second part of the chapter, in which he shows the obstinacy of the Jews by answering the objections they could have raised in their own defence.

units.la: Prima objectio est ex nexu mediorum, ad justitiam fidei ordinatorum, in hunc sensum;
units.tr: The first objection is drawn from the connection of the means ordained for the righteousness of faith, in this sense:

units.la: Cum impossibile sit, non credentes, posse invocare Dominum Iesum vel non audientes Dei verbum, posse credere; vel eos, quibus non prædicatur verbum Dei, posse audire, vel posse iis prædicari verbum, ad quos non mittuntur præcones: (qui nexus confirmatur ex verbis Isaiæ, qui connectit inter se Euangelium & Euangelizantes: missionem nunciorum, & lætitiam auditorum; pedes seu adventum prædicatorum, cum gaudio recipientium,) Sequitur excusari posse Judæos, saltem a pertinacia rejectione Euangelicæ justitiæ, quia non audiverunt Euangelium.
units.tr: Since it is impossible for those who do not believe to call upon the Lord Jesus, or for those who have not heard the word of God to believe, or for those to hear to whom the word of God is not preached, or for the word to be preached to those to whom heralds are not sent (a connection confirmed by the words of Isaiah, who links together the gospel and those who proclaim it, the sending of messengers and the joy of the hearers, the feet or coming of the preachers, received with joy), it follows that the Jews can be excused, at least from the obstinacy of rejecting evangelical righteousness, because they did not hear the gospel.

units.la: Vers. 16. Sed non omnes auscultarunt Evangelio, Esaias enim dicit, Domine, quis credidit sermoni nostro?
units.tr: Verse 16. But not all have obeyed the gospel. For Isaiah says, Lord, who has believed our report?

units.la: Respondet Apostolus, Judæos & audivisse, & non obedivisse, quod probat ex querimonia Prophetæ deplorantis, quod pauci crediderint sermoni Prophetarum. Ergo non excusandi Judæi à pertinacia.
units.tr: The Apostle answers that the Jews both heard and did not obey, which he proves from the complaint of the prophet lamenting that few believed the message of the prophets. Therefore the Jews are not to be excused from obstinacy.

units.la: Vers. 17. Ergo fides ex auditu est: auditus autem per verbum Dei.
units.tr: Verse 17. So faith comes from hearing, and hearing through the word of God.

units.la: Ex eodem testimonio confirmat nexum fidei, auditus, & verbi Dei, ut Judæos incredulos alliciat, & fideles urgeat, ad utendum mediis.
units.tr: From the same testimony he confirms the connection between faith, hearing, and the word of God, in order to draw in the unbelieving Jews and to urge the faithful to use the means.

units.la: Vers. 18. Sed (inquam ego) an non audierunt? imò verò in omnem terram exivit sonus eorum, & ad ultima orbis terrarum, verba eorum.
units.tr: Verse 18. But I say, have they not heard? Indeed they have: their sound has gone out into all the earth, and their words to the ends of the world.

units.la: Repetit objectionem, & respondet allegationem, nempe quod Judæi non audiverint Euangelium, falsam esse, quia sonus Euangelii pervasit totum mundum, ut vox diei & noctis, per orbem terrarum exivit, sicut in Psal. 19. 5. dicitur, ad quem locum alludit Apostolus.
units.tr: He repeats the objection and answers the assertion, namely that the Jews had not heard the gospel, by showing it to be false, because the sound of the gospel has pervaded the whole world, going out through the earth like the voice of day and night, as is said in Psal. 19. 5, to which place the Apostle alludes.

units.la: Vers. 19. Sed (inquam ego) num Israel non cognovit Deum? Primus Moses dicit, Ego ad æmulationem provocabo vos per gentem tem quæ non est gens: per gentem intelligentiæ expertem, ad iram vos provocabo.
units.tr: Verse 19. But I say, did Israel not know God? First Moses says, I will provoke you to jealousy by those who are not a nation; by a foolish nation I will provoke you to anger.

units.la: Alia objectio, At forsan Israelitæ non cognoverunt, seu intellexerunt Euangelii oblationem, sed per ignorantiam, doctrinam non intellectam rejecerunt, ideoque à pertinacia saltem, excusari poterint.
units.tr: Another objection: perhaps the Israelites did not recognise or understand the offer of the gospel, but through ignorance rejected a doctrine they did not understand, and so could at least be excused from obstinacy.

units.la: Hanc objectionem refellit, triplici Scripturæ testimonio. Primum est ex Mose, Deuter. 32. 21. qui propter rejectum fœdus gratiæ, seu violatum fœdus conjugale, inter Deum & Judæos prædicit fore, ut Judæi rejiciantur à fœdere, & ut Gentes in eorum locum assumantur. Ergo Judæi rei sunt gratiæ pertinaciter rejectæ.
units.tr: He refutes this objection with a threefold testimony of Scripture. The first is from Moses, Deut. 32. 21, who, because of the rejected covenant of grace (or the violated marriage covenant between God and the Jews), foretells that the Jews will be rejected from the covenant and the Gentiles taken into their place. Therefore the Jews are guilty of obstinately rejecting grace.

units.la: Verf. 20. Esaias autem utitur audacia, dicitque, Inventus sum ab iis qui me non quærebant: manifestus factus sum iis qui de me non interrogabant.
units.tr: Verse 20. But Isaiah is bold and says, I was found by those who did not seek me; I was made manifest to those who did not ask for me.

units.la: Secundum testimonium, ex Isa 65. 1. qui audacter, id est, non metuens persecutionem à populo suo, prædicit ob Judæorum pervicaciam, & gratiam ab iis pertinaciter repudiatam, fore, ut Deus repudiatis Judæis, Gentes Deum minimè quærentes, ascisceret in communionem secum per fidem, seu agnitionem sui.
units.tr: The second testimony is from Isa. 65. 1, where Isaiah, boldly, that is, not fearing persecution from his own people, foretells that, because of the obstinacy of the Jews and the grace they had stubbornly repudiated, God would take the Gentiles, who did not seek him at all, into communion with himself through faith, that is, through the knowledge of himself, after rejecting the Jews.

units.la: Verf. 21. Adversus Israelem autem dicit, Toto die expandi manus meas ad populum non obedientem & contradicentem.
units.tr: Verse 21. But to Israel he says, All day long I have stretched out my hands to a disobedient and contrary people.

units.la: Tertium testimonium, in quo ex Isa 65. 2 probat Judæos, expressis terminis, rebellionis condemnatos; Quia Deus toto die, seu toto patientiæ suæ tempore, se Judæis Patrem, expansis quasi brachiis offerebat, illi verò renuebant. Ergo Judæi, pertinaciter repudiatæ gratiæ, rei sunt, & idcirco merito à Deo rejecti.
units.tr: The third testimony, in which from Isa. 65. 2 he proves in express terms that the Jews are condemned for rebellion: God, all day long, that is, throughout the whole time of his patience, offered himself to the Jews as a Father, with arms as it were outstretched, but they refused. Therefore the Jews, having pertinaciously rejected grace, are guilty, and are justly rejected by God.

units.la: Verf. 1.
units.tr: Verse 1.

units.la: NUm igitur (inquam ego) abjecit Deus populum illum suum? Absit. Nam & ego Israelita sum, ex semine Abrahami, tribus Benjamin.
units.tr: I say then, has God cast away his people? By no means. For I too am an Israelite, of the seed of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin.

units.la: Argumentum primum; Deus non abjecit Judæos omnes & singulos: non abjecit populum suum electum: Ergo non sunt despiciendi Judæi, quasi omnes plane sint rejectitii.
units.tr: First argument: God has not cast off all and each of the Jews; he has not rejected his elect people. Therefore the Jews are not to be despised as if they were all plainly castaways.

units.la: Hoc argumentum confirmat tribus rationibus.
units.tr: He confirms this argument with three reasons.

units.la: Ratio 1. Ego Paulus, de ea gente oriundus sum, nec sum rejectitius tamen. Ergo non omnes & singuli Judæi abjecti sunt.
units.tr: First reason: I, Paul, am sprung from that nation, and yet I am not a castaway. Therefore not all and each of the Jews have been cast off.

units.la: Verf. 2. Non abjecit Deus populum illum suum, quem præcognovit:
units.tr: Verse 2. God has not cast off his people, whom he foreknew.

units.la: Ratio 2. Populus electus seu præcognitus non abjicitur propter electionis, & dilectionis immutabilitatem; Ergo non omnes sunt abjecti.
units.tr: Second reason: the elect or foreknown people are not cast off, because election and love are unchangeable. Therefore not all are cast off.

units.la: Verf. 2. An nescitis de Elia quid dicat Scriptura? quomodo interpellet Deum, adversus Israelem, dicens,
units.tr: Verse 2. Or do you not know what the Scripture says of Elijah? How he pleads with God against Israel, saying,

units.la: Verf. 3. Domine, Prophetas tuos occiderunt: & altaria tua suffoderunt, & ego relictus sum solus, & petunt animam meam.
units.tr: Verse 3. Lord, they have killed your prophets and dug down your altars, and I alone am left, and they seek my life.

units.la: Verf. 4. Sed quid dicit ei divinum responsum? Feci ut remanserint mihi septem millia virorum, qui non flexerunt genu imagini Baal.
units.tr: Verse 4. But what does the divine answer say to him? I have kept for myself seven thousand men who have not bowed the knee to the image of Baal.

units.la: Verf. 5 Ita igitur & hoc tempore reservatio secundum electionem gratuitam facta est.
units.tr: Verse 5. So too at this present time there is a remnant chosen by grace.

units.la: Ratio 3. Sicut temporibus Eliæ, cum totus populus Eliæ videbatur perditus & abjectus, reservavit sibi Deus septem millia electorum: Sic, in hac Judæorum rejectione temporali, reservavit sibi Deus aliquos, secundum electionem gratuitam: Ergo non omnes abjecti sunt.
units.tr: Third reason: just as in the time of Elijah, when the whole people seemed lost and rejected, God reserved for himself seven thousand chosen, so in this temporary rejection of the Jews God has reserved for himself some, according to gratuitous election. Therefore not all are cast off.

units.la: Verf. 6. Quod si per gratiam, non jam ex operibus: alioquin gratia jam non est gratia. Sin ex operibus, jam non est gratia: alioquin opus jam non est opus.
units.tr: Verse 6. But if it is by grace, it is no longer by works; otherwise grace is no longer grace. But if it is by works, it is no longer grace; otherwise work is no longer work.

units.la: Hinc infert Apostolus duo consectaria; primum inserviens principali epistolæ instituto, nempe, Quod electio cum gratuita sit, non fit ex operibus tibus ullis prævisis, quia in causa electionis, gratia & opera ut causæ, se mutuo tollunt: Nam si gratia causa sit electionis, opera non sunt causa: Et si opera, prævisa scilicet, causa sint electionis, gratia non est causa: At gratia causa est, ut dictum est: Ergo opera prævisa non sunt causa electionis.
units.tr: From this the Apostle draws two corollaries. The first serves the main purpose of the epistle: since election is gratuitous, it is not made on account of any foreseen works, because in the cause of election grace and works, as causes, cancel each other out. For if grace is the cause of election, works are not the cause; and if works, namely foreseen ones, were the cause of election, grace would not be the cause. But grace is the cause, as has been said; therefore foreseen works are not the cause of election.

units.la: Verf. 7. Quid igitur? Quod requirit Israel, hoc non est adeptus: sed electi adepti sunt, reliqui vero occaluerunt,
units.tr: Verse 7. What then? What Israel sought, it has not obtained; but the elect obtained it, and the rest were hardened.

units.la: Secundum consectarium, ostendens prius illud dictum, Cap. 9. versu 31. de Israelitis, qui quærebant justitiam ex operibus, & eam non sunt assequuti, intelligendum esse tantum de reprobis: nam electi ex Israele, obtinuerunt justitiam, quam ex gratia in messia, seu CHRISTO quærebant, reliqui vero, id est reprobi occalluerunt. Verf. 8. Sicut scriptum est, Dedit eis Deus spiritum soporis: oculos ut non videant, & aures ut non audiant) usque ad hodier-num diem.
units.tr: The second corollary shows that the earlier statement in chapter 9, verse 31, about the Israelites, who sought righteousness by works and did not attain it, is to be understood only of the reprobate. For the elect from Israel obtained the righteousness which they sought by grace in the Messiah, or Christ, while the rest, that is the reprobate, were hardened. Verse 8. As it is written, God has given them a spirit of stupor, eyes that they should not see, and ears that they should not hear, to this very day.

units.la: Quod occaluerint reprobi, probat duplici testimonio: Primum est Isaiæ 29. 16. & 6. 9. Ubi dicitur Deum justo suo judicio, perversum hunc populum, stuporis & cæcitatis pœna percussisse, seu ob contemptum verbi sui, in mentem judicii expertem tradidisse; ne gratiam Dei, in Euangelio oblatam, discernerent; quod judicium incumbebat multitudini, usque ad Euangelii prædicati tempora.
units.tr: That the reprobate were hardened he proves by a twofold testimony. The first is Isa. 29. 16 and Isa. 6. 9, where it is said that God, by his just judgment, struck this perverse people with the punishment of stupor and blindness, or, on account of their contempt for his word, gave them over to a mind unable to judge, so that they would not discern the grace of God offered in the gospel. This judgment lay upon the multitude until the time of the preached gospel.

units.la: Verf. 9. Et David dicit, Fiat mensa eorum in laqueum, & tendiculam, & offendiculum & retributionem ipsis.
units.tr: Verse 9. And David says, Let their table become a snare, and a trap, and a stumbling block, and a recompense unto them.

units.la: Verf. 10 Obtenebrentur oculi eorum, ut non videant: & tergum eorum semper incurva.
units.tr: Verse 10. Let their eyes be darkened, that they may not see, and bow down their back always.

units.la: Alterum testimonium, est Davidis Psal. 69. 23, 24. Qui ut typus Christi, in hostes imprecatur, ut omnia Dei beneficia, & ipsum etiam oblatum Euangelium, cedant illis in ruinæ occasionem, ut nihil nisi terrena, posteà sapiant, qui toties à Deo moniti, cælestia nolebant sapere, indque in justam ingratitudinis ipsorum ultionem.
units.tr: The second testimony is from David, Psalm 69:23, 24. As a type of Christ, he calls down curses on his enemies, so that all God's benefits, and even the Gospel itself, offered to them, may turn to their ruin. Having been so often warned by God and unwilling to be wise in heavenly things, they shall from then on be wise only in earthly things, as a just punishment for their ingratitude.

units.la: Verf. 11. Num igitur (inquam ego) impegerunt ut excidement? rent? Absit, sed per eorum offensam salus obtigit Gentibus, ut eos ad æmulationem provocaret.
units.tr: Verse 11. I ask then, have they stumbled so as to fall? Certainly not. But through their offence salvation has come to the Gentiles, to provoke them to emulation.

units.la: Repetit primum argumentum, ad probandum non esse despiciendos Judæos, & addit secundum. Non sunt rejecti Judæi, ut omnes & singuli perirent, qui sunt de hac Gente; sed ut salus per Christum, repudiata à Judæis, obveniret Gentibus, ut Gentes ad Deum conversæ, provocarent Judæos ad æmulationem, & per consequens ad resipiscentiam. Ergo non sunt despiciendi Judæi.
units.tr: He repeats the first argument, to prove that the Jews are not to be despised, and adds a second. The Jews were not rejected so that all and each of those who belong to this nation should perish. They were rejected so that salvation through Christ, refused by the Jews, might come to the Gentiles; and the Gentiles, converted to God, might provoke the Jews to emulation, and consequently to repentance. Therefore the Jews are not to be despised.

units.la: Provocantur autem ad æmulationem Judæi, quando vident se excludi à Deo, & dissipari, ne sint Ecclesia Dei, Gentes vero, ipsorum loco, à Deo recipi in ipsius sinum, in quo aliquando fovebatur Ecclesia Judaica.
units.tr: The Jews are provoked to emulation when they see themselves shut out by God and scattered, so that they are no longer the Church of God, while the Gentiles, in their place, are received by God into his bosom, in which the Jewish Church was once cherished.

units.la: Verf. 12. Quòd si eorum offensa est opulentia mundi, & diminutio eorum opulentia Gentium: quanto magis plenitudo ipsorum?
units.tr: Verse 12. Now if their offence is the riches of the world, and their loss the riches of the Gentiles, how much more their fulness?

units.la: Sicut ruina Judæorum, in bonum Gentium cessit, sic etiam, & multo magis, restitutio Judæorum cedet in mundi, seu Gentium, emolumentum. Ergo tantum abest, ut despiciendi sint Judæi, tanquam penitus rejecti, ut contra, ipsorum conversio optanda, & speranda sit.
units.tr: Just as the ruin of the Jews turned to the good of the Gentiles, so also, and much more, the restoration of the Jews will turn to the advantage of the world, that is, of the Gentiles. Therefore it is so far from being the case that the Jews are to be despised as wholly rejected, that on the contrary their conversion is to be desired and hoped for.

units.la: Verf. 13. Nam (quod vobis dico Gentibus quatenus ego quidem sum Apostolus Gentium) ministerium meum illustro:
units.tr: Verse 13. For I speak to you Gentiles, inasmuch as I indeed am the apostle of the Gentiles, I magnify my ministry.

units.la: Verf. 14. Ut experiar si quo modo ad æmulationem provocem consanguineos meos, & servos aliquos ex ipsis.
units.tr: Verse 14. If by any means I may provoke to emulation my kinsmen, and may save some of them.

units.la: Ego ipse, Apostolus Gentium, tanto acrius, vobis & aliis quam possum plurimis convertendis, ministerium meum impendo, & munus meum illustrius reddo, eo fine, ut provocem Judæos consanguineos meos, ne sinant vos filiorum Dei mensa solos frui, sed se vobis adjungant, & ita serventur. Ergo vestrum est, eos non despicere, ut penitus rejectos, sed contra, ut serventur mecum laborare.
units.tr: I, the apostle of the Gentiles, devote my ministry all the more eagerly to converting you and as many others as I can, and I make my office more glorious, with this end: that I may provoke my Jewish kinsmen, so that they do not allow you alone to enjoy the table of the sons of God, but join themselves to you, and so are saved. Therefore it is your part not to despise them as utterly rejected, but on the contrary to help them, that they may be saved along with me.

units.la: Verf. 15. Nam si abjectio eorum, est reconciliatio mundi; quae erit assumptio, nisi vita ex mortuis.
units.tr: Verse 15. For if the casting away of them is the reconciling of the world, what shall the receiving of them be, but life from the dead?

units.la: Si abjectio Judæorum, conversa est per Dei bonitatem, in occasionem reconciliandi Gentes Deo; nonne ex conversione Judæorum, tanta mutatio in melius expectanda est, inter Gentes, ut quasi resurrectio furrectio quaedam à mortuis dici possit? Ergo non despiciendi Judæi, tanquam prorsus rejecti, sed ipsorum potius conversio optanda & speranda est. Quando enim Deus, populum suum veterem, rursum assumet quid mirum si copiam sui spiritus majorem, in omnes Ecclesias effundat? quid mirum si hæreses exitiales, & scismata, quibus jam Ecclesiæ Christianæ inter Gentes, ad mortem pene laborant tollat, & inter se, & cum Ecclesia Judæorum arctius uniat? Hanc aliquando futuram Ecclesiarum felicitatem, sub tempus conversionis Judæorum, non vult nos desperare Apostolus, qui aliquam resurrectionem quasi à mortuis, in Ecclesiarum conditionis mutatione sperandam nobis proponit.
units.tr: If the rejection of the Jews has been turned by God's goodness into an occasion for reconciling the Gentiles to God, should we not expect from the conversion of the Jews so great a change for the better among the Gentiles that it could be called a kind of resurrection from the dead? Therefore the Jews are not to be despised as utterly rejected; rather their conversion is to be desired and hoped for. For when God takes back his old people, what wonder if he pours out a greater measure of his Spirit upon all the Churches? What wonder if he removes the deadly heresies and schisms by which the Christian Churches among the Gentiles are now nearly dying, and unites them more closely with one another and with the Church of the Jews? The Apostle does not want us to despair of this happiness of the Churches, which will come one day around the time of the conversion of the Jews; he holds before us a kind of resurrection from the dead, to be hoped for in the change of the Churches' condition.

units.la: Verf. 16. Quòd si primitiæ sanctæ, sancta etiam massa: & si radix sancta est, etiam rami.
units.tr: Verse 16. For if the firstfruit is holy, the lump is also holy; and if the root is holy, so are the branches.

units.la: Arg. 6. Gens Judæorum, vi fœderis cum patribus ipsorum initi, Deo est consecrata, & fœderalis sanctitatis dignitate, à parentibus fœderatis descendente, honestata est; sicut massa & messis sanctificantur in primitiis, & rami sanctificantur, seu Deo consecrantur, in radicis consecratione. Ergo Judæi non sunt despiciendi, tanquam penitus abjecti.
units.tr: Arg. 6. The Jewish nation, by virtue of the covenant made with their fathers, is consecrated to God, and is honoured with the dignity of covenant holiness descending from covenanted parents. Just as the lump and the harvest are sanctified in the firstfruits, and the branches are sanctified, or consecrated to God, in the consecration of the root, so the Jews are not to be despised as utterly cast off.

units.la: Verf. 17. Quòd si nonnulli rami defracti sunt, tu vero quum esses oleaster, insitus es pro ipsis: & particeps radicis ac pinguedinis olea factus es:
units.tr: Verse 17. And if some of the branches were broken off, and thou, being a wild olive, wert graffed in among them, and with them becamest partaker of the root and fatness of the olive;

units.la: Arg. 7. Increduli aliquot Judæi, ab Ecclesia sanctorum Patriarcharum, sicut rami ex olea, defracti sunt: Tu vero populus Gentium, cum oleaster instar esses alienus à fœdere Dei, illorum loco insitus es, atque ita privilegiorum illius Ecclesiæ, & sancti fœderis, quasi pinguedinis oleæ particeps factus es. Ergo non debes Judæos despicere.
units.tr: Arg. 7. Some unbelieving Jews were broken off from the Church of the holy patriarchs, like branches from an olive tree. But you, a people of the Gentiles, when you were like a wild olive, a stranger to the covenant of God, were grafted into their place, and so were made a partaker of the privileges of that Church and of the holy covenant, as of the fatness of the olive. Therefore you ought not to despise the Jews.

units.la: Verf. 18. Ne gloriare adversus ramos: quod si gloriaris, non tu radicem portas, sed radix te.
units.tr: Verse 18. Boast not against the branches. But if thou boastest, thou bearest not the root, but the root thee.

units.la: Arg. 8. Si gloriatus fueris adversus Judæos, quasi illis dignior esses, non minus stolide te gereres, quam si rami à radice gestati, gloriarentur adversus radicem, quæ ipsos gestat. Ergo non debes Judæos despicere.
units.tr: Arg. 8. If you boast against the Jews, as though you were worthier than they, you would behave no less foolishly than branches borne by a root that boasted against the root which bears them. Therefore you ought not to despise the Jews.

units.la: Verf. 19. Dices igitur, defracti sunt rami ut ego insererer:
units.tr: Verse 19. Thou wilt say then, The branches were broken off, that I might be graffed in.

units.la: Verf. 20. Bene : per incredulitatem defracti sunt, tu vero per fidem stas, ne effertor animo, sed metue.
units.tr: Verse 20. Well; because of unbelief they were broken off, and thou standest by faith. Be not highminded, but fear.

units.la: In solutione objectionis propositum. Verum quidem est, rejectos esse Judæos, ut hac occasione, tu in eorum locum in Ecclesia succederes: sed quum illi, propter infidelitatem rejecti sint, tu vero per fidem ex gratia stes, non suppetit inde tibi, ulla superbiendi, vel Judæos despiciendi causâ, sed metuendi potius, & tibi cavendi, ne peccessis & puniaris. Ergo non debes Judæos contemnere quasi prorsus abjectos.
units.tr: The objection is answered as follows. It is true that the Jews were rejected, so that on this occasion you might succeed them in the Church. But since they were rejected because of unbelief, and you stand by faith through grace, you have no ground from this for pride or for despising the Jews, but rather for fear, and for taking care lest you too fall and be punished. Therefore you ought not to scorn the Jews as utterly cast off.

units.la: Verf. 21. Nam si Deus naturalibus ramis non pepercit, vide ne tibi quoque non parcat.
units.tr: Verse 21. For if God spared not the natural branches, take heed lest he also spare not thee.

units.la: Confirmans superius, Si Deus non pepercit insolescentibus Judæis, Ecclesiæ sanctæ naturalibus ramis, non parcet Romanis, vel ullis Gentibus superbientibus, Ramis scilicet insitititis. Ergo non debes tu Gentilis Judæos præ te despicere.
units.tr: Confirming what was said above: if God did not spare the proud Jews, the natural branches of the holy Church, he will not spare the Romans or any Gentiles who grow proud, that is, the grafted branches. Therefore you, a Gentile, ought not to despise the Jews in comparison with yourself.

units.la: Verf. 22. Vide igitur benignitatem ac præcisam severitatem Dei in eos quidem qui ceciderunt præcisam severitatem : in te vero benignitatem, si permanseris in benignitate, alioquin & tu excideris.
units.tr: Verse 22. Behold therefore the goodness and severity of God: on them which fell, severity; but toward thee, goodness, if thou continue in his goodness: otherwise thou also shalt be cut off.

units.la: Nisi, consideratâ Dei in Judæos severitate, & in te benignitate, perseveraveris in fide, & submissa obedientia Christi, tu quoque excideris & abjicieris. Ergo, nisi abjici velles, in timore Dei te contine, & Judæos ne contemnas.
units.tr: Unless, considering God's severity toward the Jews and his goodness toward you, you persevere in faith and in humble obedience to Christ, you too will fall and be cast off. Therefore, unless you wish to be cast off, restrain yourself in the fear of God, and do not despise the Jews.

units.la: Verf. 23. Sed & illi, si non permanserint in infidelitate, inserentur, potens enim est Deus rursum eos inserere.
units.tr: Verse 23. And they also, if they abide not still in unbelief, shall be graffed in: for God is able to graff them in again.

units.la: Sicut tu, nisi permanseris in fide, excideris: Sic Judæi, nisi permanserint in infidelitate, rursus inserentur in sanctam Ecclesiam Patriarcharum, imo vero restitutio Judæorum, propter omnipotentem Dei gratiam, non desperanda est. Ergo Judæi non sunt à te despiciendi.
units.tr: Just as you will fall unless you persevere in faith, so the Jews, unless they persevere in unbelief, will be grafted again into the holy Church of the patriarchs. Indeed, the restoration of the Jews, through God's almighty grace, is not to be despaired of. Therefore the Jews are not to be despised by you.

units.la: Verf. 24. Etenim si tu ex naturali exectus es oleastro, & praeter naturam insitus es in veram oleam: quanto magis ij qui naturales sunt, inserentur propriæ oleæ?
units.tr: Verse 24. For if thou wert cut out of the olive tree which is wild by nature, and wert graffed contrary to nature into a good olive tree: how much more shall these, which be the natural branches, be graffed into their own olive tree?

units.la: Si Deus Gentes, ut ramos alienos à foederata radice, Ecclesiæ Patrifix Patriarcharum inseruit, multò magis Judæos, qui sunt naturales rami illius Ecclesiæ, restituet.
units.tr: If God grafted the Gentiles, as branches foreign to the covenanted root, into the Church of the patriarchs, much more will he restore the Jews, who are the natural branches of that Church.

units.la: Verf. 25. Nolim enim vos ignorare, fratres, mysterium hoc, (ut ne sitis apud vosmetipsos sapientes) obduratiouem ex parte Israeli evenisse, quousque plenitudo Gentium introierit.
units.tr: Verse 25. For I would not, brethren, that ye should be ignorant of this mystery, lest ye should be wise in your own conceits, that blindness in part is happened to Israel, until the fulness of the Gentiles be come in.

units.la: Verf. 26. — Et ita totus Israel salvabitur: sicut scriptum est,
units.tr: Verse 26. And so all Israel shall be saved: as it is written,

units.la: Ego vobis mysterium aperio, & ex speciali revelatione prædico, hanc Judæorum obdurationem, nec totalem seu omnium Judæorum esse, sed ex parte, seu aliquorum tantùm, nec nisi ad certum tempus duraturam, nempe dum plenitudo Gentium introierit. Ergo non debetis apud vos arrogantes esse, seu Judæos despectui habere. Plenitudinem Gentium intelligit, ingentem Gentium multitudinem, qualis ante tempora conversionis Judæorum non fuerat; cujus multitudinis accessione, ad veram religionem, provocabitur Israel, seu populus Judæorum dispersus, ad redeundum ad Dominum Iesum Christum, seu ad veram fidem in Messiam, à quo per infidelitatem discesserat: Atque ita totus Israel, id est, multitudo Judæorum, corpus dispersi populi comprehendens, convertetur.
units.tr: I tell you this mystery, and proclaim it from a special revelation: this hardening of the Jews is neither total nor universal, but partial, affecting only some of them, and it will last only until the fullness of the Gentiles has come in. Therefore you must not be arrogant among yourselves, or hold the Jews in contempt. By the fullness of the Gentiles he means the vast multitude of Gentiles, such as had not existed before the time of the conversion of the Jews. By the coming in of this multitude, Israel, that is, the Jewish people scattered abroad, will be provoked to true religion, to return to the Lord Jesus Christ, that is, to true faith in the Messiah, from whom they had fallen away through unbelief. And so all Israel, that is, the multitude of the Jews, embracing the whole body of the dispersed people, will be converted.

units.la: Verf. — 26. Veniet ex Sion ille vindex, & avertet impietates à Iacob.
units.tr: Verse 26. There shall come out of Zion the deliverer, and he shall turn away ungodliness from Jacob.

units.la: Verf. 27. Et, hoc est illis à me pactum, Quum abstulero peccata ipsorum.
units.tr: Verse 27. And this is my covenant with them, when I shall take away their sins.

units.la: Confirmat hanc Prophetiam, ex Isaiæ vaticinio, qui cap. 29. verf 26. & cap. 27. verf. 3. prædicit fore, ut Messias, ex Judæorum Ecclesia secundum carnem oriunctus, verus Redemptor, liberaret Gentem suam, à reatu & servitute peccati, condonatis illius populi iniquitatibus, & fore ut in fœdus gratiæ eos reciperet, ad peccati plenam abolitionem. Quod quo tempore futurum sit, jam dixit Apostolus.
units.tr: He confirms this prophecy from the prophecy of Isaiah, who, in chapter 29, verse 26 and chapter 27, verse 3, foretells that the Messiah, descended according to the flesh from the Jewish Church, will be the true Redeemer who will free his people from the guilt and bondage of sin, pardoning the iniquities of that people, and that he will receive them into the covenant of grace, with the full abolition of sin. The Apostle has already said when this will take place.

units.la: Verf. 28. Itaque quod ad Euangelium attinet, sunt inimici propter vos; quod ad electionem autem, dilecti propter Patres.
units.tr: Verse 28. As touching the gospel, they are enemies for your sake; but as touching the election, they are beloved for the fathers' sake.

units.la: Etiamsi, quod ad Euangelium repudiatum à Judæis illis reprobis attinet, Judæi rejecti pro inimicis habeantur à Deo, in veltram utilitatem; respectu tamen electionis hujus populi, præ omnibus aliis nationibus, ut populus Dei diceretur, & respectu Electorum in hac gente, Judæi à Deo diliguntur, propter fœdus initum inter Deum & patres ipsorum: Ergo propter eandem rationem à vobis despici non debent sed diligi potius.
units.tr: Even though, as far as the gospel rejected by those reprobate Jews is concerned, the rejected Jews are regarded by God as enemies, for your benefit, nevertheless, with respect to the election of this people above all other nations, so that they might be called the people of God, and with respect to the elect within this nation, the Jews are loved by God on account of the covenant made between God and their fathers. Therefore, for the same reason, they ought not to be despised by you but rather loved.

units.la: Versus 29. Nam dona illa & illa vocatio Dei ejusmodi sunt ut eorum ipsum pœnitere non possit.
units.tr: Verse 29. For the gifts and calling of God are such that he cannot repent of them.

units.la: Arg. 16. Cum occupatione objectionis: Etiamsi hæc natio, jure merito, excidisse suis omnibus privilegiis, videri posset, quia tamen dona specialis gratiæ, & nominatim vocatio ex proposito, sive in nationem aliquam præ reliquis, sive in hominem aliquem præ aliis collata, immutabilia sunt, quæ Deus nunquam penitus rescindet, vel revocabit, & quæ in conversione hujus populi firma tandem ostendet. Idcirco non debet hæc natio à vobis contemni, sed in honore potius haberi.
units.tr: Argument 16. With an answer to an objection: although it might seem that this nation, rightly and deservedly, has fallen from all its privileges, nevertheless the gifts of special grace, and especially the calling, which is bestowed according to purpose, whether upon some nation above others or upon some man above others, are unchangeable. God will never utterly rescind or revoke them, and he will finally show them to be firm in the conversion of this people. Therefore this nation should not be despised by you, but rather held in honour.

units.la: Versus 30. Sicut enim & vos quondam non obedivistis Deo, nunc autem estis misericordiam consecuti per illorum contumaciam:
units.tr: Verse 30. For as you also once did not obey God, but now have obtained mercy through their disobedience;

units.la: Versus 31. Sic & isti nunc non obedierunt, ut per vestram misericordiam & ipsi misericordiæ donentur.
units.tr: Verse 31. So these also have now not obeyed, that through your mercy they also may obtain mercy.

units.la: Arg. 17. Certò credendum est tantam gratiam manifestaturum esse Deum erga Judæos, ex occasione misericordiæ factæ vobis Gentibus, quantam ostendit erga vos Gentes, olim immorigeras, ex occasione incredulitatis, & contumaciæ Judæorum. Ergo non despiciendi Judæi, tanquam penitus rejecti, sed conversio ipsorum promovenda potius.
units.tr: Argument 17. It must surely be believed that God will show as great grace toward the Jews, on the occasion of the mercy shown to you Gentiles, as he showed toward you Gentiles, once disobedient, on the occasion of the unbelief and stubbornness of the Jews. Therefore the Jews are not to be despised as utterly rejected, but their conversion is rather to be promoted.

units.la: Versus 32. Conclusit enim Deus omnes illos in contumacia, ut omnium illorum miseretur.
units.tr: Verse 32. For God has shut up all of them in disobedience, that he may have mercy on all.

units.la: Arg. 18. In hunc sensum, Dei sapientissima providentia, salutis suorum negotium totum sic administravit, ut omnes deprehensi in peccatis & contumacia, gloriandi in se materia destituerentur, & quicunque salutem obtinerent, miserationi Divinæ eam totam deberent. Ergo non despiciendi Judæi, sed opus Divinæ misericordiæ erga hunc populum, tempore à Deo constituto, expectandum est.
units.tr: Argument 18. In this sense, by the most wise providence of God, he so ordered the whole business of their salvation that all, found in sin and disobedience, were stripped of any matter for boasting in themselves, and whoever obtain salvation owe it entirely to the divine mercy. Therefore the Jews are not to be despised, but the work of divine mercy toward this people is to be awaited at the time appointed by God.

units.la: Versus 33. O profundas divitias tum sapientiæ tum cognitionis Dei! quàm imperscrutabilia sunt ejus judicia, & ejus viæ investigabiles!
units.tr: Verse 33. O the depth of the riches both of the wisdom and knowledge of God! How unsearchable are his judgments, and his ways past finding out!

units.la: Hujus argumenti, atque adeo totius præcedentis doctrinæ, præsertim de electione aliquorum, & reprobatione reliquorum, usum duplicem nobis ostendit Apostolus.
units.tr: From this argument, and indeed from the whole preceding doctrine, especially concerning the election of some and the reprobation of others, the Apostle shows us a twofold use.

units.la: Primus est, ut cum ipso admiremur, & celebremus profundas divitias, ineffabilis sapientiæ Dei. Alter est, ne scrutemur plus quam revelatum est, de consiliis Dei, sed sapiamus etiam in revelatis, ad sobrietatem (quia superant Dei consilia captum nostrum, & planè inscrutabilia sunt) Deum in omnibus glorificantes.
units.tr: The first is that, with him, we should admire and celebrate the depths of the riches of the ineffable wisdom of God. The second is that we should not pry into the counsels of God further than has been revealed, but should be wise also in what has been revealed, with sobriety (since God's counsels exceed our grasp and are altogether unsearchable), glorifying God in all things.

units.la: Verf. 34 Quis enim cognovit mentem Domini? aut quis ei fuit à consilio?
units.tr: Verse 34. For who has known the mind of the Lord? Or who has been his counsellor?

units.la: Consectarii utriusque rationes addit tres.
units.tr: He adds three reasons as consequences of each of these points.

units.la: Ratio prima, Nulla creatura penetravit in mentem Dei, nulla unquam Ei fuit à consiliis. Ergo Dei consilia impervestigabilia, non debemus scrutari, sed divitias sapientiæ ejus admirari, & celebrare.
units.tr: First reason. No creature has penetrated into the mind of God; no creature has ever been his counsellor. Therefore we ought not to pry into the unsearchable counsels of God, but to admire and celebrate the riches of his wisdom.

units.la: Verf. 35. Aut quis prior dedit ei, & retribuetur ei?
units.tr: Verse 35. Or who has first given to him, and it shall be repaid to him?

units.la: Ratio 2. Deus in nullius ære est, aut esse potest; nemini quicquam debet: nemo quicquam meretur ab eo, nemo potest prodire, vel nomen edere, qui beneficio aliquo suo Deum prior obstrinxit. Ergo non possunt gloriari, ulli ex Electis, quasi ullo jure obligatus fuerit Deus, ut ipsos ad vitam designaret: neque conqueri possunt ulli ex reprobis, quasi non persolverit quod debebat, cum nemini quicquam debeat. Verf. 36. Namex eo, & per eum, & in ipsum sunt omnia. Ipsi sit gloria in secula, Amen.
units.tr: Second reason. God is in no one's debt, nor can he be; he owes nothing to anyone; no one deserves anything from him; no one can come forward or put forward a claim who has first bound God by some benefit of his own. Therefore none of the elect can boast as though God were bound by any right to designate them to life, nor can any of the reprobate complain as though God had not paid what he owed, since he owes nothing to anyone. Verse 36. For from him, and through him, and to him are all things. To him be glory for ever, Amen.

units.la: Ratio 3. Confirmans priorem, Omnia sunt ex Deo, tanquam primo autore: Omnia per Eum, ut Conservatorem, sustentantur; Omnia in Ipsum tanquam in ultimum scopum tendunt: Ergo, quandocunque Ipsi visum fuerit, suam gloriam promovere, in Judæorum rejectione, vel Gentium vocatione, in aliquorum hominum electione, & reliquorum reprobatione, ipsi in omnibus, & apud omnes, honor & gloria in æternum tribui debet. A M E N.
units.tr: Reason 3. Confirming the former: all things are from God as the first author; all things are sustained through him as preserver; all things tend toward him as their final end. Therefore, whenever it has seemed good to him to advance his glory, whether in the rejection of the Jews or the calling of the Gentiles, in the election of some men and the reprobation of others, honour and glory are to be ascribed to him in all things, and by all, for ever. AMEN.

units.la: [illegible, ~3 letters]
units.tr: [illegible]

units.la: Caput duodecimum.
units.tr: Chapter 12.

units.la: EVit prior pars Epistolæ, de via ad justificatio-nem recte capessenda, sequitur altera posterior, de vita justificatorum recte instituenda.
units.tr: The first part of the Epistle, on rightly taking up the way to justification, is followed by the second, on rightly ordering the life of the justified.

units.la: Capitis tres sunt partes; In prima, hortatur ad vitæ sanctimoniam in genere, ad versum tertium.
units.tr: The chapter has three parts. In the first, he exhorts to holiness of life in general, to verse 3.

units.la: In secunda, speciatim instruit Ecclesiæ ministros, de recto donorum usu, ad versum nonum.
units.tr: In the second, he instructs the ministers of the Church in particular about the right use of gifts, to verse 9.

units.la: In tertia, præcepta dat communia, de virtutibus Christianis.
units.tr: In the third, he gives general precepts about Christian virtues.

units.la: Verf. 1. ADhortor igitur vos, fratres per miserationes illas Dei ut sistatis corpora vestra hostiam vivam, sanctam & placentem Deo, rationalem illum cultum vestrum:
units.tr: Ver. 1. I exhort you therefore, brothers, by those mercies of God, that you present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy and pleasing to God, which is your rational worship.

units.la: Allusione facta ad typicum, sub Lege Levitica, sacrificandi ritum, amicissimè hortatur, ut justificationis gratuitæ per Christum nobis concessæ, fructum in vita sancta producamus.
units.tr: Alluding to the typical rite of sacrifice under the Levitical Law, he earnestly exhorts us to bring forth in a holy life the fruit of the justification freely given to us through Christ.

units.la: Hortationis tria sunt membra: Primum, ut corpora nostra sistamus Deo, hoc est nos totos, non animas tantum, sed etiam corpora, Deo in gratitudinis sacrificium offeramus, & consecremus: Rationes hortationis sunt quinque, quæ simul etiam requisita, seu proprietates hujus sacrificii, continent.
units.tr: The exhortation has three parts. First, that we present our bodies to God, that is, that we offer and consecrate ourselves wholly to God as a sacrifice of gratitude, not only our souls but also our bodies. The reasons for the exhortation are five, which also contain the requirements, or properties, of this sacrifice.

units.la: Prima ratio. In vehementi obsecratione, & obtestatione, comprehensa; Quia Dei miserationes supra recitatæ, nimirum electio ex misericordia, redemptio ex misericordia, vocatio ex misericordia, & justificatio ex misericordia seu gratia, exigunt jure suo hanc à vobis gratitudinem.
units.tr: First reason. It is contained in a earnest entreaty and appeal: the mercies of God recited above, namely election from mercy, redemption from mercy, calling from mercy, and justification from mercy or grace, demand this gratitude from you by their own right.

units.la: Vivam ] Ratio 2. Quia hæc hostia viva est, siquidem nihil hic mactandum præter peccatum; vos autem ipsi, Deo consecrati vivetis, & ad æternam vitam conservabimini.
units.tr: Living — Reason 2. Because this sacrifice is living, since nothing is to be slaughtered here except sin; and you yourselves, consecrated to God, will live and be preserved to eternal life.

units.la: Sanctam ] Ratio 3. Hæc hostia verè sancta est, in cujus quotidiana oblatione, ipla constat sanctitas.
units.tr: Holy — Reason 3. This sacrifice is truly holy, since holiness itself consists in its daily offering.

units.la: Acceptam ] Ratio 4. Quia hæc hostia, non rejicietur à Deo, ut umbratiles illæ legales multæ ab hypocritis oblatæ, sed accepta erit Deo.
units.tr: Acceptable — Reason 4. Because this sacrifice will not be rejected by God, unlike those many shadowy legal sacrifices offered by hypocrites, but will be acceptable to God.

units.la: Rationalem ] Ratio 5. Quia actus, quo Deo hanc hostiam offertis, est cultus ille vester rationalis seu spiritualis, cultu illo typico præfiguratus, eoque tanto præstantior, quanto spiritualia carnalibus, & corpora sanctorum, brutorum cadaveribus anteferenda sunt.
units.tr: Rational — Reason 5. Because the act by which you offer this sacrifice to God is that rational or spiritual worship of yours, prefigured by that typical worship, and it is the more excellent as spiritual things are to be preferred to carnal, and the bodies of saints to the carcasses of beasts.

units.la: Vers. 2. Et ne vos configurate seculo isti, sed transformate vos per renovationem mentis vestræ, ad hoc ut probetis quæ sit voluntas Dei, bona illa, placens ac perfecta.
units.tr: Ver. 2. And do not be conformed to this world, but be transformed by the renewing of your mind, so that you may prove what is the will of God, which is good, pleasing and perfect.

units.la: Secundum membrum hortationis; Ut caveamus in vita & conversa-tione, ne instituta, voluntatem, & mores mundanorum hominum, pro re-gula habeamus, cui nos conformemus; Ratio hortationis in hortatione continetur, quia mundani, hujus mundi, seu seculi voluptates, honores & commoda tantùm sapiunt.
units.tr: The second part of the exhortation: that we take care in our life and conduct not to take the institutions, will and manners of worldly men as a rule to which we conform. The reason for the exhortation is contained in the exhortation itself, because worldly men savour only the pleasures, honours and advantages of this world or age.

units.la: Mutemini ] Tertium hortationis membrum; ut studeamus, ingenium nostrum natura carnale, per intellectus & voluntatis nostræ quotidianam renovationem, magis magisque in spirituale transformare. Rationes hor-tationis sunt duæ.
units.tr: Be transformed — the third part of the exhortation: that we strive to transform our nature, which is carnal, more and more into the spiritual, through the daily renewal of our understanding and will. There are two reasons for the exhortation.

units.la: Discernite ] Ratio prima. Quia Dei lex, seu voluntas revelata in ver-bo, pro regula cui nos conformemus est. 1. bona, quæ bona sunt docens, ad bonum nos ducens, & bonos nos reddens: 2. Est accepta Deo, qui nullam nisi in verbo suo præscriptam obedientiam, agnoscit: 3. Est perfecta, omnia continens, quæ ad Dei cultum, & nostram salutem spectant. Idcirco mentis renovationi studendum.
units.tr: Prove — First reason. Because God's law, or his will revealed in the Word, is the rule to which we conform. It is (1) good, teaching what is good, leading us to good and making us good; (2) acceptable to God, who acknowledges no obedience except that prescribed in his Word; (3) perfect, containing all that pertains to the worship of God and our salvation. Therefore we must strive for the renewal of the mind.

units.la: Discernite ] Ratio 2. Quia non nisi mente renovata, & spirituali, discernere poterimus genuinum sensum voluntatis divinæ in verbo revelatæ; vel agnitam approbare, vel approbatam experimento cognoscere, quam bona, accepta Deo, & in se perfecta ea sit. Idcirco mentis renova-tioni studendum.
units.tr: Prove — Reason 2. Because only with a renewed and spiritual mind can we discern the genuine sense of the divine will revealed in the Word, either to approve what we have recognised, or to know by experience how good, acceptable to God, and perfect in itself it is. Therefore we must strive for the renewal of the mind.

units.la: Secunda Pars. Vers. 3. Enimverò per gratiam quæ mihi data est, edico cuivis versanti inter vos ne sapiat supra quàm oportet sapere: sed sapiat ad sobrietatem, prout cuique Deus partitus est mensuram fidei.
units.tr: Second Part. Ver. 3. For through the grace given to me I charge everyone among you not to think of himself more highly than he ought to think, but to think soberly, as God has apportioned to each a measure of faith.

units.la: Secunda pars Capitis; In qua, pro autoritate sua Apostolica, (quam gratiam vocat, quia ex ineffabili gratia ipsi erat concessa,) præcipit cuique versanti inter illos, in publico munere scilicet, vel doni alicujus excellentia.
units.tr: The second part of the chapter, in which, by his apostolic authority (which he calls grace, because it was granted to him by unspeakable grace), he commands each person among them who has a public office or an eminent gift.

units.la: {y} Vers. 3. excellentia, ne supra modum de se sentiat ne supra consortes, vel supra talenti sui valorem, seu cognitionis suae modulum se extollat: sed sobrie se gerat & moderate, in omnibus & erga omnes. Rationes hortationis, seu praecepti sunt quinque.
units.tr: Ver. 3. Not to think more highly of himself than he ought: not to exalt himself above his fellows, or above the value of his talent, or the measure of his knowledge; but to conduct himself soberly and moderately, in all things and toward all. The reasons for this exhortation, or precept, are five.

units.la: Ratio prima. Unicuique Deus est partitus, non plenitudinem, sed mensuram fidei: Ergo aequum est, ut unusquisque intra suam mensuram, modeste se contineat.
units.tr: First reason. God has apportioned to each not the fullness but the measure of faith; therefore it is fair that each should restrain himself modestly within his own measure.

units.la: Vers. 4 Quemadmodum enim in uno corpore membra multa habemus: membra vero omnia eandem non habent actionem:
units.tr: Ver. 4. For as in one body we have many members, but all the members do not have the same function.

units.la: Ratio. 2. Sicut in corpore naturali, diversa membra, diversis deputata sunt operationibus, sic in corpore Ecclesiastico fidelium, seu societate ministrorum Ecclesiae, diversae functiones diversis actionibus destinantur. Ergo aequum est, ut singuli suis officiis modeste se circumscribant.
units.tr: Reason 2. As in the natural body different members are assigned to different operations, so in the ecclesiastical body of the faithful, or the society of ministers of the Church, different functions are directed to different actions. Therefore it is fair that each should modestly confine himself to his own duties.

units.la: Vers. 5 Ita multi illi unum corpus sumus in Christo, singulatim autem, alii aliorum membra.
units.tr: Ver. 5. So we, though many, are one body in Christ, and individually members of one another.

units.la: Ratio 3. Eadem similitudine inclusa; Sicut in corpore naturali, multa membra sunt corpus unum, sic in corpore Ecclesiastico, omnes fideles, speciatim vero omnes ministri Ecclesiastici, unum sunt corpus in CHRISTO, Ergo omnes, ad unitatem corporis tuendam, pro sua quisque parte, modeste conspirare debent.
units.tr: Reason 3. Under the same likeness: as in the natural body many members make one body, so in the ecclesiastical body all the faithful, and especially all ecclesiastical ministers, are one body in Christ. Therefore all, to preserve the unity of the body, must each in his own part work together modestly.

units.la: Singulatim Ratio 4. Sicut in corpore naturali, sic etiam in corpore Ecclesiastico, membra singula, non solum totius sunt corporis, sed etiam alterum alterius: seu destinatum est unumquodque membrum, ad uniuscujusque membri usum promovendum: Ergo omnes, ad mutuas operas promovendas, sibi invicem debent servire, non vero immoderata, vel arrogantia, se mutuo impedire.
units.tr: Individually — Reason 4. As in the natural body, so also in the ecclesiastical body, each member belongs not only to the whole body but also to the others; each member is destined to promote the use of every other member. Therefore all, to promote mutual works, ought to serve one another, and not hinder one another by immoderate or arrogant behaviour.

units.la: Vers. 6. Habentes autem diversa dona pro gratia quae nobis data est, sive prophetiam prophetemus pro proportione fidei.
units.tr: Ver. 6. Having gifts that differ according to the grace given to us, whether prophecy, let us prophesy according to the proportion of faith.

units.la: Ratio 5. Quae habemus dona diversa, seu munera cum donis diversis, habemus ex gratia, & beneplacito Dei, qui ea dedit: Ergo ne insolescamus, sed modeste nos contineamus.
units.tr: Reason 5. The different gifts, or offices with their different gifts, which we have, we have from the grace and good pleasure of God, who gave them. Therefore let us not become proud, but restrain ourselves modestly.

units.la: Sive Prophetiam Descendit ad singula ordinaria munera publica, singulisque gulisque suas operationes & metas prescribit: Functionum facit duo genera. Primum est Prophetia: Secundum est Diaconi. Prophetia Verbi tractationem comprehendit, Qui habemus Prophetiam, prophetemus (inquit) secundum proportionem fidei, id est, doceamus id solum, quod Deus in Scriptura credendum propoluit, & quod solide novimus, seu credimus sensum esse Scripturæ.
units.tr: Whether prophecy — He descends to the individual ordinary public offices, and prescribes to each its operations and limits. He makes two kinds of functions: the first is prophecy; the second is the diaconate. Prophecy comprises the handling of the Word: "He who has prophecy, let him prophesy" (he says) "according to the proportion of faith", that is, let him teach only what God has proposed for belief in Scripture, and what we firmly know, or believe, to be the sense of Scripture.

units.la: Vers. 7. Sive ministerium versemur in ministrando: tum is qui docet, in docendo:
units.tr: Ver. 7. Or ministry, let us wait upon our ministry; or he who teaches, in teaching;

units.la: Secundum genus functionum Ecclesiasticarum, est Diaconia quæ munera omnia, Verbi ministerio subservientia continet, ut postea declarabit. De qua præscribit, ut qui in Diaconia versatur, in ea se contineat, nec altius ascendat, nisi ordine vocatus.
units.tr: The second kind of ecclesiastical function is the diaconate, which includes all the offices subservient to the ministry of the Word, as he will declare later. Concerning it he prescribes that whoever is engaged in the diaconate should keep within it and not rise higher unless called by due order.

units.la: Is qui docet ] Prophetiam subdividit, in officium Doctorum & Pastorum, seu Prophetas distinguit, in Doctores & Pastores; Doctores intelligit eos, qui ex officio docent, seu informandis mentibus in cognitione veritatis operam dant, & hos jubet ut facultate sua ad docendum diligenter utantur, & hic se exerceant totos.
units.tr: He who teaches — He subdivides prophecy into the office of teachers and pastors, or distinguishes the prophets into teachers and pastors. By teachers he understands those who teach by office, that is, who labour to inform minds in the knowledge of the truth, and he bids these to use their ability for teaching diligently, and to exercise themselves wholly in it.

units.la: Vers. 8. Tam qui exhortatur, in exhortatione: tum is qui distribuit, cum simplicitate: tum qui præest, cum diligentia, tum qui miseretur cum hilaritate:
units.tr: Ver. 8. He who exhorts, in exhortation; he who gives, with simplicity; he who leads, with diligence; he who shows mercy, with cheerfulness.

units.la: Pastores intelligit eos qui exhortantur, qui scilicet movendis affectibus operam dant, & facultatem habent, non tantum interpretandi sensum Scripturæ, sed etiam prudenter applicandi Scripturam in usum præsentem auditoris, cum affectus excitatione. Hos jubet exhortationi incumbere.
units.tr: Pastors — he understands those who exhort, namely those who labour to move the affections, and who have the ability not only to interpret the sense of Scripture but also to apply Scripture prudently to the present use of the hearer, with the stirring of the affections. He bids these to devote themselves to exhortation.

units.la: Qui distribuit ] Diaconorum Verbi ministerio subservientium, tres quali species enumerat; Prima est eorum qui distribuunt, id est, ex officio præfecti sunt ærario Ecclesiæ; Ecclesiæ facultates, & collectas fidelium dispensant in usus Ecclesiæ publicos; his præcipit, ut facultates Ecclesiæ distribuant cum simplicitate, id est, bona fide, sine personarum acceptione, & sine respectu proprii commodi.
units.tr: Qui distribuit (He who distributes): this refers to the deacons, who serve the ministry of the Word. He lists three kinds. The first is of those who distribute, that is, who by office are placed in charge of the Church's treasury. They dispense the Church's resources and the collections of the faithful for public church uses. He commands them to distribute the Church's resources "with simplicity," that is, in good faith, without partiality towards persons, and without regard to their own advantage.

units.la: Qui præest ] Secunda species, est eorum qui Presbyteri Gubernatores alibi dicuntur, 1 Corinth. cap. 12. verf 28. & ex officio, populi moribus inspiciendis præficiuntur, ut scandala vitentur, & auferantur ex Ecclesia; his præcipit, ut diligenter, & solicitè, suo muneri incumbant.
units.tr: Qui præest (He who rules): the second kind is of those whom elsewhere he calls elders or governors (1 Corinthians 12:28), and who by office are set over the morals of the people, to watch over them so that offences may be avoided and removed from the Church. He commands them to apply themselves to their duty diligently and carefully.

units.la: Qui miseretur ] Tertia species Diaconorum, est eorum qui ex officio miserentur, qui pauperibus, ægrotis, exulibus, aliisque in Ecclesia afflictis curandis præficiuntur; his præcipit, ut incumbant officio, cum hilaritate; ne morositate suâ amplius affligant eos, quos morbus & egestas, vel exilium, jam afflixerunt. In omnibus his præceptis, functiones diversas, donis diversis, & subjectis diversis, inter se distinxit, alios atque alios ministros, aliis atque aliis operibus præficiens; Idque simili præcipiendi forma utens in omnibus.
units.tr: Qui miseretur (He who shows mercy): the third kind of deacons is of those who by office show mercy, who are appointed to care for the poor, the sick, the exiles and others afflicted in the Church. He commands them to apply themselves to their office with cheerfulness, so that they do not by their own surliness add further affliction to those whom sickness, want or exile have already afflicted. In all these precepts he has distinguished the various functions from one another by their different gifts and different subjects, appointing different ministers to different works, and he uses the same form of command in all of them.

units.la: Tertia Pars.
units.tr: Third Part.

units.la: Vers. 9. Charitas esto minimè simulata. Estote abhorrentes à malo, agglutinati bono.
units.tr: Verse 9. Let love be without hypocrisy. Abhor what is evil; cleave to what is good.

units.la: Tertia pars Capitis, in qua præcipiendi formam mutat, & præcepta tradit de virtutibus Christianis, numero circiter sedecim.
units.tr: The third part of the chapter, in which he changes the form of exhortation and delivers about sixteen precepts on Christian virtues.

units.la: Dilectio ] Præceptum primum, Ut signa, quibus dilectionem exprimimus, ex sincero corde, sine simulatione proveniant.
units.tr: Love] Precept 1: that the signs by which we express love should come from a sincere heart, without pretence.

units.la: Abhorrentes ] Præceptum 2. Ut à malo, seu peccato ita abhorreamus, ut in ejus consortium, trahi nos non permittamus: Bonum verò, seu virtutem ita amplectamur, ut ab ea divelli nos non sinamus.
units.tr: Abhor] Precept 2: that we should so abhor evil or sin as not to let ourselves be drawn into its company, and so embrace good or virtue that we do not let ourselves be torn away from it.

units.la: Verf. 10. Fraterna charitate alij ad alios amandos propensi. Honore alij aliis præcuntes.
units.tr: Verse 10. In brotherly love inclined to one another. In honour going before one another.

units.la: Præceptum 3. Ut Charitas Christianorum inter fe, quæ gratiæ vinculo fundata elt, lit inltar charitatis fratrum, quæ naturæ vinculo fundatur, Conltans scilicet, & intensa.
units.tr: Precept 3: that the love of Christians among themselves, which is founded on the bond of grace, should be like the love of brothers, which is founded on the bond of nature, namely constant and intense.

units.la: Honore ] Præceptum 4. Ut in opinionis nostræ, de alicujus virtute, vel dignitate, per signa externa teftificatione, non expectemus quod debetur nobis, sed præeamus aliis, exhibentes honorem qui debetur illis.
units.tr: Honour] The fourth precept: that in our opinion of someone's virtue or dignity, we should not wait for outward signs of testimony to give us what is owed to us, but should go before others, showing the honour that is due to them.

units.la: Verf. 11. Studio minimè ignavi, Spiritu ferventes, Domino servientes.
units.tr: Verse 11. Not slothful in business, fervent in spirit, serving the Lord.

units.la: Præceptum 5. De sedulitate in officiis, quæ Deo & proximo debentur, ex vocatione nostrâ; ne fimus pigri, segnes, & frigidi, quasi nom curemus res gerendas, sed ut cum intentione zeli, officia obeamus infervore spiritus, occasionem rei bene gerendæ, in ipso articulo opportunitatis, arripientes; & fervorem hunc in rebus agendis, non privatis affectibus nostris, sed Deo consecrantes.
units.tr: Precept 5: concerning diligence in the duties owed to God and neighbour according to our calling; that we not be lazy, sluggish and cold, as if we did not care about the things to be done, but that with the intensity of zeal we perform our duties with fervour of spirit, seizing the opportunity to do something well at the very moment it arises, and dedicating this fervour in our work not to our private affections but to God.

units.la: Verf. 12. Spe gaudentes. In afflictione tolerantes. In oratione perdurantes.
units.tr: Verse 12. Rejoicing in hope. Patient in tribulation. Continuing instant in prayer.

units.la: Præceptum 6. De remediis adhibendis in afflictione nostra: 1. Ut ipe liberationis gloriemur: 2. Si invalescant mala, ut patientes nos præstemus: 3. Si differri videatur auxilium, ut perduremus in precibus, nec malis cedamus.
units.tr: Precept 6: on the remedies to be applied in our affliction: (1) that we glory in the hope of deliverance; (2) if evils grow strong, that we show ourselves patient; (3) if help seems to be delayed, that we persevere in prayers and do not yield to evils.

units.la: Verf. 13. Sanctorum communicantes. Hospitalitatem sectantes.
units.tr: Verse 13. Distributing to the necessity of saints. Given to hospitality.

units.la: Præceptum 7. Ut necessitatibus, & indigentiæ sanctorum, inter nos degentium præcipuè, communicemus de bonis nostris: peregrinorum verò, & exulum, ad nos divertentium afflictiones, hospitalitate ultro illis oblata, sublevemus.
units.tr: Precept 7: that we share our goods with the needs and indigence of the saints living among us, especially; and that we relieve the afflictions of strangers and exiles who turn aside to us, by hospitality freely offered to them.

units.la: Verf. 14. Benedicite iis qui vos insectantur: benedicite, inquam, & ne imprecamini.
units.tr: Verse 14. Bless them which persecute you: bless, I say, and curse not.

units.la: Præceptum 8. Ne infestationes, calumnias, & persecutionem mundi ordinariam, convitiis compensemus, sed patientiâ & benedictione frangamus. Id verò quia carni adversissimum est, bis præcipit, & tertiò prohibet contrarium.
units.tr: Precept 8: that we should not repay the ordinary harassments, slanders and persecutions of the world with reproaches, but overcome them with patience and blessing. Because this is most opposed to the flesh, he commands it twice and forbids the contrary a third time.

units.la: Verf. 15. Gaudete cum gaudentibus, & flete cum flentibus.
units.tr: Verse 15. Rejoice with them that rejoice, and weep with them that weep.

units.la: Præceptum 9. Commendat nobis συμπαθειαν fraternam, in proximorum tam rebus adversis, quam prosperis, sicut decet membra ejusdem corporis.
units.tr: Precept 9: he commends to us brotherly sympathy [συμπαθεια] in our neighbours' adversities as well as their prosperities, as befits members of the same body.

units.la: Verf. 16. Itidem alij in alios affecti. Non alta sapientes, sed humilibus obsecundantes. Ne essote prudentes apud vosmetipsos.
units.tr: Verse 16. Likewise minded one toward another. Mind not high things, but condescend to men of low estate. Be not wise in your own conceits.

units.la: Præceptum 10. Ut colamus invicem concordiam, & toleremus infirmitates ordinarias in discrepantibus sententiis, & affectibus fratrum nostrorum, & in eum finem, ne nos erigamus arroganter, adversus aut supra alios, sed inferioribus obsecundemus, quantum patitur veritas, caventes ne inflati simus unquam opinione sapientiæ propriæ.
units.tr: Precept 10: that we cultivate mutual concord and bear with the ordinary weaknesses in the differing opinions and affections of our brothers; and to this end, that we not lift ourselves up arrogantly against or above others, but yield to those lower than us as far as truth allows, taking care never to be puffed up with the opinion of our own wisdom.

units.la: Verf. 17. Nemini malum pro malo vicissim reddentes. Procurantes honesta coram omnibus hominibus.
units.tr: Verse 17. Recompense to no man evil for evil. Provide things honest in the sight of all men.

units.la: Præceptum 11. Ne injurias injuriis compensemus: & quia exceptiones facere, parata est caro, Dicit, Nemini retaliate.
units.tr: Precept 11: that we not repay injuries with injuries; and because the flesh is ready to make exceptions, he says, Retaliate to no one.

units.la: Præceptum 12. Ut studentes honestati, & vitæ innocentiæ, tam nobilipsis malefaciendi, quam adversariis, nobis nocendi, vel calumnias intentandi ansam præcidamus.
units.tr: Precept 12: that, striving for honesty and innocence of life, we cut off the occasion both for those who would do us evil and for adversaries who would harm us or bring false charges against us.

units.la: Verf. 18. Si fieri potest quantum in vobis est, cum omnibus hominibus in pace viventes.
units.tr: Verse 18. If it be possible, as much as lieth in you, live peaceably with all men.
