units.la: Verf. 9. Salutate Urbanum adjutorem nostrum in Christo, & Stachyn mihi dilectum.
units.tr: Verse 9. Greet Urbanus, our helper in Christ, and Stachys, my beloved.

units.la: Urbanus videtur unus, ex pastoribus Romanæ Ecclesiæ fuisse, & adjutor Apostolici laboris, in Evangelio.
units.tr: Urbanus seems to have been one of the ministers of the Roman Church, and a helper in the Apostolic labour of the Gospel.

units.la: Verf. 10 Salutate Apellen, probatum in Christo. Salutate eos qui sunt ex Aristobuli familiaribus.
units.tr: Verse 10. Greet Apelles, approved in Christ. Greet those who are of the household of Aristobulus.

units.la: Apelleu probatum vocat, quia constantiæ, & fidei suæ, experimenta certa dederat.
units.tr: He calls Apelles approved because he had given certain proof of his constancy and faith.

units.la: Verf. 11. Salutate Herodionem cognatum meum. Salutate eos qui sunt ex Narcissi familiaribus, eos inquam qui sunt in Domino. Aristobulum, & Narcissum non salutat, quia infideles manebant, ut conjicere licet, sed Christianos eorum servos, & domesticos, ut in fide confirmarentur, & in officio erga Dominos suos, licet infideles, permanerent.
units.tr: Verse 11. Greet Herodion, my kinsman. Greet those of the household of Narcissus, who are in the Lord. He does not greet Aristobulus and Narcissus, since, as we may guess, they remained unbelievers. He greets their Christian slaves and servants, so that they might be confirmed in the faith and remain faithful in their duty to their masters, though these were unbelievers.

units.la: Verf. 12. Salutate Tryphænam & Tryphosam, quæ laborant in Domino. Salutate Perfidam mihi dilectam, quæ multùm laboravit in Domino.
units.tr: Verse 12. Greet Tryphaena and Tryphosa, who labour in the Lord. Greet Persis, my beloved, who has laboured much in the Lord.

units.la: Salutat spectatas Matronas quæ ad promovendum Euangelium suas operas studiosè & feliciter commodârant.
units.tr: He greets distinguished matrons who had devoted their efforts diligently and fruitfully to advancing the Gospel.

units.la: Verf. 13 Salutate Rufum selectum in Domino, & matrem ejus ac meam.
units.tr: Verse 13. Greet Rufus, chosen in the Lord, and his mother and mine.

units.la: Salutat Rufum, egregium adolescentem, qui matrem habebat, studiosam Pauli, non minus quam Ruti, filij sui.
units.tr: He greets Rufus, an outstanding young man, whose mother was devoted to Paul, no less than to her own son.

units.la: Verf. 14. Salutate Asyncritum, Phlegontem, Hermanum, Patrobam, Hermen, & qui eis sunt fratres.
units.tr: Verse 14. Greet Asyncritus, Phlegon, Hermas, Patrobas, Hermes, and the brethren who are with them.

units.la: Verf. 15. Salutate Philologum & Juliam, Nereum & sororem ejus, & Olympam, & qui cum iis sunt, Omnes sanctos.
units.tr: Verse 15. Greet Philologus and Julia, Nereus and his sister, and Olympas, and all the saints who are with them.

units.la: Quia insistere non poterat, innumerandis singulis, nominatis aliquot sanctis capitibus, reliquos inter ipsos sanctos, in cumulo salutat.
units.tr: Since he could not go on naming each one, he greets the rest of the saints together in a lump, after naming a few saints by their heads.

units.la: Verf. 16. — Salutate alij alios osculo sancto,
units.tr: Verse 16. Greet one another with a holy kiss.

units.la: Quia iis temporibus, in mutuæ dilectionis signis, erat osculum, sicut nunc nobis est dextrarum conjunctio, jubet ut sine fuco, aut simulatione, sanctè, se mutuo salutent.
units.tr: Since in those times a kiss was a sign of mutual affection, as the joining of right hands is for us now, he orders them to greet one another holily, without deceit or pretence.

units.la: Verf. —15. Salutant vos Ecclesiæ Christi,
units.tr: Verses 15–16. The churches of Christ salute you.

units.la: Salutant ] Secunda pars Capitis; In qua, salutem Romanis impertit Apostolus, Ecclesiarum, inter quas versabatur, nomine, quæ nimirum ipsius propositum scribendi ad Romanos, cognoverunt.
units.tr: Salute. This is the second part of the chapter, in which the Apostle sends greetings to the Romans in the names of the churches among which he was living, who, of course, knew of his purpose of writing to the Romans.

units.la: Verf. 17. Precor autem vos, fratres, ut observetis dissidiorum & offendiculorum autores, contra doctrinam quam vos didicistis: & declinetis ab eis.
units.tr: Verse 17. Now I beseech you, brethren, mark those who cause divisions and offences, contrary to the doctrine which you have learned, and avoid them.

units.la: Intermiscet, quasi in parenthesi, admonitionem de observandis, coercendis, & excommunicandis iis, qui contra doctrinam, aut disciplinam Apostolicam, jam ab iis receptam, ad scindendam Ecclesiam quicquam moverent, & consortium vitare jubet ipsorum, postquam semel ab Ecclesia excommunicati essent.
units.tr: He inserts, as if in parentheses, an admonition about watching over, restraining, and excommunicating those who, against the Apostolic doctrine or discipline already received among them, stir up anything to split the Church. He orders them to avoid their company once they have been excommunicated by the Church.

units.la: Salutant ] Secunda pars Capitis; In qua, salutem Romanis impertit Apostolus.
units.tr: Salute. This is the second part of the chapter, in which the Apostle sends greetings to the Romans.

units.la: Verf. 18. Nam qui ejusmodi sunt, Domino nostro Iesu Christo non serviunt, sed suo ventri: & per blandiloquentiam & assentatio-nem corda hominum minime malorum seducunt.
units.tr: Verse 18. For they that are such serve not our Lord Jesus Christ, but their own belly; and by good words and fair speeches deceive the hearts of the simple.

units.la: Admonitionis, rationes addit quatuor; prima, quia istiusmodi viri, quicunque demum sint, non sunt fervi Dei, sed fervi ventris fui, studentes scilicet rebus mundanis, id est, suis affectibus, & emolumentis, non vero Ecclesiæ utilitati.
units.tr: He adds four reasons for the admonition. The first is that such men, whoever they may be, are not servants of God but servants of their own belly, that is, they are intent on worldly things, on their own passions and advantages, and not on the good of the Church.

units.la: Ratio 2. Quia nisi observarentur à prudentioribus, facile decepturi effent fimpliciores, fucatis suis dictis, atque ita Ecclesiam scissuri.
units.tr: The second reason: unless they were watched over by the more prudent, they would easily deceive the simpler sort with their disguised words, and so split the Church.

units.la: Verf. 19. Vestra enim obedientia ad omnes pervenit. Gaudeo itaque quòd ad vos attinet: sed volo vos sapientes quidem esse ad id quod bonum est, simplices verò ad malum.
units.tr: For your obedience has come to all men. I rejoice therefore over you; but I want you to be wise as to what is good, and simple as to evil.

units.la: Tertia ratio: quia periculum erat, ne Romanorum laudabilis, & nota facilitas, ad credendum prædicatoribus, quibuslibet impofturis exponeretur, nisi caverent; nempe, nisi simplicitatem illam temperarent prudentia; simplicitatem colentes tantum in nocendi artibus, in aliis verò prudentiæ studentes, ne iis noceret aliorum astutia.
units.tr: The third reason: there was a danger that the Romans' praiseworthy and well-known readiness to believe preachers would expose them to every sort of deception, unless they took care. That is, unless they tempered that simplicity with prudence, cultivating simplicity only in the arts of not doing harm, but in other matters pursuing prudence, so that the cunning of others would not harm them.

units.la: Verf. 20. Porrò Deus pacis conteret Satanam sub pedes vestros cito. Gratia Domini nostri Iesu Christi sit vobiscum Amen.
units.tr: And the God of peace shall bruise Satan under your feet shortly. The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you. Amen.

units.la: Quarta ratio, Quia etsi pugnandum illis esset cum Satana, turbarum authore, Deus tamen pacis daturus illis fuit victoriam, ubi paululum in pugna sese opposuerint turbatoribus illis, quod argumentum claudit Apostolica benedictione.
units.tr: The fourth reason: even if they had to fight with Satan, the author of disturbances, God, the giver of peace, would nevertheless grant them victory, once they had set themselves somewhat against those disturbers in the struggle. Paul closes this argument with the apostolic blessing.

units.la: Verf. 21. Salutant vos Timotheus adjutor meus, & Lucius, & Iafon, & Sofipater, cognati mei.
units.tr: Timothy my fellow-worker salutes you, and Lucius, and Jason, and Sosipater, my kinsmen.

units.la: Absoluta parenthesi, salutationes aliorum sanctorum apud se ad Romanos superaddit; quorum primus est Timotheus Euangelista, post hunc Lucius qui est (ut videtur) ille Cyrenæus, Act. 13. 1. Iafon est de quo Act. 17. 5. Sofipater, de quo Act. 20. 4.
units.tr: With the parenthesis finished, he adds to the Romans the greetings of other saints who are with him. The first of these is Timothy the evangelist; after him comes Lucius, who is (as seems likely) that Cyrenian of Acts 13:1. Jason is the one of Acts 17:5. Sosipater is the one of Acts 20:4.

units.la: Verf. 22. Saluto vos in Domino, ego Tertius, qui descripsi epistolam.
units.tr: I, Tertius, who wrote this epistle, salute you in the Lord.

units.la: Tertius, amanuensis Pauli, qui descripsit hanc Epistolam, in honorem ministerii hujus, hanc fui commemorationem, a Spiritu sancto, quasi in compensationem fidelitatis, accipit.
units.tr: Tertius, Paul's amanuensis, who wrote out this Epistle, received this mention from the Holy Spirit in honour of this ministry, as a reward, so to speak, for his faithfulness.

units.la: Verf. 23. Salutat vos Gaius hospes meus & Ecclesia totius. Salutat vos Erastus procurator urbis, & Quartus frater.
units.tr: Gaius, my host and the host of the whole Church, salutes you. Erastus, the treasurer of the city, salutes you, and Quartus the brother.

units.la: Verf. 24 Gratia Domini nostri Iesu Christi, sit cum omnibus vobis, Amen.
units.tr: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you all. Amen.

units.la: Gaius de quo Act. 20. 4. & 1. Cor. 1. 14. se Romanis commendatum habet, interim à Paulo commendatus, quod non solum Paulum hospitio exceperit, sed etiam toti Ecclesiæ domicilium, in quod ad sacra convenirent, ministrabat.
units.tr: Gaius, of whom Acts 20:4 and 1 Cor. 1:14, commends himself to the Romans, and is commended by Paul, because he not only received Paul as a guest but also provided a home for the whole Church, in which they might gather for the sacred assemblies.

units.la: Erastus, quæstor ærarius civitatis Corinthiacæ, cui additur frater nomine Quartus; has salutationes claudit repetito voto Apostolico.
units.tr: Erastus, the public treasurer of the city of Corinth, to whom is added the brother Quartus; with these greetings he closes, repeating the apostolic wish.

units.la: Verf. 25. Ei vero qui potest vos stabilire, secundum Euangelium meum & praeconium Iesu Christi, ex patefactione mysterij quod à temporibus seculorum tacitum fuit:
units.tr: Now to him who is able to establish you according to my gospel and the preaching of Jesus Christ, according to the revelation of the mystery which has been kept secret since the beginning of the ages.

units.la: Versibus tribus ultimis, celeberrimam hanc Epistolam, solenni doxologia claudit, in qua, fidem certitudinemque salutis Romanorum confirmat, adversus metum omnem, quem pericula, persecutiones, impostores, schismatici, sive ipsorum imbecillitas, sive tentationes quæcunque aliæ, ipsis creare potuissent: idque propter Dei potentiam, & benevolentiam, quas Deus per Euangelium in hac Epistola descriptum, tanquam brachia sua pro ipsorum salute extendebat.
units.tr: In the last three verses he closes this most celebrated Epistle with a solemn doxology, in which he confirms the faith and the assurance of salvation of the Romans against every fear that persecutions, dangers, impostors, schismatics, their own weakness, or any other temptations could have created for them. He does this on account of God's power and goodwill, which God extended, as his own arms, for their salvation through the Gospel described in this Epistle.

units.la: Simul etiam Euangelium suum commendat, sextuplici nomine: 1. Quia est praeconium Iesu Christi: 2. Quia est revelatio gratiæ Dei, prius celatæ; nam licet Gratia patribus significata fuerit, comparatione tamen praesentis lucis, quæ per Apostolorum doctrinam mundo affulserat, tacita & abscondita dici potuit.
units.tr: At the same time he commends his Gospel under six headings: 1. because it is the preaching of Jesus Christ; 2. because it is the revelation of the grace of God, previously hidden. For although grace was indicated to the fathers, yet compared with the present light, which had shone upon the world through the teaching of the Apostles, it can be called hidden and concealed.

units.la: Verf. 26. Nunc vero factum est manifestum, & per Scripturas propheticas, ex imperio æterni Dei ad obedientiam fidei, omnibus Gentibus innotuit.
units.tr: But now it is made manifest, and by the prophetic Scriptures, according to the command of the eternal God, has been made known to all nations for the obedience of faith.

units.la: Verf. 27. Soli, inquam, sapienti Deo, gloria per Iesum Christum in secula. Amen.
units.tr: To the only wise God, be glory through Jesus Christ for ever. Amen.

units.la: 3. Quia hoc Euangelium, congruit cum Scriptura veteri, & ex ea confirmatur, 4 Quia habet Dei imperium, & ordinationem pro authoritate: 5. Quia non continetur, sicut vetus Scriptura, angustis finibus Judæx, & unius populi, sed splendet ad usum omnium gentium: 6. Quia ad fidei obedientiam tendit, id est, ut audientes, adducti ad fidem Christi, reddantur obedientes subditi regni Gratiæ ejus: simul Deo gloriam horum omnium tribuit ut soli, in se, & à se sapienti, qui nullisapientiam suam debet: Ipsi per Christum sit gloria in secula seculorum. AMEN.
units.tr: 3. because this Gospel agrees with the old Scripture and is confirmed by it; 4. because it has the command and ordinance of God as its authority; 5. because it is not confined, as the old Scripture was, within the narrow limits of Judea and of one people, but shines for the use of all nations; 6. because it aims at the obedience of faith, that is, that those who hear, being brought to faith in Christ, may be made obedient subjects of his kingdom of grace. At the same time he ascribes the glory of all these things to God alone, the wise God who is wise in himself and from himself and owes his wisdom to no one. To him, through Christ, be glory for ever and ever. Amen.

units.la: Quintus articulus, de prudentia in matrimonij, & calibatus, & secularium vocationum casibus adhibenda, Cap. septimo.
units.tr: The fifth article, on the prudence to be employed in the cases of marriage, celibacy, and secular callings, chapter seven.

units.la: Sextus articulus, de Idolothytis vitandis, Cap. octavo, nono, decimo.
units.tr: The sixth article, on avoiding idol-meats, chapters eight, nine and ten.

units.la: Septimus articulus, de ordine, & decoro, in publico DEI cultu, maximè in Cœna Domini, observanda, Cap. undecimo.
units.tr: The seventh article, on the order and decorum to be observed in the public worship of God, especially at the Lord's Supper, chapter eleven.

units.la: Octavus articulus, de recto spiritualium bonorum usu, Cap. 12, 13, 14.
units.tr: The eighth article, on the right use of spiritual goods, chapters 12, 13 and 14.

units.la: Nonus articulus, de resurrectionis futuræ certitudine, quam, aliqui inter ipsos, in dubium vocabant, Cap. decimoquinto.
units.tr: The ninth article, on the certainty of the future resurrection, which some among them were calling into doubt, chapter fifteen.

units.la: Decimus articulus, de Eleemosyna in usum Sanctorum in Judæa colligendâ, Cap. decimosexto.
units.tr: The tenth article, on collecting alms for the use of the saints in Judea, chapter sixteen.

units.la: Caput primum, de Schismate sanando.
units.tr: Chapter 1, on healing the schism.

units.la: CApitis tres sunt partes; Prima, est proœmium totius Epistolæ, ad versum decimum.
units.tr: The chapter has three parts. The first is the preface to the whole Epistle, up to verse 10.

units.la: Secunda, est inchoata dissuasio à schismate, quo laborabant Corinthii, propositis, in eum finem, quinque argumentis, ad vers. 17
units.tr: The second is the opening dissuasion from the schism by which the Corinthians were troubled. To this end he sets out five arguments, up to verse 17.

units.la: Tertia, est illustratio, & confirmatio quinti argumenti, ad finem.
units.tr: The third is the illustration and confirmation of the fifth argument, to the end.

units.la: Totum proœmium comparatur, ad præparandos animos Corinthiorum, ut promptam obedientiam doctrinæ, & admonitionibus Apostoli præstent: Et hoc, vel simili, in eundem sensum, axiomate, poterit proœmii scopus concipi: Debetis vos Corinthii, doctrinæ meæ, & monitis meis, submissâ, & promptâ voluntate obtemperare, seu fidem habere, & obedientiam præstare.
units.tr: The whole preface is designed to prepare the minds of the Corinthians to render prompt obedience to his teaching and admonitions. The purpose of the preface may be expressed by this axiom, or one like it to the same effect: "You Corinthians ought to obey my teaching and my admonitions with a submissive and willing mind, that is, to give them credence and render obedience."

units.la: Argumenta in hunc finem insinuantur undecim, quorum alia Apostoli authoritatem magis, alia benevolum ipsius in Corinthios animum, magis exprimunt.
units.tr: Eleven arguments are put forward to this end. Some of them bring out the apostle's authority more, others his good will towards the Corinthians.

units.la: Vers. 1. Paulus vocatione Apostolus Iesu Christi, per voluntatem Dei: & Sosthenes frater.
units.tr: Verse 1. Paul, called to be an apostle of Jesus Christ by the will of God, and Sosthenes the brother.

units.la: Apostolus ] Argumentum primum, Ego Paulus, qui hæc ad vos scribo, vocatione sum Apostolus IESU CHRISTI: Ergo debetis doctrinæ meæ, & monitis fidem habere, & obedire.
units.tr: Apostle: the first argument. "I, Paul, who write these things to you, am an apostle of Jesus Christ by calling. Therefore you ought to believe and obey my teaching and admonitions."

units.la: Per voluntatem Dei ] Arg. 2. Speciali DEI voluntate, & mandato, non usurpatione meâ, ut legatione fungor, ita hæc ad vos scribo: Ergo, nisi DEI voluntati refragari velitis, debetis monenti, & docenti mihi obtemperare. Sosthenes Adjunxi mihi admonitionis hujus testem, Sosthenem fratrem, (de quo Act. cap. 18. verf. 17) ut, sub duobus testibus, testimonium hoc sanciatur. Ergo debetis, monenti & docenti mihi obtemperare, nisi utriusque testimonium, adversus vos stare velitis.
units.tr: By the will of God: the second argument. By the special will and command of God, and not by my own presumption, I perform the office of an envoy, and so I write these things to you. Therefore, unless you wish to resist the will of God, you ought to obey me as I admonish and teach. Sosthenes: I have joined with me Sosthenes the brother as a witness to this admonition (of whom see Acts 18:17), so that this testimony may be confirmed by two witnesses. Therefore you ought to obey me as I admonish and teach, unless you wish to set yourselves against the testimony of both.

units.la: Ecclesiæ Dei quæ est Corinthi, sanctificatus in Christo Iesu, id est, vocatus sanctus, cum omnibus qui invocant nomen Domini nostri Iesu Christi, quovis loco, Domini, inquam, tum ipsorum, tum nostri.
units.tr: To the church of God which is at Corinth, to those sanctified in Christ Jesus, that is, called to be saints, with all who call upon the name of our Lord Jesus Christ in every place, of the Lord, I say, both theirs and ours.

units.la: In descriptione eorum, ad quos scribit; Vos estis Ecclesia Dei, evocati ex mundo, consecrati Deo, asciti in communionem cum Christo, vocati ad sanctimoniam à Deo. Ergo, mihi docenti, & monenti ea, quæ ad sanctimoniam faciunt, si privilegiis vestris digni haberi vultis, debetis auscultare, & obtemperare.
units.tr: In the description of those to whom he writes: "You are the church of God, called out of the world, consecrated to God, admitted into fellowship with Christ, called by God to holiness." Therefore, if you wish to be deemed worthy of your privileges, you ought to listen to me, who teach and admonish you in those things which promote holiness, and obey.

units.la: Cum omnibus qui invocant Extenditur Apostolatus mei, & doctrinæ hujus authoritas, usus, & fructus, non tantum ad vos, sed etiam ad universam Dei Ecclesiam, omnesque Sanctos, qui adorant Iesum Christum, verum Deum, & Dominum nostrum: Ergo debetis doctrinæ, & monitis meis auscultare, & obedire.
units.tr: With all who call upon: the authority, use and fruit of my apostleship and of this teaching is extended not only to you but also to the whole church of God and to all the saints who worship Jesus Christ, the true God and our Lord. Therefore you ought to listen to my teaching and admonitions and obey them.

units.la: Verf. 3. Gratia vobis & pax a Deo Patre nostro, & Domino Iesu Christo.
units.tr: Verse 3. Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.

units.la: In salutatione, est Vos eos agnosco, quibus, una cum reliquis Sanctis, quovis loco degentibus, pro authoritate mihi concessa, licet Evangelii benedictionem applicare, & vobis gratiam & pacem; id est, omnia quæ ad virtutem, & gloriam: quæ ad sanctitatem, & felicitatem faciunt, comprecari, ut certiores de favore Dei per me redditi, eadem, a Deo per Mediatorem Christum, firmiori fide expectetis. Ergo debetis, alacriter doctrinæ meæ, & monitis auscultare.
units.tr: In the greeting, the meaning is: "I acknowledge you, to whom, together with the rest of the saints dwelling in every place, by the authority granted to me, I may apply the blessing of the Gospel, and wish you grace and peace, that is, all things which tend to virtue and glory, to holiness and happiness, so that, having been informed by me of the favour of God, you may await the same from God through the Mediator Christ with a firmer faith." Therefore you ought to listen eagerly to my teaching and admonitions.

units.la: Verf. 4. Gratias ago Deo meo semper de vobis, ob gratiam Dei quæ data est vobis in Christo Iesu: Verf. 5. Quod in omnibus in ipso ditati estis, omni loquendi facultate, omnique notitia:
units.tr: Verse 4. I give thanks to my God always for you, for the grace of God which was given to you in Christ Jesus. Verse 5. That in everything you were enriched in him, in all speech and in all knowledge.

units.la: Reliquis proœmii versibus, quia multa erat reprehensurus vitia in Corinthiis, commendat quod in iis bonum est, confirmat fidem ipsorum in Deum, ne acrius correpti labascerent, & suam de iis existimationem, & ergà eos benevolentiam, interea exprimit, quo finem sibi propositum, melius assequeretur. Arg. 7. Non invideo vobis, sed gratulor potius, & Deo gratias jugiter ago, de opulenta, reconciliationis potissimum gratia, vobis per Christum concessa, verf. 4. gratulor vobis, abundantiam Spiritualium donorum Ecclesiasticorum, ad cognitionem, & praedicationem Evangelii spectantium, verf 5. Ergo debetis, mihi de recto gratiae & donorum usu monenti, prompte obedire.
units.tr: In the remaining verses of the preface, since he was about to rebuke many faults in the Corinthians, he commends what is good in them and confirms their faith in God, so that they would not waver if they were sharply reproved. Meanwhile he expresses his esteem for them and his goodwill towards them, so that he may the better attain the end he has set himself. Argument 7: I do not envy you, but rather I rejoice, and I continually give thanks to God for the rich grace of reconciliation, above all, granted to you through Christ. Verse 4: I rejoice with you at the abundance of the spiritual gifts of the church, which concern the knowledge and preaching of the Gospel. Verse 5: Therefore you ought to obey promptly me, who admonish you about the right use of grace and gifts.

units.la: Verf. 6. Prout testimonium Christi confirmatum fuit in vobis.
units.tr: Verse 6. Even as the testimony of Christ was confirmed in you.

units.la: Arg. 8. In confirmationem testimonii nostri, & fidei vestrae, de hac Evangelio Christi, data sunt vobis ea dona: Ergo debetis, mihi salutaria docenti, & monenti, ab eodem authore Christo, fidem adhibere, & obedire, ut Spiritus sancti donis amplius abundetis.
units.tr: Argument 8: These gifts were given to you in confirmation of our testimony and of your faith concerning this Gospel of Christ. Therefore you ought to give credence to and obey me, who teach and admonish you in what is salutary, with the same Christ as the author, so that you may abound more in the gifts of the Holy Spirit.

units.la: Verf. 7. Adeo ut nullo dono deficiamini, expectantes donec patefiat Dominus noster Iesus Christus:
units.tr: Verse 7. So that you come short in no gift, waiting for the revealing of our Lord Jesus Christ.

units.la: Arg. 9. Donorum Ecclesiasticorum, & Spiritualium nullum genus vobis deest, quod viatoribus necessarium est, verumtamen nondum perfecti estis, sed plenitudo est expectanda in adventu Christi. Ergo ut laeti Christum ad judicium venientem excipiatis, mihi docenti, & monenti ea, quae vestram perfectionem promovere poterint, fidem habere, & obedire debetis.
units.tr: Argument 9: No kind of ecclesiastical and spiritual gift is lacking to you which is necessary for wayfarers. Nevertheless you are not yet perfect, but the fullness is to be awaited at the coming of Christ. Therefore, that you may joyfully receive Christ coming to judgement, you ought to believe and obey me, who teach and admonish you in those things which can promote your perfection.

units.la: Verf. 8. Qui Deus etiam confirmabit vos usque ad finem inculpatos, in diem Domini nostri Iesu Christi.
units.tr: Verse 8. Who will also confirm you to the end, blameless, in the day of our Lord Jesus Christ.

units.la: Arg. 10. Persuasum habeo, (de Electis loquor, quales me vos, ex charitate aestimare, aequum est) confirmaturum vos Christum, & effecturum, ut perseveretis in gratia, & purgaturum vos ab omni labe, ut tandem sine macula omni, coram Deo sistamini: Ergo mihi docenti, & monenti, in eum ipsum finem, debetis fidem habere, & obedire.
units.tr: Argument 10: I am persuaded (I speak of the elect, such as it is right for me to judge you to be out of charity) that Christ will confirm you and bring it about that you persevere in grace, and will cleanse you from every stain, so that at last you may stand before God without any spot. Therefore you ought to believe and obey me, who teach and admonish you to this very end.

units.la: Verf. 9. Fidelis est Deus, per quem vocati estis, ad communionem Filij ipsius Iesu Christi Domini nostri.
units.tr: Verse 9. God is faithful, by whom you were called into the fellowship of his Son Jesus Christ our Lord.

units.la: Arg. 11. Confirmans superius: Vocatio vestri efficax, in communionem cum Christo, quod donum est stabile, & salutiferum, simul & fidelitas Dei (qui perseverantiam, & confirmationem, in eum finem, promisit efficaciter vocatis vobis, in communionem Filii sui) persuasionis hujus meae de vobis, pignora sunt. Ergo ut expectationi meæ, & vocationi vestræ respondeatis, debetis mihi docenti, & monenti, fidem habere & obtemperare.
units.tr: Argument 11: confirming what has gone before. Your effectual calling into communion with Christ, which is a stable and saving gift, and at the same time the faithfulness of God (who has promised perseverance and confirmation, to this end, to you who are effectually called into communion with his Son), are the pledges of my persuasion concerning you. Therefore, that you may answer to my expectation and to your calling, you ought to believe and obey me, who teach and admonish you.

units.la: Secunda Pars.
units.tr: Second Part.

units.la: Verf. 10. Rogo autem vos, fratres, per nomen Domini nostri Iesu Christi, ut idem loquamini omnes, & non sint inter vos dissidia, sed sitis coagmentati eadem mente & eadem sententia.
units.tr: Verse 10. Now I beseech you, brethren, by the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that you all speak the same thing, and that there be no divisions among you, but that you be joined together in the same mind and the same judgment.

units.la: Secunda pars Capitis, in qua, revocare eos studet à schismate, hortando, ut si charus ipsis esset Christus, omisso partium studio, unitatem colant, in doctrina, & docendi modo, utque in eum finem, studio seu affectibus, & sententiis, seu intelligentia sanæ doctrinæ coagmententur.
units.tr: The second part of the chapter, in which he seeks to call them back from schism by exhorting them that, if Christ is dear to them, they should set aside partisan zeal and cultivate unity in doctrine and in the manner of teaching, and that to this end they should be joined together in affection and opinion, or rather in understanding of sound doctrine.

units.la: Verf. 11. Declaratum est enim mihi de vobis, fratres mei, à domesticis Chloes, quod lites sint inter vos.
units.tr: Verse 11. For it has been declared to me concerning you, my brethren, by those of Chloe's household, that there are contentions among you.

units.la: Ne, sine causa hortari videatur, indicat se de ipsorum schismate audivisse, à fide dignis authoribus.
units.tr: Lest he seem to exhort without cause, he indicates that he heard of their schism from trustworthy authors.

units.la: Verf. 12. Hoc autem dico, singulos vestrum dicere, Ego quidem sum Pauli: ego autem Apollo: ego vero Cephæ: ego vero CHRISTI.
units.tr: Verse 12. Now this I say, that each one of you says: I indeed am of Paul; but I of Apollos; but I of Cephas; but I of Christ.

units.la: Schisma jam attingitur: De doctoribus suis contendebant, præferentes alios aliis, quasi perfectiores; seque ab iis denominantes, cum æmulatione, & contemptu mutuo: Quos doctores non nominat, sed tacendo delinit Schismaticorum animos, ut facilius schisma sopiretur: & quasi exempli causa, nominat se, & Apollo, & Cephas, licet ex reliqua, & sequenti etiam epistola, planum fit, vaniloquos ipsorum doctores, schismatis authores, & fautores fuisse, qui ipsum etiam Paulum, apud Corinthios, in fastidium induxerant, eo usque, ut vix locum suum apud eos tenere potuerit, tantum abfuit, ut à Paulo se denominarent.
units.tr: Schism is now addressed. They were contending over their teachers, preferring some to others as more perfect, and naming themselves after them with rivalry and mutual contempt. He does not name these teachers, but by his silence he soothes the minds of the schismatics so that the schism may more easily be quieted. As an example he names himself, Apollos, and Cephas. Yet it becomes plain from the rest of this letter and from the following one that their boastful teachers, the authors and promoters of the schism, had even brought Paul himself among the Corinthians into disfavour, to such an extent that he could scarcely keep his place among them. So far was it from being the case that they named themselves after Paul.

units.la: Verf. 13. Num dispertitus est Christus? num Paulus crucifixus? est pro vobis? aut in nomen Pauli baptizati fuistis?
units.tr: Verse 13. Is Christ divided? Was Paul crucified for you? Or were you baptized in the name of Paul?

units.la: Curandum hoc schisma, & tollendum, jam contendit: Argumenta dehortationis & reprehensionis, sunt quinque.
units.tr: He now sets out to deal with this schism and remove it. The arguments of dissuasion and rebuke are five.

units.la: Argumentum primum, Schismate hoc, laceratur Christi corpus mysticum, & unitas ipsius discerpitur in tot partes, quot sunt sectæ: Schisma curandum est, & tollendum igitur. Arg. 2. Nemo ex doctoribus vestris, morte, sibi comparavit Ecclesiam: Ergo nulli hic honos debetur, ut ab eo denominetur Ecclesia, & propter eum scindatur in partes.
units.tr: The first argument: by this schism the mystical body of Christ is torn, and its unity is rent into as many parts as there are sects. This schism must therefore be dealt with and removed. Argument 2: No one of your teachers has purchased the Church for himself by his death. Therefore no honour is due to any of them, such that the Church should be named after him and split into parts on his account.

units.la: Arg. 3. In nomen nullius doctoris baptizati eratis, ut ab eo denominationem sumeretis: Ergo in gratiam doctorum, non estis in partes scindendi.
units.tr: Argument 3: You were not baptized into the name of any teacher, so as to take your name from him. Therefore you ought not to be divided into parts for the sake of teachers.

units.la: Vers. 14. Gratias ago Deo meo quod neminem vestrum baptizavi, nisi Chrispum & Gaium:
units.tr: Verse 14. I thank God that I baptized none of you, except Crispus and Gaius;

units.la: Vers. 15. Ut ne quis dicat me in meum nomen baptizasse.
units.tr: Verse 15. Lest anyone should say that I baptized in my own name.

units.la: Vers. 16. Baptizavi autem etiam Stephanæ familiam: cæterum haud scio num quem alium baptizaverim.
units.tr: Verse 16. And I baptized also the household of Stephanas; besides, I do not know whether I baptized any other.

units.la: Arg. 4. Improbandi sunt schismatici inter vos doctores, qui promiscuè multos baptizare affectando, discipulos aliis ereptos sibi studeant vendicare, quasi in suum nomen baptizarent, & quod Deus sua providentia mea opera ad paucos baptizandum utens, ab hujus mali suspicione, me liberaverit, Gratias ei ago. Ergo in gratiam doctorum non estis in partes scindendi.
units.tr: Argument 4: The schismatic teachers among you are to be condemned. Eager to baptize many indiscriminately, they seek to claim as their own the disciples taken from others, as if they were baptizing into their own name. God, using my labour through his providence, has freed me from the suspicion of this evil, and for this I give thanks to him. Therefore, for the sake of the teachers, you are not to be divided into parts.

units.la: Vers. 17. Non enim misit me Christus, ut baptizarem, sed ut evangelizarem: non tamen cum dicendi peritia,
units.tr: Verse 17. For Christ did not send me to baptize, but to preach the gospel; yet not with wisdom of speech,

units.la: Addit aliam causam, paucorum à se baptizatorum, quia muneris sibi demandati partes præcipuas studebat obire, id est, prædicando, alios post alios convertere, conversos baptizandi curam aliis committens, ne ipse distraheretur; quia non ad baptizandum, scilicet præcipuè sive cum prædicationis impedimento, misErat eum Christus, sed præcipuè ad prædicandum Evangelium.
units.tr: He adds another reason for his baptizing so few people: he was eager to discharge the principal part of the task entrusted to him, that is, preaching, and so converting one after another, while committing the care of baptizing the converts to others, so that he himself would not be distracted. For Christ sent him not chiefly to baptize, that is, with the hindrance of preaching, but chiefly to preach the gospel.

units.la: Arg. 5. Schismatici illi doctores vestri, qui speciosa sua eloquentia, post se discipulos trahere studeant, non imitantur exemplum meum in spirituali docendi modo; Ego enim non cum dicendi peritia, non in sapienti sermone, non in sermonis elegantia, & ingenii acumine, compositâ oratione: (sicut ex præceptis oratoriæ fieri præscribitur) sed in sermone plano, & simplici, ad ædificationem comparato, ex Domini nostri sententia prædicabam. Ergo, ob vanam istiusmodi doctorum eloquentiam, non scindenda erat Ecclesia vestra in partes.
units.tr: Argument 5: Those schismatic teachers of yours, who seek to draw disciples after themselves by their showy eloquence, do not imitate my example in the spiritual manner of teaching. For I did not preach with skill in speaking, nor in wise speech, nor in elegance of language and keenness of wit, with a composed oration, as the precepts of rhetoric prescribe. Rather, according to the saying of our Lord, I preached in plain and simple speech, fitted to edification. Therefore, because of the vain eloquence of such teachers, your Church ought not to be split into parts.

units.la: Vers. 17. Ne inanis reddatur crux Christi.
units.tr: Verse 17. That the cross of Christ not be made void.

units.la: Tertia pars Capitis, in qua confirmat factum suum in prædicandi modo, & simul officium suum, nempe non prædicandum fuisse ipsi, cum dicendi peritia, sed in simplicitate veritatis, ad omnium auditorum captum, & ædificationem scilicet: non ad aures aliquorum demulcendas; & probat, non mirandum esse quod Christus ipsum miserit ad prædicandum Euangelium, non cum dicendi peritia: Argumenta in hunc finem affert duodecim hoc capite, plura additurus capite sequenti.
units.tr: The third part of the chapter, in which he confirms his action in the manner of preaching and at the same time his duty: namely, that he ought not to preach with skill in speaking, but in the simplicity of truth, suited to the grasp and edification of all his hearers, and not to tickle the ears of some. He proves that it is not to be wondered at that Christ sent him to preach the gospel without skill in speaking. He brings twelve arguments to this end in this chapter, and will add more in the next.

units.la: Arg. 1. est ab affectu contrarii: Si ornate, ad regulas eloquentiæ, compositum sermonem meum, in prædicando, inanis reddita fuisset crux Christi, vel (ut est cap. 2. 5.) fides auditorum meorum, constitisset in sapientia hominum potius, quam in potentia Dei, id est, simplex & humilis doctrina, de humiliatione Christi usque ad crucem, spoliata fuisset gloria conversionis hominum; & humana eloquentia, ea gloriâ coronata fuisset. Ergo, non mirum, quod Christus me miserit ad euangelizandum, non cum dicendi peritia.
units.tr: Argument 1 is from the contrary effect: if my sermon in preaching had been composed elegantly according to the rules of eloquence, the cross of Christ would have been made void, or (as in chap. 2. 5.) the faith of my hearers would have rested on the wisdom of men rather than on the power of God. That is, the simple and humble doctrine of the humiliation of Christ unto the cross would have been robbed of the glory of converting men, and human eloquence would have been crowned with that glory. Therefore it is no wonder that Christ sent me to preach the gospel not with skill in speaking.

units.la: Verf. 18. Nam sermo ille de cruce, iis quidem qui pereunt, stultitia est: iis autem qui servantur, id est, nobis potentia Dei est.
units.tr: Verse 18. For the word of the cross is indeed foolishness to those who perish, but to us who are being saved it is the power of God.

units.la: Respondendo objectioni, subjicit arg. 2. Diceret aliquis; At, doctrina crucis reddetur contemptibilis, & ludibrio tanquam stultitia exponetur, si nullo sapientiæ splendore se fecerit commendabilem: Respondet verum esse illud apud reprobos, & in perditionis via manentes, non vero apud Electos, & Conversos: qui humilem prædicationem magni æstimant, & comperiunt eam Dei organum efficax ad salutem: Hinc argumentum, cur simplici oratione, & non operoso artificio, in prædicando, usus fuerit Apostolus. Simplici hac prædicationis ratione Deus solet potenter convertere, & promovere Electos ad salutem. Ergo non mirum, quod Christus me miserit ad euangelizandum, non cum dicendi peritia.
units.tr: Answering an objection, he adds argument 2. Someone might say: but the doctrine of the cross will be made contemptible and exposed to mockery as foolishness if it does not commend itself by some splendour of wisdom. He answers that this is true among the reprobate, who remain on the road to perdition, but not among the elect and the converted, who esteem humble preaching highly and find it an effective instrument of God for salvation. Hence the argument for why the Apostle used plain speech, and not laborious artifice, in preaching: by this simple manner of preaching God is accustomed to convert powerfully and to advance the elect to salvation. Therefore it is no wonder that Christ sent me to preach the gospel not with skill in speaking.

units.la: Verf. 19. Scriptum est enim, Abolebo sapientiam sapientum, & intelligentiam intelligentium tollam è medio.
units.tr: Verse 19. For it is written: I will destroy the wisdom of the wise, and will bring to nothing the understanding of the prudent.

units.la: Arg. 3. Deus maledicturus est sapientulis illis, qui despicientes veritatis divinæ simplicitatem, in ejus locum, surrogare audent suam sapientiam, in prædicatione Euangelii: quod probat testimonio Isaiæ, cap. 29. verf 14. Ubi Deus, studiosis verborum in Dei cultu, & non studentibus potentiam & vim pietatis, ad internam sanctificationem obtinere internere interminatur se conversurum ipsorum sapientiam in fatuitatem: Ergo, non mirum, quod Christus me miserit ad euangelizandum, non cum dicendi peritia.
units.tr: Argument 3: God will curse those little-wise men who, despising the simplicity of divine truth, dare to put their own wisdom in its place in preaching the gospel. He proves this by the testimony of Isaiah, chap. 29, verse 14, where God threatens that he will turn into foolishness the wisdom of those who are zealous for words in the worship of God, and who do not strive for the power and force of godliness in order to obtain inward sanctification. Therefore it is no wonder that Christ sent me to preach the gospel not with skill in speaking.

units.la: Verf. 20. Ubi sapiens? ubi Scriba? ubi disquisitor seculi istius? nonne infatuavit Deus sapientiam hujus mundi?
units.tr: Verse 20. Where is the wise? Where is the scribe? Where is the disputer of this age? Has not God made foolish the wisdom of this world?

units.la: Arg. 4. Ab experientia: Quia Deus, in Ecclesiæ suæ collectione, & operas, & personas sapientissimorum inter Judæos, & Gentes, contemplerit, sinendo politicorum, seu sapientum Scribarum, seu Legis interpretum, disputatorum hujus seculi, seu Philosophorum maximam partem, ire vias suas: Nam fere totam multitudinem hujus seculi sapientum, extra pomœria suæ Ecclesiæ, seu regni Cœlorum, cum sapientia sua seculari, & doctrinis suis, ut stultos, in cœno, & sordibus volutari permisit. In hoc argumento proferendo, alludit Apostolus ad oraculum Isaiæ, cap. 29. verf. 14. Nam si ubi sint sapientes, &c. Quæras? In Ecclesia non comparent, nam sapientia ipsorum, quia separata est à vera cognitione miseriæ suæ, & unici remedii in Christo, stultitia est: Argumenti vis hæc est, In Ecclesiæ collectione, & ædificatione, nec adhibuit Deus sapientes hujus mundi, nec ipsorum eloquentiam. Ergo, non mirum quod Christus me miserit ad euangelizandum, non cum dicendi peritia.
units.tr: Argument 4 is from experience. God, in the gathering of his Church, has passed over both the works and the persons of the most wise among Jews and Gentiles, allowing for the most part the politicians (whether the wise scribes, the interpreters of the Law, the disputers of this age, or the philosophers) to go their own ways. For he has permitted almost the whole multitude of the wise of this age, outside the bounds of his Church or the kingdom of heaven, with their worldly wisdom and their doctrines, to wallow in the mire and filth as fools. In bringing forward this argument the Apostle alludes to the oracle of Isaiah, chap. 29, verse 14. For where are the wise, etc.? Would you ask? They do not appear in the Church, for their wisdom, since it is separated from true knowledge of their misery and of the one remedy in Christ, is foolishness. The force of the argument is this: in the gathering and building up of the Church, God has employed neither the wise men of this world nor their eloquence. Therefore it is no wonder that Christ sent me to preach the gospel not with skill in speaking.

units.la: Verf. 21. Nam postquam in Dei sapientia mundus non cognovit Deum per eam sapientiam, placuit Deo per stultitiam prædicationis servare credentes.
units.tr: Verse 21. For since, in the wisdom of God, the world did not know God through that wisdom, it pleased God through the foolishness of the preaching to save those who believe.

units.la: Arg. 5 Superius etiam confirmans; Quia postquam in sapientia Dei, quæ in operibus creationis, & providentiæ quotidianæ splendet, mundani homines, neque per notitiam illam naturalem, in ipsis reliquam, neque per Philosophiæ subsidium, neque per ullam suam sapientiam, Deum recte agnoverunt, sed media omnia cognitionis, clausis oculis præterierunt, Deus aliam viam salutis patefecit, per simplicem, & quasi stolidum modum prædicationis Euangelii, (sicut videtur irregenitis) ut Electos, per fidem servaret: Non mirum ergo, quod Christus me miserit ad evangelizandum, non cum dicendi peritia.
units.tr: Argument 5. Confirming what was said above: since in the wisdom of God, which shines in the works of creation and in daily providence, worldly men have not rightly known God, neither through that natural knowledge which remains in them, nor through the help of philosophy, nor through any wisdom of their own, but have passed by all the means of knowledge with their eyes closed, God has opened another way of salvation, through the simple and, as it seems to the unregenerate, almost foolish manner of preaching the gospel, so that he might save the elect through faith. It is no wonder, therefore, that Christ sent me to preach the gospel, and not with skill in speaking.

units.la: Verf. 22. Quandoquidem & Judæi signum petunt & Græci sapientiam quærunt:
units.tr: Verse 22. For the Jews ask for a sign, and the Greeks seek wisdom:

units.la: Verf. 23. Nos autem prædicamus Christum crucifixum, Judæis quidem offendiculum, Græcis vero stultitiam:
units.tr: Verse 23. But we preach Christ crucified, to the Jews indeed a stumbling block, and to the Greeks foolishness:

units.la: Illustrans quæ superius dixit, addit argumentum sextum, à praxi non suâ tantum, sed & aliorum Apostolorum, qui, nec in gratiam Judæorum, miracula quærentium, nec in gratiam Gentium, sapientiam flagitantium, curiositati hominum, sermone ornato, satisfacere studebant; sed præscriptam à Deo, simplicem rationem euangelizandi sequentes, prædicabant redemptionem per Christi infirmitates, & humiliationem, nihil morantes, quod offenderentur Judæi, crucis humilitate, nec quod Gentes, hunc prædicandi modum, stultitiam exîstimarent: Non mirum ergo, quod Christus me misit ad euangelizandum, non cum dicendi peritia.
units.tr: Illustrating what he said above, he adds a sixth argument, drawn from the practice not only of himself but also of the other apostles, who, neither to please the Jews, who sought miracles, nor to please the Gentiles, who demanded wisdom, took pains to satisfy men's curiosity with ornate speech; but following the simple method of preaching prescribed by God, they proclaimed redemption through the weaknesses and humiliation of Christ, not delaying over the fact that the Jews would be offended by the humility of the cross, nor that the Gentiles would regard this manner of preaching as foolishness. It is no wonder, therefore, that Christ sent me to preach the gospel, and not with skill in speaking.

units.la: Verf. 24. Ipsis autem vocatis, tum Judæis, tum Græcis, Christum Dei potentiam, ac Dei sapientiam.
units.tr: Verse 24. But to those who are called, both Jews and Greeks, Christ the power of God and the wisdom of God.

units.la: Excipit aliquos ex Judæis, & Gentibus, & annectit Arg. 7. à judicio, & experientia Electorum, efficaciter vocatorum ex Judæis & Gentibus; qui Christum, in simplicitate sermonis prædicatum, experiuntur & agnoscunt esse potentiam Dei demonstrationem, supra omnia miracula insignem; & sapientiam Dei manifestationem, supra omnem, quam quærunt Gentes, sapientiam mundanam. Ergo non mirum, quod Christus me misit ad euangelizandum, non cum dicendi peritia.
units.tr: He excepts certain of the Jews and Gentiles, and adds argument 7, from the judgment and experience of the elect, effectually called from among Jews and Gentiles, who, having Christ preached in the simplicity of the word, experience and acknowledge him to be the power of God, a demonstration surpassing all miracles, and the wisdom of God, a manifestation surpassing all the worldly wisdom which the Gentiles seek. Therefore it is no wonder that Christ sent me to preach the gospel, and not with skill in speaking.

units.la: Verf. 25. Nam stultitia Dei sapientior est quam homines: & infirmitas Dei validior est quam homines.
units.tr: Verse 25. For the foolishness of God is wiser than men, and the weakness of God is stronger than men.

units.la: Arg. 8. Quo confirmat, hoc judicium fidelium rectum esse: quia Dei instituta, ut ut stultissima, & infirmissima videantur mundo, omni hominum sapientiâ & potentiâ validiora sunt: ut in Sacramentis videre est. Ergo non mirum, si misit me Christus ad prædicandum, non cum dicendi peritia.
units.tr: Argument 8. By this he confirms that this judgment of believers is right: because the institutions of God, however foolish and weak they may seem to the world, are stronger than all human wisdom and power, as may be seen in the sacraments. Therefore it is no wonder, if Christ sent me to preach, that it was not with skill in speaking.

units.la: Verf. 26. Videtis enim vocationem vestram, fratres, vos videlicet, non esse multos sapientes secundum carnem, non multos potentes, non multos nobiles.
units.tr: Verse 26. For you see your calling, brethren, that not many of you are wise according to the flesh, not many mighty, not many noble.

units.la: Arg. 9. Quo ostendit, Deum simplicem prædicandi modum elegisse, non verò ornatum & sublimem, à simili ipsius placito, in selectione personarum, per vocationem: elegit non multos sapientes, potentes, Nobiles secundum carnem, seu externum statum, ordinemque in mundo, sed homines, maxima ex parte, nulla sapientiâ, potentiâ, aut generis splendore conspicuos coram mundo, imo nihili æstimatos. Ergo non mirum, si Deus eligens etiam similem prædicandi rationem, me misit ad Euangelizandum, non cum dicendi peritia.
units.tr: Argument 9. By this he shows that God has chosen a simple manner of preaching, and not an ornate and lofty one, by analogy with his purpose in choosing persons through calling: he has chosen not many wise, mighty, or noble according to the flesh, that is, according to outward status and rank in the world, but men for the most part conspicuous before the world for no wisdom, power, or splendor of birth, indeed reckoned as nothing. Therefore, since God, in choosing, has likewise chosen a similar manner of preaching, it is no wonder that he sent me to preach the gospel, and not with skill in speaking.

units.la: Vers. 27. Verum quæ stulta sunt mundo elegit Deus, ut pudefaciat sapientes, & quæ sunt infirma mundi, elegit Deus ut pudefaciat robusta:
units.tr: Verse 27. But God has chosen the foolish things of the world, that he may shame the wise; and God has chosen the weak things of the world, that he may shame the strong:

units.la: Vers. 28. Et quæ ignobilia sunt in mundo, & pro nihilo habita, elegit Deus, & ea quæ non sunt, ut ea quæ sunt enervaret:
units.tr: Verse 28. And the base things of the world, and things despised, God has chosen, and things which are not, that he may bring to nothing the things that are:

units.la: Huic argumento immittet arg. 10. a fine subalterno, hujus consilii Dei; ut scilicet ostenderet, nihil se facere ea, quæ apud homines in maximo sunt pretio: ut ita pudefiant, confundantur, viles nulliusque pretii comperiantur quicunque propter illa superbiunt: nec igitur mirum, Deum simplicem prædicandi rationem eligere, & me eam tenere, ut vana illa dicendi peritia pudefiat: cum tota illa verborum pompa affectus humanos, titillare tantum comperitur, ad conversionem vero cordis, nihil efficere.
units.tr: To this argument he adds argument 10, from the subordinate end of this counsel of God: namely, to show that he does nothing through those things which are held in highest esteem among men, so that those who take pride in them may be put to shame, confounded, and found base and of no worth; hence it is no wonder that God chooses a simple manner of preaching and that I hold to it, so that that vain skill in speaking may be put to shame, since all that verbal pomp is found only to tickle human emotions, and to accomplish nothing toward the conversion of the heart.

units.la: Vers. 29. Ut ne glorietur ulla caro in ejus conspectu.
units.tr: Verse 29. So that no flesh may glory in his sight.

units.la: Arg. 11. A fine ultimo Divini beneplaciti, in elegendis rebus, personis, & mediis ad salutem infirmis, qui finis negative hic proponitur, ne quis glorietur in seipso: Non mirum ergo, Deum misisse me, ut prædicarem non cum dicendi peritia, ne glorier in meipso, nempe cum convertuntur aliqui per prædicationem meam.
units.tr: Argument 11. From the ultimate end of the divine good pleasure, in choosing things, persons, and means of salvation that are weak, an end which is here stated negatively: that no one may glory in himself. Therefore it is no wonder that God sent me to preach not with skill in speaking, lest I glory in myself, namely when some are converted through my preaching.

units.la: Vers. 30. Sed ex ipso vos estis in Christo Iesu, qui factus est nobis sapientia à Deo, justitiaque & sanctificatio, & redemptio:
units.tr: Verse 30. But of him are you in Christ Jesus, who was made to us wisdom from God, and righteousness and sanctification and redemption:

units.la: Consolatur interim Corinthios adversus hanc ipsorum exinanitionem, & abjectionem coram mundo: concedens illis quasi in compensationem nobilitatem generis in regeneratione, divitias in sapientia, & justitia, & denique liberationem ab omni peccato, & miseria in CHRISTO. Imò verò in majorem fidei ipsorum confirmationem pronunciat CHRISTUM constitutum à Deo, & datum illis in justitiam, & vitam, CHRISTUS enim hæc omnia factus est merito, imputatione, applicatione, & complemento efficaci in singulorum fidelium usum.
units.tr: Meanwhile he comforts the Corinthians against this emptying and abasement of theirs before the world, granting them, as a compensation, nobility of birth in regeneration, riches in wisdom and righteousness, and finally deliverance from all sin and misery in CHRIST. Indeed, to confirm their faith still more, he declares that CHRIST has been appointed by God and given to them for righteousness and life, for Christ is made all these things by merit, imputation, application, and effective completion for the use of each believer.

units.la: Vers. 31. Ut fiat sicut scriptum est, Qui gloriatur, in Domino gloriator.
units.tr: Verse 31. That it may be as it is written: He who glories, let him glory in the Lord.

units.la: Finem ultimum Divini beneplaciti in elegendis mediis infirmis, & personis infirmis, & in humiliandis omnibus in seipsis affirmative ponit, nempe ut (sicut habetur Jer. 9. 23.) Deo cedat tota gloria, unde arg. 12. de omnibus sic dispensat Deus, ut nemo glorietur nisi in Domino: Ergo non mirum, Deum me misisse ut euangelizarem, non in dicendi peritia, ut in effectu Euangelii gloriemur omnes in solo Deo.
units.tr: He affirmatively states the ultimate end of the divine good pleasure in choosing weak means and weak persons, and in humbling all in themselves: namely, that (as is found in Jer. 9. 23.) all glory may belong to God. Hence argument 12: God so orders all things that no one may glory except in the Lord. Therefore it is no wonder that God sent me to preach the gospel, and not in skill in speaking, so that we may all glory in God alone in the effect of the gospel.

units.la: Caput secundum.
units.tr: Chapter 2.

units.la: Eadem confirmare pergit, quam superiori capite tradebat doctrinam, quod scilicet praedicatio Euangelii repudiat splendorem Rhetoricum, gaudeat vero simplicitate, & demonstratione spirituali, non quod patrocinetur Apostolus cujusquam temeritati, vel eruditati in praedicando, quasi effutiendum sit, quicquid in buccam venerit, sine methodo, sine sensu, stilo agresti, & contemptibili loquendi genere; suam enim habet venustatem recta praedicandi ratio, quae neque fucum fert, neque sordes patitur, sed quod eloquentiae affectationem damnet, quae auditorem rapit in admirationem dicentis, magis quam in dictorum, seu Euangelii amorem; nam meditatam, & bene intellectam veritatem, (quando eam ex fide, & dilectione, profert Concionator,) sponte sequitur simplex, & ad aedificationem omnium auditorum accommodata oratio, quae sapientissimis auditoribus, supra omnes Rhetorum delicias, sapit. Hanc simplicem praedicandi rationem, artificiosa eloquentia, probat praestantiorem, octo argumentis: quorum priora petuntur ab ipsius Pauli & Corinthiorum, ad quos scribit, experientia.
units.tr: He goes on to confirm the same doctrine he set out in the previous chapter: that the preaching of the Gospel rejects rhetorical splendour and delights in simplicity and spiritual demonstration. He does not mean that the Apostle defends the rashness of any preacher, or his ignorance, as if whatever comes into the mouth should be poured out without method, without sense, in a rustic style and a contemptible manner of speaking. For sound preaching has its own elegance, which neither uses paint nor tolerates filth. Rather, he condemns the affectation of eloquence, which carries the hearer off into admiration of the speaker rather than love of what is said, or of the Gospel. For when a preacher delivers a truth that he has meditated on and understood well, out of faith and love, a plain speech fitted to the edification of all the hearers follows of its own accord, and to the wisest hearers it tastes better than all the delights of the orators. He proves this plainer way of preaching to be superior to artificial eloquence by eight arguments. The first of these is taken from the experience of Paul himself and of the Corinthians to whom he writes.

units.la: Verf. 1. Ego igitur quum venirem ad vos, fratres, veni non cum eminentia facundiae aut sapientiae, annuncians vobis testimonium Dei.
units.tr: Verse 1. And I, brethren, when I came to you, came not with excellency of speech or of wisdom, declaring unto you the testimony of God.

units.la: Argumentum primum. Ego Paulus, cum ad vos Corinthios veni praedicaturus Euangelium, per quod converti estis ad fidem, consulto abstinebam ab eminentia facundiae: Ergo simplicitas orationis praestat artificio Rhetorico in praedicatione Euangelii.
units.tr: First argument. When I, Paul, came to you Corinthians to preach the Gospel, through which you were converted to the faith, I deliberately refrained from excellency of speech. Therefore the simplicity of speech surpasses rhetorical art in the preaching of the Gospel.

units.la: Vers. 2. Non enim statui quicquam scire inter vos, nisi Iesum Christum, eumque crucifixum.
units.tr: Verse 2. For I determined not to know anything among you, save Jesus Christ, and him crucified.

units.la: Arg. 2. Nullius pretii aestimavi ego, apud vos manifestare vel prodere in me, scientiam ullius rei, praeterquam personae, officiorum, efficaciae & virtutis IESU CHRISTI, & speciatim passionum, & humiliationis ipsius: Ergo hæc ratio Euangelii prædicandi, est præstantissima.
units.tr: Second argument. I judged it of no value to show or to profess among you any knowledge of anything in me, except the person, offices, efficacy and virtue of Jesus Christ, and especially his sufferings and his humiliation. Therefore this way of preaching the Gospel is most excellent.

units.la: Verf. 3. Sed fui ego cum infirmitate, & timore, ac tremore multo apud vos.
units.tr: Verse 3. And I was with you in weakness, and in fear, and in much trembling.

units.la: Arg. 3. Ego, memor infirmitatum humanarum, in mediis periculis, sine fastu, ad humilitatem me componens, inter vos prædicabam, & solicitè & trepidè in officio me gerebam: Ergo & hæc ratio humiliter prædicandi Euangelium, est præstantissima.
units.tr: Third argument. Mindful of human weakness, amid dangers, without pride, humbling myself, I preached among you and conducted myself in my office with care and trembling. Therefore this humble way of preaching the Gospel is also most excellent.

units.la: Verf. 4. Neque sermo meus, & præconium meum versatum est in persuasoriis humanæ sapientiæ verbis, sed in demonstratione spiritali & potentiâ.
units.tr: Verse 4. And my speech and my preaching were not in persuasive words of human wisdom, but in demonstration of the Spirit and of power.

units.la: Arg. 4. Mea oratio, & prædicatio, neque splendebat acumine ingenii, nec humana Philosophia, nec ornatu verborum ad persuasionem comparatorum, sed demonstrationibus Scripturæ, & solidæ veritatis, quibus Spiritus potenter se exerebat, & operabatur in vestris animis: Ergo hæc prædicandi ratio est præstantissima.
units.tr: Fourth argument. My speech and my preaching did not shine with the keenness of wit, nor with human philosophy, nor with verbal ornament devised for persuasion, but with the demonstrations of Scripture and of solid truth, by which the Spirit powerfully made himself known and worked in your minds. Therefore this way of preaching is most excellent.

units.la: Verf. 5. Ne fides vestra consistat in sapientia hominum, sed in potentia Dei.
units.tr: Verse 5. That your faith should not stand in the wisdom of men, but in the power of God.

units.la: Rationem facti sui reddens, cur temperaverit sibi ab eloquentia humana in sermonibus, addit arg. 5. Si ego usus fuissem arte pictis sermonibus, in vestri conversione ad fidem: Ratio credendi Euangelio inter vos Corinthios fuisset eloquentia humana, & non Euangelii DEI nuda veritas, (quæ DEI dicitur potentia, quia potenter per eam in suis operatur DEUS:) atque ita fides Corinthiorum, nixa fuisset lubrico humanæ eloquentiæ fundamento: Cum autem eloquentiâ movetur aliquis ad credendum, eloquentia majori etiam moveri poterit ad renunciandum fidei veritati, sequitur ergo hanc simplicem prædicandi rationem esse præstantissimam.
units.tr: Giving the reason for his conduct, why he abstained from human eloquence in his sermons, he adds the fifth argument. If I had used the art of painted speeches in your conversion to the faith, the ground of your belief in the Gospel among you Corinthians would have been human eloquence and not the bare truth of the Gospel of God (which is called the power of God, because God works powerfully through it in his own). And so the faith of the Corinthians would have rested on the slippery foundation of human eloquence. But when someone is moved to believe by eloquence, he may also be moved by a greater eloquence to renounce the truth of the faith. It follows, therefore, that this plain way of preaching is most excellent.

units.la: Verf. 6. Sapientiam verò loquimur inter adultos: sapientiam autem non seculi hujus, neque principum seculi hujus: quæ evanescunt.
units.tr: Verse 6. Howbeit we speak wisdom among them that are perfect; yet not the wisdom of this world, nor of the princes of this world, that come to nought.

units.la: Arg. 6. A comparatione Euangelii & sapientiæ humanæ; Quod Euangelium suam habeat propriam sapientiam, eloquentiam, & venustatem, in hoc simplici prædicationis genere, Judice quovis adulto, nec magis admittere posset humanæ sapientiæ ornatum, quam pulcherrima. rima facies admittit fucum; Servitium quidem humanæ sapientiæ postulat sapientia Euangelii, in prædicaturis: non verò splendorem humanæ sapientiæ in prædicationibus.
units.tr: Sixth argument, from the comparison of the Gospel and human wisdom. The Gospel has its own wisdom, eloquence and elegance in this plain kind of preaching; any adult who judges rightly would no more admit the ornament of human wisdom into it than the fairest face admits paint. Wisdom of the Gospel indeed demands the service of human wisdom in those who preach, but not the splendour of human wisdom in sermons.

units.la: Comparatio autem sapientiæ Divinæ in simplicitate sermonis cum sapientia seculari octuplex est. Prima comparatio, perfecti seu adulti in Dei schola, qui sensus habent exercitatos, ad discernendum bonum & malum, hanc sapientiam Euangelii capiunt, admirantur, & magnificiunt! Humanam autem illam, suspiciunt, & admirantur soli reliqui, nempe rerum divinarum, vel prorsus ignari, vel rudiores, & imperfecti νηπίοι.
units.tr: Now the comparison of divine wisdom in the simplicity of speech with worldly wisdom is eightfold. The first comparison: the perfect, or adult, in God's school, who have their senses trained to discern good and evil, grasp this wisdom of the Gospel, admire it and magnify it. Human wisdom, however, is admired and esteemed only by the rest, namely those who are either wholly ignorant of divine things, or cruder and immature, the nēpioi [νήπιοι].

units.la: Comparitio 2. Humana sapientia est hujus tantum seculi, seu temporaria, sapientia vero Euangelii est futuri seculi, seu sempiterna.
units.tr: Comparison 2. Human wisdom belongs only to this age, that is, it is temporary; the wisdom of the Gospel belongs to the age to come, that is, it is everlasting.

units.la: Comparatio 3. Sapientia humana est hominum, qui licet in mundo pro principibus habeantur, cum sapientia sua pereunt tamen & abolentur.
units.tr: Comparison 3. Human wisdom belongs to men who, although they are regarded as princes in the world, perish and are brought to nothing along with their wisdom.

units.la: Verf. 7. Sed loquimur sapientiam Dei latentem in mysterio, id est, occultam illam, quam præsinierat Deus ante secula, in gloriam nostram:
units.tr: Verse 7. But we speak the wisdom of God in a mystery, that is, the hidden wisdom which God ordained before the ages for our glory.

units.la: Altera pars comparationis; Euangelii vero sapientia, est sapientia Dei viventis, & æterni Dei dicitur, quia à Deo sapienter excogitatum est Euangelium, & quia in eo revelatur sapientia Dei admiranda, de hominum salute, & redemptione.
units.tr: The other part of the comparison: the wisdom of the Gospel is the wisdom of the living God, and is called the wisdom of the eternal God, because the Gospel was wisely devised by God, and because in it the admirable wisdom of God concerning the salvation and redemption of men is revealed.

units.la: Comparatio 4. Humana Philosophia communis & obvia est cuivis naturæ dotibus prædito, Euangelii vero sapientia, est mysterium seu sapientia abscondita, quia non ratione naturali, sicut humana Philosophia, sed revelatione supernaturali scitur.
units.tr: Comparison 4. Human philosophy is common and obvious to anyone endowed with natural gifts; but the wisdom of the Gospel is a mystery, or hidden wisdom, because it is known not by natural reason, as human philosophy is, but by supernatural revelation.

units.la: Comparatio 5. In antiquitate, Sapientia Euangelii, non est heri nata, sed ante secula ab æterno à Deo præfinita; humana Philosophia verò est nuperum inventum Philosophorum, & nondum perfectum, seu finitum.
units.tr: Comparison 5. As to antiquity, the wisdom of the Gospel was not born yesterday, but was predestined by God from eternity, before the ages; whereas human philosophy is a recent invention of philosophers, and not yet perfected or finished.

units.la: Comparatio 6. Sapientia Euangelii ad gloriam, & salutem pertinet, potissimum nostram qui sub gratia vivimus; sapientia vero humana, cum hac comparata, non ad salutem, sed ad evanidam speculationem spectat.
units.tr: Comparison 6. The wisdom of the Gospel pertains to glory and salvation, chiefly to ours, who live under grace; human wisdom, when compared with it, looks not to salvation but to empty speculation.

units.la: Verf. 8. Quam nemo principum seculi hujus cognovit: nam si cognovissent, nequaquam Dominum gloriæ crucifixissent.
units.tr: Verse 8. Which none of the princes of this world knew; for had they known it, they would never have crucified the Lord of glory.

units.la: Comparatio 7. Cum humana sapientiâ consistere potest ignorantia CHRISTI, cum Euangelii verò sapientia minime; Comparatio hæc, sensibili experientia confirmatur, quia primores Judæorum, & gubernatores Gentium, qui sapientiæ nomine, principatum in mundo videbantur obtinere, nihil intellexerunt de sapientia Euangelii, quod probat à signo, quia si cognovissent quicquam de Euangelio, vel reverentiâ Numinis, vel metu abstertiti cavillent, ne CHRISTUM DOMINUM gloriosum, ignominiosè crucifixissent.
units.tr: Comparison 7. Ignorance of Christ can coexist with human wisdom, but not at all with the wisdom of the Gospel. This comparison is confirmed by sensible experience, since the chief men of the Jews and the rulers of the Gentiles, who seemed by the name of wisdom to hold the leading place in the world, understood nothing of the wisdom of the Gospel. This he proves from the sign: if they had known anything of the Gospel, they would either have reverenced the Deity or, restrained by fear, would not have ignominiously crucified the glorious Lord Christ.

units.la: Verf. 9. Sed prædicamus, sicut scriptum est, quæ oculus non vidit, nec auris audivit, nec in mentem hominis venerunt, quæ paravit Deus iis à quibus ipse diligitur
units.tr: Verse 9. But we preach as it is written, Eye has not seen, nor ear heard, neither has it entered into the heart of man, the things which God has prepared for those who love him.

units.la: Comparatio 8. Confirmans, & illustrans quartam & sextam comparationem, Philosophiæ humanæ objectum, sensibus externis, & intellectu, seu lumine rationis naturali percipitur; sapientiæ verò in Euangelio explicatæ objectum, continens bona per CHRISTUM parta, in præsenti, & futuro seculo possidenda, nec sensibus externis, nec intellectu in sensibilibus fundato, seu discursu rationis ullo absque revelatione percipi potest; quia ejus notitia, (ut Isaias dicit, cap. 64. verf. 4.) in cor hominis naturaliter ascendere non potest. Ex omnibus hujus comparationis membris, exsurgit Arg. 6. Sapientia Euangelii, quam pro concione simplex prædicandi ratio sola, optimè aperit, longè præstat omni sapientia seculari, quam solam peritia dicendi usurpata pro concione aperit, idque cum sapientiæ Euangelii obscuratione: Ergo simplex illa prædicandi ratio, longè præstantissima est. Summa est, Simplex oratio ostendit auditori profunditatem sapientiæ Divinæ. Peritia dicendi verò ostendit quam eruditus sit in seculari sapientia prædicator.
units.tr: Comparison 8. Confirming and illustrating the fourth and sixth comparisons: the object of human philosophy is perceived by the external senses and by the intellect, that is, by the natural light of reason; but the object of the wisdom explained in the Gospel, namely the goods won through Christ to be possessed in the present and future age, can be perceived neither by the external senses, nor by the intellect founded on sensible things, nor by any process of reasoning apart from revelation. For, as Isaiah says (ch. 64, v. 4), its knowledge cannot naturally rise up into the heart of man. From all the parts of this comparison arises the sixth argument: the wisdom of the Gospel, which the plain way of preaching alone sets forth well in a sermon, far surpasses all worldly wisdom, which only the skill of speaking, used in a sermon, sets forth, and that with the obscuring of the wisdom of the Gospel. Therefore that plain way of preaching is by far the most excellent. In short: plain speech shows the hearer the depth of divine wisdom; skill in speaking, on the other hand, shows how learned the preacher is in worldly wisdom.

units.la: Verf. 10. Nobis autem Deus ea revelavit per Spiritum suum. Spiritus enim omnia scrutatur, etiam profunditates Dei.
units.tr: Verse 10. But God has revealed them to us through his Spirit. For the Spirit searches all things, even the depths of God.

units.la: Hanc doctrinam illustrat solutione duarum objectionum: Prima objectio: unde ergo vos scitis Euangelium? Respondet ex Spiritus revelatione per fidem, à nobis cognoici Euangelii subjectum, quod confirmat à fine, & proprietatibus donati nobis Spiritus sancti, quia Spiritus sanctus, quasi scrutinio facto, accuratè novit omnia, etiam arcana Dei, & revelat hæc nobis mysteria.
units.tr: He illustrates this doctrine by answering two objections. First objection: how then do you know the Gospel? He answers from the revelation of the Spirit through faith, confirming that the subject of the Gospel is known to us from its end and from the properties of the Holy Spirit given to us, because the Holy Spirit, as if having made a search, knows all things accurately, even the secrets of God, and reveals these mysteries to us.

units.la: Verf. 11. Quis enim hominum novit ea quae sunt hominis, nisi Spiritus hominis qui est in eo? ita etiam ea quae sunt Dei nemo novit, nisi Spiritus Dei.
units.tr: Verse 11. For who among men knows the things of a man, except the spirit of the man that is in him? So also no one knows the things of God except the Spirit of God.

units.la: Hanc Spiritus proprietatem, probat à pari, sicut Spiritus hominis, optimè noffe potest ea quae sunt in homine, sic Spiritus Dei, solus noville potest, profunda consilia Dei, & per consequens ea revelare.
units.tr: He proves this property of the Spirit by a parallel: just as the spirit of a man can best know the things that are in a man, so the Spirit of God alone can know the deep counsels of God and consequently reveal them.

units.la: Verf. 12. Nos vero non Spiritum mundi accepimus: sed fpiritum qui est ex Deo: ut sciamus quae Deus est nobis gratificatus:
units.tr: Verse 12. But we have not received the spirit of the world, but the Spirit which is from God, that we may know the things that have been freely given us by God.

units.la: Objectio fecunda: At si solus Spiritus novit quid vobis cum Spiritu? Respondet, Spiritum datum esse nobis fidelibus, non Spiritum illum communem mundo, non eloquentiae donum, seu secularis sapientiae, sed Spiritum seu donum spiritualis gratiae ad hoc, ut sciamus dona illa Spiritualia (id est) Christum cum ipsius beneficiis, nobis à Deo gratis donata.
units.tr: Second objection: but if the Spirit alone knows, what have you to do with the Spirit? He answers that the Spirit has been given to us believers, not the Spirit common to the world, not the gift of eloquence or of secular wisdom, but the Spirit, that is, the gift of spiritual grace, so that we may know those spiritual gifts (that is, Christ with his benefits) freely given to us by God.

units.la: Verf. 13. Quae etiam loquimur, non sermonibus quos docet humana sapientia, sed quos docet Spiritus Sanctus, spiritualia, cum iis quae spiritualia sunt conferentes.
units.tr: Verse 13. Which things also we speak, not in words which human wisdom teaches, but which the Holy Spirit teaches, comparing spiritual things with spiritual.

units.la: Arg. 7. A praxi Apostolicâ confirmatum, Spiritualia tradi debent (si praxis Apostolorum est imitanda) non humanae sapientiae depictis sermonibus, sed spirituali stylo, seu sermone quem docet Spiritus sanctus. Ergo haec praedicandi ratio est praestantissima. Ornari non vult caelestis res haec, contenta est doceri; qui loquitur, inquit Petrus, loquatur ut eloquia Dei, hoc est, utatur oratione pia, reverendâ, sanctâ, loquens de rebus divinis, ut Dei eloquia decet.
units.tr: Argument 7. Confirmed from apostolic practice: spiritual things ought to be delivered (if the practice of the Apostles is to be imitated) not in words adorned with human wisdom, but in a spiritual style, or in the speech which the Holy Spirit teaches. Therefore this manner of preaching is most excellent. This heavenly matter does not wish to be decked out; it is content to be taught. He who speaks, says Peter, let him speak as the oracles of God, that is, let him use pious, reverent, holy speech, speaking of divine things as befits the oracles of God.

units.la: Spiritualia] Hoc argumentum confirmans, annectit argumentum octavum, quia rebus spiritualibus, & hominibus spiritualibus, seu Dei Spiritu praeditis, aptari debet, & conjungi stilus, modusque dicendi spiritualis, argumentis spiritualibus ex Scriptura petitis utens; quod non fiet, si induatur Euangelii praedicatio, coloribus Rhetoricis, & Philosophicis sententiis depicto sermone: Istiusmodi enim oratio tam dedecet Euangelium, quam chlamys, seu purpura Herodis, dedecebat Christum: Ergo haec ratio praedicandi est praestantissima.
units.tr: Spiritual things] Confirming this argument, he adds an eighth argument: style and manner of speaking must be fitted and joined to spiritual things and spiritual men, that is, to those endowed with the Spirit of God, using spiritual arguments drawn from Scripture. This will not happen if the preaching of the Gospel is clothed in rhetorical colours and philosophical maxims. For such speech is as unbecoming to the Gospel as Herod's cloak or purple was unbecoming to Christ. Therefore this manner of preaching is most excellent.

units.la: Verf. 14. Animalis autem homo non est capax eorum quae sunt Spiritus Dei: sunt enim ei stultitia, nec potest ea cognoscere, quia spiritualiter dijudicantur.
units.tr: Verse 14. But the natural man does not receive the things of the Spirit of God; for they are foolishness to him, nor can he know them, because they are spiritually discerned.

units.la: Hanc doctrinam illustrat, obviam eundo objectioni; Diceret aliquis, non posse ab humana ratione admitti, hanc Apostoli doctrinam; remo enim est, qui non exi∫timet ∫tultitiam e∫se, res praeclari∫simas & ∫pirituales, non (quam fieri posset) ornatissimo, & elegantissimo dicendi genere, proponere. Respondet, distinguendo homines in animales, & ∫piri-tuales, vel eundem hominem, in animalem & ∫piritualem, qui animalis dicitur, quatenus in ∫toeris naturalibus consideratur, seu quatenus in actu aliquo particulari, ∫piritu destitutus, ex intelligentia carnis judicat de rebus Divinis, adeoque de ∫pirituali modo praedicandi: Spiritualis vero dicitur, quatenus mente & affectibus renovatus, ∫piritus dictamen audit. De priori, id est, animali irregenito, seu quovis quatenus irregenitus est, concedit quod objicitur, causas indicans, cur nec capere, nec approbare posilit hanc doctrinam, neque ullam aliam rem ∫piritualem: Causae autem tres sunt; Prima, quia sunt ei ∫tultitia fatua, & ridicula, etiam ea quae sunt ∫plendidissima sapientia Dei. 2. Quia qua talis est, ob luminis defectum, & inimicitias naturalis sapientiae adversus Deum, non potest ∫piritualia capere. 3. Quia ∫piritualia dijudicantur tantum ∫piritualiter, id est, ∫piritua-li lumine, & ∫piritu intus actu monstrante objectum, quibus animalis homo destituitur. Tanta enim in nobis est mentis caecitas, hallucinatio, perversitas & ineptitudo ad ∫piritualia, ut nisi regeniti & actu a Spiritu ∫ancto in ∫ingulis illuminati, nihil in ∫piritualibus dijudicemus.
units.tr: He illustrates this doctrine by meeting an objection. Someone might say that this doctrine of the Apostle cannot be admitted by human reason, for there is no one who does not think it foolishness to set forth the most splendid and spiritual things in the most ornate and elegant style of speaking, which could be done. He answers by distinguishing men into natural and spiritual, or the same man into natural and spiritual. He who is called natural is so considered insofar as he is in his natural state, or insofar as, in some particular act, destitute of the Spirit, he judges divine things by the understanding of the flesh, and so judges the spiritual manner of preaching.
