Spiritual, however, is the man who, renewed in mind and affections, hears the dictate of the Spirit. Of the former, that is, the natural unregenerate man, or anyone insofar as he is unregenerate, he concedes what is objected, giving the causes why he can neither grasp nor approve this doctrine, nor any other spiritual thing. There are three causes. (1) Because these things are to him foolish and ridiculous, even those things which are the most splendid wisdom of God. (2) Because, as such, on account of the lack of light and the enmity of natural wisdom against God, he cannot grasp spiritual things. (3) Because spiritual things are judged only spiritually, that is, by spiritual light and by the Spirit actually showing the object within, and the natural man lacks these. For there is in us such blindness, delusion, perversity and ineptitude of mind toward spiritual things that, unless we are regenerate and actually illuminated by the Holy Spirit in each particular, we judge nothing rightly in spiritual matters.

units.la: Vers. 15. At ∫piritualis dijudicat quidem omnia, ipse vero a nemine dijudicatur.
units.tr: Verse 15. But the spiritual man indeed judges all things, yet he himself is judged by no one.

units.la: Altera pars distinctionis, Spiritualis autem homo, in quantum ∫piritualis est, omnes res Dei (scilicet de quibus sermo est) novit, & ∫piritualem seu salutarem modum tractandi mysteria Dei pro concione discernit, & agnoscit sua quisque mensura: ipse vero in ∫piritual∫i suo statu, & actionibus ∫piritualibus, a nemine qui ∫piritualis non est, vel quatenus ∫piritualis non est, discerni poterit, vel pro ∫piritual haberi.
units.tr: The other part of the distinction: the spiritual man, insofar as he is spiritual, knows all the things of God (namely those under discussion), and discerns the spiritual or saving manner of handling the mysteries of God in preaching, and each recognizes this according to his measure. But he himself, in his spiritual state and spiritual actions, can be discerned by no one who is not spiritual, or insofar as he is not spiritual, nor can he be regarded as spiritual by such a person.

units.la: Vers. 16. Quis enim novit mentem Domini, qui instruturus sit eum? nos autem mentem Christi habemus.
units.tr: Verse 16. For who has known the mind of the Lord, that he should instruct him? But we have the mind of Christ.

units.la: Mutuatâ ab Isa. 40. 13. sententia, probat responsionem datam; Quia nemo novit consilium Dei, praeter eos quibus Spiritum suum Deus dedit: Ideoque nemo animalis, de mysteriis salutis, & ∫piritualì modo tractandi Dei mysteria, judicare potest, sed soli spirituales, quatenus mentem Christi, sibi per Christi Spiritum revelatum habent: quales erant Apostoli, reliquique Fideles, sua quisque mensura.
units.tr: Borrowing the sentence from Isa. 40. 13, he proves the answer given: no one knows the counsel of God except those to whom God has given his Spirit. Therefore no natural man can judge about the mysteries of salvation and the spiritual manner of handling God's mysteries, but only spiritual men, insofar as they have the mind of Christ revealed to them through Christ's Spirit. Such were the Apostles and the other faithful, each according to his measure.

units.la: Caput tertium.
units.tr: Chapter 3.

units.la: AD superiora argumenta, humilem in docendo stilum probantia, superaddit unum, verf. 1. & 2. & dilabitur ad correctionem schismatis, reliquo capite.
units.tr: To the earlier arguments, which commend a humble style of teaching, he adds one more in verses 1 and 2, and from there he passes on to correcting the schism for the rest of the chapter.

units.la: Verf. 1. EGo porrò, fratres, non potui loqui vobis ut spiritualibus, sed loquutus sum ut carnalibus, id est, ut infantibus in Christo.
units.tr: Verse 1. And I, brethren, could not speak unto you as unto spiritual, but as unto carnal, even as unto babes in Christ.

units.la: Verf. 2. Lactis potu vos alui, & non esca: nondum enim poteratis id ferre: imò ne nunc quidem adhuc potestis.
units.tr: Verse 2. I have fed you with milk, and not with meat: for hitherto ye were not able to bear it, neither yet now are ye able.

units.la: Argumentum est à necessitate auditorum, inter quos reperiuntur rudiores, quibus sublimitas rerum spiritualium, non solùm simplicitate sermonis condienda & attemperanda est, sed etiam ad familiarem & rudiorem loquendi modum dimittenda: quod experientiâ suâ, & Corinthiorum exemplo confirmat: inter quos ut inter carnales admodùm, & infantes in Christo, coactus fit Apostolus, de virili loquendi genere remittere, & ut cum pueris, de rebus divinis balbutire: Quapropter faciliori doctrinâ, & familiari stylo eos, ut lacte pueros, alebat.
units.tr: The argument is drawn from the need of the hearers, among whom there are cruder people, so that the sublimity of spiritual things must be seasoned and adapted not only by simplicity of speech but also lowered to a familiar and cruder way of speaking. He confirms this from his own experience and the example of the Corinthians: among them, as among fleshly people and babes in Christ, the Apostle was compelled to give up the manly way of speaking and to stammer about divine things as children do. Therefore, like children, he fed them with easier teaching and a familiar style.

units.la: Non enim] Rationes facti sui reddit tres: Prima est, quia perfectiorem doctrinam, aut perfectiorem docendi modum, seu cibum duriorem non poteratis tum ferre.
units.tr: For ye were not able] He gives three reasons for his conduct. The first is that at that time you could not bear a more perfect doctrine, or a more perfect way of teaching, or harder food.

units.la: Sed nec] Ratio 2. Quia nec adhuc, dum ista scriberet, capere poterant.
units.tr: Neither yet] Reason 2: because even while he was writing these things they were still unable to grasp them.

units.la: Verf. 3. Nam adhuc carnales estis, quum enim inter vos sint livor & contentio & dissidia, nonne carnales estis, & secundum hoc minem incedtitis?
units.tr: Verse 3. For ye are yet carnal: for whereas there is among you envying, and strife, and divisions, are ye not carnal, and walk as men?

units.la: Ratio 3. Quia carnales estis, secundum quid scilicet, & comparative ad spiritualium perfectionem, ad quam aspirare debebant. Id ut probet, dilabitur, ad corripiendum schisma quod inter eos vigebat; Primò in genere, quia inter ipsos conspici poterant opera carnis, aemulatio praepostera, & ex aemulatione contentiones, & ex contentionibus divisiones, seu schismata, quod erat secundum vias hominis irregeniti, & carnalis, ambulare.
units.tr: Reason 3: because they are carnal, that is, in a certain respect, and by comparison with the perfection of spiritual things, to which they ought to aspire. To prove this, he proceeds to rebuke the schism that prevailed among them. First, in general: among them could be seen the works of the flesh, a preposterous rivalry, and from rivalry contentions, and from contentions divisions or schisms, which is to walk according to the ways of unregenerate and carnal man.

units.la: Verf. 4 Etenim quum dicit aliquis, Ego quidem sum Pauli, alter verò, Ego sum Apollo, nonne carnales estis?
units.tr: Verse 4. For while one saith, I am of Paul; and another, I am of Apollos; are ye not carnal?

units.la: Deinde in specie probat Corinthios esse carnales, & propius taxat schisma, quia certos sibi seligebant doctores, à quorum alio denominari voluit alius, ab alio vero alius; Interim vetat ne schisma foveant de doctoribus suis, propositis argumentis quatuordecim, quæ omnia probant schisma quo laborabant non esse fovendum, nec à doctoribus nec à populo.
units.tr: Then he proves in particular that the Corinthians are carnal, and more closely censures the schism, because they chose certain teachers for themselves, one wishing to be named after one, another after another. Meanwhile he forbids them to foster this schism about their teachers, setting out fourteen arguments, all of which show that the schism in which they were labouring is not to be fostered, neither by the teachers nor by the people.

units.la: Argumentum primum: Hæc de doctoribus contentio, arguit vos carnales esse: Ergo schisma non fovendum.
units.tr: First argument: this contention about teachers shows that you are carnal. Therefore the schism is not to be fostered.

units.la: Verf. 5. Quis igitur Paulus, quis autem Apollos, nisi ministri per quos credidistis, & ut cuique Dominus dedit?
units.tr: Verse 5. Who then is Paul, and who is Apollos, but ministers by whom ye believed, even as the Lord gave to every man?

units.la: Arg. 2. Præstantissimi Apostoli, vel Evangelistæ, nedum pastores vestri ordinarii (quorum nominibus parcit) sunt tantum ministri conversionis & fidei vestræ. Ergo non sunt tanti faciendi, ut ab iis denominationes sumatis, & propter eos in factiones scindamini: Ergo schisma hoc non fovendum amplius.
units.tr: Argument 2. The most excellent apostles or evangelists, not to mention your ordinary ministers (whose names he spares), are only ministers of your conversion and faith. Therefore they are not to be valued so highly that you take your names from them and are split into factions on their account. Therefore this schism is no longer to be fostered.

units.la: Verf. 6. Ego plantavi, Apollos rigavit: sed Deus dedit crescendi vim.
units.tr: Verse 6. I have planted, Apollos watered; but God gave the increase.

units.la: Verf. 7. Itaque neque is qui plantat, est aliquid, neque qui rigat: sed Deus qui dat crescendi vim.
units.tr: Verse 7. So then neither is he that planteth any thing, neither he that watereth; but God that giveth the increase.

units.la: Arg 3. Ipsorum Apostolorum, & Evangelistarum ministerium, & opera, sive in conversione, sive in ædificatione conversorum, non magis prodest, nisi Deus benedixerit, quam plantatio aut irrigatio hortulani prodesse poterit, Deo incrementum non largiente: Ergo tantus honor ut gloriemini de doctoribus, non hominibus, sed Deo tribuendus.
units.tr: Argument 3. The ministry and work of the apostles and evangelists themselves, whether in converting or in building up the converted, profits no more, unless God blesses it, than the planting or watering of a gardener can profit if God does not give the increase. Therefore the honour that you would give to teachers, so that you glory in them, is to be ascribed to God and not to men.

units.la: Verf. 8. Is vero qui plantat, & is qui rigat, unum sunt: unusquisque vero suam mercedem accipiet secundum suum laborem.
units.tr: Verse 8. Now he that planteth and he that watereth are one: and every man shall receive his own reward according to his own labour.

units.la: Arg. 4. Doctores omnes officio, laboribus, & scopo, unum esse debent, Ergo nec per eos, nec propter eos, scindenda est Ecclesia.
units.tr: Argument 4. All teachers ought to be one in office, labours and aim. Therefore the Church is to be split neither through them nor on account of them.

units.la: Arg. 5. unusquisque accipiet mercedem, secundum laborem suum. Ergo doctoribus incumbit, ut potius attendant operi suo, & mercedi reportandæ, quam factionibus fovendis.
units.tr: Argument 5. Every man shall receive his reward according to his labour. Therefore it is incumbent on the teachers to attend rather to their work and to the reward to be obtained, than to foster factions.

units.la: Verf. 9 Etenim Dei sumus administri: Dei arvum, Dei ædificium estis.
units.tr: Verse 9. For we are labourers together with God: ye are God's husbandry, ye are God's building.

units.la: Arg. 6 Doctores omnes esse debent operarii cum Deo, ejusque administri. Ergo non debent schismata per eos, aut propter eos fieri.
units.tr: Argument 6. All teachers ought to be workers with God and his ministers. Therefore schisms ought not to be made by them or on account of them.

units.la: Arg. 7. Qui ex Dei populo sunt, ut arvum, aut ædificium, arctæ um arcte inter se uniti, DOMINO inservire debent. Ergo non debent à se invicem scindi in partes.
units.tr: Argument 7. Those who belong to God's people, like a field or a building, closely joined together, ought to serve the LORD. Therefore they ought not to be divided into parties from one another.

units.la: Verf. 10. Secundum gratiam Dei quae data est mihi, ut peritus architectus fundamentum posui: alius autem superaedificat. Porro unusquisque videat quomodo superaedificet.
units.tr: Verse 10. According to the grace of God which is given unto me, as a wise masterbuilder I have laid the foundation, and another buildeth thereon. But let every man take heed how he buildeth thereon.

units.la: Arg. 8. Sub admonitionis forma propositum, quo acrius pungat ambitiosos doctores, schismatis authores, qui certabant Philosophiae, & eloquentiae ostentatione, quisque sibi discipulos parare: Argumentum hoc est, Prope est periculum, ne dum singuli ordinarii doctores, ambitioni suae serviunt, aliquod genus doctrinae superstruant fundamento Apostolicae doctrinae, quod cum fundamento non congruat. Ergo schisma hoc non est fovendum.
units.tr: Argument 8. Put forward in the form of an admonition, so that it may sting the ambitious teachers, the authors of the schism, who vied with one another in displaying philosophy and eloquence, each seeking to win disciples for himself. The argument is this: there is a danger that, while individual ordinary teachers serve their ambition, they may build on the foundation of apostolic doctrine some kind of teaching that does not agree with that foundation. Therefore this schism is not to be fostered.

units.la: Verf. 11. Nam fundamentum aliud nemo potest ponere, praeter id quod positum est, quod est Iesus Christus.
units.tr: Verse 11. For other foundation can no man lay than that is laid, which is Jesus Christ.

units.la: Rationem reddit, cur ad solos ordinarios doctores, admonitionem de superstruendo dirigat, quia summa salutaris doctrinae de CHRISTO IESU, tanquam fundamentum firmum, & unicum, ab Apostolis positum est, à quo fundamento, nec ordinariis doctoribus, nec extraordinariis liceat discedere.
units.tr: He gives the reason why he directs the admonition about building to the ordinary teachers alone: the sum of saving doctrine concerning CHRIST JESUS, as a firm and sole foundation, has been laid by the apostles, and from this foundation neither ordinary nor extraordinary teachers may depart.

units.la: Verf. 12. Quod si quis superaedificet super fundamentum hoc aurum, argentum, lapides pretiosos, ligna, foenum, stipulam:
units.tr: Verse 12. Now if any man build upon this foundation gold, silver, precious stones, wood, hay, stubble;

units.la: Comparat ergo doctrinam Euangelii aedificio, Apostolos architectis, fundamenta omnis salutaris doctrinae ponentibus: reliquos post se doctores fabris murariis, fundamento ab Apostolis posito superstruentibus: quorum alii doceant solidam doctrinam, & quoad veritatem, & quoad spiritualem tractandi modum, fundamento consentaneam: alii vero sententias, & flores Philosophorum, & sapientiam verborum, praedicationi suae inferciant, quasi lignum, stipulam, foenum, materiam non solidam, nec ad salutem tendentem aedificantes.
units.tr: So he compares the doctrine of the Gospel to a building: the apostles are the master builders who lay the foundations of all saving doctrine, and the teachers who come after them are masons building upon the foundation laid by the apostles. Of these, some teach solid doctrine, both as to its truth and as to a spiritual manner of handling it, consonant with the foundation; others insert into their preaching the opinions and flowers of the philosophers and the wisdom of words, building with wood, stubble and hay, material that is not solid and does not tend to salvation.

units.la: Verf. 13. Cujusque opus manifestum fiet: dies enim declarabit: quia per ignem retegetur: & cujusque opus quale sit ignis probabit.
units.tr: Verse 13. Every man's work shall be made manifest: for the day shall declare it, because it shall be revealed by fire; and the fire shall try every man's work of what sort it is.

units.la: Ut hic periculum esse cognoscerent, probationem fore laborum uniuscujusque, in praedicando praedicit (non minus exactam, quam illa est aurifabrorum, in probandis metallis per ignem) in die scilicet illo novissimo saltem, quo DEUS judicaturus est, de omnium & personis & factis.
units.tr: So that they might know there is danger here, he foretells that the work of each man in preaching will be tested (no less exactly than the goldsmiths' testing of metals by fire), namely on that last day, at least, on which God is to judge both the persons and the deeds of all.

units.la: Verf. 14 Si cujus opus manserit, quod superaedificaverit, mercedem accipiet:
units.tr: Verse 14. If any man's work abide which he hath built thereupon, he shall receive a reward.

units.la: Quo saltem die, quicunque superstruxerat doctrinam solidam, pretiosam, fundamento congruentem, fidelitatis mercedem, secundum Dei promissiones, reportaturus est.
units.tr: On that day at least, whoever has built up solid, precious doctrine agreeing with the foundation is to receive, according to God's promises, the reward of faithfulness.

units.la: Verf. 15. Si cujus opus exustum fuerit, damnum faciet: ipse vero servabitur, ita tamen ut per ignem.
units.tr: Verse 15. If any man's work shall be burned, he shall suffer loss: but he himself shall be saved; yet so as by fire.

units.la: Si quis vero speculationes Philosophicas, humanae sapientiae foenum, & eloquentiae verbosae stipulam, praedicationibus suis admiscuerit, vel quodcunque aliud commentum suum addiderit, quod divini judicii sententiam ferre non poterit, jacturam faciet laborum suorum; ipse vero praedicator servabitur, sed tanquam per ignem, id est, modo igneam, seu accuratam probationem Dei, sustinere poterit, qua sinceros ab hypocritis tam accurate secernet, quam ignis scoriam a metallo purgat: Summa est, Ipse praedicator servabitur si sincerus, alioqui in fide CHRISTI compertus fuerit.
units.tr: But if anyone has mixed philosophical speculations, the hay of human wisdom, and the stubble of verbose eloquence into his preaching, or has added any other invention of his own that cannot stand the sentence of divine judgment, he will suffer the loss of his labours; yet the preacher himself will be saved, but as through fire, that is, he will be able to endure God's fiery and exact testing, by which he will separate the sincere from the hypocrites as thoroughly as fire purges the dross from metal. In short: the preacher himself will be saved if he is found sincere, and otherwise if he is found in the faith of CHRIST.

units.la: Verf. 16. An nescitis vos esse templum Dei, & Spiritum Dei habitare in vobis?
units.tr: Verse 16. Know ye not that ye are the temple of God, and that the Spirit of God dwelleth in you?

units.la: Arg. 9. Doctores pariter & auditores attingens, quia cum sciant se esse Dei templum, turpe esset Ecclesiam seu Templum Dei schismate violare, aut polluere, etiam ipsorum conscientia teste: Ergo schisma hoc non amplius fovendum, nisi Spiritui Dei inhabitanti injuriam facere vellent.
units.tr: Argument 9. This addresses both the teachers and the hearers. Since they know that they are God's temple, it would be shameful for them to violate or defile the Church, or the temple of God, by schism, and their own conscience would bear witness to this. Therefore this schism should no longer be nourished, unless they wish to do an injury to the Spirit of God who dwells in them.

units.la: Verf. 17. Siquis templum Dei violat, hunc perdet Deus: nam templum Dei sanctum est, quod estis vos.
units.tr: Verse 17. If anyone violates the temple of God, God will destroy him; for the temple of God is holy, and that is what you are.

units.la: Arg. 10. A pernicioso effectu: Periculum est, ne Deus vos, vanitatibus vestris, & dissensionibus, ipsius Templum polluentes, destruat. Ergo schisma hoc amplius non est fovendum.
units.tr: Argument 10, from the pernicious effect: there is a danger that God, polluting his own temple by your vanities and dissensions, will destroy it. Therefore this schism should no longer be nourished.

units.la: Verf. 18. Nullus seipsum seducat: si quis sibi videtur esse sapiens inter vos in hoc seculo, stultus fiat, ut fiat sapiens.
units.tr: Verse 18. Let no one deceive himself. If anyone among you seems to be wise in this world, let him become a fool, so that he may become wise.

units.la: Arg. 11. Per occupationem propositum; videmini vobis in hoc schismate fovendo, sapientes, verum ἰουδαϊσμὸς vestra, vos decipit, haec causa est schismatis, ideoque cavenda; ut caveatur schisma, cavendi modum praescribit, qui hic est, ut qui humana sapientia, pollere sibi videtur renunciet vanae opinioni de sapientia sua, & tradat se in obedientiam Dei, euangelizandi simplicitatem sequens, quæ simplicitas licet stultitia videatur hominibus, sola tamen sapientes potest reddere.
units.tr: Argument 11, from the anticipation of the purpose: you seem to yourselves wise in nourishing this schism, but your [ἰουδαϊσμὸς] Judaism deceives you. This is the cause of the schism, and so it must be guarded against. To guard against the schism, he prescribes the manner of guarding: whoever seems to himself to excel in human wisdom should renounce his empty opinion of his own wisdom and surrender himself to the obedience of God, following the simplicity of the gospel. This simplicity, although it seems foolishness to men, alone can make people wise.

units.la: Verf. 19. Sapientia enim mundi hujus, stultitia est apud Deum: scriptum est enim, Carpit sapientes in versutia ipsorum.
units.tr: Verse 19. For the wisdom of this world is foolishness with God; for it is written, He catches the wise in their own craftiness.

units.la: Verf. 20. Et rursum, Dominus novit cogitationes sapientum esse vanas.
units.tr: Verse 20. And again, the Lord knows that the thoughts of the wise are vain.

units.la: Confirmat consilium datum, à Judicio Dei, de carnali sapientia, quod Deus habeat eam pro stultitia, maximè quando carnalis sapientia rejicit Dei instituta, & eorum simplicitatem despicit: quod probat Scripturarum testimonio, primum est Jobi 5. 13. Cujus sensus est; utcunque vafri homines sibi & mundo, videntur sapientes hujus mundi, Deus tamen ipsorum artes ita eludit, ut eas in retia vertat, ut suis consiliis pereant, potius quam alienis; atque ita eos stultitiæ convincit. Alterum testimonium est, Pfal. 94. 11. In quo Deus pronunciat vanas esse cogitationes sapientum, qui humana tantum sapiunt, nam quæ ad beatitudinem suam putant conferre maximè, ea conferunt minimè.
units.tr: He confirms the counsel given by the judgment of God about carnal wisdom: God counts it as foolishness, especially when carnal wisdom rejects God's ordinances and despises their simplicity. He proves this by the testimony of Scripture. The first is Job 5. 13., whose sense is this: however crafty men may seem wise to themselves and to the world, God so frustrates their arts that he turns them into nets, so that they perish by their own counsels rather than by others', and thus convicts them of foolishness. The second testimony is Psal. 94. 11., where God pronounces the thoughts of the wise to be vain, namely of those who savour only of human things. For what they think contributes most to their happiness, that contributes least.

units.la: Verf. 21. Itaque nullus glorietur in hominibus; omnia namque vestra sunt:
units.tr: Verse 21. Therefore let no one glory in men; for all things are yours.

units.la: Verf. 22. Et Paulus, & Apollos, & Cephas: & mundus, & vita, & mors, & præsentia, & futura, omnia inquam, vestra sunt:
units.tr: Verse 22. Whether Paul, or Apollos, or Cephas, or the world, or life, or death, or things present, or things to come: all things, I say, are yours.

units.la: Arg. 12. Quo schisma reprehendit per dehortationem propositum; Quia schisma, & studium partium de Doctoribus, est impia gloriatio in hominibus: Ergo, schisma hoc non amplius fovendum: Gloriabantur in Doctoribus, quando illis nimium tribuentes, pendebant ab iis, ipsosque, fidei suæ quasi Dominos faciebant, cum debuissent à Deo solo pendere, qui per Ministros loquitur, quando, & quantum, vult.
units.tr: Argument 12. He rebukes the schism by way of dissuasion: because schism, and the zeal for parties over teachers, is an impious glorying in men. Therefore this schism should no longer be nourished. They gloried in their teachers when they attributed too much to them, depended on them, and made them, as it were, lords of their faith, whereas they ought to have depended on God alone, who speaks through the ministers when, and as much as, he wills.

units.la: Omnia Hanc dehortationem confirmans, addit Arg. 13. Quia omnes vestri Doctores, minimi maximique, etiam ipsi Apostoli, & omnia quæ sunt in mundo, præsentia & futura, vita & mors, & quæcunque alia recitari possunt, ut fidelium saluti promovendæ, inserviant, à Deo destinata sunt: Ergo, non debetis propter doctorum vestrorum inanem gloriam, vos in partes scindere, aut in Doctoribus vestris gloriari, quasi Doctorum essetis peculium.
units.tr: All things. Confirming this dissuasion, he adds Argument 13: because all your teachers, the least and the greatest, even the apostles themselves, and all things that are in the world, present and future, life and death, and whatever else can be mentioned, have been appointed by God to serve the promotion of the salvation of believers. Therefore you ought not, for the sake of your teachers' empty glory, to divide yourselves into parties, or glory in your teachers, as if you were the private property of the teachers.

units.la: Verf. 23. Vos autem Christi, Christus, vero Dei.
units.tr: Verse 23. But you are Christ's, and Christ is God's.

units.la: Arg. 14. Et ultimum, versu ult; quo Doctores, pariter & populum, & dona, & dignitatem omnium, ad fontem revocans, in ordinem redigit, ut a CHRISTO, & DEO solo pendeant, denominentur, & in eo glorientur: quia scilicet, ut noster est mundus, & omnia in mundo, tanquam ad bonum nostrum destinata, sic nos sumus CHRISTI, ab eo redempti, ut essemus ei peculium; CHRISTUS vero, consideratus personaliter, est DEI, ut Filius Patris dilectissimus, in opere redemptionis ad omne officium Mediatoris se humilians, idque in gloriam DEI essentialiter consideratí. Cui sit gloria. Amen.
units.tr: Argument 14, the last, in verse 23, by which he calls teachers and people alike, and gifts and dignity of all, back to the source, and brings them into order, so that they depend on Christ and God alone, are named from him, and glory in him. This is because, just as the world and all things in the world are ours, as if destined for our good, so we are Christ's, redeemed by him so that we might be his peculiar people; and Christ, considered personally, is God's, as the most beloved Son of the Father, humbling himself in the work of redemption to every office of Mediator, and this is essentially considered for the glory of God. To whom be glory. Amen.

units.la: Caput quartum.
units.tr: Chapter 4.

units.la: Icut inter Corinthos, magni fiebant doctores gloriosi, à suis sectatoribus, ita parvi fiebant Apostoli, aliique fideles Dei Ministri, quasi cum disertis illis eloquentiae Magistris, sive donis, sive prosperitatis splendore, nequaquam essent conferendi; hoc judicium, corrigendum docet Apostolus, & schisma amplius non fovendum.
units.tr: As among the Corinthians the glorious teachers were highly esteemed by their followers, so the Apostles and the other faithful ministers of God were held in low regard, as if they could in no way be compared with those eloquent masters, whether in gifts or in the splendour of prosperity. The Apostle teaches that this judgment must be corrected and the schism no longer fostered.

units.la: Capitis duae sunt partes. In prima, pravum hoc ipsorum judicium corrigit, ad verf. 14 In secunda reprehensionem totam de schismate claudit, ad finem. Correctionis temerarii judicii ipsorum de Apostolo, ipsiusque comitibus, & aliis fidelibus Ministris CHRISTI, & iniquae comparationis, horum cum suis doctoribus, Argumenta sunt novem, quae probant iniquam comparationem Ministrorum Evangelii inter se cavendam esse, nec temerarium judicium, ex donis, de quovis ferendum esse.
units.tr: The chapter has two parts. In the first he corrects this wrong judgment of theirs, to verse 14. In the second he closes the whole rebuke of the schism, to the end. The arguments for correcting their rash judgment of the Apostle, his companions and the other faithful ministers of Christ, and for the unfair comparison of these men with their own teachers, are nine. They prove that the unfair comparison of the ministers of the Gospel with one another must be avoided, and that no rash judgment on anyone's gifts should be passed.

units.la: Verf. 1. Sic de nobis reputet homo, ut de ministris Christi, & dispensatoribus mysteriorum Dei.
units.tr: Vers. 1. Let a man so account of us, as of the ministers of Christ and stewards of the mysteries of God.

units.la: Argumentum primum, Similitudine ab oeconomis sumpta propositum: Nos, quos despectui habetis, etiam si DOMINI fidei vestrae non simus; sumus tamen Ministri CHRISTI, ex quorum manu, thesaurum salutis, & panem vitae, accipere oportet; Ergo cavenda haec iniqua doctorum ex donis comparatio.
units.tr: The first argument, proposed by a comparison taken from stewards: we, whom you despise, even if we are not the masters of your faith, are nevertheless ministers of Christ, from whose hand you ought to receive the treasure of salvation and the bread of life. Therefore this unfair comparison of teachers by their gifts is to be avoided.

units.la: Verf. 2. Quod superest autem illud requiritur in dispensatoribus, ut quisque fidus reperiatur.
units.tr: Vers. 2. Moreover, it is required of stewards that a man be found faithful.

units.la: Arg. 2. Id quod commendat Ministrum Euangelii, non est donorum excellentia, sed in donorum, & mysterii salutis dispensatione fidelitas, cujus Deus solus est æquus æstimator. Ergo, cavenda hæc iniqua doctorum ex donis, comparatio.
units.tr: Arg. 2. What commends a minister of the Gospel is not the excellence of his gifts but his faithfulness in dispensing the gifts and the mystery of salvation, and of this faithfulness God alone is the impartial judge. Therefore this unfair comparison of teachers by their gifts is to be avoided.

units.la: Vers. 3. Mihi vero pro minimo est quòd à vobis dijudicer, aut ab humano judicio: imo nec ipse me dijudico.
units.tr: Vers. 3. But with me it is a very small thing that I should be judged by you, or by man's judgment; indeed I do not even judge myself.

units.la: Arg. 3. Quia neque vobis, neque hominum ulli, neque mihi ipsi Paulo competit judicium, de meo valore, aut dignitate: Cavenda Ergo hæc iniqua Doctorum comparatio: nam si Paulus non potuit statuere in quo gradu dignitatis ipse esset ponendus, temerarii erant Corinthii, qui de ipsius, & reliquorum Doctorum dignitate, pronunciabant.
units.tr: Arg. 3. Neither to you, nor to any man, nor to Paul himself, belongs the judgment of my worth or dignity. Therefore this unfair comparison of teachers is to be avoided. For if Paul could not decide what rank of dignity he himself should be placed in, then the Corinthians were rash, who pronounced on the dignity of himself and of the other teachers.

units.la: Vers. 4. In nullo enim mihi conscius sum: sed non per hoc justificatus sum: Dominus autem is est qui me dijudicat.
units.tr: Vers. 4. For I know nothing against myself; yet am I not thereby justified; but he who judges me is the Lord.

units.la: Arg. 4. Confirmans supeiius; ego Apostolus, etiam si non sim mihi conscius male administrati officii, non audeo tamen sententiam ferre, ad mei absolutionem, vel de dignitate mea pronunciare cum aliorum injuria, sed totum hoc judicium relinquo Deo soli: Ergo, cavenda hæc iniqua doctorum ex donis comparatio.
units.tr: Arg. 4. Confirming what goes before: I, the Apostle, even if I am not conscious of having administered my office badly, do not dare to pass sentence in my own favour or to pronounce on my dignity to the injury of others. I leave all this judgment to God alone. Therefore this unfair comparison of teachers by their gifts is to be avoided.

units.la: Vers. 5. Proinde ne ante tempus præstitutum judicis partes assumite: id est, usquedum venerit Dominus, qui & illustraturus est occulta tenebrarum, & manifesta faciet consilia cordium: ac tunc laus erit unicuique à Deo.
units.tr: Vers. 5. Therefore judge nothing before the appointed time, until the Lord comes, who will both bring to light the hidden things of darkness and make manifest the counsels of the hearts; and then every man shall have his praise from God.

units.la: Arg. 5. Dehortationis forma propositum; judicium, maxime, vero comparativum, de hominum dignitate, non est tempestivum, ante Domini adventum. Cavenda ergo hæc iniqua Doctorum ex donis comparatio.
units.tr: Arg. 5. This is a form of dissuasion. Judgment, especially comparative judgment, of men's dignity is not timely before the Lord's coming. Therefore this unfair comparison of teachers by their gifts is to be avoided.

units.la: Consilia ] Arg. 6. Confirmans etiam superius; Secretæ cordium intentiones, & abdita hominum consilia in Ministerio, non patefient, ante diem Judicii, nec de hominum excellentia, judicari poterit ab ullo homine, sed à solo Deo, qui laudem, & vituperium, pro dignitate, singulis eo die distribuet: Cavenda ergo iniqua doctorum ex donis comparatio.
units.tr: Counsels] Arg. 6. Confirming also what goes before: the secret intentions of hearts and the hidden counsels of men in the ministry will not be disclosed before the day of judgment. Nor can the excellence of men be judged by any man, but only by God alone, who on that day will distribute praise and blame to each according to his worth. Therefore this unfair comparison of teachers by their gifts is to be avoided.

units.la: Vers. 6. Hæc autem, fratres, figura quadam transstuli ad metipsum & Apollo, propter vos: ut in nobis discatis, supra id quod scriptum est non sapere, ut ne alius pro alio inflemini adversus alium. Arg. 7.
units.tr: Vers. 6. These things, brethren, I have in a figure transferred to myself and Apollos for your sakes, that in us you might learn not to think of men above what is written, so that none of you be puffed up for one against another. Arg. 7.

units.la: Argument. 7. Non licet donorum excellentissimorum nomine, qualia sunt in me Paulo Apostolo, & Apollo Euangelista, quenquam Ministrum extollere, supra id quod scriptum est versu primo hujus capitis, id est, supra dignitatem œconomi evehere, & multo minus, ex pravo judicio Doctores fideles deprimere, respectu hujus vel illius doctoris deamati. Cavenda igitur haec iniqua doctorum ex donis comparatio: Hujus argumenti vim ut ostendat, aperit prudentiae suae in hoc negotio artificium, nempe, quod celatis nominibus ambitiosorum doctorum, rem totam transtulerit ad nomen suum & Apollo, eo ipso fine, ut discerent Corinthii in horum persona, qui extraordinariis donis, & dignitate excellebant, modeste de omnibus ministris sentire, & non superbire, cujusvis doctoris nomine, adversus quenquam, ut ab ullo denominationem sumerent.
units.tr: Argument 7. It is not right, under the name of the most excellent gifts, such as those in me Paul the Apostle and in Apollos the evangelist, to exalt any minister above what is written in the first verse of this chapter, that is, to raise him above the dignity of a steward. Still less is it right, by a wrong judgment, to depress faithful teachers in favour of this or that beloved teacher. Therefore this unfair comparison of teachers by their gifts is to be avoided. To show the force of this argument, he reveals the cunning of his prudence in this matter. Having concealed the names of the ambitious teachers, he has transferred the whole matter to his own name and to Apollos' name, with this very aim: that the Corinthians, in the persons of those who excelled in extraordinary gifts and dignity, might learn to think modestly of all ministers, not to be proud, and not to take their names from any teacher against anyone.

units.la: Verf. 7. Quis enim te ab aliis discernit? quid autem habes quod non recepisti? quod si etiam accepisti, quid gloriaris quasi non receperis?
units.tr: Vers. 7. For who makes you to differ from another? And what do you have that you did not receive? Now if you did receive it, why do you glory, as if you had not received it?

units.la: Arg. 8, Deus discernit unum ab alio, plus minusve donorum pro voluntate sua, tribuens huic vel illi, nemo vero seipsum discernit: cum igitur quicquid donorum habeat unusquisque à Deo acceperit, gloriari & superbire de accepto non debet, sed modeste de se & aliis sentire. Cavenda ergo haec iniqua doctorum ex donis comparatio.
units.tr: Arg. 8. God distinguishes one man from another, giving more or fewer gifts according to his will, to this one or that one; but no one distinguishes himself. Since, therefore, whatever gifts each one has, he has received from God, he ought not to glory or be proud of what he has received, but to think modestly of himself and of others. Therefore this unfair comparison of teachers by their gifts is to be avoided.

units.la: Verf. 8. Iam saturati estis, jam ditati estis, absque nobis regnum adepti estis: atque utinam sane regnum adepti sitis, ut & nos simul vobiscum regnemus.
units.tr: Vers. 8. Now you are full, now you are rich, you have reached the kingdom without us; and would indeed that you had reached the kingdom, so that we might reign together with you.

units.la: Arg 9 Haec iniqua hominum comparatio, conjunctam habet ἀνδαςεια, stolidam: Cavenda ergo haec iniqua doctorum ex donis comparatio. Gravissima Ironia perstringit Apostolus hanc ἀνδαςεια: Quia Corinthii sibi non minus placebant in donis communibus, & prosperitate mundana, quam si donorum plenitudinem nacti essent, quam si plena felicitate, & regno potiti fuissent, degentes in pacata rerum prosperarum fruitione, immemores crucis Christi, & segregati à miseriis, in quibus haerebat Apostolus: Hanc vanitatem ita taxat, ut optet illis felicitatem quam somniabant se habere: ut ipsorum felicitas consolationem afferret Apostolis, qui in afflictionibus multis jacebant.
units.tr: Arg. 9. This unfair comparison of men is joined with a stupid arrogance [ἀλαζονεία]. Therefore this unfair comparison of teachers by their gifts is to be avoided. The Apostle rebukes this arrogance with the most severe irony. The Corinthians pleased themselves no less in ordinary gifts and worldly prosperity than if they had attained the fullness of gifts, as if they had gained full happiness and possessed the kingdom. They lived in the peaceful enjoyment of prosperous things, forgetful of the cross of Christ and cut off from the miseries in which the Apostle was held. He censures this vanity in such a way that he wishes them the happiness they dreamed they already had, so that their happiness might bring consolation to the Apostles, who lay in many afflictions.

units.la: Verf. 9. Deus enim, puto, nos ultimos Apostolos spectandos propojuit, proposuit, ut morti addiḉtos. Nam speḉtaculum facti sumus mundo, & Angelis & hominibus.
units.tr: Vers. 9. For I think that God has set forth us the last Apostles, as men appointed to death; for we have become a spectacle to the world, to angels and to men.

units.la: Exponit afflictiones suas, & Barnabæ, qui Apostolorum ultimi vocantur, quia post ascensionem Christi vocati, & ad Gentes, speciali mandato, missi erant, (ut est Act. 13. 2. & 14. 14) ostendens ipsos in conspectum omnium esse productos a Deo, ut cum omnis generis molestiis, conflictarentur.
units.tr: He sets out his own afflictions and those of Barnabas, who are called the last of the Apostles, because they were called after Christ's ascension and sent to the Gentiles by special command (as in Acts 13:2 and 14:14). He shows that God has brought them forth before the eyes of all, so that they might struggle with every kind of trouble.

units.la: Verf. 10. Nos stulti propter Christum, vos autem prudentes in Christo, nos infirmi, vos autem validi: vos gloriosi, nos ignominiosi.
units.tr: Vers. 10. We are fools for Christ's sake, but you are wise in Christ; we are weak, but you are strong; you are glorious, but we are ignominious.

units.la: Deinde, comparat suas ærumnas, cum ipsorum prosperitate, & iniquam opinionem ipsorum de seipsis & Apostolo, ostendit in tribus: 1. In sapientia; nos pro stultis habemur, & a mundo, & forsan a vobis, quod nos in tanta pericula, propter Christum conjiciamus; vos videmini vobis & aliis sapientes, quod & Euangelio & rebus prosperis fruamini:
units.tr: Next, he compares his hardships with their prosperity and with their unfair opinion of themselves and of the Apostle. He shows this in three respects. 1. In wisdom: we are regarded as fools by the world, and perhaps by you, because we expose ourselves to such great dangers for Christ; you seem to yourselves and to others wise, because you enjoy both the Gospel and prosperous circumstances.

units.la: 2. In potentia, nos infirmi apparemus, ærumnis fracti scilicet; vos videmini validi, & potentes, extra pugnam & teli jactum constitui: 3. In honore; vos gloria, & authoritate splendetis; nos interim ut ignominiosi, & a vobis & ab aliis despicimur.
units.tr: 2. In power: we appear weak, broken, that is, by our hardships; you seem strong and powerful, placed outside the battle and beyond the range of the missile. 3. In honour: you shine with glory and authority; meanwhile we, as ignominious men, are despised by you and by others.

units.la: Verf. 11. Ad hoc usque tempus & esurimus, & sitimus, & nudi sumus, & colaphis cædimur, & incertis sedibus erramus:
units.tr: Vers. 11. Even to this present hour we both hunger and thirst, and are naked, and are buffeted, and have no certain dwelling place;

units.la: Verf. 12. Et laboramus, operantes propriis manibus: conviciis affecti, bene precamur: si qui nos persequantur, sufferimus.
units.tr: Vers. 12. And we labour, working with our own hands; being reviled, we bless; being persecuted, we endure it;

units.la: Verf. 13. Maledictis affecti precamur tanquam purgamenta mundi facti sumus, & tanquam omnium ramentum usque adhuc.
units.tr: Verse 13. "Being slandered, we entreat; we have become as the filth of the world, and the offscouring of all things until now."

units.la: Alias species ærumnarum suarum recensét, expositi, inquit, fumus penuriæ & injuriis, verf. 11. non nostra culpa inopes, quia manibus laboramus; non nostro merito injurias patientes; tantum enim absumus ab injuriis, verbo vel facto cuiquam inferendis, ut contra pro malo bonum reponamus, cum patientia, verf. 12, 13.
units.tr: He recounts other kinds of his hardships: "We are made," he says, "hungry and thirsty, and in want, and struck with blows" (verse 11), and we are without means through no fault of our own, because we labour with our hands; we suffer injuries without any merit of our own. For we are so far from doing injury, by word or deed, to anyone, that on the contrary we return good for evil, with patience (verses 12, 13).

units.la: Verf. 14. Non ut vos pudore suffundam hæc scribo, sed ut filios meos dilectos admoneo.
units.tr: Verse 14. "I do not write these things to shame you, but to admonish you as my beloved sons."

units.la: Altera parte Capitis, claudit totam de schismate reprehensionem, primum hortatione ad obedientiam, & imitationem sui, ad verf. 18. Secundo, interminatione severioris disciplinæ, nili admoniti resipiscant: Quod ad primum attinet, quatuor affert argumenta, quæ ad obedientiam persuadeant.
units.tr: In the second part of the chapter he concludes the whole rebuke of the schism: first by an exhortation to obedience and to imitation of himself, up to verse 18; second, by a threat of stricter discipline if they do not repent when admonished. As to the first, he brings four arguments to persuade them to obedience.

units.la: Argumentum primum, In occupatione objectionis proponitur, Non pudefaciendi vos, sed monendi causa, hæc scripsi: Ergo obedite mihi.
units.tr: The first argument: in anticipation of an objection, he states that he wrote these things not to shame them but to admonish them. Therefore, obey me.

units.la: Filios ] Arg. 2. Vos habeo & diligo ut filios: Ergo boni consulentes meam admonitionem, obedite mihi.
units.tr: "My sons": the second argument. I have you and love you as sons; therefore, take my admonition in good part and obey me.

units.la: Verf. 15. Nam etsi decem millia pædagogorum habeatis in Christo, at non multos patres habetis: in Christo enim Iesu per Evangelium ego vos genui.
units.tr: Verse 15. "For though you have ten thousand tutors in Christ, yet you have not many fathers; for in Christ Jesus I have begotten you through the Gospel."

units.la: Verf. 16. Precor vos igitur imitatores mei estote.
units.tr: Verse 16. "I beg you therefore, be imitators of me."

units.la: Arg. 3. Speciali modo, comparatione facta cum aliis doctoribus, Pater vobis sum, quia per meum ministerium conversi estis; obedite igitur mihi, & imitamini meos mores, potius quam ambitiosorum doctorum. Ego enim CHRISTI sum minister in vestri regeneratione, non doctores illi ambitiosi, qui maximum pædagogi sunt, patres non sunt.
units.tr: The third argument: in a special way, by comparison with the other teachers, I am your father, because you were converted through my ministry; therefore obey me and imitate my ways rather than those of the ambitious teachers. For I am the minister of Christ in your regeneration; those ambitious teachers, who are indeed great tutors, are not fathers.

units.la: Verf. 17. Propterea misi vobis Timotheum, qui est filius meus dilectus, & fidelis in Domino, qui vobis in memoriam revocabit quæ sint viæ meæ in Christo, sicut ubique in omnibus Ecclesiis doceo.
units.tr: Verse 17. "For this reason I have sent to you Timothy, who is my beloved and faithful son in the Lord, who will remind you of my ways in Christ, as I teach everywhere in all the Churches."

units.la: Arg. 4. Eo fine misi Timotheum ad vos, ut imitationem mei faciliorem vobis redderem; obedite mihi, & imitamini me igitur, in quibus præluceo omnibus Ecclesiis, pro ratione Apostolatus mei, in doctrina & vitæ sanctitate.
units.tr: The fourth argument: for this end I sent Timothy to you, that I might make imitation of me easier for you; therefore obey me and imitate me, in whom I go before all the Churches, according to the measure of my apostleship, in doctrine and in holiness of life.

units.la: Verf. 18. Caterum perinde quasi ego non sim venturus ad vos, inflati sunt quidam.
units.tr: Verse 18. "But as though I were not coming to you, some have become puffed up."

units.la: Verf. 19. Sed veniam cito ad vos, si Dominus voluerit, & cognoscam non verba illorum inflatorum, sed virtutem.
units.tr: Verse 19. "But I will come to you soon, if the Lord wills, and I will know not the words of those puffed up, but their power."

units.la: Quod ad alteram conclusionis partem attinet; Quia aliqui inter eos superbiebant, spe impunitatis, quasi Apostolus ad eos non fuisset venturus,
units.tr: As to the other part of the conclusion: since some among them were proud, relying on the hope of impunity, as if the Apostle would never come to them,

units.la: Minatur 1. le venturum: 2. probaturum, utrum in illis doctoribus sit vis illa Spiritus DEI, an mera verbosa eloquentia, sine evidentia Spiritus.
units.tr: he threatens, first, that he will come; second, that he will test whether in those teachers there is that power of the Spirit of God, or mere verbal eloquence without the evidence of the Spirit.

units.la: Verf. 20. Non enim in verbis situm est regnum Dei, sed in spiritus potentia.
units.tr: Verse 20. "For the kingdom of God is not in words, but in power."

units.la: Rationem dat cur eloquentiam meram, aut humanæ sapientiæ ostentatione[m] ationem nihili sit facturus, quia regnum CHRISTI, & salus hominum seu ædificatio, non promovetur verbis, seu verborum sapientia, sed virtute DEI.
units.tr: He gives the reason why he will take no account of mere eloquence or the display of human wisdom: because the kingdom of Christ and the salvation, or edification, of men is not advanced by words, or by the wisdom of words, but by the power of God.

units.la: Vers. 21. Quid vultis? cum virga veniam ad vos, an cum charitate & Spiritu lenitatis?
units.tr: Verse 21. "What do you want? Shall I come to you with a rod, or with love and a spirit of gentleness?"

units.la: Denique, ne schisma foverent Corinthii ulli, sive doctores sive discipuli eorum sectatores, optionem facit illis, utrum velint ipsum accedere, ad ipsorum correctionem, cum authoritate censurarum Ecclesiasticarum, quod futurum erat, si studia partium, & schisma foverent amplius: an potius velint ipsum ad ipsorum consolationem venire, in spiritu dilectionis & mansuetudinis, quod futurum erat, si resipiscerent.
units.tr: Finally, lest any of the Corinthians, whether teachers or their followers, should foster the schism, he gives them a choice: whether they wish him to come to correct them with the authority of ecclesiastical censures, which would happen if they continued to foster factions and schism further; or rather whether they wish him to come to comfort them in a spirit of love and meekness, which would happen if they repented.

units.la: Atque ita transitum sibi facit ad excommunicationem incestuosi.
units.tr: And thus he makes a transition to the excommunication of the incestuous man.

units.la: Caput quintum.
units.tr: Chapter 5.

units.la: Articulus Secundus de incestuoso excommunicando.
units.tr: Article 2: On excommunicating the incestuous man.

units.la: E vanam putarent comminationem, de qua sub finem superioris Capitis, incestuosum, qui novercam habebat ut uxorem, excommunicari jubet, undecim plus minus in eum sincerè, propositis argumentis.
units.tr: Since they thought the warning at the end of the previous chapter was an empty one, the Apostle, in about eleven arguments, sincerely orders the incestuous man, who had his stepmother as his wife, to be excommunicated.

units.la: Omnino auditur esse inter vos scortatio, & ejusmodi scortatio, quæ ne inter Gentes quidem nominatur, adeo ut quis uxorem patris habeat.
units.tr: It is actually reported that there is fornication among you, and such fornication as is not even named among the Gentiles, namely that a man has his father's wife.

units.la: Argumentum primum, Quia incestuosus ille, est notorio scelere pollutus, de quo ne Gentes quidem, sine detestatione loquerentur: excommunicandus igitur.
units.tr: First argument: because that incestuous man is defiled by a notorious crime, about which even the Gentiles could not speak without detestation. He is therefore to be excommunicated.

units.la: Vers. 2. Et vos infiati estis, ac non potius luxistis, ut tolleretur è medio vestri qui facinus hoc patravit.
units.tr: Verse 2. And ye are puffed up, and have not rather mourned, that he that hath done this deed might be taken away from among you.

units.la: Arg. 2. Cum reprehensione Corinthiorum conjunctum: Quia vos jamprídem jampridem lugere flagitium & flagitiosum excommunicare debuisse tis, non vero flagitium excusare, extenuare, in materiam risus convertere, & quasi de facto inflati, gloriari.
units.tr: Argument 2. Joined with a rebuke of the Corinthians: because you ought long since to have mourned the crime and excommunicated the one who committed it. Instead you have excused it, belittled it, turned it into a matter for laughter, and, as if puffed up by the deed, have boasted.

units.la: Verf. 3. Enimverò ego ut absens corpore, præsens autem spiritu, jam ut præsens judicavi, ut is qui hoc ita perpetravit.
units.tr: Verse 3. For I verily, as absent in body but present in spirit, have judged already, as though I were present, concerning him that hath so done this deed.

units.la: Verf. 4. Vobis & meo Spiritu in nomine Domini nostri Iesu Christi congregatis, cum potestate Domini nostri Iesu Christi,
units.tr: Verse 4. In the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, when ye are gathered together, and my spirit, with the power of our Lord Jesus Christ,

units.la: Verl. 5. Eju'modi inquam homo tradatur Satanæ ad interitum carnis, ut spiritus salvus sit die illo Domini Iesu.
units.tr: Verse 5. To deliver such an one, I say, unto Satan for the destruction of the flesh, that the spirit may be saved in the day of the Lord Jesus.

units.la: Arg. 3. Quia jam præter ordinariam Potestatem, quam habetis in Senatu Ecclesiastico scilicet, per hanc Epistolam, etiam extraordinaria potestate ad ipsum excommunicandum armati & obligati estis; siquidem meam Apostoli absentis, quasi præsens essem, mentem seu Spiritum, judicium, sententiam, & authoritatem de flagitioso isto habetis: Ergo in legitimo conventu Ecclesiastico, Apostolico hoc scripto, (in quo mei Apostoli Spiritus, seu mens, seu sententia continetur) & Christi authoritate, (cujus nomine, censuræ Ecclesiæ exercendæ sunt) muniti, istiusmodi flagitiosum Satanæ tradite, seu excommunicate. Satanæ tradendum dicit, quia qui per excommunicationem honore Sanctorum Ecclesiastico quoad externam hominis conditionem dejectus, & ex Ecclesia ejectus est, idem etiam, quoad externam hominis conditionem, in Satanæ regno, servitio, & potestate esse declaratur. Civem enim est: etiam in externa Ecclesia (quæ Regnum Dei dicitur) honor est insignior quam extra Ecclesiam regnare. Qui igitur excommunicatur, Capitis diminutionem patitur maximam de statu, honore, existimatione cadit, & in subditis Diaboli censetur.
units.tr: Argument 3. Because you already have, besides the ordinary power you hold in the ecclesiastical senate, also an extraordinary power to excommunicate him, armed and bound by this letter. For you have the judgment, sentence and authority of my spirit or mind, as though I, the absent Apostle, were present, concerning this disgraceful man. Therefore, being fortified in a lawful ecclesiastical assembly by this apostolic writing, in which the spirit, mind and sentence of me, the Apostle, is contained, and by the authority of Christ, in whose name the censures of the Church are to be exercised, deliver this disgraceful man to Satan, that is, excommunicate him. He says "to be delivered to Satan," because the one who, by excommunication, is cast down from the honour of the holy ecclesiastical community as to his outward condition, and is thrown out of the Church, is likewise declared to be, as to his outward condition, in the kingdom, service and power of Satan. For there is a citizenship: even in the outward Church (which is called the Kingdom of God) there is a more distinguished honour than ruling outside the Church. Therefore whoever is excommunicated suffers the greatest diminution of his standing; he falls in status, honour and reputation, and is counted among the subjects of the Devil.

units.la: Exitium carnis ] Arg. 4. A fine excommunicationis, quasi per occupationem objectionis propositum: quia excommunicatio, est medium refipiscentiæ, & salutis; siquidem hac censura carnis superbia mortificari poterit, & nova creatura servari in die judicij. Excommunicandus est ergo.
units.tr: Destruction of the flesh] Argument 4. Taken from the end of excommunication, proposed as though by anticipating an objection: because excommunication is a means of repentance and salvation, since by this censure the pride of the flesh can be mortified and the new creature preserved in the day of judgment. The man is therefore to be excommunicated.

units.la: Verf. 6. Non est bona gloriatio vestra: An nescitis paululò fermenti totam massam fermentari?
units.tr: Verse 6. Your glorying is not good. Know ye not that a little leaven leaveneth the whole lump?

units.la: Arg. 5. Ne contagione tanti sceleris inficiatur & deformetur tota Ecclesia, sicut modico fermento fermentatur & accescit tota massa: Excommunicetur incestuosus ille, hoc argumentum repetita Corinthiorum reprehensione acuitur.
units.tr: Argument 5. Lest the whole Church be tainted and disfigured by the contagion of so great a crime, just as the whole lump is leavened and soured by a little leaven. Let that incestuous man be excommunicated; this argument is sharpened by the repeated rebuke of the Corinthians.

units.la: Vers. 7. Expurgate igitur vetus fermentum, ut sitis nova massa, sicut estis fermenti expertes. Etenim Pascha nostrum pro nobis sacrificatum est, nempe Christus.
units.tr: Verse 7. Purge out therefore the old leaven, that ye may be a new lump, as ye are unleavened. For even Christ our passover is sacrificed for us.

units.la: Continua allegoria propositum, Quia non minori diligentia, purganda est Ecclesia Christiana à scandalis, imò & corda Christianorum, ab omni veteris naturæ pravitate, quam olim sub lege Judæorum domicilia purgabantur, à fermento communi, ante pascha immolatum. Ergo, excommunicandus incestuosus, &c.
units.tr: The allegory, continued, sets out the point: the Christian Church must be cleansed from scandals with no less diligence, and indeed the hearts of Christians must be cleansed from all the wickedness of the old nature, just as under the law of the Jews the houses were purged of common leaven before the Passover was sacrificed. Therefore the incestuous man is to be excommunicated, etc.

units.la: ] Arg. 7. A commodo: danda est opera ut sitis nova, & sancta incorporatio, sancta massa, seu ut comperiamini novæ creaturæ, actu & facto, sicut estis obligatione, & professione infermentati, seu sancti: Ergo excommunicandus est iste.
units.tr: Argument 7. From advantage: care must be taken that you be a new and holy body, a holy lump, so that you may be found new creatures in deed and fact, just as you are by obligation and profession unleavened, that is, holy. Therefore this man is to be excommunicated.

units.la: ] Hoc argumentum confirmans addit octavum; Quia res significata paschatis, nempe Iesu Christi sacrificium, non minus obligat Christianos, ad officia, per festi celebrationem & ceremonias repræsentata, id est, ad curandum, ut sanctitas in nobis, & in Ecclesia vigeat, quam obligavit olim Judæos, ad ceremonias festi observandas, quibus typicus agnus paschalis immolatus proponebatur.
units.tr: Confirming this argument, he adds an eighth: because the thing signified by the Passover, namely the sacrifice of Jesus Christ, binds Christians no less to the duties represented through the celebration of the feast and its ceremonies. That is, they must take care that holiness flourishes in us and in the Church, just as it once bound the Jews to observe the ceremonies of the feast, by which the typical paschal lamb was set forth as sacrificed.

units.la: Vers. 8. Itaque festum agitemus, non fermento veteri, nec fermento malitiæ & nequitiæ: sed non fermentatis panibus sinceritatis & veritatis.
units.tr: Verse 8. Therefore let us keep the feast, not with old leaven, neither with the leaven of malice and wickedness, but with the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth.

units.la: Hinc infert quasi per conclusionem hortatoriam, Argumentum nonum, ut malitiâ & pravitate segregatâ, & à se ipsis, & ab Ecclesia; & per consequens, excommunicato illo incestuoso, cultui divino hilariter incumberent in veritate moralium officiorum, ut sic sanctè Deo servirent. Vis argumenti hæc est, Non poterimus vitam nostram sanctè & justè agere, sicut significatio Epuli agni paschalis typici à nobis exigit, nisi fermento veteris vitæ, & pravorum operum, ex nobisipsis, & ex domo Dei, seu Ecclesia, expurgato, sinceritati & veritati, in nobis & Ecclesia conservandæ studeamus. Excommunicandus igitur ille.
units.tr: From this he infers, as by a hortatory conclusion, a ninth argument: that, with malice and wickedness set apart both from themselves and from the Church, and consequently with that incestuous man excommunicated, they should cheerfully apply themselves to the worship of God, in the truth of moral duties, so that they might serve God in holiness. The force of the argument is this: we cannot live our lives holily and justly, as the meaning of the feast of the typical paschal lamb requires of us, unless we strive to keep sincerity and truth in ourselves and in the Church, with the leaven of the old life and of wicked works purged out of ourselves and out of the house of God, that is, the Church. Therefore that man is to be excommunicated.

units.la: Vers. 9. Scripsi vobis in epistola, ne commisceamini cum fornicatoribus.
units.tr: Verse 9. I wrote unto you in an epistle not to company with fornicators.

units.la: Quia per Epistolam, prius vetuerat eos, cum scortatoribus commercium habere, & per consequens intelligere poterant scortatores ab Ecclesia excommunicandos esse, & multò magis incestu pollutos: Ergo jam excommunicandus ille incestuosus.
units.tr: Because in an earlier letter he had forbidden them to have dealings with fornicators, they could understand that fornicators were to be excommunicated from the Church, and much more so those polluted by incest. Therefore that incestuous man is now to be excommunicated.

units.la: Verf. 10. At non omnino cum scortatoribus hujus mundi, aut avaris, aut rapacibus, aut idololatris: alioquin debetis scilicet è mundo exire.
units.tr: Verse 10. Yet not altogether with the fornicators of this world, or with the covetous, or extortioners, or with idolaters; for then must ye needs go out of the world.

units.la: Ne excusarent se, ostendit praeceptum illud, non potuisse intelligi ab iis, de vitiosis hominibus, qui in mundo erant, seu extra Ecclesiam; quia sic praecepisset Apostolus impossibile; quoniam inter istiusmodi vitiosos necessario erat ipsis vivendum, vel discedendum de mundo: vivebant enim Corinthi, cujus cives (quibuscum necessarium erat fidelibus commercium civile) maximâ ex parte, manebant infideles.
units.tr: To forestall their excuse, he shows that this command could not be understood by them as referring to wicked men who were in the world, that is, outside the Church. For in that case the Apostle would have commanded the impossible, since they necessarily had to live among such wicked men or else leave the world. They lived at Corinth, whose citizens (with whom the faithful necessarily had civil dealings) for the most part remained unbelievers.

units.la: Verf. 11. Nunc autem scripsi vobis ne commiscearmini, id est, si quis quum frater nominetur, sit scortator, aut avarus, aut idololatra, aut conviciator, aut ebriosus, aut rapax: cum ejusmodi, inquam, ne edatis quidem.
units.tr: Verse 11. But now I have written unto you not to keep company, if any man that is called a brother be a fornicator, or covetous, or an idolater, or a railer, or a drunkard, or an extortioner; with such an one, I say, no not to eat.

units.la: Arg. 11. Si non satis hac in re instructi fuistis prius, saltem jam tenetis mentem meam, quam ex hac Epistola audiviistis, non edendum cum profesiore, seu fratre scortatore, & per consequens, excommunicandum esse illum fratrem, qui vitiorum ab Ecclesia convictus, manet vitiosus, nec resipiscit: Ergo jam incestuosum excommunicandum esse multò magis colligere debetis.
units.tr: Argument 11. If you were not sufficiently instructed in this matter before, you now at least hold my mind, which you have heard from this letter: one must not eat with a fornicator, that is, a brother who is a fornicator. Consequently that brother, who, convicted of vices, remains vicious and does not repent, is to be excommunicated. Therefore from this you ought to infer much more that the incestuous man is now to be excommunicated.

units.la: Verf. 12. Quid enim mea interest etiam de extraneis judicare? nonne de iis qui intus sunt, vos judicatis?
units.tr: Verse 12. For what have I to do to judge them also that are without? Do not ye judge them that are within?

units.la: Verf. 13. De extraneis verò Deus judicat, tollite igitur ipsum scelératum ex vobisipsis.
units.tr: Verse 13. But them that are without God judgeth. Therefore put away from among yourselves that wicked person.

units.la: Alia ratio expositionis datae, & Argumentum 12. ad excommunicandum incestuosum urgens, quia ex eo quod in eos qui extra Ecclesiam sunt, nec Apostolus, nec Ecclesia, sed solus Deus jus habeat judicandi, seu censuras Ecclesiasticas exercendi, Colligere debuerant ad seipsos pertinere judicium de Ecclesiae membris, Ergo incestuosus ille improbus per excommunicationem tollendus ex ipsis erat, qui scopus est totius Capitis.
units.tr: Another explanation of the passage given, and Argument 12, pressing for the excommunication of the incestuous man: since neither the Apostle nor the Church, but God alone, has the right to judge those who are outside the Church, or to exercise ecclesiastical censures, they ought to conclude that the judgment concerning the members of the Church belongs to themselves. Therefore that wicked incestuous man was to be removed from among them by excommunication, which is the aim of the whole chapter.

units.la: Caput sextum.
units.tr: Chapter 6.

units.la: Articulus tertius & quartus de forensi contentione, & fornicatione vitanda.
units.tr: The third and fourth article: on avoiding lawsuits before the courts and on avoiding fornication.

units.la: HOC Capite tractantur tertius & quartus Epistolæ articulus, de vitanda litigatione coram tribunali infidelium, ad verf. 12. & fornicatione vitanda, ad finem.
units.tr: In this chapter are treated the third and fourth article of the Epistle: on avoiding litigation before the tribunal of unbelievers, at verse 12, and on avoiding fornication, to the end.

units.la: Verf. 1. Sustinet aliquis vestrûm, negotium habens adversus alterum, judicio experiri sub injustis, ac non sub sanctis:
units.tr: Verse 1. Does any of you, having a matter against another, dare to go to law before the unrighteous and not before the saints?

units.la: Non esse Christianis litigandum sub Ethnicis judicibus, probat undecim argumentis. Argumentum primum. Audax est & pudendum facinus, cum suppetunt sancti judices, sub infidelibus judicio experiri. Ergo non litigandum sub judicibus infidelibus.
units.tr: That Christians must not go to law before heathen judges, he proves by eleven arguments. First argument. It is a bold and shameful deed to go to law before unbelievers when holy judges are available. Therefore one must not go to law before unbelieving judges.

units.la: Verf. 2. An ignoratis sanctos mundum judicaturos? quod si per vos de mundo judicium feretur, indigni estis minimis judiciis?
units.tr: Verse 2. Do you not know that the saints shall judge the world? And if the world is to be judged by you, are you unworthy of the smallest judgements?

units.la: Arg 2. Sancti qui judicaturi sunt mundum, digni sunt multò magis de rebus hujus seculi judicare: Ergo non sub infidelibus litigandum.
units.tr: Second argument. Those saints who are to judge the world are much more worthy to judge the affairs of this age. Therefore one must not go to law before unbelievers.

units.la: Verf. 3. An ignoratis fore ut Angelorum judices simus? nedum ut de iis quæ ad hujus vitæ usum pertinent, judices non simus?
units.tr: Verse 3. Do you not know that we shall judge angels? How much more the things that pertain to this life?

units.la: Arg. 3. Sancti judicaturi sunt Angelos, nempe malos, in die judicii, & multò magis digni sunt qui de rebus temporalibus judicent: Non ergo sub infidelibus litigandum: dicuntur sancti, mundum & Angelos judicaturi, quia ipsi jam judicio absoluti, CHRISTO quasi assessores in judicio, sententiæ judicis in hostes DEI & Ecclesiæ acclamabunt.
units.tr: Third argument. The saints are to judge the angels, namely the evil ones, on the day of judgement, and much more are they worthy to judge temporal matters. Therefore one must not go to law before unbelievers. They are said to judge the world and the angels because, already absolved of judgement, they will sit with Christ as assessors in the judgement and cry out the sentence of the judge against the enemies of God and of the Church.

units.la: Verf. 4 Itaque si judicia habeatis de iis quæ ad hujus vitæ usum pertinent, eos qui vilissimi sunt in Ecclesia, eos inquam in subselliis collocate.
units.tr: Verse 4. So if you have judgements concerning things that pertain to this life, set those who are least esteemed in the Church, I say, to sit on the benches.

units.la: Arg. 4. Potius constituendi sunt arbitri, qui minimi in Ecclesia æstimantur, quam ad infideles judices confugiendum. Ergo, &c.
units.tr: Fourth argument. Rather, those who are esteemed least in the Church should be appointed as arbiters than that one should flee to unbelieving judges. Therefore, etc.

units.la: Verf. 5. Vobis ad verecundiam adducendis hoc dico. Itane non est inter vos sapiens, ne unus quidem, qui possit judicium ferre inter fratres suos?
units.tr: Verse 5. I say this to shame you. Is there not among you a single wise man who could pass judgement between his brothers?

units.la: Hoc argumentum corrigit, ostendendo se velle, non simpliciter arbitros inepiffimos inter ipsos constitui, sed velle se hac comparativa concessione, ab eo quod agebant, pudore ipsos avocare.
units.tr: This argument corrects itself, showing that he does not mean simply that the most unskilled men should be appointed as arbiters among them, but that by this comparative concession he wishes to call them back from what they were doing by means of shame.

units.la: Itaque Arg. 5. Habetis inter vos sapientes, & tamen confugitis ad tribunalia profana, quasi desint inter vos viri sapientes, qui arbitri esse possint controversiarum: Ergo non amplius sic agendum.
units.tr: So fifth argument. You have wise men among you, and yet you flee to profane tribunals, as if there were no wise men among you who could be arbiters of disputes. Therefore this must no longer be done.

units.la: Verf. 6. Sed frater cum fratre judicio experitur, idque sub infidelibus.
units.tr: Verse 6. But brother goes to law with brother, and that before unbelievers.

units.la: Arg. 6. Cum fratres estis, non debetis inter vos judicio contendere: Ergo minime sub infidelibus.
units.tr: Sixth argument. Since you are brothers, you ought not to contend in judgement among yourselves. Therefore by no means before unbelievers.

units.la: Verf. 7. Jam igitur omnino defectus in vobis est quod judicia habeatis inter vosmetipsos, quare non potius injuriam patimini? cur non potius damnum accipitis:
units.tr: Verse 7. Now therefore there is altogether a fault in you, that you have lawsuits among yourselves. Why do you not rather suffer wrong? Why do you not rather accept loss?

units.la: Arg. 7. Lites & contentiones probant, & produnt vestram impotentiam, defectus & delictum: Ergo non litigandum praecipue non sub infidelibus.
units.tr: Seventh argument. Lawsuits and contentions prove and reveal your weakness, your defect and your fault. Therefore one must not go to law, especially not before unbelievers.

units.la: Quare Arg. 8. Praestaret, actores injuriam sive damnum pati potius, quam cum scandalo litigare: Ergo non litigandum praecipue non sub infidelibus.
units.tr: Wherefore eighth argument. It would be better for plaintiffs to suffer wrong or loss than to litigate with scandal. Therefore one must not go to law, especially not before unbelievers.

units.la: Verf. 8. At vos injuria afficitis, & fraudatis, idque fratres.
units.tr: Verse 8. But you wrong and defraud, and that your brothers.

units.la: Arg. 9. Actorum actio, inter vos, est cum injuria, & fraudatione fratrum conjuncta, scilicet quia actores vindictae cupiditate, superbia, & avaritia laborant: Ergo litigatio injusta est, & maxime sub infidelibus.
units.tr: Ninth argument. The action of plaintiffs among you is joined with wrong and with the defrauding of brothers, namely because the plaintiffs labour under the desire for revenge, pride and avarice. Therefore litigation is unjust, and especially before unbelievers.

units.la: Verf 9. An ignoratis injustos non esse Dei hereditatem possessuros? Ne erraste? neque fornicatores, neque idololatrae, neque mochi, neque molles, neque qui concumbunt cum masculis.
units.tr: Verse 9. Do you not know that the unrighteous shall not inherit the kingdom of God? Do not be deceived: neither fornicators, nor idolaters, nor adulterers, nor effeminate, nor abusers of themselves with mankind.

units.la: Verf. 10. Neque fures, neque avari, neque ebriosi, neque conviciatores, neque rapaces, regni Dei hereditatem possidebunt.
units.tr: Verse 10. Neither thieves, nor covetous, nor drunkards, nor revilers, nor extortioners, shall inherit the kingdom of God.

units.la: Arg. 10. Hae injustae litigationes sicut reliquae species, iniquitatis & abominandae impuritatis, quae hic recensentur, a regno Coelorum homines arcebunt: Ergo non litigandum.
units.tr: Tenth argument. These unjust litigations, like the other kinds of iniquity and abominable impurity that are listed here, will shut men out of the kingdom of heaven. Therefore one must not go to law.

units.la: Verf. 11. Et haec eratis quidam, sed abluti estis, sed sanctificati estis, sed justificati estis in nomine Domini Iesu, & per Spiritum Dei nostri. Arg. II. & ultimum; Cum vos Corinthii, omnibus his aut pluribus aut saltem aliquo ex his vitiis prædictis, olim fœdati fueritis, & nunc quantum licet ex charitate de vobis judicare, remissionem peccatorum fitis consecuti & sanctificati per Spiritum, & justitia CHRISTI donati, Cavendum vobis est, (ex CHRISTI gratia & virtute haultis viribus) ne in easdem sordes rursum recidatis, five lites injustas aliis movendo, sive alio quovis modo vos polluendo.
units.tr: Verse 11. And such were some of you; but you are washed, but you are sanctified, but you are justified in the name of the Lord Jesus, and by the Spirit of our God. Eleventh and last argument. Since you Corinthians were formerly defiled with all these vices, or with most of them, or at least with some of them, and now, as far as one may judge charitably of you, you have obtained remission of sins, have been sanctified by the Spirit and clothed with the righteousness of Christ, you must take care (by the grace and power of Christ, with all your strength) lest you fall back again into the same filth, either by stirring up unjust lawsuits against others or by polluting yourselves in any other way.

units.la: Verf. 12 Omnia mihi licent, at non omnia conducunt: omnia mihi licent, at ego non redigar sub ullius rei potestatem.
units.tr: Verse 12. All things are lawful for me, but all things are not expedient: all things are lawful for me, but I will not be brought under the power of anything.

units.la: Altera pars Capitis, quartum Epistolæ articulum continens, de vitanda fornicatione simplici, quæ vocatur, quam Corinthii, sicut alii ex gentibus, pro re indifferenti habebant: Aggreditur reprehensionem, occupatione defensionis quam in parato habebant: dicerent Corinthii, Indifferentia omnia nobis licent; At sicut cibus, sic & scortatio est indifferens; Ergo nobis licet. Respondet primum in genere, per limitationem majoris, licere scilicet omnia indifferentia, quatenus conducunt, & licere, modo ne intemperanti libertatis usu in servitium affectuum nostrorum redigamur: In illis enim & similibus casibus, peccatur in rerum indifferentium usu.
units.tr: The second part of the chapter, containing the fourth article of the Epistle, is on avoiding simple fornication, as it is called, which the Corinthians, like other Gentiles, regarded as a matter of indifference. He takes up the rebuttal, by means of the defence which they had ready: the Corinthians would say, All indifferent things are lawful for us; but just as food is indifferent, so too is fornication indifferent; therefore it is lawful for us. He answers first in general, by limiting the major premise: namely, that all indifferent things are lawful, insofar as they are expedient, and lawful provided that we are not brought, by an intemperate use of liberty, into the slavery of our passions. For in those and similar cases one sins in the use of indifferent things.

units.la: Verf. 13. Esca ventri destinatæ sunt, & venter escis: Deus autem & hunc, & eas abolebit: corpus vero non fornicationi, sed Domino, & Dominus corpori.
units.tr: Verse 13. Meats are for the belly, and the belly for meats: but God shall destroy both it and them. Now the body is not for fornication, but for the Lord; and the Lord for the body.

units.la: Deinde ad minorem respondet specialiter; discrimen ostendens ciborum & fornicationis; de cibis concedens, quod sit licitum cibo quovis esci, quia DEUS ad bonum naturæ ordinavit esas ventri, & ventrem esciis, sed tamen temporariâ connexione; nam sicut escas, sic ventrem abolebit DEUS, quoad usum quem nunc habet venter, ita ut in gratiam gulæ, aut ventris non debeamus adducere æternam salutem nostram, aut aliorum in discrimen, edendo cum scandalo. Quod vero ad fornicationem attinet, negat ullâ necessitate licitam esse, sicut cibus licitus est, sed simpliciter esse peccatum & fugiendum; idque probat sex argumentis:
units.tr: Then he answers the minor premise specifically, showing the difference between foods and fornication. He concedes concerning foods that any food may be eaten lawfully, because God has ordained meats for the belly and the belly for meats for the good of nature, but with a temporary connection; for as God shall destroy the meats, so he shall destroy the belly, as far as the present use of the belly goes. Thus we ought not to bring our eternal salvation, or the peril of others, into danger for the sake of gluttony or the belly, by eating with scandal. As for fornication, however, he denies that it is lawful by any necessity, as food is lawful, but says that it is simply sin and to be fled from. He proves this by six arguments:

units.la: Argumentum primum. Quia corpus non est conditum ad fornicationem, aut ad fornicationem ordinatum, sicut venter ad escas & escæ ad ventrem, sed ut sit membrum CHRISTI DOMINI, qui ordinatus est ut sit caput hominis, ad totum corpus regendum; ut sanctum conservetur; Ergo fornicatio minime licita est.
units.tr: First argument. Because the body was not made for fornication, nor ordained to fornication, as the belly is for meats and meats for the belly, but that it might be a member of Christ the Lord, who was ordained to be the head of man, to govern the whole body, so that it might be kept holy. Therefore fornication is by no means lawful.

units.la: Vers. 14. Deus autem & Dominum suscitavit, & nos suscitabit potentiâ suâ.
units.tr: Verse 14. And God hath both raised up the Lord, and will also raise up us by his own power.

units.la: Arg. 2. Corpora in resurrectione gloriosa sunt suscitanda, sicut suscitatum est Christi corpus: Ergo non debent scortatione foedari.
units.tr: Second argument. Bodies are to be raised in glorious resurrection, just as Christ's body was raised. Therefore they ought not to be defiled by fornication.

units.la: Vers. 15. An ignoratis corpora vestra ipse membra Christi? Num igitur tollens membra Christi, faciam ut sint scorti membra? Absit.
units.tr: Verse 15. Know ye not that your bodies are the members of Christ? Shall I then take the members of Christ, and make them the members of an harlot? God forbid.

units.la: Arg. 3. Fideles qui sunt membra Christi, non sunt per fornicationem scorti membra facienda, quod argumentum interrogatione acuit. Ergo, &c.
units.tr: Third argument. The faithful, who are members of Christ, are not to be made members of a harlot through fornication, which the argument sharpens by means of a question. Therefore, etc.
