units.la: Athenus de Idolothytis ex concessione, quasi essent indifferentia, disputavit: Hoc Capite, Idolothytorum usum duplicem statuit, alterum publicum in Idoleio, & simpliciter illicitum, ad verf. 23. Alterum privatum in privatis ædibus, quem extra casum scandali, licitum facit, sed in casu scandali, illicitum pronunciat, & ab eo dehortatur, ad finem. Quod ad publicum illum idolothytorum esum in idoleio, ab eo dissuadet, quinque argumentis.
units.tr: Athenus argued about things offered to idols, granting that they were indifferent. In this chapter he lays down a twofold use of idol-meats: the public use, eating in the idol's temple, which he holds to be simply unlawful (to verse 23); and the private use, eating in private houses, which he allows outside the case of offence but declares unlawful in the case of offence, and dissuades from, to the end. As for the public eating of idol-meats in the temple, he dissuades from it by five arguments.

units.la: Verf. 1. Nolim autem vos ignorare fratres, Patres nostros omnes sub illa nube fuisse, & omnes per mare transivisse.
units.tr: Verse 1. For I would not have you ignorant, brethren, that our fathers were all under that cloud, and all passed through the sea.

units.la: Verf. 2. Et omnes in Mosen baptizatos esse, nube & mari.
units.tr: Verse 2. And were all baptized unto Moses in the cloud and in the sea.

units.la: Argumentum primum: Periculum est ne incidatis in ea peccata & pœnas, in quæ inciderunt Israelitæ, si Idolothyta concupiscere & Idololatricis conviviis interesse pergatis. Ergo Idolothytis, in Idoleio non est vescendum.
units.tr: First argument: There is danger that you fall into the same sins and punishments into which the Israelites fell, if you continue to desire idol-meats and to take part in idolatrous feasts. Therefore one must not eat idol-meats in the temple.

units.la: Ut paritas exempli Israelitarum appareat; ostendit privilegia paria habuisse eos nobiscum: quia Israelitæ patres fuerunt nostri: non Judæorum tantum, sed etiam Christianorum inter Gentes, scilicet in veræ religionis professione, & propagatione ad nos ipsorum posteros: nam quemadmodum Patres solent dici, qui antiquis temporibus, cum certa aliqua ad nos propagandæ religionis relatione, vixerunt: sic Israelitas vocat patres nostros, quia præcesserunt in ejusdem religionis, in ejusdem fœderis, & in Sacramentorum analogorum participatione. Nam sub nube & mari, quæ capitibus ipsorum imminebant, ambulantes, quasi nobiscum baptizabantur in Moisis doctrinam, & professionem externam salutis, per Messiam obtinendæ.
units.tr: So that the parallel with the example of the Israelites may appear, he shows that they had privileges like ours, because the Israelites were our fathers: not only of the Jews but also of the Christians among the Gentiles, namely in the profession of the true religion and in its propagation down to us, their posterity. For just as those are commonly called fathers who lived in ancient times in some definite connection with the propagation of religion to us, so he calls the Israelites our fathers, because they went before us in the same religion, in the same covenant, and in the participation of the analogous sacraments. For walking under the cloud and the sea, which hung over their heads, they were baptized, as it were with us, into the doctrine of Moses and the outward profession of salvation to be obtained through the Messiah.

units.la: Verf. 3 Et omnes eandem escam spiritualem ediderunt.
units.tr: Verse 3. And all ate the same spiritual food.

units.la: Verf. 4. Et omnes eundem potum spiritualem bibisse. Bibebant enim ex sequente spirituali Petra: Petra vero illa erat Christus.
units.tr: Verse 4. And all drank the same spiritual drink. For they drank from the spiritual rock that followed them, and that rock was Christ.

units.la: Verf. 5. Sed plerosque illorum non habuit gratos Deus: prostrati sunt enim in deserto.
units.tr: Verse 5. But God was not pleased with most of them, for they were overthrown in the wilderness.

units.la: Eădem etiam quasi cæna Domini nobiscum participabant, edentes manna & bibentes de petra, seu aquis ex petra fluentibus, quæ sequebantur castra Israelitarum (quæ dicuntur spiritualis cibus, & potus, quia significationem spiritualem habebant, eandem Christi gratiam figurantia, quam cæna Domini) & tamen, quia Deo displicebant multi ex iis Israelitis perierunt in deserto.
units.tr: They also partook with us, as it were, of the Lord's Supper, eating the manna and drinking from the rock, or from the waters flowing out of the rock which followed the camp of Israel. These are called spiritual food and drink because they had a spiritual meaning, prefiguring the same grace of Christ that the Lord's Supper does. Yet, because God was displeased with many of those Israelites, they perished in the wilderness.

units.la: Verf. 6. Hæc autem typi nostri fuerunt, ut ne concupiscamus res malas, sicut illi concupiverunt.
units.tr: Verse 6. Now these things were our types, so that we should not lust after evil things, as they lusted.

units.la: Deinde, peccata enumerat propter quæ plagas & mortem illis in exemplum posteritatis inflixit Deus: à quibus peccatis Apostolus dehortatur Corinthios, ne etiam pereant; & primò in genere hortatur, ne concupiscant res malas, sicut illi, id est, ne indulgeant carnalibus suis cupiditatibus, sicut veteres illi Israelitæ, qui cupiditatibus suis abripiebantur extra metas à Deo positas.
units.tr: Next he lists the sins for which God inflicted plagues and death on them, as an example to posterity, and from which the Apostle warns the Corinthians, lest they also perish. First he exhorts in general that they should not lust after evil things, as those did; that is, they should not indulge their carnal desires as those ancient Israelites did, who were carried by their desires beyond the bounds set by God.

units.la: Verf. 7. Neque igitur idololatræ fiatis sicut quidam eorum, ut scriptum est, Sedit populus ad edendum ac bibendum: & surrexerunt ad ludendum.
units.tr: Verse 7. Neither therefore become idolaters, as some of them were, as it is written: The people sat down to eat and drink, and rose up to play.

units.la: Verf. 8. Neque fornicemur, sicut quidam eorum fornicati sunt, & ceciderunt uno die viginti tria millia.
units.tr: Verse 8. Neither let us commit fornication, as some of them committed fornication, and fell in one day, twenty-three thousand.

units.la: Verf. 9. Neque tentemus Christum, sicut quidam eorum tentarunt, & à serpentibus perierunt.
units.tr: Verse 9. Neither let us tempt Christ, as some of them tempted him, and perished by the serpents.

units.la: Verf. 10. Neque murmurate, sicut etiam quidam eorum murmurarunt, & perierunt à disperditore.
units.tr: Verse 10. Neither murmur, as some of them also murmured, and perished by the destroyer.

units.la: 2. In specie monet, ne sint Idololatræ, vel fornicatores, vel tentatores Christi (periculum facientes de Christi veritate, & justitia, idque modis illicitis) vel murmuratores adversus Dei providentiam, sicut de Israelitis testatur Scriptura. Hujus dehortationis sensus hic est: Ne interfitis conviviis Idolatricis, in honorem Idoli cujusvis agitatis, ne idem patiamini quod Israelitæ, in honorem vituli aurei sacrificantes, quibus gulæ & luxui indulgere, pro religione erat, verf 7. Ne abripiamini studio placendi Idololatriis, ut in eorum gratiam, misceamini cum iis, in conviviis Idolatricis, ne etiam tradat vos Deus cupiditatibus cordium veltrorum, ut cum animarum pollutione, foedetis deris etiam corpora vestra fornicationibus, & adulteriis, & sic pereatis cum Israelitis illis, verf. 8. Ne tentetis Christum, abutentes ejus cognitione, & libertatem Christianam praetexentes vestris cupiditatibus, quod nihil est aliud, quam Christum ad certamen provocare: Sicut Israelitae in deserto, provocarunt Angelum foederis, seu Christum, qui iis praeibat in deserto, & a serpentibus perierunt, verf. 9. Denique ne murmuretis, quod non liceat vobis per religionem Christianam, amicorum vestrorum Idololatricis conviviis in Idoleio interesse, ne cum Israelitis murmurantibus pereatis, verf. 10.
units.tr: 2. He warns in particular that they should not be idolaters, or fornicators, or tempters of Christ (putting Christ's truth and justice to the test, and that by unlawful means), or murmurers against God's providence, as Scripture bears witness concerning the Israelites. The sense of this dissuasion is as follows. Do not take part in idolatrous feasts, held in honour of any idol, lest you suffer what the Israelites suffered when they sacrificed in honour of the golden calf, to whom indulging in gluttony and luxury was part of their religion (verse 7). Do not be carried away by the eagerness to please idolaters, so that for their sake you mix with them at idolatrous feasts, lest God also hand you over to the desires of your hearts, so that, with the defiling of your souls, you also defile your bodies with fornications and adulteries, and so perish with those Israelites (verse 8). Do not tempt Christ, by abusing your knowledge of him and pretending Christian liberty as a cover for your desires, which is nothing other than to provoke Christ to a contest, just as the Israelites in the wilderness provoked the Angel of the covenant, or Christ, who went before them in the wilderness, and perished by the serpents (verse 9). Finally, do not murmur that it is not permitted to you, by the Christian religion, to take part in your friends' idolatrous feasts in the temple, lest you perish as the murmuring Israelites did (verse 10).

units.la: Verf. 11.
units.tr: Verse 11.

units.la: Haec autem omnia typice evenerunt eis: scripta vero sunt ad nostri admonitionem, in quos fines saeculorum devenerunt.
units.tr: Now all these things happened to them as types, and they were written for our admonition, upon whom the ends of the ages have come.

units.la: Verf. 12.
units.tr: Verse 12.

units.la: Itaque qui sibi videtur stare, videat ne cadat.
units.tr: Therefore let him who thinks he stands take heed lest he fall.

units.la: Horum exemplorum usum, postquam ostendit pertinere ad omnes viventes, reliquosque qui victuri erant, indicat periculum incidendi in eadem peccata, & casdem poenas, si idololatricis conviviis sese immiscuerint; Vellicans interim inanem confidentiam eorum, qui non metuebant periculum, sed Idolothytis, in idoleio, securè vescebantur.
units.tr: Having shown that the use of these examples pertains to all the living, and to those who were yet to live, he points out the danger of falling into the same sins and suffering the same punishments, if they mingle themselves in idolatrous feasts; at the same time he rebukes the empty confidence of those who did not fear the danger, but ate idol-sacrifices securely in the idol-temple.

units.la: Verf. 13.
units.tr: Verse 13.

units.la: Tentatio vos non cepit, nisi humana: fidelis autem est Deus, qui non sinet vos tentari supra id quod potestis, sed unà cum tentatione praestabit etiam exitum, ut possitis sufferre.
units.tr: No temptation has taken you but such as is human; but God is faithful, who will not suffer you to be tempted beyond what you are able, but with the temptation will also make the way of escape, that you may be able to bear it.

units.la: Occurrit objectioni, à metu malorum, quae ipsis imminebant, ab Idololatris concivibus suis, si tantopere ab eorum consortio abhorrerent, ut nollent ipsorum conviviis religiosis publicis interesse. Respondet tentationem illam non alius generis esse, quam quae ordinaria sit hominibus, à qua poterint sibi exitum sperare, propter Dei fidelitatem qui non permittet, ut supra modum tententur, qui studeent se ab impuritate conservare, maximè in casu confessionis; sed cum tentatione, liberationis modum à periculo, vel à peccato saltem ostendere solet, ne succumbant. Ex praecedentibus, à verf. 1. sequitur: Ergo Idolothytis non vescendum in idoleio.
units.tr: He meets the objection, drawn from the fear of the evils which hung over them from their idolatrous fellow citizens, if they so greatly abhorred their company that they would not attend their public religious feasts. He answers that this temptation is not of a different kind from that which is ordinary for men, and from which they may hope for an escape, on account of the faithfulness of God, who will not permit those who take pains to keep themselves from impurity to be tried beyond measure, especially in the case of confession; but with the temptation he is wont to show the way of deliverance from the danger, or at least from the sin, so that they do not succumb. From what has gone before, from verse 1, it follows: Therefore one must not eat of idol-sacrifices in the idol-temple.

units.la: Verf. 14.
units.tr: Verse 14.

units.la: Quapropter dilecti mihi, fugite ab idololatria.
units.tr: Wherefore, my beloved, flee from idolatry.

units.la: Arg. 2. Dehortationis ab Idolothytis in idoleio. Idololatria conjuncta est cum publico idolothytorum esu, à qua idololatria fugere debetis: Ergo, Idolothytis in Idoleio non vescendum.
units.tr: Second argument for dissuading from idol-sacrifices in the idol-temple: Idolatry is joined with the public eating of idol-sacrifices, from which idolatry you ought to flee: Therefore one must not eat of idol-sacrifices in the idol-temple.

units.la: Verf. 15.
units.tr: Verse 15.

units.la: Ut intelligentibus haec dico: judicate vos quod aio. Hoc argumentum confirmaturus, appellat auditores, seu lectores prudentes, & jubet ut perpendant & argumentum jam dictum, & argumenti confirmationem, quam subjicit, additis quinque rationibus, quibus probat hunc publicum Idolothytorum esum Idololatriæ reatu obstringere.
units.tr: I speak as to wise men; judge what I say. In order to confirm this argument, he addresses the hearers, or prudent readers, and bids them weigh both the argument already stated and the confirmation of it, which he adds, with five reasons by which he proves that this public eating of idol-sacrifices binds one with the guilt of idolatry.

units.la: Verf. 16. Poculum benedictionis cui benedicimus, nonne communio sanguinis Christi est? panis quem frangimus, nonne communio corporis Christi est?
units.tr: Verse 16. The cup of blessing which we bless, is it not the communion of the blood of Christ? The bread which we break, is it not the communion of the body of Christ?

units.la: Prima ratio: A pari exemplo Christianorum, cujus forma hæc est: Participatio elementorum in cæna Domini, est professio communionis nostræ cum Christo, & reliquis Christianis, in vera religione: Ergo, participatio Idolothytorum, in convivio diaboli unà cum Idololatris, est professio communionis cum diabolo, & Idololatris, in Idololatria, seu falsa ipsorum religione.
units.tr: First reason: from a parallel example of Christians, whose form is this: Participation in the elements at the Lord's Supper is a profession of our communion with Christ and the other Christians in the true religion: Therefore participation in idol-sacrifices at the feast of the devil, together with the idolaters, is a profession of communion with the devil and the idolaters, in idolatry, or in their false religion.

units.la: Acuit autem hanc rationem, & reliquas, interrogatione frequenti; Poculum Eucharisticum, inquit, an non est symbolum, certa efficax, & realis professio, salvificæ communionis, quam in sanguine Christi, pro nobis effuso habemus? Item sacer ille panis, quem in cœtu nostro frangimus, an non est obsignatio, & realis professio communionis, quam omnes, in corpore Christi, pro nobis crucifixo, habemus? Ergo sequitur à pari, participationem sacrificii in convivio Idololatrico, & diabolico, non minus esse obsignationem, & realem professionem, (in te, & ex intentione operis) communionis cum Idololatris, & Idolo, cui sacrificium oblatum erat.
units.tr: He sharpens this reason, and the rest, by frequent questioning: Is not the Eucharistic cup, he says, a symbol, a certain, effective and real profession of the saving communion which we have in the blood of Christ poured out for us? Likewise, is not that holy bread which we break in our assembly a sealing and a real profession of the communion which all have in the body of Christ crucified for us? Therefore it follows by parity that participation in a sacrifice at an idolatrous and diabolical feast is no less a sealing and a real profession (in the act itself and by the intention of the work) of communion with the idolaters and with the idol to which the sacrifice was offered.

units.la: Verf. 17. Quoniam unum est panis, unum corpus, nos illi multi sumus: nam omnes ex uno illo pane participamus.
units.tr: Verse 17. Because there is one bread, we who are many are one body: for we all partake of that one bread.

units.la: Explicat hanc rationem, in hunc sensum: Sicut nos Christiani licet multi, vi tamen sacramentaliter obsignatæ societatis in eodem cultu, coalescimus quasi in unum panem, id est, in unum corpus mysticum hoc ipso, quod ex uno sacramentali pane, seu Sacramento communicamus: Sic communicantes cum Idololatris, in Idololatrici sacrificii participatione, vi societatis in eodem cultu obsignatæ per convivium Idololatricum in Idoleio, coalescunt in unum corpus mysticum cum illis, hoc ipso, quod ex uno sacrificio sacramentali, una cum illis communicant.
units.tr: He explains this reason in this sense: As we Christians, though many, are by the power of a fellowship sealed in the same worship joined together as one bread, that is, into one mystical body, by the very fact that we partake of one sacramental bread, or Sacrament: so those who communicate with idolaters, in participation in the idolatrous sacrifice, by the power of a fellowship sealed in the same worship through the idolatrous feast in the idol-temple, grow together into one mystical body with them, by the very fact that they partake with them of one sacramental sacrifice.

units.la: Verf. 18. Videtis Israelem qui est secundum carnem: nonne qui edunt victimas, consortes sunt altaris?
units.tr: Verse 18. Behold Israel according to the flesh: do not those who eat the sacrifices become partners of the altar?

units.la: Ratio 2. Ab exemplo Israelitarum pari; Israelitæ edentes de victimis testabantur hoc facto, se altaris & religionis Judaicæ profefsores, & participes esse: Ergo, qui idolorum victimas in idololatrico convivio comedunt, testantur se in idololatria communicare cum Idololatris.
units.tr: Second reason: from a parallel example of the Israelites. The Israelites, eating of the sacrifices, testified by this act that they were professors of and partakers in the altar and the Jewish religion: Therefore those who eat the sacrifices of idols at an idolatrous feast testify that they share in idolatry with the idolaters.

units.la: Verf. 19. Quid ergo dico? idolum aliquid esse, aut quod idolis immolatum est, aliquid esse?
units.tr: Verse 19. What do I say then? That an idol is anything, or that what is sacrificed to idols is anything?

units.la: Verf. 20. Imo illud dico, quæ immolant Gentes, dæmoniis immolant & non Deo: nolim autem vos dæmonum consociari.
units.tr: Verse 20. But I say that the things which the Gentiles sacrifice, they sacrifice to demons and not to God; and I would not have you become partners with demons.

units.la: Ratio 3. Per solutionem objectionis proposita; Etiamsi idolum nihil habeat divinitatis, ut supra dictum est, nec idolothytum quicquam fit de cultu Dei, quem opinatur, & intendit forlan Idololatra; ex natura tamen operis, sacrificium idololatricum est Diabolorum cultus, 2 Cron II. 15. Ergo participatio Idolothyti crassissima est idololatriæ, à qua abstinere debetis.
units.tr: Third reason: by the solution of the objection proposed. Even if an idol has no divinity, as has been said above, and an idol-sacrifice is in no way a part of the worship of God, which perhaps the idolater supposes and intends; nevertheless, from the nature of the work, an idolatrous sacrifice is the worship of demons (2 Chron. 11.15). Therefore participation in an idol-sacrifice is the grossest form of idolatry, from which you ought to abstain.

units.la: Verf. 21. Non potestis poculum Domini bibere, & poculum dæmoniorum: non potestis mensæ Domini participes esse, & mensæ dæmoniorum.
units.tr: Verse 21. You cannot drink the cup of the Lord and the cup of demons: you cannot partake of the table of the Lord and the table of demons.

units.la: Arg. 3. Dehortationis ab idolothytis in idoleio: Participatio sacramentalis convivii Idolorum, seu Dæmoniorum, non potest consistere cum participatione legitima & salutari, Cænæ Dominicæ, quia hoc esset duobus Dominis, Deo & dæmoni servitium offerre, simul & utriusque servitium publicè profiteri: Ergo, non vescendum Idolothytis, in Idoleio.
units.tr: Fourth argument for dissuading from idol-sacrifices: sacramental participation in the feast of idols, or of demons, cannot consist with lawful and saving participation in the Lord's Supper, because this would be to offer service to two masters, God and the demon, and at the same time publicly to profess the service of both: Therefore one must not eat idol-sacrifices in the idol-temple.

units.la: Verf. 22. An provocamus ad æmulationem Dominum? num validiores eo sumus?
units.tr: Verse 22. Or do we provoke the Lord to jealousy? Are we stronger than he?

units.la: Arg. 4. Dehortationis ab Idolothytis; Provocatur ad zelotypiam Deus, si quis Christianum se profitetur, & de sacris dæmoniorum publicè participat. Ergo non vescendum Idolothytis.
units.tr: Fifth argument for dissuading from idol-sacrifices: God is provoked to jealousy if anyone professes himself a Christian and publicly takes part in the rites of demons. Therefore one must not eat idol-sacrifices.

units.la: Validiores ] Arg. 5. Quod pergere in hoc peccato, tam manifesto, sit Deo bellum indicere, & experiri an quis illo fortior sit: Ideoque nisi quis insaniendo putet, se Deo fortiorem esse, abstinendum est ab Idolothytis in Idoleio.
units.tr: Stronger ] Fifth argument: to persist in this sin, so manifest, is to declare war upon God and to test whether one is stronger than he; therefore, unless one is raving and thinks himself stronger than God, one must abstain from idol-sacrifices in the idol-temple.

units.la: Secunda Pars.
units.tr: Second Part.

units.la: Verf. 23. Omnia mihi licent, at non omnia conferunt: omnia mihi licent, sed non omnia ædificant.
units.tr: Ver. 23. All things are lawful for me, but not all things are expedient: all things are lawful for me, but not all things edify.

units.la: Altera parte Capitis, ut deveniat ad privatum usum Idolothytorum, proponit generalem doctrinam, de rebus mediis, quæ hæc est: Omnia (indifferentia scilicet) licita sunt, nisi cum non expedit iis uti, vel cum non ædificant.
units.tr: In the second part of the chapter, to come to the private use of food offered to idols, he sets out a general doctrine about indifferent things, which is this: all things indifferent are lawful, unless it is not expedient to use them or they do not edify.

units.la: Verf. 24. Nemo quod suum est quærat, sed quisque quod alterius est.
units.tr: Ver. 24. Let no man seek his own, but every man another's.

units.la: Quod non liceant cum non expediunt, non ædificant, seu ædificationi obsunt, rationem reddit per modum præcepti, quia in usu libertatis nostræ, potius alienæ saluti, quam nostræ temporali utilitati studendum.
units.tr: He gives the reason, in the form of a precept, why things are not lawful when they are not expedient or do not edify, or hinder edification: in the use of our liberty we must aim at the salvation of others rather than our own temporal advantage.

units.la: Verf. 25. Quicquid in macello venditur, edite, nihil discriminantes propter conscientiam.
units.tr: Ver. 25. Whatever is sold in the meat market, eat, asking no question for conscience' sake.

units.la: Præmissa generali doctrina, respondet de Idolothytis, Extra usum religiosum, (ut cum exempli causa in macello venduntur,) sine hæsitatione conscientiæ, posse quemquam iis vesci. Solebant enim venales in macello prostare carnes sacrificatæ, quarum pretium ad sacerdotes redibat.
units.tr: Having set out the general doctrine, he answers about food offered to idols: apart from religious use (for example, when it is sold in the meat market), anyone may eat such food without scruple of conscience. For meat that had been sacrificed was commonly sold in the meat market, and its price went to the priests.

units.la: Verf. 26. Domini enim est terra & plenitudo ejus.
units.tr: Ver. 26. For the earth is the Lord's, and the fulness thereof.

units.la: Ratio est, quia in illo communi statu, sunt Dei creaturæ, in usum fidelium sanctificatæ, & in liberum usum concessæ, à Domino Cœli & Terræ, &c.
units.tr: The reason is that in that common state these are God's creatures, sanctified for the use of believers and granted for free use by the Lord of heaven and earth, etc.

units.la: Verf. 27. Quod si quis infidelium vos vocat, & vultis ire, quicquid apponitur vobis, edite, nihil discriminantes propter conscientiam.
units.tr: Ver. 27. If any of them that believe not bid you to a feast, and ye be disposed to go; whatsoever is set before you, eat, asking no question for conscience' sake.

units.la: Similiter, si invitetur aliquis fidelis ab infideli aliquo ad convivium in privatis ædibus, sine scrupulo edere posse Christianum dicit, de quovis cibo proposito.
units.tr: Similarly, if a believer is invited by some unbeliever to a meal in a private house, he says that a Christian may eat without scruple of any food that is set before him.

units.la: Verf. 28. At si quis vobis dixerit, Hoc idolis immolatum est, ne edite, propter illum qui indicavit, & propter conscientiam; Domini enim est terra & plenitudo ejus.
units.tr: Ver. 28. But if any man say unto you, This is offered in sacrifice unto idols, eat not, for his sake that showed it, and for conscience' sake; for the earth is the Lord's, and the fulness thereof.

units.la: Excipit in casu scandali, si vel infidelis, vel infirmus frater significaverit, istum cibum Idolis esse immolatum, in quo casu abstinere jubet, & rationes addit septem.
units.tr: He makes an exception in the case of offence: if either an unbeliever or a weak brother points out that this food has been offered to idols, then he commands abstinence in that case and adds seven reasons.

units.la: Ratio prima, Ne si edas post admonitionem, lædatur infirmus frater qui admonuit, vel ne confirmetur in Idololatria infidelis, si forte admonuit.
units.tr: The first reason: lest, if you eat after the warning, the weak brother who gave the warning be wounded, or lest the unbeliever, if perhaps he gave the warning, be confirmed in idolatry.

units.la: Domini ] Ratio 2. Deus alios etiam sanctificavit cibos præter illum, in quo periculum est scandali, & quia Dominus terræ, non concessit potestatem, utendi indifferenter creaturis suis, cum alicujus scandalo. Ergo in hoc casu non edendum.
units.tr: Lord] Reason 2. God has sanctified other foods besides that one in which there is danger of offence, and since the Lord of the earth has not granted the power to use his creatures indiscriminately with anyone's offence, therefore in this case one must not eat.

units.la: Verf. 29 Conscientiam autem dico non tuam, sed illius alterius cur enim libertas mea damnatur ab alia conscientia?
units.tr: Ver. 29. Conscience, I say, not thine own, but the other's: for why is my liberty judged of another man's conscience?

units.la: Ratio 3. Si quis edat cum scandalo, Christiana libertas edendi condemnabitur ab alius conscientia, tanquam profana licentia: Ergo, non edendum in hoc casu.
units.tr: Reason 3. If anyone eats with offence, Christian liberty to eat will be condemned by another's conscience as profane licence. Therefore one must not eat in this case.

units.la: Verf. 30. Quod si ego per gratiam cibum participo, cur in eo ut blasphemus accusor, pro quo ego gratias ago?
units.tr: Ver. 30. If I by grace partake , why am I evil spoken of as a blasphemer, for that for which I give thanks?

units.la: Ratio 4. Peccaretur in Dei gratiam, si quis abuteretur Dei dono, (quivis autem cibus Dei donum est, sicut in gratiarum actione ante vel post cibum agnoscitur) ita ut occasionem inde præberet, malè de seipso loquendi, quasi alterius animæ rationem nullam haberet: Ergo, non edendum in hoc casu.
units.tr: Reason 4. God's grace would be sinned against if anyone abused God's gift (and every food is God's gift, as is acknowledged in giving thanks before or after the meal), so that he thereby gave occasion for speaking evil of himself, as if he had no regard for another's soul. Therefore one must not eat in this case.

units.la: Verf. 31. Sive igitur editis, sive bibitis sive quid facitis, omnia in gloriam Dei facite.
units.tr: Ver. 31. Whether therefore ye eat, or drink, or whatsoever ye do, do all to the glory of God.

units.la: Ratio 5. Per modum præcepti propositá: In omnibus actionibus, & idcirco etiam in edendo, & bibendo, studendum est ut Deus glorificetur, quod non fit quando cum scandalo comeditur: Ergo, &c.
units.tr: Reason 5. This is set forth in the form of a precept: in all actions, and therefore also in eating and drinking, we must strive that God be glorified, which does not happen when food is eaten with offence. Therefore, etc.

units.la: Verf. 32. Estote sine offendiculo, & Judæis, & Græcis, & Ecclesiæ Dei
units.tr: Ver. 32. Give none offence, neither to the Jews, nor to the Greeks, nor to the Church of God.

units.la: Ratio 6. Nulli est ponendum scandalum, sive profiteatur religionem veram sive non: Ergo in casu scandali, non edendum.
units.tr: Reason 6. Offence must be given to no one, whether he professes the true religion or not. Therefore, in a case of offence, one must not eat.

units.la: Verf. 33. Sicut & ego per omnia omnibus placeo, non quaerens meam ipsius utilitatem sed multorum, ut salventur.
units.tr: Ver. 33. Even as I please all men in all things, not seeking mine own profit, but the profit of many, that they may be saved.

units.la: Ratio 7. Omnes tenentur Apostoli exemplum imitari in omnibus rebus mediis, serviendo non temporali emolumento suo, sed aliorum saluti æternæ: Ergo sicut ille, in tali casu nolebat edere, sic tenentur omnes non edere hunc vel illum cibum in casu scandali.
units.tr: Reason 7. All are bound to imitate the Apostle's example in all indifferent matters, serving not their own temporal gain but the eternal salvation of others. Therefore, just as he was unwilling to eat in such a case, so all are bound not to eat this or that food in a case of offence.

units.la: Caput undecimum.
units.tr: Chapter eleven.

units.la: Articulus septimus de ordine & decoro.
units.tr: The seventh article, concerning order and decorum.

units.la: Epistolae articulus septimus, de decoro, & ordine, in publicis Ecclesiae conventibus, observando.
units.tr: The seventh article of the Epistle, on decorum and order, to be observed in the public assemblies of the Church.

units.la: Capitis partes duae sunt: 1. De decenti habitu virorum & mulierum, in sacris peragendis, ad vers. 17. Altera, de recta Coenae Dominicae administratione, ad finem.
units.tr: The chapter has two parts: 1. On the decent dress of men and women when performing sacred duties, to verse 17. The other, on the right administration of the Lord's Supper, to the end.

units.la: Vers. 1 Imitatores mei fiatis, sicut & ego Christi.
units.tr: Verse 1 Be ye followers of me, even as I also am of Christ.

units.la: Vers. 2. Laudo vero vos, fratres, quod omnia mea meministis & sicut tradidi vobis traditiones retinetis.
units.tr: Verse 2. Now I praise you, brethren, that ye remember me in all things, and keep the ordinances, as I delivered them to you.

units.la: Quod ad primam attinet, praemittit praeceptum de imitatione sui, quousque ipse fuerit imitator Christi, simulque commendat Corinthios, Quod aliquovique Doctrinam, & praecepta, partim scripto, partim voce viva ipsis tradita, de religione rebusque quae religionem spectabant observarint hucusque saltem, ut laudem mereantur aliquam.
units.tr: As to the first part, he begins with the precept that they imitate him, insofar as he himself is an imitator of Christ. At the same time he commends the Corinthians, because up to now at least they have observed the teaching and precepts delivered to them, partly in writing and partly by living voice, concerning religion and the matters that pertain to religion, so that they deserve some praise.

units.la: Vers. 3. Velim autem vos nosse Christum esse omnis viri caput: caput autem mulieris, virum: caput vero Christi, Deum.
units.tr: Verse 3. But I would have you know that Christ is the head of every man; and the head of the woman is the man; and the head of Christ is God.

units.la: Deinde substernit sequenti admonitioni theorema, de ordine divinitus sancito in Ecclesiae corpore mystico, nempe quod Christus proxime subordinatur Deo, qua est θεανδρωπ, mediator & caput Ecclesiae; & quod Christo dignitate proxime succedat vir: viro vero mulier: quae quantum ad sexus honorem attinet, viro ut capiti, seu supereminenti subordinatur, unde intelligerent ordinem in conventibus Ecclesiae necessario observandum.
units.tr: Next he adds to this admonition a theorem about the order divinely established in the mystical body of the Church: namely, that Christ is most immediately subordinate to God, as the God-man, the mediator and head of the Church; that next in dignity to Christ comes the man, and to the man the woman, who, as far as the honour of sex is concerned, is subordinate to the man as to a head, or one who is pre-eminent. From this they were to understand that this order must necessarily be observed in the assemblies of the Church.

units.la: Vers. 4 Omnis vir orans aut prophetans velato capite, dedecorat caput suum.
units.tr: Verse 4 Every man praying or prophesying with his head covered dishonoureth his head.

units.la: Hunc ordinem non satis observasse apparet Corinthios; Quia Ethnicorum more mulieres in publico coetu, vela deponebant, viri velo se operiebant, Caput & faciem obtegentes, (Ubi orare & prophetare dicuntur, quicunque publice conveniebant, & conspirabant, ad publicum hunc Dei cultum promovendum.) Hoc indecorum reprehendit, in viris pariter ris pariter & fœminis, nunc virum, nunc fœminam arguens indecori, novem argumentis.
units.tr: It appears that the Corinthians had not sufficiently observed this order. For in the manner of the heathen, the women laid aside their veils in the public assembly, while the men covered themselves with a veil, covering head and face. (Here, all who gathered publicly and joined together to promote this public worship of God are said to pray and prophesy.) He rebukes this indecorum equally in men and in women, now charging the man, now the woman, with indecorum, by nine arguments.

units.la: ] Argumentum primum; Velamen viri, alienum est à dignitate virilis sexus, & contra dignitatem Christi, quam repræsentare debet vir: Indecorum ergo.
units.tr: The first argument: a man's veil is foreign to the dignity of the male sex and contrary to the dignity of Christ, whom the man ought to represent. Therefore it is indecorous.

units.la: Vers. 5. Omnis verò mulier orans aut prophetans, non velato capite, dedecorat caput suum: nam id unum ac idem est ac si rasa esset.
units.tr: Verse 5. But every woman that prayeth or prophesieth with her head uncovered dishonoureth her head: for that is even all one as if she were shaven.

units.la: Vers. 6. Nam si non velatur mulier, etiam tondeatur: quod si turpe mulieri tonderi aut radi, veletur.
units.tr: Verse 6. For if the woman be not covered, let her also be shorn: but if it be a shame for a woman to be shorn or shaven, let her be covered.

units.la: Arg. 2. Velamen deponere indignum est sexu fœmineo, & contra dignitatem cum capitis sui naturalis, tum metaphorici, nempe viri, cui subjectionem, propter sexus masculini honorem debet; cujus rationem reddit, quia sine velo esse fœminam, non minùs turpe erat, quam tonderi: Indecori hic arguitur ergo fœmina, quod corrigendum est.
units.tr: Argument 2. To lay aside the veil is unworthy of the female sex, and contrary to the dignity both of her natural head and of her metaphorical head, namely the man, to whom she owes subjection on account of the honour of the masculine sex. He gives the reason: to be without a veil was no less shameful for a woman than to be shorn. Here the woman is charged with indecorum, which must be corrected.

units.la: Vers. 7. Vir enim non debet velare caput, quum is imago sit & gloria Dei: at mulier, gloria viri est.
units.tr: Verse 7. For a man indeed ought not to cover his head, forasmuch as he is the image and glory of God: but the woman is the glory of the man.

units.la: Arg. 3. Vir cum sit imago DEI, & excellentiæ ipsius gloriosæ repræsentatio, respectu fœminæ, cui ut caput statuitur, viriliter se gerendo, gloriam DEO exhibere debet: Ergo indecorum hoc, in velaminis usu ei cavendum.
units.tr: Argument 3. Since the man is the image of God and a representation of God's glorious excellence, in relation to the woman, over whom he is set as head, he ought to conduct himself manfully and so display glory to God. Therefore he must avoid this indecorum in the use of veils.

units.la: ] Arg. 4. Fœmina est gloria sexus virilis, seu imago dignitatis viri, in qua, ut in speculo, viri, in cujus bonum condita est, excellentia conspicitur; cui, subjectionem profiteri debet, per sui velationem: Ergo cum secus apud vos faciat fœmina, indecori arguitur. Nihil hoc impedit, quo minùs fœmina sit in DEI gloriam, & ad ejus imaginem, unà cum viro condita respectu animæ, & status spiritualis.
units.tr: Argument 4. The woman is the glory of the male sex, or the image of the man's dignity, in which, as in a mirror, the excellence of the man, for whose good she was created, is seen. She ought to profess subjection to him by veiling herself. Therefore, since you women act otherwise, you are charged with indecorum. Nothing here prevents the woman from being to the glory of God, and made in God's image together with the man, as regards her soul and her spiritual state.

units.la: Vers. 8 Non enim est vir ex muliere, sed mulier ex viro.
units.tr: Verse 8. For the man is not of the woman; but the woman of the man.

units.la: Arg. 5. Vir est principium materiale fœminæ, quia ex viri costa facta est: hanc ergo originis prærogativam decet marem & fœminam, in dicti decori observatione, testari. Ergo indecori rej estis, qui secus facitis.
units.tr: Argument 5. The man is the material principle of the woman, since she was made from the man's rib. Therefore it befits male and female to bear witness to this prerogative of origin by observing said decorum. Therefore you are guilty of indecorum, who act otherwise.

units.la: Vers. 9. Neque enim conditus est vir propter mulierem, sed mulier propter virum.
units.tr: Verse 9. Neither was the man created for the woman; but the woman for the man.

units.la: Arg. 6, Quum vir rationem habeat finis, fœmina vero destinati ad finem: hanc excellentiæ differentiam, convenit, decori observatione expri-mi: Ergo cum non observatur, merito reprehendendi estis.
units.tr: Argument 6. Since the man has the character of an end, and the woman that of what is destined for the end, this difference of excellence ought to be expressed in the observance of decorum. Therefore, since it is not observed, you deserve to be rebuked.

units.la: Verf. 10. Propter hoc debet mulier potestatem habere in capite, propter Angelos.
units.tr: Verse 10. For this cause ought the woman to have power on her head because of the angels.

units.la: Arg. 7. Etiam propter Angelos inspectores, & testes decori & indecori in Ecclesia, licet hominis aspectum negligeretis, deceret tamen fœminas sexus sui subjectionem, & virilis sexus potestatem, capitis velatione tan-quam signo testari: Ergo indecorum admittitur cum contra fit.
units.tr: Argument 7. Even on account of the angels, who are overseers and witnesses of decorum and indecorum in the Church, although you disregard the sight of men, it would be fitting for women to attest, by the covering of the head as a sign, the subjection of their sex and the authority of the male sex. Therefore indecorum is admitted when the contrary is done.

units.la: Verf. 11. Attamen neque vir absque muliere, neque mulier absque viro, in Domino.
units.tr: Verse 11. Nevertheless neither is the man without the woman, neither the woman without the man, in the Lord.

units.la: Verf. 12. Sicut enim mulier ex viro est, ita & vir per mulierem: omnia vero ex Deo.
units.tr: Verse 12. For as the woman is of the man, even so is the man also by the woman; but all things of God.

units.la: Hanc comparationem viri & fœminæ, ne longius trahatur ad fœminæ contemptum, triplici respectu fœminam viro æquat; primo, respectu Christi Domini, seu ratione status gratiæ in Christo; Vir & fœmina pares sunt, eodemque pretio empti, Christique Domini servitio destinati pariter: Secundò, ratione mutuæ originis, nam sicut in creatione mulier ex viro est, sic ordinariâ post creationem propagatione, vir per mulierem est, Tertiò, ratione causæ efficientis primæ & principalis, id est Dei, qui condidit marem & fœminam & omnia alia, pares sunt viri & fœminæ.
units.tr: So that this comparison of man and woman may not be drawn out to the contempt of the woman, he equates the woman with the man in three respects. First, with respect to Christ the Lord, or by reason of the state of grace in Christ: man and woman are equal, alike bought with the same price, and likewise destined for the service of Christ the Lord. Secondly, by reason of mutual origin: for as in creation the woman is from the man, so in ordinary propagation after creation the man is through the woman. Thirdly, by reason of the first and principal efficient cause, that is God, who made male and female and all other things, man and woman are equal.

units.la: Verf. 13. Apud vosipsos judicate: num decorum est mulierem non velatam Deum orare?
units.tr: Verse 13. Judge in yourselves: is it comely that a woman pray unto God uncovered?

units.la: Verf. 14. An ne natura quidem ipsa hoc vos docet, quod viro quidem comatum esse dedecori sit?
units.tr: Verse 14. Doth not even nature itself teach you, that if a man have long hair, it is a shame unto him?

units.la: Verf. 15. Contrà, mulieri comatam esse, decori sit? Nam comá pro velamine data est ei.
units.tr: Verse 15. But if a woman have long hair, it is a glory to her: for her hair is given her for a covering.

units.la: Arg. 8. Sensus communis & ipsa natura, seu naturalis inclinatio (sic vocat morem jam firmatum, & naturæ congruentem ratione decori,) dictat indecorum esse, fœminam non velatam orare, aut virum comatum seu intonsis capillis incedere, decorum vero esse si contra. Ergo decorum non observatur cum secus facitis. Coma fœminæ dari dicitur pro velamine, quia eo fine datur, ut norit caput sibi obnubendum esse.
units.tr: Argument 8. Common sense and nature itself, or natural inclination (he calls thus a custom already established and agreeing with nature by reason of decorum), dictate that it is indecorous for a woman to pray unveiled, or for a man to go about with long hair or unshorn locks, and decorous on the contrary. Therefore decorum is not observed when you act otherwise. Hair is said to be given to a woman for a covering, because it is given for this end, that she may know her head must be veiled.

units.la: Verf. 16. Quod fiquis videtur contentiosus esse, nos ejusmodi consuetudinem non habemus, neque Ecclesiæ Dei.
units.tr: Verse 16. But if any man seem to be contentious, we have no such custom, neither the churches of God.

units.la: Arg. 9. Si quis argumentis his forte non cederet, sed rixaretur, ipsorum defensionibus rixosis & contentiosis, Apostolus opponit Judæorum, & ecclesiarum reliquarum consuetudinem jam receptam & firmatam: Aliæ ecclesiæ non habent hanc consuetudinem, ut mulieres interlinc publicis coetibus, non velato capite, viri vero velato. Ergo consuetudo vestra, cum à naturali, tum ab ecclesiarum consuetudine, & decoro firmato decedens, indecora est.
units.tr: Argument 9. If anyone perhaps did not yield to these arguments, but quarrelled, the Apostle opposes to their contentious and quarrelsome defences the custom of the Jews and of the other churches, already received and established: the other churches do not have this custom, that women in the public assemblies should be uncovered while the men are covered. Therefore your custom, departing both from nature and from the custom of the churches and from established decorum, is indecorous.

units.la: Secunda Pars.
units.tr: Second Part.

units.la: Verf. 17. Hoc vero ita denuntio ut vos non laudem, quod videlicet non cum emolumento, sed cum detrimento convenitis.
units.tr: Verse 17. Now in giving this instruction I do not praise you, since when you meet together it is not for your benefit but for your harm.

units.la: Altera pars capitis; de recta Cœnæ Dominicæ administratione, in qua non laudat sed vituperat Corinthios, primum in genere, quod conventus celebrando, proficiant non in melius sed in pejus potius.
units.tr: The second part of the chapter, concerning the right administration of the Lord's Supper, in which he does not praise but blames the Corinthians. First, in general, because by assembling they profit not for the better but rather for the worse.

units.la: Verf. 18. Primùm enim quum convenitis in ecclesia, audio dissidia inter vos esse: & aliquatenus credo.
units.tr: Verse 18. For first, when you come together in the church, I hear that there are divisions among you, and I partly believe it.

units.la: Secundò specialiter magis; Quod modo, ad fovenda schismata, compositò convenant, sicut audiebat, & aliquam partem credebat etiam.
units.tr: Secondly, more particularly: they assemble deliberately to foster schisms, as he had heard, and as he also partly believed.

units.la: Verf. 19. Oportet enim etiam hæreses inter vos esse, ut qui probati sunt, manifesti fiant inter vos.
units.tr: Verse 19. For there must also be heresies among you, that those who are approved may be made manifest among you.

units.la: Rationem reddit, cur credat schismata inter eos fuisse, nempe, Quia propter diaboli & hominum malitiam, justo Dei judicio oriuntur non schismata tantum, in studiis & affectibus: sed hæreses etiam seu sectæ, quæ & oportet esse, & eo consilio à Deo permittuntur, ut probati & sinceri Christiani, id quod rectum est in partium contentione tenentes, dignoscantur, & ad majorem Dei gloriam, veræque religionis in puritate conservationem toti, mundo sinceri esse manifestentur.
units.tr: He gives the reason why he believes there were schisms among them. Through the malice of the devil and of men, by the just judgment of God, arise not only schisms in pursuits and affections but also heresies or sects. These must needs be, and by God's counsel they are permitted so that approved and sincere Christians, holding to what is right in the contention of parties, may be distinguished, and may be made manifest to the whole world as sincere, for the greater glory of God and the preservation of true religion in its purity.

units.la: Verf. 20. Quum igitur convenitis eodem loci, hoc non est Dominicam cænam edere:
units.tr: Verse 20. When therefore you come together in one place, it is not to eat the Lord's Supper.

units.la: Tertiò. Vituperat specialissimè, quod sacram Cœnam ita profanent, ac si Domini Cœna non esset; cum enim eodem loci conveniebant, in cœtu Sanctorum ita se irreligiosè gerebant, ac si Cœnam religiosam non celebrarent.
units.tr: Thirdly, he blames especially that they profane the holy Supper as if it were not the Lord's Supper. For while they came together in one place, in the assembly of the saints they behaved so irreligiously, as if they were not celebrating a religious supper.

units.la: Verf 21. Nam unusquisque propriam cœnam præoccupat in ve-scendo: & hic quidem esurit, ille vero ebrius est.
units.tr: Verse 21. For each one takes beforehand his own supper in eating: and one indeed is hungry, but another is drunk.

units.la: Hoc demonstrat quatuor notatis in Dominicæ Cœnæ apud eos celebratione, vitiis. Primum est, Unusquisque cum factione sua, exclusis reliquis Ecclesiæ membris, schismaticè sacram Cœnam capiebat. Secundum, Sacramento Cœnæ Dominicæ propriam cœnam, seu communes suas epulas, quæ agapæ dicebantur, admiscebant. Tertium, Pauperiores excludebant, qui famelici relinquebantur interim, dum ditiores cœnarent. Quartum, Epulando ad ebrietatem usque potabant.
units.tr: This shows four faults noted in their celebration of the Lord's Supper. First, each one with his own faction, the other members of the Church being excluded, took the holy Supper in a schismatic way. Second, they mixed their own supper, or their common feasts, which were called agapae [ἀγάπαι], with the sacrament of the Lord's Supper. Third, they excluded the poorer, who were left hungry while the richer dined. Fourth, in their feasting they drank even to drunkenness.

units.la: Verf. 22. Enimvero num domos non habetis ad edendum & bibendum? aut Ecclesiam Dei contemnitis & pudefacitis eos qui non habent? Quid vobis dicam? laudabo vos? in hoc non laudo.
units.tr: Verse 22. Have you not houses to eat and drink in? Or do you despise the church of God and shame those who have not? What shall I say to you? Shall I praise you? In this I do not praise you.

units.la: Idcirco reprehendit morem illum publice convivandi in Ecclesia per ἀγάπας quæ dicebantur, & quasi indignum publico conventu, ad privatas ædes relegandum censet, addita objurgatione quod hoc suo facto reverendum cœtum sanctorum vilem haberent, & contemptui exponerent vacantes commessationi, ubi incumbendum erat tantùm religioni: nec non, quia in epulis illis suis, pauperiores qui sumptus ejusmodi facere non poterant pudefaciebant: quæ omnia vituperio digna oltendit.
units.tr: Therefore he rebukes that custom of publicly feasting in the church by means of the agapae [ἀγάπαι], as they were called. He judges that, being unworthy of a public assembly, it should be relegated to private houses. He adds a rebuke: by this deed they held the venerable assembly of the saints in contempt and exposed it to scorn, giving themselves to revelry when they should have devoted themselves only to religion. Also, in those feasts they shamed the poorer, who could not make such expenses. He shows that all these things are worthy of blame.

units.la: Verf 23. Ego enim accepi à Domino quod & tradidi vobis, Dominum Iesum videlicet ea nocte qua proditus est, accepisse panem.
units.tr: Verse 23. For I received from the Lord what I also delivered to you: that the Lord Jesus, on the night in which he was betrayed, took bread.

units.la: Verf. 24. Et gratias agens fregisse ac dixisse, Accipite, edite: hoc meum est corpus quod pro vobis frangitur: hoc facite ad meam commemorationem.
units.tr: Verse 24. And giving thanks, he broke it and said: Take, eat; this is my body, which is broken for you; do this in remembrance of me.

units.la: Hos errores ut corrigat, primo repetit sacramenti institutionem, ad verf. 27. deinde hortatur, & instruit ad legitimum sacramenti usum, ad finem.
units.tr: To correct these errors, he first repeats the institution of the sacrament, down to verse 27. Then he exhorts and instructs them to the lawful use of the sacrament, to the end.

units.la: Quod ad institutionem Cœnæ, in ejus recitatione ostenditur quomodo IESUS CHRISTUS jam moriturus, testamentario jure, fœdus gratiæ (per suam mediationem, cum Deo & Ecclesia initum) obsignaverit: quo & gloriosa memoria mortis suæ celebraretur in mundo, ad secundum suum adventum, & simul fidelibus daretur, & datum judicialiter confirmaretur jus in personam suam, & personæ passiones, & passi-onum beneficia, fructus, & vitalem virtutem suam, ab ipso moriente, resurgente & exaltato promanantem, ad Fidelium sanctificationem & vitam æternam: idque per symbola convivii sacri, & sacræ cum Deo & inter se, communionis. In quem finem Christus in mensa cum Discipulis sedens, post agni paschalis comestionem: Primò, sumptum in manibus panem, & gratiis actis sanctificatum, fregit & exhibuit discipulis, jubens, ut acciperent & ederent: deinde pronunciavit panem acceptum & comestum esse corpus suum sacramentali modo repræsentatum, ut pro redemptione nostra traditum, & judiciali modo nobis applicatum; & denique imperavit, ut discipuli seu fideles omnes hoc factum imitarentur in ecclesia, in commemorationem sui, qui redemptionis pretium persolverat per corporis sui passionem.
units.tr: As to the institution of the Supper, its recital shows how Jesus Christ, about to die, by testamentary right sealed the covenant of grace, made with God and the Church through his mediation. The glorious memory of his death was to be celebrated in the world until his second coming. At the same time it was to be given to believers, and the right in his person, and the benefits of his sufferings and passion, and his vital power flowing from him as he died, rose and was exalted, were to be judicially confirmed as given to them, for the sanctification of believers and for eternal life. This was done through the signs of a sacred feast and of sacred communion with God and among themselves. To this end Christ, sitting at table with the disciples after eating the paschal lamb, first took bread in his hands, sanctified it by giving thanks, broke it and gave it to the disciples, bidding them take and eat. Then he declared that the bread taken and eaten was his body, sacramentally represented as delivered for our redemption and judicially applied to us. Finally he commanded that the disciples, or all the faithful, should imitate this act in the church in remembrance of him, who had paid the price of redemption through the passion of his body.

units.la: Verf. 25 Itidem & poculum, postquam cænasset, dicendo, Hoc poculum, est Novum illud pactum, per meum sanguinem: hoc facite quotiescunque biberitis, ad mei commemorationem.
units.tr: Verse 25. Likewise also the cup, after supper, saying: This cup is the new covenant in my blood; do this, as often as you drink it, in remembrance of me.

units.la: Quod ad alteram partem Cœnæ: In eadem mensa, post Cœnam scilicet Paschalem, & Panem distributum, Christus sumptum poculum cum vino, & gratiis actis sanctificatum, dedit Discipulis bibendum: deinde de poculo pronunciavit, Poculum sumptum & bibitum esse fœdus illud gratiæ novum, inter Deum & Ecclesiam, per sanguinem suum sancitum sacramentaliter utrinque, id est, ut à parte Dei dantis ratum, sic & à parte fidelis accipientis confirmatum, & judicialiter applicatum simul, & obsignatum. Denique imperavit, ut Discipuli hoc factum imitarentur frequentius in Ecclesia, in commemorationem sui, qui pretium redemptionis Ecclesiæ persolverat, per sanguinis sui effusionem.
units.tr: As to the other part of the Supper: at the same table, after the paschal supper and after the bread had been distributed, Christ took the cup of wine, sanctified it by giving thanks, and gave it to the disciples to drink. Then, concerning the cup, he declared that the cup taken and drunk is that new covenant of grace between God and the Church, sacramentally ratified by his blood on both sides: ratified on God's part as the one giving it, and confirmed on the part of the believer as the one receiving it, and at the same time judicially applied and sealed. Finally he commanded that the disciples should imitate this act more often in the church, in remembrance of him, who had paid the price of the Church's redemption through the shedding of his blood.

units.la: Verf. 26 Quotiescunque enim ederitis panem hunc, & poculum hoc biberitis, mortem Domini annuntiatis, usque quò venerit.
units.tr: Verse 26. For as often as you eat this bread and drink this cup, you proclaim the Lord's death until he comes.

units.la: Utque ex duobus elementis, Pane & Vino, unam fieri debere Cœnam, sæpius in Ecclesia repetendam, agnoscamus, Apostolus perpetuari vult in Ecclesia, per hujus Sacramenti frequentem repetitionem, publicam mortis Domini commemorationem; & propterea, quod Christus corpore præsens non sit futurus in Ecclesia, ante ultimum judicium, per hoc sacramentum vult ut memoria redemptionis Ecclesiæ, per ejus mortem, subinde recolatur & celebretur, donec è Cœlis adveniat in novissimo illo die.
units.tr: That one Supper, to be repeated often in the Church, should be made from the two elements, bread and wine, we acknowledge. The Apostle wills that the public commemoration of the Lord's death be perpetuated in the Church through the frequent repetition of this sacrament. And because Christ will not be present in the Church bodily before the last judgment, through this sacrament he wills that the memory of the Church's redemption by his death be recalled and celebrated from time to time, until he comes from heaven on that last day.

units.la: Verf. 27. Itaque quisquis ederit panem hunc, vel biberit poculum hoc Domini indignè, reus tenebitur corporis & sanguinis Domini.
units.tr: Verse 27. Therefore whoever eats this bread or drinks this cup of the Lord unworthily will be guilty of the body and blood of the Lord.

units.la: Post institutionem repetitam Apostolus hortatur, & instituit Corinthios ad rectum Sacramenti usum, sex modis: Primò, Ostenso periculo reatus quo tenentur profanantes hoc Sacramentum: nam quicunque absque præparatione & reverentia, secus quam dignum est, tanta mysteria tractat, Sacramento abutitur, contemnit Christum, & sceleris eorum qui Christum interfecerunt, affinis evadit.
units.tr: After repeating the institution, the Apostle exhorts and instructs the Corinthians to the right use of the sacrament, in six ways. First, by showing the danger of guilt to which those are liable who profane this sacrament. For whoever handles such mysteries without preparation and reverence, otherwise than is fitting, abuses the sacrament, despises Christ, and becomes akin to the guilt of those who crucified Christ.

units.la: Verl. 28 Exploret autem quisque seipsum, & ita de pane illo edat, & de illo poculo bibat.
units.tr: Verse 28. But let a man examine himself, and so let him eat of that bread and drink of that cup.

units.la: Secundò, Ostensa facilitate præparationis, ut digne communicet unusquisque: Tantum (inquit) se examinet quisque, ut peccati sui & miseriæ magnitudine perspectâ, quanta sibi sit necessitas remedii per Christum, videat, & quâ fide, quo sanctitatis proposito, accedere teneatur ad Christi communionem is qui sine Christo millies perditus est, consideret, & ubi se probaverit, sic edat & bibat in sacro Convivio: hoc est, sic sibi applicet rem significatam, cum signi participatione, sicut se ea opus habere animadvertit.
units.tr: Second, by showing how easy the preparation is, so that each may communicate worthily. Let each one (he says) examine himself, so that, having perceived the greatness of his sin and misery, he may see how great his need of the remedy through Christ is. Let him consider with what faith and with what purpose of holiness he ought to approach the communion of Christ, being one who without Christ is ruined a thousand times over. And when he has proved himself, let him thus eat and drink at the sacred feast: that is, let him apply to himself the thing signified, together with participation in the sign, as he perceives that he has need of it.

units.la: Verl. 29. Nam qui edit & bibit indigne, ipse sibi judicium edit & bibit, non discernens corpus Domini.
units.tr: Verse 29. For he who eats and drinks unworthily eats and drinks judgment to himself, not discerning the body of the Lord.

units.la: Tertiò, Ostensa pœna indignæ manducationis: Quod, qui sine probatione sui participat externo sacramento, indigne edendo & bibendo, attrahat sibi judicium, seu pœnas temporales, & æternas, nisi resipiscat, quia non discernit sacrum hoc Convivium, & rem significatam, à vulgari coena, sed ad Domini mensam non aliter quam ad communem aliquam, accedit.
units.tr: Third, by showing the punishment of unworthy eating: he who partakes of the outward sacrament without self-examination, eating and drinking unworthily, brings judgment upon himself, that is, temporal and eternal punishments, unless he repents. This is because he does not discern this sacred feast and the thing signified from common food, but comes to the Lord's table no differently than to some ordinary meal.

units.la: Verf. 30 Propterea inter vos multi sunt ægroti & valetudinarij & dormiunt multi.
units.tr: Verse 30: For this reason many among you are sick and infirm, and many sleep.

units.la: Quartò, Positis ob oculos exemplis temporalis iræ Dei, in morbis, plagis & morte jam inflictis in multos Corinthios, propter Sacramenti profanationem.
units.tr: Fourthly, the examples of God's temporal wrath are set before their eyes: sicknesses, plagues and deaths already inflicted on many Corinthians on account of the profanation of the Sacrament.

units.la: Verl. 31 Etenim si ipsi nos dijudicaremus, non judicaremur.
units.tr: Verse 31: For if we judged ourselves, we would not be judged.

units.la: Hanc judiciorum temporalium inflictionem, à rigore purgat, Primò, ab æquitate, quod Deus non judicantes se ipsos seu resipiscentes, sed secure in admisso peccato jacentes, juste puniat, quod non esset facturus si resipiscentes seipsos judicarent.
units.tr: He purges this infliction of temporal judgments of harshness, first, by its fairness: God justly punishes those who do not judge themselves, that is, who do not repent, but lie secure in the sin they have committed; which he would not do if they judged and repented of themselves.

units.la: Verl. 32. Sed dum judicamur, à Domino erudimur, ne cum mundo condemnemur. Deinde, quod inflictio plagarum sit paterna castigatio; qua fideles ad resipiscentiam ducantur, ne cum mundo pereant.
units.tr: Verse 32: But when we are judged, we are chastened by the Lord, so that we are not condemned along with the world. Next, the infliction of plagues is a fatherly correction, by which the faithful are led to repentance, so that they do not perish with the world.

units.la: Vers. 33. Itaque, fratres mei, quum convenitis ad vescendum, alius alium expectate.
units.tr: Verse 33: Therefore, my brothers, when you come together to eat, wait for one another.

units.la: Quintò, Apostolus Corinthios ad rectè utendum Coenâ dirigit, dato praecepto ad vitandum schisma, ut alii alios expectent, & simul sacra Coena participent; non seorsim singuli coenent, quia DOMINI coena est communis actio Ecclesiae, in Coetu publico, convivali modo celebranda.
units.tr: Fifthly, the Apostle directs the Corinthians to the right use of the Supper, giving the command to avoid schism, that they should wait for one another and take part in the holy Supper together; not each one dining alone by himself, because the Lord's Supper is a common action of the Church, to be celebrated in a public assembly and in the manner of a shared meal.

units.la: Vers. 31. Quod si quis esurit, domi edat: ne ad condemnationem conveniatis. Reliqua verò, quum venero, constituam.
units.tr: Verse 34: If anyone is hungry, let him eat at home, so that you do not come together for condemnation. The remaining matters I will set in order when I come.

units.la: Sextò, Vetando convivandi illum morem, in publico per ἀγαπας ante sacram synaxin & jubendo, ut si opus fuerit, comedant domi ad famem sedandam, repetito periculo profanationis Coenae, & judicii divini sequuturi[?]. Tandem quia impossibile erat, omnia quae ad particularem aliquam Ecclesiam spectant, perspicere aut praescribere, nisi praesens fuisset, reliqua, de ordine specialiter in Ecclesia illa observando, curaturum se pollicetur, ubi venerit.
units.tr: Sixthly, he forbids that custom of feasting in public through the love-feasts before the holy synaxis, and commands that, if necessary, they eat at home to satisfy their hunger, since the danger of profaning the Supper and the divine judgment that would follow is again at stake. Finally, because it was impossible to foresee or prescribe everything that concerns a particular church unless he were present, he promises that he will attend to the remaining matters, especially the order to be observed in that church, when he comes.

units.la: Caput duodecimum.
units.tr: Chapter 12.

units.la: Articulus octavus, de Usu dono- rum spiritualium.
units.tr: Article eight, on the use of spiritual gifts.

units.la: Octavus Epistolae articulus de Spiritualibus donis, eorumque recto usu, tribus proximè sequentibus capitibus.
units.tr: The eighth article of the Epistle, on spiritual gifts and their right use, runs through the three chapters that immediately follow.

units.la: De donis Spiritualibus alii superbiebant, & alios prae se contemnebant, alii aliis ampliorem donorum mensuram invidebant; donis abutebantur plerique non ad mutuam aedificationem, sed ad discordiam: Scopus Apostoli est, abusus hos corrigere, ab iis dehortari, ad rectum usum hortari, idque argumentis sedecim: quorum alia evidentius concludunt unum, alia aliud scopi membrum, omnia verò prudentem usum donorum urgent.
units.tr: Some were proud of their spiritual gifts and despised others on that account, while others envied their neighbours a greater measure of gifts. Most people abused the gifts, using them not for mutual edification but for discord. The Apostle's aim is to correct these abuses, to dissuade from them, and to exhort to the right use of the gifts. He does this with sixteen arguments. Some of them conclude more clearly for one part of this aim and others for another, but all of them press the prudent use of the gifts.

units.la: Verf. 1. Porro de spiritualibus donis, fratres, nolim vos in ignorantia versari:
units.tr: Verse 1. Moreover, brethren, concerning spiritual gifts, I would not have you be ignorant.

units.la: Abusum omnem comprehendit Apostolus, unâ ignoratione seu imprudentia ; rectum verò usum, contrariâ prudentiâ. Thesis confirmanda ergo ab Apostolo proposita est hæc, Non debetis in ignoratione versari, vel imprudenter vos gerere in negotio spiritualium donorum, sed prudenter.
units.tr: By "ignorance" or "imprudence" the Apostle comprehends every abuse, and by "prudence" the right use. The thesis, then, which the Apostle proposes to confirm is this: you ought not to remain in ignorance, or to behave imprudently in the matter of spiritual gifts, but to act prudently.

units.la: Verf. 2. Scitis vos Gentes fuisse, qui ad idola illa muta, prout rapi contigisset abripiebamini.
units.tr: Verse 2. You know that when you were Gentiles, you were led away to those dumb idols, however you happened to be carried off.

units.la: Argumentum primum, A comparatione pristini & præfentis status, in hunc sensum : Non ita pridem, destituti omnibus Spiritus sancti donis, pro libitu Diaboli, impuri illius spiritus abripiebamini, ut reliquæ Gentes, in crassissimum mutorum fimulachrorum cultum, seu in Idololatriam. Ergo nunc conversi, & spiritualibus donis ornati, prudenter versari debetis, attendentes, ne à malo Spiritu rapiamini, ad non minus noxia vitia, in donorum spiritualium abusu.
units.tr: The first argument is drawn from a comparison of the former and present state, in this sense: not long ago, destitute of all the gifts of the Holy Spirit, you were carried off at the will of the Devil, by that unclean spirit, as the other Gentiles were, into the grossest worship of dumb images, that is, into idolatry. Therefore, now converted and adorned with spiritual gifts, you ought to act prudently, taking care not to be carried off by the evil spirit into vices no less harmful, through the abuse of spiritual gifts.

units.la: Verf. 3 Quapropter notum vobis facio, nullum per Spiritum Dei loquentem, dicere Iesum anathema: & neminem posse dicere Iesum Dominum, nisi per Spiritum sanctum.
units.tr: Verse 3. Wherefore I make known to you that no one speaking by the Spirit of God says, "Jesus is accursed," and no one can say, "Jesus is Lord," except by the Holy Spirit.

units.la: Arg. 2. Quam certò blasphemantes Christum, destituuntur ipfius Spiritu ; tam certò omnes vos, qui fide sincera profitemini Iesum Christum Dominum vestrum, Spiritum Sanctum habetis, seu Spiritus Sancti salvificum & potissimum donum, absque quo non poffletis eum sincera fide profiteri: Ergo de aliis donis Spiritualibus, quæ non comitantur salutem necessariò, non debetis alii aliis invidere.
units.tr: Second argument. Just as certainly as those who blaspheme Christ are deprived of his Spirit, so certainly all of you who with sincere faith profess Jesus Christ your Lord have the Holy Spirit, that is, the saving and chief gift of the Holy Spirit, without which you could not profess him with sincere faith. Therefore, concerning the other spiritual gifts, which do not necessarily accompany salvation, you ought not to envy one another.

units.la: Verf. 4. Distinctiones autem donorum sunt, sed idem Spiritus:
units.tr: Verse 4. Now there are diversities of gifts, but the same Spirit.

units.la: Arg. 3. Licet sint diversa dona, omnia tamen fluunt ab eodem fonte, & uno Spiritu sancto: Ergo in usu horum donorum debetis prudenter versari, & amicè conspirare.
units.tr: Third argument. Although the gifts are diverse, they all flow from the same source and the one Holy Spirit. Therefore, in the use of these gifts you ought to act prudently and to work together in friendship.

units.la: Verf. 5. Et distinctiones miniferiorum sunt sed idem Dominus:
units.tr: Verse 5. And there are diversities of ministries, but the same Lord.

units.la: Arg. 4. Functiones, administrationes, & officia ecclefiaft ca sunt plura, sed idem Dominus, cui omnes servire debetis: Ergo prudenter debetis versari, & opus unius DOMINI promovere.
units.tr: Fourth argument. The functions, administrations and offices of the Church are many, but the Lord is the same, whom all of you ought to serve. Therefore you ought to act prudently and to advance the work of the one Lord.

units.la: Verf. 6. Et distinctiones operationum sunt, sed idem est Deus, agens omnia in omnibus.
units.tr: Verse 6. And there are diversities of operations, but it is the same God who works all in all.

units.la: Arg. 5. Diversæ sunt operationes, diversa opera, producta à diversis hominibus ut instrumentis, sed idem Deus est operans illa opera in diversis illis instrumentis: Ergo nulla de his debet esse discordia: Dona ascripsit Spiritui sancto, qui dona & ordinaria & extraordinaria, secundum necessitatem ecclesiæ distribuit, vers 4. functiones & officia ascripsit Christo, qui in domo sua Dominus ministeria quæ vult constituit, quos vult ad officia vocat, & in functionibus vocatos ut vult adhibet, v. 5. Operationes vero, seu excercitia donorum cujusvis generis, ascribit hoc versu Deo Patri, qui ut est primum omnium principium, ita intime in omnibus operatur: nec ideo hæc distinguit Apostolus, quasi dona, officia, & operationes, sic sint unius personæ, ut non sint omnium personarum, sed quod nos opus habeamus, ut per huj smodi distinctionem donorum, officiorum, & operationum, quæ ad idem opus producendum concurrunt, ad distinctionem personarum & unitatem essentiæ facilius apprehendendam manu ducamur, utque æqualitatem personarum sacrosanctæ Trinitatis, earumque in donis officiis & donorum excercitiis unitatem observaremus, & observantes, concorditer in bonum ecclesiæ, & gloriam Dei, omnes conspiraremus.
units.tr: Fifth argument. There are diverse operations and diverse works, produced by diverse men as instruments, but it is the same God who works those works in those diverse instruments. Therefore there ought to be no discord about these things. He ascribes gifts to the Holy Spirit, who distributes gifts, both ordinary and extraordinary, according to the needs of the Church. In verse 4 he ascribes functions and offices to Christ, who as Lord in his own house appoints the ministries he wills, calls whom he wills to offices, and employs the called in their functions as he wills. In verse 5, however, he ascribes operations, that is, the exercises of gifts of every kind, to God the Father, who, as the first principle of all, works inwardly in all things. Nor does the Apostle distinguish these things as if gifts, offices and operations belonged to one person so as not to belong to all the persons. Rather, we need to be led by this distinction of gifts, offices and operations, which concur in producing the same work, so that we may more easily grasp the distinction of persons and the unity of essence, and so that we may observe the equality of the persons of the most holy Trinity and their unity in the gifts, offices and exercises of the gifts. Observing this, we might all work together in harmony for the good of the Church and the glory of God.

units.la: Vers 7. Unicuique vero datur declaratio Spiritus ad utilitatem.
units.tr: Verse 7. But to each is given the manifestation of the Spirit for the common good.

units.la: Arg. 6. Spiritualia dona, seu manifestationes Spiritus, in quibus scilicet Spiritus manifestatur, dantur in unum finem, scilicet in bonum, & ædificationem totius Ecclesiæ: Ergo discordia de iis esse non debet.
units.tr: Sixth argument. Spiritual gifts, or manifestations of the Spirit, in which the Spirit is made known, are given to one end, namely the good and edification of the whole Church. Therefore there ought to be no discord about them.

units.la: Vers. 8. Nam huic quidem per Spiritum datur sermo sapientiæ: alij vero sermo cognitionis per eundem spiritum:
units.tr: Verse 8. For to one is given through the Spirit the word of wisdom, to another the word of knowledge through the same Spirit.

units.la: Hoc ostendit enumerando novem genera donorum, quæ omnia tendunt in bonum Ecclesiæ: Primum, donum, Sapientiæ verbum datur uni, quo possit doctrinam sanam ad auditores opportunè applicare, quod pastoris donum est: Secundum, Alii datur verbum cognitionis, quod doctoris donum est, quo possit sensum Scripturæ, & generalem doctrinam proponere perspicuè, licet donum commodè applicandi non habeat.
units.tr: He shows this by enumerating nine kinds of gifts, all of which tend to the good of the Church. The first, the gift of the word of wisdom, is given to one, by which he may apply sound doctrine opportunely to his hearers; this is the gift of the minister. The second, the word of knowledge, is given to another; this is the gift of the teacher, by which he can set forth the sense of Scripture and general doctrine clearly, although he may not have the gift of applying it appropriately.

units.la: Vers. 9. Alteri vero fides, per eundem Spiritum: alij vero donum sanationum per eundem Spiritum.
units.tr: Verse 9. To another faith through the same Spirit, to another the gifts of healing through the same Spirit.

units.la: Vers. 10. Alij vero operatio virtutum, alij vero prophetia, alij vero discretio spirituum. alteri vero genera linguarum: alij vero interpretatio linguarum.
units.tr: Verse 10. To another the working of miracles, to another prophecy, to another the discerning of spirits, to another various kinds of tongues, to another the interpretation of tongues.

units.la: Donum 3. Est fides, quæ miraculorum insigniorum & plurium scilicet dicitur, & capite sequenti vocatur omnis fides: 4. Est donum sanandi morbos, quod erat unum tantum genus miraculorum, ut reliqua sequentia. 5. Donum edendi signa, & potenter compelcendi dæmones, & Ecclesiæ hostes, cujus exemplum habetur Act. 13. 11. 6. Donum prædicendi futura, & revelandi secreta: 7. Donum discernendi impostituras à veris Spiritus donis: 8. Donum loquendi variis linguis: 9. Donum intelligendi varias linguas, seu interpretandi, sine dono loquendi illis linguis. Nam ut patebit infra aliqui loquebantur linguis qui non poterant interpretari, & contra: sic enim visum est Deo dona distribuere.
units.tr: The third gift is faith, which is called the faith of greater miracles and of many, and in the following chapter is called all faith. The fourth is the gift of healing diseases, which was only one kind of miracle, as are the others that follow. The fifth is the gift of working signs and of powerfully restraining demons and enemies of the Church; an example is found in Acts 13.11. The sixth is the gift of foretelling the future and revealing secrets. The seventh is the gift of discerning impostures from true gifts of the Spirit. The eighth is the gift of speaking in various tongues. The ninth is the gift of understanding various tongues, or of interpreting them, apart from the gift of speaking those tongues. For, as will become clear below, some spoke in tongues who could not interpret, and conversely, since God was pleased to distribute gifts in this way.

units.la: Verf. 11 Sed omnia hæc agit unus ille & idem Spiritus, distribuens privatim illa singulis sicut vult.
units.tr: Verse 11. But all these things one and the same Spirit works, distributing to each one individually as he wills.

units.la: Arg. 7. Ad prudentem donorum usum: Hæc diversitas donorum, & distributio eorum, est secundum arbitrium Dei facta: Ergo in ejus voluntate est acquiescendum, iisque sine discordia utendum.
units.tr: Seventh argument, concerning the prudent use of gifts. This diversity of gifts and their distribution has been made according to the will of God. Therefore we ought to acquiesce in his will and use the gifts without discord.

units.la: Verf. 12. Sicut enim corpus unum est, & membra habet multa, omnia vero illa membra corporis quod unicum est, multa sunt, sed unum sunt corpus: ita & Christus.
units.tr: Verse 12. For just as the body is one and has many members, and all the members of the body, though many, are one body, so also is Christ.

units.la: Arg. 8. CHRISTUS mysticus, seu CHRISTUS cum Ecclesia est unum corpus, ex pluribus membris, iisque instructis varietate donorum, constans: Ergo sicut in corpore humano, sic in corpore mystico, concordia debet esse in donorum usu.
units.tr: Eighth argument. Mystical Christ, that is, Christ together with the Church, is one body, made up of many members, and these are equipped with a variety of gifts. Therefore, as in the human body, so in the mystical body, there ought to be harmony in the use of the gifts.

units.la: Verf. 13 Etenim per unum Spiritum nos omnes in unum corpus baptizati sumus & Judæi, & Græci & servi, & liberi: & omnes potati sumus in unum Spiritum.
units.tr: Verse 13. For by one Spirit we were all baptized into one body, whether Jews or Greeks, whether slaves or free, and we were all made to drink of one Spirit.

units.la: Arg. 9. Sacramento Baptismi & Cœnæ Dominicæ omnes Fideles connectuntur, seu omnium Fidelium coalitio in unam Ecclesiam, & unius vitæ participationem obsignatur in Sacramentis, in unum corpus & unum Spiritum: Ergo non debetis propter diversitatem donorum, à vobis invicem diffidere.
units.tr: Ninth argument. All the faithful are joined together by the sacrament of Baptism and the Lord's Supper; the union of all the faithful into one Church is sealed, and the participation in one life is sealed in the sacraments, into one body and one Spirit. Therefore you ought not, because of the diversity of gifts, to distrust one another.

units.la: Verf. 14. Etenim corpus non est unum membrum, sed multa.
units.tr: Verse 14. For the body is not one member, but many.

units.la: Verf. 15 Si dicat pes, Quia non sum manus, non sum ex corpore: num propterea non est ex corpore.
units.tr: Verse 15. If the foot should say, "Because I am not a hand, I am not of the body," is it therefore not of the body?

units.la: Verf. 16. Etsi dicat auris, Quia non sum oculus, non sum ex corpore: num propterea non est ex corpore.
