units.la: Non cum] Arg. 2. Confirmans superius. Fons conversationis meæ erat gratia Dei, quæ sibi similis & constans est, & non verlipellis illa prudentia, quâ carnales homines suorum commodorum causa simulant erga alios studium, quo plane destituuntur. Ergo non suspicandum vobis est de meorum morum, aut affectus erga vos mutatione.
units.tr: Not with: Argument 2, confirming what was said above. The source of my conduct was the grace of God, which is like itself and constant, and not that shifting prudence by which carnal men, for the sake of their own advantage, feign zeal toward others, a zeal in which they are plainly lacking. Therefore you must not suspect a change in my conduct or in my affection toward you.

units.la: Verf. 13. Non enim alia scribimus vobis quàm quæ legitis, aut etiam agnoscitis. Spero autem vos etiam ad extremum agnituros:
units.tr: Verse 13. For we write no other things to you than what you read, or even acknowledge. And I hope you will acknowledge them to the end.

units.la: Confirmat quod dixit, & simul addit Argumentum tertium: Quia facta ipsius scriptis & dictis respondebant (in quo taxare videtur adversarios qui aliter se gerebant, ut etiam in superiori argumento) quod probat testimonio ipsorum Corinthiorum, qui licet susurris adversariorum aliquantulum turbarentur, agnoscebant tamen ipsius sinceritatem & constantiam, & porro postea erant agnituri, ut sperabat: Non ergo suspicandum sinistrè quicquam de morum ipsius mutatione.
units.tr: He confirms what he has said and at the same time adds the third argument: his deeds agreed with his writings and sayings. (In this he seems to censure the adversaries, who behaved otherwise, as also in the previous argument.) He proves this by the testimony of the Corinthians themselves, who, although somewhat disturbed by the whisperings of the adversaries, nevertheless acknowledged his sincerity and constancy, and, as he hoped, would acknowledge them still more afterwards. Therefore no unfavourable suspicion about a change in his conduct should be entertained.

units.la: Vers. 14 Sicut & aliquatenus agnovistis nos gloriationem vestram esse, quemadmodum & vos nostra estis, in diem Domini Iesu.
units.tr: Verse 14. As also you have in part acknowledged us, that we are your rejoicing, even as you are ours, in the day of the Lord Jesus.

units.la: Arg. 4. Quia aliqua ex parte (etiamsi non ea confidentia contra Pseudapostolos qua decuit) gloriabantur Corinthii se ab Apostolo conversos fuisse, & Apostolus gloriabatur de iis, ut de Apostolatus sui fructu, & gloriaturum porro se sperabat in die Judicii: Ergo nulla causa suspicionis de alienatione animi ipsius ab iis.
units.tr: Argument 4. The Corinthians, to some extent (though not with the confidence that they ought to have shown against the false apostles), boasted that they had been converted by the Apostle, and the Apostle boasted of them as the fruit of his apostleship, and he hoped to go on boasting of them in the day of judgment. Therefore there is no cause for suspicion that his mind has been alienated from them.

units.la: Vers. 15. Itaque hac fiducia prius volui ad vos venire, ut secundam gratiam haberetis:
units.tr: Verse 15. And in this confidence I was minded to come to you first, that you might have a second grace.

units.la: Vers. 16. Et per vos transire in Macedoniam, & rursum à Macedonia venire ad vos, & à vobis deduci in Judæam.
units.tr: Verse 16. And to pass by you into Macedonia, and to come again out of Macedonia to you, and to be brought on my way by you into Judea.

units.la: Arg. s. Quia ipsi propositum firmum stabat proficiscendi ad Corinthios in mutuæ benevolentiæ fiducia, ut conversionis primum beneficium cumularet, confirmatione fidei, tanquam secundo beneficio; & ut indicia benevolentiæ ipsorum erga se ab iis, in officiis quæ enumerat, etiam acciperet ad dilectionis mutuæ incrementum: Non ergo suspicandum, &c.
units.tr: Argument 5. He had a firm purpose of going to the Corinthians, in the confidence of mutual goodwill, so that he might add to the first benefit of their conversion a second benefit, the strengthening of their faith. He also meant to receive from them, in the services which he enumerates, tokens of their goodwill toward him, for the increase of mutual love. Therefore one should not suspect, etc.

units.la: Vers. 17. Hoc igitur quum deliberarem, nunquid levitate sum usus? aut num quæ delibero, secundùm carnem delibero, ut sit apud me Etiam & Non?
units.tr: Verse 17. When therefore I was deliberating this, did I use lightness? Or do I deliberate according to the flesh, so that with me there is both Yes and No?

units.la: Arg. 6. Per solutionem objectionis propositum: Adventum meum ad vos distuli diutius quam voluissem, non ex levitate animi in vos mutati, sed ut postea patebit, ex dilectione erga vos, ut vobis parcerem, quos censuris Ecclesiasticis castigare oportuisset, si ad vos prius venissem. Non ergo suspicandum est, alienatum meum à vobis animum esse. Objectio proponitur iis terminis quibus adversarii ipsum calumniabantur, quasi vanum, & levem, instar irregenitorum & carnalium loquentem, & promittentem quæ non statuerat præstare, sicut qui leviter promittunt, & leviter mutant consilium, cujus neque dictis, (& per consequens) [?]quens) neque doctrinæ constiterit certitudo aliqua, & cui idcirco fides non erat adhibenda.
units.tr: Argument 6, by answering the objection put forward. I postponed my coming to you longer than I wished, not out of a fickle mind changed toward you, but, as will afterwards be made plain, out of love for you, so that I might spare you, whom I should have had to chastise with ecclesiastical censures if I had come to you first. Therefore one must not suspect that my mind has been alienated from you. The objection is put in the terms by which the adversaries slandered him, as though he were vain and light, speaking like the unregenerate and carnal, and promising things he had not decided to perform, like those who make promises lightly and change their plans lightly. His words and his teaching therefore had no certainty, and so they should not be trusted. (Here the reading "[?]quens" stands for "consequens", and the sense is "and consequently".)

units.la: Verf. 18. Imò fidelis Deus novit sermonem nostrum apud vos non fuisse Etiam & Non.
units.tr: Verse 18. But God is faithful, and our word toward you was not Yes and No.

units.la: Respondet objectioni, & quia plus cavet ne doctrinæ imputetur quicquam, quam ne ipsius famæ derogetur, respondet primum de doctrina, & confirmat ejus veritatem quinque rationibus: Ratio prima: Quia cum doctrina ipsius fuerit Dei verbum, veram fuisse necesse erat: quia Deus verus & fidelis est, cujus dictata solum apud eos docebat, non vero modo affirmans, modo negans idem, sicut qui sibi non constant, modo etiam, modo non. Idcirco de veritate doctrinæ, non erat illis dubitandum.
units.tr: He answers the objection, and since he is more careful that nothing be imputed to his teaching than that his reputation be damaged, he first answers concerning the teaching and confirms its truth by five reasons. First reason: since his teaching was the word of God, it had necessarily to be true, because God is true and faithful, and he taught only what God had dictated to them. He did not, however, affirm one thing now and deny the same thing later, like men who are not consistent with themselves, saying now yes, now no. Therefore they had no reason to doubt the truth of his teaching.

units.la: Verf. 19. Nam Dei filius Iesus Christus, qui inter vos per nos prædicatus est, id est, per me & Sylvanum ac Timotheum, non fuit Etiam & Non, sed fuit Etiam in ipso.
units.tr: Verse 19. For the Son of God, Jesus Christ, who was preached among you by us, that is, by me and Silvanus and Timothy, was not Yes and No, but in him is Yes.

units.la: Ratio 2. Nihil aliud continebat mea doctrina, & collegarum meorum quam unum Iesum Christum, qui est Dei filius immutabilis, & æterna semper sibi constans veritas. Ergo de doctrina mea non est dubitandum.
units.tr: Second reason. My teaching and that of my colleagues contained nothing but the one Jesus Christ, who is the immutable Son of God, the eternal truth always consistent with himself. Therefore one must not doubt my teaching.

units.la: Verf. 20. Quotquot enim sunt promissiones Dei, in ipso sunt Etiam, & in ipso sunt Amen, ad Dei gloriam per nos.
units.tr: Verse 20. For however many are the promises of God, in him they are Yes, and in him Amen, to the glory of God through us.

units.la: Ratio 3. Confirmans superiorem. Omnes Dei promissiones in Christo & per Christum sunt ratæ, immutabiles, & completa: partim quatenus est Filius Dei, per quem omnia facta sunt: partim quatenus est Mediator <bl>Διαθηκης</bl>, qui promissam redemptionem nostri complevit, & merito suo impetravit, ut bona promissa præstentur nobis, & reipsa nobis applicat. Ergo prædicatio nostra quæ nihil aliud continet, necessario firma est, nec de ea dubitandum.
units.tr: Third reason, confirming the previous one. All the promises of God in Christ and through Christ are ratified, unchangeable and fulfilled: partly as he is the Son of God, through whom all things were made, and partly as he is the Mediator of the covenant [διαθήκης], who has accomplished the promised redemption of ours, obtained it by his merit, and actually applies to us the good things promised. Therefore our preaching, which contains nothing but this, is necessarily firm, and one must not doubt it.

units.la: Ratio 4. Sicut promissiones Dei sunt etiam & Amen in Christo, id est, ratæ & completæ reipsâ; sic ut etiam & Amen, id est ratæ & completæ esse agnoscantur, & prædicentur per nos, vel à nobis, ad gloriam Dei facit, qui non nisi in Christo promissiones suas compleri vult: Ergo tam firma est prædicatio nostra, quam certa est Dei glorificandi ratio in Christo, nec de ea dubitandum.
units.tr: Fourth reason. As the promises of God are also Yes and Amen in Christ, that is, ratified and actually fulfilled, so that they are acknowledged and proclaimed as also Yes and Amen, that is, ratified and fulfilled, by us or through us, to the glory of God, and as he wills his promises to be fulfilled only in Christ, our preaching is as firm as the certain way of glorifying God in Christ is certain. Therefore one must not doubt it.

units.la: Verf. 21. Porrò qui nos confirmat vobiscum in Christum, & qui unxit nos, Deus est.
units.tr: Verse 21. Now he who establishes us with you in Christ, and who has anointed us, is God;

units.la: Verf. 25. Qui etiam obsignavit nos, dedit que arrhabonem Spiritus in cordibus nostris.
units.tr: Verse 25. Who has also sealed us, and given the earnest of the Spirit in our hearts.

units.la: Ratio 5. Deus author est huius fidei nostrae in Christum, confirmans & nostram Apostolorum praedicationem, & vestram Corinthiorum, (quotquot synceri estis) fidem, partim communicando Spiritus dona varia, quasi unctionem à Christo, partim sigillum suum quasi nostrae fidei vicissim intus appendendo, dum certos reddit de Evangelii veritate, & gaudium excitat ineffabile & gloriosum, quod est quasi arrha futurae felicitatis: Ergo praedicatio nostra firma est, nec de ea dubitandum est.
units.tr: Fifth reason. God is the author of this faith of ours in Christ. He confirms both our apostolic preaching and your faith, Corinthians (all of you who are sincere), partly by imparting various gifts of the Spirit, like an anointing from Christ, and partly by inwardly affixing his seal, as it were, to our faith in return, since he makes us certain of the truth of the Gospel and stirs up an unspeakable and glorious joy, which is as it were a pledge of future happiness. Therefore our preaching is firm, and one must not doubt it.

units.la: His omnibus argumentis pensitatis, nulla ratione suspicari poterant Corinthii quod praedicationi Apostoli tot modis divinitus confirmatae, quicquam falsitatis aut incertitudinis subesse potuerit, atque ita occurrit objectioni, quatenus ad doctrinae veritatem labefactandam tendebat.
units.tr: Having weighed all these arguments, the Corinthians could by no means suspect that anything of falsehood or uncertainty could lie in the preaching of the Apostle, which had been so many ways confirmed by God. So he meets the objection, insofar as it tended to undermine the truth of the teaching.

units.la: Verf. 23. Ego verò testem Deum invoco in animam meam, me idcirco nondum venisse Corinthum, ut vobis parcam.
units.tr: Verse 23. But I call God as witness upon my soul, that I have not yet come to Corinth in order to spare you.

units.la: Jam solvit objectionem, quatenus ipsius æstimationem & mores attingebat, causam veram cur non venerit ad eos reddendo, nimirum ut dato resipiscentiae spatio, Corinthiis parceret, id est cohiberet se à severiori ipsorum tractatione, quam praesens exercere coactus fuisset; & dictum juramento confirmat, quia sic rei gravitas exigebat, non ergo levitate morum distulerat promissum suum ad eos adventum.
units.tr: He now answers the objection, insofar as it touched on his reputation and conduct, by giving the true reason why he did not come to them: namely, that by granting them a period for repentance he might spare the Corinthians, that is, restrain himself from the harsher treatment of them which he would have been forced to inflict had he been present. He confirms this with an oath, because the gravity of the matter required it; so he had not postponed his promised visit to them out of fickleness of character.

units.la: Verf. 24. Non quòd dominemur vestrae fidei, sed quòd administri simus gaudij vestri, nam fide statis.
units.tr: Verse 24. Not that we lord it over your faith, but that we are helpers of your joy; for by faith you stand.

units.la: Hinc oritur alia objectio: Ergo te ut Dominum fidei nostrae ostentas, quasi punire possis quando vis? Respondet negando dominium, & affirmando ministerii potestatem, eamque ad bonum Ecclesiae accommodandam, ut tempestivis censuris, pro Christi voluntate adhibitis, resipiscentes, tandem gauderent. Negati dominii in fidem ipsorum, rationem reddit: quia fides est vinculum conjunctionis cum Christo, per quam fidem, in gratia Dei, in jure & titulo ad Christum, in possessione praesentium, & in spe futurorum bonorum stamus, idcirco fides non admittit Dominum ullum praeter Deum, homines vero admittit duntaxat, ut Ministros Dei.
units.tr: Hence arises another objection: so do you put yourself forward as the lord of our faith, as though you could punish whenever you pleased? He answers by denying lordship and affirming the power of the ministry, and that this power is to be applied to the good of the Church, so that by timely censures, applied according to Christ's will, the repentant might at last rejoice. He gives the reason for denying lordship over their faith: because faith is the bond of union with Christ, through which we stand in the grace of God, in the right and title to Christ, in the possession of present goods, and in the hope of future goods; therefore faith admits no lord besides God, whereas it admits men only as ministers of God.

units.la: Caput Secundum.
units.tr: Chapter 2.

units.la: Apitis duæ sunt partes: in prima pergit apologiam texere, de constanti voluntate sua erga Corinthios, ad versum 14. In altera inchoat apologiam pro ministerio suo, ad finem.
units.tr: The chapter has two parts. In the first, the Apostle goes on to weave a defence of his constant goodwill towards the Corinthians, down to verse 14. In the second, he begins a defence of his own ministry, to the end.

units.la: In prima, superioribus argumentis ad probandum animum suum à Corinthiis minime alienatum, addit indicia benevolentiæ suæ in eos, etc.
units.tr: In the first part, using his earlier arguments to prove that his mind had by no means been turned away from the Corinthians, he adds further signs of his goodwill towards them, etc.

units.la: Verf. 1. Hoc autem mihi faciendum judicavi, ne rursus ad vos cum tristitia veniam.
units.tr: Verse 1. But I determined this for myself, that I would not come to you again in sorrow.

units.la: Indicium primum, Quod causa mutati consilii, de adventu suo ad eos fuerit, ne tristitiam afferret Corinthiis, in adventu suo coactus severius ipsorum mores castigare, quos emendatos cupiebat prius quam veniret.
units.tr: First sign: the reason for changing his plan about his visit to them was that he would not bring sorrow to the Corinthians. Coming to them, he would have been forced to rebuke their morals more severely, and he wanted them to be amended before he came.

units.la: Verf. 2. Nam si ego tristitia vos afficiam, quis est qui exhilaret me, nisi ipse qui tristitia afficitur ex me.
units.tr: Verse 2. For if I make you sorrowful, who then is there to make me glad, but the one who is made sorrowful by me?

units.la: Indicium 2. Quod tanta fuerit ipsi cum Corinthiis sympathia, ut nequiret nisi ipsis hilaribus gaudere, nec temperare sibi à tristitia, quamdiu quisquam inter eos per eum contristatus maneret.
units.tr: Second sign: his sympathy with the Corinthians was so great that he could not rejoice unless they rejoiced too, and he could not keep himself from sorrow as long as anyone among them remained saddened on his account.

units.la: Verf. 3. Et hoc ipsum vobis scripsi, ne, quum venero, tristitiam capiam ex iis de quibus oportebat me gaudere: confisus de vobis omnibus, meum gaudium, omnium vestrum gaudium esse.
units.tr: Verse 3. And this very thing I wrote to you, lest, when I came, I should have sorrow from those over whom I ought to rejoice, being confident of you all, that my joy is the joy of you all.

units.la: Indicium 3. Quod ipsa scriptio, non tantum superioris Epistolæ, sed etiam hujus secundæ Epistolæ, eo fine suscepta fuerit, ne si venisset ad eos, & impænitentes comperisset præter tristitiam de ipsorum peccato, coactus fuisset accersere sibi novam tristitiam, quam necessaria severitas illis, & sibi ipsi esset creatura.
units.tr: Third sign: the writing itself, not only of the earlier Epistle but also of this second Epistle, was undertaken for this purpose: that if he came to them and found them unrepentant, he would have had, besides sorrow over their sin, to bring upon himself a fresh sorrow, which their necessary severity would have caused both them and himself.

units.la: Confisus ] Indicium 4. Quod persuasum habuerit, gaudium suum ipsis etiam Corinthiis gaudii materiam fuisse, & ipsorum gaudia sibi & illis communia esse. Verf. 4. Nam ex multa oppressione & anxietate cordis, scripsi vobis per multas lacrhymas: non ut tristitia afficiamini, sed ut cognoscatis charitatem quam habeo abundantissimam erga vos:
units.tr: Being confident: Fourth sign: he was persuaded that his joy was also a cause of joy to the Corinthians themselves, and that their joys were shared between him and them. Verse 4. For out of much affliction and anguish of heart I wrote to you with many tears, not that you should be made sorrowful, but that you might know the abundant love I have for you.

units.la: Indicium 5. Quod superior Epistola, quæ necessario asperior erat, non sine lachrymis ab ipso exarata fuerit, & eo quidem fine, ut testatam faceret suam erga eos propensissimam voluntatem, non ut eos tristitia afficeret.
units.tr: Fifth sign: the earlier Epistle, which was necessarily rather harsh, was written by him not without tears, and indeed for this purpose: to show his most sincere goodwill towards them, not to make them sorrowful.

units.la: Verf. 5. Quòd si quis tristitiam attulit, non mihi tristitiam attulit, sed quadantenus (ne illum aggravem) vobis omnibus.
units.tr: Verse 5. But if anyone has caused sorrow, he has not caused sorrow to me, but in some measure (not to burden him too much) to you all.

units.la: Indicium 6. Benevoli sui animi erga Corinthios, Quod Apostolus nihili fecerit tristitiam quam incestuosus ipsi creaverat, præ mærore illo quem accersiverat omnibus Corinthiis: Addit (Ex parte) quia tristitia hæc jam conversa erat in gaudium, per resipiscentiam incestuosi, idcirco mitigandi causa se add disse dicit (ex parte) propter incestuosum jam resipiscentem, ne ei jam in se gravato, onus adjiceret, si peccatum nimis aggravaret
units.tr: Sixth sign of his kindly disposition towards the Corinthians: the Apostle made little of the sorrow which the incestuous man had caused him, compared with the grief which he had brought upon all the Corinthians. He adds "in part", because this sorrow had now been turned into joy through the repentance of the incestuous man; so, for the sake of softening, he says he has spoken "in part", on account of the incestuous man who now repents, so that he would not add a burden to one already weighed down, by making the offence seem too grave.

units.la: Verf. 6. Sufficit istiusmodi homini ista objurgatio à pluribus profecta.
units.tr: Verse 6. Sufficient to such a man is this rebuke, which was given by many.

units.la: Indicium 7. Quod jam paratus sit incestuosum pænitentem, in gratiam recipere, & sic documentum lenitatis suæ, & mansuetudinis dare, ut appareat priorem severitatem non nisi à dilectione, & studio utilitatis Ecclesiæ Corinthiacæ provenisse. In quem finem hujus incestuosi castigationem, authoritate multorum (id est, Ecclesiæ gubernatorum, conscia & consentiente Ecclesia) inflictam, & hactenus incumbentem, postquam jam constabat eum resipuisse sufficere pronunciat.
units.tr: Seventh sign: he is already prepared to receive the repentant incestuous man back into favour, and so to give proof of his gentleness and mildness, so that it may appear that his earlier severity arose only from love and concern for the good of the Corinthian Church. To this end he declares that the punishment of this incestuous man, inflicted by the authority of many (that is, of the Church's rulers, with the knowledge and consent of the Church), and continuing until now, is enough, since it was now clear that he had repented.

units.la: Verf. 7. Ut è contrario potius vos ei condonetis, eumque consolemini, ne quo modo redundante tristitia absorbeatur vir hujusmodi.
units.tr: Verse 7. So that, on the contrary, you should rather forgive him and comfort him, lest by any means such a man be swallowed up with overmuch sorrow.

units.la: Ut lenitatem suam erga incestuosum pænitentem demonstret, suadet ut ab Ecclesia Corinthiaca rursum in gratiam recipiatur, additis sex rationibus.
units.tr: To show his gentleness towards the repentant incestuous man, he urges that he be received back into favour by the Corinthian Church, adding six reasons.

units.la: Ratio prima, Quia tenentur resipiscenti ignoscere offensam, eumque consolari, non minus quam impænitentem tenebantur excommunicare.
units.tr: First reason: they were bound to forgive the offence of a repentant man and to comfort him, no less than they were bound to excommunicate the impenitent.

units.la: Ne quo ] Ratio 2. Quia alioqui periculum erat, ne nimia tristitia absorberetur, nisi jam resipiscentem in gratiam reciperent.
units.tr: Lest by any means: Second reason: otherwise there was a danger that he would be swallowed up by excessive sorrow, unless they received him back into favour now that he repented.

units.la: Verf. 8. Quapropter precor vos ut ratam faciatis in illum charitatem.
units.tr: Verse 8. Wherefore I beseech you to confirm your love towards him.

units.la: Ratio 3. Quia (sic potissimùm rogati ab Apostolo) testatum facere suum erga eum amorem tenentur, ostendendo scilicet se excommunicasse hominem illum, non ut perderent, sed ut per resipiscentiam salvum eum facerent.
units.tr: Third reason: they were bound (and this was especially asked of them by the Apostle) to show their love for him, namely by showing that they had excommunicated that man not to destroy him, but so that through repentance they might save him.

units.la: Verf. 9 Nam in hunc finem etiam scripsi, ut cognoscerem probationem vestri, id est, an ad omnia obedientes sitis.
units.tr: Verse 9. For to this end also I wrote, that I might know the proof of you, whether you are obedient in all things.

units.la: Ratio 4. Quia hoc modo se in omnibus Apostoli dicto obedientes demonstraturi erant, sicut prius in excommunicando, sic etiam nunc, eum ab excommunicationis vinculo solvendo, in quo obedientiam ipsorum probabat Apostolus.
units.tr: Fourth reason: in this way they would show themselves obedient to the Apostle's word in all things. Just as before they had obeyed him in excommunicating, so now they should obey him in loosing the man from the bond of excommunication; and in this the Apostle was testing their obedience.

units.la: Verf. 10. Cui vero condonatis, & ego condono; nam & ego siquid condonavi, cui condonavi, propter vos id feci, in conspectu Christi, ut ne superemur à Satana.
units.tr: Verse 10. To whom you forgive anything, I also forgive; for if I have forgiven anything, to whom I have forgiven it, I did it for your sakes, in the sight of Christ, lest we should be outwitted by Satan.

units.la: Verf. 11. Non enim illius machinationes ignoramus.
units.tr: Verse 11. For we are not ignorant of his schemes.

units.la: Ratio 5. Quia Apostolus in gratiam Corinthiorum veniam illi concesserat, & cuivis condonaturus erat; Æquum ergo erat ut illi propter Apostolum huic ignosceremt.
units.tr: Fifth reason: the Apostle had granted pardon to him for the sake of the Corinthians, and he was ready to pardon anyone. It was therefore fair that they should pardon him for the Apostle's sake.

units.la: Superemur ] Ratio 6. Ne per Satanæ astutiam damnum pateretur Ecclesia, nisi ei jam resipiscenti ignosceret, nimia enim severitate in desperationem, vel in secessionem ab Ecclesia adduci possent peccatores, per Satanam, cujus artes & doli ad nocendum, non latent Ecclesiam.
units.tr: Lest we should be outwitted: Sixth reason: lest the Church suffer loss through Satan's cunning, if they did not forgive him now that he repented. For by excessive severity sinners could be driven into despair or into withdrawal from the Church, by Satan, whose arts and tricks for doing harm are not hidden from the Church.

units.la: Verf. 12 Porrò quum venissem Troadem ad prædicandum Evangelium Christi, etiamsi ostium mihi apertum erat per Dominum, non habui relaxationem in spiritu meo: eo quòd non invenissem Titum fratem meum:
units.tr: Verse 12. Moreover, when I came to Troas to preach the gospel of Christ, although a door was opened to me by the Lord, I had no rest in my spirit, because I did not find Titus my brother:

units.la: Verf. 13 Sed quum illis valedixissem, abii in Macedoniam.
units.tr: Verse 13. But when I had taken my leave of them, I went away into Macedonia.

units.la: Indicium 8. Constantis benevolentiæ suæ in Corinthios, Quod nusquam quiescere potuerit etiam magna spe promovendi Euangelii oblata, ut in Troade, donec ex Tito quem Corinthum miserat de ipsorum rebus cognovisset, cujus conveniendi causa profectus est in Macedoniam, ut certior de rebus Corinthiorum per eum fieret, & an maturum esset adhuc veniendi ad Corinthios tempus, diceret: Quibus omnibus indiciis propensæ suæ in Corinthios voluntatis, consideratis, Apostolus sibi persuadet remotum iri suspicionem alienati ab iis animi sui.
units.tr: Eighth sign of his constant goodwill towards the Corinthians: he could never be at rest, even when a great hope of advancing the gospel was offered, as at Troas, until he learned from Titus, whom he had sent to Corinth, how things stood with them. For this reason he went on to Macedonia, so that he might be better informed about the Corinthians' affairs through him, and might know whether it was still the right time to go to the Corinthians. Considering all these signs of his well-disposed will towards the Corinthians, the Apostle persuades himself that any suspicion that his mind had been alienated from them will be removed.

units.la: Secunda Pars.
units.tr: The Second Part.

units.la: Verf. 14. Deo autem gratia, qui facit ut semper triumphemus in Christo; & odorem notitiæ suæ manifestum facit per nos omni in loco.
units.tr: Verse 14. But thanks be to God, who always leads us in triumph in Christ, and through us makes manifest the fragrance of his knowledge in every place.

units.la: Secunda pars Capitis, in qua suum Ministerium, defendit, & commendabile probat, quinque argumentis, obiter insinuans se non fuisse otiosum, sed in opere Domini cum fructu occupatum, dum ab eis abesset.
units.tr: The second part of the chapter, in which he defends his ministry and shows it to be commendable, by five arguments, while hinting in passing that he had not been idle but had been busily and fruitfully engaged in the Lord's work during his absence from them.

units.la: Argumentum primum, Quia ipsius Ministerio Christus, & ipse in Christo, de hostibus triumphabat, eripiendo ex potestate Satanæ plurimos, eosque adducendo ad fidem Euangelii.
units.tr: The first argument: because through his ministry Christ, and he himself in Christ, triumphed over the enemy, snatching many from the power of Satan and bringing them to the faith of the Gospel.

units.la: Arg. 2. Quia per ipsius Ministerium quicunque tandem fuerit successus, suavitas Euangelii, & efficacia manifestata est ubique locorum, dum Christi cognitio vitam vitalem spirabat, qua vivificati sunt peccatores, & ad Deum conversi.
units.tr: Argument 2: because through his ministry, whatever success it had in any place, the sweetness and power of the Gospel were made manifest everywhere, since the knowledge of Christ breathed a living life by which sinners were made alive and converted to God.

units.la: Verf. 15. Nam Christi bona fragrantia sumus Deo in iis qui servantur, & in iis qui pereunt:
units.tr: Verse 15. For we are to God the sweet fragrance of Christ among those who are being saved and among those who are perishing.

units.la: Verf. 16. His quidem, odor mortis ad mortem: illis vero, odor vitæ ad vitam: & ad hæc quis idoneus?
units.tr: Verse 16. To the one we are the smell of death leading to death; to the other the smell of life leading to life. And who is sufficient for these things?

units.la: Occupando objectionem, quod multis fæterent Apostoli, simul & ipsorum prædicatio, respondet & addit Arg. 3. Quod tamen ipsi Apostoli, cum ipsorum Ministerio, Deo accepti fuerint, & per Christum gratum odorem Deo obtulerint, non minus in convictione & perditione reproborum, quibus Euangelium per accidens odor erat mortis, quam in credentium & salvatorum fide & salute, quibus Euangelium erat & natura sua, & effectu proprio, odor vitalis ad salutem.
units.tr: Anticipating the objection that the Apostles and their preaching stank to many, he answers, and adds Argument 3: that nevertheless the Apostles themselves, together with their ministry, were acceptable to God, and through Christ offered a sweet savour to God, no less in convicting and destroying the reprobate, to whom the Gospel was by accident a smell of death, than in the faith and salvation of believers, for whom the Gospel was, by its own nature and proper effect, a living fragrance unto salvation.

units.la: Arg. 4. Quia cum pauci essent idonei & sufficientes Ministri, (ut interrogatio ostendit) quorum Ministerium secundet & acceptet Deus, ipse erat in numero eorum qui ad hæc quæ dicta sunt, idonei facti sunt; tacitè perstringens Pseudapostolos, qui non erant idonei Ministri ad peccatorum conversionem, quantumvis se Apostolis præferebant.
units.tr: Argument 4: because, since there were few suitable and sufficient ministers (as the question shows) whose ministry God would support and accept, he himself was among those who had been made fit for these things that have been said. He tacitly reproaches the false apostles, who were not fit ministers for the conversion of sinners, however much they set themselves above the Apostles.

units.la: Verf. 17. Non enim, ut plerique, cauponamur sermonem Dei, sed ut ex sinceritate, sed ut ex Deo, in conspectu Dei, de Christo, loquimur
units.tr: Verse 17. For we are not, like many, peddlers of the word of God; but as of sincerity, but as of God, in the sight of God, we speak in Christ.

units.la: Confirmat proximum argumentum, apertius notans adversarios suos & aemulos, simulque addit Arg. 5. à dissimilitudine sui, & multorum praedicatorum: illi si non admiscebant falsam doctrinam, verae tamen doctrinae admiscebant affectus suos, ambitioni & avaritiae suae inservientes, & in hominum gratiam doctrinam flectentes: Apostolus vero 1. In sinceritate, id est, neque falsam doctrinam, neque pravos affectus admiscens: 2. Ex Deo, id est, cum fiducia & authoritate, cognoscens unde veniat: 3. In conspectu Dei, id est, testem adhibens Deum, & Dei gloriam intuens. 4. In Christo, id est; in Christi virtute, & virtutis ipsius agnitione, loquebatur: Ex quibus sequitur commendabile fuisse ipsius Ministerium, & minime contemnendum.
units.tr: He confirms the preceding argument, pointing more openly at his opponents and rivals, and at the same time adds Argument 5, from the difference between himself and many preachers. Those others, if they did not mix in false doctrine, nevertheless mixed their own affections with true doctrine, serving their ambition and greed and bending doctrine to win men's favour. The Apostle, however: (1) speaks "in sincerity", that is, mixing in neither false doctrine nor corrupt affections; (2) speaks "of God", that is, with confidence and authority, knowing whence he comes; (3) speaks "in the sight of God", that is, calling God as witness and keeping the glory of God in view; (4) speaks "in Christ", that is, in the power of Christ and with knowledge of that power. From these things it follows that his ministry was commendable and by no means to be despised.

units.la: Caput Tertium.
units.tr: Chapter 3.

units.la: Ergit Ministerium suum adversus obtrectatores defendere.
units.tr: He sets himself to defend his ministry against its detractors.

units.la: Partes Capitis sunt duae. In prima probat Ministerium suum commendabile esse, quinque Argumentis, ad verf. 6. In secunda illustrat & confirmat ultimum argumentum, comparatione Ministerii Legalis seu Foederis Operum, & Evangelici, seu Foederis Gratiae.
units.tr: The chapter has two parts. In the first, he proves that his ministry is commendable by five arguments, up to verse 6. In the second, he illustrates and confirms the last argument by comparing the ministry of the Law, or Covenant of Works, with the Gospel, or Covenant of Grace.

units.la: Verf. 1. Incipimus rursus nosipsos commendare? num egemus, ut nonnulli, commendatitiis epistolis apud vos, aut a vobis commendatitiis?
units.tr: Verse 1. Are we beginning again to commend ourselves? Or do we need letters of commendation to you or from you, as some do?

units.la: Argumentum primum commendationis Ministerii sui, continens etiam purgationem sui ab inanis gloriae desiderio.
units.tr: The first argument for the commendation of his ministry, which also contains his clearing of himself from a desire for empty glory.

units.la: Adeo perspecta est omnibus Ecclesiis Ministerii mei efficacia, ut opus non habeam a quoquam, vel a vobis, vel ab aliis, ullis literis commendatitiis, neque haec dico quod inani gloriae studeam, sed ut in vestrum bonum, Ministerium meum adversus inimicos meos defendam: Ergo commendabile est meum Ministerium.
units.tr: The efficacy of my ministry is so well known to all the Churches that I have no need of any letter of commendation from anyone, either from you or from others. I do not say this because I am eager for empty glory, but so that I may defend my ministry for your good against my enemies. Therefore my ministry is commendable.

units.la: Verf. 2. Epistola nostra vos estis, inscripta in cordibus nostris, quae intelligitur & legitur ab omnibus hominibus:
units.tr: Verse 2. You are our letter, written in our hearts, which is known and read by all men.

units.la: Arg. 2. Quia vestra conversio, O Corinthii, ad fidei professionem, per Ministerium meum, sufficit in conscientia mea & vestra, pro Epistola commendatitia, quae apud omnes intelligitur & agnoscitur.
units.tr: Argument 2. Because your conversion, O Corinthians, to the profession of faith through my ministry is, in my conscience and yours, sufficient in place of a letter of commendation, which is understood and acknowledged by everyone.

units.la: Verf. 3. Dum palam fit vos esse epistolam Christi subministra tam à nobis, inscriptam non atramento, sed Spiritu Dei vivi, non in tabulis lapideis, sed in carneis tabulis cordis.
units.tr: Verse 3. Since it is made plain that you are a letter of Christ, ministered by us, written not with ink but with the Spirit of the living God, not on tables of stone but on the fleshy tables of the heart.

units.la: Arg. 3. Per confirmationem prioris. Quia meum Ministerium fuit efficax, non tantum ut vos adduceret ad professionem fidei, sed etiam ad vestri regenerationem salutiferam, per Spiritus Christi specialem operationem, hoc est quod dicit eos esse Epistolam, quam ipse Christus, per ejus Ministerium exaravit, scribendo voluntatem suam in ipsorum cordibus, per Spiritum sanctum, multo excellentiori ratione quam scribi solet aliquid atramento, in carta vel tabulis lapideis.
units.tr: Argument 3, by confirmation of the former. Because my ministry was effective not only in bringing you to the profession of faith, but also to your saving regeneration, through the special operation of Christ's Spirit. This is what he means in saying that you are the letter which Christ himself has written through his ministry, inscribing his will in your hearts through the Holy Spirit, in a far more excellent way than anything is usually written with ink on paper or on stone tablets.

units.la: Verf. 4 Fiduciam autem hujusmodi habemus per Christum apud Deum:
units.tr: Verse 4. Such confidence we have through Christ toward God.

units.la: Verf. 4. Non quod idonei simus ex nobisipsis ad cogitandum quicquam, velut ex nobisipsis, sed quod idonei sumus: id ex Deo est:
units.tr: Verse 4. Not that we are sufficient of ourselves to think anything as of ourselves, but our sufficiency is of God.

units.la: Arg. 4. Quia ipse, ut fidelem servum decet, hanc gloriandi fiduciam totam acceptam refert non sibi, sed Domino suo, Iesu Christo, in Dei conspectu.
units.tr: Argument 4. Because he himself, as a faithful servant should, ascribes all this boasting confidence not to himself but to his Lord, Jesus Christ, in the sight of God.

units.la: Quod argumentum illustrat, partim confitendo suam impotentiam naturalem etiam ad cogitandum bonum, seu ad minima initia boni operis, nedum ad convertendum Corinthios, partim agnoscendo gratiam Dei, ut fontem sufficientiae suae, quod aptus sit, ad tantam gratiam aliis impertiendam.
units.tr: He illustrates this argument partly by confessing his natural inability even to think good, or to make the smallest beginnings of a good work, let alone to convert the Corinthians; and partly by acknowledging the grace of God as the source of his sufficiency, namely, that he is fit to impart such grace to others.

units.la: Verf. 6. Qui etiam fecit ut idonei essemus ministri novi Testamenti, non litera, sed Spiritus, nam litera occidit, Spiritus autem vivificat.
units.tr: Verse 6. Who also made us able ministers of the new covenant; not of the letter, but of the Spirit: for the letter killeth, but the Spirit giveth life.

units.la: Arg. 5. Quia ipsius Ministerium est Ministerium novi foederis, non legis seu foederis operum. Hoc argumentum confirmat septuplici utriusque Ministerii comparatione.
units.tr: Argument 5. Because his ministry is the ministry of the new covenant, not of the law or the covenant of works. He confirms this argument by a sevenfold comparison of the two ministries.

units.la: Secunda Pars.
units.tr: Second Part.

units.la: ] Comparatio prima : Ministerium legis, seu fœderis operum est literæ tantum scriptæ, vel voce prolatæ, fine efficacia, fine omni spirituali virtute ad præstandum quod jubet : Ministerium vero Euangelii, seu fœderis gratiæ per Christum, est Ministerium Spiritus, quia fecundum & per illud ministratur Spiritus sanctus, quo vivificatur auditor, & viribus donatur ad amplectendum id quod proponitur.
units.tr: Comparison 1. The ministry of the law, or covenant of works, is only the letter, written or spoken aloud, without efficacy and without any spiritual power to do what it commands. But the ministry of the gospel, or covenant of grace through Christ, is the ministry of the Spirit, because the Holy Spirit is ministered according to it and through it. By the Spirit the hearer is quickened and endowed with strength to embrace what is set before him.

units.la: ] Comparatio fecunda, confirmans priorem. Ministerium legis operum, seu literæ scriptæ, convincit de peccato tantùm, & occidit peccatorem, pronunciando in eum sententiam mortis. Ministerium vero Euangelii, seu Gratiæ in novo fœdere, ostendit liberationem à peccato, absolvit peccatorem, & sic ei affert vitam.
units.tr: Comparison 2, confirming the former. The ministry of the law of works, or of the written letter, convicts only of sin and kills the sinner, pronouncing the sentence of death upon him. But the ministry of the gospel, or of grace in the new covenant, shows deliverance from sin, absolves the sinner, and so brings him life.

units.la: Verf. 7. Quòd fi mortis ministerium literis informatum in faxis, fuit gloriosum, adeò ut non possent intueri filij Israel in faciem Mosis, propter gloriam vultus ejus, quæ abolenda erat,
units.tr: Verse 7. But if the ministry of death, engraved in letters on stones, was glorious, so that the children of Israel could not look steadfastly on the face of Moses because of the glory of his countenance, which was to be done away,

units.la: Verf. 8. Quî non potius ministerium Spiritus erit gloriosum?
units.tr: Verse 8. How shall not the ministry of the Spirit be rather glorious?

units.la: ] Comparatio 3. Lex operum ministrans tantùm mortem, (nam fecundum hoc fœdus nemo justitiam vel vitam consequitur) in lapidibus insculpebatur, ad significandum quod per ipsam cor non emollitur, non renovetur: sed mortuum maneat: Euangelium verò gratiæ in carneis tabulis cordis scribitur, hoc est in cordibus vi Spiritus sancti, vivificatis & emollitis, ita imprimitur, ut virtus divinæ gratiæ, in omnibus cordis expressionibus discerni possit.
units.tr: Comparison 3. The law of works, which ministers only death (for under this covenant no one attains righteousness or life), was engraved on stones, to signify that the heart is not softened or renewed by it, but remains dead. But the gospel of grace is written on the fleshy tables of the heart, that is, in hearts quickened and softened by the power of the Holy Spirit. It is so imprinted that the power of divine grace can be discerned in every expression of the heart.

units.la: ] Comparatio 4. Ministerium fœderis operum, quod est Ministerium mortis in omnes qui peccarunt, gloriosum quidem erat, ut in Mose apparuit, (nam etiam in puniendis peccatis gloriosa est justitia) sed Ministerium novi fœderis, quod est Ministerium Spiritus vivificantis, magis est gloriosum, nam ut in Mose legis maledictionem in peccatores pronunciante, splendebat gloria corporalis: in Christi vero facie peccatores ex gratia liberantis, splendet O quanta gloria spiritualis!
units.tr: Comparison 4. The ministry of the covenant of works, which is the ministry of death to all who have sinned, was indeed glorious, as appeared in Moses (for even in punishing sins, justice is glorious). But the ministry of the new covenant, which is the ministry of the Spirit who gives life, is more glorious. For as in Moses, who pronounced the law's curse on sinners, a bodily glory shone, so in the face of Christ, who delivers sinners by grace, there shines a spiritual glory. O how great it is!

units.la: Vers. 9. Nam si ministerium condemnationis fuit gloriosum, multo magis ministerium justitiæ abundat gloria.
units.tr: Verse 9. For if the ministry of condemnation was glorious, much more does the ministry of righteousness abound in glory.

units.la: Comparatio 4. Legis seu Veteris Fœderis Operum Ministerium, est Ministerium condemnationis ob peccatum, & propterea gloriosum quidem: sed Ministerium Euangelii, seu Novi Fœderis, est Ministerium justitiæ Christi, & absolutionis à peccato, & propterea tanto gloriosius, quanto absolutio & justitia, superant condemnationem & peccatum. Quoniam ex Fœdere Operum omnes arguimur peccati, omnes condemnamur, & morti obnoxii reddimur, idcirco ejus Ministerium vocatur Ministerium peccati, condemnationis, & mortis.
units.tr: Comparison 4 (as printed). The ministry of the law, or of the Old Covenant of works, is the ministry of condemnation for sin, and therefore indeed glorious. But the ministry of the gospel, or of the New Covenant, is the ministry of Christ's righteousness and of absolution from sin, and is therefore all the more glorious, to the degree that absolution and righteousness surpass condemnation and sin. Since by the covenant of works we are all accused of sin, all condemned, and made liable to death, its ministry is rightly called the ministry of sin, condemnation and death.

units.la: Verf. 10. Etenim quod glorificatum fuit, ne glorificatum quidem fuit hac in parte, id est, quod ad superantem gloriam attinet.
units.tr: Verse 10. For what was made glorious had no glory in this respect, by reason of the glory that surpasses it.

units.la: Comparatio 5. Ministerium Legis, licet gloriosum fuerit, tam longè superatur à gloria Ministerii Euangelii seu Gratiæ, ut gloriosum non mereatur dici, sed evanescat prorsus in comparatione, sicut gloria stellarum absorbetur apparente Sole: Euangelii vero Ministerium simpliciter & excellenter est gloriosum.
units.tr: Comparison 5. The ministry of the law, though it was glorious, is so far surpassed by the glory of the ministry of the gospel or of grace that it does not deserve to be called glorious at all, but vanishes entirely in the comparison, just as the glory of the stars is swallowed up when the sun appears. The ministry of the gospel is glorious simply and excellently.

units.la: Verf. 11. Nam si quod aboletur, fuit gloriosum, multo magis est gloriosum id quod manet.
units.tr: Verse 11. For if that which is done away was glorious, much more is that which remains glorious.

units.la: Comparatio 6. Ministerium Fœderis Operum, respectu Ceremoniarum annexarum, gloriam temporalis dispensationis tantum habebat, quia tantisper duraturum erat, dum homines in Ecclesiæ infantia convicti peccatorum, & impotentiæ suæ ad seipsos liberandum, ad Christum confugere docerentur, & quasi pædagogi manu ducerentur, quæ ratio docendi Ecclesiam jam adultam, & sub splendore Euangelii revelati degentem, tollitur ut inutilis: Ministerium verò Novi Fœderis gloriam habet permanentem, in gloriosum Christi adventum usque.
units.tr: Comparison 6. The ministry of the covenant of works, with respect to the ceremonies attached to it, had only the glory of a temporary dispensation, because it was to last only while men in the infancy of the Church, convinced of their sins and of their inability to free themselves, were taught to flee to Christ and were led by the hand like children under a tutor. This method of teaching is set aside as useless for a Church that is now grown up and lives under the light of the revealed gospel. But the ministry of the new covenant has a permanent glory, lasting until the glorious coming of Christ.

units.la: Verf. 12. Itaque quum ejusmodi spem habeamus, multa in loquendo evidentia utimur: Nec sumus sicut Moses qui imponebat velamen faciei suæ, ne intuerentur filij Israel in finem ejus quod abuletur:
units.tr: Verse 12. Seeing then that we have such hope, we use great plainness of speech: and not as Moses, who put a veil over his face, that the children of Israel could not look steadfastly to the end of that which is abolished.

units.la: Comparatio 7. Ministerium Novi Fœderis planum & perspicuum est, ita ut ejus Ministri, plane & confidenter possint prædicare viam salutis, habentes Christum jam revelatum, qui venturus olim sperabatur: Ministerium vero legis, ut in typo Mosaicæ ministrationis apparebat, obscuum erat, & typis involutum.
units.tr: Comparison 7. The ministry of the new covenant is plain and clear, so that its ministers can preach the way of salvation openly and confidently, since Christ is already revealed, who was once hoped for as one to come. But the ministry of the law, as it appeared in the type of the Mosaic ministration, was obscure and wrapped in types.

units.la: Imponebat ] Hanc comparationem persequitur ad finem Capitis, posteriorem ejus partem illustrans, ad versum ultimum, in hunc sensum. Moses Minister Legis aversus à Tabernaculo, ab Altari, ab Arca, & Propitiatorio, facie velata alloquens populum significabat, & typicè referebat Legalis Fœderis Operum, cujusque Ministerii à Christo separati naturam, & figurabat etiam cæcitatem populi sub Legali Fœdere, quia Christum non cernebant finem esse legis, & Ceremoniarum temporalium jam abolitarum.
units.tr: Imponebat (he put). He pursues this comparison to the end of the chapter, illustrating its latter part, up to the last verse, in this sense. Moses, as minister of the law, turned away from the Tabernacle, the Altar, the Ark and the Mercy-seat, and spoke to the people with his face veiled. This signified and typically represented the nature of the legal covenant of works and of its ministry, separated from Christ. It also figured the blindness of the people under the legal covenant, because they did not see that Christ is the end of the law and of the temporary ceremonies now abolished.

units.la: Verf. 14. Itaque obcaluerunt mentes illorum, nam usque ad diem hodiernum, in lectione Veteris Testamenti manet non retectum velamen illud, quod per Christum tollitur:
units.tr: Ver. 14. Their minds were hardened, for to this day, at the reading of the Old Testament, that same veil remains unremoved, which is taken away through Christ.

units.la: Verf. 15. Sed ad hunc usque diem quum legitur Moses, velamen cordi eorum impositum est:
units.tr: Ver. 15. But to this day, when Moses is read, a veil lies upon their heart.

units.la: Observat Apostolus quod cæcitas etiam nunc cernatur in Judæis, qui dum Vetus Testamentum legunt, nihil præter velum Ceremoniarum vident, quia velum Ignorantiæ & Infidelitatis manet super mentes eorum, quod velum, per typum veli externi faciem Mosis obtegentis repræsentatum, in Christo aufertur ab omnibus fidelibus, qui in Christo sunt; nam justitia, vita, virtus, & omnis denique gratia & gloria, in lucem profertur, & fidelibus communicatur in Christo: verum super corda incredulorum Judæorum, hoc velum manet huc usque.
units.tr: The Apostle observes that blindness is still seen in the Jews, who, while they read the Old Testament, see nothing but the veil of the ceremonies, because the veil of ignorance and unbelief remains over their minds. This veil, represented by the type of the outward veil covering the face of Moses, is taken away in Christ from all the faithful who are in Christ; for righteousness, life, virtue, and in short all grace and glory, are brought to light and communicated to believers in Christ. But over the hearts of the unbelieving Jews this veil remains even until now.

units.la: Verf. 16. Postquam autem conversum fuerit ad Dominum, tollitur velamen.
units.tr: Ver. 16. But whenever it shall have turned to the Lord, the veil is taken away.

units.la: Spem facit conversionis Judæorum, quando per Dei gratiam cor Israelitarum, vel Mosis doctrina jam velata convertetur ab iis ad Deum, id est, referetur secundum suam typicam significationem ad Christum, qui finis est Legis: tum velum Ignorantiæ, & obscuritatis Ceremoniarum auferetur ab iis, sicut ablatum est velum à facie Mosis, quando introiit ad Deum inter cherubinos sedentem; ut perspicuè Dominum Deum suum, & Salvatorem videant Christum, eumque verum esse Legis totius finem agnoscant.
units.tr: This gives hope of the conversion of the Jews, when by the grace of God the heart of the Israelites, or the teaching of Moses now veiled, shall be turned by them to God, that is, referred according to its typical meaning to Christ, who is the end of the Law. Then the veil of ignorance and the obscurity of the ceremonies will be removed from them, just as the veil was removed from the face of Moses when he went in before God, who sits between the cherubim; so that they may clearly see the Lord their God and Saviour Christ, and acknowledge that he is the true end of the whole Law.

units.la: Verf. 17. Dominus verò Spiritus ille est: ubi autem Spiritus ille Domini illic libertas.
units.tr: Ver. 17. Now the Lord is that Spirit; and where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is liberty.

units.la: Hujus ratio redditur, quia: 1. Christus est Spiritus, seu anima Ceremoniarum omnium, utpote res spiritualis per illas significata: 2. Christus est etiam Spiritus seu anima Legis Moralis, quia est Legis complementum, in quo solo perfecta Legis justitia reperitur: 3. CHRISTUS est Spiritus, quia vivificat credentes in novam obedientiam, & vitam æternam, eosque à peccato & miseria liberat: nam cum dicitur, Ubi Spiritus Christi Domini est, seu ubi Christus est, ibi libertas, intelligenda est libertas, non ab obedientia Præceptorum, sed à Jugo Ceremoniali, à servitute Peccati, & Jugo Fœderis Legalis, omniumque malorum quæ ex ipsius violatione sequuntur; libertas inquam fidelibus datur per Spiritum Euangelii, saltem quod ad jus attinet, licet non semper quoad sensum, nec unquam ante vitæ finem, quoad plenam possessionem: licet enim altâ voce proclamet Spiritus, apertam nobis esse januam, ut ex carcere exeamus, nos tamen propter fidei imbecillitatem segniter eximus. Atque hæc est explicatio primæ partis comparationis de Ministerio Legis.
units.tr: The reason for this is given: (1) Christ is the Spirit, or soul, of all the ceremonies, as the spiritual reality signified by them; (2) Christ is also the Spirit, or soul, of the Moral Law, since he is the fulfilment of the Law, in whom alone the perfect righteousness of the Law is found; (3) Christ is the Spirit, because he quickens believers into new obedience and eternal life, and frees them from sin and misery. For when it is said, Where the Spirit of the Lord, that is, where Christ is, there is liberty, the liberty meant is not freedom from obedience to the precepts, but freedom from the ceremonial yoke, from the slavery of sin, and from the yoke of the legal covenant, and from all the evils which follow from its violation. This liberty, I say, is given to the faithful through the Spirit of the Gospel, at least as far as right is concerned, though not always as to feeling, and never before the end of life as to full possession. For although the Spirit proclaims with a loud voice that the door is open for us to leave the prison, we nevertheless come out slowly because of the weakness of our faith. And this is the explanation of the first part of the comparison concerning the ministry of the Law.

units.la: Vers. 18. Nos autem omnes retecta facie gloriam Domini ut in speculo intuentes, in eandem imaginem transformamur ex gloria in gloriam, sicut a Domini Spiritu.
units.tr: Ver. 18. But we all, with unveiled face beholding the glory of the Lord as in a mirror, are transformed into the same image, from glory to glory, as by the Spirit of the Lord.

units.la: Sequitur alterum membrum comparationis de Ministerio Euangelii in credentibus, quod in hunc sensum proponitur. Nos verò qui per Ministerium Euangelii credimus in CHRISTUM, remoto velo Ceremoniarum & ignorantiæ; remoto velo infidelitatis, & duritiei cordis, liberè admittimur ad perspicuè conspiciendum CHRISTUM, & gloriam gratiæ DEI in illo, lucentem in Euangelio, ut in speculo; & fide intuentes CHRISTUM, sanctificamur, & magis magisque beati reddimur in conformitate cum CHRISTO, aucti indies per gradus, ab una mensura gloriæ, seu sanctitatis in aliam, idque per potentem operationem SPIRITUS Sancti. Sanctificatio vocatur gloria, quia sanctificatio initium est glorificationis, per eam enim reparatur DEI in nobis imago, quæ nostra gloria est.
units.tr: There follows the second part of the comparison, concerning the ministry of the Gospel in believers, which is set out in this sense. But we who through the ministry of the Gospel believe in CHRIST, with the veil of ceremonies and ignorance removed, and the veil of unbelief and hardness of heart removed, are freely admitted to behold CHRIST clearly, and the glory of GOD's grace in him, shining in the Gospel as in a mirror; and beholding CHRIST by faith, we are sanctified, and are made more and more blessed in conformity with CHRIST, increased day by day, by degrees, from one measure of glory or holiness to another, and this through the powerful operation of the Holy SPIRIT. Sanctification is called glory, because sanctification is the beginning of glorification; for through it the image of GOD is restored in us, and this is our glory.

units.la: Caput Quartum.
units.tr: Chapter 4.

units.la: Inisterium suum pergit defendere. Capitis duae sunt partes, In prima probat suam in Ministerio fidelitatem, seu sinceritatem, septem Argumentis, ad versum 6. In secunda, confirmat septimum Argumentum, solvendo objectiones de scandalo Crucis sibi incumbentis, ad finem.
units.tr: He goes on to defend his ministry. The chapter has two parts. In the first, he proves his faithfulness, or sincerity, in the ministry by seven arguments, up to verse 6. In the second, he confirms the seventh argument by answering the objections about the scandal of the Cross that lie upon him, to the end.

units.la: Verf. 1. PROPTEREA quum ministerium hoc habeamus, prout misericordiam consecuti sumus, non segnescimus:
units.tr: Vers. 1. Therefore, since we have this ministry, as we have obtained mercy, we do not lose heart.

units.la: Argumentum primum, Conscientia adeo gloriosi Ministerii mihi commissi ex misericordia DEI, efficax redditur ad sustinendum me, ne succumbam malorum oneri in munere meo fungendo, utque invictus pergam, pro mensura gratiae mihi datae. Hinc ergo apparet me sincerum esse & fidelem. Modestiae causa adjungit alios, sed ipse in certamine potissimum ab adversariis petebatur. Verf. 2 Sed abdicavimus turpitudinis tegumenta, non incedentes cum calliditate, neque falsantes sermonem Dei, sed declaratione veritatis commendantes nosipsos apud omnem conscientiam hominum, in conspectu Dei.
units.tr: First argument: my awareness, from the mercy of God, of the glorious ministry committed to me makes me strong enough to bear up, so that I do not sink under the burden of evils in discharging my office, but press on unconquered, according to the measure of grace given to me. From this it is clear that I am sincere and faithful. For the sake of modesty he adds the others, but in the conflict he himself was chiefly attacked by his opponents. Vers. 2 But we have renounced the hidden things of shame, not walking in craftiness, nor adulterating the word of God, but by the manifestation of truth commending ourselves to every human conscience in the sight of God.

units.la: Arg. 2. Renunciavi ambitioni, avaritiæ, cæterisque pudendis affectibus, quibus aliqui clam indulgentes, tegunt hoc dedecus suum in latebris, sub aliis atque aliis velis & prætextibus. Ergo ego fidelis sum.
units.tr: Argument 2: I have renounced ambition, greed, and the other shameful passions, which some indulge in secretly, hiding this disgrace in corners under various disguises and pretexts. Therefore I am faithful.

units.la: Arg. 3. Non ambulavi in astutia dolose tractans Dei Verbum, vel illud ad hominum affectus inflectens & attemperans, ut Pseudapostoli faciunt. Fidelis sum igitur.
units.tr: Argument 3: I have not walked in cunning, handling the word of God deceitfully, or bending and adapting it to people's feelings, as the false apostles do. Therefore I am faithful.

units.la: Arg. 4. Tam candide me gessi, in perspicua praedicatione Verbi Dei, ut cogantur omnium hominum conscientiæ, meam integritatem agnoscere, cujus rei testem etiam Deum habeo: Fidelis ergo sum.
units.tr: Argument 4: I have conducted myself so openly in the plain preaching of the word of God that the consciences of all people are compelled to acknowledge my integrity, and I have God himself as witness of this. Therefore I am faithful.

units.la: Verf. 3. Quod si tectum est Euangelium nostrum, iis qui pereunt, tectum est:
units.tr: Vers. 3. But if our gospel is veiled, it is veiled to those who are perishing.

units.la: Verf. 4. In quibus Deus hujus seculi excæcavit mentes, id est, infidelibus, ne irradiet eos lumen Euangelii gloriæ Christi, qui est imago Dei.
units.tr: Vers. 4. In whom the god of this age has blinded the minds of unbelievers, so that the light of the gospel of the glory of Christ, who is the image of God, should not shine on them.

units.la: Objectio, At qui fit, ut non intelligatur doctrina tua à tot sapientibus & potentibus, si adeo perspicuè docetur? Respondet ignorantiam Evangelii tam aperte ipsis explicati, Argumentum esse non obscuritatis doctrinæ, sed incredulitatis in auditore, & perditionis sequuturæ, ex incredulorum à Diabolo (cui servit mundus) excæcatione. Diabolus enim cæcos infideles porrò excæcat, ne Deum in Christo se nobis osserentem videant; ne in Euangelio splendentem, ad salutem aspiciant Christum, qui Deum alioqui invisibilem, doctrina sua, & manifestatis in carne, suis virtutibus quasi in aspectum nostrum produxit, ut Deum in Christo, verâ Dei Patris imagine cernamus.
units.tr: Objection: But how is it that your teaching is not understood by so many wise and powerful people, if it is taught so plainly? He answers that the ignorance of the Gospel, so openly explained to them, is not a proof of obscurity in the doctrine, but of unbelief in the hearer, and of the perdition that follows from the blinding of unbelievers by the Devil, whom the world serves. For the Devil blinds unbelievers further, so that they do not see God offering himself to us in Christ, and do not look to Christ for salvation, shining in the Gospel. Christ, who otherwise brought God, invisible in himself, before our eyes by his teaching and by his virtues, when he was manifested in the flesh, so that we might see God in Christ, the true image of the Father.

units.la: Vers. 5. Non enim nosipsos prædicamus, sed Christum Iesum Dominum: nos autem, servos vestros propter Iesum.
units.tr: Vers. 5. For we do not preach ourselves, but Christ Jesus as Lord, and ourselves as your servants for Jesus' sake.

units.la: Arg. 5. Fidelitatis Apostoli. Ego (inquit) gloriam Christi solius quæro, & Christum solum Dominum in Ecclesia agnosco, me vero, & reliquos Prædicatores, ut Ministros non solum Christi, sed etiam populi ipsius, prædico, ut Christus solus emineat: Fidelem ergo me ostendo.
units.tr: Argument 5: the faithfulness of the Apostle. I (he says) seek the glory of Christ alone, and acknowledge Christ alone as Lord in the Church; and I preach myself and the other preachers as ministers not only of Christ but also of his people, so that Christ alone may stand out. Therefore I show myself to be faithful.

units.la: Vers. 6. Quoniam Deus qui dixit ut è tenebris lux splendesceret, is est, qui splenduit in cordibus nostris, ad præbendum lumen cognitionis in facie Iesu Christi.
units.tr: Vers. 6. For God, who said, "Let light shine out of darkness," is the one who has shone in our hearts, to give the light of the knowledge of the glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ.

units.la: Arg. 6. confirmans superius, In quo comparat suam conversionem à Pharisaismo, creationi lucis ex tenebris; Deus qui omnipotenti Verbo suo eduxit lucem ex tenebris, non minori efficacia me perditum eruit ex tenebris Pharisaismi & peccati, & Luce gloriosi Filii sui Christi, cor meum illuminatum, adeo potenter perinovit, ut non possim non communicare cum aliis, gloriosam hanc mihi datam cognitionem gratiæ Dei, in Christo manifestè lucentem: Fidelem me ergo oportet esse.
units.tr: Argument 6, confirming what went before. In it he compares his conversion from Pharisaism with the creation of light out of darkness. The God who by his almighty Word brought light out of darkness has, with no less power, rescued me, lost, out of the darkness of Pharisaism and sin, and by the light of his glorious Son Christ has so powerfully illuminated my heart that I cannot but share with others this glorious knowledge of the grace of God, shining clearly in Christ. Therefore I ought to be faithful.

units.la: Vers. 7. Habemus autem thesaurum hunc in testaceis vasculis, ut ejus virtutis præstantia sit Dei, & non ex nobis:
units.tr: Vers. 7. But we have this treasure in earthen vessels, so that the excellence of the power may be of God, and not from us.

units.la: Arg. 7. Deus meam in omnibus exercitiis infirmitatem ostendendo, & simul suum robur in me sustentando sub afflictionibus crebris, & constantem me hucusque præstando, commendatam omnibus reddit meam fidelitatem. Fidelem me ergo possum affirmare;
units.tr: Argument 7: by showing my weakness in all my labours, and at the same time sustaining his own strength in me under frequent afflictions, and by keeping me steadfast until now, God makes my faithfulness commended to all. I can therefore affirm that I am faithful.

units.la: Secunda Pars.
units.tr: Second Part.

units.la: HOC Argumentum ita tractat, ut interim solvat duas objectiones, ut scandalum Crucis tollat.
units.tr: He handles this argument in such a way that, meanwhile, he answers two objections, in order to remove the scandal of the Cross.

units.la: Objectio prima, Interim misera tua, & contemptibilis & abjecta est vitæ conditio, ut vasis cujusdam testacei. Respondet quatuor modis: Primò, verum quidem esse, se vas testaceum, fragile & contemptum esse, sed Thesaurum tamen Gratiæ, seu Cognitionis Euangelii, quo alii ditescant, continere.
units.tr: First objection: Meanwhile your condition of life is wretched, contemptible and abject, like that of some earthen vessel. He answers in four ways. First, it is true that he is an earthen vessel, fragile and despised, but that he nevertheless contains a treasure of grace, or of the knowledge of the Gospel, by which others are enriched.

units.la: Deinde respondet, DEI sapientiâ id evenire, ne gloria conversionis & salutis tot hominum ascriberetur Apostolorum virtuti, sed ut tota DEO cederet illibata, nam tantò magis conspicua est DEI potentia in magnis operibus, quantò instrumentorum apparet impotentia evidentius.
units.tr: Next he answers that this happens by the wisdom of God, so that the glory of the conversion and salvation of so many people would not be ascribed to the virtue of the Apostles, but that the whole of it would go untouched to God. For the power of God is all the more conspicuous in great works the more evidently the weakness of the instruments appears.

units.la: Verf. 8 Dum in omnibus premimur, at non coarctamur: haesitamus, at non prorsus haremus.
units.tr: Vers. 8. We are pressed on every side, but not crushed; we are perplexed, but not in despair.

units.la: Verf. 9. Persecutionem patimur: sed in ea non deserimur: dejicimur, at non perimus.
units.tr: Vers. 9. We are persecuted, but not forsaken; we are cast down, but not destroyed.

units.la: Respondet 3. Temperari sibi afflictiones omnes, & sustineri se à Deo in omnibus, ut non destituatur Dei ope, non succumbat oneri, non deserat Deum, non desperet, non deseratur à Deo, non destituatur vel pereat, nihil ergo refert quam infirmus sit in se. Affligimur, inquit, at non coarctamur, hoc est, Undique premimur rebus adversis, non tamen ita redigimur in angustum, ut comprimamur, sed Dei ope servamur in mediis pressuris. Haesitamus, sed non prorsus haremus, id est, Dubitamus aliquando quid facto opus sit in vitae periculis, non tamen adeo destituti sumus, ut omnis consilii inopes simus.
units.tr: He answers thirdly: all his afflictions are tempered for him, and he is sustained by God in all things, so that he is not left without God's help, does not succumb to the burden, does not forsake God, does not despair, is not forsaken by God, is not left destitute or perish. It therefore matters nothing how weak he is in himself. We are afflicted, he says, but not crushed; that is, we are pressed on every side by adverse circumstances, yet we are not reduced to such a narrow place that we are overwhelmed, but by God's help we are kept safe in the midst of the pressures. We are perplexed, but not in despair; that is, we sometimes doubt what must be done in the dangers of life, yet we are not so destitute that we are wholly without counsel.

units.la: Persecutionem patimur, sed non deserimur, id est Permittit nos Deus ab hostibus Evangelii agitari, & male multari, sed neque permittit nos occidi, ante tempus ab eo constitutum, neque consolationes suas à nobis subtrahit. Dejicimur, at non perimus, id est, Aliquando videmur ilico perituri, Deo tamen opitulante custodimur, ne pereamus.
units.tr: We are persecuted, but not forsaken; that is, God allows us to be harassed and ill-treated by the enemies of the Gospel, but he does not allow us to be killed before the time he has appointed, nor does he withdraw his consolations from us. We are cast down, but not destroyed; that is, at times we seem about to perish at once, yet with God's help we are kept so that we do not perish.

units.la: Verf. 10. Quolibet mortificationem Domini Iesu in corpore circumferentes, ut etiam vita illa Iesu in corpore nostro manifestafiat.
units.tr: Vers. 10. Always carrying about in the body the dying of the Lord Jesus, so that the life of Jesus may also be made manifest in our body.

units.la: Respondet 4. In Christi gloriam cedere afflictiones suas, eo quod in iis imago Christi patientis, & morientis conspicienda sit, & quod in sua sub tot afflictionibus sustentatione, CHRISTI viventis, virtus & efficacia appareat, nihil ergo refert quam infirmus in se sit.
units.tr: He answers fourthly: his afflictions turn to the glory of Christ, because in them the image of the suffering and dying Christ is to be seen, and because in his own sustaining under so many afflictions the power and efficacy of the living Christ appears. It therefore matters nothing how weak he is in himself.

units.la: Verf. 11. Semper enim nos qui vivimus, morti tradimur propter Iesum: ut etiam vita Iesu manifesta fiat in mortali carne nostra.
units.tr: Vers. 11. For we who live are always being delivered to death for Jesus' sake, so that the life of Jesus may also be made manifest in our mortal flesh.

units.la: Hoc confirmat, ex eo quod Apostoli, qui virtute Spiritus CHRISTI in mediis aerumnis vivebant, pro CHRISTI causa quotidie adeant Capitis periculum, ut in ipsorum infirmitate sustentanda magis magisque CHRISTI vivifica virtus appareat, in carne ipsorum, miserae illi conditioni obnoxia.
units.tr: He confirms this from the fact that the Apostles, who lived in the midst of hardships by the power of the Spirit of Christ, daily face the peril of death for Christ's cause, so that in sustaining their weakness the life-giving power of Christ may appear more and more in their flesh, which is subject to that wretched condition.

units.la: Verf. 12. Itaque mors quidem in nobis agit, vita vero in vobis.
units.tr: Vers. 12. So death works in us, but life in you.

units.la: Objectio 2. At non necessario, quia CHRISTI servus es, ideo etiam miser & abjectus esses: nos enim Corinthii Christiani sumus, & tamen prosperius agimus; Respondet quatuor modis:
units.tr: Second objection: But is it not necessary that, because you are a servant of Christ, you should also be wretched and abject? For we Corinthians are Christians, and yet we fare more prosperously. He answers in four ways.

units.la: Primum concedendo ita esse; Divina tamen sapientia evenire istud, quod in aliquibus Christianis adultioribus, ut Apostolis appareat magis, coram mundo saltem, imago CHRISTI morientis: in aliis vero, ut Corinthiis infirmioribus, appareat magis, coram mundo, fructus & efficacia viventis CHRISTI, Corinthios ne multum affligerentur custodientis.
units.tr: First, by conceding that it is so; yet this happens by divine wisdom, so that the image of the dying Christ appears more in some more mature Christians, such as the Apostles, at least before the world, while the fruit and efficacy of the living Christ appear more, before the world, in others, such as the weaker Corinthians, keeping the Corinthians from being greatly afflicted.

units.la: Verf. 13. Et quia habemus eundem Spiritum fidei secundum illud quod scriptum est, Credidi, & ideo loquutus sum: nos quoque credimus, quamobrem etiam loquimur.
units.tr: Verse 13. And since we have the same spirit of faith, according to what is written, "I believed, and therefore I spoke": we also believe, and therefore we also speak.

units.la: Verf. 14. Scientes fore ut qui excitavit Dominum Iesum, nos quoque per Iesum excitet, & sistat vobiscum.
units.tr: Verse 14. Knowing that he who raised up the Lord Jesus will raise us also through Jesus, and will present us with you.

units.la: Respondet 2. Etiamsi affligantur Apostoli magis quam Corinthii, eundem tamen esse Spiritum fidei in se & in Corinthiis, ex qua fide, cum Davide credens, Psal. 116. 10. Apostolus audeat gloriosam resurrectionem una cum Corinthiis sibi polliceri, licet jam magis sub cruce prematur quam ipsi.
units.tr: He answers second: even if the Apostles are afflicted more than the Corinthians, nevertheless there is the same spirit of faith in him and in the Corinthians; from this faith, believing with David (Ps. 116:10), the Apostle dares to promise himself, together with the Corinthians, the glorious resurrection, although he is now pressed under the cross more than they are.

units.la: Verf. 15. Nam haec omnia propter vos, ut gratia illa copiosissima, pluribus gratias agentibus, redundet in gloriam Dei.
units.tr: Verse 15. For all these things are for your sake, so that that most abundant grace, through the thanksgiving of many, may overflow to the glory of God.

units.la: Respondet 3. Se affligi in ipsorum consolationem, & confirmationem, simul etiam ut ex afflictionibus & liberationibus suis non tantum occasio precandi, & patiendi una cum Apostolis praebeatur Corinthiis, sed etiam occasio gratias DEo agendi, una cum illis pro eximiis ex angustiis liberationibus, quas subinde Deus sibi & reliquis Apostolis concedebat, & concessurus erat.
units.tr: He answers third: that he is afflicted for their consolation and confirmation, and at the same time so that from his afflictions and his deliverances the Corinthians are given not only an occasion of praying and of suffering together with the Apostles, but also an occasion of giving thanks to God together with them for the remarkable deliverances from distress, which God from time to time granted, and was going to grant, to himself and the rest of the Apostles.

units.la: Verl. 16. Propterea non segnescimus : sed etiamsi externus homo noster corrumpitur, internus tamen renovatur quotidie.
units.tr: Verse 16. Therefore we do not lose heart; but even if our outward man is wasting away, yet our inward man is renewed day by day.

units.la: Respondet 4. Se non fatiscere, neque defatigari in suis afflictionibus: cujus subjungit tres rationes.
units.tr: He answers fourth: that he does not faint or grow weary in his afflictions; for this he adds three reasons.

units.la: Ratio prima, Quia quantum imminuebatur de bonis illis, quae ad statum praesentis vitae tuendum faciunt, tantum accedebat sanctitatis ad spiritualem vitam augendam.
units.tr: The first reason: because as much as those goods which serve to preserve the state of the present life were diminished, so much holiness was added to increase the spiritual life.

units.la: Verf. 17. Momentanea enim levitas oppressionis nostrae excellenter aeternum pondus gloriae conficit nobis.
units.tr: Verse 17. For our momentary light affliction works for us an eternal weight of glory, far beyond all comparison.

units.la: Ratio 2. Quia ineffabile pondus futurae gloriae, (ad quam promovendam, afflictiones, ut instrumenta & media mortificationis & sanctificationis faciunt) efficiebat ut nulla ratio habenda sit afflictionum, imo vero ut afflictionum momentanea levitas in comparatione cum gloria futura, plane evanesceret, & nihili fieret.
units.tr: The second reason: because the ineffable weight of future glory (to which afflictions, as instruments and means of mortification and sanctification, help to advance) made it so that no account should be taken of afflictions; indeed, the momentary lightness of affliction, in comparison with the future glory, simply vanishes and becomes nothing.

units.la: Verf. 18. Dum non spectamus ea quae cernuntur, sed ea quae non cernuntur, nam quae cernuntur temporaria sunt : at quae non cernuntur, aeterna.
units.tr: Verse 18. While we look not at the things which are seen, but at the things which are not seen; for the things which are seen are temporal, but the things which are not seen are eternal.

units.la: Ratio 3. Cur non fatiscat in afflictionibus est, Quia per fidem, inquit, respicio aeterna & invisibilia, prae quibus temporalia & visibilia despicio, hoc est, opes & honores, & voluptates, &c. non respicio, quia ad tempus tantum duratura sunt illa: sed in Coelestia bona & aeterna quae Deus promisit, animum intentum habeo, propterea dispendium rerum temporarum non moror, Ex quibus omnibus Apostolus confirmat Corinthios, ne ipsius afflictionibus offendantur.
units.tr: The third reason why he does not faint under afflictions is this: because, he says, through faith I look to the eternal and invisible things, in comparison with which I despise the temporal and visible things, that is, I do not regard wealth, honours, pleasures, and so on, because those things will last only for a time; rather, I keep my mind fixed on the heavenly and eternal good things which God has promised, and therefore I do not dwell on the loss of temporal things. From all of which the Apostle confirms the Corinthians, so that they may not be offended by his afflictions.

units.la: Caput Quintum.
units.tr: Chapter 5.

units.la: Ergit fidelitatem suam in Ministerio amplius ostendere, commemoratis septem causis impellentibus, quibus ad fidelitatem in munere suo exequendo movebatur.
units.tr: He goes on to show his faithfulness in the ministry more fully, having set out seven impelling causes which moved him to be faithful in carrying out his office.

units.la: Verf. 1. Scimus enim nos, si terrestris hujus domus nostrae tabernaculum dissolutum fuerit, ædificium ex Deo habituros, Domicilium videlicet non manufactum, æternum in cælis.
units.tr: Verse 1. For we know that if the earthly house of this tabernacle of ours is dissolved, we shall have a building from God, that is, a house not made with hands, eternal in the heavens.

units.la: Prima causa impellens ad fidelitatem in Ministerio, est ipsius certa confidentia de beata immortalitate, quæ ipsum & reliquos fideles <bl>Chri-</bl> <bl>sti</bl> Ministros manebat post mortem, cujus felicitatis particeps futurum est etiam corpus in resurrectione. Persuasum habeo inquit, post dissolutionem hujus mei fragilis corpusculi, felicitate animæ, & gloriosa corporis resuscitati immortalitate, me perpetuò fruiturum. Qui igitur fidelis non essem, quamdiu in corpore mortali habito?
units.tr: The first impelling cause to faithfulness in the ministry is his own sure confidence in blessed immortality, which awaited him and the other faithful ministers of Christ after death, and in which the body too will share at the resurrection.
