He says: I am persuaded that after the dissolution of this frail body of mine, I shall enjoy perpetually the happiness of the soul and the glorious immortality of the raised body. Why, then, should I not be faithful for as long as I dwell in this mortal body?

units.la: Verf. 2. In hoc enim suspiramus, expetentes domicilio nostro, quod è cælo est, superindui.
units.tr: Verse 2. For in this we groan, longing to be clothed upon with our house which is from heaven.

units.la: Hujus confidentiæ seu persuasionis soliditas, septem indiciis confirmatur, quæ omnia ad fidelitatem acuebant ejus animum.
units.tr: The firmness of this confidence or persuasion is confirmed by seven signs, all of which spurred on his mind to faithfulness.

units.la: Primum indicium est desiderium migrandi ex hac vita, ut immortalitate potiretur, & immortali gloriâ vice corruptibilis corporis induueretur. Argumentum certè animi sinceritatis suæ conscii, & de felicitate futura certiorati.
units.tr: The first sign is the desire to depart from this life, so as to possess immortality and to be clothed with immortal glory in place of the corruptible body. This is a strong argument for one who is conscious of the sincerity of his own mind and assured of future happiness.

units.la: Verf. 3. Siquidem etiam induti, non nudi reperiemur.
units.tr: Verse 3. Since indeed, being clothed, we shall not be found naked.

units.la: Limitat hoc indicium & privilegium, de induenda cœlesti gloria. Quod pertineat ad eos tantum, qui ex vita decedentes ad statum immortalem, & immutabilem, non reperiuntur nudi, id est, destituti integumento illo vero, quo tegitur fœda nostra nuditas, quod integumentum est <bl>Christus</bl>, seu <bl>Christi</bl> justitia, quæ peccata nostra in quibus nuditas nostra consistit, sola tegere potest: Hoc ergo secundum est indicium solidi desiderii ad migrandum ex hac vita, & animi de fideli administratione muneris sui benè conscii, quod sciat se esse ex numero eorum, ad quos solos pertinet certitudo de superinduenda gloria, nempe ex iis, qui jam induti sunt illo integumento, quo fœda peccatorum nuditas tegitur, id est, justitia Christi, qua nisi quis induatur in hac vita, nudus comperietur in altera, & manebit nudus in æternum.
units.tr: This limits the sign and privilege of being clothed with heavenly glory. It belongs only to those who, departing from life, are not found naked in the immortal and unchangeable state, that is, stripped of that true covering by which our foul nakedness is hidden. That covering is Christ, or the righteousness of Christ, which alone can cover our sins, in which our nakedness consists. So this is the second sign of a firm desire to depart from this life, and of a mind well aware of its faithful administration of its office: he knows that he belongs to those alone to whom the certainty of being clothed with glory pertains, namely those who are already clothed with that covering by which the foul nakedness of sins is concealed, that is, the righteousness of Christ. Unless a person is clothed with this in this life, he will be found naked in the next, and will remain naked for ever.

units.la: Verf. 4. Etenim qui sumus in hoc tabernaculo, suspiramus onerati: in quo non cupimus exui, sed superindui, ut absorbeatur mortalitas à vita.
units.tr: Verse 4. For we who are in this tabernacle groan, being burdened, in which we do not wish to be unclothed, but to be clothed upon, so that mortality may be swallowed up by life.

units.la: Indicium 3. Quod desiderium migrandi ex hac vita, ortum ex hac fiducia, sanctum fuerit, id est, non tam ex tædio naturalis vitæ, quam ex spe melioris vitæ derivatum; Hoc est quod dicit, etiamsi gravetur, & subti istis sit in hoc corpore, non tamen tam cupiat corpore exui, quam immortalitatem superinduere corpori, & mortalitatem absorberi, ab immortalitate.
units.tr: Sign 3. The desire to depart from this life, arising from this confidence, is holy; that is, it does not spring so much from weariness of natural life as from hope of a better life. This is what he means: even though he is weighed down and groans in this body, he does not so much desire to be stripped of the body as to have immortality put on over the body, and mortality swallowed up by immortality.

units.la: Verf. 5. Porrò Deus, is est qui nos ad hoc ipsum condidit, qui etiam dedit nobis arrhabonem Spiritus.
units.tr: Verse 5. Now God is he who made us for this very thing, and who also gave us the earnest of the Spirit.

units.la: Indicium 4. Quod desiderium hoc non sit naturale, sed opus Dei supernaturale, à speciali Dei operatione excitatum & formatum in cordibus suorum, Deus est qui nos ad hoc condidit, formavit, & creavit. Confidentia sclida est igitur.
units.tr: Sign 4. This desire is not natural but a supernatural work of God, stirred up and formed in the hearts of his people by a special operation of God. God is he who made us for this: he formed and created us. The confidence is therefore solid.

units.la: Qui etiam ] Indicium 5. Quod fiducia hæc melioris vitæ obsignata sit per arrhabonem Spiritus, dato quasi illius vitæ gustu & experimento, in pace & gaudio Spiritus, id est, in primitiis venturæ felicitatis.
units.tr: Who also: Sign 5. This confidence in a better life is sealed by the earnest of the Spirit, given as it were a taste and experience of that life, in the peace and joy of the Spirit; that is, in the firstfruits of the happiness to come.

units.la: Verf. 6. Confidentes igitur semper sumus, scientes nos dum adsumus in corpore, peregre abesse à Domino:
units.tr: Verse 6. Therefore we are always confident, knowing that while we are at home in the body, we are absent from the Lord.

units.la: Indicium 6. Quod hæc fiducia solidè fundata sit, in persuasione certa propinquioris accessus sui ad Dominum, concedendi sibi post mortem, quando scilicet quasi in una domo cum Deo habitaturus sit, qui nunc in corpore quasi peregrinatur à Domino:
units.tr: Sign 6. This confidence is solidly founded on the sure persuasion of his nearer access to the Lord, which is to be granted him after death, when he will dwell, as it were, in one house with God. Meanwhile, while in the body, he is like a stranger away from the Lord.

units.la: Verl. 7. (Per fidem enim incedimus, non per aspectum)
units.tr: Verse 7. (For we walk by faith, not by sight.)

units.la: Verf. 8 Confidimus autem, & probamus potius migrare è corpore, & ad Dominum ire habitatum.
units.tr: Verse 8. We are confident, and would rather be absent from the body and be at home with the Lord.

units.la: Indicum 7. Confirmans superius. Quod sciat se in hac vita fide incedere, & non aspectu visionis beatificæ, quæ in vita futura manet nos quinostro sensu absumus à Domino, dum præsentes sumus in corpore. Idcirco & vehementius cupiebat, & confidentius eligebat migrare ad Dominum, potius quam manere in corpore.
units.tr: Sign 7. This confirms what was said above: he knows that in this life he walks by faith and not by the sight of the blessed vision, which is kept for the life to come. In our present state we are absent from the Lord while we are present in the body. Therefore he desired all the more eagerly, and chose all the more confidently, to depart and go to the Lord rather than remain in the body.

units.la: Verf. 9. Quapropter etiam ambimus, & incolentes, & migrantes, ei esse accepti.
units.tr: Verse 9. Therefore we also make it our aim, whether at home or away, to be well pleasing to him.

units.la: Quod hæc confidentia, tot sinceritatis indiciis confirmata, fuerit causa impellens ad fidelitatem in Ministerio, expressè jam declarat. Quia quæcunque mutatio versus vitam vel mortem ipsi accidebat, semper ex hac confidentia, non minori intensione quam ii qui contendunt de honore, studebat Deo placere, ut & in vita seu peregrinatione, & in morte seu ad Deum appropinquatione, Deo acceptus redderetur.
units.tr: That this confidence, confirmed by so many signs of sincerity, was the cause impelling him to faithfulness in the ministry, he now declares plainly. Whatever change came upon him, towards life or towards death, he always strove, from this confidence and with no less intensity than men who contend for honour, to please God, so that he might be acceptable to God both in his life or pilgrimage and in his death or approach to God.

units.la: Verf. 10. Omnes enim nos comparere oportet coram tribunali Christi, ut unusquisque reportet quae in corpore fecerit, congruenter ad id quod fecerit, vel bonum vel malum.
units.tr: Verse 10. For we must all appear before the judgment seat of Christ, so that each one may receive what he has done in the body, according to what he has done, whether good or evil.

units.la: Secunda causa impellens ad fidelitatem in Ministerio, est consideratio poenarum & praemiorum, quae expectant singulos secundum opera, in extremo judicio, quo Deus impiis inflicturus est poenas: piis vero (quibus post remissa peccata supersunt tantum bona opera) praemia daturus.
units.tr: The second impelling cause to faithfulness in the ministry is the consideration of the punishments and rewards that await each person according to his works at the last judgment, when God will inflict punishments on the wicked, and will give rewards to the godly, to whom, once their sins are forgiven, only good works remain.

units.la: Verf. 11. Scientes igitur terrorem illum Domini, homines ad fidem adducimus, Deo autem manifesti sumus: & spero nos etiam conscientiis vestris manifestos ess.
units.tr: Verse 11. Knowing therefore the terror of the Lord, we persuade men; but we are manifest to God, and I hope we are also manifest in your consciences.

units.la: Quod hoc argumentum impulerit ipsum ad fidelitatem in Ministerio ostendit, testes diligentiae appellans Deum & Corinthiorum conscientias: terribilis enim illius futuri judicii apprehensio effecit, ut omnes hortaretur ad reconciliationem erga Deum per fidem.
units.tr: That this argument moved him to faithfulness in the ministry is shown by his calling God and the consciences of the Corinthians to witness his diligence. For the dreadful apprehension of that future judgment led him to exhort all to be reconciled to God through faith.

units.la: Verf. 12. Enimvero non iterum nosipsos commendamus vobis, sed vobis occasionem praebemus gloriandi de nobis: ut habeatis quod dicatis adversus eos qui ex facie gloriam captant, at non ex corde.
units.tr: Verse 12. Indeed, we do not commend ourselves to you again, but give you occasion to boast about us, so that you may have something to say against those who boast in appearance and not in heart.

units.la: Solvit duas objectiones: Quae tantopere glorianti de sua fidelitate objici possent ab adversariis: Objectio 1. Tu gloriolam captas Paule, (diceret aliquis) dum teipsum laudas. Respondet se non eo fine haec dicere, sed ut Corinthii habeant quod in defensione ipsius reponerent vanis & gloriosis suis doctoribus, qui authoritatem Apostoli inter ipsos ibant imminutum, & coram hominibus gloriabantur, secus quam ipsorum conscientia, & rei veritas permittebant; nam gloriabantur in eloquentia sua fucata, destituti pietate, seu gloriandi materia in corde.
units.tr: He answers two objections which his adversaries might raise against one who boasts so much of his own faithfulness. Objection 1: You seek your own little glory, Paul, someone might say, when you praise yourself. He replies that he says this not for that purpose, but so that the Corinthians may have something to set against their vain and boastful teachers, who were diminishing the authority of the Apostle among them and boasting before men in a way that did not agree with their own conscience and the truth of the matter. For they boasted in their false eloquence, lacking godliness, which is the true matter of boasting in the heart.

units.la: Verf. 13. Nam sive insanimus, Deo insanimus, sive sana mente sumus, vobis sana mente sumus.
units.tr: Verse 13. For whether we are beside ourselves, it is for God; or whether we are sober, it is for you.

units.la: Objectio 2. At insanis Paule, qui tam aperte perstringis tales doctores: Respondet se non disputaturum, sed facti rationem redditurum, ut sapientem decebat, nempe se ista non nisi studio divinae gloriae, & salutis ipsorum proferre: nam si meum (inquit) Ministerium laudo, quod insani videtur; in gloriam Dei facio, ne vilescat Euangelium meum: si humiliter de me loquor, ut sobrii solent, in vestram utilitatem facio.
units.tr: Objection 2: But you are mad, Paul, who so openly denounce such teachers. He answers that he will not dispute, but will give an account of the facts, as a wise man ought, namely that he says these things only for the sake of God's glory and their salvation. For if I praise my ministry (he says), which may seem mad, I do it for God's glory, so that my gospel is not cheapened. If I speak humbly of myself, as sober men usually do, I do it for your benefit.

units.la: Verf. 14 Charitas enim illa Christi constringit nos: Tertia causa impellens ad fidelitatem, continens superioris dicti rationem, est dilectio qua diligebat CHRISTUM, quae ei quasi vincula injecit, & constrinxit plum, ut sui immemor, ea tantum quae CHRISTI gloriam, & Ecclesiae bonum promoverent, diceret & faceret.
units.tr: Verse 14. For the love of Christ constrains us. The third impelling cause to faithfulness, which contains the reason for what was said above, is the love by which he loved Christ. This love, like chains laid upon him, bound him so that, forgetting himself, he would say and do only what promoted the glory of Christ and the good of the Church.

units.la: Verf. 15 Ut qui hoc statuerimus, si unus pro omnibus mortuus fuit, nempe omnes fuisse mortuos, & illum pro omnibus mortuum esse, ut qui vivunt, posthac non sibi vivant, sed ei qui pro ipsis mortuus est & resurrexit.
units.tr: Verse 15: Since we judge this: that if one died for all, then all were dead; and he died for all, so that those who live should no longer live for themselves, but for him who died for them and rose again.

units.la: Hujus dilectionis rationem reddit, & quartam addit causam impellentem, nempe dilectionem CHRISTI erga nos: CHRISTUS, inquit, quando nos omnes mortui eramus, meriti nostri & justitiae DEI respectu, mortuus est unus, vice nostra omnium, qui credimus in eum: ut nos liberati a perditione merita, non nobis, sed CHRISTO liberatori inserviremus. Quidni igitur in CHRISTI negotio fidelis essem?
units.tr: He gives the reason for this love and adds a fourth cause impelling him, namely Christ's love toward us. Christ, he says, when we were all dead, with respect to our merit and the justice of God, died one in our place, for all of us who believe in him, so that we, freed from destruction, should serve not ourselves but Christ our liberator. Why, then, should I not be faithful in Christ's business?

units.la: Verf. 16. Itaque nos posthac neminem novimus secundum carnem: quod si etiam novimus Christum secundum carnem, nunc tamen non amplius novimus.
units.tr: Verse 16: Therefore from now on we know no one according to the flesh; and even if we have known Christ according to the flesh, yet now we know him no longer.

units.la: Occurrit objectioni, quam in eum finem videtur occupare, ut rationem redderet cur gloriosos istos Corinthiorum Doctores perstrinxerit, nec pepercerit suae apud imperitos aestimationi, ut CHRISTI gloriam, & Ecclesiae salutem promoveret. Diceret aliquis, At parcere oportebat dignitati tantorum inter Corinthios Doctorum, qui eloquentia, eruditione, opibus, honore & nobilitate generis splendent: Horum enim aliqui ex Judaeis erant, & forte gloriati sunt, quod de tribu Judae fuerint, & cognatione CHRISTUM attigerint, ut ex sequentibus verisimile est.
units.tr: He meets an objection, which he seems to raise for this purpose: he gives the reason why he attacked those glorious teachers of the Corinthians and did not spare his own reputation among the unlearned, so that he might promote Christ's glory and the salvation of the Church. Someone might say: "But he ought to have spared the dignity of such great teachers among the Corinthians, who shine in eloquence, learning, wealth, honour and nobility of birth. For some of them were Jews, and perhaps they boasted that they were of the tribe of Judah and related to Christ, as is likely from what follows."

units.la: Respondet tribus modis, singulas suas responsiones quasi consectaria, ex verf. 12. deducens.
units.tr: He replies in three ways, deducing each of his answers as a consequence from verse 12.

units.la: Responsio prima, Quod non respiciat opes, honores, genus, eloquentiam, & cetera, nec aestimaturus sit quemquam ex rebus externis, ex quibus aestimatio hominum augetur vel minuitur apud mundanos & carnales.
units.tr: The first answer: he does not regard wealth, honours, birth, eloquence and the rest, nor will he value anyone for external things, by which people's esteem is raised or lowered among worldly and carnal folk.

units.la: Quod si] Responsio 2. Quod non sit amplius judicaturus de ipso CHRISTO, secundum externum ipsius statum, vel detracturus de ejus existimatione, propter paupertatem vel ignominiam apud mundum, sicut olim errans æstimaverat, & idcirco neque pluris existimaturus quenquam propter divitias, honores, genus, &c.
units.tr: But if: the second answer: he will no longer judge Christ himself according to his external state, nor detract from his reputation because of poverty or disgrace in the world, as he once wrongly did; and therefore he will not value anyone more highly for riches, honours, birth, and so on.

units.la: Vers. 17, Siquis igitur est in Christo, nova creatura est: vetera præterierunt · ecce nova facta sunt omnia.
units.tr: Verse 17: Therefore if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creature; the old things have passed away; behold, all things have become new.

units.la: Responsio 3. Ostendens officium Fidelium, qui Christo insiti sunt, hoc esse, ut tanquam novæ creaturæ novitati recti judicii, & sanctæ vitæ studeant: res verò mundanas quibus vetus homo gaudet, non magni faciant: quod probat ex Esa. 65. 17 ubi abolitionem rerum veterum, novum Cœlum, novamque terram, i. omnia nova promittit Deus sub Christi regno se daturum. Unde sequitur, ea tantùm in æstimatione esse debere apud Christianos, quæ novam creaturam seu regenerationem attingunt; Omnia autem redduntur renovatis nova, quando illi Deo reconciliati, omnes creaturas habent sibi quasi reconciliatas, iisque nunc utuntur novo modo, in Dei gloriam, & suam salutem, uniuscujusque rei pretium statuentes, pro ut ad regnum Dei in se, & in aliis promovendum facit, vel non facit.
units.tr: The third answer, showing that the duty of believers, who are implanted in Christ, is to strive, as new creatures, for the newness of right judgment and holy life, and not to set great store by worldly things in which the old man rejoices. He proves this from Isaiah 65:17, where God promises that under Christ's kingdom he will give the abolition of old things, a new heaven and a new earth, that is, all things new. From this it follows that among Christians only those things should be valued which concern the new creature or regeneration. All things, however, become new for the renewed, when, reconciled to God, they have all creatures as though reconciled to them as well, and now use them in a new way, for God's glory and their own salvation, setting the worth of each thing according as it helps or does not help to advance God's kingdom in themselves and in others.

units.la: Vers. 18, Hæc autem omnia sunt ex Deo, qui reconciliavit nos sibi per Iesum Christum, dedit〈que〉 ministerium reconciliationis:
units.tr: Verse 18: Now all these things are from God, who reconciled us to himself through Jesus Christ and gave us the ministry of reconciliation.

units.la: Quinta causa impellens ad fidelitatem in ministerio, est gratia & bonitas Dei erga se, quam causam, rediens ad institutum affert ascendendo ad Deum, novæ creaturæ, (de qua loquebatur proximè) & gratiarum omnium, authorem: quia autem gratia Dei erga seipsum contulerat in ipsius sinum duplex beneficium, reconciliationem scilicet per Christum, & delegationem ministerialem ad reconciliationem aliorum, inde duplicem ortam sibi obligationem, ad fidelitatem in ministerio, agnoscit. Quidni igitur fidelem se præstaret?
units.tr: The fifth cause impelling him to faithfulness in the ministry is God's grace and goodness toward himself. Returning to his subject, he brings this cause forward as he ascends to God, the author of the new creature (of which he spoke just before) and of all graces. Since God's grace toward himself had bestowed on him a twofold benefit, namely reconciliation through Christ and the ministerial commission for the reconciliation of others, he acknowledges that a twofold obligation arose for him to be faithful in the ministry. Why, then, should he not show himself faithful?

units.la: Vers. 19, Nempe quia Deus erat in Christo mundum reconcilians sibi, non imputando eis peccata ipsorum: posuitque in nobis sermonem hunc reconciliationis.
units.tr: Verse 19: Namely, because God was in Christ reconciling the world to himself, not imputing their sins to them, and has placed in us the word of this reconciliation.

units.la: Sexta causa impellens, est doctrinæ prædicandæ excellentia, cujus brevem summulam proponit. In qua: 1. Pater qui propter peccatum procul à nobis remotus erat, declaratur prope ad nos accessisse in Christo, qui verus Immanuel est. 2. Pater reconciliatus, quantùm ad partes suas attinet, electo suo mundo, declaratur id agere in Christo, ut Electi perspectis inimicitiis inter se & Deum, quantum ad ipsorum partes spectat, per CHRISTUM redeant in gratiam cum DEO, & reconcilientur. 3. Ostenditur ratio qua in gratiam cum DEO redeant homines, scilicet per remissionem, seu non imputationem peccatorum, quam DEUS gratiosissimè offert. 4 Ostenditur instrumentum applicandi gratiam reconciliationis à CHRISTO partam, sermo scilicet reconciliationis commissus Apostolis, reliquisque Ministris. In quo tam excellenti & necessario Ministerio, non potuit non esse fidelis, cum ista sibi ob oculos posita haberet.
units.tr: The sixth cause impelling him is the excellence of the doctrine to be preached, of which he sets out a brief summary. In it: (1) the Father, who was far removed from us because of sin, is declared to have drawn near to us in Christ, who is the true Immanuel. (2) The Father, reconciled so far as his part goes, is declared to be doing this in Christ toward his chosen world: that the elect, with the enmities between themselves and God set aside so far as their part is concerned, return through Christ into favour with God and are reconciled. (3) The means by which men return into favour with God is shown, namely by the remission, or non-imputation, of sins, which God offers most graciously. (4) The instrument for applying the grace of reconciliation obtained by Christ is shown: namely the word of reconciliation committed to the apostles and the other ministers. In so excellent and necessary a ministry he could not but be faithful, since he had these things set before his eyes.

units.la: Verf. 20. Itaque nomine Christi legatione fungimur, velut Deo vos precante per nos: oramus Christi nomine reconciliamini Deo.
units.tr: Verse 20: Therefore we act as ambassadors in the name of Christ, as though God were pleading through us; we beg you in Christ's name, be reconciled to God.

units.la: Septima causa impellens ad fidelitatem est, personae quam gerit excellentia; quam causam proponit, simulque eam cum tota praecedente doctrina in usum convertit, ipso facto fidelitatis suae studium ostendens: In hunc finem, cum authoritate, ut DEI Legatus, simul etiam submisse & amanter, quasi DEI personam sustinens, rogat omnes & diligenter urget, ut reconciliationem à DEO oblatam interius ad cor suum singuli admittant, ut sublatis inimicitiarum reliquiis, quas intus fovet incredulitas, in unum cum DEO spiritum omnes coalescant.
units.tr: The seventh cause impelling him to faithfulness is the excellence of the person he bears. He sets this cause forth and, together with all the preceding teaching, turns it to use, thereby showing by the very act his zeal for faithfulness. To this end, with authority as God's ambassador, and at the same time humbly and lovingly, as one bearing God's person, he asks all and urgently exhorts each one to admit inwardly into his heart the reconciliation offered by God, so that, with the remnants of enmity which unbelief nourishes within them removed, all may come together into one spirit with God.

units.la: Verf. 21: Fecit enim ut qui non novit peccatum, pro nobis peccatum esset ut nos efficeremur justitia Dei in eo.
units.tr: Verse 21: For he made him who knew no sin to be sin for us, so that in him we might become the righteousness of God.

units.la: Denique, ut persuadeat ad obedientiam fidei, & pleniorem reconciliationis mensuram admittendam, ostendit viam ad reconciliationem apertam & expeditam esse, quia CHRISTUS Mediator innocens, & purus à peccato, ex consensu & pactione cum PATRE, peractus est judiciali modo, reus nostri peccati; imo vero factus est sacrificium expiatorium pro nostro peccato, in eum expresse finem, ut nos credentes in CHRISTUM, justitiae CHRISTI judicialiter participes per imputationem fieremus, & sic perfectissimè justi, & quasi ipsa justitia quae DEO summè placeat, redderemur, per hanc excellentem & divinam justificandi rationem, quam DEI sapientia excogitavit, & gratia nostram fecit.
units.tr: Finally, to persuade them to the obedience of faith and to admit a fuller measure of reconciliation, he shows that the way to reconciliation is open and clear. Christ, the innocent Mediator, pure from sin, by agreement and covenant with the Father, was dealt with in a judicial manner as guilty of our sin; indeed he was made an expiatory sacrifice for our sin, with the express purpose that we, believing in Christ, might by imputation be judicially made partakers of Christ's righteousness, and so be rendered perfectly righteous, as it were that very righteousness which most pleases God. This comes through the excellent and divine way of justifying, which God's wisdom devised and his grace made ours.

units.la: Addit autem, In ipso, ut intelligamus necessario fide nos inserendos esse CHRISTO, quo haec nobis justitia obtingat, quia ex conjunctione nostri cum CHRISTO per fidem, sequitur unio judicialis nostri cum CHRISTO, & ex hac unione, adjudicatio obedientiae & justitiae CHRISTI nobis, & tandem applicatio omnium donorum ejus ad perfectam felicitatem tem usque. Quibus penitatis quid efficacius dici potest ad movendum nos omnes, ut agnitis inimicitiis, & nostra necessitate, oblatam in Christo reconciliationem amplectamur.
units.tr: He adds in him, so that we understand that we must necessarily be ingrafted into Christ by faith, through which this righteousness may come to us. For from our conjunction with Christ through faith follows a judicial union of ourselves with Christ, and from this union the adjudication to us of Christ's obedience and righteousness, and finally the application of all his gifts, even to perfect happiness. What can be said that is more effective for moving us all, that, recognising our enmities and our need, we embrace the reconciliation offered in Christ?

units.la: Summa igitur horum trium versuum est, Quod Apostolus cum redemptionis hominum œconomiam, & rationem adducendi electos ad reconciliationem & salutem perpenderet, non potuerit se in Ministerio suo non strenuè & fideliter exercere: Nam cum sciret in pacto, de redemptione electorum, inter Deum & filium, secundam Trinitatis personam, officio Mediatoris & sponsoris vestitam, inito, tam abundè satisfactum esse Deo, ut Deus jam propitius erga Redemptorum seu Electorum mundum factus, concurrat cum Christo Mediatore ad applicandam impetratam reconciliationem omnibus redemptis: eosque in Christo, & in servis Christi, Ministris Euangelii, non minus seriò quam ipse Redemptor roget, oretque, ut sibi jam reconciliato sen propitio facto, reconcilientur: Cum, inquam, hæc sciret Apostolus, & sibi commissam esse provinciam, ut reconciliationem hanc promoveret, Quid mirum si obnixè contenderit, ut homines ad Deum converterentur? Et cum sciret ex pacto Christum in se recepisse peccata omnia omnium Redemptorum, & factum esse victimam piacularem pro expiandis peccatis suorum ipsi imputatis, sub hac conditione, ut Redempti (quales se ostendunt omnes fideles) justitia illa Dei, seu justitia Christi amicti, pro justissimis in Dei mente haberentur, & per Spiritum sanctum tandem plene renovati, redderentur, Quid mirum si confidenter & constanter prosequutus fuerit negotium reconciliationis, & fidelem se præstiterit, in Ministerio suo exequendo?
units.tr: The sum, then, of these three verses is this: the Apostle, weighing the economy of human redemption and the way of bringing the elect to reconciliation and salvation, could not but exercise his ministry vigorously and faithfully. For he knew that in the covenant concerning the redemption of the elect, made between God and the Son, the second person of the Trinity, clothed with the office of Mediator and surety, satisfaction had been made to God so fully that God, now become propitious toward the redeemed or elect world, concurs with Christ the Mediator in applying the obtained reconciliation to all the redeemed, and asks and begs them, in Christ and in Christ's servants, the ministers of the gospel, no less earnestly than the Redeemer himself, that they be reconciled to him, now reconciled or made propitious. Since, I say, the Apostle knew these things, and knew that the task committed to him was to promote this reconciliation, what wonder if he strove earnestly that men be converted to God? And since he knew from the covenant that Christ had taken upon himself all the sins of all the redeemed, and had been made a propitiatory victim to expiate the sins imputed to his own, on this condition, that the redeemed (such as all believers show themselves to be), clothed in that righteousness of God, or the righteousness of Christ, should be held most just in God's mind, and at last, fully renewed by the Holy Spirit, be made such: what wonder if he pursued the business of reconciliation confidently and constantly, and showed himself faithful in carrying out his ministry?

units.la: Caput Sextum.
units.tr: Chapter Six.

units.la: Ut Ministerii sui exercitium adhuc amplius Corinthiorum conscientiis commendatum reddat, opere & exemplo fidelem ministrum ob oculos illis ponens, ex superioribus deduxit hortationem triplicem, ut ministerii ipsius fructus ferant. Capitis tres sunt partes, quarum prima est hortatio ad seriò recipiendam gratiam a se oblatam, ad vers. 11. Secunda est hortatio ad recipiendum ipsum pro Apostolo Christi ad verf. 14. Et tertia est, hortatio ad vitandam contagionem idololatrarum, ad finem.
units.tr: To make the exercise of his ministry still more commended to the consciences of the Corinthians, setting before their eyes a faithful minister in work and example, he drew from what precedes a threefold exhortation, that they should bear the fruits of his ministry. The chapter has three parts. The first is an exhortation to receive seriously the grace offered by him, to v. 11. The second is an exhortation to receive him as an apostle of Christ, to v. 14. And the third is an exhortation to avoid the contagion of idolaters, to the end.

units.la: Verf. 1, SEd & , ut operam nostram ei accomodantes, hortamur ne frustrà gratiam Dei vos receperitis.
units.tr: Verse 1. And working together with him, we exhort you that you do not receive the grace of God in vain.

units.la: Prima hortatio est, ut gratiam reconciliationis serió magis & cum fructu recipiant, nec permittant ut gratia Dei in Euangelio oblata, ipsorum vitio, fructu suo pleno in ipsis careat, sed ut justitiam, pacem, vitam, omninoque omnia quæ Christus redemptis impetravit, obtineant: Propositio quam urget hæc est. Non debetis gratiam Dei frustra recipere, id est, externa professione tantum, sine interna ipsius virtute, hanc probat argumentis tribus.
units.tr: The first exhortation is that they should receive the grace of reconciliation more earnestly and with greater profit, and not allow the grace of God offered in the Gospel to lack its full fruit in them through their own fault, but obtain righteousness, peace, life, and in short all the things that Christ has procured for the redeemed. The proposition he urges is this: you ought not to receive the grace of God in vain, that is, by outward profession only, without its inward power. He proves this by three arguments.

units.la: Argumentum primum, Nos Ministri Dei cooperarii, ut ejus opus in vobis promoveatur, ab eo vobis gratuito dono concessi, nostram operam pollicentes ad salutem vestram promovendam, à vobis obnixè id petimus: Ergo non debetis frustra gratiam Dei recipere.
units.tr: The first argument: we, the ministers of God, are fellow workers, promoting his work among you. Having been granted this by him as a free gift, and promising our labour to advance your salvation, we earnestly ask this of you. Therefore you ought not to receive the grace of God in vain.

units.la: Verf. 2. Dicit enim Deus, Tempore accepto exaudivi te, & in die salutis succurri tibi: ecce nunc tempus acceptum, ecce nunc dies salutis.
units.tr: Verse 2. For God says, "In an acceptable time I have heard you, and in a day of salvation I have helped you." Behold, now is the acceptable time; behold, now is the day of salvation.

units.la: Arg. 2. In parenthesi interjectum, Quia jam tempus est acceptum, quo per Christi intercessionem, gratia Dei futura est efficax ad fructus producendos, in omnibus qui cum serio cordis affectu Euangelium recipiunt, & fructum ferre cupiunt, quod probat ex Isaiæ 49. 8. ubi Pater alloquitur Mediatorem pro suis intercedentem, & in iis per Spiritum suum suspirantem: Ergo cavendum ne hæc gratiæ opportunitas frustra vobis sit oblata.
units.tr: Second argument, inserted in parentheses: now is the acceptable time, in which, through the intercession of Christ, the grace of God will be effective to produce fruits in all who receive the Gospel with earnest affection of heart and desire to bear fruit. He proves this from Isaiah 49:8, where the Father addresses the Mediator, who intercedes for his people and sighs in them through his Spirit. Therefore care must be taken that this opportunity of grace is not offered to you in vain.

units.la: Verf. 3. Nullam ulla in re præbentes offensionem, ne vituperetur ministerium:
units.tr: Verse 3. Giving no offence in anything, that the ministry be not blamed:

units.la: Arg. 3. Cum verf. 1. connexum, Nos Ministri qui vos hortamur, & ego nominatim Paulus, omnibus modis probati sumus, & comperti fideles in Ministerio Euangelii, nullum vobis obicem ponentes, quo minus per Ministerium nostrum proficiatis, adeo ut nihil prætendere poteritis, quo minus in Euangelii gratia promoveatis: Ergo non debetis frustra Dei gratiam recipere, sed ad virtutem Euangelii imbibendam, & exprimendam contendere. Antecedens confirmat inductione virtutum, quæ Ministros fideles probant, quibus ipse imprimis per Dei gratiam ornabatur, batur: Inductionis 5. sunt membra, In primo membro removet à se ea vitia, quibus ignavi paltores offendiculum Euangelio creare solent, moribus suis in Dei ædificio plus demolientes, quam doctrinâ ædificant, & occasionem præbentes impiis male loquendi de ipso Ministerio, seu Ministrorum munere.
units.tr: Third argument, connected with v. 1. We ministers, who exhort you, and I, Paul, by name, have been proved in every way and found faithful in the ministry of the Gospel, placing no hindrance before you that would keep you from profiting through our ministry. So much so that you cannot allege anything to prevent you from advancing in the grace of the Gospel. Therefore you ought not to receive the grace of God in vain, but strive to imbibe and express the power of the Gospel. He confirms the antecedent by an enumeration of the virtues which prove faithful ministers, with which he himself was especially adorned through the grace of God. The enumeration has five members. In the first member he removes from himself those vices by which idle ministers are wont to create a stumbling block for the Gospel, by their conduct pulling down more in God's building than they build up by doctrine, and giving the wicked occasion to speak evil of the ministry itself, or of the office of ministers.

units.la: Verf. 4 Sed & in omnibus nos approbantes, ut Dei ministri, toleran'tia multa in oppressionibus, in necessitatibus, in angustiis, Verf. 5. In plagis, in carceribus, in tumultuationibus, in laboribus, in vigiliis, in jejuniis:
units.tr: Verse 4. But in all things approving ourselves as the ministers of God: in much patience, in afflictions, in necessities, in distresses, Verse 5. In stripes, in imprisonments, in tumults, in labours, in watchings, in fastings.

units.la: In secundo membro varia virtutum genera recenset, quibus Ministerium suum ornatum est, nominatim autem patientiæ facit mentionem, in novem generibus malorum exercitæ: in quibus omnibus sine murmuratione, Ministerii sui munia patienter exequebatur: nam itinerum molestias cum inopia & periculis, persequutorum plagas, carcerem, & tumultus, adversus ipsum excitatos, & in prædicando, laborem, vigilias, jejunia sustinebat fortiter, nec in opere Domini fatiscebat.
units.tr: In the second member he recounts the various kinds of virtue with which his ministry was adorned. Especially he mentions patience, shown in nine kinds of evils. In all of these he performed the duties of his ministry patiently and without murmuring. For he endured bravely the hardships of journeys with want and dangers, the blows of persecutors, prison, and the tumults raised against him, and in preaching, labour, watchings and fastings, and he did not faint in the work of the Lord.

units.la: Verf. 6. Puritate, scientia, lenitate, bonitate, Spiritu Sancto, charitate non simulata,
units.tr: Verse 6. By purity, knowledge, longsuffering, kindness, the Holy Spirit, unfeigned love,

units.la: In tertio membro, patientiæ adjungit sex alias virtutes: Quarum prima, est Immunitas à pollutionibus mundi, dum inter mundanos versabatur:
units.tr: In the third member he adds six other virtues to patience. The first of these is freedom from the pollutions of the world, while he lived among worldly men.

units.la: 2. Discretio in tractandis auditoribus: 3. Longanimitas in provocationibus: 4. Mansuetudo in commercio cum difficilioribus: 5. Spiritualis in omnibus dispositio: 6. Dilectio sincera erga omnes.
units.tr: (2) Discernment in dealing with hearers; (3) longanimity under provocations; (4) gentleness in dealings with the more difficult; (5) a spiritual disposition in all things; (6) sincere love towards all.

units.la: Verf 7. Sermone veritatis, virtute Dei, armis justitiæ dextris ac sinistris.
units.tr: Verse 7. By the word of truth, by the power of God, by the armour of righteousness on the right hand and on the left.

units.la: In quarto membro enumerat virtutes quæ ad officii sui munia attinebant: 1. Nihil prædicabat præter Dei veritatem: 2. Demonstrabat in sermone suo Spiritus potentiam: 3. Decertabat contra omnes hostes armis spiritualibus, id est, mediis legitimis, in rebus prosperis à dextra, & in rebus adversis à sinistra, omninoque in omni mutatione, & rerum vicissitudine constans permanebat, ne vel illecebris vel terroribus à recta via deflecteret.
units.tr: In the fourth member he lists the virtues which pertained to the duties of his office: (1) he preached nothing but the truth of God; (2) he demonstrated in his speech the power of the Spirit; (3) he fought against all enemies with spiritual weapons, that is, with lawful means, using the right hand in prosperous circumstances and the left in adverse ones. And in every change and vicissitude of affairs he remained constant, lest he be turned from the right way either by allurements or by terrors.

units.la: Verl. 8 Per gloriam & ignominiam, per convicia & laudes: ut seductores, & tamen veraces;
units.tr: Verse 8. By honour and dishonour, by evil report and good report; as deceivers, and yet true;

units.la: Verf. 9. Ut ignoti, & tamen noti: ut morientes, & ecce vivimus: ut qui castigamur, nec tamen occidimur:
units.tr: Verse 9. As unknown, and yet well known; as dying, and behold we live; as chastened, and not killed;

units.la: Verf. 10. Ut dolentes, semper tamen gaudentes: ut pauperes, sed multos ditantes: ut nihil habentes, sed omnia obtinentes.
units.tr: Verse 10. As sorrowful, yet always rejoicing; as poor, yet making many rich; as having nothing, and yet possessing all things.

units.la: In membro quinto, gloriatur quod rectam viam semper tenuerit, sive ignominia & infamia, sive gloria & fama inde sequerentur: nam cum habebatur ut impostor, veracem se praestabat.
units.tr: In the fifth member he glories that he always kept to the right way, whether dishonour and infamy or glory and fame followed. For when he was regarded as an impostor, he showed himself to be true.

units.la: Cum habebatur ut ignobilis, & contemptibilis; se factis manifestabat, ita ut qui oculos haberent, ipsum cognoscerent servum esse DEI altissimi: Videbatur quasi mortuus; & in media morte gestiebat tamen officium praestare ut vivus: Castigatus verberibus fere ad necem, custodiebatur a DEO ne moreretur: Propter mala quae ipsum premebant, nonnunquam specie subtristis erat: sed Spiritu in DEO semper gaudebat. Inops habebatur; Per Euangelium tamen, ex DEI benedictione multiplici, ditabat multos, non tantum contentationis modum ostendendo in Euangelio, sed etiam ad virtutem & pietatem, quae ad omnia utilis est, homines instruendo. Carebat possessionibus & reditibus, & tamen contentus sorte sua, rerum omnium usu, quantum opus erat, gaudebat.
units.tr: When he was regarded as ignoble and contemptible, he made himself manifest by his deeds, so that those who had eyes might know him to be the servant of the most high God. He seemed as one dead, and in the midst of death he still undertook to perform his office as one alive. Beaten with stripes almost to death, he was kept by God so that he should not die. Because of the evils that pressed upon him, he sometimes appeared somewhat sad, but in the Spirit he always rejoiced in God. He was thought poor; yet through the Gospel, by the manifold blessing of God, he made many rich, not only by showing the measure of contentment in the Gospel, but also by instructing people in virtue and piety, which is profitable for all things. He lacked possessions and income, and yet, content with his lot, he rejoiced in the use of all things as much as was needed.

units.la: Secunda Pars.
units.tr: Second Part.

units.la: Verf. 11. Os nostrum apertum est erga vos, Corinthii, cor nostrum dilatatum est.
units.tr: Verse 11. Our mouth is open toward you, Corinthians; our heart is enlarged.

units.la: Secunda pars Capitis, in qua habetur secunda Pauli hortatio ad Corinthios, ut ipsum redamarent Apostolum scilicet CHRISTI, qui tantos labores in Ministerio sustinuerat in ipsorum bonum. Huic hortationi Argumenta praemittit quinque.
units.tr: This is the second part of the chapter, in which Paul gives a second exhortation to the Corinthians, that they should love in return the Apostle of Christ, who had endured such great labours in the ministry for their good. He prefaces this exhortation with five arguments.

units.la: Argumentum primum, Candide, & aperte, ut cum amicis parrefia utor, liberrime, corde dilatato, & ore aperto proferens, quam intus foveo erga vos benevolentiam. Quidni ergo vicem mihi rependatis?
units.tr: The first argument: I speak frankly and openly, as I use freedom with friends, with an enlarged heart and an open mouth, declaring the goodwill I cherish towards you within. Why then should you not repay me in return?

units.la: Verf. 12. Non habitatis angustie in nobis: sed angusti estis in visceribus vestris.
units.tr: Verse 12. You are not straitened in us, but you are straitened in your own bowels.

units.la: Verf. 13. Loquor autem ut filiis de pari compensatione: dilatamini & vos
units.tr: Verse 13. Now I speak as to children: in like recompense, be enlarged also you.

units.la: Arg. 2. Non per me stat, quo minus dilectionem meam percipiatis, sed per vestri ipsorum cordis angustias, qui non creditis tantam meam erga vos dilectionem.
units.tr: Argument 2: It is not on my side that you fail to receive my love, but on account of the narrowness of your own hearts, which do not believe in my so great love towards you.

units.la: Nor Non habitatu ] Arg. 3. Redamare me tenemini, qui impense amo vos. Ergo tanquam ex æquitate vicem referte, me amando, & vos à me amari persuasum habendo.
units.tr: You are not straitened: Argument 3: You are bound to love me in return, since I love you intensely. Therefore, as a matter of fairness, repay me in kind, by loving me and by being persuaded that you are loved by me.

units.la: Ut filii ] Arg. 4. Pater sum vester, & vos filii mei: Ergo ut filii mei, me amate ut patrem vestrum.
units.tr: As to children: Argument 4: I am your father, and you are my children. Therefore, as my children, love me as your father.

units.la: Compensatione ] Arg. 5. Jam debitum à vobis exigo: Ergo dilatamini, id est, corde dilatato admittite dilectionis meæ persuasionem, & paternas meas admonitiones ex dilectione profectas, & vicissim me diligite.
units.tr: In like recompense: Argument 5: Now I demand the debt from you. Therefore be enlarged, that is, with an enlarged heart admit the persuasion of my love and my paternal admonitions, which proceed from love, and in turn love me.

units.la: Tertia pars Capitis.
units.tr: Third Part of the Chapter.

units.la: Verf. 14. Ne impari jugo compulsmini cum infidelibus, quod enim consortium justitiæ cum iniquitate? & quæ communio lucis cum tenebris?
units.tr: Verse 14. Be not unequally yoked with unbelievers. For what fellowship has righteousness with iniquity? And what communion has light with darkness?

units.la: Verf. 15. Et quæ concordia Christo cum Belial? aut quæ pars fideli cum infideli?
units.tr: Verse 15. And what concord has Christ with Belial? Or what part has the believer with the unbeliever?

units.la: Tertia hortatio, ut abstineant ab omni illicita societate cum infidelibus, qua impediri ne Deo servirent, vel alienari à vera religione, vel ullo modo polluì possent: hujus generis societas quidem est matrimonium contrahendum, quo facillime viri, vel mulieres ad impietatis consensum implicantur ab Idololatris, eo quod omnium societatum humanarum hæc sit arctissima. Verum quam hic videtur taxare imprimis, est fidelium Corinthiorum cum concivibus infidelibus, societas seu communio in externa idololatria, quâ se polluebant, unà cum illis vescentes idolothytis in idoleio, ut superiori Epistola, Cap. 8. apparet, in qua idololatria, aut in quovis alio peccato, commune plaustrum cum ipsis, aut jugum impietatis trahere vetat. Hortationis argumenta sunt quatuor.
units.tr: The third exhortation: that they abstain from every unlawful fellowship with unbelievers, by which they might be hindered from serving God, or estranged from true religion, or in any way defiled. Of this kind of fellowship is marriage, by which men or women are most easily drawn into agreement with impiety by idolaters, since this is the closest of all human partnerships. But what he seems chiefly to censure here is the fellowship or communion of the Corinthian believers with their unbelieving fellow citizens in external idolatry, by which they were defiling themselves, eating idol-offerings together with them in the temple of an idol, as appears from the earlier Epistle, chapter 8, where he forbids drawing a common yoke with them in idolatry or in any other sin. The arguments of this exhortation are four.

units.la: Quod enim ] Argumentum primum, Conditio & Professio vestra Christianorum ex una parte, & peccata quæ palam profitentur idololatræ ex altera parte, non minus sibi invicem opponuntur, quam justitia & iniquitas: lux & tenebræ, Christus & Diabolus, fides & infidelitas, Templum Dei & Idola, inter quæ nulla potest esse communio. Ergo nulla communio vobis Christianis debet esse cum infidelibus in Idololatria, vel in peccatis ullis aliis, quæ palam infideles profitentur, vel in ulla alia necessitudine, ex qua oriatur difficulter superabile periculum, communicandi ipsorum peccatis: Nam non vetabat in eadem civitate habitare cum iis, nec negotiari, nec cibum sumere, si invitati essent ad prandium vel coenam.
units.tr: For what: Argument 1: Your condition and profession as Christians, on the one hand, and the sins which idolaters openly profess, on the other, are no less opposed to each other than righteousness and iniquity, light and darkness, Christ and the Devil, faith and unbelief, the temple of God and idols, between which there can be no communion. Therefore there ought to be no communion between you Christians and unbelievers in idolatry, or in any other sins which unbelievers openly profess, or in any other association from which arises a danger, hard to overcome, of sharing in their sins. For he did not forbid living in the same city with them, nor trading with them, nor taking food if they were invited to a dinner or a supper.

units.la: Vers. 16. Et quae consensio templo Dei cum simulachris? nam vos templum estis Dei viventis, sicut dixit Deus, Habitabo in eis & inambulabo: & ero illorum Deus, & ipsi erunt mihi populus.
units.tr: Verse 16. And what agreement has the temple of God with idols? For you are the temple of the living God, as God said: I will dwell in them and walk among them, and I will be their God, and they shall be my people.

units.la: Arg 2 Vos estis templum Dei sanctum, Quod probat testimonio Moisis, Lev. 26. 12. & Zech. 2. 10. Ergo non licet vobis vosmet polluere societate cum infidelibus, potissimum in eo in quo ex professo sunt templa idolorum.
units.tr: Argument 2: You are the holy temple of God, which he proves by the testimony of Moses, Lev. 26. 12. and Zech. 2. 10. Therefore it is not lawful for you to defile yourselves by fellowship with unbelievers, especially in that matter in which idol temples are professedly concerned.

units.la: Vers. 17. Quapropter exite e medio eorum, & separamini, dicit Dominus, & impurum ne attingite: tum ego excipiam vos:
units.tr: Verse 17. Wherefore come out from among them, and be separate, says the Lord, and touch not the unclean thing; then I will receive you.

units.la: Vers. 18. Et ero vobis Pater, & vos eritis mihi filii ac filiae, dicit Dominus omnipotens
units.tr: Verse 18. And I will be a Father to you, and you shall be my sons and daughters, says the Lord Almighty.

units.la: Arg. 3. Deus iussit separationem fieri ab idololatrarum, & mundi pollutionibus, ne attingatis eas. Ergo cavendum vobis ab iis.
units.tr: Argument 3: God commanded that separation be made from the pollutions of idolaters and of the world, so that you do not touch them. Therefore you must beware of them.

units.la: Ego suscipiam] Arg. 4. A promissionibus quas Deus fecit iis, qui purificant se servant a mundi inquinamentis, nec participant aliorum peccatis; praestabit se Deus ipsis patrem, hoc est, in compensationem omnium incommodorum, & consolationem plenam, adversus omnia mala quae cavent sibi ab alienis peccatis sufferre poterunt, Deus seipsum ipsis communicabit, & paternum suum affectum erga eos opere manifestabit.
units.tr: I will receive you: Argument 4: From the promises which God made to those who purify themselves, keep themselves from the defilements of the world, and do not share in the sins of others: God will show himself a Father to them. That is, in recompense for all the inconveniences, and as full consolation against all the evils which they may have to suffer for keeping themselves from others' sins, God will communicate himself to them and will show his paternal affection towards them in deed.

units.la: Caput Septimum.
units.tr: Chapter Seven.

units.la: Vers. 1. HAS igitur promissiones quum habeamus, Dilecti, purgemus nosipsos ab omni inquinamento carnis ac spiritus, perficientes sanctificationem cum timore DEI.
units.tr: Verse 1. Since we therefore have these promises, beloved, let us cleanse ourselves from every defilement of flesh and spirit, perfecting holiness in the fear of God.

units.la: Versus primus huius Capitis pertinet ad Caput praecedens: in quo ex superioribus promissionibus hortationem deducit, ut non modo caveant ab idololatria, & externa eius specie, sed etiam ab omni inquinamento Spiritus & corporis, hoc est, a peccatis, quae vel mentem intra polluunt, vel mentem simul & corpus inquinant, & contra studeant perficiendae sanctimoniae, pergentes & proficientes in melius in timore Dei, argumento utens uno pro omnibus; praeditae promissiones vobis a Deo factae, jure merito a vobis id exigunt. Ergo in haec officia sedulo incumbite.
units.tr: The first verse of this chapter belongs to the preceding chapter. There he draws an exhortation from the earlier promises: they should not only beware of idolatry and its outward appearance, but also of every defilement of spirit and body, that is, of sins which either pollute the mind within or defile both mind and body together. Instead, they should strive to perfect holiness, going on and making progress toward better things in the fear of God. He uses one argument for all: since God has made these promises to you, they rightly demand this of you. Therefore, apply yourselves diligently to these duties.

units.la: Verf. 2. Accipite nos: nemini injuriam fecimus, neminem corrupimus, neminem expilavimus.
units.tr: Verse 2. Make room for us: we have wronged no one, we have corrupted no one, we have defrauded no one.

units.la: ELIquo Capite devincire sibi nititur Corinthiorum corda, suæ dilectionis erga eos allatis indiciis, in quibus explicandis insistit ad finem: Propositio confirmanda aperte proponitur. Debetis nos recipere, O Corinthii, hoc est, Persuasi de meo erga vos amore, debetis redamare me, & hortationes meas in cordibus dilatatis reponere; Argumenta petuntur tria ex indiciis tribus benevolentiæ Apostoli erga eos.
units.tr: In this chapter he seeks to bind the hearts of the Corinthians to himself, by the signs of his love toward them. He persists in setting these out to the end. The proposition to be confirmed is plainly stated: You ought to receive us, O Corinthians, that is, being persuaded of my love for you, you ought to love me in return and keep my exhortations in your widened hearts. Three arguments are taken from three signs of the Apostle's goodwill toward them.

units.la: Neminem Argumentum primum, Ut Apostolum reciperent, & Indicium primum voluntatis minime malæ in eos est, Quia non male meritus sum de quoquam, vel contumeliam inferendo, perversa doctrina vel exemplo corrumpendo, vel quenquam ullo modo fraudando.
units.tr: No one. This is the first argument, that they should receive the Apostle; and it is the first sign of his entirely good will toward them. I have not wronged anyone by any injury, nor corrupted anyone by perverse teaching or example, nor defrauded anyone in any way.

units.la: Verf. 3. Ad condemnationem vestri non loquor: nam antè dixi vos in cordibus nostris esse, ad simul moriendum, & simul vivendum.
units.tr: Verse 3. I do not speak to condemn you: for I have said before that you are in our hearts, to die together and to live together.

units.la: Arg. 2. & Indic. 2. Quia cum hæc quæ præcesserunt mei purgandi causa duntaxat dixerim, tantum abest ut obliquè condemnem, aut perstringam Ecclesiam fidelium Corinthiorum, ut contra ex dilectione statutum mihi sit, vobis adhærere in rebus prosperis & adversis, in vita & in morte, ut nulla mutatio amorem meum à vobis unquam divellat.
units.tr: Argument 2 and sign 2. When I said these things that went before, I said them only for the sake of clearing myself. So far am I from condemning you indirectly, or censuring the church of the faithful Corinthians, that on the contrary it has been determined by my love that I should cling to you in prosperity and adversity, in life and in death, so that no change ever tears my love away from you.

units.la: Verf. 4. Multa mihi loquendi libertas apud vos, multa mihi gloriatio de vobis: impletus sum consolatione, vehementer exundo gaudio in omni afflictione nostra.
units.tr: Verse 4. Great is my freedom of speech toward you, great is my boasting about you: I am filled with comfort, I overflow with joy in all our affliction.

units.la: Arg. 3. & Ind. 3. Quia accepto nuncio de vestra respicientia cor meum in mediis afflictionibus adeo perfusum est gaudio, ut securè eloqui audeam, animi mei de vestra perseverantia fiduciam apud vos, & de vobis gloriari apud alios.
units.tr: Argument 3 and sign 3. Because, when I received news of your repentance, my heart in the midst of afflictions was so flooded with joy that I dare to speak confidently to you of my trust in your perseverance, and to boast of you among others.

units.la: Verf. 5. Etenim quum venissemus in Macedoniam, nullam habuit relaxationem caro nostra, sed in omnibus fuimus oppressi: foris pugnæ, intus terrores.
units.tr: Verse 5. For when we came into Macedonia, our flesh had no rest, but we were troubled on every side: fightings without, fears within.

units.la: Verf. 6. Sed qui consolatur abjectos, consolatus est nos Deus, adventu Titi.
units.tr: Verse 6. But God, who comforts the downcast, comforted us by the coming of Titus.

units.la: Hoc experimentum suæ in eos benevolentiæ explicaturus, proponit afflictiones quibus in Macedonia, dum nuntium ab iis expectaret premebatur, partim persecutione hostium, partim intestinis Ecclesiæ malis, partim animi anxietate, simul & corporis moleltiis ita constrictus, ut externo homini nulla data sit requies. Contra quas omnes molestias, ex Dei misericordia, consolatio suppeditata erat ipsi per adventum Titi, qui à Corinthiis jam redierat, & lætum nuncium de ipsorum statu retulerat.
units.tr: Intending to explain this proof of his goodwill toward them, he sets out the afflictions by which he was oppressed in Macedonia while waiting for news from them. These were partly persecution by enemies, partly the inner troubles of the Church, partly anxiety of mind, and at the same time troubles of the body, so that he was so constrained that no rest was given to his outward man. Against all these troubles, God in his mercy supplied him with comfort through the coming of Titus, who had already returned from the Corinthians and brought a joyful report of their state.

units.la: Verl. 7. Non solum autem adventu illius, sed etiam consolatione quam ille accepit ex vobis, quum renuntiaret nobis vestrum vehemens desiderium, vestrum ejulatum, vestrum pro me zelum: adeo ut magis gavisus fuerim.
units.tr: Verse 7. And not only by his coming, but also by the comfort with which he was comforted in you, as he reported to us your earnest desire, your mourning, your zeal for me; so that I rejoiced the more.

units.la: Apostolus causas lætitiæ suæ enumerat octo, quorum pleraque indicia erant ipsius in eos benevolentiæ: 1. Causa quia Titus salvus reversus erat: 2. Quia Titus consolationem à vobis Corinthiis acceperat: 3. Quia audiveram à Tito de vestro erga me pio affectu, & mei conspiciendi desiderio: de fletu ob admissum inter vos scelus, & ob meam suspectam indignationem: & de zelo adversus incestuosum, & adversus mei obtrectatores; unde gaudium mihi longe supra prius conceptum hac de re dolorem meum omnem, abundavit.
units.tr: The Apostle enumerates eight causes of his joy, most of which were signs of his goodwill toward them. (1) The first cause: Titus had returned safe. (2) The second: Titus had received comfort from you Corinthians. (3) The third: I had heard from Titus of your dutiful affection toward me and your desire to see me; of your mourning over the sin committed among you and over my suspected displeasure; and of your zeal against the incestuous man and against my detractors. From this my joy rose far above the sorrow I had conceived before over this matter, and all my grief was overcome.

units.la: Verl. 8. Nam etiamsi tristitia vos affeci per epistolam, non me pænitet, etiamsi pœnituerit: video enim epistolam illam, tametsi ad tempus, tristitia vos affecit:
units.tr: Verse 8. For even if I grieved you with my letter, I do not regret it, though I did regret it: for I see that the letter, though for a time, grieved you.

units.la: Antequam quartam causam consolationis proponat, solvit objectionem, cujus solutio ad propositum magnopere faciebat, dixerint illi, superiori Epistola tristitia nos affecisti.
units.tr: Before he sets out a fourth cause of consolation, he answers an objection, the answer to which greatly served his purpose: they had said that by the earlier letter he had grieved them.

units.la: Responsio quadruplex est: Responsio prima, Coactus & non sine dolore vis contritavi, dolor autem hic per vestram resipiscentiam evanuit. Nam cum Apostolus scripsit Epistolam, incertus de eventu tristis erat, hoc est, quod pœnituisse se dicit: cum vero eventum vidit dolore liberatus est, hoc est, quod jam non pænitere se dicit: Responsio 2. Tristitia illa ab Epistola mea excitata, brevis fuit.
units.tr: The answer is fourfold. The first answer: I wrote with reluctance and not without pain, but that pain has vanished through your repentance. For when the Apostle wrote the letter, he was uncertain of the outcome and was sorrowful; that is why he says he regretted it. But when he saw the outcome, he was freed from grief; that is why he now says he does not regret it. The second answer: the sorrow that my letter caused was brief.

units.la: Verl. 9. Nunc gaudeo, non quod tristitia affecti fueritis sed quod tristitia affecti fueritis ad resipiscentiam: nam tristitia affecti fuistis secundum Deum ut nulla in re detrimento sitis affecti per nos.
units.tr: Verse 9. Now I rejoice, not that you were grieved, but that you were grieved to repentance: for you were grieved in a godly way, so that you suffered no loss through us in anything.

units.la: Verl. 10. Nam qui secundum Deum est dolor, is resipiscentiam efficit ad salutem: cujus nunquam pœniteat: at mundi dolor mortem efficit.
units.tr: Verse 10. For godly grief produces repentance that leads to salvation and leaves no regret; but worldly grief produces death.

units.la: Respondet 3. Tristitia illa conversa est in gaudium, & vobis, & mihi, quia comperta jam est pia & utilis ad resipiscentiam, quod probat: Quia resipiscentiam non poenitendam produxit, secus quam tristitia mundana solet, quae peccatum & miseriam duntaxat auget, & mortem cum animae tum corporis affert.
units.tr: Third answer: that sorrow has been turned into joy, both for you and for me, because it has now been proved godly and useful for repentance, as this shows: it has produced a repentance that is not to be regretted, unlike worldly sorrow, which only increases sin and misery and brings death to both soul and body.

units.la: Vers. 11. Ecce enim ipsum hoc, quod secundum Deum tristitia affecti fuistis, quantum in vobis effecit studium? imo defensionem, imo indignationem, imo timorem, imo vehemens desiderium, imo zelum, imo vindicationem, per omnia testatum fecistis vos esse puros in hoc negotio.
units.tr: Verse 11. For see what this very thing, that you were grieved in a godly way, has produced in you: what earnestness, what defence, what indignation, what fear, what vehement longing, what zeal, what avenging! In every way you have shown yourselves to be pure in this matter.

units.la: Probat tristitiam ipsorum secundum Deum fuisse, seu piam, quia produxit in iis septem effecta, totidem resipiscentiae ipsorum indicia. Quorum primum fuit, securitatis excusatio cum solicitudine corrigendi quod peccatum erat. 2. Est apologia, quod scilicet jam nullo modo probent vel factum incestuosi, vel negligentiam suam: 3. Est indignatio adversus peccatum, & incestuosi, & ipsum, in eo tolerando. 4. Est metus ne judicio divino, vel novo peccato implicarentur. 4. Desiderium est tollendi scandali, & bonis omnibus satisfaciendi. 5. Zelus & fervor desiderii ad prosequenda omnia media ad malum removendum & damnum reparandum. 7. Est vindicta in castigando incestuoso, & ipsorum etiam corpore, quibus omnibus Corinthii resipiscentiam suam declaraverant, & se nullo modo scelere illo delectari, sed puros se esse ostenderant.
units.tr: He proves that their sorrow was godly, that is, pious, because it produced in them seven effects, each a sign of their repentance. The first was an excuse for their carelessness, together with anxiety to correct what was sin. (2) The second is a defence: that they now in no way approve either the deed of the incestuous man or their own negligence. (3) The third is indignation against the sin, both of the incestuous man and of themselves for tolerating it. (4) The fourth is fear lest they be caught in divine judgement or in some new sin. (5) The fifth is longing to remove the scandal and to make satisfaction to all good people. (6) The sixth is zeal and the fervour of desire to pursue every means of removing the evil and repairing the harm. (7) The seventh is vengeance in punishing the incestuous man, and in punishing themselves too. By all these things the Corinthians had declared their repentance, and had shown that they were in no way delighted with that crime, but were pure.

units.la: Vers. 12. Nempe etiamsi scripsi vobis, non scripsi vobis ejus causa qui injuriam fecerat, nec ejus causa qui injuria affectus fuerat, sed ut apud vos manifestum fieret studium illud nostrum pro vobis in conspectu Dei.
units.tr: Verse 12. So although I wrote to you, I did not write for the sake of him who had done the wrong, nor for the sake of him who had suffered the wrong, but so that my earnest care for you might be made plain to you in the sight of God.

units.la: Responsio quarta ad objectionem est, Non scripsi Epistolam illam, vel solum vel praecipue, ut in castigatione incestuosi satisfieret patri ejus, cujus uxorem stupraverat filius, vel ut ipse incestuosus corrigeretur, (quod quidem non erat negligendum) sed praecipue in hunc finem, ut paterna mea cura de vobis, O Corinthii, sincera, & in Dei conspectu approbata omnibus appareret.
units.tr: The fourth answer to the objection is this: I did not write that letter either solely or chiefly so that satisfaction might be made to the father of the man whose son had defiled his wife in the punishment of the incestuous man, or so that the incestuous man himself might be corrected (which indeed was not to be neglected). Rather, I wrote chiefly for this end: that my fatherly care for you, O Corinthians, sincere and approved in the sight of God, might be apparent to all.

units.la: Vers. 13. Propterea consolationem accepimus ex consolatione vestri, sed longe plurimum gavisi sumus ob gaudium Titi, quod refocillatus sit Spiritus ejus ab omnibus vobis: Soluta objectione quartam addit causam suae consolationis; quod acceperim, inquit, vos boni consuluisse reprehensionem a me, & jam consolationem administrasse.
units.tr: Verse 13. "Therefore we have been comforted in your comfort, but we rejoiced far more at the joy of Titus, because his spirit has been refreshed by all of you." Having dealt with the objection, he adds a fourth reason for his comfort: he says that he has learned that you have taken my rebuke in good part and have now given consolation.

units.la: Titi ] Quinta causa consolationis, Quia omnes refocillare studuistis Spiritum Titi.
units.tr: "Of Titus." The fifth reason for comfort: because you all took pains to refresh the spirit of Titus.

units.la: Vers. 14. Et siquid apud eum de vobis gloriatus sum, non fui pudefactus: sed ut omnia vere loquuti sumus vobis, ita & gloriatio nostra, qua usus eram apud Titum, vera comperta sit.
units.tr: Verse 14. "And if I have boasted anything to him about you, I have not been put to shame; but as we spoke all things truly to you, so also our boasting, which I made before Titus, has been found to be true."

units.la: Sexta causa, Quod reapse comprobaveritis, quae ego de vobis glorians, Tito confidenter praedixeram.
units.tr: The sixth reason: that you have in fact confirmed what I, boasting about you, had confidently told Titus beforehand.

units.la: Vers. 15. Et viscera ejus amplius erga vos affecta sint, dum reminiscitur obedientia omnium vestrum, ut qui cum timore ac tremore ipsum exceperitis.
units.tr: Verse 15. "And his affection towards you is all the greater, as he remembers the obedience of you all, how you received him with fear and trembling."

units.la: Septima causa. Quia vestris officiis & virtutibus animum Titi vobis devinxistis, quod in lucro magno deputare poteritis: Reveriti enim sunt Titum, ut Evangelistam, & servum Dei extra ordinem ad se missum, & sic Titi animum sibi conciliarant.
units.tr: The seventh reason: because by your duties and virtues you have won the heart of Titus to yourselves, which you may count as a great gain. For they revered Titus as an evangelist and as a servant of God sent to them beyond the ordinary course, and so they won his affection for themselves.

units.la: Vers. 16 Gaudeo igitur quod penitus confidam de vobis.
units.tr: Verse 16. "I rejoice therefore that I may be fully confident about you."

units.la: Octava causa consolationis, quod experientia hac animatus imposterum audeam de vobis omnibus, & mihi & aliis, optima quaeque polliceri.
units.tr: The eighth reason for comfort: that, encouraged by this experience, I may henceforth dare to promise all good things about all of you, both to myself and to others.

units.la: Caput Octavum.
units.tr: Chapter 8.

units.la: Ecunda pars Epistolae in qua confirmatis jam Corinthiis de dilectione sua erga ipsos, hortatur ad eleemosynas alacri animo largiendas in usum pauperum Judaeorum, adhibitis in hunc finem hoc capite 13 Argumentis, quibus addit plura, capite sequenti.
units.tr: The second part of the epistle. Having now confirmed the Corinthians in his love toward them, he urges them to give alms cheerfully for the use of the poor Jews. For this purpose he uses thirteen arguments in this chapter, and adds more in the next.

units.la: Verf. 1. Porro notam facimus vobis, fratres, gratiam Dei praestitam Ecclesiis Macedonum.
units.tr: Ver. 1. Moreover, brethren, we make known to you the grace of God bestowed on the churches of Macedonia.

units.la: Argumentum primum. Ab exemplo Macedonum, Ecclesiae Macedonum contribuerunt: Ergo & vos idem facite. Horum liberalitatem commendat novem rationibus. Prima ratio. Quia donum erat Dei ex gratia in ipsos profectum, quod in usum pauperum Judaeorum quicquam contribuerint.
units.tr: Argument 1. From the example of the Macedonians: the churches of Macedonia contributed, therefore you also should do the same. He commends their liberality by nine reasons. First reason: because it was a gift of God, bestowed on them out of grace, that they contributed anything for the use of the poor Jews.

units.la: Verf. 2 Nam in multa probatione abundans gaudium ipsorum, & profunda eorum paupertas redundavit in copiosam benignitatem ipsorum.
units.tr: Ver. 2. For in a great trial of affliction, the abundance of their joy and their deep poverty overflowed into the riches of their generosity.

units.la: Quia data est eleemosyna ab iis eo tempore, cum ipsi probabantur gravibus afflictionibus.
units.tr: Because the alms were given by them at a time when they were being tested by severe afflictions.

units.la: Ratio 3. Quia cum gaudio contribuerunt.
units.tr: Reason 3. Because they contributed with joy.

units.la: Ratio 4. Quia in paupertate liberales erant.
units.tr: Reason 4. Because they were generous in their poverty.

units.la: Verf. 3 Nam pro viribus (testor) & supra vires voluntarii fuerunt.
units.tr: Ver. 3. For, I bear witness, they gave according to their means, and even beyond their means, willingly.

units.la: Ratio 5. Quia largius dare volebant, quam ipsorum ferebant facultates.
units.tr: Reason 5. Because they wished to give more than their resources allowed.

units.la: Verf. 4. Multis cum precibus nos rogantes, ut gratiam & societatem subministrationis quae in sanctos impenditur, suscipiemus.
units.tr: Ver. 4. Begging us with much entreaty that we would accept the grace and the fellowship of the ministering that is done for the saints.

units.la: Ratio 6. Quia sponte, non provocati aliorum exemplo obtulerunt, sed autores aliis potius erant, ne in hoc officio charitatis deessent.
units.tr: Reason 6. Because they offered of their own accord, not prompted by the example of others; rather they were leaders for others, so as not to be wanting in this duty of charity.

units.la: Ratio 7. Quia instabant precibus, ut acciperetur quod dabant.
units.tr: Reason 7. Because they pressed with entreaties that what they were giving should be accepted.

units.la: Ratio 8. Quia rogabant Apostolum, ut una cum aliis provinciam suscipere colligendi & dispensandi, quod ipsi & alii daturi erant.
units.tr: Reason 8. Because they asked the Apostle to take up, together with others, the task of collecting and distributing what they themselves and others were about to give.

units.la: Verf. 5. Ac non sicut sperabamus ita fecerunt sed semet ipsos dederunt primum Domino, deinde & nobis, per Dei voluntatem.
units.tr: Ver. 5. And not as we hoped, but they first gave their own selves to the Lord, and then to us, by the will of God.

units.la: Ratio 9. Quia supra quam Apostolus sperare poterat, se & sua omnia Deo consecrabant, & Apostolo se committebant, ut ab eo secundum voluntatem Dei, in omnibus regerentur.
units.tr: Reason 9. Because, beyond what the Apostle could hope, they consecrated themselves and all their goods to God, and committed themselves to the Apostle, to be directed by him in all things according to the will of God.

units.la: Verf. 6. Ut adhortaremur Titum, ut sicut ante coepit, ita etiam absolvat apud vos hanc quoque gratiam.
units.tr: Ver. 6. So that we urged Titus that, as he had begun, so he would also complete this grace among you.

units.la: Arg. 2. Ad liberalem eleemosynam; Quia rogatu Macedonum, ego Titum rogavi, ut perficiendam eleemosynam vestram curaret, quam rem jam agressus est: Idcirco curate ne frustra sit hoc nostrum studium.
units.tr: Arg. 2. To generous almsgiving: because at the request of the Macedonians I asked Titus to see to the completion of your alms, a task he has already begun. Therefore take care that our zeal is not in vain.

units.la: Verf. 7. Itaque sicut in omnibus abundatis fide, & sermone, & cognitione & omni studio, & vestra in nos charitate, videte ut in hac quoque gratia abundetis.
units.tr: Ver. 7. Therefore, as you abound in faith, in speech, in knowledge, in all diligence, and in your love toward us, see that you abound in this grace also.

units.la: Arg. 3. Quia cum aliis virtutibus excellatis, decet vos dare operam ne in hac deficiatis; vel cum abundent in vobis dona Spiritus, fides miraculorum, dona cognitionis, & eloquentiae, studium de salute fratrum, & charitas erga me, cavendum ne hoc donum deesse vobis comperiatur.
units.tr: Arg. 3. Because you excel in other virtues, it becomes you to take care not to be lacking in this one; or, since the gifts of the Spirit abound among you, the gift of miracles, the gifts of knowledge and eloquence, zeal for the salvation of the brethren, and love toward me, care must be taken lest this gift be found to be wanting in you.

units.la: Verf. 8. Non ex imperio loquor, sed aliorum studio, vestrae queque dilectionis sinceritatem reddens exploratam.
units.tr: Ver. 8. I speak not by command, but by the zeal of others, proving the sincerity of your love also.

units.la: Arg. 4. Quia jam probanda vobis est sinceritas Christianae dilectionis vestrae, in hac eleemosyna erogande, cujus rei gratia sedulo vos hortor, rogatu Macedonum, & nihil pro imperio praecipiens. Idcirco specimen liberalitatis ostendite.
units.tr: Arg. 4. Because the sincerity of your Christian love must now be proved to you in giving this alms, for which purpose I earnestly exhort you, at the request of the Macedonians, and commanding nothing by authority. Therefore show a sample of your liberality.

units.la: Verf. 9. Noftis enim beneficentiam Domini nostri Iesu Christi, eum videlicet propter vos pauperem factum esse, quum esset dives: ut vos illius paupertate ditesceretis.
units.tr: Ver. 9. For you know the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, that though he was rich, yet for your sake he became poor, so that you through his poverty might become rich.

units.la: Arg. 5. CHRISTUS pauperem se fecit, ut vos ditesceretis: Ergo ut ejus causa erogetis eleemosynam, cum petitur à vobis æquum est.
units.tr: Arg. 5. Christ made himself poor that you might become rich. Therefore it is fitting that, when you are asked, you give alms for his sake.

units.la: Verf. 10. Et sententiam in ea re meam edo: nam hoc vobis conducit, qui non solum, facere sed etiam velle ante coepistis anno superiore.
units.tr: Ver. 10. And I give my judgment in this matter, my judgment, for this is expedient for you, who began not only to do but also to desire it a year ago.

units.la: Arg. 6. Quia consultum est, & utile vobis, & respectu famae vestrae, & respectu benedictionis sequuturae, ut in hoc negotio minime desitis, sed collectam jam inchoatam tandem absolvatis.
units.tr: Arg. 6. Because it is advisable and useful for you, both with respect to your reputation and with respect to the blessing that will follow, that you should by no means give up this business, but at last complete the collection already begun.

units.la: Verf. 11. At nunc etiam illud ipsum facere absolvite: ut sicut adfuit promptum illud velle, ita etiam adsit ipsum perficere ex eo quod habetis
units.tr: Ver. 11. Now therefore finish the doing of it also, so that as there was a readiness to will, so there may be a completion out of what you have.

units.la: Verf. 12. Etenim si prius adsit promptus animus, aliquis acceptus est pro eo quod habet, non pro eo quod non habet.
units.tr: Ver. 12. For if the willing mind is present first, it is accepted according to what a man has, not according to what he does not have.

units.la: Verf. 13. Non enim ut aliis relaxatio sit, vobis autem oppressis: sed pari conditione hoc tempore vestra abundantia supplet illorum defectum.
units.tr: Ver. 13. For I do not mean that others should be relieved and you burdened, but on equal terms, at this time your abundance supplies their lack.

units.la: Arg. 7. Quia decorum est & conveniens, ut prompta vestra voluntas quam
units.tr: Arg. 7. Because it is seemly and fitting that your ready will

units.la: Gratia ] Prima ratio. Quia donum erat Dei ex gratia in ipsos profectum, quod in usum pauperum Judaeorum quicquam contribuerint.
units.tr: Grace]. First reason: because it was a gift of God, bestowed on them out of grace, that they contributed anything for the use of the poor Jews.

units.la: Verf. 2 Nam in multa probatione abundans gaudium ipsorum, & profunda eorum paupertas redundavit in copiosam benignitatem ipsorum.
units.tr: Ver. 2. For in a great trial of affliction, the abundance of their joy and their deep poverty overflowed into the riches of their generosity.

units.la: Ratio 2. Quia data est eleemosyna ab iis eo tempore, cum ipsi probabantur gravibus afflictionibus.
units.tr: Reason 2. Because the alms were given by them at a time when they were being tested by severe afflictions.

units.la: Gaudium ] Ratio 3. Quia cum gaudio contribuerunt.
units.tr: Joy] Reason 3. Because they contributed with joy.
