units.la: Profunda ] Ratio 4. Quia in paupertate liberales erant.
units.tr: Deep] Reason 4. Because they were generous in their poverty.

units.la: Verf. 3 Nam pro viribus (testor) & supra vires voluntarii fuerunt.
units.tr: Ver. 3. For, I bear witness, they gave according to their means, and even beyond their means, willingly.

units.la: Ratio 5. Quia largius dare volebant, quam ipsorum ferebant facultates.
units.tr: Reason 5. Because they wished to give more than their resources allowed.

units.la: Verf. 4. Multis cum precibus nos rogantes, ut gratiam & societatem subministrationis quae in sanctos impenditur, suscieremus.
units.tr: Ver. 4. Begging us with much entreaty that we would accept the grace and the fellowship of the ministering that is done for the saints.

units.la: Ratio 6. Quia sponte, non provocati aliorum exemplo obtulerunt, sed autores aliis potius erant, ne in hoc officio charitatis deesset.
units.tr: Reason 6. Because they offered of their own accord, not prompted by the example of others; rather they were leaders for others, so that they might not be wanting in this duty of charity.

units.la: Precibus ] Ratio 7. Quia instabant precibus, ut acciperetur quod dabant.
units.tr: Entreaties] Reason 7. Because they pressed with entreaties that what they were giving should be accepted.

units.la: Societatem ] Ratio 8. Quia rogabant Apostolum, ut una cum aliis provinciam suscipere colligendi & dispensandi, quod ipsi & alii daturi erant.
units.tr: Fellowship] Reason 8. Because they asked the Apostle to take up, together with others, the task of collecting and distributing what they themselves and others were about to give.

units.la: Verf. 5. Ac non sicut sperabamus ita fecerunt sed semet ipsos dederunt primum Domino, deinde & nobis, per Dei voluntatem.
units.tr: Ver. 5. And not as we hoped, but they first gave their own selves to the Lord, and then to us, by the will of God.

units.la: Ratio 9. Quia supra quam Apostolus sperare poterat, se & sua omnia Deo consecrabant, & Apostolo se committebant, ut ab eo secundum voluntatem Dei, in omnibus regerentur.
units.tr: Reason 9. Because, beyond what the Apostle could hope, they consecrated themselves and all their goods to God, and committed themselves to the Apostle, to be directed by him in all things according to the will of God.

units.la: Verf. 6. Ut adhortaremur Titum, ut sicut ante coepit, ita etiam absolvat apud vos hanc quoque gratiam.
units.tr: Ver. 6. So that we urged Titus that, as he had begun, so he would also complete this grace among you.

units.la: Arg. 2. Ad liberalem eleemosynam; Quia rogatu Macedonum, ego Titum rogavi, ut perficiendam eleemosynam vestram curaret, quam rem jam agressus est: Idcirco curate ne frustra sit hoc nostrum studium.
units.tr: Arg. 2. To generous almsgiving: because at the request of the Macedonians I asked Titus to see to the completion of your alms, a task he has already begun. Therefore take care that our zeal is not in vain.

units.la: Verf. 7. Itaque sicut in omnibus abundatis fide, & sermone, cognitione & omni studio, & vestra in nos charitate, videte ut in hac quoque gratia abundetis.
units.tr: Ver. 7. Therefore, as you abound in faith, and speech, and knowledge, and all diligence, and in your love toward us, see that you abound in this grace also.

units.la: Arg. 3. Quia cum aliis virtutibus excellatis, decet vos dare operam ne in hac deficiatis; vel cum abundent in vobis dona Spiritus, fides miraculorum, dona cognitionis, & eloquentiæ, studium de salute fratrum, & charitas erga me, cavendum ne hoc donum deesse vobis comperiatur.
units.tr: Arg. 3. Because you excel in other virtues, it becomes you to take care not to be lacking in this one; or, since the gifts of the Spirit abound among you, the gift of miracles, the gifts of knowledge and eloquence, zeal for the salvation of the brethren, and love toward me, care must be taken lest this gift be found to be wanting in you.

units.la: Verf. 8. Non ex imperio loquor, sed aliorum studio, vestræ quoque dilectionis sinceritatem reddens exploratam.
units.tr: Ver. 8. I speak not by command, but by the zeal of others, proving the sincerity of your love also.

units.la: Arg. 4. Quia jam probanda vobis est sinceritas Christianæ dilectionis vestræ, in hac eleemosyna eroganda, cujus rei gratia sedulo vos hortor, rogatu Macedonum, & nihil pro imperio præcipiens. Idcirco specimen liberalitatis ostendite.
units.tr: Arg. 4. Because the sincerity of your Christian love must now be proved to you in giving this alms, for which purpose I earnestly exhort you, at the request of the Macedonians, and commanding nothing by authority. Therefore show a sample of your liberality.

units.la: Verf. 9. Nostis enim beneficentiam Domini nostri Iesu Christi, eum videlicet propter vos pauperem factum esse, quum esset dives: ut vos illius paupertate ditesceretis.
units.tr: Ver. 9. For you know the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, that though he was rich, yet for your sake he became poor, so that you through his poverty might become rich.

units.la: Arg. 5. Christus pauperem se fecit, ut vos ditescceretis: Ergo ut ejus causa erogetis eleemosynam, cum petitur à vobis æquum est.
units.tr: Arg. 5. Christ made himself poor that you might become rich. Therefore it is fitting that, when you are asked, you give alms for his sake.

units.la: Verf. 10. Et sententiam in ea re meam edo: nam hoc vobis conducit, qui non solum, facere sed etiam velle ante cœpistis anno superiore.
units.tr: Verse 10. And I give my opinion on this matter, for this is to your advantage, you who began not only to act but also to be willing a year ago.

units.la: Arg. 6. Quia consultum est, & utile vobis, & respectu famæ vestræ, & respectu benedictionis sequuturæ, ut in hoc negotio minime desitis, sed collectam jam inchoatam tandem absolvatis.
units.tr: Argument 6. It is good counsel, and useful for you, both with respect to your reputation and with respect to the blessing that will follow, that you not give up in this business at all, but finally complete the collection you have already begun.

units.la: Verf. 11. At nunc etiam illud ipsum facere absolvite: ut sicut adfuit promptum illud velle, ita etiam adsit ipsum perficere ex eo quod habetis.
units.tr: Verse 11. But now finish the doing of that same thing too, so that just as the ready willingness was present, so the completion may also be present, out of what you have.

units.la: Verf. 12. Etenim si prius adsit promptus animus, aliquis acceptus est pro eo quod habet, non pro eo quod non habet.
units.tr: Verse 12. For if the ready mind is present first, a gift is accepted according to what a person has, not according to what he does not have.

units.la: Verf. 13. Non enim ut aliis relaxatio sit, vobis autem oppressio, sed pari conditione hoc tempore vestra abundantia supplet illorum defectum.
units.tr: Verse 13. For it is not that others should have relief and you oppression, but on equal terms, at this time your abundance supplies their lack.

units.la: Arg. 7. Quia decorum est & conveniens, ut prompta vestra voluntas quam præ vobis tulistis superiori anno, actione compleatur, & turpe futurum est, fi secus acciderit.
units.tr: Argument 7. It is fitting and proper that your ready will, which you displayed to others last year, be carried through by action, and it would be shameful if it turned out otherwise.

units.la: Quod habetis ] Arg. 8. Quia nihil petitur nisi quod æquum esse ipsi potestis perspicere, rogatur enim ut pro facultatibus detis, ex æquo sine vestro dispendio notabili, siquidem exiguum à pauperioribus si prompto animo dederint, acceptum erit Deo, etiamsi multum, quod non habent, non dederint: si vero promptus animus non adsit, nihil respicitur à Deo, quantumcunque detur. Ne hic desitis igitur.
units.tr: "What you have"] Argument 8. Nothing is asked except what you yourselves can see to be fair, for it is requested that you give according to your means, on equal terms and without any considerable loss to yourselves. For if the poorer give even a small amount with a ready mind, it will be acceptable to God, even if they do not give much, which they do not have; but if the ready mind is not present, God takes no account of whatever is given, however much it is. Do not, then, give up here.

units.la: Verf. 14. Ut & illorum abundantia vestrum defectum suppleat, ut fiat æquabilitas,
units.tr: Verse 14. So that their abundance may also supply your lack, that there may be equality,

units.la: Arg. 9. Quia vobis expectandum est, ut si opus fuerit aliquando retributio reddenda sit, & e copia Ecclesiarum in Judæa succurratur inopiæ vestræ, ut sic quod æquale elt, fiat.
units.tr: Argument 9. You must expect that, if there is ever need, a return will be made to you, and that from the abundance of the churches in Judea your want will be relieved, so that what is equal may come about.

units.la: Verf. 15. Sicut scriptum est, Qui multum collegit, non habuit amplius; & qui paulum, non habuit minus.
units.tr: Verse 15. As it is written: He who gathered much had nothing over, and he who gathered little had no lack.

units.la: Arg. 10. Quia in Mannæ exemplo indicatum est, neminem abundantiam suam debere supprimere cum aliorum inedia, sed eatenus servandam æqualitatem, ut nulli desit quantum necesse est; nam sicut in colligenda Manna factum elt, quisque Omer sibi mensurabat, reliquum cedebat iis qui minus collegerant, Exod. 16, 18. 19. sic in divitiis collectis, quod supereft post vestros usus, in usum egenorum cedere debet.
units.tr: Argument 10. In the example of the manna it was shown that no one should hoard his abundance while others go hungry, but that equality must be kept to the extent that no one lacks what is needed. For just as in gathering the manna it was done that each measured out an omer for himself, and the surplus went to those who had gathered less (Exod. 16:18, 19), so in gathered riches, what remains after your own uses ought to go to the use of the needy.

units.la: Verf. 16. Gratia autem sit Deo, qui cordi Titi indidit idem studium pro vobis.
units.tr: Verse 16. But thanks be to God, who put the same zeal for you into the heart of Titus.

units.la: Verf. 17. Quod tum exhortationem illam gratam habuit, tum vero majore studio ultro ad vos abiit.
units.tr: Verse 17. For he not only welcomed that exhortation, but, being even more eager, went to you of his own accord.

units.la: Arg. 11. Quia fideles, strenui & optimæ famæ fratres aliquot excitati sunt à Deo, (compar. verf. 18. 22.) & missi à me, qui totum hoc negotium promoverent, non in colligenda eleemosyna tantum, sed etiam in ea perferenda ad manus Judæorum inopum. Ex his fratribus primus erat Titus, propter cujus solicitudinem & promptitudinem animi ad negotium hoc conficiendum Deum laudat.
units.tr: Argument 11. God has stirred up several faithful, diligent brothers of good reputation (compare verses 18 and 22), and I have sent them to promote the whole business, not only in gathering the alms but also in carrying them to the hands of the poor Jews. Of these brothers the first was Titus, for whose care and readiness of mind in completing this business he praises God.

units.la: Verf. 18. Misimus autem una cum eo fratrem illum, cujus laus est in Euangelio per omnes Ecclesias.
units.tr: Verse 18. And we have sent with him that brother whose praise is in the gospel throughout all the churches.

units.la: Verf. 19. Nec id solum, sed etiam suffragiis delectus est ab Ecclesiis socius peregrinationis nostræ, cum hac beneficentia quæ administratur ministratur a nobis ad ipsius Domini gloriam, & comprobandum promptum animum vestrum.)
units.tr: Verse 19. And not only that, but he was also chosen by the churches as our companion on our journey, in this grace which is administered by us, to the glory of the Lord himself and to prove your ready mind.

units.la: Secundus delegatus describitur, Quod in Euangelio promovendo diligenter laboraverit, sive fuerit Barnabas, sive alius, non refert. Nam quisquis fuerit, ab Ecclesiis (synodice ut videtur convocatis) delegatus est, ut fide dignus cui res haec committeretur.
units.tr: The second delegate is described: that he has labored diligently in advancing the gospel, whether he was Barnabas or someone else does not matter. For whoever he was, he was delegated by the churches (apparently gathered in a synod) as a man worthy of trust to whom this matter might be committed.

units.la: Gloriam] Arg. 12. Quia haec eleemosyna curatur & administratur a me & aliis ad Christi gloriam, & promptitudinem animi vestri demonstrandam.
units.tr: Glory] Argument 12. This alms is managed and administered by me and by others to the glory of Christ and to show the readiness of your mind.

units.la: Vers. 20. Vitantes hoc, ne quis nos vituperet in hac exuberantia quae administratur a nobis.
units.tr: Verse 20. Avoiding this, that anyone should blame us for this abundance which is administered by us.

units.la: Vers. 21. Ut qui procuremus honesta, non solum coram Domino, sed etiam coram hominibus.
units.tr: Verse 21. For we take care to do what is honorable, not only before the Lord but also before men.

units.la: Rationem reddit, cur sibi adjunxerit tam spectatae fidei collegas, in hac Ministratione beneficentiae, collectae in usum Ecclesiae Hierosolymitanae, nempe ut ansam obtrectandi adversariis suis praecideret, qui alioqui de summa pecuniae collectae interceptum aliquid calumniari potuissent: Et ut consuleret famae suae apud omnes homines, sicut conscientiae suae apud Deum prospexerat, in sancto proposito integritatis suae, in hoc negotio, conservandae.
units.tr: He gives the reason why he has joined to himself such well-tested brothers in this ministry of beneficence, the collection for the church at Jerusalem: namely, to cut off the occasion for slander from his adversaries, who otherwise might have accused him of diverting some part of the sum of money collected. And he wished to look to his reputation before all men, just as he had looked to his conscience before God, in keeping his integrity in this business by a holy purpose.

units.la: Vers. 22. Misimus autem cum eis fratrem nostrum, quem saepe in multis probavimus studiosum, nunc autem multo studiosiorem, ob multam fiduciam quam habeo in vobis.
units.tr: Verse 22. And we have sent with them our brother, whom we have often proved to be zealous in many things, but now much more zealous, because of the great confidence I have in you.

units.la: Tertium delegatum commendat, sive fuerit Lucas, sive alius, non refert, sed hinc vis argumenti undecimi apparet, dum dicit se ex confidentia de Corinthiorum liberalitate misisse ad eos tam egregios viros, quorum expectationem non veretur, ne frustrentur, unde sequitur liberaliter contribuendum esse.
units.tr: He commends a third delegate, whether it was Luke or someone else does not matter. But the force of the eleventh argument appears here, since he says that from confidence in the generosity of the Corinthians he has sent to them such outstanding men, whose expectation he does not fear will be disappointed. From this it follows that they must contribute generously.

units.la: Vers. 23. Sive de Tito quaeritur, socius meus est, & apud vos adjutor: sive de fratribus nostris, legati sunt Ecclesiarum, & gloria Christi.
units.tr: Verse 23. If anyone asks about Titus, he is my partner and your helper; if about our brothers, they are messengers of the churches and the glory of Christ.

units.la: Postquam singulos seorsim delegatos suo quemque elogio ornavit, nunc Titum specialiter, & omnes commendat conjunctim, quod sint Apostoli Ecclesiarum, id est, delegati ab Ecclesiis ad hanc eleemosynam colligendam: & secundo quod sint gloria Christi, sic dicti, quia ipsius gratia gloriosè in illis splendebat, & per eos ejus gloria illustrabatur. •
units.tr: After praising each delegate separately with his own commendation, he now commends Titus specially, and all of them together: first, that they are apostles of the churches, that is, delegates from the churches for collecting this alms; and second, that they are the glory of Christ, so called because his grace shone gloriously in them, and his glory was made illustrious through them.

units.la: Verf. 24. Itaque demonstrationem charitatis vestræ, & nostræ de vobis gloriationis edite in eos, in conspectu Ecclesiarum.
units.tr: Verse 24. Therefore show to them, in the sight of the churches, the proof of your love and of our boasting about you.

units.la: Hortatione repetitâ, addit Arg. 13. Hæc liberalitas ut futura est documentum charitatis veltræ, sic etiam confirmatio erit gloriationis meæ de vobis minimè vanæ, in conspectu delegatorum, qui Ecclesiarum nomine in hoc negotio præsentes veltram liberalitatem conspicient. Ergo vobis liberaliter contribuendum est.
units.tr: With the exhortation repeated, he adds argument 13: as this generosity will be a proof of your love, so it will also confirm my boasting about you, which is by no means vain, in the sight of the delegates who, in the name of the churches, will be present in this business and see your liberality. Therefore you must contribute generously.

units.la: Caput Nonum.
units.tr: Caput Nonum.

units.la: Ergit de collecta agere: Capitis duæ sunt partes: In prima reddit rationes cur miserit ad eos tres fratres delegatos, ubi argumenta interserit ad persuadendum ut accelerent collectam, ad verf. 6. In altera addit argumenta plura ad movendum, ut dent liberaliter sicut sanctos decebat.
units.tr: He treats of the collection. The chapter has two parts. In the first he gives the reasons why he sent the three brothers as delegates to them, and there he interposes arguments to persuade them to hasten the collection, up to verse 6. In the second he adds several further arguments to move them to give generously, as became saints.

units.la: NAm de subministratione quidem quæ fit in sanctos, supervacaneum est mihi scribere vobis. Verf. 1.
units.tr: For concerning the ministering to the saints, it is superfluous for me to write to you. Verse 1.

units.la: Quod ad primam partem attinet: Ne in deteriorem partem interpretarentur missionem legatorum, quasi suspicionem de ipsorum promptitudine in hoc negotio foveret, causam mittendorum fratrum ostendit fuisse, non ut docerentur, neque ut redderentur voluntarii ad collectam faciendam, quia ob eam causam supervacaneum fuisset scripsisse, nedum fratres ad eos misisse.
units.tr: As to the first part: lest the sending of the delegates be taken in a worse sense, as if it cast suspicion on their readiness in this business, he shows that the reason for sending the brothers was not that they might be taught, nor that they might be made willing to make the collection. For had that been the reason, it would have been superfluous to write, let alone to send brothers to them.

units.la: Verf. 2. Novi enim promptum animum vestrum, quem de vobis jacto apud Macedones, Achajam videlicet paratam esse ab anno superiore: & ex vobis ortus zelus provocavit complures.
units.tr: Verse 2. For I know your readiness of mind, which I boast of concerning you among the Macedonians, that Achaia has been prepared since the year before; and your zeal has provoked very many.

units.la: Confirmat dictum tribus rationibus.
units.tr: He confirms what he has said by three reasons.

units.la: Novi] Ratio prima, Quia ipsorum promptitudinem animi probè ante noverat.
units.tr: "I know": the first reason, because he had known their readiness of mind well beforehand.

units.la: Jacto] Ratio 2. Quia de illorum alacritate gloriatus fuerat.
units.tr: "Boast": the second reason, because he had boasted of their eagerness.

units.la: Rebus] Ratio 3. Quia ipsorum studium in hoc negotio provocaverat multos, ad similem alacritatem & zelum.
units.tr: "Zeal": the third reason, because their earnestness in this business had provoked many to a similar eagerness and zeal.

units.la: Vers. 3. Misi autem hos fratres, ne gloriatio nostra de vobis inanis fiat hac in parte: ut (sicut dicebam) parati sitis:
units.tr: Verse 3. But I have sent these brothers, lest our boasting concerning you should prove empty in this respect; so that (as I was saying) you may be ready.

units.la: Veras vero rationes cur mis..rit fratres proponit quinque: Ratio prima, Ut pararent beneficentiam ipsorum eo citius ad deportationem, & ut jam collecta pecunia inveniretur à legatis, sicut pollicitus fuerat iplorum nomine Apostolus.
units.tr: He sets out five true reasons why he sent the brothers. Reason 1: that they might prepare their generous gift for the carrying away the sooner, and that the money, now collected, might be found ready by the delegates, as the Apostle had promised in their name.

units.la: Ratio 2. Ne gloriatio Apostoli de illis vana comperiretur.
units.tr: Reason 2: lest the Apostle's boasting about them should be found to be empty.

units.la: Vers. 4. Ne quo modo, si mecum venerint Macedones, & offenderint vos imparatos, pudefiamus (ut ne vos dicam) in praesidente ista gloriatione.
units.tr: Verse 4. Lest in any way, if Macedonians come with me and find you unprepared, we be put to shame (not to say you) in this confident boasting.

units.la: Ratio 3. Ex superiori sequens: Ne & ego & vos pudefiamus, si imparati deprehensi fueritis, quando ego una cum Macedonibus, qui gloriantem me de vobis audiverunt, venerimus ad vos.
units.tr: Reason 3, following from the previous one: lest both I and you be put to shame, if you are found unprepared when I come to you together with the Macedonians, who heard me boasting of you.

units.la: Vers. 5. Itaque necessarium putavi adhortari fratres, ut primum eant ad vos, & prius absolvant antea indictam beneficentiam vestram, ut ea sit parata ita ut beneficentia, & non ut extortum aliquid.
units.tr: Verse 5. Therefore I thought it necessary to exhort the brothers that they should go to you first, and first complete the bounty you have already promised, so that it may be ready as a bounty and not as something extorted.

units.la: Ratio 4. Misi ad vos fratres, ut in colligenda pecunia à fratribus delegatis juvemini, quo paratiora omnia sint.
units.tr: Reason 4: I sent the brothers to you so that you might be helped by the delegates in collecting the money, so that everything may be more ready.

units.la: Ratio 5. Misi ad vos fratres, qui curarent inter colligendum, ne quis urgeatur ad plus quam vellet, contribuendum, & ne in colligentibus avaritia, vel in contribuentibus parsimonia se prodat, sed ut qui dant, liberaliter & sponte dent, & sic tota collectio liberalis quasi benedictio, in meo adventu appareat.
units.tr: Reason 5: I sent the brothers to you who would take care, during the collecting, that no one is pressed to give more than he wishes, and that avarice does not show itself in the collectors, nor meanness in the contributors; but that those who give may give freely and willingly, and so the whole collection may appear at my coming as a liberal blessing.

units.la: Secunda Pars.
units.tr: Secunda Pars.

units.la: Vers. 6. Illud autem dico, Qui serit parce, parce etiam metet: & qui serit benigne, benigne etiam metet.
units.tr: Verse 6. But this I say: He who sows sparingly will also reap sparingly; and he who sows bountifully will also reap bountifully.

units.la: Secunda pars Capitis, in qua ut liberaliter, & sicut decebat sanctos eleemosynam hanc erogarent, addit argumenta decem.
units.tr: The second part of the chapter, in which he adds ten arguments that they should bestow this alms freely and as became saints.

units.la: Argumentum primum, Quia quicunque vel nihil, vel non pro facultatum ratione, vel non ex cordis propósito dabunt (quod est parce seminare)
units.tr: First argument: because whoever gives nothing, or not in proportion to his means, or not from a purpose of the heart (which is to sow sparingly),

units.la: parce parcè etiam messuri sunt, hoc est, vel nihil vel temporaneam tantùm mer-cedem reportaturi: Idcirco liberaliter date.
units.tr: will also reap sparingly, that is, will gain either nothing or only a temporary reward. Therefore give generously.

units.la: ] Arg. 2. Quia qui liberaliter, & ex dilectione dabunt (quod est in benedictionibus seminare) liberalem messem habituri sunt. Liberaliter ergo date.
units.tr: Argument 2: because those who give generously and from love (which is to sow in blessings) will have a generous harvest. Therefore give generously.

units.la: Vers. 7. Quisque sicut præ ptat corde, ita agat; non ex tristitia aut necessitate; nam hilarem datorem diligit Deus.
units.tr: Verse 7. Let each one act as he has purposed in his heart, not out of sadness or necessity; for God loves a cheerful giver.

units.la: Postquam expoluit quid sit liberaliter dare, seu in benedictionibus seminare, (nempe ex animi proposito dare, non ex tristitia vel ex necessitate: Qui enim sic dat, pacè dat quantumcunque dat, & nihil daturus esset si animi sui propositum sequi liceret) addit Arg. 3. Deus diligit hilare n datorem, & per consequens tristem datorem, & involuntarium non diligit, non approbat, non ei benedicit. Hilariter ergo & liberaliter date.
units.tr: Having explained what it is to give generously, that is, to sow in blessings (namely, to give from a purpose of the heart, not out of sadness or necessity; for he who gives in that way gives freely, however much he gives, and would give nothing if he were allowed to follow the purpose of his own mind), he adds argument 3: God loves a cheerful giver, and consequently does not love, does not approve, and does not bless a sad giver or one who gives unwillingly. Therefore give cheerfully and generously.

units.la: Vers. 8. Potens est autem Deus efficere, ut omnis gratia in vos redundet; ut in omnibus semper omnino quantum sufficiat penes vos habentes, abundetis ad omne opus bonum.
units.tr: Verse 8. And God is able to make all grace abound toward you, so that you, always having in all things all sufficiency, may abound to every good work.

units.la: Arg. 4. In solutione obiectionis tacitè proponitur. Tantùm abest (inquit) ut metuatis inopiam, si copiosiùs tribuatis, ut contra expectetis potius, Deum ex gratia & potentia sua largiturum vobis, quantum satis erit rerum temporalium, ut non tantùm vestra forte contenti sitis, sed etiam ad omne opus bonum, in aliis juvandis abundetis; Ergo liberaliter date. Verl. 9 (Sicut scriptum est, Dispersit, dedit pauperibus: beneficentia ejus manet in seculum.
units.tr: Argument 4, tacitly proposed in answer to an objection: Far from it, he says, that you should fear want if you give more abundantly; rather, you should expect that God, out of his grace and power, will bestow on you as much temporal goods as will suffice, so that you are not only content with your own, but also abound in helping others in every good work. Therefore give generously. Verse 9 (As it is written, He has scattered abroad, he has given to the poor; his righteousness endures for ever.

units.la: Confirmat hoc argumentum ex Psal. 112. 9. Ubi dicitur justus bona sua dispergere, & pauperibus largiri, & benignitas tamen ejus durare in perpetuum, ubi insinuatur Arg. 5. Quod sit proprietas viri justi pauperibus bona sua largiri, & Dei in eum ordinaria benedictio sit, ut quæ porro largiatur, habeat: Idcirco liberaliter dando justos vos declarate.
units.tr: He confirms this argument from Psalm 112:9, where it is said that the just man scatters his goods and gives freely to the poor, and his righteousness endures for ever. There is implied argument 5: it is the property of a righteous man to bestow his goods on the poor, and it is God's ordinary blessing upon him that he who keeps giving should also have. Therefore by giving generously, declare yourselves righteous.

units.la: Vers 10. Porrò qui suppeditat semen serenti, is quoque panem vobis ad escam suppeditet, & multiplicet sementem vestram, & augeat fructus beneficentiæ vestræ.)
units.tr: Verse 10. Now he who supplies seed to the sower will also supply bread for food, and will multiply your seed and increase the fruits of your bounty.

units.la: Arg 6. Voto & similitudine inclusum, sicut Deus suppeditat agricolæ, & semen ante sementem, & panem post messem, sic & vobis suppeditabit. ditabit semen ad eleemosynam faciendam, & fructum ex semente suppeditabit, utque multiplicet vobis facultates ad benefaciendum, & ad fructus justitiæ & misericordiæ ferendum, opto. Sementem ergo in hac eleemosyna eroganda ne dubitate facere.
units.tr: Argument 6, contained in a wish and a comparison: just as God supplies the farmer both seed before sowing and bread after the harvest, so he will also supply you. He will supply seed for giving alms, and will bring fruit from the seed; and I pray that he will multiply your resources for doing good and for bearing the fruits of righteousness and mercy. Therefore do not doubt to sow in this giving of alms.

units.la: Verf. 11. Ut inquam abundetis, in omnibus ditati ad omnem benignitatem, quæ per nos efficit, ut gratiæ agantur Deo.
units.tr: Verse 11. That, I say, you may abound, being enriched in everything for all liberality, which through us works thanksgiving to God.

units.la: Arg. 7. Vos gratia Dei locupletati, & abundantes od omnem liberalitatem, efficietis ut per nos qui observamus charitatem vestram, gratiæ agantur Deo: Ergo vel hoc nomine liberaliter date.
units.tr: Argument 7: you, enriched by the grace of God and abounding in all liberality, will bring it about that, through us who observe your love, thanks are given to God. Therefore, for this reason too, give generously.

units.la: Verf. 12. Nam subministratio oblationis istius non solum supplet sanctorum inopiam, sed etiam redundat in multas gratiarum actiones apud Deum.
units.tr: Verse 12. For the ministry of this offering not only supplies the want of the saints, but also overflows in many thanksgivings to God.

units.la: Hoc argumentum confirmat ex eo, quod functio sacri hujus Ministerii suscepti de colligenda & contribuenda hac eleemosyna, non tantum suppletura sit necessitates sanctorum in Judæa, sed etiam effectura ut per multos sanctos gratiæ agantur Deo.
units.tr: He confirms this argument from the fact that the performance of this sacred ministry, undertaken in collecting and contributing this alms, will not only supply the needs of the saints in Judea, but will also cause thanks to be given to God by many saints.

units.la: Verf. 13 ( Dum per hanc istius subministrationis experientiam Deum glorificant de consentiente vestra subjectione in Euangelium Christi, deque benigna in se, & omnes communicatione.)
units.tr: Verse 13. While through the proof of this ministry they glorify God for your obedience in confessing the gospel of Christ, and for the liberality of your communication to them and to all.

units.la: Arg. 8. Hæc vestra liberalitas erit indicium fidei vestræ, & subjectionis animi in obedientiam Christi, & confessionis Euangelii ejus, & glorificandi Dei materia, & denique indicium liberalitatis vestræ in reliquos omnes pauperes ubi datur occasio: Date igitur liberaliter.
units.tr: Argument 8: this your liberality will be a sign of your faith, of the submission of your mind to the obedience of Christ and to the confession of his gospel, a matter for glorifying God, and finally a sign of your liberality toward all the other poor wherever occasion is given. Therefore give generously.

units.la: Verf. 14. Et illorum preces pro vobis propenso amore vos diligentium propter gratiam Dei in vobis exuberantem.
units.tr: Verse 14. And their prayers for you, with their deep affection toward you, because of the abundant grace of God in you.

units.la: Arg 9. Sancti in Judæa refocillati vestra liberalitate orabunt Deum pro vobis: Dandum igitur liberaliter.
units.tr: Argument 9: the saints in Judea, refreshed by your liberality, will pray to God for you. Therefore give generously.

units.la: Amore ] Arg. 10. Vestra hæc liberalitas excitabit in Judæis sanctis dilectionem erga vos, & desiderium vos videndi, & existimationem vestri non exiguam fovebit apud eos, propter eminentem in vobis Dei gratiam: Ne hic desitis ergo.
units.tr: "Affection": Argument 10: this your liberality will stir up in the holy Jews love toward you and a desire to see you, and will foster no small esteem for you among them, on account of the eminent grace of God in you. Therefore do not stop here.

units.la: Verf. 15. Gratia autem sit Deo super inenarrabili suo munere.
units.tr: Verse 15. But thanks be to God for his indescribable gift.

units.la: Quasi jam voti compos, & prospiciens multiplicem hujus liberalitatis fructum futurum, quem Dei gratia productura erat, ex fratrum in Judæa refocillatione, gratias agit Deo pro dono Dei in liberalitate Corinthiorum, quod verbis pro dignitate satis explicari non potuit.
units.tr: As one now having his wish, and foreseeing the manifold fruit that this liberality would bear, which the grace of God was going to produce through the refreshing of the brothers in Judea, he gives thanks to God for the gift of God in the liberality of the Corinthians, which could not be sufficiently explained in words worthy of it.

units.la: Caput Decimum.
units.tr: Chapter 10.

units.la: Ertia pars Epistolæ: In qua Apostolus suam autoritatem vendicat à Pseudapostolorum asperssionibus, quibus ipsius authoritati apud Corinthios detrahere laborabant: Hoc capite; quia vitio vertebant Paulo, quod præsens inter Corinthios humiliter se gessisset, absens verò authoritatis gravitatem literis suis ostentasset, hanc calumniam amolitur, factum defendendo.
units.tr: The third part of the Epistle: in which the Apostle vindicates his authority against the aspersions of the false apostles, by which they laboured to detract from his authority among the Corinthians. In this chapter, since they found fault with Paul for conducting himself humbly while present among the Corinthians, but showing the gravity of his authority in his letters while absent, he removes this calumny by defending his conduct.

units.la: Capitis duæ sunt partes: In prima probat octo argumentis se minimè contemnendum, ad versum 12. In secunda modestè se cum æmulis comparat, ad finem.
units.tr: The chapter has two parts. In the first, he proves by eight arguments that he is by no means to be despised, up to verse 12. In the second, he modestly compares himself with his rivals, to the end.

units.la: Cæterum precor vos per clementiam & æquitatem Christi, ego ipse Paulus, qui coram quidem humilis sum inter vos, absens verò sum erga vos confidens.
units.tr: Now I beseech you by the meekness and gentleness of Christ, I Paul myself, who am indeed humble among you when present, but bold toward you when absent.

units.la: Argumentum primum, Continetur in obtestatione per lenitatem & æquitatem Christi, ne factum suum secus quam par erat interpretarentur: quasi diceret, Humilitas illa mea erat ipsissima mansuetudo & imitatio mansuetudinis Christi, quam vobis in memoriam revoco, ut in me Domini nostri imitationem recognoscentes, de me recte judicetis. Non ergo despiciendus vobis sum.
units.tr: The first argument is contained in the entreaty, by the gentleness and equity of Christ, that they should not interpret his conduct otherwise than it ought to be interpreted. It is as if he said: "That humility of mine was true meekness and the imitation of the meekness of Christ, which I call to your memory, so that, recognising in me the imitation of our Lord, you may judge of me rightly. Therefore I am not to be despised by you."

units.la: Hoc autem rogo, ne, quum præsens adero, sim confidens ea fiducia qua cogito audax esse in quosdam, qui nos æstimant, ut si secundum carnem incederemus.
units.tr: But I ask this, that when I am present I may not have to be bold with that confidence with which I think of being bold against certain people, who consider us as if we walked according to the flesh.

units.la: Arg. 1. Cavendum vobis est, ne vestra culpa cogar audacter potestatem meam exercere in quosdam ex vobis, cum venero, sicut statui exercere adversus eos, qui de nobis existimant quasi metu vel spe ducti, instar carnalium & irregenitorum, mores nostros mutaremus, non igitur despiciendus sum.
units.tr: Argument 1. You must take care that through your fault I am not forced to exercise my power boldly against some of you when I come, as I have resolved to exercise it against those who think of us as if, moved by fear or hope, we changed our manners like carnal and unregenerate men. Therefore I am not to be despised.

units.la: Verf. 3. Nam in carne incedentes, secundum carnem non gerimus bellum,
units.tr: For though we walk in the flesh, we do not war according to the flesh,

units.la: Arg. 3. Quamvis non immunis ab humanis infirmitatibus vitam dego in fragili carne; in executione tamen officii mei, & Ministerialis militiae meae, non secutus sum carnales affectus, metu vel cupiditate ductus, ut illi calumniantur, quando nunc humiliter, nunc pro officii dignitate & authoritate, me gerebam. Ergo non contemnendus sum.
units.tr: Argument 3. Although I live my life in frail flesh, not free from human infirmities, yet in the discharge of my office and my ministerial warfare I have not followed carnal affections, moved by fear or desire, as they falsely charge, when I have conducted myself now humbly, now according to the dignity and authority of my office. Therefore I am not to be despised.

units.la: Verf. 4. Arma enim militiae nostrae non carnalia sunt, sed divinitus valida, ad subversionem munitionum.
units.tr: For the weapons of our warfare are not carnal, but mighty through God to the pulling down of strongholds.

units.la: Arg. 4. Superius confirmans, Non opus erat mihi armis carnalibus, ut in versipelli mutatione morum, nunc adulatione, nunc jactantia, aliisve similibus malis artibus uterer, sed sufficiebant mihi arma mea spiritualia, qualia sunt, in veritate parre sia, disciplinae Ecclesiasticae exercendae authoritas, zelus, patientia, fortitudo Christiana, & caeterae virtutes, quibus instructus militiam meam milito: Ergo non contemnendus sum. Horum armorum triplicem vim ostendit: 1. vis est, Quod virtute divina valida satis sint ad evertendum omnes sapientiae humanae munitiones, & ad demoliendum callidos praetextus & consilia omnia, quibus, pro erroribus & vitiis suis, contra Euangelium decertantes, defendere se solent, carnales.
units.tr: Argument 4. Confirming what precedes: I had no need of carnal weapons, to use in a shifting change of manners, now by flattery, now by boasting, or by other similar wicked arts. My spiritual weapons were sufficient for me, such as plain speaking of the truth, the authority to exercise ecclesiastical discipline, zeal, patience, Christian fortitude, and the other virtues with which, being armed, I wage my warfare. Therefore I am not to be despised. He shows the threefold force of these weapons. (1) The first force is that, by divine virtue, they are strong enough to overthrow all the fortifications of human wisdom and to demolish the crafty pretexts and all the counsels by which carnal men, fighting against the Gospel in defence of their errors and vices, are accustomed to protect themselves.

units.la: Verf. 5. Dum ratiocinationes evertimus, omnemque sublimitatem quae extollitur adversus cognitionem Dei: & captivam ducimus omnem cogitationem ad obediendum Christo.
units.tr: Casting down imaginations, and every high thing that exalteth itself against the knowledge of God, and bringing into captivity every thought to the obedience of Christ.

units.la: Secunda vis. Arma illa etiam valida esse docet, sicut ad superbiam humanae mentis, & altitudinem secularis scientiae dejiciendam, sic etiam ad convertendum, seu subigendum summa ingenia, ut obediant, & humiliter captivorum more submittant se CHRISTO per fidem. Intellige de electis & ordinatis ad salutem.
units.tr: The second force. He teaches that those weapons are also strong enough to bring down the pride of the human mind and the loftiness of worldly learning, and likewise to convert, or subdue, the greatest minds, so that they obey and humbly submit themselves to Christ through faith, like captives. This is to be understood of the elect and those ordained to salvation.

units.la: Verf. 6. Et paratum habemus quo vindicemus omnem contumaciam, postquam impleta fuerit vestra obedientia.
units.tr: And being in readiness to revenge all disobedience, when your obedience shall be fulfilled.

units.la: Tertia vis, Sufficiunt arma illa verbi DEI, & censurarum Ecclesiasticarum, &c. Ad ulciscendum rebelles & inobedientes, ut quae paratam habitura sint executionem, partim in hac vita, partim in futura; quae arma expediturus erat Apostolus in adversarios, postquam Corinthiorum gregem ab illis seductum, in ordinem & obedientiam revocasset: statuebat enim prudenter censuras Ecclesiasticas exercere.
units.tr: The third force. Those weapons, the word of God and ecclesiastical censures, suffice to punish rebels and the disobedient, since they will have their execution ready, partly in this life and partly in the future. The Apostle was about to use these weapons against his adversaries after he had brought the Corinthian flock, seduced by them, back into order and obedience; for he prudently resolved to exercise ecclesiastical censures.

units.la: Verf. 7. Quæ ob oculos sunt aspicitis: si quis apud se considit se Christi esse, hoc vicissim cogitet ex se, quemadmodum ipse Christi est, ita & nos Christi esse.
units.tr: Do ye look on things after the outward appearance? If any man trust to himself that he is Christ's, let him think this again of himself, that, as he is Christ's, even so are we Christ's.

units.la: Arg. 5. Quo probat se non contemnendum, Quia de Apostoli dignitate non debet fieri judicium ex facie, & externa humilitatis specie: interrogatio enim negati officii vim habet, idemque valet quod
units.tr: Argument 5. By this he proves that he is not to be despised, because judgment about the Apostle's dignity ought not to be made from the face and the external appearance of humility; for a question has the force of a denial of office, and the same holds as

units.la: Arg. 6. Mea humilitas nihil detrahit de dignitate Ministerii mei, quin ipse sim æquiparandus cuivis ex æmulis, & tot nominibus Christo propinquus, quam quivis ex iis. Non ergo despiciendus sum.
units.tr: Argument 6. My humility takes nothing from the dignity of my ministry, so that I am to be put on a par with any of my rivals; I am as near to Christ by all these titles as any of them. Therefore I am not to be despised.

units.la: Verf. 8. Nam si amplius etiam quippiam glorier de potestate nostra quam dedit Dominus nobis ad ædificationem, ac non ad subversionem vestri, non pudefiam:
units.tr: For though I should boast somewhat more of our authority, which the Lord hath given us for edification, and not for your destruction, I should not be ashamed:

units.la: Arg. 7. Quia utcunque, nunc humiliter, nunc pro autoritate me gessero, possum tamen sine vanitate de Apostolica mea autoritate gloriari. Interim ne potestatis commemoratio molesta esset, dicit hanc autoritatem datam sibi esse, ut ad salutem foret illis utilis, non vero ut ipsorum salutem impediret quovis modo.
units.tr: Argument 7. However I have conducted myself, now humbly, now in accordance with my authority, I can nevertheless glory in my apostolic authority without vanity. Meanwhile, lest the mention of his power be troublesome, he says that this authority was given to him so that it might be useful to them for salvation, and not so that it would in any way hinder their salvation.

units.la: Verf. 9. Ne videar seu perterrefacere vos per epistolas.
units.tr: That I may not seem as if I would terrify you by letters.

units.la: Verf. 10. Nam epistolæ quidem (inquit) graves sunt & validæ sed præsentia corporis infirma est, & sermo nihili.
units.tr: For his letters, say they, are weighty and powerful, but his bodily presence is weak, and his speech contemptible.

units.la: Verf. 11. Hoc cogitet qui ejusmodi est, quales sumus verbo per epistolas quum absumus, tales etiam fore reipsa quum aderimus.
units.tr: Let such a one think this: that such as we are in word by letters when we are absent, such we will be also in deed when we are present.

units.la: Arg. 8. Ne videar affectare per Epistolas authoritatem quam non habeo, verf. 9. Sicut calumniatores mei insinuare satagunt dicteriis suis, verf. 10. Facto ostensurus sum, authoritatem meam cum ad eos venero eandem esse, quam per Epistolas ostendere soleo: Ne ergo me contemnite.
units.tr: Argument 8. Lest he seem to aim, through letters, at an authority he does not have (v. 9), as my calumniators strive to insinuate with their taunts (v. 10), I will show by deed, when I come to them, that my authority is the same as I usually display through letters. So do not despise me.

units.la: Secunda Pars.
units.tr: The Second Part.

units.la: Verf. 12. Non enim audemus nos inferere aut conferre cum quibusdam qui seipsos commendant: sed non intelligunt quod ipsi sese seipsis metiuntur, & sese sibi ipsis comparant.
units.tr: Verse 12. For we do not dare to class ourselves or compare ourselves with certain persons who commend themselves; but they do not understand that they measure themselves by themselves, and compare themselves with themselves.

units.la: Secunda pars Capitis in qua vanitatem æmulorum detegit, qui se ita efferebant, quasi non ausus fuisset Apostolus se ipsis æquiparare: Cum his se comparat Apostolus in quintuplici dissimilitudine.
units.tr: The second part of the chapter, in which he exposes the vanity of his rivals, who boasted as if the Apostle had not dared to equate himself with them. The Apostle compares himself with them in a fivefold dissimilarity.

units.la: Prima dissimilitudo: Nos humiliter & modestè nos gerentes, certè non sumus eorum similes, qui ambitiosè & gloriosè nobis insultant, (quasi cum illis non essemus conferendi,) commendantes seipsos, supra quam res ipsa eos commendari patitur.
units.tr: First dissimilarity: We, conducting ourselves humbly and modestly, are certainly not like those who insult us ambitiously and boastfully (as if we were not to be compared with them), commending themselves beyond what the matter itself allows them to be commended.

units.la: Secunda dissimilitudo: Illi insipientiam suam produnt, metientes se ex sua ipsorum æstimatione, magnosque se facientes, ex suo & sui similium judicio: nos vanitatem hanc vitamus.
units.tr: Second dissimilarity: They betray their folly, measuring themselves by their own estimation and making themselves great by their own judgment and that of their like; we avoid this vanity.

units.la: Vers. 13. At nos non in gloriabimur de iis quæ mensuræ nostræ non sint, sed secundum dimensionem regularem ejus mensuræ quam Deus nobis dispertitus est gloriabimur nos pervenisse ad vos etiam usque.
units.tr: Verse 13. But we will not glory beyond our measure, but according to the regular measure of that measure which God has apportioned to us, and we will glory that we have come even as far as to you.

units.la: Vers. 14 Non enim ut si non pervenissemus usque ad vos, extendimus nosipsos supra modum: nam usque ad vos etiam pervenimus in Evangelio Christi.
units.tr: Verse 14. For it is not as if we had not come as far as you, that we stretch ourselves beyond due measure; for we have indeed come even as far as you in the Gospel of Christ.

units.la: Tertia dissimilitudo: Nos non gloriamur ultra regulam seu mensuram donorum, & vocationis nostræ, quasi missi essemus ad prædicandum iis quibus missi non sumus, sed continemus nos intra mensuram Apostolicæ vocationis, assignatam nobis à Deo, quæ pertingit ad prædicandum vobis Corinthiis, qui nostra opera conversi eratis ad fidem: Non sic se continent noltri æmuli, sed currunt ad eos quibus missi non sunt; & supra donorum, & benedictionis divinæ in labores suos mensuram, gloriantur.
units.tr: Third dissimilarity: We do not glory beyond the rule or measure of our gifts and calling, as if we had been sent to preach to those to whom we have not been sent; but we keep ourselves within the measure of the apostolic calling assigned to us by God, which extends to preaching to you Corinthians, who were converted to the faith through our labour. Our rivals do not keep themselves within this limit, but run to those to whom they have not been sent, and glory beyond the measure of their gifts and of the divine blessing on their labours.

units.la: Vers. 15. Non de iis quæ mensuræ nostræ non sunt, gloriantes, id est, de alienis laboribus, sed sperantes nos, augescente fide vestra, per vos admodum amplificatum iri in assignata nostra mensura.
units.tr: Verse 15. Not glorying in things beyond our measure, that is, in the labours of others; but hoping that, as your faith increases, we shall be greatly enlarged through you within our assigned measure.

units.la: Vers. 16. Ut in iis regionibus quæ ultra vos sunt evangelizem: non ut in alteri assignata mensura, de præparatis gloriemur.
units.tr: Verse 16. So that I may preach the gospel in regions beyond you, and not glory in what has been prepared within another's assigned measure.

units.la: Quarta dissimilitudo: Nos non gloriamur in alienis laboribus, quasi convertissemus ad fidem, quos non convertimus; sicut æmuli, qui gloriantur in vobis Corinthiis, quos non converterunt; sed speramus postquam vos confirmatiores in fide evaseritis, fore ut audeatis etiam propagando Euangelio nostro operam dare, & cum vicinis vestris agere, ut audiant me prædicantem: nam spero certè abundè magis ampliatum iri per vos Ministerii nostri fines, idque secundùm vocationis meæ regulam, cui Apostolatus ad Gentes committitur. Spero inquam fore, ut Euangelium prædicemus, etiam in regionibus quæ ultra vos sunt, ita ut non sit mihi futurum opus in aliena messe, per labores alienos præparata, gloriam captare, sicut Pseudapostoli jam faciunt, gloriantes in vobis, quos ego ad salutem converti: non illi.
units.tr: Fourth dissimilarity: We do not glory in the labours of others, as if we had converted those whom we have not converted, as our rivals do, who glory in you Corinthians, whom they have not converted. Rather, we hope that once you have grown stronger in the faith, you will be able to help further our Gospel by spreading it and by working with your neighbours so that they may hear me preach; for I certainly hope that the limits of our ministry will be enlarged far more through you, and that according to the rule of my calling, to which the apostleship to the Gentiles is committed. I say I hope that we shall preach the Gospel even in the regions beyond you, so that there will be no need for me to seek glory in another's harvest, prepared by the labours of others, as the false apostles now do, glorying in you whom I have converted to salvation; they do not.

units.la: Versf. 17. Ceterùm qui gloriatur, in Domino glorietur.
units.tr: Verse 17. But let him who glories glory in the Lord.

units.la: Quinta dissimilitudo per modum præcepti proposita: Ego Apostolus gloriaturus sum tantùm in Domino, non in rebus malis, non in fictis, falsisve, non in donis Dei quasi meis, non in meipso, sicut æmuli mei in seipsis gloriantur; sed prout me approbaturus est Dominus, in Deo solo.
units.tr: Fifth dissimilarity, set forth in the manner of a precept: I, the Apostle, will glory only in the Lord, not in evil things, not in fictions or falsehoods, not in the gifts of God as if they were mine, not in myself, as my rivals glory in themselves; but as the Lord shall approve me, in God alone.

units.la: Vers. 18. Non enim qui seipsum commendat, is probatus est, sed is quem Dominus commendat.
units.tr: Verse 18. For it is not he who commends himself who is approved, but he whom the Lord commends.

units.la: Hujus rationem reddit, Quia nemo probatus est, qui seipsum ex sua opinione commendat, sed qui Deo probatus est, & ab eo obtinet testimonium: Hujus regulæ examen æmuli Apostoli non poterant subire.
units.tr: He gives the reason for this: because no one is approved who commends himself by his own opinion, but he who is approved by God and obtains testimony from him. My rivals, the false apostles, could not undergo the test of this rule.

units.la: Caput Undecimum.
units.tr: Chapter Eleven.

units.la: Ontra Pseudapostolos pergit sanctè gloriari. Capitis duæ sunt partes: In prima, ad gloriationem futuram parata sibi via cum reprehensione Corinthiorum gloriationis rationes reddit: Larvam obiter detrahens Pseudapostolis, ad verf. 21. In altera gloriandi materiam adversus æmulos amplissimam aperit, ad finem.
units.tr: He goes on to boast wisely against the false apostles. The chapter has two parts. In the first, having prepared the way for the boasting to come, he gives his reasons for boasting, while rebuking the Corinthians for their own boasting, and along the way he strips off the mask from the false apostles, up to verse 21. In the second, he opens up the very ample matter for boasting against his rivals, to the end.

units.la: Vers 1. Utinam tolleraretis paulisper insipientiam meam: immò etiam tolerate me.
units.tr: Verse 1: Would that you could bear with me a little in my folly; indeed, bear with me.

units.la: Quod ad primam attinet, etiamsi statuerat non nisi sanctè & castè in Domino gloriari, quia tamen primâ facie propria laus speciem habet insipientiæ; idcirco optat & rogat, ut tanquam insipientem paulisper ipsum tolerent, per concessionem loquens (alioqui, reipsa in Apostolo jam loquebatur Spiritus sanctus) ut prudentiæ suæ rationes in hoc facto melius ipsis patefaceret; Nam quia eos à vanis quibusdam & astutis hominibus, non sine Satanæ fraude deceptos videbat, ipsorum bono ad hanc gloriationem coactus est.
units.tr: As for the first part: although he had determined to boast only in the Lord, and only in holiness and purity, yet because at first sight praise of oneself has the look of folly, he therefore wishes and asks that they would bear with him for a little while as if he were a fool. He speaks by way of concession (otherwise the Holy Spirit was in fact already speaking through the Apostle), so that he might more clearly lay open to them the reasons for his prudence in this matter. For, seeing that they had been deceived by certain empty and crafty men, not without the cunning of Satan, he was compelled, for their own good, to this boasting.

units.la: Verf. 2. Ambio enim vos Dei zelotypia. Præparavi enim vos quos uni viro (ut virginem puram) sistam nempe Christo:
units.tr: Verse 2: For I am jealous over you with a godly jealousy. For I have betrothed you to one husband, to present you as a pure virgin to Christ.

units.la: Decem autem affert rationes, quibus necessitatem gloriandi demonstrat. Ratio prima, Quia zelotypia sancta in causa Christi ad hanc gloriationem adigor. Ergo gloriatio necessaria. Hanc rationem declarat, quia ut paranymphus studebat, non sibi, sed Christo in conjugium, tanquam castam virginem, Corinthios adducere, & in ejus societate eos retinere.
units.tr: He offers ten reasons to show the necessity of boasting. The first reason: because I am driven to this boasting by a holy jealousy for the cause of Christ, therefore boasting is necessary. He explains this reason: as a go-between, he was eager to bring the Corinthians, as a chaste virgin, to Christ in marriage, not to himself, and to keep them in fellowship with him.

units.la: Verf. 3. Sed metuo ne quo modo sicut serpens ille Evam seduxit calliditate sua, ita corrupta mentes vestræ degenerent à simplicitate quæ est in Christo.
units.tr: Verse 3: But I fear lest somehow, as the serpent deceived Eve by his cunning, so your minds should be corrupted and fall away from the simplicity that is in Christ.

units.la: Ratio 2. Metuo, ne sicut Eva per calliditatem Diaboli seducta fuit, sic vos à virginali simplicitate Euangelii Christi, per Pseudapostolos corrupti, dimoveamini, pro sapientia Dei amplectentes sapientiam humanam, & fermentum Legalium Ceremoniarum admittentes, ad corrumpendam doctrinam gratiæ Euangelii inter vos. Necessaria ergo hæc gloriatio mea.
units.tr: Reason 2: I fear that, just as Eve was seduced by the cunning of the Devil, so you may be turned away from the virginal simplicity of the gospel of Christ, corrupted by the false apostles, embracing human wisdom in place of the wisdom of God, and admitting the leaven of legal ceremonies, so as to corrupt among you the doctrine of the grace of the gospel. Therefore this boasting of mine is necessary.

units.la: Verf. 4. Enimverò si veniat qui alium Iesum prædicet quem non prædicavimus, aut si Spiritum alium acciplatis quem non accepistis, aut Euangelium aliud quod non accepistis, recte eum toleraveritis.
units.tr: Verse 4: For if someone comes preaching another Jesus whom we have not preached, or if you receive another spirit which you have not received, or another gospel which you have not accepted, you would rightly bear with him.

units.la: Ratio 3. Meritò sufferretis gloriantem Thrasonicum aliquem prædicatorem, si posset ille impertiri vobis alium Christum, quod impossibile est, aut excellentiora Spiritus dona, aut aliud præstantius Euangelium, quam vos nostro Ministerio accepistis, & admisistis. Verùm cum istud impossibile sit, merito debetis ferre me Apostolum gloriantem, per cujus prædicationem, facti eltis participes & Christi, & donorum Spiritus ipsius.
units.tr: Reason 3: You would rightly put up with some boastful preacher, if he could bestow on you another Christ (which is impossible), or more excellent gifts of the Spirit, or another gospel more outstanding than the one you received and accepted through our ministry. But since this is impossible, you ought rightly to bear with me, the Apostle, boasting, through whose preaching you have been made partakers both of Christ and of the gifts of his Spirit.

units.la: Verf. 5. Puto enim me nihilo inferiorem fuisse summis Apostolis.
units.tr: Verse 5: For I consider that I am in no way inferior to the chief apostles.

units.la: Ratio 4. Confirmans priorem; Non esse inferiorem me Petro, Iacobo, & Ioanne (Apostolis illis qui maximi æstimantur) puto ipsos iniicias non ituros: quia communicato cum illis Euangelio, Galat. 2. nihil illi mihi contulerunt. Ergo necessaria est, & justa gloriatio mea adversus Pseudapostolos.
units.tr: Reason 4, confirming the earlier one: I think that I am not inferior to Peter, James and John (those apostles who are esteemed the greatest). They will not contradict me, since, although I shared the gospel with them, as in Galatians 2, they added nothing to me. Therefore my boasting against the false apostles is both necessary and just.

units.la: Vers. 6. Quod si rudis sum sermone, non tamen sum rudis cognitione: sed omnino manifesti sumus in omnibus apud vos.
units.tr: Verse 6: But even if I am rude in speech, yet I am not rude in knowledge; but we have been thoroughly made manifest among you in all things.

units.la: Ratio 5. Quia licet de ornato sermone, seu eloquentia cum aemulis contendere nollem, in cognitione tamen mysteriorum salutis, nulli cessurus sum, cujus rei testes appellat ipsos Corinthios, qui probè noverant ipsius scientiam.
units.tr: Reason 5: Although I would not contend with my rivals about ornate speech or eloquence, in knowledge of the mysteries of salvation I will yield to no one. He calls the Corinthians themselves as witnesses of this, since they had well known his knowledge.

units.la: Vers. 7. Num peccavi quum meipsum demitterem ut vos attolleremini, quod jue gratuitò Euangelium Dei evangelizavcrim vobis?
units.tr: Verse 7: Did I sin in humbling myself so that you might be exalted, because I preached the gospel of God to you free of charge?

units.la: Ratio 6 In qua occurrit objectioni: Diceret aliquis, at dum Corinthi praesens esses ex labore manuario vivebas. Resp. Mea humiliatio, tantum abest ut vitio vertenda sit mihi, ut potius laude digna sit, quia in commodum vestrum cedebat, quorum ego salutem tanti faciebam, ut commodis meis posthabitis, gratuitò vobis Euangelium praedicaverim. Ergo vel hoc nomine mihi licet gloriari.
units.tr: Reason 6, in which he meets an objection. Someone might say: but while you were present at Corinth you lived by manual labour. Answer: my humbling of myself is so far from being a fault to be laid against me that it is rather worthy of praise, since it turned to your advantage, and I valued your salvation so highly that, setting aside my own advantages, I preached the gospel to you free of charge. Therefore, on this ground at least, I am permitted to boast.

units.la: Vers. 8. Alias Ecclesias spoliavi, accepto ab eis stipendio, ut vobis inservirem: & quum apud vos essem & egerem, non obtorpui cum cujusquam incommodo.
units.tr: Verse 8: I robbed other churches, taking wages from them, so as to serve you; and when I was with you and was in need, I did not become a burden to anyone.

units.la: Vers. 9. Inopiam enim meam supplerunt fratres qui venerant à Macedonia: & in omnibus me praestiti vobis minimè onerosum, & praestabo.
units.tr: Verse 9: For the brothers who came from Macedonia supplied my want; and in all things I have kept myself, and will keep myself, from being burdensome to you.

units.la: Factum suum clarius explicat metaphorâ lepidâ, ostendens se ab aliis Ecclesiis pauperioribus, per Euangelium triumphatis, quasi spolia reportasse stipendium ad se alendum, ut gratis Corinthiis posset melius inservire, vers. 8. Nominatim à Macedonibus Philippensibus, ne Corinthiis esset onerosus.
units.tr: He explains his action more clearly with a witty metaphor, showing that he had carried off from the other, poorer churches, won over by the gospel, the wages by which he might support himself, so that he could serve the Corinthians more freely, verse 8. He names in particular the Philippians in Macedonia, so that he would not be a burden to the Corinthians.

units.la: Vers. 10. Est veritas Christi in me quod haec gloriatio non obstruetur contra me in regionibus Achaiae.
units.tr: Verse 10: As the truth of Christ is in me, this boasting of mine will not be stopped against me in the regions of Achaia.

units.la: Vers. 11. Quapropter? an quod non diligam vos? Deus novit.
units.tr: Verse 11: Why? Is it because I do not love you? God knows.

units.la: Vers. 12. Sed quod facio, etiam faciam, ut amputem occasionem iis qui optant occasionem ut in eo de quo gloriantur reperiantur quales & nos.
units.tr: Verse 12: But what I do, I will also continue to do, so that I may cut off the opportunity from those who desire an opportunity to be found equal to us in the things they boast of.

units.la: Ne facti sui poenitere ipsum videatur, statuit posthac onerosum se non futurum illis, seu stipendium non accepturum, quod confirmat juramento, verf. 10. & ne ægre ferrent quasi ex defectu dilectionis, nollet stipendium ab ipsis recipere, profitetur ex speciali dilectione erga eos, se id statuisse, Deum testatus de sermonis sui veritate, verf. 11. idque in hunc finem, ne in hac gloriatione superiores esse viderentur Pseudapostoli, quibus calumniandi ansam voluit sic auferri, qui alioqui dixissent Paulum rei familiaris augendæ causa, Corinthiis prædicasse.
units.tr: So that he should not seem to repent of what he had done, he resolves that from now on he will not be a burden to them, that is, he will not accept wages from them, and he confirms this with an oath, verse 10. And lest they should bear it badly, as if it came from a lack of love, he declares that he had resolved this out of a special love towards them, calling God to witness to the truth of his words, verse 11. He did this with this end in view: that the false apostles should not seem superior to him in this boasting. He wished to take from them the occasion for slander, since otherwise they would have said that Paul preached to the Corinthians for the sake of increasing his wealth.

units.la: Verf. 13. Nam istiusmodi pseudoapostoli, operarii dolosi sunt, transformati in Apostolos Christi.
units.tr: Verse 13: For such men are false apostles, deceitful workers, disguising themselves as apostles of Christ.

units.la: Verf. 14. Neque id mirum: ipse enim Satanas transformatur in angelum lucis.
units.tr: Verse 14: And no wonder, for Satan himself disguises himself as an angel of light.

units.la: Verf. 15. Non magnum est igitur si transformentur ut ministri justitiæ, etiam ejus ministri quorum finis erit secundum opera eorum.
units.tr: Verse 15: It is therefore no great thing if his ministers also disguise themselves as ministers of righteousness, whose end will be according to their works.

units.la: Ratio 7. Gloriationis necessitatem ostendens, Quia æmulorum ipsus nequitia ad hanc gloriationem impellebat, Illi enim mentiebantur se Apostolos Christi, & operarios esse in Dei vinea, cum interea non Dei, sed sua negotia solum curarent; Prædicabant enim Euangelium emolumenti & honoris sui gratia: mentiebantur se Christi Ministros, cum essent tantum personati histriones, verf. 13. neque hoc mirandum, cum essent hi nebulones Apostoli Satanæ, imitantes Diabolum (qui speciem aliquando induit Cœlestis alicujus angeli, ut sub prætextu zeli & pietatis, hominibus imponat) cujus mores sequebantur æmuli ipsius, præ se ferentes studium gloriæ Christi: cum interim ventri, crumenæ, & honori suo, omne studium suum sacrificarent, susque deque habentes quid de Apostolis, quid de Ecclesiis fieret, modo ipsi votis suis potirentur: quibus propterea minatur Apostolus mortem æternam, secundum ipsorum merita.
units.tr: Reason 7, showing the necessity of boasting: because the wickedness of my rivals itself drove me to this boasting. For they lied that they were apostles of Christ and workers in God's vineyard, while in the meantime they cared not for God's business but only for their own. For they preached the gospel for the sake of gain and honour. They lied that they were ministers of Christ, when they were merely masked actors, verse 13. Nor is this to be wondered at, since these rogues were apostles of Satan, imitating the Devil (who sometimes puts on the appearance of some heavenly angel, so as to deceive men under the pretext of zeal and piety), whose ways his imitators followed, putting forward a zeal for the glory of Christ, while all the while they devoted every effort to their belly, their purse and their own honour, caring not a whit what became of the Apostles or the churches, so long as they might obtain their desires. For these men the Apostle threatens eternal death, according to their deserts.

units.la: Verf. 16. Rursum dico, ne quis me putet insipientem esse: alioquin etiam ut insipientem accipite me, ut paululum quiddam & ego glorier.
units.tr: Verse 16: Again I say, let no one think me foolish; but if you do, receive me even as a fool, so that I may boast a little myself.

units.la: Verf. 17. Quod dico, non dico secundum Dominum, sed ut insipienter, in præsidente ista gloriatione.
units.tr: Verse 17: What I say, I do not say according to the Lord, but as it were in foolishness, in this confident boasting.

units.la: Ratio 8. Quia sapienter factum comperturi erant, quod sic glorietur in hac tanta necessitate: quod ut advertant, rogat; si vero ipsius in gloriando necessitatem justam, & prudentiam, in præsentiarum, minus possent perspicere, rogat saltem ut patienter ferant aliquantisper, quasi insipienter gloriantem, usque dum orationem & apologiam absolveret, verf. 16. concedens tantum, non vero affirmans, se gloriari insipienter, seu non ut Deo dignum erat: alioqui enim Apostolus summa cum Spiritus sapientia, ad Dei gloriam, & salutem Ecclesiæ justissimè in hoc negotio toto gloriabatur.
units.tr: Reason 8: Because they would find out that it was wise to boast in this way in such great necessity. He asks them to notice this; but if they could not yet see clearly the necessity and prudence of his boasting, he asks at least that they bear patiently with him for a while, as with a man boasting foolishly, until he finishes his speech and defence. In verse 16 he concedes only this, and does not affirm that he boasts foolishly or in a way unworthy of God. Indeed, the Apostle, with the highest wisdom of the Spirit, boasted most justly in this whole matter, for the glory of God and the salvation of the Church.

units.la: Verf. 18. Quandoquidem multi gloriantur secundum carnem: & ego gloriabor.
units.tr: Ver. 18. Since many glory according to the flesh, I too will glory.

units.la: Ratio 9. Quia falsò gloriabantur adversus eùm Pseudapostoli, ideo æquum esse contendit ut ipse glorietur verè in defensione sui.
units.tr: Reason 9. Because the false apostles gloried falsely against him, he argues that it is only right that he should glory truly in defending himself.

units.la: Verf. 19 Libenter enim toleratis insipientes, quum sitû sapientes.
units.tr: Ver. 19. For you gladly tolerate fools, since you yourselves are wise.

units.la: Ratio 10. Sapientes tolerare solent eos qui stolidiores videntur, ut experientia novistis: Quid ni ergo me necessario gloriantem etiamsi quibuldam ex vobis insipiens hic videar, sufferatis?
units.tr: Reason 10. Wise people are accustomed to tolerate those who seem more foolish, as you know from experience. Why then should you not bear with me, who of necessity glory, even though to some of you I may seem foolish here?

units.la: Verf. 20. Toleratis enim siquis vos in servitutem adigat, siquis exedit, siquis accipit, siquis attollit sese, siquis vos in faciem cadit.
units.tr: Ver. 20. For you tolerate it if anyone brings you into bondage, if anyone devours you, if anyone takes from you, if anyone exalts himself, if anyone strikes you on the face.

units.la: Ratio 11. Quia toleratis multo duriora quam stultitiam hanc (ut videri potest) gloriationis meæ: nam primo importunos homines qui redigunt vos in servitutem toleratis: tales erant Pseudapostoli qui dominationem in ipsos exercebant, Ecclesiam Corinthiorum in factiones dividebant, & seipsos duces & dominos suorum, inter Corinthios, sequacium, tanquam militum & servorum, statuebant: 2. Toleratis eos qui devorant vos: tales erant Pseudapostoli lauta convivia affectantes & exedentes Corinthiorum rem familiarem: 3. Toleratis spoliatores, quales etiam erant Pseudapostoli, qui stipendia certè nolebant habere, interim muneribus inhiabant, eaque à Corinthiis captabant & emulgebant: 4. Toleratis vestri contemptores; quales erant Pseudapostoli qui propter genus, & nationem Hebræam, & dona aliqua Spiritus sibi data supra Ecclesiam Corinthiorum, ex Gentibus illiteratis & ignobilibus collectam, in immensum se efferebant: 5. Toleratis cædentes vos in faciem, seu qui contumeliosè vos tractant. Quid ni igitur meam hanc justam toleretis gloriationem.
units.tr: Reason 11. Because you tolerate things much harsher than this folly (as it may appear) of my boasting. For first, you tolerate troublesome men who reduce you to bondage: such were the false apostles, who exercised lordship over them, divided the Church of the Corinthians into factions, and set themselves up as leaders and masters of their followers among the Corinthians, as of soldiers and slaves. 2. You tolerate those who devour you: such were the false apostles, who aimed at sumptuous banquets and devoured the household goods of the Corinthians. 3. You tolerate plunderers, such as the false apostles also were, who certainly did not wish to have a salary, yet greedily coveted gifts and sought them from the Corinthians and drained them. 4. You tolerate your despisers: such were the false apostles, who, on account of their race and Hebrew nation, and some gifts of the Spirit given to them above the Church of the Corinthians, which was gathered from unlettered and ignoble Gentiles, puffed themselves up immeasurably. 5. You tolerate those who strike you on the face, that is, who treat you with insult. Why then should you not tolerate this my just boasting?

units.la: Verf. 21. Quantum ad contumeliam dico, nempe quia nos infirmi fuimus: imò in quocunque audacia uti velit aliquis (insipienter loquor) audacia velim uti & ego: Exponit in os cædere, intelligendum esse, non de externa violentia, sed contumeliæ respectu, cujusmodi nonnihil ipse cum Corinthiis à falsis illis doctoribus expertus erat; cum Pseudapostoli Corinthus exprobrabant in os animi abjectionem, quod Paulo opificium manuale exercenti, se subjecerint: quid enim aliud erat hoc, quam Corinthios in os cædere, & sancto Apostolo insultare.
units.tr: Ver. 21. I speak concerning dishonour, namely that we have been weak. But in whatever respect anyone is bold (I speak foolishly), I too will be bold. The phrase "to strike on the face" is to be understood not of external violence but with respect to insult, of which kind Paul himself had had some experience with the Corinthians from those false teachers; for the false apostles reproached him to his face in Corinth for the abjectness of spirit by which he had subjected himself to the manual craft, for what else was this than striking the Corinthians on the face and insulting the holy Apostle?

units.la: Secunda Pars.
units.tr: Second Part.

units.la: Secunda pars Capitis, in qua via jam sibi parata ad gloriationem juštam, & gloriationis necessitate demonstratâ, comparat se cum gloriosulis illis doctoribus, ex indiciis dignitatis suæ quatuor, probans se illis non inferiorem, sed multis nominibus præferendum esse.
units.tr: The second part of the chapter, in which, the way now being prepared for a just boasting and the necessity of boasting having been demonstrated, he compares himself with those boastful teachers, by four marks of his dignity, proving that he is not inferior to them but in many respects to be preferred.

units.la: Primum indicium dignitatis in genere propositum: Quod in nulla fuerit illis inferior, quocunque se verterent in gloriatione sua: interim modestè concedit speciem stultitiæ in hac gloriatione, quam tamen sapienter prosequitur.
units.tr: The first mark of dignity is proposed in general: that he was in no respect inferior to them, whichever way they turned in their boasting; meanwhile he modestly concedes the appearance of folly in this boasting, which nevertheless he pursues wisely.

units.la: Verf. 22. Hebræi sunt? sum & ego? Israelitæ sunt? sum & ego? semen Abrahæ sunt? sum & ego?
units.tr: Ver. 22. Are they Hebrews? So am I. Are they Israelites? So am I. Are they the seed of Abraham? So am I.

units.la: Secundum indicium dignitatis speciale est, quod generis nobilitate æquiparabilis sit illis: nam si à Gente sancta gloriam quærerent, Ille ex ea familia quæ non se comiscuerat, cum Gentibus oriundus erat: ex parentibus Hebræis Hebræus erat; si prosapiæ nobilitate gloriari vellent, ille ex nobilioribus Israelitis oriundus erat, quia ex Tribu Benjamin erat oriundus: fuit autem Benjamin filius Rachel fœminæ liberæ: aliquæ autem tribus ex ancillis originem habebant: Si religionis antiquitate certarent, quod in fœdere manserint ut Abrahamidæ veri, hic etiam par cuivis erat.
units.tr: The second special mark of dignity is that he was equal to them in nobility of birth: for if they sought glory from the holy nation, he was descended from that family which had not mingled itself with the Gentiles; he was a Hebrew born of Hebrew parents. If they wished to glory in the nobility of lineage, he was descended from the more noble Israelites, since he was of the tribe of Benjamin; and Benjamin was the son of Rachel, a free woman, whereas some tribes derived their origin from handmaids. If they contended in the antiquity of religion, that they had remained in the covenant as true children of Abraham, he too was equal to anyone in this.

units.la: Verf. 23. Ministri Christi sunt? (ut desipiens loquor) supero ego? in fatigationibus amplius, in vulneribus supra illos, in carceribus, amplius, in mortibus, sæpe.
units.tr: Ver. 23. Are they ministers of Christ? (I speak as one beside himself) I am more so: in labours more abundantly, in stripes above measure, in prisons more frequently, in deaths often.

units.la: Indicium 3. Si muneris dignitate certarent, hic modestè ut coactus se illis præfert respectu Apostolatus, & officii extra ordinem ipsi concessi, major sum, inquit, quia Apostolus sum.
units.tr: Mark 3. If they contended in the dignity of office, he modestly sets himself above them, as one compelled, with respect to the Apostleship and the office conferred on him outside the ordinary order: I am greater, he says, because I am an Apostle.

units.la: Indicium 4. Dignitatis, est Sinceritas in officio suo administrando. ministrando: hujus sinceritatis Testimonia affert Novem: In primo profert, labores seu diligentiam. In secundo Passiones in genere, quæ valetudinem & libertatem corporis spectabant, & capitis pericula.
units.tr: Mark 4. Of dignity is sincerity in administering one's office. He brings forward nine testimonies of this sincerity. In the first he sets forth his labours or diligence. In the second, his sufferings in general, which concerned bodily health and freedom, and dangers to life.

units.la: Verf. 24. A Judæis quinquies accepi quadragenas plagas, unâ minus.
units.tr: Ver. 24. Five times I received from the Jews forty stripes less one.

units.la: Tertium Testimonium affert passiones speciales à Judæis, Quod plagis cæsus sit à Judæis quinquies, ad numerum plagarum secundum legem maleficis infligendarum, nam Judæi licet crudeles, intra legem tamen, Deut 25.3. se continuisse videri volebant.
units.tr: The third testimony he brings is his special sufferings at the hands of the Jews: that he was scourged five times by the Jews, up to the number of stripes which by law were inflicted on malefactors; for the Jews, although cruel, wished to appear to have kept within the law, Deut. 25.3.

units.la: Verf. 25. Ter virgis cæsus fui, semel fui lapidatus, ter naufragium feci, noctem ac diem in profundo egi:
units.tr: Ver. 25. Three times I was beaten with rods, once I was stoned, three times I suffered shipwreck, a night and a day I spent in the deep.

units.la: Quartum Testimonium perhibent ipsius passiones à Gentibus, quod à lictoribus Gentium, fustibus seu virgis ter sit cæsus, & semel lapidatus; 5. Quod naufragium ter fecerit, in quorum uno postquam viginti quatuor horas in mari profundo undis agitatus esset, potenti Dei manu liberatus est.
units.tr: The fourth testimony is given by his sufferings at the hands of the Gentiles: that he was three times beaten with rods or clubs by the lictors of the Gentiles, and once stoned; and fifth, that he suffered shipwreck three times, in one of which, after he had been tossed by the waves in the deep sea for twenty-four hours, he was freed by the mighty hand of God.

units.la: Verf. 26. In itineribus sæpe fui, in periculis fluminum, periculis latronum, periculis à meis gentilibus, periculis in Gentibus, periculis in civitate, periculis in deserto, periculis in mari, periculis inter falsos fratres;
units.tr: Ver. 26. In journeys often, in perils of rivers, perils of robbers, perils from my own countrymen, perils from the Gentiles, perils in the city, perils in the wilderness, perils at sea, perils among false brethren;

units.la: Sextum sinceritatis Testimonium continet itinerum labores, & octo genera periculorum; Quæ variis in locis, & à diversis hominum generibus ipsum exceperunt.
units.tr: The sixth testimony of sincerity contains the labours of journeys and eight kinds of dangers, which in various places and from various kinds of men befell him.

units.la: Verf. 27. In fatigatione & ærumna, in vigiliis sæpe, in fame & siti, in jejuniis sæpe, in frigore & nuditate:
units.tr: Ver. 27. In toil and hardship, in watchings often, in hunger and thirst, in fastings often, in cold and nakedness.
