units.la: Septimum, habet quinque molestiarum genera, quibus dum Ministerii opus persequebatur, exercitus est sæpius, in quibus delassatus, pro quiete coactus est novos labores capessere.
units.tr: The seventh has five kinds of troubles, with which, while he pursued the work of the ministry, he was exercised more than once; in these, being worn out, he was compelled to undertake new labours for rest.

units.la: Verf. 28. Absque iis quæ extrinsecus eveniunt, urget agmen illud in me quotidie consurgens, id est, solicitudo de omnibus Ecclesiis.
units.tr: Ver. 28. Apart from those things which happen from without, there presses upon me daily that crowd, that is, anxiety for all the Churches.

units.la: Octavum Testimonium, Invicta patientia in quotidianis negotiis publicis, cum solicitudine animi de omnibus Christi Ecclesiis.
units.tr: The eighth testimony: unconquered patience in daily public business, together with anxiety of mind for all the Churches of Christ.

units.la: Verf. 29 Quis affligitur, quin ego affligar? quis offenditur, quin ego uror? Nonum Testimonium sinceritatis, est sympathia cum omnibus afflictis, & scandalo aliquo offensis.
units.tr: Ver. 29. Who is afflicted, and I am not afflicted? Who is offended, and I do not burn? The ninth testimony of sincerity is sympathy with all the afflicted and those offended by any scandal.

units.la: Verf. 30. Si gloriari oporteat, de iis quæ infirmitatis meæ sunt gloriabor.
units.tr: Ver. 30. If it behoves me to glory, I will glory in the things of my infirmity.

units.la: Retorquet objectionem adversariorum: At omnia hæc contemptibilem reddiderunt te, & miserum hominem. Respondet quod dedita opera statuerit tamen in his gloriari, ut quæ sinceritatem ipsius magis commendarent, quam Pseudapostolorum res prosperæ ipsos ornarent.
units.tr: He turns back the objection of his adversaries: "But all these things have made you contemptible and a wretched man." He answers that he deliberately resolved nevertheless to glory in these things, since they commended his sincerity more than the prosperous circumstances adorned the false apostles.

units.la: Verf. 32. Deus & Pater Domini nostri Iesu Christi, laudandus in secula, novit me non mentiri.
units.tr: Ver. 31. The God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, blessed for ever, knows that I do not lie.

units.la: Verf. 32 In urbe Damasci, gentis præfectus nomine Aretæ regis, præsidio tenebat Damascenorum urbem, cupiens me prehendere.
units.tr: Ver. 32. In the city of Damascus, the governor under King Aretas guarded the city of the Damascenes, wishing to seize me.

units.la: Verf. 33. Sed per fenestram in sporta demissus fui per mœnia, & ejus manus effugi.
units.tr: Ver. 33. But I was let down through a window in a basket, through the wall, and escaped his hands.

units.la: Denique, quia incredibilia videri poterant quæ commemoravit, quod scilicet sustinendis tot malis unus par esse potuerit, præmisso juramento de veritate tam dictorum quam dicendorum, commemorat speciale periculum Capitis, ex quo nullus patebat exitus, nisi Deus ipsum incolumem servare in bonum Ecclesiæ voluisset, & viam ad evadendum speciali providentia sua aperuisset, de quo vide Act. 9. 23.
units.tr: Finally, because the things he recounted might seem incredible, namely that one man could be equal to bearing so many evils, after premising an oath about the truth of both what had been said and what was to be said, he recalls a special danger to his life, from which there was no visible exit unless God had willed to preserve him unharmed for the good of the Church and had opened a way of escape by his special providence; concerning which see Acts 9.23.

units.la: Caput Duodecimum.
units.tr: Chapter 12.

units.la: DErgit in sancta Gloriatione: Capitis tres sunt partes, in prima Cœlestem visionem sibi oblatam, una cum ejusdem eventu explicat, ad verf. 11. In secunda probat Corinthios debuisse hac gloriationis necessitate ipsum liberasse, seu ipsum defendisse, ad verf. 19. In tertia, causas solicitudinis suæ affert.
units.tr: He proceeds to the holy boasting. The chapter has three parts. In the first he explains the heavenly vision shown to him, together with its outcome, up to verse 11. In the second he proves that the Corinthians ought to have freed him from this necessity of boasting, or rather defended him, up to verse 19. In the third he sets out the causes of his anxiety.

units.la: Verf. 1. GLoriari sane non expedit mihi: veniam enim ad visiones, & revelationes Domini.
units.tr: Vers. 1. Indeed it is not expedient for me to glory; for I will come to visions and revelations of the Lord.

units.la: Præmissa præfatione, quod non sua causa glorietur, quia nimirum illud non expediebat ipsi, (mihi enim hic emphaticum est) sed Corinthiis & Ecclesiæ ; quorum intereat Apostoli autoritatem sartam tectam conservari accedit ad revelationes extraordinarias , quarum unam incipit historicè narrare.
units.tr: After a preface saying that he does not boast for his own sake, since it was not expedient for him (for for me is emphatic here), but for the sake of the Corinthians and the Church, whose interest it was that the authority of the Apostle be kept intact and safe, he comes to his extraordinary revelations, one of which he begins to relate as history.

units.la: Vers. 2. Novi hominem in Christo ante annos quatuordecim, (an in corpore nescio: an extra corpus nescio ; Deus novit) raptum in tertium usque cælum.
units.tr: Vers. 2. I know a man in Christ fourteen years ago (whether in the body I know not, or out of the body I know not; God knows), caught up to the third heaven.

units.la: Hujus revelationis præstantiam, suamque in certando modestiam novem argumentis insinuat.
units.tr: He conveys the excellence of this revelation, and his own modesty in boasting of it, by nine arguments.

units.la: Argumentum primum , Quod vix audeat nomen suum edere in hoc negotio, sed ne nimium sibi arrogare videatur, in tertia persona de seipso loqui cogatur.
units.tr: First argument: he hardly dares to put his own name to this business, but, lest he seem to claim too much for himself, he is compelled to speak of himself in the third person.

units.la: Arg. 2. Quod etiamsi videatur hæc revelatio supra communem hominum sortem ipsum extollere, non aliam affectet tamen excellentiam , quam in Christo, seu in fidelium numero esse, qui sibi ipsis renunciarunt, ut in uno Christo glorientur.
units.tr: Second argument: although this revelation seems to raise him above the common lot of men, he nonetheless aims at no other excellence than being in Christ, that is, being among the number of the faithful, who have renounced themselves so that they may glory in Christ alone.

units.la: Arg. 3. Quod tacitus apud se suppresserit hujus gloriosæ revelationis mentionem jam totos 14. annos; numquam eam prolaturus, nisi coactus fuisset æmulorum importunitate , qui ipsius autoritati Apostolicæ, in Euangelii & Ecclesiarum detrimentum detrahere operam dabant
units.tr: Third argument: he had kept silent in his own mind about the mention of this glorious revelation for now fourteen years, never intending to bring it forward unless he were compelled by the importunity of his rivals, who were working to detract from his apostolic authority, to the detriment of the Gospel and the Churches.

units.la: Arg. 4. Quod raptus fuerit in Cælum supremum , supra omnia sidera , in locum beatorum Spirituum, ubi Deus suam gloriam maximè manifestat.
units.tr: Fourth argument: he was caught up into the highest heaven, above all the stars, into the place of the blessed spirits, where God especially manifests his glory.

units.la: Arg. 5. Quod nesciat an raptus sit locali corporis translatione in Cælum, an anima extra ordinem ad tempus separata, & in Cælum sublata, fuerit : de altero tamen certus.
units.tr: Fifth argument: he does not know whether he was caught up by a bodily translation into heaven, or whether his soul, separated out of the ordinary course for a time, was taken up into heaven. Of the latter, however, he is certain.

units.la: Vers. 3. Et novi hujusmodi hominem (an in corpore, an extra corpus, nescio: Deus novit) Vers. 4. Raptum fuisse in Paradisum , & audisse ineffabilia verba, quæ non liceat homini loqui.
units.tr: Vers. 3. And I know such a man (whether in the body or out of the body, I know not: God knows) Vers. 4. that he was caught up into Paradise, and heard unspeakable words, which it is not lawful for a man to utter.

units.la: Arg 6. Quod certum sciat rem gestam, & se raptum in paradisum , seu in beatam illam sedem gloriæ Dei , (propterea secundo repetit, novi hominem) & audiisse ibi ineffabilia verba, quæ non licebat homini loqui, id est, quorum alia explicari non poterant ; alia vero fas non erat ipsi exprimere, quæ alioqui nisi prohibitio impedivisset explicari plicari potuissent: siquidem quæ revelabantur, privatam ejus confirmationem & præparationem ad certamina quæ subiturus erat, spectasse certum est.
units.tr: Sixth argument: he knows for certain the event itself, and that he was caught up into paradise, that is, into that blessed seat of God's glory (for this reason he repeats a second time, I know a man), and that there he heard unspeakable words, which it was not lawful for a man to utter. That is, some of them could not be explained, and others it was not right for him to express, though otherwise they could have been explained had a prohibition not stood in the way. For it is certain that what was revealed bore on his private confirmation and preparation for the struggles he was about to undergo.

units.la: Vers. 5. De ejusmodi re gloriabor: de meipso verò non gloriabor, nisi de infirmitatibus meis.
units.tr: Vers. 5. Of such a one will I glory; but of myself I will not glory, except in my infirmities.

units.la: Arg. 7. Quod de hujusmodi homine, id est, de se, ut de servo Dei exaltato hunc in modum, in gloriam Dei gloriaturus quidem sit: non autem de seipso in se spectato, propterea quod in se nihil haberet in quo gloriaretur præter infirmitates suas.
units.tr: Seventh argument: concerning a man of this kind, that is, concerning himself as a servant of God so exalted, he will indeed glory, to the glory of God; but not concerning himself considered in himself, because in himself he has nothing to glory in except his infirmities.

units.la: Vers. 6. Nam si voluero de iis gloriari, non ero insipiens: veritatem enim dicam, sed parcè loquor, ne quis de me cogitet supra id quod videt esse in me, aut quod audit ex me.
units.tr: Vers. 6. For if I should wish to glory in these things, I would not be foolish; for I would be speaking the truth. But I refrain, lest anyone think of me beyond what he sees in me, or hears from me.

units.la: Arg. 8. Quod etiamsi gloriandi materia satis ampla ex hac revelatione oblata sit, ut verè & solidè sine vanitate, multò amplius gloriari posset, statuerit tamen parcè admodum hac de re loqui, ne nimiam sui æstimationem excitaret.
units.tr: Eighth argument: although matter for boasting, ample enough, has been offered by this revelation, so that he could truly and soundly glory, without vanity, far more than this, he has nevertheless decided to speak very sparingly on this subject, lest he stir up an excessive estimation of himself.

units.la: Vers. 7. Et ne excellentia revelationum supra modum efferrer, datus est mihi surculus infixus carni, & angelus Satanæ, ut me colaphis cædat, ne supra modum efferrer.
units.tr: Vers. 7. And lest the excellence of the revelations should exalt me beyond measure, there was given me a thorn fixed in the flesh, a messenger of Satan to buffet me, lest I be exalted beyond measure.

units.la: Arg. 9. Quod revelationis excellentia tanta fuerit, ut ad præcavendam superbiam, missus sit Angelus Satanæ, ad Apostoli humiliationem.
units.tr: Ninth argument: the excellence of the revelation was so great that, to guard against pride, a messenger of Satan was sent to humble the Apostle.

units.la: Describit autem humiliandi sui rationem ita, ut humiliationis rationes insinuet tres.
units.tr: He describes the manner of his humbling in such a way that he sets out three reasons for the humiliation.

units.la: Ratio prima, Quod materia humiliationis, fuerit reliquiarum peccati aliquid in carne sua, seu natura corrupta nondum penitus abolita, hærens; motio scilicet concupiscentiæ aliqua, ad porrò peccandum tendens, quam motionem comparat surculo in cædua silva reliquo, quia non minorem molestiam sancto Dei servo exhibebat, quam surculus infixus pedi viatoris creare solet.
units.tr: First reason: the matter of the humiliation was some remnant of sin in his flesh, or a corrupt nature not yet wholly abolished, clinging to him; namely, a certain stirring of concupiscence tending to further sinning. He compares this stirring to a shoot left in a coppice wood, because it caused the holy servant of God no less trouble than a splinter fixed in the foot usually causes a traveller.

units.la: Ratio humiliationis 2. Quod hæc motio, adjunctam habuerit speciale m tentationem, ad aperiendum aditum, diabolo & locum dandum peccato.
units.tr: Second reason for the humiliation: this stirring had attached to it a special temptation, which opened a way for the devil and gave room to sin.

units.la: Ratio 3. Quod hæc tentatio emissa à diabolo adeò violenter ad peccandum ipsum solicitaverit, ut coactus sit opem divinam implorare, ne tentationi succumberet: quod exercitium ut non mirandum est, legenti Cap. 7. ad Rom. sic agnoscendum ex eodem illo Cap. medium fuisse ad humilitationem Apostoli efficacissimum: qui enim magno animo omnes molestias & pugnas cum hostibus corporeis & spiritualibus fere solebat, in sola luêta cum carne sua ejulare auditur, & exclamare, Me miserum, quis me eripiet, &c.
units.tr: Third reason: this temptation, sent by the devil, pressed him so violently to sin that he was compelled to implore divine help, lest he succumb to the temptation. This struggle is not surprising to anyone who reads chapter 7 of Romans, where, as is clear from that same chapter, the means were most effective for the Apostle's humility. For he who used to face all troubles and battles with bodily and spiritual enemies with a great spirit is heard only wailing and crying out in his struggle with his own flesh, Wretched man that I am, who will deliver me, etc.

units.la: Versus 8. Super hoc ter Dominum rogavi, ut abscederet a me.
units.tr: Verse 8. Concerning this I besought the Lord three times that it might depart from me.

units.la: Sequitur ipsa humiliatio Apostoli, cujus indicia affert quatuor: Indicium primum, Quod saepius Deum precibus solicitaverit ad se liberandum a tentatore.
units.tr: There follows the Apostle's own humbling, of which he gives four indications. First indication: that he often pressed God with prayers to free him from the tempter.

units.la: Vers. 9. Et dixit mihi, Sufficit tibi gratia mea: nam potentia mea per infirmitatem perficitur. Libentissime igitur gloriabor potius de infirmitatibus meis, ut inhabitet in me potentia CHRISTI.
units.tr: Vers. 9. And he said to me, My grace is sufficient for you: for my power is made perfect in weakness. Therefore I will most gladly glory rather in my infirmities, that the power of Christ may dwell in me.

units.la: Indicium 2. Quod acquieverit in Dei responsione, qua docebat ipsum partim de sufficientia gratiae suae, ad sustinendum luctantem servum suum, ne a tentatore superaretur, & abluendam omnem pollutionem quam in luêta contraheret: Partim de fine Consilii sui in servorum suorum exercitatione, qui est ut quanto infirmior servus aliquis Dei, in luêta aliqua comperitur, tanto Dei virtus in eo sustinendo, clarius & perfectius se demonstraret.
units.tr: Second indication: he acquiesced in God's answer, by which God taught him partly about the sufficiency of his grace, to sustain his struggling servant so that he would not be overcome by the tempter, and to wash away every pollution he might contract in the struggle; and partly about the end of his counsel in the exercising of his servants, which is that the weaker a servant of God is found to be in some struggle, the more clearly and perfectly the power of God is shown in sustaining him.

units.la: Libentissime ] Indicium 3. Quod ex hoc exercitio sequuta sit constantior humilitas, qua jam statuerit in omnibus rebus infirmitatem suam, & defectus suos agnoscere, in eum ipsum finem, ut Christi virtutem inhabitantem, tanto potentius & luculentius manifestatam in se experiretur.
units.tr: Most gladly: third indication: from this exercise there followed a more constant humility, by which he had now resolved to acknowledge his infirmity and his defects in all things, to this very end, that he might experience the power of Christ dwelling in him, manifested all the more mightily and brightly.

units.la: Vers. 10. Propterea oblector in infirmitatibus, in contumeliis, in necessitatibus, in persequutionibus, in angustiis pro Christo: quum enim impotens sum, tunc potens sum.
units.tr: Vers. 10. Therefore I take pleasure in infirmities, in reproaches, in necessities, in persecutions, in distresses, for Christ's sake: for when I am weak, then am I strong.

units.la: Indicium 4. Quod jam didicerit, non modo fortiter ferre omnes afflictiones pro Euangelio quae ipsum humiliorem reddere possent, sed etiam ex illis voluptatem maximam percipere: quia cum se infirmum maxime percipiebat, ad Christum confugiens, praesentiorem ipsius potentiam experiebatur, ad ipsum sustinendum, consolandum, & victorem reddendum.
units.tr: Fourth indication: he had now learned not only to bear bravely all the afflictions for the Gospel that could make him more humble, but also to derive the greatest delight from them. For when he most perceived himself to be weak, fleeing to Christ, he experienced the presence of Christ's power more closely, to sustain him, to console him, and to make him victorious.

units.la: Secunda Pars.
units.tr: Second Part.

units.la: Verf. 11. Fui insipiens in gloriando: vos me coegistis: nam ego debueram à vobis commendari: nulla enim in re inferior fui summis Apostolis, tametsi nihil sum.
units.tr: Verse 11. I have been foolish in boasting; you have compelled me. For I ought to have been commended by you. For in nothing was I inferior to the chief Apostles, although I am nothing.

units.la: Secunda pars Capitis continens gloriationem in Apostolatus sui, potenter & sincerè administrati inter Corinthios, manifestatione. Hanc gloriationem purgat ab insipientia, quam objicere possent aliqui, conjectá in Corinthios culpâ; ex quorum neglectu oriebatur Apostolo necessitas gloriandi: nam illi dignitatem ipsius debebant asserere contra Pseudapostolos. Debueram à vobis commendari, inquit, seu vestrum erat me defendere; hujus propositionis, & simul etiam gloriationis rationes affert novem.
units.tr: The second part of the chapter, containing Paul's boasting about the manifestation of his apostolate, which was exercised powerfully and sincerely among the Corinthians. He cleanses this boasting of folly, which some might object, by laying the blame on the Corinthians; from their neglect arose the necessity for the Apostle to boast, for they ought to have asserted his dignity against the false apostles. He says: "I ought to have been commended by you, or it was your duty to defend me." He brings nine reasons for this proposition and at the same time for the boasting.

units.la: Nulla enim ] Ratio prima, Quia licet Apostolus in se nullus erat, tamen gratia Dei non inferior erat summis Apostolis, ipsis etiam Corinthiis testibus: Idcirco debuit ab iis defendi & commendari.
units.tr: For in nothing] First reason: although the Apostle was nothing in himself, yet by the grace of God he was not inferior to the chief Apostles, the Corinthians themselves being witnesses. Therefore they ought to have defended and commended him.

units.la: Vers. 12. Indicia quidem Apostoli edita sunt apud vos per omnem tolerantiam, & signa & prodigia & virtutes.
units.tr: Verse 12. Truly the signs of an apostle were wrought among you in all patience, by signs and wonders and mighty deeds.

units.la: Ratio 2. Confirmans priorem. Quia inter vos signa Apostolatus mei apparent, Partim in admiranda laborum, molestiarum & injuriarum patientia: Partim in apostolatus mei effectis & indiciis; in prodigiis scilicet, miraculis, & potentibus operibus. Ergo debueram à vobis commendari.
units.tr: Second reason, confirming the first: because the signs of my apostleship appear among you, partly in the admirable patience in labours, troubles and injuries, and partly in the effects and evidences of my apostleship, namely in wonders, miracles and mighty works. Therefore I ought to have been commended by you.

units.la: Vers. 13. Nam quid est in quo fueritù inferiores cæteris Ecclesiis, nisi quòd ego ipse non obtorpui cum vestro incommodo: condonate mihi hanc injuriam.
units.tr: Verse 13. For what is there in which you were inferior to the other churches, except that I myself did not burden you? Forgive me this wrong.

units.la: Ratio 3. Quia Corinthiaca Ecclesia tam illustribus donis Spiritus sancti dotata est, per meum Ministerium, quam quævis alia Ecclesia, sive ab aliis Apostolis, sive à meipso fundata. Ergo meum Ministerium à vobis defendi debuit.
units.tr: Third reason: because the Corinthian church has been endowed with the illustrious gifts of the Holy Spirit through my ministry, as much as any other church, whether founded by other apostles or by myself. Therefore my ministry ought to have been defended by you.

units.la: Nisi quod ] Ratio 4. Quia zelus ipsius in propagando inter illos Euangelio, tantus erat, ut gratis Corinthiis prædicaret Euangelium, de quo si injuria fit, urbanâ ironiâ veniam deprecatur, beneficium datum illis insinuans: Defendi ergo ab iis debuerat. Vers. 14. Ecce, tertiò paratus sum venire ad vos, ne cum vestro incommodo obtorpescam, non enim quaero quae vestra sunt, sed vos. Non enim debent filii parentibus thesauros congerere, sed parentes filiis
units.tr: Except that] Fourth reason: because his zeal in propagating the gospel among them was so great that he preached the gospel to the Corinthians free of charge. If a wrong is done to him in this, he seeks pardon with urbane irony, hinting at the benefit given to them. He ought therefore to have been defended by them. Verse 14. Behold, I am ready to come to you a third time, and I will not burden you, for I do not seek what is yours, but you. For children ought not to lay up treasure for their parents, but parents for their children.

units.la: Ratio 5. Confirmans priorem. Quia idem adhuc Apostoli animus manebat erga illos de stipendio in posterum non accipiendo, cum venturus esset ad eos; nam jam tertio parabat se ad iter, licet secundus conatus impeditus fuerit, ut, 1. ad Cor. 1. habetur.
units.tr: Fifth reason, confirming the first: because the same attitude of the Apostle towards them remained, namely not to accept support in future when he came to them; for now he was preparing for the journey a third time, although the second attempt was prevented, as is found in 1 Cor. 1.

units.la: Vestra ] Ratio 6. Confirmans priorem, Quia quaerebat Corinthiorum salutem, non verò ipsorum bona in familiarem rem suam convertere: Debebant igitur ipsum defendere.
units.tr: Yours] Sixth reason, confirming the first: because he sought the salvation of the Corinthians, not to convert their goods to his own private use. They ought therefore to have defended him.

units.la: Non enim ] Ratio 7. Quia licet Pater spiritualis sit, qui alī debeat à grege seu liberis suis, præ ipsorum studio tamen imitari studuerat parentes naturales, qui thesaurizant filiis suis, intelligè ordinariam agendi rationem. Nam alioqui si opus habeant parentes, non est dubium quin liberos deceat mutua parentibus officia præstare, ipsosque alen-do honorare.
units.tr: For] Seventh reason: although a spiritual father is one who ought to be fed by his flock or children, yet he had been careful to imitate, in preference to their concern, natural parents, who lay up treasure for their children, that is, the ordinary manner of acting. For otherwise, if parents are in need, there is no doubt that it is fitting for children to render mutual duties to their parents and to honour them by feeding them.

units.la: Verf. 15. Ego vero libentissime impendam, & expendar pro animabus vestris: etiam si, abundè vos diligens, minus diligar.
units.tr: Verse 15. But I will most gladly spend and be spent for your souls; even if, loving you abundantly, I am loved less.

units.la: Ratio 8 Quia paratus erat & bona sua, & vitam ipsam in eorum salutem impendere: Quam vehementem dilectionem amplificat ex Corinthiorum ingratitudine, qui interim vt eam non reddebant amoris, sed æmulos ipsius Pseudapostolos, recipiebant, & pluris faciebant eos quam ipsum Apostolum patrem suum.
units.tr: Eighth reason: because he was ready to spend both his goods and his very life for their salvation. He amplifies this vehement love from the ingratitude of the Corinthians, who in the meantime did not return it as love, but received instead his rivals, the false apostles, and valued them more than the Apostle, their father himself.

units.la: Verf 16 Sed esto, ego vos non gravavi: sed quum sim callidus, dolo vos cepi.
units.tr: Verse 16. But granted, I did not burden you; but being crafty, I caught you by guile.

units.la: Verf. 17. Numquem quemquam eorum quos misi ad vos, expilavi vos?
units.tr: Verse 17. Did I take advantage of any of those whom I sent to you?

units.la: Verf. 18. Precatus sum Titum & cum eo misi fratrem: nunquid vos expilavit Titus? nonne eodem Spiritu incessimus? nonne iisdem vestigiis?
units.tr: Verse 18. I asked Titus and sent with him a brother. Did Titus take advantage of you? Did we not walk in the same Spirit? Did we not walk in the same steps?

units.la: Ratio 9. In qua occupat objectionem, Diceret aliquis, etiamsi tuipse non recepisti ab illis stipendium, fortasse tamen per alios emissarios tuos eos exuxisti. Respondet ipsius comites & legatos, quos ad Corinthios miserat, simili studio cavisse, ne Corinthios sumptibus aut acceptis muneribus gravarent. Obiter autem perstringit adversarios, dum se purgat ab iis artibus, quibus dolosi illi operarii utebantur, qui cum ipsi nolle quicquam accipere videri volebant, alios subornabant qui in ipsorum usum acciperent à Corinthiis quantum emungere poterant: Ergo Corinthii qui ista optime noverant, Paulum defendere debebant, & ipsius loco responsionem obtrectatoribus in os reponere.
units.tr: Ninth reason, in which he meets an objection: someone might say, "Even if you yourself did not receive support from them, perhaps you nevertheless drained them through your other emissaries." He answers that his companions and legates, whom he had sent to the Corinthians, took equal care not to burden the Corinthians with expenses or with gifts received. In passing, he also strikes at the adversaries, while he clears himself of those tricks which those deceitful workers used: they wished to appear as if they accepted nothing, yet they procured others who would receive from the Corinthians as much as they could squeeze out for their own use. Therefore the Corinthians, who knew these things very well, ought to have defended Paul and put the answer to the detractors in their mouths in his place.

units.la: Tertia Pars.
units.tr: Third Part.

units.la: Verf. 19. Rursum putatu quòd nos vobis excusemus? in conspectu Dei, in Christo loquimur: omnia tamen hac, charissimi pro vestri ædificatione.
units.tr: Verse 19. Do you think again that we are excusing ourselves to you? We speak in the sight of God, in Christ; but all these things, beloved, for your edification.

units.la: Tertia pars Capitis in qua per occupationem objectionis, defensionis suæ adeò solicitæ causas reddit: Diceret aliquis, quorsum ista scribis; quorsum ista defensio; num alicujus mali conscius es, vel an gloriam apud nos captas? Respondet afferendo tantæ suæ solicitudinis causas quinque.
units.tr: The third part of the chapter, in which, by anticipating an objection, he gives the reasons for his so anxious defence. Someone might say: why do you write these things, why this defence? Are you conscious of some wrong, or are you seeking glory among us? He answers by giving five reasons for his great anxiety.

units.la: Prima, Non eò hæc scripsi, ut (quasi mali alicujus conscius essem, aut gloriam captarem) me apud vos purgem, aut excusem! Sed ex dilectione erga vos, ut vestram ædificationem & salutem promoverem, ne vos scilicet minus honorificè de meo Apostolatu sentientes, per Pseudapostolos à simplicitate Euangelii demoveremini: In cujus asseverationis meæ Testimonium, invoco testes, Deum, qui novit meum animum, & Christum, cujus negotium ago.
units.tr: The first: I have not written this in order to clear myself or make excuses to you, as though I were conscious of some wrong or sought glory. Rather, it comes from my love for you, so that I may promote your edification and salvation, lest, thinking less highly of my apostleship, you be drawn away from the simplicity of the Gospel by false apostles. As a witness to this assertion of mine, I call on God, who knows my heart, and on Christ, whose business I am conducting.

units.la: Verf. 20. Nam metuo ne quo modo, quum venero, non quales velim repe tam vos, & ego reperiar vobis qualem nolitis: ne quo modo sint lites, æmulationes, iræ, contentiones, obtrectationes, susurri, tumores, tumultuationes:
units.tr: Verse 20. For I fear that, when I come, I may not find you such as I wish, and that I may be found by you such as you do not wish: that there may perhaps be quarrels, jealousies, angers, factions, slanders, whisperings, swellings, tumults.

units.la: Secunda causa, Metuo ne labefactata inter vos, per Pseudapostolos, mea authoritate & Doctrina, cum venero comperiam vos quales nollem, id est, infectos illis malis, quæ schismata sequuntur: qualia sunt lites seu contentiones in verbis: æmulationes, seu invidia de donis Dei: excandescentiæ, seu iræ ex mutuarum injuriarum apprehensione: rixæ seu mutuæ provocationes: obtrectationes & susurri, quibus aperte & clam alii aliorum famam lædere solent: tumores & animi quasi inflationes ex superbia: & denique seditiones tumultuosæ. Et ego] Tertia causa, Metuo ne me severiorem quam velletis experiamini, nisi tempestive meis admonitionibus emendati, doctrinae & autoritati meae in DOMINO vos submittatis.
units.tr: The second reason: I fear that, because of the false apostles, my authority and teaching have been weakened among you, so that when I come I shall find you as I would not wish, that is, infected with those evils that follow schisms. Such are quarrels, or contentions in words; jealousies, or envy about the gifts of God; outbursts, or angers arising from the sense of mutual injuries; brawls, or mutual provocations; slanderings and whisperings, by which people commonly injure one another's reputation openly and secretly; swellings, or puffings up of the mind through pride; and finally riotous seditions. And I The third reason: I fear that you may find me more severe than you would like, unless, corrected in time by my admonitions, you submit yourselves in the Lord to my teaching and authority.

units.la: Ne iterum ubi venero, me deprimat Deus meus apud vos, & lugeam multos eorum qui ante peccarunt, nec resipuerunt super impuritate, & fornicatione, & protervia quam patrarunt.
units.tr: Lest again, when I come, my God humble me among you, and I mourn many of those who sinned before and have not repented of the uncleanness, fornication, and wantonness that they committed.

units.la: Quarta causa, Metuo ne si despiciatur mea apud vos autoritas, multi ex vobis impaenitentes permansuri sint in impuritate, fornicationibus, & similibus peccatis, quae ego in priori Epistola reprehendi.
units.tr: The fourth reason: I fear that if my authority is despised among you, many of you will remain unrepentant in uncleanness, fornication, and similar sins, which I rebuked in my earlier letter.

units.la: Deprimat me] Quinta causa, Metuo ne me affligat Dominus, cum venero ad vos, nempe ne pudorem, tristitiam & luctum mihi creent peccata vestra, & scandala in vobis, qui mea gloria & gaudium estis, si sicut filios decet vos geratis; pudoris vero & tristitiae causa futuri estis, si secus feceritis.
units.tr: Humble me The fifth reason: I fear that the Lord may humble me when I come to you, namely, that your sins and the scandals among you, who are my glory and joy, may bring me shame, sorrow, and grief, if you behave as becomes sons; but you will be the cause of shame and sorrow if you act otherwise.

units.la: Ut his malis obviam iretur, & scandala inter ipsos scatentia auferrentur, necessarium erat Apostoli, & Apostolicae doctrinae, autoritatem sartam, tectam, inter eos conservari, in eumque finem necessaria erat haec Apostoli apologia.
units.tr: So that these evils might be met and the scandals flourishing among them removed, it was necessary that the authority of the Apostle and of apostolic teaching be kept intact and preserved among them, and to this end this apology of the Apostle was necessary.

units.la: Caput Decimumtertium.
units.tr: Chapter 13.

units.la: Apite hoc ultimo pergit autoritatem suam Apostolicam a contemptu vindicare, eamque metuendam & amabilem ipsis reddere: propositio confirmanda est, Reverendi vobis debet esse autoritas mea. Argumenta, quae hanc thesin confirmant sunt decem.
units.tr: Here at last he goes on to defend his apostolic authority from contempt and to make it both feared and loved by them. The proposition to be confirmed is: My authority ought to be reverenced by you. There are ten arguments that confirm this thesis.

units.la: Tertia hac vice venio ad vos: Ex ore duorum testium aut trium, firmum erit omne verbum. Verf. 1.
units.tr: This third time I am coming to you: in the mouth of two or three witnesses every word shall be established. Verse 1.

units.la: Argumentum primum, Praemoneo, pro autoritate mihi data, de meo proposito ad vos veniendi, jam tertia vice repetito, ut praemonitiones duae vel tres de meo adventu, duorum aut trium testium loco sint, ad firmum meum propositum declarandum, de judicio Ecclesiastico inter vos exercendo: Metuenda vobis igitur autoritas mea.
units.tr: Argument 1. I forewarn you, by the authority given to me, of my intention to come to you, now repeated for the third time. Let these two or three forewarnings about my coming serve as the testimony of two or three witnesses, to declare my firm purpose of exercising church judgment among you. My authority, therefore, is something you should fear.

units.la: Verf. 2. Prædixi & secundò prædico, ut præsens, & absens nunc scribo iis qui antè peccarunt, & reliquis omnibus, fore ut, si denuò venero, non parcam:
units.tr: Verse 2. I told you before, and now I tell you again, as if present, and being absent I now write, to those who sinned before and to all the rest: that if I come again, I will not spare.

units.la: Arg. 2. A comminatione severitatis exercendæ cum advenerit, in impœnitentes, qui prius peccaverant, & non resipuerant: Persuasum habete me severè animadversurum in impœnitentes cum venero. Metuite & resipiscite igitur.
units.tr: Argument 2. From the threat of severe discipline to be exercised when I arrive against the unrepentant, who had sinned before and not repented: be assured that I will deal severely with the unrepentant when I come. Fear, therefore, and repent.

units.la: Verf. 3. Quandoquidem experimentum quæritis in me loquentis Christi, qui erga vos non est infirmus, sed potens est in vobis.
units.tr: Verse 3. Since you seek a proof of Christ speaking in me, who is not weak toward you, but is mighty among you.

units.la: Rationem reddit comminationis tam severæ: Quia tentabant & CHRISTUM & Apostolum, dubitantes an CHRISTUS in Apostolo, vel Apostolus ex autoritate CHRISTI loqueretur, & simul addit Arg. 3. ad vindicandam suam autoritatem. CHRISTUS potenter per meum Ministerium se inter vos manifestavit, partim gratia peccatoribus data; partim donis Spiritus in Presbyteros & alios, collatis; Partim miraculis inter vos editis; partim castigatione peccatorum pertinacium. Metuite igitur.
units.tr: He gives the reason for so severe a threat: they were testing both Christ and the Apostle, doubting whether Christ spoke in the Apostle, or whether the Apostle spoke by the authority of Christ. At the same time he adds Argument 3, to vindicate his authority. Christ has shown himself mightily among you through my ministry: partly by the grace given to sinners, partly by the gifts of the Spirit conferred on the elders and others, partly by miracles worked among you, and partly by the chastisement of the obstinate sinners. Fear, therefore.

units.la: Verf. 4. Nam etsi crucifixus fuit ex infirmitate, vivit tamen ex potentia Dei: nam & nos infirmi sumus cum eo, sed vivemus cum eo, ex virtute Dei apud vos.
units.tr: Verse 4. For though he was crucified through weakness, yet he lives by the power of God. For we also are weak in him, but we shall live with him by the power of God toward you.

units.la: Arg. 4. Sicut CHRISTUS in carnis infirmitate fuit crucifixus, sed in Spiritu & potentia Deitatis suæ vivere comperitur, sic ego specie infirmus sum, & humiliter me gessi propter CHRISTUM, ut CHRISTO conformis essem, sed virtute Dei potens fui, & futurus sum etiam potens in Ministerio meo, ubi res postulaverit: Metuenda ergo vobis mea autoritas.
units.tr: Argument 4. Just as Christ was crucified in the weakness of the flesh, yet is found to live in the Spirit and the power of his Deity, so I appear weak, and I have conducted myself humbly for Christ's sake, that I might be conformed to Christ; but I am mighty by the power of God, and I shall be mighty also in my ministry, wherever the situation requires. Therefore my authority is something you should fear.

units.la: Verf. 5. Vosipsos tentate annon fitis in fide; vosipsos probate, annon agnoscitis vosmetipsos, videlicet Iesum Christum in vobis esse, nisi reprobi estis.
units.tr: Verse 5. Examine yourselves whether you are in the faith; prove yourselves. Do you not recognise that namely Jesus Christ is in you, unless you are reprobates?

units.la: Arg. 5. Omnes vos, post vestri probationem, cognoscere poteritis CHRISTUM in vobis habitare per ministerium meum, nisi aliqui ex vobis sint rejectanei, & indigni fidelium nomine, talem nondum regeniti. Ergo mei Apostolatus autoritas reverenda vobis esse debet.
units.tr: Argument 5. After your testing, all of you will be able to recognise that Christ dwells in you through my ministry, unless some among you are castaways and unworthy of the name of believers, not yet regenerate in that way. Therefore the authority of my apostleship ought to be reverenced by you.

units.la: Verf. 6. At spero fore ut cognoscatis nos non esse reprobos.
units.tr: Verse 6. But I hope you will recognise that we are not reprobates.

units.la: Arg. 6. Quales quales vos jam sitis, spero fore ut tandem veritate victi, & indicis mei Apostolatus convicti, cognoscatis me esse genuinum CHRISTI servum, & Apostolum non adulterinum seu rejectaneum: Ergo reverenda vobis debet esse autoritas mea.
units.tr: Argument 6. Whatever state you are now in, I hope that at last, overcome by the truth and convicted by the evidence of my apostleship, you will recognise that I am the genuine servant of Christ and an Apostle, not a counterfeit or a castaway. Therefore my authority ought to be reverenced by you.

units.la: Verf. 7. Opto vero à Deo nequid mali faciatis: non ut nos probati comperiamur, sed ut quod honestum est faciatis, nos vero velut reprobi simus.
units.tr: Verse 7. Now I pray to God that you do nothing evil: not that we may be found approved, but that you may do what is honourable, and that we may be as reprobates.

units.la: Arg. 7. Quo non solum autoritatem suam vindicat à contemptu, sed etiam ex animi sui moderatione amabilem reddit: Impensè cupio vos à malo omni abstinere, & bonum facere, ne sit opus autoritatis meæ inter vos exercitio: in eumque finem DEUM oro, nihil solicitus de mea æstimatione, sive approbatus sive reprobus ab hominibus judicer, susque deque habens, modo vobis bene sit. Ergo reverenda vobis debet esse autoritas mea.
units.tr: Argument 7. By which he not only vindicates his authority from contempt, but also makes it lovable through the moderation of his own spirit: I earnestly desire that you abstain from every evil and do good, so that there may be no need for the exercise of my authority among you. To this end I pray to God, being in no way anxious about my reputation, whether I am judged approved or reprobate by men, and caring nothing for it, provided it goes well with you. Therefore my authority ought to be reverenced by you.

units.la: Verf. 8. Non enim possumus quicquam adversus veritatem, sed pro veritate.
units.tr: Verse 8. For we can do nothing against the truth, but only for the truth.

units.la: Arg. 8. Confirmans superius, Autoritas mea non valet contra veritatem, aut justitiam, ut illæ destruantur, sed pro veritate conservanda, ideoque si vos nihil mali faceretis, autoritas mea contra vos cessatura esset. Amabilis igitur ea vobis debet esse.
units.tr: Argument 8. Confirming what was said above: my authority has no force against truth or justice, so as to destroy them, but only to preserve the truth. Therefore, if you did no wrong, my authority would cease to act against you. It ought therefore to be lovable to you.

units.la: Verf. 9. Gaudemus enim quum nos infirmi fuerimus, vos autem validi fueritis. Hoc autem etiam optamus, vestram videlicet instaurationem.
units.tr: Verse 9. For we rejoice when we are weak and you are strong. And this also we wish, namely your restoration.

units.la: Arg. 9. Confirmans septimum: Gaudeo quando subtractâ occasione autoritatis exercendæ, ego (quasi nullam haberem,) meam potestatem non oltendo, nihil magis in votis habens, quam vestram integritatem, ut rebus omnibus bene compositis, & membris Ecclesiæ quæ jam luxata sunt in locum suum restitutis, nunquam opus habeam, me ipsum extollere ad vestrum terrorem: Ergo reverenda & amabilis vobis esse debet mea autoritas.
units.tr: Argument 9. Confirming the seventh: I rejoice when, the occasion for exercising authority being removed, I do not display my power, as though I had none, having nothing more in my prayers than your integrity; so that, with all things well ordered and the members of the Church, which are now dislocated, restored to their place, I may never have need to exalt myself to your terror. Therefore my authority ought to be both reverenced and lovable to you.

units.la: Verf. 10. Propterea hæc absens scribo, ne præsens severitate utar, ex potestate quam dedit mihi Dominus ad ædificationem, ac non ad destructionem.
units.tr: Verse 10. Therefore I write these things while absent, so that when present I may not use severity, according to the power which the Lord gave me for building up, and not for destruction.

units.la: Arg. 10. Jam severius per literas ago vobiscum, ut resipiscatis, ne præsens cogar severius agere in impænitentes, secundum potestatem datam in vestrum bonum, non vero detrimentum: Idcirco reverenda debet esse mea apud vos autoritas.
units.tr: Argument 10. I now deal with you more severely by letter, so that you may repent, and so that I may not be forced, when present, to act more severely against the unrepentant, according to the power given for your good and not for your harm. Therefore my authority ought to be reverenced by you.

units.la: Versf. 11. Quod superest, fratres, valete, inflauramini, consolationem habete, idem sentite, in pace agite, & Deus charitatis acpacis author erit vobiscum.
units.tr: Verse 11. Finally, brethren, farewell; be perfected, be comforted, be of one mind, live in peace; and the God of love and peace shall be the author with you.

units.la: Verf. 12. Salutate alii alios sancto osculo, Salutant vos sancti omnes.
units.tr: Verse 12. Greet one another with a holy kiss. All the saints salute you.

units.la: Verf. 13. Gratia Domini Iesu Christi, & charitas Dei, & communicatio Spiritus sancti sit cum omnibus vobis, Amen.
units.tr: Verse 13. The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ, and the love of God, and the communion of the Holy Spirit be with you all. Amen.

units.la: Concludit Epistolam appositissima hortatione sextuplici: Prima, Ut obtemperando ipsius monitionibus gaudium solidum gaudeant: 2. Ut perfecti sint seu integri, & remoto schismate interse coagmentati: 3. Ut de malis omnibus consolationem capiant ipsi obtemperando: 4. Ut sententiis inter se conveniant: 5. Ut affectibus juncti pacem colant: quas hortationes confirmat promissione divinae praesentiae in donis gratiae amplioribus, quae Deus qui pace & dilectione gaudet, pacis & dilectionis studiosis concedere solet.
units.tr: He concludes the Epistle with a most fitting exhortation of six parts: (1) that by obeying his admonitions they may rejoice in a solid joy; (2) that they may be perfect, or whole, and, with schism removed, joined together among themselves; (3) that by obeying they may take comfort in all their troubles; (4) that they may agree among themselves in their opinions; (5) that, joined in their affections, they may cultivate peace. He confirms these exhortations with the promise of the divine presence in the greater gifts of grace, which God, who delights in peace and love, is accustomed to grant to those who strive for peace and love.

units.la: Salutate ] Sexto hortatur, ut mutuae dilectionis signa, sine dissimulatione, ut decet sanctos, sibi invicem exhibeant.
units.tr: Greet] Sixthly, he urges them to show signs of mutual love to one another, without pretence, as befits saints.

units.la: Gratia Domini ] Post salutem dictam nomine sanctorum, in fine per benedictionem Apostolicam applicat illis, & optat porro concedi non solum jus ad omnia salutaria beneficia Christi, sed etiam agnitionem, sensum, fruitionemque ampliorem, primum gratiae reconciliationis factae per Christum, deinde amoris Divini, qui per Christum descendit ad nos: & tertio, omnis generis donorum Spiritus sancti, votum & spem obsignans quasi sigillo suo. Amen.
units.tr: Grace of the Lord] After the greeting given in the name of the saints, at the end he applies to them the apostolic blessing, and prays that there may be granted to them not only the right to all the saving benefits of Christ, but also a fuller knowledge, sense and enjoyment: first, of the grace of reconciliation made through Christ; secondly, of the divine love which comes down to us through Christ; and thirdly, of every kind of gift of the Holy Spirit, sealing his wish and hope as with his own seal. Amen.

units.la: ANALYTICA EPISTOL- Æ AD GALATAS EXPOSI- TIO. Summarium.
units.tr: Analytical Exposition of the Epistle to the Galatians. Summary.

units.la: GAlatia regio est minoris Asiæ, in qua Ecclesias studiosè plantaverat Apostolus, Act. 16. & 18 Huc profecti ex Iudæa Pharisæi quidam, qui fidem Christi professione tenus amplexi erant, observationem Legis Mosaicæ, unà cum fide Euangelii ad salutem necessario conjungendam esse docuerant, & plerisque, si non omnes istius regionis Ecclesias, errore suo infecerant; prætendebant interim impostores illi, missos se fuisse ab Apostolis Petro, Iacobo, & Ioanne, & secundùm eorum sententiam se omnia sui dogmata docuisse falsò affirmabant. Quapropter illos tres Apostolos in immensum extollebant, Paulo verò nomen & jus Apostoli detrahebant, quasi non ascito in societatem Apostolorum à Christo, nec pro Apostolo ab Apostolis reliquis agnito. Quare in hac Epistola (refutata hac Pseudapostolorum calumnia) agit Apostolus cum Galatis, ut ad sanitatem fidei redeant.
units.tr: Galatia is a region of Asia Minor, where the Apostle had diligently planted churches (Acts 16 and 18). Certain Pharisees came there from Judea. They had embraced the faith of Christ in name only, and they taught that observance of the Mosaic Law must be joined necessarily with faith in the Gospel for salvation. They had infected most of the churches of that region with their error, if not all of them. Meanwhile these impostors claimed that they had been sent by the Apostles Peter, James and John, and they falsely asserted that they had taught all their doctrines according to those men's opinion. Therefore they praised those three Apostles beyond measure, and they stripped Paul of the name and authority of an Apostle, as though he had not been taken into the fellowship of the Apostles by Christ and had not been recognised by the other Apostles as an Apostle. Accordingly, in this Epistle, having refuted this calumny of the false apostles, the Apostle deals with the Galatians so that they may return to the soundness of faith.

units.la: Epistolæ (præter Præfationem & Conclusionem) tres sunt partes præcipuæ: In Prima agit cum Galatis, ut renuncient errori quem imbiberant: obiter verò ut calumniantibus occurreret, Apostolatum suum animosè asserit, ne summis quidem tribus illis Apostolis, in autoritate Apostolica cedens, Cap. primo, & priori parte Capitis secundi.
units.tr: The Epistle, apart from the Preface and Conclusion, has three main parts. In the First Part he urges the Galatians to renounce the error they had imbibed. Along the way, to meet the slanderers, he boldly asserts his apostolic office, yielding nothing in apostolic authority even to those three highest Apostles: in the first chapter and the first part of the second chapter.

units.la: In Secunda parte disputat ex professo, de justificatione per fidem, deque temporario usu, & abrogatione Legis Mosaicæ, posteriori parte Capitis secundi, Capite tertio, & quarto.
units.tr: In the Second Part he argues expressly about justification by faith, and about the temporary use and abrogation of the Mosaic Law: in the latter part of the second chapter, and in the third and fourth chapters.

units.la: Denique in Tertia Parte, præmissâ hortatione ad perseverandum in libertate Christiana, præcipit ut ea rectè utantur, & ostendit quæ sint Christianorum vera exercitia, ne vel dissolutâ licentia, vel superstitiosa Cæremoniarum observatione, præcipua Christianorum officia negligerent, Capite quinto & sexto.
units.tr: Finally, in the Third Part, after a preface exhorting them to persevere in Christian liberty, he instructs them to use it rightly, and shows what the true Christian exercises are, so that they neither neglect the principal duties of Christians through loose licence nor through superstitious observance of ceremonies, in chapters five and six.

units.la: Capitis
units.tr: Chapter

units.la: Apitis tres sunt partes: In Prima est praefatio, ad verf. 6. In fecunda incipit agere cum Galatis, ut redeant in viam ab errore suo, in observatione Legu Levitica, & imaginaria conjunctione justi-ficationis per opera, cum justificatione per fidem, quasi hoc fuisset possibile, propositis in eum finem aliquot argumentis, ad verf. 13. In tertia confirmat Apostolus ultimum Argumentum, de doctrinae suae divinitate ex signis, ad finem.
units.tr: The chapter has three parts. The first is the preface, to verse 6. In the second he begins to deal with the Galatians, so that they may return from their error to the right way, namely the observance of the Levitical Law and the imaginary union of justification by works with justification by faith, as if that were possible. To this end he sets forth several arguments, to verse 13. In the third the Apostle confirms his last argument, concerning the divine origin of his doctrine from the signs, to the end.

units.la: Verf. 1. Paulus Apostolus (non ab hominibus, neque per hominem, sed per Iesum Christum, ac Deum Patrem, qui suscitavit eum ex mortuis)
units.tr: Verse 1. Paul, an apostle (not from men, nor through man, but through Jesus Christ and God the Father, who raised him from the dead).

units.la: Praefatio tota comparatur ad parandum animum Galatarum, ut Doctrinae suae de CHRISTI gratia obtemperent. Scopus, hac vel simili in eund um sensum propositione concipi potest: Debetis mihi commonefacienti de vera justificationis & sanctificationis ratione, fidem habere, & optemperare: Argumenta insinuantur in hunc scopum, octo. Quorum alia in inscriptione, verf. 1. 2. Alia in salutatione, verf. 3. Alia in CHRISTI descriptione, verf. 4. Alia in doxologia continentur, verf. 5.
units.tr: The whole preface is designed to prepare the minds of the Galatians to obey his teaching about the grace of Christ. The aim may be expressed in this or a similar proposition: "You must believe me and obey me when I remind you about the true manner of justification and sanctification." Eight arguments are hinted at to this end. Some of them are contained in the inscription, verses 1 and 2; others in the greeting, verse 3; others in the description of Christ, verse 4; and others in the doxology, verse 5.

units.la: Verf. 2. Quique mecum sunt omnes fratres, Ecclesiis Galatiae: Gratia vobis & Pax à DEO Patre, & Domino nostro IESV CHRISTO.
units.tr: Verse 2. And all the brothers who are with me, to the churches of Galatia: grace to you and peace from God the Father and our Lord Jesus Christ.

units.la: Arg. 4. Advocavi in societatem hujus admonitionis ad vos Scriptae, omnes fratres qui mecum sunt, qui unà mecum vos salutant, Testimonium nium adversus vos aliquando dicturi, nisi Doctrinæ meæ obediatis. Credendum ergo & obtemperandum mihi.
units.tr: Argument 4. I have called all the brothers who are with me into the fellowship of this admonition which I write to you, who greet you along with me, as a witness against you at some time, unless you obey my doctrine. Therefore you ought to believe me and obey me.

units.la: Ecclesiis ] Arg. 5. Etiamsi periculoso errore infecti fitis, habendos vos tamen censeo in Ecclesiarum numero. Mihi ergo vicem rependite, & ut Apostolo ad Ecclesias misso, credendum & obtemperandum esse agnoscite.
units.tr: Churches. Argument 5. Even though you have been infected with a dangerous error, I consider that you should nonetheless be counted among the churches. Therefore repay me in kind, and acknowledge that I am to be believed and obeyed as an Apostle sent to the churches.

units.la: Verf. 3. Gratia vobis & pax à Deo Patre & Domino nostro Iesu Christo:
units.tr: Verse 3. Grace to you and peace from God the Father and our Lord Jesus Christ.

units.la: Arg. 6. Ego pro autoritate Divinitus mihi tributa, non dubito jus ad benedictionem Euangelii vobis applicare, & comprecari Gratiam, id est, uberiorem agnitionem, sensum, fructumque gratuitæ Dei misericordiæ, reconciliationis, & remissionis peccatorum, reliquorumque essectuum gratiæ Dei ad sanctitatem facientium; Vnà cum Pace, seu solida cordium tranquillitate, reliquisque bonis quæ ad felicitatem spectant, ut ad vos deriventur omnia, à Deo pacis & Domino Mediatore Christo; unico gratiæ pacisque omnis fonte. Ergo aperienti mihi rationem hujus gratiæ & pacis vobis communicandæ, credendum & obtemperandum est.
units.tr: Argument 6. By the authority divinely given to me, I do not hesitate to apply to you the right to the blessing of the Gospel, and to wish grace for you, that is, a fuller knowledge, sense and fruit of God's free mercy, of reconciliation and of the forgiveness of sins, and of the other effects of God's grace that make for holiness; together with peace, that is, a firm tranquillity of heart, and the other good things that pertain to happiness, so that all of them may flow down to you from God of peace and the Lord Mediator Christ, the sole fount of all grace and peace. Therefore you must believe me and obey me when I explain to you the manner in which this grace and peace are to be communicated to you.

units.la: Verf. 4. Qui dedit semetipsum pro peccatis nostris, ut eximeret nos ex præsenti seculo malo, secundum voluntatem Dei & Patris nostri:
units.tr: Verse 4. Who gave himself for our sins, that he might deliver us from this present evil age, according to the will of God and our Father.

units.la: Describit Christum ab opere redemptionis, ut ostendat totam salutem nostram, per ejus meritum, ex Dei gratia provenire: unde.
units.tr: He describes Christ from the work of redemption, to show that our whole salvation comes from God's grace through his merit. Hence:

units.la: Arg. 7. Salus nostra seu redemptio nostri, à perdita conditione improborum, qui sunt de hoc mundo extra Christum, per solius Christi mortem impetratur: idque ex decreto & instituto Dei Patris, qui hanc solam rationem salutis gratuitam ordinavit. Ergo mihi commonefacienti, ut hanc solam salutis rationem agnoscatis, credendum & obtemperandum.
units.tr: Argument 7. Our salvation, or our redemption from the lost condition of the wicked, who are in this world apart from Christ, is obtained by the death of Christ alone. This comes from the decree and appointment of God the Father, who ordained this one way of salvation, freely given. Therefore, when I remind you that you must acknowledge this one way of salvation, you ought to believe me and obey me.

units.la: Verf. 5. Cui sit gloria in seacula seculorum. Amen.
units.tr: Verse 5. To whom be glory for ever and ever. Amen.

units.la: Arg. 8. Deus dignus est, & Christus etiam, cui pro tanto beneficio & ineffabili gratia, gloria tribuatur ab omnibus in æternum: Ergo mihi vindicanti apud vos hanc gratiæ Christi gloriam, ne humanorum operum merito obfuscetur, vel tollatur, credendum & obtemperandum est.
units.tr: Argument 8. God is worthy, and Christ too, to whom glory is to be given by all for ever for so great a benefit and inexpressible grace. Therefore, when I claim for this glory of Christ's grace among you, so that it may not be obscured or taken away by the merit of human works, you ought to believe me and obey me.

units.la: Secunda Pars.
units.tr: Second Part.

units.la: Verf. 6. Miror vos ita cito, deserto eo qui vocavit vos in gratiam Christi, transferri in aliud Euangelium:
units.tr: Verse 6. I marvel that you are so quickly turned away from him who called you into the grace of Christ, to another gospel:

units.la: Secunda pars Capitis, in qua probat renunciandum esse errori, de imaginaria & impossibili conjunctione justificationis ex operibus, & justificationis ex gratia, seu fide in Christum: quo errore implicati jam erant per Pseudapostolos, qui docebant observationem Legis Mosaicae, etiam credentibus in Christum, ad justificationem & salutem esse necessariam, Argumenta quibus urget, ut errori renuncient, sunt novem, quorum alia insinuantur in reprehensione; alia apertius proferuntur in sequenti disputatione.
units.tr: The second part of the chapter, in which he proves that one must renounce the error concerning the imaginary and impossible conjunction of justification by works and justification by grace, or faith in Christ. Those entangled in this error were already being led astray by the false apostles, who taught that the observance of the Mosaic Law, even for believers in Christ, was necessary for justification and salvation. The arguments by which he urges them to renounce the error are nine, some of which are hinted at in the rebuke, while others are set out more openly in the following discussion.

units.la: Argumentum primum, Admiranda est defectio vestra, O Galatae, a gratia Christi ad merita operum humanorum, quod ita cito post recens admissam Christi fidem, & Gratiam in conversione vestra acceptam deficiatis ab ea: Renunciandum ergo huic errori.
units.tr: First argument: Your defection, O Galatians, from the grace of Christ to the merits of human works is astonishing, that you should so quickly after the recently admitted faith in Christ, and the grace received in your conversion, fall away from it. This error must therefore be renounced.

units.la: Arg. 2. Deseruistis in hoc veltro errore Deum, qui vocavit vos in Christi gratiam, & confugistis ad opera humana: Renunciandum ergo huic errori.
units.tr: Argument 2. In this your recent error you have forsaken God, who called you into the grace of Christ, and have fled to human works. This error must therefore be renounced.

units.la: Arg. 3. Per hunc errorem transferimini ab Euangelio Christi, in aliud nescio quod ab hominibus confictum Euangelium: Renunciandum ergo huic errori.
units.tr: Argument 3. Through this error you are being transferred from the gospel of Christ to another gospel, I know not what, devised by men. This error must therefore be renounced.

units.la: Verf. 7. Quod non est aliud, sed nonnulli vos turbant, & volunt invertere Euangelium Christi,
units.tr: Verse 7. Which is not another; but there are some that trouble you, and would pervert the gospel of Christ.

units.la: Arg. 4. Praeter unum verum Euangelium, a me inter vos praedicatum, nullum est aliud, sed ficta & fucata est omnis alia doctrina Euangelii, quae cum doctrina mea non concordat: Renunciandum ergo huic errori.
units.tr: Argument 4. Besides the one true gospel preached by me among you, there is no other; every other doctrine of the gospel that does not agree with my teaching is a fiction and a counterfeit. This error must therefore be renounced.

units.la: Arg. 5. Doctores qui vos seduxerunt, hostes sunt pacis vestrae, quia pacem quam habent justificati per fidem erga Deum, vobis eripiunt: Renunciandum eorum doctrinae ergo.
units.tr: Argument 5. The teachers who have seduced you are enemies of your peace, since they snatch from you the peace which the justified have through faith toward God. Their doctrine must therefore be renounced.

units.la: Arg. 6. Euangelii Christi supplantatores & eversores sunt, seductores illi veltri, qui Doctores videri volunt: nihil enim magis est contrarium Euangelio de gratuita justificatione per fidem, quam justificatio ex operibus. Renunciandum ergo huic errori.
units.tr: Argument 6. Those seducers of yours, who wish to be seen as teachers, are subverters and overthrowers of the gospel of Christ; for nothing is more contrary to the gospel of justification freely by faith than justification by works. This error must therefore be renounced.

units.la: Verf. 8: Sed etiam si nos aut angelus e caelo euangelizet vobis, praeter id quod vobis euangelizavimus, anathema esto.
units.tr: Verse 8: But though we, or an angel from heaven, preach any other gospel unto you than that which we have preached unto you, let him be accursed.

units.la: Arg. 7. Quisquis fuerit qui aliud euangelizaverit, praeter id quod ego vobis praedicavi, is anathematis maledictionis aeternae obnoxius est, meipsum non excipio, imo nec Angelos, si fieri posset, ut ego aliam doctrinam. strinam docerem, vel ut illi aliam proponerent quam eam, quæ prædicata est à me: Renunciandum ergo errori huic.
units.tr: Argument 7. Whoever shall preach another gospel besides that which I have preached to you is liable to the anathema of eternal damnation; I do not exclude myself, nor even angels, if it were possible that I should teach another doctrine, or that they should propose another than that which was preached by me. This error must therefore be renounced.

units.la: Vers 9. Ut ante diximus, etiam nunc iterum dico, Si quis vobis euangelizaverit prater id quod accepistis, anathema esto.
units.tr: Verse 9. As we said before, so say I now again: If any man preach any other gospel unto you than that ye have received, let him be accursed.

units.la: Hoc argumentum inculcat, ut intelligerent non ex animi perturbati- one dictum de maledictione prolata in eos, qui vel contra, vel præter doctrinam ipsius, Euangelio quicquam asluendum prædicarent.
units.tr: This argument he repeats so that they may understand that the curse pronounced against those who preach anything to be added to the gospel, whether against his doctrine or beyond it, was not spoken in a disturbed state of mind.

units.la: Vers. 10. Nunc enim utrum homines an Deum suadeo? aut quaero hominibus placere: Enimvero si adhuc hominibus placerem, Christi servus non essem.
units.tr: Verse 10. For do I now persuade men, or God? or do I seek to please men? For if I yet pleased men, I should not be the servant of Christ.

units.la: Arg. 8. A comparatione sui cum Pseudapostolis: Mea doctrina non audiendos homines suadet, sicut seductorum vestrorum doctrina, qui autoritatem tot Judæorum semper crepant. Sed suadet doctrina mea, audiendum esse Deum: Ego non quæro ut hominibus placeam, sicut seductores vestri, qui in vestri seductione gratum facere student Judæis non conversis, vel legis superstitiose zelotis: Renunciandum ergo errori quem illi vos docuerunt.
units.tr: Argument 8. From a comparison of himself with the false apostles: My doctrine does not persuade us to listen to men, as the doctrine of your seducers does, who constantly boast of the authority of so many Jews. But my doctrine persuades us that God is to be obeyed. I do not seek to please men, as your seducers do, who in seducing you take pains to please the unconverted Jews or the superstitious zealots of the Law. This error which they taught you must therefore be renounced.

units.la: Enimvero ] Confirmat hoc argumentum. Quia si studeret adhuc placere hominibus, sicut olim fecerat cum Pharifæus esset, non posset esse Christi servus, sed hominum, eorum scilicet quibus placere studeret.
units.tr: For ] He confirms this argument. For if he were still striving to please men, as he once did when he was a Pharisee, he could not be a servant of Christ, but of men, namely of those whom he was striving to please.

units.la: Vers. 11. Notum autem vobis facio, fratres, Euangelium prædicatum à me non esse secundum hominem.
units.tr: Verse 11. But I certify unto you, brethren, that the gospel which was preached of me is not after man.

units.la: Vers. 12. Neque enim ego ab homine id accepi, neque edoctus sum, sed patefaciente mihi Iesu Christo.
units.tr: Verse 12. For I neither received it of man, neither was I taught it, but by the revelation of Jesus Christ.

units.la: Arg. 9. Doctrina mea cœlestis est, ex immediata revelatione Dei, non ab homine confiɛta, nec per hominem merum ordinario modo à Deo ad me derivata, sed immediatè revelata per Iesum Christum: Ergo debetis perseverare in ea, & errori contrario renunciare.
units.tr: Argument 9. My doctrine is heavenly, derived from the immediate revelation of God, not devised by man, nor conveyed to me from God by an ordinary way through mere man, but revealed immediately through Jesus Christ. Therefore you ought to persevere in it and renounce the contrary error.

units.la: Tertia Pars.
units.tr: Third Part.

units.la: Vers. 13. Audistis enim quomodo versatus sum olim in Judaismo, me videlicet summè persequutum esse Ecclesiam DEI, & eam vastasse.
units.tr: Verse 13. For you have heard how I formerly conducted myself in Judaism, namely that I persecuted the Church of God most severely and laid it waste.

units.la: Hujus rei signa dat sex hoc Capite: Primum est hostilis animus quem gerebat adversus CHRISTUM, & ipsius Ecclesiam, olim cum Pharisæus esset. quem animum nunquam mutasset, nisi Deus de Cœlo convictum convertillet ad fidem.
units.tr: In this chapter he gives six signs of this. The first is the hostile spirit he bore against Christ and his Church while he was still a Pharisee. He would never have changed that spirit unless God had converted him to the faith by striking him down from heaven.

units.la: Verf. 14. Et profecisse in Judaismo super multos æquales meos in genere meo, quum vehementiore studio tenerer traditionum quas à patribus meis acceperam.
units.tr: Verse 14. And I advanced in Judaism beyond many of my own age in my nation, since I was held with the greater zeal by the traditions which I had received from my fathers.

units.la: Secundum signum est, quod scientiâ Legis, & zelo paternarum traditionum falsinatus, Euangelii veritatem nec videre, nec ferre potuerit, nisi divinitus de veritate edoctus, nedum ejus mysteria intima scire & prædicare.
units.tr: The second sign is that, corrupted by his knowledge of the Law and his zeal for ancestral traditions, he could neither see nor bear the truth of the Gospel, unless he had been taught that truth by God. Much less could he have known or preached its inner mysteries.

units.la: Verf. 15. Sed quando placuit Deo, qui separavit me ob utero matris meæ, & vocavit per gratiam suam,
units.tr: Verse 15. But when it pleased God, who set me apart from my mother's womb and called me through his grace,

units.la: Verf. 16. Ketegere Filium suum in me, ut euangelizarem ipsum inter Gentes, non statim contuli cum carne & sanguine.
units.tr: Verse 16. to reveal his Son in me, that I might preach him among the Gentiles, I did not immediately confer with flesh and blood.

units.la: Tertium signum est admiranda & gratuita ipsius vocatio ad fidem & Apostolatum, (cujus historia habetur, Act. 9.) potenter fluens à Dei prædestinantis consilio. Quam gratiam clarissime quidem patefecit Deus in ipsius legatione ad Gentes, viam vero ad gratiæ manifestationem æternebat providentia, in ejus nativitate & educatione: Quod enim talibus parentibus, tali corporis temperamento, & constitutione natus sit, quod ad pedes Gamalielis educatus esset, quod Pharisæus fuerit, quod Dei providentia de ipso, in omnibus, præcipuâ observatione digna comperta sit, effecit ut diceret se ab utero se præparatum, & paratum, ad prædicandum Euangelium Gentibus: adeo ad præparationem Apostoli ad hoc negotium, faciebant ex Dei consilio omnia.
units.tr: The third sign is his wonderful and undeserved calling to faith and apostleship (the history of which is in Acts 9), flowing powerfully from the counsel of God who predestines. God made this grace most clearly manifest in his mission to the Gentiles, but providence prepared the way for that manifestation in his birth and upbringing. That he was born of such parents, with such bodily temperament and constitution; that he was educated at the feet of Gamaliel; that he was a Pharisee; and that God's providence concerning him is found in all things worthy of special notice, caused him to say that he was set apart from the womb and prepared to preach the Gospel to the Gentiles. So much did everything, by God's counsel, work toward the preparation of the Apostle for this task.

units.la: Non contuli ] Quartum signum, quod de certitudine oraculi, & vocatione sua immediata tam manifeste convictus, & persuasionis firmæ satis superque habens, non aulus fuerit deliberare de re tam certa, neque humanas rationes & consilia audire, quæ possent ipsum ab obedientia vocationis avocare.
units.tr: I did not confer] The fourth sign: being so clearly convinced of the certainty of the oracle and of his immediate calling, and having more than enough firm persuasion, he did not dare to deliberate about a matter so certain, nor to listen to human reasons and counsels, which might have drawn him away from obedience to his calling.

units.la: Verf. 17. Neque redii Hierosolymam ad eos qui ante me fuerant Apostoli, sed abii in Arabiam, ac denuò reversus sum Damascum.
units.tr: Verse 17. Nor did I go up to Jerusalem to those who were apostles before me, but I went away into Arabia, and returned again to Damascus.

units.la: Verf. 18. Deinde tribus post annis redii Hierosolymam, ut viserem Petrum: & mansi apud eum dies quindecim.
units.tr: Verse 18. Then after three years I went up to Jerusalem to visit Peter, and stayed with him fifteen days.

units.la: Verf. 19. Alium autem ex apostolis non vidi quenquam, nisi Iacobum fratrem Domini.
units.tr: Verse 19. But I saw none of the other apostles, except James the brother of the Lord.

units.la: Quintum signum, quod satis institutus in mysterio salutis per CHRISTUM ipsum immediate; non adierit Apostolos ante se vocatos, sed Euangelium in Arabia, & Damasci, primo triennio sui Apostolatus prædicaverit.
units.tr: The fifth sign: being sufficiently instructed in the mystery of salvation immediately by Christ himself, he did not approach the apostles who had been called before him. Instead, he preached the Gospel in Arabia and Damascus during the first three years of his apostleship.

units.la: Et post triennium, Hierosolymam profectus, inviserit Petrum & Iacobum solos, paucos apud eos dies commoratus, idque familiaritatis, non cognitionis suæ confirmandæ causâ.
units.tr: After three years, having set out for Jerusalem, he visited Peter and James alone, staying with them only a few days, and that for the sake of familiarity rather than to confirm his knowledge.

units.la: Vers. 20. In iis porrò quæ scribo vobis, ecce coram Deo, non mentior.
units.tr: Verse 20. Now in what I write to you, behold, before God, I do not lie.

units.la: In cujus historiæ confirmationem, præter testes in vivis agentes, qui rei tam notabilis ignari esse non poterant, juramentum adhibet.
units.tr: To confirm this account, besides witnesses who were still living and could not have been ignorant of so notable a matter, he adds an oath.

units.la: Vers. 21. Deinde veni in regiones Syriæ & Ciliciæ.
units.tr: Verse 21. Then I came into the regions of Syria and Cilicia.

units.la: Vers. 22. Eram autem ignotus facie Ecclesiis Judææ, quæ erant in Christo;
units.tr: Verse 22. And I was unknown by face to the churches of Judea which were in Christ;

units.la: Vers. 23. Sed solùm audierant qui dicerent, Qui persequeba-tur nos aliquando, nunc annuntiat fidem quam olim vastabat.
units.tr: Verse 23. But they had only heard it said: He who once persecuted us now preaches the faith which he once laid waste.

units.la: Vers. 24. Et glorificabant Deum de me.
units.tr: Verse 24. And they glorified God in me.

units.la: Sextum signum, quod publicè docuerit, idque Apostolicâ autoritate in Syria, & Ciliciâ, approbantibus Apostolis, & Ecclesiis omnibus, & nominatim Judæis fidelibus, qui ipsum nunquam viderant, de ipsius tamen conversione à persecutore in prædicatorem certiores facti, Deum glorificabant. Quæ omnia signa, fidem faciunt de Doctrinæ ipsius cœlesti origine.
units.tr: The sixth sign: he taught publicly, and with apostolic authority, in Syria and Cilicia, with the apostles and all the churches approving. Especially the faithful Jews, who had never seen him, glorified God when they were informed of his change from persecutor to preacher. All these signs make it certain that his doctrine has a heavenly origin.

units.la: Caput Secundum.
units.tr: Chapter 2.

units.la: VÆ sunt Capitis partes, In prima pergit historiam texere quam narrabat, & Apostolatus sui, seu divinæ doctrinæ suæ, signa reliqua adaere, ad vers. 15. Reliqun capite, justitiam esse ex fide, & non ex operibus legis, confirmat.
units.tr: There are two parts to this chapter. In the first, he goes on to relate the history he was narrating and to add the remaining signs of his apostleship, or of his divine doctrine, down to verse 15. In the rest of the chapter, he confirms that justification is by faith, and not by the works of the law.

units.la: Verf. 1. DEinde interjectis annis quatuordecim, rursum ascendi Hierosolymam, una cum Barnaba, assumpto simul & Tito.
units.tr: Verse 1. Then, after fourteen years had passed, I went up again to Jerusalem with Barnabas, taking Titus along with me also.

units.la: Verf. 2. Ascendi autem ex revelatione, & exposui eis Evangelium quod prædico inter Gentes: sed privatim cum eis qui sunt in pretio, ne quomodo frustra currerem aut cucurrissem.
units.tr: Verse 2. I went up in obedience to a revelation, and I set before them the gospel that I preach among the Gentiles, but privately before those who were of repute, lest somehow I should run, or had run, in vain.

units.la: Præcesserunt lex signa cœlestis & divinæ doctrinæ Apostoli, sequuntur quinque alia signa: Primum, Quod Deus Ministerii ipsius curriculum speciali revelatione direxerit, ut quo & quorsum proficisceretur sciret, cujus exemplum ponit in ascensu Hierosolymam ex revelatione: quæ revelatio erat Apostolatus, & doctrinæ ipsius, divina approbatio.
units.tr: The signs of the Apostle's heavenly and divine doctrine that have gone before are now followed by five others. The first is that God directed the course of his ministry by a special revelation, so that he would know where and whither he was going. Paul gives an example of this when he says he went up to Jerusalem by revelation. That revelation was a divine approval of his apostleship and of his doctrine.

units.la: Exposui ] Signum 2. Quod doctrinæ suæ inter Gentes traditæ rationem cum Apostolis communicaverit, ut ipsius consensus cum illis patefieret, & nominatim cum Petro Iacobo & Ioanne, ne fructu Ministerii sui, apud quosdam privaretur, per æmulorum calumnias, qui dissentire Apostoli Pauli doctrinam, à reliquorum Apostolorum doctrinâ mentiebantur.
units.tr: I set before them] The second sign: he communicated the account of the doctrine he had delivered among the Gentiles to the Apostles, so that its agreement with theirs would be made plain, and especially with Peter, James and John. This was so that he would not be deprived of the fruit of his ministry among some people, through the slanders of rivals who falsely claimed that Paul's teaching dissented from the doctrine of the other Apostles.

units.la: Verf. 3. Sed neque Titus qui mecum erat, quum esset Græcus, coactus fuit circumcidi.
units.tr: Verse 3. But not even Titus, who was with me, though he was a Greek, was compelled to be circumcised.

units.la: Verf. 4. Nempe propter emissarios falsos fratres qui irrepserant ad explorandam libertatem nostram quam habemus in Christo Iesu, ut nos in servitutem adigerent:
units.tr: Verse 4. This was because of false brothers, secretly brought in, who had slipped in to spy out our freedom that we have in Christ Jesus, so that they might bring us into bondage.

units.la: Verf. 5 Quibus ne ad momentum quidem cessimus per subjectionem, ut veritas Evangelii permaneret apud vos.
units.tr: Verse 5. To them we did not yield in submission even for an hour, so that the truth of the gospel might remain with you.

units.la: Signum 3, Quod coram Apostolis, hanc ipsam causam de liberatione Christianorum à jugo circumcisionis, in persona Titi egerit: eumque defenderit ne circumcideretur, contra falsos fratres, qui præreptum ibant fidelibus libertatem Christianam, ut in servitutem redigerent Ecclesias Christi, quibus Apostolus minimè cessit, ut sinceritas doctrinæ Evangelii inter Gentes, & nominatim inter Galatas, inviolata permaneret; quod evidens erat signum cœlestis & divinæ ipsius doctrinæ, in qua Galatas instituerat.
units.tr: The third sign: before the Apostles he pleaded this very cause, the liberation of Christians from the yoke of circumcision, in the person of Titus. He defended Titus against being circumcised, against false brothers who were trying to snatch away Christian liberty from the faithful, in order to reduce the churches of Christ to slavery. The Apostle did not yield to them at all, so that the purity of the doctrine of the gospel among the Gentiles, and especially among the Galatians, would remain unviolated. This was a clear sign of the heavenly and divine character of the doctrine in which he had instructed the Galatians.

units.la: Verf. 6 Ab iis autem qui putantur esse aliquid, qualescunque fuerint, nihil mihi differepat, personam hominis Deus non accipit: nam qui sunt in pretio, nihil mecum præterea contulerunt. Signum 4. Cujus 4. Sunt membra, 1. membrum, Quod Apostoli præcipui qui vocabantur, Petrus, Jacobus, & Johannes, audita ejus Doctrina, nihil correxerint, nihil addiderint ejus cognitioni: Interim occurrit objectioni de eorum personalibus prærogativis, de quibus non vult agere, veluti quod viderint Christum in carne, quod priores vocati sint ad Apostolatum, quod consanguinitate Christum propius attigerint, &c.
