Quia illa & similia ad doctrinam, ad Apostolicam auctoritatem, ad commendationem hominis coram Deo, nihil faciebant, cum Deus personas hominum non acceptet.
units.tr: Verse 6. But from those who are considered to be something, whatever they were, it makes no difference to me; God does not accept the person of man. For those who were of repute added nothing to me. The fourth sign has four parts. The first part is that the leading Apostles, who were called Peter, James and John, when they heard his doctrine, corrected nothing and added nothing to his knowledge. Meanwhile, he meets the objection about their personal privileges, which he does not wish to discuss: that they saw Christ in the flesh, that they were called to the apostleship earlier, that they were closer to Christ by kinship, and so on. For such things, and others like them, had no bearing on the doctrine, on apostolic authority, or on a man's commendation before God, since God does not accept the persons of men.

units.la: Verf. 7. Imo è contrario quum vidissent mihi concreditum fuisse Euangelium præputii: sicut Petro circumcisionis;
units.tr: Verse 7. On the contrary, when they saw that the gospel of the uncircumcision had been committed to me, just as the gospel of the circumcision was to Peter,

units.la: Verf. 8. (Nam qui efficax fuit per Petrum ad Apostolatum circumcisionis, efficax fuit etiam per me erga Gentes)
units.tr: Verse 8. (for he who worked effectively through Peter in his apostleship to the circumcision also worked effectively through me toward the Gentiles).

units.la: Secundum membrum, Quod Apostoli illi tres, Apostolatum Pauli inter Gentes agnoverint, non minus autoritatis & efficaciæ à Deo habuisse, quam Petri Apostolatum inter Judæos.
units.tr: The second part is that those three Apostles acknowledged that Paul's apostleship among the Gentiles had no less authority and efficacy from God than Peter's apostleship among the Jews.

units.la: Verf. 9. Quumque cognovissent gratiam mihi datam, Iacobus & Cephas & Iohannes, qui putantur esse columnæ, dextras dederunt mihi ac Barnabæ societatis; ut nos inter Gentes, ipsi vero inter circuncisos, Apostolatu fungeremur.
units.tr: Verse 9. And when James, Cephas and John, who are considered to be pillars, had recognised the grace given to me, they gave the right hands of fellowship to me and Barnabas, that we should go to the Gentiles, and they to the circumcised.

units.la: Tertium membrum, Quod tres illi Apostoli perspectis donis & signis Apostolatus in Paulo, dextram societatis dederint Paulo & Barnabæ, ut pari autoritate fungerentur officio Apostolico inter Gentes, ac ipsi inter Judæos.
units.tr: The third part is that those three Apostles, having observed the gifts and signs of apostleship in Paul, gave the right hand of fellowship to Paul and Barnabas, so that they might carry out the apostolic office among the Gentiles with the same authority as they themselves had among the Jews.

units.la: Verf. 10. Solum monuerunt ut pauperum meminissemus: quod & ipsum studui facere.
units.tr: Verse 10. They only asked us to remember the poor, which very thing I was also eager to do.

units.la: Quartum membrum, Quod tres illi Paulum & Barnabam rogaverint ut collectam procurarent faciendam ab Ecclesiis Gentium, in usum pauperum Judæorum, id quod Paulus & Barnabas strenuè præstiterunt.
units.tr: The fourth part is that those three asked Paul and Barnabas to arrange a collection to be made from the churches of the Gentiles for the use of the poor Jews. Paul and Barnabas carried this out diligently.

units.la: Verf. 11. Quum autem venisset Petrus Antiochiam, in os ei restiti, eo quod condemnandus esset.
units.tr: Verse 11. But when Peter came to Antioch, I withstood him to his face, because he stood condemned.

units.la: Signum 5. Cœlestis & divinæ ipsius doctrinæ, nominatim in articulo de vitando jugo ceremoniali Moisis, est. Quod Paulus ipsum Petrum facto deflectentem ab hac doctrina, palam reprehenderit, & in viam reduxerit: quæ res tota ut melius appareat observanda sunt quæ sequuntur. Decreto Synodi Hierosolymitanæ, Act. 15. Necessitas ceremonialis legis inter Judæos abrogata elt, & libertate relicta Judæis, utendi ceremoniis ad tempus ! ab Ecclesiis Christianis inter Gentes arcetur omnis Leviticarum ceremoniarum observatio, utpote quibus lex de ceremoniis nullo modo, unquam data aut destinata est: Tantùm jubentur in esculentis nonnullis temperare sibi, ne libertate utantur cum scandalo infirmorum Judæorum,idque vi moralis legis, quæ in rebus simpliciter mediis libertatis usum scandali cancellis circumscribit: Petrus Apostolus Antiochiam descendens, ex decreti Synodi Hierosolymitanæ sententia, libertate sua utitur, & cibum sumit cum fratribus Gentilibus; descendunt interea à Jacobo Antiochiam, nonnulli, qui tenaces erant ceremoniarum Mosis: debebat hic Petrus Christianam libertatem quam pridie profitebatur minimè dissimulare, sed in consortio cum Christianis Gentilibus manere, & factum suum, auctoritate Synodi defendere; sed metuens Petrus ne incurreret in odium Judæorum, qui à Jacobo descenderant, subducit se à mensâ Christianorum Gentilium, & non amplius edit cum illis; Petri exemplum imitantur alii: Serpit malum, ad Barnabam etiam in eandem dissimulationem trahendum: malò hoc exemplo scandalum ponebatur Judæis, ut confirmarentur in Judaismo; ne Jugum Mosis (jam authoritate Dei in Synodo solutum, & confractum) unquam deponerent; scandalum etiam ponitur Gentilibus Christianis, qui exemplo tanti Apostoli coguntur, vel ceremoniarum Jugum suscipere, vel Apostoli societati renunciare; Paulus quid hic ex officio faceret? certè sicut decebat, restitit Petro in os, eumque publicè reprehendit.
units.tr: The fifth sign is of his heavenly and divine doctrine, especially in the article concerning the avoidance of the ceremonial yoke of Moses. In that Paul openly rebuked Peter, who had turned aside from this doctrine by his conduct, and brought him back to the right way. To see this matter more clearly, the following points must be noted. By the decree of the Synod of Jerusalem (Acts 15), the necessity of the ceremonial law among the Jews was abolished, and while the Jews were left free to use the ceremonies for a time, the observance of the Levitical ceremonies was entirely excluded from the Christian churches among the Gentiles, since the law of ceremonies was in no way ever given or intended for them. They were only commanded to abstain from certain foods, so that they would not use their liberty to the scandal of the weak Jews. This was enjoined by the force of the moral law, which limits the use of liberty in matters that are indifferent by the bounds of avoiding scandal. Peter the Apostle, going down to Antioch, in accordance with the judgment of the decree of the Synod of Jerusalem, used his liberty and ate with the Gentile brothers. Meanwhile, some people who were zealous for the ceremonies of Moses came down from James to Antioch. Peter ought not to have concealed the Christian liberty that he had professed the day before, but should have remained in fellowship with the Gentile Christians and defended his action by the authority of the Synod. But Peter, fearing that he would incur the hatred of the Jews who had come down from James, withdrew himself from the table of the Gentile Christians and no longer ate with them. Others imitated Peter's example. The evil spread, and even Barnabas was drawn into the same dissimulation. By this bad example a stumbling block was placed before the Jews, so that they would be confirmed in Judaism and would never lay down the yoke of Moses (which had now been loosed and broken by the authority of God in the Synod). A stumbling block was also placed before the Gentile Christians, who by the example of so great an Apostle were compelled either to take up the yoke of ceremonies or to renounce fellowship with the Apostle. What, then, should Paul have done in his office? Certainly, as was fitting, he withstood Peter to his face and rebuked him publicly.

units.la: Vers. 12. Nam antequam venissent quidam à Jacobo, unà cum Gentibus edebat: quum autem venissent, subduxit se, ac separavit ab eis, metuens eos qui erant ex circumcisione.
units.tr: Verse 12. For before certain men came from James, he ate with the Gentiles; but when they came, he drew back and separated himself from them, fearing those who were of the circumcision.

units.la: Rationes reprehensionis sunt tres: Ratio prima, Quia dissimulavit Christianorum liberationem à jugo Mosis, ex metu odii Judæorum aliquot, cum metuere oportuisset potius, ne scandalum poneret Judæis vel Gentibus.
units.tr: There are three reasons for the rebuke. The first reason: he dissembled about the liberation of Christians from the yoke of Moses, out of fear of the hatred of certain Jews, when he ought rather to have feared putting a stumbling block before the Jews or the Gentiles.

units.la: Vers. 13. Ac simulabant unà cum eo reliqui etiam Judæi; itaque etiam Barnabas simul abreptus fuit in illorum simulationem.
units.tr: Verse 13. And the rest of the Jews dissembled along with him, so that even Barnabas was carried away by their dissimulation.

units.la: Ratio 2. Quia exemplo suo trahebat alios in eandem secum dissimulationem.
units.tr: The second reason: by his example he drew others into the same dissimulation along with himself.

units.la: Ratio 3. Verf. 14. Sed quum vidissem eos non recto pede incedere, ut veritati Euangelii congruebat, dixi Petro coram omnibus, Si tu, quum sis Judæus, Gentiliter vivis, ac non Judaice, cur Gentes cogis judaizare?
units.tr: The third reason. Verse 14. But when I saw that they were not walking uprightly, according to the truth of the gospel, I said to Peter before them all, "If you, though you are a Jew, live like a Gentile and not like a Jew, why do you compel the Gentiles to live like Jews?"

units.la: Ratio 3. Propter quam jure Paulus reprehendit Petrum, quia cum prædicaret hominem justificari sola fide, sine operibus legis, facto hoc suo, confirmabat falsam doctrinam eorum, qui legem Moisis ad salutem necessario observandam docebant: quod erat claudicare in cursu suo, versus Euangelicæ veritatis metam; seu rationem pessimam inire, ut doctrinam gratiæ puram conservaret. Quod Pauli factum erat signum manifestissimum, doctrinam ipsius quam Ecclesias Galatiæ docuerat de justificatione per Christi gratiam, & de liberatione a jugo ceremoniarum, fuisse adeo Cœlestem & divinam, ut ex ea convicerit ipsum Petrum erroris, quando consentanea huic doctrinæ non faciebat.
units.tr: The third reason is the one for which Paul rightly rebuked Peter. Although he was preaching that a man is justified by faith alone, without the works of the law, by this conduct of his he confirmed the false doctrine of those who taught that the law of Moses had to be observed as necessary for salvation. This meant he was limping in his course toward the goal of evangelical truth, or was taking a very bad course in order to preserve the pure doctrine of grace. Paul's action was a most manifest sign that the doctrine he had taught the churches of Galatia, concerning justification by the grace of Christ and concerning liberation from the yoke of ceremonies, was so heavenly and divine that by it he convicted Peter himself of error, when Peter did not act in agreement with this doctrine.

units.la: Secunda pars.
units.tr: Second part.

units.la: Verf. 15. Nos natura Judæi, & non ex Gentibus peccatores:
units.tr: Verse 15. We are Jews by nature, and not sinners from among the Gentiles:

units.la: Verf. 16 Scientes non justificari hominem ex operibus Legis, sed per fidem Iesu Christi; etiam nos inquam in Christum Iesum credidimus, ut justificaremur ex fide Christi, & non ex operibus Legis: propterea quod non justificabitur ex operibus legis caro ulla:
units.tr: Verse 16. Knowing that a man is not justified by the works of the Law, but by faith in Jesus Christ; even we, I say, have believed in Christ Jesus, so that we might be justified by the faith of Christ and not by the works of the Law, because no flesh shall be justified by the works of the Law:

units.la: Ex occasione disceptationis suæ cum Petro, dilabitur Paulus ad alteram Partem Capitis, in qua sicut in Epistola ad Romanos, confirmat, justificationem non esse ex operibus legis, sed tantum ex fide, quam doctrinam dum asserit, sermonem suum habitum ad Petrum repetit, ut scirent omnes non se aliud docuisse Galatas, quam quod palam (audientibus plurimis fidelibus ex Judæis & Gentibus) ad Petri convictionem loquens antea docuerat & defenderat, nempe. Nos natura Judæi, &c. Quorum verborum sensus est, si referantur ad Petrum. Nos qui Judæi natura, seu propagatione, ex fœdere cum Deo sancti sumus, & non peccatores, id est, alieni à fœdere, ut Gentes; nos (inquit) Judæi & Apostoli, scientes hominem justificari non ex operibus legis, sed per fidem Christi, confugimus fide ad Christum, in hunc finem ut justificemur fide & non operibus legis. Ergo non sunt cogendi Gentiles ad judaizandum daizandum, & ad jugum legis subeundum, quasi essent ullo modo sub fœdere operum.
units.tr: Arising from his dispute with Peter, Paul turns to the second part of the chapter, in which, as in the Epistle to the Romans, he confirms that justification is not by the works of the Law but by faith alone. In asserting this doctrine he returns to the speech he had addressed to Peter, so that everyone would know that he had taught the Galatians nothing other than what he had openly taught and defended before, when he spoke to Peter's rebuke in the hearing of many believers from both Jews and Gentiles, namely: We are Jews by nature, etc. The sense of these words, if they are referred to Peter, is this: we who are Jews by nature, that is by birth, are holy by covenant with God and are not sinners, that is, aliens from the covenant as the Gentiles are; we (he says), Jews and Apostles, knowing that a man is justified not by the works of the Law but through faith in Christ, have fled by faith to Christ, to this end, that we might be justified by faith and not by the works of the Law. Therefore the Gentiles are not to be compelled to Judaize, or to submit to the yoke of the Law, as if they were in any way under the covenant of works.

units.la: Si vero referantur hæc verba ad principale institutum, propositio est doctrinæ, & in specie illius, quam docuerat Galatas, & ad quam revertı eos jam hortatur, in hunc sensum; Nos Judæi qui ex fœdere nascimur Sanctus Dei populus, & non alieni à fœdere, ut vos Gentes, renunciare cogimur operibus legis in causa justificationis, & justitiam quærere per fidem in Christum. Ergo multo magis id vobis Gentilibus Galatis est faciendum: Hanc doctrinam deinceps confirmat hoc capite tribus argumentis, solutis interim obiter objectionibus.
units.tr: If, however, these words are referred to the principal purpose of the letter, they state the proposition of the doctrine, and in particular of that which he had taught the Galatians and to which he now urges them to return, in this sense: we Jews, who are born within the covenant, the holy people of God, and are not aliens from the covenant as you Gentiles are, are compelled to renounce the works of the Law as the cause of justification, and to seek righteousness by faith in Christ. Therefore it must much more be done by you Gentile Galatians. He confirms this doctrine in this chapter with three arguments, meanwhile resolving objections on the way.

units.la: Argumentum primum, Nulla caro justificabitur ex operibus Legis: ergo neque Judæi neque Gentes.
units.tr: The first argument: no flesh will be justified by the works of the Law; therefore neither Jews nor Gentiles.

units.la: Vers. 17. Quod si, dum quærimus justificari per CHRISTUM, reperimur & ipsi peccatores, num Christus peccati Minister est? Absit.
units.tr: Verse 17. But if, while we seek to be justified by Christ, we ourselves are found to be sinners, is Christ then a minister of sin? By no means.

units.la: Conversâ oratione ad Galatas, solvit objectionem adversariorum; Dicerent adversarii, Si dum quæritis per Christum justificari, & non per legem seu opera, comperimini peccatores, ut ex vestra ipsorum confessione, & ore vestro, licet de vobis judicare; tum licebit vobis Christianis per fidem Christi justificatis, peccato indulgere; & per vos, Christus erit author, & Minister, seu Doctor peccati, ut ejus auctoritate peccetis.
units.tr: Turning his speech to the Galatians, he answers an objection of the opponents. The opponents would say: if, while you seek to be justified by Christ and not by the Law or works, you are found to be sinners, as by your own confession and from your own mouth (we may judge you thus), then it will be lawful for you Christians, justified by faith in Christ, to indulge in sin; and through you, Christ will be the author, minister, or teacher of sin, so that you sin by his authority.

units.la: Respondet aversando objectum, ut blasphemiam: Absit (inquit) confidenter negans sequi ex doctrina justificationis, licere justificato per fidem, indulgere peccato, vel Christum peccati Ministrum seu Doctorem dici posse.
units.tr: He replies by rejecting the consequence as blasphemy: By no means, he says, confidently denying that it follows from the doctrine of justification that a man justified by faith may indulge in sin, or that Christ can be called a minister or teacher of sin.

units.la: Ver. 18. Nam si quæ destruxi, ea rursum ædifico, transgressorem meipsum constituo.
units.tr: Verse 18. For if I rebuild what I have destroyed, I make myself a transgressor.

units.la: Responsionis rationes reddit quatuor: Prima hæc est, Ego confugiendo ad justificationem per fidem Christi, inivi solidam rationem ad destruendum peccatum, quia confugi ad Christum, ut & remittat mihi peccatum, & gratiam suppeditet ad mortificationem peccati; Si igitur rursum operam darem peccato (sicut objicitur) & opus Diaboli rursum ædificarem in me, mihi ipsi contrarius essem; transgredererer rationem jam positam ad peccatum destruendum, atque ita stolidus & insanus essem, doctrinam justificationis per fidem minimè sequens: Ergo ex principiis justificationis per fidem, impossibile est ut abutar gratia, seu CHRISTI nomine, ad liberius peccandum.
units.tr: He gives four reasons for his answer. The first is this: by fleeing to justification by faith in Christ, I have laid a firm foundation for destroying sin, because I have fled to Christ, that he may both forgive me my sin and supply grace for the mortifying of sin. If then I were to labour again at sin (as is objected) and rebuild in myself the work of the devil, I would be contrary to myself; I would overturn the foundation already laid for destroying sin, and so I would be foolish and mad, not at all following the doctrine of justification by faith. Therefore, from the principles of justification by faith, it is impossible that I should abuse grace, or the name of Christ, for the sake of sinning more freely.

units.la: Verf. 19. Ego enim per Legem Legi mortuus sum, ut DEO viverem.
units.tr: Verse 19. For I through the Law died to the Law, that I might live to God.

units.la: Ratio 2. Ego per vim legis, interfectus sum in CHRISTI internecione, & respectu legis seu foederis legalis mortuus sum legi, & sic liberatus a foedere legis, eo fine, non ut indulgerem peccato, sed ut viverem DEO, & ipsi obedirem. Ergo ex hujus Doctrinae principiis peccato indulgere non possum. Valet argumentum, nam si per Legem seu foedus operum, CHRISTUS justificandorum nomine mortuus est, eo fine ut justificati viverent DEO; Impossibile est ut justificati qui in CHRISTO legi mortui, & a foedere operum liberati censeri volunt, non etiam agnoscant teneri se vivere DEO, & per consequens se non debere peccato indulgere.
units.tr: Reason 2. Through the force of the Law I was put to death in the destruction of Christ, and with respect to the Law, or the legal covenant, I died to the Law, and so was freed from the covenant of the Law, not to this end that I should indulge in sin, but that I should live to God and obey him. Therefore, from the principles of this doctrine I cannot indulge in sin. The argument holds: for if through the Law, or the covenant of works, Christ died in the name of those to be justified, to this end, that the justified should live to God, then it is impossible that those justified who want to be considered dead to the Law in Christ and freed from the covenant of works should not also acknowledge that they are bound to live to God, and consequently that they must not indulge in sin.

units.la: Verf. 20. Una cum Christo crucifixus sum. Vivo autem, non amplius ego, sed vivit in me Christus: & vitam quam nunc vivo in carne, vivo per fidem Filii Dei, qui dilexit me, & tradidit semetipsum pro me.
units.tr: Verse 20. I have been crucified with Christ. Yet I live, but not now I, but Christ lives in me: and the life which I now live in the flesh, I live by the faith of the Son of God, who loved me and gave himself for me.

units.la: Ratio 3. Priorem confirmans: Ego fide justificatus, judicialiter unitus sum Christo crucifixo, & in illo, ad moriendum peccato, & ad crucifigendum veterem hominem judicialiter obstringor: Ergo peccato indulgere ex principiis doctrinae de justificatione per fidem, non possum. Ratio haec est; CHRISTUS Sponsor in cruce, non tantum expiavit peccata redemptorum, sed etiam ipsorum nomine spopondit fore, ut morerentur peccato, & crucifigerent corruptam suam naturam. Ergo qui per fidem apprehendit judicialem unionem sui cum CHRISTO crucifixo, agnoscat etiam necesse est obligationem suam, ad moriendum peccato, seu ad crucifigendam veterem suam naturam per virtutem CHRISTI.
units.tr: Reason 3, confirming the previous one: I, justified by faith, am judicially united with Christ crucified, and in him am judicially bound to die to sin and to crucify the old man. Therefore I cannot indulge in sin from the principles of the doctrine of justification by faith. The reasoning is this: Christ, as surety on the cross, not only made atonement for the sins of the redeemed, but also in their name promised that they would die to sin and crucify their corrupt nature. Therefore whoever apprehends by faith his judicial union with Christ crucified must also necessarily acknowledge his own obligation to die to sin, or to crucify his old nature, by the power of Christ.

units.la: Vivo autem] Ratio 4. Ego justificatus fide, nova sum creatura per Spiritum CHRISTI in me viventem, ita ut non amplius ego, quoad veterem hominem, vivam. sed CHRISTUS, in me habitans vita hac naturali utatur ut organo, & membro suo, efficiatque ut per fidem, in virtute ipsius, vitam hanc agam negotia mea omnia curem, & ut Spiritum in DEI obedientia quasi ducam, idque ex eadem dilectione sua erga me, qua mortuus est pro me. Ergo peccato induigere ex principiis fidei justificantis non possum. Argumenti vis breviter hæc est, justificatos nos per fidem Christi Spiritus animat ad sanctè vivendum. Ergo justificatio per fidem non laxat habenas peccato.
units.tr: But I live] Reason 4. I, justified by faith, am a new creature through the Spirit of Christ living in me, so that I no longer live, as regards the old man, but Christ lives in me; he dwells in me and uses this natural life as his instrument and member, and brings it about that by faith, in his power, I live this life, attend to all my affairs, and, as it were, lead my spirit into obedience to God, and this from the same love of his toward me by which he died for me. Therefore I cannot indulge in sin from the principles of justifying faith. The force of the argument is briefly this: having been justified through the faith of Christ, we are animated by his Spirit to live holily. Therefore justification by faith does not loosen the reins for sin.

units.la: Verf. 21. Non abrogo gratiam Dei, nam si per Legem est justitia, igitur Christus sine causa mortuus est.
units.tr: Verse 21. I do not set aside the grace of God; for if righteousness is through the Law, then Christ died in vain.

units.la: Sublata est objectio: Sequitur Argumentum secundum pro justificatione per Fidem, & non per opera Legis: Si justificatio sit per opera Legis, frustra est Gratia Dei, & irrita redditur; nam si Justificatio sit per Opera, non potest esse per Gratiam, ut Rom. Cap. 11. verf. 6. Absit autem ut ego irritam faciam gratiam: Absit igitur etiam ut Justificationem statuam per Opera.
units.tr: The objection is removed. There follows the second argument for justification by faith and not by the works of the Law: if justification were by the works of the Law, the grace of God would be in vain and made void; for if justification is by works, it cannot be by grace, as Rom. 11, verse 6. Far be it, then, that I should make grace void; far be it therefore that I should establish justification by works.

units.la: Nam si Arg. 3. Si per Legem est Justificatio, Christus frustra est mortuus, quia tum & aliter, & facilius obtineri potuisset Justificatio, quam per Christi mortem: At absurdum est Christum frustra mortuum esse. Ergo non per Legem, sed per Fidem est Justificatio.
units.tr: For if Third argument. If justification is by the Law, Christ died in vain, because justification could then have been obtained in another way and more easily than by the death of Christ. But it is absurd that Christ died in vain. Therefore justification is not by the Law but by faith.

units.la: Caput Tertium.
units.tr: Chapter 3.

units.la: Mentes Galatæ, quis vos fascinavit, ne obsequeremini veritati; quibus ob oculos Iesus Christus prius fuerat depictus, inter vos crucifixus? Verf. 1.
units.tr: O foolish Galatians, who has bewitched you, that you should not obey the truth, before whose eyes Jesus Christ was set forth, crucified among you? Verse 1.

units.la: QUia sciebat animos Galatarum falsa opinione præoccupatos, idcirco ne ad sequentem disputationem languerent, gravi objurgatione veterum iis excutit, & quatuor quasi aculeis pungit ipsorum conscientias. Primo enim Amentes & Stolidos vocat; quia, licet non malitia, imprudentia tamen sua turpiter se decipi passi sunt: 2. Fascinatos vocat, id est, præstigiis impostorum dementatos: 3. Objicit illis defectionem à veritate Euangelii de Christi gratia salutifera: 4. Amplificat crimen ex eo quod tam evidenter prædicatus sit Christus inter eos, & Christi passiones, cum causis passionum ipsius, tam perspicuè explicatæ sint, quam si ad oculum depicta res tota esset in tabella.
units.tr: Because he knew that the minds of the Galatians were preoccupied with a false opinion, he therefore, so that they would not grow sluggish for the disputation that follows, shakes them with a severe rebuke and pricks their consciences with four stings. First, he calls them foolish and senseless, because, although not from malice, they had shamefully allowed themselves to be deceived through their own imprudence. Second, he calls them bewitched, that is, made mad by the tricks of impostors. Third, he charges them with defecting from the truth of the gospel concerning Christ's saving grace. Fourth, he aggravates the crime by the fact that Christ had been preached so plainly among them, and his sufferings, with their causes, had been explained as clearly as if the whole matter had been painted before the eye on a tablet.

units.la: Præmissa hac præfatione, pergit justificationem per fidem, & non per opera Legis, confirmare argumentis viginti quatuor.
units.tr: With this preface made, he goes on to confirm, by twenty-four arguments, that justification is by faith and not by the works of the Law.

units.la: Verf. 2. Hoc solum cupio discere ex vobis, Ex operibus Legù Spiritum accepistis, an ex fide per auditum percepta?
units.tr: Verse 2. I wish to learn this one thing from you: did you receive the Spirit by the works of the Law, or by faith heard through the preaching?

units.la: Argumentum primum, Vos non accepistis Spiritum regenerationis, reliquasque gratias (quibus inter vos Euangelii prædicatio obsignata est) ex operibus seu ex doctrinâ de Fœdere Operum receptâ, sed ex fide, seu ex doctrina de Fœdere Gratiæ per fidem applicata. Ergo non justificamini ex operibus, sed ex fide.
units.tr: First argument. You did not receive the Spirit of regeneration and the other graces (by which the preaching of the gospel has been confirmed among you) from works, that is, from the doctrine of the covenant of works accepted, but from faith, that is, from the doctrine of the covenant of grace applied through faith. Therefore you are justified not by works but by faith.

units.la: Verf. 3. Adeò amentes estis? quum Spiritu inceperitis, nunc carne perficimini?
units.tr: Verse 3. Are you so foolish? Having begun in the Spirit, are you now being made perfect by the flesh?

units.la: Arg. 2. Licet vobis persuaserint impostores aliqui justificationis initium esse ex fide, complementum vero habere ex operibus, damnanda tamen est hæc sententia amentia; propterea quod impossibile sit, ut spiritualis ratio justificandi per fidem, conciliat cum carnali illa ratione justificationis per opera, nedum ut illa perfectionem suam ab hac capiat. Ergo non justificamur ex operibus, sed ex fide. Dicitur autem justitia ex operibus Caro. 1. quia etiamsi jam impossibilis sit hujusmodi justificatio; carnis tamen, seu corruptæ naturæ commune figmentum est demens, justificatio hæc per opera, & per superbam, seu gloriabundam carnem passim defenditur. 2. Quia hominis irregeniti, seu non justificati per fidem, opera omnia per quæ justificationem quærit, sunt mera caro, seu corruptæ carnis effecta, quatenus proficiscuntur à non justificatis: Tam absurdum est igitur hominem justificari per opera justificationem præcedentia, quam justificari per Legis continuam violationem, seu justitiam acquirere per peccata. Quod autem ad opera quæ justificationem seu remissionem peccatorum sequuntur, non possunt esse causa rei jam præteritæ, antequam extiterunt, vel exstitere potuerunt, nisi justificationem accipias pro justificationis jam pronunciatæ à Deo, declaratione apud homines.
units.tr: Second argument. Although some impostors have persuaded you that justification begins from faith but is completed by works, this opinion is to be condemned as madness, because it is impossible for the spiritual way of being justified by faith to agree with that carnal way of justification by works, let alone for the former to receive its perfection from the latter. Therefore we are justified not by works but by faith. Now justification by works is called flesh: (1) because, although such justification is already impossible, it is a foolish fiction common to the flesh, or corrupt nature, and this justification by works is everywhere defended by the proud, or boastful, flesh; (2) because all the works of an unregenerate man, that is, one not justified by faith, by which he seeks justification, are mere flesh, or effects of corrupt flesh, insofar as they proceed from men not yet justified. It is therefore as absurd for a man to be justified by works that precede justification as it is to be justified by continual violation of the Law, that is, to acquire righteousness through sins. As for works that follow justification, or the remission of sins, they cannot be the cause of a thing already past, before they existed or could have existed, unless you take justification to mean the declaration, before men, of a justification already pronounced by God.

units.la: Verf. 4. Tam multa passi estis frustra? si modo etiam frustra.
units.tr: Verse 4. Have you suffered so many things in vain? If indeed it was in vain.

units.la: Arg. 3. Si in amentia vestra perrexeritis quærere justificationem per opera, vel partim fide, partim operibus justificari; amittetis omnem fructum constantiæ vestræ hactenus, & afflictionum, quas pro tuenda justitia per fidem jam perpessi estis, sed spero meliora. Ergo non justificamini ex operibus, sed ex fide solum.
units.tr: Third argument. If you persist in your folly in seeking justification by works, or in being justified partly by faith and partly by works, you will lose all the fruit of your constancy hitherto and of the afflictions which you have already endured for defending justification by faith, but I hope for better things. Therefore you are not justified by works but by faith alone.

units.la: Verf. 5. Qui igitur subministrat vobis Spiritum, & efficit virtutes in vobis, ex operibus Legis an ex fide per auditum percepta subministrat?
units.tr: Verse 5. He, then, who supplies you with the Spirit and works miracles among you, does he do so by the works of the Law, or by faith heard through the preaching?

units.la: Arg. 4. Ministri per quos Deus Spiritum dat, & miracula & virtutes operatur inter vos, soli sunt illi, qui docent justificationem non ex operibus, sed ex fide in Christum tantum. Ergo justificatio ex fide solum, est Deo probata, non vero illa quae fingitur ex operibus.
units.tr: Fourth argument. The ministers through whom God gives the Spirit and works miracles and powers among you are those alone who teach that justification is not by works but by faith in Christ alone. Therefore justification by faith alone has been approved by God, not that justification which is invented from works.

units.la: Verf. 6. Sicut Abraham credidit Deo, & imputatum est ei ad justitiam.
units.tr: Verse 6. Just as Abraham believed God, and it was reckoned to him for righteousness.

units.la: Arg. 5. Abraham quamvis virtutibus maximè florebat, sola tamen fide justificatus clt; Credidit enim Deo, & imputatum est ei in justitiam. Deus enim promisit benedicendas omnes Gentes in semine ipsius, id est, in Christo. Ille hanc benedictionem, quae in se continet justitiam & vitam aeternam in Christo, sibi applicavit credendo. Ergo justificamur non ex operibus, sed ex fide. Verf. 7. Ita nostus nempe eos qui ex fide sunt, esse filios Abrahæ.
units.tr: Fifth argument. Although Abraham flourished most of all in virtues, he was nevertheless justified by faith alone; for he believed God, and it was reckoned to him for righteousness. For God promised that all nations would be blessed in his seed, that is, in Christ. By believing, he applied to himself this blessing, which contains in itself righteousness and eternal life in Christ. Therefore we are justified not by works but by faith. Verse 7. So you should know that those who are of faith are the sons of Abraham.

units.la: Arg. 6. Soli illi qui ex fide sunt, seu quærunt justificari per fidem, & non ex operibus, sunt filii Abrahami. Ergo unica ratio justificationis est per fidem.
units.tr: Sixth argument. Only those who are of faith, or who seek to be justified by faith and not by works, are the sons of Abraham. Therefore the one reason for justification is faith.

units.la: Vers. 8. Providens autem Scriptura Deum ex fide justificaturum Gentes, ante evangelizavit Abrahæ, Benedicentur, inquiens, in te omnes Gentes.
units.tr: Verse 8. And the Scripture, foreseeing that God would justify the Gentiles by faith, preached the gospel beforehand to Abraham, saying: In you shall all the nations be blessed.

units.la: Arg. 7. Spiritus qui est Scripturarum autor, novit hoc esse consilium Dei, ut justificentur Gentes per fidem, & prævidens hoc futurum, prædicavit Abrahamo doctrinam de benedicendis Gentibus in ipso, ut in Patre, exemplo, & typo fidelium: in ipso, in quo semen benedictum Christus includebatur, utpote in ipsius lumbis jam quasi existens, sicut de Levi dicitur, Heb. 7. 10. Ergo necessario sola hæc justificandi ratio firma est.
units.tr: Seventh argument. The Spirit, who is the author of the Scriptures, knew that this was God's counsel, that the Gentiles should be justified by faith; and foreseeing that this would come to pass, he preached to Abraham the doctrine about the blessing of the Gentiles in him, as in a father, an example and type of believers; in him, in whom the blessed seed, Christ, was included, as being already, as it were, in his loins, just as is said of Levi in Heb. 7. 10. Therefore this one way of justification necessarily stands firm.

units.la: Verf. 9. Itaque qui ex fide sunt, Benedicuntur cum fideli illo Abraham.
units.tr: Verse 9. So those who are of faith are blessed with that faithful Abraham.

units.la: Arg. 8. Soli fideles, seu qui ex fide quærunt justitiam, benedictionem cum Abrahamo fideli consequuntur: Ergo unica illa ratio justitiæ per fidem est solida,
units.tr: Eighth argument. Only believers, or those who seek righteousness by faith, obtain the blessing with the faithful Abraham. Therefore that one way of righteousness by faith is sound.

units.la: Verf. 10. Nam quotquot ex operibus Legis sunt, sub execratione sunt. Scriptum est enim, Execrabilis quisquis non manserit in omnibus quae scripta sunt in libro Legis, ut faciat ea.
units.tr: Verse 10. For as many as are of the works of the Law are under the curse. For it is written: Cursed is everyone who does not continue in all the things written in the book of the Law, to do them.

units.la: Arg. 9. Quotquot ex lege sunt, seu justificationem ex operibus legis quaerunt, sub maledictione sunt, quia operum foederi adhaerent, nec tamen conditionem hujus foederis, id est, perfectam obedientiam legi praestant: Ergo justificatio non est ex operibus, sed ex fide.
units.tr: Ninth argument. As many as are of the Law, or who seek justification by the works of the Law, are under a curse, because they cling to the covenant of works, and yet do not render the condition of that covenant, that is, perfect obedience to the Law. Therefore justification is not by works but by faith.

units.la: Scriptum est ] Confirmat antecedens, quia ex Scriptura, Deut. 27. 26. Maledictus est quisquis non implet totam legem: Quaerentes autem justificationem ex operibus, non implent totam legem: Ergo sunt maledicti.
units.tr: It is written] He confirms the antecedent, because from Scripture, Deut. 27. 26: Cursed is everyone who does not fulfil the whole Law. But those who seek justification by works do not fulfil the whole Law. Therefore they are cursed.

units.la: Verf. 11. Nullum autem per Legem justificari apud Deum, manifestum est: siquidem justus ex fide vivet.
units.tr: Verse 11. Now that no one is justified before God by the Law is evident, for the just shall live by faith.

units.la: Arg. 10. Scriptura, Habac. 2. 4. Pronunciat solum justum ex fide, viturum: Ergo nullus per legem, seu opera justificabitur apud Deum. Addit apud Deum, quia apud homines justificari nos ex operibus non negat. Nam justificatio apud homines, nihil aliud est quam justificationis jam factae per Fidem apud Deum, agnitio & declaratio, propter fructus fidei manifestatos.
units.tr: Tenth argument. Scripture, Habac. 2. 4, pronounces only that the just man, by faith, shall live. Therefore no one is justified before God by the Law, or by works. He adds before God, because he does not deny that we are justified by works before men. For justification before men is nothing other than the recognition and declaration, on account of the fruits of faith made manifest, of a justification already made by faith before God.

units.la: Verf. 12. Lex autem non est ex fide: sed qui fecerit ea homo, vivet in ipsis.
units.tr: Verse 12. But the Law is not of faith; rather, the man who does these things shall live by them.

units.la: Arg. 11. Argumenti superioris probans consequentiam: Lex, seu justificandi ratio per opera, non consistit cum fide, seu cum justificandi ratione per fidem, quia promissio legalis est de vita danda facienti, & praestanti Legem, seu ei qui perfectam inhaerentem justitiam habet: Fides vero affert justitiam imputatam credenti in eum qui impium justificat: seu justitiam affert ei, qui propria justitia destituitur. Ergo si justitia ulla datur, ex Fide datur, & ex Lege non datur, & per consequens Fidei justitia sola est agnoscenda.
units.tr: Eleventh argument, proving the consequence of the preceding argument. The Law, or the way of justification by works, does not agree with faith, or with the way of justification by faith, because the legal promise is of life to be given to the one who does and performs the Law, or to the one who has a perfect inherent righteousness. But faith brings imputed righteousness to the believer in him who justifies the ungodly; that is, it brings righteousness to one who is destitute of his own righteousness. Therefore, if any righteousness is given, it is given by faith and not by the Law, and consequently the righteousness of faith alone is to be acknowledged.

units.la: Verf. 13. At Christus nos redemit ab execratione Legis, dum pro nobis factus est execratio. Scriptum est enim, Execrabilis quisquis pendet in ligno.
units.tr: Verse 13. But Christ has redeemed us from the curse of the Law, having become a curse for us. For it is written: Cursed is everyone who hangs on a tree.

units.la: Arg. 12. Christus redemit nos ab execratione Legis, factus execratio pro nobis in cruce, seu mortem subiens execrabilem in cruce pro nobis, ut patet ex Scriptura, quae genus illud mortis quod Christus ex Dan Dei consilio subiturus erat, (suspendium scilicet in ligno) maledictum pronunciavit. Ergo non ex Lege, sed ex fide in Christum, qui liberat nos à maledictione Legis, est justificatio.
units.tr: Argument 12. Christ redeemed us from the curse of the Law, having become a curse for us on the cross; that is, by undergoing for us on the cross a cursed death. This is clear from Scripture, which pronounced under a curse that kind of death which Christ was to undergo by God's determined counsel, namely hanging on a tree. Therefore justification comes not from the Law but from faith in Christ, who frees us from the curse of the Law.

units.la: Verf. 14. Ut in Gentibus benedictio Abrahæ extet in Christo Iesu, & ut promissum illum Spiritum accipiamus per fidem.
units.tr: Verse 14. That the blessing of Abraham might come upon the Gentiles in Christ Jesus, and that we might receive the promised Spirit through faith.

units.la: Arg. 13. CHRISTUS eo fine factus est execratio, ut in CHRISTO per fidem apprehenso, benedictio Abrahæ, id est, justitia & vita æterna in semine benedicto emineret inter Gentiles, qui opera non habent, quibus se confidere prætendant: Ergo justificatio est per fidem, & non per opera:
units.tr: Argument 13. Christ was made a curse for this end: that in Christ, laid hold of by faith, the blessing of Abraham, that is, righteousness and eternal life in the blessed seed, might reach the Gentiles, who have no works in which they may claim to trust. Therefore justification is by faith, and not by works.

units.la: Accipiemus. Mutat personam, & jungit se & reliquos fideles Judæos Gentibus fidelibus, addens Arg. 14. CHRISTUS eo fine factus est execratio, ut omnes nos, conflati ex Judæis & Gentibus, fideles coalescentes in unum semen Abrahæ, accipiemus promissum Spiritum adoptionis per fidem. Ergo per fidem est justificatio omnium nostrum, Gentium & Judæorum, nisi statuamus Christum sine suo fructrari.
units.tr: We might receive. He changes the person and joins himself and the other faithful Jews to the faithful Gentiles, adding Argument 14. Christ was made a curse for this end: that all of us, joined together from Jews and Gentiles, coalescing as believers into one seed of Abraham, might receive the promised Spirit of adoption through faith. Therefore justification of all of us, Gentiles and Jews, is by faith, unless we hold that Christ labours in vain for his own.

units.la: Verf. 15. Fratres, humano more loquor, Hominis licet pactionem authoritate confirmatam, nemo abrogat, aut aliquid ei superaddit.
units.tr: Verse 15. Brethren, I speak after the manner of men: though it is only a man's covenant, once it has been confirmed, no one annuls it or adds anything to it.

units.la: Verf. 16. Abrahæ vero dictæ sunt promissiones, & semini ejus: Non dicit, Et seminibus, ut de multis, sed ut de uno, Et semini tuo: qui est Christus.
units.tr: Verse 16. Now the promises were spoken to Abraham and to his seed. He does not say, "and to seeds," as of many, but as of one, "and to your seed," which is Christ.

units.la: Verf. 17 Hoc autem dico, pactionem ante confirmatam à Deo, rejectu Christi, Lex quæ post annos quadringentos, & triginta cæpit, non facit irritam, ut aboleat promissionem.
units.tr: Verse 17. But this I say: the covenant previously confirmed by God, the Law, which came four hundred and thirty years later, does not annul it so as to make the promise void, since Christ has been rejected.

units.la: His tribus versibus est Arg 15. Confirmans superius. Rite Pacta & Conventa, ne inter homines quidem possunt rescindi, vel superadditione mutari, verf. 15. At rite Pactum & Conventum est, inter Deum & Abrahamum, de uniendis omnibus fidelibus ex Judæis & Gentibus, in unum semen CHRISTUM, facta incorporatione CHRISTI capitis & omnium membrorum ejus, in unum CHRISTUM mysticum, per fidem, verf. 16. Ergo hoc pactum non potest rescindi, nec superadditione legis mutari: atque ita stabit justificatio per fidem: Hoc argumentum ut intelligatur, verf. 15. Apostolus occupat objectionem: Diceret aliquis justificandi rationem esse mutatam, nec eandem esse rationem justificandi Abrahamum, ante legem, & posteros ejus, quibus lata est lex. Nam posteriora derogare solent prioribus: Respondet in pacto rato, & Testamentariis tabellis jam confirmato, ne inter homines quidem rescindi posse, vel mutari quicquam, nedum in divino Pacto, Testamentario more, jam stabilito. Deinde verf. 16. assumit sic pactum esse D eum cum Abrahamo, de benedictione gratis danda credentibus in Christum, ut ejus sobolem, quae ex Gentibus & Judaeis constat, per pacti verba in unum corpus colligeret: Hoc probat ex verbis promissionis, quia Deus non dixit feminibus (ac si plura futura essent femina, nempe Gentes seorsim, & seorsim Judaei) sed dixit, Semini tuo, ut de uno, nempe Christo rem intelligens, in quo fideles ex Judaeis & Gentibus coalescerent in unum semen, id est, in unum Christum mysticum per fidem.
units.tr: These three verses contain Argument 15, confirming what was said above. Covenants and agreements that have been duly made cannot be rescinded or altered by any addition, not even among men (verse 15). But a covenant was duly made between God and Abraham concerning the uniting of all the faithful, from Jews and Gentiles, into one seed, Christ, by the incorporation of Christ the head and all his members into one mystical Christ, through faith (verse 16). Therefore this covenant cannot be rescinded, nor altered by the addition of the Law; and so justification by faith will stand. In order that this argument be understood: in verse 15 the Apostle meets an objection. Someone might say that the reason for justification has changed, and that the reason by which Abraham was justified before the Law is not the same as that for his posterity, to whom the Law was given; for later laws commonly override earlier ones. He answers that in a ratified covenant, already confirmed by testamentary tablets, nothing can be rescinded or changed even among men, much less in a divine covenant already established after the manner of a testament. Then, in verse 16, he assumes that the covenant of God with Abraham was about a blessing freely given to those who believe in Christ, so that by the words of the promise he would gather his offspring, made up of Gentiles and Jews, into one body. He proves this from the words of the promise: God did not say "to seeds," as though there were to be several seeds, namely the Gentiles separately and the Jews separately, but said "to your seed," as of one, namely Christ, understanding the matter so that the believers from Jews and Gentiles would coalesce into one seed, that is, into one mystical Christ through faith.

units.la: Denique, verf. 17. Concludit hoc pactum, per sacrificium testamentario more confirmatum, & ratum habitum a Deo, cum relatione ad Christum, non potuisse rescindi, vel inutile reddi, per legem quae post annos quadringentos, & triginta extitit.
units.tr: Finally, in verse 17, he concludes that this covenant, confirmed by sacrifice after the manner of a testament, and ratified by God with reference to Christ, could not be rescinded or made void by the Law which came four hundred and thirty years later.

units.la: Promissionem ] Rationem includit cur hoc pactum non potuerit mutari a Lege; nempe, quia pactum, est Dei absoluta promissio, quae Deum promittentem quasi obligat ita ut non possit mutare eam: Lex vero mandati naturam habet, quae non legislatorem, sed subditum ligat: Potest enim legislator leges mutare; absolutas vero promissiones mutare non potest. Ergo lex post tot annos lata, pactum cum Abrahamo, seu promissionem absolute factam Abrahamo, non potuit abolere.
units.tr: Promise] He includes the reason why this covenant could not be altered by the Law: namely, because the covenant is God's absolute promise, which in a sense binds the promising God so that he cannot change it. The Law, however, has the nature of a command, which binds not the lawgiver but the subject. For a lawgiver can change laws, but he cannot change absolute promises. Therefore the law given so many years later could not abolish the covenant with Abraham, or the promise absolutely made to Abraham.

units.la: Verf. 18. Nam si ex Lege est hereditas, non jam ex promissione: Abrahae vero per promissionem gratificatus est Deus hereditatem.
units.tr: Verse 18. For if the inheritance is by the Law, it is no longer by promise. But God gave it to Abraham by promise.

units.la: Ne quis objiceret conjungi posse legem & promissionem: Respondet, & addit Arg. 16. Si ex lege seu ex operibus est hereditas, tum non ex promissione gratuita, quia horum alterum tollit alterum; At hereditas gratis data est Abrahae per gratuitam promissionem: Ergo non ex lege; & per consequens, quia haereditas, seu vita aeterna non est ex lege, seu operibus ullis, neque justificatio erit ex lege, sed tantum ex gratia, per fidem.
units.tr: Lest anyone object that law and promise can be joined, he answers and adds Argument 16. If the inheritance is by the Law, or by works, then it is not by free promise, since the one excludes the other. But the inheritance was given freely to Abraham through a gratuitous promise. Therefore it is not by the Law. And consequently, since the inheritance, or eternal life, is not by the Law or by any works, justification too will not be by the Law but only by grace, through faith.

units.la: Verf. 19. Quid igitur Lex? Transgressionum gratia addita est, usque quo veniret semen illud cui facta est promissio: Lex, inquam, ordinata per Angelos per manum interuntii.
units.tr: Verse 19. What then is the Law? It was added because of transgressions, until the seed should come to whom the promise was made. The Law, I say, was ordained through angels by the hand of a mediator.

units.la: Verf. 10. Internuncius autem, unius non est: Deus verò unus est.
units.tr: Verse 20. Now a mediator is not of one, but God is one.

units.la: Quæstionem movet de usu latæ legis, quærens quosfum lex lata sit. Respondet & addit Argumentum 17. Lex data est, ut transgressiones manifestarentur, & aliquo quasi fræno cohiberentur, usque quo veniret <bl>Christus</bl>, qui semen est cui promissio benedictionis facta est. Ergo cum per legem veniat peccati tantum manifestatio, non est justificatio per legem, sed per Christum, seu per fidem: opus autem erat ad peccati manifestationem, ut lex renovaretur, quia peccabant Judæi, & tamen nec peccati vim, nec suam impotentiam ad obediendum legi agnoscebant. Idcirco urgebatur lex, usque dum dirutâ macerie inter Judæos & Gentes surgeret plenum semen illud, coagmentatum ex Judæis & Gentibus, in unum corpus cum Capite suo Christo per fidem conjunctis.
units.tr: He raises the question about the use of the Law that was given, asking for what purpose the Law was given. He answers and adds Argument 17. The Law was given so that transgressions might be made manifest, and be restrained as with a kind of bridle, until Christ came, who is the seed to whom the promise of blessing was made. Therefore, since through the Law there comes only the manifestation of sin, justification is not by the Law but by Christ, that is, by faith. The Law had to be renewed for the manifestation of sin, because the Jews were sinning, and yet they acknowledged neither the power of sin nor their own inability to obey the Law. For this reason the Law was pressed upon them until, the dividing wall having been broken down between Jews and Gentiles, that full seed would arise, joined together from Jews and Gentiles into one body, united with its head Christ through faith.

units.la: Ordinata ] Arg. 18. Terribilis modus tradendi legem, per Ministerium Angelorum, & per manum internuncii, seu Mediatoris, signum fuit dissidii potius, quam pacis & concordiæ inter Deum & homines: quia Mediator seu internuncius non solet esse unius tantum partis, (cum nemo à seipso dissideat) sed partium, quarum unâ secessionem fecit altera; Deus autem unus est & semper sibi constans: pars ergo diffidens est homo, & id significabat & arguebat tradendæ legis modus. Argumenti vis hæc est, Quo dato non ponitur reconciliatio, sed manet dissidium inter Deum & homines, per illud non est justificatio: At data lege non ponitur reconciliatio, sed manet dissidium inter Deum & populum, ut apparet ex modo tradendi Legem. Ergo per Legem non est justificatio.
units.tr: Ordained] Argument 18. The terrible manner of delivering the Law, through the ministry of angels and by the hand of a go-between, or mediator, was a sign of division rather than of peace and concord between God and men. For a mediator or go-between is not usually of one party only (since no one is at odds with himself), but of parties, one of which has withdrawn from the other. God, however, is one and always consistent with himself. The party at odds, then, is man; and the manner of delivering the Law signified and proved this. The force of the argument is this: where this is given, reconciliation is not set in place, but division remains between God and men; through that there is no justification. But when the Law was given, reconciliation was not set in place, but division remained between God and the people, as is evident from the manner of delivering the Law. Therefore there is no justification by the Law.

units.la: Verf. 21. Num igitur Lex addita est adversus promissiones Dei? Absit. nam si data fuisset Lex quæ posset vivificare, vere ex Lege esset justitia.
units.tr: Verse 21. Is the Law then against the promises of God? God forbid. For if a law had been given which could give life, then truly righteousness would be by the law.

units.la: Proponit aliam quæstionem, Num Lex sit promissioni contraria, contrariam justificandi rationem ostendens hominibus?
units.tr: He raises another question: whether the Law is contrary to the promise, showing men a justification of a different kind.

units.la: Respondet negando, & addit Argumentum 19. Si data fuisset Lex, quæ peccatoribus vitam, & vires ad præstandum quæ præcipiebantur, communicare potuisset, certè justificatio fuisset per Legem. Assumere licet; At talis Lex peccatoribus neque data est, neque dari potuit, Rom. 3. 3. Ergo per Legem non est justificatio.
units.tr: He answers by denying, and adds Argument 19. If a Law had been given which could impart life to sinners, and the strength to perform what was commanded, then justification would certainly have been by the Law. This may be assumed. But such a Law has neither been given to sinners nor could have been given (Rom. 3. 3). Therefore justification is not by the Law.

units.la: Verf. 22. Sed conclusit Scriptura omnia sub peccatum, ut promissio ex fide Iesu Christi daretur credentibus.
units.tr: But the Scripture has concluded all things under sin, so that the promise by faith in Jesus Christ might be given to those who believe.

units.la: Arg. 20. Lex Dei, & tota Scriptura, omnes homines, & quicquid ab homine proficiscitur, conclusit sub peccatum, & omnes homines peregit reos peccati, ut jam nihil aliud superesse posset homini, quam fides in Iesum Christum; per quam credentibus omnibus promissio gratuitæ benedictionis contingat: Ergo non per legem, sed per fidem est justificatio: nam si omnes sunt peccatores, nemo ex operibus, nemo nisi fide servari potest.
units.tr: Argument 20. The law of God and the whole of Scripture, and whatever proceeds from man, have concluded all men under sin and made all men guilty of sin, so that nothing remains for man but faith in Jesus Christ, through which the promise of the free blessing comes to all who believe. Therefore justification is not by the law but by faith: for if all are sinners, no one can be saved by works, and no one can be saved except by faith.

units.la: Verf. 23. Antequam autem venisset fides, sub Legis præsidio tenebamur, conclusi in eam fidem quæ erat revelanda.
units.tr: Verse 23. But before faith came, we were kept under the custody of the law, shut up to that faith which was to be revealed.

units.la: Arg. 21. A fine & usu œconomiæ, seu externæ disciplinæ, ante Christi adventum in Ecclesia Judæorum, qui quotidie urgebantur sub pœna maledictionis, ad legem secundum pactum præstandam: quotidie per ceremoniarum impositarum jugum & observationem, erudiebantur de obedientia præceptis debita, de impotentia sua ad legem observandam, deque multiplici suo peccato; quotidie etiam instituebantur ut confugerent ad altare, ad sacrificium, ad lotiones, ut ex hac disciplina cognoscerent se peccatores esse, nec posse liberari nisi per oblationem Agni Dei venturi, & per expiationem in ejus sanguine, seu per fidem in Messiam promissum.
units.tr: Argument 21. From the end and use of the economy, or external discipline, before Christ's coming in the Church of the Jews, who were daily urged under penalty of the curse to perform the law according to the covenant. Daily, through the yoke and observance of the imposed ceremonies, they were taught the obedience owed to the precepts, their own inability to keep the law, and their manifold sin. Daily too they were instructed to flee to the altar, to the sacrifice, and to the washings, so that from this discipline they might know that they were sinners, and could not be freed except by the offering of the coming Lamb of God, and by atonement in his blood, that is, by faith in the promised Messiah.

units.la: Hinc argumentum; Ante Christi adventum, seu antequam veniret plena revelatio doctrinæ fidei, nos Judæi sub externa legalis fœderis disciplina, tanquam sub præsidio custodiebamur, cancellis quasi circumscripti, ne quoquo nos converteremus à maledictione, nisi ad solam eam fidem quæ erat revelanda, id est, ad justitiam & benedictionem quærendam in promisso Messia: Ergo tantum abest ut ex lege fit justitia, ut contra ex legis disciplina, in angustias conclusa fuerit vetus Ecclesia, & coacta ad solam justificationem per fidem respicere. Verum quidem est plerosque abusos fuisse legis disciplina in contrarium finem, sed hic erat finis legalis disciplinæ à Deo institutus.
units.tr: Hence the argument: before Christ's coming, that is, before the full revelation of the doctrine of faith came, we Jews were guarded under the external discipline of the legal covenant, as if under a custody, hemmed in as if by barriers, so that we could turn from the curse nowhere except to that faith alone which was to be revealed, that is, to seek righteousness and blessing in the promised Messiah. Therefore, far from righteousness coming by the law, the old Church was rather shut up in straits by the discipline of the law and compelled to look only to justification by faith. It is true that most people abused the discipline of the law to the opposite end, but this was the end of the legal discipline as instituted by God.

units.la: Verf. 24. Itaque Lex pædagogus noster fuit in Christum respiciens, ut ex fide justificaremur.
units.tr: Verse 24. So the law was our schoolmaster leading us to Christ, that we might be justified by faith.

units.la: Arg. 22. Superius illustrans & confirmans: Lex, seu fœderis legalis externa forma, instar pædagogi nobis à Deo appositi instituebat nostram puerilem Ecclesiam, & manu ducebat ad CHRISTUM, ut ex fide justificaremur. Ergo tantum abest ut per legem justificemur, ut contra, nisi per fidem justificemur, Lex suo fine frustretur. Quid enim aliud agebat lex proponendo moralia praecepta, quam ut in speculo ostenderet Ecclesiae quam longe abesse homines a justitia? Quid legales promissiones & minae, aliud loquebantur, quam si has conditiones praestare non poteris, si jam eas omnes turpiter violaveris, actum est de te, plane perditi, nisi aliam rationem salutis quaerendae ineas? Denique eodem tendebant Ceremoniae. Quorsum enim sacrificia & ablutiones, nisi ut in assidua sordium & damnationis meritae meditatione exercerentur, & in imagine innoxii animalis ante oculos suos caesi, ecclesiam redemptionis suae, per MESSIAM, (qui est Agnus ille DEI immaculatus) contemplarentur, inque eum credentes justificarentur?
units.tr: Argument 22. Illustrating and confirming the above: the law, or the external form of the legal covenant, like a schoolmaster appointed by God, instructed our childish Church and led her by the hand to Christ, that we might be justified by faith. Therefore, far from our being justified by the law, on the contrary, unless we are justified by faith, the law is frustrated of its end. For what else did the law do in proposing moral precepts, than show the Church in a mirror how far men are from righteousness? What did the legal promises and threats say, except: if you cannot fulfil these conditions, if you have already shamefully violated them all, it is all over for you, you are plainly lost, unless you seek out another way of salvation? Finally, the ceremonies tended to the same end. For to what purpose were the sacrifices and ablutions, except that they might be exercised in constant meditation on uncleanness and deserved condemnation, and, with the image of an innocent animal slain before their eyes, the Church might contemplate her redemption through the Messiah (who is that spotless Lamb of God), and be justified by believing in him?

units.la: Vers. 25. At postquam venit fides, non amplius sub paedagogo sumus.
units.tr: Verse 25. But now that faith has come, we are no longer under a schoolmaster.

units.la: Arg. 23. Ab externae disciplinae foederis legalis abolitione, quam innuebat vers. 23. Cum hujus disciplinae usum ante tempus Evangelii, & usque ad tempus fidei fuisse, determinabat; & vers 24. Cum hanc disciplinam paedagogo, (cujus officium puerili tantum aetati destinatur) comparabat. Argum. est; Postquam CHRISTUS patefactus est, & tempus Evangelii, tempus foederis gratuiti manifestandi, seu tempus fidei jam venit, non amplius sumus sub paedagogia foederis legalis, seu disciplina illa externa qua excercenda erat Ecclesia tantum usque ad CHRISTI adventum, hoc est, usque ad, & non ultra tempus Fidei. Ergo tantum abest ut justificemur per Legem, ut tota ratio disciplinae legalis externae jam sub Evangelio abolita sit. Non dicit Legem Moralem esse abolitam, sed dicit paedagogicam illam rationem urgendi foedus legale, una cum ceremoniarum appendicibus, abolitam esse. Nam licet liberentur fideles a Lege pacisente, vel quatenus pactum operum importat, non tamen manumit untur a Lege mandante, vel quatenus regula morum est, sed potius ex foedere gratiae ad legi obediendum, arctiori & suaviori nexu, obligantur.
units.tr: Argument 23. From the abolition of the external discipline of the legal covenant, which verse 23 hinted at, when it determined the use of this discipline to be before the time of the Gospel and until the time of faith; and verse 24, when it compared this discipline to a schoolmaster (whose office is destined only for childish age). The argument is: now that Christ has been made manifest, and the time of the Gospel, that is, the time of making known the free covenant, or the time of faith, has come, we are no longer under the schoolmastering of the legal covenant, or that external discipline by which the Church was to be exercised only until Christ's coming, that is, up to and not beyond the time of faith. Therefore, far from our being justified by the law, the whole rationale of the external legal discipline has now been abolished under the Gospel. It does not say that the moral law is abolished, but that the pedagogical manner of pressing the legal covenant, together with the appendages of the ceremonies, is abolished. For although the faithful are freed from the law as a covenant of works, or insofar as it carries the covenant of works, they are not freed from the law as commanding, or insofar as it is the rule of morals; rather, under the covenant of grace they are bound to obey the law by a closer and sweeter bond.

units.la: Vers. 26. Omnes enim filii Dei estis, per fidem in Christo Iesu. Applicat argumentum superius ad Galatas fideles, & probat eos non esse sub pædagogia legali, sed exemptos è Jugo ceremoniarum Leviticarum, rationibus tribus.
units.tr: Verse 26. For you are all sons of God through faith in Christ Jesus. He applies the above argument to the faithful Galatians, and proves by three reasons that they are not under the legal schoolmastering, but freed from the yoke of the Levitical ceremonies.

units.la: Ratio prima, Omnes vos fideles Galatæ estis in censu filiorum, nempe adultorum, propter fidem vestram in Christum manifestatum: Ergo non estis sub pædagogia puerili ceremoniarum, vel legalis disciplinæ.
units.tr: First reason: you Galatian believers are all counted among the sons, that is, the adults, on account of your faith manifested in Christ. Therefore you are not under the childish schoolmastering of the ceremonies or of the legal discipline.

units.la: Vers. 27. Nam quicunque in Christo baptizati estis, Christum induistis.
units.tr: Verse 27. For as many of you as have been baptized into Christ have put on Christ.

units.la: Ratio 2. Confirmans priorem. Cassa jam facta circumcisione, vos per Sacramentum Baptismi, ita induitis Christum filium Dei, & coram Deo nomen ac personam Christi ita geritis, ut in ipso, & non in vobis ipsis esse censeamini: Ergo filii Dei adulti estis, exempti à pædagogia legis.
units.tr: Second reason, confirming the first. Circumcision having now been set aside, you have through the sacrament of Baptism put on Christ the Son of God, and before God you bear the name and person of Christ in such a way that you are reckoned to be in him and not in yourselves. Therefore you are adult sons of God, freed from the schoolmastering of the law.

units.la: Vers. 28. Non est Judæus neque Græcus, non est servus neque liber, non est masculus ac fœmina. omnes enim vos unus estis in Christo Iesu.
units.tr: Verse 28. There is neither Jew nor Greek, there is neither bond nor free, there is neither male nor female; for you are all one in Christ Jesus.

units.la: Ratio 3. Occurrens tacitæ objectioni, & ostendens quod non opus habeant Gentiles Ceremoniis legalibus, ut per eas jungantur, more proselytorum, cum Dei populo. Quia in fidei negotio nullum est discrimen nationis Judæus ne sis an Græcus; neque conditionis, servus ne sis an liber; neque sexus masculus ne sis an fœmina. Omnes enim vos, quicunque vera fide præditi estis, velut unam personam in Christo constituitis: Ergo vos Galatæ non minus filii adulti eitis, quam nos Apostoli, vel Judæi alii quilibet fideles, ideoque exempti estis à puerili Ceremoniarum pædagogia per Christum.
units.tr: Third reason, meeting an unspoken objection and showing that the Gentiles have no need of the legal ceremonies, to be joined to God's people through them in the manner of proselytes. For in the matter of faith there is no distinction of nation, whether you are Jew or Greek; nor of condition, whether slave or free; nor of sex, whether male or female. For all of you who are endowed with true faith constitute one person in Christ. Therefore you Galatians are no less adult sons than we Apostles, or any other Jewish believers, and so you are freed from the childish schoolmastering of the ceremonies through Christ.

units.la: Vers. 29. Quod si vos estis Christi, nempe Abrahæ semen estis, & secundum promissionem hæredes.
units.tr: Verse 29. And if you are Christ's, then you are Abraham's seed, and heirs according to the promise.

units.la: Occurit alteri objectioni tacitæ, innuenti quasi non possent aliter semen Abrahæ esse quam insitione in populum Dei per Circumcisionem & Ceremoniarum observationem, & simul affert Argumentum vicesimumquartum, ad probandum justificationem non esse per legem, sed per fidem, quod sic formari potest, Qui per fidem Christo sunt uniti, & sic semen illud benedictum Abrahæ facti, & hæredes secundum promissionem, & non secundum legem seu fœdus operum futuri sunt, illi non justificantur ex operibus legis, sed per fidem promissionis. At vos estis Christo uniti, & Abrahami semen facti secundum promissionem, & non secundum legem hæredes futuri : Ergo non ex operi bus legis, sed per fidem promissionis justificamini.
units.tr: He meets another unspoken objection, which suggested that they could not be Abraham's seed otherwise than by being grafted into God's people through circumcision and observance of the ceremonies; and at the same time he brings forward the twenty-fourth argument, to prove that justification is not by the law but by faith, which can be formed thus: those who are united to Christ by faith, and so have become that blessed seed of Abraham, and heirs according to the promise, and not according to the law or the covenant of works, are not justified by the works of the law but by the faith of the promise. But you are united to Christ and have become Abraham's seed according to the promise, and are heirs not according to the law. Therefore you are justified not by the works of the law but by the faith of the promise.

units.la: Caput Quartum.
units.tr: Chapter 4.

units.la: Res sunt Capites partes : In prima hortatur Apostolus ut renuncient Ceremoniarum jugo, ad versum 12. In secunda, est blanda invitatio, ut redeant ad sanam mentem & ad suam doctrinam, quam ipsos de justitia per fidem initio docuerat, ad versum 21. In tertia totam disputationem confirmat, & illustrat insigni allegoria, ad finem. Quod ad primam Capitis partem attinet, disputationem convertit in hortationem ad Galatas, ut renunciantes servili legis jugo, se gerant ut Christi liberi tos. Propositio hortatoria hæc est, Debetis Ceremoniarum jugo renunciare. Argumenta ad confirmationem sunt decem.
units.tr: The chapter has two parts. In the first, the Apostle exhorts them to renounce the yoke of the ceremonies, up to verse 12. In the second, he gives a tender invitation to return to a sound mind and to his teaching, which had first instructed them about justification through faith, up to verse 21. In the third, he confirms and illustrates the whole disputation with a striking allegory, to the end. As for the first part of the chapter, the disputation turns into an exhortation to the Galatians: renouncing the servile yoke of the law, they should conduct themselves as free men of Christ. The hortatory proposition is this: You ought to renounce the yoke of the ceremonies. There are ten arguments in confirmation.

units.la: Verf. 1. Hoc autem dico, Quandiu hæres est infans, nihil differt à servo, quamvis sit dominus omnium.
units.tr: Verse 1. Now I say that as long as the heir is a child, he differs nothing from a servant, although he is lord of all.

units.la: Verf. 2. Sed sub tutoribus & curatoribus est, usque ad tempus quod pater præfinierit.
units.tr: Verse 2. But he is under guardians and governors until the time set by the father.

units.la: Verf. 3. Ita & nos, quum essemus infantes, sub elementis mun- di eramus in servitutem redacti:
units.tr: Verse 3. So also we, when we were children, were held in bondage under the elements of the world.

units.la: Argumentum primum, A servili & puerili externa conditione in qua Ecclesia ante Christi adventum constituta erat, quam similitudine hac illustrat. Quemadmodum hæres quandiu infans seu minorennis est, licet Dominus sit omnium bonorum paternorum quoad jus, respectu possessionis & exercitii juris tamen, seu quoad externam libertatem, non differt à servo, verf. 1. Sed sub tutoribus & curatoribus manet subjugatus, usque ad tempus præfinitum à Patre suo, verf. 2. Sic Ecclesia Dei, cujus nos sumus membra, quoad externum statum sub terrenis figuris, & mundanis elementis, seu rudimentis ceremoniarum legalium, quasi Abecedaria, vel quasi hærens in discernendis rudimentis, A B C. Duram serviebat servitutem, usque ad Christum.
units.tr: First argument: from the servile and childish external condition in which the Church was placed before Christ's coming, which he illustrates with this likeness. Just as the heir, as long as he is an infant or minor, although he is lord of all the paternal goods by right, does not differ from a servant with respect to possession and the exercise of his right, or as to external liberty (verse 1), but remains subject under guardians and curators until the time fixed by his father (verse 2), so the Church of God, of which we are members, was in its external state under earthly figures and worldly elements, that is, the rudiments of the legal ceremonies, like a primer, or like someone stuck on the first rudiments, A B C. It served a hard bondage until Christ.

units.la: Hinc argumentum; Puerile & servile est Jugum Ceremoniarum legalium, Ecclesiæ infanti & minorenni ante <bl>Christi</bl> adventum tantum destinatum: Ergo vos Galatæ qui sub Euangelio estis, debetis ei renunciare.
units.tr: Hence the argument: the yoke of the legal ceremonies is childish and servile, and was destined only for the Church as an infant and minor before Christ's coming. Therefore you Galatians, who live under the Gospel, ought to renounce it.

units.la: Verf. 4. At postquam venit plenum tempus, emisit Deus Filium suum factum ex muliere, factum Legi obnoxium:
units.tr: Verse 4. But when the fullness of time had come, God sent forth his Son, made of a woman, made subject to the law,

units.la: Verf. 5. Ut eos qui Legi erant obnoxii, redimeret, ut adoptionem accciperemus.
units.tr: Verse 5. That he might redeem those who were under the law, so that we might receive adoption.

units.la: Dixit de servili & puerili conditione Ecclesiæ ante Christum, quoad externum hominem, (nam quoad Spiritum & interiorem hominem, fideles qui videbant Christi diem, liberi erant, & gaudebant in Domino) jam sequitur modus liberandi Ecclesiam per Christi adventum.
units.tr: He has spoken of the servile and childish condition of the Church before Christ, as to the outward man (for as to the Spirit and the inner man, the faithful who saw Christ's day were free and rejoiced in the Lord). Now follows the manner of freeing the Church through Christ's coming.

units.la: Plenum tempus ] Arg. 2. Venit jam plenum tempus, quod Pater præstituerat pædagogicæ œconomiæ legali, & finita est tutela illa seu puerilis pædagogia illa Ceremoniarum legalium: Ergo earum jugo vobis Christianis est renunciandum.
units.tr: The fullness of time ] Argument 2. The fullness of time, which the Father had appointed for the pedagogical economy of the law, has now come, and that guardianship, or childish schooling in the legal ceremonies, is at an end. Therefore you Christians ought to renounce their yoke.

units.la: Emisit filium ] Arg. 3. Dei filius missus est in mundum, carnem assumplit, & natus est ex Maria virgine, & subjecit se fœderi operum, & legalium ceremoniarum jugo, ut eos qui legi erant subjecti, redimeret: Ergo vos Christiani redempti ab hoc jugo, ei renunciare debetis.
units.tr: He sent his Son ] Argument 3. The Son of God was sent into the world, took on flesh, was born of the Virgin Mary, and subjected himself to the covenant of works and the yoke of the legal ceremonies, in order to redeem those who were subject to the law. Therefore you Christians, redeemed from this yoke, ought to renounce it.

units.la: Ut adoptionem ] Arg. 4. Eo fine Christus subjectus factus est legi, ut nos sub Euangelio exhibitam adoptionem, seu privilegium filiorum adultorum aperte adiremus. Ergo nos sub Euangelio renunciare debemus Ceremoniarum servili & puerili Jugo, nisi callum nobis reddere vellemus beneficium redemptionis.
units.tr: That we might receive adoption ] Argument 4. Christ was made subject to the law for this end: that we might openly come to the adoption offered under the Gospel, that is, the privilege of adult sons. Therefore we under the Gospel ought to renounce the servile and childish yoke of the ceremonies, unless we wished to make the benefit of redemption useless to ourselves.

units.la: Verf. 6. Quoniam autem estis filii, emisit Deus Spiritum filii sui in corda vestra, clamantem, Abba, id est Pater.
units.tr: Verse 6. And because you are sons, God sent forth the Spirit of his Son into your hearts, crying, Abba, that is, Father.

units.la: Arg. 5. In Testimonium adoptionis vestræ, & evectionis in adultorum filiorum privilegium, donavit vos Deus Spiritu sancto, per quem una cum aliis Dei filiis ex Judæis & Gentibus, Deum in quavis lingua confidenter vocare possitis Patrem vestrum. Ergo nili vos gerere veletis tanquam indignos hoc privilegio, Ceremoniarum puerili & servili Jugo renunciandum est.
units.tr: Argument 5. As a testimony of your adoption and of your elevation to the privilege of adult sons, God has given you the Holy Spirit, through whom, together with the other sons of God from Jews and Gentiles, you may confidently call God your Father in any language. Therefore, unless you wish to act as though you were unworthy of this privilege, you must renounce the childish and servile yoke of the ceremonies.

units.la: Verf. 7. Itaque non amplius es servus, sed filius: quod si filius etiam heres Dei per Christum,
units.tr: Verse 7. So you are no longer a servant, but a son; and if a son, then an heir of God through Christ.

units.la: Arg. 6. Non estis amplius in servili illa conditione sub Jugo Ceremoniarum, sed in Statu Libero, ut filii adulti, & haeredes actu jam participes bonorum paternorum, seu gratiarum spiritualium, in ampliori mensura, quam Vetus Ecclesia, idque per Christum in carne manifestatum. Ergo servili illi & puerili Jugo vobis jam renunciandum est.
units.tr: Argument 6. You are no longer in that servile condition under the yoke of the ceremonies, but in a free state, as adult sons and heirs, already actually sharing in the paternal goods, that is, the spiritual graces, in a fuller measure than the Old Church, and this through Christ manifested in the flesh. Therefore you must now renounce that servile and childish yoke.

units.la: Verf. 8. Imo tum quidem ignorantes Deum, serviebatis iis qui natura non sunt dii.
units.tr: Verse 8. Indeed, then, not knowing God, you served those who by nature are not gods.

units.la: Verf. 9. At nunc cum cognoscatis Deum, imo potius edocti sitis a Deo, quomodo convertimini retrorsum ad impotentia & egena elementa, quibus regressi ad superiora servire vultis?
units.tr: Verse 9. But now that you know God, or rather are known by God, how is it that you turn back again to the weak and beggarly elements, to which you wish to be in bondage once more?

units.la: Ingratitudinem iis exprobrat cum reprehensione propter observationem legalium Ceremoniarum, ut dierum & mensium &c, in quibus nec nati, nec educati erant.
units.tr: He rebukes them for their ingratitude, reproving them for observing the legal ceremonies, such as days and months, etc., in which they had neither been born nor brought up.

units.la: Sed tunc quidem ] Arg. 7.
