Priusquam estis filii, in deteriori eratis conditione quam Judaei, nempe Idololatrae eratis, verum Deum ignorantes, & nctis idolis servientes, nunc autem postea quam ab illa ignorantia conversi, Deum cognovistis, vel potius ex praeveniente Dei gratia cogniti & dilecti, a Deo attracti, ad eum cognoscendum, & in libertatem filiorum vindicati, estis, quomodo de novo quasi nullam antea servitutem passi, convertitis vos ad ceremonialis servitutis abolitae Jugum? Ergo huic jugo renunciandum est. Vis argumenti haec est, Minori cum praetextu excusationis, & cum ingratitudinis insigniori nota, quam Judaei sub jugo nati & educati, jugum ceremoniarum gerebant. Ergo huic renunciandum est vobis.
units.tr: But then indeed ] Argument 7. Before you were sons, you were in a worse condition than the Jews: you were idolaters, ignorant of the true God and serving idols. But now, after being converted from that ignorance, you have come to know God, or rather, you have been known and loved by God through prevenient grace, drawn by God to know him, and vindicated into the liberty of sons. How is it that, as though you had suffered no servitude before, you turn back to the yoke of the abolished ceremonial servitude? Therefore this yoke must be renounced. The force of the argument is this: the Jews, who were born and brought up under the yoke, bore the yoke of the ceremonies with a lesser pretext of excuse and with a more striking mark of ingratitude. Therefore you must renounce it.

units.la: Retrorsum ] Arg. 8. Provectis ad libertatem filiorum adultorum, indignum est retrorsum ad servitutis jugum ultro redire, & servire velle. Ergo jugo huic vobis renunciandum est.
units.tr: Backward ] Argument 8. For those who have been advanced to the liberty of adult sons, it is unworthy to return willingly to the yoke of servitude and to wish to serve again. Therefore you must renounce this yoke.

units.la: Egena ] Arg. 9. Ceremoniae illae legales, quarum jugum jam affectatis, etiamsi usum suum paedagogicum habuerint antequam Christus venit, post Christi adventum tamen nullum habent usum, sed infirma & egena rudimenta sunt, quae nec virtutem habent ad justificandum, nec vim ad consolationem afferendam, nec usum veterem ad praefigurandum Christum. Ergo huic jugo tam inutili renunciare debetis. Verf. 10. Dies observatis & menses, & tempora, & annos. Verf. 11. Metuo de vobis ne frustrà fatigatus sim apud vos,
units.tr: Beggarly ] Argument 9. Those legal ceremonies whose yoke you now desire, even if they had their pedagogical use before Christ came, have no use since Christ's coming. They are weak and beggarly rudiments, which have neither the power to justify, nor the force to bring consolation, nor their former use of foreshadowing Christ. Therefore you must renounce so useless a yoke. Verse 10. You observe days, and months, and seasons, and years. Verse 11. I am afraid for you, lest I have laboured over you in vain.

units.la: Arg. 10. Inchoata vestra servitus in observatione Ceremoniarum Legalium, ex. gra. dierum, Sabbatorum, neomeniarum, festorum anniversariorum, & annorum Sabbaticorum &c. Justam mihi caulam metuendi dat, ne frustra vobis Euangelium de gratuita justificatione praedicaverim. Quia hoc indicium est, vos à justificatione per fidem, seu Gratia Christi, deficere ad justificationem quaerendam per opera legis. Ergo nisi Euangelio renunciare velletis, renunciandum est huic Jugo.
units.tr: Argument 10. Your servitude, begun in the observance of the legal ceremonies, such as days, Sabbaths, new moons, annual feasts, sabbatical years, etc., gives me just cause to fear that I have preached the Gospel of free justification to you in vain. For this is a sign that you are falling away from justification by faith, that is, from the grace of Christ, to seek justification by the works of the law. Therefore, unless you are willing to renounce the Gospel, you must renounce this yoke.

units.la: Secunda Pars.
units.tr: Second Part.

units.la: Verf. 12. Estote quasi ego; nam ego sum quasi vos: fratres, rogo vos. nihil mihi fecistis injuria. Secunda pars capitis, in qua continetur amica hortatio ad redeundum in viam, & sanam sententiam de justificatione ex gratia, per fidem absque operibus Legis.
units.tr: Verse 12. Be as I am, for I also am as you are: brethren, I beg you, you have done me no wrong. This second part of the chapter contains a friendly exhortation to return to the right path, and a sound teaching on justification by grace through faith, apart from the works of the Law.

units.la: Hortationis propositio hæc statui potest. Redeundum vobis ad meam doctrinam de justitia per fidem absque operibus Legis, Estote, in-quit, sicut ego, seu in eadem mecum estote sententia: argumenta hortationis sunt duodecim.
units.tr: The proposition of this exhortation may be stated thus: you must return to my teaching on righteousness through faith apart from the works of the Law. Be, he says, as I am, that is, be of one mind with me. There are twelve arguments for the exhortation.

units.la: Argumentum primum, Quia ego licet olim Pharisæus, tenacissimus fuerim justitiæ per Legem, nunc tamen Christianus factus, sum sicut vos, & veštram vobiscum salutem quæro, non minus quam ipsi vos quæritis. Idcirco redeundum vobis in meam sententiam.
units.tr: First argument: although I was once a Pharisee and most tenacious of righteousness under the Law, I have now become a Christian, and I am like you. I seek your salvation with you, no less than you yourselves seek it. Therefore you must return to my opinion.

units.la: Arg. 2. Metus meus de vobis, nec alienavit à vobis animum meum, nec dubium fecit judicium charitatis de vobis, quin fratres compellem, & ut fratres rogem, ut redeatis: Redite igitur.
units.tr: Second argument: my fear for you has not alienated my mind from you, nor has my charitable judgement of you become doubtful. Therefore I address you as brethren and beg you as brethren to return. Return, then.

units.la: Arg. 3. Aflperior mea objurgatio, non ex ira vel odio orta est adversus vos, qui nulla me privata injuria affecistis, sed ex salutis vestræ studio. Redite igitur.
units.tr: Third argument: my sharper rebuke does not arise from anger or hatred against you, who have done me no private injury, but from zeal for your salvation. Return, then.

units.la: Verf. 13. Nositis autem me per infirmitatem carnis vobis prius evangelizasse:
units.tr: Verse 13. You know that because of the infirmity of the flesh I preached the gospel to you at the first:

units.la: Arg. 4. Ego pro Euangelio vobis prædicato multa sum passus, no-stis enim me per infirmitates, & contemptibilem externi hominis conditionem, ad quam per afflictiones redactus sum, constanter vobis Evangelium praedicasse. Redite ergo ad sanam Doctrinam meis perpessionibus obsignatam.
units.tr: Fourth argument: I have suffered many things for the gospel I preach to you. You know that, through infirmities and the contemptible condition of my outward man, to which I was reduced by afflictions, I preached the gospel to you constantly. Therefore return to sound doctrine, sealed by my sufferings.

units.la: Verf. 14. Et experimentum mei quod fiebat in carne mea, non pro nihilo habuistis, neque respuistis: sed me ut Angelum Dei, ut Christum Iesum excepistis.
units.tr: Verse 14. And my trial which was in my flesh you did not despise or reject, but received me as an angel of God, even as Christ Jesus.

units.la: Arg. 5. Olim causam mearum afflictionum probastis, nec contemnistis me, dum tentationibus in carne exercerer, sed ut Angelum, ut <bl>Christi</bl> personam gerentem excepistis. Ergo & idem nunc facite, & redite ad eandem mentem.
units.tr: Fifth argument: in the past you approved the cause of my afflictions, and you did not scorn me while I was exercised by trials in the flesh, but received me as an angel, as one bearing the person of Christ. Therefore do the same now, and return to the same mind.

units.la: Verf. 15. Quae igitur erat beatitatis vestrae praedicatio? testimonium enim reddo vobis, vos, si fieri potuisset, oculos vestros effossos daturos mihi fuisse.
units.tr: Verse 15. What then was your blessedness of which you spoke? For I bear you witness that, if it had been possible, you would have plucked out your own eyes and given them to me.

units.la: Arg. 6. Olim per meum ministerium beatos vos censebatis: Ergo si beati esse vultis, meae doctrinae constanter agglutinari opportet: Hanc beatitudinem, quia videbantur obliti, Interrogatione vellit iis autem.
units.tr: Sixth argument: in the past you thought yourselves blessed through my ministry. Therefore, if you wish to be blessed, you must steadfastly cling to my doctrine. Since they seemed to have forgotten this blessedness, he asks them by a question.

units.la: Testimonium ] Arg. 7. Olim ut mihi gratum faceretis, rebus vestris charissimis non pepercisset. Redite igitur, & meo exemplo jugum legale rejicite. Si gratum mihi facere vultis.
units.tr: Witness] Seventh argument: in the past you would have spared your dearest possessions to please me. Return, then, and by my example cast off the legal yoke, if you wish to please me.

units.la: Verf. 16. Itaque num inimicus factus sum vobis, dum vobis vera loquor.
units.tr: Verse 16. Have I therefore become your enemy, because I tell you the truth?

units.la: Arg. 8. Tantum abest ut acriori hac reprehensione offensi, inimicum me existimare debeatis, quem ideirco nolletis imitari, ut contra, quia vobis veritatem dico in vestrum bonum, tenearmini, me, & meam hortationem majoris facere.
units.tr: Eighth argument: you ought to think of me not as an enemy, though you were offended by this sharper rebuke, and so you should not wish to imitate him. On the contrary, since I tell you the truth for your good, you are bound to hold me and my exhortation in greater esteem.

units.la: Verf. 17. Desperant vos non bene, imo excludere vos volunt, ut se desperatis.
units.tr: Verse 17. They zealously court you, but not for good; indeed they want to shut you out, so that you may court them.

units.la: Arg. 9. A dissimilitudine sui, & seductorum. Pseudapostoli, inquit, qui magno studio contendunt, ut jugum legale subeatis & geratis, male vobis consulunt, & praepostero erga vos zelo feruntur, imo vero ipsa vos eunt perditum, cupientes vos excludere a me, meaque Doctrina, & a societate Christi per consequens, ut ipsos sectemini, & ipsorum discipuli fiatis. Redite igitur ad meam Doctrinam.
units.tr: Ninth argument: from the unlikeness of himself and of the seducers. The false apostles, he says, who strive with great eagerness that you should submit to and bear the legal yoke, give you bad counsel and are carried away by a perverse zeal for you. Indeed, they seek to cut you off from me and my doctrine, and so, by consequence, from the fellowship of Christ, so that you may follow them and become their disciples. Return, then, to my doctrine.

units.la: Verf. 18. Sed praeclarum est vehementer amare in re bona semper, & non solùm dum praesens sum apud vos.
units.tr: Verse 18. But it is good to be zealously affected always in a good thing, and not only when I am present with you.

units.la: Arg. 10. Zelus meus pro vobis bonus est, & in re bona, & constans dum absum, non minus quam cum adsum: aemulorum meorum de vobis zelotypia perversa est, & simulata: Redite igitur ad meam Doctrinam.
units.tr: Tenth argument: my zeal for you is good, and it is for a good thing, and it is constant when I am absent no less than when I am present. The jealousy of my rivals concerning you is perverse and feigned. Return, then, to my doctrine.

units.la: Verf. 19. Filioli mei, quos iterum parturio, usque quò formetur Christus in vobis.
units.tr: Verse 19. My little children, for whom I travail in birth again until Christ be formed in you.

units.la: Arg 11. CHRISTI imago, in cognitione & fide veritatis de CHRISTO consistens, deformatur in vobis per vestram defectionem ad jugum legis, & justificationem per opera: Ergo redite ad meam doctrinam.
units.tr: Eleventh argument: the image of Christ, which consists in the knowledge and faith of the truth concerning Christ, is deformed in you by your defection to the yoke of the Law and to justification by works. Therefore return to my doctrine.

units.la: Parturio ] Arg. 12. Non minus serio anxius sum de vestra resipiscentia, nec minus solicitè laboro de reparatione fidei vestrae, & imaginis CHRISTI in vobis, quam parturiens in fætu enitendo, vel quam ipse laborabam olim in vestri conversione ad fidem: Ergo ad meam doctrinam redite.
units.tr: Travail] Twelfth argument: I am no less anxiously concerned for your repentance, and no less diligently labour for the restoration of your faith and of the image of Christ in you, than a woman in labour strains in giving birth, or than I myself once laboured in your conversion to faith. Therefore return to my doctrine.

units.la: Verf. 20 Velim autem nunc adesse apud vos, & mutare vocem meam, quoniam haesito in vobis.
units.tr: Verse 20. I would wish to be present with you now and to change my voice, for I am perplexed about you.

units.la: Hanc animi perplexam anxietatem confirmat, à signo, desiderio nempe suo coram eos videndi & erudiendi, seque ad ipsorum necessitatem accommodandi: deinde à causa anxietatis, scilicet quod haesitet iniis incertus, leniter ne an severè, vel qua tandem ratione eos tractaret: nam quam alte radices egerit error in illis, quot infecti, quomodo singuli in hoc negotio affecti fuerint, nisi praesens fuisset, constare ipsi facilè non poterat.
units.tr: He confirms this perplexed anxiety of mind: first from the sign, namely his own desire to see and teach them in person, and to accommodate himself to their need; then from the cause of his anxiety, namely that he is uncertain about them, whether he should deal with them gently or severely, and by what method he should treat them. For how deeply error had taken root in them, how many were infected, and how each of them was affected in this matter, could not easily be ascertained by him unless he were present.

units.la: Tertia Pars.
units.tr: Third Part.

units.la: Verf. 21 Dicite mihi qui sub Lege vultis esse, Legem non audistis?
units.tr: Verse 21: Tell me, you who want to be under the Law, do you not hear the Law?

units.la: Tertia pars Capitis in qua totam disputationem confirmat & illustrat, ex historia conditionis familiae Arahami, in qua per allegoriam typicam, DEUS rem totam jam in disputatione positam praefiguravit: Cujus summa haec est; DEUS olim praefiguravit, eos qui ex operibus seu foedere operum justificationem quaerunt, in servili, misera & maledicta conditione jam esse, & tandem a DEI facie & societate sanctorum ejicendos esse: eos vero qui ex gratia quaerunt justificationem per fidem in CHRISTUM, jam esse liberos DEI familiæ Filios, & beatos, tandemque hæreditatem vitæ æternæ plenè adituros. Quid igitur adeò amentes estis, O Galatæ, ut ultro affectetis hanc servilem, miseram & maledictam rationem justificationis, per Legis Opera, quærendæ?
units.tr: The third part of the chapter, in which he confirms and illustrates the whole disputation from the history of the condition of Abraham's family. In this history, by a typical allegory, God had already foreshadowed the whole matter now under discussion. Its sum is this: God long ago foreshadowed that those who seek justification from works, or the covenant of works, are already in a servile, wretched and cursed condition, and will at last be cast out from the face of God and the fellowship of the saints. But those who seek justification through faith in Christ, by grace, are already free sons of God's family and blessed, and will at last fully enter the inheritance of eternal life. Why, then, O Galatians, are you so foolish as to willingly seek this servile, wretched and cursed way of justification through the works of the Law?

units.la: In hunc finem, Apostolus in hac ultima capitis parte, primò provocat ad Legem, seu libros Mosis, ut tota quæstio decidatur, verf. 21. Deinde typicam historiam conditionis familiæ Abrahami proponit, verf. 22, 23. Tertio exponit typum & mysterium aperit, verf. 24, 25, 26. Quarto confirmat expositionem ex Isaia, verf. 27. Quinto allegoriam seu typum applicat ad Christianos verè fideles, & consolatur se & reliquos adversus persecutionem falsorum fratrum, à gratia DEI alienorum. verf. 28, 29, 30, 31.
units.tr: To this end the Apostle, in this last part of the chapter, first appeals to the Law, that is, the books of Moses, so that the whole question may be decided (verse 21). Second, he sets forth the typical history of the condition of Abraham's family (verses 22, 23). Third, he expounds the type and opens the mystery (verses 24, 25, 26). Fourth, he confirms the exposition from Isaiah (verse 27). Fifth, he applies the allegory or type to true Christian believers, and comforts both himself and the others against the persecution by false brothers, who are strangers to the grace of God (verses 28, 29, 30, 31).

units.la: Dicite] Quod ad primam attinet, arguit Galatas duplicis erroris. Primus error est, quod ultro affectarint esse sub lege, hoc est, sub fœdere legali, seu fœdere operum; cujus hæc conditio est, ut tu te altringas ad legem perfectè præstandam, & Deus tecum agat secundùm legis pactum, id est, servet te, si in nullo peccaveris, maledicat verò & perdat, si in tantillo quod scriptum est in libro legis peccati reus peragaris, seu à norma deflexisse comperiaris: nam alioqui, sub lege ut regula, seu norma vitæ fideles omnes sunt, ut ei studeant sincere in omnibus obedire, per Gratiam à CHRISTO ministratam. Secundus error est, quod legis seu librorum Scriptorum à Mose, sensum scopumque plane ignoraverint.
units.tr: Dicite] As to the first point, he charges the Galatians with a twofold error. The first error is that they willingly desired to be under the Law, that is, under the legal covenant or covenant of works. The condition of this covenant is that you bind yourself to perform the law perfectly, and God deals with you according to the terms of the law: he preserves you if you have sinned in nothing, but curses and destroys you if you are found guilty of even the smallest transgression written in the book of the law, or are found to have swerved from the rule. For otherwise, all believers are under the law as a rule or norm of life, so that they may sincerely strive to obey it in all things, by the grace ministered by Christ. The second error is that they utterly misunderstood the sense and aim of the law, or of the writings of Moses.

units.la: Verf. 22. Scriptum est enim, Abrahamum duos filios habuisse: unum ex ancilla, & unum ex libera.
units.tr: Verse 22: For it is written that Abraham had two sons, one by the bondwoman and one by the free woman.

units.la: Verf. 23. Sed is qui ex ancilla natus est, secundum carnem natus est: qui verò ex libera, per promissionem.
units.tr: Verse 23: But he who was born of the bondwoman was born according to the flesh; but he who was born of the free woman was born through promise.

units.la: Secundo loco proponit, ex Gen. 16. & 21. Typicam historiam conditionis familiæ Abrahami, in qua familia duæ erant uxores Matres, Agar & Sara: conditio matrum duplex; Agar fuit serva, Sara libera seu ingenua: Duo filii Ismael servus ex matre serva: Isaac liber ex matre ingenua: Duplex principium nativitatis, nempe naturæ vis secundum carnem, eminens in nativitate Ismaelis ex juvencula, & vis promissionis, seu virtutis divinæ supernaturalis, In nativitate Isaaci ex Sara vetula, & sterili conspicua.
units.tr: Second, he sets forth, from Genesis 16 and 21, the typical history of the condition of Abraham's family. In this family there were two wives, two mothers, Hagar and Sarah. The condition of the mothers was twofold: Hagar was a slave, Sarah was free-born. The two sons: Ishmael, a slave, from a slave mother; Isaac, free, from a free mother. There was a twofold principle of birth: the power of nature according to the flesh, evident in the birth of Ishmael from a young woman; and the power of promise, or of supernatural divine virtue, evident in the birth of Isaac from Sarah, who was old and barren.

units.la: Hinc dissimile ingenium Ismaelis & Isaaci, & dissidium tantum, ut Ismael: persequutus sit Isaacum & dissimilis utriusque conditio in exitu; Ismael ejectus ex familia est, Isaac vero potitus est haereditate. Quo typo Deus figurabat Ecclesiae visibilis & profitentium Dei cultum diversam conditionem, ex diversis principiis, & causis natam. Nam, 1. Ut duae uxores Agar & Sara, sic duo sunt foedera Dei cum hominibus, foedus operum seu legale, & foedus gratiae seu Euangelicum; 2. Utraque uxor habebat prolem, sic utrumque foedus habet suos cultores, & professores, ut foederis prognatos: 3. Sicut Agar juvencula secundum naturam seu carnem genuit: Sara vero sterilis & vetula, juxta vim divinae promissionis: Ita lex seu foedus operum vim naturae ordinariam, seu liberi arbitrii vires pro fundamento habet; Euangelium vero seu foedus gratiae, specialem Dei gratiam, & spiritualem virtutem pro fundamento habet: 4. Sicut Ismael servili, & malitioso fuit ingenio, ut qui fratrem persequeretur: Isaac autem liberali & pio ingenio praeditus, persecutionem patienter ferens; Sic quotquot justitiarii sunt, quaerentes justitiam ex operibus, servili & perverso sunt ingenio; veroque Dei Filios exagitant: Vere Fideles vero, & Filii promissionis, ingenua pietate Deum colunt, & persecutiones, ut decet, patiuntur.
units.tr: Hence came the different disposition of Ishmael and Isaac, and such discord that Ishmael persecuted Isaac; and the different condition of each at the outcome: Ishmael was cast out of the family, but Isaac obtained the inheritance. By this type God foreshadowed that the visible Church and those who profess the worship of God would have different conditions, born from different principles and causes. For: (1) as there were two wives, Hagar and Sarah, so there are two covenants of God with men, the covenant of works or legal covenant, and the covenant of grace or Gospel covenant; (2) each wife had offspring, so each covenant has its worshippers and professors, as the children of that covenant; (3) just as Hagar, a young woman, bore a child according to nature or the flesh, but Sarah, barren and old, bore one according to the power of divine promise, so the Law or covenant of works has as its foundation the ordinary power of nature, or the powers of free will; but the Gospel, or covenant of grace, has as its foundation special grace of God and spiritual power; (4) just as Ishmael was of a servile and malicious disposition, as one who persecuted his brother, while Isaac was endowed with a free and pious disposition, bearing persecution patiently, so all who are legalists, seeking righteousness from works, are of a servile and perverse disposition, and they harass the true sons of God; but true believers, the sons of promise, worship God with free and sincere piety, and bear persecution as is fitting.

units.la: Verf. 24. Ter quae aliud figuratur. Nam hae sunt duae illae passiones, una quidem quae est Agar, ex monte Sina, generans prolem ad servitutem.
units.tr: Verse 24: Which things are an allegory. For these are the two covenants: one indeed, from Mount Sinai, which is Hagar, generating children to slavery.

units.la: Tertio loco Apostolus typi significationem exponit, quantum ad praesens institutum attinet; & primo, duas uxores ostendit figuras esse duorum foederum, seu pactorum, quorum alterum est foedus operum, repraesentatum per Agar: Alterum est foedus gratiae, seu fidei, repraesentatum per Saram. Quod ad Agar, seu foedus operum, docet Apostolus primo, hoc foedus ortum habere a Sina monte; quia in illo monte lata est Lex, & sancitum hoc foedus inter Deum & populum. Secundo docet hoc foedus generare prolem ad servitutem, seu discipulos & professores suos servos tantum reddere, id est, mercenarios cultores Dei; qui nihil agant nisi externum opus: idque vel metu vel spe mercedis ducti; quique ignorantes finem Legis hunc esse, ut agnoscentes peccata confugiant ad Christum, abutantur Lege; quaerentes per eam, impossibilem justitiam, quam nunquam assequuntur, sed manent in peccatis suis non liberati, meri hypocritae.
units.tr: Third, the Apostle explains the meaning of the type, as far as the present argument requires. First, he shows that the two wives are figures of two covenants, or pacts: one is the covenant of works, represented by Hagar; the other is the covenant of grace or faith, represented by Sarah. As for Hagar, that is, the covenant of works, the Apostle teaches, first, that this covenant had its origin from Mount Sinai, because the Law was given on that mountain, and this covenant was sanctioned between God and the people there. Second, he teaches that this covenant generates children to slavery, that is, it makes its disciples and professors mere servants, that is, mercenary worshippers of God, who do nothing but external works, and that from fear or from hope of reward; and who, ignorant that the aim of the Law is that, acknowledging their sins, they flee to Christ, abuse the Law. Seeking righteousness through it, which is impossible, they never attain it, but remain unliberated in their sins, mere hypocrites.

units.la: Verf. 25. Sinaenim mons est in Arabia, pari autem ferte respondet et Hierusalem qua nunc est, fervit que cum filiis suis.
units.tr: Verse 25: For Mount Sinai is in Arabia, and it corresponds to the Jerusalem that now is, and is in slavery with her children.

units.la: Expositionis convenientiam ostendit: primò, ex eo quod mons Sina in Arabia situs, & à terra promissa longè remotus, vocetur apud Arabes & Caldæos Agar, speciali Dei providentia. Secundò, quod cognationem habeat cum terrena Hierosolyma, (qualis jam erat Apostoli tempore) seu cum Synagoga Judaica, infideli nempe, quæ servire dicitur cum filiis suis: quia tenax erat fœderis Operum, & in feivili sua conditione, alienata à Redemptore, & gratuita per eum liberatione, cum discipulis luis, manebat.
units.tr: He shows the agreement of the exposition: first, because Mount Sinai, situated in Arabia and far removed from the promised land, is called Hagar by the Arabs and Chaldeans, by the special providence of God. Second, because it has a kinship with the earthly Jerusalem (such as it was already in the Apostle's time), or with the Jewish Synagogue, namely the unbelieving one, which is said to be in slavery with her children, because she clung to the covenant of works and, alienated from the Redeemer and from the free deliverance through him, remained in her servile condition, with her disciples.

units.la: Verf. 26. Illa vero jublimis Hierusalem, libera est, quæ est mater omnium nostrûm.
units.tr: Verse 26: But the Jerusalem above is free, which is the mother of us all.

units.la: Exponit quid figuratum fit per Sara liberam, nempe fœdus Fidei seu Gratiæ, cujus tenax elt Ecclesia Christianorum verè Fidelium, quæ cœlestis & superna est Hierosolyma, à Deo procreata, & rerum cœlestium studiosa, mater omnium Fidelium ex Judæis & Gentibus evocatorum.
units.tr: He explains what is figured by Sarah, the free woman, namely the covenant of faith or grace, to which the Church of true Christian believers clings. This is the heavenly and supernal Jerusalem, created by God, zealous for heavenly things, the mother of all believers called from Jews and Gentiles.

units.la: Verf. 27. Scriptum est enim, Lætare sterilis quæ non parit: erumpe & clama quæ non parturit, quoniam plures sunt liberi deserta, quàm ejus quæ habet virum.
units.tr: Verse 27: For it is written: Rejoice, you barren woman who does not bear; break forth and cry, you who are not in labour; for the desolate has more children than she who has a husband.

units.la: Quarto loco probat Apostolus expositionem datam, ex Ifa. 54. 1. ub Ecclesia Fidelium, superior Hierosolyma, mater nostra, repræsentatur per sterilem & quasi viduam Sara: Synagoga verò Judæorum, infidelis & tenax fœderis Operum, repræsentatur per Agar fœcundam, cum marito habitantem. Comparatur autem Ecclesia Fidelium ante Christum, sterili quasi viduæ, quia ejus maritus, fœdus Gratiæ, ignorabatur fere ab omnibus, exceptis paucis, qui dispersi huc illuc cœtum non faciebant: nec comparebat gratia, sed latebat instar mariti absentis aut demortui sub ceremoniarum involucris. Comparatur verò Synagoga infidelium juftitiariorum, uxori fœcundæ, habitanti cum marito suo, nempe fœdere Operum, in externa Legis œconomia, conspicuo. Et prædicitur à Propheta fore, ut Fidelium Ecclesia, fœcundata per promissiones Dei, plures liberos fit paritura, sub Euangelio, quam Synagoga peperit servos sub Lege, & propterea jubetur letari, & Deum laudare.
units.tr: Fourth, the Apostle proves the exposition given, from Isaiah 54:1. The Church of believers, the Jerusalem above, our mother, is represented by Sarah, barren and as it were a widow; the Synagogue of the Jews, unbelieving and clinging to the covenant of works, is represented by Hagar, fruitful and dwelling with her husband. The Church of believers before Christ is compared to a barren, almost widowed woman, because her husband, the covenant of grace, was known almost by no one except a few who, scattered here and there, did not form a congregation; nor did grace appear, but lay hidden, like an absent or dead husband, under the veils of ceremonies. But the Synagogue of unbelieving legalists is compared to a fruitful wife dwelling with her husband, namely the covenant of works, conspicuous in the external economy of the Law. And the Prophet foretells that the Church of believers, made fruitful by the promises of God, will bring forth more children under the Gospel than the Synagogue brought forth slaves under the Law; and therefore she is commanded to rejoice and praise God.

units.la: Verf. 28. Nos igitur, fratres, fecundùm Ifaac, promissionis filii fumus. Ultimo loco applicat hanc typicam historiam, & vere fideles Christianos partim admonet, partim consolatur, argumentis quatuor:
units.tr: Verse 28. Therefore we, brothers, like Isaac, are children of promise. Last of all he applies this typical history, partly to admonish and partly to comfort true Christian believers, with four arguments.

units.la: Argumentum primum, Quod justificati per fidem simus Filii Redempti, & vere Liberi, vi promissionum Euangelicarum regeniti, ad similitudinem Isaaci, qui natu major est aliis post eum civibus coelestis Hierosolymæ.
units.tr: The first argument is one of admonition: that we who are justified through faith are redeemed sons and truly free, regenerated by the force of the evangelical promises, like Isaac, who was the elder of the other citizens of the heavenly Jerusalem.

units.la: Vers. 29. Sed quemadmodum tunc is qui secundum carnem genitus fuerat, persequebatur eum qui natus erat secundum Spiritum: ita & nunc.
units.tr: Verse 29. But as then he who was born according to the flesh persecuted him who was born according to the Spirit, so also now.

units.la: Arg. 2. Consolationis, Quod persequutionem patientes à falsis fratribus, liberi arbitrii & justitiæ operum Patronis, nihil alienum à sorte Isaaci experiamur: cum enim in Abrahami familia, is qui naturæ vi ordinaria tantum genitus est, persequutus sit eum, qui divinitus & spirituali ratione est genitus; Quid mirum si idem nunc usu veniat nobis?
units.tr: Second argument, of consolation: because we who suffer persecution from false brothers, the defenders of free will and of justification by works, experience nothing foreign to the lot of Isaac. For since in Abraham's family he who was born only by the ordinary power of nature persecuted him who was born by divine power and in a spiritual manner, why is it strange if the same thing now happens to us?

units.la: Vers. 30. Sed quid dicit Scriptura? Ejice ancillam & filium ejus: non enim hæres erit filius ancillæ cum filio liberæ.
units.tr: Verse 30. But what does Scripture say? Cast out the bondwoman and her son: for the son of the bondwoman shall not be heir with the son of the free woman.

units.la: Arg. 3. Quod persequutores fidelium, & patroni justitiæ ex operibus, quum liberati non sint per filium, ejicendi sint à societate Sanctorum, & vitæ æternæ hæreditate; sicut figuratum fuit in Dei sententia, de ejectione Ismaelis cum matre sua ex familia, & exclusione ab hæreditate, cum Isaaco fruenda.
units.tr: Third argument: that the persecutors of believers and the defenders of justification by works, since they have not been freed through the Son, are to be cast out from the fellowship of the saints and from the inheritance of eternal life; just as was prefigured in God's sentence concerning the expulsion of Ishmael with his mother from the household, and his exclusion from the inheritance to be enjoyed with Isaac.

units.la: Vers. 31. Nempe, fratres, non sumus ancillæ filii, sed liberæ.
units.tr: Verse 31. Indeed, brothers, we are not children of the bondwoman, but of the free woman.

units.la: Quartum argumentum ex comparatione hujus versus cum superiori: Quod, cum simus filii non ancillæ sed liberæ, hæreditatem vitæ æternæ certo simus consequuturi: quod argumentum cum superioribus vim habet sicut consolationis, sic etiam admonitionis, ne hæreant in errore suo de justitia ex operibus quærendâ, & insuper etiam hortationis, ut justitiam ex gratia per fidem, in Christum mordicus teneant, nisi velint ab hæreditate seipsos excludere.
units.tr: The fourth argument arises from comparing this verse with the previous one: that since we are children not of the bondwoman but of the free woman, we will certainly obtain the inheritance of eternal life. This argument, like the preceding ones, has the force of consolation, but also of admonition, that they should not cling to their error of seeking righteousness from works; and, further, of exhortation, that they should hold fast to righteousness by grace through faith in Christ, unless they wish to exclude themselves from the inheritance.

units.la: Caput
units.tr: Chapter

units.la: Caput Quintum.
units.tr: Chapter 5.

units.la: DUÆ sunt Capitis partes: In prima pergit urgere ut excusso jugo fœderis Operum & Ceremoniarum Legalium, libertatem Christianam tueantur, ad verf. 13. In altera præcepta dat de recto usu libertatis Christianæ, ad finem.
units.tr: There are two parts to this chapter. In the first he goes on urging them, having shaken off the yoke of the covenant of works and of the legal ceremonies, to maintain Christian liberty, down to verse 13. In the second he gives precepts on the right use of Christian liberty, to the end.

units.la: Verf. 1. IN libertate igitur qua Christus nos liberavit, perstate, & ne è contrario implicamini servitutis jugo.
units.tr: Verse 1. Stand firm, then, in the liberty with which Christ has set us free, and do not be caught again under the yoke of slavery.

units.la: Propositio in priori parte confirmanda, apertè proponitur sub hortationis forma. Perstandum vobis est in libertate Christiana, quæ scopus est superioris doctrinæ & disputationis, ex eaque deducitur tanquam conclusio. Argumenta ad confirmandam hanc propositionem sunt tredecim.
units.tr: The proposition to be confirmed in the first part is set out plainly in the form of an exhortation: you must persist in Christian liberty, which is the aim of the preceding teaching and argument, and is drawn from it as a conclusion. There are thirteen arguments to confirm this proposition.

units.la: Argumentum primum, Libertas à servili jugo legalis fœderis & Ceremoniarum ipsius, parta est per CHRISTI sanguinem: Ergo vobis perstandum est in ea.
units.tr: First argument: liberty from the servile yoke of the legal covenant and of its ceremonies has been won through the blood of Christ. Therefore you must persist in it.

units.la: Verf. 2. Ecce, ego Paulus dico vobis, si circumcidamini, Christum nihil vobis profuturum.
units.tr: Verse 2. Behold, I, Paul, say to you that if you are circumcised, Christ will profit you nothing.

units.la: Arg. 2 Obtestatione Apostolica sancitum. Si ex lege Ceremoniali jam abolita circumcidamini, & vel unam hanc Ceremoniam ad gratuitam justificationem per CHRISTUM addatis; CHRISTUS, quem hoc facto imperfectum Servatorem declaratis, non est vobis profuturus ad salutem. Perstandum ergo. Nam si justificari non poterant nisi unâ cum gratia CHRISTI iungerent circumcisionem, dimidium justitiæ suæ facientes CHRISTUM, perdebant totum; imperfectum Salvatorem statuentes, faciebant eum sibi nullum.
units.tr: Second argument, sanctioned by an apostolic solemn appeal. If you are circumcised under the ceremonial law, now abolished, and add this one ceremony to justification freely given through Christ, then Christ, whom by this act you declare to be an imperfect Saviour, will not profit you for salvation. Therefore persist. For if they could not be justified unless they joined circumcision to the grace of Christ, making Christ only half of their righteousness, they would lose the whole; by declaring him an imperfect Saviour, they would make him no Saviour at all to them.

units.la: Verf. 3. Testor enim rursum omni homini qui circumciditur, eum esse debitorem totius Legis servandæ.
units.tr: Verse 3. For I testify again to every man who is circumcised that he is a debtor to keep the whole Law.

units.la: Arg. 3. Eadem obtestatione sancitum, Abrogato fœdere operum & lege ceremoniali jam abolitâ. si quis redeat ad circumcisionem, sacramentum inaugurale hujus legalis fœderis, seipsum facit debitorem ex pacto totius legis, & per consequens obligat se ad maledictionem, nisi legem perfecte praestiterit ex viribus suis, quae est conditio foederis Operum. Res patet. Quia, licet circumcisio ex Dei instituto fidelibus MESSIAM expectantibus usque ad CHRISTUM, sacramentum fuerit justitiae fidei, (quomodo Abrahamus circumcisus est) & licet tolerationis tempore usque ad Christianae libertatis claram manifestationem, Judaeis natis, circumcisio fuerit in rebus mediis; (quomodo Timotheus ex matre Judaea circumcisus est, & Titus non est circumcisus.) Omnibus tamen Judaeis, & Proselytis ex Gentibus, justitiam ex operibus seu lege quaerentibus, Circumcisio facta est pars justitiae legalis, seu obedientiae foederis Operum: imo & Sacramentum illius foederis. Et hoc modo Pseudapostoli urgebant Circumcisionem inter Galatas, quibus illicita erat Circumcisio religiosa, omni modo. Non mirum ergo si dicat CHRISTUM non profuturum iis, si circumciderentur, quia circumcisi foedus Operum amplectebantur ipso facto.
units.tr: Third argument, sanctioned by the same solemn appeal. The covenant of works has been abrogated and the ceremonial law is now abolished. If anyone returns to circumcision, the inaugural sacrament of this legal covenant, he makes himself by that very act a debtor under the terms of the agreement to the whole law, and so binds himself to the curse, unless he has perfectly kept the law by his own strength, which is the condition of the covenant of works. The matter is plain. For although circumcision, by God's institution, was a sacrament of the righteousness of faith for believers who awaited the Messiah until Christ (as Abraham was circumcised), and although, during the time of toleration, until the clear manifestation of Christian liberty, circumcision was a matter indifferent for Jews by birth (as Timothy, born of a Jewish mother, was circumcised, and Titus was not circumcised), nevertheless for all Jews, and for proselytes from the Gentiles, who sought righteousness by works or by the law, circumcision became a part of legal righteousness, or of obedience to the covenant of works, and indeed a sacrament of that covenant. In this way the false apostles pressed circumcision upon the Galatians by every means, although for them religious circumcision was unlawful. It is no wonder, then, that he says Christ will not profit them if they are circumcised, since by being circumcised they embraced the covenant of works by that very fact.

units.la: Vers. 4. Facti estis inanes Christi, quicunque per Legem justificamini, & a gratia excidistis.
units.tr: Verse 4. You are estranged from Christ, you who are justified by the Law; you have fallen from grace.

units.la: Arg. 4. Confirmans superius. Quicunque ad circumcisionem & legales ritus abolitos reditis, justificationem quaerentes per Legem, CHRISTO, & foederi gratiae, ipso facto renunciatis; quia foedus operum & foedus gratiae in CHRISTO, se mutuo excludunt, neque consistere possunt. Nam si justificatio est ex operibus, non est ex gratia, & contra: Ergo perstandum est in libertate, nisi a CHRISTO & Gratia separari velletis.
units.tr: Fourth argument, confirming the above. Whoever of you return to circumcision and the abolished legal rites, seeking justification through the Law, by that very fact renounce Christ and the covenant of grace. For the covenant of works and the covenant of grace in Christ exclude each other and cannot stand together. If justification is by works, it is not by grace, and conversely. Therefore you must persist in liberty, unless you wish to be cut off from Christ and from grace.

units.la: Vers. 5. Nos enim Spiritu ex fide spem justitiae expectamus.
units.tr: Verse 5. For we, through the Spirit, by faith, wait for the hope of righteousness.

units.la: Arg. 5. Nos Judaei & Apostoli circumcisi, post nostram conversionem ad fidem, per Spiritum edocti, renunciavimus foederi operum & ritibus legalibus, & expectamus vitam aeternam, ut fructum justificationis per fidem: vos natura Gentiles, neque poteritis aliter, seu per Legem vel Circumcisionem justificari & servari. Idcirco in libertate Christiana vobis perstandum.
units.tr: Fifth argument: we Jews and apostles were circumcised, and after our conversion to faith, taught by the Spirit, we renounced the covenant of works and the legal rites, and we await eternal life as the fruit of justification through faith. You, Gentiles by nature, cannot be justified and saved in any other way, that is, through the Law or circumcision. Therefore you must persist in Christian liberty.

units.la: Vers. 6. Nam in Christo Iesu neque circumcisio quicquam valet, neque praeputium, sed fides per charitatem agens.
units.tr: Verse 6. For in Christ Jesus neither circumcision avails anything, nor uncircumcision, but faith working through love.

units.la: Arg. 6. Confirmans superius. In CHRISTI regno, seu novo statu Ecclesiae sub foedere Gratiae, sublatum est discrimen circumcisionis & praeputii: ad justificationem nihil illa prodest, nihil istud nocet: Ergo perstandum in libertate a jugo legis. Sed fidei] Arg. 7. Sola fides vera, seu quæ per charitatem est efficax, absque respectu ad circumcisionem vel præputium, ad justificandi actum valet. Ergo in hac justificationis ratione, vobis qui in Christi regno estis, perstandum est necessario.
units.tr: Sixth argument, confirming the above. In the kingdom of Christ, that is, the new state of the Church under the covenant of grace, the distinction between circumcision and uncircumcision has been removed: circumcision contributes nothing to justification, and uncircumcision harms nothing. Therefore persist in liberty from the yoke of the law. But faith: Seventh argument. Faith alone, true faith, which is effective through love, without regard to circumcision or uncircumcision, avails for the act of justifying. Therefore, in this manner of justification, you who are in the kingdom of Christ must necessarily persist.

units.la: Verf. 7. Currebatis pulchrè, quis vos interpellavit, ut non obsequeremini veritati?
units.tr: Verse 7. You were running well; who hindered you from obeying the truth?

units.la: Arg. 8. In studio veritatis doctrinæ hujus currebatis benè non itaque pridem, nec potest reddi ratio defectionis ab hac veritate: Ergo pergendum adhuc, & perstandum in illo cursu.
units.tr: Eighth argument: in the pursuit of the truth of this doctrine you were running well not long ago, and no reason can be given for your falling away from this truth. Therefore you must still press on and persist in that course.

units.la: Verf. 8. Hæc persuasio non est ex eo qui vocat vos.
units.tr: Verse 8. This persuasion is not from him who calls you.

units.la: Arg. 9. Per occupationem objectionis. Etiamsi forsan persuasum vobis sit, vos rectam viam adhuc tenere; credulitas tamen ista, & persuasio ad recedendum ab eo, quod à me accepistis, non est à DEO vos vocante, sed aliunde, scilicet ab impostoribus, à vestra inconstantia, & à Diabolo: Ergo rejicienda hæc persuasio & in libertate perstandum vobis est.
units.tr: Ninth argument, by way of anticipating an objection. Even if you are perhaps persuaded that you still hold the right way, that credulity and that persuasion to turn away from what you received from me are not from God who calls you, but from elsewhere: namely from impostors, from your own inconstancy, and from the devil. Therefore this persuasion is to be rejected, and you must persist in liberty.

units.la: Verf. 9. Paulum fermenti totam massam fermentat.
units.tr: Verse 9. A little leaven leavens the whole lump.

units.la: Arg. 10. Per occupationem objectionis. Etiamsi videri posset, non contendendum esse de paucorum aliquot rituum introductione, concordiæ causâ, & ut Judæi facilius lucrifierent; hoc tamen paululum fermenti legalis seu Judaismi, totam sinceritatem doctrinæ fidei corrumpit: Ergo cavendum ab eo, & perstandum in libertate.
units.tr: Tenth argument, by way of anticipating an objection. Even if it might seem that one should not contend over the introduction of a few ritual observances, for the sake of concord and so that the Jews might be won more easily, yet this little leaven of the legal or Judaizing spirit corrupts the whole purity of the doctrine of faith. Therefore one must beware of it and persist in liberty.

units.la: Verf. 10. Ego confido de vobis in Domino, vos nihil aliud esse sensuros; sed qui turbat vos, auferet condemnationem, quisquis fuerit.
units.tr: Verse 10. I am confident of you in the Lord that you will think nothing otherwise; but he who troubles you will bear his judgment, whoever he is.

units.la: Arg. 11. Etiamsi erroris periculum, & vestra inconstantia suspicionem mihi injiciunt de eventu; meliora tamen sperare jubet charitas, & gratiæ divinæ constantia, quam dum respicio, persuasum habeo vos rediturros in eandem mecum sententiam de Legis jugo abjiciendo, & libertate tuenda per fidem in Christum. Ergo expectationi meæ satisfacere æquum est.
units.tr: Eleventh argument: even if the danger of error and your inconstancy give me cause to doubt the outcome, charity and the steadfastness of divine grace bid me hope for better things. While I consider these, I am persuaded that you will come back with me to the same judgment, to cast off the yoke of the Law and to maintain liberty through faith in Christ. Therefore it is right that my expectation should be satisfied.

units.la: Turbat] Arg. 12 Seductores vestri, qui vestram fidem turbant, in quacunque tandem sunt apud vos existimatione, graves Deo luent pœnas, ne igitur & vos illdem plagis implicemini sed resipiscite, & in libertate perstate. Verf 11. Egò autem, fratres, si circuncisionem etiam prædico, quid adhuc perfequutionem patior? nempè abolitum est offendiculum crucis.
units.tr: Troubles: Twelfth argument: your seducers, who disturb your faith, whatever esteem they may enjoy among you, will pay heavy penalties to God. Therefore, lest you too be caught up in the same plagues, repent and persist in liberty. Verse 11. But I, brethren, if I still preach circumcision, why do I still suffer persecution? Surely the stumbling-block of the cross has been removed.

units.la: Refellit calumniam adversariorum, & affert Arg. 13. Tuipse doces circumcisionem, quia circumcidisti Timotheum; Ergo immeritò nos reprehendis: Respondet negando se docere Circumcisionem, quia licet Timotheum ex Judæa matre oriundum circumciderit, (nam Judæis Ceremoniarum usus, post fractum jugum necessitatis ex decreto Synodi, ad tempus liber relictus est) nunquam tamen prædicabat circumcisionem observandam, sed & Judæos monebat de abolitione Ceremoniarum, & Ceremonias legales nulla ratione inter Gentes recipiendas docebat: Quod probat; Quia hoc nomine persequutionem patiebatur à Judæis, & quia non offensi fuissent Judæi prædicatione Euangelii seu crucis Christi, sed libenter toleràssent Apostolum, si promovisset rituum Judaicorum inter Gentes receptionem.
units.tr: He refutes the calumny of his opponents and brings a thirteenth argument: "You yourself teach circumcision, since you circumcised Timothy; therefore you rightly reprove us." He answers by denying that he teaches circumcision. Although he circumcised Timothy, born of a Jewish mother (for after the yoke of necessity was broken, by the decree of the Synod, the Jews were left free for a time to use the ceremonies), he never preached that circumcision was to be observed. Rather, he warned the Jews of the abolition of the ceremonies, and taught that the legal ceremonies were by no means to be received among the Gentiles. This is proved because on this account he suffered persecution from the Jews, and because the Jews would not have been offended by the preaching of the gospel or of the cross of Christ, but would gladly have tolerated the apostle if he had promoted the reception of Jewish rites among the Gentiles.

units.la: Argumenti vis hæc est, Ego persequutionem pati malo, quam circumcisionem prædicare cum Euangelio jungendam; nam si conjungerem, cessaret offensio crucis, tolerarent Judæi meam prædicationem Christi crucifixi, Ego autem latum unguem non audeo recedere ab Euangelii puritate. Ergo & vobis in ea perstandum est.
units.tr: The force of the argument is this: I would rather suffer persecution than preach that circumcision must be joined to the gospel. For if I joined them, the offence of the cross would cease, and the Jews would tolerate my preaching of the crucified Christ; but I do not dare to depart a hair's breadth from the purity of the gospel. Therefore you too must persist in it.

units.la: Verf. 12. Utinam etiam abscindantur qui vos inquietant.
units.tr: Verse 12. Would that those who trouble you were even cut off.

units.la: Tandem ut claudat totam disputationem, Spiritu Apostolico, exitium imprecatur, & denunciat impostoribus, à quibus Galatæ decepti erant;
units.tr: Finally, to close the whole discussion, he calls down ruin, in the spirit of an apostle, upon the impostors by whom the Galatians had been deceived.

units.la: Secunda Pars.
units.tr: Second Part.

units.la: Verf. 13. Vos enim ad libertatem vocati estis, fratres, tantum ne libertatem arripite, ut detis carni occasionem, sed ex charitate servite alii aliis.
units.tr: Verse 13. For you were called to liberty, brethren; only do not use liberty as an opportunity for the flesh, but through love serve one another.

units.la: Secunda pars Capitis, in qua reddita ratione imprecationis, quia nempe seductores ad jugum revocabant, & retrahebant eos, quos Deus ad libertatem vocabat, sub hortationis forma, tria dat præcepta de recto usu libertatis Christianæ.
units.tr: The second part of the chapter. Having given the reason for his curse, namely that the seducers were calling them back under the yoke and drawing away those whom God had called to liberty, he gives, in the form of exhortation, three precepts concerning the right use of Christian liberty.

units.la: Tantum Primum præceptum, Ut carnem seu pravam corruptæ naturæ concupiscentiam frænantes (ne illa effrænis libertatem Christianam nam traheret in peccandi licentiam ) sibi invicem serviant in charitatis officiis.
units.tr: Only. The first precept: that, restraining the flesh, that is, the depraved lust of corrupt nature (lest it, unbridled, turn Christian liberty into licence to sin), they serve one another in the duties of love.

units.la: Verl. 14. Nam tota Lex uno verbo completur isto, videlicet, Diliges proximum tuum ut teipsum.
units.tr: Verse 14. For the whole law is fulfilled in one word, namely, You shall love your neighbour as yourself.

units.la: Rationes hujus praecepti dat duas. Prima, Quia charitate impletur lex, & non jejunis ceremoniis.
units.tr: He gives two reasons for this precept. The first is that the law is fulfilled by love, and not by empty ceremonies.

units.la: Verf. 15. Quod si alii alios mordetis & devoratis, videte ne vicissim alii ab aliis consumamini.
units.tr: Verse 15. But if you bite and devour one another, take heed that you are not consumed by one another.

units.la: Ratio 2. Quia nisi charitati studeant, contentionibus se mutuo conficient, devorabunt & perdent.
units.tr: Reason 2: because, unless they devote themselves to love, they will destroy, devour and ruin one another by contentions.

units.la: Verl. 16. Hoc autem dico, spiritu incedite, & quod concupiscit caro, ne perficite.
units.tr: Verse 16. But I say, walk in the Spirit, and you shall not fulfil the lust of the flesh.

units.la: Secundum praeceptum in subsidium primi, ut ductum Spiritus sancti sequantur, prout ipse ex Scriptura incedendum suggesserit iplorum cordibus.
units.tr: The second precept, in support of the first: that they follow the guidance of the Holy Spirit, walking as he, from Scripture, suggests to their hearts.

units.la: Et quod ] Rationes praecepti sunt sex: Ratio prima, Quia sic concupiscentia carnis non dominabitur vobis, ut jussa ejus tanquam servi exequamini. Idcirco Spiritus ductum sequimini.
units.tr: And that ] There are six reasons for the precept. The first reason: thus the lust of the flesh will not rule over you, so that you carry out its commands as slaves. Therefore follow the guidance of the Spirit.

units.la: Verf. 17. Nam caro concupiscit adversus Spiritum, Spiritus autem adversus carnem. Haec autem inter se opposita sunt, ut non quaecunque volueritis, eadem faciatis.
units.tr: Verse 17. For the flesh lusts against the Spirit, and the Spirit against the flesh. These are opposed to one another, so that you do not do whatever you will.

units.la: Ratio 2. confirmans superiorem, Quia qui sequitur Spiritus ductum, superior evadet in lucta carnis & Spiritus. Ut haec ratio plana sit, tria praesupponit Apostolus: 1. Eum qui Spiritu ducitur, naturam habere ex parte renovatam, quae Spiritus dicitur: & ex parte corruptam, quae Caro dicitur. 2. Praesupponit haec duo principia contrariis studiis invicem pugnare, ut neque bonum, neque malum sine oppositione, & mutuo impedimento, possit executioni mandari. 3. Praesupponit SPIRITUM sanctum, in lucta credenti auxilium afferre, per Verbum & Gratiam. Unde conficitur eum qui auscultat SPIRITUI, superiorem in lucta evadere.
units.tr: Reason 2, confirming the previous one: whoever follows the guidance of the Spirit will prevail in the struggle between flesh and Spirit. To make this reason plain, the apostle presupposes three things: (1) that the one who is led by the Spirit has a nature partly renewed, which is called Spirit, and partly corrupt, which is called flesh; (2) that these two principles fight against each other with opposing aims, so that neither good nor evil can be carried into effect without opposition and mutual hindrance; (3) that the Holy Spirit brings help to the believer in the struggle, through the Word and grace. Hence it follows that the one who listens to the Spirit prevails in the struggle.

units.la: Verf. 18. Quod si Spiritu ducimini, non estis sub Lege.
units.tr: Verse 18. But if you are led by the Spirit, you are not under the law.

units.la: Ratio 3. confirmans superiorem, Quia qui Spiritus ductum sequuntur, non sunt mancipia peccati sub servili foedere Legis; quibus notitia tantum datur peccati, non vero victoria, vel vires adversus peccatum, sed liberti Dei sub fœdere Gratiæ, qui vires à Deo nanciscuntur, ut peccato resistant.
units.tr: Reason 3, confirming the previous one: those who follow the guidance of the Spirit are not slaves of sin under the servile covenant of the law, to whom only the knowledge of sin is given, and not victory or strength against sin; they are free men of God under the covenant of grace, who receive from God the strength to resist sin.

units.la: Vers. 19. Porrò manifesta sunt opera carnis: quæ sunt, adulterium, fornicatio, impuritas, protervia,
units.tr: Verse 19. Now the works of the flesh are manifest, which are these: adultery, fornication, uncleanness, lasciviousness,

units.la: Vers. 20. Idololatria, veneficium, inimicitiæ, lis, æmulationes, iræ, contentiones, dissidia, hæreses,
units.tr: Verse 20. Idolatry, witchcraft, hatreds, strife, jealousies, wrath, contentions, dissensions, heresies,

units.la: Vers. 21. Invidiæ, cædes, ebrietates, comessationes, & his similia: quæ prædico vobis, sicut prædixi, eos videlicet, qui talia agunt, Regni Dei non fore hæredes.
units.tr: Verse 21. Envyings, murders, drunkenness, revellings, and things like these, of which I tell you beforehand, as I have also told you, that those who do such things shall not inherit the kingdom of God.

units.la: Ratio 4. Quia si Spiritum non sequantur, sed carnem potiùs, facientes opera carnis, (qualia enumerat septemdecim) tum regni Dei non sunt futuri hæredes.
units.tr: Reason 4: if they do not follow the Spirit, but rather the flesh, doing the works of the flesh (which he lists as seventeen in number), then they will not be heirs of the kingdom of God.

units.la: Verf. 22. At fructus Spiritus, est charitas, gaudium, pax, lenitas, benignitas, bonitas, fides, mansuetudo, temperantia.
units.tr: Verse 22. But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, kindness, goodness, faith, meekness, temperance.

units.la: Verf. 23. Adversus eos qui sunt ejusmodi, non est Lex.
units.tr: Verse 23. Against such there is no law.

units.la: Ratio 5. Quia si Spiritum sequantur, & fructus tales ferant (quales enumerat novem) non sunt habituri legem sibi adversam, id est, ipsis maledicentem, & ipsos condemnantem: sed propter ipsorum reconciliationem erga DEUM, legem amicam experturi. Idcirco Spiritum sequi oportebat.
units.tr: Reason 5: if they follow the Spirit and bear such fruits (which he lists as nine), they will not have a law opposed to them, that is, one that curses them and condemns them, but, through their reconciliation with God, they will experience the law as a friend. Therefore it was right to follow the Spirit.

units.la: Verf. 24. Qui enim sunt Christi, carnem crucifixerunt cum affectibus & concupiscentiis.
units.tr: Verse 24. For those who are Christ's have crucified the flesh with its affections and lusts.

units.la: Probat non habituros legem adversam, Quia qui CHRISTI sunt, & in CHRISTO judicialiter crucifixi, in satisfactionem Legis, etiam judicialiter obligati sunt, ad Corpus peccati, id est, corruptam naturam cum ipsius affectibus, & concupiscentiis crucifigendum. Quapropter qui actu studeant, id praestare, & fructus SPIRITUS ferre, non possunt Legem sibi adversam habere, utpote qui Legis fini & scopo promovendo jam sedulo studeant.
units.tr: He proves that they will not have a law opposed to them: because those who belong to Christ, and have been judicially crucified in Christ, have also been judicially bound, in satisfaction of the law, to crucify the body of sin, that is, corrupt nature with its affections and lusts. Therefore those who actively strive to accomplish this, and to bear the fruits of the Spirit, cannot have a law opposed to them, since they already diligently labour to advance the end and purpose of the law.

units.la: Verf. 25. Si vivimus Spiritu, Spiritu etiam incedamus.
units.tr: Verse 25. If we live by the Spirit, let us also walk by the Spirit.

units.la: Ratio 6. Quia habemus per Spiritum consolationem, pacem & gaudium, in quibus vita consistit: Ergo Spiritus ductum sequi debemus.
units.tr: Reason 6: because through the Spirit we have consolation, peace and joy, in which life consists. Therefore we ought to follow the guidance of the Spirit.

units.la: Verf. 26. Ne simus inanis gloriæ cupidi, alii alios provocantes, alii aliis invidentes. Tertium Præceptum est speciale, de vitanda ambitione, cum istius vitii asseclis, obtrectatione scilicet & invidiâ, quibus malis Ecclesiæ infestari solent. Quia autem obnoxii sunt his vitiis imprimis Ecclesiæ Doctores: idcirco se includit in exhortatione cum reliquis, ut Galatæ exhortationem facilius admittant.
units.tr: Verse 26. Let us not be desirous of vainglory, provoking one another, envying one another. The third precept is a special one, concerning the avoiding of ambition, with its companions, namely backbiting and envy, by which evils the Church is usually troubled. And because the teachers of the Church are especially liable to these vices, he includes himself with the rest in the exhortation, so that the Galatians may more readily accept the exhortation.

units.la: Caput Sextum.
units.tr: Chapter Six.

units.la: Efficia Christiana pergit Galatis præscribere, Ceremoniis illis legalibus multò præstantiora, & digniora, in quibus se exerceant. Capitis duæ sunt partes, in prima ad superiora præcepta addit alia duo, ad versum undecimum. In altera, se cum Pseudapostolis comparat, & merito se illis præfert, ne ipsorum admiratione deciperentur Galatæ.
units.tr: The Christian exhortation now goes on to prescribe to the Galatians things far more excellent and worthy than those legal ceremonies, in which they should exercise themselves. The chapter has two parts. In the first, he adds two further precepts to the above, up to verse eleven. In the second, he compares himself with the false apostles, and rightly prefers himself to them, so that the Galatians may not be deceived by their admiration.

units.la: Vers. 1. Fratres, etiam si præoccupatus fuerit homo in aliqua offensa, vos spirituales, instaurate huiusmodi homines cum spiritu mansuetudinis: considerans temetipsum, ne & tu tenteris.
units.tr: Verse 1. Brethren, even if a man has been overtaken in some offence, you who are spiritual, restore such a man in a spirit of gentleness, considering yourself, lest you too be tempted.

units.la: Præceptum primum de leniter tractandis fratribus, qui ex infirmitate labuntur, ut in Spiritu mansuetudinis instaurentur, ab iis qui confirmatiores Spiritu videntur, speciatim vero Presbyteros alloquitur, quibus ex officio incumbit lapsos in scandalum per censuras Ecclesiasticas, ad resipiscentiam revocare, & luxata Ecclesiæ membra, in locum suum restituere: Hos jubet lenitate uti erga eos, qui ex infirmitate lapsi sunt, nec severius eos tractare, quod proculdubiò pertinet ad eos, qui jus animadvertendi in peccatores habent. Rationes præcepti sunt sex. Ratio prima, Quia idem accidere potest ex tentatione, cuivis, etiam spiritualibus.
units.tr: The first precept concerns gently dealing with brothers who fall through weakness, that they may be restored in a spirit of gentleness by those who seem stronger in the Spirit. He addresses especially the elders, to whom it falls by office to recall those who have fallen into scandal to repentance through ecclesiastical censures, and to restore the dislocated members of the Church to their place. He bids them use gentleness toward those who have fallen through weakness, and not treat them more severely, which doubtless pertains to those who have the right of punishing sinners. There are six reasons for the precept. The first reason: the same thing can happen to anyone through temptation, even to spiritual men.

units.la: Vers. 2. Alii aliorum onera portate, & ita complete Legem CHRISTI
units.tr: Verse 2. Bear one another's burdens, and so fulfil the law of Christ.

units.la: Ratio 2. Quia cum præsupponendum sit, fratres peccantes de lapsibus illis & peccatis suis tristari, & gravari: idcirco æquum est ut omni animi moderatione & sympathia dejecti, & jacentes peccatores subleventur, & in onere suo portando adjuvantur.
units.tr: The second reason: since it must be presupposed that brothers who sin are saddened and weighed down by their lapses and sins, it is only fair that those who have been cast down and lie as sinners be raised up with all moderation of mind and sympathy, and helped to carry their burden.

units.la: Et ita] Ratio 3. Quia id a nobis exigit lex dilectionis à Christo renovata.
units.tr: And so The third reason: the law of love renewed by Christ requires this of us.

units.la: Verf. 3 Nam si quis sibi videtur aliquid, quum nihil sit, hunc suus ipsius animus fallit.
units.tr: Verse 3. For if anyone thinks himself to be something, when he is nothing, his own mind deceives him.

units.la: Ratio 4. Qui alios ex infirmitate labentes despicit, & sibiipsi videtur robustior, fallit seipsum, & inter infirmissimos ipse est, imo homo nihili est.
units.tr: The fourth reason: whoever despises others who fall through weakness, and thinks himself the stronger, deceives himself, and is himself among the weakest; indeed, he is nothing.

units.la: Verf. 4. Opus autem suum probet unusquisque, & tunc in semetipso gloriationem habebit, & non in alio.
units.tr: Verse 4. But let each one prove his own work, and then he will have his boasting in himself, and not in another.

units.la: Ratio 5. Per modum praecepti proposita, ad ἀυτασθεναν retundendam faciens, & contemptum fratris labentis evitandum. Quia si unusquisque se probaret, & secundum regulam legis divinae examinaret suas actiones, non arriperet sibi quisquam laudem sanctitatis, ex alienis peccatis, sed ex suis recte factis tantum, si quae laude digna inveniret. Dictum hoc in illos, qui nullum finem faciunt exaggerandi peccatum alienum, ut ipsi videantur sanctiores.
units.tr: The fifth reason: proposed in the form of a precept, serving to beat down self-conceit [ἀυτασθεναν] and to avoid contempt for a fallen brother. For if each one tested himself and examined his actions by the rule of the divine law, no one would snatch for himself the praise of holiness from other men's sins, but only from his own right deeds, if he found any worthy of praise. This is said against those who never stop magnifying the sin of others so that they themselves may seem holier.

units.la: Verf. 5. Nam unusquisque onus suum portabit.
units.tr: Verse 5. For each one will bear his own burden.

units.la: Ratio 6. Confirmans praecedentem, Quia unusquisque reddet rationem factorum suorum Deo, non collatus cum aliis, sed per se spectatus: Ergo despicere labentes in peccatum & efferri, quia tu non similiter lapsus es, non est tutum.
units.tr: The sixth reason, confirming the previous one: each one will render account of his deeds to God, not compared with others but judged on his own. Therefore to despise those who fall into sin, and to be puffed up because you have not fallen in the same way, is not safe.

units.la: Verf. 6. Communicet autem qui instituitur in sermone, ei qui se instituit, omnia bona.
units.tr: Verse 6. But let him who is taught in the word share all good things with him who teaches him.

units.la: Secundum praeceptum ad populum spectat, de liberalitate erga verbi Ministros exercenda, ut communicemus corporalia bona iis, qui nobis ex officio communicant spiritualia, & huic negotio vacant.
units.tr: The second precept concerns the people, and the liberality to be shown to ministers of the Word: that we share bodily goods with those who, by their office, share spiritual goods with us and devote themselves to this business.

units.la: Verf. 7. Ne fallimini: Deus non irridetur, quicquid enim seminaverit homo, hoc & metet.
units.tr: Verse 7. Do not be deceived: God is not mocked; for whatever a man sows, that he will also reap.

units.la: Rationes Praecepti dat sex, quae omnes extenduntur ad beneficentiam in genere, & praeceptum confirmant de benefaciendo Pastoribus, à fortiori. Ratio prima supponens eos qui ingrati sunt erga Doctores, tenaces etiam esse, & ad omne opus bonum tardos, quia tenacitatis excusationes sunt avarorum deceptiones, quibus ludificari sibi non patietur DEus.
units.tr: He gives six reasons for the precept. All of them extend to beneficence in general, and confirm, all the more, the precept about doing good to ministers. The first reason presupposes that those who are ungrateful to teachers are also tenacious and slow to every good work, since the excuses of tightfistedness are the deceptions of the greedy, by which God will not allow himself to be mocked.

units.la: ] Ratio 2. Quia secundùm facta feret fructum unusquisque, qui verba tantùm dederit, & qui gratitudinem reipsa præstare recusaverit, dignum ingratitudine recipiet premium, & contra.
units.tr: The second reason: each one will bear fruit according to his deeds; whoever has given only words, and has refused to show gratitude in deed, will receive a reward fitting his ingratitude, and conversely.

units.la: Verf 8. Nam qui seminat carni suæ, ex carne metet interitum: qui verò seminat Spiritui, ex Spiritu metet vitam æternam.
units.tr: Verse 8. For he who sows to his flesh will from the flesh reap corruption; but he who sows to the Spirit will from the Spirit reap eternal life.

units.la: Hoc argumentum explicat in specie: Qui bona seu facultates, & actiones suas ad carnis suæ cupiditates explendas refert, is ex factis reportaturus est interitum: qui verò contra se suaque omnia impendit ad DEI gloriam, & opera Spiritus promovenda, reportaturus est mercedem ex gratiâ, vitam æternam.
units.tr: He explains this argument in particular: whoever refers his goods, means and actions to satisfying the desires of his flesh will reap destruction from those deeds; but whoever spends all he has, himself included, for the glory of God and the advancement of the works of the Spirit, will receive eternal life as a reward, by grace.

units.la: Verf. 9 Torrò ne benefaciendo fegnescamus: tempore enim suo metemus, si non elanguerimus.
units.tr: Verse 9. And let us not grow weary in doing good, for in due season we shall reap, if we do not lose heart.

units.la: Ratio 3. Quia quæcunque dici poterint de beneficentia ab aliquo jam præstita, quasi satis ab ipso jam actum sit, tenendum tamen est, quod non sufficiant benefacta præterita, nisi perseveremus in benefaciendo.
units.tr: The third reason: whatever may be said about beneficence already shown by someone, as if he had already done enough, it must still be held that past good deeds do not suffice unless we persevere in doing good.

units.la: ] Ratio 4. Priorem illustrans & confirmans. Quia solis perseverantibus in benefaciendo, & non succumbentibus, vel defatigatis in bene agendo, messis præmiorum certò futura est, tempore idoneo.
units.tr: The fourth reason, illustrating and confirming the former: only to those who persevere in doing good, and do not give way or grow weary in acting well, will the harvest of rewards certainly come, at the proper time.

units.la: Verf. 10. Nempe igitur dum tempus habemus, simus benefici erga omnes, maximè verò erga domesticos fidei.
units.tr: Verse 10. Therefore, as we have opportunity, let us do good to all, especially to the household of faith.

units.la: Ratio 5. Quia breve tempus est beneficentiæ exercendæ, & ideo occasio observanda, dum vita & facultates suppetunt: nam satis lera est legatio morientium.
units.tr: The fifth reason: the time for exercising beneficence is short, and so the opportunity must be watched while life and means remain; for the errand of the dying is short enough.

units.la: ] Ratio 6. Commune naturæ vinculum beneficentiam requirit erga omnes egenos: vinculum fraternitatis majorem beneficentiam requirit erga fideles domesticos fidei; quantò igitur magis requirit vinculum gregis ad Pastores ut vellere & lacte gregis alatur Pastor.
units.tr: The sixth reason: the common bond of nature requires beneficence toward all the needy; the bond of brotherhood requires greater beneficence toward the faithful, the household of faith. How much more, then, does the bond of the flock require that the shepherd be fed with the fleece and milk of the flock.

units.la: Secunda Pars.
units.tr: The Second Part.

units.la: Verf. 11. Videtis quàm longis literis vobis scripserim mea manu. Secunda pars capitis, in qua post comparatam suam doctrinam cum errore adversariorum, jam comparat doctores cum doctoribus, id est, le cum seductoribus Galatarum, idque in eorum aedificationem, qui in admiratione habebant personatos istos doctores seductores suos.
units.tr: Verse 11. You see with how long a letter I have written to you with my own hand. This is the second part of the chapter. Having compared his own doctrine with the error of his opponents, he now compares teachers with teachers, that is, true teachers with the seducers of the Galatians, and he does so for the building up of those who were admiring those masked seducers of theirs.

units.la: Ante comparationem praemittit commendationem suae dilectionis sincerae in Galatas, Quod hanc Epistolam tam copiosam, manu propria, sine opera amanuensis alicu jus descripserit, in amplissimum testimonium solicitudinis suae, de ipsorum salute.
units.tr: Before the comparison he sets out a commendation of his sincere love towards the Galatians: that he wrote this letter so long, in his own hand and without the help of any scribe, as the strongest evidence of his concern for their salvation.

units.la: Verf. 12. Quicunque volunt speciosi apparere in carne, ii cogunt vos circuncidi, tantum ne ob crucem Christi persequutionem patiantur. Ingreditur comparationem, & probat aemulorum hypocrisin ex 4 indiciis:
units.tr: Verse 12. As many as desire to make a fair show in the flesh, they constrain you to be circumcised; only lest they should suffer persecution for the cross of Christ. He enters on the comparison and proves the hypocrisy of his rivals from four signs:

units.la: Verf. 13. Nam ne ipsi quidem qui circuncidantur, Legem servant: sed volunt vos circumcidi, ut de vestra carne glorientur.
units.tr: Verse 13. For neither they themselves who are circumcised keep the law; but they desire to have you circumcised, that they may glory in your flesh.

units.la: Verf. 14. At me vero absit gloriari, nisi in cruce Domini nostri Iesu Christi: per quem mundus mihi crucifixus est, & ego mundo.
units.tr: Verse 14. But God forbid that I should glory, save in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ, by whom the world is crucified unto me, and I unto the world.

units.la: In altera parte comparationis, Apostoli sinceritas demonstratur in his duobus. 1. Quod glorietur tantum in Christi crucifixi gratuita redemptione, & in passionibus suis pro hac doctrina. 2. Quod pompam mundanam non affectet, sed mundum qui ipsum persequebatur, & contemnebat; propter doctrinam crucis, vicissim contemnat cum omni pompa & gloria mundana, & per crucem discat indies magis magisque mundum contemnere.
units.tr: In the other part of the comparison, the sincerity of the Apostle is shown in these two things. First, that he glories only in the free redemption of Christ crucified, and in his own sufferings for this doctrine. Second, that he does not aim at worldly pomp, but, as the world which persecuted him and despised him is despised by him in turn for the doctrine of the cross, so he despises all worldly pomp and glory, and learns through the cross to despise the world more and more each day.

units.la: Verf. 15. Nam in Christo Iesu, neque circumcisio quicquam valet, neque praeputium, sed nova creatio.
units.tr: Verse 15. For in Christ Jesus neither circumcision availeth any thing, nor uncircumcision, but a new creature.

units.la: Rationes studii sui reddit Quæ totidem sunt sinceritatis indicia: Ratio 1. Scio in Christi regno neque respici à Deo circumcisionem, neque præputium, sed novam tantùm creaturam, hoc est, Scio necesse esse, ubi per fidem jam admissus sit aliquis in Christi regnum, & justificatus, ut magis magisque renovetur, & sanctificetur, reliqua verò privilegia nullius esse pretii absque vitæ renovatione. Idcirco gloriabor tantùm in cruce Christi, &c.
units.tr: He gives the reasons for his zeal, which are as many signs of sincerity. Reason 1: I know that in the kingdom of Christ God regards neither circumcision nor uncircumcision, but only a new creature. That is, I know it is necessary that, where anyone has already been admitted by faith into the kingdom of Christ and justified, he should be renewed and sanctified more and more; whereas other privileges are of no worth apart from renewal of life. Therefore I will glory only in the cross of Christ, etc.

units.la: Vers. 16. Et quicunque secundùm hanc regulam incedent, pax erit super eos & misericordia, & super Israelem Dei.
units.tr: Verse 16. And as many as walk according to this rule, peace be on them, and mercy, and upon the Israel of God.

units.la: Ratio 2. Instituti mei regula est summa totius Scripturæ Canonicæ, ad quam tanquam unicam regulam seu Canonem unicum, doctrina & vita omnium sit conformanda. Idcirco gloriabor in cruce Christi &c.
units.tr: Reason 2: The rule of my office is the sum of the whole canonical Scripture, to which, as to the one rule or the one canon, the doctrine and life of all men must be conformed. Therefore I will glory in the cross of Christ, etc.

units.la: Ratio 3. Persuasum habeo, quod quicunque fidem & vitam suam ad hunc Canonem composituri sunt, Pacem etiam, id est, sensum reconciliationis suæ erga Deum, omnimodam benedictionem, seu cumulationem bonorum, & misericordiam, seu remedium ad averruncanda omnia mala consequuturi sint. Idcirco gloriabor tantùm in cruce Christi &c.
units.tr: Reason 3: I am persuaded that all who shape their faith and life by this canon will obtain peace, that is, the sense of their reconciliation with God, complete blessing, or an abundance of goods, and mercy, or a remedy for averting all evils. Therefore I will glory only in the cross of Christ, etc.

units.la: Ratio 4. Soli sequentes hunc Canonem sunt verus Israel Dei. Idcirco ego rebus aliis, susque deque habitis, gloriabor tantùm in cruce Christi per, &c. Verf. 17 De cætero, nequis mihi molestias exhibeto: ego enim stigmata Domini Iesu in corpore meo porto.
units.tr: Reason 4: Only those who follow this canon are the true Israel of God. Therefore I, setting other things at nought, will glory only in the cross of Christ, etc. Verse 17. From henceforth let no man trouble me: for I bear in my body the marks of the Lord Jesus.

units.la: Post comparationem; ut victor de æmulis triumphat, vetans ne amplius facessant ipsi negotium, sive obloquendo ejus doctrinæ, sive detrahendo ejus autoritati; eò quod insignia gestet suæ in CHRISTUM fidelitatis, stigmata scilicet servi CHRISTO addictissimi, hoc est, habeat omnia signa Apostoli, & fidelis Martyris aperte in se conspicienda.
units.tr: After the comparison, as a victor triumphs over his rivals, he forbids them to give him any further trouble, whether by speaking against his doctrine or by detracting from his authority, because he bears the badges of his fidelity to CHRIST, namely the marks of a servant most devoted to CHRIST. That is, he has all the signs of an Apostle and a faithful Martyr, which are plainly to be seen upon him.

units.la: Verf. 18. Gratia Domini nostri Iesu Christi sit cum Spiritu vestro, fratres. Amen.
units.tr: Verse 18. Brethren, the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit. Amen.

units.la: Consueto signaculo Epistolam claudit, optans, ut in ipsorum mentibus, cordibus, & tota vita, gratia IESU CHRISTI, patefacta, credita, &c. ta, & opere efficax insideat, ut inde consolationem hauriant in vita & morte, cui subjicitur Amen, in Testimonium voti & fidei Apostoli, & in Sigillum veritatis praecedentis Doctrinae.
units.tr: He closes the Epistle with his customary seal, wishing that the grace of JESUS CHRIST, made manifest, believed, and effective in deed, may dwell in their minds, hearts, and whole life, so that they may draw consolation from it in life and in death.
