To this is added Amen, as the Apostle's attestation of his wish and faith, and as the seal of the truth of the preceding doctrine.

units.la: EXPOSITIO ANALYTICA EPISTOLAE PAULI AD EPHESIOS.
units.tr: EXPOSITIO ANALYTICA EPISTOLAE PAULI AD EPHESIOS.

units.la: Summarium.
units.tr: Summary.

units.la: VRbs Ephesiorum Metropolis fuit Asiae minoris, in qua Apostolus totum biennium Euangelium praedicavit, Act. 19. Et cum postremo Hierosolymam ascenderet, Ephesiis imminentem Ecclesiae mutationem praedixit, Act. 20. adversus quam ipsos munit per hanc Epistolam, cum jam Romae captivus teneretur, deque reditu suo plane desperaret, animosque eorum in fide & veritate confirmare satagit.
units.tr: The city of Ephesus was the metropolis of Asia Minor, where the Apostle preached the Gospel for two whole years (Acts 19). When he finally went up to Jerusalem, he foretold to the Ephesians the change that was threatening the Church (Acts 20). Against this he fortifies them by the present Epistle, written while he was already held captive at Rome and had quite despaired of his return, and he labours to confirm their minds in faith and truth.

units.la: Partes Epistolae, praeter Praefationem & Epilogum, duae sunt principales: Prima est doctrina Gratiae, spectans ad confirmationem Fidei, ad caput 4. Altera est doctrina Gratitudinis, tendens ad sanctitatem vitae, ad finem.
units.tr: Apart from the Preface and the Epilogue, the Epistle has two main parts. The first is the doctrine of grace, which bears on the confirmation of faith, up to chapter 4. The second is the doctrine of gratitude, which aims at holiness of life, to the end.

units.la: Quod ad primam partem attinet: Primo ostendit totam rationem salutis nostrae gratuitam esse, & in Christo solide fundatam, Capite primo. Deinde amplificat gratiam hanc a pristina Ephesiorum miseria, Capite secundo.
units.tr: As for the first part: first, he shows that the whole reason of our salvation is free and solidly founded in Christ, in chapter 1. Then he amplifies this grace by setting it against the former misery of the Ephesians, in chapter 2.

units.la: Tertio sublato scandalo Crucis sibi incumbentis, per gloriosam Commendationem Ministerii sui, & expositionem Causae pro qua patiebatur, hortatur eos ad Constantiam, & Progressum faciendum in Fide, Capite tertio.
units.tr: Third, having removed the stumbling-block of the Cross that lay upon him, by a glorious commendation of his ministry and an account of the cause for which he suffered, he exhorts them to steadfastness and to progress in faith, in chapter 3.

units.la: In secunda parte Præcepta dat de Ecclesia unitate servanda: De Vitæ sanctitate, cum in genere, tum in specie, in vitiis fugiendis, & virtutibus sectandis, quibus vita uniuscujusque, Christianum in modum componatur, Capite quarto, & priori parte Capitis quinti.
units.tr: In the second part he gives precepts concerning the preservation of unity in the Church, and concerning holiness of life, both in general and in particular: in shunning vices and pursuing virtues, by which the life of each person is shaped in a Christian manner, in chapter 4 and the first part of chapter 5.

units.la: Iste hæc descendit ad Officia œconomica: ad quæ & reliqua omnia officia Christiana præstanda, Fideles armat, posteriori parte Capitis quinti, & priori parte Capitis sexti.
units.tr: From here he descends to domestic duties, and by these he arms the faithful to perform all the other Christian duties, in the latter part of chapter 5 and the first part of chapter 6.

units.la: Caput Primum.
units.tr: Chapter 1.

units.la: Capitis Partes post Præfationem duæ sunt, in prima est gratiarum actio, tendens ad demonstrandam totam rationem salutis, & Judæorum, & Gentilium merè gratuitam, & totam in CHRISTO fundatam esse, ad verf. 15. In altera est commemoratio assiduæ gratiarum actionis, cum precatione ab Apostolo Deo oblata pro Ephesiis, tendens ad fidei confirmationem, de certitudine salutis ipsorum, & omnium verè fidelium perficiendæ, ad finem.
units.tr: The parts of the chapter after the Preface are two. The first is thanksgiving, which aims to show that the whole plan of salvation, for both Jews and Gentiles, is wholly by grace and is founded entirely in Christ, to verse 15. The second is a recollection of the Apostle's constant thanksgiving, together with the prayer he offers to God for the Ephesians, which aims to confirm their faith concerning the certainty of their own salvation and that of all truly faithful people, to the end.

units.la: Præfatio, duobus primis versibus, in directione Epistolæ, & salutatione Ephesiorum continetur: Est autem ea brevis admodum, quia res ei hic est non cum æmulis vel hostibus, sed cum morigeris, quibus brevis significatio auctoritatis divinæ in Epistolæ hujus scriptione, & benevolentiæ Apostoli erga ipsos, & existimationis ipsius de iis sufficiebat.
units.tr: The Preface is contained in the first two verses, in the address of the letter and the greeting to the Ephesians. It is very brief, because the Apostle is dealing here not with rivals or enemies but with compliant readers, for whom a short indication of the divine authority behind this letter, of the Apostle's goodwill towards them, and of his good opinion of them was sufficient.

units.la: Verf. 1. P Aulus Apostolus Iesu Christi, per voluntatem Dei, sanctis qui agunt Ephesi, & fidelibus in Iesu Christo.
units.tr: Verse 1. Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ, by the will of God, to the saints who are at Ephesus, and to the faithful in Jesus Christ.

units.la: Vers. 1. IN directione Epistolæ descriptio est primùm Scriptoris, à nomine, officio & autoritate. Deinde eorum ad quos scribit, à statu in quo erant apud Deum, & à loco in quo habitabant in terra. Scriptor est Paulus Apostolus qui ex voluntate Dei à Christo, de Cœlo loquente, extra ordinem legatus missus est ad Ecclesiam Christo colligendam, satis hic autoritatis. Illi ad quos scribit sunt sancti, fidelesque Ephesii in Christo, qui scilicet per fidem Christo insiti, ad Deo servien-dum consecrati erant. Satis hic æstimationis.
units.tr: Verse 1. In the address of the letter, the writer is first described by his name, office and authority, and then those to whom he writes are described by the status they had before God and by the place where they lived on earth. The writer is Paul the Apostle, who was sent out of the ordinary course, by the will of God, by Christ speaking from heaven, to gather the Church for Christ; this gives him sufficient authority. Those to whom he writes are the saints, the faithful Ephesians in Christ, who, clearly, had been grafted into Christ by faith and set apart to serve God. This gives them sufficient esteem.

units.la: Vers. 2. Gratia sit vobis & pax à Deo Patre nostro, & Domino Iesu Christo. V V
units.tr: Verse 2. Grace be to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.

units.la: In salutatione continetur Apostolica benedictio, in qua primò optat Ephesiis gratiam, id est, omnia bona cœlestia quæ ad sanctificationem & salutem necessaria sunt. Secundò optat illis specialem fructum hujus gratiæ, Pacem scilicet, seu omnia qua ad felicitatem faciunt, imprimis vero animi tranquillitatem ex redemptione Christi ortam; quæ redemptio ipsis per Verbum & Spiritum Dei applicata, de reconciliatione erga Deum certos, & de liberatione à malo securos, eos redderet. 3. Fontem & canalem gratiæ & pacis optatæ aperit, Deum nempe à quo, & Christum Mediatorem, per quem, & propter quem, gratia & pax ad nos derivantur. Satis hic benevolentiæ erga Ephelios. Satis etiam argumentorum ad parandum ipsorum animos, ut doctrinam sequentem admitterent eâ quâ decebat animi submissione & benevolentia.
units.tr: In the greeting is contained the apostolic blessing. In it he first wishes the Ephesians grace, that is, all the heavenly blessings that are necessary for sanctification and salvation. Secondly, he wishes them the special fruit of this grace, namely peace, or everything that contributes to happiness, and above all tranquillity of mind arising from the redemption of Christ. This redemption, applied to them through the Word and Spirit of God, would make them certain of reconciliation with God and secure in their deliverance from evil. Thirdly, he opens the source and channel of the grace and peace he wishes, namely God, from whom they come, and Christ the Mediator, through whom and for whose sake grace and peace are conveyed to us. This shows sufficient goodwill towards the Ephesians. It also provides enough reasons to dispose their minds to accept the teaching that follows with the humility and goodwill that befit them.

units.la: Vers. 3. Benedictus Deus & Pater Domini nostri Iesu Christi, qui benedixit nobis omni benedictione spirituali in cœlis in Christo.
units.tr: Verse 3. Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who has blessed us with every spiritual blessing in the heavenly places in Christ.

units.la: Post præfationem proponitur Gratiarum actio, continens propositionem probandam, in priori hujus Capitis parte, quæ hæc est; Dei gratia in Christo cum benedictionis divinæ, erga nos agnitione celebranda est, in tota ratione salutis fidelium. Nam nostrum benedicere ad Deum relatum, nihil aliud est quam Deum omnis benedictionis seu gratiæ erga nos authorem modis omnibus agnoscere.
units.tr: After the Preface comes the thanksgiving, which contains the proposition to be proved. In the first part of this chapter the proposition is this: the grace of God in Christ is to be celebrated, together with the acknowledgment of the divine blessing towards us, in the whole plan of salvation for the faithful. For our blessing directed towards God is nothing other than acknowledging in every way that God is the author of every blessing or grace towards us.

units.la: In hac autem propositione distinguit Deum Patrem ab Iesu Christo Mediatore [Greek] ut melius appareant Mediatoris persona & officium: Et Deum patrem vocat Deum Christi: 1. Propter gratiam, qua prædestinata est humana Christi natura ad unionem personalem cum [Greek] filio. 2. Propter fœdus redemptionis initum inter Deum & Mediatorem Christum. Deinde Patrem vocat Iesu Christi, primo propter æternam Filii generationem, qua Pater totam infinitam suam essentiam ei ab æterno communicavit. 2. Propter humanæ naturæ assumptæ personalem unionem, qua filius hominis factus est filius Dei.
units.tr: In this proposition, the Apostle distinguishes God the Father from Jesus Christ the Mediator [Greek], so that the person and office of the Mediator may appear more clearly. He calls God the God of Christ: (1) on account of the grace by which the human nature of Christ was predestined to personal union with the [Greek] Son; (2) on account of the covenant of redemption entered into between God and Christ the Mediator. Then he calls him the Father of Jesus Christ: first, on account of the eternal generation of the Son, by which the Father from eternity communicated to him his whole infinite essence; secondly, on account of the personal union of the assumed human nature, by which the Son of God became the Son of man.

units.la: Argumenta ad probandam propositionem prædictam principalia sunt tredecim.
units.tr: There are thirteen principal arguments for proving the above proposition.

units.la: Benedixit] Argumentum primum, Deus & Pater Christi benedixit nobis fidelibus, seu gratuito cumulavit nos omnibus beneficiis spiritualibus & cœlestibus in Christo: Ergo benedicendus est à nobis, seu gratia ejus celebranda est à nobis: Ad hunc scopum ut Dei gratia appareat & celebretur, tendunt singula hujus argumenti verba, quae omnia gratiam spirant. Nam primò donator beneficiorum vocatur Deus, & Pater Iesu Christi, & per consequens Deus & Pater nostrum omnium, qui sumus in Christo; idque ex foedere inter Patrem & Christum, de nobis inito: & per consequens Pater noster qui affectu paterno omnia nobis donat.
units.tr: Blessed] The first argument: God and the Father of Christ has blessed us who believe, that is, has freely loaded us with all spiritual and heavenly benefits in Christ. Therefore he is to be blessed by us, that is, his grace is to be celebrated by us. Each word of this argument tends to this aim, that the grace of God may appear and be celebrated; all of them breathe grace. For, first, the giver of the benefits is called God, and Father of Jesus Christ, and consequently God and Father of all of us who are in Christ; and this is by the covenant between the Father and Christ made concerning us; and consequently he is our Father, who gives us all things with paternal affection.

units.la: Benedixit] 2. Beneficiorum donatio vocatur active Dei benedictio, id est, actualis seu efficax gratiae Dei secundum verbum suum, in opere erga nos demonstratio. Benedixit nobis] 3. Et hic gratia est: Nam Nos quibus benedixit Deus, natura filii irae sumus, & maledictioni Dei obnoxii, in quibus nihil est, nec esse potest, quod bonum aliquod promereri possct. Omni benedictione] 4. Ipsorum beneficiorum natura & ratio involvit gratiam; nam benedictio passive sumpta, nihil aliud est quam beneficium ex gratia mera ortum habens.
units.tr: Blessed] Secondly, the bestowing of benefits is called God's blessing in the active sense, that is, the demonstration in deed of the actual or effective grace of God according to his word towards us. Has blessed us] Thirdly, here too is grace: for we, to whom God has given his blessing, are by nature children of wrath and liable to the curse of God, and in us there is nothing, nor can there be anything, that could merit any good. With every blessing] Fourthly, the very nature and reason of the benefits themselves involve grace; for blessing taken in the passive sense is nothing other than a benefit arising from pure grace.

units.la: Benedictione spirituali] 5. Et hic gratia est; Nam beneficia quae nobis prae aliis donantur sunt spiritualia, ad salutem aeternam spiritus, seu animae spectantia, quae excedunt omnem commensum proportionis ad opera terrena & temporalia, quae à nobis in hoc corpore nostro praestari possunt, & idcirco sunt gratuita.
units.tr: With spiritual blessing] Fifthly, here too is grace. For the benefits given to us above others are spiritual, pertaining to the eternal salvation of the spirit or soul, and they far exceed any proportion to the earthly and temporal works that we can perform in this body of ours; and therefore they are free gifts.

units.la: Omni benedictione] 6. Et hoc ad gratiam spectat; Quia omne donum spirituale, quod ad salutem animarum spectat, nobis datur: ex quibus donis nullum est, quod non ex gratiae seu benedictionis fonte fluat, & gratis donetur nobis, sine omni nostro merito, seu respectu ad opera nostra, sive sit cognitio DEI, sive agnitio peccati nostri, sive resipiscentia, sive fides, sive fidei effectus aliquis, sive sit opus aliquod bonum, sive intentio boni operis: omne illud gratis ab illo datur, qui omni spi-rituali benedictione nobis benedixit. Ergo gratuita omnia sunt.
units.tr: With every blessing] Sixthly, this too belongs to grace. Because every spiritual gift that pertains to the salvation of souls is given to us; and among these gifts there is none that does not flow from the fountain of grace or blessing, and is given to us freely, without any merit of ours or regard to our works, whether it be the knowledge of God, or the recognition of our sin, or repentance, or faith, or some effect of faith, or some good work, or the intention of a good work. Every such thing is given freely by him who has blessed us with every spiritual blessing. Therefore all things are free.

units.la: 7. Et hic gratiæ radius est, Quia beneficia hæc, quibus nos præ aliis beamur, sunt cœlestia, quæ scilicet à Cœlo originem trahunt, in Cœlo conservantur, & in Cœlo complebuntur, nec nostram carnem ullo modo sapiunt, sed nostram conditionem in terra nobis condiunt.
units.tr: Seventhly, here is a ray of grace: because these benefits, by which we are blessed above others, are heavenly, that is, they draw their origin from heaven, are kept in heaven, and will be fulfilled in heaven; nor do they in any way savour of our flesh, but they season our condition on earth for us.

units.la: Hic gratiæ oceanus aperitur, Nam omnia hæc beneficia, nostra sunt in Christo, qui ipse noster est, & omnia hæc nostra fiunt in Illo, ut in radice & fonte, Capite & Parente nostro communi, antequam perveniant ad nos, ut per Eum ad nos deriventur: In quo, prout ipsi uniti sumus, possidemus quæ habemus, & in quo jus habemus ad ea quæ nondum accepimus, & per quem postea quæ supersunt sumus accepturi; quique ut omnia nobis acquisivit, sic in Se, ea in nostrum usum, & nos, ut iis utamur, fruamur, conservat. Ex quibus singulis & omnibus sequitur omnia spiritualia beneficia esse gratuita, seu meræ gratiæ effecta, & propterea celebrandam esse Dei gratiam à nobis, ut fontem & causam omnium.
units.tr: Here the ocean of grace is opened. For all these benefits are ours in Christ, who himself is ours, and all these things become ours in him, as in the root and fountain, our common Head and Parent, before they reach us, so that they may flow down to us through him. In whom, as we are united to him, we possess what we have, and in whom we have a right to those things we have not yet received, and through whom we shall afterwards receive whatever remains. He who, as he has acquired all things for us, so in himself preserves them for our use, and preserves us so that we may use them and enjoy them. From each and all of these it follows that all spiritual benefits are free, or the effects of pure grace; and therefore God's grace is to be celebrated by us as the fountain and cause of all.

units.la: Verf. 4. Sicut elegit nos in ipso, antequam jacerentur fundamenta mundi, ut simus sancti & inculpati coram eo per charitatem.
units.tr: Verse 4. Even as he chose us in him before the foundation of the world, that we should be holy and blameless before him in love.

units.la: Arg. 2. Confirmans prius, Deus actu in tempore, gratuito nobis benedicit omnibus spiritualibus benedictionibus in Christo, quemadmodum ante tempora nos elegit ex gratia in Ipso, ut omnia illa beneficia tandem consequeremur. Ergo à nobis benedicendus est: Omnia etiam hujus argumenti verba argumenta sunt gratuitæ electionis.
units.tr: Arg. 2. Confirming what was said before: God, acting in time, freely blesses us with all spiritual blessings in Christ, just as before time began he chose us by grace in Him, so that we might at last obtain all those benefits. Therefore we must bless him for it. All the words of this argument are arguments for free election.

units.la: Primo enim electio à Deo fuit Nostri ad vitam, præ aliis nostris consortibus in eadem conditione constitutis, quibus præteritis & relictis Deus nos elegit. Ergo ex gratia electi sumus.
units.tr: First, the election by God was of us, to life, above our other companions who were placed in the same condition, and whom God passed over and left behind when he chose us. Therefore we are chosen by grace.

units.la: Secundò, Elegit nos in Christo, ut in capite primò electo, ut in communi electorum parente, radice & fonte? Post quem in momento dignitatis & ordinis, & in quo nos, ut ejus corpus, membra & progeniies, ordine naturæ posteriores eligimur. Gratuita ergo electio nostri est, cujus nulla causa in nobis, sed in solo Deo quærenda est.
units.tr: Secondly, he chose us in Christ, as in the head, who was chosen first, as in the common parent, root and fountain of the elect? After whom, in the moment of dignity and order, and in whom, we are chosen, as his body, members and offspring, later in the order of nature. Therefore our election is free, and its cause is to be sought not in us but in God alone.

units.la: Tertiò, Elegit nos ante jacta mundi fundamenta, id est, ab æterno, priusquam mundus fuit; nedum antequam ulla nostra opera extiterunt; elegit nos antequam ulla ratio mundi conditi habita est, nedum antequam ratio ullorum nostrorum operum, seu operationum habita est: nam elegit nos ordine naturæ, antequam mundus futurus decerneretur: Decretum enim de mundo condendo, subservit ut medium producendi in effectum salutem decretam jam Electorum: Ergo ex Gratia elegit nos, & non ex prævisis operibus.
units.tr: Thirdly, he chose us before the foundations of the world were laid, that is, from eternity, before the world existed; much less before any of our works came into being. He chose us before any account was taken of the created world, much less before any account was taken of our works or actions. For he chose us in the order of nature before the world to come was decreed. For the decree concerning the creation of the world serves as the means of bringing into effect the salvation already decreed for the elect. Therefore he chose us by grace, and not on account of foreseen works.

units.la: Elegit nos, ut essemus Sancti Quartò, Non elegit nos quia eramus Sancti, aut quia prævidit futuros Sanctos, sed elegit nos fine sanctitatis ullius in nobis consideratione, imò ut non habentes sanctitatem elegit, in eum finem, ut jam electi, sancti fieremus, & inculpati tandem redderemur in conspectu ejus, id est, ut Deo consecrati, gradatim vere ac sincere sanctificaremur, & tandem plene, perfectèque sancti in {Q}tiin Coelo sisteremur: imò verò etiam ut inculpati sine macula, sine ruga, sine vestigio, non peccati solùm, sed etiam omnis miseriæ, beati & gloriosi compareremus tandem coram ipso: Ergo electio non est ex fide prævisa aut prævisis operibus, sed ex gratia merâ, quæ simul causa est electionis, & simul etiam sanctitatis omnis, & felicitatis quæ sequitur electionem.
units.tr: That we should be holy. Fourthly, he did not choose us because we were holy, or because he foresaw that we would be holy, but he chose us for the end of holiness, with no consideration of any holiness in us. Indeed, not having holiness, he chose us to this end: that, being already elect, we should become holy, and at last be presented blameless in his sight; that is, that, consecrated to God, we should be gradually and truly and sincerely sanctified, and finally presented in heaven fully and perfectly holy. Indeed, we should appear before him at last blameless, without spot, wrinkle or trace, free not only of sin but of all misery, blessed and glorious. Therefore election does not rest on foreseen faith or foreseen works, but on mere grace, which is at once the cause of election and of all the holiness and happiness that follow election.

units.la: In charitate ] Dilectio seu charitas merè gratuita est, in qua sicut elegit nos, ut redderemur sancti & inculpati, sic etiam ut in charitate illa sua, perficeret hanc nostram felicitatem: quam charitatem Deus tum demum plenè exeret, cum sanctitatem & felicitatem nostram plenè consummabit. Atque ita charitas Dei, est & electionis causa, & bonorum, quæ electionem sequuntur complementum, & per consequens electio non tantùm est ex gratia, sed etiam ad possessionem perfectam gratuitæ felicitatis, in conspectu Dei.
units.tr: In love. Love or charity is purely free, and in it, just as he chose us that we should be made holy and blameless, so also in that his love he would bring this our happiness to completion. God will fully display this love only when he has completely consummated our holiness and happiness. Thus the love of God is both the cause of election and the completion of the blessings that follow election; and consequently election is not only by grace, but also leads to the full possession of free happiness in the sight of God.

units.la: Vers. 5. Qui prædestinavit nos, quos adoptaret in filios per Iesum Christum in se, ex benevolo affectu voluntatis suæ:
units.tr: Verse 5. Who predestinated us to adopt us as sons through Jesus Christ to himself, according to the good pleasure of his will:

units.la: Arg. 3. Sic ex gratia in tempore nobis benedixit Deus, sicut ex gratia prædestinavit nos ad hæreditatem filiorum obtinendam per Christum in se, juxta beneplacitum voluntatis suæ: Ergo gratia ipsius à nobis celebranda est. Hujus rationis partes idem probant quod tota.
units.tr: Arg. 3. So God blessed us in time by grace, just as by grace he predestinated us to obtain the inheritance of sons through Christ in himself, according to the good pleasure of his will. Therefore his grace is to be celebrated by us. The parts of this argument prove the same thing as the whole.

units.la: Prædestinavit nos ] 1. Sicut fuit gratuita electio nostri ante tempora, sic etiam & prædestinatio fuit nostri ante secula ad vitam æternam, & ad omnia idonea media quæ ad eum finem nos ducerent efficaciter: Ergo prædestinatio Gratuita est, utpote quæ non tantùm finem & personas definivit, sed & media statuit, per quæ ad finem perveniremus.
units.tr: He predestinated us. 1. Just as our election was free before time, so also our predestination to eternal life was ours before the ages, together with all the fitting means that would lead us effectively to that end. Therefore predestination is free, since it not only defined the end and the persons, but also appointed the means by which we would reach the end.

units.la: Quos adoptaret in filios ] 2. Etiam hic Dei gratiam ostendit Apostolus. Prædestinamur non quia jam filii prævisi sumus, sed ut non filii, ex gratia adoptionem filiorum consequeremur. Adoptio autem filiorum hæc quatuor includit: 1. Vocationem efficacem seu fidem ad amplectendam oblatam communionem cum Christo filio unigenito: 2. Indolem & ingenium filiorum, seu renovationem naturæ ad Deum diligendum ut patrem: 3. Dignitatem seu honorem filiorum: 4 Divitias seu hæreditatem filiorum, usque ad glorificationem corporum, Rom. 8 23. Ergo & prædestinatio & adoptio nostri est gratuita, & non ex aliquo opere nostro.
units.tr: To adopt us as sons. 2. Here too the Apostle shows the grace of God. We are predestinated not because we were already foreseen as sons, but so that, though not sons, we might by grace obtain adoption as sons. Now this adoption of sons includes four things: (1) effectual calling, or faith, to embrace the communion with Christ the only-begotten Son that is offered; (2) the disposition and nature of sons, that is, renewal of nature so that we love God as Father; (3) the dignity or honour of sons; (4) the riches or inheritance of sons, extending to the glorification of our bodies (Rom. 8:23). Therefore both predestination and adoption are ours by grace, and not from any work of ours.

units.la: 3. Et hoc ad gratiam illustrandam facit, Prædestinamur ad obtinendam adoptionem filiorum per Iesum Christum, qui filius est primogenitus, & unigenitus, ut per ejus meritum & efficaciam omnes prædictos gradus adoptionis consequeremur: Ergo prædestinamur ex mera gratia.
units.tr: 3. This also serves to illustrate grace: we are predestinated to obtain the adoption of sons through Jesus Christ, who is the firstborn and only-begotten Son, so that through his merit and efficacy we might attain all the aforesaid degrees of adoption. Therefore we are predestinated by mere grace.

units.la: 4. Ut appareat gratia, finem adoptionis ostendit: Prædestinavit nos Deus, ut filiorum adoptionem consequeremur per Christum, ad sese, seu in usum suum, scilicet, ad honorem sui prædestinantis, seu Christi per quem nobis communicat gratiam, & gloriam illam filiorum Dei: Ergo prædestinatio est gratuita, alioqui enim non rediret honor ad Deum, vel Christum, ex adoptione nostri.
units.tr: 4. That grace may appear, he shows the end of adoption: God predestinated us so that we might obtain adoption as sons through Christ, to himself, or for his own use, namely, to the honour of himself who predestinates, or of Christ through whom he communicates grace to us and that glory of the sons of God. Therefore predestination is free; otherwise no honour would return to God or Christ from our adoption.

units.la: 5. Hic causas omnes excludit extra Deum, & gratiam Dei solam facit causam. Nam prædestinavit nos juxta beneplacitum voluntatis suæ. Sola igitur Dei gratia, sola voluntas, solum beneplacitum Dei causa est prædestinationis nostri, nullum vero opus nostrum.
units.tr: 5. Here he excludes all causes outside God and makes the grace of God alone the cause. For he predestinated us according to the good pleasure of his will. Therefore the sole grace of God, the sole will, the sole good pleasure of God is the cause of our predestination, and no work of ours at all.

units.la: Verf. 6. Ad laudem gloriosæ suæ gratiæ, qua nos gratis effecit sibi gratos in illo dilecto:
units.tr: Verse 6. To the praise of the glory of his grace, by which he made us freely acceptable to him in the beloved:

units.la: Arg. 4. Deus eo ipso fine ut laudem gratiæ suæ gloriosæ consequeretur, elegit & prædestinavit nos in adoptionem filiorum. Necessario sequitur ergo Deum ex gratia elegisse, & prædestinasse nos: alioqui, finem illum assequi non potuisset; & per consequens celebranda est nobis Dei gratia, & benedicendum Deo, qui benedixit nobis.
units.tr: Arg. 4. God, for this very end, that he might obtain the praise of his glorious grace, chose and predestinated us to the adoption of sons. It necessarily follows, therefore, that God chose and predestinated us from grace; otherwise he could not have attained that end. Consequently the grace of God is to be celebrated by us, and God, who has blessed us, is to be blessed.

units.la: Gloriosæ ] Emphasin etiam habent hujus rationis verba, siquidem s. Gratia hæc gloriam habet in se, id est, gloriosa est omni modo, & dignissima in se, quam maximi æstimaremus, quam agnosceremus, & prædicaremus, quia Deus optimus maximus nos pessimos & indignissimos, dignatus est ad dignitatem filiorum, & divitias hæreditatis filialis evehere. Ad laudem ] Deinde Deus laudem hujus gratiæ gloriosæ, & intendit & expectat a nobis, ut beneficium agnoscamus verbis & factis, & ut quibuscumque poterimus modis, hanc admirandam Dei gratiam celebremus.
units.tr: Glorious. The words of this argument also carry emphasis, since s. This grace has glory in itself, that is, it is glorious in every way and most worthy in itself, such that we should esteem it most highly, acknowledge it and proclaim it, because God, the best and greatest, has deigned to raise us, the worst and most unworthy, to the dignity of sons and the riches of a filial inheritance. To the praise. Further, God both intends and expects from us the praise of this glorious grace: that we acknowledge the benefit in word and deed, and that by whatever means we can we celebrate this admirable grace of God.

units.la: In qua ] Arg. 5. Hac ipsa gratia qua Deus nos elegit & prædestinavit ad sanctitatem & felicitatem ante tempora, hac ipsa (inquam) gratia gratos nos acceptosque reddidit sibi, in filio suo dilecto. Ergo nobis celebranda est hæc Dei gratia. In qua ratione insinuat quatuor: 1. DEUM ex gratia salutem intendisse nostram in electione & praedestinatione, actu vero & opere gratiam exerere cepisse in efficaci vocatione nostri ad fidem. CHRISTUM non solum ut filium, sed ut Mediatorem spondentem pro nobis, & persolventem pro nobis pretium Redemptionis nostrae, dilectum esse & gratum Deo, in quo Patri plene nostro nomine complacitum est. 3. In illo, & per illum, removeri peccatum, quod posset gratiae cursum erga nos inhibere: 4. Denique insinuat, per CHRISTUM, & in CHRISTO, dissoluta peccatorum nube, gratiam Dei respledere erga nos, nosque complecti & fovere, ut reconciliatos, ut gratos jam acceptosque in CHRISTO, qui ut sponsor, & communis noster parens, in se nos omnes comprehendit.
units.tr: In which. Argument 5. By this very grace by which God chose and predestinated us to holiness and happiness before time, by this very grace (I say) he made us pleasing and acceptable to himself in his beloved Son. Therefore this grace of God is to be celebrated by us. In this argument he hints at four things: (1) that God intended our salvation by grace in election and predestination, and began actually to exercise grace in working our effectual calling to faith; (2) that Christ is beloved and pleasing to God not only as Son but as Mediator, who undertook on our behalf and paid on our behalf the price of our redemption, and in whom it has pleased the Father fully, in our name; (3) that through him and in him sin, which could hinder the course of grace toward us, is removed; (4) finally, he hints that, through Christ and in Christ, the cloud of sins having been dissolved, the grace of God shines again upon us, and embraces and cherishes us as reconciled, and now pleasing and accepted in Christ, who, as surety and our common parent, comprehends us all in himself.

units.la: Vers. 7. In quo habemus redemptionem per sanguinem ipsius, remissionem, inquam, peccatorum ex divite ipsius gratia.
units.tr: Verse 7. In him we have redemption through his blood, that is, the forgiveness of sins, according to the riches of his grace.

units.la: Arg. 6. In CHRISTO ex divite Dei gratia, Redemptionem & remissionem peccatorum consequimur. Ergo celebranda nobis sola Dei gratia in salute nostra. In hunc scopum tendunt omnes hujus rationis partes.
units.tr: Argument 6. In Christ, by the rich grace of God, we obtain redemption and the forgiveness of sins. Therefore the grace of God alone is to be celebrated in our salvation. All the parts of this argument aim at this goal.

units.la: Redemptionem Primo, Fuimus nos in nobis perditi, & captivi detenti in caecitatis, peccati, irae & mortis vinculis, unde nosmet ipsos liberare nullo modo poteramus: unde nullus exitus dabatur, nisi gratia, & eam aperuisset, & nos eduxisset: Ergo ex gratia salus nostra.
units.tr: Redemption. First, we were lost in ourselves and held captive in the chains of blindness, sin, wrath and death, from which we could in no way free ourselves. No way out was open to us unless grace opened it and led us out. Therefore our salvation is from grace.

units.la: In quo 2. CHRISTUS solus sine ullo nostro merito aut adjumento nos redemit, redemptionis pretio pacto, & persoluto a se solo; ne laudis quicquam decederet Dei gratiae.
units.tr: In whom. Second, Christ alone redeemed us, without any merit or help of ours, having paid the price of redemption by himself alone, so that no part of the praise would be taken from the grace of God.

units.la: Per Sanguinem 3. Non redempti sumus argento vel auro, sed sanguine CHRISTI filii Dei, ut ipsum pretium ostenderet discrimen in quo versabamur, & Dei gratiam commendaret.
units.tr: Through his blood. Third, we were redeemed not with silver or gold but with the blood of Christ, the Son of God, so that the price itself would show the peril in which we were placed and would commend the grace of God.

units.la: Remissio 4. Per CHRISTI sanguinem impetrata est in specie remissio peccatorum nostrorum, in quibus jacebamus polluti, quibus solis divites eramus in Dei conspectu, & omni opere bono destituti, ut gratia Dei in nostris peccatis, & indignitate magis splenderet.
units.tr: Forgiveness. Fourth, through the blood of Christ the forgiveness of our sins, in which we lay defiled, has been obtained in its kind. We were rich in the sight of God only in these sins, and destitute of every good work, so that the grace of God would shine all the more in our sins and unworthiness.

units.la: In Quo 5. Hanc redemptionem, & peccatorum remissionem, jam fideles facti, habemus non in nobis seorsim a CHRISTO, sed in CHRISTO ut Sponsore, Redemptore & Capite nostro, ipsi per fidem insiti & uniti. Ex divite 6. Sola causa & mensura tanti beneficii est dives Dei gratia, juxta cujus opulentiam CHRISTUS, & redemptio in CHRISTO, nobis donantur: Ergo celebranda merito sola DEI gratia, ut salutis nostrae causa.
units.tr: In whom. Fifth, now that we have become believers, we have this redemption and forgiveness of sins not in ourselves apart from Christ, but in Christ, our Surety, Redeemer and Head, to whom we are engrafted and united by faith. According to the riches. Sixth, the sole cause and measure of so great a benefit is the rich grace of God, according to whose abundance Christ, and redemption in Christ, are given to us. Therefore the grace of God alone is rightly to be celebrated as the cause of our salvation.

units.la: Verf. 8. Qua redundavit in nos omni sapientia & intelligentia.
units.tr: Verse 8. Which he has made to abound toward us in all wisdom and understanding.

units.la: Arg. 7. Ex abundanti hac gratia tanquam fonte, CHRISTUS seu Pater in CHRISTO, in efficaci vocatione nostri in summa sua sapientia communicavit nobis perfectam sapientiam & prudentiam, i. dedit nobis fidem salvificam, in cujus objecto omnis sapientiae, & intelligentiae summa & perfectio consistit; nam licet fides salvifica in se imperfecta sit, per eam tamen CHRISTUM, thesaurum omnis sapientiae & prudentiae salutiferae, agnitum applicamus nobis in panaceam, seu remedium omnium malorum, quod sapientiae & prudentiae compendium est: In hac argumento singula idem probant. In Nos Primo, Nos in nobis una cum reliquo mundo, insipientes, imprudentes & stulti errabamus, in caecitate & vanitate mentis nostrae. Ex gratia igitur est quod nos donati simus sapientia. Ille exundavit 2. CHRISTUS author fidei nostrae prior supervenit, & donavit nos fide quae consistit in cognitione & applicatione salutaris DEI veritatis, quae est vera sapientia & prudentia. Ex gratia igitur. Qua scilicet gratia 3. Aperte asseritur gratia, Ex gratia effudit in nos hanc sapientiam & prudentiam. Exundavit 4. Ipse plenus gratiae, talem se ostendebat in hoc actu, ut qui gratiam amplius intra se quasi non posset continere, superabundans redundavit in nos. Ergo in efficaci vocatione, & fidei donatione obtinet sola gratia, quae idcirco merito celebranda est.
units.tr: Argument 7. From this abundant grace, as from a fountain, Christ, or the Father in Christ, in our effectual calling, has in his supreme wisdom imparted to us perfect wisdom and prudence; that is, he has given us saving faith, in whose object the sum and perfection of all wisdom and understanding consists. For although saving faith is itself imperfect, through it we apply to ourselves Christ, the treasure of all wisdom and saving prudence, as known, as a panacea or remedy for all evils, which is the epitome of wisdom and prudence. All the individual parts of this argument prove the same. Toward us. First, we, together with the rest of the world, were foolish, imprudent and senseless, wandering in the blindness and vanity of our minds. Therefore it is from grace that we have been given wisdom. He has made to abound. Second, Christ, the author of our faith, came before us and gave us faith, which consists in the knowledge and application of the saving truth of God, which is true wisdom and prudence. Therefore it is from grace. Which, namely grace. Third, grace is plainly asserted: he has poured this wisdom and prudence upon us from grace. Made to abound. Fourth, full of grace himself, he showed himself in this act in such a way that, as if unable to contain grace any longer within himself, he overflowed and abounded toward us. Therefore grace alone obtains in the effectual calling and the bestowal of faith, and for this reason is rightly to be celebrated.

units.la: Verf. 9. Patefacto nobis mysterio voluntatis suae, secundum gratuitam suam benevolentiam, quam proposuerat in se.
units.tr: Verse 9. Having made known to us the mystery of his will, according to his gracious goodwill, which he had purposed in himself.

units.la: Arg. 8. Patefactio arcanae voluntatis DEI de ratione salutis consequendae per CHRISTUM, ad fidem seu cognitionem & prudentiam suis communicandam, est ex DEI mera voluntate, secundum beneplacitum ipsius, quod in se proposuerat: Ergo & patefactae voluntatis DEI, & donatae fidei etiam nomine, DEI gratia merito celebranda est. Horsum tendunt omnes partes hujus argumenti. Mysterium Primo, Voluntas DEI de ratione salutis per CHRISTUM perficiendae, mysterium erat secretum ab aeterno in pectore DEI, obsignatum, & quod in apertam lucem producere, neque hominum, neque angelorum ullus unquam potuisset, nisi Deus illud revelasset ex gratia.
units.tr: Argument 8. The disclosure of the hidden will of God concerning the way of salvation to be attained through Christ, and its communication to his own for faith or knowledge and prudence, comes from the mere will of God, according to his good pleasure, which he had purposed in himself. Therefore the grace of God is rightly to be celebrated both for the will disclosed and for the faith bestowed. All the parts of this argument tend to this. Mystery. First, the will of God concerning the way of accomplishing salvation through Christ was a mystery, a secret sealed in the bosom of God from eternity, which no man or angel could ever have brought into open light unless God had revealed it out of grace.

units.la: 2. Mysterium hoc curavit Deus, non tantùm ut prædicaretur, sed& ablatâ cæcitate mentium & cordium nostrorum, ex gratia effecit ut à nobis intelligeretur. 3. Nobis præ aliis manifestavit Gratiæ Euangelium.
units.tr: Second, God took care that this mystery should not only be preached, but also, by removing the blindness of our minds and hearts, he effected out of grace that it should be understood by us. Third, before others he made the gospel of grace known to us.

units.la: 4. Gratis hoc præstitit Deus, non inductus, non excitatus ab aliqua causa extra se, sed secundùm beneplacitum suum, seu gratuitam prædestinationem, & æternum suum propositum in se. Merito ergo celebranda nobis est Dei gratia.
units.tr: Fourth, God granted this freely, not moved or stirred up by any cause outside himself, but according to his own good pleasure, or his gratuitous predestination, and his eternal purpose in himself. Therefore the grace of God is rightly to be celebrated by us.

units.la: Vers. 10. Nempe ut in pleni temporis dispensatione recolligeret omnia in Christo, tum quæ in Cælis sunt, tum quæ in terra:
units.tr: Verse 10. Namely, that in the dispensation of the fullness of time he might gather together all things in Christ, both those in heaven and those on earth.

units.la: Arg. 9. Ex Dei mera voluntate & arbitrio pendet, tempus plenum & opportunum præfigere, quo mysterium voluntatis ipsius in hominum notitiam veniat, quid, quantum, & quando, unicuique ætati, vel homini singulari de hoc mysterio dispensandum sit. Ergo etiam in tempore præfigendo quo fides danda sit, obtinet Dei voluntas, eoque nomine celebranda est gratia Dei.
units.tr: Argument 9. It depends on the mere will and decision of God to appoint the full and fitting time at which the mystery of his will comes to men's knowledge, and what, how much and when each age, or each individual man, is to be dispensed of this mystery. Therefore in appointing the time when faith is to be given, too, the will of God prevails, and on that account the grace of God is to be celebrated.

units.la: Hoc ipsum insinuant singula quæ hoc Argumento continentur.
units.tr: The individual points contained in this argument indicate the same thing.

units.la: Primo gratia agnoscenda est, quia hic œconomia seu libera Patrisfamilias de rebus suis domesticis dispensatio est, quâ unusquisque sicut vult de suo statuit: quæ libertas sicut unicuique Patri familias jure concedenda est, Sic etiam & Deo, ut pro libitu suo agat.
units.tr: First, grace is to be acknowledged here, because this is an economy, that is, the free disposition of a head of the household over his domestic affairs, by which each one decides about what is his as he wishes. This freedom must be granted to every head of a household by right; so also to God, that he may act at his pleasure.

units.la: Secundò, est temporis maturA opportunitas, in quâ singulis ætatibus & hominibus, quid & quantum idoneum sit revelare de Dei arcanâ voluntate, penes Deum solùm est statuere, & propterea quodcunque & quantumcunque nobis revelatum est, ex gratia est. Nam beneplacitum Dei quod in seipso proposuerat, de quo verf 9. ad hanc de tempore dispensationem pertingit: Merito ergo hic etiam ejus gratia agnoscenda est.
units.tr: Second, there is the proper opportunity of the ripe time, and it rests with God alone to determine, for each age and each man, what and how much is fitting to reveal of the hidden will of God. Therefore whatever and however much has been revealed to us is from grace. For the good pleasure of God, which he had purposed in himself, of which verse 9 speaks, extends to this dispensation of time. Therefore his grace is rightly to be acknowledged here also.

units.la: Arg. 10. Recollectio, & Demonstratio recollectionis omnium Electorum, seu Redemptorum, palantium alioqui, & à Deo separatorum, in unum caput Christum, summa est & finis revelati mysterii. Gratia ergo Dei qua nos cum aliis recolligimur, à nobis celebranda est. Verum quidem est per peccatum Angelorum & Hominum, totum mundum, tanquam lacerum & examine corpus, cujus membra à se invicem divulsa & dissipata sunt, perditioni proximum factum fuisse, nisi Christus electos Angelos confirmasset, & ruentem mundum ltillet; tisset; sed hic potissimùm respicit Apostolus restaurationem electorum hominum, quâ Christus homines ad se recollectos Deo reconciliavit, & in unum quasi regnum Angelos electos, & spiritus Justorum in Cœlo, Judæos & Gentes in terra, arctissimâ inter se unione, coiligavit.
units.tr: Argument 10. The gathering together, and the showing of the gathering together, of all the elect or redeemed, who would otherwise be scattered and separated from God, into one head, Christ, is the sum and purpose of the revealed mystery. Therefore the grace of God by which we are gathered together with others is to be celebrated by us. It is true that through the sin of angels and men the whole world, like a torn and mangled body whose members have been pulled apart and scattered from one another, had come near to ruin, unless Christ had confirmed the elect angels and held up the falling world. But the Apostle here chiefly has in view the restoration of the elect men, by which Christ, having gathered men to himself, reconciled them to God, and bound together, in a most close union, the elect angels and the spirits of the just in heaven, and Jews and Gentiles on earth, as one kingdom.

units.la: Vers. 11. In ipso, inquam, in quo etiam in sortem asciti sumus, quum essemus prædestinati secundùm propositum ejus qui omnia efficit ex consilio voluntatis suæ.
units.tr: Verse 11. In him, I say, in whom we have also been made a heritage, since we were predestined according to the purpose of him who works all things according to the counsel of his will.

units.la: Arg. 11. Cum applicatione ad Judæos: In Christo vitæ æternæ hæreditas datur nobis Judæis electis, non ex operibus, aut arbitrii nostri viribus acquisita, sed sorte, seu dispensatione divinâ, donata nobis prædestinatis, secundùm propositum Dei, qui operatur omnia secundùm voluntatis suæ consilium. Ergo gratia Dei à nobis Judæis, & ab omnibus celebranda est. Ad gratiam ostendendam omnia hic faciunt.
units.tr: Argument 11. With application to the Jews: in Christ the inheritance of eternal life is given to us elect Jews, not acquired by works or by the strength of our own will, but bestowed upon us predestined ones by lot, or by divine dispensation, according to the purpose of God, who works all things according to the counsel of his will. Therefore the grace of God is to be celebrated by us Jews and by all. All the points here serve to show grace.

units.la: Sorte asciti sumus in hereditatis possessionem] Primò, Vita æterna seu glorificatio est hæreditas, quam nos ipsi non aquisivimus, sed quam sorte seu dispensatione divina nacti sumus. 2. Illam hæreditatem non valemus per nos, ne quidem accipere oblatam; vel nobis jam designatam hæreditatem ipsi adire non possumus; sed forte facti sumus hæreditatis possessores; nam ἐκληρώθημεν passivum est: quid igitur hic nostrum est, & non ex gratia?
units.tr: We have been made partakers by lot of the possession of the inheritance] First, eternal life, or glorification, is an inheritance that we did not acquire ourselves but obtained by lot, or by divine dispensation. 2. We cannot even receive that inheritance when it is offered, nor can we approach an inheritance already assigned to us. Rather, we have been made possessors by lot of the inheritance, for [ἐκληρώθημεν] is passive. What, then, is ours here, and not of grace?

units.la: Prædestinati] 3. Prædestinati sumus à Deo, ut vocaremur ad possessionem illius hæreditatis: non adhibuit nos Deus in consilium suum, cum de nostra felicitate statuit.
units.tr: Predestined] 3. We were predestined by God to be called to possession of that inheritance. He did not take us into his counsel when he decided about our happiness.

units.la: Operatur] 4. Deus qui prædestinavit nos ad hanc felicitatem, operatur omnia, non felicitatem ipsam tantùm præparando, nec solùm nos ad eam adeundam formando, sed etiam omnia media efficaciter, quæ ad nostri introductionem in possessionem faciunt, adhibendo.
units.tr: He works] 4. God, who predestined us to this happiness, works all things. He does not only prepare the happiness itself, or only form us to approach it, but also effectually applies all the means that contribute to our introduction into possession.

units.la: Ex consilio] 5. Neque egreditur Deus extra se, ad quærendum causas propositi, seu operationis suæ, sed omnia operatur ex consilio, seu ex libera sapientissimaque sua voluntate. Ergo glorificatio vel salus nostra est ex gratia, & non ex operibus, nec ex liberi nostri arbitrii electione; nam quod arbitrium nostrum feratur ad eligendum bonum & vitam, & quod nos operemur ulla bona opera, ex mero est libero beneplacito Dei, qui operatur omnia bona ex consilio voluntatis suæ: Merito ergo celebranda est ejus gratia.
units.tr: From counsel] 5. Nor does God go outside himself to seek the causes of his purpose or of his working, but he works all things from counsel, that is, from his free and most wise will. Therefore our glorification or salvation is of grace, and not of works, nor of the choice of our free will. That our will is directed to choose the good and life, and that we perform any good works at all, comes from the mere free good pleasure of God, who works all good things according to the counsel of his will. Rightly, then, his grace is to be celebrated.

units.la: Verf. 12. Ut nos simus laudi gloriæ ipsius, qui priores speravimus in Christo:
units.tr: Verse 12. That we should be to the praise of his glory, who first hoped in Christ.

units.la: Arg. 12. A fine ultimo vocationis Judæorum prædestinatorum in possessionem hæreditatis. Sicut Deus nobis electis Judæis hanc præstitit gratiam, ut priores, seu prius quam Gentes crederemus in Christum venturum, & priores etiam crederemus in præsentem, seu exhibitum Christum, sic etiam secundum prærogativam datam ex gratia Genti nostræ, priores nos ascivit in jus hæreditatis cœlestis, in eum ipsum finem, ut gloriam gratiæ suæ in nobis, & à nobis consequeretur. Ergo meritò Deus benedictus agnoscendus est, ejusque gratia celebranda à nobis Judæis, & aliis omnibus.
units.tr: Argument 12. From the ultimate end of the calling of the predestined Jews into possession of the inheritance. Just as God has granted us elect Jews this grace, that we should be first, that is, before the Gentiles, to believe that Christ would come, and also first to believe in Christ now present and revealed, so too, according to the privilege granted by grace to our nation, he has taken us first into the right of the heavenly inheritance, to this very end, that he might obtain the glory of his grace from us and in us. Therefore God is rightly to be acknowledged as blessed, and his grace is rightly to be celebrated by us Jews and by all others.

units.la: Verf. 13. In quo speraftis & vos audito sermone veritatis, id est Evangelio salutis vestræ: in quo etiam postquam credidistis, obsignati estis Spiritu illo promissionis sancto:
units.tr: Verse 13. In whom you also hoped, after you heard the word of truth, the gospel of your salvation. In whom also, after you believed, you were sealed with that Holy Spirit of promise.

units.la: Arg. 13. Cum applicatione ad Gentiles, nominatim ad Ephesios. Vos etiam Gentiles, non ita pridem alieni à republica Israelis, jam vocati & ascíti estis in jus ad hanc ipsam hæreditatem, in hunc ipsum finem, scilicet in laudem gloriosæ gratiæ Dei. Ergo vobis Gentibus, & omnibus nobis agnoscenda & prædicanda est Dei gratia. Probat autem Ephesios consortes hæreditatis factos esse cum Judæis, sex rationibus.
units.tr: Argument 13. With application to the Gentiles, namely to the Ephesians. You also, Gentiles, who not long ago were aliens from the commonwealth of Israel, have now been called and taken into the right of this very inheritance, to this very end, namely to the praise of the glorious grace of God. Therefore the grace of God is to be acknowledged and proclaimed by you Gentiles and by all of us. He proves that the Ephesians were made fellow heirs with the Jews by six reasons.

units.la: Speraftis ] Ratio prima, Credidistis in Christum. Ergo consortes hæreditatis facti estis.
units.tr: You hoped] The first reason: you believed in Christ. Therefore you have been made fellow heirs.

units.la: Audito ] Ratio 2. Misit Deus verbum Veritatis suæ, seu Evangelium salutiferum ad vos, ut audientes crederetis, & salutem consequeremini: Ergo non ut olim, tanquam Proselyti, sed pari honore, cum Judæis ornati, consortes hæreditatis facti estis.
units.tr: Having heard] The second reason: God sent the word of his truth, that is, the saving gospel, to you, so that, hearing, you might believe and obtain salvation. Therefore you have been made fellow heirs, not as formerly, as proselytes, but adorned with equal honour with the Jews.

units.la: Obsignati ] Ratio 3. Ex arrha salutis data ipsis, & ejus usu primo. Postquam credidistis, obsignati estis in peculium Deo, per Spiritus sancti donationem: Ergo consortes hæreditatis facti estis.
units.tr: Sealed] The third reason: from the earnest of salvation given to them and its first use. After you believed, you were sealed as a people for God's own possession, through the gift of the Holy Spirit. Therefore you have been made fellow heirs.

units.la: Promissiones ] Ratio 4. Ab obsignationis usu secundo, Promissiones de hæreditate obsignatæ sunt vobis à Spiritu promisso, qui promissiones confirmat credentibus. Ergo in sortem ascíti estis.
units.tr: Promises] The fourth reason: from the second use of the sealing. The promises concerning the inheritance have been sealed to you by the promised Spirit, who confirms the promises to believers. Therefore you have been taken into the lot.

units.la: Verf. 14. Qui est arrabo hæreditatis nostræ, dum in libertatem vindicamur, ad laudem gloriæ ipsius.
units.tr: Verse 14. Who is the earnest of our inheritance, while we are being claimed for liberty, unto the praise of his glory.

units.la: Ratio 5. Ab obsignationis seu arrhæ salutis datæ usu tertio. Spiritus sancti donatio est arrabo hæreditatis, pignus scilicet & pars felicitatis vestræ tandem consummandæ. Ergo, &c.
units.tr: The fifth reason: from the third use of the sealing, or of the earnest of salvation given. The gift of the Holy Spirit is the earnest of the inheritance, that is, the pledge and part of your happiness, which is finally to be consummated. Therefore, etc.

units.la: Ad obtinendum ] Ratio 6. A quarto usu obsignationis: Ad consolationem vestram Spiritus est mansurus vobiscum, & non discessurus priusquam redemptio plena plene sit perfecta & completa, in plena liberatione animarum & corporum vestrorum ab omnibus peccati & miseriæ vinculis: Ergo in sortem hæreditatis ascíti estis.
units.tr: To obtain] The sixth reason: from the fourth use of the sealing. For your comfort the Spirit will remain with you, and will not depart until the full redemption is fully perfected and completed, in the full deliverance of your souls and bodies from all the bonds of sin and misery. Therefore you have been taken into the lot of the inheritance.

units.la: Ad laudem ] Denique finem indicat omnium horum beneficiorum esse laudem gloriosæ gratiæ Dei, ut in his & præcedentibus omnibus benedictus agnoscatur Deus, & celebretur ejus gratia, nempe in nostri Electione, Prædestinatione, Redemptione, Vocatione, Fidei donatione, Peccatorum remissione, Adoptione, Recollectione ad Christum, & societatem populi ipsius, Assumptione ad sortem hæreditatis adeundæ, & Obsignatione per Spiritum sanctum.
units.tr: To the praise] Finally, he indicates that the end of all these benefits is the praise of the glorious grace of God, so that in these and all the preceding things God may be acknowledged as blessed and his grace celebrated: namely, in our election, predestination, redemption, calling, bestowal of faith, remission of sins, adoption, gathering to Christ and fellowship with his people, assumption to the lot of the inheritance to be entered upon, and sealing through the Holy Spirit.

units.la: Verf. 15. Propterea etiam ego, quum audivissm eam quæ in vobis est fidem in Domino Iesu, & charitatem in omnes sanctos.
units.tr: Verse 15. Wherefore I also, after I heard of the faith that is among you in the Lord Jesus, and of the love toward all the saints.

units.la: Transit ad secundam partem Capitis, in qua fidem Ephesiorum confirmare nititur, Propositio confirmanda hoc vel simili axiomate in hunc sensum concipi potest; Vos Ephesii in fide Euangelii corroborari debetis. Argumenta ad propositionem confirmandam sunt quindecim.
units.tr: He passes to the second part of the chapter, in which he seeks to confirm the faith of the Ephesians. The proposition to be confirmed may be conceived in this or a similar axiom: You Ephesians ought to be strengthened in the faith of the gospel. The arguments for confirming this proposition are fifteen.

units.la: Fide in ] Argumentum primum, Vestra fides in Iesum Christum non est mortua illa & hypocritica, sed viva & efficaciter operans per charitatem, erga omnes sanctos, & palam manifestata mihi Apostolo & aliis: Ergo vos Ephesii debetis in fide corroborari.
units.tr: Faith in] The first argument: your faith in Jesus Christ is not dead and hypocritical, but living and working effectually through love toward all the saints, and openly manifested to me the Apostle and to others. Therefore you Ephesians ought to be strengthened in faith.

units.la: Verf. 16. Non desino gratias agere pro vobis, mentionem vestri faciens in precibus meis:
units.tr: Verse 16. I do not cease to give thanks for you, making mention of you in my prayers.

units.la: Arg. 2. Digni comperti estis, pro quibus jugiter Deo gratiæ ab omnibus agantur, sicut à me fit: Ergo in fide Euangelii corroborari debetis.
units.tr: Argument 2. You have been found worthy, for whom thanks are continually given to God by all, as they are by me. Therefore you ought to be strengthened in the faith of the gospel.

units.la: Mentionem ] Arg. 3. Propter vestræ fidei manifestatam sinceritatem in dilectione Sanctorum, constanter in memoria vos retineo, & mentionem vestri in precibus meis jugiter facio, orans, ut consummetur in vobis Dei opus, & confirmetur vestra fides: Ergo nisi instinctum Spiritus, in me precante, frustra esse putetis: Corroborari in Fide debetis.
units.tr: Mention] Argument 3. On account of the manifested sincerity of your faith in love for the saints, I constantly keep you in remembrance and continually make mention of you in my prayers, praying that God's work may be brought to completion in you and your faith confirmed. Therefore, unless you think that the prompting of the Spirit in my praying is in vain, you ought to be strengthened in faith.

units.la: Verf. 17. Vt Deus Domini nostri Iesu Christi, Pater ille gloria, det vobis Spiritum sapientiæ & revelationis, per agnitionem ipsius:
units.tr: Verse 17. That the God of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of glory, may give you the spirit of wisdom and revelation in the knowledge of him.

units.la: Proponit precationis suæ pro iis summam, in qua reliqua continentur Argumenta confirmationis Fidei ipsorum.
units.tr: He sets out the summary of his prayer for them, in which the remaining arguments for confirming their faith are contained.

units.la: Precando ut Deus det illis Spiritum sapientiæ & revelationis, insinuat eos causas confirmationis Fidei suæ plures & graviores habere (in Scriptura scilicet, quæ fons est sapientiæ, & summa revelationis salvificæ,) quam adhuc intelligant, quod Argumentum quartum est. Habetis vestræ corroborationis in fide Argumenta tot & talia in Scriptura, ut nihil potius vobis optarim ad Fidei confirmationem, quam largiorem mensuram operationis Spiritus Dei, ut ampliori sapientiâ vobis data, & mysteriis Verbi clarius reclusis, agnoscatis Christi & Dei erga vos animum: Ergo debetis vel ex hoc meo testimonio & voto, in Fide confirmari.
units.tr: By praying that God would give them the Spirit of wisdom and revelation, he suggests that they have more and weightier causes for confirming their faith (namely in Scripture, which is the fountain of wisdom and the sum of saving revelation) than they yet understand. This is the fourth argument. You have in Scripture so many and such arguments for your strengthening in faith that I could wish nothing more for you, for the confirmation of your faith, than a larger measure of the working of God's Spirit, so that, with greater wisdom given to you and the mysteries of the Word more clearly unlocked, you may recognise the mind of Christ and of God toward you. Therefore you ought to be confirmed in faith, at least from this my testimony and prayer.

units.la: Arg. 5. A descriptione Dei, à quo petitur hoc donum. Deus qui Spiritum Fidei, seu Sapientiæ largitur Sanctis, est Deus & Pater gloriosus Domini nostri, & nostrum omnium Christi servorum, qui & ex pacto, ut Deus noster, & ex Paterno affectu, ut Pater noster, velit dare Spiritum Fidei vobis, comprecantibus nobis. Ergo vel ex relationibus quæ inter Deum, & Christum, & vos intercedunt Corroborari in fide debetis.
units.tr: Argument 5. From the description of God, from whom this gift is sought. God, who bestows the Spirit of faith, or wisdom, on the saints, is the God and glorious Father of our Lord and of all us servants of Christ. He, both by covenant, as our God, and by fatherly affection, as our Father, is willing to give the Spirit of faith to you when we pray. Therefore, from the relations that exist between God, Christ and you, you ought to be strengthened in faith.

units.la: Verf. 18. Illuminatis oculis mentis vestræ: ut sciatis quæ sit spes illa vocationis ipsius, & quæ opes gloriæ hæreditatis ipsius in Sanctis:
units.tr: Verse 18. Having the eyes of your understanding enlightened, that you may know what is the hope of his calling, and what the riches of the glory of his inheritance are in the saints:

units.la: Arg. 6. Non possum fando explicare, quæ quantaque bona sint, quæ Deus vos ad Christum vocando iperare jussit, vel quam gloriosæ sint opes hæreditatis, quæ vobis præparatur in Cœli Sanctuario, tantum precor, ut illuminentur oculi vestri ad illa cognoscenduin: Corroborari igitur in fide debetis.
units.tr: Argument 6. I cannot put into words how great and how good are the blessings which God commanded to be promised to you when he called you to Christ, or how glorious are the riches of the inheritance prepared for you in the sanctuary of heaven. I only pray that the eyes of your mind may be enlightened to know them. Therefore you ought to be strengthened in faith.

units.la: Verf. 19. Et quæ sit excellens illa magnitudo potentiæ ipsius in nobis qui credimus, pro efficacitate fortis roboris ipsius.
units.tr: Verse 19. And what is the exceeding greatness of his power toward us who believe, according to the working of his mighty strength.

units.la: Arg. 7. Ineffabilis est illa Dei potentia, quam in vobis convertendis, & hactenus in fide sustinendis actu exeruit, & quam quasi oppigneravit se porro exerturum, ut pro infinita efficacia roboris sui, credentes ad salutem promoveantur, tantum precor ut illuminatis oculis eam sciatis. Ergo corroborari in fide debetis.
units.tr: Argument 7. That power of God is beyond words, which he has already put forth in converting you and sustaining you in faith until now, and which he has as good as pledged to put forth further, so that by the infinite efficacy of his strength believers are advanced to salvation. I only pray that you may know it with enlightened eyes. Therefore you ought to be strengthened in faith.

units.la: Hoc argumentum confirmat triplici comparatione. Prima est potentiae Dei cum omni adversaria potestate, & cum Ephesiorum imbecillitate, quo respectu dicit superexcellentem esse magnitudinem potentiae, actu jam in illis demonstratae, ut intelligerent, nullam esse potentiam in Satana, mundo, peccato, morte, vel ullo impedimento extra ipsos, quod non superet, & superatura sit in immensum, magnitudo potentiae Dei: nec ea in ipsis imbecillitas, quam haec potentia non sit sublevatura. Secunda comparatio est potentis operis Dei in conversione ipsorum cum operis fonte, id est, Dei omnipotentiâ, quo respectu mentionem facit efficaciae roboris fortitudinis ejus, ut intelligerent opus Dei in ipsis convertendis, fide & sanctitate imbuendis, omnipotentiae congruentem esse, & Deo omnipotente dignam expressionem efficaciae illius, quae procedit ab actuali & exerto robore omnipotentis Dei, opus scilicet plane dignum Deo.
units.tr: This argument is confirmed by a threefold comparison. The first is of the power of God with every adverse power, and with the weakness of the Ephesians. In this respect he says that the greatness of the power is exceeding, since it has already been demonstrated in them, so that they might understand that there is no power in Satan, the world, sin, death, or any hindrance outside themselves which the greatness of God's power does not overcome, and will overcome infinitely; nor is there any weakness in them which this power will not relieve. The second comparison is of the mighty work of God in their conversion with the source of that work, namely the omnipotence of God. In this respect he mentions the efficacy of the working of his strength, so that they might understand that the work of God in converting them, and imbuing them with faith and holiness, is worthy of his omnipotence, and that this efficacy, which proceeds from the actual and exerted strength of almighty God, is a fitting expression of God, namely a work plainly worthy of God.

units.la: Tertia comparatio est potentiae Dei jam actu demonstratae in ipsorum conversione, cum potentia illa quam demonstravit Deus in suscitando Christo a mortuis: Primo, ut intelligerent non minoris esse potentiae hominem convertere, regenerare, & fide, reliquisque gratiis salvificis ornare, quam mortuum & sepultum a mortuis resuscitare, deinde ut intelligerent eandem numero potentiam exerceri in nostri conversione, quae se exerebat in Christi suscitatione: Denique ut intelligerent, non minus facile Deum effecturum reliqua, quae ad salutem perficiendam restabant, quam supra dicta praestitit.
units.tr: The third comparison is of the power of God already demonstrated in their conversion with the power which God showed in raising Christ from the dead. First, so that they might understand that it takes no less power to convert a man, to regenerate him, and to adorn him with faith and the other saving graces, than to raise up from the dead one who was dead and buried. Second, so that they might understand that the same power, in number, is exercised in our conversion as was displayed in the resurrection of Christ. Finally, so that they might understand that God will bring to completion the rest that remains for perfecting salvation no less easily than he has accomplished what was said above.

units.la: Verf. 20. Quam exeruit in Christo, quum excitavit eum ex mortuis, & collocavit ad dextram suam in Caelis,
units.tr: Verse 20. Which he wrought in Christ, when he raised him from the dead, and set him at his own right hand in the heavenly places,

units.la: Arg. 8. A suscitatione Capitis nostri Christi. Deus Caput nostrum Christum nomine nostro interfectum, nostro nomine, & bono suscitavit a mortuis, ad vitam immortalem. Vos ergo ejus membra etiam in mediis afflictionibus, adeoque morte ipsa, in fide liberationis vestrae corroborari debetis.
units.tr: Argument 8. From the resurrection of our Head, Christ. God raised our Head Christ, who was slain in our name, from the dead, in our name and for our good, to immortal life. You, therefore, as his members, ought to be strengthened in faith of your deliverance, even amid afflictions, and so even in death itself.

units.la: Collocavit ] Arg. 9. A Christi ascensione, & sessione ad dextram Patris. Christus Redemptor noster ascendit in Coelum, & regnat cum Patre, consors imperii summi, ut redemptos in societatem felicitatis, & loci in quo est, consortes faciat. Ergo in fide & spe futurae glorificationis vestrae in coelis corroborari debetis, nisi frustra esse CHRI- STI regnum putetis.
units.tr: Set] Argument 9. From the ascension of Christ and his session at the right hand of the Father. Christ our Redeemer ascended into heaven and reigns with the Father, a partner in supreme dominion, so that he may make the redeemed partners in the fellowship of his happiness and of the place where he is. Therefore you ought to be strengthened in faith and in hope of your future glorification in the heavens, unless you think that the kingdom of Christ is in vain.

units.la: Vers. 21. Longè supra omne imperium ac potestatem, & potentiam, & Dominium, & omne nomen quod nominatur, non solum in hoc seculo, verumetiam in futuro:
units.tr: Verse 21. Far above all principality, and power, and might, and dominion, and every name that is named, not only in this world, but also in that which is to come:

units.la: Arg. 10. Confirmans superius. CHRISTUS etiam in sua carne exaltatus est longè supra omnes sive homines sive Angelos, ita ut nihil sit tam sublime, vel potens, vel illustre, sive in terra, seu seculo praesenti: sive in Coelo, seu seculo futuro, quo CHRISTUS non sit in immensum sublimior etiam qua homo, adeo ut nihil ei deesse possit ad perficiendam nostram felicitatem, neque illi quicquam resistere possit, quin eam perficiat: Ergo in fide Evangelii corroborari debetis, Verf. 21. Et omnia subjecit ejus pedibus, eumque constituit caput super omnia ipsi Ecclesiæ;
units.tr: Argument 10. Confirming what was said above. Christ, even in his flesh, has been exalted far above all, whether men or angels, so that nothing is so lofty, or powerful, or illustrious, whether on earth or in the present age, or in heaven or the age to come, that Christ is not infinitely more exalted than it, even as man. So nothing can be lacking to him for completing our happiness, and nothing can resist him so that he does not complete it. Therefore you ought to be strengthened in the faith of the Gospel. Verse 21. And hath put all things under his feet, and gave him to be the head over all things to the church,

units.la: Arg. 11. Hostes omnes nostri, Diabolus, impii in mundo, persequutores, hæretici & impostores, peccati in nobis potestas, carceres; exilium, & mortis omne genus, subjiciuntur Christi pedibus, ut de iis omnibus statuat in bonum nostrum, subjiciatque hæc omnia pedibus nostris: Ergo in fide corroborari debetis.
units.tr: Argument 11. All our enemies, the Devil, the impious in the world, persecutors, heretics and impostors, the power of sin in us, prisons, exile, and every kind of death, are subjected to the feet of Christ, so that he may dispose of all of them for our good, and place all these things under our feet. Therefore you ought to be strengthened in faith.

units.la: Arg. 12. Christus constitutus est caput super omnia ipsi Ecclesiæ, id est, plenam rerum omnium potestatem & administrationem illi commisit Pater, ut ipse solus esset Ecclesiæ, catholicæ caput conjunctissimum: ad ipsius Ecclesiæ omniumque ejus membrorum illuminationem, vivificationem, excitationem ad omnia spiritualia officia, & vitæ spiritualis in illis conservationem, per Spiritus sui immediatam in tota Ecclesia, & singulis ejus membris præsentiam & operationem: Ergo nisi de Capitis veltri sapientia, potentia, & fidelitate in officio dubitare vultis, in fide corroborari debetis.
units.tr: Argument 12. Christ has been set as head over all things to the Church, that is, the Father has committed to him the full power and administration of all things, so that he alone may be the most closely united head of the Church, the catholic Church, for the enlightening and quickening of that Church and all its members, for their stirring up to all spiritual duties, and for the preservation of spiritual life in them, through the immediate presence and working of his Spirit in the whole Church and in each of its members. Therefore, unless you wish to doubt the wisdom, power, and faithfulness of your Head in his office, you ought to be strengthened in faith.

units.la: Verf. 23. Quæ est corpus ipsius, & complementum ejus qui omnia implet in omnibus.
units.tr: Verse 23. Which is his body, the fulness of him that filleth all in all.

units.la: Arg. 13. Ecclesia est corpus Christi mysticum, & singuli fideles, membra ipsius. Ergo dubitandum non est quin vestræ salUti perficiendæ prospecturus, & incubituus sit, nisi fideles membra ejus esse negetis.
units.tr: Argument 13. The Church is the mystical body of Christ, and individual believers are its members. Therefore there is no doubt that he will provide for and watch over the completion of your salvation, unless you deny that you are his members.

units.la: Arg. 14. Ecclesia est complementum Christi, quatenus tenus Christus est caput mysticum, ita ut perfici se & impleri non existimet, donec omnes & singuli electi in unum congregentur plene ipsi uniantur, plenum incrementum, singulis membris conveniens & destinatum, nancisci antur, & tandem plena cum ipso felicitate fruantur: Ergo tam certi esse poteritis de salute vestra perficienda, quam quod Christus non passurus sit se incompletum, imperfectum aut mutilum permanere.
units.tr: Argument 14. The Church is the complement of Christ, insofar as Christ is the mystical head, so that he does not think himself made perfect and complete until all and each of the elect are gathered into one and fully united to him, and obtain the full growth suited and destined for each member, and at last enjoy full happiness with him. Therefore you may be as certain of the completion of your salvation as you are that Christ will not allow himself to remain incomplete, imperfect, or maimed.

units.la: Implet ] Arg. 15. Christus implet omnia in omnibus, id est, secundum uniuscujusque creaturae mensuram, ut Deus naturae operatur omnia, & ut caput Ecclesiae perficit omnia, quae pertinent ad vitam spiritualem, ad sanctificationem & salutem fidelium, omnia membra gradatim implens: Ergo non dubitandum est, quin inchoatum opus fidei, sanctificationis, & salutis, in vobis impletur us sit. Adjectum autem est hoc, quod impleat omnia in omnibus, per correctionem seu expositionem superioris dicti, de Complemento Christi per Ecclesiam, ne putemus Perfectionem Christi, vel nostri, pendere ab alio quam ab ipso, qui sibi hanc necessitatem communicandi se nobis indignis hominunculis ex libera sua dilectione fecit; qui hoc nostri desiderium in seipso excitavit; qui suo desiderio satisfaciendi potestatem ipse habet, & desiderium suum de nobis sanctificandis, & salute plena donandis gradatim implet, & implere perget, donec compleverit omnia ad salutem complendam necessaria: idque in omnibus fidelibus maximis, minimisque. Ei sit gloria Gratiae, Potentiae & Constantiae suae, in saecula saeculorum. AMEN.
units.tr: Fills] Argument 15. Christ fills all in all, that is, according to the measure of each creature, as God works all things in nature, and as the Head of the Church brings to perfection all things that pertain to the spiritual life, to the sanctification and salvation of the faithful, filling each member step by step. Therefore we must not doubt that the work of faith, sanctification, and salvation begun in you will be completed. This phrase, that he fills all in all, is added by way of correction or explanation of the earlier words about the complement of Christ through the Church, lest we think that the perfection of Christ, or of ourselves, depends on anyone other than himself, who from his free love has made it his own necessity to communicate himself to us unworthy little men. He has stirred up this desire of ours in himself; he has the power himself to satisfy his own desire, and he fills up step by step his own desire to sanctify us and to grant us full salvation, and will continue to fill it until he has completed all things necessary for completing our salvation, and this in all the faithful, both the greatest and the least. To him be glory for his grace, power, and constancy, for ever and ever. AMEN.

units.la: Caput Secundum.
units.tr: Chapter 2.

units.la: Deus argumentum prosequitur, probans nunc in hypothesi fideles Ephesios, nunc in thesi, omnes fideles ex gratia servari. Propositio confirmanda est: Gratia servati estis, O Ephesii, vel ex gratia servantur fideles. Argumenta sunt quindecim, in quorum ultimo insistit, ad finem Capitis.
units.tr: God pursues his argument, proving now in the hypothetical form that the faithful Ephesians, and now in the thetical form, that all the faithful are saved by grace. The proposition to be confirmed is: You, O Ephesians, have been saved by grace, or the faithful are saved by grace. There are fifteen arguments, and he dwells on the last of them to the end of the chapter.

units.la: Verf. 1. ET vos una vivificavit, quum essetis mortui in offensis & peccatis vestris. Argumentum primum, Si in communi statu naturæ consideremini, O Ephelii, comperietur ea vestra fuisse conditio, ut inde non nisi gratia liberari potuisletis. Hujus argumenti septem sant partes, quarum singulæ pristinam miseriam ostendunt, & solam gratiam salutis esse causam probant.
units.tr: Verse 1. And you he made alive, when you were dead in your offences and sins. The first argument: if you, O Ephesians, are considered in the common state of nature, it will be found that your condition was such that you could not have been freed from it except by grace. This argument has seven parts, each of which shows your former misery and proves that grace alone is the cause of salvation.

units.la: 1. In statu naturæ non tantum jacebatis in peccato inquinati, sed etiam mortui: & non tantum mortui judicialiter, quia rei mortis, seu morti obnoxii, sed etiam reipsa in effectu spiritualiter mortui; ita ut non magis potuissetis vos inde liberare, vel quicquam boni spiritualis facere, quam mortui seipsos resuscitare, vel actiones viventium agere possunt: Ex gratia ergo servati estis.
units.tr: 1. In the state of nature you lay not only polluted in sin but also dead: and dead not merely in a judicial sense, as liable to death or under the sentence of death, but actually dead in effect and spiritually; so that you could no more free yourselves from that state, or do anything spiritually good, than the dead can raise themselves or the living can perform the actions of the living. Therefore you have been saved by grace.

units.la: Vers. 2. In quibus olim versati estis, ut est vita mundi hujus, secundum principem cui potestas est aeris, & spiritus nunc agentis in hominibus contumacibus.
units.tr: Verse 2. In which you once walked, according to the course of this world, according to the prince of the power of the air, the spirit who now works in the disobedient.
