units.la: Secundo, Quod ad vitam hanc naturalem attinet, eam totam transigebatis in peccatis, toti occupati & ambulantes in illis, seu proficientes in pejus: Ex gratia igitur servati estis.
units.tr: Second, as far as this natural life is concerned, you spent all of it in sins, wholly occupied with them and walking in them, or advancing for the worse. Therefore you have been saved by grace.

units.la: Tertio, Mundanorum & carnalium hominum, qui vitam hanc naturalem tantum sapiunt, mores & consuetudinem, tanquam vitæ regulam sectati estis, & secundùm eam ambulastis: Ex gratia ergo servati estis.
units.tr: Third, you followed the manners and customs of worldly and carnal men, who savour only this natural life, as the rule of life, and you walked according to them. Therefore you have been saved by grace.

units.la: Quarto, Sequuti estis ducem viæ, diabolum principem impurorum Spirituum, qui cum suis satellitibus, seu reliquis malis Angelis, in aere circumvolans, regnat, & efficaciter imperium exercet.
units.tr: Fourth, you followed the guide of the way, the devil, the prince of impure spirits, who with his attendants, or the other evil angels, flying about in the air, reigns and effectively exercises power.

units.la: Quinto, In vobis ante conversionem regnabat diabolus, & voluntatem suam in vobis exequebatur, ut nunc in contumacibus exequitur: Ergo ex gratia servati estis.
units.tr: Fifth, before your conversion the devil ruled in you and carried out his will in you, as he now does in the disobedient. Therefore you have been saved by grace.

units.la: Vers. 3. Inter quos & nos omnes conversati sumus olim in cupiditatibus carnis nostræ, facientes quæ carni ac cogitationibus libebant: eramusque natura filii iræ, ut etiam reliqui.
units.tr: Verse 3. Among whom we also all once lived in the lusts of our flesh, doing the desires of the flesh and of the thoughts, and were by nature children of wrath, even as the rest.

units.la: Sexto, Exequuti estis cupiditates carnis vestræ, & in illis volutati estis, quicquid vana mens dictabat, quicquid corrupti appetitus, & affectus carnis præscribebant, peragentes: His se annumerat Apostolus ante conversionem suam, ut sciremus argumentum hoc in hypothesi propositum, ad probandam thesin generalem facere. Septimo, Natura eratis filii irae, id est, rei mortis & irae divinae obnoxii, quam iram merito effundere in nos poterat Deus ad extremam perditionem. His adjungit reliquos omnes homines, quatenus instatu naturae spectantur. Gratiae ergo debemus quod servati sumus.
units.tr: Sixth, you carried out the desires of your flesh and wallowed in them, doing whatever the vain mind dictated and whatever the corrupt appetites and affections of the flesh prescribed. The Apostle counts himself among these before his conversion, so that we may know that this argument, proposed in the hypothetical form, serves to prove the general thesis. Seventh, you were by nature children of wrath, that is, liable to death and to the divine wrath, which God could justly pour out upon us to utter destruction. To these he adds all the rest of men, insofar as they are viewed in the state of nature. We owe it to grace, therefore, that we have been saved.

units.la: Vers. 4. Sed Deus qui dives est misericordia, propter multam charitatem suam qua dilexit nos.
units.tr: Verse 4. But God, who is rich in mercy, because of his great love with which he loved us.

units.la: Arg. 2. Deus ex divite sua misericordia & dilectione a miserrima hac conditione liberavit nos fideles omnes: Ergo ex gratia servati sumus. Hujus argumenti partes idem probant.
units.tr: Arg. 2. Out of his rich mercy and love God has freed all of us faithful from this most wretched condition. Therefore we have been saved by grace. The parts of this argument prove the same thing.

units.la: Primo, Ponitur liberationis autor Deus solus, qui tanto operi solus par est. Secundo, Ut gratia appareat, Causa salutis nostrae datur, copiosa, seu dives misericordia Dei, qua Deus quasi sensu miseriae nostrae tactus nos liberavit. Tertio, Dilectio, qua Deus nos ab aeterno dilexit, ponitur ut causa & misericordiae, & salutis. Quarto, Ex gratia est quod Deus voluerit nos pre aliis complecti, & eligere in filios: Ergo ex gratia servati sumus.
units.tr: First, the author of deliverance is stated to be God alone, who alone is equal to so great a work. Second, so that grace may appear, the cause of our salvation is given as abundant, or rich, mercy of God, by which God, as if touched by a sense of our misery, freed us. Third, the love by which God loved us from eternity is put forward as the cause both of mercy and of salvation. Fourth, it is of grace that God willed to embrace us before others and to choose us as sons. Therefore we have been saved by grace.

units.la: Vers. 5. Etiam quum per offensas mortui essemus, una vivificavit nos per Christum, cujus gratia estis servati.
units.tr: Verse 5. Even when we were dead in offences, he made us alive together in Christ, by whose grace you have been saved.

units.la: Arg. 3. In momento redemptionis nostrae per Christum, & regenerationis per Christi Spiritum, nos ut mortui in peccatis vivificamur una cum Christo, id est, in Christo, & per Christum. Ergo ex gratia servati sumus; Nam ex gratia est, quod in pacto redemptionis inter Deum & Mediatorem inito, nos ut mortui in peccatis, traditi simus Filio Redemptori designato, ut per eum ad vitam restituaeremur. Ex gratia est, quod in pacti pretii redemptionis persolutione, vita in Christo a mortuis vivificato, danda nobis, adjudicata fit. Ex gratia est quod in redemptionis applicatione, in momento regenerationis, vita in, & a Christo actu nobis communicata fit, ut cum aliis Sanctis Christo insiti, communi cum illis vita spirituali frueremur, & adolescemus in illo; quibus rationibus vita nostra a vita Christi semper dependet, & cum ea nexu indissolubili copulatur.
units.tr: Arg. 3. In the moment of our redemption through Christ, and of regeneration through the Spirit of Christ, we who were dead in sins are made alive together with Christ, that is, in Christ and through Christ. Therefore we have been saved by grace. For it is of grace that, in the covenant of redemption entered into between God and the Mediator, we, as dead in sins, were delivered to the Son designated as Redeemer, so that through him we might be restored to life. It is of grace that, in the payment of the price of redemption, life in Christ, who was made alive from the dead, was adjudged to be given to us. It is of grace that, in the application of redemption, at the moment of regeneration, life in and from Christ was actually communicated to us, so that, grafted into Christ with the other saints, we might enjoy a common spiritual life with them and grow up in him; by these reasons our life always depends upon the life of Christ and is joined to it by an indissoluble bond.

units.la: Vers. 6. Unaque excitavit, unaque collocavit in coelis in Christo Iesu.
units.tr: Verse 6. And raised us up together and made us sit together in the heavenly places in Christ Jesus.

units.la: Arg. 4. Deus in suscitato Christo una suscitavit nos, & incollocato Christo in Coelis una collocavit nos. Ergo ex gratia nos servavit serviuit. Nam sicut nostrum censetur In Dei judicio, quicquid Christus nostro nomine & loco vel fecit, vel passus est, sic etiam nostrum censetur quicquid Christus accepit nostro loco & nomine. Ergo in resurrectione Christi, redempti unà resurrexerunt judicialiter, seu modo judiciali, ex fœdere redemptionis; In Christi ascensione in Cœlum, redempti judicialiter una ascenderunt; In Christi sessione, seu gloriosa possessione vitæ æternæ, redempti judiciali modo unà collocantur & sedent. Hoc jus redemptis à Christo impetratum est, ante fidem actu datam: In conversione verò, per fidem, olim impetratum jus actu speciali nobis applicatur, ut sicut ascendenti Christo licuit dicere ex fœdere inter Deum & Mediatorem inito, seu ex fœdere redemptionis, Ego ascendo nomine Redemptorum, quibus hoc jus impetravi, ut in me ascendere censeantur: sic confugientibus ad Christum & credentibus in eum singulis licet dicere, jam mihi jus factum est, Ex fœdere salutis inter Deum & Ecclesiam per Mediatorem inito, ut resurrectionem Christi meam jure censeam, ascensionem Christi meam jure censeam, & sic in cæteris. Quanta hîc gratia est?
units.tr: Arg. 4. God, in the raising of Christ, raised us up together with him, and in the seating of Christ in heaven, he seated us together. Therefore he saved us and preserved us by grace. For just as, in God's judgment, whatever Christ did or suffered in our name and place is reckoned ours, so too whatever Christ received in our place and name is reckoned ours. Therefore, in the resurrection of Christ, the redeemed rose together with him judicially, or in a judicial manner, by the covenant of redemption; in the ascension of Christ into heaven, the redeemed ascended together with him judicially; in the session of Christ, or his glorious possession of eternal life, the redeemed are judicially placed and seated together with him. This right was obtained for the redeemed by Christ before faith was actually given. But in conversion, through faith, the right once obtained is applied to us by a special act, so that, just as Christ, ascending, was entitled to say, by the covenant entered into between God and the Mediator, or by the covenant of redemption, "I ascend in the name of the redeemed, for whom I obtained this right, so that they are reckoned to ascend in me," so each of those who flee to Christ and believe in him may say, "The right has now been made mine by the covenant of salvation entered into between God and the Church through the Mediator," so that I may justly reckon Christ's resurrection to be mine, Christ's ascension to be mine, and so on for the rest. How great is the grace here?

units.la: Vers. 7. Ut ostenderet seculis succedentibus summas opes suæ gratiæ, sua erga nos benignitate in Christo Iesu.
units.tr: Verse 7. That he might show in the ages to come the exceeding riches of his grace in his kindness towards us in Christ Jesus.

units.la: Arg. 5. Finis propter quem nos perditi peccatores ex Judæis & Gentibus donati sumus salute in Christo, etiam post tam flagitiosam anteactam vitam, est, ut qui posterioribus seculis victuri sunt, videant & agnoscant gratiam Dei superabundantem; & ut in exemplo nostro, discant accedere ad Deum, fontem salutis in Christo, ut similiter gratiam, etiam indignißimi consequantur. Ergo ex sola gratia servati sumus.
units.tr: Arg. 5. The purpose for which we, lost sinners, both Jews and Gentiles, have been granted salvation in Christ, even after so shameful a former life, is that those who are to live in later ages may see and acknowledge the superabundant grace of God, and that, by our example, they may learn to draw near to God, the fountain of salvation in Christ, so as to obtain grace likewise, even the most unworthy. Therefore we have been saved by grace alone.

units.la: Verl. 8. Gratia enim estis servati per fidem: idque non ex vobis: Dei donum est.
units.tr: Verse 8. For by grace you have been saved through faith, and that not of yourselves; it is the gift of God.

units.la: Propositionem probandam in terminis profert, & addit Arg. 6. Per fidem servamur, Ergo per gratiam. Fides enim renunciat meritis nostris, & recumbit in gratuitam promissionem Dei: & quod Deus constituerit instrumentum salutis fidem, (cujus natura requirit ut nostris operibus, & viribus; nostræ sapientiæ & dignitati renunciantes, exeamus e nobis, ut salutem quæramus in Deo) etiam illud ex gratia est.
units.tr: He sets forth the proposition to be proved in its own terms, and adds Arg. 6. We are saved through faith; therefore through grace. For faith renounces our merits and rests upon the free promise of God; and that God has appointed faith as the instrument of salvation (whose nature requires that we go out of ourselves, renouncing our works and powers, our wisdom and dignity, so as to seek salvation in God) is itself also of grace.

units.la: Et hoc Arg. 7. Neque ex nobis servamur, neque ex nobis seu nostris viribus naturalibus est fides, sed sicut salus, sic etiam fides, est donum DEI gratuitum. Ergo ex gratia servamur. Cum enim SPIRITUS DEI incipit in nobis conversionem operari, mortuos in peccatis comperit nos, qui nisi vivificemur ab ipso, ad nostri regenerationem & salutem conferre nihil possumus; imò ne fidem quidem DEI promissionibus habere valemus, nisi supernè nobis fides, fideique actus concedatur.
units.tr: And this is the seventh argument: we are saved not from ourselves, nor is faith from ourselves or from our natural powers. Rather, as salvation is, so faith too is a free gift of God. Therefore we are saved by grace. For when the Spirit of God begins to work conversion in us, he finds us dead in sins; unless we are made alive by him, we can contribute nothing to our regeneration and salvation. Indeed, we cannot even hold faith in God's promises unless faith and the act of faith are granted to us from above.

units.la: Vers. 9. Non ex operibus, ne quis glorietur,
units.tr: Vers. 9. Not of works, lest anyone should boast,

units.la: Arg. 8. Non ex operibus servamur. Ergo ex gratia, hæc enim se mutuò tollunt.
units.tr: Argument 8. We are not saved by works. Therefore by grace, for these mutually exclude each other.

units.la: Arg. 9. Si ex operibus servaremur, & non ex mera gratia, gloriandi materia nobis suppeteret, At hoc est absurdum: Ergo ex gratia servamur, ut Rom. 3.
units.tr: Argument 9. If we were saved by works, and not by mere grace, we would have material for boasting. But this is absurd. Therefore we are saved by grace, as in Rom. 3.

units.la: Vers. 10. Nam ipsius sumus opus, conditi in Christo Iesu ad opera bona, quæ præparavit Deus ut in eis ambulemus.
units.tr: Verse 10. For we are his workmanship, created in Christ Jesus unto good works, which God prepared beforehand that we should walk in them.

units.la: Arg. 10. Nos quatenus regeniti, quatenus vita spirituali donati, CHRISTO inserimur, sumus opus DEI, & nova creatura, DEI solius potentia de novo creati, priusquam ullum opus bonum edere possemus. Ergo non servamur ex operum merito, sed ex gratia mera.
units.tr: Argument 10. We, insofar as we are regenerated, insofar as we are endowed with spiritual life, are grafted into Christ. We are God's workmanship and a new creation, created anew by the power of God alone, before we could produce any good work. Therefore we are not saved by the merit of works, but by mere grace.

units.la: Arg. 11. In CHRISTO sumus conditi ad bona opera edenda, & eādem gratiâ qua CHRISTO inserimur, destinati sumus ad opera bona facienda. Ergo nulla vi bonorum operum nostrorum servamur.
units.tr: Argument 11. We have been created in Christ for the performance of good works, and by the same grace by which we are grafted into Christ, we are destined to do good works. Therefore we are saved by no power of our good works.

units.la: Arg. 12. Ea opera quæ facturi sumus post regenerationem, præparata sunt à DEO, ut ea agamus, & ad ea agenda præparatur nostrer intellectus, præparatur & formatur voluntas, & præparantur vires nobis dandæ à DEO, qui operatur in nobis, & ut velimus, & ut perficiamus. Ergo non servamur ex operibus sed tantum ex gratia.
units.tr: Argument 12. The works which we are going to do after regeneration have been prepared by God so that we might do them. For the doing of them our understanding is prepared, our will is prepared and formed, and the powers to be given to us by God are prepared, for he works in us both to will and to perform. Therefore we are not saved by works, but only by grace.

units.la: Arg 13. Finis præparatorum bonorum operum est, ut jam vivificati, & CHRISTO insiti, & renati, & justificati, & jus plenum consequuti, ad justitiam & salutem in CHRISTO obtinendum, ambularemus in iis, tanquam in via regia ad possessionem salutis, jam emptæ per CHRISTUM, & nobis jam concessæ in CHRISTO. Ergo non servamur ex operibus, sed solâ gratiâ.
units.tr: Argument 13. The purpose of the prepared good works is that we, now made alive, grafted into Christ, reborn and justified, and having obtained full right, should walk in them, as on the royal road, to attain righteousness and salvation in Christ, to the possession of salvation which has already been purchased by Christ and already granted to us in Christ. Therefore we are not saved by works, but by grace alone.

units.la: Verf. 11. Propterea mementote vos quondam Gentes in carne, qui dicebamini Praeputium ab ea quæ vocatur Circumcisio in carne, & quæ manibus fit.
units.tr: Verse 11. Therefore remember that you, once Gentiles in the flesh, who were called the uncircumcision by those who are called the circumcision, which is made in the flesh by hands.

units.la: Arg. 14. Continens amplificationem gratiæ factæ Ephesiis, respectu peculiaris ipsorum pristini status in Ethnicismo. Si vos Ephesii in speciali vestro statu, quatenus Gentiles eratis, spectemini, adeò misera & deplorata apparebit vestra conditio, ut non nisi gratiâ liberari inde potuisletis. Ergo vel vestræ conditionis mutatio, demonstrabit salutem esse ex gratia. Miserum hunc statum describet in his octo: 1. Erant in carne viventes secundum carnem, ita ut Deo placere non potuerint. 2. Erant incircumcisi, id est, in ignominia apud Judæos, qui externæ seu manufactæ circumcisionis honore gaudent.
units.tr: Argument 14. This contains an amplification of the grace given to the Ephesians, with respect to their former peculiar state in heathenism. If you Ephesians are considered in your particular state, insofar as you were Gentiles, your condition will appear so wretched and hopeless that you could not have been freed from it except by grace. Therefore the change of your condition demonstrates that salvation is by grace. He describes this miserable state in eight points: 1. They were in the flesh, living according to the flesh, so that they could not please God. 2. They were uncircumcised, that is, in disgrace among the Jews, who take pride in the honour of external, man-made circumcision.

units.la: Verf. 12. Vos inquam, illo tempore fuisse absque Christo, alienis à republica Israelis, & extraneos à pactis promissionis, spem non habentes, & Dei expertes in mundo:
units.tr: Verse 12. That you, I say, were at that time without Christ, alienated from the commonwealth of Israel, and strangers to the covenants of promise, having no hope and without God in the world.

units.la: 3. Erant sine Christo, seu destituti omni actuali applicatâ communione cum Christo in Spiritu. 4. Alieni à republica Israelis, id est, extra Ecclesiam Dei. 5. alieni à pactis promissorum, id est, à jure ad applicandum sibi pacta & promissiones Dei. 6. Destituebantur omnis futuri boni spe certa. 7. Erant sine Deo vero, id est, sine ejus cognitione & cultu. 8. Erant mundani, seu pars mundi, qui jacet in malo, & qui regnum est Satanæ. Ergo quod liberati sint ab hoc statu tam misero, non potuit non esse ex gratia.
units.tr: 3. They were without Christ, that is, deprived of every actual applied communion with Christ in the Spirit. 4. They were alienated from the commonwealth of Israel, that is, outside the Church of God. 5. They were strangers to the covenants of promise, that is, lacking the right to apply to themselves the covenants and promises of God. 6. They were without any certain hope of future good. 7. They were without the true God, that is, without knowledge and worship of him. 8. They were worldly, or part of the world, which lies in evil and which is the kingdom of Satan. Therefore, that they were delivered from so miserable a state could only have been by grace.

units.la: Verf. 13. At nunc in Christo Iesu, vos qui olim eratis procul, propinqui facti estis, per sanguinem inquam Christi.
units.tr: Verse 13. But now in Christ Jesus, you who once were far off have been brought near by the blood of Christ, I say.

units.la: Arg. 15. Si felicitas præsentis status comparetur cum pristino statu, tanta est, ut non aliunde quam à gratia ipsis contingere potuisset. Hujus argumenti octo sunt partes, quæ eodem tendunt. Prima pars, Ephesii qui longe aberant à fœdere & ab Ecclesia, ejusque bonis, jam propinqui facti sunt, aditu ipsis ad fœdus, & Ecclesiam patefacto, cujus beneficii causa meritoria est sanguis Christi; instrumentalis verò fides, per quam insiti sunt in Christum, & per consequens ex gratia.
units.tr: Argument 15. If the happiness of the present state is compared with the former state, it is so great that it could have come to them from nothing other than grace. This argument has eight parts, all tending to the same point. The first part: the Ephesians, who were far from the covenant and from the Church and its benefits, have now been brought near, the way to the covenant and the Church having been opened to them. The meritorious cause of this benefit is the blood of Christ; the instrumental cause is faith, through which they have been grafted into Christ, and consequently it is by grace.

units.la: Verf. 14. Ipse enim est pax nostra, qui utraque fecit unum, & intergerini parietis septum solvit.
units.tr: Verse 14. For he himself is our peace, who has made both one, and has broken down the dividing wall of the fence.

units.la: Secunda pars argumenti confirmans priorem. Christus reconciliavit Gentes & Judæos sibi invicem; Mediator pacificus, & causa Ipse pacis; conjunxit utrumque populum in unum corpus, Sustulit legem ceremonialem, quæ tanquam maceries, septum, paries intergerinus, dividebat Gentes à Judæis, & inimicitiarum causam præbebat. Per passionem suam in carne, pacem hanc procuravit: Quomodo non ex gratia omnia illa?
units.tr: The second part of the argument, confirming the first. Christ has reconciled Gentiles and Jews to one another. He is the peacemaking Mediator and himself the cause of peace. He has joined both peoples into one body. He has abolished the ceremonial law, which, like a wall, a fence, a dividing partition, separated the Gentiles from the Jews and provided a cause of enmity. He procured this peace through his suffering in the flesh. How could all this not be by grace?

units.la: Verf' 15 Inimicitiis, id est, lege mandatorum quæ in ritibus posita est, per carnem suam abolitis: ut ex duobus illis conderet in semetipso unum novum hominem, faciens pacem.
units.tr: Verse 15. The enmity, that is, the law of commandments which consists in ordinances, abolished in his flesh, so that from the two he might create in himself one new man, making peace.

units.la: Tertia argumenti pars, quæ specialius, & propriis verbis proponitur: Christus abrogavit legem mandatorum in decretis sitam, id est, legem positivam ceremonialem, quæ complementum nacta erat in ejus adventu, ut illa lege sublata, per quam inimicitiæ erant inter duos populos, in semetipso capite communi reconciliatos sibi invicem, utrosque quasi unum redderet hominem novum, compingens in unum mysticum Christum, seu ut unius mystici corporis membra conjungens Judæos & Gentes in unum corpus, cujus caput Christus ipse esset. Et hic etiam summa gratia conspicienda est.
units.tr: The third part of the argument, which is proposed more specifically and in its own words: Christ abrogated the law of commandments consisting in decrees, that is, the positive ceremonial law, which had reached its fulfilment at his coming. By this law, taken away, enmity existed between the two peoples. He reconciled them to one another in himself, the common head, and made both into one new man, joining them into one mystical Christ, or joining the Jews and Gentiles as members of one mystical body, whose head would be Christ himself. Here also the highest grace is to be seen.

units.la: Verf. 16. Et utrosque in uno corpore reconciliaret Deo per crucem, peremptis inimicitiis per eam.
units.tr: Verse 16. And might reconcile both in one body to God through the cross, having slain the enmity by it.

units.la: Quarta argumenti pars, in qua ostendit alium finem abrogatæ legis, nempe ut in uno suo corpore, utrumque populum non sibi invicem tantum, sed etiam Deo reconciliaret, pretium Redemptionis ipsorum à peccatis, per mortem crucis persolvendo, interfectis inimicitiis inter Deum & populum redemptum, per interfectionem sui, seu mortem suam. Hic amplius splendet gratia,
units.tr: The fourth part of the argument, in which he shows another purpose of the abrogated law: that in his one body he might reconcile both peoples not only to one another but also to God, by paying the price of their redemption from sins through death on the cross, the enmity between God and the redeemed people being killed by his slaying, that is, by his death. Here grace shines more brightly.

units.la: Verf. 17 Et veniens evangelizavit pacem vobis qui procul eratis; & iis qui prope erant.
units.tr: Verse 17. And he came and preached peace to you who were far off, and to those who were near.

units.la: Quinta argumenti pars, in qua ostendit quomodo hæc pax innotuerit mundo, nempe in prædicatione Evangelii per Iesum Christum, qui ut author fuit pacis, sic etiam primarius est præco hujus pacis in Evangelio, in consolationem & salutem Judæorum (qui propinqui dicti erant, propter fœdus) & Gentilium salutem (qui procul esse dicti erant, propter ipsorum alienationem à fœdere) Etiam hic se exerit gratia.
units.tr: The fifth part of the argument, in which he shows how this peace has become known to the world: namely, in the preaching of the Gospel by Jesus Christ, who as the author of peace is also the chief herald of this peace in the Gospel, for the comfort and salvation of the Jews (who were called near because of the covenant) and the salvation of the Gentiles (who were called far off because of their alienation from the covenant). Grace also displays itself here.

units.la: Verf. 18. Quoniam utrique per ipsum habemus aditum per unum Spiritum ad Patrem.
units.tr: Verse 18. For through him we both have access by one Spirit to the Father.

units.la: Sexta argumenti pars, in qua rationem reddit prædicatæ pacis utrisque, quia per unum Christum persoluto jam pretio, unus aditus & accessus datur & Judæis & Gentibus, ut possimus Judæi pariter & Gentes, in uno Spiritu unum Patrem invocare, & idcirco Judæis & Gentibus pax prædicatur. Nihil hic præter gratiam.
units.tr: The sixth part of the argument, in which he gives the reason for the peace preached to both: because through the one Christ, the price now having been paid, one approach and access is given to both Jews and Gentiles, so that we, Jews and Gentiles alike, in one Spirit, may call upon one Father. Therefore peace is preached to Jews and Gentiles. Nothing here but grace.

units.la: Verf 19. Nempe igitur non amplius estis hospites & inquilini, sed cives Sanctorum, ac domestici Dei:
units.tr: Verse 19. Therefore you are no longer strangers and sojourners, but fellow-citizens of the saints, and members of the household of God:

units.la: Septima argumenti pars, in qua tanquam per corrolarium colligit Ephesios jam non amplius hospites seu peregrinos, sed cives esse civitatis Sanctorum, & domesticos familiæ Dei, quod etiam nostrum omnium credentium privilegium est.
units.tr: The seventh part of the argument, in which, as a corollary, he concludes that the Ephesians are no longer strangers or foreigners, but citizens of the city of the saints and members of the household of God; which is also the privilege of all of us who believe.

units.la: Verf. 20. Superstructi super fundamentum Apostolorum ac Prophetarum, cujus imus angularis lapis est ipse Iesus Christus.
units.tr: Verse 20. Built upon the foundation of the Apostles and Prophets, the chief cornerstone being Jesus Christ himself.

units.la: Octava argumenti pars, in qua amplius explicans unionem Ephesiorum cum Christo, & sanctâ Ecclesiâ, declarat eos esse vivos lapides Templi Dei, non minus arctè cum aliis fidelibus & cum Christo constrictos; quam lapides ædificii uniuntur fundamento: & hic depingit Ecclesiam graphicè in Templi similitudine, cujus membra sunt 3. Primum, Ecclesia est similis Templo Dei, cujus fundamentum est Christus, non solùm sustentans totum ædificium, sed etiam diversos parietes Judæos & Gentes in seipso, inter se conjungens, atque uniens: 2. Apostoli aliique post eos fideles Ministri architecti sunt, qui Templi hujus unicum docent fundamentum Christum (qui solus molem totam, ut Redemptionis, sic etiam salutis, sustinere valet) & docendo ædificant Sanctos super Christum secundùm doctrinam Prophetarum & Apostolorum: 3. Lapides hujus Templi sunt electi, seu verè fideles omnes, qui superstruuntur Christo, per veritatis prædicationem, inter quos erant Ephesii fideles.
units.tr: The eighth part of the argument, in which, explaining more fully the union of the Ephesians with Christ and with the holy Church, he declares that they are living stones of the Temple of God, joined no less closely to the other faithful and to Christ than the stones of a building are joined to its foundation. Here he portrays the Church vividly under the likeness of a Temple, whose members are three. First, the Church is like the Temple of God, whose foundation is Christ, who not only sustains the whole building but also joins together and unites in himself the diverse walls, Jews and Gentiles. Second, the Apostles and the faithful ministers who came after them are the architects, who teach that Christ is the one foundation of this Temple (he alone is able to sustain the whole mass, as of redemption, so also of salvation), and by teaching they build up the saints upon Christ according to the doctrine of the Prophets and Apostles. Third, the stones of this Temple are the elect, or truly faithful, all who are built upon Christ through the preaching of the truth, among whom were the faithful Ephesians.

units.la: Verf. 21. In quo totum ædificium congruenter coagmentatum, crescit, ut sit templum sanctum Domino.
units.tr: Verse 21. In whom the whole building, fitly framed together, grows into a holy temple to the Lord.

units.la: Pergit in allegorica descriptione Ecclesiæ veræ catholicæ, & quatuor conditiones ac proprietates Ecclesiæ, seu templi Dei explicat: 1.
units.tr: He goes on with an allegorical description of the true catholic Church, and explains four conditions and properties of the Church, or temple of God: 1.

units.la: Templum hoc dicitur affabrè factum, seu congruenter coagmentatum, quia summa cum prudentia totum ædificium Ecclesiæ, ejusque membra omnia congruenter coagmentantur, cum Christus & ipsius voluntas prædicatur, ita ut quisque fidelis convenientem habeat locum, & functionem, pro qualitate donorum Spiritus sancti, ut alii in munere publico, alii in privata sua statione ad ædificationem totius Templi, pro sua quisque parte concurrant: 2. Templum hoc est vivum, quia fundamentum vivum, & vivificans, est Christus: & vera ejus membra, singuli fideles, sunt lapides vivi, à Christo vitali fundamento, vivificati, & in vita spirituali conservati: 3. Templum hoc vegetum est sicut arbor; quia totum ædificium per accessionem lapidum, seu conversorum fidelium, & per nutrimentum verbi Dei quod singuli lapides vivi, ut rami à radice trahunt à Christo per Spiritum sanctum, tenentes caput Christum, infixi radici Christo, quotidie crescunt in pietate: 4. Templum hoc rationale & spirituale est, quia Templum sanctum est, id est, societas non terrenorum, profanorum, & immundorum hominum, sed societas Sanctorum spiritualis, quasi domicilium cœleste, in quo Deus verè habitet, verè cognoscatur, ametur, invocetur, & colatur.
units.tr: This temple is said to be fitly framed, or fitly joined together, because with the greatest prudence the whole building of the Church and all its members are fitly joined together, when Christ and his will are proclaimed, so that each faithful person has a suitable place and function, according to the quality of the gifts of the Holy Spirit, so that some in public office and others in their private station each contribute their part to the building up of the whole Temple. 2. This temple is living, because its foundation is living and life-giving, namely Christ; and its true members, all the faithful individually, are living stones, made alive by Christ the living foundation and kept in spiritual life. 3. This temple is flourishing like a tree, because the whole building grows daily in godliness, through the addition of stones, that is, of converted believers, and through the nourishment of the Word of God, which the individual living stones draw from Christ through the Holy Spirit, as branches draw from a root, holding fast to Christ the head and grafted into Christ the root. 4. This temple is rational and spiritual, because the holy temple is not a society of earthly, profane and unclean men, but a spiritual fellowship of the saints, like a heavenly dwelling, in which God truly dwells, is truly known, loved, invoked and worshipped.

units.la: Vers. 22. In quo & vos unà ædificamini, ut sitis habitaculum Dei per Spiritum.
units.tr: Verse 22. In whom you also are built together for a habitation of God through the Spirit.

units.la: Applicat ista ad Ephesios, omnes partes argumenti contrahens in unum, ut felicitas conditionis ipsorum in Christo, appareat simul & semel, ut sciant se esse habitaculum Dei, seu partem hujus templi, & communicare cum catholica Ecclesia; & per Spiritum Sanctum habitantem in ipsis, participes esse proprietatum Ecclesiæ; ex quibus omnibus conficitur tantam felicitatem nactos esse Ephesios, quantam sola gratia poterat largiri.
units.tr: He applies these things to the Ephesians, gathering all the parts of the argument into one, so that the happiness of their condition in Christ may appear at once and together: that they may know that they are the dwelling place of God, or part of this temple, and share in the catholic Church; and that, through the Holy Spirit dwelling in them, they are partakers of the properties of the Church. From all these things it follows that the Ephesians had obtained so great a happiness as grace alone could bestow.

units.la: Caput Tertium.
units.tr: Chapter 3.

units.la: HOc capite, Ephesios Apostolus hortatur, ut superati scandalo crucis Christi sibi ipsi incumbentis, pro Euangelii defensione, constanter perseverent in gratia Dei tuenda, hoc est ut firmiter credant, & aperte confiteantur, & in omnibus angustiis accurate defendant, nos esse per gratiam electos in Christo, per gratiam redemptos, per gratiam vocatos, per gratiam justificari, per gratiam fide donari, per gratiam regenerari, per gratiam omnia bona in nobis perfici, ex gratia sola nos servari, & tandem glorificari in Christo, per fidem & non ex operibus; & fidem non esse ex nobis, sed Dei donum esse, ut in tota ratione salutis nostrae Dei gratia sola glorificetur. Summa est, ut inoffenso pede pergant, & proficiant in fide Euangelii.
units.tr: In this chapter the Apostle exhorts the Ephesians that, having got past the offence of the cross of Christ, which is a stumbling-block to people, they should persevere constantly in defending the grace of God for the defence of the Gospel. That is, they should firmly believe, openly confess, and carefully defend in all their troubles that we have been chosen in Christ by grace, redeemed by grace, called by grace, justified by grace, given faith by grace, regenerated by grace, have every good thing in us brought to completion by grace, are saved by grace alone, and at last are glorified in Christ, through faith and not from works; and that faith is not from ourselves but is the gift of God, so that in the whole account of our salvation the grace of God alone may be glorified. The sum is that they should go on with unstumbling feet and make progress in the faith of the Gospel.

units.la: Capitis partes sunt duae: In prima ne Ephesii offendantur crucis & captivitatis Apostoli scandalo, Ministerii sui & vinculorum suorum gloriam ostendit Apostolus, ad versum 14. In secunda parte continetur Apostoli precatio pro Ephesiorum perseverantia & profectu in fide, ad finem. Primae partis summa hoc enthymemate comprehenditur. Magna est gloria Ministerii mei & vinculorum meorum, peto igitur ne offendamini afflictionibus meis: Antecedens habetur, ad versum 13. Consequens, versu 13.
units.tr: The chapter has two parts. In the first, lest the Ephesians be offended by the scandal of the cross and of the Apostle's captivity, the Apostle shows the glory of his ministry and of his chains, up to verse 14. The second part contains the Apostle's prayer for the Ephesians' perseverance and progress in faith, to the end. The sum of the first part is comprehended in this enthymeme: My ministry and my chains are glorious; I beg you therefore not to be offended by my afflictions. The antecedent is found at verse 13, and the consequent at verse 13.

units.la: Vers. 1. Hujus rei gratia ego Paulus sum captivus ille Christi Iesu pro vobis Gentibus:
units.tr: Ver. 1. For this cause I, Paul, am the prisoner of Jesus Christ for you Gentiles:

units.la: Argumenta Commendationis Ministerii sui affert duodecim.
units.tr: He brings twelve arguments in commendation of his ministry.

units.la: Hujus rei gratia ] Argumentum primum, Quia propter supra descriptam veritatem a me praedicatam, de salute in Christo, Judaeis pariter & Gentibus per fidem obtinenda vinctus sum, & idcirco vinctus Christi, seu pro Christi gloria asserta captivus, & pro vobis Gentibus, seu pro jure vestro ad salutem, una cum Judaeis, asserto. Commendatum vobis idcirco debet esse Ministerium meum.
units.tr: For this cause] The first argument: because of the truth described above, which I preach, concerning salvation in Christ to be obtained through faith by Jews and Gentiles alike, I am bound, and therefore I am a prisoner of Christ, that is, a prisoner for the sake of asserting Christ's glory, and for you Gentiles, that is, for the asserting of your right to salvation along with the Jews. My ministry therefore ought to be commended to you.

units.la: Vers. 2. Siquidem audistis dispensationem gratiae Dei quae data est mihi apud vos:
units.tr: Ver. 2. If indeed you have heard of the dispensation of the grace of God which was given to me toward you:

units.la: Arg. 2. Ego Paulus à CHRISTO peculiaris Apostolas Gentium constitutus sum, si modo probè intellexistis dispensationem gratiæ, seu doctrinæ Euangelicæ, quæ commissa fuit mihi, ut eam vobis Gentibus prædicarem: Ergo commendatum debet esse vobis meum Ministerium.
units.tr: Arg. 2. I, Paul, have been appointed by Christ as the special Apostle of the Gentiles, provided that you have rightly understood the dispensation of grace, that is, the Gospel doctrine, which was committed to me so that I might preach it to you Gentiles. Therefore my ministry ought to be commended to you.

units.la: Verf. 3. Deum videlicet per revelationem notum mihi fecisse mysterium illud, (sicut ante scripsi paucis:
units.tr: Ver. 3. That is, that by revelation God made known to me that mystery, (as I wrote before briefly,

units.la: Arg. 3. Cognitio Euangelii quâ donatus sum, certissima fuit, quippe quam à Deo immediatè per revelationem extraordinariam accepi, non autem ab hominibus: Ergo commendatum, &c.
units.tr: Arg. 3. The knowledge of the Gospel with which I was endowed was most certain, since I received it immediately from God by an extraordinary revelation, and not from men. Therefore my ministry, etc., is to be commended.

units.la: Verf. 4. Ex quo perlecto potestis intelligere quæ sit mea intelligentia in mysterio Christi)
units.tr: Ver. 4. By which, when you have read it, you can understand my insight into the mystery of Christ)

units.la: Arg. 4. Intelligentiæ & cognitionis meæ mensura, quâ mysterium gratiæ revelatum scio, non mediocris est, ut ex iis quæ ex primo & secundo capite hujus Epistolæ scripta sunt à me, attentè legentibus manifestum esse poterit: Ergo &c.
units.tr: Arg. 4. The measure of my understanding and knowledge, by which I know the revealed mystery of grace, is not small, as will be clear to those who read attentively what I have written in the first and second chapters of this Epistle. Therefore, etc.

units.la: Verf. 5. Quod aliis filiis hominum, ut nunc retectum est sanctis Apostolis & Prophetis per Spiritum:
units.tr: Ver. 5. Which in other generations was not made known to the sons of men, as it has now been revealed to the holy Apostles and Prophets by the Spirit:

units.la: Arg. 5. Mysterium hujus Euangelii non innotuit multis, neque ulli tam perspicuè præteritis seculis, quam nunc revelatum est per Spiritum Sanctum, nobis Apostolis & Prophetis, quibus extra ordinem Deus cognitionem Scripturarum, & suæ de salute hominum voluntatis, concessit: Ergo commendatum, &c.
units.tr: Arg. 5. The mystery of this Gospel was not known to many, nor was it made plain in any past age as it is now revealed by the Holy Spirit to us Apostles and Prophets, to whom God, beyond the ordinary way, granted knowledge of the Scriptures and of his will concerning the salvation of men. Therefore my ministry, etc., is to be commended.

units.la: Verf. 6. Gentes videlicet esse cohæredes & concorpores, consortesque promissionis ejus in Christo per Euangelium:
units.tr: Ver. 6. That the Gentiles should be fellow-heirs, and of the same body, and partakers of his promise in Christ through the Gospel:

units.la: Arg. 6. Pars illa mysterii, quæ est de complemento omnium promissionum gratiæ in CHRISTO, & de vocatione Gentium incircumcisarum in societatem hæreditatis cœlestis, ut in unionem Ecclesiæ Israeliticæ, & participationem CHRISTI per fidem Euangelii, absque circumcisione, & reliquis Ceremoniis, à Deo reciperentur, non minus quam Israelitæ; Pars hæc, inquam, non ita pridem manifestata fuit. Ergo, &c. Neque enim ipse Petrus Apostolus hoc admittebat, priusquam de ea speciali revelatione edoctus fuisset, Act. 10.
units.tr: Arg. 6. That part of the mystery which concerns the fulfilment of all the promises of grace in Christ, and the calling of uncircumcised Gentiles into fellowship in the heavenly inheritance, into union with the Israelite Church and participation in Christ through faith in the Gospel, without circumcision and the rest of the ceremonies, and that they should be received by God no less than the Israelites: this part, I say, was not revealed long ago. Therefore, etc. For the Apostle Peter himself did not accept this before he had been taught by a special revelation about it, Acts 10.

units.la: Verf. 7. Cujus factus sum minister ex dono gratiæ Dei, quod datum est mihi secundùm efficacitatem potentiæ ipsius.
units.tr: Ver. 7. Of which I was made a minister, according to the gift of the grace of God, which was given to me according to the working of his power.

units.la: Arg. 7. Authoritas ad dispensandum hanc Dei gratiam mihi commissa, conjuncta est, & cum donis necessariis ad munus Apostolicum, & cum efficaci Dei benedictione, ubicunque & quandocunque datur praedicandi opportunitas. Ergo, &c.
units.tr: Arg. 7. The authority committed to me to dispense this grace of God is joined with the gifts necessary for the Apostolic office, and with the effective blessing of God wherever and whenever the opportunity to preach is given. Therefore, etc.

units.la: Verf. 8. Mihi inquam, longè minimo omnium sanctorum, data est hæc gratia, evangelizandi inter Gentes impervestigabiles opes CHRISTI,
units.tr: Ver. 8. To me, I say, who am the least of all the saints, this grace was given, to preach among the Gentiles the unsearchable riches of Christ,

units.la: Arg. 8. Gratia mihi facta in vocatione ad Apostolatum tantò illustrior est, quantò ipse olim hostis Ecclesiæ eram infestior, omnibusque Sanctis eo nomine inferior, quantoque Gentium multarum amplitudo major est, & denique quantò gloriosior est materia à me praedicanda, nempe gratiæ Christi opulentia impervestigabilis. Ergo, &c
units.tr: Arg. 8. The grace shown to me in my calling to the Apostleship is all the more illustrious, the more hostile I once was to the Church, and the more I am inferior to all the saints on that account; and the more the number of the many Gentiles is great, and finally, the more glorious is the subject I preach, namely the unsearchable richness of Christ's grace. Therefore, etc.

units.la: Verf. 9. Et in lucem proferendi omnibus quæ sit communio mysterii quod erat abscondituum à seculis in Deo, qui omnia condidit per Iesum Christum:
units.tr: Ver. 9. And to bring to light for all men what is the fellowship of the mystery which from the ages has been hidden in God, who created all things through Jesus Christ:

units.la: Arg. 9. Fines ministerii mei gloriosi sunt: 1. Ut res occultæ, in Dei consilio latentes, in lucem proferantur. 2. Ut cæci illuminentur ad videndum & intelligendum revelata. 3. Ut omnes sciant, participes salutis reddi posse homines per fidem solam Iesu Christi, sine circumcisione & operibus Legis. 4. Ut perspiciant omnes excellentiam Christi; non modò ut Redemptoris, sed etiam ut Creatoris, per quem ut redempta est Ecclesia, sic etiam & creatus est mundus, & omnia quæ in mundo sunt: Ergo commendatum vobis esse debet meum ministerium.
units.tr: Arg. 9. The ends of my ministry are glorious: (1) that hidden things, lying hidden in the counsel of God, may be brought to light; (2) that the blind may be enlightened to see and understand what has been revealed; (3) that all may know that men can be made partakers of salvation through faith alone in Jesus Christ, without circumcision and the works of the Law; (4) that all may perceive the excellence of Christ, not only as Redeemer but also as Creator, through whom the Church has been redeemed, and through whom the world and all that is in it has also been created. Therefore my ministry ought to be commended to you.

units.la: Verf. 10. Ut nota nunc fiat per Ecclesiam imperiis ac potestatibus quæ in Cœlis sunt multiformis illa sapientia Dei:
units.tr: Ver. 10. So that now through the Church the manifold wisdom of God may be made known to the principalities and powers in the heavenly places:

units.la: Arg. 10. Gloriosus est usus hujus mei Ministerii, quia per illud multiformis Dei sapientia in apertione consilii sui de Ecclesia ex circumcisis & incircumcisis colligenda, clarius quam unquam prius patefacta est, etiam Sanctis Angelis in Cœlo, nedum hominibus in terra. Ergo, &c. Angeli enim nisi ex revelatione facta Ecclesiæ de mysterio salutis humanæ nihil intelligunt.
units.tr: Arg. 10. The use of this my ministry is glorious, because through it the manifold wisdom of God, in the disclosure of his purpose to gather the Church from circumcised and uncircumcised, has been made clearer than ever before, even to the holy Angels in heaven, not to mention men on earth. Therefore, etc. For the Angels understand nothing of the mystery of human salvation except from the revelation made to the Church.

units.la: Verf. 11 Secundum propositum æternum, quod constituit in Christo Iesu Domino nostro:
units.tr: Ver. 11. According to the eternal purpose which he made in Christ Jesus our Lord:

units.la: Arg. 11. Totum hoc non fortuito factum est, sed secundum propositum æternum Dei, quod, sicut in Christo constituit & fundavit, sic etiam in eodem tandem reipsa complevit atque perfecit. Ergo.
units.tr: Arg. 11. All this was not done by chance, but according to the eternal purpose of God, which he established and founded in Christ, and in the same Christ he has at last actually fulfilled and completed. Therefore.

units.la: Verf. 12. In quo habemus libertatem & aditum cum fiducia, per fidem ipsius.
units.tr: Ver. 12. In whom we have boldness and access with confidence, through his faith.

units.la: Arg. 12, Fructus hujus Ministerii gloriosus est, quia per prædicationem Euangelii credentibus in Christum Judæis & Gentibus, ex æquo conceditur libertas in Christo, adeundi Deum in fiducia, & liberè cum eo agendi, de omnibus ipsorum necessitatibus, ut cum Patre amicissimo. Ergo commendatum vobis esse debet Ministerium meum.
units.tr: Arg. 12. The fruit of this ministry is glorious, because through the preaching of the Gospel, to Jews and Gentiles alike who believe in Christ, freedom is equally granted in Christ to approach God with confidence and to deal freely with him about all their needs, as with a most loving Father. Therefore my ministry ought to be commended to you.

units.la: Verf. 13. Quapropter peto ne segnescatis ob afflictiones meas pro vobis, quæ est gloria vestra.
units.tr: Ver. 13. Therefore I ask that you do not lose heart because of my afflictions for you, which are your glory.

units.la: Ex omnibus præcedentibus, tanquam ex antecedente uno Apostolus infert consequens seu conclusionem, Quod non debeant ipsius vinculis seu captivitate offendi, id est, nec fatiscere, nec defatigari, nec segniores esse in causa fidei ob afflictiones ipsius, sed potius perseverare & profectus facere constanter. Cui hortationi annectit duas rationes: 1. Quia patiebatur has afflictiones pro ipsis, id est, pro ipsorum privilegiis in Christo assertis, & pro fidei ipsorum confirmatione; 2. Quia ipsius afflictiones Ephesis gloriosæ erant; inde enim apparebat quanti eos Deus faceret, cum Apostolos ad eos miserit, qui non solum viam salutis eos docerent, sed etiam sustinerent afflictiones in testimonium veritatis prædicatæ, & confirmationem fidei ipsorum.
units.tr: From all the preceding, as from one antecedent, the Apostle infers the consequent or conclusion: that they ought not to be offended by his chains or captivity, that is, that they should neither faint nor grow weary, nor become more slack in the cause of faith because of his afflictions, but rather persevere and make progress constantly. To this exhortation he adds two reasons: (1) because he suffered these afflictions for them, that is, for their privileges in Christ which he asserts, and for the confirmation of their faith; (2) because his afflictions were a glory to the Ephesians. For from them it appeared how highly God esteemed them, since he sent to them Apostles who not only taught them the way of salvation but also endured afflictions as a witness to the truth preached and to the confirmation of their faith.

units.la: Secunda Pars.
units.tr: Second Part.

units.la: Verf. 14. Hujus rei gratia, flecto genua mea ad Patrem Domini nostri Iesu Christi,
units.tr: Verse 14. For this cause I bow my knees to the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ,

units.la: Secunda pars Capitis in qua continetur Apostoli precatio ut Ephesii perseverent, & progressus faciant in fide Euangelii. Quæ precatio non obscurè hortationem includit ad perseverantiam & constantiam in fide, infertis in eum finem argumentis duodecim. Quæ omnia probant constanter ipsis pergendum in fide.
units.tr: This is the second part of the chapter, which contains the Apostle's prayer that the Ephesians persevere and make progress in the faith of the Gospel. This prayer clearly includes an exhortation to perseverance and constancy in the faith, and to that end he sets out twelve arguments. All of them prove that they must continue steadfastly in the faith.

units.la: Hujus rei gratia ] Argumentum primum, Habetis me flexis quotidie genibus comprecantem in eum finem, ut inoffenso pede pergatis in fide. Pergendum igitur eo alacrius.
units.tr: For this cause] First argument: you have me daily praying on my knees to this end, that you may go on in the faith without stumbling. You should therefore press on all the more eagerly.

units.la: ] Arg. 2. Propitium habemus, & facilè exorabilem Deum, qui hanc vobis det gratiam, Patrem Domini nostri, & Patrem nostrum omnium servorum Iesu Christi, qui perseverantiam comprecantibus nobis, non recusabit vobis largiri: Sub hac spe pergendum igitur.
units.tr: ] Argument 2. We have a God who is merciful and easily entreated, who gives you this grace: the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, and the Father of all of us who serve Jesus Christ. When we ask for perseverance, he will not refuse to bestow it on you. Under this hope, you should therefore press on.

units.la: Vers. 15. Ex quo tota familia in Coelis & in terra nominatur.
units.tr: Verse 15. From whom the whole family in heaven and earth is named.

units.la: Arg. 3. Deus nolter, perseverantiæ largitor, Pater familias est Ecclesiæ catholicæ in Christo adoptatæ, qui Gentibus & Judæis fidelibus ex æquo favet, eodemque paterno affectu militantes vos in terra domesticos suos complectitur, quo triumphantes in Cœlo, voisque filios suos unà cum illis à se denominari vult, veltram infirmitatem & indignitatem in gremium suum admittere minimè erubescens. Animose ergo vobis in fide progrediendum est.
units.tr: Argument 3. Our God, the giver of perseverance, is the Father of the family of the Church catholic, adopted in Christ. He shows equal favour to believing Gentiles and Jews, and with the same fatherly affection he embraces you, who are fighting on earth, as his household. He wills that you, his sons, be named by him together with those who triumph in heaven, and he is not ashamed to admit your weakness and unworthiness into his bosom. You should therefore advance boldly in the faith.

units.la: Vers. 16. Ut det vobis, pro divite sua gloria, ut fortiter corroboremini per Spiritum suum in interiore homine_ ;
units.tr: Verse 16. That he would grant you, according to the riches of his glory, to be strengthened with might by his Spirit in the inner man;

units.la: ] Arg. 4. Dives & gloriosa est Dei misericordia, & quæ gaudet pro gloriosa magnitudine sua illustranda, proficiendi in fide gratiam petentibus abundè largiri. Confidenter igitur gratiam petite, & pergite in fide.
units.tr: Argument 4. The mercy of God is rich and glorious, and it delights in making its glorious greatness known. It abundantly grants grace to advance in the faith to those who ask for it. Ask for grace confidently, therefore, and press on in the faith.

units.la: ] Arg. 5. Etiamsi vos infirmi estis & impotentes ad superandum viæ difficultates, satis tamen est roboris vobis communicandi in Patre veltro, ad veltri confirmationem propensissimo, pro qua gratia non frustra Deum comprecamur: Ergo confidenter vobis pergendum est in fide.
units.tr: Argument 5. Even if you are weak and unable to overcome the difficulties of the way, you still have enough strength to be given to you in the Father, who is most inclined to strengthen you. We do not pray for this grace to God in vain. Therefore you should press on in the faith with confidence.

units.la: ] Apostolus interim insinuat ne quidem in interiori homine & intimis animæ regenitæ facultatibus, ullas esse liberi arbitrii vires, nec ullum esse boni operis meritum, vel efficaciam, quæ sufficiat ad perseverantiam, sed opus esse Spiritu Sancto, qui ipsis & velle & facere suppeditet, qui robur & potentiam ad perseverandum subinde subminis-tret, & ex gratia sua divite, prateritis ipsorum peccatis, constanter in illis opus suum foveat & promoveat.
units.tr: Meanwhile the Apostle implies that not even in the inner man and the innermost faculties of the regenerate soul is there any power of free will, nor any merit or efficacy of good works sufficient for perseverance. Rather, there is need of the Holy Spirit, who supplies them both to will and to do, who from time to time supplies strength and power to persevere, and who, from his rich grace, having overlooked their past sins, constantly fosters and advances his work in them.

units.la: Vers 17. Ut inhabitet Christus per fidem in cordibus vestris.
units.tr: Verse 17. That Christ may dwell in your hearts by faith.

units.la: Arg. 6. Etiamsi vos infirmi estis, & potens sit Diabolus contra vos dimicans; fortior tamen est Christus per fidem habitans in vobis, ad imaginem. ginem suam vos formans, confirmans, & gubernans ad voluntatis suæ obedientiam; qui ut constanter & plenius habitet in vobis, non deerunt vota nostra & preces ad Deum: Ergo confidenter vobis pergendum in fide.
units.tr: Argument 6. Even if you are weak, and the Devil fights against you with power, yet Christ dwelling in you by faith is stronger. He forms you after his own image, strengthens you, and guides you to obey his will. So that he may dwell in you more constantly and fully, our wishes and prayers to God will not be lacking. Therefore you should press on in the faith with confidence.

units.la: Verf. 18. Ut in charitate radicati & fundati, valeatis asse-qui cum omnibus sanctis, quæ sit illa latitudo & longitudo, & profunditas, & sublimitas:
units.tr: Verse 18. That you, being rooted and grounded in love, may be able to comprehend with all the saints what is the breadth and length and depth and height;

units.la: Arg. 7. Charitas Dei erga vos immutabilis, firmiter jam posita est tanquam viva radix & solidum fundamentum salutis vestræ perficiendæ, unde & stabilitatem & incrementum capiatis; de qua charitate persuasi constantissimè in fide perseverare poteritis, quæ persuasio ut vobis detur comprecor ego: Confidenter ergo pergite. Latitudo ] Arg. 8. Gratiâ Dei in Euangelio vobis offertur comprehendenda in immensa longitudine ab æterno in æternum pertingens: in latitudine sua ad omnia secula, & ordines hominum se extendens: in profunditate sua se demittens ad abyssum peccati & miseriæ, unde homines eruat: & denique in altitudine sua se ad supremam in Cœlo felicitatem erigens: imo verò oblata hæc gratia vos jam comprehendit, cuius cognitionem ampliorem vobis opto, ut sitis firmiores in fide, donec tandem in plena felicitate, cum reliquis omnibus fidelibus experimento plenè cognoscatis, & comprehendatis hanc Dei dilectionem: Pergite igitur & promovete indies in fidei obedientia.
units.tr: Argument 7. God's love towards you is unchanging. It has already been firmly planted as a living root and a solid foundation for bringing your salvation to completion. From this root you may receive both stability and growth. Persuaded of this love, you will be able to persevere most steadfastly in the faith, and I pray that this persuasion may be given to you. Press on confidently, then. Breadth] Argument 8. The grace of God is offered to you in the Gospel to be grasped in its immense length, reaching from eternity to eternity. In its breadth it extends to all ages and all orders of men. In its depth it descends to the abyss of sin and misery, from which it rescues men. And finally, in its height it lifts them up to supreme blessedness in heaven. Indeed, this grace, now offered, already embraces you. I wish you a fuller knowledge of it, so that you may be firmer in the faith, until at last, in full blessedness, you may know and comprehend this love of God by experience together with all the other believers. Press on, then, and advance daily in obedience to the faith.

units.la: Verf. 19. Et cognoscere charitatem illam Christi omni cognitione superiorem: ut impleamini ad omnem usque plenitudinem illam DEI.
units.tr: Verse 19. And to know that love of Christ which surpasses all knowledge, that you may be filled up to all the fullness of God.

units.la: Arg 9 Tanta est dilectio Dei erga vos in Christo, & dilectio Christi tanta est erga suos omnes, & erga vos, ut satis sciri nunquam poterit, quippe quæ superat omnium cum hominum, tum Angelorum intellectum, cujus ampliorem cognitionem vobis opto, ut firmi in fide perseveretis.
units.tr: Argument 9. The love of God towards you in Christ is so great, and the love of Christ towards all his people, and towards you, is so great, that it can never be sufficiently known. Indeed, it surpasses the understanding of all men and angels. I wish you a fuller knowledge of it, so that you may persevere firm in the faith.

units.la: Ut impleamini ] Arg. 10, Omnis plenitudo Dei, quæ vobis implendis, & ad salutem plenè perficiendis sufficit, in Euangelio vobis aperitur & communicatur, ut per fidem magis magisque uniti Deo in Christo, magis magisque participes fiatis sanctitatis, seu divinæ naturæ, & magis magisque beati reddamini per Christi pleniorem inhabitationem, donec tandem impleamini Deo, in futuro seculo, in quo Deus erit omnia in omnibus, ad summam vestram sanctitatem & felicitatem: Quod ut fiat Deum assiduè oro. Ergo cum fiducia vobis pergendum est.
units.tr: That you may be filled up] Argument 10. All the fullness of God, which suffices to fill you and to bring you to complete salvation, is opened and communicated to you in the Gospel. Through faith you are more and more united to God in Christ, more and more made partakers of holiness, or of the divine nature, and more and more blessed through the fuller indwelling of Christ, until at last you are filled up to God in the future age, when God will be all in all, to your highest holiness and blessedness. I constantly pray to God that this may come to pass. Therefore you must press on with confidence.

units.la: Ei verò qui infinita cum redundantia potest omnia facere supra ea quæ petimus, aut mente concipimus, pro vi illa agente in nobis,
units.tr: Now to him who is able to do exceedingly abundantly above all that we ask or think, according to the power that works in us,

units.la: Concludit precationem cum gratiarum actione, addito argumento 11. Deus & potens est ad dandum plura quam petimus, & ad dandum copiosè magis quam petere, vel desiderare possumus, & simul etiam benevolus est, ut velit quæ potest facere, Imo & jam potentiam & benevolentiam actu exeruit, in nobis convertendis, & etiamnum exerit in conservandis. Ergo animari decet vos ad constanter pergendum in fide.
units.tr: He concludes the prayer with thanksgiving, adding argument 11. God is both able to give more than we ask, and to give abundantly more than we can ask or desire. He is also benevolent, so that he wills what he is able to do. Indeed, he has already put forth his power and benevolence in converting us, and he still puts them forth in preserving us. Therefore it befits you to be encouraged to press on steadfastly in the faith.

units.la: Sit gloria in Ecclesia per Christum Iesum in omnes ætates sæculi sæculorum, Amen.
units.tr: To him be glory in the Church through Christ Jesus throughout all ages, world without end. Amen.

units.la: Arg 12. Laus perennis benevolentiæ & potentiæ efficacis Dei, ad salutem fidelium perficiendam per Christum, in Ecclesia perpetua futura est: Et huic veritati tenemini mecum Amen subscribere, Ergo in fide, ad finem Deum glorificantes pergite, & progressus facite. Ex his argumentis nonnulla probant etiam perseverantiam Sanctorum solidè fundatam, & certam esse.
units.tr: Argument 12. The perpetual praise of God's goodwill and his effective power, which will be exercised through Christ in the Church to bring the faithful to perfect salvation, will last forever. You are bound to subscribe with me to this truth, saying "Amen." Therefore press on and make progress in the faith, glorifying God to the end. Some of these arguments also prove that the perseverance of the saints is solidly founded and certain.

units.la: Caput Quartum.
units.tr: Chapter Four.

units.la: Secunda pars Epistolæ sequitur, In qua de Vitæ, Morumque sanctitate præcepta dat. Capitis duæ sunt partes; in priori hortatur omnes conjunctim, ad studium Pacis & Concordiæ Christianæ in Ecclesia, ad versum 17. In secunda præcepta dat de vita Singulorum seorsim sumptorum sanctè componenda, ad finem.
units.tr: The second part of the Epistle follows, in which he gives precepts on the holiness of life and conduct. The chapter has two parts. In the first he exhorts everyone together to pursue peace and Christian concord in the Church, up to verse 17. In the second he gives precepts on holily ordering the life of each individual taken separately, to the end.

units.la: Precor itaque vos, ego captivus in Domino, ut ambuletis ita ut dignum est vocatione qua vocati estis,
units.tr: I therefore beseech you, I a prisoner in the Lord, that you walk worthily of the calling with which you have been called,

units.la: Verf. 2. Cum omni modestia ac mansuetudine, cum animi lenitate, tolerantes alii alios per charitatem:
units.tr: Verse 2. With all lowliness and meekness, with gentleness of spirit, bearing with one another in love,

units.la: Verf. 3. Studentes servare unitatem Spiritus per vinculum pacis.
units.tr: Verse 3. Endeavouring to keep the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace.

units.la: Quod ad primam attinet, praemissa gravi obsecratione & hortatione generali ad sanctam conversationem, (quae communiter spectat omnia sequentia) nempe ut sancti essent, licut Deus qui vocavit eos sanctus est, verf. 1. Descendit ad specialem hortationem ad studium pacis & concordiae, propositis septem specialibus virtutibus quae ad unitatem Ecclesiae servandam necessario requiruntur, ut concordia in omnibus membris vigeat. Quarum prima est, Humilitas, cui opponitur Superbia: 2. Est mansuetudo, cui opponitur ferocia: 3. Est animi lenitas, cui opponitur iracundia: 4. Est tolerantia, cui opponitur vindicta: 5 Est charitas, unde reliquas virtutes & tolerantiam praecipue oriri vellet, cui opponitur odium proximi, & φιλαυτία, absque quibus virtutibus unitas Ecclesiae conservari non potest, verf. 2. 6. Virtus est Unitas Spiritus, in fide & in sententiis suis, de rebus ad religionem spectantibus: 7 Pax seu concordia externa: quibus praemiilis ipsa Unitas Ecclesiae & spiritualis & externa iuadetur, ut cum his virtutibus una & eadem opera retineatur, verf. 3.
units.tr: As to the first, having set out a weighty entreaty and a general exhortation to holy conduct (which commonly looks to all that follows), namely that they should be holy as God who called them is holy (verse 1), he descends to a particular exhortation to the pursuit of peace and concord. He sets out seven special virtues which are necessarily required for keeping the unity of the Church, so that concord may flourish in all the members. (1) The first is humility, opposed to pride; (2) meekness, opposed to ferocity; (3) gentleness of spirit, opposed to anger; (4) forbearance, opposed to revenge; (5) charity, from which he wishes the remaining virtues and forbearance chiefly to arise, opposed to hatred of neighbour and to self-love [φιλαυτία]. Without these virtues the unity of the Church cannot be preserved (verse 2). (6) The virtue is the unity of the Spirit, in faith and in its opinions on matters pertaining to religion; (7) peace, or external concord. By these premises both the spiritual and the external unity of the Church is urged, so that these virtues are kept together by one and the same work (verse 3).

units.la: Verf. 4 Unum est corpus & unus Spiritus, sicut & vocati estis in unam spem vocationis vestrae:
units.tr: Verse 4. There is one body and one Spirit, as you also were called in one hope of your calling:

units.la: Argumenta hortationis sunt 15. Argumentum primum, Ecclesia est unum corpus ex variis membris conflatum. Ergo unitati & concordiae Ecclesiasticae studendum.
units.tr: The arguments of the exhortation are fifteen. The first argument: the Church is one body made up of various members. Therefore concord and unity in the Church are to be pursued.

units.la: Arg. 2. Unus est Spiritus sanctus, quo totum corpus vivificatur & regitur. Ergo unitati studendum.
units.tr: Arg. 2. There is one Holy Spirit, by whom the whole body is quickened and governed. Therefore unity is to be pursued.

units.la: Arg 3 Omnes vocantur in unam spem vocationis, id est, ad eandem felicitatem aeternam. Ergo concordiae studendum.
units.tr: Arg. 3. All are called into one hope of their calling, that is, to the same eternal happiness. Therefore concord is to be pursued.

units.la: Verf. 5. Unus Dominus, una fides, unum baptisma.
units.tr: Verse 5. One Lord, one faith, one baptism.

units.la: Arg. 4. Unus est Dominus omnium Christus, cui omnes inservire tenemur, qui in membris suis non debet dividi. Ergo unitati studendum.
units.tr: Arg. 4. There is one Lord of all, Christ, whom we are all bound to serve, and who ought not to be divided in his members. Therefore unity is to be pursued.

units.la: Arg 5. Una est fides, seu doctrina quae credenda est, & ejusdem generis est salvificum illud donum gratiae, fides nempe justificans qua credimus. Ergo fidelium unitas servanda.
units.tr: Arg. 5. There is one faith, or doctrine, which is to be believed, and of the same kind is that saving gift of grace, namely justifying faith, by which we believe. Therefore the unity of the faithful is to be preserved.

units.la: Baptisma
units.tr: Baptism

units.la: Arg. 6. Unum est Baptisma, & quoad symbolum & quoad rem significatam, omnes in unius corporis mysticî societatem obsignans; Ergo baptizatis colenda est Concordia.
units.tr: Arg. 6. There is one Baptism, both as to the sign and as to the thing signified, sealing all into the fellowship of the one mystical body. Therefore concord is to be cultivated among the baptized.

units.la: Vers. 6. Unus Deus, & Pater omnium, qui est super omnia, & per omnia, & in omnibus vobis.
units.tr: Verse 6. One God and Father of all, who is above all, and through all, and in you all.

units.la: Arg. 7. Omnibus nobis est unus Deus, qui cultores unanimes exigit, & unus Pater omnium, qui Filios suos fraterno amore inter se conjungi vult, qui excellentiâ infinitè superat omnia, qui providentiâ suâ sustentat & regit omnia, & qui speciali modo ex gratia habitat in Electis omnibus. Ergo Concordiam inter vos colere debetis.
units.tr: Arg. 7. For all of us there is one God, who demands worshippers of one mind, and one Father of all, who wills that his sons be joined to one another in brotherly love; who by his excellence infinitely surpasses all things, who by his providence sustains and governs all things, and who in a special way dwells by grace in all the elect. Therefore you ought to cultivate concord among yourselves.

units.la: Vers. 7. Sed unicuique nostrum data est gratia pro mensura doni CHRISTI.
units.tr: Verse 7. But to each one of us grace has been given according to the measure of the gift of Christ.

units.la: Arg. 8. Utcunque varia sint dona, non tamen inde rumpi debet Unitas Ecclesiæ, sed foveri potiùs, quia unicuique data est gratia pro mensura doni quod Christus censuit dandum. Colenda igitur Concordia.
units.tr: Arg. 8. However varied the gifts may be, the unity of the Church ought not on that account to be broken, but rather fostered, because to each one grace has been given according to the measure of the gift which Christ thought fit to bestow. Therefore concord is to be cultivated.

units.la: Vers. 8. Quapropter dicit, quum ascendisset in sublime, captivam duxit captivitatem, & dedit dona hominibus.
units.tr: Verse 8. Wherefore he says, When he ascended on high, he led captivity captive, and gave gifts to men.

units.la: Hoc argumentum de donis, & variâ mensurâ donorum confirmat testimonio Psalmi 68. ubi vaticinium habetur primò de Christi ascensione, deinde de triumphatis ab eo hostibus, diabolo, morte, & peccato; & denique de distributione donorum in usum Ecclesiæ.
units.tr: He confirms this argument about gifts and the varied measure of gifts by the testimony of Psalm 68, where a prophecy is found: first of Christ's ascension, then of the enemies conquered by him, the devil, death, and sin, and finally of the distribution of gifts for the use of the Church.

units.la: Vers. 9. Caterum illud ascendit, quid est, nisi quòd etiam descenderat prius in inferiores partes terræ?
units.tr: Verse 9. Now that he ascended, what is it but that he also first descended into the lower parts of the earth?

units.la: Ex hoc vaticinio de ascensione Christi, primò probat Apostolus Christi humiliationem præcedentem præsupponi necessariò, id est, incarnationem, & demissionem sui ad carnis infirmitates communes, ad passionem tum animæ tum corporis, & ad sepulturam: Unde ad unitatem Ecclesiæ servandam suppeditatur Argumentum nonum.
units.tr: From this prophecy about Christ's ascension, the Apostle first proves that Christ's prior humiliation must necessarily be presupposed, that is, the incarnation, and his lowering himself to the common weaknesses of the flesh, to the passion of both soul and body, and to burial. Hence the ninth argument is supplied for keeping the unity of the Church.

units.la: Ad Ecclesiam in unum colligendam, & Deo uniendam Christus descendit in inferiores partes terræ, (hac ipsa phrasi David suam describit conceptionem in utero, Psal. 139.18) & in eundem finem rursus ascendit. Ergo unitas Ecclesiæ colenda.
units.tr: Christ descended into the lower parts of the earth to gather the Church into one and unite it to God (David describes his conception in the womb by this very phrase, Psal. 139.18), and to the same end he ascended again. Therefore the unity of the Church is to be cultivated.

units.la: Vers. 10. Qui descendit, ipse est qui etiam ascendit longe supra omnes cœlos, ut impleret omnia. Ex eodem vaticinio colligit Christum Deum incarnandum descendentem, ut carnem assumeret, non factum esse alium, seu aliam personam, quando ascendit Deus incarnatus; neque humanam naturam assumptam, aliquid ad personam Filii Dei constituendam, vel perficiendam addidisse, sed in unitatem personæ assumptam fuisse, & idcirco Christum & descendentem & ascendentem eundem esse, sicut qui vestem induit, idem est qui prius erat, non vestitus.
units.tr: Verse 10. He who descended is the same who also ascended far above all the heavens, that he might fill all things. From the same prophecy he gathers that Christ God, who descended to be incarnate in order to assume flesh, was not made another, or another person, when God incarnate ascended; nor did the assumed human nature add anything to constitute or perfect the person of the Son of God, but was assumed into the unity of the person. Therefore Christ who descended and Christ who ascended are the same, just as he who puts on a garment is the same person who was before, not clothed.

units.la: Finem porro ascensionis indicans, addit Arg. 10. Christus in Cœlum ascendit, ut compleret omnia, quæ ei complenda erant, scilicet ad Ecclesiam colligendam & servandam, eique quæcunque necessaria sunt, communicandum. Ergo unitati Ecclesiæ impensè studendum.
units.tr: Indicating further the end of the ascension, he adds the tenth argument: Christ ascended into heaven that he might fulfil all things which were to be fulfilled by him, namely to gather and preserve the Church and to communicate to it whatever is necessary. Therefore the unity of the Church is to be eagerly pursued.

units.la: Vers. 11. Dedit igitur ipse alios quidem Apostolos: alios verò Prophetas: alios autem, Evangelistas: alios autem Pastores & doctores.
units.tr: Verse 11. And he himself gave some indeed to be Apostles; and some Prophets; and some Evangelists; and some Pastors and Teachers.

units.la: Quomodo compleverit omnia, ostendit ex parte, quantum ad institutum sufficit, enumerando varios ordines Ecclesiastici Ministerii, partim temporarios & extraordinarios, ut Apostolos, Prophetas, Evangelistas, ad fundamenta jacienda omnium Ecclesiarum, partim ordinarios & perpetuos, ut Pastores & Doctores, ad Ecclesiam perpetuandam institutos.
units.tr: How he fulfilled all things he shows in part, as far as the purpose suffices, by enumerating the various orders of the ecclesiastical ministry: partly temporary and extraordinary, such as Apostles, Prophets and Evangelists, for laying the foundations of all Churches; partly ordinary and perpetual, such as Pastors and Teachers, instituted to perpetuate the Church.

units.la: Vers. 12. Ad coaugmentationem sanctorum, ad opus Ministerii, ad ædificationem, inquam corporis Christi.
units.tr: Verse 12. For the perfecting of the saints, for the work of the ministry, for the edifying, I say, of the body of Christ.

units.la: Arg. 11. A fine & usu in quem Christus dedit hæc officia & dona: 1. Ut instaurentur Sancti, tanquam luxata membra in proprium locum reducta: 2. Ut Ministri otio & dominationi renunciantes, opus Ministerii facerent, quo singuli electi, ut oves palantes ad Christum Pastorem revocentur, & in eo maneant: 3. Ut exædificetur totum corpus Ecclesiæ, & singuli proficiant in fide & sanctitate, ad incrementum corporis totius, unde Arg. Christus functiones in Ecclesia instituit, ut hominum Ministerio omnes Sancti sic coalescant, ut unum Christi corpus mysticum constituant: Ergo unitati studendum est.
units.tr: Arg. 11. From the end and use for which Christ gave these offices and gifts: (1) that the saints might be restored, like dislocated limbs brought back into their proper place; (2) that ministers, renouncing idleness and domination, might do the work of the ministry, by which each of the elect, like wandering sheep, is recalled to Christ the Shepherd and remains in him; (3) that the whole body of the Church might be built up, and each might make progress in faith and holiness, for the increase of the whole body. Hence the argument: Christ instituted the functions in the Church so that by the ministry of men all the saints might so cohere as to constitute one mystical body of Christ. Therefore unity is to be pursued.

units.la: Vers. 13. Donec evadamus omnes in unitatem Fidei, & agnitionis Filii Dei, in virum perfectum, ad mensuram statura adulti CHRISTI.
units.tr: Verse 13. Until we all attain to the unity of the faith and of the knowledge of the Son of God, to a perfect man, to the measure of the stature of the fulness of Christ.

units.la: Arg. 12. A termino durationis Ministerii. Durabit Ministerium, donec nos omnes electi perveniamus in unitatem fidei & cognitionis Christi, id est, donec non solum uniamur Christo per fidem, & cognitionem quae est ex fide, sed etiam donec omnes nos redempti, seu electi quotquot vivimus vel victuri sumus perveniamus (inquam) omnes, alii polt alios, ad perfectam cognitionem in visione immediata, seu ad perfectam regenerationem, & incorporationem in Christo, quando jam omnes electi uniti & perfecti constituemus unum Christum mysticum, qui omnibus numeris sit absolutus, & plenam suam staturam aequatus, quod fiet in resurrectione: Ergo ut hic finis promoveatur unitati studendum est.
units.tr: Arg. 12. From the term of the duration of the ministry. The ministry will endure until we all, the elect, arrive at the unity of faith and knowledge of Christ; that is, until we are not only united to Christ through faith and the knowledge which comes from faith, but until all of us redeemed, or elect, as many as live or are to live, arrive (I say) all, one after another, at perfect knowledge in immediate vision, or at perfect regeneration and incorporation in Christ, when all the elect, now united and perfected, will constitute one mystical Christ, who will be complete in every respect and equal to his full stature, which will happen in the resurrection. Therefore, in order that this end may be advanced, unity is to be pursued.

units.la: Verf. 14. Ut ne simus amplius pueri, qui fluctuemus & circumferamur quovis vento doctrinae in hominum alea, veteratoria ad insidiose fallendum versutias:
units.tr: Verse 14. That we may no longer be children, tossed about and carried hither and thither by every wind of doctrine, by the dice-game of men, by the cunning tricks of the cheat to deceive by stealth:

units.la: Arg. 13. Ab alio fine instituti Ministerii. Instituit Christus Ministerium, ne maneamus perpetuo pueri, ignari eorum quae scire debemus; ne fluctuemus agitati vento contrariarum doctrinarum, ne separemur a Christo, & ejus Ecclesia ex instabilitate in fide, ne decipiamur hominum corruptorum calliditate, astutia, & insidiosa seductione: Ergo ut hic finis promoveatur quantum per nos fieri potest, unitati Ecclesiae studendum est.
units.tr: Argument 13. From another end of the appointed Ministry.
