Christ instituted the Ministry so that we should not remain children forever, ignorant of those things which we ought to know; so that we should not be tossed about by the wind of contrary doctrines, so that we should not be separated from Christ and his Church through instability in the faith, so that we should not be deceived by the craftiness, cunning and insidious seduction of corrupt men. Therefore, so that this end may be advanced as far as lies in us, we must strive for the unity of the Church.

units.la: Verf. 15. Sed veritatem sectantes cum charitate, prorsus adolescamus in eum per omnia, qui est caput nempe Christus:
units.tr: Verse 15. But, following the truth in love, let us grow up in every way into him who is the head, namely Christ:

units.la: Arg. 14. A tertio fine instituti Ministerii. Instituit Christus Ministerium in Ecclesia, non tantum ut vitemus seductionem, sed etiam ut veritatem doctrinae Coelestis cum charitate sectemur, & sic per veritatem & charitatem adolescamus in virtutibus omnibus in unum Christum mysticum: Ergo unitati Ecclesiae, & charitati, in hunc finem studendum est, ut Christus caput nostrum, inter nos emineat, & nos qui non nisi in ipso crescere poterimus, in eo fortes & proceri evadamus.
units.tr: Argument 14. From the third end of the appointed Ministry. Christ instituted the Ministry in the Church not only that we may avoid seduction, but also that we may pursue the truth of heavenly doctrine in love, and thus, through truth and love, grow up in all virtues into the one mystical Christ. Therefore we must strive for the unity of the Church and for love to this end, so that Christ our head may stand out among us, and we, who can grow only in him, may become strong and tall in him.

units.la: Verf. 16 Ex quo totum corpus congruenter coagmentatum, & compactum per omnes suppeditatas commissuras, ex vi intus agente pro mensura uniuscujusque membri, incrementum capit corpori convenieas, ad sui ipsius extructionem per charitatem.
units.tr: Verse 16. From whom the whole body, fitly joined together and compacted by every joint that supplies, working by the power within according to the measure of each single member, makes the body grow to build itself up in love.

units.la: Arg. 15. A descriptione CHRISTI mystici, seu CHRISTI & Ecclesiæ, in qua descriptione, per similitudinem capitis & corporis naturalis, illustrat quod dixit de incremento faciendo, in veritatis cognitione & charitate, ad CHRISTI gloriam, & Ecclesiæ bonum augendum: in qua descriptione ostendit: 1. Quod ex CHRISTO ut capite, & fonte, dependeat totum corpus Ecclesiæ, & ab eo omne corporis sui alimentum, id est, omnis veritas salutifera, unà cum vitali CHRISTI SPIRITU in omnia vera membra dimanet, ita ut nemo quicquam sciat, nisi instituatur à CHRISTO: 2. Quod pro diversitate donorum Spiritus, & functionum, & conditionis uniuscujusque membri Ecclesiæ Catholicæ, corpus congruenter fit coagmentatum, seu ordine pulcherrimo, & maximè concinno compositum, & vinculo arctissimo Spiritus, fidei & charitatis alligatum CHRISTO, & in se compactum, accedentibus variis relationibus, partim inter CHRISTUM & nos (quales sunt Capitis & membrorum, sponsi, Patroni, sponsoris, &c.) Partim inter nos mutuò (quales sunt relationes fratrum & sororum, cohæredum, Pastorum & gregis, Parentum & liberorum, &c.) quibus arctiùs cum CHRISTO & inter nos indies vinciri poterimus: 3. Quod sint variæ junctura subministrationis alimenti, per quas, tanquam per canales, à CHRISTO derivatur veritatis salutiferæ cognitio, fides, sensus & efficacia, in variis functionibus & officiis in Ecclesia: in quibus sunt Apostolatus, Pastoratus, Doctoratus, Presbyteratus, &c. 4. Quod mera administratio seu Ministerium sit in membris: nam ipsa dispensatio benedictionis, efficaciæ, & virtutis pendet immediatè à solo CHRISTO: 5. Quod inter membra distributio sit necessaria, quæ propter finitam cujusque mensuram opus habent communicatione mutua, ut mutuò se ædificent: 6. Quod incrementum fiat per efficacem ejusdem Capitis CHRISTI operationem in Ministerio, & mutua membrorum inter se communicatione: 7. Quod pro mensura ac ratione cujusque membri, unumquodque membrum augescat, & proficiat in vita DEI, in pietate, in vera Religione, sicut visum est DOMINO unicuique distribuere: 8. Quod augmentum illud demum utile fit, & ex CHRISTI virtute profectum, quod universo corpori aliquid addit, & Ecclesiæ in communi aliquid affert, non verò illud incrementum, quod videtur accedere paucis cum reliquorum membrorum detrimento, aut paucis aliquot Ecclesiis cum reliquarum dispendio: 9. Denique, Quod per charitatem membrorum
units.tr: Argument 15. From the description of the mystical CHRIST, or of CHRIST and the Church; in which description, by the likeness of the head and the natural body, he illustrates what he said about making progress in the knowledge of truth and in love, for the glory of CHRIST and the increase of the good of the Church. In this description he shows: 1. That the whole body of the Church depends on CHRIST as head and fountain, and from him every nourishment of his body, that is, every saving truth, together with the living SPIRIT of CHRIST, flows into all the true members, so that no one knows anything unless he is taught by CHRIST. 2. That, according to the diversity of the gifts of the Spirit, and of the functions and condition of each member of the Catholic Church, the body is fitly joined together, or composed in a most beautiful and most harmonious order, and bound to CHRIST and compacted within itself by the closest bond of the Spirit, of faith and of love, with various relations added, partly between CHRIST and us (such as those of head and members, bridegroom, patron, surety, etc.), partly between ourselves mutually (such as the relations of brothers and sisters, co-heirs, pastors and flock, parents and children, etc.), by which we can be bound ever more closely to CHRIST and to one another from day to day. 3. That there are various joints of supply, through which, as through channels, the knowledge, faith, sense and efficacy of saving truth are derived from CHRIST in the various functions and offices in the Church; among which are the apostolate, the pastorate, the teachership, the eldership, etc. 4. That the bare administration, or Ministry, lies in the members; for the very dispensing of blessing, efficacy and power depends immediately on CHRIST alone. 5. That a distribution among the members is necessary, since, because of each one's finite measure, they need mutual communication, so that they may build one another up. 6. That the increase is made through the effective working of the same Head, CHRIST, in the Ministry, and through the mutual communication of the members among themselves. 7. That each member grows and advances, according to the measure and manner of each, in the life of God, in piety, in true Religion, as it has seemed good to the LORD to distribute to each. 8. That this increase is at last useful, and proceeds from the power of CHRIST, when it adds something to the whole body and brings something to the Church in common; not that increase which seems to accrue to a few to the detriment of the remaining members, or to a few churches to the loss of the rest. 9. Finally, that through the love of the members toward one another, this communication of knowledge and Christian doctrine and the building up of the body is made, and cannot be made without love.

units.la: Arg. 15. marg. (not separately printed; no marginal notes) membrorum inter se, hæc communicatio cognitionis & Doctrinæ Christianæ, & exædificatio corporis fiat, & sine charitate fieri non possit. Hinc arg. Sicut in corpore naturali & organico se res habet: Sic in Ecclesia, CHRISTUS qui Caput est Ecclesiæ, non eadem, sed alia atque alia charismata membris suis infundit, singulis distribuens, pro ut locus cujusque quem in corpore habet, postulat, ut hac ratione corpus totum crescat, dum singula membra suo quæque loco, dona sua in communem utilitatem conferunt, quod non nisi per concordiam fieri potest: Ergo concordiæ & unitati Ecclesiæ in hunc finem studiosè incumbendum est.
units.tr: Argument 15, margin (not separately printed; no marginal notes). Hence the argument: As it stands in the natural and organic body, so it is in the Church: CHRIST, who is the Head of the Church, pours into his members not the same but different and various gifts, distributing to each as the place each holds in the body requires, so that in this way the whole body grows, while each member, in its own place, contributes its own gifts to the common benefit, which can be done only through concord. Therefore we must earnestly labour for concord and unity in the Church to this end.

units.la: Secunda Pars,
units.tr: Second Part,

units.la: Verf. 17. Hoc itaque dico, & obtestor per Dominum, ne amplius versemini sicut reliquæ Gentes versantur in vanitate mentis suæ:
units.tr: Verse 17. Therefore I say this, and I testify before the Lord, that you no longer walk as the other Gentiles walk, in the vanity of their mind.

units.la: Verf. 18. Cogitationem habentes obscuratam, & abalienatam à vita DEI propter ignorantiam quæ est in ipsis, ex obduratione cordis eorum.
units.tr: Verse 18. Having their understanding darkened, and alienated from the life of God, because of the ignorance that is in them, through the hardening of their heart.

units.la: Verf. 19. Qui postea quam dedolucrunt, semetipsos dediderunt protervia, ad certatim patrandam impuritatem omnem.
units.tr: Verse 19. Who, having become past feeling, have given themselves over to wantonness, to work every uncleanness with greediness.

units.la: Secunda pars Capitis, in qua præcepta dat septem de vita singulorum seorsim sumptorum sanctè componenda.
units.tr: The second part of the chapter, in which he gives seven precepts for holily ordering the life of each individual taken separately.

units.la: Primum præceptum, Ne amplius ambulent sicut reliquæ Gentes, sed sicut decet eos qui à statu peccati, ad CHRISTUM efficaciter vocati sunt. Rationes præcepti seu hortationis sunt quatuor:
units.tr: The first precept: that they no longer walk as the other Gentiles, but as becomes those who have been effectually called from the state of sin to Christ. The reasons for the precept or exhortation are four:

units.la: Dico ] Ratio prima, Ego Apostolus ex autoritate DEI mihi tributa, obtestor vos per Dominum, cui ratio reddenda est vobis, si hanc meam obtestationem contempseritis: Obedite igitur.
units.tr: I say ] The first reason: I, the Apostle, by the authority of God given to me, testify to you before the Lord, to whom an account must be rendered by you if you despise this my testimony. Obey therefore.

units.la: Vanitate ] Ratio 2. A misera conditione Gentium, atque adeo omnium non renatorum; quæ conditio his septem membris exprimitur. Primum, quod mens vana illis fuerit pro viæ duce, quæ nihil certi in rebus divinis dictat, & in nullum utilem finem humanas actiones dirigit, verf. 17.
units.tr: Vanity ] The second reason: from the wretched condition of the Gentiles, and indeed of all the unregenerate, which condition is expressed in seven members. The first is that a vain mind has been their guide on the way, one which dictates nothing certain in divine things and directs human actions to no useful end, verse 17.

units.la: Tenebris ] Membrum 2. Quod ratiocinatio non renatorum Gentilium, in rebus quæ ad DEUM & felicitatem spectant, obtenebrata & excæcata sit: 3. Quod alienati sint à vita Dei spirituali, & ab omni cum Deo communione: 4. Quod nullam salutarem Dei cognitionem habeant, sed plane ignorent Deum ad salutem, seu pro ut in Ecclesia patefactus est in Christo: 5. Quod habeant cor induratum induratione naturali, voluntaria, & judiciali: nam cum se sponte in peccato obfirmarint, etiam justo Dei judicio porro obfirmati sunt in peccato, & mentis caecitate, verf 18.
units.tr: Darkness ] Member 2: that the reasoning of unregenerate Gentiles, in matters that concern God and happiness, is darkened and blinded. 3: that they are alienated from the spiritual life of God, and from all communion with God. 4: that they have no saving knowledge of God, but are plainly ignorant of God unto salvation, or as he has been revealed in the Church in Christ. 5: that they have a hardened heart, hardened naturally, voluntarily and judicially; for since they had of their own accord fixed themselves in sin, by the just judgment of God they were further confirmed in sin and in blindness of mind, verse 18.

units.la: Dedoluerunt ] 6. Quod stupore & indolentia sopiti, non amplius metuant peccare, nec sentiant naturales conscientiae morsus: 7. Quod effraeni libidine peccandi abripiantur Gentes, non ad concupiscendum tantum, sed etiam ad perpetrandum omnem immunditiem cum aviditate, & ad pergendum in suis voluptatibus, cum inexplebili desiderio & studio eis satisfaciendi, verf. 19. Hinc ratio 2. Miserrima est reliquorum Gentilium conditio. Ne ambuletis igitur sicut illi. Verf. 20. Vos autem non ita didicistis Christum:
units.tr: They became past feeling ] 6: that, lulled by stupor and insensibility, they no longer fear to sin, nor feel the natural stings of conscience. 7: that the Gentiles are carried away by unbridled lust for sinning, not only to desire but also to commit every uncleanness with greediness, and to persist in their pleasures with insatiable desire and zeal to satisfy them, verse 19. Hence the second reason: the condition of the rest of the Gentiles is most wretched; do not walk therefore as they do. Verse 20: But you have not so learned Christ:

units.la: Verf. 21. Si modo eum audistis, & per eum edocti fuistis, sicut est veritas in Iesu:
units.tr: Verse 21: If indeed you have heard him, and have been taught by him, as truth is in Jesus:

units.la: Ratio 3. Cognitio Christi, seu doctrina fidei in Christum, in qua instituti estis, & quam didicistis, aliam vitæ rationem quam sequuntur Gentes, exigit à vobis. Ne igitur Gentes imitemini, verf. 20.
units.tr: Reason 3: The knowledge of Christ, or the doctrine of faith in Christ, in which you have been instructed, and which you have learned, requires of you a different manner of life from that which the Gentiles follow. Therefore do not imitate the Gentiles, verse 20.

units.la: Simodo ] Limitat superiorem rationem, & restringit ad verè renatos, qui sincerè & verè audiverunt Christum, & efficaciter edocti sunt per ipsius Spiritum, quæ sit illa in Christo vera sanctitas, quæ sit præscripta illa ab eo recta vivendi ratio, quanta sit virtus & vis spiritualis in illo, ad efficiendum ut ipsius genuini discipuli vivant, secundum ipsius instituta, apud tales saltem valebit (inquit) superior ratio, verf. 21.
units.tr: If indeed ] This limits the previous reason and restricts it to those who are truly regenerate, who have sincerely and truly heard Christ and have been effectually taught by his Spirit what that true holiness in Christ is, what that right rule of living prescribed by him is, and how great the virtue and spiritual power in him is for bringing it about that his genuine disciples live according to his institutions. The higher reason, he says, will hold good at least among such, verse 21.

units.la: Verf. 22. Nempe deponere quod ad pristinam conversationem attinet, veterem illum hominem qui deceptricibus cupiditatibus corrumpitur:
units.tr: Verse 22: Namely, to put off, as concerns your former conduct, the old man, who is corrupted by deceitful lusts:

units.la: Verf. 23. Renovari verò Spiritu mentis vestræ,
units.tr: Verse 23: And to be renewed in the spirit of your mind,

units.la: Verf. 24 Et induere novum illum hominem, qui secundum Deum conditus est ad justitiam & sanctimoniam veram.
units.tr: Verse 24: And to put on the new man, who is created according to God in true righteousness and holiness.

units.la: Ratio 4. Christi doctrina expressè requirit à fidelibus, ut hæc tria præstentur: Primùm, ut resipiscentiam sectantes, magis magisque hominem veterem, seu corruptam naturam, quæ in priltina ipsorum conversatione satione se prodebat, exuant, & deponant, quæ corrupta natura, seu vetus homo deterior & corruptior indies fit, per seductrices cupiditates, atque ita magis magisque hominem corrumpit & perdit, verf. 22.
units.tr: Reason 4: The doctrine of Christ expressly requires of the faithful that three things be performed. First, that, pursuing repentance, they put off more and more the old man, or corrupt nature, which showed itself in their former conduct; this corrupt nature, or old man, becomes worse and more corrupt daily through deceitful lusts, and thus more and more corrupts and destroys the man, verse 22.

units.la: Alterum est, Ut renoventur magis magisque in Spiritu mentis suæ, id est, ut fideles dent operam, per verbum & Spiritum Dei, magis magisque spiritualem reddere suum ipsorum intellectum, qui natura sua sapientiæ Divinæ adversatur, & contra eam disputat.
units.tr: The second is that they be renewed more and more in the spirit of their mind; that is, that the faithful take pains, through the word and the Spirit of God, to make their own understanding more and more spiritual, which by its nature opposes divine wisdom and argues against it.

units.la: Tertium est, Ut fideles induant novum hominem, seu studeant exhibere, & reipsa ostendere in se actiones, & qualitates novæ creaturæ ad imaginem Dei renovatæ, atque ita obedientiam legi divinæ sedulò præstare in iis quæ spectant Deum & proximum. Hinc Arg. Christiana doctrina exigit à vobis ut exuentes veteris hominis mores, renovatâ mente studeatis vos novas esse creaturas, in justitiæ & sanctimoniæ exercitiis facto demonstrare: Ergo non ambulandum ut reliquæ Gentes.
units.tr: The third is that the faithful put on the new man, or strive to show forth, and in fact display in themselves, the actions and qualities of the new creature renewed after the image of God, and thus diligently render obedience to the divine law in those things which concern God and neighbour. Hence the argument: Christian doctrine requires of you that, putting off the manners of the old man, you strive with renewed mind to show by deeds that you are new creatures in the exercises of righteousness and holiness. Therefore one must not walk as the other Gentiles do.

units.la: Verf. 25. Quapropter depositio mendacio, loquimini veritatem quisque proximo suo: nam sumus alii aliorum membra.
units.tr: Verse 25: Therefore, putting away lying, let each one speak the truth with his neighbour; for we are members one of another.

units.la: Præceptum 2. In quo speciatim consuetudinem mentiendi deponere, & veritatem loqui jubet: Hortationis seu præcepti rationem affert unam. Quia nempe sumus alii aliorum quasi membra; sicut igitur in corpore naturali, si membra se invicem fraudarent, monstri simile esset: sic in Ecclesia haberi debet, cum ex iis qui fidem profitentur, alius alium decipit.
units.tr: Precept 2: In which he specifically bids them put off the habit of lying and speak the truth. He gives one reason for the exhortation or precept: namely, that we are, as it were, members one of another. Just as in the natural body, if the members defrauded one another, it would be like a monster, so in the Church it ought to be held that, when among those who profess the faith one deceives another, the same monstrosity results.

units.la: Verf. 26. Irascimini, & ne peccate: sol ne occidat super iracundiam vestram.
units.tr: Verse 26: Be angry, and sin not; let not the sun go down upon your wrath.

units.la: Verf. 27. Neque date locum Diabolo.
units.tr: Verse 27: Neither give place to the devil.

units.la: Præceptum 3. De moderandâ ira, ne vel injusta sit, vel diuturnior. Ne peccetis irascendo, id est, ne vel temerè vel nimium irascamini, ne foveatis iram in animis vestris, nec eam vobiscum dormire sinatis, sed etiam in justâ irâ modum servetis, & si injustè irasci contigerit, quod usu plerunque evenit, ut iram quam ociissimè deponatis suadeo.
units.tr: Precept 3: On moderating anger, lest it be either unjust or lasting. Do not sin by being angry, that is, do not be angry either rashly or excessively; do not nurse anger in your minds, nor allow it to sleep with you. But also keep measure in just anger; and if it happens to be kindled unjustly, which by usage commonly occurs, I advise that you lay the anger down as quickly as possible.

units.la: Nec diabolo Præcepti ratio est ab incommodo. Si ira foveatur, diabolo locus dabitur, ut vos ad amplius peccandum solicitet, & instiget, cui locus dari minimè debet, neque in hoc, neque in ullo alio peccato fovendo.
units.tr: Nor give place to the devil ] The reason for the precept is drawn from the harm it does. If anger is nursed, room will be given to the devil, so that he may solicit and incite you to sin further. To him room ought by no means to be given, neither by nursing this sin nor any other.

units.la: Verf. 28. Qui furabatur, non amplius furetur: sed potius laboret, operando manibus, quod bonum sit, ut possit impertiri cui opus fuerit. Præceptum 4. De consuetudine furandi, & fraudulenter agendi deponenda. Ratio præcepti est, Quia ad laborem manuarium vos ipsos demittere, quò & vestris, & aliorum necessitatibus succurratis, quam surari longè satius est.
units.tr: Verse 28: Let him who stole steal no more; but rather let him labour, working with his hands at what is good, so that he may have something to share with him who has need. Precept 4: On putting off the habit of stealing and acting fraudulently. The reason for the precept is that you should lower yourselves to manual labour, by which you may help both your own and others' needs, which is far better than stealing.

units.la: Vers. 29. Nullus sermo corruptus ex ore vestro egreditor, sed siquis est commodus ad ædificationis usum, ut gratiam auditoribus adferat.
units.tr: Verse 29: Let no corrupt speech proceed out of your mouth, but only what is good for building up, so that it may impart grace to the hearers.

units.la: Vers. 30. Et ne contristetis Spiritum illum sanctum Dei, per quem obsignati estis in diem redemptionis.
units.tr: Verse 30: And grieve not the holy Spirit of God, by whom you have been sealed for the day of redemption.

units.la: Præceptum 5. Ad cavendum vitium linguæ. Ne loquamini turpia noxia vel inutilia, quæ neque ad gloriam Dei, neque ad ullam vestram, vel aliorum utilitatem faciant; & contra, ea quæ honesta sunt, & quæ ad ædificationem proximi faciunt, loquimini.
units.tr: Precept 5: For avoiding the vice of the tongue. Do not speak filthy, harmful or useless things, which serve neither God's glory nor your own or others' benefit; and on the contrary, speak what is honest and what builds up one's neighbour.

units.la: Et ne contristetis ] Ratio præcepti additur, Ne Spiritus Sanctus, qui in vobis habitat, putridis & obscænis sermonibus contristetur. Hanc rationem urget, & graviorem reddit, ex eo, quod obsignati fuerint in diem redemptionis, à Spiritu Sancto, & ipsius præsentia quasi notati, & insigniti, tanquam Dei peculium, ut in die redemptionis consummatæ, qui est dies resurrectionis, introducantur in Dei domicilium, cui Spiritui gratiam meliorem referre debebant, quam spurcitie suâ cum offendere.
units.tr: And grieve not ] The reason for the precept is added: lest the Holy Spirit, who dwells in you, be grieved by foul and obscene talk. He presses this reason and makes it weightier by the fact that they have been sealed by the Holy Spirit for the day of redemption, and marked and signed by his presence as God's own possession, so that on the day of the consummated redemption, which is the day of resurrection, they may be brought into God's dwelling. They ought to render better thanks to that Spirit than to offend him with their filthiness.

units.la: Vers. 31. Omnis amaritudo, & excandescentia, & ira, & clamor, & maledicentia, tollatur, ex vobis, cum omni malitia.
units.tr: Verse 31. "Let all bitterness, and wrath, and anger, and clamour, and evil speaking, be put away from you, with all malice."

units.la: Præceptum 6. Quo vetantur amaritudo, & animi rancor, & iracundia, & clamor, & maledicentia, & omnis generis acerbitas, & malitia, seu perversitas adversus proximum.
units.tr: Precept 6. By which bitterness, and rancour of mind, and irascibility, and clamour, and evil speaking, and every kind of harshness and malice, or perversity, against one's neighbour, are forbidden.

units.la: Vers. 32. Sed estote alii in alios benigni misericordes, condonantes vobis mutuò offensas, sicut & Deus in CHRSTO condonavit vobis.
units.tr: Verse 32. "But be ye kind one to another, tender-hearted, forgiving one another, even as God for Christ's sake hath forgiven you."

units.la: Præceptum 7. Quo in contrarium præcipitur, mutua misericordia & benignitas, & offensarum condonatio mutua. Cui additur ratio præcepti gravissima, Quia Deus in Christo condonavit vobis peccata vestra, & gratiam fecit vobis multiplicem in Christo. Ergo alii in alios benigni & misericordes sitis.
units.tr: Precept 7. By which the contrary is commanded: mutual mercy and kindness, and the mutual forgiveness of offences. To this is added the most weighty reason for the precept: because God in Christ has forgiven you your sins, and has bestowed upon you manifold grace in Christ. Therefore be ye kind and merciful one to another.

units.la: Caput Quintum.
units.tr: Chapter 5.

units.la: Apitis partes sunt duæ, prior continet novem generalia præcepta de sanctimonia colenda, quæ communiter omnes fideles attingunt, ad versum 21. Altera de officiis œconomicis præcepta specialiora continet quatuor, ad finem.
units.tr: The chapter has two parts. The first contains nine general precepts about cultivating holiness, which apply to all the faithful in common, up to verse 21. The second contains four more specific precepts about domestic duties, to the end.

units.la: Verf. 1, EStote igitur imitatores Dei, ut Filii dilecti.
units.tr: Verse 1: Be therefore imitators of God, as dear children.

units.la: Præceptum primum, De sanctitate in genere, Ut studeant Deum in sanctitate imitari: Ratio præcepti est, Quia estis Filii Dei dilecti. Idcirco Deum Patrem vestrum, qui sanctus est, imitari debetis.
units.tr: Precept 1: Concerning holiness in general, that they should strive to imitate God in holiness. The reason for the precept is that you are beloved children of God. Therefore you ought to imitate God your Father, who is holy.

units.la: Verf. 2. Et versamini cum charitate, sicut & Christus dilexit nos, & tradidit semetipsum pro nobis oblationem ac victimam Deo, in odorem bonę fragrantia. Præceptum 2. Ut ambulent in charitate mutua : Ratio præcepti additur, Quia CHRISTUS adeò dilexit nos, ut se in sacrificium obtulerit pro nobis, ut nobis peccata à DEO remitterentur; Hujus sacrificii efficacitas declaratur ex eo, quod DEO placuerit, eumque placaverit erga nos: faciunt etiam hæc duo præcepta ad confirmandam hortationem, quæ præcessit in fine superioris capitis, de condonandis mutuis offensis.
units.tr: Verse 2: And walk in love, as Christ also loved us, and gave himself up for us as an offering and a sacrifice to God, for a sweet-smelling savour. Precept 2: that they walk in mutual love. The reason for the precept is added: Christ loved us so much that he offered himself as a sacrifice for us, so that our sins might be remitted by God. The efficacy of this sacrifice is shown by the fact that it pleased God and appeased him toward us. These two precepts also serve to confirm the exhortation at the end of the previous chapter, to forgive one another's offences.

units.la: Verf. 3. Scortatio verò & omnis impuritas aut avaritia, ne nominator quidem inter vos, sicut decet sanctos:
units.tr: Verse 3: But fornication, and all uncleanness, or covetousness, let it not even be named among you, as becomes saints.

units.la: Præceptum 3. De cavenda scortatione, & omnis generis immunditie & avaritia, ut sine detestatione ne vel nominentur inter eos, nedum perpetrentur: Ratio præcepti est, Quia sic decet Sanctos se gerere, qui ad DEI sanctissimi servitium consecrantur.
units.tr: Precept 3: Concerning avoiding fornication and every kind of uncleanness and covetousness, so that they are not even named among them without abhorrence, much less committed. The reason for the precept is that it becomes saints to behave thus, since they are consecrated to the service of the most holy God.

units.la: Verf. 4 Et obscœnitas, & stultiloquium, & dicacitas, quæ non conveniunt: sed potius gratiarum actio.
units.tr: Verse 4: Nor filthiness, nor foolish talking, nor jesting, which are not fitting; but rather giving of thanks.

units.la: Verf. 5. Nam hoc nostiï, nullum scortatorem aut impurum aut avarum qui est idololatra, habere hæreditatem in regno CHRI-STI & DEI,
units.tr: Verse 5: For this you know, that no fornicator, or unclean or covetous person, who is an idolater, has an inheritance in the kingdom of Christ and God.

units.la: Verf. 6. Ne quisquam vos seducat inanibus sermonibus, propter hæc enim venit ira Dei in homines contumaces.
units.tr: Verse 6: Let no one deceive you with empty words, for because of these things the wrath of God comes upon the disobedient.

units.la: Præceptum 4. Ut obscænitas sermonis, stultiloquium & scurrilitas vitentur: Horum duorum præceptorum rationes reddit quinque.
units.tr: Precept 4: That filthy speech, foolish talk and buffoonery be avoided. He gives five reasons for these two precepts.

units.la: Ratio prima, Quia impurus sermo minime convenit sanctis.
units.tr: First reason: impure speech is by no means fitting for saints.

units.la: Ratio 2, Quia materia lætitiæ aliunde suppetit, nempe ex beneficiis Dei ad gratiarum actionem, verf. 4.
units.tr: Second reason: the matter of joy is supplied from elsewhere, namely from God's benefits, for thanksgiving (verse 4).

units.la: Ratio 3. Quia impuritas & avaritia excludunt à regno Cœlorum, quod Dei Patris & Christi dicitur, quia commune est regnum utriusque.
units.tr: Third reason: impurity and covetousness exclude from the kingdom of heaven, which is called the kingdom of God the Father and of Christ, because the kingdom is common to both.

units.la: Ratio 4. Quia avaritia idololatria est, creaturam in creatoris locum surrogans; Idem etiam intelligi potest de aliis vitiis, verf. 5.
units.tr: Fourth reason: covetousness is idolatry, setting a creature in the place of the Creator. The same may also be understood of the other vices (verse 5).

units.la: Ratio 5. Quia quicunque his vitiis deditî sunt, censebuntur inter filios inobedientiæ, seu in Deum rebelles, & gravissimam iram Dei sentient, quicquid contra seductores gactiant, verf. 6.
units.tr: Fifth reason: all who are given over to these vices will be counted among the sons of disobedience, or rebels against God, and will feel the most grievous wrath of God, whatever they boast against the seducers (verse 6).

units.la: Verf. 7. Ne igitur efiote consortes eorum.
units.tr: Verse 7: Therefore do not become partners with them.

units.la: Tanquam consectarium infert Præceptum 5. Quo generaliter dehortatur à consortio prædictorum vitiorum, & aliorum omnium quibus filii inobedientiæ se polluunt. Rationes præcepti sunt octo: Ratio prima præcessit. Ne fierent participes iræ in rebelles incumbentis, & superventuræ.
units.tr: As a consequence he infers Precept 5, by which he generally dissuades from fellowship with the aforementioned vices and all others by which the sons of disobedience defile themselves. There are eight reasons for the precept. The first has already been given: that they not become partakers in the wrath which falls upon rebels and is about to come.

units.la: Verf. 8. Eratis enim olim tenebræ, nunc autem lux in Domino ut Filii lucis incedite:
units.tr: Verse 8: For you were once darkness, but now are you light in the Lord. Walk as children of light.

units.la: Ratio 2. A mutato ipsorum statu, Quia ante conversionem vestram ad fidem, eratis mancipia ignorantiæ & flagitiorum, nunc vero in Christo, sapientiæ & sanctitatis luce illustrati estis, ut lumen aliis præferatis (unde infertur præceptum idem affirmative, scilicet, ut ambulent non ut filii tenebrarum, sed ut filii lucis, obedientes verbo Dei, quod lucem ad vitam rectè instituendam exhibet) Idcirco ne consortes sitis contumacium.
units.tr: Second reason: from their changed state. Before your conversion to the faith you were slaves of ignorance and wickedness, but now in Christ you have been illuminated by the light of wisdom and holiness, so that you may bear that light to others. Hence the same precept follows in positive form: that they walk not as sons of darkness but as sons of light, obeying the word of God, which sets forth the light for ordering life rightly. Therefore do not be partners with the disobedient.

units.la: Verl. 9 (Nam fructus Spiritus situs est in omni bonitate & justitia & veritate)
units.tr: Verse 9 (for the fruit of the Spirit is in all goodness and righteousness and truth).

units.la: Ratio 3. Quia fructus Spiritus Sancti, per quem translati estis à tenebris ad lucem, situs est in bonitate, justitiâ, & veritate: Ergo fructus hos debetis proferre, non vero consortes esse contumacium in fructibus carnis.
units.tr: Third reason: the fruit of the Holy Spirit, through whom you have been transferred from darkness to light, consists in goodness, righteousness and truth. Therefore you ought to bring forth these fruits, and not be partners with the disobedient in the works of the flesh.

units.la: Verf. 10. Probantes quid sit acceptum Domino.
units.tr: Verse 10: Proving what is acceptable to the Lord.

units.la: Ratio 4. Qua etiam praeceptum explicat de ambulando in luce, Quia studentes ut filii lucis ambulare, poteritis experimento cognoscere & exploratum habere, quid sit Deo acceptum, quidnon. Idcirco ne sitis ambulando in tenebris consortes contumacium.
units.tr: Fourth reason: by which he also explains the precept about walking in the light. By striving to walk as children of light you will be able to know by experience, and to have tested, what is acceptable to God and what is not. Therefore do not be partners with the rebels by walking in darkness.

units.la: Verf. 11. Et ne commercium habetis cum operibus illis infructuosis tenebrarum: sed potius etiam arguite.
units.tr: Verse 11: And have no fellowship with the unfruitful works of darkness, but rather expose them.

units.la: Ratio 5. Qua etiam explicatur & repetitur praeceptum. Quia ambulantes ut filii lucis, non tantum non communicabitis aliorum peccatis, sed etiam exemplo sanctae vitae vestrae redarguetis aliorum peccata. Ne idcirco illorum consortes sitis, sed ab ipsorum moribus potius alienissimi.
units.tr: Fifth reason: by which the precept is also explained and repeated. Walking as children of light, you will not only refrain from sharing in others' sins, but by the example of your holy life you will also rebuke their sins. Therefore be not their companions, but rather wholly alien from their ways.

units.la: Verf. 12. Nam quae occulte fiunt ab illis, turpe est vel dicere.
units.tr: Verse 12: For it is shameful even to speak of the things that are done by them in secret.

units.la: Ratio praecepti 6. Quia opera tenebrarum quae occulte perpetrant reliqui non conversi Ethnici, prae foeditate indigna sunt Christianis auribus. Ergo commercium habere cum ipsorum peccatis non debetis, sed potius redarguere ea, ut filii lucis.
units.tr: Precept/reason 6: the works of darkness which the remaining unconverted heathen commit in secret are, on account of their foulness, unworthy of Christian ears. Therefore you ought not to share in their sins, but rather to rebuke them, as children of light.

units.la: Verf. 13. Sed omnia, dum arguuntur, a luce manifesta fiunt; lux enim illud est quod omnia facit manifesta.
units.tr: Verse 13: But all things, when they are reproved, are made manifest by the light; for whatever makes manifest is light.

units.la: Ratio praecepti 7. Quia reprehensio occultorum peccatorum, quae fit per vestram spectatam in luce vitam sanctam, impiorum conscientias punget, & manifestum faciet quod opera ipsorum sint mala: hoc autem ad ipsorum conversionem magnopere faciet: sic enim adduci poterunt in sui cognitionem.
units.tr: Seventh reason: the rebuke of hidden sins, which is made by your holy life lived in the light, will prick the consciences of the impious and make it plain that their works are evil. This will greatly contribute to their conversion, for in this way they may be brought to knowledge of themselves.

units.la: Lux Confirmat hanc rationem, & probat vitam sanctam esse lucem. Quia lucis proprietatem habet, quatenus manifestat impiis, quod ipsorum opera mala sint.
units.tr: Light confirms this reason and proves that a holy life is light, because it has the property of light, in that it shows the impious that their works are evil.

units.la: Verf. 14. Quapropter dicit, Excitare qui dormis, & surge a mortuis, & illuminabit tibi Christus.
units.tr: Verse 14: Wherefore he says, Awake, you who sleep, and arise from the dead, and Christ will give you light.

units.la: Ratio 8. Confirmans priorem, Quia Spiritus Sancti vox in Scripturis, seu Prophetica & Apostolica doctrina, summatim sumpta huc tendit, ut dormientes & mortui in peccatis excitentur ad resipiscentiam, & veniant ad Christum per fidem, ut luce gratiae Christi illuminentur & ferventur: Ergo omnes filii lucis hanc doctrinam verbo & factis praeferre aliis, & propagare debent ad conversionem aliorum, & simul etiam commercium peccatorum vitare.
units.tr: Eighth reason, confirming the former: the voice of the Holy Spirit in the Scriptures, that is, the prophetic and apostolic doctrine taken as a whole, tends to this end, that those sleeping and dead in sins be roused to repentance and come to Christ by faith, to be enlightened and warmed by the light of Christ's grace. Therefore all sons of light ought to prefer this doctrine to others, by word and deed, and to propagate it for the conversion of others, and at the same time to avoid fellowship in sins.

units.la: Vers. 15. Videte igitur quomodo accuratè incedatis, non ut insipientes, sed ut sapientes:
units.tr: Verse 15: See then that you walk carefully, not as fools but as wise,

units.la: Praeceptum 6. Ad observandum superius conducens. Ut adhibeant studium ad accuratè incedendum, sicut decet imbutos sapientiâ Dei in Euangelio revelatâ, & ne de via deflectant decepti, sicut qui ignari sunt voluntatis divinae.
units.tr: Precept 6: serving to observe what has been said above. That they apply diligence to walking carefully, as befits those imbued with the wisdom of God revealed in the Gospel, and not turn aside from the way, deceived like those who are ignorant of the divine will.

units.la: Vers. 16. Redimentes occasionem, quoniam dies mali sunt.
units.tr: Verse 16: Redeeming the time, because the days are evil.

units.la: Praeceptum 7. Eodem tendens. Ne sinant tempus in otio & voluptatibus sibi eripi, & infructuosè perire, sed ut cum jactura voluptatum, vel inertis otii, vel inutilis negotii, captent, & quasi redimant occasiones bene agendi; Rationem reddit, Quia tempora periculorum plena erant, propter malitiam hominum, qui ipsis (incertum quam citò) libertatem, bona, & vitam ipsam cum bene agendi occasione omni, auferre possent.
units.tr: Precept 7: tending to the same end. That they not allow time to be taken from them by idleness and pleasures and perish unfruitfully, but that, at the cost of giving up pleasures, idle leisure or unprofitable business, they seize, as it were redeem, the opportunities of doing good. He gives the reason: the times were full of dangers, on account of the malice of men, who could take from them (uncertain how soon) liberty, goods and life itself, together with every opportunity of doing good.

units.la: Vers. 17. Propterea ne estote imprudentes, sed intelligentes quae sit voluntas Domini.
units.tr: Verse 17: Therefore do not be foolish, but understand what the will of the Lord is.

units.la: Ex hac ratione infert conclusionem: Ergo (inquit) prudentes estote, & non insipientes, observantes quid à vobis Deus requirat ut praestetis diligenter & sine cunctatione, dum datur tempus.
units.tr: From this reason he draws a conclusion: therefore (he says) be prudent and not foolish, observing what God requires of you, that you may perform it diligently and without delay, while time is given.

units.la: Vers. 18. Et ne inebriamini vino, in quo luxus est, sed implemini Spiritu:
units.tr: Verse 18: And do not be drunk with wine, in which is excess; but be filled with the Spirit.

units.la: Praeceptum 8. Vetans ne inebrientur vino vel potu quovis. Ratio praecepti est, Quia in hac ebrietate perditio est fortunarum, famae, corporis, & animae.
units.tr: Precept 8. Forbidding them to become drunk with wine or any other drink. The reason for the precept is that drunkenness brings the ruin of one's fortune, reputation, body and soul.

units.la: Implemini] Praeceptum 9. Per antithesin propositum ut impleantur potius, & le exhilarent salutari aqua Spiritus Sancti, id est, ut studeant abundare in sensu laetitiae, quae est à Dei Spiritu: in qua repletione non datur excessus.
units.tr: Be filled] Precept 9. Set out by way of antithesis: that they should rather be filled and gladdened by the saving water of the Holy Spirit; that is, that they should strive to abound in a sense of joy, which comes from the Spirit of God. In this filling there is no excess.

units.la: Vers. 19. Loquentes inter vos mutuò per Psalmos & hymnos, & cantiones spirituales: canentes & psallentes in corde vestro, Domino:
units.tr: Vers. 19. Speaking to one another in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing and making melody in your heart to the Lord:

units.la: Ratio praecepti à fructibus melioribus, quos gignit spirituale gaudium, quales sunt omnis generis spirituales cantus, praecipuè illi qui in sacris literis extant, quibus se mutuò ædificent, & ex corde seu spiri-tuali affectu DEUM glorificent: Psalmus est sacra cantio in genere, præsertim quæ fit citharæ pulsu. Hymnus proprie DEI laudes continet. Ode, seu canticum nomen generale est.
units.tr: The reason for the precept is drawn from the better fruits that spiritual joy produces, such as every kind of spiritual song, especially those found in the holy writings, by which they may build one another up and glorify God from the heart, that is, from a spiritual affection. A psalm is a sacred song in general, especially one sung to the plucking of the lyre. A hymn properly contains the praises of God. Ode, or canticle, is a general name.

units.la: Vers. 20. Gratias agentes semper de omnibus in nomine Domini nostri Iesu Christi, Deo & Patri.
units.tr: Vers. 20. Giving thanks always for all things in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, to God and the Father.

units.la: Usum & finem specialem cantionum Christianarum ostendit, ut gratias semper agamus per IESUM CHRISTUM Deo, & Patri nostro, de omnibus suis beneficiis, in quocunque itatu fuerimus.
units.tr: He shows the use and special purpose of Christian songs: that we should always give thanks to God our Father through Jesus Christ for all his benefits, in whatever state we may be.

units.la: Secunda Pars. Vers. 21. Subjecti estote alii alii, cum timore Dei.
units.tr: Second Part. Vers. 21. Submit yourselves one to another in the fear of God.

units.la: Secunda pars Capitis, in qua ut descendat ad œconomica præcepta, præmittit hortationem de mutua submissione in genere, ut servato ordine qui à DEO ponitur, omnes mutuas sibi præstent operas, & officia mutua; nam ubicunque regnat charitas, ibi mutua est servitus: Addit in timore DEI, quia ab hoc fonte fluere oportet hujus præcepti sinceram ex animo obedientiam in gloriam DEI: solus enim timor CHRISTI nostram ferociam domare potest, ne jugum recusemus, & subigere arrogantiam, ne servire proximis nos pudeat.
units.tr: This is the second part of the chapter, in which, in order to descend to the precepts of household life, he first sets out a general exhortation to mutual submission: that, with the order that God has appointed kept, all should render mutual services and duties to one another. For wherever love reigns, there is mutual service. He adds "in the fear of God," because sincere obedience to this precept, from the heart, for the glory of God, ought to flow from this source. For only the fear of Christ can tame our fierceness, so that we do not refuse the yoke, and subdue our arrogance, so that we are not ashamed to serve our neighbours.

units.la: Vers. 22. Uxores propriis viris subjectæ estote, ut Domino:
units.tr: Vers. 22. Wives, submit yourselves to your own husbands, as unto the Lord:

units.la: Sequuntur præcepta œconomica. Primum est, Ut uxores subjiciant se suis viris caste, sincere, ex animo, & in rebus licitis. Rationes præcepti sunt quatuor.
units.tr: The precepts concerning household life follow. The first is that wives should submit themselves to their husbands chastely, sincerely, from the heart, and in lawful matters. There are four reasons for the precept.

units.la: Ut Domino Christo Ratio prima, Quia CHRISTUS præcipit ut uxor subjiciatur marito suo, subjectionemque illam, ut obedientiam sibi præstitam interpretatur, & similiter uxoris rebellionem adversus maritum judicat rebellionem adversus seipsum.
units.tr: As unto the Lord Christ. The first reason: because Christ commands that the wife be subject to her husband, and he interprets that subjection as obedience rendered to himself; likewise he judges a wife's rebellion against her husband to be rebellion against himself.

units.la: Vers. 23. Quoniam vir est caput uxoris, ut & Christus est caput Ecclesiæ: & is est qui salutem dat corpori.
units.tr: Vers. 23. For the husband is the head of the wife, as Christ also is the head of the Church, and he is the Saviour of the body.

units.la: Ratio 2. Quia vir dignitate seu authoritate superior est, sicut Caput est corpore superius. Æquum ergo est ut Uxor ei subjiciatur.
units.tr: Reason 2. Because the husband is superior in dignity or authority, as the head is above the body. It is fitting, therefore, that the wife be subject to him.

units.la: Ut Christus Ratio 3. Quia in viri autoritate supra uxorem extare voluit DEUS similitudinem autoritatis CHRISTI in Ecclesiam.
units.tr: As Christ. Reason 3. Because God willed that the husband's authority over the wife should bear a likeness to Christ's authority over the Church.

units.la: Et ut est Ratio 4. Illustrata eâdem similitudine, Sicut CHRISTUS est caput Ecclesiæ in bonum ipsius: sic Vir est caput Uxoris in bonum Uxoris, quam defendere, alere, & consolari debet in omnibus: Et sicut Ecclesiæ prodest ut Christo subjiciatur, ita Uxori prodest ut Marito subjiciatur.
units.tr: And as. Reason 4. Illustrated by the same likeness: as Christ is the head of the Church for its good, so the husband is head of the wife for the good of the wife, whom he ought to defend, nourish and comfort in all things. And just as it profits the Church to be subject to Christ, so it profits the wife to be subject to her husband.

units.la: Verf. 24. Itaque sicut Ecclesia subjecta est Christo, ita & uxores suis viris subjectæ sunto in omnibus.
units.tr: Vers. 24. Therefore, as the Church is subject to Christ, so let wives also be subject to their husbands in all things.

units.la: Ex his rationibus infert conclusionem: necessarium scilicet esse ut uxor Marito subjiciatur in omnibus, quæ subjectionem debitam Deo & Christo non impedjunt.
units.tr: From these reasons he draws the conclusion: namely, that it is necessary for the wife to be subject to her husband in all things, provided they do not hinder the subjection owed to God and Christ.

units.la: Verf. 25. Viri, diligite uxores vestras, sicut & Christus dilexit Ecclesiam, & semetipsum exposuit pro ea:
units.tr: Vers. 25. Husbands, love your wives, as Christ also loved the Church and gave himself up for it:

units.la: Præceptum secundum, Datum viris de diligendis uxoribus suis; Rationes præcepti sunt quinque.
units.tr: The second precept, given to husbands, concerns loving their wives. There are five reasons for the precept.

units.la: Sicut ] Ratio prima ab exemplo dilectionis Christi erga Ecclesiam, quam dilectionem commendat Apostolus ex his quatuor indiciis: 1. est quod Christus ex dilectione tradiderit semetipsum pro Ecclesia jam perdita.
units.tr: As. The first reason is drawn from the example of Christ's love for the Church, which love the Apostle commends by four signs: 1. that Christ, out of love, gave himself up for the Church when it was already lost.

units.la: Verf. 26 Ut eam sanctificaret, postquam eam purgasset lavacro aquæ per verbum:
units.tr: Vers. 26. That he might sanctify it, having cleansed it by the washing of water through the word:

units.la: Indicium 2. Quod dilexerit Ecclesiam, & tradiderit se pro ea in eum finem ut eam sanctificaret, seu e profana & impura sanctam redderet.
units.tr: Sign 2. That he loved the Church and gave himself up for it with the purpose that he might sanctify it, that is, make it holy out of what was profane and unclean.

units.la: Lavacro ] Indicium 3. Quod Christus efficaciter Ecclesiam mundet sanguinis sui, & promissionis suæ gratuitæ virtute, quam per ordinaria media baptismi, & verbi, nobis applicat, tanquam per instrumenta Spiritus sui, ad fidem confirmandam & virtutem communicandam, ordinata.
units.tr: By the washing. Sign 3. That Christ effectively cleanses the Church by his blood and by the power of his free promise, which he applies to us through the ordinary means of baptism and the word, as through instruments of his Spirit, appointed to confirm faith and to communicate power.

units.la: Verf. 27. Ut sisteret eam sibi gloriosam, id est, Ecclesiam non habentem maculam, aut rugam, aut quicquam ejusmodi, sed ut esset sancta & inculpata.
units.tr: Vers. 27. That he might present it to himself glorious, that is, the Church not having spot, or wrinkle, or any such thing, but that it should be holy and without blame.

units.la: Indicium 4. Quod eo fine Ecclesiam dilexerit, ut tandem sistat eam sibi in cœlo gloriosam, sine ullo vestigio vel peccati vel miseriæ, semper prosequuturus opus suum, donec effectum reddiderit.
units.tr: Sign 4. That with this end in view he loved the Church, so that at last he might present it to himself in heaven glorious, without any trace of sin or misery, always continuing his work until he has brought it to completion.

units.la: Verf. 28. Ita debent viri diligere suas uxores, ut sua ipsorum corpora; qui diligit suam uxorem, seipsum diligit.
units.tr: Vers. 28. So ought husbands to love their wives as their own bodies; he who loves his wife loves himself.

units.la: Ratio 2. Præcepti viris dati, de diligendis uxoribus suis. Quia uxores sunt suorum virorum corpora, secundum Deı legem illam. Erunt duo in unam carnem.
units.tr: Reason 2 of the precept given to husbands, to love their wives: because wives are their husbands' bodies, according to that law of God: They shall be two in one flesh.

units.la: Qui diligit ] Ratio 3. Quia qui diligit suam ipsius uxorem, diligit seipsum, & sibi ipsi dilectionis officium præstat, siquidem in viri commodum ista dilectio uxoris propriæ, modis omnibus redundat.
units.tr: He who loves. Reason 3. Because he who loves his own wife loves himself and performs a duty of love toward himself, since indeed love for one's own wife redounds in every way to the husband's advantage.

units.la: Verf. 29 Nullus enim unquam suam ipsius carnem odio habuit, imo enutrit ac fovet eam, sicut & Dominus Ecclesiam:
units.tr: Vers. 29. For no one ever hated his own flesh, but nourishes and cherishes it, as the Lord also does the Church:

units.la: Ratio 4. Quia tam est alienum à sapienti & bono viro, uxorem propriam non diligere, quam carnem suam odisse, & rationi tam consentaneum est uxorem alere & fovere, quam carnem propriam curare.
units.tr: Reason 4. Because it is as foreign to a wise and good man not to love his own wife as it is to hate his own flesh; and it is as reasonable to nourish and cherish a wife as it is to care for one's own flesh.

units.la: Sicut ] Hanc rationem confirmat & illustrat exemplo Christi, quod semper nobis ante oculos positum vult, tanquam perfectissimum dilectionis exemplar.
units.tr: As. He confirms and illustrates this reason by the example of Christ, which he wants always set before our eyes as the most perfect pattern of love.

units.la: Verf. 30. Quoniam membra sumus corporis ejus, ex carne ejus, & ex ossibus ejus.
units.tr: Vers. 30. For we are members of his body, of his flesh and of his bones.

units.la: Probat Christum diligere nos ut carnem suam, nec odisse posse, sed ex dilectione quasi constringi, ut nos nutriat & foveat: quia sumus membra corporis ejus: caro ex carne ejus, & os ex ossibus ejus, id est, tam ipsi conjuncti, quam Eva conjuncta fuit Adamo, nam quod Eva debebat Adamo in corpore, nos debemus Christo in Spiritus nostri regeneratione, & amplius multo. In Evæ formatione jacturam fecit Adam unius tantum costæ: In Ecclesiæ reformatione jacturam fecit Christus vitæ suæ. Sola Evæ materia est ab Adamo: à Christo vero est Ecclesiæ formatio naturalis, & reformatio Spiritualis respectu & corporis & animæ uniuscujusque membri.
units.tr: He proves that Christ loves us as his own flesh, and cannot hate us, but is bound, as it were, by love to nourish and cherish us, because we are members of his body: flesh of his flesh, and bone of his bones. That is, we are joined to him as closely as Eve was joined to Adam. For what Eve owed to Adam in body, we owe to Christ in the regeneration of our spirit, and much more besides. In the forming of Eve, Adam suffered the loss of only one rib; in the reforming of the Church, Christ suffered the loss of his own life. Eve's material alone came from Adam; but from Christ comes the natural formation of the Church and its spiritual reformation, with respect both to the body and to the soul of each member.

units.la: Verf. 31. Propterea derelinquet homo Patrem ac Matrem; & agglutinabitur uxori suæ, & qui duo erant fient una caro.
units.tr: Vers. 31. For this cause shall a man leave his father and mother, and shall cleave to his wife, and the two shall be one flesh.

units.la: Ratio 5. Qua simul probat Ecclesiam debere Christo originem suam; simul etiam probat, diligendas esse uxores à maritis, ex conjugii nimirum institutione, quæ requirit ut propter conjunctionem Mariti & uxoris, relinquat vir patrem & matrem, & agglutinetur uxori suæ, & hi duo uniantur in unam carnem, per vinculum conjugii, per quod jam mutuum jus est & potestas utriusque in se invicem; cujus institutionis verbaꝰ typicum habent sensum: nam Deus, Gen. 2. 23. dicendo, Tu caro es ex carne mea, & os ex ossibus meis, intendebat Christi & Ecclesiæ unionem repræsentare, & docere nos esse os ex ossibus Christi, & carnem ex carne Christi, id est, arctissimè nos uniri Christo, quia in Adami sermone ad Evam præfiguratum fuit, Christum (ut esset una caro nobiscum, & nos efficeret unam carnem cum seipso per conjugium spirituale) quasi derelicturum fuisse Patrem suum (seposita modo quodam gloriâ illâ quam habebat cum Patre, se exinaniendo cum in forma Dei esset, & formam servi accipiendo.) Similiter etiam præfiguratum est Christum, Matrem suam Mariam relicturum fuisse, ut moriendo sibi emeret Ecclesiam sponsam, cum qua esset una caro.
units.tr: Reason 5. By which he proves at once that the Church owes its origin to Christ; and at the same time that wives ought to be loved by their husbands, from the very institution of marriage. This institution requires that, for the sake of the union of husband and wife, the husband leave his father and mother, and cleave to his wife, and that the two be united into one flesh through the bond of marriage, by which each has a mutual right and power over the other. The words of this institution also have a typical sense. For God, in saying, Gen. 2. 23. "You are flesh of my flesh and bone of my bones," intended to represent the union of Christ and the Church, and to teach us that we are bone of Christ's bone and flesh of Christ's flesh, that is, that we are most closely united to Christ. For in Adam's speech to Eve there was foreshadowed Christ, who (in order that he might be one flesh with us, and make us one flesh with himself through a spiritual marriage) would, as it were, leave his Father behind, setting aside for a time that glory which he had with the Father, emptying himself when he was in the form of God and taking the form of a servant. Similarly, it was also foreshadowed that Christ would leave behind his mother Mary, so that by dying he might win for himself the Church as his bride, with whom he would be one flesh.

units.la: Vers. 32. Mysterium hoc magnum est: loquor autem de Christo, & de Ecclesia.
units.tr: Verse 32. "This is a great mystery: but I speak concerning Christ and the Church."

units.la: Hoc postremum respiciens Apostolus, magnum vocat mysterium, non conjuugium carnale, sed unionem Christi cum Ecclesia: & ne quis secus intelligeret dictum, expressis verbis significat se non de conjugio carnali Viri & Uxoris, dictum illud de mysterio intelligere, sed de spirituali Christi & Ecclesiæ conjunctione, quæ Spiritus non carnis virtute, fide, non aliquo naturali nexu, constat.
units.tr: Looking at this last point, the Apostle calls it a great mystery, not a carnal marriage but the union of Christ with the Church. And lest anyone understand the saying otherwise, he states in plain words that he is not understanding that saying about the mystery as referring to the carnal marriage of husband and wife, but to the spiritual conjunction of Christ and the Church, which exists by the power of the Spirit and by faith, not by the power of the flesh or by any natural bond.

units.la: Vers. 33. Itaque & nos singuli ita facite, suam quisque uxorem ita diligat, ut seipsum: uxor autem videat, ut revereatur virum.
units.tr: Verse 33. "Nevertheless let every one of you in particular so love his wife even as himself; and the wife see that she reverence her husband."

units.la: Missō mysterio, redit ad præcepta de Mariti & Uxoris officiis, & ponit ultimo loco Præceptum tertium, In quo omnia officia virorum revocat ad dilectionem sinceram, qualis est dilectio qua Vir diligit seipsum, & hanc dilectionem urget; Ex altera parte omnia officia Uxorum revocat ad timorem seu reverentiam erga virum, ne eum offendat, sed ei in Domino placeat in omnibus.
units.tr: Setting the mystery aside, he returns to the precepts concerning the duties of husband and wife, and he places as the last, third precept, one in which he reduces all the duties of husbands to sincere love, such as the love by which a husband loves himself, and he presses this love. On the other side, he reduces all the duties of wives to fear, or reverence, toward the husband, so that they do not offend him but please him in all things in the Lord.

units.la: Caput Sextum.
units.tr: Chapter 6.

units.la: DErgit Præcepta dare de Officiis Christianùs Œconomi- cùs, & Communibus. Capitù partes sunt duæ: Prima continet quatuor præcepta de Officiis œconomicis, ad versum 10. In altera est Conclusio Epistolæ, continens communia officia aliquot, ad finem.
units.tr: He now gives precepts about the Christian duties of household life and of common duties. The chapter has two parts. The first contains four precepts on domestic duties, down to verse 10. The second contains the conclusion of the Epistle, with several common duties, to the end.

units.la: Verf. 1. Liberi, auscultate in Domino parentibus vestris: id enim est justum.
units.tr: Ver. 1. Children, obey your parents in the Lord: for this is right.

units.la: Præceptum primum Liberis datum, de honorandis Parentibus de observantia & obedientia præstanda erga Parentes in omnibus, quantum per Dei voluntatem fieri potest. Ratio-nes præcepti sunt quatuor: Primâ, Quia omni, & jure Divino, & jure [illegible, ~3 letters] ræ jucтum est, ut liberi obediant Parentibus.
units.tr: The first precept, given to children, concerns honouring parents: the obedience and submission to be rendered to parents in all things, so far as God's will allows. There are four reasons for this precept. First, because obedience of children to parents is just by divine law and by natural law.

units.la: Verf. 2. Honora Patrem tuum & Matrem tuam: (quod est præceptum primum cum promissione.)
units.tr: Ver. 2. Honour thy father and thy mother; (which is the first commandment with promise.)

units.la: Ratio 2. Quia expressè in Decalogo exigitur liberorum obedientia, ut pars honoris Parentibus debiti, & in Lege præscripti.
units.tr: Second reason: because the obedience of children is expressly required in the Decalogue, as part of the honour due to parents and prescribed in the Law.

units.la: Quod est ] Ratio 3. Quia hoc Præceptum est primum, quod habet spe- cialem promissionem specialiter applicatam.
units.tr: Which is] Third reason: because this is the first commandment that has a specific promise specifically applied to it.

units.la: Verf. 3. Ut bene tibi sit, & sis longævus super terram.
units.tr: Ver. 3. That it may be well with thee, and thou mayest live long on the earth.

units.la: Ratio 4. Quia obedientia liberorum erga Parentes in bonum liberorum cedit, & in benedictionem specialem, per vitæ temporalis proroga- tionem: quæ promissio vel simpliciter impletur, vel per commutatio- nem hujus beneficii in multo majus vitæ melioris.
units.tr: Fourth reason: because the obedience of children to parents turns to the children's good and to a special blessing, by the lengthening of temporal life. This promise is either fulfilled simply, or it is exchanged for a much greater benefit of a better life.

units.la: Verf. 4. Et vos patres, ne provocate ad iram liberos vestros, sed cautrite eos in doctrina & monitis Domini.
units.tr: Ver. 4. And ye fathers, provoke not your children to wrath, but bring them up in the nurture and admonition of the Lord.

units.la: Præceptum 2. De officio Parentum in liberos, ne vel ex altera parte nimia in liberos suos severitate, abutantur patria sua potestate, (ne animos liberorum à se alienent) vel ne ex altera parte, nimiâ indul- gentiâ juvenilem petulantiam in liberis suis foveant; sed ut studeant pe- tius vitia eorum corrigere, & bonos mores in Dei timore, eos docere.
units.tr: The second precept concerns the duty of parents towards children: that they should not, on the one hand, abuse their paternal authority by excessive severity towards their children (which alienates the children's hearts from them), nor, on the other hand, indulge their children so much that they foster youthful wantonness. Rather, they should strive to correct their children's faults and to teach them good morals in the fear of God.

units.la: Verf. 5. Servi, auscultate iis qui vestri Domini sunt, secundùm carnem carnem cum timore ac tremore, cum simplicitate cordis vestri, ut CHRISTO.
units.tr: Ver. 5. Servants, be obedient to them that are your masters according to the flesh, with fear and trembling, in singleness of your heart, as unto Christ.

units.la: Præceptum 3. De officio servorum in Dominos: cujus partes sunt sex. 1. Ut obediant Dominis suis, agnoscentes suam externam servilem conditionem, à Deo esse, & quod non exempti sint à servitute politica per Christum, qui politias nec tollit nec mutat. 2. Ut meminerint Dominos suos non esse conscientiarum Dominos, sed carnis, seu externi hominis, & in rebus quæ hanc vitam attingunt. 3. Ut serviant in reverentia, & metu iræ ipsorum. 4. Ut sepositio dolo candidè & sincerè agant cum Dominis suis. 5. Ut propter Christi mandatum illis serviant, atque ita in illis observandis Christo serviant.
units.tr: The third precept concerns the duty of servants towards their masters, and it has six parts. 1. That they obey their masters, acknowledging that their outward servile condition comes from God, and that they are not freed from civil servitude by Christ, who neither removes nor changes civil order. 2. That they remember their masters are not lords of their consciences, but of the flesh, that is, of the outward man, and of matters that concern this life. 3. That they serve with reverence and fear of their anger. 4. That they act candidly and sincerely, without deceit, towards their masters. 5. That they serve them for Christ's command, and so in observing these things they serve Christ.

units.la: Vers. 6. Non ad oculum servientes, ut qui hominibus placere studGent, sed ut servi Christi, facientes ex animo quæ vult Deus.
units.tr: Ver. 6. Not with eye-service, as men-pleasers; but as the servants of Christ, doing the will of God from the heart.

units.la: Vers. 7. Cum benevolentia servientes Domino, & non hominibus:
units.tr: Ver. 7. With good will doing service, as to the Lord, and not to men:

units.la: Sexta Præcepti pars, ut sine fraude adulatoria, res dominorum suorum procurent omnes, non minus cum Domini absunt, quam cum præsentes ipsos inspectant, & non tam in eum finem ut Dominis placeant, quam ut Deo placeant. Denique, Ut serviant, non ex φιλαυτία, vel metu mero, sed ex benevolentiâ ut Deo non hominibus servientes: Servit enim Deo, qui præcipienti Deo, ut serviat hero suo, obtemperat.
units.tr: The sixth part of the precept is that all servants should, without deceitful flattery, look after their masters' affairs, no less when the masters are absent than when they are watching them present, and not so much with the aim of pleasing their masters as of pleasing God. Finally, they should serve not out of self-love [φιλαυτία] or mere fear, but with goodwill, as serving God and not men. For he serves God who obeys God's command to serve his master.

units.la: Vers. 8. Ut qui illud sciatis, singulos, quicquid fecerint boni, hoc reportaturos à Domino, sive servus fuerit, sive liber.
units.tr: Ver. 8. Knowing that whatsoever good thing any man doeth, the same shall he receive of the Lord, whether he be bond or free.

units.la: Præter argumenta quæ tacitè in prioribus comprehenduntur, ad præceptum confirmandum, addit ipsem mercedis reportandæ à Deo, qui liberaliter remuneratur opera suorum servorum, sive sint in carne liberi, sive servi.
units.tr: Besides the arguments that are tacitly included in the earlier verses, to confirm the precept he adds the reward to be received from God, who liberally rewards the works of his servants, whether they are free or slaves in the flesh.

units.la: Vers. 9. Et vos Domini, eadem facite erga illos, remissis minis: scientes vestrum etiam ipsorum Dominum esse in Cælis, nec personæ respectum esse apud eum.
units.tr: Ver. 9. And, ye masters, do the same things unto them, forbearing threatening: knowing that your Master also is in heaven; neither is there respect of persons with him.

units.la: Præceptum 4. De officio dominorum in servos, ut easdem virtutes sibi ex proportione applicantes, Christianum in modum exerceant herilem suam potestatem in servos: & in specie, ut temperent sibi in minis ne tyrannicè imperitent.
units.tr: The fourth precept concerns the duty of masters towards servants: that, applying the same virtues to themselves in proportion, they exercise their lordly power over servants in a Christian manner, and in particular that they restrain themselves from threats, so as not to rule tyrannically.

units.la: Scientes] Rationes præcepti addit duas: 1. Quia Dominum habent supra se, qui potens est ad ulciscendum impotens ipsorum imperium: 2. Quia ¶. Quia Deus justus est, qui non acceptat personam Domini vel servi, sed causam & opus utriusque spectat secundùm æquitatem.
units.tr: Knowing] He adds two reasons for the precept: 1. Because they have a Lord above them, who is powerful to avenge their unjust rule. 2. Because God is just, who does not accept the person of master or servant, but regards the cause and the work of each according to equity.

units.la: Secunda Pars.
units.tr: Second Part.

units.la: Versf. 10. Quod superest, fratres mei, corroboramini per Dominum, & forte in fortitudine virtutis ejus.
units.tr: Verse 10. Finally, my brethren, be strong in the Lord, and in the power of his might.

units.la: Altera pars Capitis, continens Epistolæ conclusionem; cujus quatuor sunt articuli: In primo hortatur ad constantiam in fide & vitæ sanctitate, & ad induendam armaturam spiritualem contra omnes hostes, cum quibus pugnandum est nobis, quamdiu vivimus, Fratres (inquit) corroboramini in Domino. Argumenta hortationis sunt tria: Argumentum primum, Quia communionem habetis cum Domino, in quo est potentia & robur; in quo si maneatis per fidem, ejusque gratia utamini, habebitis ipsum paratum in subsidium, cum potentiâ & efficaci operatione, ut audeatis, & valeatis vos fortiter opponere omnibus hostibus, & impedimentis. Corroboramini igitur in Domino.
units.tr: The second part of the chapter, containing the conclusion of the Epistle, has four articles. In the first, he urges them to constancy in the faith and holiness of life, and to put on the spiritual armour against all the enemies with whom we must fight as long as we live: Brethren, he says, be strong in the Lord. There are three arguments for this exhortation. The first: because you have fellowship with the Lord, in whom is power and strength; if you abide in him through faith and make use of his grace, you will have him ready to help you, with his power and effective working, so that you may dare and be able to oppose all enemies and hindrances boldly. Therefore, be strong in the Lord.

units.la: Versf. 11. Induite universam illam armaturam Dei, ut possitis stare adversus insidias Diaboli.
units.tr: Verse 11. Put on the whole armour of God, that ye may be able to stand against the wiles of the devil.

units.la: Arg. 2. Quia muniti estis omni genere armorum, quæ ad bellum requiruntur. Ad quæ induenda hortatur eos ut possint in pugna adversus Diaboli insultus & insidias stare.
units.tr: Argument 2. Because you are armed with every kind of weapon that war requires. He exhorts them to put these on, so that they may stand in battle against the assaults and snares of the devil.

units.la: Verf. 12. Quoniam non est nobis lucta adversus sanguinem & carnem, sed adversus imperia, adversus potestates, adversus mundi dominos, rectores tenebrarum seculi hujus, adversus spiritualesmalitias quæ sunt in sublimi.
units.tr: Verse 12. For we wrestle not against flesh and blood, but against principalities, against powers, against the rulers of the darkness of this world, against spiritual wickedness in high places.

units.la: Arg. 3. Quia non est nobis lucta simpliciter adversus homines, sive adversus nostram carnem, sive adversus homines solum, (quæ pugna videri posset tolerabilis) sed est pugna nobis adversus omnium horum malorum autorem, Diabolum, totumque exercitum impurorum spirituum, qui non sunt imbecilles & gregarii milites, sed omnes sunt principatus & potestates, seu Spiritus qui dominantur in mundanos: & regunt impios (qui tenebræ hic & alibi dicuntur) eosque excitant adversus nos: quique ut potentissimi sunt & astutissimi, sic & pravissimi: Et denique spirituales sunt, quos oculis discernere non possumus, & in toto aperto hoc aere volitant, ut possint quando volunt nos aggredi incautos, nisi vigilemus.
units.tr: Argument 3. Because our struggle is not simply against men, whether against our own flesh or against men alone (a fight which might seem tolerable), but our fight is against the author of all these evils, the devil, and the whole army of unclean spirits. These are not feeble common soldiers, but all of them are principalities and powers, or spirits who rule over worldly men and govern the wicked (who are called darkness here and elsewhere), and stir them up against us; and as they are most powerful and most crafty, so also they are most wicked. Finally, they are spiritual, so that we cannot discern them with our eyes, and they fly about in all this open air, so that they can attack us when they wish, while we are off our guard, unless we keep watch.

units.la: Verf. 13. Propterea assumite universam illam armaturam Dei, ut possitis resistere tempore adverso, & omnibus confectis stare.
units.tr: Verse 13. Wherefore take unto you the whole armour of God, that ye may be able to withstand in the evil day, and having done all, to stand.

units.la: Hinc repetit hortationem, ut armaturam Dei totam induant, ut & in die malo, seu die tentationis, & in die victoriae, possint stare, expectantes novas hostis impressiones, & tandem expugnatis hostibus, triumphare.
units.tr: Here he repeats the exhortation that they should put on the whole armour of God, so that they may stand both in the evil day, that is, the day of temptation, and in the day of victory, awaiting the enemy's new assaults, and finally, when the enemies are overcome, triumph.

units.la: Verf. 14. State igitur lumbis circumcincti veritate, & induti thorace justitiae.
units.tr: Verse 14. Stand therefore, having your loins girt about with truth, and having on the breastplate of righteousness.

units.la: Similitudine sumpta a militia corporali, subsidia nominat adversus diabolum, quae armaturae corporali respondent, ad defensionem, & ad depellendum hostem accommodatae; & in hunc finem stare jubet unumquemque, id est, in vocatione sua generali, & speciali, se continere, & vigilare adversus hostem. Partes autem armaturae ad defensionem veritatis, sunt septem.
units.tr: Taking his comparison from bodily warfare, he names the defences against the devil, which correspond to bodily armour and are fitted for defence and for driving off the enemy. To this end he bids each one stand, that is, hold himself within his general and particular calling and keep watch against the enemy. There are seven parts of the armour for the defence of the truth.

units.la: Lumbis Prima, est constantia in doctrina veritatis, quam balteo comparat, qui laxiores corporis partes continet ne diffluant: nam cognitio ne vacillemus ob infirmitatem, nos corroborat.
units.tr: Loins. The first is constancy in the doctrine of truth, which he compares to a girdle, which holds in the looser parts of the body so that they do not fall apart; for the knowledge of the truth strengthens us so that we do not waver through weakness.

units.la: Induti Pars 2. Armaturae est Thorax justitiae, quo nomine intelligimus justitiam CHRISTI nobis applicatam, cui semper adnascitur sanctae vitae, bonaeque conscientiae studium; quod munit quasi pectus nostrum adversus impetus adversarii in fidem nostram, eamque sinceram esse demonstrat.
units.tr: Having on. The second part of the armour is the breastplate of righteousness, by which we understand the righteousness of Christ applied to us, to which there always grows the zeal for a holy life and a good conscience; this guards our breast, as it were, against the attacks of the adversary on our faith, and shows that it is sincere.

units.la: Verf. 15. Calceatis pedibus praeparatione Evangelii pacis.
units.tr: Verse 15. And your feet shod with the preparation of the gospel of peace.

units.la: Pars 3. Est animi promptitudo ad Evangelium confitendum & promovendum, pro vocatione nostra, contra omnia impedimenta, & difficultates: hoc est, calceari pedes praeparatione euangelii.
units.tr: The third part is readiness of mind to confess and promote the gospel, according to our calling, against all hindrances and difficulties. This is what it means: your feet shod with the preparation of the gospel.

units.la: Verf. 16. Insuper assumpto scuto fidei, quo possitis omnia jacula mali illius ignita extinguere.
units.tr: Verse 16. Above all, taking the shield of faith, wherewith ye shall be able to quench all the fiery darts of the wicked.

units.la: Pars 4. Est scutum fidei, seu fiducia in CHRISTUM, qua tanquam scuto excipiuntur, & refelluntur omnes venenatae tentationes diaboli, quas ut tela vibrat in nos hostis ille.
units.tr: The fourth part is the shield of faith, that is, trust in Christ, by which, as with a shield, all the poisoned temptations of the devil are received and repelled, which that enemy hurls at us like missiles.

units.la: Verf. 17. Galeam etiam salutarem accipite, & gladium spiritualem, hoc est verbum Dei.
units.tr: Verse 17. And take the helmet of salvation, and the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God.

units.la: Pars 5. Est Galea salutis, seu spes certa de salute futura, qua muniti & de victoria certi reddPiti, in pugna confidentius perseverare poterimus.
units.tr: The fifth part is the helmet of salvation, that is, the sure hope of future salvation, by which, armed and assured of victory, we shall be able to persevere more confidently in the fight.

units.la: Gladius ] Pars 6. Gladius Spiritus, seu verbum DEI, quo districto & vibrato Diabolum ipsum depellere & in fugam vertere possimus.
units.tr: Sword. The sixth part is the sword of the Spirit, that is, the word of God, by which, when it is drawn and brandished, we can drive off the devil himself and put him to flight.

units.la: Verf. 18. Omni prece & supplicatione, precantes omni tempore per Spiritum, & illi ipsi rei invigilantes cum omni perseverantia & supplicatione pro omnibus sanctis:
units.tr: Verse 18. Praying always with all prayer and supplication in the Spirit, and watching thereunto with all perseverance and supplication for all saints.

units.la: Pars 7. Est Precatio quâ Christianus miles conversus ad Imperatorem suum CHRISTUM, auxilium ejus implorat, non semel sed omni tempore, quo necessitas urget, non frigide in labiis, sed in Spiritu ardenti: non languidè, quasi hostem non metuens, sed summo studio in hoc officio vigilans, non tantum pro se, sed etiam pro totâ Ecclesiâ, seu toto DEI exercitu, & pro singulis sanctis, pro ut ipsorum necessitas ipsi innotescit. Vers. 19. Et pro me, ut mihi detur sermo ad aperitionem oris mei cum libertate, ut notum faciam mysterium Euangelii:
units.tr: The seventh part is prayer, by which the Christian soldier, turned to his Emperor Christ, implores his help; not once only, but at every time when need presses, not coldly on the lips, but in a burning spirit; not languidly, as though not fearing the enemy, but watching in this duty with the greatest zeal; not only for himself, but also for the whole Church, or the whole army of God, and for each of the saints, as their need is made known to him. Verse 19. And for me, that utterance may be given unto me, that I may open my mouth boldly, to make known the mystery of the gospel.

units.la: Artic. 2. Conclusionis est, Hortatio ut precentur pro Apostolo, ut Deus det ei plenè, plane & intrepidè confiteri & prædicare Euangelium.
units.tr: Article 2 of the conclusion is an exhortation that they pray for the Apostle, that God may give him to confess and preach the gospel fully, plainly and fearlessly.

units.la: Vers. 20. Cujus causa legatione sungor in catena ut, inquam, de eo libere loquar, sicut oportet me loqui.
units.tr: Verse 20. For which I am an ambassador in bonds; that therein I may speak boldly, as I ought to speak.

units.la: Rationes hortationis sunt tres. Ratio prima, Quia hujus causa ego Apostolus legatus sum cum autoritate, ut Euangelium patefaciam.
units.tr: There are three reasons for the exhortation. The first reason: because for this cause I, an Apostle, am sent as an ambassador with authority, to make the gospel known.

units.la: In vinculis ] Ratio 2. Quia in vinculis detineor propter Testimonium datum, in quo vobis comprecantibus confirmari me à Deo necesse est. Vt oportet ] Ratio 3. Quia decet me Apostolum Euangelium cum parrefia, & libera agendi ratione prædicare.
