units.tr: In bonds. The second reason: because I am held in bonds on account of the testimony given, in which, with your prayers joined to mine, I must necessarily be strengthened by God. As I ought. The third reason: because it becomes me as an Apostle to preach the gospel with boldness and with freedom of speech.

units.la: Vers. 21. Vt autem sciatis & vos res meas, & quid agam, omnia vobis nota faciet Tychicus, charus frater, & fidus Minister in DOMINO:
units.tr: Verse 21. But that ye also may know my affairs, and how I do, Tychicus, a beloved brother and faithful minister in the Lord, shall make known to you all things.

units.la: Vers. 22 Quem misi ad vos ob id ipsum ut cognoscatis respe-stras, & consoletur corda vestra.
units.tr: Verse 22. Whom I have sent unto you for the same purpose, that ye might know our affairs, and that he might comfort your hearts.

units.la: Artic. 3, Est de missione Tychici ad ipsos, cujus rationem reddit, à fine, nempe, ut sic Ephelii cognoscerent de Apostoli rebus, & consolationem caperent, propter Dei cum ipso in vinculis præsentiam, atque ita confirmarentur in fide.
units.tr: Article 3 concerns the sending of Tychicus to them, and he gives the reason from the end: namely, that the Ephesians might know the Apostle's affairs and receive comfort, because God was present with him in his bonds, and so they might be strengthened in the faith.

units.la: Vers. 23. Pax sit vobis fratribus & charitas cum fide à Deo Patre & Domino Iesu Christo.
units.tr: Verse 23. Peace be to the brethren, and love with faith, from God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.

units.la: Verf. 24. Gratia sit cum omnibus diligentibus Dominum nostrum Iesum Christum ad immortalitatem, Amen.
units.tr: Verse 24. Grace be with all them that love our Lord Jesus Christ in sincerity. Amen.

units.la: Artic. 4. Est benedictio Apostolica in qua sub voti formā pronunciat pacem in fratres fideles, & charitatem cum fide, à Deo & Christo amplius in eos effundendam & communicandam.
units.tr: Article 4 is the apostolic benediction, in which, in the form of a wish, he pronounces peace upon the faithful brethren, and love with faith, to be poured out and communicated to them more fully by God and Christ.

units.la: Deinde gratiam pronunciat in omnes qui sincero affectu diligunt Christum: quæ gratia fons est fidei illius quæ operatur per charitatem, & per quam pacem habemus cum Deo in æternum.
units.tr: Then he pronounces grace upon all who love Christ with a sincere affection. This grace is the fountain of that faith which works through love, and through which we have peace with God for ever.

units.la: EXPOSITIO ANALYTICA EPISIOLÆ PAULI AD PHILIPPENSES. Summarium.
units.tr: ANALYTICAL EXPOSITION OF THE EPISTLE OF PAUL TO THE PHILIPPIANS. Summary.

units.la: Hilippi, Vrbs Macedonia, in qua ut fundaret Ecclesiam Apostolus, & fecit insignia & passus est, ut Act. 16. patet.
units.tr: Philippi, a city of Macedonia, where the Apostle, in order to found the Church there, both performed notable deeds and suffered, as Acts 16 shows.

units.la: Occasio scribendae Epistolae haec fuit; Miserant Philippenses Pastorem suum Epaphroditum ad Apostolum cum pecunia, ad ejus egestatem sublevandam, dum Romae in vinculis detineretur: Hac arreptâ occasione scribit hanc Epistolam Apostolus, ut confirmaret eos in fide & pietate: Primo corda ipsorum muniendo contra scandalum crucis, seu vinculorum suorum, & ad Constantiam hortando, Capite primo. Secundo, hortando ad Concordiam inter se, reliquasque virtutes quae huc spectabant, Capite secundo. Tertio, hortando ad dequiescendum cum gaudio in Christi gratia & virtute, tanquam ad sanctimoniam & salutem abunde sufficiente; utque caveant sibi a Pseudapostolis, & imitentur Apostolorum, & sanctorum Ministrorum Christi exemplar, Capite tertio. Denique, Post praecepta data de Christianis virtutibus, gratitudinem suam, pro ipsorum erga se liberalitate, ostendendo, Cap. 4.
units.tr: The occasion for writing this Epistle was this: the Philippians had sent their minister Epaphroditus to the Apostle with money, to relieve his want while he was being held in chains at Rome. Seizing this opportunity, the Apostle writes this Epistle in order to strengthen them in faith and piety. First, by fortifying their hearts against the scandal of the cross, that is, of his chains, and by exhorting them to constancy, chapter 1. Second, by exhorting them to concord among themselves and to the other virtues that bear on this, chapter 2. Third, by exhorting them to rest with joy in the grace and power of Christ, as in a sufficient holiness and salvation, and to beware of false apostles, and to imitate the examples of the Apostles and of the holy ministers of Christ, chapter 3. Finally, after giving precepts concerning Christian virtues, by showing his gratitude for their generosity towards him, chapter 4.

units.la: Caput Primum.
units.tr: Chapter One.

units.la: Praeter Epistolae praefationem, quae versu 1. & 2. continetur. Capitis tres sunt partes: Prima est confirmatio Philippensium in fide, in qua etiam Apostolus certos eos reddit de sua erga ipsos dilectione, ad vers. 12. Altera est remotio scandali, ne offenderentur Philippenses afflictionibus quibus ipse exercebatur, ad vers. 27. Tertia est hortatio ad pergendum in cursu pietatis pede inoffenso, ad finem.
units.tr: Apart from the preface of the Epistle, which is contained in verses 1 and 2, the chapter has three parts. The first is the confirmation of the Philippians in the faith, in which the Apostle also assures them of his love for them, to verse 12. The second is the removal of a stumbling block, so that the Philippians would not be offended by the afflictions with which he himself was troubled, to verse 27. The third is an exhortation to press on in the course of godliness with an unstumbling foot, to the end.

units.la: Vers. 1.
units.tr: Verse 1.

units.la: Paulus & Timotheus servi Iesu Christi, omnibus sanctis in Christo Iesu, qui sunt Philippi, una cum episcopis ac diaconis.
units.tr: Paul and Timothy, servants of Jesus Christ, to all the saints in Christ Jesus who are at Philippi, together with the bishops and deacons.

units.la: Praefatio continetur directione Epistolae, & salutatione Philippensium. Directio Epistolae est a Paulo & Timotheo discipulo, tanquam testE Apostolicae diligentiae, in hac sua ad Ecclesiam Philippensium parenesi, ejusque Episcopos & Diaconos, id est, Pastores, & alios rerum Ecclesiasticarum Moderatores, qui Pastoribus adjuncti erant, ad vitae & morum, aliarumque necessitatum Ecclesiae, curationem.
units.tr: The preface contains the address of the Epistle and the greeting to the Philippians. The address is from Paul and Timothy, his disciple, as witnesses of apostolic diligence, in this exhortation of his to the Church of the Philippians, and to its bishops and deacons, that is, the ministers and the other administrators of Church affairs who were joined with the ministers for the care of the life and conduct of the Church and of its other needs.

units.la: Vers. 2.
units.tr: Verse 2.

units.la: Gratia vobis & pax a Deo Patre nostro, & Domino Iesu Christo.
units.tr: Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.

units.la: Salutatio continet Apostolicam benedictionem, qua optat illis Gratiam & Pacem a Deo per Christum, sicut optare solebat aliis Ecclesiis ad quas scribebat. Nota erat satis huic Ecclesiae autoritas Apostoli: aestimatione enim & gratia apud Philippenses plurimum valebat; breviorem idcirco esse in autoritate sua apud eos confirmanda, & benevolentia ipsorum erga se comparanda, consentaneum erat.
units.tr: The greeting contains the apostolic blessing, by which he wishes them grace and peace from God through Christ, as he was accustomed to wish to other Churches to which he wrote. The authority of the Apostle was already well known to this Church, for he was held in high esteem and favour among the Philippians; it was therefore fitting that he should be briefer in confirming his authority among them and in securing their goodwill towards himself.

units.la: Vers. 3.
units.tr: Verse 3.

units.la: Gratias ago Deo meo cum summa memoria vestri,
units.tr: I thank my God with every remembrance of you,

units.la: Prima pars Capitis, in qua confirmat Philippenses in fide Evangelii, & de sua dilectione erga eos, argumentis septem. Propositio confirmanda est, Debetis corroborari, seu confirmari in fide: Argumentum primum, Status vester in gratia Dei dignus est, pro quo Deo jugiter gratias agam, quoties vestri meminerim. Ergo in fide corroborari debetis.
units.tr: The first part of the chapter, in which he confirms the Philippians in the faith of the Gospel and speaks of his love for them, by seven arguments. The proposition to be confirmed is: you ought to be strengthened, or confirmed, in the faith. The first argument: your state in the grace of God is worthy that I should continually give thanks to God for it whenever I remember you. Therefore you ought to be strengthened in the faith.

units.la: Verf. 4. ( Semper in omni precatione mea pro omnibus vobis cum gaudio preces faciens )
units.tr: Verse 4. ( Always in every prayer of mine, making my requests for all of you with joy )

units.la: Arg. 2. Adeo persuasum mihi est de salute vestra, ut non nisi cum gaudio possim pro vobis precari. Ergo.
units.tr: Argument 2. I am so persuaded of your salvation that I can pray for you only with joy. Therefore.

units.la: Verf. 5. Super vestri in Euangelio participatione, à primo die usque ad hoc tempus:
units.tr: Verse 5. For your participation in the Gospel from the first day until now:

units.la: Arg. 3. Postquam vocati estis ad societatem Euangelii constanter gestistis vos: sicut Fideles & Sanctos decebat, ut mihi semper suavissima fuerit communio vestra & societas in Euangelio. Ergo.
units.tr: Argument 3. Since you were called to the fellowship of the Gospel, you have conducted yourselves steadfastly, as befits faithful and holy people, so that your fellowship and partnership in the Gospel have always been most sweet to me. Therefore.

units.la: Verf. 6. Persuasum habens hoc ipsum, fore ut qui coepit in vobis opus bonum, perficiat usque ad diem Iesu Christi:
units.tr: Verse 6. Being confident of this very thing, that he who began a good work in you will complete it until the day of Jesus Christ:

units.la: Arg. 4. Persuasum habeo, Deum opus specialis gratiae inchoasse in vobis, & non deserturum opus illud suum in vobis, donec illud absolverit in vestra perseverantia, & absolutum ostenderit in adventu Christi: Ergo corroborari debetis in fide.
units.tr: Argument 4. I am persuaded that God has begun a work of special grace in you, and will not abandon his work in you, but will bring it to completion in your perseverance, and will show it finished at the coming of Christ. Therefore you ought to be strengthened in the faith.

units.la: Verf. 7. Sicut justum est ut ego id sentiam de omnibus vobis, propterea quod animo teneam vos, & in vinculis meis & in defensione & confirmatione Euangelii, vos inquam, omnes una mecum fuisse gratiae meae participes:
units.tr: Verse 7. It is right for me to think this of you all, because I hold you in my heart, both in my chains and in the defence and confirmation of the Gospel; you, I say, all of you, have been partakers of grace with me:

units.la: Arg. 5 Confirmans superius. Æquum est ut ita de vobis sentiam, quippe qui ex certis indiciis compertum habeam, vos vere fideles, & viva Christi membra esse? Cujus rei signum est, quod animo & opere participes fueritis, factae mihi gratiae, (id est, passionum mearum, quas per Dei gratiam sustinui pro Euangelio, quando in vinculis jacebam) & participes etiam laborum meorum, quos in defendendo & propagando Euangelio exantlavi: Ergo corroborari in fide debetis.
units.tr: Argument 5, confirming what was said above. It is fitting that I should think this of you, since I have clear evidence that you are truly faithful and living members of Christ? The sign of this is that you have shared in the grace given to me (that is, in my sufferings, which I endured for the Gospel by the grace of God when I lay in chains), and also in my labours, which I undertook in defending and spreading the Gospel. Therefore you ought to be strengthened in the faith.

units.la: Verf. 8. Testis enim mihi est Deus quàm propense amem vos omnes in visceribus Iesu Christi.
units.tr: Verse 8. For God is my witness, how I long for you all with the affection of Jesus Christ.

units.la: Arg. 6. Testis est Deus, qui animum meum vobis agglutinavit, quantopere in visceribus Christi, seu Christianae dilectionis affectu intimo, vos diligam, vestràque societate frui cupiam: Confirmari igitur in fide, & de mea erga vos dilectione debetis.
units.tr: Argument 6. God is the witness, who has bound my heart to you, how greatly I love you in the bowels of Christ, that is, with the inward affection of Christian love, and how much I desire to enjoy your fellowship. Therefore you ought to be confirmed in the faith and to believe in my love for you.

units.la: Verf. 9. Et hoc precor, ut charitas vestra adhuc magis ac magis redundet in cognitione, & omni sensu:
units.tr: Verse 9. And this I pray, that your love may abound still more and more in knowledge and in all discernment:

units.la: Arg. 7. Sicut agnosco in vobis non mediocrem fidem & charitatem, sensumque rerum divinarum experientiâ confirmatum, sic sub spe futuri incrementi oro, ut abundet magis magisque charitas vestra ex abundantiori cognitione & sensu dilectionis Dei erga vos in Christo: Ergo nisi meam, de vobis spem, & pro vobis, orationem assiduam minoris faciatis quam par est, in fide corroborari debetis.
units.tr: Argument 7. As I recognise in you no small faith and love, and a sense of divine things confirmed by experience, so with hope of future growth I pray that your love may abound more and more from a fuller knowledge and sense of God's love towards you in Christ. Therefore, unless you value my hope concerning you and my constant prayer for you less than is right, you ought to be strengthened in the faith.

units.la: Verf. 10. Ut dignoscatis quæ discrepant, ut sitis syncepи, & inoffenso cursu pergatis ad diem usque Christi:
units.tr: Verse 10. So that you may approve the things that differ, and be sincere and without offence, and go on in your course until the day of Christ:

units.la: Verf. 11. Repleni fructibus justitiæ, qui insunt vobis per Iesum Christum, ad gloriam & laudem Dei.
units.tr: Verse 11. Filled with the fruits of righteousness, which are in you through Jesus Christ, to the glory and praise of God.

units.la: Fines ostendit hujus precationis suæ quatuor, & simul tot alios precationis suæ articulos addit: 1. Ut valeant discrepantia explorare, id est, discernere verum à falso in doctrina, & bonum à malo in vita instituenda: & id quod excellentius est eligere: 2. Ut sint sinceri sine mistura humanarum traditionum in cultu & corde, simul etiam, in vita & moribus puri: 3. Ut & inoffenso pede, & sine offendiculo aliis posito, ambulent & profectus faciant in fide in occursum Domini: 4. Ut repleantur fructibus justitiæ, qui oriuntur ex fide in Christum, & in gloriam Dei tendunt.
units.tr: He sets out four ends of this prayer of his, and at the same time adds as many further points to his prayer: (1) that they may be able to test what differs, that is, to distinguish truth from falsehood in doctrine and good from evil in the conduct of life, and to choose what is more excellent; (2) that they may be sincere, without any admixture of human traditions in worship and in heart, and at the same time pure in life and conduct; (3) that they may walk with an unstumbling foot, and without placing a stumbling block before others, and make progress in faith as they come to meet the Lord; (4) that they may be filled with the fruits of righteousness, which arise from faith in Christ and tend to the glory of God.

units.la: Secunda Pars,
units.tr: Second Part,

units.la: Verf. 12. Volum autem vos scire, fratres, quæ mihi acciderunt, magis ad profectum Euangelii evenisse:
units.tr: Ver. 12. But I want you to know, brothers, that what has happened to me has turned out rather for the progress of the gospel:

units.la: Secunda pars Capitis, in qua removet scandalum quod objici ipsis fortè posset ab afflictionibus suis, in quibus pro Euangelio versabatur; idque præstat propositis Arg. 9. Quæ probant non debere Philippenses Apostoli afflictionibus offendi.
units.tr: The second part of the chapter, in which he removes the stumbling block that might be raised against them because of his afflictions, in which he was engaged for the gospel. He does this with the nine arguments set out below, which prove that the Philippians ought not to be offended by the Apostle's afflictions.

units.la: Argum. 1. generalius: Afflictiones meæ evenerunt ad profectum Euangelii, & non ad ejus impedimentum: Ergo iis non debetis offendi.
units.tr: Argument 1, more general: My afflictions have turned out for the progress of the gospel and not for its hindrance. Therefore you ought not to be offended by them.

units.la: Verf. 13. Adeo ut vincula mea in Christo celebria sint in toto prætorio, ac reliquis omnibus locis: Arg. 2. specialius. Causa Euangelii pro qua passus sum, est celebrior facta, & in aula Neronis, & in aliis locis, ex afflictionibus meis. Ergo iis non debetis offendi, sed ex mea in vinculis Constantia corroborati potiùs.
units.tr: Ver. 13. So that my chains in Christ have become known throughout the whole praetorium and in all the other places: Argument 2, more specific. The cause of the gospel, for which I have suffered, has become more widely known, both in Nero's court and in other places, through my afflictions. Therefore you ought not to be offended by them, but rather strengthened by my constancy in chains.

units.la: Verf. 14. Et plerique ex fratribus in Domino, freti vinculis meis, magis audeant impavidè sermonem loqui.
units.tr: Ver. 14. And most of the brothers in the Lord, emboldened by my chains, dare all the more to speak the word fearlessly.

units.la: Arg. 3. Plures ex fratribus animati sunt ad Euangelium liberius prositendum & praedicandum. Ergo non debetis cruce mea offendi, sed aliorum exemplo edocti, confirmari potiùs in fide,
units.tr: Argument 3. Many of the brothers have been encouraged to proclaim and preach the gospel more freely. Therefore you ought not to be offended by my cross, but instructed by the example of others, and rather strengthened in faith.

units.la: Verf. 15. Ac nonnulli quidem per invidiam & contentionem, nonnulli verò etiam propensa voluntate Christum praedicant.
units.tr: Ver. 15. Some indeed preach Christ out of envy and rivalry, but others also with a good will.

units.la: Verf. 16. Alii quidem, inquam, per contentionem Christum annuntiant non pure, existimantes sese afflictionem addere vinculis meis:
units.tr: Ver. 16. Some, I say, proclaim Christ out of rivalry, not purely, supposing that they add affliction to my chains:

units.la: Verf. 17. Alii rursus ex charitate, scientes me ad defensionem Euangelii constitutum esse.
units.tr: Ver. 17. But others out of love, knowing that I am appointed for the defence of the gospel.

units.la: Arg. 4. Occupatione objectionis propositum. Etiamsi verum sit aliquos invidere meae gloriae, ex constantia in vinculis reportatae, quales sunt Judaei Pseudapostoli aliquot, qui litem mihi movere solent de legalibus suis Ceremoniis, & praedicant <bl>Christi</bl> Euangelium fermento suo admixtum, partim ut mihi molestiam, & invidiam creent, ab auditoribus suis, partim ne ego in quovis supra ipsos eminere videar, partim denique ut his rationibus afflictionem addant vinculis meis: Alii tamen sunt qui bono animo Christum praedicant, & meam causam ex dilectione sustinere nituntur, scientes me à Christo in defensionem Euangelii constitutum esse Apostolum, & jam vinculorum gloriâ ornatum. Ergo ob catenam meam non debetis erubescere, nec cruce meâ offendi.
units.tr: Argument 4, anticipating an objection. Even if it is true that some envy my glory, which I have won through constancy in chains, such as the Jewish false apostles, who are accustomed to stir up strife against me about their legal ceremonies, and who preach <bl>Christ's</bl> gospel mixed with their leaven: partly so that they may cause me trouble and envy among their hearers, partly so that I may not seem to stand out above them in anything, and partly finally so that by these means they may add affliction to my chains. Nevertheless there are others who preach Christ with a good spirit and strive to bear my cause out of love, knowing that I have been appointed by Christ as Apostle for the defence of the gospel, and already adorned with the glory of chains. Therefore you ought not to be ashamed of my chain, nor offended by my cross.

units.la: Verf. 18. Quid igitur? attamen quovis modo, sive in speciem, sive sincerè, Christus annuntiatur: de hoc quoque gaudeo, atque etiam gaudebo:
units.tr: Ver. 18. What then? Nevertheless, in every way, whether in pretence or in sincerity, Christ is proclaimed; in this I rejoice, and I will also rejoice:

units.la: Arg. 5. Ego sùsque deque habeo quo fine Æmuli mei Euangelium praedicent; de hoc gaudeo, quod Christi nomen ex meis vinculis, & ex praedicatione aliorum, quali quali, inclaruerit. Ergo etiam & vos mecum laetari debetis, nec vinculis meis offendi.
units.tr: Argument 5. I care nothing for the purpose for which my rivals preach the gospel; I rejoice in this, that the name of Christ has become renowned, however it may be, through my chains and through the preaching of others. Therefore you too ought to rejoice with me and not be offended by my chains.

units.la: Verf. 19. Novi enim fore, ut hoc mihi cedat saluti per vestras preces, & subministrationem Spiritus Iesu Christi,
units.tr: Ver. 19. For I know that this will turn out to my salvation through your prayers and the supply of the Spirit of Jesus Christ,

units.la: Arg. 6. Tantum abest, ut ego hac afflictione animo dejiciar, ut contra persuasum habeam fore, ut hæc quoque afflictio mihi ad salutem cedat, utque etiam interventu precum vestrarum Spiritus Christi copiosius indies mihi suppeditetur. Ergo nihil est quod meis vinculis offendamini.
units.tr: Argument 6. Far from my being cast down in spirit by this affliction, I am rather persuaded that this affliction too will turn out to my salvation, and that through the intercession of your prayers the Spirit of Christ will be supplied to me more abundantly every day. Therefore there is nothing for you to be offended at in my chains.

units.la: Verf. 20. Secundum intentam expectationem & spem meam, quod nulla in re pudefiam, sed cum omni libertate, ut semper, ita nunc quoque magnificabitur Christus in corpore meo, sive per vitam sive per mortem.
units.tr: Ver. 20. According to my eager expectation and hope, that I shall in no way be put to shame, but that with all boldness, as always, so now also Christ will be magnified in my body, whether through life or through death.

units.la: Hanc persuasionem explicat specialius, & addit Arg. 7. Exerto Capite sperans expecto, fore, ut non tantum nunquam pudefiam, tanquam destitutus auxilio Christi, sed etiam fore, ut libera prædicatione, & confessione Euangelii glorificetur Christus in me, sive vitam producero, sive Martyrio eam finiero: Ergo non debetis offendi meis afflictionibus.
units.tr: He explains this persuasion more particularly and adds Argument 7. Looking forward with outstretched head, I hope and expect that not only shall I never be put to shame, as one forsaken by Christ's help, but also that Christ will be glorified in me through the free preaching and confession of the gospel, whether I prolong my life or end it by martyrdom. Therefore you ought not to be offended by my afflictions.

units.la: Verf. 21. Mihi enim est Christus, & in vita & in morte lucrum.
units.tr: Ver. 21. For to me Christ is life, and in death gain.

units.la: Arg. 8. Paratus sum ad moriendum pro Christo, & perinde habeo sive vivam sive moriar, sive affligar, sive non, modo Christus glorificetur: siquidem Christus mihi pro lucro est, si diutius vixero, quia vivus Christum prædicaturus sum, & in lucro est Christus etiamsi brevi moriar, quia tum Christum aditurus sum, & cum eo perpetuo mansurus. Ergo & vos, nihil spectantes præter id quod in gloriam Christi cedat, mea catena non debetis offendi.
units.tr: Argument 8. I am ready to die for Christ, and I am equally content whether I live or die, whether I suffer or not, provided Christ is glorified. For Christ is my gain if I live longer, because while alive I shall preach Christ; and Christ is my gain even if I die soon, because then I shall go to Christ and remain with him for ever. Therefore you too, looking to nothing but what turns to the glory of Christ, ought not to be offended by my chain.

units.la: Verf. 22. Utrum verò vivere in carne mihi operæpretium sit, & quid eligam, ignoro.
units.tr: Ver. 22. But whether to live in the flesh is worth my while, and what I shall choose, I do not know.

units.la: Hoc argumentum confirmat ex eo quod difficilis esset futura electio, si optio ipsi daretur vivendi vel moriendi; nam ad vivendum nihil alliciebat, præter fructum operis sui in Ministerio: ad moriendum vero, alliciebat desiderium potiundi Christo, ita ut non facile statuere potuerit, utrum ex his eligeret. Unde perspicuum erat Apostolum suis vinculis non moveri, quamdiu in Christi gloriam cedere possent.
units.tr: He confirms this argument by the fact that the choice would be difficult if the option of living or dying were given to him. For nothing attracted him to life except the fruit of his work in the ministry; but to death he was drawn by the desire to possess Christ, so that he could not easily decide which of these he would choose. Whence it was clear that the Apostle was not moved by his chains, as long as they could turn to the glory of Christ.

units.la: Verf. 23 Coarctor enim utrinque, desiderans migrare, & esse cum Christo: nam id longè optimum est:
units.tr: Ver. 23. For I am hard pressed between the two, having the desire to depart and be with Christ, for that is far better:

units.la: Verf. 24. Sed permanere in carne, magis necessarium est propter vos,
units.tr: Ver. 24. But to remain in the flesh is more necessary for your sake,

units.la: Idem amplius illustrat, ostendens se coarctari maxime, ab altera parte desiderio fruendi Christo; quo nihil optabilius esse poterat, si suum emolumentum respiceret, ex altera vero parte in Ecclesiae utilitatem cessurum videbat, si vita animalis ipsi prorogaretur. Manifestum igitur erat mortem etiam gratam futuram, non afflictionem tantum pro Christo.
units.tr: He illustrates the same point further, showing that he is most strongly drawn on the one side by the desire to enjoy Christ, than which nothing could be more desirable if he regarded only his own advantage; and on the other side he saw that it would turn to the good of the Church if his animal life were prolonged. It was therefore plain that death too would be welcome to him, not merely affliction for Christ.

units.la: Vers. 25. Et hoc confisus, novi me mansurum esse, & una permansurum cum vobis omnibus, ad vestrum profectum & gaudium Fidei.
units.tr: Ver. 25. And being confident of this, I know that I shall remain and stay with you all, for your progress and joy in the faith,

units.la: Vers. 26. Ut abundet gloriatio vestra in Christo Iesu de me, mea rursus apud vos praesentia.
units.tr: Ver. 26. So that your boasting in Christ Jesus may abound through me, by my presence with you again.

units.la: Arg. 9. Ad amoliendum scandalum crucis ipsi incumbentis, insuper addit, Etiamsi paratus sim ad moriendum, ex revelatione tamen novi me nondum esse moriturum, sed mansurum in vivis, ad promovendam vestram salutem, & fidei vestrae gaudium, & quod sim ad vos rediturus, & vobiscum versaturus, ut gloriatio vestra in Christo abundet, ex observata & spectata Christi potentia in mei liberatione, & reditu. Ergo meis vinculis offendi non debetis, sed in fide confirmari potius.
units.tr: Argument 9. In order to remove the stumbling block of the cross that lies upon them, he adds further: even though I am ready to die, yet from revelation I know that I am not yet to die, but to remain among the living, to advance your salvation and the joy of your faith, and that I shall return to you and live with you, so that your boasting in Christ may abound, from the observed and evident power of Christ in my deliverance and return. Therefore you ought not to be offended by my chains, but rather strengthened in faith.

units.la: Tertia Pars.
units.tr: Third Part.

units.la: Vers. 27. Tantum ut dignum est Evangelio Christi, vos gerite, ut sive venero & videro vos, sive absens fuero, audiam de rebus vestris, vos perstare in uno Spiritu, uno pariter animo decertantes per fidem Evangelii.
units.tr: Verse 27. Only let your conduct be worthy of the gospel of Christ, so that whether I come and see you, or am absent and hear of your affairs, you stand fast in one Spirit, striving together with one mind for the faith of the gospel.

units.la: Tertia pars Capitis, continens hortationem ad constantiam in Fide, Ut unanimes perstent in professione Evangelii, decertantes per fidem, adversus omnes adversarios. Argumenta hortationis quae probant constanter esse perseverandum in fidei professione sunt novem.
units.tr: The third part of the chapter, containing an exhortation to constancy in the faith, that they should remain of one mind in the profession of the gospel, striving through faith against all adversaries. There are nine arguments of the exhortation which prove that one must persevere constantly in the profession of the faith.

units.la: Tantum Argumentum primum, Hoc unicum requiro a vobis, ut incedatis digne Evangelio, id est, ut vestram conversationem ad normam Doctrinae Evangelicae componatis, vestrum officium tantum respicientes, de reliquo vero securi. Ergo quicquid vobis accidere poterit, pergendum constanter in Fide Evangelii.
units.tr: Only The first argument: I require this one thing of you, that you walk worthily of the gospel, that is, that you order your conduct according to the rule of evangelical doctrine, looking only to your own duty and being free of care about the rest. Therefore, whatever may befall you, you must go on steadfastly in the faith of the gospel.

units.la: Digne Arg. 2. Dignitas Evangelii Christi, & vestrum jus in civitatem Sanctorum id postulat à vobis : Perseverandum ergo constanter.
units.tr: Worthily Argument 2. The dignity of the gospel of Christ, and your right to the citizenship of the saints, demand this of you. Therefore you must persevere constantly.

units.la: Vt sive ] Arg. 3. Ex vestra fortitudine & constantia in fide consolationem acceptURUS sum, sive absens sive praesens : Constanter ergo vobis pergendum.
units.tr: So that whether Argument 3. I shall receive comfort from your fortitude and constancy in the faith, whether absent or present. Therefore you must go on constantly.

units.la: Vers. 28. Nec ulla in re territos ab iis qui se opponunt: quod illis quidem est exitii indicium, vobis autem salutis: idque à Deo:
units.tr: Verse 28. And in nothing terrified by those who oppose you; which for them is indeed a sign of destruction, but for you of salvation, and that from God.

units.la: Arg. 4. Nulla causa est, propter quam terreamini adversariorum minis vel potentia : Pergendum igitur fortiter.
units.tr: Argument 4. There is no cause on account of which you should be terrified by the threats or power of adversaries. Therefore you must press on bravely.

units.la: Arg. 5. Imminentis omnibus vestris persecutoribus perditionis praesagium est, quod hostili sint adversus vestram Ecclesiam animo: Ergo sine metu perseverandum est vobis.
units.tr: Argument 5. For all your persecutors, the omen of their ruin is that they are hostile to your Church. Therefore you must persevere without fear.

units.la: Arg 6. Constans vestra defensio Euangelii adversus oppugnatores, indicium est & signum firmissimum victoriae & salutis à Deo, vobis Euangelii defensoribus concedendae : Confidenter igitur perseverandum.
units.tr: Argument 6. Your steadfast defence of the gospel against its assailants is a sure sign and token of the victory and salvation from God to be granted to you, the defenders of the gospel. Therefore you must persevere with confidence.

units.la: Arg. 7. A Deo procedit ex speciali consilio ad salutem vestram qui defenditis Euangelium, quod cum adversariis committamini : Constanter ergo pergendum est vobis.
units.tr: Argument 7. He who defends the gospel proceeds from God by a special counsel for your salvation, in that you are matched against adversaries. Therefore you must go on constantly.

units.la: Vers. 29. Quia vobis datum est in Christi negotio, non solùm in eum credere, sed etiam pro eo affligi:
units.tr: Verse 29. For to you it has been granted, on behalf of Christ, not only to believe in him, but also to suffer for him.

units.la: Arg. 8. Datum est donum singulare vobis, præ multis aliis fidelibus, idque propter CHRISTI meritum, ut non tantùm credatis in CHRISTUM, sed etiam jam passi, vel postea passuri, estis pro fide CHRISTI.
units.tr: Argument 8. A singular gift has been given to you, above many other faithful, and that on account of the merit of Christ: that you not only believe in Christ, but also, having already suffered or being about to suffer, you are suffering for the faith of Christ.

units.la: Vers. 30. Idem certamen sustinendo quale vidistis in me, & nunc auditis de me.
units.tr: Verse 30. Having the same conflict which you saw in me, and now hear to be in me.

units.la: Arg. 9. Habetis me socium & commilitonem in afflictionibus vestris, qui, ut nostis, & Philippis, & alibi saepius, multa passus sum, & nunc Romae patior vincula : Ergo vobis sine metu pergendum in fide, & professione Euangelii.
units.tr: Argument 9. You have me as a companion and fellow soldier in your afflictions, who, as you know, both at Philippi and elsewhere very often, suffered many things, and now at Rome I suffer bonds. Therefore you must go on in the faith and profession of the gospel without fear.

units.la: Caput Secundum.
units.tr: Chapter Two.

units.la: Hilippenses armatos contra hostes, hortatur Apostolus ad concordiam cum fratribus.
units.tr: The Apostle exhorts the Philippians, who are armed against enemies, to concord with the brethren.

units.la: Capitis duae sunt partes: Prima continet hortationem ad mutuam concordiam, ad verf. 19. Altera continet ipsorum consolationem. Ad Concordiam suadendam Argumenta affert 15. Quae omnia probant concordiam in fide, charitate, & studio bonorum operum colendam.
units.tr: The chapter has two parts. The first contains the exhortation to mutual concord, up to verse 19. The second contains their consolation. To persuade them to concord he brings fifteen arguments. All of them prove that concord must be cultivated in faith, in love, and in zeal for good works.

units.la: Verf. 1. Siqua igitur consolatio est in Christo, si quod solatium charitatis, si qua communio Spiritus, si quae viscera ac miserationes,
units.tr: Verse 1. If there is therefore any consolation in Christ, if any comfort of love, if any fellowship of the Spirit, if any bowels and mercies,

units.la: Argumentum primum valde patheticum est, Cujus sensus est, Ego vos obnixe rogo, ut concordiam inter vos colatis, per vestra officia, & omnia charissima, vos obtestans: Ergo, Si vel Apostolica exhortatio apud vos locum ullum habeat, vel si ullam experti estis consolationem in Christo, Si mihi vincto solatium aliquod a vobis expectari potest, Si vobis mecum aliqua est Spiritus communio: Si vultis aliquam misericordiam erga me ostendere, Concordia inter vos mutua colenda est.
units.tr: The first argument is very emotional. Its sense is this: I earnestly beg you, and entreat you by your duties and by everything most dear to you, to cultivate concord among yourselves. Therefore, if the apostolic exhortation has any weight with you, if you have ever felt any consolation in Christ, if any comfort can be expected from you by me in my chains, if there is any fellowship of the Spirit between you and me, and if you wish to show any mercy towards me, then mutual concord among you must be cultivated.

units.la: Verf. 2. Explete meum gaudium, ut itidem sitis affecti, eandem charitatem habentes, unanimes, & sententiis uni.
units.tr: Verse 2. Fulfil my joy, that you be likeminded, having the same love, being of one accord, of one mind.

units.la: Arg. 2. Gaudium mihi jam variis modis creastis, quod superest, si concordiam coluerítis, gaudium meum complebitis: Ergo studendum ut eadem credatis, & eadem velitis, seu ut unanimes in charitate idem sapiatis, pariterque sitis affecti, animis & cordibus inter vos uniti: Atque hic expresse habetur hortatio.
units.tr: Argument 2. You have already given me joy in various ways. What remains is that, if you cultivate concord, you will make my joy complete. Therefore you must strive to believe the same things and to will the same things, or to be of one accord in love, to think alike, and to be joined together in spirit and heart. Here the exhortation is expressly stated.

units.la: Verf. 3. Nihil gerite per contentionem, aut per inanem gloriam, sed ex modestia alium quisque se praestantiorem existimet.
units.tr: Verse 3. Let nothing be done through strife or vainglory, but in lowliness of mind let each esteem other better than themselves.

units.la: Subjungit quatuor adminicula, quae hortationis suae obedientiam reddant faciliorem, quaeque pro membris hortationis numerari, simul & pro argumentis ad Thesin probandam, inservire possunt.
units.tr: He adds four aids which make obedience to his exhortation easier, and which may be counted as parts of the exhortation and at the same time serve as arguments for proving the thesis.

units.la: Adminiculum primum, & primum membrum hortationis, Ut vitent contentionem & inanem gloriam, quibus si quis indulgeat concordiam statim rumpet. Hinc Arg. 3. Si contentioni, & inani gloriae renunciaveritis, ritis, concordiam coletis: Ergo nisi velitis hæc vitia profiteri, Concordia vobis colenda est.
units.tr: The first aid, and the first part of the exhortation, is that they should avoid strife and vainglory, to which, if anyone gives way, he will at once break concord. Hence Argument 3: If you renounce strife and vainglory, you will cultivate concord. Therefore, unless you wish to profess these vices, concord must be cultivated by you.

units.la: Sed ex ] Adminiculum 2. & membrum hortationis secundum, Ut studeant in humilitate animi alios sibiipsis ex animo præferre, tanquam meliores: quæ quidem cogitatio cum veritate, & sine deceptione consistere potest, quia nostra hæc de aliis nostris fratribus sententia, non requirit absolutum judicium, sed contenta est partim suspenso, partim negativo judicio, quo vel dicitur, forte comparatis comparandis ille me melior est, vel quantum de me & illo mihi cognitum est, non illi me præfero; sed illum mihi, nempe quia ignoro occulta cordis illius, sed mei cordis perversitatem video. Hinc Arg. 4. Si ex animi humilitate alios vobis præcellere existimaretis Concordiam colere poteetis. Ergo nisi superbiam vestram profiteri velletis, Concordia vobis colenda est: nam non æstimatur hominis præstantia ex donorum mensura, sed ex fidelitatis, sincerita-tis, & probitatis mensura.
units.tr: But in lowliness: the second aid and the second part of the exhortation is that they should strive, in humility of mind, to prefer others to themselves from the heart, as better. This thought can indeed stand together with truth and without deception, because this our judgment about our brethren does not require an absolute verdict. It is content with a judgment that is partly suspended and partly negative: either one says, "Perhaps, when the things to be compared are compared, he is better than I," or, "So far as I know of myself and of him, I do not prefer myself to him, but him to myself." The reason is that I do not know the hidden things of his heart, but I see the perversity of my own heart. Hence Argument 4: If you thought, from humility of mind, that others surpass you, you could cultivate concord. Therefore, unless you wished to profess your pride, concord must be cultivated by you. For a man's excellence is not measured by the measure of his gifts, but by the measure of his faithfulness, sincerity and uprightness.

units.la: Vers. 4. Ne sua quisque spectetis, sed unusquisque etiam quæ sunt aliorum.
units.tr: Verse 4. Look not every man on his own things, but every man also on the things of others.

units.la: Adminiculum 3. & tertium membrum hortationis, tendens ad humilitatem simul, & concordiam fovendam, Ut unusquisque consideret, non suas virtutes tantum, nec quæ ad commoditatem suam spectant tantum, sed etiam aliorum virtutes, & quæ ad uniuscujusque utilitatem spectant; sic enim alios pluris, nosmet vero minoris æstimaremus, & minus iniqui in omnibus futuri essemus: Hinc Arg. 5. Si aliorum virtutes & commoda sicut vestra spectaretis, concordiam facile coleretis: Ergo nisi iniqui esse, & haberi statuatis, Concordia vobis colenda est.
units.tr: The third aid and third part of the exhortation, tending both to foster humility and concord, is that each one should consider not only his own virtues, nor only what looks to his own advantage, but also the virtues of others and what looks to the advantage of each one. For in this way we would esteem others more highly and ourselves less, and we would be less unjust in all things. Hence Argument 5: If you looked on the virtues and advantages of others as you look on your own, you would easily cultivate concord. Therefore, unless you resolve to be unjust and to be thought so, concord must be cultivated by you.

units.la: Vers. 5. Itaque ut sit affectus in vobis qui fuit & in Christo Iesu.
units.tr: Verse 5. Let this mind be in you, which was also in Christ Jesus.

units.la: Adminiculum 4. & membrum quartum hortationis est exemplum CHRISTI, quod imitandum ipsis proponitur, ut humilitatem discant, & simul veram charitatem ad concordiam exerceant, Hic primum ingenere requirit ut idem sit affectus in iis, qui fuit in CHRISTO, Hinc Arg. 6. Tenemini sic animo affici erga vos invicem, sicut CHRISTUS est affectus erga nos, ipsius modestiam & morum suavitatem imitantes. Ergo debetis concordiæ inter vos impensè studere.
units.tr: The fourth aid, and the fourth part of the exhortation, is the example of Christ, which is set before them to be imitated, so that they may learn humility and at the same time exercise true love for the sake of concord. Here he first requires in general that the same disposition be in them which was in Christ. Hence Argument 6: You are bound to be disposed towards one another in the same way as Christ is disposed towards us, imitating his humility and the sweetness of his manners. Therefore you ought to devote yourselves earnestly to concord among yourselves.

units.la: Vers. 6. Qui quum esset in forma Dei, non duxit rapinam, parem esse cum DEO. Arg. 7. specialius attingit exempli in Christo propositi imitationem, verf. 6. & 7. in hunc sensum, Christus licet Patri æqualis, humiliavit se tamen ad mortem crucis, ut Pacem & Concordiam inter Patrem & nos conciliaret. Ergo multò magis debetis Concordiæ inter vos colendæ causa, vosmet humiliare. Describitur autem Christi excellentia hoc versu : Humiliatio vero ipsius, duobus sequentibus.
units.tr: Verse 6. Who, being in the form of God, thought it not robbery to be equal with God. Argument 7 touches more specifically on the imitation of Christ set before them, verses 6 and 7, in this sense: Christ, although equal to the Father, nevertheless humbled himself even to the death of the cross, so that he might reconcile peace and concord between the Father and us. Therefore, for the sake of cultivating concord among yourselves, you ought much more to humble yourselves. Christ's excellence is described in this verse; his humiliation is described in the two following verses.

units.la: In forma Dei ] Christi excellentia in se ante assumptam carnem in his 5. describitur: 1. Quod sit persona subsistens: 2. In forma Dei, id est, quod habeat essentiam Dei, naturalibus proprietatibus Deitatis imbutam, seu quod sit verus Deus. 3. Quod sit imago Patris substantialis. 4. Quod sit Patri æqualis per omnia; quia eandem habet cum Patre Deitatem: 5. Quod perfecte sciat se nullam Patri injuriam facere, dum æqualem se Patri affirmat, & nullam ei injuriam facturum fuisse, si non posito decreto de ipsius humiliatione, voluisset in gloria suæ Deitatis coram mundo se ostendere; hæc est Christi excellentia.
units.tr: In the form of God. Christ's excellence in himself, before he assumed flesh, is described in these five points: (1) that he is a subsisting person; (2) that in the form of God, that is, he has the essence of God, endowed with the natural properties of the Godhead, or that he is true God; (3) that he is the substantial image of the Father; (4) that he is equal to the Father in all things, because he has the same Godhead as the Father; (5) that he knows perfectly that he does no injury to the Father in affirming himself equal to the Father, and that he would not have done any injury to him, even if, the decree of his humiliation not having been made, he had willed to show himself before the world in the glory of his Godhead. This is Christ's excellence.

units.la: Vers. 7.
units.tr: Verse 7.

units.la: Sed ipse se exinanivit, forma servi accepta similis hominibus factus :
units.tr: But he emptied himself, taking the form of a servant, made in the likeness of men:

units.la: Vers. 8. Et habitu compertus ut homo, ipse se submisit, factus obediens usque ad mortem, mortem autem crucis.
units.tr: Verse 8. And being found in fashion as a man, he humbled himself, becoming obedient unto death, even the death of the cross.

units.la: Sequitur Christi voluntaria humiliatio, quæ exinanitio sui ipsius dicitur, non quod desierit esse in se, quod erat, sed quod gloriæ & majestatis suæ manifestationem seposuerit, & abdiderit in forma servi, quasi nullam habuisset, vel quali ita abjecisset, ut nec à mundo, imò nec ab oculatis suis servis, nisi per rimas verborum & operum conspici posset, quantum œconomia operis redemptionis postulabat.
units.tr: There follows Christ's voluntary humiliation, which is called emptying himself. This does not mean that he ceased to be what he was, but that he set aside the manifestation of his glory and majesty and hid it in the form of a servant, as if he had none, or as if he had so laid it aside that he could be seen, not by the world, nor even by his own eyewitnesses, except through the chinks of words and deeds, to the extent that the economy of the work of redemption required.

units.la: Gradus seu partes hujus voluntariæ humiliationis, seu exinanitionis sunt quinque, Primus gradus in eo consistit, quod sumpserit, seu assumpserit formam servi, seu veram naturam humanam, (qualis in servis vilissimis, seu infimæ sortis hominibus reperitur) naturamque humanam personali unione sibi univerit: hic se demisit à cœlo ad terram. Secundus gradus in eo consistit, Quod in humana natura demiserit se infra statum liberorum hominum, ad conditionem externam inter homines abjectissimam, id est, servilem: assumpsit enim formam servi.
units.tr: The degrees or parts of this voluntary humiliation, or emptying, are five. The first degree consists in his taking, or assuming, the form of a servant, that is, true human nature (such as is found in the lowest slaves, or men of the meanest rank), and uniting human nature to himself in personal union. Here he came down from heaven to earth. The second degree consists in his lowering himself within human nature below the status of free men, to the most abject external condition among men, namely servile, for he took the form of a servant.

units.la: Similis ] Declarat veritatem incarnationis, quod factus sit similis nobis, sicut unus ex nobis, in naturæ humanæ partibus essentialibus, corpore pore & anima ; similis in proprietatibus naturæ humanæ naturalibus, & affectibus omnibus ; similis in infirmitatibus communibus, quæ speciem humanam sequuntur : Denique quod sit nobis in omnibus similis, excepto peccato.
units.tr: Made in the likeness: This declares the truth of the incarnation, that he was made like us, as one of us, in the essential parts of human nature, body and soul; like us in the natural properties of human nature and in all its affections; like us in the common infirmities that follow the human species. Finally, that he is like us in all things, apart from sin.

units.la: Habitu inventus ] Confirmat incarnationis veritatem, quod habitu compertus sit ut homo, nam omnes qui cum eo versati sunt, boni pariter & mali, omnibus modis quibus quivis homo comperitur homo, observarunt & comperierunt eum esse hominem verum, & certò cognoverunt, ex vera corporis humani forma & substantia, ex veris humanæ vitæ actionibus, verisque verè hominis proprietatibus, omnique habitu in quo invenitur ullus homo.
units.tr: Being found in fashion: This confirms the truth of the incarnation, that he was found in fashion as a man. For all who dealt with him, good and bad alike, observed him in every way in which any man is recognised as a man, and they found and knew for certain that he was a true man, from the true form and substance of a human body, from the true actions of human life, from the true properties of a man, and from every appearance in which any man is found.

units.la: Ipse se submisit ] Tertius gradus humiliationis in eo est, quod cum jam homo factus esset, nec nisi ex pacto voluntario ad manendum in terra, vel jugum legis (meris hominibus impositum) subeundum obligatus fuerit, (quippe non merus homo, licet verus homo, sed Deus in carne, cujus caro erat caro DEI, & idcirco DOMINUS legis, non sublex erat) se tamen ipse submisit, seu ex voluntaria œconomia, se Patre minorem in humiliationis statu fecit. (nam naturæ divinæ respectu, quæ eadem est Patris & filii, minor esse non potuit) jugumque legis, meris hominibus destinatæ, in se recepit, nec id solum, sed etiam absolute se submisit, ut faceret omnia quæ Pater imperaret ad hominum redemptionem perficiendam.
units.tr: He humbled himself: The third degree of humiliation is that, although he had already become man, and was bound only by a voluntary agreement to remain on earth, or to undertake the yoke of the law (imposed on mere men), (for he was not a mere man, though a true man, but God in the flesh, whose flesh was God's flesh, and therefore he was the Lord of the law, not subject to it), nevertheless he himself humbled himself, or by voluntary economy, made himself lesser than the Father in the state of humiliation. (For in respect of the divine nature, which is the same in Father and Son, he could not be lesser.) He took upon himself the yoke of the law, destined for mere men, and not only that, but he submitted himself absolutely, so that he would do all that the Father commanded to accomplish the redemption of men.

units.la: Factus obediens usque ] Quartus gradus in eo consistit. Quod susceptum jugum tota vita patienter gesserit, in omnibus mandata Patris exequens, usque ad mortem, seu depositionem vitæ humanæ, pro ovibus suis, ex mandato Patris.
units.tr: Becoming obedient unto: The fourth degree consists in this: that having taken up that yoke, he bore it patiently through his whole life, carrying out the Father's commands in all things, even unto death, that is, the laying down of his human life, for his sheep, by the Father's command.

units.la: Crucis ] Quintus gradus in eo est, quod ad violentam, maledictam, ignominiosissimam mortem crucis obediens fuerit.
units.tr: The cross: The fifth degree is that he was obedient to the violent, accursed and most ignominious death of the cross.

units.la: Vers. 9. Quapropter etiam Deus ipsum in summam extulit sublimitatem, ac donavit ei nomen quod est supra omne nomen:
units.tr: Verse 9. Wherefore God also hath highly exalted him, and given him a name which is above every name:

units.la: Vers. 10. Ut ad nomen Iesu omne genu se flectat, cælestium ac terrestrium, & subterraneorum:
units.tr: Verse 10. That at the name of Jesus every knee should bow, of things in heaven, and things in earth, and things under the earth:

units.la: Vers. 11. Omnisque lingua confiteatur Dominum esse Iesum Christum, ad gloriam Dei Patris.
units.tr: Verse 11. And that every tongue should confess that Jesus Christ is Lord, to the glory of God the Father.

units.la: Sequitur tribus his versibus CHRISTI propter nos humiliati secundum humanam naturam remuneratio, per ipsius exaltationem propter nos: Unde deducitur Arg. 3. in hunc sensum, Sicut Christus postquam se humiliavit ad reconciliandos Deo homines, pacemque inter partes confirmandam à Deo est exaltatus, & gloriâ coronatus: Sic etiam vobis Concordiæ in Ecclesia tuendæ causa, vosmet humiliantibus expectanda est exaltatio. Ergo si verum iter ad gloriam tenere vultis, imitamini Christum, & Concordiæ fovendæ causa vosmet humiliate.
units.tr: These three verses set out the reward of Christ, who was humbled for us according to his human nature, through his exaltation for our sake. From this an argument (the third) can be drawn, in this sense: Just as Christ, after he humbled himself to reconcile men to God and to confirm peace between the parties, was exalted by God and crowned with glory, so too for you, for the sake of preserving concord in the Church, exaltation awaits you if you humble yourselves. Therefore, if you wish to keep to the true path to glory, imitate Christ, and humble yourselves for the sake of cherishing concord.

units.la: Quapropter ] Sensus est, Quia Christus propter nos in nostra carne ultro se humiliavit, obediens factus usque ad mortem, Deus eum propter nos, in carne nostra etiam in summam extulit sublimitatem: Nam suscitato Christo à mortuis ad vitam gloriosam & immortalem, elevato ad supremum Cœlum, & collocato ad dextram suam in dignitate & imperio, supra omnes creaturas; dedit secundùm gratiosam suam voluntatem, & dispensationem negotii de salute nostra gratiosam, nomen supra omne nomen, glorificans Eum ea gloriâ quam olim habuit apud Patrem, (patefactâ scilicet gloria Deitatis, quæ prius occultabatur, & patefactâ hypostaticâ unione humanæ naturæ) imperans & efficiens, ut Christus crucifixus, ubique prædicaretur, dominaretur, adoraretur, invocaretur ut verus Deus, & unigenitus Dei Filius.
units.tr: Wherefore: The sense is this: because Christ willingly humbled himself for our sake in our flesh, becoming obedient unto death, God, for our sake, has also exalted him in our flesh to the highest majesty. For, having raised Christ from the dead to a glorious and immortal life, lifted him up to the highest heaven, and placed him at his right hand in dignity and rule, above all creatures, he has given him, according to his gracious will and the gracious ordering of the business of our salvation, a name above every name, glorifying him with that glory which he once had with the Father (namely, the glory of the Godhead, previously hidden, now revealed, and the hypostatic union of human nature being made manifest), commanding and bringing it about that Christ crucified should be preached everywhere, should rule, be adored, and be called upon as the true God and the only-begotten Son of God.

units.la: Ad nomen ] Efficaciam & effectum hujus exaltationis Christi sequuturum ostendit Apostolus, nempe; Quod omnis creatura tandem subjicienda sit Christo, ita ut nisi sponte se submittat, cogenda sit tandem, nomen, seu potestatem, autoritatem, & dominium ejus agnoscere (quod Metonymia Genuflexionis exprimitur). Quod ad Cœlestia attinet, non est dubium, quin Angeli, & Spiritus Justorum ei genuflectant, hoc est, ei se submittant; nam Spiritus genua proprie non habent. Quod ad terrestria; Omnes homines tandem confitebuntur, si non sponte, saltem invīti & coacti, Christum qui crucifixus elt, Judicem esse, & Dominum, & Dei Filium. Denique, quod ad subterranea attinet: (quo nomine intelliguntur Dæmones, & spiritus damnatorum, qui jam sunt in carcere) sistendi sunt impuri omnes spiritus illi, ad ejus Tribunal, nolint velint, & sententiam Judicis cum agnitione Majestatis, & Dominii ejus admissuri. Atque ita tandem genuflectent, etiam omnes ejus hostes, quicunque nunc se ei opponunt.
units.tr: At the name: The Apostle shows the efficacy and effect that will follow from this exaltation of Christ, namely, that every creature is finally to be made subject to Christ, so that, unless it submits willingly, it will at last be compelled to acknowledge his name, that is, his power, authority and dominion (which is expressed by the metonymy of bending the knee). As far as heavenly things are concerned, there is no doubt that the angels and the spirits of the just bow the knee to him, that is, submit themselves to him; for spirits do not properly have knees. As far as earthly things are concerned, all men will at last confess, if not willingly, at least unwillingly and under compulsion, that Christ, who was crucified, is Judge, and Lord, and Son of God. Finally, as far as things under the earth are concerned (by which name demons and the spirits of the damned, who are already in prison, are understood), all those unclean spirits must be brought before his tribunal, whether they will or not, and must accept the sentence of the Judge, with acknowledgement of his majesty and dominion. And so in the end all his enemies too, whoever now set themselves against him, will bow the knee.

units.la: Omnisque lingua ] Denique, ne agnitio nominis, & potestatis Christi tota differri videatur ad ultimum usque judicium, declarat fore ut omnis lingua, seu ex omni gente & natione, gloriam accepturus sit Christus, vel in voluntaria conversorum ex Gentibus agnitione & professione, quod CHRISTUS sit Dominus, idque in gloriam PATRIS (qui vult honorari in FILII sui Unigeniti glorificatione) vel quia multi non convertentur fore tandem in Die Judicii, ut clarissimè & plenissimè patefiat CHRISTI dominium, cum omnes Creaturæ in Cœlo, Terra, & Inferno ipsum agnoscent DOMINUM.
units.tr: And every tongue: Lastly, lest the acknowledgement of the name and power of Christ should seem to be wholly deferred until the last judgement, he declares that every tongue, that is, people from every nation and race, will give glory to Christ, either by the willing acknowledgement and profession, by converts from the Gentiles, that Christ is Lord, and this to the glory of the Father (who wills to be honoured in the glorifying of his only-begotten Son); or, since many will not be converted, that on the Day of Judgement the dominion of Christ will be made most clearly and fully manifest, when all creatures in heaven, earth and hell will acknowledge him as Lord.

units.la: Verf. 12. Proinde, dilecti mei, sicut semper obedistis, non ut in præsentia mea solùm, sed nunc multò magis in absentia mea, cum timore ac tremore vestram ipsorum salutem conficite.
units.tr: Verse 12. Therefore, my beloved, as ye have always obeyed, not as in my presence only, but now much more in my absence, work out your own salvation with fear and trembling.

units.la: Arg. 9. Ad concordiam colendam, conclusionis forma ex superioribus deductum: Semper mihi auscultastis hactenus, & cum præsens essem, obedivistis meis exhortationibus. Ergo huic exhortationi ad Concordiam inter vos colendam obedire debetis multo magis in absentia mea, cum pauciora adjumenta ad ædificationem, & plures inimicos, qui vos in partes scindant, habetis.
units.tr: Argument 9. For cultivating concord, a form of conclusion drawn from what has gone before: You have always listened to me hitherto, and when I was present you obeyed my exhortations. Therefore you ought to obey this exhortation to cultivate concord among yourselves much more in my absence, since you have fewer aids to edification and more enemies who would split you into parties.

units.la: Cum timore ] Arg. 10. Cursus ad salutem inchoatus, in studio justitiæ conscendus est vobis in timore & tremore, ne offendatis in via, vel DEUM ullo modo provocetis ad iram: Ergo colenda est vobis inter vos Concordia; nempe in Fide, Charitate, & Studio bonorum Operum, ut verf. 2. habetur.
units.tr: With fear: Argument 10. The course towards salvation, begun, must be run by you in the pursuit of righteousness, with fear and trembling, lest you stumble on the way, or in any way provoke God to anger. Therefore concord must be cultivated among you, namely in faith, charity and the zeal for good works, as is stated in verse 2.

units.la: Verf. 13. Deus enim is est qui efficit in vobis, & ut velitis, & ut efficiatis, pro gratuita sua benevolentia.
units.tr: Verse 13. For it is God who works in you both to will and to work, for his gracious goodwill.

units.la: Arg. 11. Confirmans superius, Nihil habetis in vobis propter quod superbiatis, aut alii alios, in contentione contemnatis: Sed omne bonum in vobis est à DEO, qui & ipsum velle bonum, & ipsum agere efficit in vobis, pro gratuita sua benevolentia: Ergo colenda est concordia in fide, charitate & studio bonorum operum, & vobis conficiendus est inchoatus salutis cursus in timore & tremore, ne DEUM in vobis operantem provocetis.
units.tr: Argument 11. Confirming what was said above: you have nothing in yourselves for which to be proud, or for which to despise one another in contention. But every good thing in you is from God, who causes in you both the willing of good and the working of it, for his gracious goodwill. Therefore harmony is to be cultivated in faith, love and zeal for good works, and the course of salvation that has begun is to be completed by you in fear and trembling, lest you provoke God who works in you.

units.la: Verf. 14. Omnia facite absque murmurationibus ac disceptationibus.
units.tr: Verse 14. Do all things without murmurings and disputings.

units.la: Arg. 12. Hortationis forma propositum, Alieni esse debetis tum ab omni maligna & occulta simulatate, tum ab apertis contentionibus & rixis: Ergo colenda est inter vos concordia in fide, &c.
units.tr: Argument 12. A form of exhortation with its proposition: you ought to keep far from all malicious and hidden duplicity, and from open contentions and quarrels. Therefore harmony among you is to be cultivated in faith, etc.

units.la: Verf. 15. Ut sitis irreprehensi & sinceri, Filii, inquam, Dei, inculpati, in medio nationis pravæ ac perversæ; inter quos homines splendetis ut luminaria in mundo,
units.tr: Verse 15. That you may be blameless and sincere, sons, I say, of God, without rebuke, in the midst of a crooked and perverse nation, among whom you shine as lights in the world,

units.la: Vers. 16. Sermonem vitæ prætendentes: ut gloriari possim in die Christi me non frustrà cucurrisse, nec in vanum laborasse.
units.tr: Verse 16. Holding forth the word of life, that I may rejoice in the day of Christ that I have not run in vain, nor laboured in vain.

units.la: Arg. 13. Studendo concordiæ, & vitando contentiones (& non aliter) præstabitis vos verè Christianos in conspectu impiorum; Ergo colenda est vobis concordia, & vitandæ contentiones: generalia autem quæ hic requirit officia Christianorum, aliis atque aliis expressionibus commendat, Debetis enim, inquit, inculpati esse, qui jure à quoquam argui non possitis, & simplices seu sinceri, in quibus innocentia & candor appareat, & ut filii Dei inculpati Deum patrem vestrum sanctitate & innocentia referre, ut ne hostes pravi & perversi jure reprehendant, sive culpent quidquam in vobis; debetis tanquam luminaria spiritualia majora & minora, verbo & opere, exemplaria justitiæ vos mundo in tenebris jacenti ostendere. Denique illuminati à Sole justitiæ in Euangelio, seu sermone Dei vivifico, debetis hujus sermonis lucem, veritatem & virtutem verbis & operibus pereunti mundo præferre & exhibere, ut salventur, quantum fieri potest.
units.tr: Argument 13. By striving for harmony and avoiding contentions (and not otherwise) you will show yourselves truly Christian in the sight of the impious. Therefore harmony is to be cultivated by you and contentions avoided. He commends the general duties of Christians, which he requires here, in various expressions. For, he says, you ought to be blameless, so that you cannot rightly be accused by anyone; and sincere or simple, in whom innocence and candour appear; and as sons of God without blame, reflecting God your Father in holiness and innocence, so that the wicked and perverse enemies cannot rightly find fault or blame anything in you. As lights, greater and lesser spiritual lights, you ought to show by word and deed examples of righteousness to the world lying in darkness. Finally, enlightened by the Sun of righteousness in the Gospel, or the living word of God, you ought to hold forth and exhibit the light, truth and power of this word, by words and deeds, to the perishing world, so that they may be saved, as far as it can be done.

units.la: Ut gloriari Arg. 14. Si concordes vixeritis, & vos, ut decet fideles, geratis, gloriabor ego in salute vestra in die judicii, quando labores mei in Euangelio non frustra fuisse, sed ad vestram salutem cessisse comperientur: Ergo nisi & mihi, & vobis invideatis tantam felicitatem, concordiæ in fide, & studio bonorum operum, vobis incumbendum est.
units.tr: That I may rejoice. Argument 14. If you live in harmony and conduct yourselves as befits faithful people, I shall glory in your salvation on the day of judgement, when it will be found that my labours in the Gospel were not in vain but have turned to your salvation. Therefore, unless you grudge both me and yourselves so great a happiness, you must devote yourselves to harmony in faith and to zeal for good works.

units.la: Vers. 17. Quin etiam si pro libamento offerar super hostia sacrificioque fidei vestræ, gaudeo & gratulor omnibus vobis.
units.tr: Verse 17. Yea, if I am offered upon the sacrifice and service of your faith, I joy and rejoice with you all.

units.la: Vers. 18. Itidem autem & vos gaudete, & gratulamini mihi. Arg. 15. Consolationem includens, ne afflictionibus Apostoli contristentur, in hunc sensum, Ego per Euangelium adduxi vos ad Christum, tanquam sacrificium, ut mactatis affectibus vestris pravis, hostia sancta, & accepta Deo sistamini; Et jam si Martyrii mei sanguine, tanquam libamento addito, perfici poterit mei Ministerii, & vestræ fidei spirituale sacrificium, gauderem de meo bono, & gratularer vobis omnibus de vestro: Ergo vos mihi vicem rependite, & in unanimi sacrificii hujus perfectione gaudete, & de fructu laborum meorum mihi quidquid acciderit gratulamini: Quod idem est cum thesi, verf. 2. Gaudium meum explete, ut idem sapiatis, eandem charitatem habentes, &c.
units.tr: Verse 18. For the same cause also do ye joy, and rejoice with me. Argument 15. Including consolation, so that the Apostle's afflictions do not sadden them, in this sense: I have brought you through the Gospel to Christ as a sacrifice, so that, your evil affections being slain, you may stand as a holy victim acceptable to God. And now, if the perfecting of my ministry and of your faith as a spiritual sacrifice can be accomplished, with the blood of my martyrdom added as a libation, I would rejoice in my own good and congratulate you all on yours. Therefore repay me in kind, rejoice in the perfecting of this unanimous sacrifice, and congratulate me on whatever befalls me from the fruit of my labours. This is the same as the thesis, verse 2. Fulfil my joy, that you may be of one mind, having the same love, etc.

units.la: Secunda Pars Capitis.
units.tr: Second Part of the Chapter

units.la: Verf. 19 Spero autem in Domino Iesu, me Timotheum brevi mitturum vobis, ut & ego bono sim animo, cognito statu vestro.
units.tr: Verse 19. But I trust in the Lord Jesus to send Timothy to you shortly, that I also may be of good comfort, when I know your state.

units.la: Secunda pars Capitis, in qua consolatur Philippenses, ex commendatione Timothei ad eos venturi; (addita spe adventus sui) & Epaphroditi jam profecti ad ipsos: opus enim erat Philippensibus his auxiliis adversus seductores, & male feriatos homines, qui ipsis insidiabantur, eisque negotium facesIebant:
units.tr: The second part of the chapter, in which he comforts the Philippians by commending the coming of Timothy to them (with hope of his own coming added), and of Epaphroditus, who has already been sent to them. For the Philippians needed these helps against seducers and idle, ill-living men, who lay in wait for them and gave them trouble.

units.la: Ut & ego Finem missionis Timothei ostendit Apostolus hunc esse, ut & illi consolationem caperent ex nuncio liberationis suiipsius à vinculis, ad eos perlato per Timotheum, & ut ipse per rediturum ab iis Timotheum consolationem etiam caperet ex nuncio, de prospero ipsorum statu.
units.tr: That I also. The Apostle shows that the purpose of Timothy's sending is that they may take comfort from the news of his own deliverance from chains, carried to them through Timothy, and that he himself may also take comfort from the news of their prosperous state, which Timothy would bring back from them.

units.la: Verf. 20. Neminem enim habeo pari animo praeditum, qui germanè res vestras curaturus sit.
units.tr: Verse 20. For I have no man likeminded, who will truly care for your state.

units.la: Argumenta commendationis Timothei sunt tria: 1. Quia nemo tam prompto & sincero animo affectus erat ad salutem, seu res ipsorum curandas, & ipsorum consolationem promovendam, quam Timotheus.
units.tr: There are three arguments for the commendation of Timothy: 1. because no one was so eagerly and sincerely disposed towards their salvation, or towards attending to their affairs and promoting their comfort, as Timothy was.

units.la: Verf. 21. Nam omnes quae sua ipsorum sunt quaerunt, non quae Christi Iesu.
units.tr: Verse 21. For all seek their own, not the things which are Jesus Christ's.

units.la: Arg. 2. Confirmans superius, quia cum omnes ferè alii qui cum ipso erant, commoda & quietem suam sequentes detrectabant tam longi itineris suscptionem ad Philippensium consolationem; solus Timotheus ad iter paratus fuerit, CHRISTI & Ecclesiae negotiis, commoda sua & quietem suam, posthabens.
units.tr: Argument 2. Confirming what was said above: because almost all the others who were with him pursued their own advantage and rest and shrank from undertaking so long a journey for the Philippians' comfort; Timothy alone was ready to go, setting aside his own advantage and rest for the affairs of Christ and the Church.

units.la: Verf. 22. Porrò probationem ejus nostu, quòd veluti cum patre filius, mecum servierit in Euangelio.
units.tr: Verse 22. But ye know the proof of him, that, as a son with the father, he hath served with me in the gospel.

units.la: Arg. 3. Commendationis, Quia non ita pridem Timotheus eodem cum Apostolo animo Philippis servierat in Euangelio, quod ipsis experientia notum erat.
units.tr: Argument 3, of commendation: because not long ago Timothy had served at Philippi in the Gospel with the Apostle in the same spirit, which was known to them by experience.

units.la: Verf. 23. Hunc igitur spero me missurum simulatque videro rerum mearum statum.
units.tr: Verse 23. Him therefore I hope to send presently, so soon as I shall see how it will go with me.

units.la: Verf. 24. Confido autem in Domino, me quoque citò venturum ad vos. Tempus missionis Timothei ostendit futurum, quam citò sibi de su-ex vinculis liberatione certò constiterit, Simul ipem facit adventus sui, sperabat enim fore propediem per Dei bonitatem, ut è carcere liberaretur.
units.tr: Verse 24. But I trust in the Lord that I also shall come shortly unto you. The verse shows that the time of Timothy's sending lies in the future, as soon as the Apostle is certain of his own deliverance from chains. At the same time it indicates his own coming, for he hoped that by God's goodness he would soon be released from prison.

units.la: Verf. 25. Sed necessarium duxi, Epaphroditum fratrem & collegam ac commilitonem meum, vestrum autem legatum, quique mihi subministravit quibus mihi opus erat, ad vos mittere.
units.tr: Verse 25. Yet I supposed it necessary to send to you Epaphroditus, my brother, companion in labour and fellow soldier, but your messenger, who ministered to my needs.

units.la: Fuit spes adventus Timothei, & ipsius etiam Apostoli, sequitur remissio Epaphroditi Pastoris Philippensium, qui pecuniam in Pauli usum attulerat, & Paulo in carcere ad tempus ministraverat: Hunc commendat quinque Epithetis honorificis: 1. Ut fratrem: 2. Cooperarium: 3. Commilitonem: 4. Fidelem legatum Philippensium: & 5. Publicum Ministrum necessitatis Apostoli in carcere.
units.tr: There was the hope of Timothy's coming, and of the Apostle's own coming too; there follows the sending back of Epaphroditus, pastor of the Philippians, who had brought money for Paul's use and had ministered to him in prison for a time. He commends him with five honourable epithets: 1. as brother; 2. fellow worker; 3. fellow soldier; 4. faithful messenger of the Philippians; and 5. public minister of the Apostle's need in prison.

units.la: Verf. 26. Quoniam expetebat omnes vos, & gravissimè angebatur, propterea quòd audissetis eum ægrotasse.
units.tr: Verse 26. For he longed after you all, and was full of heaviness, because ye had heard that he had been sick.

units.la: Causas remissionis ipsius ostendit quatuor, quæ & commendationis sunt Argumenta. Prima est Epaphroditi in Philippenses Pastoralis amor: 2. Solicitudo ejus de Philippensium dolore, quia sciebat eos de ipsius morbo certiores factos, & de recuperata valetudine nihil audisse.
units.tr: He shows four causes of his sending back, which are also arguments of commendation. The first is Epaphroditus' pastoral love for the Philippians; the second is his concern for their grief, since he knew they had been informed of his illness and had heard nothing of his recovered health.

units.la: Verf. 27. Et certè ægrotavit proximè mortem: sed Deus misertus est ejus, nec ejus solum, sed & mei, ne dolorem haberem super dolorem.
units.tr: Verse 27. For indeed he was sick nigh unto death, but God had mercy on him; and not on him only, but on me also, lest I should have sorrow upon sorrow.

units.la: Rumorem de Epaphroditi morbo confirmat, & commendat specialem Dei gratiam factam, & erga Epaphroditum, & erga se, qua Deus curabat, restituendum Epaphroditum, ad sanitatem ne Apostolus nimis affligeretur.
units.tr: He confirms the report of Epaphroditus' illness, and commends the special grace of God shown both to Epaphroditus and to himself, by which God cared to restore Epaphroditus to health, lest the Apostle be too greatly afflicted.

units.la: Verf. 28. Eo studiosius itaque eum misi, ut quum videretis eum rursus, gaudeatis, & ego magis vacem dolore,
units.tr: Verse 28. I sent him therefore the more carefully, that, when ye see him again, ye may rejoice, and that I may be the less sorrowful.

units.la: Tertia causa eum remittendi, fuit gaudium Philippensium; Quarta causa fuit levatio ægritudinis Apostoli, qui in Philippensium gratiam maluit se privari Epaphroditi servitio, alioqui perneccssario, quam ferre ut illi diutius carerent suo ministro.
units.tr: The third cause of sending him back was the joy of the Philippians; the fourth was the relief of the Apostle's distress, for he preferred, for the Philippians' sake, to be deprived of Epaphroditus' service, though it was otherwise very necessary, rather than bear that they should go without their minister for longer.

units.la: Verf. 29. Excipite igitur eum in Domino cum omni gaudio: & tales in pretio habete. Hinc hortatur ut eum excipiant sicut dignus erat, & tanquam gemmam aut thesaurum, eum & similes Ministros in pretio habeant.
units.tr: Verse 29: "Receive him therefore in the Lord with all joy, and hold such men in honour." Here he urges them to receive him as he deserved, and to hold him and men like him in high esteem, as a jewel or a treasure.

units.la: Verf 30. Nam propter opus Christi accessit ad mortem usque, non habita vitæ ratione, ut suppleret defectum vestri erga me officii.
units.tr: Verse 30: "For because of the work of Christ he came close to death, not regarding his life, so that he might supply what was lacking in your service to me."

units.la: Hortationis rationes addit quatuor: Primò, Quia opus CHRISTI peregerat in Apostolo consolando: 2. Quia cum periculo vitæ Apostolo ministraverat: 3. Quia servitium susceптum prætulerat vitæ suæ, negligentior valetudinis suæ, quam rerum Apostoli curandarum: 4. Quia supplevérat absentiam Philippensium, qui (sicut ex debito tenebantur) studiosè cupiebant Apostoli necessitatibus inservire.
units.tr: He adds four reasons for the exhortation. First, because he had carried out the work of Christ in consoling the Apostle. Second, because he had served the Apostle at risk to his life. Third, because he had preferred the service he had undertaken to his own life, being less careful of his health than of attending to the Apostle's affairs. Fourth, because he had made up for the absence of the Philippians, who (as they were bound to do) eagerly desired to minister to the Apostle's needs.

units.la: Caput Tertium.
units.tr: Chapter 3.

units.la: [OC] Capite hortatur Apostolus, ut acquiescentes cum lætitia in solo Christo, seu solâ ejus justitiâ, gratia & virtute, tanquam ad sanctitatem & felicitatem abundè sufficiente, caveant sibi à Pseudapostolis, & sequantur exempla Apostolorum, & fidelium Ministrorum Christi.
units.tr: In this chapter the Apostle exhorts them to rest with joy in Christ alone, that is, in his righteousness, grace and power alone, as being fully sufficient for holiness and happiness, and to beware of false apostles, and to follow the examples of the Apostles and of the faithful ministers of Christ.

units.la: Hortationis primæ tria sunt membra tribus primis versibus proposita: Primum, Ut gaudeant in uno Christo. Secundum, Ut caveant sibi à falsis doctoribus judaizantibus. Tertium, Ut imitentur exemplum Apostolorum & Fidelium, qui Christo toti adhærent. Argumenta hortationis sunt novem, quæ omnia urgent, ut adhærentes Christo, imitentur Apostolorum exemplum.
units.tr: The first exhortation has three parts, set out in the first three verses: first, that they rejoice in Christ alone; second, that they beware of the false teachers who judaize; third, that they imitate the example of the Apostles and the faithful, who cling wholly to Christ. There are nine arguments for the exhortation, and all of them press the point that, cleaving to Christ, they should imitate the example of the Apostles.

units.la: Vers. Quod superest, Fratres mei, gaudete in Domino. Eadem scribere vobis, me quidem haud piget, vobis autem tutum est.
units.tr: Verse 1. Finally, my brethren, rejoice in the Lord. To write the same things to you is not irksome to me, and for you it is safe.

units.la: Primum hortationis membrum, ut gaudeant in Christo, id est, cum lætitia acquiescant in ejus justitia & virtute, nec sibi extra eum subsidia quærant ad salutem: proponitur autem illud quasi finis totius superioris doctrinæ, & Christianorum omnium officiorum compendium.
units.tr: The first part of the exhortation is that they rejoice in Christ, that is, that they rest with joy in his righteousness and power, and seek no help for salvation apart from him. This is set forth as the aim of all the preceding teaching and as a summary of all the duties of Christians.
