units.la: Eadem Argumentum primum, Per occupationem objectionis, Usque adeò utilis vobis est hæc hortatio, ut mihi non sit molestum eam saepius repetere & inculcare, nec debet vobis esse molestum eandem saepius audire: Ergo hanc doctrinam de Christi sufficientia penitus imbibentes, ipsi adhaerete.
units.tr: Eadem is the first argument, by anticipating an objection: this exhortation is so useful to you that it is no trouble to me to repeat and impress it often, and it ought not to be a trouble to you to hear the same thing often. Therefore, drink this doctrine of Christ's sufficiency deep into yourselves, and cling to it.

units.la: Verf. 2. Cavete canes, cavete malos operarios, cavete concisionem.
units.tr: Verse 2. Beware of dogs, beware of evil workers, beware of the concision.

units.la: Secundum membrum hortationis, Ut caveant sibi a Pseudapostolis, qui justitiam ex operibus & ceremoniis legis cum gratuita justificatione per fidem, nexu impossibili, conjungebant. Pseudapostoli ex Judaeis judaizantes, justitiam legis cum justitia fidei confundentes, & sic in justitia Christi sola non acquiescendum docentes, non sunt sancti Dei cultores, ut praefe ferunt, sed impuri canes oblatrantes purae Evangelii doctrinae, & sinceros Christi servos conviciis proscindentes: non sunt bonorum operum Patroni, sed mali operarii, non digni qui circumcisionis honore gaudeant, sed concisionis & perditionis autores audiant, quippe qui falsa sua doctrina seipsos & alios a Christo abscindunt & perdunt, a quibus, quia periculum imminet, vobis cavendum est: Ergo in Christi gratia & virtute sola acquiescendum est.
units.tr: The second part of the exhortation is that they beware of the false apostles, who joined together, in an impossible bond, righteousness from works and ceremonies of the Law and free justification by faith. These false apostles, Jews who judaize, confuse the righteousness of the Law with the righteousness of faith, and so teach that one must not rest in the righteousness of Christ alone. They are not worshippers of the holy God, as they pretend, but impure dogs, barking at the pure doctrine of the Gospel and tearing apart the sincere servants of Christ with insults. They are not patrons of good works, but evil workers, not worthy to rejoice in the honour of circumcision, but to be called the concision and authors of ruin, since by their false doctrine they cut off and destroy both themselves and others from Christ. Because danger threatens from them, you must beware of them. Therefore one must rest in the grace and power of Christ alone.

units.la: Verf. 3. Nos enim sumus circuncisio, qui Spiritu servimus Deo, & gloriamur in Christo Iesu, nec confidimus in carne.
units.tr: Verse 3. For we are the circumcision, who serve God in the Spirit, and glory in Christ Jesus, and put no confidence in the flesh.

units.la: Tertium membrum hortationis. In quo proponit exemplum Apostolorum & fidelium, qui Christo toti adhaerebant; Primo in genere, deinde specialius, subinde repetita exhortatione, usque ad verf. 18. Soli nos Apostoli, reliquique Fideles, titulo vere circumcisorum honorandi sumus, qui acquiescimus in Christi justitia, qui nempe 1. interno & spirituali cordis affectu Deum colimus: & 2. in Iesu Christo, ut unico & sufficiente Servatore gloriamur: 3. Non autem fiduciam nostram in ceremoniis, in carnali circumcisione, in externis privilegiis ullis, aut aliis ejusmodi praesidiis repositam habemus. Ergo vobis in sola Christi gratia & virtute nobiscum acquiescendum est, si vere circumcisi haberi vultis.
units.tr: The third part of the exhortation. Here he sets forth the example of the Apostles and the faithful, who clung wholly to Christ: first in general, then more particularly, and then, repeating the exhortation, down to verse 18. We Apostles, and the other faithful, are alone to be honoured with the title of true circumcision, since we rest in the righteousness of Christ. For (1) we worship God with an inward and spiritual affection of the heart; (2) we glory in Jesus Christ as our only and sufficient Saviour; (3) we do not place our confidence in ceremonies, in carnal circumcision, in any external privileges, or in any other such supports. Therefore, if you wish to be counted truly circumcised, you must rest with us in the grace and power of Christ alone.

units.la: Verf. 4. Quamquam ego habeo de quo confidam etiam in carne. Si quisquam alius videtur fiduciam habere in carne, ego maxime habeo:
units.tr: Verse 4. Though I have reason to trust even in the flesh. If anyone else seems to have confidence in the flesh, I have more:

units.la: A speciali Apostoli exemplo, per occupationem objectionis propositum: Ego Paulus, cui materia gloriandi in carnalibus, seu externis privilegiis, amplior quam Pseudapostolis ullis suppetit, rejecta omni confidentia in privilegiis vel operibus meis, acquiesco in solo CHRISTO, & in sanctitate ad salutem per solum CHRISTUM proficere studeo. Ergo etiam vobis in CHRISTI solius gratia & virtute mecum acquiescendum est.
units.tr: Proposed by way of anticipating an objection, from a particular example of the Apostle himself: I, Paul, who have more matter for boasting in carnal things, that is, in external privileges, than any of the false apostles, reject all confidence in my privileges or works, and rest in Christ alone, and strive to make progress in holiness unto salvation through Christ alone. Therefore you too must rest with me in the grace and power of Christ alone.

units.la: Verf. 5. Circumcisus octavo die, ex gente Israelis, tribu Benjamin, Hebraeus ex Hebraeis, religione Pharisaeus:
units.tr: Verse 5. Circumcised on the eighth day, of the stock of Israel, of the tribe of Benjamin, a Hebrew of Hebrews, as touching the law a Pharisee:

units.la: Verf. 6. Quod ad zelum attinet, persequens Ecclesiam: quod ad justitiam quae est in Lege irreprehensum.
units.tr: Verse 6. Concerning zeal, persecuting the Church; concerning the righteousness which is in the Law, blameless.

units.la: Suum hoc exemplum explicat luculenter, enumerando octo gloriationis carnalis causas, verf. 5. & 6. 1. Circumcisus sum, & in populum Dei relatus. 2. Circumcisus octavo die, secundum Legem praecise, non ut Proselyta quivis, sed ut natus Judaeus: 3. Ex nobilissimo populo Israelitico: 4. Et ex nobiliori tribu Israelitarum, nempe Benjamin, qui ex Rachel matre libera, una cum Josepho natus est, ex qua tribu primus rex Saul electus erat, ad cujus nomen datum videtur Apostolo nostro nomen Sauli: 5. Hebraeus ex Hebraeis sum, id est, ex ea familia quae non commiscuit se matrimonio cum Gentibus: 6. Pharisaeus eram, ex Secta inter Judaeos clarissima: 7. Zelo supra reliquos Pha-risaeos fervens eram, usque ad persecutionem Ecclesiae; hic zelus licet pessimus fuerit in se, in oculis tamen eorum qui zelo Legis gloriabantur, gloriosus erat: 8. In justitia externa, quae quidem ex Lege obtineri po-test, irreprensibilis eram coram hominibus.
units.tr: He explains this example clearly, listing eight causes for carnal boasting, verses 5 and 6. (1) I was circumcised and was counted among the people of God. (2) I was circumcised on the eighth day, according to the Law exactly, not as any proselyte would be, but as one born a Jew. (3) I come from the most noble people of Israel. (4) And from the nobler tribe of the Israelites, namely Benjamin, who was born of Rachel, a free mother, together with Joseph; from this tribe the first king, Saul, was chosen, and from his name our Apostle seems to have received the name Saul. (5) I am a Hebrew of Hebrews, that is, of that family which did not mix itself by marriage with the Gentiles. (6) I was a Pharisee, of the most famous sect among the Jews. (7) I burned with zeal above the other Pharisees, even to the point of persecuting the Church; though this zeal was very bad in itself, yet in the eyes of those who boasted in zeal for the Law it was glorious. (8) In external righteousness, which indeed can be obtained from the Law, I was blameless before men.

units.la: Verf. 7. Sed quae erant mihi lucro, ea duxi propter Christum damnum esse.
units.tr: Verse 7. But whatever things were gain to me, those I counted loss for Christ.

units.la: Primo enumeravit privilegia sua, & gloriandi in externis ampliorem materiam, quam Pseudapostolis suppetebat. Secundo loco abjicit haec ornamenta religionis, quae magni aestimabantur a Judaizantibus: Et licet ea olim in lucro posuerit ante conversionem ad CHRISTUM, falso exi-stimans ea plurimum ad salutem contulisse, nunc tamen postquam CHRISTI cognitionem adeptus est, a SPIRITU Sancto edoctus nihili ea facit, imo vero propter CHRISTUM ista omnia damnosa esse judicat, quatenus a CHRISTI Fide abducebant ipsum, vel quatenus constabant ei aliquo negotio & labore, ut omnibus his renunciaret, purumque se conservaret, ne ista fidem ipsius in CHRISTUM quovis modo impedirent. Difficile enim est his qui in aliquo excellunt, vel qui privilegia aliqua habent nullatenus iis niti, seu confidere.
units.tr: First, he listed his privileges, and matter for boasting in external things greater than the false apostles had. Second, he casts away these ornaments of religion, which were highly valued by the judaizers. And although he once counted them as gain before his conversion to Christ, falsely thinking they contributed much to salvation, yet now, since he has attained the knowledge of Christ and has been taught by the Holy Spirit, he regards them as nothing. Indeed, he judges all these things to be loss for Christ, insofar as they drew him away from faith in Christ, or insofar as they cost him some trouble and labour, so that he renounced them all and kept himself pure, lest these things hinder his faith in Christ in any way. For it is hard for those who excel in something, or who have some privileges, not to lean on them or trust in them.

units.la: FFf
units.tr: FFf

units.la: Verf. 8. Quin etiam certè duco omnia damnum esse propter eminentiam cognitionis Christi Iesu Domini mei: propter quem omnibus istis meipsum multavi, eaque duco pro stercoribus, ut Christum lucrifaciam:
units.tr: Verse 8. Indeed, I surely count all things loss because of the excellence of the knowledge of Christ Jesus my Lord, for whom I have suffered the loss of all things, and count them dung, that I may gain Christ.

units.la: Tertio loco, praeter ea quibus in Judaismo aemulis suis superior erat, omnia etiam alia abjicit. Notum enim est, quod millia multa animarum ad Deum converterit: quod multa egerit & passus sit pro Christo; in quibus si quisquam posset gloriari, ille magis: omnem tamen hanc suam justitiam inhaerentem, seu opera omnia bona, etiam post fidem facta vel facienda, in causa justificationis simul omnia rejicit tanquam σκύβαλα & damna, non quod poenituerit eum laborum, vel quod non expectarit proximum ex gratia mercedem, sed quod privilegia illa, & operum fiducia prorsus impedivissent justitiae Christi applicationem, si illa in causa justificationis attulisset ad Dei Tribunal, ubi opera excludunt gratiam, & gratia excludit opera: nec poenitet eum hujus jacturae; quippe quae compensatur superabunde per excellentiam justitiae Christi imputatae, & per fidem magis magisque sibi applicandae.
units.tr: Third, besides those things in which he was superior to his rivals in Judaism, he casts aside all other things as well. It is well known that he turned many thousands of souls to God, and that he did and suffered much for Christ; if anyone could boast in these, he could more. Yet he rejects all this righteousness of his own, that is, all his good works, including those done or to be done after faith, together, as far as the cause of justification is concerned, as dung [σκύβαλα] and loss. He does not do this because he regretted his labours, or because he did not expect a reward from grace in the future; rather, those privileges and the trust in works would have wholly hindered the application of Christ's righteousness, if he had brought them as a cause of justification before God's tribunal, where works exclude grace and grace excludes works. Nor does he regret this loss, since it is more than made up by the excellence of the imputed righteousness of Christ, and by faith in applying it to himself more and more.

units.la: Sinceritatem propositi sui de rejiciendis omnibus rebus prae studio habendae justitiae Christi probat duobus indiciis. Indicium 1. est, Quod jam jacturam fecerit amicorum, patriae, & omnium, quae chara ipsi esse poterant in carne, quando primum se ad Christum praedicandum, & crucem ejus ferendam contulit. Indicium 2. est, Quod jam rejecta contemnat tanquam quisquilias, prae justitia Christi, seu prae Christo per fidem in justitiam applicato. Hinc argumenti vis melius jam apparet, Ego qui privilegiis externis & operibus possem confidere si quisquam, omnibus illis renuncio, ut in Christi justitia & virtute acquiescam. Ergo & vobis una mecum in Christo acquiescendum est.
units.tr: He proves the sincerity of his purpose to reject all things for the sake of pursuing the righteousness of Christ by two signs. The first sign is that he has already lost friends, country, and everything that could be dear to him in the flesh, when he first devoted himself to preaching Christ and bearing his cross. The second sign is that he now despises what he has rejected as trifles, compared with the righteousness of Christ, or with Christ applied to us for righteousness through faith. From this the force of the argument appears more clearly: I, who could trust in external privileges and works more than anyone, renounce all of them, so as to rest in the righteousness and power of Christ. Therefore you too must rest with me in Christ.

units.la: Rationes sententiae suae fixae reddit varias, quae pro argumentis ad hortationem confirmandam faciunt.
units.tr: He gives various reasons for his fixed opinion, which serve as arguments to confirm the exhortation.

units.la: Arg. 5. Ego omnibus privilegiis, & operum meorum meritis renuncio, ut lucrifaciam Christum, qui se suamque justitiam non communicat ulli, nisi ei qui justitiae propriae renunciaverit, fiduciamque omnem in operibus & dignitate propria abjecerit. Ergo & vobis idem mecum faciendum est, nisi Christum amittere velletis.
units.tr: Argument 5. I renounce all privileges and the merits of my works, so that I may gain Christ, who does not impart himself or his righteousness to anyone except one who has renounced his own righteousness and cast off all confidence in works and his own worth. Therefore you too must do the same with me, unless you are willing to lose Christ.

units.la: Arg. 6. Renunciando fiduciæ in operibus & privilegiis meis, Christumque ipsorum loco amplectendo, Christum & Christi omnia lucrifacio, tantùm abest, ut quicquam amiserim hac privilegiorum & operum meorum renunciatione: Ergo & vos similiter una mecum omnem carnalem fiduciam abjicite, & in Christo acquiescentes ipsum lucrifacite.
units.tr: Argument 6. By renouncing confidence in my works and privileges, and embracing Christ in their place, "Christ and the things of Christ I gain," I have lost nothing at all by this renunciation of my privileges and works. Therefore you too, in the same way, cast off all carnal confidence with me, and, resting in Christ, gain him.

units.la: Verf. 9. Et comperiar in eo, non habens meam justitiam, nempe quæ est ex Lege; sed eam quæ per fidem est Christi, id est, justitiam quæ est ex Deo per fidem.
units.tr: Verse 9. "And be found in him, not having my own righteousness, which is from the Law, but that which is through the faith of Christ, that is, the righteousness which is from God by faith."

units.la: Arg. 7. Explicans superius, Cum venerit Deus ad judicium, non nisi renunciando meis meritis inveniri potero in Christo, destitutus omni fiducia in meorum operum inhærente justitia, & indutus imputata illa Christi justitia, quæ à Deo gratis datur, & per fidem nobis applicatur. Ergo vobis una mecum renunciandum est vestris meritis, & in Christi justitia & virtute acquiescendum, nisi extra Christum invenire velletis in die judicii.
units.tr: Argument 7. Explaining what he said above: when God comes to judgment, I can be found in Christ only by renouncing my merits, stripped of all confidence in the righteousness inherent in my works, and clothed with that imputed righteousness of Christ which is freely given by God and applied to us through faith. Therefore you too must renounce your merits with me and rest in the righteousness and power of Christ, unless you wish to be found outside Christ on the day of judgment.

units.la: Verf. 10. Ut cognoscam eum, & vim resurrectionis ipsius, & communionem perpessionum ipsius, dum conformis fio ipsius morti.
units.tr: Verse 10. "That I may know him, and the power of his resurrection, and the fellowship of his sufferings, being made conformable to his death."

units.la: Pendet sententia à versu 8. Constructio hujusmodi est. Omnem materiam fiduciæ extra Christum pro stercore duco, eo ipso fine ut cognoscam Christum, &c. Unde Arg. 8. Quia non nisi magis magisque renunciando omni materiæ, seu objecto fiduciæ extra Christum, experientiâ solide cognoscere potero, quam verax, bonus, potens, &c. Christus sit, nec experimento percipere virtutem resurrectionis ejus ad liberandum me à reatu & potestate peccati, nec experimento percipere communionem & virtutem perpessionum ejus; in quibus consistit conformitas cum ejus morte; propterea omnia pro stercore habeo, ut hoc fructu magis magisque potiar; Ergo & vos una mecum, renunciantes omnibus excellentiis vestris, in Christo acquiescite, ut magis magisque virtutem & gratiam ejus experiamini.
units.tr: The sentence depends on verse 8. The construction is this: I count all material of confidence outside Christ as dung, for the very purpose that I may know Christ, etc. Hence Argument 8: because only by renouncing more and more every matter or object of confidence outside Christ can I come to know solidly by experience how true, good, powerful, etc., Christ is, and experience the power of his resurrection to free me from the guilt and dominion of sin, and experience the fellowship and power of his sufferings, in which conformity with his death consists. Therefore I count all things as dung, so that I may gain this fruit more and more. Therefore you too, renouncing all your excellences with me, rest in Christ, so that you may experience more and more his power and grace.

units.la: Verf. 11. Experiens ecquo modo perveniam ad resurrectionem mortuorum.
units.tr: Verse 11. "Experiencing how I may attain to the resurrection of the dead."

units.la: Explicat quod dixit de communione perpessionum Christi & conformitate cum ejus morte, & addit Arg. 9. In hunc sensum, Postquam jam renunciavi omnibus privilegiis meis, & omni operum meorum dignitati, tanquam stercoribus, ut lucrifacerem Christum, etiam amsi mihi in itinere ad salutem insistendum esse sciam CHRISTI vestigiis, per continuas crucis aerumnas, & communionem perpessionum ejus, bene tamen mecum actum existimo, si quovis modo deveniam tandem ad sanctimoniae & felicitatis perfectionem in resurrectione mortuorum: Ergo & vos una mecum idem sentite & agite.
units.tr: He explains what he said about fellowship in Christ's sufferings and conformity with his death, and adds Argument 9. To this effect: since I have now renounced all my privileges and the worth of my works as dung, so that I might gain Christ, even though I know I must walk in the way to salvation in Christ's footsteps, through constant afflictions of the cross and fellowship in his sufferings, I still judge that it goes well with me if I somehow at last attain to the perfection of holiness and happiness in the resurrection of the dead. Therefore you too, with me, think and act in the same way.

units.la: Secunda pars Capitis.
units.tr: The second part of the chapter.

units.la: Verf. 12. Nedum ut jam metam apprehenderim, aut jam persectus sim: sed persequor, experiens, an quoque apprehendam cujus etiam rei causa apprehensus sum à Christo Jesu.
units.tr: Verse 12. "Not that I have already obtained, or am already made perfect; but I press on, if I may apprehend that for which I was also apprehended by Christ Jesus."

units.la: Secunda pars Capitis, in qua hortatur Apostolus ut imitantes seipsum, & alios fideles Ministros proficiant in sanctimonia, adhibitis septem argumentis: & hic etiam seipsum in exemplum illis proponit, per occupationem objectionis. Diceret forsan aliquis. O beatum Paulum, qui omnibus renunciavit, ut CHRISTUM cognosceret, eumque lucrifaceret, quique jam adeo conformis est factus CHRISTO, ut nihil ei restet, praeter praemium immortalitatis. Respondet non esse hunc sensum dictorum suorum: quasi diceret, Non eo haec dico quod sanctimoniae perfectionem assequutus sim, aut jam sim consummatus, sed persequor metam persectionis: Unde Argumentum primum, Ego non sum consummatus in sanctimonia sed persequor perfectionem. Ergo & vos itidem imperfecti una mecum idem agite.
units.tr: The second part of the chapter, in which the Apostle exhorts that, imitating himself and the other faithful ministers, they should make progress in holiness, using seven arguments; and here too he proposes himself as an example to them, by anticipating an objection. Someone might perhaps say: "O blessed Paul, who renounced everything that he might know Christ and gain him, and who has become so conformed to Christ that nothing remains for him except the reward of immortality." He replies that this is not the sense of his words, as if he were saying: I do not say this because I have attained the perfection of holiness or am already consummated, but I press on toward the goal of perfection. Hence the first argument: I am not consummated in holiness, but I press on toward perfection. Therefore you, likewise imperfect, do the same with me.

units.la: Verf. 13. Fratres, ego meipsum nondum arbitror metam apprehendisse.
units.tr: Verse 13. "Brethren, I do not count myself to have apprehended the goal yet."

units.la: Verf. 14. Unum autem ago, ea quidem quae a tergo sunt oblivis cens, ad ea vero quae a fronte sunt contendens, scopum versus feror ad palmam supernae vocationis Dei, in Christo Jesu,
units.tr: Verse 14. "But one thing I do: forgetting what lies behind, and straining toward what lies ahead, I press on toward the goal, to the prize of the upward calling of God in Christ Jesus."

units.la: Verf. 15. Quotquot itaque perfecti sumus, hoc sentiamus: quod siquid aliter sentitis, hoc quoque vobis Deus revelabit.
units.tr: Verse 15. "Therefore let as many of us as are perfect think this way; and if in anything you think otherwise, God will also reveal this to you."

units.la: Arg. 3. Ego ex sensu imperfectionis meae in sanctimonia, progressus quos jam feci non respicio, nec in mentem revoco, sed quanta contentione possum percurro stadium mihi propositum, ut metam in hujus vitæ fine, & præmium vitæ æternæ, ad quam Deus supernè in Christo vocavit me tandem asequar: Ergo & vos omnes, etiam qui jam adulti estis, & maximos progressus hactenus fecistis vel fecisse videmini, sive aliis, sive vobis ipsis, unà mecum idem sentite & studete; hoc est, Abdicatâ omni carnali fiducia, in sola Christi justitia gloriantes aspirate in ejus virtute ad proficiendum in sanctimonia: ut ad beatam resurrectionem tandem perveniatis.
units.tr: Argument 3. From my sense of my own imperfection in holiness, I do not look back on the progress I have already made, nor do I recall it to mind, but with all the effort I can, I run through the course set before me, so that I may at last reach the goal at the end of this life and the prize of eternal life, to which God has called me from above in Christ. Therefore you all, even those who are already grown and have made, or seem to have made, the greatest progress hitherto, whether in the eyes of others or your own, think and strive together with me in the same way; that is, having abandoned all carnal confidence, boast only in the righteousness of Christ, and aspire in his power to make progress in holiness, so that at last you may attain the blessed resurrection.

units.la: Quod si] Arg. 4. Si quid de perfectione Christiana aliter sentiatis, seducti à Pseudapostolis, spero Deum qui vos convertit ad fidem Evangelii, etiam hanc veritatem vobis ostensurum, & vel effecturum ut idem sentiatis mecum de justitia Christi & virtute ipsius ad sanctimoniæ velstræ incrementum, vel periculo & magno malo vestro vos in aliam à mea doctrina sententiam fecesisse, revelaturum: Ergo vos unà mecum idem de perfectione Christiana sentite.
units.tr: "But if" — Argument 4. If you think anything otherwise about Christian perfection, led astray by the false apostles, I hope that God, who has converted you to the faith of the gospel, will also show you this truth, and either bring it about that you think with me about the righteousness of Christ and his power for the increase of your holiness, or reveal that you have departed to a different opinion from my doctrine to your danger and great harm. Therefore you, together with me, think the same about Christian perfection.

units.la: Verf. 16, Attamen in eo ad quod pervenimus, eadem incedamus regula & itidem simus affecti.
units.tr: Verse 16. "Nevertheless, let us walk by the same rule to which we have attained, and be of the same mind."

units.la: Initiat spem suam de salutari revelatione veritatis, de qua agit ad studiosos veritatis & pacis, per specialem hortationem eos incitans ad constantiam, & sinceram concordiam colendam, in ea veritate in qua jam consentiebant, de gratia & salute per Christum secundùm Scripturæ Canonem, bene sperare ausus de illis solis qui hanc regulam sequuturi erant: quasi diceret, Nos qui veritatis & pacis cultores sumus, & Scripturam veritatis salutiferæ Canonem amplexi sumus, perseveremus in eo ad quod Dei beneficio pervenimus, & secundùm hunc Canonem incedentes, eodem animo affecti simus; reliquos verò Deo & disciplinæ ipsius in Scriptura positæ relinquamus.
units.tr: He begins his hope concerning the saving revelation of the truth, about which he speaks to those who seek truth and peace, by specially exhorting them to keep steadfastly and cultivate sincere concord in that truth in which they already agreed, concerning grace and salvation through Christ according to the canon of Scripture; he has ventured to hope well only of those who were going to follow this rule. It is as if he said: we who are cultivators of truth and peace, and have embraced Scripture as the canon of saving truth, let us persevere in that to which we have attained by God's benefit, and, walking according to this canon, let us be of the same mind; but the rest we leave to God and to the discipline laid down for it in Scripture.

units.la: Verf. 17. Estote simul imitatores mei, fratres, & eos considerate qui ita incedunt, sicut habetis nos pro exemplari.
units.tr: Verse 17. "Be imitators of me together, brethren, and mark those who walk so as you have us as an example."

units.la: Arg. hortationis 5. Præter me habetis alios Dei servos, qui eandem tenent viam quam ego, in doctrinæ & vitæ degendæ ratione, qui nihil præter fidem in Christum, & sanctimoniam per illum obtinendam spirant: Ergo & vos imitamini hæc exemplaria.
units.tr: Argument of exhortation 5. Besides me you have other servants of God, who hold the same way as I do in the teaching and manner of living, who breathe nothing but faith in Christ and the holiness to be obtained through him. Therefore you too imitate these examples.

units.la: Verf. 18 Nam complures incedunt, quos sæpe dixi vobis, nunc autem & flens dico, hostes esse crucis Christi:
units.tr: Verse 18. "For many walk, of whom I have often told you, and now tell you even weeping, that they are enemies of the cross of Christ."

units.la: Arg. 6.
units.tr: Arg. 6.

units.la: Arg. 6. Hortationis, confirmans superius: Multi sunt doctores Pseudapostoli, & falsi fratres, qui inimici sunt crucis Christi, id est, qui alia ratione quam per solam Christi crucem, peccata expiari, & homines servari docent, & qui profiteri nolunt veritatem Christi, ubi periculum est crucis, seu persecutionis: Ergo doctrinae vitaeque meae, & mihi similium pastorum, rationem tanto diligentius observate, & imitamini.
units.tr: Argument 6, of exhortation, confirming what was said above: There are many teachers, false apostles and false brothers, who are enemies of the cross of Christ; that is, who teach that sins are expiated and men saved by some means other than the cross of Christ alone, and who refuse to profess the truth of Christ where there is danger from the cross, or persecution. Therefore observe and imitate, the more diligently, the teaching and manner of life of me and of ministers like me.

units.la: Hoc argumentum de vitandis impostoribus (qui a justitia & sanctitate, quae est per Christi crucem, abducebant) confirmat septem rationibus: Ratio prima, Quia non jam primum, sed prius saepius, de hujusmodi nebulonibus venturis, praemonui vos.
units.tr: This argument, concerning the avoidance of impostors (who turn people away from the righteousness and holiness that come through the cross of Christ), is confirmed by seven reasons. The first reason: because I have warned you not for the first time, but earlier and often, about such scoundrels who are to come.

units.la: Ratio 2. Quia nunc flens admoneo de illis vitandis, sed dolens, quod istiusmodi irrepserint in Ecclesiam, & pro veris doctoribus ab aliquibus recepti sint.
units.tr: Reason 2: because I now warn you with tears about avoiding them, but grieving that such people have crept into the Church and have been received by some as true teachers.

units.la: Ratio 3. Quia sunt Christi hostes hoc ipso nomine quod sint virtutis passionum Christi hostes: & qui crucem Christi pro veritatis defensione nolunt ferre.
units.tr: Reason 3: because they are enemies of Christ by this very name, that they are enemies of the power of Christ's sufferings, and those who are unwilling to bear the cross of Christ in defence of the truth.

units.la: Vers. 19. Quorum finis est exitium, quorum Deus est venter, & gloria in confusione ipsorum, qui terrestria curant.
units.tr: Verse 19. Whose end is destruction, whose God is their belly, and whose glory is in their shame, who mind earthly things.

units.la: Ratio 4. Quia perituri sunt illi impostores, & quicunque eorum viam sequuturi sunt: Vitate eos igitur.
units.tr: Reason 4: because those impostors will perish, and whoever shall follow their way. Avoid them, therefore.

units.la: Ratio 5. Quia servi sunt & cultores ventris sui, id est, nec Deum, nec hominum salutem curant, sed cutem & voluptates suas tantum.
units.tr: Reason 5: because they are slaves and worshippers of their own belly; that is, they care neither for God nor for the salvation of men, but only for their skin and their pleasures.

units.la: Ratio 6. Quia quam affectant gloriam inter homines, ex divitiis, prosperitate, & carnalibus praerogativis, ipsorum dedecus est.
units.tr: Reason 6: because the glory they seek among men, from riches, prosperity and carnal privileges, is their own disgrace.

units.la: Ratio 7. Quia terrena tantum sapiunt, ut opes, honores, amicos, gulam, voluptates, & cetera similia: Ergo vitandi sunt a vobis qui spiritualem & coelestem vitam expetitis.
units.tr: Reason 7: because they savour only earthly things, such as wealth, honours, friends, gluttony, pleasures and the like. Therefore they are to be avoided by you, who desire a spiritual and heavenly life.

units.la: Vers. 20. Nos enim ut municipes coelorum nos gerimus: unde etiam Servatorem expectamus Dominum Iesum Christum:
units.tr: Verse 20. For our citizenship is in heaven; from which also we look for the Saviour, the Lord Jesus Christ.

units.la: Arg. hortationis 7. Coelestis admodum est nostra conditio, qui sola Christi gratia & virtute freti, contendimus ad proficiendum in sanctimonia: Nos veri sumus coelorum municipes, & in coelo, animo & affectu versamur, ubi aliquando glorificandi sumus. Ergo nostrum exemplum imitamini. Felicitas autem vere fidelium declaratur in
units.tr: Argument 7 of exhortation: Our condition is entirely heavenly, we who, relying only on the grace and power of Christ, strive to make progress in holiness. We are truly citizens of heaven, and we live in heaven in mind and affection, where we are one day to be glorified. Therefore imitate our example. The happiness of true believers is declared in these four things.

units.la: his quatuor. Primum est, Quod jus in civitatem cœlestem habeamus in qua jam animo & affectu versamur, ut cives regni Superni: Secundum est, Quod scientes Christum corporaliter & localiter esse in cœlis, expectemus Christum ex eo loco in die novissimo venturum, non judicem qui condemnet nos, sed Servatorem nostrum, qui salutem nostram omnibus numeris absolvat.
units.tr: The first is that we have a right to the heavenly city, in which we already live in mind and affection, as citizens of the heavenly kingdom. The second is that, knowing Christ to be bodily and locally in heaven, we look for Christ to come from that place on the last day, not as a judge who will condemn us, but as our Saviour, who will complete our salvation in every respect.

units.la: Versf. 21. Qui transformabit corpus nostrum humile, ut conforme fit corpori suo glorioso, pro efficacitate qua potest etiam subjicere sibi omnia.
units.tr: Verse 21. Who will transform our lowly body, that it may be made conformable to his glorious body, according to the working whereby he is able even to subdue all things to himself.

units.la: Tertium est, Quod etiamsi corpora nostra jam sint corruptibilia, vilia & misera, ea tamen olim Christus immutabit prorsus, quo ad conditionem in qua nunc sunt, & à corruptibilitate liberabit.
units.tr: The third is that, even though our bodies are now corruptible, base and wretched, Christ will one day change them completely, as to the condition in which they now are, and will free them from corruptibility.

units.la: Conforme ] Quartum est, Quod Christus corpora nostra conformia reddet corpori suo glorioso, ut sicut secundum substantiam, & lineamenta, idem manet Christi corpus, quod prius in terra erat, sed qualitatibus mutatum est: sic etiam & corpora nostra manebunt eadem substantia, & qualitatibus vilibus liberata, gloriosis induentur.
units.tr: Conformable: The fourth is that Christ will make our bodies conformable to his glorious body, so that, just as the body of Christ remains the same in substance and features as it was on earth, but has been changed in its qualities, so our bodies too will remain the same in substance, and, freed from base qualities, will be clothed with glorious ones.

units.la: Pro efficacitate ] Hujus conditionis futurae certitudinem confirmat à Christi potestate & efficacia, qua potest mortem & sepulchrum abolere, omnesque adeo creaturas sibi subjicere, & proinde etiam corpora nostra quibus vult qualitatibus induere.
units.tr: According to the working: He confirms the certainty of this future condition from the power and efficacy of Christ, by which he is able to abolish death and the grave, and so to subject all creatures to himself, and therefore also to clothe our bodies with whatever qualities he wills.

units.la: Caput Quartum.
units.tr: Chapter 4.

units.la: Restat confirmationis Philippensium in fide & sanctimonia ratio ultima, per hortationes aliquot, & liberalitatis ipsorum erga se commendationem.
units.tr: The final reason for confirming the Philippians in faith and holiness remains, by way of several exhortations, and by commending their generosity towards him.

units.la: Capitis duae sunt partes præcipuae: In prima hortatur ad virtutes Christianas, ad verl. 10. In altera gratitudinem suam ostendit erga Philippenses, ob honorarium ab iis ad se missum, ad verf. 20. post quae sequitur Epistolae totius Conclusio.
units.tr: The chapter has two main parts. In the first he exhorts them to Christian virtues, up to verse 10. In the second he shows his gratitude towards the Philippians for the gift sent to him by them, from verse 10 onward, after which follows the conclusion of the whole Epistle.

units.la: Versf. 1. Itaque, fratres mei chari & exoptati, gaudium & corona mea, ita state in Domino, dilecti.
units.tr: Verse 1. Therefore, my brothers, dearly loved and longed for, my joy and crown, stand firm thus in the Lord, beloved.

units.la: Hortationes ad Christianas virtutes sunt septem: Hortatio prima, Ut sartam tectam conservent doctrinam de Christi gratia & virtute, constanter in Fide & Sanctitate perseverantes. Argumenta hortationis sunt duo: Primum à vehementi hortantis erga eos dilectione, quam variis Epithetis explicat. Alterum, Hactenus adeo constantes fuistis, & profecistis in Fide Euangelii, ut mihi Doctori vestro, & gaudio, & ornamento fueritis. Ergo perstate.
units.tr: There are seven exhortations to Christian virtues. The first exhortation: that they keep whole and sound the teaching about Christ's grace and power, persevering constantly in faith and holiness. The arguments for this exhortation are two. The first is from the apostle's warm affection towards them, which he explains with various epithets. The second: you have been so steadfast up to now, and have made such progress in the faith of the gospel, that you have been to me, your teacher, both a joy and an ornament. Therefore persevere.

units.la: Verf. 2. Euodiam precor & Syntychen precor, ut sint itidem affectæ in Domino:
units.tr: Verse 2. I beg Euodia and I beg Syntyche, that they be likewise minded in the Lord.

units.la: Hortatio 2. est speciālis ad duas fœminas in Ecclesia non obscuras, quæ in rebus ad religionem spectantibus, ut videtur, non consentiebant cum Ecclesia, & inter se etiam dissidium fovebant, quas nominatim rogat, ut positis dissidiis in sententiis & affectibus, Concordiam piam & sinceram colant, qualem Dominus approbaturus esset.
units.tr: The second exhortation is special, addressed to two women well known in the Church who, as it seems, did not agree with the Church in matters pertaining to religion, and who also nursed a quarrel between themselves. He asks them by name that, setting aside their disagreements in opinions and feelings, they cultivate a pious and sincere harmony, such as the Lord would approve.

units.la: Verf. 3. Et rogo te quoque, germane socie, adjuva eas, quæ in Euangelio una mecum certarunt, una cum Clemente quoque, & reliquis adjutoribus meis, quorum nomina sunt in libro vitæ.
units.tr: Verse 3. And I ask you too, true yokefellow, help those women who laboured together with me in the gospel, along with Clement too, and the rest of my helpers, whose names are in the book of life.

units.la: Hortatio 3. ad unum aliquem ex Pastoribus, qui Apostolo familiaris, & præ aliis cognitus erat, ut operam suam accommodet ad has duas fœminas in viam rectam, & concordiam inter se reducendas. Ratio redditur, Quia quum primùm Apostolus Ecclesiam Philippis colligeret, hæ duæ mulieres studiosè pro Euangelii negotio promovendo, pro statione sua laborarunt & decertarunt, unà cum aliis aliquot fratribus, ex quibus erat Clemens, & alii privati aliquot fideles Adjutores Apostoli in Ecclesia Philippensium colligenda, quos omnes etiamsi nihil opus erat nominare, eorum nomina scripta tamen esse dicit in libro vitæ, id est, ex Electis eos affirmat, quod satis iis esse potuit.
units.tr: The third exhortation is addressed to one of the ministers who was familiar to the apostle and better known to him than the others, that he should apply his efforts to bringing these two women back to the right path and to harmony with one another. The reason given is this: when the apostle first gathered the Church at Philippi, these two women laboured and strove zealously for the advancement of the business of the gospel, each in her own station, together with several other brothers, among whom was Clement, and some other private faithful helpers of the apostle in gathering the Church of the Philippians. Although there was no need to name them all, he says that their names are written in the book of life, that is, he affirms that they are among the elect, which could well be enough for them.

units.la: Verf. 4. Gaudete in Domino semper: rursum inquam, gaudete.
units.tr: Verse 4. Rejoice in the Lord always: again I say, rejoice.

units.la: Hortatio 4. Vt in rebus prosperis & adversis, omninoque in omni statu ipsorum mutatione, lætitiæ materiam in Christo agnoscentes, solidum gaudeant gaudium.
units.tr: The fourth exhortation: that in prosperity and adversity, and indeed in every state and change of their condition, recognising in Christ the matter of their joy, they may rejoice with a solid joy.

units.la: Verf. 5. Moderatio vestra nota sit omnibus hominibus. Dominus prope est.
units.tr: Verse 5. Let your moderation be known to all men. The Lord is near.

units.la: Hortatio 5. Ne cum proximis stricto jure agant, sed potius conditionem proximorum considerantes de jure suo remittant, utque omnes hanc ipsorum moderationem experiantur. Ratio redditur, Quia Dominus in medio nostri versatur, per SPIRITUS sui praesentiam, & non longè abest adventus Ejus visibilis ad Judicium.
units.tr: The fifth exhortation: that they not deal with their neighbours in strict justice, but rather, considering the condition of their neighbours, relax their own right, and let all experience this moderation of theirs. The reason given is this: the Lord dwells in the midst of us through the presence of his Spirit, and his visible coming to judgment is not far off.

units.la: Vers. 6. De nulla re solliciti estote: sed omni in re precibus & supplicatione cum gratiarum actione petitiones vestrae innotescant apud Deum.
units.tr: Verse 6. Be anxious about nothing; but in everything, by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving, let your requests be made known to God.

units.la: Hortatio 6 Ut studentes officiis suis satisfacere, caveant sibi à diffidenti anxietate in omni negotio, & curas suas in precationibus & deprecationibus, cum Gratiarum actione in DEI gremium conjiciant.
units.tr: The sixth exhortation: that, while they study to satisfy their duties, they beware of distrustful anxiety in every business, and cast their cares into the bosom of God by their prayers and entreaties, with thanksgiving.

units.la: Vers. 7. Et pax Dei quae superat omnem intellectum, praesidio erit cordibus vestris, & mentibus vestris in Christo Iesu.
units.tr: Verse 7. And the peace of God, which surpasses all understanding, will be a guard for your hearts and your minds in Christ Jesus.

units.la: Ratio hortationis, quia sic fieret, ut Pax, seu animi Tranquillitas (superans omnem captum rationis naturalis) quae fidelibus à DEO conceditur, quasi militari praesidio custodiret ipsorum corda, adversus Satanae & mundi tentationes, & mentes ipsorum stabiles in CHRISTO conservaret.
units.tr: The reason for the exhortation is that thus the peace, or tranquillity of mind (surpassing all the grasp of natural reason), which God grants to the faithful, would guard their hearts as with a military garrison against the temptations of Satan and the world, and keep their minds steadfast in Christ.

units.la: Vers. 8. Quod reliquum est, fratres, quaecunque sunt vera, quaecunque veneranda, quaecunque justa, quaecunque pura, quaecunque amabilia, quaecunque boni nominis, si qua virtus, & si qua laus est, haec cogitate:
units.tr: Verse 8. Finally, brothers, whatever things are true, whatever things are honourable, whatever things are just, whatever things are pure, whatever things are lovely, whatever things are of good report, if there is any virtue and if there is any praise, think on these things.

units.la: Hortatio 7. Ne abhorreant à virtute ulla, quam inter Ethnicos observarent, sed contra, post seriam examinationem amplectantur quodcunque verum, grave seu venerandum, justum & purum, & quodcunque in moribus amabile, vel commendatione dignum perspicerent.
units.tr: The seventh exhortation: that they should not shrink from any virtue which the heathen practised, but on the contrary, after serious examination, embrace whatever is true, grave or honourable, just and pure, and whatever they perceive to be lovely in conduct or worthy of commendation.

units.la: Vers. 9. Quae & didicistis, & accepistis, & audistis, & vidistis in me, haec, inquam, facite, & Deus pacis autor erit vobiscum.
units.tr: Verse 9. The things which you have both learned and received, and heard and seen in me, these things, I say, do, and the God of peace will be with you.

units.la: Hanc hortationem confirmat duobus Argumentis: Arg. 1. Ab exemplo suo, quod Apostolus haec & docuerit, & actu fecerit, quando inter ipsos versabatur, ut ipsi Testes erant. Et Deus] Arg. 2. Ab eventu salutari, quod hoc pacto pacem DEI, & communionem cum DEO Pacis, constantiorem experturi essent.
units.tr: He confirms this exhortation with two arguments. Argument 1: from his own example, since the apostle both taught these things and actually practised them when he was among them, as they themselves are witnesses. And God] Argument 2: from the saving outcome, that in this way they would experience more constantly the peace of God and communion with the God of peace.

units.la: Secunda Pars Capitis.
units.tr: The Second Part of the Chapter.

units.la: Vers. 10. Gavisus sum autem in Domino magnopere, quod jam tandem reviruistis in vestra pro me cura: qua de re tamen solliciti eratis, sed destituebamini opportunitate. Secunda pars Capitis, In qua ut gratitudinem suam ostendat erga Phi‐lippenses, pro pecunia ad ipsum missa per Epaphroditum, commendat ipsorum factum decem Argumentis: 1. Quia gratum sibi fuerat illud ab ipsis missum subsidium: 2. Quia missum honorarium ex virtute seu habitu Christianæ liberalitatis quæ in ipsis erat, provenerat; qui habitus tanquam viva radix in hoc actu reviruerat: 3. Quia hinc perspici poterat ipsorum tarditatem ad mittendum hoc subsidium, non ex defectu charitatis, sed opportunitatis potius provenisse.
units.tr: Verse 10. But I rejoiced in the Lord greatly, that now at the last your care of me has flourished again; wherein indeed you were careful, but you lacked opportunity. The second part of the chapter. In it, to show his gratitude to the Philippians for the money sent to him through Epaphroditus, he commends their deed with ten arguments: (1) because the aid sent by them was welcome to him; (2) because the gift arose from the virtue, or habit, of Christian liberality that was in them, which habit, like a living root, had flourished again in this act; (3) because it could be seen from this that their delay in sending the aid arose not from a lack of love but rather from a lack of opportunity.

units.la: Verf. 11. Non quòd penuriæ meæ respectu loquar: nam ego didici, in quibus sum, iis ipsis contentus esse.
units.tr: Verse 11. Not that I speak in respect of want: for I have learned, in whatever state I am, therewith to be content.

units.la: Verf. 12. Novi autem deprimi, novi etiam abundare: ubique & in omnibus initiatus sum, & ad saturitatem & ad esuritionem, id est, tum ad abundantiam, tum ad inopiam.
units.tr: Verse 12. I know both how to be abased, and I know how to abound; everywhere and in all things I am instructed, both to be full and to be hungry, that is, both to abound and to suffer want.

units.la: Obiter occupando objectionem, amolitur à se suspicionem, quasi tristior fuisset ante acceptum subsidium, vel quod sua causa gavisus fuisset post missam pecuniam: Argumento sumpto ab æquanimitate sua in omni conditione, ut qui didicerat utramque fortem æquo animo ferre, iisque vitæ subsidiis, quæ prælto erant, contentus esse.
units.tr: Touching on an objection in passing, he removes from himself the suspicion that he had been sadder before receiving the aid, or that he had rejoiced on his own account after the money was sent. He takes the argument from his evenness of mind in every condition, since he had learned to bear either state with an equal mind and to be content with whatever means of life were at hand.

units.la: Verf. 13. Omnia valeo per Christum qui me corroborat.
units.tr: Verse 13. I can do all things through Christ who strengthens me.

units.la: Hujus æquanimitatis, & moderati in omnibus animi sui gloriam ascribit Christo, cujus virtute ad hoc corroboratus fuit.
units.tr: He ascribes the glory of this evenness and moderation of mind in all things to Christ, by whose power he was strengthened for it.

units.la: Verf. 14. Attamen recte fecistis, quòd simul communicastis meæ oppressioni.
units.tr: Verse 14. Nevertheless you have done well, that you communicated with my affliction.

units.la: Quarto commendat factum, quod esset communicatio cum ipsius afflictione.
units.tr: Fourthly, he commends the deed as a sharing in his affliction.

units.la: Verf. 15. Nostis autem & vos, Philippenses, cum initio Evangelii profecisset è Macedonia, nullam mihi Ecclesiam communicasse in ratione dati & accepti, nisi vos solos;
units.tr: Verse 15. Now you Philippians know also, that in the beginning of the Gospel, when I departed from Macedonia, no Church communicated with me as concerning giving and receiving, but you only.

units.la: Arg. 5. Commendationis Philippensium: Quod soli illi ex omnibus Macedoniæ Ecclesiis inde ab initio prædicationis Evangelii, in ratione dati & accepti, cum eo communicassent.
units.tr: Argument 5, in commendation of the Philippians: that they alone, of all the churches of Macedonia, from the beginning of the preaching of the Gospel, communicated with him in the matter of giving and receiving.

units.la: Verf. 16. Nam etiam Thessalonicam semel & iterum quod opus erat mihi misistis.
units.tr: Verse 16. For even in Thessalonica you sent once and again for my necessity.

units.la: Arg. 6. Quod jam tertio liberalitatem erga se ostendissent.
units.tr: Argument 6: that they had already shown their liberality towards him a third time.

units.la: Verf. 17. Non quod requiram donum: sed requiro fructum exuberantem qui in rationem vestram indatur.
units.tr: Verse 17. Not that I seek a gift: but I seek fruit that may abound to your account.

units.la: Arg. 7. Quod hic fructus fuerit ipsorum fidei, quem Deus compensaturus est in die judicii, quo fructu profitetur se magis delectari, quam suo ullo privato commodo.
units.tr: Argument 7: that this fruit is the fruit of their faith, which God will repay on the day of judgment. By this fruit he declares that he takes more delight in it than in any private benefit of his own.

units.la: Verf. 18 Accepi autem omnia, & abundo: expletus sum, inquam, acceptis ab Epaphrodito quae à vobis missa fuerunt, odore bonae fragrantiae hostia Deo accepta ac grata:
units.tr: Verse 18. But I have all, and abound: I am full, I say, having received from Epaphroditus the things sent from you, an odour of a sweet smell, a sacrifice acceptable and well pleasing to God.

units.la: Arg. 8. Quod summa pecuniae de qua scripserant ad eum, satis ampla fuerit (saltem respectu aestimationis & frugalitatis Apostoli) quam summam totam & integram sibi redditam esse per Epaphroditum agnoscit.
units.tr: Argument 8: that the sum of money of which they had written to him was ample enough (at least by the Apostle's estimate and in view of his frugality). He acknowledges that the whole and entire sum was returned to him through Epaphroditus.

units.la: Odorem ] Arg. 9. Quod haec beneficentia Deo non minus fuerit grata & accepta, quam oblata hostia quae iuxta lege offerri solebat cum fragrantissimo suffitu.
units.tr: Odour: Argument 9: that this beneficence was no less pleasing and acceptable to God than the offered sacrifice which, according to the law, was customarily offered with the most fragrant incense.

units.la: Verf. 19. Deus autem meus supplebit quicquid opus fuerit vobis secundum divitias suas gloriose, in Christo Iesu.
units.tr: Verse 19. But my God shall supply all your need according to his riches in glory by Christ Jesus.

units.la: Arg. 10. Quod Deus etiam in hac vita remuneraturus sit quicquid in eum contulerant, idque non ex ipsorum merito, sed ex divite & gloriosa sua gratia per Christum.
units.tr: Argument 10: that God will also reward, even in this life, whatever they had contributed to him, and that not in return for their merit but out of his rich and glorious grace through Christ.

units.la: Verf. 20. Deo autem & Patri nostro sit gloria in saecula saeculorum, Amen.
units.tr: Verse 20. Now unto God and our Father be glory for ever and ever. Amen.

units.la: Restat conclusio Epistolae, Cujus tres sunt articuli: In primo pro omnibus antedictis beneficiis praestitis & praestandis, laudatur Deus, ut Deus, & Pater Fidelium, qui ex Foedere & Paterno affectu largitus erat, & largiturus erat omnia bona.
units.tr: There remains the conclusion of the Epistle, which has three parts. In the first, for all the aforesaid benefits bestowed and to be bestowed, God is praised as God and as the Father of the faithful, who out of covenant and paternal affection has bestowed, and will bestow, all good things.

units.la: Verf. 21. Salutate omnes sanctos in Christo Iesu. Salutant vos qui mecum sunt fratres.
units.tr: Verse 21. Salute every saint in Christ Jesus. The brethren who are with me salute you.

units.la: Verf. 22. Salutant vos omnes sancti, maxime vero qui sunt ex Caesaris domo.
units.tr: Verse 22. All the saints salute you, chiefly those who are of Caesar's household.

units.la: In secundo articulo ponit salutationes suas, & Euangelistarum qui secum erant, quos speciatim fratres vocat, respectu officii Pastoralis, & addit reliquorum Sanctorum qui Romae erant salutationes, posita distinctione inter fratres, in Euangelii Ministerio laborantes, & Sanctos alios, inter quos speciatim designat domesticos Neronis, ut intelligerent fuisse etiam Aulicos in aula Neronis, qui CHRISTI fidem, & cum Christianis alibi diligentibus, communionem profiteri audebant.
units.tr: In the second part he sends his own greetings, and those of the evangelists who were with him, whom he calls brethren with respect to their pastoral office. He adds the greetings of the other saints who were at Rome, drawing a distinction between the brethren labouring in the ministry of the Gospel and the other saints. Among these last he particularly names the members of Nero's household, so that we may understand that there were also courtiers in Nero's court who dared to profess faith in Christ and fellowship with Christians who were otherwise despised.

units.la: Versf. 23. Gratia Domini nostri Iesu Christi cum omnibus vobis, Amen.
units.tr: Verse 23. The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you all. Amen.

units.la: In tertio articulo claudit Epistolam, usitatâ benedictione Apostolicâ, favorem CHRISTI, & omnia bona quae inde fluunt Philippensibus optans.
units.tr: In the third part he closes the Epistle with the customary apostolic blessing, wishing the Philippians the favour of Christ and all the good things that flow from it.

units.la: EXPOSITIO ANALYTICA EPISTOLAE PAULI AD COLOSSENSES. Summarium.
units.tr: Analytical Exposition of Paul's Epistle to the Colossians. Summary.

units.la: Rbs Colossensium sita fuit in Asia minori, nempe in ea regione quae Phrygia Pacatiana dicebatur, non procul Hierapoli & Laodicea; quarum urbium Apostolus diserte in hac Epistola meminit.
units.tr: The church of the Colossians was situated in Asia Minor, namely in that region which was called Phrygia Pacatiana, not far from Hierapolis and Laodicea, which cities the Apostle expressly mentions in this Epistle.

units.la: Occasio scribendi fuisse apparet, quod Apostolus ex Epaphra Colossensium Pastore, & aliis testibus fide dignis, accepisset Colossenses solicitatos fuisse à Pseudapostolis, partim ad Judaicas Ceremonias, partim ad Philosophicas speculationes, de Angelis adorandis, admittendas. Idcirco, ut in veritate ipsos stabiliret, evidenter ostendit in solo CHRISTO, ejusque Evangelio universam divinae voluntatis cognitionem, adeoque omnia salutis aeternae praesidia sufficienter nobis esse exposita, & proinde in hoc rerum genere nihil extra CHRISTUM, ejusque doctrinam quaerendum esse.
units.tr: The occasion for writing is evident: the Apostle had learned from Epaphras, minister of the Colossians, and from other trustworthy witnesses, that the Colossians had been pressed by false apostles to admit, partly Jewish ceremonies, and partly philosophical speculations about worshipping angels. Therefore, in order to establish them in the truth, he clearly shows that the whole knowledge of the divine will, and so all the safeguards of eternal salvation, have been sufficiently set out for us in Christ alone and in his Gospel, and that accordingly in this matter nothing is to be sought outside Christ and his doctrine.

units.la: Ejusdem est argumenti haec Epistola cum illa ad Ephesios, & haec illius compendium, merito dici potest.
units.tr: This Epistle is of the same subject as that to the Ephesians, and it may rightly be called its summary.

units.la: Principales partes hujus Epistolæ, præter directionem & epilogum, (in quo salutationes & res privatæ continentur) sunt duæ. In prima, ad fidem Colossensium confirmandam, commendat doctrinam in qua ab Epaphra instituti sunt, speciatim, verò Christum cum suis beneficiis magnificè describit; hortatur-que ad Constantiam in fide Christi, & ad fugiendum corruptelas sanæ doctrinæ contrarias, Capite 1. & 2.
units.tr: The main parts of this Epistle, apart from the address and the conclusion (which contains the greetings and personal matters), are two. In the first, to confirm the faith of the Colossians, he commends the doctrine in which they were instructed by Epaphras, and especially Christ he describes magnificently with his benefits; and he exhorts them to constancy in the faith of Christ, and to flee from corruptions contrary to sound doctrine, Chapters 1 and 2.

units.la: In secundâ parte, Præcepta dat communia ad vitam omnium Fidelium rectè instituendam spectantia, admistis interim specialibus præceptis, ad omnes ordines in familia dirigendos, inservientibus, Capite 3. & 4.
units.tr: In the second part he gives general precepts bearing on the right ordering of the life of all the faithful, mixed meanwhile with special precepts for directing every order within the household, serving these purposes, Chapters 3 and 4.

units.la: Caput Primum.
units.tr: Chapter 1.

units.la: Capite primo, post Epistolæ directionem, verf. 1. & 2. confirmat fidem Colossensium, & suum in eos amorem, quatuor modis. Primo, gratias agendo pro ipsorum sincera conversione, ad verf. 9. Secundo, pro iis precando, ad verf. 12. Tertio, Eucharisticè prædicando, certitudinem Redemptionis nostræ fundatam in gratia DEI, & excellentia Christi, ad verf. 23. Quarto, Hortando eos ad perseverantiam, ad finem Capitis.
units.tr: In the first chapter, after the address of the letter, in verses 1 and 2, he confirms the faith of the Colossians and his own love toward them in four ways. First, by giving thanks for their sincere conversion, to verse 9. Second, by praying for them, to verse 12. Third, by a eucharistic proclamation of the certainty of our redemption, founded on the grace of God and the excellence of Christ, to verse 23. Fourth, by exhorting them to perseverance, to the end of the chapter.

units.la: Verf. 1. Paulus Apostolus Iesu Christi per voluntatem Dei, & Timotheus frater,
units.tr: Verse 1. Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ by the will of God, and Timothy our brother,

units.la: IN Epistolæ directione describuntur primò personæ salutantes, Paulus & Timotheus: Paulus, ab authoritate legationis, à Christo immediatè, à Deo Patre verò mediante Christo concessæ: per cujus voluntatem Apostolatu fungebatur: Timotheus verò (qui testis diligentiæ Apostolicæ in confirmandis Colossensibus assumitur) describitur à consortio cum Paulo, ut frater ipsius, non propter fidei professionem tantùm sed etiam propter officium prædicationis ejusdem Euangelii.
units.tr: In the address of the letter, the persons who send greetings are first described: Paul and Timothy. Paul is described by his authority as an envoy, granted to him immediately by Christ, but ultimately by God the Father through Christ, by whose will he performed the apostolic office. Timothy, who is taken as a witness to the apostolic diligence in strengthening the Colossians, is described by his association with Paul, as his brother, not only because of his profession of faith but also because of his office of preaching the same Gospel.

units.la: Verf. 2. Iis qui sunt Colossis, sanctis ac fidelibus fratribus in Christo, Gratia vobis & pax à Deo Patre nostro, & Domino Iesu Christo.
units.tr: Verse 2. To those who are at Colossae, the holy and faithful brethren in Christ: grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.

units.la: Deinde describuntur personæ salutatæ, seu membra Ecclesiæ Colossensis & vocantur, 1. Fratres, quia regeniti ab eodem Patre, in eandem spem hæreditatis: 2. Sancti, quia Deo consecrati, & à Spiritu RITU Sancto sanctificati; & 3. Fideles, quia per fidem CHRISTO insiti fuerunt: Denique, per benedictionem Apostolicam applicantur Colossensibus Gratia & Pax: Gratia comprehendit omnia specialia DEI favoris effecta, quae per modum sanctificationis ad felicitatem tendunt: Pax vero comprehendit omnes felicitatis gradus, usque ad perfectionem in Coelo; Autor & efficiens bonorum statuitur DEUS PATER, & IESUS CHRISTUS, qua Filius & Mediator, in efficiendo, Patre suo ordine posterior.
units.tr: Next, the persons greeted are described, that is, the members of the Colossian Church, and they are called: (1) brethren, because they have been born again from the same Father, into the same hope of inheritance; (2) holy, because they have been consecrated to God and sanctified by the Holy Spirit; and (3) faithful, because they have been grafted into Christ through faith. Finally, grace and peace are applied to the Colossians by the apostolic blessing. Grace comprehends all the special effects of God's favour, which tend by way of sanctification toward happiness; peace comprehends all the degrees of happiness, up to perfection in heaven. God the Father and Jesus Christ are set forth as the author and efficient cause of these good things, Christ as the Son and Mediator in effecting them, being in order after his Father.

units.la: Vers. 3. Gratias agimus Deo & Patri Domini nostri Iesu Christi semper pro vobis precantes:
units.tr: Verse 3. We give thanks to God and the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, always praying for you,

units.la: Vers. 4. Audita fide vestra in Christo Iesu, & charitate in omnes sanctos:
units.tr: Verse 4. Having heard of your faith in Christ Jesus and of the love you have toward all the saints:

units.la: Primus modus confirmationis fidei Colossensium est per gratiarum actionem, pro ipsorum sincera conversione. Hujusmodi argumenta sunt septem, quae omnia probant corroborari in fide debere Colossenses: Argumentum primum, Post acceptum nuncium de vestra conversione ad fidem, amplam mihi materiam praebuistis gratiarum actionis & precationis ad DEUM: Ergo vel hoc nomine confirmari debetis in fide.
units.tr: The first way of confirming the faith of the Colossians is by thanksgiving for their sincere conversion. There are seven arguments of this kind, all of which prove that the Colossians ought to be strengthened in faith. The first argument: after receiving news of your conversion to the faith, you have given me ample matter for thanksgiving and prayer to God. Therefore, for this reason alone you ought to be confirmed in faith.

units.la: Charitate Arg. 2. Fidei vestrae in CHRISTO sinceritas per dilectionem erga omnes Sanctos, palam innotuit, cujus rei fama ad meas aures pervenit, Ergo in fide corroborari vos consentaneum est.
units.tr: By love Argument 2. The sincerity of your faith in Christ has become openly known through your love toward all the saints. The report of this has reached my ears. Therefore it is fitting that you be strengthened in faith.

units.la: Vers. 5. Propter spem sepositam vobis in coelis; quam prius audistis per sermonem veritatis, id est, Euangelii.
units.tr: Verse 5. On account of the hope laid up for you in heaven, which you heard of before in the word of truth, that is, the Gospel.

units.la: Arg. 3. Certo scio repositam esse vobis in coelo speratam felicitatem, & tanquam DEI beneficio jam vobis dato DEO gratias ago: Corroborari debetis igitur in fide.
units.tr: Argument 3. I know for certain that the happiness hoped for is laid up for you in heaven, and I give thanks to God as for a benefit of God already given to you. You ought therefore to be strengthened in faith.

units.la: Audistis Arg. 4. Confirmans superius, Pro fundamento fidei & spei vestrae, habetis indubitatum verbum DEI, verbum veritatis Euangelii: In fide confirmari debetis igitur.
units.tr: You heard Argument 4. Confirming what was said above: for the foundation of your faith and hope you have the indubitable word of God, the word of the truth of the Gospel. Therefore you ought to be confirmed in faith.

units.la: Vers. 6. Quod pervenit ad vos, sicut & in totum mundum, & fructum profert, sicut apud vos quoque, ex quo die verè audivistis & cognovistis Dei gratiam.
units.tr: Verse 6. Which has come to you, as it also has in all the world, and bears fruit, as it does among you also, from the day you heard and truly knew the grace of God.

units.la: Arg. 5. Verbum Euangelii, per quod vos conversi estis, idem illud Euangelium est, quod per Apostolos personuit in reliquo mundo eandemque habet efficaciam ad fructificationem inter vos, ab eo die quo per fidem amplexi estis DEI gratiam, quam habet in reliquis Ecclesiis Christianis: Ergo in fide corroborari vos æquum est.
units.tr: Argument 5. The word of the Gospel, through which you were converted, is that same Gospel which has sounded through the Apostles in the rest of the world, and it has the same efficacy for bearing fruit among you, from the day on which you embraced by faith the grace of God, which it has in the other Christian Churches. Therefore it is right that you be confirmed in faith.

units.la: Verf. 7, Sicut & didicistis ex Epaphra dilecto conservo nostro, qui est fidus pro vobis minister Christi:
units.tr: Verse 7. As you also learned from Epaphras, our beloved fellow servant, who is a faithful minister of Christ on your behalf:

units.la: Arg. 6. Pastor vester Epaphras, non alia docuit vos quam quod nos Apostoli passim docemus, qui idcirco Epaphram nostrum conservum & fidelem CHRISTI Ministrum, lubentes agnoscimus: In fide igitur stabiliri debetis.
units.tr: Argument 6. Your minister Epaphras taught you nothing other than what we Apostles teach everywhere. For this reason we gladly acknowledge Epaphras, our fellow servant and a faithful minister of Christ. You ought therefore to be established in faith.

units.la: Verf. 8. Qui & declaravit nobis vestram per Spiritum charitatem.
units.tr: Verse 8. Who also declared to us your love in the Spirit.

units.la: Arg. 7. Speciale indicium sincerae vestrae fidei dedistis, nempe Christianae dilectionis vestrae erga me demonstrationem, cujus rei testem habeo Epaphram vestrum Ministrum. Quod ut reliqua superiora omnia, & mihi gratiarum actionis erga DEUM, & vobis confirmationis fidei in DEUM, argumenta suppeditat.
units.tr: Argument 7. You have given a special indication of your sincere faith, namely the demonstration of your Christian love toward me, of which I have Epaphras, your minister, as a witness. This, like all the preceding arguments, supplies both a ground for my thanksgiving to God and an argument for confirming you in faith toward God.

units.la: Verf. 9. Propterea & nos ex quo die id audivimus, non desinimus pro vobis orare, & petere ut impleamini omni agnitione voluntatis ejus, cum omni sapientia & intelligentia spirituali:
units.tr: Verse 9. For this reason we also, from the day we heard of it, have not ceased to pray for you, and to ask that you may be filled with the knowledge of his will in all wisdom and spiritual understanding,

units.la: Secundus modus confirmationis fidei Colossensium, & dilectionis Apostoli erga eos, est ardens & constans ipsius precatio pro ipsis excitata per famam fidei ipsorum in CHRISTUM, & dilectionis erga Sanctos; precationis autem articuli sunt sex. Articulus 1. Precor ut amplam mensuram cognitionis voluntatis divinae revelatae in verbo Euangelii de CHRISTO, ejusque beneficiis adipiscamini.
units.tr: The second way of confirming the faith of the Colossians, and of the Apostle's love toward them, is his ardent and constant prayer for them, stirred up by the report of their faith in Christ and of their love toward the saints. There are six articles of this prayer. Article 1: I pray that you may obtain an ample measure of the knowledge of the divine will revealed in the word of the Gospel concerning Christ and his benefits.

units.la: In quem ] Articulus 2. Precor ut haec cognitio in vobis abundet in sapientia & intelligentia spirituali, id est, in sancta contemplatione mysteriorum fidei spiritualium, & in prudenti applicatione cognitionis datae ad praxin, in uniuscujusque virtutis exercitio.
units.tr: In whom ] Article 2: I pray that this knowledge may abound in you in wisdom and spiritual understanding, that is, in holy contemplation of the spiritual mysteries of faith, and in prudent application of the knowledge given to practice, in the exercise of each virtue.

units.la: Verf. 10. Ut incedatis sicut Domino dignum est, ut per omnia placeatis, omni opere bono fructum proferentes, & crescentes in agnitionem DEI.
units.tr: Verse 10. That you may walk worthily of the Lord, that you may please him in all things, bearing fruit in every good work and growing in the knowledge of God.

units.la: Articulus 3. est, Precor ut incedatis, seu vitam degatis, sicut dignum est Domino, seu ut decet conversos in conspectu DEI, nempe ut per omnia ei placeatis.
units.tr: Article 3: I pray that you may walk, that is, live, as is worthy of the Lord, or as becomes those converted in the sight of God, namely that you may please him in all things.

units.la: Omni ] Articulus 4. Precor ut fructificetis non in uno tantum, sed in omni genere bonorum operum. Crescatis ] Articulus 5. Precor ut crescatis in experientia, & vivæ agnitione virtutis Divinæ per obedientiam voluntatis ipsius, studentes cum magis magisque cognoscere diligere, eique adhærere.
units.tr: All ] Article 4: I pray that you may bear fruit not in one kind only, but in every kind of good work. Growing ] Article 5: I pray that you may grow in experience and in the living knowledge of the divine power, through obedience to his will, striving to know him more and more, to love him, and to cleave to him.

units.la: Verf. 11. Omni robore corroborati, secundum gloriosam vim ipsius ad omnem tolerantiam & animi lenitatem cum gaudio:
units.tr: Verse 11. Strengthened with all might, according to his glorious power, unto all endurance and patience with joy:

units.la: Articulus 6. Precor ut ea mensura roboris cœlestis, ex divite penu gloriosæ potentiæ Dei vobis suppeditetur, ut quodvis onus afflictionis, seu persecutionis fortiter pati, idque quamdiu Deo visum fuerit, cum longanimitate sustinere possitis, non tantum sine animi ægritudine, sed & maxima cum delectatione & gaudio: Ergo corroborari in fide debetis, nisi preces meas quas Spiritus Sanctus excitat in corde meo pro vobis irritas putetis.
units.tr: Article 6: I pray that such a measure of heavenly strength may be supplied to you from the rich storehouse of the glorious power of God, that you may bear bravely any burden of affliction or persecution, and endure it with patience for as long as God sees fit, not only without bitterness of spirit but even with the greatest delight and joy. Therefore you ought to be strengthened in faith, unless you consider my prayers, which the Holy Spirit stirs up in my heart for you, to be in vain.

units.la: Verf. 12 Gratias agentes Patri, qui idoneos nos fecit ad participandam sortem sanctorum in luce
units.tr: Verse 12. Giving thanks to the Father, who has made us fit to share in the inheritance of the saints in light.

units.la: Tertius modus confirmationis ipsorum fidei, est eucharistica prædicatio certudinis nostræ redemptionis, fundatæ in gratia Dei, & excellentia personæ Christi. Rationes εὐχαριστίας seu gratiarum actionis sunt quinque. Ratio 1. est, Quia præparavit nos Deus Pater ad regnum cœleste adeundum: hoc beneficium specialius perspicitur in sequentibus: 1. Beneficii donator, ponitur Deus Pater, omnis boni autor, & fons primus, paternum erga nos gerens affectum: 2. Cum dicimur idonei facti, &c. Miseria nostra præsupponitur, & quod natura sumus inidonei, tenebriones nati, peccato inquinati, & filii iræ: 3. Etiamsi inidonei fuerimus, gratia Dei tamen nos idoneos reddidit, per efficacem vocationem, & nostri regenerationem: 4. Felicitas ad quam vocamur est permanens hæreditas, κληρος quæ forte aditur, id est, non merito aliquo humano, sed electione gratuita obtinetur, & data semel non aufertur: 5. Sanctorum vocatur hæreditas, quia in ea nobis societas futura est cum solis Sanctis, quorum communio hæreditatem nobis faciet jucundiorem. 6. Hæreditas hæc consistit in luce perfectissima nempe cognitionis, sanctitatis, gaudii, gloriæ, vitæque immortalis seu æternæ.
units.tr: The third way of confirming their faith is a eucharistic proclamation of the certainty of our redemption, founded on the grace of God and the excellence of the person of Christ. The reasons for thanksgiving [εὐχαριστίας] are five. Reason 1: because God the Father has prepared us to enter the heavenly kingdom. This benefit is seen more specifically in what follows. (1) The giver of the benefit is named as God the Father, the author of every good and the first fountain, bearing a fatherly affection toward us. (2) When we are said to have been made fit, our misery is presupposed, and that by nature we are unfit, born in darkness, polluted by sin, and children of wrath. (3) Even though we were unfit, the grace of God has nevertheless made us fit, through effectual calling and our regeneration. (4) The happiness to which we are called is a lasting inheritance [κληρος], which is obtained perhaps not by any human merit but by free election, and once given is not taken away. (5) It is called the inheritance of the saints, because in it we shall have fellowship with the saints alone, whose communion will make the inheritance more pleasant to us. (6) This inheritance consists in the most perfect light, namely of knowledge, holiness, joy, glory, and immortal or eternal life.

units.la: Verf. 13. Qui, inquam, liberavit nos à potestate tenebrarum ac transtulit in regnum Filii sibi dilecti.
units.tr: Verse 13. Who, I say, has delivered us from the power of darkness and transferred us into the kingdom of his beloved Son.

units.la: Secunda ratio gratiarum actionis explicans priorem, Quia Pater eripuit nos è nos è potestate tenebrarum, & transstulit in regnum filii dilectionis suæ: hoc beneficium commendatur nobis ex his quatuor: 1. Quod vis adhibita sit perversæ nostræ naturæ, & potestati Satanæ, à quo vincti, detinebamur: unde Deus vi nos eripuit: 2. Quod eripuerit nos à tenebris ignorantiæ, peccati & miseriæ: 3. Quod ereptos nos non siverit vagari & errare sine rege & defensore, sine regimine & societate, sed transtulerit in melius regnum, id est, regnum lucis, cognitionis, sanctitatis & vitæ spiritualis, ubi tutò & securè possimus agere, ne relabamur aut revocemur in tenebras: 4. Quod regnum in quod transferimur sit regnum filii sui; regnum Deo amicissimum, in quo præsidet & regnat filius Dei, filius dilectionis, quem Pater intimè diligit, & qui dilectione erga nos Patrem repræsentat, cujus regnum & res omnes sunt Deo dilectissimæ, imo in cujus regno omnes subditi sunt filii dilecti.
units.tr: The second reason for giving thanks, explaining the first, is that the Father snatched us out of the power of darkness and transferred us into the kingdom of his beloved Son. This benefit is commended to us on four grounds: (1) force was applied to our perverse nature and to the power of Satan, by which we were bound and held captive, so God rescued us by force; (2) he rescued us from the darkness of ignorance, sin and misery; (3) having rescued us, he did not allow us to wander and stray without a king and defender, without rule and fellowship, but transferred us into a better kingdom, that is, a kingdom of light, knowledge, holiness and spiritual life, where we may act safely and securely and not slip back or be recalled into darkness; (4) the kingdom into which we are transferred is the kingdom of his Son, a kingdom most dear to God, in which the Son of God presides and reigns, the Son of love, whom the Father loves intimately and who represents the Father's love towards us, whose kingdom and all whose affairs are most dear to God, indeed in whose kingdom all the subjects are beloved sons.

units.la: Vers. 14. In quo habemus redemptionem per sanguinem ipsius, id est, remissionem peccatorum.
units.tr: Verse 14. In whom we have redemption through his blood, that is, the forgiveness of sins.

units.la: Tertia ratio gratiarum actionis est beneficium liberationis à Dei justitia vindicatrice; hoc beneficium specialius apparet in his quinque: 1. Nos non tantùm vi detinebamur in potestate tenebrarum, unde ut eriperemur requirebatur vis major, sed etiam legis & justitiæ captivi fuimus, unde non nisi pretio persoluto emitti poteramus, quod pretium ubi jam persolutum est, redemptio legitima jam facta est: 2. Redemptionem hanc habemus nostram factam, ex consensu partium, jure optimo: 3. Habemus eandem in persona filii, qui Advocatus est noster, & qui nos noştraque omnia custodit: 4. Habemus eam per sanguinem filii, qui in forma Dei existens, id est verus Deus assumpsit naturam nostram, in eaque obediens factus usque ad mortem crucis, persolvit pro nobis pretium redemptionis: 5. Redemptio hæc est gratuita respectu nostri, qui nihil persolvimus, & tamen peccatorum remissionem consequuti sumus, & per consequens etiam gratuitam liberationem ab ira & morte, quæ persequuntur peccata.
units.tr: The third reason for giving thanks is the benefit of deliverance from God's avenging justice. This benefit appears more particularly in these five points: (1) we were held not only by force in the power of darkness, so that a greater force was needed to set us free, but we were also captives of the law and of justice, so that we could not be released except once the price had been paid; and when that price has been paid, the legal redemption is already accomplished; (2) we have this redemption made in our favour, by the agreement of the parties, by the best right; (3) we have it in the person of the Son, who is our Advocate and who keeps us and all that is ours; (4) we have it through the blood of the Son, who, existing in the form of God, that is, being true God, assumed our nature, and in that nature, becoming obedient even unto the death of the cross, paid the price of redemption for us; (5) this redemption is free so far as we are concerned, for we paid nothing, and yet we have obtained the forgiveness of sins and, consequently, also a free deliverance from the wrath and death that follow sin.

units.la: Vers. 15. Qui est imago Dei invisibilis, primogenitus omnis rei creatæ:
units.tr: Verse 15. Who is the image of the invisible God, the firstborn of every creature:

units.la: Quarta ratio gratiarum actionis, ostendens soliditatem fundamenti redemptionis, in descriptione excellentiæ Christi Redemptoris, cujus descriptionis Articuli sunt duodecim.
