units.tr: The fourth reason for giving thanks, showing the firmness of the foundation of redemption, lies in the description of the excellence of Christ the Redeemer. There are twelve articles in this description.

units.la: Articulus 1. CHRISTUS imago est perfectissima Dei invisibilis, non tantùm quia est substantialis character personæ Patris, substantialiter Patrem repræsentans, ita ut Pater non nisi in Filio & splendore ipsius conspici possit, sed etiam quia filius incarnatus verbo & opere, sanctitate, potentia, misericordia, Patris naturam, voluntatem & bonitatem mundo repræsentavit.
units.tr: Article 1. CHRIST is the most perfect image of the invisible God, not only because he is the substantial character of the person of the Father, representing the Father in substance, so that the Father can be seen only in the Son and in his brightness, but also because the Son, made flesh, has represented to the world the nature, will and goodness of the Father by word and deed, by holiness, power and mercy.

units.la: Articulus 2. CHRISTUS primogenitus est omnis creaturæ, id est, ab æterno genitus ante omnem creaturam, & propter æternam generationem ex Patre, jure Dominus omnium creaturarum est, sicut in lege primogenitus est Dominus fratrum & familiæ.
units.tr: Article 2. CHRIST is the firstborn of every creature, that is, begotten from eternity, before every creature, and because of his eternal generation from the Father he is by right Lord of all creatures, just as in the law the firstborn is lord of the brothers and of the household.

units.la: Vers. 16. Nam per eum condita sunt omnia quæ in cælis sunt, & quæ in terra, visibilia & invisibilia, sive throni, sive dominia, sive imperia, sive potestates: omnia, inquam, per eum & ejus respectu condita sunt.
units.tr: Verse 16. For by him were all things created that are in heaven and that are in earth, visible and invisible, whether thrones or dominions or principalities or powers: all things, I say, were created by him and with respect to him.

units.la: Articulus 3. Illustrans superiorem: CHRISTUS est efficiens seu Creator omnium creaturarum: per eum enim omnia condita sunt: hunc Articulum amplificat triplici distributione creaturarum: 1. A loco in quo sunt, in cœlo & in terra: 2. A natura sua, in visibiles & invisibiles: 3. Divisione Angelorum à dignitate & officio & nominibus honorificis: ex quibus apparet gloria CHRISTI qui creavit omnes.
units.tr: Article 3. Illustrating the previous article: CHRIST is the efficient cause or Creator of all creatures, for by him all things were created. This article is amplified by a threefold division of creatures: (1) by the place where they are, in heaven and on earth; (2) by their nature, into visible and invisible; (3) by the division of the angels according to their dignity, office and honourable names. From these it appears the glory of Christ, who created all.

units.la: Articulus 4. CHRISTUS est finis omnium, propter quem seu cujus gloriam omnia condita sunt: nam quæcunque & qualiacunque condita sunt, ea omnia in gloriam CHRISTI Θεάνθρωπος condita sunt; ille Alpha & Omega est omnium, cujus gloriæ omnia inservire necesse est, suo quæque modo, ut media ad finem.
units.tr: Article 4. CHRIST is the end of all things, for whose sake, that is, for whose glory, all things were created; for whatever and whatever kind of things have been created, all of them have been created for the glory of Christ the God-man [Θεάνθρωπος]. He is the Alpha and Omega of all, and all things must serve his glory, each in its own way, as means to an end.

units.la: Vers. 17. Estque ipse ante omnia, & omnia per eum consistunt,
units.tr: Verse 17. And he is before all things, and in him all things consist.

units.la: Articulus 5. CHRISTUS est æternus, quia in se ante omnes creaturas est, nec mutuatur ad sui subsistentiam à creaturis quicquam.
units.tr: Article 5. CHRIST is eternal, because he exists in himself before all creatures, and he borrows nothing from creatures for his subsistence.

units.la: Articulus 6. CHRISTUS non Creator tantùm, sed & conservator & sustentator omnium est.
units.tr: Article 6. CHRIST is not only the Creator but also the preserver and sustainer of all things.

units.la: Vers. 18. Estque caput corporis Ecclesiæ, principium & primogenitus ex mortuis, ut in omnibus primas teneat:
units.tr: Verse 18. And he is the head of the body, the Church; the beginning, the firstborn from the dead, that in all things he may have the preeminence.

units.la: Articulus 7. CHRISTUS est Caput Ecclesiæ, id est, sui corporis, unde influit vitalis Spiritus, sensus motusque spiritualis in omnia membra, quique regit & protegit ea omnia.
units.tr: Article 7. CHRIST is the Head of the Church, that is, of his own body, from whom the vital Spirit, spiritual sense and motion flow into all the members, and who rules and protects them all.

units.la: Articulus 8. CHRISTUS est principium, fons & scaturigo Ecclesiæ, novus scilicet ille Adam, radix & principium regenerationis Sanctorum, cujus virtute procreantur Sancti omnes.
units.tr: Article 8. CHRIST is the beginning, the fountain and spring of the Church, namely that new Adam, the root and origin of the regeneration of the saints, by whose power all the saints are brought forth.

units.la: Primogenitus ] Articulus 9. Christus est primogenitus ex mortuis, & primitiæ eorum qui obdormiverunt, quia solus virtute sua resurrexit, & causa est resurrectionis mortuorum ad vitam æternam.
units.tr: Firstborn ] Article 9. Christ is the firstborn from the dead and the firstfruits of those who have fallen asleep, because he alone rose by his own power, and he is the cause of the resurrection of the dead to eternal life.

units.la: Ut inter ] Articulus 10. Ille in omnibus primatum tenet, & tenere debet in Angelos & homines, in viventes & mortuos: Et hic finis est superiorum graduum excellentiæ Christi.
units.tr: That in ] Article 10. He holds the preeminence in all things, and ought to hold it over angels and men, over the living and the dead. And this is the end of the higher degrees of Christ's excellence.

units.la: Verf. 19 Quoniam in eo placuit Patri, ut omnis plenitudo inhabitaret:
units.tr: Verse 19. For it pleased the Father that in him should all fullness dwell:

units.la: Articulus 11. Confirmans primatum Christi, & primatus dignitatem, quia ex Dei beneplacito in Christo homine habitat, non tantum donorum Spiritus plenitudo, sed etiam deitas ipsa plenissime comprehendens omnem plenitudinem.
units.tr: Article 11. Confirming the preeminence of Christ and the dignity of that preeminence: by God's good pleasure there dwells in Christ as man not only the fullness of the gifts of the Spirit, but also the Godhead itself, comprehending all fullness most completely.

units.la: Verf. 20 Et pace per sanguinem crucis ejus facta, per eum reconciliare omnia sibi, per eum, inquam, tum quæ in terra, tum quæ in cœlis.
units.tr: Verse 20. And having made peace through the blood of his cross, by him to reconcile all things to himself, by him, I say, whether things in earth or things in heaven.

units.la: Articulus 12. Christus ex Dei beneplacito, & propposito Mediator est, per quem voluit Deus expiationem peccatorum fieri, posita ejus vita in cruce, & expiatione per ejus mortem facta, reconciliationem fieri, seu amicitiæ redintegrationem inter Deum & eos qui sunt membra Ecclesiæ: non minus inter Deum & ea membra quæ sunt in terra, quam inter Deum & ea membra quæ sunt in cœlo: imo & reconciliationem, fieri voluit in se ἐν ἀνθρ seu intuitu gloriæ ipsius inter Angelos cœlestes, & homines terrestres, inter quos propter peccatum naturale dissidium est: Denique confirmari voluit electos Angelos, quorum natura varia & mutabilis jam demonstrata est per lapsum Angelorum reproborum. idque recapitulatione facta illorum ad seipsum. Nam Angeli quasi auctarium additi sunt Christo in fœdere redemptionis, in usum corporis sui, id est, Ecclesiæ, ut essent Spiritus ministrantes in usum Redemptorum hominum: Quæ omnia ut soliditatem & certitudinem redemptionis, sic fidem Colossensium in Christum magnopere confirmabant, & nostram etiamnum confirmare debent.
units.tr: Article 12. Christ, by God's good pleasure and purpose, is the Mediator through whom God willed that the expiation of sins should be made; his life being laid down on the cross, and expiation being made by his death, reconciliation is effected, or the restoration of friendship between God and those who are members of the Church: no less between God and those members who are on earth than between God and those members who are in heaven. Indeed, he willed that reconciliation be effected in himself [ἐν ἀνθρ] or with a view to his own glory, between the heavenly angels and earthly men, between whom there is discord on account of natural sin. Finally, he willed that the elect angels be confirmed, whose nature has already been shown to be variable and changeable through the fall of the reprobate angels; and this was done by a recapitulation of them to himself. For the angels were added to Christ, as it were as an addition, in the covenant of redemption, for the use of his body, that is, the Church, so that they might be ministering spirits for the use of redeemed men. All these things, as they strengthened the solidity and certainty of redemption, so they greatly confirmed the faith of the Colossians in Christ, and ought still to confirm ours.

units.la: Verf. 21. Itaque vos quondam abalienatos & hostes, mente operibus malis intenta, nunc jam reconciliavit,
units.tr: Verse 21. And you, who were once alienated and enemies in your mind, engaged in evil works, now he has reconciled,

units.la: Vers. 22. In corpore illo carnis suæ, per mortem, ut sisteret vos sanctos & irreprehensos & inculpatos coram se:
units.tr: Verse 22. In the body of his flesh, through death, so as to present you holy and blameless and unreproachable before himself.

units.la: Quinta ratio gratiarum actionis est Gratia reconciliationis facta Colossensibus nominatim. Hoc beneficium novem Argumentis amplificat: 1. Quod aliquando abalienati fueritis, inquit, à Deo, extranei à republica Israelis, & vita Dei: 2. Extranei non tantum nati, sed magis magisque extranei facti fuistis per peccatorum consuetudinem: 3. Neque id tantum, sed etiam quod hostes, & hostili animo Deum aversati, & profequuti fueritis: 4. Quod hostes fueritis non appetitu sensibili, & affectibus tantum, sed etiam ipsa mente vestra, quam accepistis esse præstantissimam facultatem, & aliarum Dominam ac ducem: 5. Quod inimicitias mente conceptas operibus malis expressertis. 6. Quod nihilominus tamen Christus nunc vos reconciliaverit: 7. Quod in corpore carnis suæ assumendo humanam naturam, nobis in omnibus, excepto peccato, similem, reconciliationem impetraverit: 8. Quod per mortem redemptionis & reconciliationis vestræ, pretium persolverit: 9. Quod Christus statuerit apud se vos Sanctos in conspecta suo, & Dei, tandem sistere, sine omni peccati & miseriæ labe, nempe in die adventus sui; quorum singula apprime faciebant ad fidem ipsorum fulciendam.
units.tr: The fifth reason for thanksgiving is the grace of reconciliation granted to the Colossians by name. Paul amplifies this benefit with nine arguments: (1) that you were once alienated from God, strangers to the commonwealth of Israel and to the life of God; (2) that you were not only born strangers, but became more and more strangers through the habit of sin; (3) and not only that, but that you were enemies and turned away from God and pursued him with a hostile mind; (4) that you were enemies not merely in sensible appetite and affections, but in your very mind, which you have received as the most excellent faculty, the mistress and leader of the others; (5) that you expressed the enmity conceived in your mind by evil works; (6) that nevertheless Christ has now reconciled you; (7) that by assuming human nature in the body of his flesh, like us in all things except sin, he obtained reconciliation for us; (8) that through the death of your redemption and reconciliation he paid the price; (9) that Christ determined to present you holy before himself and before the sight of God, without any stain of sin or misery, namely on the day of his coming. Each of these especially served to strengthen their faith.

units.la: Vers. 23. Siquidem permanetis in fide fundati & firmi, nec dimovemini a spe Euangelii quod audistis, Euangelii, inquam, prædicati omni creaturæ quæ sub cælo est: cujus factus sum ego Paulus minister: Sequitur quartus modus confirmationis fidei Colossensium per hortationem ad perseverantiam in fide Euangelii, ad quam transit, addita cautione in hunc finem ut suspendat beneficium communiter illis applicatum, data quasi characteristica nota eorum ad quos beneficium reconciliationis pertineat, nempe quod quicunque jus habent ad hæc beneficia, permaneant in fide Christi, unde reliqui gradus perseverantiæ dependent: Argumenta hortationis præcipua sunt tria. Siquidem ] Argumentum primum, Est in conditione perseverantiæ positum, Constantia vestra in fide Christi, & spe Euangelii, indicium est non tantum reconciliationis factæ per Christum, sed etiam sanctitatis & salutis vestræ per eum perficiendæ: Perseverate ergo. Interim ad ipsorum perseverantiam requirit tria: 1. Ut fundentur in fide, id est, fundamenta fidei, in DEI veritate, bonitate, & potentia, jacta solide apprehendant: 2. Ut firmi sint, id est, jam fundati in CHRISTO sedem fixam teneant, CHRISTO adhaereant, & agglutinentur veritati ejus: 3. Ut resistant omnibus tentationibus, quibus possent ullo modo a vitae aeternae & bonorum in Evangelio promissorum spe dimoveri: Argumenti vis haec est, Praedicta bona in vestram non venient possessionem, nisi perseveraveritis in fide, Perfistite igitur.
units.tr: Verse 23. If indeed you continue grounded and steadfast in the faith, and are not moved away from the hope of the gospel which you have heard, the gospel, I say, preached to every creature which is under heaven, of which I, Paul, am made a minister. Here follows the fourth way of confirming the faith of the Colossians, by exhortation to perseverance in the faith of the gospel. He turns to it, adding a caution with this end in view: he makes conditional the benefit commonly applied to them, giving as it were a distinguishing mark of those to whom the benefit of reconciliation belongs, namely that all who have a right to these benefits remain in the faith of Christ, on which the remaining steps of perseverance depend. The principal arguments of the exhortation are three. If indeed: the first argument lies in the condition of perseverance. Your constancy in the faith of Christ and the hope of the gospel is a sign not only of the reconciliation made through Christ, but also of the holiness and salvation to be brought to completion in you through him. Persevere, then. Meanwhile, for their perseverance he requires three things: (1) that they be grounded in faith, that is, that they firmly grasp the foundations of faith laid in the truth, goodness and power of God; (2) that they be steadfast, that is, already grounded, they hold a fixed seat in Christ, cling to Christ and are cemented to his truth; (3) that they resist all temptations by which they might in any way be moved from the hope of eternal life and of the good things promised in the gospel. The force of the argument is this: the aforesaid good things will not come into your possession unless you persevere in the faith. Persist, therefore.

units.la: Arg. 2. Hortationis ad perseverantiam; Evangelium quod audivistis a Pastore vestro Epaphra, idem est cum Evangelio ab aliis DEI servis annunciato in toto mundo omni creaturae, seu omnis generis hominibus Judaeis & Gentibus sine discrimine. Permanete ergo in illa fide fundati & stabiles.
units.tr: Argument 2 for exhortation to perseverance: the gospel which you have heard from your minister Epaphras is the same as the gospel announced by other servants of God throughout the whole world to every creature, that is, to men of every kind, Jews and Gentiles without distinction. Remain, therefore, grounded and stable in that faith.

units.la: Arg. 3. Hujus Evangelii Gentibus praedicandi ego ipse Paulus factus sum Minister, magna cum DEI approbatione, & benedictione effusa in omnes qui ex Gentibus sunt Fideles: Perseverate ergo in illa Fide.
units.tr: Argument 3: I, Paul, have been made a minister of this gospel to be preached to the Gentiles, with great approval and blessing from God poured out on all the faithful from the Gentiles. Persevere, then, in that faith.

units.la: Vers. 24. Qui nunc gaudeo de iis quae patior pro vobis, & reliquias afflictionum Christi vicissim expleo in carne mea, pro corpore ipsius, id est Ecclesia:
units.tr: Verse 24. I who now rejoice in the sufferings I endure for you, and in my flesh fill up what is lacking of the afflictions of Christ, on behalf of his body, that is, the Church.

units.la: In hoc Argumento insistit, suumque Ministerium illis commendat Argumentis 14. quae omnia gloriosum ejus Ministerium confirmant: 1. In hujus Evangelii administratione ego Paulus cum gaudio fero afflictiones. Gloriosum ergo est meum Ministerium: 2. Pro vobis Colossensibus, seu pro vestra confirmatione in fide eas afflictiones sustineo. Gloriosum apud vos igitur meum Ministerium: 3. Cum sint personales & antitypa CHRISTI passiones, reliquae maneant passiones Martyrum, in testimonium veritatis doctrinae CHRISTI, ego Paulus aliqua ex parte harum afflictionum mensuram destinatam impleo ita, ut vel morte mea obsignare hoc meum Ministerium paratus sim. Gloriosum igitur hoc meum Ministerium est: 4 Ego pro CHRISTI honore & aedificatione totius Ecclesiae CHRISTI, scilicet ut coagmentetur in fide corpus ejus mysticum, afflictiones eas patior. Gloriosum igitur Ministerium meum. Haec omnia etiam ad tollendum offendiculum crucis Apostolo incumbentis faciunt.
units.tr: In this argument he insists, and commends his ministry to them by fourteen arguments, all of which confirm the glory of his ministry. (1) In the administration of this gospel I, Paul, bear afflictions with joy. My ministry is therefore glorious. (2) I endure those afflictions for you Colossians, that is, for your confirmation in the faith. My ministry is therefore glorious among you. (3) Since the sufferings of Christ are personal and antitypes, the remaining sufferings are those of the martyrs, endured in witness to the truth of Christ's doctrine. I, Paul, in some part fill up the measure of these afflictions appointed for me, so that I am ready to seal this my ministry even by my death. This ministry of mine is therefore glorious. (4) For the honour of Christ and the building up of the whole Church of Christ, namely that his mystical body may be knit together in the faith, I suffer these afflictions. My ministry is therefore glorious. These things also serve to remove the stumbling-block of the cross which lies upon the Apostle.

units.la: Vers. 25. Cujus Ecclesiae factus sum minister ex dispensatione Dei, quae data est mihi erga vos, ad implendum Dei sermonem:
units.tr: Verse 25. Of which Church I am made a minister, according to the dispensation of God which was given to me toward you, to fulfil the word of God.

units.la: Arg. 5.
units.tr: Argument 5.

units.la: Ecclesiæ Catholicæ sum Minister constitutus, & speciali autoritate, & dispensatione Divinâ Gentium Apostolus factus sum. Gloriosum ergo Ministerium meum.
units.tr: I have been appointed a minister of the Catholic Church, and by special authority and divine dispensation I have been made Apostle of the Gentiles. My ministry is therefore glorious.

units.la: Arg. 6. In Apostolatu constitutus sum in eum speciale finem, ut plene manifestando Euangelium inter Gentes non tantùm munus meum, sed etiam Dei decretum & prophetias de vocandis Gentibus & de gratia Christi ad eas venturas, per meum Ministerium implerem: Gloriosum igitur est hoc meum Ministerium.
units.tr: Argument 6. I have been constituted an Apostle for this special end: that by fully manifesting the gospel among the Gentiles I might fulfil, through my ministry, not only my office but also God's decree and the prophecies concerning the calling of the Gentiles and the coming of the grace of Christ to them. This my ministry is therefore glorious.

units.la: Verf. 26. Nempe ministerium abscônditum à seculis & ætatibus, nunc autem illud patefactum est sanctis ejus,
units.tr: Verse 26. Namely, the mystery hidden from ages and generations, but now made manifest to his saints,

units.la: Arg. 7. Sermo hic Euangelii administratus inter vos, ejusque futura inter Gentes annunciatio, olim fuerat mysterium: nunc vero planius quam unquam ab initio mundi patefit per nos Apostolos, fidelibus: Ergo.
units.tr: Argument 7. This word of the gospel, administered among you and its future announcement among the Gentiles, was once a mystery; but now, more plainly than ever since the beginning of the world, it is revealed to the faithful through us Apostles. Therefore...

units.la: Verf. 27. Quibus voluit Deus notum facere quæ sint divitiæ gloriosi hujus mysterii inter Gentes, id est, Christi inter vos, qui est spes illa gloriæ:
units.tr: Verse 27. To whom God willed to make known what are the riches of the glory of this mystery among the Gentiles, that is, Christ among you, who is the hope of glory:

units.la: Arg. 8. Revelatio hujus mysterii per meum Ministerium facta est Sanctis, non ex ipsorum merito, sed ex Dei beneplacito: Ergo.
units.tr: Argument 8. The revelation of this mystery through my ministry has been made to the saints not from their own merit but from God's good pleasure. Therefore...

units.la: Arg. 9. Gloriosa & dives est gratia hujus mysterii jam revelati, omnia quæ ad plenam felicitatem faciunt perspicuè aperiens: Ergo.
units.tr: Argument 9. The grace of this mystery, now revealed, is glorious and rich, clearly setting out all that contributes to full happiness. Therefore...

units.la: Arg. 10. Summa hujus gloriosæ & divitis gratiæ per meum Ministerium manifestata, est Christus per fidem receptus & habitans in vobis: Gloriosum igitur.
units.tr: Argument 10. The sum of this glorious and rich grace, manifested through my ministry, is Christ received by faith and dwelling in you. Therefore it is glorious.

units.la: Arg. 11. Christus à me prædicatus & in vobis habitans per fidem est spes illa gloriæ futuræ, jam in arrabone & primitiis manifestatæ; nempe quia Christus est author, pignus & complementum omnis spei nostræ: nullam enim aliam gloriam quærunt fideles, quam ut Christo potiantur magis magisque in hac vita, & tandem plenè in vita futura.
units.tr: Argument 11. Christ, preached by me and dwelling in you through faith, is that hope of future glory, already made manifest in the earnest and firstfruits; namely because Christ is the author, pledge and fulfilment of all our hope. For the faithful seek no other glory than to possess Christ more and more in this life, and at last fully in the life to come.

units.la: Verf. 28: Quemque nos annuntiamus, admonentes quemvis, & quemvis erudientes omni sapientia: ut quemvis sistamus persectum in Christo Iesu:
units.tr: Verse 28. Whom we proclaim, admonishing every man and teaching every man in all wisdom, that we may present every man perfect in Christ Jesus:

units.la: Arg. 12. Finis mei Ministerii & prædicati Christi hic est, ut omnis generis homines admoneam, & instituam in Euangelii doctrina, quæ est perfectissima sapientia, ut credentes tandem sistam in conspectu Dei, omnibus sanctitatis & felicitatis numeris in Christo, absolutos: Gloriosum ergo est hoc meum Ministerium.
units.tr: Argument 12. The aim of my ministry and of my preaching of Christ is this: that I may admonish and instruct men of every kind in the doctrine of the gospel, which is the most perfect wisdom, so that at last I may present them, believing, before the sight of God, made complete in Christ in every point of holiness and happiness. This my ministry is therefore glorious.

units.la: Vers. 29. Ad quod etiam enitor, decertans secundum efficacitatem ipsius agentem in me potenter.
units.tr: Verse 29. For which I also labour, striving according to his working, which works in me mightily.

units.la: Arg. 13. Strenuè hactenus per Dei gratiam profequutus sum meum Ministerium, decertans contra omnes hostes & impedimenta quæ mihi objiciebantur: Unde gloriosum redditum est Ministerium meum:
units.tr: Argument 13. Hitherto I have pursued my ministry vigorously by the grace of God, contending against all the enemies and hindrances which were set against me. Hence my ministry has been rendered glorious.

units.la: Secundum vim ] Arg. 14. Denique per Dei operantis in me gratiam & potentiam, Ministerium meum potens & efficax redditum est ad effectum destinatum, id est, ad salutem Electorum & reliquorum convictionem: Quæ omnia, sicut commendationis Ministerii Paulini argumenta, sic etiam totidem argumenta sunt hortationis ad Colossenses, ut in fide Euangelii à Paulo prædicati perseverent: Ex omnibus enim sequitur: Ergo in fide Euangelii cujus Ministerium adeò gloriosum est, constanter permanete & promovete.
units.tr: According to the power: Argument 14. Finally, by the grace and power of God working in me, my ministry has been made powerful and effective for its intended end, namely the salvation of the elect and the conviction of the rest. All these things, like the arguments commending the Pauline ministry, are likewise as many arguments for exhorting the Colossians to persevere in the faith of the gospel preached by Paul. For from all of them it follows: therefore, hold fast and advance in the faith of the gospel, whose ministry is so glorious.

units.la: Caput Secundum.
units.tr: Chapter 2.

units.la: Apitis tres sunt partes, in prima parat sibi viam ad hortationem, ut uno Christo contenti, fugiant corruptelas quæ à Christo abducerent, idque ostendendo studium suum de ipsorum constantia in fide; ad vers. 6. In secunda hortationem prosequitur, ut Christo mordicus adhæreant, cavantque in genere quicquid à Christo posset ipsos abducere, ad vers. 16.
units.tr: The chapter has three parts. In the first, he prepares the way for his exhortation, that they, content with Christ alone, should flee the corruptions that would draw them away from Christ, and he shows his concern for their steadfastness in the faith; to verse 6. In the second, he pursues the exhortation, that they should cling to Christ with their teeth, and guards in general against whatever could draw them away from Christ; to verse 16.

units.la: In tertia, admonitio est specialis, ut caveant sibi à corruptelis specialibus, ad finem.
units.tr: In the third, the admonition is specific, that they should beware of particular corruptions; to the end.

units.la: Vers. 1 Volùm enim vos scire quantum certamen sustineam pro vobis, & iis qui sunt Laodiceæ, & quotquot non viderunt faciem meam in carne:
units.tr: Verse 1: For I would have you know how great a conflict I sustain for you, and for those who are at Laodicea, and for as many as have not seen my face in the flesh.

units.la: Quod ad primam attinet, Studium suum de ipsorum salute, & constantia in fide ostendit membratim; membra sex sunt. 1. Solicitus sum de omnibus Ecclesiis quæ me non viderunt coram, & nominatim, de vobis Collossensibus, & vicinis vestris Laodicensibus, ne igitur vos neglectos à me putate.
units.tr: As to the first part, he shows his concern for their salvation and steadfastness in the faith, point by point; there are six points. 1. I am anxious about all the churches that have not seen me face to face, and by name about you Colossians and your neighbours the Laodiceans; so do not think that you have been neglected by me.

units.la: Vers. 2. Ut consolationem accipiant eorum corda ipsis charitate compactis, & omni opulentia certò persuasa intelligentia, ad cognitionem mysterii Dei & Patris & Christi:
units.tr: Verse 2: That their hearts may be comforted, being knit together in love, and unto all the riches of the full assurance of understanding, to the acknowledgement of the mystery of God, both of the Father and of Christ.

units.la: Membrum 2. Operam do, ut scientes vos mihi non minùs charos esse quam alias Ecclesias à me plantatas, consolationem capiatis in cordibus vestris ex eodem Euangelio. Charitate ] Membrum 3. Percupio, ut Ecclesiæ illæ omnes inter se, & cum aliis Ecclesiis, evitatis vel sublatis dissidiis, & quæstionibus quæ à Diabolo ipsiusque membris excitantur, nexu charitatis compingantur.
units.tr: Point 2. I take care that, knowing you are no less dear to me than the other churches planted by me, you may take comfort in your hearts from the same Gospel. In love: point 3. I desire that all those churches, with one another and with the other churches, having avoided or removed the dissensions and disputes that the Devil and his members stir up, be bound together by the bond of love.

units.la: Omni ] Membrum 4. In votis habeo, & non mediocre certamen sustineo, ut in fide & spe coagmententur omnes illæ Ecclesiæ. Hoc explicatur specialius, studebat enim ut intelligentiam nanciscerentur: quia fides cæca seu ignara esse non debet; nec ut fidei gustum aliquem tantùm haberent, sed πληροφορίαν consequerentur, qua hæsitationes ex ipsorum cordibus excluderentur; nec ut persuasionem tantùm, sed etiam omnem opulentiam persuasionis in fide haberent, ut fides in ipsis abundaret, inque solida & tranquilla certitudine corroboraretur, & stabileretur in omni opulentia plene certioratæ intelligentiæ: adhuc specialius, studebat Apostolus, ut proficerent in cognitione mysterii, seu Euangelii olim abscondití, sed nunc revelati, de Christi gratia quæ extenditur erga Gentes, non minus quam Judæos: his addit, ut proficerent non in cognitione tantùm, sed etiam in agnitione mysterii ex vivo sensu, & experientia suavissimæ gratiæ Christi, quæ ab hominum captu naturali longissimè removetur. Denique operam dabat specialissimè, ut proficerent in agnitione mysterii de unitate essentiæ divinæ, de distinctione personarum & officiis Mediatoris Christi, & in usum suum ista magis magisque applicantes conquiescerent in tanti boni cognitione, & primitiis, donec per Christum felicitate plena perfruerentur.
units.tr: All: point 4. I have in my prayers, and I undergo no small struggle, that all those churches be joined together in faith and hope. This is explained more specifically: he wished them to obtain understanding, because faith ought not to be blind or ignorant; nor should they merely have a taste of faith, but attain full assurance [πληροφορίαν], by which doubts would be excluded from their hearts; nor should they have only persuasion, but also all the riches of the assurance of persuasion in faith, so that faith might abound in them, be strengthened in solid and tranquil certainty, and be established in all the riches of a fully assured understanding. Even more specifically, the Apostle wished them to make progress in the knowledge of the mystery, that is, of the Gospel once hidden but now revealed, concerning Christ's grace which extends to the Gentiles no less than to the Jews. To this he adds that they should make progress not only in the knowledge, but also in the acknowledgement of the mystery from a living sense and experience of the most sweet grace of Christ, which is far removed from the natural grasp of men. Lastly, he labored most especially that they should make progress in the acknowledgement of the mystery concerning the unity of the divine essence, the distinction of the persons, and the offices of Christ the Mediator, and, applying these things more and more to their own use, that they might rest in the knowledge of so great a good, and in its first fruits, until they should enjoy it in full felicity through Christ.

units.la: Vers. 3. In quo sunt omnes thesauri sapientiæ ac cognitionis abscondití.
units.tr: Verse 3: In whom are all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge hidden.

units.la: Rationem huius desiderii reddit, ab excellentia Christi, qui Summa est, & Fundamentum Euangelii, cuius gloriam describit non tantùm à perfectione personæ ipsius per se spectatæ (in qua abscondití sunt omnes thesauri sapientiae & intelligentiae, infinite quoad divinam naturam, & quantum capere potest quoad humanam, sed etiam & potissimum à perfectione personae ipsius, quatenus officio Mediatoris vestitur, quatenus ille est Christus unctus ille Dei, objectum, author & consummator fidei nostrae, seu omnis cognitionis salutiferae: quo respectu in Christo est omni sufficientia ad salutem aeternam, ut non opus sit quicquam nosse praeter eum, qui factus est nobis à Deo Sapientia, Justitia, Sanctificatio, & Redemptio: Hanc Christi sufficientiam vocat thesauros, & omnes thesauros, & abscondites thesauros, quos mundus non potest perspicere, quos perscrutari non potest Sanctorum sagacitas, nec exhaurire omnium necessitas.
units.tr: He gives the reason for this desire, from the excellence of Christ, who is the sum and foundation of the Gospel. He describes his glory not only from the perfection of his person considered in itself (in whom are hidden all the treasures of wisdom and understanding, infinite as to the divine nature, and as much as can be grasped as to the human nature), but also and chiefly from the perfection of his person insofar as he is clothed with the office of Mediator, insofar as he is that anointed one of God, the object, author and perfecter of our faith, or of all saving knowledge. In this respect there is in Christ all sufficiency for eternal salvation, so that there is no need to know anything apart from him, who has been made to us by God wisdom, righteousness, sanctification and redemption. He calls this sufficiency of Christ treasures, and all the treasures, and hidden treasures, which the world cannot perceive, which the keen insight of the saints cannot search out, and which the need of all cannot exhaust.

units.la: Vers. 4.
units.tr: Verse 4.

units.la: Hoc autem dico, ne quis vobis imponat probabilitate sermonis.
units.tr: But this I say, lest anyone deceive you with persuasive speech.

units.la: Membrum 5. Studii & solicitudinis Apostoli est, ne seducantur Colossenses per Pseudapostolos, & ut muniantur adversus omnes impostures Pseudapostolorum, qui docendo quod Christus non docuit, instabiles & incautos à Christo abducebant, partim Paralogismis & Sophistis Argumentationibus, partim fucata eloquentia errores suos insinuantes & tegentes: ad quas Pseudapostolorum artes digitum intendit in vocibus παραλογισμοῖς & πιθανολογία.
units.tr: Point 5. It is the Apostle's concern and care that the Colossians not be seduced through false apostles, and that they be fortified against all the deceits of the false apostles, who, by teaching what Christ did not teach, drew away the unstable and the incautious from Christ, partly by paralogisms [παραλογισμοῖς] and sophistical arguments, partly by insinuating and concealing their errors with varnished eloquence. To these arts of the false apostles he points with the words paralogisms [παραλογισμοῖς] and persuasive speech [πιθανολογία].

units.la: Vers. 5.
units.tr: Verse 5.

units.la: Etsi enim corpore absum, Spiritu tamen sum vobiscum, gaudens ac cernens vestrum ordinem, & soliditatem vestrae in Christum fidei.
units.tr: For though I am absent in body, yet I am with you in spirit, rejoicing and beholding your good order and the steadfastness of your faith in Christ.

units.la: Membrum 6. Studii sui de ipsorum salute est, Gaudium quod de recte constitutâ inter eos doctrinâ & disciplinâ percipiebat, non ex relatione Epaphrae tantum, sed ex Spiritu Prophetico, seu inspiratione Spiritus Sancti dictantis hanc Epistolam; nam licet corpore absens fuerit, Spiritu tamen contemplatus omnia, perfusus fuit gaudio ex observatione ordinis in omnibus rebus Ecclesiasticis pulcherrimi, & fidei ipsorum in Christum solidae: adeo ut non potuerit non esse solicitus de tam praeclari inter eos Divini operis conservatione, ne Pseudapostolorum & Diaboli artibus perturbaretur ordo, vel corrumperetur doctrina.
units.tr: Sixth member of his concern for their salvation: he rejoiced at the well-ordered doctrine and discipline established among them, and he knew this not only from Epaphras's report but from the prophetic Spirit, that is, from the inspiration of the Holy Spirit who dictated this Epistle. For although he was absent in body, he beheld everything in spirit, and he was filled with joy at the observation of the most beautiful order in all ecclesiastical affairs and at the solid faith of the Colossians in Christ. So much so that he could not but be anxious lest so excellent a work of God among them be preserved in anything less than full measure, lest the order be disturbed or the doctrine corrupted by the arts of the false apostles and of the Devil.

units.la: Secunda pars Capitis.
units.tr: Second part of the chapter.

units.la: Vers. 6.
units.tr: Verse 6.

units.la: Sicut igitur accepistis Christum Iesum Dominum, ita in eo incedite: Secunda pars Capitis, in qua ex suo de ipsorum salute studio, & causis suscepta hujus disputationis adversus Pseudapostolos, infert hortationem ad perseverandum in fide CHRISTI, & ad cavendas corruptelas. Hortationis membra sunt quinque: 1. Ut fide jam receptum unicum & verum Salvatorem IESUM CHRISTUM retineant, nec alium confictum a Pseudapostolis admittant. 2. Ut in CHRISTO insiti per fidem maneant, & vitam suam ad ejus praescriptum traducant, sequentes Spiritus CHRISTI ductum.
units.tr: As therefore you have received Christ Jesus the Lord, so walk in him: The second part of the chapter, in which, from his concern for their salvation and the causes of this dispute against the false apostles, he draws an exhortation to persevere in the faith of Christ and to avoid corruptions. The members of the exhortation are five: (1) that they hold fast to the one true Saviour Jesus Christ, whom they have already received by faith, and not admit another invented by the false apostles; (2) that, rooted in Christ through faith, they remain in him and shape their lives according to his rule, following the leading of the Spirit of Christ.

units.la: Verf. 7. Radicati & superstructi in eo, ac confirmati fide, sicut edocti estis, abundantes ea cum gratiarum actione.
units.tr: Verse 7. Rooted and built up in him, and established in the faith, as you have been taught, abounding in it with thanksgiving.

units.la: Tertium membrum, ut arctissimae & firmissimae cum CHRISTO conjunctioni studeant per fidei suae corroborationem, secundum doctrinam Epaphrae: Hanc fidei solidítatem illustrat similitudine sumpta partim a firmitate arborum, altas radices in terra agentium; partim a stabilitate aedificiorum, solide fundatorum.
units.tr: The third member: that they strive for the closest and firmest union with Christ by strengthening their faith, according to the teaching of Epaphras. He illustrates this solidity of faith by a comparison drawn partly from the firmness of trees that send deep roots into the earth, and partly from the stability of buildings solidly founded.

units.la: Exundantes ] Membrum quartum, Ut non solum confirmentur in fide; verumetiam in ea proficiant, & proficiendo abundent, per pleniorem mysteriorum CHRISTI cognitionem; idque cum quotidiana gratiarum actione erga DEUM, hujus tanti boni authorem.
units.tr: Abounding] The fourth member: that they should not only be confirmed in the faith but also make progress in it, and by progressing abound, through a fuller knowledge of the mysteries of Christ; and this with daily thanksgiving to God, the author of so great a good.

units.la: Verf. 8. Videte nequis sit qui vos depraedetur per philosophiam & inanem deceptionem, secundum traditionem hominum, secundum elementa mundi, & non secundum Christum.
units.tr: Verse 8. Beware lest anyone take you captive through philosophy and empty deceit, according to the tradition of men, according to the elements of the world, and not according to Christ.

units.la: Membrum 5. Hortationis, ut caveant sibi a seductoribus, qui imposturis suis tanquam retibus, DEI populum veluti pecora capiunt, & in praedam abigunt. Impostarum autem tres species recenset; quarum prima est Philosophia, seu inanis deceptio, sic dicta, non simpliciter, sed quatenus suos limites excedit, & allurgit ad res coelestes seu spirituales, deque doctrina in DEI Verbo statuit ex modulo corrupti & carnalis judicii: quo respectu licet speciem Sapientiae prae se ferat, inanis tamen deceptio comperitur: Altera species est Traditio Hominum, de vanis & superstitiosis ritibus, ab humano ingenio confictis. Tertia species est Injunctio Legalium, seu Leviticorum Rituum, qui hic dicuntur Elementa mundi, quia sunt mundana & carnalia rudimenta veteris populi, quibus tanquam Paedagogo ducebatur ante CHRISTI adventum, quaeque post adventum CHRISTI, tanquam umbrae evanuerunt. - Verf. 9. Nam in eo inhabitat omnis plenitudo deitatis corporaliter:
units.tr: Fifth member of the exhortation: that they beware of seducers who, with their deceptions as with nets, catch the people of God like cattle and drive them off as prey. He lists three kinds of deceit. The first is philosophy, or empty deceit: so called not simply, but insofar as it exceeds its proper limits, aspires to heavenly or spiritual things, and judges the doctrine of God's Word by the measure of a corrupt and carnal judgment. In this respect, although it puts on the appearance of wisdom, it is found to be empty deception. The second kind is the tradition of men, concerning vain and superstitious rites devised by human ingenuity. The third kind is the imposition of legal observances, or the rites of Leviticus, which are here called the elements of the world, because they are the worldly and carnal rudiments of the old people, by which they were led as by a schoolmaster before the coming of Christ, and which, after Christ came, vanished like shadows. - Verse 9. For in him dwells all the fullness of the Godhead bodily:

units.la: Argumenta hortationis subjungit decem, quæ omnia probant non esse recedendum vel latum unguem à Christo.
units.tr: He adds ten arguments for the exhortation, all of which prove that one must not withdraw so much as a finger's breadth from Christ.

units.la: Argumentum primum, Frustra quærendum est extra Christum quidvis ad salutem necessarium, cum in ipso seu ejus persona plenitudo deitatis hypostaticè unita humanæ naturæ comperiatur; adeo ut necessariò extra Deum quærat aliquid ad salutem, qui extra Christum quærit quidvis salutiferum: Ergo non recedendum à Christo.
units.tr: First argument: it is vain to seek outside Christ anything necessary for salvation, since in him, or in his person, the fullness of the Godhead is found hypostatically united to human nature. So that whoever seeks anything saving outside Christ must necessarily seek it outside God. Therefore one must not withdraw from Christ.

units.la: Verf. 10 Et estis in eo completi, qui est caput omnis imperii ac potestatis:
units.tr: Verse 10. And you are complete in him, who is the head of all rule and authority:

units.la: Arg. 2. Non tantum fons plenissimus est Christus in se, sed etiam plenè complet omnes fideles in ipsum credentes, quatenus justitiam & vitam æternam quam in se habet, communicat illis, primum imputatione, deinde gratiæ pro gratia infusione, donec tandem perficiantur. Ne ergo quæramus aliquid extra eum.
units.tr: Second argument: Christ is not only a most full fountain in himself, but he also fully completes all the faithful who believe in him, insofar as he communicates to them the righteousness and eternal life that he has in himself, first by imputation, then by the infusion of grace upon grace, until at last they are made perfect. Therefore let us not seek anything outside him.

units.la: Caput ] Arg. 3. Ille est Caput omnis principatus & potestatis, etiam excellentissimarum creaturarum, & in terra & in Cœlo, partim quia creavit omnia, & gubernat etiam ipsos Angelos; partim quia influxu virtutis suæ, sustinet etiam Angelos, nedum homines, communicatque illis quicquid habent: Ab eo ergo solo, & nec vel à præstantissimis etiam Angelis expectemus quicquam boni.
units.tr: Head] Third argument: he is the Head of every principality and power, even of the most excellent creatures, both in earth and in heaven, partly because he created all things and governs even the angels themselves, and partly because by the influence of his power he also sustains the angels, let alone men, and communicates to them whatever they have. Therefore we should expect any good from him alone, and not even from the most eminent angels.

units.la: Verf. 11. In quo etiam circumcisi estis circumcisione quæ fit sine manibus, corpore peccatorum carnis exuto in circumcisione Christi:
units.tr: Verse 11. In whom you were also circumcised with a circumcision not made with hands, by putting off the body of the sins of the flesh, in the circumcision of Christ:

units.la: Arg. 4. Veritas omnium legalium ceremoniarum est in Christo: nam in eo fideles habent rem per illas præfiguratam, Verbi causa, Spiritualem habent circumcisionem, Spiritu Christi factam in corde, quæ consistit in depositione veteris hominis, seu carnis, seu corporis peccati, quæ circumcisio in manufacta carnali circumcisione præfigurabatur. Ergo non est quod in carnali judaizantium circumcisione quicquam quæratis extra Christum.
units.tr: Fourth argument: the truth of all legal ceremonies is in Christ. For in him the faithful have the reality prefigured by those rites. For example, they have a spiritual circumcision, wrought in the heart by the Spirit of Christ, which consists in the putting off of the old man, or of the flesh, or of the body of sin. This circumcision was prefigured by the circumcision made with hands in the flesh. Therefore you should seek nothing in the fleshly circumcision of the Judaizers outside Christ.

units.la: Verf. 12. Consepulti cum eo per Baptismum, per quem etiam cum eo resurrexistis, per fidem Dei efficaciter agentis, qui excitavit eum ex mortuis.
units.tr: Verse 12. Buried with him in baptism, in which you also were raised with him through faith in the working of God, who raised him from the dead.

units.la: Arg. 5. Baptismum externum internæ circumcisionis legitimum signum, num, surrogatum in locum circumcisionis à Christo, habetis vos fideles in Christo, adeo ut nec res interna, imo nec externum quidem signum rei internæ, extra Christum quærendum sit. Non igitur à Christo recedendum.
units.tr: Fifth argument: baptism, the outward sign that is the lawful counterpart of inward circumcision and was substituted by Christ in the place of circumcision, you have in Christ as believers. So that neither the inward reality nor even the outward sign of the inward reality is to be sought outside Christ. Therefore we must not withdraw from Christ.

units.la: Arg. 6. Vos fideles jus habetis ad Christum mortuum & sepultum, & communionem cum ipso, in morte & sepultura, adeoque jus ad omnia beneficia & effecta mortis, & sepulturæ ipsius, in baptismo, & per baptismum vobis obsignatum; adeo ut nihil opus sit extra Christum quicquam quærere, quod ad plenum redemptionis pretium persolvendum attinet: Non igitur ab eo recedendum.
units.tr: Sixth argument: you believers have a right to Christ dead and buried, and communion with him in his death and burial, and thus a right to all the benefits and effects of his death and burial, which are sealed to you in baptism and through baptism. So that there is no need to seek anything outside Christ for the full payment of the price of redemption. Therefore we must not withdraw from him.

units.la: Arg. 7. Vos fideles per Baptismum adducti estis in communionem resurrectionis Christi, seu victoriæ ejus de morte & peccato reportatæ, per quam non tantum resurrexistis ad vitæ novitatem in sanctitate, sed etiam resurgetis respectu corporum, ad vitam gloriosam & immortalem, ita ut ad sanctitatem & vitam æternam, extra Christum nihil desiderandum sit. Non ergo ab eo vel minimum recedendum est.
units.tr: Seventh argument: you believers, through baptism, have been brought into communion with the resurrection of Christ, that is, with his victory over death and sin. Through this you have risen not only to newness of life in holiness, but you will also rise, as to your bodies, to a glorious and immortal life. So that for holiness and eternal life nothing is to be desired outside Christ. Therefore we must not withdraw from him even in the slightest degree.

units.la: Cæterum ne externo baptismo nimium tribuatur, ex opere (quod dicunt) operato, requirit in baptizatis fidem Dei efficaciter agentis, id est, ut credamus Deum qui potenter suscitavit Christum ex mortuis secundum promissiones suas, eundem etiam efficaciter secundum promissiones resuscitaturum nos ad omnimodam vitæ novitatem. Quanto enim arctius amplectimur virtutem Dei quæ suscitavit Christum Caput nostrum à mortuis, tanto proficiemus magis in vitæ novitate.
units.tr: Moreover, lest too much be attributed to outward baptism, as if by what they call the work done, the apostle requires in the baptized faith in the working of God, that is, that we believe God, who powerfully raised Christ from the dead according to his promises, will also powerfully raise us, according to his promises, to every kind of newness of life. For the more tightly we embrace the power of God which raised Christ our Head from the dead, the more we shall progress in newness of life.

units.la: Vers. 13. Vosque mortuos in peccatis & præputio carnis vestræ, cum eo vivificavit, condonatis vobis omnibus peccatis,
units.tr: Verse 13. And you, being dead in your sins and in the uncircumcision of your flesh, he made alive together with him, having forgiven you all your sins,

units.la: Arg. 8. Vos Colossenses olim mortuos in peccatis, & jacentes in naturæ irregenitæ incircumcisione, Deus participes fecit vitæ Christi, sanctæ & immortalis, & quoad jus, & quoad possessionem inchoatam, ex gratia condonatis omnibus peccatis vestris: Ergo ad plenariam remissionem peccatorum, vitamque sanctam & immortalem, nihil extra Christum quærendum est. Dicitur autem hoc beneficium vivificatio cum Christo, licet Christus ante aliquot annos resurrexisset, priusquam illi conversi essent, quia quo momento quis per fidem unitur Christo, eodem etiam jam regnanti in Cælo, judiciali seu forensi modo unitur, imo & morienti, & sepulto, & resurgenti, adeoque in omnibus in quibus nostram personam sustinuit vel sustinet, non minus quam si Physico modo fuissemus praesentes, & consensissemus in omnem actum ejus pro nobis.
units.tr: Eighth argument: you Colossians, once dead in sins and lying in the uncircumcision of unregenerate nature, God has made partakers of the life of Christ, holy and immortal, both as to right and as to the beginning of possession. By grace he has forgiven all your sins. Therefore, for full remission of sins and for a holy and immortal life, nothing is to be sought outside Christ. This benefit is called being made alive together with Christ, although Christ had risen some years before you were converted, because at the moment a person is united to Christ by faith, he is also united to Christ, who now reigns in heaven, in a judicial or forensic manner; indeed, he is united to Christ dying, buried and rising, and thus in all the things in which Christ bore or bears our person, no less than if we had been physically present and had consented to every act he performed for us.

units.la: Vers. 14. Ac deleto quod adversum nos erat rituum Chirographo, quod, inquam, erat nobis contrarium, ipse vero cruci assixum e medio sustulit:
units.tr: Verse 14. "And blotting out the handwriting of ordinances that was against us, which, I say, was contrary to us, he himself took it away out of the way, nailing it to the cross."

units.la: Arg 9. In quo etiam explicat quomodo CHRISTUS remissionem peccatorum nobis impetraverit, nostrum Chirographum scilicet tollendo, in hunc sensum, Foedus operum seu legale, quasi Chirographum, partim comminationibus, partim decretis positivis ceremonialibus, Gentes ab Ecclesia secludentibus, sancitum, adversus nos erat, & nobis contrarium: CHRISTUS vero chirographum hoc sublatum e medio & affixum cruci delevit: Ergo vobis non est retrospiciendum ad foedus legale, vel ceremonialia decreta, ut in iis aliquid quaeratis, nec vobis est a CHRISTI, morte, (per quam liberati estis ab illo Chirographo) vel latum unguem recedendum: Hoc foedus operum cum appendicibus, comparat Chirographo, quo quis se obligat ad debitum persolvendum; nam per naturae lucem quicunque convicti tenentur peccati; ex vi foederis operum obnoxii etiam sunt irae, & quotiescunque arguimur peccati, toties etiam per naturam mortis poenam, seu foederis legalis conditionem, conscientiae nostrae sententia adversus nos ipsos, quasi calculo, seu Chirographo nostro confirmamus; Multo magis id praestat conscientia uniuscujusque qui legem scriptam accepit, & poenam violatae legis quotidie audit. Maxime vero omnium coguntur huic Chirographo subscribere justitiarii omnes, qui justitiam nullam agnoscunt praeter inhaerentem, seu eam quae est ex operibus: ex quibus erant judaizantes, & ceremoniarum observatores, qui foederi huic adhaerebant, quaerentes ex operibus & ceremoniarum decretis, justitiam: nam quanto manifestius hoc modo justitiam suam stabilire conabantur, tanto apertius mortem, violatae legis poenam, vi pacti in se derivabant: Nemo enim foedus init quin etiam foederis conditiones omnes admittat.
units.tr: Argument 9. In this verse he also explains how Christ obtained the forgiveness of sins for us, namely by taking away our handwriting, in this sense: the covenant of works, or the legal covenant, which was enacted partly by threats and partly by positive ceremonial decrees excluding the Gentiles from the Church, was, as it were, a handwriting, and was against us and contrary to us. But Christ blotted out this handwriting, took it away out of the way and nailed it to the cross. Therefore you must not look back to the legal covenant or the ceremonial decrees in order to seek anything in them, nor must you withdraw so much as a hair's breadth from Christ's death, through which you have been freed from that handwriting. This covenant of works with its appendages is compared to a handwriting, by which a man binds himself to pay a debt. For by the light of nature all who are convicted are held guilty of sin; by the force of the covenant of works they are also liable to wrath, and as often as we are charged with sin, so often also, through the nature of death, that is the condition of the legal covenant, we confirm against ourselves the sentence of our conscience, as it were by our own reckoning or handwriting. Much more does the conscience of everyone who has received the written law and hears daily the penalty of the violated law bear witness to this. Above all, all the justiciaries are compelled to subscribe to this handwriting, who acknowledge no righteousness except inherent righteousness, or that which is from works. Among these were the Judaizers and the observers of ceremonies, who clung to this covenant, seeking righteousness from works and from the decrees of ceremonies. For the more clearly they tried in this way to establish their own righteousness, the more openly they drew upon themselves death, the penalty of the violated law, by force of the compact. For no one enters a covenant without also accepting all its conditions.

units.la: Dicitur Chirographum in decretis positum, vel potius decretis subscriptum, quatenus qui mandata seu decreta illa legalia recipiebant in se, perficienda, obligabant etiam se, ad poenam mandatorum violatorum sustinendam. Vocat Chirographum adversus nos seu contrarium nobis, partim quia Judaeos a Gentibus, & Gentes a Judaeis separabat, partim quia erat jugum, quod nec ipsi, nec patres eorum poterant ferre: partim denique, quia quotiescunque opus aliquod legis sive moralis, sive ceremonialis justificandi sui causa exercebant, toties per imperfectionem operis, & imperfectionis professionem in exercitio Levitica Ceremoniae, se reos peragebant, seu potius se reos agnoscebant mortis. Exempli causa cum sacrificia offerebant, eaque repetebant, non tantum agnoscebant se peccatores adversus Legem Moralem, sed etiam reipsa confitebantur repetita sacrificia non potuisse conscientiam suam a peccato mundare, atque ita Chirographum Foederis Operum semper erat illis contrarium: Sed Christus hoc Chirographum delevit, & cruci affixum e medio sustulit, quatenus in gratiam suorum, per mortem crucis multam ex Chirographo debitam pro Redemptis persolvit; & decreta positiva de Ceremoniis umbratilibus reali Corporis sui sacrificio semel oblato, complevit & abolevit.
units.tr: It is called "a handwriting set down in decrees," or rather "subscribed to decrees," inasmuch as those who took upon themselves those legal commands or decrees to be performed also bound themselves to bear the penalty of the commands violated. He calls it a handwriting "against us," or contrary to us, partly because it separated Jews from Gentiles and Gentiles from Jews, partly because it was a yoke which neither they nor their fathers could bear, and finally, because as often as they performed any work of the law, whether moral or ceremonial, for the sake of justifying themselves, so often by the imperfection of the work, and by the confession of imperfection in the exercise of the Levitical ceremonies, they made themselves guilty, or rather acknowledged themselves guilty of death. For example, when they offered sacrifices and repeated them, they not only acknowledged themselves to be sinners against the moral law, but in fact confessed that the repeated sacrifices could not cleanse their conscience from sin; and thus the handwriting of the covenant of works was always against them. But Christ blotted out this handwriting and took it away out of the way, nailed to the cross, in that for the sake of his own, by the death of the cross, he paid for the redeemed the great debt owed by the handwriting; and he fulfilled and abolished the positive decrees about shadowy ceremonies by the real sacrifice of his body once offered.

units.la: Vers. 15. Et expoliata imperia ac potestates traduxit palam triumphatis illis per eam.
units.tr: Verse 15. "And having spoiled principalities and powers, he made a shew of them openly, triumphing over them in it."

units.la: Arg. 10. Christus omnes diabolos, potestatem & tyrranidem in Electos exercentes, per pretium Redemptionis in cruce persolutum re ipsa prostratos, palam etiam in conspectu Dei, Angelorum, & Hominum quorum oculi aperti sunt, gloriose triumphatos, traduxit in ipsorum ignominiam, & nostram liberationem. Nihil ergo restat extra Christum quaerendum.
units.tr: Argument 10. Christ, by the price of redemption paid on the cross, has in fact laid low all the devils who exercise power and tyranny over the elect, and openly, in the sight of God, the angels and men whose eyes are opened, has gloriously triumphed over them and led them forth to their shame and our deliverance. Nothing therefore remains to be sought outside Christ.

units.la: Dicuntur Cacodaemones Principatus & Potestates: 1. Quia in mundo potenter imperium exercent in omnes reprobos filios inobedientiae, & in omnes irregenitos, qui nihil aliud agunt, quam ut voluntatem Diaboli exequantur: 2. Quia sunt lictores exequentes Dei judicium, captivos detinentes eos qui Deo non reconciliantur in Christo: 3. Quia pugnant contra Christum Redemptorem, nec dimittunt Redemptos, & Reconciliatos ex carcere tenebrarum, nisi a Christi fortiori potestate coacti.
units.tr: The evil spirits are called "principalities and powers" for three reasons: (1) because in the world they exercise dominion powerfully over all the reprobate sons of disobedience and over all the unregenerate, who do nothing else than carry out the will of the Devil; (2) because they are the officers who execute God's judgment, holding captive those who are not reconciled to God in Christ; (3) because they fight against Christ the Redeemer and do not release the redeemed and reconciled from the prison of darkness unless they are compelled by Christ's stronger power.

units.la: Dicuntur spoliati a Christo in Cruce, 1. Quatenus Christus persoluto pretio redemptionis, ex pacto a Patre obtinuit, ut omnes Redempti ex carcere tenebrarum, ignorantiae, peccati & mortis liberarentur: 2. Quatenus Christus potentia infinitus, ubi semel justitiae satisfecerat in cruce, claustra & retinacula peccati, judicii & legis, quibus Diaboli constrictos tenebant redemptos, effregit ut amplius nullam vim possint habere. 3. Quatenus redemptos suos fecit possessionem & peculium suum, ne amplius essent Satanæ pecus.
units.tr: They are said to be "spoiled by Christ" on the cross for three reasons: (1) inasmuch as Christ, having paid the price of redemption, obtained from the Father by covenant that all the redeemed should be freed from the prison of darkness, ignorance, sin and death; (2) inasmuch as Christ, infinite in power, once he had satisfied justice on the cross, broke the bars and fetters of sin, judgment and law, by which the devils held the redeemed bound, so that they could no longer have any power; (3) inasmuch as he made his redeemed his possession and his own property, so that they should no longer be Satan's flock.

units.la: Dicitur Christus Diabolos traduxisse, & de iis palam triumphasse in cruce: 1. Quatenus omnes ipsorum tentationes & venenata tela, sive immediatè ab iis projecta, adversus se in cruce pendentem, sive per venenatas linguas furentium adversariorum contorta, sive per suorum discipulorum fugientium ab ipso ingratitudinis provocationem vibrata, fortiter excepit, superavit & extinxit: 2. Quatenus malitiam Diabolorum, artes & machinationes omnes ipsorum (quibus illi ipsius vitam petebant, indesinenter insligantes mancipia sua ad ipsum crucifigendum, donec in crucem egerunt) convertit Christus in Diabolorum perniciem, & apertissimam dominii ipsorum ruinam: 3. Quatenus se Cœli terræque Dominum, signis & prodigiis demonstravit, ipso tempore crucifixionis: 4. Quatenus palam exeruit potestatem suam per conversionem furis illius ad dextram pendentis; & centurionis ad pedes stantis; 5. Quatenus pretio redemptionis jam persoluto, victor non in conspectu Dei tantum, & Angelorum, sed etiam in conspectu ipsorum Diabolorum, & auditu insuper omnium inspectantium, clamavit opus suum consummatum esse, idque in gloriam suam æternam, & hostium perpetuam ignominiam: Ex quibus sequitur à Christo non esse recedendum, vel ut quicquam boni adipiscamur, vel ut ab ullo malo liberemur.
units.tr: Christ is said to have led the devils captive and openly triumphed over them on the cross: (1) inasmuch as he bravely received, overcame and extinguished all their temptations and poisoned darts, whether hurled at him directly while he hung on the cross, or launched through the venomous tongues of raging adversaries, or aimed through the provocation of ingratitude from his disciples who fled from him; (2) inasmuch as Christ turned the malice of the devils, all their arts and schemes (by which they sought his life, constantly urging their henchmen to crucify him until they brought him to the cross), to the ruin of the devils and the most manifest overthrow of their dominion; (3) inasmuch as he showed himself to be Lord of heaven and earth by signs and wonders at the very time of the crucifixion; (4) inasmuch as he openly displayed his power through the conversion of the thief hanging at his right hand and of the centurion standing at his feet; (5) inasmuch as, the price of redemption now paid, he, victorious not only in the sight of God and the angels but also in the sight of the devils themselves and in the hearing of all who looked on, cried out that his work was finished, to his own eternal glory and the perpetual shame of his enemies. From these things it follows that we must not withdraw from Christ, either to obtain any good or to be delivered from any evil.

units.la: Tertia Pars Capitis.
units.tr: The Third Part of the Chapter.

units.la: Vers. 16. Nequis igitur vos damnet ob cibum, vel potum, aut respectu diei festi, aut novilunii, aut sabbathorum:
units.tr: Verse 16. Let no one therefore judge you in food or drink, or with regard to a festival day, a new moon, or the sabbaths:

units.la: Tertia pars Capitis, In qua per consectarium infert admonitionem specialem de cavendis Pseudapostolorum specialibus quibusdam corruptelis.
units.tr: The third part of the chapter, in which, as a corollary, he gives a special warning to beware of certain particular corruptions of the false apostles.

units.la: Admonitiones sunt tres: Admonitio 1. Ne curent sententiam seu censuram ullius qui audebit eos condemnare, propter non observatas ceremonias Mosaicas, exempli causa, propter cibum aut potum assumptum, vel propter ullum diem festum, vel aliquam diei festi partem neglectam, vel propter non observatum Sabbatum Judæorum.
units.tr: There are three admonitions. Admonition 1: they should not care about the opinion or censure of anyone who dares to condemn them for not observing the Mosaic ceremonies, for example, for the food or drink they have taken, or for any festival day, or some part of a festival day that they have neglected, or for not observing the Jewish Sabbath.

units.la: Vers. 17 Quæ sunt umbra rerum futurarum, at corpus, est CHRISTI. Ratio admonitionis est, quia Ceremoniæ illæ legales erant umbræ rerum futurarum, duraturæ tantùm usque dum corpus, seu veritas & substantia illarum Christus, veniret; quæ idcirco post ejus adventum cessare debent.
units.tr: Verse 17. Which are a shadow of things to come, but the body is Christ's. The reason for the admonition is that those legal ceremonies were shadows of things to come, to last only until the body, that is, the truth and substance of them, Christ, should come. Therefore they ought to cease after his coming.

units.la: Vers. 18. Nullus voluntarius moderator de vobis statuat in submissione & cultu angelorum, sese ingerens in ea quæ non vidit, & temerè turgens carnis suæ sensu:
units.tr: Verse 18. Let no one who takes pleasure in humility and the worship of angels rob you of your prize, intruding into things he has not seen, and vainly puffed up by his fleshly mind:

units.la: Admonitio 2. est, Ut caveant sibi à cultu & invocatione Angelorum: Argumenta in hunc finem affert septem. Arg. 1. Quia quicunque hunc cultum vos docet, reipsa dat operam, ut vos præmio religionis, seu vita æterna defraudet. Arg. 2. Quia non ex Dei autoritate, sed ex sua voluntate & libidine hanc doctrinam tradit. Arg. 3. Quia qui cultum Angelorum docet, abutitur hypocriticè prætextu humilitatis. Arg. 4. Quia qui Angelorum cultum docet, audacter incedit sine luce verbi Dei, imò sine lumine rationis rectæ: nam nec in sacris literis, nec oculis corporeis, nec sanæ rationis lumine quicquam de hac doctrina unquam vidit. Arg. 5. Quia quicunque cultum Angelorum docet, non est humilis, sicut præ se fert, sed carnali suo judicio turgens vanissimè inflatur.
units.tr: Admonition 2 is that they should beware of the worship and invocation of angels. He brings seven arguments to this end. Argument 1: whoever teaches this worship in fact works to defraud you of the reward of religion, that is, of eternal life. Argument 2: he hands down this doctrine not by God's authority but by his own will and lust. Argument 3: whoever teaches the worship of angels hypocritically abuses the pretext of humility. Argument 4: whoever teaches the worship of angels walks boldly without the light of God's Word, indeed without the light of right reason; for he has never seen anything about this doctrine either in the sacred writings, or with his bodily eyes, or by the light of sound reason. Argument 5: whoever teaches the worship of angels is not humble, as he pretends, but, puffed up by his carnal judgment, is inflated to the greatest vanity.

units.la: Vers. 19. Neque obtinens caput, ex quo totum corpus per commissuras & compages suppeditatum & compactum, augescit Dei augmento.
units.tr: Verse 19. And not holding the Head, from whom the whole body, supplied and knit together through its joints and bands, increases with the increase of God.

units.la: Arg. 6. Quia quicunque angelorum cultum docet, expers est veræ fidei, non conjungitur, non adhæret Christo: licet sciat alia omnia, ignarus tamen est virtutis Christi, & gratiæ quæ est in ipso, imo à Christo capite nostro divellitur, eique renunciat.
units.tr: Argument 6: whoever teaches the worship of angels lacks true faith; he is not joined to Christ and does not cling to him. Although he may know everything else, he is ignorant of the power of Christ and of the grace that is in him. Indeed, he is torn away from Christ our Head and renounces him.

units.la: Arg. 7. Quia in Christo solo est promptuarium ex quo omnis gratia, & quicquid ad vitam & vegetationem spiritualem requiritur, abundè in omnia ejus membra derivatur, adeò ut nec sit opus ab Angelis quicquam petere, nec sine Christi opprobrio quicquam petiposit, Angelos invocando, vel quovis modo eos colendo. Idcirco Cavenda Angelorum invocatio.
units.tr: Argument 7: in Christ alone is the storehouse from which all grace, and whatever is required for spiritual life and growth, flows abundantly into all his members. So there is no need to seek anything from the angels, and nothing is to be sought from them without dishonour to Christ, whether by invoking angels or by worshipping them in any other way. Therefore the invocation of angels is to be avoided.

units.la: In hoc argumento comparatione capitis humani naturalis describitur Christus, sextuplici similitudine: 1. Ut caput humanum naturale habet corpus sibi subjectum, sic Christus habet Ecclesiam sibi subjectam, ut corpus suum mysticum: 2. Ut ex capite humano derivatur sensus motusque in corpus totum, & omnia ejus membra, sic ex Christo sensus motusque spirituales derivantur in omnia membra Ecclesiae: 3. Ut ex capite humano protenduntur commissurae nervorum & vinculorum, quae totum corpus pervadunt, sic a capite Christo profluit Spiritus Sanctus, & fides in Christum, & charitas in proximum, quae per totum corpus mysticum diffunduntur: 4 Ut per illas commissuras suppeditatur corpori toti vita, motus & sensus, sic per has commissuras, omnis gratia spiritualis suppeditatur fidelibus: 5. Ut per illas compinguntur membra cum capite & inter se, sic per has, Christus & membra ipsius uniuntur: 6. Ut per illas in corpore naturali; sic per has, in corpore Christi mystico incrementum fit primum singulorum membrorum, deinde totius corporis mystici: 7. Sicut illic incrementum est naturae, sic hic est gratiae, Dei incrementum, id est, magnum & solidum, pro mensura doni uniuscujusque.
units.tr: In this argument, Christ is described by comparison with the natural human head, in a sixfold likeness. (1) As the natural human head has the body subject to it, so Christ has the Church subject to him as his mystical body. (2) As sense and motion flow from the human head into the whole body and all its members, so spiritual sense and motion flow from Christ into all the members of the Church. (3) As the joints of nerves and ligaments stretch out from the human head and pervade the whole body, so the Holy Spirit, faith in Christ, and love for neighbour flow from Christ the head and are spread through the whole mystical body. (4) As life, motion and sense are supplied to the whole body through those joints, so all spiritual grace is supplied to the faithful through these joints. (5) As the members are fastened to the head and to one another through those joints, so Christ and his members are united through these. (6) As growth takes place first in the individual members and then in the whole body in the natural body, so growth takes place first in the individual members and then in the whole mystical body of Christ. (7) As there the growth is of nature, so here it is of God's grace, that is, great and solid, according to the measure of each one's gift.

units.la: Vers. 20. Itaque si mortui cum Christo, liberi estis ab elementis mundi; quid ut viventes in mundo, ritibus oneramini?
units.tr: Verse 20. Wherefore if you are dead with Christ to the elements of the world, why, as though living in the world, are you burdened with ordinances?

units.la: Tertia admonitio cum reprehensione, quod se subjecerint decretis seu traditionibus humanis, & doctrinis hominum religionem statuentium in iis, in quibus Deus religionem non statuit; Admonitionis seu reprehensionis argumenta sunt quinque: 1. Quia liberati estis per mortem Christi a quibuscunque carnalibus initiamentis religionis, quales sunt Ceremoniae Judaicae, ita ut cum illis nihil amplius habeatis negotii, Non debetis decreta & praecepta hominum admittere, quasi adhuc more puerorum rudimentariorum, istiusmodi elementis obnoxii estis.
units.tr: Admonition 3, with a rebuke: they had submitted themselves to human decrees or traditions, and to the doctrines of men who establish religion in matters where God has not established it. The arguments of this admonition or rebuke are five. Argument 1: because you have been freed through the death of Christ from every carnal beginning of religion, such as the Jewish ceremonies, so that you have no further business with them, you ought not to admit human decrees and precepts, as if you were still like children in the rudiments, subject to such elements.

units.la: Primi hujus argumenti vis consistit in his quinque: 1. Christus implevit quod praefiguratum fuit per Ceremonias Mosis, & morte sua abrogavit Ceremonias illas typicas, & umbratilem illum modum docendi Ecclesiam, & colendi Deum, ita ut nihil ab ipso exigere posset foederis legalis forma, plus quam in ejus morte persolutum est & persectum: 2 Moriente Christo, judicialiter commortui sunt omnes foederati, quorum personam sustinuit Christus, Nihil igitur amplius potuit fœdus legale exigere ab illis, quorum nomine CHRISTUS mortuus est, quam leges hominum exigunt à mortuis: censentur enim omnes in illo ut mortui: 3. Ceremonialia omnia præcepta respectu authoritatis præcipientis divina, & Cœlestia erant usque ad CHRISTUM: sed jam abolita per CHRISTUM, cessarunt esse divina, & cæperunt esse elementa seu rudimenta humana, mundana & carnalia, non tam quoad res imperatas, quam quoad imperandi autoritatem mundanam: 4. Quandiu Colossenses non erant conversi ad CHRISTUM, sed in mundo vivebant mundani, ut liberi à justitia, sic mancipia erant diabolorum & hominum, obnoxii omnigenæ servituti, & omnis generis malo: 5. Nunc vero postquam CHRISTO concorpores, erant per fidem facti liberi, etiam erant ab omni malo liberati, nec se ulli jugo submittere debebant, nisi cui CHRISTUS eos subjugari voluit, & per consequens non debebant hominum dogmatibus & traditionibus in religionis negotio subjici.
units.tr: The force of the first argument rests on these five points. (1) Christ fulfilled what was prefigured by the ceremonies of Moses, and by his death abrogated those typical ceremonies and that shadowy manner of teaching the Church and worshipping God. So the form of the legal covenant could demand nothing from him beyond what was paid and perfected in his death. (2) When Christ died, all the covenanted died judicially with him, since he bore their person. Therefore the legal covenant could demand nothing further from those in whose name Christ died than human laws demand from the dead, for all are reckoned dead in him. (3) All ceremonial precepts were divine and heavenly, with respect to the authority commanding them, until Christ. But now, abolished through Christ, they have ceased to be divine and have begun to be human, worldly and carnal elements or rudiments, not so much as to the things commanded as to the worldly authority of commanding. (4) As long as the Colossians were not converted to Christ, but lived in the world as worldly people, free from righteousness, they were slaves of devils and of men, subject to every kind of servitude and every kind of evil. (5) But now, since they have been made one body with Christ, they have been made free through faith, and freed from every evil. Nor ought they to submit to any yoke except that to which Christ wished them to be subjected. Consequently they ought not to be subjected to human dogmas and traditions in matters of religion.

units.la: Vers. 21. Ne attigeris, neque gustaris, neque contrectaris.
units.tr: Verse 21. Do not touch, nor taste, nor handle.

units.la: Arg. 2. Quia superstitiosi illi dictatores vestri, & decretorum humanorum autores, præcisa suâ prohibitione rerum liberarum, tyrannidem simul & hypocrisin suam intolerabilem produnt in rigida exactione mandatorum suorum, qualia μηδὲ ἅψῃ & cum indignatione recitat aliqua, ne gustate, ne attingite, & similibus, in quibus non solum legem Leviticam Deo invito continuare volebant, sed etiam superaddere legi abolitæ rigidas exactiones suas: Ne ergo illis vos subjiciatis.
units.tr: Argument 2. Because those superstitious dictators of yours, and the authors of human decrees, by their bare prohibition of things that are lawful, reveal at the same time their tyranny and their intolerable hypocrisy in the rigid enforcement of their commands. Such are the words they recite, with indignation, "Μηδὲ ἅψῃ" [do not touch], "do not taste, do not touch," and similar phrases, in which they wanted not only to keep the Levitical law against God's will, but also to add to the abolished law their own rigid exactions. Therefore do not submit yourselves to them.

units.la: Vers. 22. Quæ omnia ipso usu pereunt, præscripta ex mandatis & doctrinis hominum:
units.tr: Verse 22. All of which perish by the very using: prescribed by the commandments and doctrines of men.

units.la: Arg. 3. Quia res illæ corporeæ à Deo institutæ sunt ad usum, ut in usu tandem absumantur & pereant, &c. Iniquum ergo est sub specie religionis prohibere illarum usum, Ne ergo his institutis vos subjiciatis.
units.tr: Argument 3. Because those bodily things were instituted by God for use, so that in use they might at last be consumed and perish, etc. It is therefore unjust to forbid their use under the appearance of religion. Therefore do not submit yourselves to these ordinances.

units.la: Hominum Arg. 4. Quia decreta istiusmodi non sunt mandata Dei, sed mandata hominum, secundum quæ Deus declaravit se nolle colli: Ne ergo admittite ea.
units.tr: Of men Argument 4. Because decrees of this kind are not commandments of God but commandments of men, by which God has declared that he does not wish to be worshipped. Therefore do not admit them.

units.la: Vers. 23. Quæ rationem quidem habent sapientiæ in cultu voluntario, & submissione animi, & in eo quod corpori non parcant, non tamen ullius sunt pretii, quum ad ea spectent, quibus satiatur caro. Arg. 5. Cum refutatione objectionis, quia etiamsi hæ observationes speciem habeant sapientiæ, tanquam partes voluntarii & non coacti cultus, tanquam humilitatis erga Angelos, & obedientiæ erga Ecclesiæ gubernatores, exercitia, tanquam ad carnis mortificationem non nihil facientia; reipsa tamen meram speciem tantùm sapientiæ habent, & nullius sunt pretii vel æstimationis coram Deo: Denique quantum corpori detrahere videntur, tantùm adjiciunt ad satisfactionem carnis, seu corruptæ naturæ, quæ in suis figmentis circa religionem sibi satisfacere semper avidissimè cupit.
units.tr: Verse 23. Which indeed have a show of wisdom in voluntary worship, and humility of mind, and in not sparing the body, but are of no value whatever, since they serve only the satisfying of the flesh. Argument 5.
