With a refutation of an objection: for even if these observances have the appearance of wisdom, as parts of a voluntary and not a compelled worship, as exercises of humility towards the angels and of obedience towards the governors of the Church, and as contributing somewhat to the mortification of the flesh; yet in reality they have only the mere appearance of wisdom, and are of no worth or esteem before God. Finally, however much they seem to take away from the body, they add only to the satisfaction of the flesh, that is, of corrupt nature, which in its own inventions about religion always most eagerly desires to satisfy itself.

units.la: Caput Tertium.
units.tr: Chapter 3.

units.la: Ecunda pars Epistolæ de studiis Christianæ vitæ. Capitis duæ sunt partes, in prima continentur hortationes generales, pertinentes ad veram pietatem & vitæ sanctimoniam, ad vers. 18. In altera sunt speciales hortationes, quæ spectant ad certas & particulares hominum conditiones, ad finem.
units.tr: The second part of the Epistle, on the pursuits of the Christian life. The chapter has two parts. The first contains general exhortations, pertaining to true piety and holiness of life, up to verse 18. The second contains special exhortations, which concern certain particular conditions of men, to the end.

units.la: Itaque si resurrexistis cum Christo, superna quærite, ubi Christus est ad dextram Dei sedens:
units.tr: If then you have been raised with Christ, seek the things that are above, where Christ sits at the right hand of God:

units.la: Hortationes generales sunt novem: 1. Est ad studium rerum Cœlestium, ne amplius terrenis voluptatibus, honoribus, & divitiis acquirendis operam & laborem impendant, sed ut quærant Christianas virtutes, & quæ ad vitam æternam pertinent.
units.tr: There are nine general exhortations: (1) the first is to the pursuit of heavenly things, so that they no longer spend effort and labour on acquiring earthly pleasures, honours and riches, but seek Christian virtues and those things which pertain to eternal life.

units.la: Si resurrexistis] Argumenta hortationis sunt sex. Quæ omnia studendum esse rebus Cœlestibus probant: 1. In Baptismo recepistis in vos studium resurrectionis, seu novæ & spiritualis vitæ prosequendæ, & insiti per fidem in Christum communionem habetis cum Christo resurgente; qui nomine suorum ad spiritualem vitam, ut sponsor resurrexit, recepitque in se fore, ut fideles resurgerent, virtute resurrectionis suæ ipsis communicatâ: Ergo studendum rebus Cœlestibus.
units.tr: If you have been raised] There are six arguments for the exhortation. All of them prove that heavenly things must be pursued: (1) In baptism you received in yourselves the pursuit of resurrection, that is, of a new and spiritual life, and, implanted through faith in Christ, you have communion with the risen Christ. He rose as surety for his people to spiritual life, and received into himself that the faithful would rise, by the power of his resurrection communicated to them. Therefore heavenly things must be pursued.

units.la: Ubi Christus] Arg. 2: In sublimi, id est, in Coelo quoad localem praesentiam corporis, est Christus caput nostrum, & fons omnis felicitatis nostrae: Ergo ut eo potiamini superna quaerenda sunt.
units.tr: Where Christ] Argument 2: On high, that is, in heaven as regards the local presence of his body, Christ is our head and the fount of all our happiness. Therefore, that you may attain him, the things above are to be sought.

units.la: Dextrum] Arg. 3. Christus ad dextram Dei sedet, etiam qua homo, summam sublimitatem nactus, & nomen super omne nomen, ut possit nobis omnia superna concedere: Ergo superna quaerenda sunt vobis.
units.tr: At the right hand] Argument 3: Christ sits at the right hand of God, even as man, having obtained the highest exaltation and the name above every name, so that he can grant us all heavenly things. Therefore the things above are to be sought by you.

units.la: Vers. 2. Superna curate, non terrestria:
units.tr: Verse 2. Set your minds on things above, not on things on the earth:

units.la: Amplificat hanc hortationem, jubens ut sapiant res coelestes, id est, ut cognoscere studeant, in aestimatione habeant, curent, affectent, cum desiderio prosequantur quae ad vitam coelestem pertinent, & non quae ad vitam hanc terrestrem: quae licet licita & necessaria sint, obiter tamen curanda sunt.
units.tr: He amplifies this exhortation by bidding that heavenly things be savoured, that is, that they study to know them, esteem them, care for them, desire them, and pursue with longing those things which pertain to the heavenly life, and not those which pertain to this earthly life. Although these are lawful and necessary, they are to be attended to only in passing.

units.la: Vers. 3. Nam mortui estis, & vita vestra abscondita est cum Christo in Deo.
units.tr: Verse 3. For you are dead, and your life is hidden with Christ in God.

units.la: Arg. 4. Per fidem in baptismo participes estis mortis Christi, & obligati ad commoriendum mundo & peccato, per virtutem mortis ipsius; imo mortui estis illis, seu illorum respectu, nempe judiciali & spirituali modo, ne illa terrena amplius sapiatis, vel iis serviatis: Ergo superna & coelestia, non terrestria sapere & sectari debetis.
units.tr: Argument 4: Through faith in baptism you are partakers of the death of Christ, and bound to die together with the world and sin, through the power of his death. Indeed you are dead to them, or with respect to them, namely in a judicial and spiritual manner, so that you no longer savour those earthly things or serve them. Therefore you ought to savour and pursue the things above and heavenly, not the earthly.

units.la: Et vita] Arg. 5. Licet vita illa vestra, id est, adoptio vestra, justitia vestra, haereditas vestra, plena sanctificatio, & glorificatio vestra, mundo, imo vobis ipsis magna ex parte abscondita sit (jam enim eam tantum per fidem & primitiarum exiguam possessionem percipitis) conservatur tamen in coelo in suis causis, cum Christo, in Deo abscondita: Ergo sapere & quaerere debetis ea quae ad hanc vitam spectant.
units.tr: And your life] Argument 5: Although that life of yours, that is, your adoption, your righteousness, your inheritance, your full sanctification and your glorification, is for the most part hidden from the world and even from yourselves (for now you receive it only through faith and a small first-fruits possession), it is nonetheless preserved in heaven in its causes, hidden with Christ in God. Therefore you ought to savour and seek those things which pertain to this life.

units.la: Vers. 4. Quando Christus vita illa nostra, patefactum fuerit, tum & vos cum eo patefietis gloriosi.
units.tr: Verse 4. When Christ, who is our life, shall be made manifest, then you also shall be manifested with him in glory.

units.la: Arg. 6. Per solutionem objectionis, ex superiori argumento oriundae. Quamvis vita vestra abscondita jam sit, plenè & aperte tamen aliquando communicabitur vobis, & nos gloriose producemur in conspectu omnium Angelorum & hominum, cum Christus manifestabitur in secundo suo adventu; cujus ratio redditur, quia Christus est vita nostra; Sic dictus: 1. Quia vitam aeternam nobis acquisivit: 2. Quia vitam illam habet in se nobis communicandam: 3. Quia actu cepit nobis vitam illam, per Spiritum suum communicare, quam tandem plenè consummabit; 4. Quia est objectum vitæ illius nostræ: nam nostra felicitas consistit in communione cum Illo, ut Eum cognoscamus, cum Eo simus & conversemur, & Eo plenè tandem fruamur: Ergo sub spe vitæ nobis revelandæ superna quærite.
units.tr: Argument 6: By the answer to an objection arising from the previous argument. Although your life is now hidden, it will at some time be communicated to you fully and openly, and we shall be gloriously displayed in the sight of all angels and men, when Christ is revealed at his second coming. The reason is given: Christ is our life, thus called: (1) because he has acquired eternal life for us; (2) because he has that life in himself to be communicated to us; (3) because he has already begun to communicate that life to us through his Spirit, which he will at last fully complete; (4) because he is the object of that life of ours, for our happiness consists in communion with him, that we may know him, be with him and converse with him, and at last fully enjoy him. Therefore, under the hope of the life to be revealed to us, seek the things above.

units.la: Verf. 5. Mortificate igitur membra vestra terrestria, scortationem, impuritatem, mollitiem, cupiditatem malam, & avaritiam, quæ est idololatria.
units.tr: Verse 5. Mortify therefore your earthly members: fornication, uncleanness, inordinate affection, evil concupiscence, and covetousness, which is idolatry.

units.la: Hortatio 2. Tanquam corrolarium, ex superioribus illata, qua jubet mortificare vitiosos motus, affectusque corruptæ naturæ, per quos deforme corpus peccati inhabitantis, tanquam per membra, operatur omnia actualia peccata, inque membris corporis ita se exerit, ut illa reddat quasi sui ipsius membra, & vitiorum instrumenta: Hæc mortificatio fit non solùm externos actus peccati non perpetrando, verùm etiam pravos motus internos ad illa peccata incitantes in ipso limine necando.
units.tr: Exhortation 2: As a corollary drawn from what precedes, it bids us mortify the sinful motions and affections of corrupt nature, through which the deformed body of sin dwelling within works all actual sins as through members, and so exerts itself in our members that it makes them, as it were, its own members and instruments of vice. This mortification is effected not only by not committing the external acts of sin, but also by killing at the very threshold the wicked inward motions that incite to those sins.

units.la: Vers. 6. Ob quæ venit ira Dei in filios contumaces.
units.tr: Verse 6. On account of these things the wrath of God comes upon the sons of disobedience.

units.la: Arg. 2. Quia etiamsi levia videantur hæc peccata, iram Dei tamen acceisunt, adversus eos qui contumaces sunt, nec resipiscunt.
units.tr: Argument 2: Because, even if these sins seem slight, they nonetheless provoke the wrath of God against those who are disobedient and do not repent.

units.la: Vers. 7. Quibus in vitiis & vos versabamini quondam, quum in iis viveretis.
units.tr: Verse 7. In these things you also once walked, when you lived in them.

units.la: Vers. 8. At nunc deponite etiam vos hæc omnia, iram, excandescentiam, malitiam, maledicentiam, verborum turpitudinem ab ore vestro.
units.tr: Verse 8. But now put away also all these things: anger, wrath, malice, slander, filthy speech out of your mouth.

units.la: Vers. 9. Ne mentimini alius adversus alium, quum exveritis veterem illum hominem cum factis ipsius:
units.tr: Verse 9. Do not lie to one another, seeing that you have put off the old man with his deeds:

units.la: Hortatio 3. Ex proximo argumento ducta, in qua jubet exuere, deponere, & non resumenda rejicere sex vitia, quae sunt: 1. Ira injusta:
units.tr: Exhortation 3: Drawn from the nearest argument, in which it bids us strip off, put away, and cast off, not to be taken up again, six vices, which are: (1) unjust anger;

units.la: 2. Indignatio seu excandescentia, quae superior gradus est irae: 3. Malitia seu maligna invidia, & odium in quod convertitur ira permanens, seu pernoctans: 4. Convicium seu blasphemia contra alicujus famam: 5. Turpiloquium seu scurrilitas, & 6. denique mendacium.
units.tr: (2) indignation, or wrath, which is a higher degree of anger; (3) malice, or malignant envy, and hatred, into which lasting or overnight anger turns; (4) reproach, or blasphemy, against another's reputation; (5) filthy talk, or buffoonery; and (6) finally, lying.

units.la: Exuti ] Rationes hortationis sunt duae: 1. Quia in baptismo sacramentali voto, obligatione & inchoatione exuistis veterem hominem cum actionibus suis, id est, renunciastis veteri vestrae corruptae naturae, ejusque servitio: Idcirco his vitiis renunciandum est.
units.tr: Having put off] There are two reasons for the exhortation: (1) because in the sacramental vow of baptism, by obligation and inception, you have put off the old man with his deeds, that is, you have renounced your old corrupt nature and its service. Therefore these vices are to be renounced.

units.la: Vers. 10. Et indueritis novum illum, qui renovatur in agnitionem congruentem imagini ejus qui ipsum condidit.
units.tr: Verse 10. And have put on the new man, who is renewed in knowledge after the image of him who created him.

units.la: Ratio 2. Quia ex dono Dei, fide, voto, & inchoata vitae novitate in regeneratione induistis novum hominem, id est, novas spirituales qualitates, quasi novam naturam: Idcirco his vitiis renunciandum est.
units.tr: Reason 2: Because by the gift of God, through faith, vow and the inchoate newness of life in regeneration, you have put on the new man, that is, new spiritual qualities, as it were a new nature. Therefore these vices are to be renounced.

units.la: Novum autem hominem describit in quatuor: 1. Quod sit sanctitatis naturae nostrae in Adamo amissae renovatio in Christo: 2. Quod consistat in agnitione mysterii Euangelii, id est, in istiusmodi illuminatione, quae cor ita mutet, & vitam simul externam, ut a nobis, mente, affectu, & opere, gratia Dei in Christo re ipsa agnoscatur: 3. Quod archetypus seu exemplar secundum quod conditur & renovatur iste novus homo sit imago Dei Creatoris, qui solus condidit hominem ut esset, & solus etiam refingit hominem ut sit novus.
units.tr: The new man is described in four respects: (1) that he is the renewal in Christ of the holiness of our nature lost in Adam; (2) that it consists in the knowledge of the mystery of the gospel, that is, in such an illumination as changes the heart and at the same time the outward life, so that by us, in mind, affection and deed, the grace of God in Christ is really acknowledged; (3) that the archetype or pattern according to which this new man is formed and renewed is the image of God the Creator, who alone made man so that he might exist, and who alone also re-forms man so that he may be new; (4) that it is enough for the new man to have Christ (which one thing suffices for all things required for salvation), or that in this work of renewal through Christ, outward condition neither hinders nor helps, and no account is taken before God of outward condition. (It makes no difference whether someone is of the Gentiles or of the Jews, circumcised or uncircumcised, born of this or that nation, learned or ignorant of letters, slave or free.) This was said aptly on account of the false apostles, who urged legal ceremonies and human traditions, as if all other things were nothing unless one Judaized.

units.la: Vers. 11. Ubi non est Graecus & Judaeus, Circumcisio & Praeputium, Barbarus, Scytha, servus, liber: sed omnia & in omnibus CHRISTUS.
units.tr: Verse 11. Where there is neither Greek nor Jew, circumcision nor uncircumcision, barbarian, Scythian, slave, free; but Christ is all, and in all.

units.la: 4. Quod novo homini satis sit Christum habere, (quod unum pro omnibus ad salutem requisitis sufficit) seu quod in hoc negotio renovationis per Christum, externa conditio neque obsit, neque prosit, neque in hoc opere ratio ulla habeatur apud Deum externae conditionis. (Fit ne aliquis ex Gentibus, an Judaeis, circumcisus ne an incircumcisus, ex hac ne an illa Gente oriundus, literatus ne an rei literariae ignarus, servus ne an liber) quod appositè dictum est propter Pseudapostolos, qui ceremonias legales & hominum traditiones urgebant, quasi reliqua omnia nihil essent nisi quis judaizaret.
units.tr: (4) That it is enough for the new man to have Christ, (which one thing suffices for all things required for salvation), or that in this work of renewal through Christ, outward condition neither hinders nor helps, and no account is taken before God of outward condition. (It makes no difference whether someone is of the Gentiles or of the Jews, circumcised or uncircumcised, born of this or that nation, learned or ignorant of letters, slave or free.) This was said aptly on account of the false apostles, who urged legal ceremonies and human traditions, as if all other things were nothing unless one Judaized.

units.la: Vers. 12. Induimini igitur, ut electi Dei, sancti & dilecti, visceribus miserationum, benignitate, modestia, mansuetudine, lenitate:
units.tr: Verse 12. Put on therefore, as the elect of God, holy and beloved, bowels of mercies, kindness, humbleness of mind, meekness, longsuffering:

units.la: Hortatio 4. Ad quinque virtutes, nempe: 1. Ad teneram misericordiam erga afflictos: 2. Ad benignitatem erga egenos: 3. Ad humilitatem seu modestiam in omnibus: 4. Ad mansuetudinem seu comitatem in conversatione cum aliis: 5. Ad longanimitatem ubi injuriae inferuntur.
units.tr: Exhortation 4. To five virtues, namely: (1) to tender mercy towards the afflicted; (2) to kindness towards the needy; (3) to humility or modesty in all things; (4) to meekness or courtesy in dealing with others; (5) to long-suffering where injuries are inflicted.

units.la: Electi ] Argumenta hortationis sunt tria: 1. Quia estis electi DEI, non tantum speciali vocatione a mundo segregati, sed etiam aeterno decreto a reprobis separati.
units.tr: Elect] There are three arguments of the exhortation: (1) Because you are the elect of God, not only set apart from the world by a special calling, but also separated from the reprobate by an eternal decree.

units.la: Sancti ] Arg. 2. Quia sancti estis, & DEO consecrati.
units.tr: Holy] Argument 2. Because you are holy and consecrated to God.

units.la: Dilecti ] Arg. 3. Quia dilecti estis a DEO: Idcirco his virtutibus vos ornate, ut dignos tantis elogiis vos praestetis.
units.tr: Beloved] Argument 3. Because you are loved by God. Therefore adorn yourselves with these virtues, so that you show yourselves worthy of such titles of honour.

units.la: Verf. 13. Tolerantes alii alios, & condonantes vobis mutuo, si quis adversus aliquem habuerit querelam: sicut & Christus condonavit vobis, ita & vos.
units.tr: Verse 13. Bearing with one another, and forgiving one another, if any man have a quarrel against any: even as Christ forgave you, so also do ye.

units.la: Hortatio 5. Ut non tantum ex longanimitate mutuo tolerent alii aliorum infirmitates, & morum asperitatem, sed etiam mutuo condonent injurias.
units.tr: Exhortation 5. That believers should not only bear with one another's weaknesses and roughness of manners out of long-suffering, but also mutually forgive injuries.

units.la: Sicut Christus ] Ratio hortationis est, quia CHRISTUS condonavit vobis offensas vestras multo graviores: Idcirco vos alii aliis condonate injurias.
units.tr: Even as Christ] The reason for the exhortation is that Christ forgave you your offences, which were far greater; therefore forgive one another's injuries.

units.la: Verf. 14. Ad haec autem omnia induimini charitate, quae est vinculum perfectionis.
units.tr: Verse 14. And above all these things put on charity, which is the bond of perfectness.

units.la: Hortatio 6. Ut charitatem induant imprimis & ante omnes alias virtutes, quippe quae a radice fidei orta, ut truncus arboris, reliquas omnes virtutes tanquam ramos emittit; easque fovet & nutrit.
units.tr: Exhortation 6. That they should put on charity first and above all other virtues, since it springs from the root of faith like the trunk of a tree, sends forth all the other virtues as branches, and cherishes and nourishes them.

units.la: Quae est ] Ratio hortationis est, Quia charitas est mutuum vinculum perfectae colligationis, quo fideles omnes in unum corpus compinguntur, & quo omnes perficiuntur, hoc est, participes fiunt omnium donorum in Ecclesia vigentium, ita ut quaecunque sunt vel totius corporis privilegia, vel alicujus membri dona, evadant etiam singulorum membrorum bona, quoad usum seu utilitatem.
units.tr: Which is] The reason for the exhortation is that charity is the mutual bond of perfect union, by which all believers are knit together into one body, and by which all are made perfect, that is, become partakers of all the gifts flourishing in the Church, so that whatever are the privileges of the whole body or the gifts of any single member, they also become the goods of each individual member as to use and profit.

units.la: Verf. 15. Et pax Dei imperet in cordibus vestris, ad quam etiam vocati estis in unum corpus: & grati estote.
units.tr: Verse 15. And let the peace of God rule in your hearts, to the which also ye are called in one body; and be ye thankful.

units.la: Hortatio 7. Ut si contentio oriretur aliqua inter ipsos, pax Dei statueretur contentionis & omnium affectuum moderatrix, præmiumque quasi habens in manu sua, decerneret quid agendum.
units.tr: Exhortation 7. That if any strife should arise among them, the peace of God should be set up as the moderator of strife and of all the passions, holding as it were the prize in its hand, and should decide what is to be done.

units.la: Pacem Dei nominat, quæ a Deo est, quæ Deo placet, & quæ nec veritatis, nec virtutis ullius, sed affectuum nostrorum carnalium tantum jacturam imperat.
units.tr: He names the peace of God, which is from God, which pleases God, and which demands the loss not of any truth or virtue, but only of our carnal passions.

units.la: Ad quam ] Rationes hortationis sunt tres: 1. Quia Deus vocavit vos ad pacem cum seipso, & inter vos colendam: 2. Quia omnes estis membra unius corporis: 3. Quia gratitudinem hanc debetis Deo, qui pacem inivit vobiscum, cum potuisset tanquam inimicos vos tractare: Idcirco pacem inter vos colentes grati estote.
units.tr: To which] There are three reasons for the exhortation: (1) Because God has called you to peace with himself, and to be cultivated among you; (2) because you are all members of one body; (3) because you owe this thankfulness to God, who made peace with you when he could have treated you as enemies. Therefore, cultivating peace among yourselves, be thankful.

units.la: Vers. 16. Sermo Christi inhabitet in vobis copiosè, cum omni sapientia: docendo & commonefaciendo vos mutuo psalmis, hymnis, & cantionibus spiritualibus cum gratia, cantantes in corde vestro, DOMINO.
units.tr: Verse 16. Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly in all wisdom; teaching and admonishing one another in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing with grace in your hearts to the Lord.

units.la: Hortatio 8. Ad studium & exercitium verbi Dei, Hortationis membra sunt quinque: 1. Ut sermo Christi, seu doctrina christiana in Scriptura propositá accersatur ex fontibus, & tanquam hospes gratissimus animis & cordibus excipiatur: non ut inde recedat postmodum, sed ut ibi constanter commoretur: 2. Ne contenti sint sermonem Christi degustasse, aut aliquatenus cognovisse, sed ut operam dent ad mensuram locupletem & copiosam sibi comparandam: 3. Ut inde sapere discant, ad salutem suam & utilitatem aliorum: 4. Ne sermonem Christi sinant in se otiosum esse, sed in usum proximorum prudenter proferant: ut mutuis instructionibus alii aliorum cognitionem promoveant, mutuis admonitionibus alii aliorum mores in melius formént, singulique suos ipsorum & aliorum affectus excitent cantionibus Psalmorum sacrorum, hymnorum, & spiritualium odarum, de quavis materia spirituali per Spiritum compositarum, & ad mutuam ædificationem facientium. 5. Ut canant affectibus ad sanctimoniam compositis, pro gratiæ mensura sibi data, ita ut cantus Deo gratus sit, & gratiam auditoribus ministret, in cordis sui sinceritate, Dei gloriam in cantu suo intuentes.
units.tr: Exhortation 8. To the study and practice of the Word of God. The parts of the exhortation are five: (1) That the word of Christ, that is, Christian doctrine as set forth in Scripture, should be drawn from its sources and received in minds and hearts as a most welcome guest, not to depart afterwards, but to remain there constantly; (2) that they should not be content to have tasted the word of Christ or to have known it in some measure, but should labour to acquire for themselves an abundant and copious store; (3) that they should learn from it to be wise for their own salvation and the profit of others; (4) that they should not allow the word of Christ to lie idle in themselves, but should prudently bring it forth for the use of their neighbours, so that by mutual instruction they may advance one another's knowledge, by mutual admonition they may form one another's manners for the better, and each may stir up his own and others' affections by singing sacred psalms, hymns and spiritual odes, composed on any spiritual subject through the Spirit and serving for mutual edification; (5) that they should sing with affections composed to holiness, according to the measure of grace given to them, so that the song may be pleasing to God and minister grace to the hearers, in the sincerity of their heart, looking to the glory of God in their singing.

units.la: Vers. 17. Et quicquid egeritis sermone aut facto, in nomine Domini Iesu facite, gratias agentes Deo & Patri, per eum.
units.tr: Verse 17. And whatsoever ye do in word or deed, do all in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks to God and the Father by him.

units.la: Hortatio 9. Ut omnia faciant in Christo, id est, ejus nomine & auspicio, per Eum seu ejus gratiam, & in Eum, seu ejus gloriam: Et quia id fieri non potest, quin subinde habeant nova divinæ benignitatis in se experimenta, ut gratias agant Deo jugiter in omnibus per Christum, sine quo Deus Pater ne laudari quidem à nobis vult, nec nisi per Filium quicquam nobis concedere, & in quo quæcunque nobis à Deo immittuntur, in bonum nostrum convertuntur. Atque hæ sunt hortationes generales ad communia officia.
units.tr: Exhortation 9. That they should do all things in Christ, that is, in his name and under his auspices, through him, that is, through his grace, and unto him, that is, to his glory. And since this cannot be done without their having from time to time new experiences of divine kindness in themselves, they should give thanks to God continually in all things through Christ, without whom God the Father does not even wish to be praised by us, nor to grant us anything except through the Son, and in whom whatever is sent to us from God is turned to our good. And these are the general exhortations to common duties.

units.la: Secunda pars Capitis.
units.tr: The second part of the chapter.

units.la: Verf. 18. Uxores, subjectæ estote propriis viris, ut convenit in DOMINO.
units.tr: Verse 18. Wives, submit yourselves to your own husbands, as is fitting in the Lord.

units.la: Sequitur altera pars Capitis, continens speciales hortationes ad omnes in familia ordines, hortationes sunt quinque.
units.tr: There follows the other part of the chapter, containing special exhortations to every member of the household. There are five exhortations.

units.la: Hortatio prima est ad uxores, à quibus incipit, quia conditio ipsarum est durior & difficilior quam virorum, & idcirco non mirum si eas primo alloquatur Deus: ab his exigit, ut subjiciantur propriis viris, id est, ut obedientiam, honorem & reverentiam eis exhibeant, sed cum limitatione in Domino, ut in licitis fiat obedientia, & propter mandatum Domini, cui uxores primo subjiciuntur, & obedientiam debent.
units.tr: The first exhortation is to wives, and it comes first because their condition is harder and more difficult than the husbands'. It is therefore no wonder that God addresses them first. He requires them to submit to their own husbands, that is, to show them obedience, honour and reverence. But the limitation in the Lord is added, so that the obedience is given in lawful things and for the sake of the Lord's command, to which wives first submit and owe obedience.

units.la: Ut convenit Arg. hortationis est ab æquitate & decoro, nam quod præcipitur convenit ex ordinatione Divina, & ex Lege naturæ.
units.tr: The argument of the exhortation, as is fitting, is drawn from equity and propriety, for what is commanded is fitting both by divine ordinance and by the law of nature.

units.la: Verf. 19. Viri, diligite uxores, & ne sitis adversus eas amarulenti.
units.tr: Verse 19. Husbands, love your wives, and do not be bitter against them.

units.la: Hortatio 2 ad viros, Quibus præcipit primo ut diligant uxores proprias, idque affectu singulari & sancto, qui conquiescat in una uxore propria; deinde vetat ne sint amarulenti erga eas, vel sermone, vel factis, licet ab earum infirmitatibus irritentur, sed ut prudenter eas regant, sicut decet viros.
units.tr: The second exhortation is to husbands. First he commands them to love their own wives, with a singular and holy affection that rests in one's own wife. Then he forbids them to be bitter towards their wives, in word or in deed, even when they are provoked by their weaknesses. Instead they are to rule them wisely, as is becoming for men.

units.la: Verf 20. Liberi, auscultate parentibus in omnibus: hoc enim gratum est Domino.
units.tr: Verse 20. Children, obey your parents in all things, for this is pleasing to the Lord.

units.la: Hortatio 3. ad filios, à quibus incipit sicut prius ab uxoribus, & postea à servis incipiet, quia conditio eorum est durior, & opus habent Dei institutione, ut sponte faciant quod necesse est facere: ab his exigit obedientiam ex animo erga parentes in omnibus, scilicet quæ Pater cœlestis non prohibuit: Argumentum hortationis est, Quia hoc officium præstitum Deo est gratissimum.
units.tr: The third exhortation is to children. It comes after the one to wives, as before, and the one to servants will come after it, because their condition is harder and they need God's institution so that they may willingly do what they must do. He requires from them obedience from the heart towards their parents in all things, that is, in all things which the heavenly Father has not forbidden. The argument of the exhortation is that this duty is most pleasing to God.

units.la: Verf. 21. Patres, ne irritate liberos vestros, ne desponde-ant animum.
units.tr: Verse 21. Fathers, do not provoke your children, lest they lose heart.

units.la: Hortatio 4. Specialiter ad Patres, qui severiores solent esse quam matres; ne conviciis, injuriis, verberibus severioribus, animos liberorum suorum à se alienent: praeter rationes quae in appellationibus Patrum & liberorum continentur, addit expresse hanc unam, ne liberi severius habiti tandem desperent de Patris dilectione, atque ita desponde-ant animum.
units.tr: The fourth exhortation is addressed specifically to fathers, who are usually more severe than mothers. They must not, by reproaches, injuries or harsher beatings, alienate the hearts of their children. Besides the reasons contained in the terms "fathers" and "children", he expressly adds this one: that children who are treated too harshly may in the end despair of their father's love, and so lose heart.

units.la: Verf. 22. Servi auscultate per omnia iis qui domini sunt secundum carnem, non obsequiis ad oculum exhibitis, ut qui hominibus placere student, sed cum simplicitate cordis, timentes Deum.
units.tr: Verse 22. Servants, obey in all things those who are your masters according to the flesh, not with eye-service, as men-pleasers, but in singleness of heart, fearing God.

units.la: Hortatio 5. ad servos, In qua diutius insistit, quia eorum conditio durissima: Hortationis membra sunt sex, In primo, conditionem servitutis mitigat, ex eo quod tantum ad carnem, & carnalia huius vitae officia pertineat, nec ullam inferat parendi necessitatem in illicitis. In secundo imperat, ut in omnibus licitis pareant & serviant, etiam cum mandata durissima sunt. 3. Ut fideliter & sincere id faciant, non in Dominorum conspectu tantum, sed etiam quum illi absunt, ne negligentiam reprehendere possint. 4. Ut in timore Domini serviant in cordis sinceritate.
units.tr: The fifth exhortation is to servants, and he dwells on it at greater length because their condition is most harsh. The exhortation has six parts. In the first, he softens the condition of servitude, in that it pertains only to the flesh and to the carnal duties of this life, and does not impose any necessity of obeying in unlawful things. In the second, he commands them to obey and serve in all lawful things, even when the commands are very harsh. Third, that they do this faithfully and sincerely, not only in their masters' sight but also when they are absent, so that they cannot be charged with negligence. Fourth, that they serve in the fear of the Lord, with sincerity of heart.

units.la: Verf. 23. Et quicquid feceritis, ex animo facite, tanquam Domino, & non hominibus.
units.tr: Verse 23. And whatever you do, do it heartily, as to the Lord and not to men.

units.la: 5. Ut in servitio omni, externa actio originem ducat ex animo, & interioribus affectibus, unde externa actio derivetur ad manum: 6. Ut imperium Dei agnoscant in mandatis Dominorum suorum, & quod faciant Dei voluntatem dum praestant quod Domini volunt.
units.tr: Fifth, that in all service the outward action arises from the mind and from inner affections, from which the outward action is carried through to the hand. Sixth, that they acknowledge God's authority in their masters' commands, and that in doing what their masters want they do the will of God.

units.la: Verf. 24. Scientes vos à Domino receptur os mercedem hereditatis: Domino Christo servitis.
units.tr: Verse 24. Knowing that from the Lord you will receive the reward of the inheritance; you serve the Lord Christ.

units.la: Hortationis argumenta sunt quatuor: 1. Quia Deus rependet illis mercedem meliorem quam Domini pacisc untur vel dare possunt, nempe vitam aeternam, pro haereditate gratuita.
units.tr: There are four arguments of the exhortation: (1) because God will repay them with a better reward than their masters agree to give or are able to give, namely eternal life, in return for a free inheritance;

units.la: Nam] Arg. 2. Quia certi esse possunt de remuneratione gratuita, ex eo quod Christo serviant, qui non potest servos suos negligere.
units.tr: For the second argument: they can be certain of the free reward, because they serve Christ, who cannot neglect his servants.

units.la: Verf. 25. Qui vero injuriam intulerit, referet injuriam quam intulerit: neque est personarum respectus. Arg. 3. Quia Deus vindicabit injurias à Dominis servis illatas, & simul injurias servorum in Dominos, nisi præcepto huic sese submittant.
units.tr: Verse 25. But he who does wrong will receive back the wrong he has done, and there is no partiality. The third argument: because God will avenge the wrongs done by masters to servants, and at the same time the wrongs of servants against masters, unless they submit to this precept.

units.la: Nec est] Arg. 4. confirmans superius; Quia Deus nec acceptat personam Domini, neque servi in judicando, sed justitiam exercet in puniendis malis.
units.tr: And there is no partiality: the fourth argument, confirming what was said above: because God does not accept the person of the master, nor of the servant, in judging, but exercises justice in punishing evils.

units.la: Caput Quartum.
units.tr: Chapter Four.

units.la: HOC Capite post hortationem ad Dominos, quæ pertinet ad præcedens caput, habentur generales hortationes, ad verf.
units.tr: In this chapter, after the exhortation to masters, which belongs to the preceding chapter, come general exhortations, down to verse

units.la: 7. reliquo Capite res privatæ.
units.tr: 7. The rest of the chapter deals with private matters.

units.la: Verf. 1. VOS Domini, æquitatem & æquabilitatem servis exhibete, scientes vos quoque habere Dominum in Cœlis.
units.tr: Verse 1. Masters, give your servants what is just and equal, knowing that you also have a Master in heaven.

units.la: Vicissim hortatur Dominos ad æquabilem & rationi congruam servorum tractationem, hoc est, ut non tantùm victum, amictum. & mercedem pactam illis persolvant, sed etiam hilaritatem servitii ipsorum, liberalitatis aliquâ demonstratione agnoscant, hoc enim est, quod æquum est iis tribuere.
units.tr: Conversely, he exhorts masters to treat their servants evenly and reasonably. That is, they should not only supply food, clothing and the agreed wages, but also acknowledge the willingness of their service with some display of generosity, for this is what is fair to give them.

units.la: Vt qui ] Arg. hortationis est, Quia nisi fecerint quod æquum est, Dominus cœlestis imminet ipsorum capitibus, qui iis secundùm opera retribuet.
units.tr: Knowing that ] The argument of the exhortation: unless they do what is fair, the heavenly Lord hangs over their heads, and he will repay them according to their works.

units.la: Verf. 2. In precibus perdurate, invigilantes iis cum gratiarum actione:
units.tr: Verse 2. Continue steadfastly in prayer, keeping watch in it with thanksgiving.

units.la: Hortationes generales sunt tres: Prima ad precationem, cujus membra sunt quatuor: 1. Ne in hoc exercitio defetiscantur, sed constanter perseverent, quia quotidie urget necessitas aliqua: 2. Ut observent & captent omnes occasiones precandi à Deo oblatas, & sine oscitantia frequenter prosequantur petitiones suas: 3. Ut semper adjungant gratiarum actionem precationibus suis, si modo cupiant nova beneficia sibi à Deo dari.
units.tr: There are three general exhortations. The first concerns prayer, and its parts are four: (1) they should not grow weary in this exercise, but persevere constantly, since some need presses on them every day; (2) they should watch for and seize every opportunity of praying that God offers, and without drowsiness frequently pursue their requests; (3) they should always join thanksgiving to their prayers, if they really want new benefits to be given them by God.

units.la: Verf. 3. Precantes simul etiam pro nobis, ut Deus aperiat no bis, ostium sermonis, ut loquamur mysterium Christi, propter quod etiam sum vinctus:
units.tr: Verse 3. Praying at the same time also for us, that God may open to us a door for the word, to speak the mystery of Christ, on account of which I am also in bonds.

units.la: Verf. 4. Ut, inquam, illud patefaciam, sicut oportet me loqui.
units.tr: Verse 4. That I may, I say, make it manifest, as I ought to speak.

units.la: Membrum 4. Ut in precationibus suis orent Deum, ut currat Euangelium cum successu, per Apostoli & aliorum Dei servorum Ministerium: In hunc finem proponit hortationis tria Argumenta. Arg. 1. Quia sic liberam facultatem prædicandi Euangelium, seu patefaciendi salutis mysterium in Christo Deus concessurus erat, aperiendo os ministri sui, & cor Auditorum.
units.tr: The fourth part: that in their prayers they should pray to God that the Gospel may run with success through the ministry of the Apostle and of the other servants of God. To this end he sets out three arguments. Argument 1: because God was going to grant them free opportunity to preach the Gospel, that is, to make known the mystery of salvation in Christ, by opening the mouth of his minister and the heart of the hearers.

units.la: Ut loquamur ] Arg. 2. Quia ego Apostolus vinctus pro Euangelii prædicatione, commendatam vobis volo libertatem Euangelii potius quam meam ipsius.
units.tr: That we may speak] Argument 2: because I, the Apostle, am in bonds for preaching the Gospel, I want you to commend the freedom of the Gospel rather than my own.

units.la: Sicut oportet ] Arg. 3. Quia interest multum, ut mihi aperiatur os, ut accommodatè loquar ad persuadendum cum demonstratione potentiæ spiritualis, quemadmodum decet me Apostolum loqui.
units.tr: As I ought to speak] Argument 3: because it matters much that my mouth be opened, so that I may speak fittingly, to persuade with a demonstration of spiritual power, as befits me as an Apostle.

units.la: Verf. 5. Sapienter vos gerite erga extraneos, opportunitatem redimentes,
units.tr: Verse 5. Conduct yourselves wisely towards outsiders, redeeming the time.

units.la: Hortatio 2. Generalis, Ut vitam sapienter instituant secundum Dei voluntatem, caventes sedulò, ne ipsorum conversatio mala vel imprudens offendat extraneos, id est, non conversos Ethnicos, eosque arceat à Dei civitate: Et ne ipsi infidelium corruptis sermonibus vel moribus corrumpantur; utque in hunc finem etiam cum jactura rerum minùs pretiosarum opportunitatem redimant benè agendi, & mali vitandi, & speciatim extraneos lucrifaciendi.
units.tr: Exhortation 2, general: that they should order their life wisely according to the will of God, taking careful heed that their conduct, if evil or imprudent, does not offend outsiders, that is, the unconverted Gentiles, and so keep them away from the city of God; and that they themselves not be corrupted by the corrupt talk or morals of unbelievers. And to this end, even at the cost of less valuable things, they should redeem the opportunity of doing good and avoiding evil, and especially of winning outsiders.

units.la: Verf. 6. Sermo vester semper cum gratia sit sale conditus, ut sciatù quomodo oportet vos unicuique respondere,
units.tr: Verse 6. Let your speech always be with grace, seasoned with salt, so that you may know how you ought to answer each one.

units.la: Hortatio 3. Ne sermo ipsorum unquam sit futilis vel otiosus, qui nullam auditori afferat utilitatem; sed ut semper sit cum gratiâ ad ædificationem auditoris; in eumque finem hortatur, ut sermo ipsorum semper sale sanctitatis sit conditus: Arg. hortationis est, ut ex perpetua consuetudine sanctè loquendi acquiratur prudentia & discretio, ad apte & appositè respondendum unicuique de re quavis interroganti.
units.tr: Exhortation 3: that their speech should never be idle or trifling, bringing no benefit to the hearer; but that it should always be with grace, for the edification of the hearer. To this end he exhorts that their speech always be seasoned with the salt of holiness. The argument of the exhortation is that from a constant habit of speaking holily, prudence and discernment are acquired, so as to answer each person fittingly and to the point, on whatever matter he asks.

units.la: Secunda pars Capitis.
units.tr: Second part of the chapter.

units.la: Verf. 7. Res meas omnes vobis notas faciet Tychicus dilectus frater, & fidus minister, ac conservus in Domino:
units.tr: Verse 7. Tychicus, the beloved brother and faithful minister and fellow servant in the Lord, will make known to you all my affairs.

units.la: Verf. 8. Quem misi ad vos ob hoc ipsum, ut cognoscat res vestras & corda vestra consoletur:
units.tr: Verse 8. Whom I have sent to you for this very purpose, that he may know your state and comfort your hearts.

units.la: Verf. 9 Cum Onesimo fido & dilecto fratre, qui est ex vobis: Omnia igitur vobis exponent quae hic aguntur:
units.tr: Verse 9. With Onesimus, the faithful and beloved brother, who is one of you. They will tell you everything that is done here.

units.la: Altera pars Capitis de rebus privatis sex habet articulos: Art. primus spectat legatos, Tychicum Euangelistam, & Onesimum Colossensem, qui una cum hac Epistola missi sunt: 1. Ut certiores redderent Colossenses quomodo res Apostoli se haberent, quam fortiter ferret vincula pro Euangelio: & quaecunque alia scire eorum referebat, significarent.
units.tr: The second part of the chapter, on private matters, has six articles. The first concerns the messengers, Tychicus the evangelist and Onesimus of Colossae, who were sent together with this Epistle: (1) that they should inform the Colossians how the Apostle was faring, how bravely he bore his bonds for the Gospel, and that they should report whatever else he told them to make known.

units.la: 2. Ut redeuntes certiores postea redderent Apostolum de statu Colossensium: 3. Ut consolarentur Colossensium corda; quem in finem utrumque commendat, sed Tychicum imprimis.
units.tr: (2) that on their return they should inform the Apostle in turn about the state of the Colossians; (3) that they should comfort the hearts of the Colossians. He commends them for both purposes, but Tychicus especially.

units.la: Verf. 10 Salutat vos Aristarchus meus in captivitate socius, & Marcus consobrinus Barnabae, de quo accepistis mandata: si venerit ad vos, excipite eum.
units.tr: Verse 10. Aristarchus, my fellow prisoner, greets you, and Mark, the cousin of Barnabas, about whom you received instructions; if he comes to you, receive him.

units.la: Articulus 2. De missis salutationibus, quarum prima erat ab Aristarcho, qui in vinculis jacebat cum Apostolo, propter defensam fidem Euangelii: Salutatio 2. a Marco consobrino Barnabae (de quo contentio erat inter Paulum & Barnabam,) quem nunc receptum in gratiam speciali-ter illis commendatum vult, si ad eos veniret, idque eo fine, ut intelligerent eum in pretio haberi ab Apostolo.
units.tr: Article 2, on the greetings sent. The first was from Aristarchus, who lay in chains with the Apostle for defending the faith of the Gospel. The second greeting is from Mark, cousin of Barnabas (over whom there was dispute between Paul and Barnabas), whom he now wants commended to them in particular as one received back into favour, if he should come to them; and he wants this so that they may understand that he is held in high esteem by the Apostle.

units.la: Verf. 11 Et Iesus qui vocatur Justus, qui sunt ex circumcisione: hi soli adjutores in regno Dei fuere mihi solatio.
units.tr: Verse 11. And Jesus, who is called Justus, who are of the circumcision: these alone are my fellow workers in the kingdom of God, and they have been a comfort to me.

units.la: Salutatio 3. est ab Iesu cognomento Justo, qui cum supra nominatis duobus in praedicando Euangelio Apostolum juvabat; & hi tres soli erant ex Judaeis, qui Apostolo solatio erant.
units.tr: Greeting 3 is from Jesus surnamed Justus, who with the two named above helped the Apostle in preaching the Gospel; and these three alone were Jews who were a comfort to the Apostle.

units.la: Verf. 12. Salutat vos Epaphras, qui ex vobis est, servus Christi, semper decertans pro vobis in precibus, ut stetis perfecti, & completi in omni voluntate Dei. Verf. 13. Hoc enim de eo testor, cum multo vestri studio ardere, & eorum qui sunt Laodicea, & eorum qui Hierapoli.
units.tr: Verse 12. Epaphras, who is one of you, a servant of Christ, always striving for you in prayers, greets you, that you may stand perfect and complete in all the will of God. Verse 13. For I bear him witness that he has great zeal for you, and for those who are in Laodicea, and those who are in Hierapolis.

units.la: Salutatio 4. ab Epaphra Colossensium pastore, quem commendat:
units.tr: Greeting 4, from Epaphras, minister of the Colossians, whom he commends:

units.la: 1. A sinceritate in officio; quod servus sit CHRISTI: 2. A speciali cura gregis sui, pro quo ardenter DEUM assiduè orabat, ut membra Ecclesiæ istius, in cognitione, in fide & obedientia divinæ voluntatis, constanter perseverarent, & incrementum ad perfectionem facerent: 3. A zelo ipsius pro Colossensium, Laodicensium, & Hierapolensium salute, de cujus zeli ardore testimonium perhibet suum Apostolus.
units.tr: 1. From his sincerity in his office, in that he is a servant of CHRIST. 2. From his special care for his flock, for whom he prayed to GOD earnestly and continually, that the members of this Church might persevere steadfastly in the knowledge, faith and obedience of the divine will, and make progress toward perfection. 3. From his zeal for the salvation of the Colossians, Laodiceans and Hierapolitans, to the ardour of which zeal the Apostle himself bears witness.

units.la: Verf. 14. Salutat vos Lucas, Medicus ille Dilectus, & Demas.
units.tr: Verse 14. Luke, the beloved physician, and Demas greet you.

units.la: Salutatio 5. missa à Luca Medico, & à Dema, qui nondum ab Apostoli societate defectionem fecerat.
units.tr: Greeting 5, sent by Luke the physician and by Demas, who had not yet fallen away from the Apostle's company.

units.la: Verf. 15. Salutate fratres qui sunt Laodicea, & Nympham, & Ecclesiam quæ in domo illius est.
units.tr: Verse 15. Greet the brethren who are in Laodicea, and Nympha, and the Church which is in her house.

units.la: Articulus 3. Continet salutationem missam ab Apostolo ipso, quâ jubet salutari suo nomine fratres Laodicenses & Nympham, cum Ecclesia quæ erat domi ipsius. Sic vocat familiam Nymphæ, quia tota piè instituta erat, & rite gubernata, sicut solent esse Ecclesiæ.
units.tr: Article 3. This contains a greeting sent by the Apostle himself, by which he bids the brethren of Laodicea and Nympha be saluted in his name, together with the Church which was in her house. He calls Nympha's household a Church because the whole of it was piously ordered and duly governed, as Churches are wont to be.

units.la: Verf. 16. Et quum perlecta fuerit apud vos Epistola, facite ut etiam in Laodicensium Ecclesia recitetur: & eam quæ scripta est ex Laodicea, ut vos quoque legatis.
units.tr: Verse 16. And when this epistle has been read among you, cause that it be read also in the Church of the Laodiceans; and that you likewise read the one which is written from Laodicea.

units.la: Articulus 4. De communicanda hac Epistola cum Laodicensibus, qui opus habebant eadem hac doctrina propter simile ipsorum à Pseudapostolis periculum: Meminit autem alius Epistolæ Laodiceâ scriptæ, quam aliqui putant fuisse ab Apostolo scriptam, dum Laodiceæ esset, eamque jam interiisse. Sed certum est ab Apostolo nostro scribi non potuisse aliquam Epistolam Laodiceâ, quippe qui testatur, Cap. 2. verf. 1. neque Laodicenses, neque Colossenses faciem ejus in carne unquam vidisse, seu corpore præsentem conspexisse. Verisimilius est intelligi Epistolam ab ipsis Laodicensibus ad Apostolum scriptam, quæ statum illius Ecclesiæ ipsi significaret. Cui Epistolæ per hanc Epistolam Apostolus voluit responsum & satisfactum esse. Quicquid erat, certum est interfuisse Colossensis loflensis Ecclesiæ eam Epistolam apud ipsos legi, & hanc Laodicensibus communicarii
units.tr: Article 4. On sharing this epistle with the Laodiceans, who needed this same teaching because of the similar danger to them from false apostles. He mentions another epistle written from Laodicea, which some think was written by the Apostle while he was at Laodicea, and that it has since perished. But it is certain that no epistle could have been written by our Apostle from Laodicea, since he testifies (chap. 2, verse 1) that neither the Laodiceans nor the Colossians had ever seen his face in the flesh, or beheld him present in body. It is more probable that the epistle is understood to have been written to the Apostle by the Laodiceans themselves, signifying to him the state of that Church. To this epistle the Apostle wished this present letter to serve as a reply and satisfaction. Whatever the case, it is certain that the Colossian Church had a part in having that epistle read among them, and in sharing this one with the Laodiceans.

units.la: Vers. 17. Et dicite Archippo, Vide ut ministerium quod accepisti, in Domino impleas.
units.tr: Verse 17. And say to Archippus: See that you fulfil the ministry which you have received in the Lord.

units.la: Articulus 5. De commonefaciendo Archippò Colossensium Ministro, & Epaphræ Collega, qui (ut apparet) negligentior erat, & opus habebat admonitione ab Ecclesiæ suæ Synedrio, seu Compresbyteris; quibus Apostolus mandat, 1. Ut excitent eum ad officii sui partes, & muneris sui gravitatem pensitandum: 2. Ut de ratione reddenda legationis sibi à Christo commissæ, ad Ministerium exequendum commonefaciant: 3. Ut ad implendum officium sibi commissum, propterea serió hortentur: atque hæc à Colossensibus requirit Apostolus, ut Archippus moveretur magis cum adverteret non esse sine Apostolica autoritate, quod Ecclesia ipsum de officio exequendo admonitura esset.
units.tr: Article 5. On admonishing Archippus, minister of the Colossians and colleague of Epaphras, who (as appears) was somewhat negligent and needed admonition from the consistory of his Church, or fellow elders. To these the Apostle commits: 1. that they should rouse him to the duties of his office and to weigh the weight of his function; 2. that they should remind him to render an account of the embassy committed to him by Christ, for the carrying out of the ministry; 3. that they should therefore urge him earnestly to fulfil the office committed to him. The Apostle requires these things of the Colossians so that Archippus might be moved more, when he perceived that it was not without Apostolic authority that the Church would admonish him to discharge his office.

units.la: Vers. 18. Salutatio mea manu Pauli. Memores estote vinculorum meorum. Gratia sit vobiscum. Amen.
units.tr: Verse 18. The greeting of me, Paul, with my own hand. Remember my bonds. Grace be with you. Amen.

units.la: Articulus 6. Continens Epistolæ conclusionem, quam solebat Apostolus in omnibus Epistolis, non per amanuensem, ut reliquum corpus Epistolæ, sed sua ipsius propria manu scribere, in qua primò salutat omnes: 2. Epistolarum suarum characteristicam notam indigitat, ne ullam Epistolam genuinam agnoscerent, tanquam ab ipso missam, cui ipse propria manu non subscriberet: 3. Hortatur, ut precantes pro ipso in vinculis jam jacente, patientiam & fidem tam illustri exemplo invitati discerent: 4. Denique, Gratiam Dei, (unde ut ex fonte omnia bona ad eos fluant) iis exoptat, & communicandam sperat: omnia quæ hactenus scripserat quasi sigillo fidei obsignans: Amen.
units.tr: Article 6. Containing the conclusion of the epistle, which the Apostle was accustomed to write in all his epistles, not through an amanuensis, as the rest of the body of the epistle, but with his own hand. In it, first, he greets everyone; 2. he points out the distinguishing mark of his epistles, so that they might acknowledge no epistle as genuine as if sent by him unless he had subscribed it with his own hand; 3. he urges those who pray for him, now lying in bonds, to learn patience and faith, being invited by so illustrious an example; 4. finally, he wishes grace from God (from whom, as from a fountain, all good things flow to them) and hopes it will be shared with them, sealing with his seal of faith all that he had hitherto written. Amen.

units.la: EXPOSITIO
units.tr: EXPOSITION

units.la: EXPOSITIO ANALYTICA EPISTOLAE PRIORIS, AD THESSALONICENSES. Summarium.
units.tr: ANALYTICAL EXPOSITION OF THE FIRST EPISTLE TO THE THESSALONIANS. Summary.

units.la: THessalonica Metropolis olim fuit totius Macedoniae, in qua Paulus & Silas (ut habetur Act. 17) multos ex Judaeis simul & Gentilibus ad fidem Christianam exiguo tempore converterunt: sed postquam ab incredulis, seditione excitata, per vim illinc ejecti fuissent, Apostolus primo Beream, deinde Athenas se contulit: & primo quidem Timotheum ad eos ablegat, qui afflictos consolaretur. Deinde reverso jam Timotheo, & intellecta Thessalonicensium constantia, mittit hanc Epistolam, in qua confirmat ipsos in fide, & ad vitam sanctâ professione suâ dignam hortatur.
units.tr: Thessalonica was once the metropolis of all Macedonia. There Paul and Silas (as we read in Acts 17) in a short time converted many, both Jews and Gentiles, to the Christian faith. But after they had been driven out of the city by violence, a riot having been stirred up by the unbelievers, the Apostle went first to Berea and then to Athens. First, indeed, he sent Timothy to them, to comfort those who were afflicted. Then, when Timothy had returned and he had learned of the steadfastness of the Thessalonians, he sent this Epistle, in which he confirms them in the faith and exhorts them to a life worthy of their holy profession.

units.la: Epistolae partes principales sunt duae: In prima postquam operam dedit ut in fide Christi, & persuasione de suo ipsius erga eos affectu confirmarentur, animat ad Constantiam, Capite 1, 2, 3.
units.tr: The principal parts of the Epistle are two. In the first, after he has labored to have them confirmed in faith in Christ and in the persuasion of his own affection toward them, he encourages them to constancy, chapters 1, 2, 3.

units.la: In altera instruit & hortatur ad vitam sanctam, interjectâ consolatione de resurrectione Mortuorum, Capite 4, 5.
units.tr: In the second, he instructs and exhorts them to a holy life, with a consolation about the resurrection of the dead interposed, chapters 4, 5.

units.la: Caput Primum.
units.tr: Chapter 1.

units.la: POst salutationem Apostolicam, versu primo. Toto reliquo Capite confirmat Thessalonicenses in Fide, Gratias agendo Deo pro sincera ipsorum Conversione.
units.tr: After the apostolic salutation, in verse 1: for the whole rest of the chapter he confirms the Thessalonians in the faith, giving thanks to God for their sincere conversion.

units.la: PAulus & Sylvanus & Timotheus Ecclesiae Thessalonicensium, quae est in Deo Patre, & Domino Jesu Christo, Gratia sit vobis & pax à Deo Patre nostro, & Domino Jesu Christo.
units.tr: Paul, and Silvanus, and Timotheus, unto the church of the Thessalonians which is in God the Father and in the Lord Jesus Christ: Grace be unto you, and peace, from God our Father, and the Lord Jesus Christ.

units.la: Personæ salutantes sunt Paulus, Timotheus & Sylvanus, qui aliàs Silas dicitur, quos ut Thessalonicensibus de facie notos, & qui præsentes ipsos docuerant, asciscit sibi in societatem Testimonii de veritate doctrinæ hujus, & studii sui erga Thessalonicenses.
units.tr: The persons greeting are Paul, Timothy and Silvanus, who is also called Silas. He takes them into partnership as witnesses to the truth of this doctrine and as sharing his concern for the Thessalonians, since they were known to them by sight and had taught them in person.

units.la: Ecclesia salutata describitur à sancta communione sua, non tantùm cum Deo Patre, quem falsò jactabant infideles Judæi se colere, sed etiam cum Filio Christo, quem infideles Ethnici & Judæi rejiciebant: præterea precatur iis gratiam & pacem, à Deo Patre & Christo; significans à gratia Dei proficisci veram felicitatem, quæ sicut merito Christi credentibus comparatur, sic per intercessionem & operationem Christi applicanda est.
units.tr: The church greeted is described by its holy fellowship, not only with God the Father, whom the unbelieving Jews falsely boasted of worshipping, but also with the Son Christ, whom the unbelieving Gentiles and Jews rejected. He further prays for them grace and peace from God the Father and Christ, signifying that true happiness proceeds from the grace of God; and just as it is obtained for believers by the merit of Christ, so it is to be applied through the intercession and working of Christ.

units.la: Verf. 2. Gratias agimus Deo semper de omnibus vobis, mentionem vestri facientes in precibus nostris:
units.tr: Verse 2. We give thanks to God always for you all, making mention of you in our prayers:

units.la: Reliquo Capite gratias agendo pro Thessalonicensium sincera conversione, confirmat ipsos in fide, Argumentis novem, quæ & probant corroborari debere eos in fide, & tot etiam rationes continent gratiarum actionis.
units.tr: Giving thanks for the sincere conversion of the Thessalonians throughout the rest of the chapter, he confirms them in the faith by nine arguments. These arguments both show that they ought to be strengthened in the faith and also contain as many reasons for giving thanks.

units.la: Argumentum primum, Jucundissima mihi est memoria vestræ conversionis ad fidem, de qua non possum non Deo gratias agere, & assiduò precari ut perseveretis. Ergo in fide corroborari debetis.
units.tr: The first argument: The memory of your conversion to the faith is most delightful to me, and for it I cannot but give thanks to God and pray constantly that you may persevere. Therefore you ought to be strengthened in the faith.

units.la: Verf. 3. Indesinenter memoria repetentes efficacem vestram fidem, & laboriosam charitatem, & tolerantem illam spem in Domino nostro Iesu, coram Deo Patre nostro:
units.tr: Verse 3. Remembering without ceasing your work of faith, and labour of love, and patience of hope in our Lord Jesus Christ, in the sight of God and our Father;

units.la: Arg. 2. Vestra sincera fides quæ vivam se ostendit, & per opera efficacem; Indefatigabilis charitas vestra, spectanda in assiduis laboribus, & diligentia, potissimum in beneficentia vestra erga Sanctos: Et denique viva spes vestra in patientia & tolerantia afflictionum pro Christo demonstrata, impressionem sui reliquerunt in me indelebilem ut non possim coram Deo & hominibus de iis mentionem non facere: Ergo in fide corroborari vos consentaneum est. Vocat autem eas virtutes Christi, quia à Christo oriebantur, ab eo fluebant, & in eum tendebant. Dicit autem coram DEO, quia ejusmodi erant quæ in conspectu Dei pro genuinis, seu minimè fucatis comperiebantur.
units.tr: Argument 2. Your sincere faith, which shows itself alive and effective through works; your tireless love, seen in constant labours and diligence, above all in your kindness towards the saints; and finally your living hope, displayed in patience and endurance of afflictions for Christ, have left an indelible impression on me, so that I cannot fail to mention them before God and men. Therefore it is fitting that you be confirmed in the faith. He calls these virtues "of Christ" because they arose from Christ, flowed from him and tended towards him. He says "in the sight of God" because they were such as were found to be genuine, that is, not at all feigned, in the sight of God.

units.la: Verf. 4. Ut qui sciamus fratres dilecti, vos esse à Deo electos:
units.tr: Verse 4. Knowing, brethren beloved, your election of God.

units.la: Arg. 3. Ex indiciis certis certò scio vos electos esse, & genuinos in Christo fratres meos. Ergo est quod in fide corroboremini.
units.tr: Argument 3. From certain signs I know for certain that you are elect and genuine brethren of mine in Christ. Therefore there is reason for you to be strengthened in the faith.

units.la: MMM Verf. 5. Quoniam Euangelium nostrum constitit apud vos non loquutione duntaxat, sed etiam virtute, cum in Spiritu sancto, tum in certa persuasione multa: sicut nostis quales fuerimus inter vos vestra causa.
units.tr: Verse 5. For our gospel came not unto you in word only, but also in power, and in the Holy Ghost, and in much assurance; as ye know what manner of men we were among you for your sake.

units.la: Arg 4. confirmans superius, Perspectum habeo Euangelium meum apud vos fuisse efficax, sermonem enim meum vobis prædicatum commutabatur: 1. Vis & potentia spiritualis ad fidem in vobis gignendam: 2. SPIRITUS Sanctus obsignabat in vobis admissam veritatem interno suo testimonio, & donis insuper datis: 3. Multa certioratio & persuasio sequebatur in cordibus vestris, quæ omnem hæsitationem à vobis sustulit: 4. Talis erat operatio, & præsentia DEI in vobis audientibus, qualis erat visenda in nobis Apostolis docentibus, sicut ipsi novistis: Est ergo quod in fide corroboremini.
units.tr: Argument 4, confirming what was said above: I am well aware that my gospel was effective among you, for the word I preached to you was changed: (1) it had spiritual power and force to beget faith in you; (2) the Holy Spirit sealed the truth admitted among you by his inward testimony, and moreover by the gifts bestowed; (3) much certainty and persuasion followed in your hearts, which removed all hesitation from you; (4) the working and presence of God in you as hearers was such as could be seen in us Apostles teaching, as you yourselves know. There is therefore reason for you to be strengthened in the faith.

units.la: Vers. 6. Et vos imitatores nostri facti fuistis, & DOMINI, recepto sermone cum oppressione multa, cum gaudio SPIRITUS Sancti.
units.tr: Verse 6. And ye became followers of us, and of the Lord, having received the word in much affliction, with joy of the Holy Ghost:

units.la: Arg. 5. illustrans superius, Vos Euangelium amplectendo, ipsumque firmiter cum gaudio retinendo, in mediis afflictionibus similes redditi estis & Domino Christo, & nobis servis ejus praedicantibus illud Euangelium cum gaudio, in mediis oppressionibus. Est ergo quod in fide corroboremini.
units.tr: Argument 5, illustrating what was said above: By embracing the gospel, and holding it firmly with joy, you have become like the Lord Christ and like us, his servants, who preached that gospel with joy amid oppressions. There is therefore reason for you to be strengthened in the faith.

units.la: Verf. 7. Adeo ut fueritis exemplaria omnibus credentibus in Macedonia, & in Achaia.
units.tr: Verse 7. So that ye were ensamples to all that believe in Macedonia and Achaia.

units.la: Arg. 6 confirmans superius, Facti fuistis typi, & exemplaria omnibus in vicinis regionibus habitantibus, fidei invictae, summaque alacritatis & patientiae, in recipiendo & retinendo Euangelio: Ergo est quod in fide corroboremini.
units.tr: Argument 6, confirming what was said above: You have become types and examples to all who dwell in the neighbouring regions, of unconquered faith, and of the greatest eagerness and patience in receiving and holding fast the gospel. Therefore there is reason for you to be strengthened in the faith.

units.la: Verf. 8. A vobis enim non solum personuit sermo Domini in Macedonia & in Achaia, verumetiam in omni loco, fides vestra quae est in DEVM, dimanavit, ut necesse non habeamus quicquam loqui.
units.tr: Verse 8. For from you sounded out the word of the Lord not only in Macedonia and Achaia, but also in every place your faith to God-ward is spread abroad; so that we need not to speak any thing.

units.la: Arg. 7: Fides vestra evasit celeberrima, non in proximis regionibus tantum, sed etiam in longe dissitis, ut non sit opus longiori probatione, Est igitur quod confirmemini in fide. Verf. 9. Siquidem ipsi de nobis annuntiant qualem ingressum habuerimus ad vos, & quomodo conversi fueritis ad Deum, relictis idolis, ut servireris Deo vivo & vero:
units.tr: Argument 7: Your faith has become most famous, not only in the nearby regions but also in far distant ones, so that there is no need for any longer proof. Therefore you ought to be confirmed in the faith. Verse 9. For they themselves shew of us what manner of entering in we had unto you, and how ye turned to God from idols to serve the living and true God;

units.la: Arg. 8. In conversione vestri apparuit Dei virtus adeo admiranda ut fideles ubique locorum depraedicaverint conversionis Thessalonicensium historiam, quomodo scilicet Apostolus cum manifesto Capitis periculo praedicaverit Euangelium apud vos, & quomodo vos eo audito mirum in modum renunciaveritis idolis fictitiis, vosque, in servitium unius veri & viventis Dei addixeritis. Est ergo quod in fide corroboremini.
units.tr: Argument 8: In your conversion there appeared the power of God, so admirable that the faithful everywhere have spread abroad the account of the conversion of the Thessalonians: namely, how the Apostle preached the gospel among you at manifest peril to his life, and how you, on hearing it, renounced the false idols in a remarkable manner and devoted yourselves to the service of the one true and living God. There is therefore reason for you to be strengthened in the faith.

units.la: Vers. 10. Et expectaretis Filium ejus e cælis, quem excitavit a mortuis, nempe Iesum qui liberat nos ab ira illa ventura.
units.tr: Verse 10. And to wait for his Son from heaven, whom he raised from the dead, even Jesus, which delivered us from the wrath to come.

units.la: Arg. 9. Conversio vestra non fuit ad Deum, sine Filio suo Christo, sicut Judæi infideles falsa conversionem suam jactitant: sed ad Deum in Christo, seu ad Patrem, & ad Christum, ut Dei Filium incarnatum, Redemptorem, mortuum, & resuscitatum pro nobis; qui e Cœlo Judex venturus est ad perdendum omnes infideles, & ad liberandum suos ab ira quæ ventura est in reliquos, quæ fides unica est salvifica: Ergo debetis hæc Dei in vobis operâ recolentes in fide confirmari.
units.tr: Argument 9: Your conversion was not to God without his Son Christ, as the unbelieving Jews falsely boast of their conversion; but it was to God in Christ, that is, to the Father and to Christ as the incarnate Son of God, the Redeemer who died and was raised again for us, who as Judge will come from heaven to destroy all unbelievers and to deliver his own from the wrath that is to come upon the rest; this faith alone is saving. Therefore, recalling these works of God in you, you ought to be confirmed in the faith.

units.la: Caput Secundum.
units.tr: Chapter 2.

units.la: Ergit ad Fidei ipsorum Confirmationem, Ministerii sui sinceritatem, ejusque efficaciam inter ipsos commendare, suumq; erga ipsos benevolum affectum ostendere.
units.tr: He turns to the confirmation of their faith: to commend the sincerity of his ministry and its effectiveness among them, and to show his benevolent affection towards them.

units.la: Capitis partes sunt tres, In prima revocat iis in mentem manifesta indicia divinæ legationis suæ ad eos, ad vers. 13. In secunda ostendit manifesta vestigia divinæ gratiæ in ipsorum conversione, ad vers. 17. In tertia confirmat benevolum suum erga eos affectum, ne putarent se ab Apostolo non satis curari.
units.tr: The chapter has three parts. In the first he recalls to their minds the clear signs of his divine embassy to them, down to verse 13. In the second he shows the manifest traces of divine grace in their conversion, down to verse 17. In the third he confirms his benevolent affection towards them, lest they think the Apostle does not care for them enough.

units.la: Vers. 1. Nam ipsi nostis, fratres, ingressum nostrum ad vos non fuisse vanum:
units.tr: Verse 1. For you yourselves know, brothers, that our coming to you was not in vain.

units.la: Indicia spiritualis sincerae & divinae suae legationis ad eos, & fidelis administrationis officii sui toto tempore quo Euangelium inter eos primo praedicavit, enumerat tredecim.
units.tr: He lists thirteen indications of his spiritual, sincere and divine embassy to them, and of his faithful administration of his office during the whole time in which he first preached the Gospel among them.

units.la: Indicium primum, Ipsi testes estis, nihil habuisse vanitatis ingressum nostrum ad vos, nec fructu caruisse ministerium meum, cum inter vos incepi praedicare Euangelium.
units.tr: First indication: You yourselves are witnesses that our coming to you had no vanity in it, and that my ministry was not without fruit, when I began to preach the Gospel among you.

units.la: Verf. 2. Imo etiam quum ante afflicti fuissemus, & contumeliis affecti Philippis, sicut nostis libertate usi sumus in Deo nostro ad annuntiandum apud vos Euangelium Dei cum multo certamine.
units.tr: Verse 2. But even after we had suffered before and been treated shamefully at Philippi, as you know, we were bold in our God to speak to you the Gospel of God with much conflict.

units.la: Indicium 2. Persecutio magna, quam ante non ita multo passus fueram Philippis, non impedivit quo minus auderem vobis etiam in praesenti Capitis periculo praedicare: nam intrepide loquendi libertate usus sum, sola Dei virtute fretus, contra omnes hostes strenue decertans.
units.tr: Second indication: The great persecution which I had suffered not long before at Philippi did not stop me from daring to preach to you even in the present danger of my life. For I used the freedom of speaking fearlessly, relying on the power of God alone and striving bravely against all enemies.

units.la: Verf. 3. Exhortatio enim nostra non fuit ex impostura, neque ex impuritate, neque cum dolo:
units.tr: Verse 3. For our exhortation was not of deceit, nor of uncleanness, nor in guile.

units.la: Indicium 3. confirmans superius, Doctrina, hortatio, & consolatio a me administrata, non erat similis doctrinae Pseudapostolorum, nam, 1. Non erat adulterata & composita ad deceptionem, sed sincera, sine omni impostura: nec fovebam, nec tolerabam impuritatem (sicut Pseudapostoli in sua doctrina) sed doctrina mea ab omni immunditie aliena erat, minime dololum in modum tractata, ut solet ab iis tractari, qui gloriam suam & commodum suum in praedicando captant.
units.tr: Third indication, confirming what was said above: The teaching, exhortation and consolation I gave was not like the teaching of the false apostles. For (1) it was not adulterated and composed to deceive, but sincere and free of all imposture. I did not foster or tolerate impurity, as the false apostles did in their teaching; my teaching was alien to all uncleanness and in no way handled deceitfully, as is usually done by those who seek their own glory and advantage in preaching.

units.la: Verf. 4. Sed sicut placuimus Deo, quibus crederetur Euangelium ita loquimur, non ut hominibus placentes, sed Deo qui approbat corda nostra.
units.tr: Verse 4. But as we were approved by God to be entrusted with the Gospel, so we speak, not as pleasing men, but God, who tests our hearts.

units.la: Indicium 4. Ex conscientia electionis, & vocationis meae ad tam excellens munus, (in quo credita est mihi Euangelii annunciatio,) sanctum Dei verbum, sancta & sincera mente praedicare statui, & non hominibus, sed Deo placere, qui scrutatur corda, & testimonium fert mihi ut servo suo fideli.
units.tr: Fourth indication, drawn from the consciousness of my election and calling to so excellent an office, in which the proclamation of the Gospel has been entrusted to me: I resolved to preach the holy Word of God with a holy and sincere mind, and to please not men but God, who searches the hearts and bears witness to me as his faithful servant.

units.la: Verf. 5. Neque enim unquam sermone assentatorio usi sumus, sicut nostis, nec avaritiae causa quicquam praetexuimus: DEUS testis est.
units.tr: Verse 5. For we never used flattering speech, as you know, nor did we cover up anything for the sake of greed; God is witness.

units.la: Indicium 5. Specialius explicans quod superius est, Assentatoria oratione nunquam apud vos usus sum, cuius rei testes vos ipsos advoco.
units.tr: Fifth indication, explaining more specifically what was said above: I never used flattering speech among you, and I call you yourselves as witnesses of this.

units.la: Nec
units.tr: Nor

units.la: Indicium 6. Nunquam avaritiæ causa quicquam sub specie pie-tatis feci, ut Pseudapostoli solent: cujus rei testem Deum invocat.
units.tr: Sixth indication: I never did anything for the sake of greed under the appearance of piety, as the false apostles do; of this he calls God as witness.

units.la: Verf. 6. Neque ex hominibus quærentes gloriam, nec à vobis, nec ab aliis: quum possemus oneri esse ut Apostoli Christi,
units.tr: Verse 6. Nor did we seek glory from men, neither from you nor from others, though we might have been a burden as the apostles of Christ,

units.la: Indicium 7. Tam longè abfui ab ambitione, simul & avaritia, ut debitum mihi honorem, seu stipendium honorarium, nunquam exegerim sive a vobis, sive ab aliis, cum tamen oneri vobis esse jure potuissem, ut Apostolus Christi.
units.tr: Seventh indication: I was so far from ambition and greed that I never demanded the honour due to me, or an honorary stipend, either from you or from others, although I could rightly have been a burden to you, as an apostle of Christ.

units.la: Verf. 7. Sed fuimus placidi in medio vestri, ut si nutrix foveat suos fœtus,
units.tr: Verse 7. But we were gentle among you, as a nurse cherishes her children.

units.la: Indicium 8. Ego dum inter vos versarer, (vitatâ omni elatione, morositate, & imperio; sepositoque omni respectu, ad Generis mei nobilitatem, ad officii mei, & donorum mihi concessorum excellentiam, omniumque aliorum privilegiorum, quorum ratio in vita civili haberi solet) placidissimè me gessi, ut unum ex vobis, imò ut infimis ex vobis æqualem.
units.tr: Eighth indication: While I lived among you, I avoided all haughtiness, moroseness and domineering, and I set aside every regard for the nobility of my birth, the excellence of my office and the gifts given to me, and all the other privileges that are usually taken into account in civil life. I conducted myself most gently, as one of you, indeed as equal to the lowest among you.

units.la: Verf. 8, Ita cupidi vestri, avebamus impertiri vobis non solum Euangelium Dei, sed etiam nostras ipsorum animas, quod chari nobis essetis.
units.tr: Verse 8. So, being affectionately desirous of you, we were willing to impart to you not only the Gospel of God but also our own souls, because you were dear to us.

units.la: Indicium 9: Sicut mater liberos fovet, suo Spiritu calefacit, lacte suo alit, & (si posset) animam suam illis communicare parata est: Sic ego cupidè arripiens conventuum omnium Ecclesiasticorum occasiones, summa cum animi complacentia, unà cum Euangelio prædicato, Spiritum quasi meum, præ vehementi erga vos amore, vobis impertiri cupiebam.
units.tr: Ninth indication: As a mother cherishes her children, warms them with her own spirit, feeds them with her milk, and is ready, if she could, to impart her own soul to them, so I, eagerly seizing every opportunity of the ecclesiastical gatherings, with great delight of mind, along with the Gospel preached, desired to impart to you my spirit, as it were, out of vehement love for you.

units.la: Verf. 9. Meminisiis enim, fratres, laboris nostri ac ærumnæ: nocte enim ac die operando, ne quem vestrum gravaremus prædicavimus apud vos Euangelium Dei.
units.tr: Verse 9. For you remember, brothers, our labour and toil: working night and day, so as not to burden any of you, we preached to you the Gospel of God.

units.la: Indicium 10. Explicans & confirmans superius, Totum tempus quod restabat mihi à prædicatione Euangelii impendebam in manuarium laborem, ne quisquam ex vobis gravaretur, præbendo mihi victum ut Apostolo.
units.tr: Tenth indication, explaining and confirming what was said above: I spent all the time left to me from preaching the Gospel on manual labour, so that none of you would be burdened, providing my own food as an apostle.

units.la: Verf. 10. Vos testes estis & Deus, quomodo sanctè & justè & inculpatè vobis, qui credidistis, vixerimus. Indicium 11. In omnibus juste, sancte & inculpate me gerebam apud vos: cujus rei testes advoco vos ipsos, quod ad externa attinet, & Deum invoco testem interioris mei sinceri in omnibus affectus.
units.tr: Verse 10. You are witnesses, and God also, how holily and justly and blamelessly we conducted ourselves among you who believed. Eleventh indication: I conducted myself among you justly, holily and blamelessly in all things. Of this I call you yourselves as witnesses, as far as external matters go, and I call God as witness to the sincerity of my inner affections in all things.

units.la: Vers. 11. Sicut nostis quomodo unumquemque vestrum, tanquam pater liberos suos, hortabamur & consolabamur:
units.tr: Verse 11. As you know, how we exhorted and comforted each one of you, as a father does his own children,

units.la: Indicium 12. Sicuti meminisse potestis, singulos vos privatim hortabar, consolabar, non secus ac Pater solet liberos suos hortari & consolari.
units.tr: Twelfth indication: As you can remember, I exhorted and comforted each of you in private, just as a father is accustomed to exhort and comfort his children.

units.la: Vers. 12. Et obtestabamur ut ambularetis sicut dignum est Deo vocante vos ad suum regnum ac gloriam.
units.tr: Verse 12. And we charged you that you should walk worthy of God, who calls you into his own kingdom and glory.

units.la: Indicium 13.
