Nihil reliqui faciebam ad summam fidem & diligentiam, ut vos vitam sanctam degeretis, utque in omnibus placeretis Deo, qui ex gratia vocavit vos ad regni sui & gloriae coelestis participationem: Haec sunt indicia coelestis legationis Pauli, & fideliter administrati ab eo munere Apostolici inter Thessalonicenses.
units.tr: Thirteenth indication: I left nothing undone, with the utmost faith and diligence, to make you lead a holy life and so please God in all things, who by grace called you to share in his kingdom and heavenly glory. These are the indications of Paul's heavenly embassy, and of the apostolic office faithfully administered by him among the Thessalonians.

units.la: Secunda pars Capitis.
units.tr: The second part of the chapter.

units.la: Vers. 13. Propterea etiam nos gratias agimus Deo indesinenter, quod accepistis de Deo sermonem quem audistis: ex nobis, excepistis non ut sermonem hominum, sed (sicut est vere) ut Dei sermonem, qui operatur in vobis qui creditis.
units.tr: Verse 13. For this reason we also give thanks to God without ceasing, because when you received the word of God which you heard from us, you accepted it not as the word of men, but (as it truly is) as the word of God, which also works in you who believe.

units.la: Secunda pars Capitis, in qua continentur manifestae indicia divinae erga Thessalonicenses gratiae in ipsorum conversione; quae postquam cum gratiarum actione protulit, confirmat eos adversus scandalum crucis & persecutionis, quam ab Evangelii hostibus contribulibus suis patiebantur. Indicia gratiae divinae erga Thessalonicenses in ipsorum conversione sunt tria: 1 Est, quod sermonem (inquit) Evangelii a me praedicatum attente audivistis, non ut humanum, sed divinum, eumque vera fide accepistis.
units.tr: The second part of the chapter, in which are set out the clear signs of God's grace toward the Thessalonians in their conversion. After giving thanks for these, Paul strengthens them against the scandal of the cross and the persecution which they suffered from their fellow countrymen, the enemies of the gospel. There are three signs of God's grace toward the Thessalonians in their conversion: (1) that you listened attentively to the message of the gospel preached by me, not as human but as divine, and that you received it with true faith.

units.la: Quietiam] Indicium 2. Quod sermo ille Dei fide receptus in vobis efficaciter etiamnum operetur, testeturque se divinum esse efficacia sua in vobis non minori, quam in aliis credentibus se patefacit.
units.tr: Second sign: that this word of God, received in faith, still works effectively in you, and shows by its power in you that it is divine, no less than it shows itself in the other believers.

units.la: Vers. 14. Vos enim, fratres, imitatores facti estis Ecclesiarum Dei quae sunt in Judea, in Christo Jesu, ut qui eadem passi estis & vos a propriis contribulibus, sicut & ipsi a Judaeis.
units.tr: Verse 14. For you, brothers, became imitators of the churches of God which are in Judea, in Christ Jesus, because you also suffered the same things from your own countrymen, just as they did from the Jews.

units.la: Indicium 3. Confirmans praecedentia, quod constantes hactenus fueritis in perferendis persequutionibus à vestris amicis, cognatis & contribulibus propter Euangelium, similesque vos ostenderitis Ecclesiis Christianis in Judaea, quae constanter persequutiones patiuntur à reliquis Judaeis infidelibus: Ex quorum numero aliqui, etiam vobis sunt infesti.
units.tr: Third sign. Confirming what has gone before: you have so far stood firm in enduring persecutions for the gospel from your friends, relatives and fellow countrymen, and you have shown yourselves like the Christian churches in Judea, which steadily endure persecutions from the other unbelieving Jews, some of whom are hostile to you as well.

units.la: Vers. 15. Qui etiam Dominum Iesum occiderunt, & proprios Prophetas, & nos exegerunt, neque Deo placent, & omnibus hominibus adversantur:
units.tr: Verse 15. who killed the Lord Jesus and their own prophets, and drove us out, and do not please God, and are opposed to all men.

units.la: Ut scandalum tollat persecutionis, qua vexabantur Ecclesiae Christiane ab infidelibus Judaeis, qui se Populum Dei vocabant, detrahit larvam perversis illis Euangelii hostibus, ipsorum pingens peccata acerrima criminatione, cujus leptem sunt membra: 1. Infideles Judaei ipsum CHRISTUM occiderunt: 2. Non pepercerunt propriis suis & popularibus Prophetis: 3. Persequuti sunt nos Apostolos; quod dicit ut consolationem caperent Thessalonicenses ex consortio passionum CHRISTI, & servorum ejus: 4. Adversarii sunt DEI, & tum maxime cum putant se DEO placere, in persecutione servorum ipsius: 5. Ut publici hostes humani generis impediunt, quantùm possunt, communem homiminum salutem.
units.tr: In order to remove the scandal of the persecution by which the Christian churches were harassed by the unbelieving Jews, who called themselves the People of God, he strips away the mask of those perverse enemies of the gospel, painting their sins with a most bitter accusation, whose members are seven: (1) the unbelieving Jews killed CHRIST himself; (2) they spared not their own prophets, who were of their own people; (3) they persecuted us, the apostles, which he says so that the Thessalonians might take comfort from sharing the sufferings of CHRIST and of his servants; (4) they are enemies of GOD, and especially when they think they please GOD, in persecuting his servants; (5) as public enemies of mankind, they hinder, as far as they can, the common salvation of men.

units.la: Vers. 16. Trohibentes nos Gentibus loqui ut serventur, ut semper, compleant peccata sua, occupavit enim eos ira ad extremum usque.
units.tr: Verse 16. forbidding us to speak to the Gentiles that they may be saved, so that they always fill up the measure of their sins; for wrath has come upon them to the uttermost.

units.la: 6. Hostes sunt Gentium, prohibentes pro virili, ne Apostoli Gentibus Euangelium salutis prædicent, ne Gentes serventur, si per eos fieri posset: 7. Ista & alia multa perpetrando, mensuram peccatorum suorum quotidie magis magisque implent, Criminibus recitatis, subnectit judicium, iramque Dei quæ ad extremum usque eos jam occupaverat.
units.tr: (6) They are enemies of the Gentiles, hindering with all their strength the apostles from preaching the gospel of salvation to the Gentiles, so that the Gentiles may not be saved, if that could be done through them. (7) By committing these and many other deeds, they fill up daily more and more the measure of their sins. Having recited these crimes, he adds the judgment, and the wrath of God which had already come upon them to the uttermost.

units.la: Tertia pars Capitis.
units.tr: The third part of the chapter.

units.la: Vers. 17. Nos verò fratres orbati vobis ad tempora, momentum, conspectu, non animo, eo vehementius studuimus videre faciem vestram, cum multo desiderio.
units.tr: Verse 17. But we, brothers, being bereft of you for a short time, in sight but not in heart, were the more eager to see your face with great longing.

units.la: Tertia pars Capitis, in qua ne existimarent negligi se in afflictionibus suis ab Apostolo, quod ad ipsos in tantis miseriis versantes tes non accurrerit, confirmat suum in ipsos benevolum animum, argumentis sex.
units.tr: The third part of the chapter, in which, so that they would not think that he had neglected them in their afflictions, and had not hastened to them while they were in such great miseries, he confirms his well-disposed heart toward them by six arguments.

units.la: Argumentum primum, Absentia mea à vobis non minus mihi molesta fuit, quam solet esse absentia cuivis Patri à liberis suis; imo vero condolebam vobis, ut solet frater orphanus fratribus suis orphanis.
units.tr: First argument: my absence from you was no less painful to me than the absence of any father is usually from his children; indeed I grieved for you as an orphaned brother usually does for his orphaned brothers.

units.la: Absentiam meam spero fore non diuturnam, sed ad momentum horæ tantum.
units.tr: I hope that my absence will not be long, but only for the space of an hour.

units.la: Corde & affectu non aberam à vobis, licet corpore abfuerim. Quo ægrius fero absentiam meam à vobis, eo vehementius studeo coram vos videre.
units.tr: In heart and affection I was not absent from you, although I was absent in body. The more painfully I bear my absence from you, the more eagerly I strive to see you face to face.

units.la: Verf. 18. Ideo voluimus venire ad vos ( ego quidem Paulus) semel atque iterum, sed impedivit nos Satanas.
units.tr: Verse 18. Therefore we wished to come to you (I, Paul, indeed) once and again, but Satan hindered us.

units.la: Arg. 5. In procinctu stabam paratus ad veniendum, semel atque iterum, ut vos in fide confirmarem, sed negotium mihi facessebat Satan & impedimenta objiciebat, ne venirem.
units.tr: Fifth argument: I stood ready, prepared to come, once and again, so as to strengthen you in the faith; but Satan made trouble for me and placed obstacles in the way, so that I could not come.

units.la: Verf. 19. Nam quæ est nostra Spes aut Gaudium, aut Corona de qua glorier? Annon & vos in conspectu Domini nostri Iesu Christi in ejus adventu?
units.tr: Verse 19. For what is our hope, or joy, or crown of which we boast? Are not even you, in the presence of our Lord Jesus Christ at his coming?

units.la: Verf. 20. Itaque vos estis gloria nostra & gaudium.
units.tr: Verse 20. For you are our glory and joy.

units.la: Arg. 6. confirmans superius, Spes mea de vestra perseverantia tanta est; Gaudium de conversione vestri tantum est, Corona gloriationis meæ in Ministerii mei fructibus, & in vobis ea est, ut cum præcipuis Ecclesiis, per meum Ministerium ad fidem conversis, numerandi sitis. Et nisi vos tales habendi essetis, de quibus quæso bene sperarem, gauderem, vel gloriarer? Certè vos eritis inter præcipuos per me conversos, in conspectu Domini nostri, in ejus adventu. Id quod repetita asseveratione vobis confirmo. Idcirco de meo erga vos benevolo affectu persuasissimi estote.
units.tr: Sixth argument, confirming what was said above: my hope concerning your perseverance is so great, my joy at your conversion is so great, and the crown of my boasting lies in the fruits of my ministry, and in you it is such that you are to be counted among the chief churches converted to the faith through my ministry. And unless you were such people that I could hope well of you, would I rejoice or glory? Surely you will be among the chief converts made through me, in the presence of our Lord Jesus, at his coming. This I confirm to you with a repeated assurance. Therefore be fully persuaded of my well-disposed affection toward you.

units.la: Caput Tertium.
units.tr: Chapter 3.

units.la: Ergit hoc Capite suam in eos dilectionem confirmare, eosq; in fide quam eos docuerat stabilire.
units.tr: In this chapter he confirms his love for them and sets them firm in the faith he had taught them.

units.la: QUamobrem hoc desiderium non amplius ferentes, optimum duximus soli Athenis relinqui.
units.tr: Therefore, no longer able to bear this longing, we thought it best to be left alone at Athens.

units.la: Argumenta in hunc finem sunt decem, Quae omnia probant Thessalonicenses Apostolo charissimos esse.
units.tr: There are ten arguments to this end, all of which prove that the Thessalonians were most dear to the Apostle.

units.la: Argumentum primum. Prae desiderio vos confirmandi in fide, malui in multis persecutionum procellis Athenis solus commorari, quam committere, ut vos diutius consolatione & confirmatione destitueremini. Ergo mihi charissimi estis.
units.tr: First argument. Out of longing to strengthen you in the faith, I preferred to remain alone at Athens amid the many storms of persecution, rather than allow you to be deprived for longer of consolation and confirmation. Therefore you are dear to me.

units.la: Versi. 2. Misimusque Timotheum fratrem nostrum, ac ministrum Dei, & adjutorem nostrum in Euangelio Christi, ad vos stabiliendos & exhortandos super fide vestra:
units.tr: Verse 2. And we sent Timothy, our brother and minister of God and our fellow worker in the gospel of Christ, to establish you and exhort you concerning your faith.

units.la: Arg. 2. Misi ad vos Timotheum mihi pernecessarium, qui etiamsi frater intimus, & Minister Dei strenuus, & Coadjutor meus sit, in Euangelio Christi, volui tamen ejus consortio privari, ut vos Consolationem & Confirmationem caperetis in fide. Charissimos mihi igitur vos esse oportet.
units.tr: Argument 2. I sent to you Timothy, who is very necessary to me. Although he is my closest brother, a diligent minister of God and my co-worker in the gospel of Christ, I still chose to be deprived of his company, so that you might receive consolation and confirmation in the faith. You must therefore be dear to me.

units.la: Versi. 3. Ut nemo commovcatur in oppressionibus istis: ipsi enim nostis nos ad id esse constitutos.
units.tr: Verse 3. That no one be moved by these afflictions; for you yourselves know that we are appointed to this.

units.la: Arg. 3. Plus metuebam ne vos offenderemini afflictionibus meis pro Euangelio, quam curabam meam ipsius molestiam: Idcirco jam adversus hoc scandalum confirmari vos volo: 1. Quia didicistis ex Euangelio a Deo constitutum fuisse, ut nos Apostoli ante omnes alios, pro veritate Euangelii adversa multa pateremur.
units.tr: Argument 3. I feared more that you would be offended by my afflictions for the gospel than I cared about my own discomfort. So I wish now to fortify you against this stumbling block: 1. Because you have learned from the gospel that God has appointed that we apostles, before all others, should suffer many adversities for the truth of the gospel.

units.la: Versi. 4. Etenim quum apud vos essemus, praedicebamus vobis fore ut affligeremur: quod & evenit, & nostis.
units.tr: Verse 4. For when we were with you, we foretold that we would be afflicted; and this came to pass, as you know.

units.la: 2. Quia praedixeram vobis afflictiones pro Euangelio me manere, sicut eventus comprobavit.
units.tr: 2. Because I had told you beforehand that afflictions for the gospel awaited me, as the outcome has shown.

units.la: Versi. 5. Quamobrem etiam ego non amplius ferens vestri desiderium misi eum, ut cognoscerem fidem vestram, ne quo modo tentasset vos tentator ille, & inanis redditus esset labor noster.
units.tr: Verse 5. Therefore I too, no longer able to bear your longing, sent him to learn of your faith, lest somehow the tempter had tempted you and our labour had been in vain.

units.la: Arg. dilectionis 4 Metuebam ne Diabolus aliqua suâ arte dimovisset vos à fide, & sic periisset labor meus: quam ob causam misi ad vos Timotheum qui de vestra in fide constantia cognosceret. Ergo.
units.tr: Argument from love, 4. I feared that the Devil had by some art drawn you away from the faith, and so my labour would have perished; for this reason I sent Timothy to you, to learn of your steadfastness in the faith. Therefore.

units.la: Vers 6. Nuper autem quum venijset Timotheus ad nos à vobis, & annunciasset nobis fidem ac charitatem vestram, vosque bonam nostri memoriam retinere, semper cupientes nos videre, sicut nos quoque vos:
units.tr: Verse 6. But recently, when Timothy came to us from you and brought us word of your faith and love, and that you keep a good memory of us, always desiring to see us, as we also do you:

units.la: Arg. 5. Maximo gaudio perfusus sum ex nuncio, quod retulit Timotheus de vestra fide erga Christum, charitate erga Sanctos, & vestrome coram videndi desiderio. Ergo.
units.tr: Argument 5. I was overwhelmed with great joy at the news Timothy brought of your faith toward Christ, your love toward the saints, and your longing to see us. Therefore.

units.la: Vers. 7. Propterea consolationem accepimus, fratres, ex vobis, in omni afflictione & necessitate nostra, per vestram fidem:
units.tr: Verse 7. For this reason, brethren, we have been comforted concerning you in all our affliction and distress, through your faith:

units.la: Arg. 6. Consolatio mihi ministrata ex vestra fide condivit, & superavit omnem meum dolorem, quem capiebam ex afflictionibus & necessitatibus mihi vel incumbentibus, vel imminentibus: Ergo.
units.tr: Argument 6. The consolation supplied to me from your faith sweetened and surpassed all my sorrow, which I felt from the afflictions and distresses that either weighed upon me or threatened me. Therefore.

units.la: Vers. 8. Nunc enim vivimus, si vos perstatis in Domino:
units.tr: Verse 8. For now we live, if you stand fast in the Lord:

units.la: Arg. 7. Qualis felicitas quaedam futura est mihi, si vos constantes in fide permanseritis. Charissimos igitur vos mihi esse necesse est.
units.tr: Argument 7. What a kind of happiness will be mine if you remain steadfast in the faith. It is necessary, therefore, that you be dear to me.

units.la: Vers. 9 Quam enim gratiarum actionem possimus Deo rependere de vobis, super omni gaudio quo gaudemus propter vos coram, DEO nostro,
units.tr: Verse 9. For what thanksgiving can we render to God for you, for all the joy with which we rejoice for your sake before our God,

units.la: Arg. 8. confitemur superius, Sincerè, & coram Deo, gaudendi materia tanta fuit mihi suppeditata ex vestra perseverantia, ut quam gratiarum actionem Deo rependam, nesciam: Ergo.
units.tr: Argument 8. I confess, sincerely and before God, that the matter of rejoicing has been supplied to me in such abundance by your perseverance that I do not know what thanksgiving to render to God. Therefore.

units.la: Vers. 10 Noćte ac die quam vehementissimè precantes, ut videamus vestram faciem, & quae desunt fidei vestrae, compleamus.
units.tr: Verse 10. Night and day praying most earnestly that we may see your face and supply what is lacking in your faith.

units.la: Arg 9. Assiduo Deum oro, ut liceat mihi coram vos videre, & fidei vestrae defectus corrigere, fideique mensuram augere, vobis explicando amplius mysterium Euangelii. Ergo.
units.tr: Argument 9. I constantly pray to God that I may be allowed to see you face to face, and to correct the defects of your faith, to increase the measure of faith by explaining to you more fully the mystery of the gospel. Therefore.

units.la: Vers. 11. Ipse verò Deus, & Pater noster, & Dominus noster Iesus Christus dirigat viam nostram ad vos.
units.tr: Verse 11. Now may our God and Father himself, and our Lord Jesus Christ, direct our way to you.

units.la: Arg. 10. Quam chari mihi sitis, ex orationis meae pro vobis summulta, colligite. Precationis articuli sunt tres: 1. est, Jugiter oro, ut Deus concedat mihi prosperum iter ad vos, quo confirmem vos in Fide.
units.tr: Argument 10. Gather from the very many prayers I offer for you how dear you are to me. The articles of this prayer are three: 1. I constantly pray that God grant me a prosperous journey to you, by which I may strengthen you in the faith.

units.la: Versf. 12. Faxit autem Dominus, ut abundetis & exuberetis mutua inter vos charitate, & in omnes, quemadmodum & nos in vos:
units.tr: Verse 12. And may the Lord make you increase and abound in love toward one another, and toward all, just as we do toward you:

units.la: Articulus 2. Item oro, ut Deus vobis concedat incrementum & abundantiam charitatis mutuae, & erga omnes, quemadmodum mea charitas abundat erga vos.
units.tr: Article 2. Likewise I pray that God grant you the increase and abundance of mutual love, both toward one another and toward all, just as my love abounds toward you.

units.la: Verf. 13. Ut corda vestra inculpata stabiliat in sanctimonia coram Deo & Patre nostro, in adventum Domini nostri Iesu Christi, cum omnibus sanctis ejus.
units.tr: Verse 13. So that he may establish your hearts blameless in holiness before God our Father, at the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ with all his saints.

units.la: Articulus 3. Denique oro, ut Deus stabilia reddat corda vestra, & conscientias vestras efficiat inculpatas in vera sanctitate, quae coram Deo & Patre nostro requiritur, ut tandem in adventu Domini nostri, una cum omnibus sanctis ipsius, (id est, Angelis & hominibus,) absque pudore consistere possitis: Nulli igitur dubitate quin mihi fitis charissimi.
units.tr: Article 3. Finally, I pray that God make your hearts firm and render your consciences blameless in true holiness, which is required before God our Father, so that at last, at the coming of our Lord, together with all his saints (that is, angels and men), you may be able to stand without shame. Therefore do not doubt that you are most dear to me.

units.la: Caput Quartum.
units.tr: Chapter 4.

units.la: Precatione ad Deum in fine superioris Capitis, transit ad secundam partem Epistolae, quae continet hortationes, & praecepta ad sanctimoniae officia, inspersa obiter doctrina de resurrectione, & ultimo Judicio.
units.tr: Having ended the prayer to God at the close of the previous chapter, he passes to the second part of the Epistle, which contains exhortations and precepts concerning the duties of holiness, with teaching on the resurrection and the last Judgment interspersed along the way.

units.la: Partes Capitis sunt duae, Prior est hortatoria, ad verf. 13. Altera consolatoria, ad finem.
units.tr: The chapter has two parts. The first is hortatory, to verse 13; the second is consolatory, to the end.

units.la: Verf. 1.
units.tr: Verse 1.

units.la: QUod superest igitur, fratres, rogamus vos, & precamur per Dominum Iesum, ut sicut accepistis a nobis quomodo oporteat vos incedere, & placere Deo, magis excellatis.
units.tr: Finally then, brethren, we beseech and entreat you through the Lord Jesus, that as you received from us how you ought to walk and please God, so you may excel more and more.

units.la: Prima pars Capitis, continens hortationes septem: Hortatio prima, est generalis, Ut eorum quae ex Apostolo audiverunt sint memores, & ut indies magis magisque proficiant in studio sancte vivendi, & Deo placendi, ut quotidie se ipsos quasi superent: Rationes hortaticnis, tationis, addit quatuor: 1. Ego Apostolus in nomine DOMINI id amicè à vobis flagito. Oporteat vos ] Ratio 2. Justificatis hoc necessarium est: nam oportet vos sic ambulare.
units.tr: The first part of the chapter contains seven exhortations. The first exhortation is general: that they should remember what they have heard from the Apostle, and that they should advance day by day more and more in the pursuit of holy living and of pleasing God, so that they daily surpass themselves. He adds four reasons for this exhortation: (1) I, the Apostle, in the name of the LORD, ask this of you in a friendly way. That you ought: Reason 2. For you who are justified this is necessary, for you ought to walk in this way.

units.la: Verf. 2. Nostis enim quæ mandata dederimus vobis per Dominum Iesum.
units.tr: Verse 2. For you know what commandments we gave you through the Lord Jesus.

units.la: Ratio 3. Jam accepistis in hanc rem à DOMINO mandata, & accepta novistis.
units.tr: Reason 3. You have already received commandments from the LORD on this matter, and you know what you have received.

units.la: Verf. 3. Nam hæc est voluntas Dei, nempe sanctificatio vestra, id est, ut abstineatis à scortatione:
units.tr: Verse 3. For this is the will of God, namely your sanctification, that is, that you abstain from fornication:

units.la: Ratio 4. Hæc est DEI voluntas, ut sanctificemini animo pariter & corpore, cui voluntati qui studet obedire, DEO placebit.
units.tr: Reason 4. This is God's will, that you be sanctified in both soul and body; he who strives to obey this will pleases God.

units.la: Abstineatis ] Hortato 2. est specialis, Cujus tria sunt membra: 1. Ut abstineant ab omni scortatione seu fœda libidine.
units.tr: That you abstain: The second exhortation is particular, and it has three parts. (1) That they abstain from all fornication and foul lust.

units.la: Verf. 4. Et sciat vestrum unusquisque suum vas possidere cum sanctificatione & honore:
units.tr: Verse 4. And let each one of you know how to possess his own vessel in sanctification and honour:

units.la: Membrum 2. Ut unusquisque edoctus à Deo, corpus suum ut vas Domino consecratum constanter conservet in castitate & honore, ad usus à Deo sanctificatos, nec se ipsos polluant.
units.tr: Part 2. That each one, taught by God, should constantly keep his body, as a vessel consecrated to the Lord, in chastity and honour, for the uses sanctified by God, and not defile themselves.

units.la: Verf. 5. Non cum morbo cupiditatis, sicut Gentes quæ non noverunt DEUM:
units.tr: Verse 5. Not in the disease of lust, like the Gentiles who do not know God:

units.la: Membrum 3. Ut extinguere studeant internæ concupiscentiæ febriculosos ardores & flammas; cujus hortationis ratio redditur, ne sint similes Gentibus quæ DEUM non noverunt, & ut per honestatem seu puritatem discernantur ab iis.
units.tr: Part 3. That they should strive to quench the feverish heats and flames of inward concupiscence. The reason given for this exhortation is that they should not be like the Gentiles who do not know God, and that by their honesty or purity they should be distinguished from them.

units.la: Verf. 6. Ne quis opprimat aut circumveniat in negotio fratrem suum: nam ultor est Dominus omnium istorum, sicut & ante diximus vobis, ac testificati sumus.
units.tr: Verse 6. That no one oppress or defraud his brother in business: for the Lord is an avenger of all these things, as we also told you before and solemnly testified.

units.la: Hortatio 3. De cavenda avaritia; ne fraude, vi, vel malis artibus ex aliorum damnis commoda sua comparent, opprimendo vel decipiendo fratres suos. Nam vindex ] Rationes addit quatuor: 1. Deus ulciscetur ejusmodi injurias: 2. Sicut prius monui, sic etiam rursum moneo vos, & obtestor per DEUM, ut caveatis.
units.tr: The third exhortation concerns avoiding avarice: that no one should gain his advantage from the losses of others by fraud, force or wicked arts, oppressing or deceiving his brothers. For the avenger: he adds four reasons: (1) God will avenge such wrongs; (2) as I warned you before, so again I warn you and adjure you before God that you beware.

units.la: Verf. 7. Non enim vocavit nos Deus ad impuritatem, sed ad sanctificationem.
units.tr: Verse 7. For God has not called us to uncleanness, but to sanctification.

units.la: Ratio 3. A fine vocationis nostræ ad gratiam Christi, qui non est ut polluamus nos ullo genere peccati, sed ut sanctificemur in omni genere virtutis.
units.tr: Reason 3. From the end of our calling to the grace of Christ, which is not that we should defile ourselves with any kind of sin, but that we should be sanctified in every kind of virtue.

units.la: Vers. 8. Proinde qui hæc rejicit, non rejicit hominem, sed Deum, qui etiam dedit nobis Spiritum suum sanctum.
units.tr: Verse 8. Therefore he who rejects these things does not reject man, but God, who also gave us his Holy Spirit.

units.la: Ratio 4. Quia qui non obedit huic hortationi reus peragetur rejectæ autoritatis divinæ: Qui etiam] Ratio 5. Quia nobis veris Christianis dedit Deus Spiritum Sanctum, quo discernamus quid à Deo sit, quid ipsi abominationi sit, & quæ immineant judicia peccatoribus.
units.tr: Reason 4. Because whoever does not obey this exhortation will be guilty of rejecting divine authority. Who also: Reason 5. Because God has given the Holy Spirit to us, true Christians, by whom we may discern what is from God, what is an abomination to himself, and what judgments are impending over sinners.

units.la: Vers. 9. Cæterum, de fraterna charitate non necesse habetis ut scribam vobis: ipsi namque divinitus docti estis, ut diligatis alii alios.
units.tr: Verse 9. But concerning brotherly love, you have no need that I write to you; for you yourselves are taught of God to love one another.

units.la: Hortatio 4. Ad fraternam charitatem & beneficentiam erga omnes in futuro exercendam: Rationes sunt tres: 1. Quia jam propendetis adeo ad fraternam charitatem, ut non necesse sit multùm urgere hoc officium.
units.tr: The fourth exhortation: to practise brotherly love and beneficence towards all in the future. There are three reasons: (1) because you already incline so strongly to brotherly love that there is no need to press this duty much.

units.la: Ratio 2. Edocti jam estis, ut diligatis alii alios.
units.tr: Reason 2. You have already been taught to love one another.

units.la: Vers. 10. Nam & facitis hoc erga cunctos fratres qui sunt in tota Macedonia: obsecramus autem vos, fratres, ut magis excellatis.
units.tr: Verse 10. For indeed you do this toward all the brethren who are in all Macedonia. But we beseech you, brethren, that you excel more and more.

units.la: Ratio 3. confirmans priorem, Facto jam ostendistis hanc beneficentiam erga cunctos fratres vicinos: Pergite ergo, & excellite in hoc officio.
units.tr: Reason 3, confirming the former: by your deed you have already shown this beneficence towards all the neighbouring brethren. Go on, then, and excel in this duty.

units.la: Vers. 11. Et contendatis quieti esse, & res vestras agere, ac operari propriis manibus vestris, sicut vobis denuntiavimus:
units.tr: Verse 11. And that you study to be quiet, and to attend to your own affairs, and to work with your own hands, as we commanded you;

units.la: Vers. 12. Ut vos geratis honestè erga extraneos, & nulla re vobis sit opus.
units.tr: Verse 12. That you may walk honestly towards outsiders, and have need of nothing.

units.la: Sequuntur aliæ hortationes tres breviter copulatæ his duobus versibus.
units.tr: Three further exhortations follow, briefly joined together in these two verses.

units.la: Hortatio 5. Ne sitis πολυπραγμονες ingerentes vos aliorum negotiis, sed quietè & placidè vos gerite.
units.tr: The fifth exhortation: do not be busybodies [πολυπραγμονες], meddling in the affairs of others, but conduct yourselves quietly and peaceably.

units.la: Operari] Hortatio 6. Ne sitis otiosi ventres, sed res vestras privatas curate, & negotia vestra agite, & manibus vestris operamini sicut prius præcepi.
units.tr: To work: The sixth exhortation: do not be idle bellies, but attend to your private concerns and carry on your own business, and work with your hands as I commanded before.

units.la: Ut vos] Hortatio 7. Decenter vos gerite erga eos, & coram iis qui non sunt in Ecclesia; & in his omnibus officiis, inter vos quasi de honore certate; in hunc specialem finem præter alios, ne opus habeatis vel à domesticis fidei, vel ab extraneis quicquam mendicare.
units.tr: That you: The seventh exhortation: conduct yourselves becomingly towards those who are outside the Church, and in all these duties strive together among yourselves, as it were, for honour; for this special purpose, besides others, that you may have no need to beg anything either from the household of faith or from strangers.

units.la: Secunda pars Capitis.
units.tr: The second part of the chapter.

units.la: Verf. 13. Nolim autem vos in ignorantia versari, fratres, quod ad eos attinet qui obdormierunt, ut ne deleatis, sicut & caeteri qui spem non habent.
units.tr: Verse 13. I would not have you be ignorant, brothers, concerning those who have fallen asleep, that you may not grieve, as the others also do who have no hope.

units.la: Secunda pars Capitis, consolationem continens adversus immodicum luctum de obitu amicorum, quem dissuadet duobus argumentis.
units.tr: The second part contains consolation against excessive mourning for the death of friends, which the author dissuades with two arguments.

units.la: Argumentum primum, Luctus immoderatus pertinet ad Ethnicos & infideles, qui ipsem resurrectionis nullam habent. Non igitur vos decet luctus immodicus.
units.tr: The first argument: excessive mourning belongs to the heathen and unbelievers, who have no hope of the resurrection itself. Therefore excessive mourning does not befit you.

units.la: Verf. 14. Nam si credimus IESVM mortuum esse, & resurrexisse, ita etiam & DEVS eos qui obdormierint in IESU, adducet cum eo.
units.tr: Verse 14. For if we believe that Jesus died and rose again, so also God will bring with him those who have fallen asleep in Jesus.

units.la: Arg. 2. Quam certò credimus CHRISTUM resurrexisse à mortuis, tam certò etiam scire poterimus fideles in CHRISTO mortuos, resurrecturos, & vivos sistendos esse in CHRISTI comitatu, in die judicii: Cavendus ergo luctus immodicus.
units.tr: The second argument: just as we surely believe that Christ rose from the dead, so too we may surely know that believers who have died in Christ will rise again and be presented alive in the company of Christ on the day of judgment. Excessive mourning is therefore to be avoided.

units.la: Verf. 15. Hoc enim vobis dicimus verbo Domini, fore ut nos vivi qui vel qui erimus in adventu Domini, non praeveniamus eos qui obdormierint.
units.tr: Verse 15. For this we tell you by the word of the Lord, that we who are alive and remain until the coming of the Lord shall not precede those who have fallen asleep.

units.la: Ut haec consolatio firma sit, ex revelatione Domini praedicit adventus CHRISTI, & resurrectionis modum, qui his sex articulis continetur.
units.tr: So that this consolation may be firm, the Lord's revelation foretells the coming of Christ and the manner of the resurrection, which is contained in these six articles.

units.la: Articulus primus, Fideles quicunque vivi erunt in adventu DOMINI, non antevertent resurrectionem defunctorum in CHRISTO.
units.tr: The first article: all believers who are alive at the coming of the Lord will not go before the resurrection of the dead in Christ.

units.la: Verf. 16. Nam ipse Dominus cum hortatione clamore, & voce Archangeli ac Dei tuba, descendet è Coelo: & qui mortui fuerint in Christo, resurgent primum.
units.tr: Verse 16. For the Lord himself will descend from heaven with a shout, with the voice of the archangel and the trumpet of God; and the dead in Christ will rise first.

units.la: Articulus 2. CHRISTUS descendet de coelo, cum omnibus Angelis.
units.tr: The second article: Christ will descend from heaven with all the angels.

units.la: Cum voce Articulus 3. Modus veniendi erit cum Imperii & Majestatis multa significatione, nam ut summus JUDEX mandabit pro imperio, ut unumquodque elementum reddat mortuos suos, unde omnes mortui congregabuntur ad ipsius Tribunal. Promulgabitur autem mandatum per praecipuum aliquem Angelum, Clanget Tuba, seu vox vicem Tubae supplens, sonuisque audietur ubicunque terrarum. Mortui resuscitandi erunt. Et qui] Articulus 4. Mortui in Christo resurgent priùs quam mutatio fiat viventium.
units.tr: With the voice The third article: the manner of his coming will be with great signs of power and majesty. For as the supreme Judge he will command, by his authority, that each element give back its dead, whence all the dead will be gathered before his tribunal. The command will be published through a certain chief angel; a trumpet will sound, or a voice taking the place of a trumpet, and the sound will be heard wherever on earth. The dead are to be raised. And those who] The fourth article: the dead in Christ will rise before the living are changed.

units.la: Verf. 17. Deinde vos vivi, qui reliqui erimus, rapiemur simul cum eis in nubes, in occursum Domini, in aëra, & ita semper cum Domino erimus.
units.tr: Verse 17. Then we who are alive and remain will be caught up together with them in the clouds, to meet the Lord in the air; and so we shall always be with the Lord.

units.la: Articulus 5. Fideles viventes in adventu Domini, repente momento, in oculi ictu, à mortalitate ad immortalitatem mutati, unà cum resuscitatis Sanctis rapientur sursum in occursum Domini in aëra.
units.tr: The fifth article: believers living at the coming of the Lord, in a moment, in the twinkling of an eye, changed from mortality to immortality, will be caught up together with the raised saints on high, to meet the Lord in the air.

units.la: Et ita] Articulus 6. Post judicium migrabunt Sancti cum Domino in Cœlum, & cum Eo manebunt in æternum. De reprobis nihil dicit, quia ad hos Consolatio non pertinet; nec de his, ubi moriuntur, consolatio ulla capi potest.
units.tr: And so] The sixth article: after the judgment the saints will go with the Lord into heaven and will remain with him forever. He says nothing about the reprobate, because consolation does not pertain to them; nor can any consolation be drawn from the fate of those who die in that condition.

units.la: Verf. 18. Itaque consolamini alii alios iisdem sermonibus.
units.tr: Verse 18. Therefore comfort one another with these words.

units.la: Prophetiam applicat in usum Thessalonicensium, ut ex resurrectione, unusquisque Fidelis doloris sui solatium quaereret, & aliis Fidelibus etiam ministraret.
units.tr: He applies the prophecy to the use of the Thessalonians, so that from the resurrection each believer might seek relief for his own grief, and also bring it to other believers.

units.la: Caput Quintum.
units.tr: Chapter 5.

units.la: N eodem Argumento pergit: Capitis partes tres sunt, In prima continuat doctrinam de adventu Christi, ad judicium universale, ad verf. 6. In secunda affert varias Hortationes, ad omnis generis virtutes Christianas, ad versum 13. In tertia continetur Epilogus tertius Epistolæ.
units.tr: He pursues the same subject. The chapter has three parts. In the first he continues the teaching about the coming of Christ to the universal judgment, up to verse 6. In the second he gives various exhortations to every kind of Christian virtue, up to verse 13. In the third is the third epilogue of the Epistle.

units.la: Verf. 1. Porrò de temporibus & opportunitatibus, fratres, non est opus ut vobis scribam.
units.tr: Verse 1. But concerning the times and seasons, brethren, I have no need to write to you.

units.la: De adventu Domini adduntur quatuor alii Articuli: 1. Tempus & hora adventus Domini non revelatur, sed in secretis Dei latet, neque expedit de illo curiosè quicquam scisscitari vel scribere.
units.tr: Four further articles are added concerning the Lord's coming: (1) The time and hour of the Lord's coming is not revealed, but lies hidden in the secret counsels of God. Nor is it expedient to inquire or write about it with undue curiosity.

units.la: Verf. 2. Ipsi enim penitus scitis diem illum Domini ut furem in nocte, ita venturum esse.
units.tr: Verse 2. For yourselves know perfectly that the day of the Lord so cometh as a thief in the night.

units.la: Articulus 2. Continens rationem prioris, Non minus ex improviso venturus est <bl>Christus</bl>, quam fur nocturnus in alienas aedes inopinato irrepere solet.
units.tr: Article 2, containing the reason for the first: Christ will come no less unexpectedly than a thief in the night, who is wont to creep unawares into another man's house.

units.la: Vers. 3. Quum enim dicent, Pax & tuta omnia, tunc repentinum eis imminet exitium, sicuti dolor partus mulieri uterum ferenti: nec effugient.
units.tr: Verse 3. For when they shall say, Peace and safety, then sudden destruction cometh upon them, as travail upon a woman with child; and they shall not escape.

units.la: Articulus 3. Explicans priorem, eumque ad impaenitentes applicans. Sicut ex improviso certo & necessario dolores partus occupant praegnantes, sic etiam dies irae DOMINI inexpectatus de improviso impaenitentes securos in peccatis occupabit.
units.tr: Article 3, explaining the previous one and applying it to the unrepentant. Just as the pains of labour seize pregnant women suddenly and inevitably, so also the day of the wrath of the Lord will come unexpectedly and suddenly upon the unrepentant who are secure in their sins.

units.la: Vers. 4. At vos, fratres, non estis in tenebris, ut dies ille vos tanquam fur deprehendat.
units.tr: Verse 4. But ye, brethren, are not in darkness, that that day should overtake you as a thief.

units.la: Articulus 4 In quo explicat hanc doctrinam porro, & ad consolationem fidelium applicat: Vos Fideles, non necesse habetis diem illum formidare, nam quia vos non jacetis in tenebris peccati, & ignorantiae, dies novissimus non potest vos (ut fur nocturnus) deprehendere.
units.tr: Article 4, in which he further explains this doctrine and applies it to the comfort of the faithful: you believers do not need to dread that day. For since you do not lie in the darkness of sin and ignorance, the last day cannot overtake you as a thief in the night does.

units.la: Vers. 5. Omnes vos filii lucis estis, ac filii diei: non sumus noctis, neque tenebrarum.
units.tr: Verse 5. Ye are all the children of light, and the children of the day: we are not of the night, nor of darkness.

units.la: Rationem reddit, Quia omnes quotquot in <bl>Christum</bl> vere credunt, Filii lucis, & diei sunt, versantes in luce Fidei & Pietatis: Et ideo non potest ullus ex nobis ignorantiae vel peccati mancipium esse.
units.tr: He gives the reason: all who truly believe in Christ are children of light and of day, living in the light of faith and godliness. Therefore none of us can be a slave of ignorance or sin.

units.la: Secunda pars Capitis.
units.tr: The second part of the chapter.

units.la: Vers. 6. Nempe igitur ne dormiamus ut reliqui, sed vigilemus & sobrii simus.
units.tr: Verse 6. Therefore let us not sleep, as do others; but let us watch and be sober.

units.la: Secunda pars Capitis, continens tredecim hortationes, ad officia Christiana: 1. Hortatio ex doctrina judicii extremi illata, ad vigilantiam & sobrietatem, ut diem illum sine formidine expectemus: Ne secure (inquit) dormiamus, aut peccatis indulgeamus sicut infideles, sed contra studentes moderationi in omnibus terrenis, sanctis operibus incumbamus.
units.tr: The second part of the chapter contains thirteen exhortations to Christian duties. (1) The first exhortation, drawn from the doctrine of the final judgment, urges watchfulness and sobriety, so that we may await that day without fear. Let us not sleep securely, he says, nor indulge in sins like unbelievers, but on the contrary, striving for moderation in all earthly things, let us devote ourselves to holy works.

units.la: Vers. 7. Nam qui dormiunt, nocte dormiunt: & qui inebriantur, nocte sunt ebrii.
units.tr: Verse 7. For they that sleep sleep in the night; and they that be drunken are drunken in the night.

units.la: Rationes hortationis sunt sex: 1. Quia qui secure dormiunt, & quicunque crapulæ & ebrietati corporeæ se dedunt, noctu & in tenebris id agere solent, quod vos non decet.
units.tr: There are six reasons for the exhortation: (1) Those who sleep securely, and all who give themselves over to drunkenness and bodily excess, are wont to do by night and in darkness what does not befit you.

units.la: Vers. 8. At nos qui sumus diei, sobrii simus, induti thorace fidei & pro galea, spe salutis.
units.tr: Verse 8. But let us, who are of the day, be sober, putting on the breastplate of faith and charity; and for an helmet, the hope of salvation.

units.la: Ratio 2. Quia Christiani qui filii sunt diei, & luce fidei versantur, sobrietati & corporis, & mentis studere tenentur.
units.tr: Reason 2: Christians, who are children of the day and live in the light of faith, are bound to devote themselves to sobriety, both of body and of mind.

units.la: Induti ] Ratio 3. confirmans priorem, Quia Christiani ut in militia versari debent, armati spirituali armatura, induti fide & charitate, tanquam Thorace: & spe Salutis tanquam galea, Fidei addit Charitatem, ut fidem pro thorace agnoscamus eam solam, quæ per charitatem est efficax.
units.tr: Putting on: Reason 3, confirming the previous one. Christians ought to live as soldiers, armed with the spiritual armour, clothed with faith and love as with a breastplate, and with the hope of salvation as with a helmet. He adds love to faith, so that we recognise that faith alone which is effective through love as the breastplate.

units.la: Vers. 9. Nam non constituit nos Deus ad iram, sed ad salutem obtinendam, per Dominum nostrum Iesum Christum,
units.tr: Verse 9. For God hath not appointed us to wrath, but to obtain salvation by our Lord Jesus Christ,

units.la: Ratio 4. Deus non prædestinavit nos ad iram: Ergo ne indulgeamus cupiditatibus, & vitiosis desideriis, propter quæ ira Dei venit super filios inobedientiæ.
units.tr: Reason 4: God has not predestined us to wrath. Therefore let us not indulge our lusts and vicious desires, on account of which the wrath of God comes upon the children of disobedience.

units.la: Per Dominum ] Ratio 5. Deus elegit & prædestinavit nos ad salutem per Iesum Christum. Ergo ad salutem contendamus in viis Domini.
units.tr: By our Lord: Reason 5: God has chosen and predestined us to salvation through Jesus Christ. Therefore let us strive for salvation in the ways of the Lord.

units.la: Vers. 10. Qui mortuus est pro nobis: ut sive vigelemus, sive dormiamus, simul cum eo vivamus.
units.tr: Verse 10. Who died for us, that, whether we wake or sleep, we should live together with him.

units.la: Ratio 6. Quia Christus in eum finem mortuus est pro nobis, ut non cum Diabolo & mundo in peccatis, sed cum ipso in viis sanctitatis ambulemus & vivamus, sive vigilantes, sive dormientes, id est, dies noctesque transigentes in ejus obedientia, & morientes in communione vitæ ipsius vivificæ. Ergo non indormiendum peccatis, sed invigilandum operibus Sanctis.
units.tr: Reason 6: Christ died for us to this end, that we should walk and live not with the devil and the world in sin, but with him in the ways of holiness, whether waking or sleeping. That is, spending our days and nights in his obedience and dying in communion with his life-giving life. Therefore we should not slumber in sins, but be watchful in holy works.

units.la: Vers. 11. Quapropter adhortamini alii alios, & ædificate singuli singulos, sicut & facitis
units.tr: Verse 11. Wherefore comfort yourselves together, and edify one another, even as also ye do.

units.la: Hortatio 2. ex prioribus illata, Ut se mutuo hortentur, consolentur & ædificent in fide & pietate: Laudata interim præsenti ipsorum diligentia in hujus præcepti obedientia.
units.tr: Exhortation 2, drawn from the foregoing: that they should encourage, comfort and build up one another in faith and godliness. He praises their present diligence in obeying this precept.

units.la: Vers. 12 Rogamus autem vos, fratres, ut agnoscatis eos qui laborant inter vos, & præsunt vobis in Domino, & admonent vos:
units.tr: Verse 12. And we beseech you, brethren, to know them which labour among you, and are over you in the Lord, and admonish you;

units.la: Hortatio 3. ad populum spectans, Ut observent Pastores & Presbyteros, & totum consessum seniorum docentium & gubernantium, nempe, & eos qui laborabant inter ipsos in verbo & doctrina, & eos qui præerant in Domino, gubernantes in rebus Ecclesiasticis, & ex officio admonebant ubi opus erat: de his præcipit ut Sancti, sicut non ingratos decebat, corde, verbis, factis, Presbyteros omnes agnoscant, pro Ministris Christi ad salutem ipsorum constitutos.
units.tr: Exhortation 3, addressed to the people: that they should honour the pastors and elders, and the whole body of elders who teach and govern, namely both those who laboured among them in the word and doctrine, and those who presided over them in the Lord, governing in ecclesiastical affairs and admonishing them as their office required. On these he enjoins that the saints, as is fitting for those who are not ungrateful, should acknowledge all the elders in heart, word and deed, as ministers of Christ appointed for their salvation.

units.la: Rationes hortationis sunt tres. Ratio prima, Quia ego Apostolus amanter & studiosè id rogo.
units.tr: There are three reasons for the exhortation. The first reason: I, an apostle, ask and beg this lovingly and earnestly.

units.la: Ratio 2. Quia digni sunt Ministri hoc honore, utpote qui laborant in vobis ædificandis, & præsunt vobis, seu vos gubernant in CHRISTI nomine in omnibus rebus Ecclesiasticis, & quæ ad DEI cultum spectant, vosque de officiis vestris admonent cum authoritate, privatim & publicè.
units.tr: Reason 2: The ministers are worthy of this honour, since they labour in building you up, and preside over you, that is, they govern you in the name of Christ in all ecclesiastical matters and in whatever pertains to the worship of God, and they admonish you of your duties with authority, both in private and in public.

units.la: Vers. 13. Et quàm maximè charos ducatis, propter opus ipsorum, & pacem celite inter vos mutuò.
units.tr: Verse 13. And to esteem them very highly in love for their work's sake. And be at peace among yourselves.

units.la: Ratio 3. Quia opus DEI de salvandis fidelibus, cui fideles Ministri incumbunt, exigit ut singularem in modum diligantur à Populo, & in pretio habeantur.
units.tr: Reason 3: Because the work of God, the saving of the faithful, to which faithful ministers devote themselves, requires that they be loved by the people in a special way and held in high esteem.

units.la: Hortatio 4. ad populum potissimum, Ut pacem colant & inter se, & cum Pastoribus, à quibus solet Diabolus alienare animos Populi, etiam cum Pastores optimè de eo merentur.
units.tr: Exhortation 4, addressed chiefly to the people: that they cultivate peace both among themselves and with the pastors, since the devil is accustomed to alienate the minds of the people from them, even though the pastors deserve the best from them.

units.la: Vers. 14. Precamur autem vos, fratres, monete inordinatos, consolamini eos qui pusillo animo sunt, sublevate infirmos, patientes esse erga omnes.
units.tr: Verse 14. Now we exhort you, brethren, warn them that are unruly, comfort the feebleminded, support the weak, be patient toward all men.

units.la: Hortatio 5. ad Presbyteros, (quos superiori versu à Populo distinxit, & hic ex officiis, quæ speciali ratione ad gubernationem Ecclesiæ ex muneris ipsorum authoritate spectant, describit,) ut diligenter exequantur munus suum, dilolutè viventes de officio suo admonendo, pusillanimes consolando, infirmos charitate sua sublevando. Denique mansuetum animum erga omnes ostendendo: Ne si secus fecerint authoritate abutentes, opus Domini quod intendunt, impediant.
units.tr: Exhortation 5, addressed to the elders (whom he distinguished from the people in the previous verse, and here describes by the duties which, by virtue of their office and authority, belong in a special way to the government of the Church). He urges them to carry out their office diligently: admonishing those who live disorderly about their duty, comforting the fainthearted, and supporting the weak with their charity. Finally, they should show a gentle spirit toward all, lest, if they act otherwise and abuse their authority, they hinder the work of the Lord which they intend to advance.

units.la: Vers. 15. Videte ne quis malum pro malo cuipiam reddat; sed beneficentiam semper sectamini, tum inter vos mutuò, tum erga omnes.
units.tr: Verse 15. See that none render evil for evil unto any man; but ever follow that which is good, both among yourselves, and to all men.

units.la: Hortatio 6. Promiscuè erga omnes, ut à privata vindicta abstinentes, prosequantur beneficentiam cum inter se mutuò, tum erga quosvis etiam extraneos.
units.tr: Exhortation 6, addressed to all in general: that, refraining from private revenge, they should pursue kindness both toward one another and toward everyone, even strangers.

units.la: Verf. 16. Semper gaudete.
units.tr: Verse 16. Rejoice evermore.

units.la: Hortatio 7. Ut fide radicati in gratuita Dei erga se dilectione studeant in Christo, & ejus justitia imputata ad vitam æternam, in rebus prosperis & adversis, lætari, & animi tranquillitatem fovere.
units.tr: Exhortation 7: that, rooted in faith in God's free love toward them, they should strive in Christ, and in his righteousness imputed to them for eternal life, to rejoice in prosperous and adverse circumstances alike, and to cherish tranquillity of mind.

units.la: Verf. 17. Indesinenter orate.
units.tr: Vers. 17. Pray without ceasing.

units.la: Hortatio 8. Ut in omni conditione prospera & adversa, & in omni negotio se ad Deum convertant, precantes prout res poltularet.
units.tr: Exhortation 8. That in every condition, prosperous and adverse, and in every business, they turn to God, praying as the matter requires.

units.la: Verf. 18. In omnibus gratias agite: hæc enim est voluntas Dei per Christum Iesum erga vos.
units.tr: Vers. 18. In everything give thanks: for this is the will of God in Christ Jesus concerning you.

units.la: Hortatio 9. Ut cum sciant diligentibus Deum, omnia cedere, in bonum in omni conditione, etiam maxime adversa expiscentur materiam gratias agendi Deo.
units.tr: Exhortation 9. That, since they know that all things work together for good for those who love God, in every condition, even the most adverse, they seek out material for giving thanks to God.

units.la: Hæc enim ] Hortationis ratio est, Quia Deus hoc officium ab omnibus exigit, & potissimum à Christianis, in quos gratiam suam & dilectionem effudit in Christo.
units.tr: For this is] The reason for the exhortation is that God requires this duty from all, and especially from Christians, on whom he has poured out his grace and love in Christ.

units.la: Verf. 19. Spiritum ne extinguite:
units.tr: Vers. 19. Quench not the Spirit.

units.la: Hortatio 10. Ne dona Spiritus Sancti qualiacunque, sive negligentia, sive male agendo suffocent: Sed ut contra assiduo labore, precibus, aliisque mediis omnibus à Deo sanctificatis, ea suscitent & indies augeant.
units.tr: Exhortation 10. That they do not suffocate the gifts of the Holy Spirit, of whatever kind, either by negligence or by misconduct; but rather that, by constant labour, prayers and all the other means sanctified by God, they revive them and increase them daily.

units.la: Verf. 20. Prophetias ne pro nihilo habete:
units.tr: Vers. 20. Despise not prophesyings.

units.la: Hortatio 11. Ne exercitationes sacras publicas, in quibus Ministri Ecclesiarum Scripturam interpretantur, contemnant vel negligant.
units.tr: Exhortation 11. That they do not despise or neglect the public sacred exercises in which the ministers of the churches expound Scripture.

units.la: Verf. 21. Omnia explorate: quod bonum fuerit retinete:
units.tr: Vers. 21. Prove all things; hold fast that which is good.

units.la: Hortatio 12. Ne temere quicquam in negotio religionis amplectantur, sed ad regulam verbi divini, seu analogiam fidei examinent singula, & quod sanum, bonum, & Deo acceptum comperitur, constanter teneant, & strenuè defendant.
units.tr: Exhortation 12. That they do not rashly embrace anything in the matter of religion, but examine each thing by the rule of the divine Word, or the analogy of faith, and that they hold constantly to what is found sound, good and acceptable to God, and defend it vigorously.

units.la: Verf. 22. Ab omni specie mali abstinete.
units.tr: Vers. 22. Abstain from all appearance of evil.

units.la: Hortatio 13. Ut non tantum quod malum est, in cultu Dei vel moribus caveant, sed etiam quæcunque speciem mali habent: cujusmodi sunt phrases periculosæ in doctrina, & indifferentia in praxi, quæ propter mali speciem offendiculum aliis præbere possent.
units.tr: Exhortation 13. That they guard not only against what is evil in the worship of God or in conduct, but also against whatever has the appearance of evil: such as dangerous phrases in doctrine, and indifference in practice, which could give offence to others on account of their appearance of evil.

units.la: Tertia pars Capitis,
units.tr: Third part of the chapter

units.la: Ipse autem Deus pacis author sanctificet vos totos, ut integer vester Spiritus, & anima & corpus inculpatè in adventum Domini nostri Iesu Christi servetur.
units.tr: And the very God of peace sanctify you wholly; and I pray God that your whole spirit, soul and body may be preserved blameless unto the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ.

units.la: Tertia pars Capitis, Continens epilogum, cujus articuli sunt sex. In primo precatur Deum pacis, seu fontem sanctitatis & felicitatis, ut eos sanctificet magis magisque: 1. Quoad Spiritum seu mentem à Spiritu Dei jam collustratam, quae animae rationalis suprema facultas est: 2. Quoad animam seu voluntatem & affectus; &, 3. quoad corpus, seu externas actiones, ita ut in adventu Domini, quando perficienda est sanctitas fidelium, nihil in illis reperiatur nisi inculpatum & laudabile.
units.tr: The third part of the chapter, containing the epilogue, has six articles. In the first, he prays to God, the fountain of holiness and happiness, the God of peace, that he sanctify them more and more: (1) as regards the spirit, or mind, already illumined by the Spirit of God, which is the highest faculty of the rational soul; (2) as regards the soul, that is, the will and affections; and (3) as regards the body, that is, external actions, so that at the coming of the Lord, when the holiness of the faithful is to be perfected, nothing may be found in them but what is blameless and praiseworthy.

units.la: Verf. 24. Fidelis est qui vocavit vos, qui etiam id efficiet.
units.tr: Vers. 24. Faithful is he that calleth you, who also will do it.

units.la: Articulus 2. In quo de praecedentis precationis exauditione apud Deum, certos eos reddit, 1. Ex Dei praecedenti vocatione efficaci: 2. Ex Dei fidelitate, qua praestat id in suis, ad quod ipsos vocat, & inchoatum bonum opus non deserit.
units.tr: Article 2. In which he makes them certain that the preceding prayer will be heard by God, from (1) God's previous effectual calling, and (2) God's faithfulness, by which he brings about in his people that to which he calls them, and does not abandon the good work he has begun.

units.la: Verf. 25. Fratres orate pro nobis.
units.tr: Vers. 25. Brethren, pray for us.

units.la: Articulus
units.tr: Article

units.la: 3. In quo Apostolus non dedignatur votorum & precationum subsidium, a minimis inter fideles rogare.
units.tr: 3. In which the Apostle does not disdain to seek the aid of vows and prayers even from the least of the faithful.

units.la: Verf. 26. Salutate fratres omnes cum osculo sancto.
units.tr: Vers. 26. Greet all the brethren with an holy kiss.

units.la: Articulus 4. In quo jubet salutari nomine suo omnes fratres per hanc Epistolam, non minus amanter quam si coram ipsos ordinario salutationis signo (id est, osculo minime simulato, ab affectu Christiano profluente) eos salutasset.
units.tr: Article 4. In which he bids all the brethren be greeted in his name through this Epistle, no less lovingly than if he had greeted them in person with the ordinary sign of greeting (that is, a kiss by no means feigned, flowing from Christian affection).

units.la: Verf. 27. Adjuro vos per Dominum, ut recitetur haec Epistola omnibus sanctis fratribus.
units.tr: Vers. 27. I charge you by the Lord that this epistle be read unto all the holy brethren.

units.la: Articulis 5. In quo Dei nomine mandat, & adjurat, ut Ministri seu Ecclesiae gubernatores (ad quos proximè hanc Epistolam misisse apparet) hanc Scripturae partem in ulum communem Ecclesiae proferrent & legendam publicè curarent, minatus divinam vindictam, nisi eam toti Ecclesiae publicarent.
units.tr: Article 5. In which, in God's name, he commands and adjures that the ministers or governors of the churches (to whom this Epistle was evidently sent directly) bring this part of Scripture into the common use of the Church and see to it that it is read publicly, threatening divine vengeance unless they make it known to the whole Church.

units.la: Verf. 28. Gratia Domini nostri Iesu Christi sit vobiscum. Amen.
units.tr: Vers. 28. The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you. Amen.

units.la: Articulus 6. Et ultimus in quo totam Epistolam concludit, optando illis gratiam Christi, quae omnia bona in se continet, Amen.
units.tr: Article 6. And the last, in which he concludes the whole Epistle, wishing them the grace of Christ, which contains all good things within itself. Amen.

units.la: EXPOSITIO
units.tr: EXPOSITION

units.la: EXPOSITIO ANALYTICA EPISTOLAE SECUNDAE, AD THESSALONICENSES.
units.tr: EXPOSITIO ANALYTICA EPISTOLAE SECUNDAE, AD THESSALONICENSES.

units.la: Summarium.
units.tr: Summarium.

units.la: OCCASIO scribendi hanc Epistolam fuisse videtur, quod doctrina de adventu Christi inopinato, aliqui ex Thessalonicensibus abusi sint ad negligentiam in suis vocationibus, & ad rei suae familiaris profusionem, quasi non fuisset opus rem familiarem amplius curare, cum Christus venturus esset forsan cras, forsan perendie, ut putabant, alii vero simplicitate & errore nonnullorum abutebantur, & de aliorum bonis vivere satagentes, operari desinebant. Fervebat interim persecutio hostium, & concurrebat ad errorem hunc fovendum. Quare Apostolus scripta ad eos hac secunda Epistola, solvit nodum, & primo consolatur ipsos adversus persecutiones seu afflictiones, Capite Primo.
units.tr: The occasion for writing this Epistle seems to have been that some of the Thessalonians had abused the teaching about Christ's unexpected coming. They neglected their callings and squandered their property, as if there were no need to attend to their household affairs any longer, since Christ was to come perhaps tomorrow, perhaps the day after, as they supposed. Others, through the simplicity and error of some, took advantage of this and, eager to live at the expense of others' goods, ceased to work. Meanwhile the persecution by enemies was raging and contributed to fostering this error. Therefore the Apostle, by writing this second Epistle, untied the knot: first he comforts them against persecutions or afflictions, in the First Chapter.

units.la: Secundo explicat doctrinam de Christi adventu, non prius futuro quam Antichristiana defectio a vera fide CHRISTI fieret, & patefieret mundo, Capite secundo.
units.tr: Secondly, he explains the teaching about Christ's coming, which will not take place before the Antichristian defection from the true faith of CHRIST has happened and been revealed to the world, in the second chapter.

units.la: Denique hortatur ad Christiana officia, & nominatim ad diligentiam in unius cujusque vocatione, Capite tertio.
units.tr: Finally, he exhorts them to Christian duties, and in particular to diligence in each one's calling, in the third chapter.

units.la: Caput Primum.
units.tr: Chapter One.

units.la: Verf. 1. PAulus & Sylvanus & Timotheus Ecclesiae Thessalonicensium, quae est in Deo Patre, & Domino IESU CHRISTO:
units.tr: Verse 1. Paul, and Silvanus, and Timothy, to the Church of the Thessalonians, which is in God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ:

units.la: Verf. 2. Gratia fit vobis & pax à Deo Patre nostro, & Domino IESU CHRISTO.
units.tr: Verse 2. Grace be to you, and peace, from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.

units.la: In Epistolæ directione iidem salutant Thessalonicenses qui in superiore: De autoritate Apostoli nihil hic, nec in priori Epistola dicitur, quia satis erant omnes in hac Ecclesia de Pauli Apostolatu confirmati, tantùm communionis ipsorum cum uno vero Deo & Filio ipsius Iesu Christo mentionem faciendo, discriminat hanc Ecclesiam & ab Ethnicorum & infidelium Judæorum cœtibus: & optando illis gratiam & pacem, certos reddit de omnibus, quæ ad salutem æternam & justitiam faciunt, à Deo per Christum in ipsos, derivandis.
units.tr: In the address of the Epistle, the same persons greet the Thessalonians as in the earlier one. Nothing is said here about the Apostle's authority, nor in the former Epistle, because everyone in this Church was already sufficiently assured of Paul's apostleship. By mentioning only their fellowship with the one true God and with his Son Jesus Christ, he distinguishes this Church both from the assemblies of the Gentiles and from those of the unbelieving Jews. And by wishing them grace and peace, he assures them that everything that leads to eternal salvation and righteousness will be conveyed to them from God through Christ.

units.la: Vers. 3. Gratias agere debemus Deo semper, de vobis, fratres, ut dignum est, quòd vehementer augescat fides vestra, & abundet mutua uniuscujusque omnium vestrûm charitas:
units.tr: Verse 3. We ought always to give thanks to God for you, brethren, as is fitting, because your faith grows exceedingly and the love each of you has for one another abounds:

units.la: Reliquo Capite gratias Deo agendo de ipsis, simul confirmat eorum fidem, & consolationem iis ministrat adversus omnem persecutorum rabiem qua vexabantur: Argumenta consolationis & confirmationis fidei sunt octo: Quæ omnia probant debere eos in fide corroborari, & consolationem capere sub persecutionibus suis.
units.tr: In the rest of the chapter, by giving thanks to God for them, he at the same time confirms their faith and offers them comfort against all the rage of the persecutors by which they were being harassed. There are eight arguments for comfort and for the confirmation of faith. All of them show that they ought to be strengthened in faith and to take comfort under their persecutions.

units.la: Argumentum primum, Felicissima est me judice vestræ Ecclesiæ conditio in conspectu Dei, in qua omnes (nemine excepto quantum sciri potest) Dominum Iesum sincerâ fide, & alii alios sincerâ charitate amplectimini, & in utraque virtute promovetis, & magis magisque de die in diem abundatis. Ergoquæcunque sit conditio vestra in conspectu mundi, consolationem capere debetis, & in fide corroborari.
units.tr: First argument: in my judgement, the condition of your Church is most happy in the sight of God. In it all of you (no one excepted, so far as can be known) embrace the Lord Jesus with sincere faith, and one another with sincere love, and you advance in both virtues and abound more and more from day to day. Therefore, whatever your condition may be in the sight of the world, you ought to take comfort and be strengthened in faith.

units.la: Vers. 4. Adeò ut nosipsi de vobis gloriemur apud Ecclesias Dei, id est, de tolerantia vestra & fide in omnibus persequutionibus vestris & oppressionibus quas toleratis.
units.tr: Verse 4. So that we ourselves glory in you among the Churches of God, that is, in your endurance and faith in all your persecutions and afflictions which you bear.

units.la: Arg. 2. Vestra fidei constantia & patientia in mediis persecutionibus & afflictionibus quas sustinetis, tanta est, ut cogar vos coram aliis Ecclesiis laudare, & in exemplum aliis proponere: Ergo consolationem capere & in fide corroborari debetis.
units.tr: Argument 2. The constancy and patience of your faith in the midst of the persecutions and afflictions you endure is so great that I am compelled to commend you before the other Churches and to set you forth as an example to them. Therefore you ought to take comfort and be strengthened in faith.

units.la: Vers. 5. Quæ res manifesto est indicio justi judicii Dei: ut digni censeamini regno Dei, pro quo etiam ípsa patimini:
units.tr: Verse 5. This is a clear sign of the righteous judgement of God, that you may be counted worthy of the kingdom of God, for which you also suffer:

units.la: Arg. 3. Vestræ afflictiones quas suffertis ab impiis persecutoribus, manifesto sunt indicio fore tandem universale judicium: in quo malis malè erit, & bonis bene, quando vos idonei pronunciandi estis, qui dignatione divinâ regno Dei potiamini, quippe qui pro Dei regno promovendo tot tantaque mala passi estis.
units.tr: Argument 3. Your afflictions, which you suffer at the hands of ungodly persecutors, are a clear sign that a universal judgement will come at last, in which it will go ill with the wicked and well with the good. You are fit to be declared worthy, since you, by the grace of God, are to obtain the kingdom of God, having suffered so many and such great evils in promoting the kingdom of God.

units.la: Vers. 6. Siquidem justum est apud Deum, vicissim reddere iis qui affligunt vos, afflictionem:
units.tr: Verse 6. For it is just with God to repay affliction to those who afflict you,

units.la: Vers. 7. Vobis verò qui affligimini, relaxationem nobiscum quum patefiet Dominus Iesus de Cælo, cum angelis potentia sua.
units.tr: Verse 7. and to give relief to you who are afflicted, together with us, when the Lord Jesus is revealed from heaven with the angels of his power,

units.la: Vers. 8. Cum flammeo incendio, infligens ultionem iis qui Deum non noverunt, neque auscultant Euangelio Domini nostri Iesu Christi:
units.tr: Verse 8. in flaming fire, inflicting vengeance on those who do not know God and who do not obey the Gospel of our Lord Jesus Christ;

units.la: Vers. 9. Qui pœnam pendent æterni exitii, damnati à præsente Domino, & potente ipsius gloria:
units.tr: Verse 9. who shall pay the penalty of eternal destruction, condemned by the present Lord and the glory of his power:

units.la: Arg. 4. Explicans prius: Deus pro suâ justitia persecutores vestros puniturus est in die judicii, & vos liberaturus ab omni malo: Ergo consolationem capere, & in fide confirmari debetis.
units.tr: Argument 4. Explaining the earlier point: God, for his righteousness, will punish your persecutors on the day of judgement, and will deliver you from every evil. Therefore you ought to take comfort and be confirmed in faith.

units.la: Nobiscum ] Arg. 5. Unà nobiscum & cum reliquis Martyribus Christi tanquam commilitonibus vestris, relaxationem ab omni malo & miseria tandem estis consequuturi: Ergo & unà nobiscum consolationem capere debetis, & in fide corroborari.
units.tr: Together with us: Argument 5. Together with us, and with the other martyrs of Christ, as your fellow soldiers, you will at last obtain relief from every evil and misery. Therefore you too, together with us, ought to take comfort and be strengthened in faith.

units.la: In revelatione ] Arg. 6. Ab iis circumstantiis judicii extremi quæ terribilem reddunt vindictam in impios sumendam: Dominus Iesus 1. manifestabitur, & de Cœlo visibiliter veniet Judex & ultor injuriarum: 2. Comitatum secum adducet potentissimorum Angelorum, qui sententiam Judicis exequentur, vers. 7. 3. Ignem flammantem accendet, quo totus hic mundus conflagrabit: 4. Ulciscetur eos omnes qui cognitione salutari (quæ cum fide & obedientia conjuncta est) destituti comperientur, & qui non obtemperaverunt Euangelio vers. 8.
units.tr: In the revelation: Argument 6. From the circumstances of the last judgement, which make the vengeance to be taken on the ungodly terrible: (1) the Lord Jesus will be made manifest, and will come visibly from heaven as Judge and avenger of wrongs; (2) he will bring with him a retinue of the most mighty angels, who will carry out the Judge's sentence (verse 7); (3) he will kindle a flaming fire by which this whole world will be consumed; (4) he will take vengeance on all those who are found lacking the saving knowledge (which is joined with faith and obedience), and who have not obeyed the Gospel (verse 8).

units.la: Quinto, tum luent impii supplicium æterni exitii: 6. Infligetur hoc supplicium ab irato Judice, qui à facie sua eos rejiciet in æternum.
units.tr: Fifthly, the ungodly will then pay the penalty of eternal destruction. (6) This punishment will be inflicted by an angry Judge, who will cast them away from his face forever.

units.la: A facie ] 7. Dominus quam gloriosum robur suum sit, ostendet omnibus, in iis potenter puniendis: Ergo consolationem capere, & confirmari in fide debetis.
units.tr: From his face: (7) The Lord will show to all how glorious his strength is in punishing these people powerfully. Therefore you ought to take comfort and be confirmed in faith.

units.la: Vers. 10. Quum venerit ut glorificetur in sanctis suis, & admirandus fiat in fidelibus omnibus, (quòd fides habita sit testimonio nostro apud vos) in die illo. Arg. 7. Consolationis, ab iis circumstantiis judicii extremi, quae gloriosam & laetam reddent liberationem piorum: nam, 1. Eodem die quo Christus perditurus est adversarios, liberaturus est fideles suos, & vos speciatim: 2. Gloriam suam cum Sanctis suis communicabit, & in eorum glorificatione gloriam suam manifestabit: 3. Superabit gloria illa omnem nostram spem, & apprehensionem; nam admirandus erit Christus, in gloriae communicatae amplitudine: 4. In omnibus credentibus gloriam suam ostendet, ita ut nullus futurus sit fidelis, in quo Christus non sit admirabilis futurus, obiter rationem consolationis illis applicatae reddit, quia Thessalonicenses crediderant testimonio Apostoli praedicantis Euangelium, ideo confidenter audet praedictam consolationem illis applicare, quam reipsa comperturi erant, in illo die: Ergo &c.
units.tr: Verse 10. When he comes to be glorified in his saints, and to be admired in all believers (because our testimony to you was believed), on that day. Argument 7: a comfort drawn from the circumstances of the last judgement, which will make the deliverance of the godly glorious and joyful. For (1) on the same day on which Christ will destroy his adversaries, he will deliver his faithful, and you in particular; (2) he will share his glory with his saints, and will display his glory in their glorification; (3) that glory will surpass all our hope and understanding, for Christ will be admirable in the greatness of the glory bestowed on them; (4) he will show his glory in all who believe, so that there will be no believer in whom Christ will not be admirable. In passing, he gives the reason for the comfort applied to them: because the Thessalonians had believed the testimony of the Apostle preaching the Gospel, he confidently dares to apply to them the aforesaid comfort, which they would in fact find on that day. Therefore, etc.

units.la: Vers. 11.
units.tr: Verse 11.

units.la: Cujus etiam rei gratia precamur semper pro vobis, ut vos dignetur ista vocatione Deus noster, & compleat omnem suae bonitatis gratuitam benevolentiam, & opus fidei potenter:
units.tr: For this reason also we always pray for you, that our God would make you worthy of this calling, and fulfil every good pleasure of his goodness and the work of faith with power:

units.la: Arg. 8. Consolationis & confirmationis ipsorum in fide. Habetis nos assiduo comprecantes, ut ad metam feliciter perveniatis: Ergo consolationem capere in afflictionibus & in fide corroborari debetis: Precationis articuli sunt quatuor: Articulus primus; Precor, ut Deus qui ex foedere gratuito noster est, ex sua dignatione idoneos vos reddat ad vocationem, seu gloriam ad quam vocati estis, possidendam: Hic articulus Dei gratiae, seu dignationi ascribit, cum gloriam ipsam ad quam vocamur, tum omnem, quae ad eam ducit, praeparationem.
units.tr: Argument 8, for the comfort and confirmation of their faith. You have us praying for you constantly that you may arrive happily at the goal. Therefore you ought to take comfort in your afflictions and be strengthened in faith. The petition has four parts. The first part: I pray that God, who is our God by a gracious covenant, would by his own kindness make you fit for the calling, or for possessing the glory to which you have been called. This part ascribes to God's grace, or to his kindness, both the glory itself to which we are called and every preparation that leads to it.

units.la: Et compleat ] Articulus 2. Precor ut Deus omne beneplacitum bonitatis suae, seu omnimodam suam benignitatem, pro gratuita benevolentia sua in vobis compleat: in quo articulo non salutem tantum, sed omnia media ad salutem fundari ostendit in Dei beneplacito, nihil nisi Dei gratiam agnoscens in toto salutis cursu, & in omnibus ejus partibus.
units.tr: And fulfil] The second part. I pray that God would fulfil in you every good pleasure of his goodness, that is, all his kindness, in return for his free benevolence towards you. In this part the Apostle shows that not only salvation but all the means to salvation are founded in God's good pleasure, acknowledging nothing but God's grace in the whole course of salvation and in all its parts.

units.la: Et opus fidei ] Articulus 3. Oro ut Deus compleat opus fidei in vobis potenter, In quo articulo fidem asserit Dei opus esse, quod ille operatur in suis, & fidei initium, incrementa, & complementum partem beneplaciti statuit: Denique fidem ostendit non tantum non esse opus nostrarum virium, sed superare quicquid in nobis esse potest, & potentiam Dei requirere, absque qua neque inchoari, neque consistere posset, nedum augeri vel compleri. Vers. 12. Verf. 12. Ut glorificetur nomen Domini nostri IESU CHRISTI in vobis, & vos in eo, ex gratia DEI nostri, & Domini Iesu Christi.
units.tr: And the work of faith] The third part. I pray that God would powerfully complete the work of faith in you. In this part he affirms that faith is God's work, which he performs in his own people, and he establishes that the beginning, growth and completion of faith are a part of his good pleasure. Finally, he shows that faith is not only not the work of our own powers, but surpasses whatever can be in us, and requires the power of God, without which it could neither begin nor continue, much less grow or be completed. Verse 12. Verf. 12. That the name of our Lord Jesus Christ may be glorified in you, and you in him, according to the grace of our God and Lord Jesus Christ.

units.la: Articulus 4. Precor ut & in hac vita, & in futura, CHRISTUS in vobis, ut in suis membris glorificetur, & vos glorificemini in Illo, tanquam in veltro Capite, qui finis est superiorum articulorum: Neque in hoc articulo gratiam DEI reticeri vult, sed totam gloriam quam accipit CHRISTUS à suis, vel quam suis communicat, soli gratiae DEI & CHRISTI, ascribendam docet: In quibus omnibus Thessalonicenses non exigua consolationis lux, & in fide confirmationis firmamenta habebant.
units.tr: The fourth part. I pray that both in this life and in the life to come Christ may be glorified in you, as in his members, and that you may be glorified in him, as in your Head, which is the end of the earlier parts. In this part too he does not wish God's grace to be passed over in silence, but teaches that all the glory which Christ receives from his people, or which he communicates to them, is to be ascribed to the grace of God and of Christ alone. In all these things the Thessalonians had no small light of comfort, and firm supports for their faith.

units.la: Caput Secundum.
units.tr: Chapter Two.

units.la: Equitur solutio dubii de Christi subito adventu. Capitis duae sunt partes, in prima refutat errorem de futuro adventu Christi, dum viverent Thessalonicenses illi, ad verf. 13. In altera confirmat Thessalonicensium fidem.
units.tr: There follows the resolution of the doubt about the sudden coming of Christ. The chapter has two parts: in the first he refutes the error about the future coming of Christ, as if it would happen while those Thessalonians were still alive, to verse 13; in the second he confirms the faith of the Thessalonians.

units.la: Verf. 1. ROgamus autem vos, fratres, per adventum Domini nostri Iesu Christi, & nostri in Eum aggregationem:
units.tr: Verse 1. We ask you, brothers, by the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ and our gathering together to him:

units.la: Irrepserat error inter Thessalonicenses, de adventu CHRISTI statim dum ipsi viverent, futuro, quem errorem fovebat Diabolus, ut ob alias causas, sic etiam ob hanc, ut saltem post illam aetatem, doctrinam Christianam totam simul cum hoc articulo ludibrio exponeret, idcirco hortatur Apostolus, ne patiantur se à sano sensu, & fide hujus articuli dimoveri.
