Interim affirmat duas res certissimas esse, de quibus nolebat ipsos dubitare: prima erat, venturum quidem CHRISTUM, sicut ante docuerat, statuto suo tempore: Altera erat, fore ut omnes fideles in occursum Domini congregarentur, à quatuor plagis mundi: verum obtestatur ipsos, si consultum sibi vellent in illo die, ut caverent ab isto errore, de quo dicebamus. Verf. 2. Ne citò à mente dimoveamini, neque turbemini, neque per Spiritum, neque per sermonem, neque per Epistolam tanquam per nos scriptam, quasi instet dies ille Christi.
units.tr: An error had crept in among the Thessalonians, that the coming of Christ, which was yet future, would take place immediately while they themselves were still alive. The Devil fostered this error, so that, for other reasons as well as this one, he might at least after that generation expose the whole Christian doctrine, together with this article, to mockery. Therefore the Apostle urges them not to allow themselves to be moved from the sound sense and faith of this article. Meanwhile he affirms that there are two things most certain, about which he did not want them to doubt. The first was that Christ would indeed come, as he had taught before, at his appointed time. The second was that all the faithful would be gathered together to meet the Lord from the four quarters of the world. But he earnestly entreats them, if they wish to consult their own good on that day, to beware of that error of which we have been speaking. Verse 2. That you be not quickly shaken from your mind, nor troubled, neither by the Spirit, nor by word, nor by letter as if from us, as though the day of Christ were at hand.

units.la: Quia impostores jactabant partim revelationes à Spiritu, partim sermonem aliquem Apostoli; quem se audivisse affirmabant, partim constare dicebant per Epistolam priorem ad Thessalonicenses ab Apostolo conscriptam, quasi capite 4. & 5. docuisset venturum Christum ipsis viventibus, jubet Apostolus cavere, ne hac vel aliqua simili impostura deciperentur, turbarentur, vel ullo modo à fide dimoverentur.
units.tr: Because impostors boasted partly of revelations by the Spirit, partly of some saying of the Apostle which they claimed to have heard, and partly said that it was confirmed by the earlier letter written by the Apostle to the Thessalonians, as if in chapters 4 and 5 he had taught that Christ would come while they were still alive, the Apostle bids them beware lest they be deceived by this or any similar imposture, be troubled, or in any way be moved from the faith.

units.la: Verf. 3. Nequis vos seducat ullo modo: non enim adveniet dies Christi quin venerit defectio prius, & retectus fuerit homo ille sceleratus, filius inquam ille perditionis,
units.tr: Verse 3. Let no one deceive you in any way; for the day of Christ will not come unless the falling away comes first, and that wicked man is revealed, the son of perdition,

units.la: Rationem reddit dehortationis, quia Christus non erat venturus, priusquam Antichristiana defectio fieret, & revelaretur Antichristus, praecipuus hujus defectionis dux & patronus. Praecedere ergo oportet duo antequam Christus adveniat, defectionem à recepta fide, (de qua, 1 Tim. 4. 1.) & revelationem Antichristi illius praecipui, seu magni: Quod ad defectionem attinet, non intelligit defectionem unius aut paucorum, aut multorum in multis Ecclesiis: Siquidem de die in diem illis temporibus transfugae erant non pauci à castris Christi, per omnes fere Ecclesias; & errorum plurimorum sectatores plurimi; sed defectionem intelligit universalem externae seu visibilis Ecclesiae, adeò ut falsa Euangelioque contraria dogmata ab iis qui Christiano nomine gloriaturi erant, reciperentur, & defenderentur palam, & communiter in visibili Ecclesia Christiana.
units.tr: He gives the reason for his warning: Christ was not going to come before the Antichristian apostasy happened and Antichrist, the chief leader and patron of this apostasy, was revealed. Two things must therefore come before Christ comes: a falling away from the faith received (of which see 1 Tim. 4. 1), and the revelation of that Antichrist who is chief, or great. As for the apostasy, he does not mean the defection of one or a few or many in many churches; for in those times there were not a few deserters from Christ's camp, almost in all the churches, and very many followers of very many errors. He means rather a universal defection of the external or visible Church, so that doctrines false and contrary to the Gospel are received and openly and commonly defended in the visible Christian Church by those who were going to boast of the Christian name.

units.la: Quod ad eum attinet qui futurus erat caput hujus apostasiae, praedicit fore ut reveletur à Deo, partim permittendo ut regnum suum in Ecclesia erigeret, seque Antichristum apertè, seu reipsa ostenderet; partim per Euangelii doctrinam, (quae ipsius impostauras perspicuas, apertasque redderet iis omnibus, qui decipi nollent) Antichristum conspicuum reddendo. De quo Antichristo, seu Capite Apostatarum, ut melius posset ab oculatis discerni tempore suo, proponit Apostolus articulos accuratè observandos, septem.
units.tr: As for the one who was going to be the head of this apostasy, he foretells that he would be revealed by God, partly by God's permitting him to set up his kingdom in the Church and to show himself openly as Antichrist in fact, and partly by the doctrine of the Gospel, which would make his impostures clear and evident to all who did not wish to be deceived, thereby making Antichrist conspicuous. Concerning this Antichrist, or Head of the Apostates, so that in his own time he might be more easily discerned by those who see clearly, the Apostle sets out seven articles to be carefully observed.

units.la: Articulus primus, Continet descriptionem & notas Antichristi novem, quae omnes & singulae nulli melius, imo nulli alii quam Pontifici Romano quadrant, ut apparebit observantibus.
units.tr: The first article contains a description and nine marks of Antichrist, all and each of which fit no one better, indeed no one else, than the Roman Pontiff, as will appear to those who observe them.

units.la: Homo ] Nota 1. Erit homo, contra eos qui in gratiam Papæ, caccodæmonem fingunt Antichristum istum futurum dicitur: idcirco ἀνθρώπῳ natura & specie, & ὁ ἀνθρωπος ille homo in singulari numero, ut insignem & præcipuum, & magnum Antichristum, in specie sic dictum, describi ostendat, non tamen insinuet individuum aliquem hominem, seu personam singularem, sed seriem succedentium in una sede nebulonum, sicut Heb. 9. 7. 25. ὁ Ἀρχιερεὺς totam Pontificum seriem sive successionem denotat, & ὁ ἀνθρωπος τε Θεῖ, 1 Tim. 3. 17. non unum Pastorem, sed Mi nistrorum fidorum seriem significat: idque secundum Prophetarum stylum, cum de serie regum loquuntur, ut Dan. 7. 2.
units.tr: Man] Mark 1. He will be a man. He is said to be a man in opposition to those who, to flatter the Pope, imagine that this future Antichrist will be a cacodaemon. Therefore the Apostle describes him as ἀνθρώπῳ [anthrōpō] in nature and kind, and ὁ ἄνθρωπος [ho anthrōpos], that man, in the singular, to show that he is described as a notable, principal and great Antichrist, so named in kind. Yet this does not suggest some individual man or a single person, but a succession of scoundrels following one another in one seat. Just as ὁ Ἀρχιερεὺς [ho archiereus] in Heb. 9. 7, 25 denotes the whole series or succession of high priests, and ὁ ἄνθρωπος τοῦ Θεοῦ [ho anthrōpos tou Theou] in 1 Tim. 3. 17 signifies not one minister but a series of faithful ministers. This is in accordance with the style of the Prophets, when they speak of a series of kings, as in Dan. 7. 2.

units.la: Peccati ] Nota 2. erit Homo peccati, tum quia peccator insigniter, imo maximè addictus peccato: tum quia alius autor insignis ad peccandum, qua fraude & imposturis, qua vi & tyrannica compulsione, futurus erat.
units.tr: Of sin] Mark 2. He will be the man of sin, both because he is a notably, indeed most of all, a sinner given over to sin, and because he is a notable author of sin, who would bring others to sin, whether by fraud and imposture, or by force and tyrannical compulsion.

units.la: Filius ille] Nota 3. Erit filius perditionis, seu successor Judæ proditoris: Nam hoc titulo Christus Judam in Testamento suo insignivit olim, Joh.17.12. quem Judam Antichristus partim Apostolicæ vocationis titulo assumpto, partim dissimulatione, avaritiâ, sævitiâ, pertinaciâ, & finali perditione repræsentat, multis afferens perniciem, & sibi maximam, ἀπωλειαν, & ἀπολλυμενος, alios perdens, & ipse perditus.
units.tr: That son] Mark 3. He will be the son of perdition, that is, the successor of Judas the traitor. For Christ once marked Judas with this title in his testimony, John 17. 12. Antichrist represents this Judas partly by assuming the title of apostolic calling, and partly by dissimulation, avarice, cruelty, obstinacy and final perdition, bringing great ruin on many and on himself ἀπωλειαν [apōleian], and being ἀπολλυμενος [apollymenos], destroying others and himself being destroyed.

units.la: Verf. 4. Sese opponens & efferens adversus quicquid dicitur Deus, aut numen: adeò ut in templo Dei tanquam Deus sedeat, præ se ferens se esse Deum.
units.tr: Verse 4. Opposing and exalting himself against everything that is called God, or divinity, so that he sits in the temple of God as God, showing himself to be God.

units.la: Nota 4. erit ἀντικείμενος adversarius, qui reipsa & factis se opponet Deo, ipsiusque ordinationibus, quicquid aperte præ se fert, adversarium reipsa se præbebit & probabit, qui etiam in fundamentalibus se opponet Christi Euangelio, quales indigitat aliquos ejus præcursores Apostolus, 1 Cor. 16. 9. Erit enim ipsi Christo adversarius, quoad mores, officia, & beneficia Christi, qualem jam vidimus Pontificem Romanum, qui plus, & in pluribus, & crudelius, & subtilius, & diutius se Christo oppositi, quam quisquam unquam.
units.tr: Note 4. The word ἀντικείμενος [antikeimenos] will mean an adversary, one who by his deeds and actions sets himself against God and his ordinances. Whatever he openly professes, he will show and prove himself an adversary in fact. He will also oppose the fundamentals of Christ's Gospel. The Apostle points to some of his forerunners in 1 Cor. 16. 9. He will be an adversary of Christ himself in his conduct, his offices and his benefits. We have already seen such a man in the Roman Pontiff, who has opposed Christ more, in more matters, more cruelly, more subtly and for longer than anyone ever has.

units.la: Efferens ] Nota 5. erit ὑπερηφανος, suâ superbiâ elatus supra omnem qui vocatur Deus, seu omne cui veneratio exhibetur, id est, supra Om s Magistratus, Principes, Reges, & Imperatores, qui in Scriptura Dii vocantur, vel coluntur tanquam σεβαστοι Augusti, ut Act. 25. 21. 25. & Psal. 82. 1 In templo vel templum] Nota 6. erit in templo Dei, seu in visibili Ecclesia externa Christiana, quae profitebitur quidem Christi fidem, & le templum Dei venditabit.
units.tr: Lifted up [Efferens]: Note 5. The word will be ὑπερηφανος [hyperēphanos], lifted up by his own pride above everything that is called God, or everything that receives worship, that is, above all magistrates, princes, kings and emperors, who are called gods in Scripture or are honoured as σεβαστοι [sebastoi], Augusti, as in Acts 25. 21. 25 and Psalm 82. 1. In the temple [In templo] or the temple [templum]: Note 6. This will mean in the temple of God, or in the visible external Christian Church, which will indeed profess faith in Christ and will boast that it is the temple of God.

units.la: Sedeat] Nota 7. Sedebit in societate illa, quae se Templum Dei profitebitur, id est, munus publicum Ecclesiasticum, sedem seu cathedram Episcopalem tenebit.
units.tr: Sit [Sedeat]: Note 7. He will sit in that society which professes itself the temple of God, that is, he will hold the public ecclesiastical office, the episcopal seat or chair.

units.la: Nota 8. Καθίσαι εις ναον, praeficiet se templo, sedebit superincumbens Ecclesiae, summam sibi sedem, praefecturam, Episcopatum, Pontificatum in Ecclesia Christiana arrogans. Ere se ferens]
units.tr: Note 8. Καθίσαι εις ναον [Kathisai eis naon], he will set himself over the temple. He will sit, towering over the Church, arrogating to himself the highest seat, command and episcopate, the pontificate in the Christian Church. Lifting himself up [Efferens se ferens].

units.la: Nota 9. Ostentabit seipsum, ac si Deus esset, hoc est, non satis habens se extulisse supra rem publicam, & supra Ecclesiam Dei, tanquam ejus Princeps & summus Gubernator, conabitur etiam se gerere ut Deum: partim falso jactando se habere omnem Christi potestatem sibi communicatam, se esse per delegationem Christi Vicarium, hoc est, se esse Vice-Christum, seu Ἀντίχριστον, secundum significationem praepositionis ἀντί, in vocibus ἀντιθεος, Deo similis, Deo aequalis, & ἀντιβασιλεύς Prorex: partim assumendo titulos qui proprii Deo sunt, quales sunt Princeps Pastorum, Pontifex noster, Caput Ecclesiae, &c., qui tituli soli Christo debentur. Denique privilegia sibi arrogando in Coelo, Terra, & Inferno, quae soli Deo competunt, qualia jam in Romano Pontifice sine pudore agnoscunt Pontificii. De quibus fusius in controversiis de Pontifice Romano, apud controversiarum Scriptores, legere est.
units.tr: Note 9. He will display himself as if he were God, that is, not content to have raised himself above the state and above the Church of God as its prince and supreme governor, he will also try to behave as God. Partly he will falsely boast that he possesses all the power of Christ, communicated to him, and that by delegation he is Christ's vicar, that is, that he is Vice-Christ, or Ἀντίχριστος [Antichristos], taking the meaning of the preposition ἀντί [anti] as in the words ἀντιθεος [antitheos], like God, equal to God, and ἀντιβασιλεύς [antibasileus], viceroy. Partly he will assume titles that belong properly to God, such as Prince of Pastors, our Pontiff, Head of the Church, and so on, which titles are due to Christ alone. Finally, he will arrogate to himself privileges in heaven, on earth and in hell, which belong to God alone. The Papists now acknowledge such privileges without shame in the Roman Pontiff. These matters can be read more fully in the writers on controversies, under the controversies concerning the Roman Pontiff.

units.la: Vers. 5. Annon meministis me, quum adhuc essem apud vos, haec dixisse vobis?
units.tr: Verse 5. Do you not remember that when I was still with you I told you these things?

units.la: Articulus 2. Continens certitudinem hujus Prophetiae, utpote quam Apostolus docuerat prius, & de qua praesens Thessalonicenses instituerat; & nunc absens repetit, ut veritatem confirmet, eorumque memoriae infigat.
units.tr: Section 2. Containing the certainty of this prophecy, as the Apostle had taught it earlier and as he had instructed the present Thessalonians about it. Now, though absent, he repeats it, to confirm the truth and to fix it in their memory.

units.la: Vers. 6. Nunc vero quid obstet nostis, ut in suo tempore retegatur.
units.tr: Verse 6. Now you know what restrains it, so that it may be revealed in its own time.

units.la: Articulus 3. Continens impedimentum revelationis Antichristi, cujus spiritus jam moliebatur thronum sibi erigere, verum non potuit, quia nondum sedes vacua erat, throno Antichristi recipiendo destinata, in civitate illa septicolli Roma, sicut eam Spiritus Dei describit, Apocal. 17. 9. Auferendum enim erat Romanum imperium in occidente: auferendus erat Caesar ex illa civitate, priusquam revelari posset, Antichristus: In quo consentientes habemus etiam Pontificios: De hoc impedimento Apostolus noster, diversis verbis, coram monuerat Thessalonicenses, & sciebat ipsos novisse, & memoria tenuisse, sed graves erant causae propter quas DEI SPIRITUS nolebat in hac ad eos Epistola illud impedimentum exprimere: nam in eorum rem, non erat ut exprimeret, imo tacitum esse oportuit hoc mysterium a mundo: Partim ut facilius compleretur a DEO decreta permissio mysterii iniquitatis; Partim ne persequendis Christianis hinc ansa daretur ulla: nam si Imperatores intellexissent futurum aliquem ex CHRISTI professoribus, qui Thronum sibi erecturus esset Romae, utque locus ei daretur tollendum e medio fuisse imperium, & Imperatorem Romanum, existimassent omnes jure merito saeviri potuisse in totum Christianum nomen.
units.tr: Section 3. Containing the hindrance to the revelation of Antichrist. His spirit was already striving to set up a throne for himself, but could not, because the empty seat destined to receive the throne of Antichrist was not yet vacant. That seat was in the seven-hilled city of Rome, as the Spirit of God describes it in Rev. 17. 9. For the Roman empire in the West had to be removed, and the Caesar had to be removed from that city, before Antichrist could be revealed. On this point we also agree with the Papists. Our Apostle had warned the Thessalonians about this hindrance in various words when he was with them, and he knew that they had learned it and kept it in memory. But there were serious reasons why the Spirit of God did not want to express that hindrance in this letter to them. It was not for their sake that he should express it; rather, this mystery had to be kept silent from the world. Partly this was so that the permission of the mystery of iniquity, decreed by God, might be fulfilled more easily. Partly it was so that no occasion might be given for persecuting Christians. For if the emperors had understood that some professor of Christ would one day set up a throne at Rome, and that room would be made for him by removing the empire and the Roman emperor, they would all have thought they could rightly rage against the whole Christian name.

units.la: Verf. 7. Jam enim peragitur mysterium iniquitatis: tantum qui nunc obstat, obstabit usquedum e medio sublatus fuerit:
units.tr: Verse 7. For the mystery of iniquity is already at work; only he who now restrains will do so until he is taken out of the way.

units.la: Articulus 4. Continens, una cum obstaculo revelationis Antichristi, initium etiam defectionis seu Antichristianismi, qui hic mysterium iniquitatis vocatur: Quia sicut totus Christianismus, cujus Caput est CHRISTUS est magnum mysterium pietatis, sic totus Antichristianismus (cujus caput est Antichristus) est magnum mysterium iniquitatis. Hujus mysterii semina in ambitione, avaritia, nequitia Doctorum, in ceremoniis humanis, erroribus, & falsa doctrina, ab initio praedicati Euangelii Diabolus prius sparserat in Ecclesia, & de die in diem jam tum fovebat, sedulo navans operam, ut Antichristi regnum sub praetextu pietatis in Ecclesia externa palam tandem aliquando erigeret, sed obstaculum a DEO positum manebat dum haec scriberentur. Tenebat Romam sedem futuram Antichristi, Romanus Imperator, quam postea vacantem invasurus erat Antichristus, & ad se rapturus simul, & hominum & DEI imperium.
units.tr: Section 4. Containing, together with the obstacle to the revelation of Antichrist, also the beginning of the defection or anti-Christianity, which is here called the mystery of iniquity. For just as the whole of Christianity, whose head is Christ, is a great mystery of godliness, so the whole of anti-Christianity, whose head is Antichrist, is a great mystery of iniquity. The seeds of this mystery lie in the ambition, greed and wickedness of teachers, in human ceremonies, in errors and false doctrine. From the beginning of the preaching of the Gospel the Devil had already sown them in the Church, and day by day he was now fostering them, diligently working to raise openly at last the kingdom of Antichrist in the external Church under the pretext of piety. But the obstacle placed by God remained while these things were being written. The Roman emperor held Rome, which was to be the seat of Antichrist. Later, when that seat was vacant, Antichrist was to seize it and at the same time snatch to himself the rule of both men and God.

units.la: Verf. 8. Et tunc retegetur impius ille, quem Dominus conficiet Spiritu oris sui, & illustri adventu suo abolebit.
units.tr: Verse 8. And then that wicked one will be revealed, whom the Lord will consume with the breath of his mouth, and will destroy by the brightness of his coming.

units.la: Articulus 5. Continet Antichristi apertum regnum, seu regni ini- tium, medium, & finem.
units.tr: Article 5. It contains the open reign of Antichrist, or the beginning, middle and end of his reign.

units.la: Quod ad regni initium attinet, Quamprimum Romanum imperium seu Romanus imperator tolletur a sede futura Antichristi, id est, Roma, tum in urbe illa cristas eriget Antichristianismi patronus, qui supra omnes leges se efferendo, & se nullis, neque civilibus, neque Ecclesiasticis legibus teneri, & etiam in divinis dispensandi potestatem le habere, aperte profitendo Q rofitendo reipsa se esse τοῦ ἀνομου, seu exlegem illum (de quo prædixerat Dei Spiritus,) indicio suo prodet, hic erit ejus revelandi modus, & regni aperte occupati initium. Talem, ab eo tempore quo Roma imperii sedes esse desiit, hucusque se ostentat Papa Romanus, qui legum repagula impudenter effringit, supra jus & leges se extollit, leges à Deo latas refigit, deque iis dispensat, ut dicunt, aliasque ipsarum loco figit, suam voluntatem pro ratione ponit, sicut abunde manifestum fecerunt orthodoxi in controversiis suis: neque hæc Pontificii de suo Pontifice, aliaque multa istiusmodi, verecundantur profiteri, scriptisque publicè defendere, ita ut nihil opus sit amplius inquirere, quis sit ille qui in Templo, seu externa titulo tenus Ecclesiâ, sedet Antichristus, cum sciamus nomen ἀντίχριστος duo significare posse, pro præpositionis ἀντί varia acceptione: Nempe Christi vicarium, & Christi adversarium, Papamque Romanum audimus jactartem se Antichristum in altera significatione, id est, Christi vicarium se profitentem, interim vero quasi ἐν ἀντιφωρᾳ eundem deprehendimus inter Christianos aperte afferentem, se neque civilibus, neque Ecclesiasticis legibus subditum, sed omnibus superiorem se esse profiteri minime erubescentem: quumque jam mundo constet Pontificis Romani autoritatem ab ipso, & allectis suis extolli supra Scripturam, seu leges divinas, quoad Canonis constitutionem, sensus determinationem, controversiarum judicium & decisionem, dispensationem (quæ dicitur) de divinis præceptis, &c. An dubitabimus quis sit ille qui in Templo Dei, seu inter Christianæ religionis professores, sedet ὁ ἀνομος seu exlex ille? Quod ad se cundum, seu regni possessionem attinet, non possidebit Antichristus regnum suum sine bello; pugnabit adversus eum Christus gladio oris sui, id est, per prædicationem veritatis in Euangelio revelatæ, & per potentiam spiritus sui, cum Verbo concurrentis.
units.tr: As to the beginning of the reign: as soon as the Roman empire, or the Roman emperor, is removed from the seat that is to belong to Antichrist, that is, Rome, then the champion of antichristianism will raise his horns in that city. Exalting himself above all laws, and openly professing that he is bound by neither civil nor ecclesiastical laws, and that he has the power to dispense even in divine matters, he will show by his own conduct that he is in fact the lawless one [τοῦ ἀνομου], or the outlaw, of whom the Spirit of God foretold. This will be the manner of his revelation and the beginning of his openly seized reign. The Roman Pope has shown himself to be such a one from the time when Rome ceased to be the seat of the empire until now. He shamelessly breaks through the barriers of the laws, raises himself above right and law, and overturns the laws given by God. He dispenses from them, as they say, and puts others in their place, setting his own will in place of reason. The orthodox have made this abundantly clear in their controversies. Nor are the Papists ashamed to profess this about their Pope, and many things of this kind, and to defend them publicly in writing. So there is no need to inquire further who it is that sits as Antichrist in the Temple, that is, in the outward Church in name only. We know that the name ἀντίχριστος [antichristos] can mean two things, depending on the different senses of the preposition ἀντί: namely, the vicar of Christ and the adversary of Christ. We hear the Roman Pope boasting that he is Antichrist in the first sense, that is, professing himself to be the vicar of Christ. Yet we also find him caught red-handed [ἐν ἀντιφωρᾳ], as it were, openly asserting among Christians that he is subject to neither civil nor ecclesiastical laws, and not in the least ashamed to profess that he is superior to all. And since it is now plain to the world that the authority of the Roman Pontiff is exalted by himself and his followers above Scripture, or the divine laws, in matters such as the constitution of the canon, the determination of the sense, the judgment and decision of controversies, and the so-called dispensing from divine precepts, etc., shall we doubt who that lawless one is, who sits in the Temple of God, that is, among the professors of the Christian religion? As to the second point, the possession of the kingdom: Antichrist will not possess his kingdom without war. Christ will fight against him with the sword of his mouth, that is, through the preaching of the truth revealed in the Gospel, and through the power of his Spirit working together with the Word.

units.la: Quod ad tertium, De regni Antichristi fine, seu de belli & regni ejus exitu: Christus Antichristi mendacia, fraudes, scelera, tyrannidem, falsas interpretationes & allegationes Scripturarum deteget, confutabit, ejusque regnum gradatim demolietur, consumet & conteret, tandemque destruet & abolebit, illustri manifestatione factâ adventus sui appropinquantis, ad ultimum judicium universale.
units.tr: As to the third point, the end of Antichrist's reign, that is, the outcome of the war and of his kingdom: Christ will expose and refute the lies, frauds, crimes, tyranny, false interpretations and misapplications of Scripture by Antichrist. He will gradually demolish, consume and crush his kingdom, and at last destroy and abolish it by the clear manifestation of his approaching coming, at the final universal judgment.

units.la: Vers. 9 Illum, inquam, cujus adventus est ex efficacia Satanæ, cum omni potentia & signis, ac prodigiis mendacibus,
units.tr: Verse 9: That one, I say, "whose coming is after the working of Satan, with all power and signs and lying wonders,"

units.la: Articulus 6. In quo resumit, & porro describit Antichristi ortum, & progressum, arma, artes & adjumenta, quibus regnum acquiret, & fulciet quantum poterit.
units.tr: Article 6. In which he resumes and further describes the rise and progress of Antichrist, the weapons, arts and aids by which he will gain and strengthen his kingdom as far as he can.

units.la: Primum Adjumentum est, Satanas, qui multiplicibus suis technis Antichristum instruet, & per ipsum, ἐνεργείαν suam fortiter exerturus est toto dominatus Antichristi tempore.
units.tr: The first aid is Satan, who will equip Antichrist with his many devices, and who through him will vigorously exert his energy [ἐνέργειαν] throughout the whole time of Antichrist's dominion.

units.la: Adjumentum 2. est, Simulata facultas seu potentia edendi quaevis miracula, cum signis & prodigiis mendacibus, ad confirmationem falsorum dogmatum comparatis: qualia in legendis, quae vocantur, Pontificiorum, legas aliquot millia.
units.tr: The second aid is a pretended faculty or power of working any miracles whatever, with signs and lying wonders, prepared to confirm false doctrines. You may read a few thousand such things in the so-called legends of the Papists.

units.la: Vers. 10. Et cum omni fraude injustitia in iis qui pereunt: pro eo quod amorem veritatis non receperunt, ut salvi fierent.
units.tr: Verse 10: "And with all deceit of unrighteousness among those who perish, because they did not receive the love of the truth, that they might be saved."

units.la: Adjumentum 3. est, Omnis deceptio injustitiae, seu omnis fallacia injusta & fraudulenta, quales sunt falsae, fucatae, seu blandientes doctrinae, disputationes Sophisticae, illecebrae opum, honorum & dignitatum hujus seculi, una cum minis & terroribus; cujus deceptionis apex & fastigium in eo erit, quod non palam & aperte, seu directe CHRISTUM oppugnabit, sed occulte, & quasi per cuniculos actos rem aggredietur, simulans se CHRISTI causam agere, cum eam labefactat quam potest maxime.
units.tr: The third aid is every deception of unrighteousness, that is, every unjust and fraudulent deceit: false, painted or flattering doctrines, sophistical disputations, the allurements of the wealth, honours and dignities of this age, together with threats and terrors. The peak and height of this deception will be this: he will not attack Christ openly and directly, but will go about the matter secretly, as if by tunnels dug underground. He will pretend to be defending the cause of Christ, while in fact he undermines it as much as he can.

units.la: Articulus 7. De Antichristi subditis, eorumque perditione, & perditionis causis: Describuntur autem asseclae Antichristi proprie dicti domestici & familiares ejus, qui obstinatis animis pertinaciter ad finem usque ei adhaerent, & in quibus, maxime efficax est Diabolus: 1. A proprietate reproborum, praeunt, sunt e numero perenuntium: 2. A perditionis causa meritoria, oblatam veritatem in Dei verbo non receiverunt cum amore, ut salvi fierent.
units.tr: Article 7. Concerning the subjects of Antichrist, their perdition, and the causes of their perdition. The followers of Antichrist are described, properly speaking his household and familiars, who cling to him stubbornly with obstinate minds until the end, and in whom the Devil is most powerfully active. (1) From the nature of the reprobate, they are of the number of those who perish. (2) From the meritorious cause of their perdition, they did not receive with love the truth offered in the Word of God, that they might be saved.

units.la: Vers. 11. Propterea igitur mittit illis Deus efficaciam deceptionis, ut credant mendacio:
units.tr: Verse 11: "For this reason God sends them a working of error, that they should believe a lie."

units.la: Describuntur 3. A Judicis justissima in eos vindicta, peccata peccatis puniente, & illos Diabolo excaecandos tradente, ut qui lucem aspicere recusarunt, & veritati divinae renunciarunt, fidem etiam haberent erroribus, praestigiis, hominum commentis, crassissimis fabulis, & mendaciis, atque ita perirent.
units.tr: Third, they are described by the most just vengeance of the Judge upon them, who punishes sins with sins and hands them over to be blinded by the Devil. Since they refused to look upon the light and renounced the divine truth, they also give credence to errors, delusions, the inventions of men, the grossest fables and lies, and so they perish.

units.la: Vers. 12. Ut damnentur omnes qui non crediderunt veritati, sed acquieverunt in injustitia.
units.tr: Verse 12: "That all may be condemned who did not believe the truth, but took pleasure in unrighteousness."

units.la: Describuntur 4. Ab ipsorum conditione novissima, & causa meritoria condemnationis repetita. Aeternum damnabuntur omnes in novissimo illo judicio, quia non crediderunt simplici veritati DEI in Euangelio patefactæ, sed plenâ voluntate, injustissimè acquieverunt in fide mendaciorum, & obedientiâ suarum cupiditatum carnalium: Et hic est exitus eorum qui Pontifici Romano ipsiusque erroribus pertinaciter adhærent, à SPIRITU DEI, prædictus.
units.tr: Fourth, they are described from their final condition, and the meritorious cause of their condemnation is repeated. All of them will be eternally condemned in that last judgment, because they did not believe the plain truth of God revealed in the Gospel. Instead, with full will and most unjustly, they gave their assent to the faith of lies and obeyed their carnal desires. This is the outcome, foretold by the Spirit of God, for those who stubbornly cling to the Roman Pope and his errors.

units.la: Secunda pars Capitis.
units.tr: The second part of the chapter.

units.la: Verf. 13. Nos autem debemus gratias agere Deo semper de vobis, fratres dilecti à DOMINO, quod elegerit vos DEVS ab initio ad salutem per sanctificationem Spiritus, & Fidem habitam veritati:
units.tr: Verse 13. But we ought to give thanks to God always for you, brethren beloved of the Lord, because God chose you from the beginning to salvation through the sanctification of the Spirit and faith in the truth:

units.la: Altera pars Capitis, in qua Thessalonicensium fidem, ne hac tristi Prophetia commoverentur, confirmat, idque tribus modis: 1. Per gratiarum actionem ipsorum nomine: 2. Per hortationem ipsorum ad constantiam; & 3. Per precationem pro ipsis: Quod ad primum modum, in gratiarum actione tria Argumenta confirmationis fidei ipsorum affert.
units.tr: The other part of the chapter, in which he confirms the faith of the Thessalonians, lest they be moved by this sorrowful prophecy, and does so in three ways: (1) through thanksgiving offered in their name; (2) through exhortation to steadfastness; and (3) through prayer for them. As to the first way, in the thanksgiving he brings forward three arguments for confirming their faith.

units.la: Fratres dilecti Argumentum primum, Vos estis fratres nostri, eadem DEI dilectione nobiscum comprehensi: Ergo non est quod metuatis vobis, ne cum Antichristiana secta pereatis.
units.tr: Brethren beloved. The first argument: you are our brethren, embraced together with us by the same love of God. Therefore there is no reason for you to fear that you will perish along with the Antichristian sect.

units.la: Elegit Arg. 2. In decreto, de fine & mediis salutaribus, DEus elegit vos, ut salutem consequamini per fidem & sanctificationem à SPIRITU Sancto, tanquam per media quibus perveniatis ad salutem, gratuito vobis destinatam. Ergo.
units.tr: Chose. Second argument: in the decree concerning the end and the saving means, God chose you so that you might obtain salvation through faith and sanctification by the Holy Spirit, as through the means by which you reach salvation, freely destined for you. Therefore...

units.la: Verf. 14. Quò vocavit vos per Euangelium nostrum, ad obtinendam gloriam Domini nostri Iesu Christi,
units.tr: Verse 14. To which he called you through our gospel, to obtain the glory of our Lord Jesus Christ,

units.la: Arg. 3. DEus jam vocavit vos efficaciter per Euangelium à me praedicatum, ut obtineatis gloriam à CHRISTO partam. Ergo non est quod tristi hac prophetia commoveamini.
units.tr: Argument 3. God has already effectually called you through the gospel preached by me, so that you may obtain the glory purchased by Christ. Therefore there is no reason for you to be moved by this sorrowful prophecy.

units.la: Verf. 15. Nempe igitur, fratres, perstate, & tenete traditam doctrinam quam edocti estis, sive per sermonem, sive per Epistolam nostram.
units.tr: Verse 15. So then, brethren, stand fast and hold the traditions which you have been taught, whether by word or by our epistle.

units.la: Secundus modus confirmationis fidei ipsorum, per hortationem ad Constantiam in Iide, ut persteant, & contra omnes hostes fortiter retineant traditiones, seu doctrinas ipsis traditas ab Apostolo, quas doctrinas didicerant, vel viva voce dum coram adesset Paulus, vel scripto, ut in priori & hac Epistola, reliquaque Scriptura acceperant. Verf. 16. Ipse verò Dominus noster Iesus Christus, & Deus ac Pater noster, qui dilexit nos, & dedit consolationem æternam & spem bonam per gratiam,
units.tr: The second way of confirming their faith is by exhortation to constancy in the faith, that they persevere and firmly hold, against all enemies, the traditions or doctrines delivered to them by the Apostle, which they had learned either by word of mouth while Paul was present with them, or in writing, as they had received them in the former and this epistle, and in the rest of Scripture. Verse 16. Now may our Lord Jesus Christ himself, and God and our Father, who loved us and gave us everlasting consolation and good hope through grace,

units.la: Vers. 17. Consoletur vestra corda, & stabiliat vos in omni sermone & opere bono.
units.tr: Verse 17. Comfort your hearts and establish you in every good word and work.

units.la: Tertius modus Confirmationis fidei ipsorum est, Precatio ad Deum, ut consoletur ipsorum corda efficaciter, & stabiliat in fide Euangelii, seu omnis sanæ doctrinæ, & in sanctitate vitæ. Argumenta precationis, & confirmationis fidei sunt quatuor. Argument. 1. A relatione CHRISTI & DEI ad ipsos, IESUS CHRISTUS est Dominus noster, & DEUS Pater, est Pater noster. Ergo in fide confirmabit nos, seu vos nobiscum stabiliet. Dilexit ] Arg. 2. Quia Deus dilexit nos.
units.tr: The third way of confirming their faith is prayer to God, that he would effectually comfort their hearts and establish them in the faith of the gospel, or of all sound doctrine, and in holiness of life. The arguments of the prayer and of the confirmation of their faith are four. Argument 1: from the relation of Christ and God to them: Jesus Christ is our Lord, and God the Father is our Father. Therefore he will confirm us in faith, or establish you along with us. Loved Argument 2: because God loved us.

units.la: Et dedit ] Arg. 3. Quia Deus dedit nobis solidas rationes perpetuæ consolationis, & jus ad ea omnia, quæ consolentur nos in æternum
units.tr: And gave Argument 3: because God gave us solid grounds for perpetual consolation, and a right to all those things which console us for ever.

units.la: Et spem ] Arg. 4. Quia Deus dedit bonam spem, id est, non tantum bonæ spei objectum optimum, & rationes seu causas bene sperandi optimas, sed etiam ipsius spei, ut habitus, amplam mensuram, & quia concessit ea omnia ex gratia & favore suo mero, nullis nostris meritis bonis, quæ nulla sunt, inductus; nec malis nostris meritis, quæ magna & multa sunt, impeditus: Idcirco confirmabit vos una nobiscum, ne erroribus Antichristi decipiamini, & pereatis.
units.tr: And hope Argument 4: because God gave a good hope, that is, not only the best object of good hope and the best reasons or grounds for hoping well, but also a large measure of hope itself as a habit; and because he granted all these things out of his own pure grace and favour, moved by no good merits of ours, which are none, and hindered by no evil merits of ours, which are great and many. Therefore he will confirm you together with us, so that you are not deceived by the errors of Antichrist and perish.

units.la: Caput Tertium.
units.tr: Chapter 3.

units.la: HOC Capite hortatur partim expressè, partim indirectè ad Christiana Officia aliqua. Post quæ Epistolam clausit. Hortationes sunt septem.
units.tr: In this chapter he exhorts, partly expressly and partly indirectly, to certain Christian duties. After these he closes the Epistle. There are seven exhortations.

units.la: Verf. 1. Quod superest, precamini, fratres, pro nobis, ut sermo Domini currat, & glorificetur, sicut & apud vos:
units.tr: Verse 1. Finally, brothers, pray for us, that the word of the Lord may run and be glorified, as it also is among you;

units.la: Hortatio prima, Ut petant à Deo hæc duo: 1. Ut per Apostoli Ministerium, cum fructu celeriter propagetur Euangelium, & magni fiat inter alias gentes, sicut inter ipsos magnificebat.
units.tr: First exhortation: that they should ask God for these two things: (1) that through the ministry of the Apostle the Gospel may be quickly spread with fruit, and may be magnified among other nations, as it was magnified among themselves.

units.la: Verf. 2. Et ut eripiamur à potervis ac sceleratis hominibus, non enim omnium est fides.
units.tr: Verse 2. And that we may be delivered from unreasonable and wicked men; for not all have faith.

units.la: Secundum, Ut Deus Apostolum custodiret, & liberaret ab insidiis hostium, qui absque omni specie rationis perversè le ipsi opponebant: hostilis animi rationem reddit, quia fide vera destituti erant multi, à quibus idcirco ut liberaretur, opus erat divino auxilio.
units.tr: Second, that God would guard the Apostle and deliver him from the snares of enemies, who opposed him perversely and without any appearance of reason. He gives the reason for their hostile spirit: many were destitute of true faith, and therefore he needed divine help to be delivered from them.

units.la: Verf. 3. Sed fidelis est DOMINUS, qui stabiliet vos & tuebitur à malo.
units.tr: Verse 3. But the Lord is faithful, who will establish you and guard you from evil.

units.la: Hortatio 2. Indirecta, ad fiduciam & robur animi, Ne præmoniti de infidelitate & apostasia aliquorum, vel mentione jam facta periculorum Apostoli, percellerentur, vel infirmiores aliquo modo redderentur. In quem finem certiorari & confirmari ipsos vult de Dei erga ipsos proposito, quod scilicet stabiliturus fuerit eos in bono, hoc est, in fide & sanctitate: & defensurus à malo, seu à periculis & tentationibus Satanæ, & organorum ejus; cujus rationem reddit, quia Deus qui ipsos efficaciter vocaverat, Constans & Fidelis est ad opus suum promovendum, & complendum in ipsis.
units.tr: Second exhortation, indirect, to confidence and strength of mind: lest, forewarned of the unbelief and apostasy of some, or with the dangers of the Apostle already mentioned, they should be dismayed or in some way made weaker. To this end he wishes them to be assured and strengthened concerning God's purpose toward them, namely that he will establish them in good, that is, in faith and holiness, and will defend them from evil, or from the dangers and temptations of Satan and his instruments. He gives the reason: God, who had effectually called them, is constant and faithful in carrying forward and completing his work in them.

units.la: Verf. 4. Confidimus autem per Dominum de vobis, vos, quæ denuntiamus vobis, & facere & facturos esse.
units.tr: Verse 4. And we are confident in the Lord concerning you, that you both do and will do the things we command you.

units.la: Hortatio 3. Ad obedientiam præstandam Apostolicis mandatis, quæ nomine Domini illis dederat, aut daturus erat. Hanc hortationem indirecte proponit per commendationem promptitudinis ipsorum, ad obediendum, de qua alacritate jam sibi perluaserat.
units.tr: Third exhortation: to render obedience to the apostolic commands which he had given, or was about to give, in the Lord's name. He proposes this exhortation indirectly, by commending their readiness to obey, about which he had already been persuaded of their eagerness.

units.la: Verf. 5. Porrò Dominus dirigat corda vestra ad Dei charitatem, & Christi expectationem.
units.tr: Verse 5. May the Lord direct your hearts into the love of God and the patience of Christ.

units.la: Hortatio 4. ad dilectionem Dei & patientiam, usque ad DOMINI adventum, involuta precatione ad SPIRITUM Sanctum, quem Dominum vocat, orans pro iis, ut Dominus viam illis præeat, & in recta semita eos retineat & dirigat.
units.tr: Fourth exhortation: to the love of God and to patience until the coming of the Lord, with a prayer implied to the Holy Spirit, whom he calls the Lord, praying for them that the Lord would go before them on the way and keep and direct them in the straight path.

units.la: Verf. 6 Denuntiamus autem vobis, fratres, per nomen Domini nostri Iesu Christi, ut subducatis vos ab omni fratre qui inordinatè se gerit, & non ex traditA doctrina quam accepit à nobis.
units.tr: Verse 6. Now we command you, brothers, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that you withdraw yourselves from every brother who walks disorderly and not according to the tradition which he received from us.

units.la: Hortatio 5. Ut otiosos ventres, & fucos alvearia depascentes, censuris Ecclesiasticis coercerent, & idoneis modis corrigerent omnes, qui nullo honesto labore, seu negotio occupati, alienis bonis inhiabant: Censura horum est ( post adhibita admonitionum, & leviorum censura- rum remedia ) excommunicatio: Vetat enim, ne iis familiariter utan- tur; scilicet, post rejectas privatas admonitiones, & publicam Ec- clefiæ lententiam : & ut fe ab illis subducant, nec in consortium suum admittant, quod est consequens excommunicationis: Rationes præ- cepti sunt quinque: Ratio prima, Quia hoc vult Christus, cujus authoritate istud præcipit.
units.tr: Fifth exhortation: that they should restrain by ecclesiastical censures the idle bellies and drones devouring the hives, and correct by suitable means all who, occupied with no honest labour or business, coveted the goods of others. The censure of these men (after the remedies of admonitions and lighter censures have been applied) is excommunication. For he forbids them to associate with them familiarly, namely after private admonitions and the public sentence of the Church have been rejected, and that they should withdraw from them and not admit them to their fellowship, which is the consequence of excommunication. There are five reasons for the precept. The first reason: because Christ wills it, by whose authority he commands this.

units.la: Inordinate ] Ratio 2. Continetur in peccati descriptione, quia qui- cunque vivunt inordinatè, & non fecundùm doctrinæ regulam, Ec- clefiæ traditam à me, excommunicandi sunt.
units.tr: "Disorderly": the second reason is contained in the description of the fault: whoever lives disorderly and not according to the rule of doctrine handed down to the Church by me is to be excommunicated.

units.la: Verf. 7 Nam ipsi sciti quomodo oporteat nos imitari: quoniam non inordinatè nos gessimus inter vos;
units.tr: Verse 7. For you yourselves know how you ought to imitate us, since we did not behave disorderly among you;

units.la: Verf. 8. Neque gratis panem edimus acceptum à quoquam, sed cum labore & ærumna nocte dieque operantes, ne quem vestrûm gravaremus.
units.tr: Verse 8. Nor did we eat bread from anyone for nothing, but worked with toil and labour night and day, so as not to burden any of you.

units.la: Ratio 3. Quia, qui inordinatè vivit, non gerit fe fecundùm exemplum meum, qui diligenter laboravi diu noctuque, ne cuiquam effem oneri.
units.tr: Third reason: because whoever lives disorderly does not conduct himself according to my example, for I laboured diligently night and day so as not to be a burden to anyone.

units.la: Verf. 9. Non quòd nobis id non liceat, sed ut nofmetipfos pro exemplari exhibeamus vobis ad nos imitandos.
units.tr: Verse 9. Not that we did not have the right, but that we might present ourselves as a model to you, to imitate us.

units.la: Confirmatio rationis per occupationem obiectionis, ex eo, quod Apo- ftolus uti potuisset jure suo, & debitum stipendium ab iplis exigere, & tamen sponte ceffierit hoc jure, ut illis exemplar proponeret. Ergo tene- bantur inertes fuci illi, & nemini utiles laborare: ut fi nollent aliis esse utiles, saltem aliis non effent oneri.
units.tr: Confirmation of the reason by anticipating an objection: the Apostle could have used his own right and demanded a due stipend from them, and yet he willingly gave up this right, so as to set before them an example. Therefore those idle drones were bound to labour and be useful to no one: so that, if they were unwilling to be useful to others, at least they should not be a burden to others.

units.la: Verf. 10. Etenim quum effemus apud vos, hoc denuntiabamus vobis, quòd fi quis nolit operari, etiam non edito.
units.tr: Verse 10. For when we were with you, we declared this to you: that if anyone is unwilling to work, neither let him eat.

units.la: Ratio 4. Quia æquum est ut victus ei subtrahatur, qui fe honesto la- bori subtiahit, sicut prius monui.
units.tr: Fourth reason: because it is just that food be withdrawn from one who withdraws himself from honest labour, as I warned before.

units.la: Verf. 11. Audimus enim quosdam versari inter vos inordi- natè nihil operòs facientes, sed curiosè agentes.
units.tr: Verse 11. For we hear that some among you walk disorderly, doing no work at all, but busybodies.

units.la: Ratio 5. In qua causam cur urgeat hoc præceptum profert, quia otium iners alit curiosam περιεργασίαν, sicut aliquorum exemplis testatum habebant inter fe: aliqui enim ipsis jam satis cogniti, in suis rebus nihil honesti operabantur, sed curiosè vagantes rerum alienarum ad se nihil pertinentium satagebant.
units.tr: Fifth reason, in which he gives the cause why this precept is urgent: because idle sloth nourishes curious busybodying (περιεργασία), as they had attested among themselves by the examples of some. For some of them were already well known to them, who did nothing honest in their own affairs, but wandering about inquisitively, busied themselves with the affairs of others which did not concern them.

units.la: Verf. 12. Iis autem qui sunt ejusmodi, denuntiamus & eos obsecramus per Dominum nostrum Iesum Christum, ut cum quiete operantes, suo pane vescantur.
units.tr: Verse 12. Now those who are such we command and beseech in the Lord Jesus Christ, that working quietly they eat their own bread.

units.la: In hujusmodi otiosorum gratiam hortationem repetit & applicat.
units.tr: He repeats and applies the exhortation for the sake of such idlers.

units.la: Verf. 13. Vos autem, fratres, ne Segnescite in benefaciendo.
units.tr: Verse 13. But you, brothers, do not grow weary in doing good.

units.la: Hortatio 6. Ne interim defatigentur benefaciendo egenis (verè pauperibus qui non per inertiam, sed per calamitatem ad paupertatem redacti sunt) & ne segnescant in ullius virtutis actionibus, sed strenuè pergant, quæ præclara, seu pulchra sunt agere.
units.tr: Sixth exhortation: that they should not in the meantime grow weary of doing good to the needy (truly poor, who have been reduced to poverty not through idleness but through calamity), and should not grow slack in any act of virtue, but press on vigorously to do what is noble and fair.

units.la: Verf. 14. Quòd siquis non auscultat nostro per epistolam sermoni, hunc notate, & ne commercium habete cum eo, ut eum pudeat.
units.tr: Verse 14. But if anyone does not obey our word through this letter, mark that man, and have no company with him, that he may be ashamed.

units.la: Hortatio 7. Ut notam inurant refractariis, & stigmate insigniant, non obedientes doctrinæ Apostolicæ, hoc est, ut excommunicent eos, quod patet ex eo, quod mandet ne cum notato commercium habeant, quod est consequens excommunicationis, & in eum finem mandatum, ut excommunicatus ab aliorum consortio segregatus, pudefactus in se descenderet, & resipiscerit.
units.tr: Seventh exhortation: to brand the refractory with a mark and stigmatise those who do not obey the apostolic teaching, that is, to excommunicate them. This is evident from the command that they should have no fellowship with the marked man, which is the consequence of excommunication, and the purpose of the command is that the excommunicated man, separated from the company of others and put to shame, should come to himself and repent.

units.la: Verf. 15. Neque ut inimicum ducite, sed admonete ut fratrem.
units.tr: Verse 15. Yet do not regard him as an enemy, but admonish him as a brother.

units.la: Exponit mandatum, ne hostili sint animo in excommunicatum, aut eum habeant tanquam hostem, sed ita ostendant suum odium, in ipsius peccatum, ut intelligat excommunicatus sub severa illa correctione, subesse fraternam charitatem, & sic adducatur ad redeundum in gratiam cum Deo & Ecclesia, per resipiscentiam.
units.tr: He explains the command: that they should not bear a hostile spirit toward the excommunicated man, nor regard him as an enemy, but should show their displeasure only at his sin, so that the excommunicated man may understand that under this severe correction brotherly love lies hidden, and so be brought to return to grace with God and the Church through repentance.

units.la: Verf. 16. Ipse autem Dominus pacis author semper det vobis pacem omni modo, Dominus sit cum omnibus vobis.
units.tr: Verse 16. Now the Lord of peace himself give you peace always in every way. The Lord be with you all.

units.la: Restat Epilogus, Cujus articuli sunt tres, In primo precatur Deum pacis, ut ita dirigat ipsorum vias, & ita frænet immorigerorum turbulentos spiritus, ut erga Deum, & inter se, & cum exteris, pace frui possent: quod opus, divinam manum requirebat: Deinde precatur, ut Deus gratiosa præsentia sua, semper adsit ipsis omnibus.
units.tr: There remains the Epilogue, which has three parts. In the first he prays to the God of peace that he would so direct their ways and so restrain the turbulent spirits of the disobedient that they might enjoy peace toward God, among themselves and with outsiders; this work required the divine hand. Then he prays that God, by his gracious presence, would always be with them all.

units.la: Verf. 17. Salutatio, mea manu Pauli, quod est signum in omni Epistola: ita scribo.
units.tr: Verse 17. The greeting of me, Paul, with my own hand, which is a sign in every epistle: so I write.

units.la: Articulus 2. Continet obsignationem Epistolæ, per subscriptionem ipsius Pauli, qui maximâ ex parte utebatur opera amanuensium in uniuscujusque Epistolæ corpore describendo, sed propria manu subscribebat in conclusione, ut genuinae ejus Epistolae dignoscerentur ab adulteriniis & mentitis, quae Pauli nomine circumferebantur & obtrudebantur Ecclesiis per impostores.
units.tr: Second part: it contains the sealing of the Epistle by the signature of Paul himself, who for the most part used the work of amanuenses in writing out the body of each Epistle, but signed with his own hand at the close, so that his genuine Epistles might be distinguished from the forged and counterfeit ones that were circulated and foisted upon the Churches under Paul's name by impostors.

units.la: Vers. 18. Gratia Domini nostri Iesu Christi sit cum omnibus vobis, Amen.
units.tr: Verse 18. The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you all. Amen.

units.la: Articulus 3. Continet votum Apostolicum propria manu descriptum, quo optat gratiae CHRISTI (ut fontis omnium bonorum) perennem erga eos fluxum, in ipsorum sanctificationem & salutem.
units.tr: Third part: it contains the apostolic wish, written with his own hand, by which he desires the perpetual flow of the grace of Christ (as the fountain of all good things) toward them, for their sanctification and salvation.

units.la: EXPOSITIO ANALYTICA EPISTOLAE PRIORIS, AD TIMOTHEUM.
units.tr: EXPOSITION OF THE FIRST EPISTLE TO TIMOTHY, ANALYSED.

units.la: Summarium.
units.tr: Summary.

units.la: Phesso discedens in Macedoniam Apostolus non satis habuit Ecclesiam Ephesinam jam publice constitutam, Pastorum ordinariorum curae committere, sed etiam rogavit Timotheum Evangelistam, ut aliquantisper ibi commoraretur, ad stabiliendam Ecclesiam in omnibus quae ad Disciplinam & Doctrinam spectabant: quo opere confecto, Apostolus eum ad seipsum revocaturus erat, & ejus opera usurus, ad alias etiam Ecclesias confirmandas, ut ex fine Epistolae posterioris, & aliis locis apparet. Interim quia Juvenis erat Timotheus, ne auctoritate non satis instructus videretur, ad protervos homines cohibendos, qui contra eum forsan insurgerent, scripta hac ad eum Epistola, non tam monet ipsum officii (utpote quem probe instructum jam noverat) quam Ecclesias omnes, earumque Gubernatores de auctoritate Timothei, & ipsorum officiis, commonefacit.
units.tr: When the Apostle was leaving Ephesus for Macedonia, he did not think it enough to entrust the Church of Ephesus, now publicly constituted, to the care of its ordinary ministers. He also asked Timothy the Evangelist to stay there for a while, to establish the Church in all matters that concerned discipline and doctrine. Once this work was finished, the Apostle was going to recall him to himself and make use of his labours to strengthen other churches as well, as appears from the end of the later Epistle and from other places. Meanwhile, because Timothy was young, lest he seem to lack sufficient authority to restrain the headstrong men who might rise up against him, the Apostle wrote this Epistle to him. It admonishes him less about his duty (since he already knew him to be well instructed) than it reminds all the churches and their governors of Timothy's authority and of their own duties.

units.la: Epistolae partes speciales sunt sex, secundum numerum Capitum. Capite primo ostendit rationem praedicandi legem, & Evangelium rite, & cum fructu.
units.tr: The special parts of the Epistle are six, according to the number of chapters. In the first chapter he shows the reason for preaching the law and the Gospel rightly and with fruit.

units.la: Capite secundo, praescribit quomodo in publicis precibus & conventibus Ecclesiasticis, se rectè gerere debeant Pastores & auditores, viri & mulieres.
units.tr: In the second chapter he prescribes how ministers and hearers, men and women, ought to conduct themselves properly in public prayers and ecclesiastical assemblies.

units.la: Capite tertio, tractat de rectè instituendis Pastoribus & Diaconis, & de doctrinæ articulis ab iis specialiter curandis.
units.tr: In the third chapter he treats of the proper appointment of ministers and deacons, and of the articles of doctrine which they especially must attend to.

units.la: Capite quarto, agit de vitanda apostasia ventura, & de diligentia à vigilanti Pastore adhibenda, in eum finem.
units.tr: In the fourth chapter he deals with avoiding the apostasy to come, and with the diligence a watchful minister must apply to that end.

units.la: Capite quinto, instituit de privatis admonitionibus à Presbyteris adhibendis, & quomodo se gerere debeant, Presbyteri erga viduas, & Presbyteros alios.
units.tr: In the fifth chapter he instructs concerning private admonitions to be given by elders, and how they ought to conduct themselves, the elders towards widows and towards other elders.

units.la: Capite sexto, Præcepta dat Timotheo, quibus instituatur quid de officiis Christianis, tum privatorum, tum Ministrorum, docere debeat.
units.tr: In the sixth chapter he gives Timothy precepts by which he is to be taught what to teach concerning Christian duties, both of private persons and of ministers.

units.la: Caput Primum.
units.tr: Chapter 1.

units.la: Praeter inscriptionem quae continetur duobus primis versibus: Tres sunt Capitis partes, In prima praecipit Timotheo, ut rectam docendi rationem conservet, & ut coerceat perversos Legis doctores, ad versum 12. In secunda asserit suum Apostolatum, ut cum authoritate, quod jusserat, praestaretur à Timotheo, ad versum 18. In tertia Timotheum animat ad strenuè se gerendum in ministerio suo.
units.tr: Apart from the inscription, which is contained in the first two verses, the chapter has three parts. In the first, he instructs Timothy to maintain the sound method of teaching and to restrain the perverse teachers of the Law (to verse 12). In the second, he asserts his apostolic office, so that what he had ordered might be carried out by Timothy with authority (to verse 18). In the third, he encourages Timothy to conduct himself vigorously in his ministry.

units.la: Verf. 1 Paulus Apostolus Iesu Christi ex ordinatione Dei servatoris nostri, & Domini Iesu Christi spei nostræ,
units.tr: Verse 1: Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ by the commandment of God our Saviour, and of the Lord Jesus Christ, who is our hope,

units.la: Epistolæ inscriptio, in qua, 1. ad conciliandam authoritatem huic Epistolæ, Paulus asserit se in ea scribenda apostolicâ legatione fungi pro CHRISTO, 2. Apostolatum confirmat speciali mandato DEI Patris (quem Servatorem vocat, quia salutis nostræ Author est) qui ad officium Apostolatus ipsum vocaverat, & ad muneris exequutionem in præsenti quod agebat negotio adhibuerat: 3. Apostolatum confirmat, mandato DOMINI nostri IESU CHRISTI, quem spem nostram vocat, quia spei nostræ Author, Causa meritoria, Objectum, & Consummator est.
units.tr: The inscription of the letter. Here, (1) to win authority for this letter, Paul asserts that in writing it he discharges an apostolic commission on behalf of Christ. (2) He confirms his apostleship by the special command of God the Father, whom he calls Saviour because he is the author of our salvation, and who had called him to the office of apostle and equipped him for carrying out that office in the business he was then engaged in. (3) He confirms his apostleship by the command of our Lord Jesus Christ, whom he calls our hope, because he is the author, meritorious cause, object and consummator of our hope.

units.la: Verf. 2. Timotheo germano filio in fide, gratia sit tibi, misericordia & pax à Deo Patre nostro, & Christo Iesu Domino nostro:
units.tr: Verse 2: To Timothy, my true son in the faith: grace, mercy and peace be to you from God our Father and Christ Jesus our Lord.

units.la: Timotheus, ad quem scribitur, vocatur germanus filius Apostoli, non simpliciter, sed in fide, quia ipsius discipulus erat, & sicut filius Patrem repræsentat facie & moribus, sic Timotheus doctrinâ & sanctâ conversatione Paulum referebat.
units.tr: Timothy, to whom the letter is written, is called the true son of the apostle, not simply, but in the faith, because he was Paul's disciple; and just as a son resembles his father in face and manner, so Timothy resembled Paul in doctrine and holy conduct.

units.la: In salutatione optat Timotheo, 1. Gratiam, id est, instaurationem imaginis Dei, ex fonte gratuitæ benevolentiæ Dei: 2. Misericordiam, id est, remissionem peccatorum gratuitam, quia sciebat sanctum juvenem, sensu peccatorum suorum affectum, multis cum lachrymis quotidie coram Deo prostratum fuisse: 3. Pacem optat, id est, tranquillitatem conscientiæ, & lætitiam ex sensu Divini favoris: & denique, plenam felicitatem in vita futura, quæ sub pace comprehenditur.
units.tr: In the greeting he wishes Timothy: (1) grace, that is, the restoration of the image of God, flowing from the fountain of God's free goodwill; (2) mercy, that is, the free forgiveness of sins, because he knew that this holy young man, moved by the sense of his sins, had daily lain prostrate before God with many tears; (3) peace, that is, tranquillity of conscience and joy arising from the sense of God's favour; and finally, full happiness in the life to come, which is included under peace.

units.la: Verf. 3. Quemadmodum te sum precatus, ut permaneres Ephesi quum proficisceret in Macedoniam, permaneto, ut denunties quibusdam ne diversam doctrinam doceant:
units.tr: Verse 3: As I begged you when I was setting out for Macedonia to remain at Ephesus, remain, so that you may charge certain men not to teach a different doctrine.

units.la: Prima pars Capitis, de recta docendi ratione: in qua postquam confirmavit Timotheo, non Episcopatum ordinarium Ecclesiæ Ephesinæ, sed commissionem specialem temporariam & extraordinariam, repetit mandatum ei datum, de coercendis perversis quibusdam legis zelotis, & de iis commonendis, ne diversam ab Apostolica, doctrinam ullam docerent. In quibus præscribendis, maluit Apostolus rogandi & precandi verbis uti, quam pro imperio loqui, ut vicem rependeret Timotheo qui etiam Apostoli precibus vix solvi potuit (ne ad tempus quidem) a societate Pauli jucundissima.
units.tr: The first part of the chapter concerns the sound method of teaching. In it, after he has made clear to Timothy that he holds not the ordinary episcopate of the church of Ephesus but a special, temporary and extraordinary commission, he repeats the command given to him to restrain certain perverse zealots for the Law, and to warn them not to teach any doctrine different from the apostolic one. In laying down these instructions the apostle preferred to use the words of request and entreaty rather than speak with command, in order to repay Timothy, who could hardly be parted (not even for a time) from Paul's most pleasant company, even by the apostle's entreaties.

units.la: Verf. 4. Nec attendant fabulis & genealogiis infinitis, quæ potius quæstiones præbent, quam ædificationem Dei, quæ est per fidem.
units.tr: Verse 4: Nor should they give heed to fables and endless genealogies, which give rise to questions rather than to the edifying of God, which is in faith.

units.la: Pro exemplo, Vitari jubet speciatim fabulas & genealogias Judaicas, hoc est, dogmata commentitia (sive traditiones præter sacras Scripturas) & curiosas speculationes, de non necessariis, quales sunt Talmudicæ & Cabalisticæ quamplurimæ, quales etiam reperias multas in Scriptoribus, qui Scholastici audiri volunt.
units.tr: As an example, he especially bids them avoid Jewish fables and genealogies, that is, invented doctrines (or traditions beside the holy Scriptures) and curious speculations about things that are not necessary, of which there are very many in the Talmud and the Cabbala, and of which you will find many also in those writers who wish to be heard as scholastics.

units.la: Nunquam ] Rationes admonitionis sunt sex: Ratio prima, Quia inanes illæ speculationes otiosæ sunt, & interminatæ, quarum nec usus est, nec finis.
units.tr: Nor: there are six reasons for the admonition. The first reason: because those empty speculations are idle and endless, having neither use nor end.

units.la: Quæ potius ] Ratio 2. Quia gignunt curiosas & contentiosas quæstiones, nec promovent cognitionem pietatis, quæ ad Deum ducit, liquidem ædificatio non fit per probabiles & incertas opiniones, sed per solidam fidem sermonis Divini.
units.tr: Which give rise: the second reason: because they beget curious and contentious questions and do not advance the knowledge of godliness, which leads to God; for edification is not achieved through probable and uncertain opinions, but through the solid faith in the word of God.

units.la: Verf. 5 Porro finis mandati est charitas ex puro corde, & conscientia bona, & fide non simulata.
units.tr: Verse 5: Now the end of the command is charity out of a pure heart, and a good conscience, and faith unfeigned.

units.la: Ratio 3. Quia doctores illi qui toti sunt in discutiendis minutiis, quae in lege captari possunt, licet zelo legis Mosaicae duci videantur, non tamen referunt legem ad verum suum finem, seu ad scopum genuinum totius Scripturae, qui est ut homines per legem adducti ad cognitionem peccati & miseriae meritae, serio confugiant ad Christum per fidem non fictam.
units.tr: The third reason: because those teachers who are wholly occupied with examining the trifles that can be picked out of the Law, although they seem to be moved by zeal for the Mosaic Law, nevertheless do not refer the Law to its true end, that is, to the genuine aim of the whole of Scripture, which is that men, led by the Law to the knowledge of sin and of deserved misery, should earnestly flee to Christ by a faith that is not feigned.

units.la: Charitas] Hanc fidem describit a triplici effectu: 1. Quod fides vera conscientiam bonam seu tranquillam, & quietam reddat in Christi sanguine propitiatorio: 2. Quod peccata jam conscientia, fides non permittat, ut cor in malo delectetur, sed contendat potius ut mundetur, & ab omnibus pravis affectibus purgetur: 3. Quod fides vera otiosa non sit in bono, sed hominem excitet ad operandum gnaviter in uniuscujusque praecepti obedientia, per charitatem erga Deum & homines.
units.tr: Charity: he describes this faith by a threefold effect: (1) that true faith makes the conscience good, that is, calm and quiet, in the blood of Christ, the propitiatory; (2) that faith, once the conscience has been made aware of sins, does not allow the heart to take delight in evil, but strives rather to be cleansed and purged of all wicked affections; (3) that true faith is not idle in good, but stirs a man to work diligently in obedience to every precept, through love towards God and men.

units.la: Vers. 6. A quibus quum quidam ut a scopo aberrarent, deflexerunt ad vaniloquentiam:
units.tr: Verse 6: From which certain men, having strayed from the mark, have turned aside to vain talking:

units.la: Ratio 4. confirmans priorem, Quia experientia aliquorum comprobatum est, nisi Doctores ab inanibus suis commentis abstinentes, oculos intentos habeant in aedificationem hominum, in fide & in charitate, non posse eos non abripi a simplicitate doctrinae, in loquacem vanitatem: ubi autem est vanitas, non est ibi veritas.
units.tr: The fourth reason, confirming the former: because experience has shown in some cases that unless teachers, abstaining from their empty inventions, keep their eyes fixed on the edification of men in faith and in charity, they cannot fail to be drawn away from the simplicity of doctrine into garrulous vanity; and where there is vanity, there is no truth.

units.la: Vers. 7. Quum velint esse Legis doctores, nec intelligant quae loquuntur, neque de quibus asseverant.
units.tr: Verse 7: Wishing to be teachers of the Law, yet not understanding what they say, nor the matters about which they make assertions.

units.la: Ratio 5. Quia experientia etiam compertum est, ambitiosos illos doctores dum affectarent novam docendi rationem, & laudem ex cognitione legis captarent, ignorantiam suam prodidisse. dum nec quaestiones de quibus, nec argumenta ex quibus disputabant, intelligerent: Ergo evitatis otiosis speculationibus, curandum erat Timotheo, ne in Apostolica doctrina vel ejus docendae ratione, quicquam novaretur a quoquam.
units.tr: The fifth reason: because experience has also shown that those ambitious teachers, while they aimed at a new method of teaching and sought praise from their knowledge of the Law, revealed their ignorance, since they understood neither the questions they discussed nor the arguments they used. Therefore, once idle speculations were set aside, Timothy had to take care that nothing new was introduced by anyone into the apostolic doctrine or into the manner of teaching it.

units.la: Vers. 8. Scimus autem bonam esse Legem, si quis ea legitime utatur.
units.tr: Verse 8: But we know that the Law is good, if a man use it lawfully.

units.la: Respondet objectioni: Ergone legi divinae adversaris, qui tam studiose ejus doctores vellicas? Respondet Apostolus nihil se detrahere legi, reprehendendo eos qui lege abutuntur, sed commendare & docere potius rectum legis usum.
units.tr: He answers an objection: are you, then, opposed to the divine Law, since you so eagerly attack its teachers? The apostle answers that he takes nothing away from the Law by rebuking those who abuse it, but rather commends and teaches the right use of the Law.

units.la: Vers. 9. Nempe sciens Legem justo positam non esse, sed Legis contemgù contemptoribus, & iù qui subjici nescíunt, impiis & peccatoribus, nefariis & profanis, patricidis & matricidis, homicidis,
units.tr: Verse 9: Knowing this, that the Law is not made for the righteous, but for the lawless and disobedient, for the ungodly and sinners, for the wicked and profane, for murderers of fathers and of mothers, for manslayers,

units.la: Vers. 10. Scortatoribus, masculorum concubitoribus, plagiariis, & mendacibus, perjuris, & si quid aliud est quod sanæ doctrinæ sit oppositum:
units.tr: Verse 10: For whoremongers, for those who lie with men, for kidnappers, for liars, for perjurers, and if there is anything else that is contrary to sound doctrine:

units.la: Vers. 11 Quæ est secundum gloriosum Euangelium beati Dei, quod concreditum est mihi,
units.tr: Verse 11: According to the glorious gospel of the blessed God, which was committed to my trust.

units.la: Confirmat responsionem tribus rationibus: Prima est à fine legis seu legalis Fœderis, quatenus opponitur Euangelio, Lex lata est non ut fideles justificati jam per fidem in Christum, justificarentur per legem (sicut perversi legis doctores intendebant) sed ut injusti & infideles, quales sunt omnes flagitiosi & profani per legem condemnati, suam injustitiam & meritam condemnationem agnoscerent, resipiscerent, & ad Christum confugerent: Nihil igitur Apostolica doctrina legi detrahit.
units.tr: He confirms the answer with three reasons. The first is drawn from the end of the Law, or of the legal covenant, as it is opposed to the gospel: the Law was given not so that the faithful, already justified through faith in Christ, should be justified by the Law (as the perverse teachers of the Law intended), but so that the unrighteous and unbelieving, such as all the wicked and profane who are condemned by the Law, might recognise their unrighteousness and deserved condemnation, repent, and flee to Christ. Therefore apostolic doctrine takes nothing away from the Law.

units.la: Secundum ] Ratio 2. Omnia peccata quæ prohibentur à lege, prohibentur etiam à sana doctrina gloriosi Euangelii, & omnia officia quæ lege præcipiuntur, studiosè docentur, & urgentur in Euangelio, quantum scilicet ad obedientiam Deo præstandam, ad gratitudinem erga ipsum ostendendam sufficit, & ad fidei sinceritatem in fructibus sanctitatis probandam attinet. Nihil ergo doctrina Euangelii detrahit legi.
units.tr: Secondly: the second reason: all the sins forbidden by the Law are also forbidden by the sound doctrine of the glorious gospel, and all the duties commanded by the Law are diligently taught and urged in the gospel, as far as is needed for rendering obedience to God, for showing gratitude towards him, and for proving the sincerity of faith by the fruits of holiness. Therefore the doctrine of the gospel takes nothing away from the Law.

units.la: Concreditum ] Ratio 3. Ego Apostolus cui concreditum est Euangelium Dei, (in se beatissimi, & omnis benedictionis erga nos Authoris) non minus urgeo hanc sanam doctrinam de sanctitatis, & omnium bonorum operum quæ in lege præcipiuntur, studio, quam quivis legis zelota, licet non eodem fine: Ergo Apostolica doctrina legi ne quicquam detrahit.
units.tr: Committed: the third reason: I, the apostle to whom the gospel of God has been committed (God being most blessed in himself and the author of every blessing towards us), urge this sound doctrine of holiness, and of all good works which are commanded in the Law, no less earnestly than any zealot for the Law, although not with the same aim. Therefore apostolic doctrine takes nothing away from the Law at all.

units.la: Secunda pars Capitis.
units.tr: The second part of the chapter.

units.la: Vers. 12. Gratiam igitur ei habeo, qui me robustum effecit, id est, Christo Iesu Domino nostro, quod me fidelem duxerit, ut qui me in ministerio constituerit:
units.tr: Verse 12. I thank him who has made me strong, that is, Christ Jesus our Lord, because he judged me faithful and appointed me to the ministry:

units.la: Secunda pars Capitis in qua autoritatem sui Apostolatus vendicat adversus eos, qui vel eam negarent, vel propter anteactam vitam extenuarent idque gratias agendo pro gratia sibi concessa, Gratiarum actiones onis rationes sunt septem, quæ omnes probant nihil detrahendum autoritati Apostolatus Pauli.
units.tr: The second part of the chapter, in which he claims the authority of his apostleship against those who either denied it or belittled it because of his former life. He does this by giving thanks for the grace granted to him. There are seven reasons for this thanksgiving, and all of them show that nothing should be taken away from the authority of Paul's apostleship.

units.la: Ratio prima, Christus me infirmum, & olim mancipium peccati, Diaboli, & Mundi, Apostolum à se constitutum, gratia Spiritus Sancti roboravit, ut tanquam Antesignanus pro Euangelii defensione invicto starem animo, contra omnes mundi, carnis, & Satanæ insultus: Ergo de confirmatione Apostolatus mei Deo gratiæ agendæ sunt, tantum abest, ut meæ authoritati quicquam detrahi debeat.
units.tr: First reason: Christ strengthened me, though I was weak and once a slave of sin, of the Devil and of the world, and he appointed me an apostle by the grace of the Holy Spirit. He did this so that, like a standard-bearer defending the gospel, I might stand with an unconquered mind against all the assaults of the world, the flesh and Satan. Therefore thanks are to be given to God for the confirmation of my apostleship. So far is it from being the case that anything should be taken from my authority.

units.la: Fidum duxerit ] Ratio 2. Christus me Apostolum constitutum, donis sui Spiritus imbuit, & eousque honoravit, ut amicum suum fidelem me & faceret & haberet, cui thesaurum Euangelii sui committeret, dispensandum pauperibus suorum electorum animabus: Ergo authoritati meæ nihil detrahendum.
units.tr: Judged faithful: second reason. Christ, having appointed me an apostle, endowed me with the gifts of his Spirit and honoured me so greatly that he made me his faithful friend and regarded me as such. He entrusted to me the treasure of his gospel, to be dispensed to the souls of his poor elect. Therefore nothing is to be taken from my authority.

units.la: Constituit ] Ratio 3. Christus ipse Dominus me constituit in Ministerio, id est, in officio Apostolatus, ut prædicationi Euangelii totus incumberem segregatus à mundo ad hoc negotium: Quis ergo est qui meæ autoritati detractum ire audeat?
units.tr: Appointed: third reason. Christ the Lord himself appointed me to the ministry, that is, to the office of apostle, so that I should devote myself wholly to the preaching of the gospel, set apart from the world for this work. Who then would dare to detract from my authority?

units.la: Verf. 13. Qui prius eram blasphemus & persequutor, & injurios: sed mei misertus est, nam ignorans id faciebam fidei expers.
units.tr: Verse 13. I who was before a blasphemer, and a persecutor, and injurious: but I obtained mercy, because I did it ignorantly, in unbelief.

units.la: Ratio 4. Per scelera & pestilina merita vitæ meæ anteactæ Deus non est impeditus, ne assumeret me in servum suum, qui olim eram hostis. Quis igitur meæ autoritati detrahat ob prioris vitæ scelera?
units.tr: Fourth reason. Through the crimes and pestilential deserts of my former life, God was not prevented from taking me into his service, though I had once been his enemy. Who then would detract from my authority on account of the crimes of my earlier life?

units.la: Nam ignorans ] Occurrit objectioni, Diceret enim aliquis quomodo fieri potuit, ut tam apertus Christi hostis consequeretur veniam?
units.tr: For ignorantly: he meets an objection. For someone might say: how could it happen that so open an enemy of Christ obtained pardon?

units.la: Respondet peccatum suum fuisse ex ignorantia: atque ita probat peccatum suum non fuisse irremissibile illud peccatum in Spiritum Sanctum, seu malitiosam illam insurrectionem adversus Christum, qua Diabolici hostes Euangelii hostiliter, scientes, volentes se opponunt regno Christi cognito, sed peccatum ex ignorantia admissum, dum adhuc infidelis esset.
units.tr: He answers that his sin came from ignorance. In this way he shows that his sin was not that unpardonable sin against the Holy Spirit, namely the malicious rebellion against Christ by which the diabolical enemies of the gospel knowingly and willingly set themselves hostilely against the kingdom of Christ once it is known. His sin was committed in ignorance, while he was still an unbeliever.

units.la: Verf. 14 Superabundavit autem Domini nostri cum fide & dilectione in Christo Iesu
units.tr: Verse 14. But the grace of our Lord was exceedingly abundant, with faith and love which are in Christ Jesus.

units.la: Ratio 5. Non mediocrem seu ordinariam mensuram fidei, & dilectionis concessit mihi Deus, sed superabundanter gratiam suam ostendit in eximia donorum salvificorum collatione: Idcirco non est quod quis autoritati meæ propter anteactam vitam meam quicquam detrahat.
