units.tr: Fifth reason. God granted me not a mediocre or ordinary measure of faith and love, but showed his grace superabundantly in the outstanding bestowal of saving gifts. Therefore there is no reason why anyone should detract from my authority on account of my former life.

units.la: Verf. 15. Fidus est hic sermo, & modis omnibus dignus quem amplectamur, Christum Iesum venisse in mundum, ut peccatores salvaret, quorum primus sum ego.
units.tr: Verse 15. This is a faithful saying, and worthy of all acceptation, that Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners, of whom I am chief.

units.la: Ratio 6. Christus eximia sua in me misericordia effecit, ut experientia edoctus sententiæ illi Euangelicæ, de Christi persona, officio, adventu, virtute, merito & efficacia ad servandum peccatores primus subscribere cogar, tanquam peccatorum meo judicio dux, ita ut illius sententiæ veritatem & utilitatem non possim, quin palam toti mundo deprædicem. Nam expertus dico: Certus est hic sermo, &c. Nihil ergo autoritati meæ detrahendum, qui non tantum quod commissum mihi est, ipse credo, sed etiam quod expertus sum prædico.
units.tr: Sixth reason. By his remarkable mercy towards me, Christ has made it so that, taught by experience, I am bound to be the first to subscribe to that evangelical saying concerning the person, office, coming, power, merit and efficacy of Christ in saving sinners. In my own judgement I am the leader of sinners, so I cannot but openly proclaim to the whole world the truth and usefulness of that saying. For I speak from experience: This saying is certain, etc. Therefore nothing is to be taken from my authority, since I not only believe what has been committed to me, but also proclaim what I have experienced.

units.la: Verf. 16. Verum ideo misertus est mei, ut in me primo ostenderet Iesus Christus omnem clementiam, ut essem exemplo credituris ipsi in vitam æternam.
units.tr: Verse 16. Howbeit for this cause I obtained mercy, that in me first Jesus Christ might show forth all long-suffering, for a pattern to them which should hereafter believe on him to life everlasting.

units.la: Ratio 7. Dominus posuit me in exemplum suæ longanimitatis, misericordiæ, bonitatis, & gratiæ admirabilis; ita ut peccatores in finem usque mundi, qui meam conversionem admirabilem, & Dei erga me benignitatem audient, confirmari possint abundè de Christi misericordia, & bene sperare de simili erga se bonitate ostendenda, oculos dirigentes in me, tanquam typum & exemplar ineffabilis misericordiæ. Ergo maximè idoneus fuit, quem Christus suæ gratiæ præconem constitueret, tantum abest ut quidquam detrahatur autoritati meæ, propter priorem conversationem, dum infidelis eram.
units.tr: Seventh reason. The Lord has set me forth as an example of his long-suffering, mercy, goodness and wonderful grace. Sinners until the end of the world, who hear of my remarkable conversion and of God's kindness towards me, may be fully confirmed in the mercy of Christ and hope well of a similar goodness shown towards themselves, fixing their eyes on me as a type and pattern of ineffable mercy. Therefore he was most fitting to be appointed by Christ as the herald of his grace. So far is it from being the case that anything should be taken from my authority on account of my earlier conduct, when I was an unbeliever.

units.la: Verf. 17. Regi autem æterno, immortali, invisibili, soli sapienti Deo, honor & gloria in secula seculorum. Amen.
units.tr: Verse 17. Now unto the King eternal, immortal, invisible, the only wise God, be honour and glory for ever and ever. Amen.

units.la: Apostolus beneficii magnitudine jam affectus, nec sibi in ejus amplificatione satisfaciens, gratiarum actione pathetice sermonem concludit, cum insigni celebratione Christi, cujus quatuor epitheta obiter adducit, quæ sic Christo conveniunt, ut Patri etiam, & Spiritui Sancto conveniant: 1. Epithetum est Deus seu Christus qua Deus, est Rex seculorum, id est, per Hebraismum, Rex æternus, ut distinguatur à mundanis & mortalibus regibus: 2. Epithetum incorruptibilis, quia Deus omnis alterationis, mutationis, & corruptionis est expers, & semper est idem ipse sui similis: 3. Epithetum invisibilis, quia neque oculis, neque ullis sensibus comprehendi potest, quippe quorum facultates sunt corporeæ, & angustis finibus terminatæ: 4. Est solus Sapiens, quia solus novit omnia, non per objecta, neque per λογισμόν, sed in seipso, per seipsum, & à seipso, utpote in quo omnia sunt, ut in efficiente primo, & ut in fine ultimo. Hinc Apostolus ascribit Deo honorem, seu testificationem eminentiæ, & gloriam, quæ est clara fama cum laude, quæ Deo debentur in æternum, appendens Amen, tanquam fidei & voluntatis suæ impensæ ad Deum glorificandum, sigillum.
units.tr: The apostle, already moved by the greatness of the benefit and not satisfied in himself with its magnification, concludes his thanksgiving with a fervent note. He gives a notable celebration of Christ, briefly adducing four epithets which belong to Christ in such a way that they also belong to the Father and the Holy Spirit. (1) The first epithet is that God, or Christ as God, is the King of ages, that is, by Hebraism, the eternal King, so as to be distinguished from worldly and mortal kings. (2) The epithet incorruptible, because God is free from all alteration, change and corruption, and is always the same as himself. (3) The epithet invisible, because he cannot be comprehended by the eyes or by any of the senses, since their faculties are corporeal and confined within narrow limits. (4) He is the only Wise, because he alone knows all things, not through objects or through reasoning, but in himself, through himself and from himself, since all things are in him, as in the first efficient cause and in the final end. Hence the apostle ascribes to God honour, that is, the testimony of eminence, and glory, which is clear fame with praise, due to God for ever. He appends Amen as a seal of his faith and of the will he has devoted to glorifying God.

units.la: Tertia pars Capitis.
units.tr: The third part of the chapter.

units.la: Verf. 18. Hoc mandatum commendo tibi, fili Timothee, nempe ut secundum prægressa de te prophetias, milites per eas bonam illam militiam.
units.tr: Verse 18. This charge I commit to you, son Timothy, namely that, in keeping with the prophecies made about you beforehand, you wage by them that good warfare.

units.la: Tertia pars Capitis, in qua hortatur Timotheum ut strenuè se gerat in Ministerio, nempe ut militet bonam militiam, seu ut contra omnes hostes, & omnia impedimenta se paret ad pugnam, omnemque fidem & diligentiam adhibeat, ne quid detrimenti Dei Ecclesia capiat à quoquam.
units.tr: The third part of the chapter, in which he urges Timothy to conduct himself vigorously in the ministry, namely to wage the good warfare: that is, to arm himself for battle against all enemies and all hindrances, and to bring all faith and diligence to bear, so that the Church of God suffers no loss from anyone.

units.la: Secundum ] Argumenta hortationis sunt duo: Argumentum 1. Quia de te quædam Prophetice divino quodam instinctu à viris piis prædicta sunt, quæ spem insignem faciebant rerum à te præclarè gerendarum, (ut apparet ex Act. 16. 2.) Militia igitur bonam militiam.
units.tr: Secundum] The arguments for the exhortation are two. Argument 1: because certain things were foretold about you by pious men through a kind of divine prompting, things which raised a remarkable hope that you would do excellent work (as appears from Acts 16:2). Therefore wage the good warfare.

units.la: Verf. 19. Retinens fidem & bonam conscientiam, quia repulsa, nonnulli fidei naufragium fecerunt.
units.tr: Verse 19. Holding fast faith and a good conscience, which some, having thrust it away, have made shipwreck of faith.

units.la: Hortationem explicat, ostendendo militandi modum, nempe ut sanam doctrinam firmiter tueatur & profiteatur, & simul sancte vivendo secundum prædicatam à se veritatem, bonæ conscientiæ lucem & pacem conservet, quæ ipsum interius admonitura erat de officio erga Deum & homines, si loquentem audiret, & consolationem ministratura, si pro veritatis defensione quicquam pateretur.
units.tr: He explains the exhortation by showing the manner of warfare: namely, that he firmly guard and profess sound doctrine, and at the same time, by living holily in accordance with the truth he has preached, preserve the light and peace of a good conscience. This conscience would inwardly admonish him about his duty toward God and men, if he listened to the one speaking, and would minister consolation, should he suffer anything in defence of the truth.

units.la: Qua expulsi ] Arg. 2. Quia nisi strenuè te geras, & hanc militiæ legem de jungenda bona conscientia cum fidei professione observes, periculum est, ne amissa bona conscientia naufragium sanæ doctrinæ, seu professionis fidei etiam facias, sicut jam fecerunt nonnulli: Idcirco militia bonam militiam: Interim hic non injicit Timotheo scrupulum de perseverantiæ ipsius incertitudine, sed adhibet optimum argumentum & efficacissimum ad persuadendum ut perseveret: Nihil enim refert in hypotheticis potheticis propositionibus, quod ejus partes separatim, & categoricè sumptæ sint falsæ vel impoflibiles, satis est ad connexi axiomatis veritatem, quod connexio partium sit certa.
units.tr: Qua expulsi] Argument 2: unless you conduct yourself vigorously, and observe this law of warfare of joining a good conscience with the profession of faith, there is a danger that, having lost a good conscience, you will also make shipwreck of sound doctrine, or of the profession of faith, as some have already done. Therefore wage the good warfare. Meanwhile he does not here cast into Timothy's mind a doubt about his own perseverance; rather he applies a very good and most effective argument to persuade him to persevere. For it makes no difference in hypothetical propositions that their parts, taken separately and categorically, are false or impossible; it is enough for the truth of the connected statement that the connection of the parts is certain.

units.la: Vers. 20. Ex qubus Hymenæus & Alexander: quos tradidi Satanæ, ut discerent non blasphemare.
units.tr: Verse 20. Of whom are Hymenaeus and Alexander, whom I delivered to Satan, that they might learn not to blaspheme.

units.la: Pro exemplo Apostolus nominat duos Apostatas, Hymenæum & Alexandrum, quos non ita pridem tradiderat Satanæ, id est, excommunicaverat: nam qui à facie Dei lucente in Ecclesiâ ejiciuntur, cadunt in Satanæ regnum, quo ad externi hominis conditionem, seu quo ad privilegiorum Ecclesiasticarum possessionem: Hujus excommunicationis finem ostendit hunc esse, ut poenitentia ducti desinerent doctrinam fidei blasphemare, utque humiliati ad veritatem rectè cognoscendam, & profitendam reverterentur: nam de ipsorum fide in Christum plane deperditâ Apostolus non pronunciat, sed contia, spem fovet de ipsorum resipiscentia & salute possibili, & futura.
units.tr: As an example the Apostle names two apostates, Hymenaeus and Alexander, whom not long before he had delivered to Satan, that is, excommunicated. For those who are cast out from the face of God shining in the Church fall into the kingdom of Satan, as regards the condition of the outward man, or as regards the possession of ecclesiastical privileges. He shows that the end of this excommunication was that, led to repentance, they might cease to blaspheme the doctrine of faith, and that, humbled, they might return to know and profess the truth rightly. For the Apostle does not pronounce that their faith in Christ was utterly lost; on the contrary, he cherishes hope of their repentance and of their possible and future salvation.

units.la: Caput Secundum.
units.tr: Chapter Two.

units.la: HOC Capite praecepta dat quatuor, quibus instituantur omnes Fideles, quomodo in publicis Ecclesiæ conventibus se rectè gerere debeant, viri pariter & fœminæ.
units.tr: In this chapter he gives four precepts, by which all the faithful are taught how men and women alike ought to conduct themselves rightly in the public assemblies of the Church.

units.la: Verf. 1. Adhortor igitur ante omnia, ut fiant deprecationes, preces, postulationes, gratiarum actiones pro quibusvis hominibus:
units.tr: Verse 1. I exhort therefore, that first of all, supplications, prayers, intercessions, and thanksgivings be made for all men:

units.la: Præceptum primum, Ne in conventu Ecclesiæ potissimùm negligantur preces, sed ut fiant deprecationes pro malis avertendis, & precationes pro bonis obtinendis, & intercessiones pro aliis hominibus, & gratiarum actiones pro beneficiis acceptis in publicis precibus, quas tota Ecclesia præeunte Pastore concipere debet, & quidem pro quibuslibet (cujuscunque sint conditionis vel sortis) hominibus.
units.tr: The first precept: that in the assembly of the Church prayers must not be neglected. Supplications are to be made for averting evils, petitions for obtaining good things, intercessions for other men, and thanksgivings for benefits received. These are to be offered in public prayers, which the whole Church ought to frame with the minister leading, and indeed for men of every condition and rank.

units.la: Verf. 2. Pro regibus & quibusvis in eminentia constitutis: ut tranquillam ac quietam vitam degamus, cum omni pietate, & honestate. Explicat praeceptum specialius, & precari jubet nominatim pro regibus, & quibusvis magistratibus in eminentia constitutis, qui quoniam ad clavum reipublicae sedent, nobis debent esse clarissimi, eorumque mentio in Ecclesiae precationibus eo ipso nomine à nobis, debet fieri.
units.tr: Verse 2. For kings and all that are in authority, that we may lead a quiet and peaceable life, in all godliness and honesty. He explains the precept more specifically and bids us pray by name for kings and all magistrates set in high place. Since they sit at the helm of the commonwealth, they ought to be most illustrious to us, and for that very reason their mention must be made by us in the Church's prayers.

units.la: Ut tranquillam ] Rationes praecepti sunt novem: Ratio prima à fine utili, quia magistratibus salvis, & in pace officium suum administrantibus, licebit fidelibus pacatam & tranquillam vitam degere, in pietate, seu obedientia primae tabulae; & honestate, seu obedientia secundae tabulae: Ergo pro iis orandum.
units.tr: That we may lead a quiet] There are nine reasons for the precept. The first is from a useful end: when magistrates are safe and administer their office in peace, the faithful will be permitted to live a peaceful and quiet life, in godliness, that is, obedience to the first table of the law, and in honesty, that is, obedience to the second table. Therefore we must pray for them.

units.la: Verf. 3. Nam hoc bonum est & acceptum coram Servatore nostro DEO:
units.tr: Verse 3. For this is good and acceptable in the sight of God our Saviour:

units.la: Ratio 2. Precari pro regibus & cujusvis ordinis hominibus, bonum est (seu acceptum Deo: Ergo pro quibusvis orandum, Dicitur Deus noster Servator, quia etiamsi Christus Servator sit, officio speciali, operatione tamen in officii executione non nisi cum Patre & Spiritu Sancto nos actu servat.
units.tr: Reason 2. To pray for kings and for men of every rank is good, that is, acceptable to God. Therefore we must pray for all men. God is called our Saviour because, although Christ is Saviour by a special office, yet in executing that office he actually saves us only together with the Father and the Holy Spirit.

units.la: Verf. 4. Qui quosvis homines vult servari, & ad agnitionem veritatis venire.
units.tr: Verse 4. Who will have all men to be saved, and to come unto the knowledge of the truth.

units.la: Ratio 3. confirmans priorem: Deus vult omnis generis homines, (& proinde aliquos ex regibus & magistratibus, & cujusvis ordinis hominibus) servari, & ad fidem Euangelii pervenire. Ergo etiam vult nos pro omnis generis hominibus precari, & nominatim pro regibus, & in eminentia constitutis, de quibus tenemur bene sperare.
units.tr: Reason 3, confirming the previous one: God wills men of every kind (and therefore some of the kings and magistrates, and men of every rank) to be saved and to come to the faith of the Gospel. Therefore he also wills us to pray for men of every kind, and by name for kings and those set in high place, concerning whom we are bound to hope well.

units.la: Verf. 5. Unus enim Deus, unus etiam Mediator Dei & hominum, homo Christus Iesus:
units.tr: Verse 5. For there is one God, and one mediator between God and men, the man Christ Jesus:

units.la: Ratio 4. Etiamsi multis modis à se invicem distinguantur, & discriminentur inter se homines, multique ordines sint, quorum multi alieni sunt à fide, & multi insuper fidei etiam hostes, satis tamen est ad precandum pro quibusvis, quod Deus sit unus: sub cujus potestate & imperio omnes continentur, & quod Deus sit pariter Deus Judaeorum & Gentium sine προσωπολημψια: Ergo pro quibusvis orandum.
units.tr: Reason 4. Even if men are distinguished and set apart from one another in many ways, and there are many orders of them, many of whom are foreign to the faith and many of whom are even enemies of the faith, it is nevertheless enough, for praying for all, that God is one, under whose power and rule all are contained, and that God is equally the God of Jews and Gentiles, without partiality [προσωπολημψία]. Therefore we must pray for all.

units.la: Vnus etiam Mediator ] Ratio 5: Quaecunque sunt inter homines intervalla & distantiae, quibus à se invicem separari possint, satis tamen est ad precandum pro quibusvis, quod omnibus Gentibus, & omnis conditionis hominibus, unicus Mediator positus sit inter Deum & homines, per quem accessus patet omnibus ad eum accedentibus. Ergo pro quibusvis est orandum.
units.tr: One mediator also] Reason 5. Whatever intervals and distances there are between men, by which they may be separated from one another, it is nevertheless enough, for praying for all, that a single Mediator has been set between God and men for all Gentiles and men of every condition, through whom access lies open to all who come to him. Therefore we must pray for all.

units.la: Homo ] Ratio 6. Satis est ad precandum pro quibusvis hominibus, quod unus ille omnium Mediator sit Homo, per incarnationem Verbi, communi vinculo naturæ humanæ, hominibus omnibus conjunctus, nempe I e sus C h r i s t u s, qui pro quibusvis, hoc est, pro ovibus suis, ex omni hominum genere collectis intercedit. Ergo pro quibusvis est orandum.
units.tr: Man] Reason 6. It is enough, for praying for all men, that that one Mediator of all is Man, through the incarnation of the Word, joined to all men by the common bond of human nature. This is Jesus Christ, who intercedes for all, that is, for his sheep gathered from every kind of men. Therefore we must pray for all.

units.la: Vers. 6. Qui semetipsum dedit redemptionis pretium pro quibusvis, Christus inquam, testimonium illud suis temporibus destinatum-
units.tr: Verse 6. Who gave himself a ransom for all, Christ I mean, to be testified in due time-

units.la: Ratio 7. C h r i s t u s dedit semetipsum plenum & sufficiens pretium redemptionis, pro omnis generis hominibus: Ergo pro quibusvis, seu pro omnis generis hominibus precandum est.
units.tr: Reason 7. Christ gave himself as a full and sufficient price of redemption for men of every kind. Therefore we must pray for all, that is, for men of every kind.

units.la: Testimonium ] Ratio 8. Euangelium seu testimonium de C h r i s t i redemptione omnis generis hominum, quod Deus idoneis temporibus revelare destinaverat, jam patefactum est: Ergo etiam per preces fusas, pro quovis genere hominum, in Christianis Ecclesiis proferendum est hujus veritatis Testimonium.
units.tr: Testimony] Reason 8. The Gospel, or testimony of Christ's redemption of men of every kind, which God had determined to reveal in fitting times, has now been made known. Therefore this testimony of the truth must also be set forth in the Christian churches, through prayers poured out for every kind of men.

units.la: Vers. 7 Cujus constitutus sum ego Præco & Apostolus (veritatem dico per Christum, non mentior) Doctor, inquam, Gentium cum fide ac veritate.
units.tr: Verse 7. Whereunto I am ordained a preacher, and an apostle (I speak the truth in Christ, and lie not), a teacher of the Gentiles in faith and verity.

units.la: Ratio 9. Prædicatio hujus Testimonii seu Euangelii, & doctrinæ de pretio Redemptionis pro omnis generis hominibus, à C h r i s t o persoluto, specialiter commissa est mihi, ut sim Doctor etiam Gentium, ad eas instituendum in fide, & veritate omni, quæ ad vitam æternam ducit, Cum ergo ego sciam servandos esse multos ex Gentibus, idque jam publice vos doceam, precationes pro quibusvis hominibus publice fieri debent in Christianis Ecclesiis omnibus. Interim, quia noverat aliquot ex Judæis ægre laturos mentionem Apostolatus sui, & legationis ad Gentes, confirmat dictum de missione sua ad Gentes gravi asseveratione, ne quis dubitaret.
units.tr: Reason 9. The preaching of this testimony, or Gospel, and of the doctrine concerning the price of redemption for men of every kind, paid by Christ, has been specially committed to me, so that I should be a teacher also of the Gentiles, to instruct them in faith and in all truth that leads to eternal life. Since therefore I know that many of the Gentiles are to be saved, and already teach you this publicly, prayers for all men must be made publicly in all Christian churches. Meanwhile, because he knew that some of the Jews would bear the mention of his apostleship and his mission to the Gentiles with difficulty, he confirms what he said about his sending to the Gentiles with a solemn asseveration, lest anyone should doubt it.

units.la: Vers. 8. Velim igitur viros precari in quovis loco, puras manus attollentes, absque ira & disceptatione.
units.tr: Verse 8. I will therefore that men pray every where, lifting up holy hands, without wrath and doubting.

units.la: Reliqua quæ sequuntur spectant ad circumstantias publici cultus, Sequitur ergo præceptum 2. De personis ad publicas preces in Ecclefia concipiendas, idoneis: Item de loco & dispositionibus, cum ani- mæ tum corporis, ad eam rem accommodatis.
units.tr: The remaining things that follow concern the circumstances of public worship. Therefore there follows a second precept, concerning the persons fit to offer public prayers in the Church; likewise concerning place and bodily and spiritual dispositions suited to that purpose.

units.la: Quod ad personas attinet, Jubet viros tantùm in Ecclesia loqui, & cætui in precibus præcedere, non fœminas.
units.tr: As to persons, he bids only men, and not women, to speak in the Church and to lead the assembly in prayer.

units.la: Quod ad locum attinet, discrimen locorum quod erat in veteri Testamento (quando ad Templum Hierofolymitanum ter quotannis conveniendum, & facies convertenda erat ad Sanctuarium, sive propius sive longius abessent à Templo,) ostendit sublatum jam esse secundùm prædictionem Christi, Ioan 4. & libertatem jam concessam esse, ut quovis loco Christiani honestè & decorè cœtus suos celebrarent.
units.tr: As to place, the distinction of places that existed in the Old Testament (when they had to gather at the Temple of Jerusalem three times a year, and to turn their faces toward the sanctuary, whether they lived nearer or farther from the Temple) he shows to be now abolished, according to Christ's prediction, John 4, and freedom has now been granted for Christians to celebrate their assemblies honestly and decently in any place.

units.la: Quod ad corpus attinet, Requirit ut gestus istiusmodi sit, qui testificetur reverentiam Divini Numinis, ardoremque precandi accendat, qualis gestus, Exempli gratia est, manuum elevatio, sive illæ expansæ, sive junctæ fuerint.
units.tr: As to the body, he requires a gesture of such a kind as witnesses reverence for the divine majesty and kindles the fervour of prayer. Such a gesture is, for example, the lifting up of hands, whether they are held outstretched or joined.

units.la: Quod ad totum hominem, animamque imprimis spectat, requirit, primo, vitæ integritatem & innocentiam, quam per manuum puritatem intelligit: 2. Ut absint iræ, simultates, omnesque pravi affectus, ut ὁμοθυμαδὸν inter se consentiant omnes: 3 Ut ablit disceptatio seu dubitatio, an Deus audire velit, seu concedere quæ secundùm ipsius voluntatem revelatam petimus ab Eo nos, quicunque accedimus ad Ipsum per Christum.
units.tr: As to the whole man, and especially the soul, he requires, first, integrity and innocence of life, which he understands by purity of hands; second, that anger, quarrels, and all wicked affections be absent, so that all agree together with one mind [ὁμοθυμαδόν]; third, that doubt or disputing be absent, whether God is willing to hear us, and to grant those things which we ask according to his revealed will, we who approach him through Christ.

units.la: Verf. 9. Itidem & mulieres amictu honesto, cum verecundia & modestia ornare sese, non cincinnis, vel auro, vel margaritis, vel pretioso vestitu:
units.tr: Verse 9. In like manner also, that women adorn themselves in modest apparel, with shamefastness and sobriety; not with broided hair, or gold, or pearls, or costly array;

units.la: Præceptum 3. Ut mulieres dum unà cum cœtu precantur, sacrisque reliquis interfuint, in vestitu, reliquoque omni habitu, componant se ad honestatem, verecundiam & modestiam, quæ majori futura sunt ipsis ornamento, quam si cincinnis, vel auro, vel margaritis, vel pretiolo vestitu amictæ prodirent in publicum: in quibus si luxus appareat, ornatus illicitus est, & hoc loco prohibitus.
units.tr: Precept 3. That women, while they pray together with the assembly and take part in the rest of the sacred duties, should arrange their dress and all other attire toward decency, modesty and sobriety, which will be a greater ornament to them than if they came out in public adorned with braided hair, gold, pearls, or costly clothing. If luxury appears in these things, the ornament is unlawful and is forbidden in this place.

units.la: Verf. 10. Sed (quod decet mulieres pietatem spondentes) operibus bonis.
units.tr: Verse 10. But (as is fitting for women who profess godliness) by good works.

units.la: Requirit præterea ad ornatum mulierum, & privatum & publicum, ut bonis operibus inclarefcant: cujus ratio redditur à professione Christiana, fiana, qua in Baptismo spoponderunt se vanitati, & pompæ mundanæ renunciaturas.
units.tr: Moreover, it is required of women's adornment, both private and public, that they shine forth with good works. The reason for this is given from their Christian profession, by which, in Baptism, they promised that they would renounce vanity and worldly pomp.

units.la: Vers. 11. Mulier cum silentio discito cum omni subjectione.
units.tr: Verse 11. Let the woman learn in silence with all subjection.

units.la: Præceptum 4. Ut mulieres in Ecclesiasticis conventibus discentium partes obeant semper; docentium nunquam: & ut discant cum silentio, idque in agnitione infirmitatis, & subjectionis naturalis sui sexus, licet dotibus personalibus, multis Viris quædam Fœminæ superiores esse possint.
units.tr: Fourth precept: that women in ecclesiastical assemblies always take the part of learners, never of teachers; and that they learn in silence, acknowledging their weakness and natural subjection of their sex, even though some women may be superior to many men in personal gifts.

units.la: Vers. 12. Mulieri enim docere non permitto, neque authoritatem usurpare in virum, sed esse in silentio.
units.tr: Verse 12. For I do not permit a woman to teach, nor to usurp authority over the man, but to be in silence.

units.la: Explicat præceptum specialius, & pro authoritate prohibet fœminas publicè docendi partibus.
units.tr: He explains the precept more specifically, and on the basis of authority he forbids women the role of teaching publicly.

units.la: Neque authoritatem ] Rationes prohibitionis sunt tres: Ratio prima in posteriori parte prohibitionis continetur, quia si mulier doceret publicè, authoritatem etiam haberet mulier in virum; præesset, & institueret virum illa, quæ subesse, & subjici viro debet cum silentio.
units.tr: "Nor to usurp authority" — There are three reasons for the prohibition. The first reason is contained in the latter part of the prohibition: if a woman taught publicly, she would also have authority over the man; she would preside over him and instruct him, she who ought to be subordinate and subject to the man in silence.

units.la: Vers. 13. Adam enim prior formatus est, deinde Eva.
units.tr: Verse 13. For Adam was formed first, then Eve.

units.la: Ratio 2. confirmans priorem, Dignior est virilis sexus quam muliebris: Nam Adam Mas prior formatus est, & non propter Evam fœminam, sed Eva fœmina posterior propter marem Adamum formata est: Ergo arceri debet fœmina à docendi officio in Ecclesia.
units.tr: The second reason, confirming the first: the male sex is more worthy than the female. For Adam, the male, was formed first, and not on account of Eve the female; rather Eve, the female, was formed later, on account of the male Adam. Therefore the female ought to be kept from the office of teaching in the Church.

units.la: Vers. 14. Et Adam non fuit seductus: sed mulier seducta causa transgressionis fuit.
units.tr: Verse 14. And Adam was not deceived, but the woman, being deceived, was in the transgression.

units.la: Ratio 3. Seductio prima, & peccatum primum non fuit per marem, seu Adamum primò, sed per Evam, quæ decepta à diabolo maiito suasit, ut transgrederetur mandatum: Idcirco à Deo constitutum est, ut postea viro esset subdita, non verò virum publice doceret; Atque hæ rationes sufficiunt ut saltem in Ecclesia, ubi de animabus agitur, non præsideat fœmina.
units.tr: The third reason: the first deception and the first sin came not through the man, or Adam first, but through Eve, who, deceived by the devil, persuaded her husband to transgress the command. For this reason God ordained that she should afterwards be subject to her husband, and should not publicly teach the man. And these reasons are sufficient to ensure that, at least in the Church, where souls are the concern, a woman should not preside.

units.la: Vers. 15. Servabitur tamen liberos gignendo, si manserit in fide ac charitate, & sanctificatione cum modestia.
units.tr: Verse 15. Yet she shall be saved through bearing children, if they continue in faith and charity, and in holiness with modesty.

units.la: Solvit objectionem, & consolatur fœminam adversus seclusionem, ab officio Pastorali Ecclesiastico, adversus introitum peccati in mundum per eam, adversus subjectionem sexus, & adversus reliqua quæ fœmineum genus consequuntur, incommoda, ex eo quod neque hæc prohibitio hibitio à Paftoratu Ecclesiastico, neque mala hæc recitata impeditura essent mulieris, seu mulierum salutem, modò verâ fide præditæ fuerint, & in ea permanserint, constanter colentes charitatem, sanctitatem & modestiam, cæterosque veræ fidei fructus in vocatione sua domestica, quæ plerunque, & ordinariò exercetur in liberis pariendis, alendis, & educandis, (sub quo officio, metonymicè continentur officia omnia reliqua, quæ ad familiam pertinent, ad quæ destinata est fœmina, ut ea curet pro munere suo in privatis ædibus) & promittit Apostolus fore, ut verè fideles fœminæ, non minùs quam fideles viri, vel fideles Pastores Ecclesiæ, salutem consequantur æternam in hac ipsarum subjectione, tam certò & facilè, quam si ad Ecclesiasticum docendi munus admissæ fuissent; in quo munere non possent salvari, nisi etiam præditæ essent ejusmodi fide quæ per dilectionem & opera bona veram & efficacem se demonstraret.
units.tr: The Apostle answers the objection and comforts the woman against her exclusion from the ecclesiastical pastoral office, against the entry of sin into the world through her, against the subjection of her sex, and against the other disadvantages that follow the female kind. He does so because neither this prohibition from the pastoral office of the Church, nor the evils just recited, would hinder the woman, or women, from salvation, provided they are endowed with true faith and remain in it, constantly cultivating charity, holiness and modesty, and the other fruits of true faith in their domestic calling. This calling is ordinarily exercised in bearing, nourishing and educating children (under which office are metonymically included all the remaining duties that pertain to the household, for which the woman is destined, that she may attend to them in her proper role within the private home). And the Apostle promises that truly faithful women, no less than faithful men or faithful pastors of the Church, will obtain eternal salvation in this subjection of theirs, as surely and as easily as if they had been admitted to the ecclesiastical office of teaching. In that office they could not be saved unless they also possessed such faith as shows itself to be true and effective through love and good works.

units.la: Caput Tertium.
units.tr: Chapter Three.

units.la: Apitò duæ sunt partes: In prima de Ministrorum Ecclesiæ electione agitur, ad vers. 14. In altera de præcipuis doctrinæ articulis in Ecclesia tenendis, ad finem.
units.tr: There are clearly two parts. The first deals with the choice of ministers of the Church, down to verse 14. The second deals with the chief articles of doctrine to be held in the Church, to the end.

units.la: Officia Ecclesiastica dividit Apostolus noster, Rom. 12. in Prophetiam & Diaconiam, sub Prophetia comprehendens Pastores & Doctores, qui hoc capite Episcopi vocantur, sub Diaconia complectens, ut hic, & Seniores eos qui mores Ecclesiæ curabant, & Diaconos proprie dictos, qui curabant bona Ecclesiastica & pauperes.
units.tr: Our Apostle divides the offices of the Church (Rom. 12) into prophecy and service. Under prophecy he includes pastors and teachers, who in this chapter are called bishops. Under service he includes, as here, the elders who looked after the morals of the Church, and the deacons properly so called, who looked after the goods of the Church and the poor.

units.la: Vers. 1. Fidus est hic sermo, Siquis Episcopatum appetit, præclarum opus desiderat.
units.tr: Verse 1. This is a faithful saying: if anyone desires the office of a bishop, he desires a good work.

units.la: Hoc versu ut viam parat ad descriptionem proprietatum Episcopi, commendat pastorale munus (præmissâ gravi asseveratione) tanquam functionem præclarissimam & officium laboriosum, quod qui appetit eo fine, ut in Euangelio laborando deducat homines ad salutem æternam, per rectum Dei cultum, elogio dignus est.
units.tr: In this verse, as he prepares the way for describing the qualities of a bishop, he commends the pastoral office (with a solemn assurance placed first) as a most excellent function and a laborious duty. Whoever desires it for the purpose of leading people to eternal salvation by labouring in the Gospel, through the right worship of God, deserves praise.

units.la: Vers. 2. Oportet igitur Episcopum irreprehensum esse, unius uxoris virum, vigilantem, sobrium, compositum, hospitalem, aptum ad docendum:
units.tr: Verse 2. A bishop must therefore be blameless, the husband of one wife, vigilant, sober, of good behaviour, given to hospitality, apt to teach.

units.la: Describit officium, dotes & proprietates Episcopi, id est, Pastoris & Doctoris, partim affirmativè, partim negativè, præscribens quasi certos canones in electione Episcopi observandos.
units.tr: He describes the office, and the gifts and qualities of a bishop, that is, of a pastor and teacher, partly positively and partly negatively, prescribing as it were fixed rules to be observed in the election of a bishop.

units.la: Proprietates seu requisita Episcopi, sunt numero sedecim: Primo, Oportet Episcopum esse vitæ inculpatæ, id est, à scandalis alienum, ita ut jure ab hominibus accusari non possit, non qui omnino expers sit peccati, sed qui sit sine vitiis.
units.tr: The qualities or requirements of a bishop are sixteen in number. First, a bishop must be of blameless life, that is, free from scandals, so that he cannot rightly be accused by men. This does not mean one who is wholly without sin, but one who is without vices.

units.la: 2. proprietas. Oportet esse μονογαμον; quæ proprietas non ponitur præceptivè, quasi necesse sit Pastorem esse conjugatum, sed limitativè, quia si in animum induxerit uxorem ducere, oportet uxore una contentum esse, quamdiu ea vixerit, & à polygamiæ vitio (quod illis temporibus frequens erat) liberum esse. Oportet esse in officio suo vigilantem, qui prospicere valeat quid sibi incumbat ad gregis sui ædificationem, & conservationem, ab hostium spiritualium insidiis.
units.tr: 2. Quality. He must be monogamous [μονογαμον]. This quality is not laid down as a command, as if a minister must necessarily be married, but as a limit: if he has resolved to take a wife, he must be content with one wife as long as she lives, and be free of the vice of polygamy, which was common in those times. He must be vigilant in his office, able to foresee what falls to him for the building up and preservation of his flock against the snares of spiritual enemies.

units.la: 4. Oportet esse in victu & amictu sobrium, adeoque in rebus gerendis moderatum, qui omnia cum recta ratione administret, nihil leviter aut temere suscipiens, sed graviter omnia sua dicta librans & ponderans.
units.tr: 4. He must be sober in food and dress, and so moderate in conducting affairs, managing everything with right reason, undertaking nothing lightly or rashly, but weighing and considering all his words with gravity.

units.la: 5. Compositum esse oportet, seu moribus compositis ornatum, qui neque rusticitate sua, neque stoicâ severitate contemptui se exponat.
units.tr: 5. He must be well-ordered, or adorned with orderly conduct, so that he does not expose himself to contempt either by rustic roughness or by Stoic severity.

units.la: 6. requiritur, Ut sit hospitalis qui pro facultatibus suis paratus sit ad Dei servos, egentes potissimum peregrinos & exules refocillandos & fovendos.
units.tr: 6. It is required that he be hospitable, ready according to his means to refresh and cherish the servants of God, especially needy strangers and exiles.

units.la: 7. requiritur, Ut aptus sit ad docendum, id est, ut non solum sit theologiæ consultus, & in doctrina Christiana probè instructus, sed etiam is qui verbum Dei recte sciat secare, & ad auditoris captum seu ædificationem appositè proferre & accommodare.
units.tr: 7. It is required that he be apt to teach, that is, that he not only be learned in theology and well instructed in Christian doctrine, but also one who knows how to rightly divide the word of God and to present and adapt it fittingly to the capacity and edification of the hearer.

units.la: Vers. 3. Non vinosum, non percussorem, non turpis lucri cupidum: sed moderatum, alienum à pugnis, alienum ab avaritia:
units.tr: Verse 3. Not given to wine, not a striker, not greedy of filthy lucre; but patient, not contentious, not covetous.

units.la: 8. Requiritur ut non sit vinosus, seu potationi deditus, vel qui pitissando & sorbillando diem producere soleat.
units.tr: 8. It is required that he not be given to wine, that is, not addicted to drinking, or one who is accustomed to spend the day in tippling and sipping.

units.la: 9. Ut non sit percussor seu plagosus, qui proclivis sit ad percutiendum, sive famulos suos, sive alios quosvis.
units.tr: 9. That he not be a striker, or quarrelsome, one prone to hitting, whether his servants or anyone else.

units.la: 10. Ut non faciat turpem quæstum, vel ut non sit turpis lucripeta, qui lucrum quærat cum dignitatis Ministerii dispendio.
units.tr: 10. That he not make dishonest gain, or be a greedy seeker of lucre, one who seeks profit at the cost of the dignity of the ministry.

units.la: 11. Ut sit æquus, seu moderatus in contractibus suis, & qui cum opus est de suo jure remittere paratus sit.
units.tr: 11. That he be fair, or moderate, in his dealings, and ready, when necessary, to give up some of his right.

units.la: 12. Ut sit alienus à pugnis, & contentionibus verberum vel verborum.
units.tr: 12. That he be far from fighting and quarrels, whether of blows or of words.

units.la: 13. Ut sit alienus ab avaritia, qui rei familiari augendæ non nimium studeat.
units.tr: 13. That he be free from covetousness, one who does not too eagerly seek to increase his household wealth.

units.la: Qui suæ domui bene præsit, qui liberos contineat in subjectione cum omni honestate.
units.tr: He who rules his own house well, who keeps his children in subjection with all honesty.

units.la: 14. Ut familiam suam, id est, uxorem, liberos & domesticos (si modo habeat) norit bene regere, seu in obedientia, & in honesto exercitio continere.
units.tr: 14. That he know how to govern well his household, that is, his wife, children and servants (if he has any), keeping them in obedience and in honest discipline.

units.la: (Nam si quis propriæ domui præesse nescit, quomodo Ecclesiam Dei curabit?)
units.tr: (For if a man does not know how to rule his own house, how will he take care of the Church of God?)

units.la: Rationem huius requisiti reddit, quia qui propriæ domui, aut parvæ familiæ præesse nescit, Ecclesiam Dei prudenter regere vel curare non poterit.
units.tr: He gives the reason for this requirement: whoever does not know how to rule his own house, or a small family, will not be able to govern or care for the Church of God prudently.

units.la: Non novitium, ne inflatus, in criminationem incidat Diaboli.
units.tr: Not a novice, lest being puffed up he fall into the condemnation of the devil.

units.la: 15. Requirit ut non sit Novitius, seu nova Ecclesiæ plantula, id est, qui recens ad veram religionem sit conversus, non satis in mysteriis instructus, vel experientia confirmatus, non satis subactus & humiliatus per Christiana exercitia: Cujus ratio redditur, ne si subito evehatur ad culmen Ecclesiasticæ dignitatis, inflatus incidat in crimen & condemnationem diaboli, qui præ superbia non mansit in statione sua, & propterea à Deo rejectus est.
units.tr: 15. He requires that he not be a novice, that is, a new little plant of the Church, one who has recently been converted to the true religion, not sufficiently instructed in the mysteries, not confirmed by experience, not sufficiently tamed and humbled through Christian exercises. The reason is given: if he were suddenly raised to the height of ecclesiastical dignity, he might, puffed up, fall into the crime and condemnation of the devil, who, through pride, did not remain in his station and was therefore cast off by God.

units.la: Oportet autem cum etiam bonum habere testimonium ab extraneis; ne in probrum incidat & laqueum Diaboli.
units.tr: Moreover he must have a good testimony from those outside, lest he fall into reproach and the snare of the devil.

units.la: 16. Et ultimum requisitum, Ut habeat bonum testimonium ab extraneis, seu iis qui alieni sunt ab Ecclesia, id est, Ut sit bonæ famæ apud omnes, cujus mores etiam inimici non possunt jure carpere: Cujus ratio redditur, ne in probrum & ignominiam incidat, & in laqueum diaboli, qui non tantum ex ea occasione personam, & officium ipsius criminationibus vel calumniationibus oneret, sed etiam perfricatæ frontis hominem, & famæ suæ negligentem, & tandem moribus dissolutum ipsum efficiat.
units.tr: 16. And the last requirement: that he have a good testimony from outsiders, that is, from those who are not of the Church, so that he is of good reputation with all, and even his enemies cannot rightly find fault with his morals. The reason given is that he should not fall into disgrace and shame, and into the devil's snare; for the devil would use such an occasion not only to burden his person and office with accusations and calumnies, but also to make the man shameless, careless of his reputation, and at last dissolute in his morals.

units.la: Vers. 8. Diaconos itidem honestos, non bilingues, non multo vino deditos, non turpiter lucri cupidos:
units.tr: Verse 8. Likewise the deacons must be honest, not double-tongued, not given to much wine, not greedy of filthy lucre.

units.la: Quod ad Seniorum, & aerarii publici curatorum electionem attinet, Virtutes in iis requirit novem: 1 Ut sint graves, id est, honestis moribus ornati: 2. Ut non sint mendaces, bilingues aut fraudulenti: 3. Ut non sint vino dediti: 4. Ut non affectent turpe lucrum, quod ipsorum aestimationi apud bonos aliquid detrahat.
units.tr: As to the election of elders and of those who look after the public treasury, he requires nine virtues in them: (1) that they be grave, that is, adorned with honest morals; (2) that they not be liars, double-tongued or deceitful; (3) that they not be given to wine; (4) that they not pursue base gain, which would detract from their esteem among good people.

units.la: Vers. 9. Tenentes mysterium fidei cum pura conscientia.
units.tr: Verse 9. Holding the mystery of the faith with a pure conscience.

units.la: 5. Ut in fide seu doctrina Euangelii supernè revelati rite sint instituti, eamque firmâ professione retineant, unâ cum vitae sanctitate, quae puritatem conscientiae, & sincerita-tem fidei ipsorum testetur.
units.tr: 5. That they be properly instructed in the faith, or the doctrine of the Gospel revealed from above, and hold to it with a firm profession, together with holiness of life, which bears witness to the purity of their conscience and the sincerity of their faith.

units.la: Vers. 10. Atque hi etiam probentur primum, deinde ministrent, si sint inculpati.
units.tr: Verse 10. And let these also first be proved, then let them minister, if they are blameless.

units.la: 6. Ut non tantum Pastores, & Candidati superiorum munerum, sed etiam Diaconi probentur; priusquam ad functionem admittantur, hoc est, ne temere & sine delectu obtrudantur Ecclesiae quilibet, sed ut illi solli eligantur, quos antea acta vita commendat; ita ut examine habito constet esse idoneos, & qui jure culpari non possint.
units.tr: 6. That not only pastors and candidates for the higher offices, but also deacons, be tested before they are admitted to their function. That is, they should not be thrust rashly and without choice upon the Church, but only those be chosen whom their previous life commends, so that after an examination it is established that they are fit and cannot rightly be blamed.

units.la: Vers. 11. Uxores itidem honestas, non calumniosas, sobrias sint in omnibus.
units.tr: Verse 11. Likewise their wives must be honest, not slanderers, sober, faithful in all things.

units.la: Quia uxorum & liberorum mores dissoluti in probrum Virorum verti possunt, requirit septimò, ut Uxores & Pastorum, & Diaconorum sint graves, & honestis moribus praeditae: non calumniatrices, seu quae proximorum famae detrahant: studiosae sobrietatis, & denique in omni negotio fidae.
units.tr: Because the dissolute morals of wives and children can turn to the disgrace of the husbands, he requires in the seventh place that the wives of both pastors and deacons be grave and adorned with honest morals; not slanderers, that is, not those who detract from the good name of their neighbours; diligent in sobriety; and, finally, faithful in every business.

units.la: Vers. 12. Diaconi sint nuius uxoris mariti, qui liberis recte praesint, & propriis domibus.
units.tr: Verse 12. Let the deacons be the husbands of one wife, who rule their children well and their own houses.

units.la: 8. Requirit, ut Diaconi sint uxoris unius mariti, id est, à polygamiae vitio alieni: 9. Requirit, Ut sciant familiam suam rectè regere, & sanctae disciplinae cancellis suos domesticos continere.
units.tr: 8. He requires that the deacons be the husbands of one wife, that is, free from the vice of polygamy. 9. He requires that they know how to rule their household well, and to keep their domestics within the bounds of holy discipline.

units.la: Vers. 13. Nam qui bene ministraverint, gradum sibi bonum acquirunt, & multam libertatem per fidem, quae est in Christo Iesu.
units.tr: Verse 13. For those who have served well gain for themselves a good standing, and great boldness in the faith which is in Christ Jesus.

units.la: Ne quis Diaconatum tanquam officium vile spernat, docet eos qui bene functi fuerint hoc officio, & honore dignos esse, dum in munere illo versantur, & fundamentum etiam ponere, ut ad altiorem gradum in Ecclesia elesia promoveantur; Et denique acquirere sibi amplam materiam confirmandae suae fiduciae erga Deum per fidem in Christo, quam fidelis administratio Diaconatus, ut testimonium & indicium sinceritatis fidei non mediocriter confirmare debet.
units.tr: Lest anyone despise the diaconate as a mean office, he teaches that those who have served well in this office are worthy of honour while they hold it, and that they also lay a foundation for advancing to a higher rank in the Church. Finally, they gain for themselves ample ground for strengthening their confidence toward God through faith in Christ, since the faithful administration of the diaconate ought to confirm no small amount of their faith's sincerity as evidence and proof. ## The second part of the chapter.

units.la: Secunda pars Capitis.
Verf. 14. Haec tibi scribo, sperans fore ut celerius ad te veniam:
units.tr: Ver. 14. I write these things to you, hoping that I shall come to you more quickly:

units.la: Verf. 15. Quod si tardius venero, ut noris quomodo oporteat in domo Dei versari, quae est Ecclesia Dei vivi, columna & stabilimentum veritatis.
units.tr: Ver. 15. But if I am delayed, that you may know how one ought to conduct oneself in the house of God, which is the Church of the living God, the pillar and ground of the truth.

units.la: Altera pars Capitis, in qua tres praecipuos doctrinae articulos in Ecclesia tenendos proponit. Articulus primus continet doctrinam de fine scriptae hujus Epistolae, & speciatim praecedentium praeceptorum, qui hic est, Ut regula regendae Ecclesiae, per Apostolum exorata, prae oculis habeatur, quam Apostolus adveniens porro explicaturus & confirmaturus erat, prout opus esset; & per quam (si tardius veniret Apostolus) dirigere posset Timotheus gubernatores Ecclesiae, quomodo in Dei familia, seu Ecclesia regenda versari debeant.
units.tr: The second part of the chapter, in which he sets forth three principal articles of doctrine to be held in the Church. The first article contains the doctrine concerning the purpose of this written Epistle, and especially of the preceding precepts. It is this: that the rule for governing the Church, set out by the Apostle, should be kept before the eyes. The Apostle was about to explain and confirm it further when he came, as the need required. And by this rule (if the Apostle should come later), Timothy could direct the governors of the Church in how they ought to conduct themselves in ruling the household, that is, the Church, of God.

units.la: Ecclesia Dei Articulus 2. Continet doctrinam de excellentia Ecclesiae: 1. Quod sit domus Dei, in qua Deus habitat, & familiam alit, & in qua colitur: 2. Quod sit Ecclesia Dei viventis, seu coetus evocatus ex mundo per Deum viventem, praeter quem omnes illi dii quos Ethnici colunt, mortua sunt idola: 3. Quod sicut Ecclesia per veritatem evocatur, generatur, alitur, & conservatur a Deo, ut sit Ecclesia Dei viventis & vivifici; Sic veritas per Ecclesiam sustentatur, ut per columnam & stabilimentum quoddam. Quia Ecclesia veritatem tanquam in archivis collocatam conservat, In Ecclesia sola veritas divina mundo prostat, sedemque suam & domicilium habet, & sola Ecclesia est quae per Ministros suos hanc ipsam veritatem, ubique praedicandam, promulgandam, & communicandam curat, eamque tuetur & defendit, idque propriis veritatis armis, contra omnes adversarios.
units.tr: The Church of God. The second article contains the doctrine concerning the excellence of the Church: (1) that it is the house of God, in which God dwells, nourishes his family, and is worshipped; (2) that it is the Church of the living God, that is, the assembly called out of the world by the living God, apart from which all those gods that the heathen worship are dead idols; (3) that just as the Church is called, begotten, nourished and preserved by God through the truth, so that it may be the Church of the living and life-giving God, so also the truth is sustained through the Church, as by a certain pillar and ground. Because the Church keeps the truth as if laid up in archives, the divine truth is displayed to the world only in the Church, and the Church alone has its seat and dwelling there. The Church alone, through its ministers, takes care that this same truth is preached, published and communicated everywhere, and it guards and defends it, using the truth's own weapons against all adversaries.

units.la: Verf. 16. Et sine controversia magnum est pietatis mysterium: Deus conspicuus factus est in carne, justificatus est in Spiritu, conspectus est ab angelis, praedicatum est Gentibus, fides illi habita est in mundo, sursum receptus est in gloriam.
units.tr: Ver. 16. And without controversy, great is the mystery of godliness: God was manifested in the flesh, justified in the Spirit, seen by angels, preached among the Gentiles, believed on in the world, received up into glory.

units.la: Articulus 3. Continet magnum pietatis mysterium, & totius veritatis Euangelicæ columnam & stabilimentum, seu prima Euangelii fundamenta, quibus reliqua tota salutaris doctrina innititur, quæ fundamenta oportet Pastores Ecclesiæ omni ratione tueri.
units.tr: The third article contains the great mystery of godliness, and it is the pillar and ground of all evangelical truth, or the first foundations of the Gospel, on which the whole rest of saving doctrine rests. The ministers of the Church ought by every means to defend these foundations.

units.la: Fundamentales autem Doctrinæ, quæ hoc articulo continentur; quæque necessario, communi, & unanimi consensu, omnium verè Christianorum agnoscendæ sunt, propununtur septem: Prima hæc est, Summa Euangelii est mysterium pietatis, & illud quidem magnum. Euangelium autem Mysterium dicitur, quia naturali rationi abscónditum est, nec sine divina patefactione, seu revelatione supernaturali à quoquam intelligi potest: adeo ut rationi nostræ in hoc mysterio minimè fidendum sit, sed Dei verbo unicè inhærendum: utque Dei verbum intelligamus, Spiritus Sancti illuminatio à Deo expetenda est. Mysterium pietatis vocatur, quia pro scopo & Materia habet Christianam pietatem, quæ in fide & obedientia mandatorum Christi, sive in fide per charitatem operante, consistit.
units.tr: There are seven fundamental doctrines contained in this article, which must necessarily be acknowledged by all truly Christian people with common and unanimous consent. The first is this: The sum of the Gospel is the mystery of godliness, and indeed a great one. The Gospel is called a mystery because it is hidden from natural reason, and no one can understand it without divine disclosure, that is, supernatural revelation. Hence we must not trust our reason in this mystery, but cling solely to the Word of God. And that we may understand the Word of God, we must seek the illumination of the Holy Spirit from God. It is called the mystery of godliness because its aim and matter is Christian godliness, which consists in faith and obedience to the commands of Christ, or in faith working through love.

units.la: Magnum vocatur ] Quia de Deo, de Christo, de redemptionis magno negotio, de gloria justitiæ, & gratiæ divinæ, & de nostra salute, quæ res omnium maximæ sunt, agit.
units.tr: It is called great: because it treats of God, of Christ, of the great business of redemption, of the glory of divine justice and grace, and of our salvation, which are the greatest of all things.

units.la: Deus ] Doctrina 2. Fundamentalis hæc est, In Christi persona, Deus conspicuus factus est in carne. Deus ] Nempe unigenitus Dei Filius ac proinde verus æternusque Deus. Conspicuus factus est, ] Toti scilicet orbi, visibilis, palpabilis, & audibilis exhibitus.
units.tr: God. The second fundamental doctrine is this: In the person of Christ, God was made visible in the flesh. God: namely, the only-begotten Son of God, and therefore true and eternal God. Was made visible: that is, was displayed to the whole world, visible, tangible and audible.

units.la: In carne, ] Scilicet in humana natura, & quidem mortali & fragili, sed à peccato alienâ se conspiciendum obtulit verum Immanuelem, & nobiscum Deum. Et hic designantur duæ naturæ, divina quæ assumpsit, & humana quæ assumpta est, & tota Christi exinanitio in carne hic continetur.
units.tr: In the flesh: that is, in human nature, indeed mortal and frail, yet, free from sin, he offered himself to be seen as the true Immanuel, God with us. Here are designated the two natures: the divine, which he assumed, and the human, which was assumed. And the whole emptying of Christ in the flesh is contained here.

units.la: Justificatus ] Doctrina 3. In Christi persona, Deus manifestatus in carne, justificatus est per Spiritum; hoc est, Christus per divinam illam efficaciam suam (quæ in universa ipsius doctrina & vita, itemque in miraculis, & præsertim in gloriosa à mortuis resurrectione Iese exeruit) non modo Justus & Verax, sed & Unigenitus Dei Filius, & porrò supremus Ecclesiæ Propheta, itemque Rex & Pontifex æternus, abundè declaratus, ac confirmatus est, & ab omnium Judæorum & hostium calumniis, & obtrectationibus absolutus.
units.tr: Justified: The third doctrine is this: in the person of Christ, God manifested in the flesh was justified in the Spirit. That is, Christ, by that divine efficacy of his (which he displayed in his whole teaching and life, and likewise in his miracles, and especially in his glorious resurrection from the dead), was abundantly declared and confirmed not only as just and truthful, but also as the only-begotten Son of God, and further as the supreme Prophet of the Church, likewise as the eternal King and Priest. He was also freed from the slanders and attacks of all the Jews and enemies.

units.la: Ab Angelos ]
units.tr: By the angels.

units.la: Doctrina 4. Deus conspicuus factus in carne, conspectus est ab Angelis, id est, agnitus est Christus ab Angelis, & per clariorem Majestatis suæ, simul & voluntatis Divinæ patefactionem, Christus clarius conspectus est ab Angelis Deus incarnatus; & idcirco Angeli ut idonei, à Deo adhibiti sunt testes, de Christi conceptione, nativitate, passione, & resurrectione; qui hoc mysterium etiamnum admirantur, novitate & excellentia rei perculsi, cupiuntque altius in illud penetrare, dimittentes se, ut intueantur ea quæ per Spiritum Ecclesiæ revelantur, 1. Tet. 1. 12. Ephes. 3. 10. Nam de modo redemptionis cœlatos oportuit etiam ipsos Angelos, ad tempus, quo plus admirationis haberet Dei bonitas.
units.tr: The fourth doctrine: God, made visible in the flesh, was seen by the angels. That is, Christ was recognised by the angels, and, through a clearer disclosure of his majesty and at the same time of the divine will, the incarnate God was more clearly seen by the angels. For this reason the angels, as fit witnesses, were employed by God concerning Christ's conception, birth, passion and resurrection. They still marvel at this mystery, struck by the newness and excellence of the thing, and they desire to penetrate deeper into it, stooping down to look at those things which are revealed by the Spirit to the Church (1 Pet. 1. 12; Eph. 3. 10). For the manner of redemption had to be hidden even from the angels themselves for a time, so that God's goodness might have more to be wondered at.

units.la: Doctrina 5. Deus conspicuus factus in carne, & prædicatus Gentibus magnum est mysterium: Nam mirum & stupendum est, quod Gentes (quæ hactenus in cæcitate mentis erraverant) dignatus sit Deus revelatione Filii sui, quæ doctrina ipsos Apostolos initio, & cœlestes etiam Angelos latuerat.
units.tr: The fifth doctrine: God, made visible in the flesh and preached among the Gentiles, is a great mystery. For it is wonderful and astonishing that God deigned, by the revelation of his Son, to reach the Gentiles, who until then had wandered in blindness of mind. This doctrine had been hidden at first even from the Apostles themselves and the heavenly angels.

units.la: Doctrina 6. Mysterii magni non exigua pars est, quod in mundo, (qui in malo est pontus, & planè Deo contrarius) operâ hominum abjectorum, & nullo humano splendore commendabilium efficacia Euangelii tanta fuerit, ut cum aditus omnes præclusi & obserati essent, fides Christi obtinuerit, & per omnes difficultates eluctata, incredibili victoriæ genere victrix evaserit, adeo ut Christi nomen creditum, & agnitum sit in mundo, quocunque pervasit Euangelii prædicatio.
units.tr: The sixth doctrine: It is no small part of the great mystery that, in the world (which is a sea of evil and utterly contrary to God), by the work of lowly men, commended by no human splendour, the efficacy of the Gospel was so great that, although all approaches were closed and barred, the faith of Christ prevailed; and, struggling through all difficulties, it proved victorious by an incredible kind of victory. So much so that the name of Christ has been believed and acknowledged in the world wherever the preaching of the Gospel has spread.

units.la: Doctrina 7. Mysterium magnum est, & admiratione dignum, quod Christus qui in carnis infirmitate, & abjectissima servi conditione, tot annos in mundo latuerat, & tandem in crucem actus, vitam suam finire miserrime visus erat, nihilominus ad dextram Patris, & in communionem gloriæ Dei evectus sit: Unde misso Spiritu Sancto, & donis datis, hominibus in hunc usque diem gloriam Deitatis suæ manifestat, & quod tantam habeat potestatem in Cœlo, & in Terra, ut omnia subjecta sint pedibus ipsius aperte demonstrat. Hæ sunt doctrinæ quas firmiter tenere vult Ecclesias; unde omnes reliquæ suam originem trahunt & stabilimentum.
units.tr: The seventh doctrine: It is a great mystery and worthy of admiration that Christ, who in the weakness of the flesh and in the most abject condition of a servant lay hidden in the world for so many years, and at last, driven to the cross, seemed most miserably to end his life, was nevertheless exalted to the right hand of the Father and into the fellowship of God's glory. Hence, after sending the Holy Spirit and bestowing gifts on men down to this day, he manifests the glory of his Godhead, and he plainly demonstrates that he has such power in heaven and on earth that all things are subject to his feet. These are the doctrines which the Church wishes to hold firmly; all the others draw their origin and stability from them.

units.tr: [Catchword/annotation at lower left, illegible]

units.la: Caput Quartum.
units.tr: Chapter Four.

units.la: ERgit Timotheum instituere, quomodo in Ecclesia, siu Dei domo recte versari debeat. Capitis duae sunt partes, In prima praemonet de Apostasia à fide rectâ, ultimis temporibus in Ecclesia futura, ad vers. 6. In altera, officia describit boni Pastoris, & Gubernatorum Ecclesiae: quibus se & populum suum à defectione immunes conservare possint.
units.tr: Paul teaches Timothy how he ought to behave in the Church, or house of God. The chapter has two parts. In the first he forewarns of the apostasy from the sound faith which will occur in the Church in the last times, up to verse 6. In the second he describes the duties of a good minister and of the governors of the Church, by which they may keep themselves and their people free from defection.

units.la: Vers. 1.
units.tr: Verse 1.

units.la: Spiritus autem diserte dicit fore, ut posterioribus temporibus descisscant quidam à fide, spiritibus deceptoribus attendentes ad doctrinam daemoniorum.
units.tr: Now the Spirit expressly says that in later times some will fall away from the faith, attending to deceiving spirits and the doctrines of demons.

units.la: Quod ad Prophetiam de Apostasia futura à fide, seu sana Euangelii doctrina, quatuor praemittit, quorum primum est defectionis certitudo, quia Spiritus Sanctus non obscurè, seu in aenigmate, sed expresse praemonebat de hac Apostasia, & de sequuturis statim temporibus praedicebat, quibus defectio à fide fieri inciperet, & invalesceret in visibili Ecclesia.
units.tr: As to the prophecy of the future apostasy from the faith, or from the sound doctrine of the gospel, he sets out four points beforehand. The first is the certainty of the defection: the Holy Spirit did not speak obscurely or in an enigma, but expressly forewarned of this apostasy and foretold that in the times immediately following, defection from the faith would begin and grow strong in the visible Church.

units.la: Secundum continet causas defectionis tres: Prima causa, sunt spiritus deceptores, id est, Diaboli, autores omnis generis errorum & impostturarum: Causa 2. Sunt Doctores falsi, qui per inspirationem Diaboli falsas doctrinas, seu doctrinas Daemoniorum, à Diabolis excogitatas in Ecclesia docturi, & propugnaturi erant: Causa 3. Est attentio, auscultatio, & fides illis doctoribus, & Diabolis à miseris hominibus adhibita.
units.tr: The second point contains three causes of the defection. The first cause is the deceiving spirits, that is, the devils, the authors of every kind of error and imposture. The second cause is the false teachers, who, by the inspiration of the devil, were going to teach and defend in the Church false doctrines, or doctrines of demons, devised by the devils. The third cause is the attention, listening and faith which miserable men give to those teachers and to the devils.

units.la: Vers. 2.
units.tr: Verse 2.

units.la: Per hypocrisin falsiloquorum, quorum conscientia cauterio resecta est,
units.tr: Through the hypocrisy of liars, whose conscience is seared with a branding iron,

units.la: Describit tertio loco Diabolicos illos doctores, seu daemoniorum instrumenta, per quae daemones falsas illas doctrinas in Ecclesiam invecturi, & sparguri erant, à duabus proprietatibus: 1. Erunt hypocritae simulantes se esse veritatis cultores in omnibus: etiam tum cum falsa sua dogmata Ecclesiae obtrudunt. Sanctimoniam mentientur, dum sua figmenta Dei cultum esse venditant; 2. Conscientias cauterio inultas habituri sunt, quippe qui contra conscientiae dictamen, multa dicturi & facturi sunt, nec tamen sensuri ullum dolorem, poltquam sacrilegiis, fagitiis, fallis suis doctrinis D e u m offenderunt, & animas hominum perdiderunt.
units.tr: In the third place he describes those diabolical teachers, the instruments of demons through whom the demons were going to bring in and spread those false doctrines in the Church, by two properties. (1) They will be hypocrites, pretending in everything to be worshippers of the truth, even while they foist their false dogmas on the Church. They will feign holiness while they peddle their inventions as the worship of God. (2) They will have consciences seared with a branding iron, since they will say and do many things against the dictate of conscience, and yet feel no pain after they have offended God by sacrileges and crimes and by their false doctrines, and have destroyed the souls of men.

units.la: Verf. 3. Prohibentium contrahere matrimonium jubentium abstinere à cibis, quos Deus creavit ad participandum cum gratiarum actione, fidelibus, & iis qui cognoverint veritatem.
units.tr: Verse 3. Forbidding to contract marriage, commanding abstinence from foods which God created to be received with thanksgiving by the faithful and by those who have known the truth.

units.la: Quarto loco harum doctrinarum Diabolicarum exempla in rebus in-differentibus proponit duo, per quas doctrinas tanquam per certas no-tas, Diabolicos illos doctores, cum Apostatis Sectatoribus ipsorum dignoscamus. Prima est, prohibitio matrimonii, qui error quoscunque post Diabolum autores habuerit, non refert, defensores nactus est Pontificios, inter quos jam diu obtinuit, & etiamnum obtinet, ab eo tem-pore quo clericis suis omnibus coelibatum indixerunt. Altera doctrina Diabolorum est, de delectu ciborum habendo, & abstinendo à quibusdam cibis, tanquam impuris, qui error inter Romanenses magis reli-giosè urgetur, observatur & defenditur, quam pleraque pietatis & justitiae praescripta à Deo exercitia.
units.tr: In the fourth place he sets out, as examples of these diabolical doctrines in indifferent things, two teachings. By these doctrines, as by certain marks, we may recognise those diabolical teachers together with their apostate followers. The first is the prohibition of marriage. Whatever author after the devil this error had, it has found defenders among the Papists, among whom it has long prevailed and still prevails, ever since they imposed celibacy on all their clergy. The second devilish doctrine concerns the making of distinctions among foods and abstaining from certain foods as unclean. This error is urged, observed and defended among the Romanists more zealously than most of the exercises of piety and justice prescribed by God.

units.la: Quos Deus] Posteriorem hanc doctrinae speciem de prohibitione certorum ciborum religionis causâ, probat esse falsam & daemoniacam, sex rationibus: Prima, A fine creationis, Quia Deus omnis generis cibos creavit, eo fine ut participentur, id est, comedantur. Diabolica ergo est doctrina quæ de vitandis aliquibus cibis præcipit, quan- do Deus eos affert & usus eorum opportunus & utilis esset.
units.tr: Which God [created]: he proves by six reasons that this latter kind of doctrine, forbidding certain foods for the sake of religion, is false and demonic. The first, from the end of creation: God created foods of every kind so that they might be partaken of, that is, eaten. Therefore the doctrine which teaches avoiding some foods is diabolical, when God offers them and their use would be opportune and useful.

units.la: Gratiarum ] Ratio 2. Vult Deus omne genus ciborum pro beneficiis agnosci, & cum gratiarum actione, idcirco accipi. Ergo doctrina de vitandis & rejiciendis aliquibus cibis, quando Deus eos offert, & ipsorum usus opportunus & utilis esset.
units.tr: With thanksgiving: the second reason. God wills every kind of food to be acknowledged as a benefit and therefore received with thanksgiving. Therefore the doctrine of avoiding and rejecting certain foods, when God offers them and their use would be opportune and useful, is diabolical.

units.la: Fidelibus ] Ratio 3. Usus creaturarum fidelibus præcipuè (seu iis qui veritatem Euangelii cognitam habent, & Deo reconciliantur per Christum) quandocunque utilis esse poterit, à Deo conceditur: Ergo prohibere ullis cibis Christianos, quibus jus imprimis datum est in eos, quandocunque ipsorum usus utilis, & naturæ conveniens esse possit, doctrina dæmoniorum est.
units.tr: To the faithful: the third reason. The use of creatures is granted by God chiefly to the faithful (that is, to those who have the truth of the gospel known and are reconciled to God through Christ), whenever it can be useful. Therefore to forbid Christians any foods, over which right has especially been given to them, whenever their use may be useful and agree with nature, is a doctrine of demons.

units.la: Vers. 4. Nam quicquid creavit Deus, bonum est, nec quicquam rejiciendum est, si cum gratiarum actione sumatur. Ratio 4. Generalis, prohibitionem conjugii simul & ciborum attingens, Quicquid Deus creavit bonum est, in legitimo suo usu, ut cibus, conjugium, reliquaeque creaturae omnes: Respexit enim Deus quod creaverat, & ecce valde bonum erat. Ergo doctrina prohibens legitimum usum naturalem creaturarum Dei, est diabolica.
units.tr: Verse 4. For whatever God created is good, and nothing is to be rejected, if it is received with thanksgiving. The fourth reason is general, touching both the prohibition of marriage and that of foods: whatever God created is good in its lawful use, as food, marriage and all the other creatures. For God looked on what he had made, and behold, it was very good. Therefore a doctrine forbidding the lawful natural use of God's creatures is diabolical.

units.la: Ratio 5. Nihil rejiciendum est ex Dei creaturis, seu ordinationibus, ii usurpetur legitime, & cum gratiarum actione. Ergo doctrina rejiciens conjugium vel cibos, quum ipsorum usus legitimus & utilis esse possit, Doctrina est daemoniorum.
units.tr: The fifth reason: nothing from God's creatures or ordinances is to be rejected, if it is used lawfully and with thanksgiving. Therefore a doctrine rejecting marriage or foods, when their lawful and useful use is possible, is a doctrine of demons.

units.la: Verf. 5. Sanctificatur enim per verbum Dei, & preces.
units.tr: Verse 5. For it is sanctified through the word of God and prayer.

units.la: Ratio 6. confirmans priorem, Omnis Dei creatura, ut cibus, conjugium, &c. sanctificatur nobis ad legitimum usum, cum bona conscientia conjunctum, per Dei Verbum & Preces: (nam per Dei Verbum, seu Divinam Ordinationem, libertatem & jus nobis restitui in Christo intelligimus, & per preces Dei donum agnoscimus, & benedictionem ejus expetimus) Ergo Doctrina jubens abstinere a Dei creaturis, easque nobis impuras reddens, quando Deus eas sanctificavit, & ad sanctum usum praeparavit, & nobis obtulit, diabolica est.
units.tr: Reason 6, confirming the former: every creature of God, such as food, marriage, etc., is sanctified to us for lawful use, joined with a good conscience, through the Word of God and prayer (for through the Word of God, that is, the divine ordinance, we understand that liberty and right are restored to us in Christ, and through prayer we acknowledge God's gift and seek his blessing). Therefore a doctrine that commands abstinence from God's creatures, and makes them unclean for us, when God has sanctified them, prepared them for holy use, and offered them to us, is diabolical.

units.la: Secunda pars Capitis.
units.tr: The second part of the chapter.

units.la: Verf. 6. Haec si subjeceris fratribus, bonus eris minister Iesu Christi, innutritus in sermonibus fidei, bonaeque doctrinae, quam assecutus es.
units.tr: Verse 6. If you put these things before the brothers, you will be a good minister of Jesus Christ, nourished in the words of faith and of sound doctrine, which you have attained.

units.la: Altera pars Capitis, continens officia Timothei in praesenti sua legatione praestanda. Hortationes sunt quatuor.
units.tr: The second part of the chapter, containing the duties which Timothy is to perform in his present commission. There are four exhortations.

units.la: Hortatio prima, Ut admonitiones hactenus expositas fratribus proponat, ipsque subinde easdem in memoriam revocet: Rationes hortationis sunt duae. Ratio prima, Si feceris, ostendes teipsum praeclarum Christi Ministrum, & studiosum ut omnia fiant in domo Dei ex sua ipsius voluntate.
units.tr: The first exhortation: that he should set before the brothers the admonitions explained so far, and repeatedly recall them to their memory. There are two reasons for this exhortation. The first reason: if you do so, you will show yourself to be an outstanding minister of Christ, and eager that all things be done in the house of God according to his own will.

units.la: Ratio 2. Demonstrabis teipsum hactenus innutritum esse sana doctrina, tanquam salubri cibo, quam me docente (a cujus latere nunquam discesseris) assectatus es.
units.tr: Reason 2. You will demonstrate that you have hitherto been nourished by sound doctrine, as by wholesome food, which you have pursued under my teaching (from whose side you have never departed).

units.la: Verf. 7. Ceterum profanas & aniles fabulas rejice: sed exerce teipsum ad pietatem.
units.tr: Verse 7. But reject profane and old-wives' fables; and exercise yourself rather unto godliness.

units.la: Hortatio 2. Ut rejectis humanis traditionibus, & commentis hominum, ad traditiones suas fulciendas excogitatis (tanquam profanis fabulis quibus anus & pueri capiuntur potius quam prudentes viri) exerceat se in virtutibus solidis, quae a Deo praescribuntur ad pietatem, seu Dei cultum promovendum, & ut alii in iis se exerceant, curet.
units.tr: The second exhortation: that, having rejected human traditions and the inventions of men, devised to prop up their own traditions (like profane fables with which old women and children are captivated rather than prudent men), he should exercise himself in solid virtues, which are prescribed by God for godliness, that is, for promoting the worship of God, and that he should take care that others too exercise themselves in these.

units.la: Verf. 8. Nam corporalis exercitatio paululum habet utilitatis: at pietas ad omnia utilis est, ut quae promissionem habeat vitae praesentis ac futurae.
units.tr: Verse 8. For bodily exercise profiteth little; but godliness is profitable unto all things, having promise of the life that now is, and of that which is to come.

units.la: Rationes hortationis sunt quatuor: 1. Quia corporales illae exercitationes in vigiliis, abstinentia a cibis, & similes spontaneae afflictionis species, quae hominum praeceptis praescribuntur, ad pauca utiles sunt, id est, utilitate sua non compensant laborem, seu plane inutiles sunt; nam recte usurpatae quando Deus extraordinem nos ad has exercitationes vocat, prosunt ut adjumenta; imperatae vero ab hominibus, ut superstitiones, nocent.
units.tr: The reasons for this exhortation are four: 1. Because those bodily exercises, such as vigils, abstinence from food, and similar kinds of voluntary affliction, which are prescribed by human precepts, are of little use, that is, their usefulness does not repay the labour, or they are plainly useless; for when used rightly, when God calls us to these exercises beyond the ordinary course, they help as aids; but when imposed by men, as superstitions, they harm.

units.la: Ratio 2. Christiana pietas quae divinis praeceptis exigitur, ad omnia utilis est, sive nosipsos, sive alios, sive praesens hoc saeculum sive futurum spectemus, quippe quae divinam promissionem felicitatis in praesenti & futura vita habet.
units.tr: Reason 2. The Christian godliness which is required by divine precepts is profitable for all things, whether we look to ourselves, or to others, or to this present age or the future, since it has the divine promise of happiness in the present and future life.

units.la: Verf. 9. Fidus est hic sermo, & dignus qui omnibus modis recipiatur.
units.tr: Verse 9. This is a faithful saying, and worthy of all acceptation.

units.la: Ratio 3. Confirmans & hortationem, & praecedentem rationem: Quia haec doctrina de rejiciendis hominum commentis, & sequendis exercitiis verae pietatis, est certus sermo, qui neminem decipiet, & doctrina plane salutaris, ideoque doctrina quam omnes amplecti & tueri debent.
units.tr: Reason 3, confirming both the exhortation and the preceding reason: because this doctrine, concerning the rejection of men's inventions and the pursuit of the exercises of true godliness, is a sure saying which will deceive no one, and a doctrine wholly salutary, and therefore a doctrine which all ought to embrace and hold fast.

units.la: Verf. 10. Nam idcirco etiam fatigamur & probrii afficimur, quod speremus in Deo vivo, qui est conservator omnium hominum, maxime vero fidelium.
units.tr: Verse 10. For therefore we both labour and suffer reproach, because we trust in the living God, who is the Saviour of all men, specially of those that believe.
