units.la: Ratio 4. confirmans etiam rationes priores, Quia propter rejecta hominum commenta, & defensam veram pietatem, quae in exercitiis fidei & obedientiae consistit, afflictiones & aerumnas, laborum satis & infamiae, ab injustis persequutoribus patimur, eaque fortiter perferimus, ex spe promissionum quae nobis hanc viam tenentibus factae sunt. Idcirco rejectis hominum commentis pietati studeamus.
units.tr: Reason 4, confirming also the earlier reasons: because on account of rejecting men's inventions and defending true godliness, which consists in the exercises of faith and obedience, we suffer afflictions and hardships, much toil and infamy, at the hands of unjust persecutors, and we bear them bravely, from the hope of the promises made to us who keep this way. Therefore, having rejected men's inventions, let us be zealous for godliness.

units.la: Vive Vivo ] Hanc rationem amplificat & confirmat ex duabus proprietatibus Dei, in quo speramus: Prima est, Deus est vivus, non solum subjective actuosus, sed etiam effective, seu respectu nostri vivificus, qui nobis promissa ita praestat, ut sciamus eum veritatis & vitae auctorem esse. 2. Deus est Servator omnium hominum, sicut dicitur in Psal. 36, Tu servas homines & jumenta; generali sua bonitate alens & sustentans omnes, Solem suum oriri faciens super justum & injustum: Maxime vero & specialissima ratione Servator est Fidelium, qui ipsius promissionibus de felicitate in futura vita fidentes, humanis commentis & placitis, etiam in periculo persequutionis renunciant, & pietatis exercitia sectantur.
units.tr: "Living God": he amplifies and confirms this reason from two properties of God, in whom we hope. The first is that God is living, not only subjectively, as active, but also effectively, that is, with respect to us, as quickening, who fulfils his promises to us in such a way that we know him to be the author of truth and of life. 2. God is the Saviour of all men, as it is said in Psalm 36, "Thou preservest man and beast"; by his general goodness nourishing and sustaining all, making his sun rise on the just and the unjust. Yet most of all, and by a most special reason, he is the Saviour of believers, who, trusting in his promises of happiness in the future life, renounce human inventions and opinions, even in danger of persecution, and pursue the exercises of godliness.

units.la: Vers. 11. Haec denuntia & doce.
units.tr: Verse 11. These things command and teach.

units.la: Repetit & amplificat hanc hortationem, ut Timotheus pro autoritate, utilem hanc doctrinam commendet fratribus docendam, & urgendam, & ut ipse sedulo eam inculcet, rogat.
units.tr: He repeats and amplifies this exhortation, asking that Timothy, with authority, commend this useful doctrine to the brothers to be taught and urged, and that he himself diligently inculcate it.

units.la: Vers. 12. Nemo tuam juventutem despiciat, sed esto exemplar fidelium in sermone, in conversatione, in charitate, in Spiritu, in fide, in puritate.
units.tr: Verse 12. Let no man despise thy youth; but be thou an example of the believers, in word, in conversation, in charity, in spirit, in faith, in purity.

units.la: Hortatio 3. Ut confervandae autoritati studeat, inque hunc finem, Ne quis justam haberet causam despiciendi in eo juventam; jubet ut in doctrina & vita, in verbis & factis, se exemplar, & quasi loquentem regulam exhibeat, in quo eluceant charitas erga Deum & proximum; Spiritualis affectus, fidelitas in officio, & castitas, seu puritas ab inquinamentis, quibus se polluere solent, qui carnalibus voluptatibus dediti sunt.
units.tr: The third exhortation: that he should strive to keep his authority, and to this end, that no one might have a just cause for despising his youth, he bids him show himself in doctrine and life, in words and deeds, as an example and, as it were, a speaking rule, in whom love towards God and neighbour shines forth; spiritual affection, faithfulness in duty, and chastity, that is, purity from the defilements with which those are wont to pollute themselves who are given over to carnal pleasures.

units.la: Vers. 13, Interim dum venio, attende lectioni exhortationi doctrinae.
units.tr: Verse 13. Till I come, give attention to reading, to exhortation, to doctrine.

units.la: Hortatio 4. Ut munus docendi strenue excolat & augeat: Partim assidua Scripturae lectione, partim crebra concionandi exercitatione, potissimum quandiu consistere posset uno in loco: & nominatim quandiu esset Ephesi: occasio enim istiusmodi, post Apostoli adventum, propter peregrinationes in Apostoli comitatu, non erat facile sperenda.
units.tr: The fourth exhortation: that he should vigorously cultivate and increase the office of teaching, partly by constant reading of Scripture, partly by frequent practice in preaching, chiefly for as long as he could remain in one place, and particularly as long as he was at Ephesus; for an opportunity of this kind was not easily to be hoped for after the Apostle's arrival, because of journeys in the Apostle's company.

units.la: Vers. 14. Ne negligito donum quod in te est: quod datum est tibi ad prophetandum. cum impositione manuum presbyterii.
units.tr: Verse 14. Neglect not the gift that is in thee, which was given thee by prophecy, with the laying on of the hands of the presbytery.

units.la: Rationes hortationis, saepius interim repetitae, & inculcatae, sunt quinque: 1. Quia sacrum illud munus Evangelistae ad quod vocatus es, Dei est ex gratia donum, & ideo non negligendum. Datum] Ratio 2. Quia datûm est hoc tibi munus prædicandi Euan Non ergo negligentius in eo versandum tibi est.
units.tr: The reasons for this exhortation, meanwhile often repeated and inculcated, are five: 1. Because that sacred office of evangelist, to which you have been called, is a gift of God's grace, and therefore not to be neglected. "Given"] Reason 2. Because this office of preaching the gospel has been given to you. Therefore you must not be more careless in exercising it.

units.la: Impositione] Ratio 3. Quia etiam ab Ecclesia vocatus es ad hoc munus, per impositionem manuum, seu faultam precationem Presbyterii, id est, Collegii Presbyterorum. Inter quos præsidebat pro tempore ipse Paulus, nomine Presbyterii, & unà cum aliis Presbyteris, manus ei imponebat, ut ex comparatione 2 Timoth. 1 6. apparet. Per quam manuum impositionem significabant hominem Deo sacrum & dicatum: Ergo muneris adeo solenniter his modis demandati, executio non est tibi negligenda.
units.tr: "By the laying on"] Reason 3. Because you were also called to this office by the Church, through the laying on of hands, or the solemn prayer of the presbytery, that is, the college of elders. Among whom Paul himself presided for the time, in the name of the presbytery, and together with the other elders laid hands upon him, as appears from a comparison with 2 Timothy 1:6. By which laying on of hands they signified a man consecrated and dedicated to God. Therefore the execution of an office so solemnly committed in these ways is not to be neglected by you.

units.la: Verf. 15. Hæc exerce, in his esto: ut tuus profectus manifestus sit inter omnes.
units.tr: Verse 15. Meditate upon these things; give thyself wholly to them: that thy profiting may appear to all.

units.la: Ratio 4. Quia Ministerium hoc ita curandum est, ut profectus tuus in doctrina, simul & vita, seu omnibus Ministerii partibus, evidenter appareat omnibus: Ergo serio & non perfunctorie ex deliberato consilio & meditatione adhibita, huic muneri incumbendum, & inhærendum est.
units.tr: Reason 4. Because this ministry is to be so managed that your progress, both in doctrine and in life, that is, in all parts of the ministry, may be evident to all: therefore you must apply yourself to this office earnestly, and not carelessly, with deliberate counsel and applied meditation, and cling to it.

units.la: Verf. 16. Attende tibiipsi & doctrinæ: persiste in iis, id enim si fecerus, & teipsum servabis, & eos qui te audierint.
units.tr: Verse 16. Take heed unto thyself, and unto the doctrine; continue in them: for in doing this thou shalt both save thyself, and them that hear thee.

units.la: Ratio 5. Quia sic & te & tuos auditores adduces ad salutem æternam, ut causa instrumentalis: Ergo in hoc tuo Ministerio, vitæ & doctrinæ tuæ constanter attendendum est.
units.tr: Reason 5. Because by this you will bring both yourself and your hearers to eternal salvation, as an instrumental cause: therefore in this your ministry you must constantly attend to your life and your doctrine.

units.la: Caput Quintum.
units.tr: Chapter 5.

units.la: Timotheum hoc Capite instituit, quomodo in privatis admonitionibus erga omnes, & quomodo erga Viduas eleemosynarias, & Presbyteros, se gerere debeat. Capitis partes sunt tres: In prima agitur de privatis admonitionibus, ad versum 3. In secunda de Viduis, ad versum 17. In tertia de Presbyteris, ad finem.
units.tr: In this chapter he instructs Timothy how to conduct himself in private admonitions toward all, and toward the widows who receive alms and toward the elders. The chapter has three parts: the first deals with private admonitions, at verse 3; the second with widows, at verse 17; the third with elders, to the end.

units.la: Verf. 1. Seniorem ne increpato, sed hortare ut Patrem; juniores, ut fratres:
units.tr: Verse 1. Do not rebuke an elder, but entreat him as a father; the younger men as brothers.

units.la: Quod ad primam præcepti partem attinet de pravitis admonitionibus, quatuor sunt ejus membra: 1. De natu grandioribus, quos leniter vult tractari, modestæ hortationis potius, quam acerbæ increpationis modo, ut honor ipsorum ætati, secundum quintum præceptum haberi perspiciatur: 2. Ut natu minores admoneantur, cum fraternæ dilectionis significatione.
units.tr: As for the first part of the precept, concerning private admonitions, it has four members: (1) Older men are to be handled gently, by way of modest exhortation rather than harsh rebuke, so that honour is shown to their age, in keeping with the fifth commandment. (2) Younger men are to be admonished with an expression of brotherly love.

units.la: Vers. 2. Mulieres natu grandiores, ut Matres: juniores, ut sorores, cum omni puritate.
units.tr: Verse 2. Older women as mothers, younger women as sisters, with all purity.

units.la: Membrum 3. Ut fœminæ natu grandiores, cum honoris ætati ipsarum debiti significatione, admoneantur, ut sic gratior esset admonitio. 4. Ut fœminæ juniores, tanquam sorores admoneantur. Sed addit cum omni castitate, seu castitatis significatione, ne privatorum colloquiorum occasione, inter admonendum, diabolus posset pudicitiæ vel famæ, sive admonentis Timothei, sive admonitæ fœminæ insidiari.
units.tr: (3) Older women are to be admonished with the honour due to their age, so that the admonition may be more acceptable. (4) Younger women are to be admonished as sisters. But he adds with all chastity, or with a sign of chastity, lest in the course of admonishing, in private conversations, the devil should lay a snare for the chastity or reputation either of Timothy who admonishes or of the woman who is admonished.

units.la: Secunda pars Capitis.
units.tr: The second part of the chapter.

units.la: Vers. 3. Viduas honora quæ veré viduæ sunt.
units.tr: Verse 3. Honour widows who are truly widows.

units.la: Secunda pars Capitis, In qua septem præcepta dat, de viduis eleemosynariis, quæ publicis Ecclesiæ sumptibus alendæ erant.
units.tr: The second part of the chapter, in which he gives seven precepts concerning widows who receive alms, who were to be supported from the public funds of the Church.

units.la: Præceptum primum, Ut honoraret viduas veras, id est, publicis sumptibus Ecclesiæ alendas curaret, atque ita ipsarum æstimationi consuleret, ne ob inopiam destitutæ, despectui haberentur.
units.tr: The first precept: he should honour true widows, that is, see that they are supported from the public funds of the Church, and thus provide for their esteem, so that, left destitute through poverty, they are not held in contempt.

units.la: Vers. 4. Quod si qua vidua liberos aut nepotes habet, discant in primis in propriam domum pietatem exercere, & vicem rependere parentibus: hoc enim est honestum & acceptum coram Deo.
units.tr: Verse 4. But if any widow has children or grandchildren, let them first learn to show piety at home and to repay their parents; for this is good and acceptable before God.

units.la: Præceptum 2. Ne gravaret Ecclesiam alendo viduas illas, quæ à liberis vel nepotibus suis ali possent, sed curaret, ut liberi, & nepotes pietatis officio defungerentur, imprimis erga domesticos suos, matres vel avias suas alendo. Rationes præcepti sunt duæ: Prima, Quia sic vicem reponderent parentibus suis, qui liberos suos educarunt in eam spem, ut liberi (si opus esset) possent ἀντιπελαργεῖν, seu ciconiarum more parentes suos, ætate & viribus effetos, & re familiari destitutos, alere & fovere.
units.tr: The second precept: the Church is not to be burdened by supporting those widows who can be supported by their children or grandchildren; rather, he should see that the children and grandchildren discharge the duty of piety, especially towards their own household, supporting their mothers or grandmothers. There are two reasons for the precept. The first: because in this way they repay their parents, who reared their children in the hope that, if need arose, the children could antipelargein [ἀντιπελαργεῖν], that is, after the manner of storks, support and cherish their parents, worn out by age and strength and destitute of means.

units.la: Hoc enim ] Ratio 2. Quia hoc officium erga parentes præstitum, Deo est gratum, utpote ab ipso imperatum.
units.tr: For this ] The second reason: because this duty performed towards parents is pleasing to God, as being commanded by him.

units.la: Vers. 5. Porrò quæ veré vidua ac sola est, speret in Deo, & permanet in supplicationibus & precibus nocte ac die.
units.tr: Verse 5. Now she who is truly a widow and alone trusts in God, and continues in supplications and prayers night and day.

units.la: Præceptum 3. Ut in Electione viduarum observet, ne vidua eligenda destituatur verè viduæ, seu viduæ Christianæ ab Ecclesia alendæ, proprietatibus; quarum hic enumerat quatuor: 1. Requiritur ut sola sit, id est, destituta liberis & nepotibus, & omni ope humana: 2. Ut sit fidelis, in Deum speransr nullis artibus malis sibi victum comparare studens, sed à Deo pendens: 3. Ut dedita sit exercitiis pietatis assiduè.
units.tr: The third precept: in the choosing of widows he should observe that the widow to be chosen, a true widow, or a Christian widow to be supported by the Church, has the following qualities, of which he lists four: (1) It is required that she be alone, that is, without children or grandchildren and without any human help. (2) That she be faithful, trusting in God, not seeking to obtain her living by any wicked arts, but depending on God. (3) That she be constantly devoted to the exercises of piety.

units.la: Verf. 6. At quæ in luxu vivit, ea vivens mortua est.
units.tr: Verse 6. But she who lives in pleasure is dead while she lives.

units.la: 4. Ne sit de numero lascivientium viduarum, quæ otio, suo & voluptatibus tantum studeant, de pietatis exercitiis securæ.
units.tr: (4) She must not be among the number of wanton widows, who devote themselves to idleness and pleasures, and are careless of the exercises of piety.

units.la: Mortuæ ] Ratio hujus requisiti redditur, quia illæ inutiles mulierculæ sunt tanquam mortuæ dum vivunt, & respectu Dei, cum non serviunt, & respectu societatis humanæ, cui nihil ulla sua opera prodesse studeant.
units.tr: Dead ] The reason for this requirement is given: such useless women are as dead while they live, both in respect of God, since they do not serve him, and in respect of human society, to which they strive to do no good by any work of theirs.

units.la: Verf. 7. Hæc igitur denuntiato, ut sint irreprehensæ.
units.tr: Verse 7. These things therefore command, that they may be blameless.

units.la: Claudit præceptum de urgendis proprietatibus verarum viduarum, ratione reddita à fine, ut omnes viduæ quæcunque demum sint, discant vitam agere inculpatam.
units.tr: He concludes the precept concerning the urging of the qualities of true widows, giving as the reason its end: that all widows, whatever they may be, may learn to live blamelessly.

units.la: Verf. 8. Quod si quis suis, & maximè domesticis non providet, fidem abnegavit, & est infideli deterior.
units.tr: Verse 8. But if anyone does not provide for his own, and especially for those of his household, he has denied the faith and is worse than an unbeliever.

units.la: Præceptum 4. De judicio habendo in eos qui viduas matres vel avias suas alere recusant, sicut præcepto secundo hujus Capitis præscriptum est, nempe ut excommunicentur ab Ecclesia, & ut habeantur pro Christianæ doctrinæ desertoribus, pro Ethnicis seu infidelibus, donec resipuerint, quod est consequens excommunicationis.
units.tr: The fourth precept: concerning the judgement to be passed on those who refuse to support their widowed mothers or grandmothers, as was prescribed in the second precept of this chapter; namely, that they be excommunicated from the Church, and be regarded as deserters of Christian doctrine, as heathens or unbelievers, until they repent, which follows from excommunication.

units.la: Verf. 9. Vidua eligatur non minor annis sexaginta, quæ fuerit unius viri uxor.
units.tr: Verse 9. Let a widow be chosen who is not less than sixty years old, who has been the wife of one husband.

units.la: Præceptum 5. De observandis tribus aliis requisitis in admissione viduarum ad communem mensam, ut sustententur ex publicis sumptibus. Primum est, ut Vidua sit annorum sexaginta minimum, quā ætate defervere solent cupiditates carnis, & homines ad victum comparandum manuario aliquo exercitio impotentes sunt. 2. Ut univira fuerit, seu quæ Matrimonii leges non violaverit, ex quo spes sit pudicæ, & continentis fœminæ.
units.tr: The fifth precept: concerning the observance of three other requirements for the admission of widows to the common table, to be sustained from the public funds. The first is that the widow be at least sixty years old, an age at which the desires of the flesh usually cool, and people are unable to earn their living by any manual labour. (2) That she have been the wife of one husband, that is, one who has not violated the laws of marriage, from which there is hope of a chaste and continent woman.

units.la: Verf. 10. In operibus bonis idoneo testimonio ornata, si liberos educavit, educavit, si fuit hospitalis, si sanctorum pedes lavit, si afflictis subvenit, si omne bonum opus est assiduè secutus.
units.tr: Verse 10. Well reported of for good works; if she has brought up children, if she has lodged strangers, if she has washed the feet of the saints, if she has relieved the afflicted, if she has diligently followed every good work.

units.la: Requisitum 3. Ut testimonium habeat pietatis, factis & operibus declaratæ, potissimum in his quinque, quæ servientibus pauperibus ægrotis idoneam demonstrent: Nempe, primò, Si liberos honestè educaverit:
units.tr: The third requirement: that she have a testimony of piety, shown by deeds and works, especially in these five, which show her fit to serve the poor and the sick. Namely: first, if she has brought up children honourably;

units.la: 2. Si hospitalitatem exercuerit: 3. Si ad infima officia charitatis, etiam in lavandis pedibus, ubi opus erat, se dimiserit, vel dimittere parata fuerit: 4 Si afflictis ex commiseratione subvenerit: Denique, si omne genus bonorum operum secuta fuerit.
units.tr: (2) if she has practised hospitality; (3) if she has humbled herself to the lowliest duties of charity, even to washing feet where that was needed, or has been ready to do so; (4) if she has relieved the afflicted out of compassion; and finally, if she has pursued every kind of good work.

units.la: Vers. 11. Porrò juniores viduas recusa; postquam enim lascivire coeperint adversus Christum, nubere volunt:
units.tr: Verse 11. But refuse the younger widows; for when they have begun to wax wanton against Christ, they will marry.

units.la: Præceptum 6. Ne admittant in collegium viduarum juniores viduas.
units.tr: The sixth precept: they are not to admit younger widows into the college of widows.

units.la: Postquam] Rationes reddit duas: Prima, Quia periculum est, ne sanctitate pane Ecclesiæ lascivire incipiant adversus Christum (sicut aliquæ juniores viduæ jam fecerant) & desperantes de connubio in Ecclesia, meditentur apostasiam à fide Christi, & postea apertè deficiant, ut infideli alicui extra Ecclesiam nubant.
units.tr: After] He gives two reasons. The first: there is a danger that, fed by the Church's bounty, they may begin to wax wanton against Christ (as some younger widows had already done), and, despairing of marriage within the Church, may plan apostasy from the faith of Christ, and afterwards openly fall away, to marry some unbeliever outside the Church.

units.la: Vers. 12. ex eo damnandæ quòd primam fidem rejecerint;
units.tr: Verse 12. to be condemned because they have cast off their first faith;

units.la: Hujus generis aliquas apostatas viduas notare videtur, quarum conditionem miseram & damnabilem ostendit, ex eo quod fidei professionem in baptismo primùm editam rejecerint.
units.tr: He seems to mark out some apostate widows of this sort, whose wretched and damnable condition he shows, from the fact that they have cast off the profession of faith first made in baptism.

units.la: Vers. 13. Simul autem etiam otiosæ, discunt circumire domos imò non solùm otiosæ, sed etiam nugaces & curiosæ, garrientes quæ non oportet.
units.tr: Verse 13. And at the same time they learn also to be idle, going about from house to house; and not only idle, but also tattlers and busybodies, speaking things which they ought not.

units.la: Ratio 1. Quia viduæ juniores, (ut experientia etiam tum comprobatum fuisse videtur) evadent otiosæ, vagæ, nugaces, curiosæ, loquaces, discurrentes per alienas domos, in alienà negotia curiosè inquirentes, & garrientes quæ non oportet.
units.tr: The first reason: because younger widows (as experience seems to have shown even then) turn out idle, wandering, gossiping, nosy, talkative, running through other people's houses, inquiring curiously into others' affairs, and speaking things they should not.

units.la: Vers. 14. Vélim igitur juniores nubere; liberos gignere, domum administrare, nullam occasionem dare adversario ad maledicendum.
units.tr: Verse 14. I will therefore that the younger women marry, bear children, rule the household, and give no occasion to the adversary to speak reproachfully.

units.la: Præceptum 7. vel concessio, Ut juniores viduæ nubant in Domino, potius quam Ecclesiæ sint oneri, & ut domestica officia curent, quæ decent uxores. Nullam] Rationes præcepti addit duas: Prima, Ne adversariis seu infidelibus ansam male loquendi de Evangelii professoribus, per suam inconstantiam & peccata alia præbeant.
units.tr: The seventh precept, or permission: that younger widows should marry in the Lord, rather than be a burden to the Church, and that they should attend to domestic duties, which become wives. No] He adds two reasons for the precept. The first: that they should not give the adversaries or unbelievers an occasion to speak evil of the professors of the Gospel, through their inconstancy and other sins.

units.la: Verf. 15. Jam enim nonnulla deflexerunt, sequuntę satanam.
units.tr: Verse 15. For some have already turned aside after Satan.

units.la: Ratio 2. Quia experientia jam compertum est aliquas juniores viduas à vera religione deflexisse, & in Satanæ castra extra Ecclesiæ pomœria ultro recesserint.
units.tr: The second reason: because experience has already shown that some younger widows have turned away from the true religion, and of their own accord have withdrawn into the camp of Satan, outside the bounds of the Church.

units.la: Verf. 16. Quod siquis fidelis aut siqua fidelis habet viduas, eis subvenito, & non onerator Ecclesia, ut iis quæ verè viduæ sunt subveniat:
units.tr: Verse 16. If any faithful man or woman has widows, let them relieve them, and let not the Church be burdened, so that it may relieve those who are truly widows.

units.la: Inculcat præceptum secundum, de quo verf. 4. de alendis viduis à suis liberis vel nepotibus, additis duabus rationibus: 1. Ne gravetur Ecclesia non necessariis sumptibus: 2. Ne non sufficiant sumptus alendis veris viduis. Unde patet, quod si nullæ fuissent in Ecclesia lexagenariæ pauperes & probæ viduæ, non necesse fuisset ullas viduas alere; & per consequens ministerium fœminarum in diaconatu non esse necessarium, nisi per accidens cum publico sumptu alendæ sunt, ne planè sint inutiles.
units.tr: He inculcates the second precept, mentioned in verse 4, about supporting widows by their own children or grandchildren, adding two reasons: (1) so that the Church is not burdened with unnecessary expenses; (2) so that the means are not insufficient to support the true widows. Hence it is clear that if there were no sixty-year-old, poor and upright widows in the Church, it would not have been necessary to support any widows; and consequently the ministry of women in the diaconate would not be necessary, except incidentally, when they must be supported at public expense, lest they be wholly useless.

units.la: Tertia pars Capitis.
units.tr: Third part of the chapter.

units.la: Verf. 17. Qui bene præsunt presbyteri, duplici honore digni habentur: maximè qui laborant in sermone & doctrina:
units.tr: Verse 17. Let the elders who rule well be counted worthy of double honour, especially those who labour in the word and doctrine.

units.la: Tertia pars Capitis de Presbyteris, de quibus præcepta dat quinque: Primum, Ut honorarium, seu stipendium cum honore conjunctum omnibus Presbyteris, qui pascendæ Ecclesiæ bene præsunt, honestè exhibeatur. Dicitur autem Digni habentur, Quia si forte in aliquibus Ecclesiis, ut pauperioribus, facultates non suppetant, vel si Presbyteris quibusdam suas ob rationes visum fuerit Ecclesiæ gratis servire, in tali casu æquum est, ut digni saltem habeantur duplici, seu liberali stipendio, sive exigant, sive non.
units.tr: The third part of the chapter concerns the elders, and he gives five precepts. The first: that a salary, or stipend joined with honour, be honourably provided for all elders who rule well in feeding the Church. They are said to be "counted worthy" because, if in some congregations, the poorer ones, the resources do not suffice, or if some elders, for their own reasons, have chosen to serve the Church without pay, then in such a case it is fair that they be counted worthy at least of a double, or liberal, stipend, whether they demand it or not.

units.la: Maxime ] Horum Presbyterorum duos facit ordines: Alterum eorum qui laborant in sermone & doctrina, quales sunt Pastores & Doctores. Alterum eorum qui bene quidem præsunt, i. gubernandæ Ecclesiæ in vita & moribus incumbunt, & non laborant in sermone & doctrina, quales sunt Seniores qui Gubernatores vocantur, 1 Cor. 12 28. Rom 12. 8. Utrumque genus Presbyterorum rectè suo munere fungentium honore insigni dignos haberi vult, sed maximè seu potissimum laborantes in sermone & doctrina, quia illi toti segregantur ad sermonem & precationem. Idcirco ut illi liberaliter sustententur, æquum est. Vocat autem Sti-pendium perdium ipsis datum honoris nomine, quia tanti momenti labor non potest pretio ullo aestimari: Et quia quod datur stipendium, non mercedis, sed honorarii nomine dandum est.
units.tr: Especially] He divides these elders into two orders: one of those who labour in the word and doctrine, such as the ministers and teachers; and another of those who indeed rule well, that is, attend to governing the Church in life and conduct, and do not labour in word and doctrine, such as the elders who are called governors, 1 Cor. 12:28; Rom. 12:8. He wishes both kinds of elders who discharge their office rightly to be counted worthy of distinguished honour, but especially, or chiefly, those who labour in word and doctrine, because they are wholly set apart for preaching and prayer. Therefore it is fair that they be supported generously. He calls the stipend given to them "honour" by name, because labour of such weight cannot be valued at any price; and because what is given is to be given not as wages but under the name of an honorarium.

units.la: Verf. 18. Dicit enim Scriptura, Bovi trituranti non obligabis os. Et, Dignus est operarius mercede sua.
units.tr: Verse 18. For the Scripture says, You shall not muzzle the ox that treads out the corn. And, The labourer is worthy of his hire.

units.la: Rationes praecepti dat duas: 1. Est ex Deuter. 25. 4. Ubi ex allegoria bovis triturantis, & pedibus triticum excutientis jubet Deus ali Pastores Ecclesiae: a minori ad majus, argumentatione facta.
units.tr: He gives two reasons for the precept. The first is from Deut. 25:4, where, by an allegory of the ox treading out the grain and threshing it with its feet, God orders the ministers of the Church to be fed: an argument from the less to the greater.

units.la: Dignus ] Altera ratio ex Levit. 9. vel Luc. 18. 7. Ubi ex praecepto de mercede debita reddenda mercenario, colligitur a minori ad majus, honos multo magis rependendus ei, qui non est mercenarius, sed Pater, & Pastor laboriosus.
units.tr: Worthy] The second reason is from Lev. 9 or Luke 10:7, where from the precept that the wages due must be paid to the hireling, it is inferred, from the less to the greater, that honour must much more be repaid to him who is not a hireling but a father and a laborious pastor.

units.la: Verf. 19. Adversus presbyterum accusationem ne admittito, nisi sub duobus aut tribus testibus.
units.tr: Verse 19. Do not receive an accusation against an elder, except under two or three witnesses.

units.la: Praeceptum 2. Ne accusatio admittatur, seu pro vera recipiatur adversus Presbyterum, nisi ex Testimonio trium, aut saltem duorum testium fide dignorum, confirmetur: quod autem hic dicitur uni Timotheo, dicitur omnibus in Presbyterio sedentibus, quia alibi, toti Presbyterio Judicium commendatum est, imo vero quod hic Timotheo dicitur, toti Presbyterio Ephesino dicitur, de administranda tota Ecclesiae disciplina, Act. 20. 28. Potuit interim Timotheus Euangelista extraordinariam potestatem exercere, qua Euangelista & Legatus Apostoli.
units.tr: Precept 2. An accusation against an elder must not be admitted, or received as true, unless it is confirmed by the testimony of three, or at least two, trustworthy witnesses. What is said here to Timothy alone is said to all who sit in the eldership, because elsewhere the judgment is committed to the whole eldership; indeed, what is said here to Timothy is said to the whole Ephesian eldership, concerning the administration of the whole church discipline, Acts 20:28. Meanwhile Timothy, as an evangelist, could exercise an extraordinary power, as an evangelist and legate of the Apostle.

units.la: Verf. 20 Eos qui peccant, coram omnibus argue, ut & reli-qui timeant.
units.tr: Verse 20. Those who sin, rebuke in the sight of all, so that the rest also may fear.

units.la: Praeceptum 3. de scandalis vitandis, Si palam peccaverint Presbyteri, vel quivis alii in Ecclesia, ut publice arguantur & reprehendantur. Ratio redditur, Ut reliqui timeant eorum exemplo moniti, caveantque sibi ne peccent.
units.tr: Precept 3, concerning the avoiding of scandals: if elders, or any others in the Church, sin openly, they are to be publicly rebuked and reproved. The reason is given: that the rest, warned by their example, may fear and take care not to sin.

units.la: Verf. 21. Obtestor in conspectu Dei, & Domini Iesu Christi, & electorum angelorum ut haec serves absque eo ut unum alteri praeferas, nihil faciens in alteram partem declinando.
units.tr: Verse 21. I charge you in the sight of God, and of the Lord Jesus Christ, and of the elect angels, to keep these things without preferring one to another, doing nothing by inclining to either side.

units.la: Praeceptum 4 In quo (quasi per Epiphonema) gravissime Timotheum, & in eo omnes Ecclesiasticos Judices obtestatur, ne quid in censuris vel rebus Ecclesiasticis studio partium ab iis fiat, vel in hisce praeceptis ex aliqua Protopolepsia, quicquam immutetur.
units.tr: Precept 4. In it, as if by an epiphonema, he most solemnly adjures Timothy, and in him all ecclesiastical judges, that nothing be done in censures or ecclesiastical matters from partisan zeal, and that nothing in these precepts be altered from any preconceived opinion.

units.la: Verf. 22. Manus cito ne cui imponito, neque communicato peccatis alienis: temetipsum purum serva.
units.tr: Verse 22. Lay hands hastily on no one, nor share in the sins of others: keep yourself pure.

units.la: Præceptum 5. Ne temere quenquam ad sacrum ministerium recipiat, aut sine maturo consilio, & prævia examinatione habita cuiquam manus imponat, quod erat ordinationis signum. Rationes addit duas.
units.tr: Precept 5. He must not rashly receive anyone into the sacred ministry, nor lay hands on anyone, which was the sign of ordination, without mature counsel and prior examination. He adds two reasons.

units.la: Neque] Prima, Ne si ineptum ordinaret, hoc ipso communicaret illius peccatis, & pœnis per consequens.
units.tr: Nor] The first: lest, if he ordained an unfit man, he would by that very act share in his sins, and consequently in his punishments.

units.la: Temetipsum] Ratio 2. Quia in omni re castum te purumque ab inquinamentis conservare debes. Et propterea etiam ab ordinatione indigni. Si forte aliquando reliqui Presbyteri statuerint admittendum ad ministerium ineptum aliquem, aut non comprobatum, ut te purum conservres, nec consentias, sed studeas omni modo castitatem & puritatem ita conservare ut ab affinitate omnis peccati abssis, quam poteris longissime, & in hoc, & in omni alio negotio. Hujus præcepti partes explicat duobus proximè sequentibus versiculis, sensum posterioris partis de puritate servanda verf. 23. & prioris partis sensum ostendendo, verf. 24.
units.tr: Keep yourself] The second reason: because in every matter you ought to keep yourself chaste and pure from defilements. And therefore also from ordaining the unworthy. If at any time the other elders decide to admit to the ministry some unfit or unapproved person, you must keep yourself pure, not consent, but strive in every way to keep chastity and purity, so as to stay as far as you can from any association with every sin, both in this and in every other business. He explains the parts of this precept in the two following verses: the sense of the latter part, on keeping purity, in verse 23, and the sense of the former part he shows in verse 24.

units.la: Verf. 23. Ne amplius esto abstemius; sed vino pauculo utere, propter stomachum tuum & crebras tuas infirmitates.
units.tr: Verse 23. No longer be a water-drinker, but use a little wine for your stomach and your frequent infirmities.

units.la: Quod ad posteriorem partem, depuritate servanda, attinet: Quia Apostolus noverat Timotheum præ puritatis, seu castitatis studio, valetudinem suam jam læsisse: idcirco obiter admonet, ne sic Præceptum de conservandâ puritate accipiat, ut valetudinem suam negligat, seque ad officia vocationis ineptum reddat, sed prudentiâ utatur sanctâ, & in frænando corpore per aquæ bibitionem modum servet, & pauculo vino quasi pro medicina, & necessitate valetudinis utatur, ne si pergeret debilitato jam stomacho & infirmitatibus crebris laboranti corpori suo non parcere, statim rueret corpusculi ipsius tabernaculum, atque ita utili instrumento defraudaretur Ecclesia.
units.tr: As to the latter part, on keeping purity: since the Apostle knew that Timothy, from zeal for purity or chastity, had already impaired his health, he therefore admonishes in passing that the precept on keeping purity should not be so taken that he neglects his health and renders himself unfit for the duties of his calling; but that he should use holy prudence, keep moderation in restraining the body by drinking water, and use a little wine as a medicine and out of necessity for his health. Otherwise, if he went on not sparing his body, already weakened in the stomach and labouring under frequent infirmities, the tabernacle of that little body would soon collapse, and the Church would be deprived of a useful instrument.

units.la: Verf. 24. Quorundam hominum peccata ante manifesta sunt, præeuntia damnationi: quosdam vero subsequuntur:
units.tr: Verse 24. The sins of some men are evident beforehand, going before to judgment; but for some they follow after:

units.la: Quod ad sensum prioris partis præcepti attinet, ne communicaret peccatis alienis, ostendit se loqui de peccatis manifestis, quæ cognosci & caveri possunt, non de occultis quæ observari non possunt, quod autem cavere possit, ne alienis peccatis communicet, & ne tenere manus alicui imponat ostendit ex eo, quod adhibita examinatione, manifesta peccata cujusvis indigni dignosci possint: sicut etiam manifestæ virtutes idonei viri qui ri qui ad Ministerium Euangelii admittatur. Nam aliquorum candidatorum Ministerii, peccata adeo manifesta sunt, ut Examen & Judicium Ecclesiæ autevertant, ita ut facilè rejici possint: Priusquam enim Judicium Ecclesiasticum de iis statui poslit, parata est materia in manife- stis ipsorum peccatis ad damnationem ipsorum, seu rejectionem à Ministerio ex sententia Senatus Ecclesiastici: aliorum vero peccata præmisso examine & judicio Ecclesiastico de iis habito, in lucem educuntur.
units.tr: As to the sense of the former part of the precept, that he should not share in the sins of others, he shows that he is speaking of manifest sins, which can be known and guarded against, not of hidden sins, which cannot be observed. That one can guard against sharing in others' sins, and against laying hands on anyone, he shows from the fact that, with examination applied, the manifest sins of any unworthy person can be discerned, just as the manifest virtues of a fit man who is to be admitted to the ministry of the Gospel can be. For the sins of some candidates for the ministry are so manifest that they anticipate the examination and judgment of the Church, so that they can easily be rejected: for before a church judgment can be made about them, the matter is ready in their manifest sins for their condemnation, or rejection from the ministry by the sentence of the ecclesiastical senate. But the sins of others, once examination and ecclesiastical judgment on them have been held, are brought to light.

units.la: Vers. 25. Itidem & bona opera ante manifesta sunt: & ea quæ secus habent, occultari non possunt.
units.tr: Verse 25. Likewise good works are manifest beforehand, and those that are otherwise cannot be hidden.

units.la: Similiter & quorundam candidatorum Ministerii virtutes, & opera bona adeò nota sunt, ut facilè sit Ecclesiæ de illis judicare quod admittendi sint. Quorum vero opera secùs se habent, vel examine habito & inquisitione facta non patefiunt, vel adeo sunt occulta, ut sciri non possint ab hominibus, relinquenda sunt Deo, nec possunt tamen diu latere, quin suo tempore in lucem proferantur, ut si Ecclesia cavere non possit, quin admittantur hypocritæ isti ad Ministerium, curare tamen poterit ubi jam manifesti facti sint, ut pro ratione disciplinæ Ecclesiasticæ tractentur.
units.tr: Similarly, the virtues and good works of some candidates for the ministry are so well known that it is easy for the Church to judge of them that they are to be admitted. But whose works are otherwise, and are not disclosed after examination and inquiry, or are so hidden that they cannot be known by men, are to be left to God; yet they cannot long remain concealed, but in their time will be brought to light, so that if the Church cannot prevent such hypocrites from being admitted to the ministry, it will nevertheless be able to take care, once they have been made manifest, that they are dealt with according to the manner of ecclesiastical discipline.

units.la: Caput Sextum.
units.tr: Chapter 6.

units.la: HOC Capite Præcepta dat Timotheo septem, quibus instituatur in doctrina de officiis privatorum, & de officiis Ministrorum, quomodo & erga Populum, & erga Presbyteros se gerere debeat.
units.tr: In this chapter he gives Timothy seven precepts, by which he is instructed in the teaching on the duties of private persons and on the duties of ministers, and on how he ought to conduct himself both towards the people and towards the elders.

units.la: Vers. 1. Quicunque sub jugo sunt servi, suos dominos omni honore dignos ducunto, ne nomen DEI & doctrina blasphemetur.
units.tr: Vers. 1. As many as are servants under the yoke, let them count their own masters worthy of all honour, that the name of God and the doctrine be not blasphemed.

units.la: Primum præceptum de instituendis servis Christianis, qui conditione sunt servi, & alieno jugo subditi, est, Ut suos Dominos, etiam infideles, omni honore dignos æstiment, quibus ipsi serviant, tanquam in altiori gradu ex DEI providentia collocatis.
units.tr: The first precept, concerning the instruction of Christian servants, who are in the condition of slaves and subject to another's yoke, is that they should regard their masters, even unbelieving ones whom they serve, as worthy of all honour, since they have been placed by the providence of God in a higher rank.

units.la: Ne Dei] Ratio præcepti est, Ne si secùs fecerint, malè audiat Euangelium, & conviciis incessatur ab infidelibus, servorum Christiano-rum iminorigerorum vitio.
units.tr: Lest the name of God: the reason for the precept is that otherwise the Gospel would be ill spoken of and reviled by unbelievers, through the fault of Christian servants who behave badly.

units.la: Vers. 2 Qui vero fideles habent Dominos, ne eos despiciant quòd fratres sint: sed potius inserviant, quòd fideles sint ac dilecti, ut qui sint beneficii Dei participes, Hæc doce & exhortare.
units.tr: Vers. 2. But those who have believing masters, let them not despise them because they are brethren, but rather let them serve them all the more, because they are believers and beloved, and partakers of the benefit. These things teach and exhort.

units.la: Sin vero fideles sint Domini, retorquet quod objicere parati erant servi; & quia fraternitas Christianorum non tollit diversitatem conditionum in politia, vetat ne servi Dominos suos eo nomine, quasi pares in CHRISTO, contemnant, jubetque ut tanto promptius iis serviant, propterea, quod, Domini ipsorum fide præditi, & Deo dilecti essent, & hanc ob causam tanto magis digni, qui servitii ipsorum fructum perciperent; hæc ut ipse Timotheus doceat, & alios Pastores hortetur ad idem docendum, præcipit.
units.tr: But if the masters are believers, Paul turns back what the servants were ready to object. Since the brotherhood of Christians does not abolish the difference of conditions in civil society, he forbids servants to despise their masters on the ground that they are equals in Christ, and he orders them to serve them all the more readily, for the reason that their masters, endowed with faith and beloved of God, are for this very cause all the more worthy that they should receive the fruit of their service. Paul instructs Timothy himself to teach these things and to exhort the other ministers to teach the same.

units.la: Vers. 3. Siquis diversam docet doctrinam, neque accedit sanis sermonibus Domini nostri Iesu Christi, & ei quæ secundùm pietatem est doctrina,
units.tr: Vers. 3. If anyone teaches a different doctrine, and does not consent to the sound words of our Lord Jesus Christ, and to the doctrine which is according to godliness,

units.la: Præceptum 2. De vitandis perversis doctoribus, id est, à Ministerio vel arcendis, vel ejiciendis, vel ab Ecclesia excommunicandis: quales multi erant tum temporis ἑτεροδιδασκαλοι, qui vel à veritate Apostolica in sermonum materia, vel à simplicitate Apostolica, in ratione docendi discedebant, docentes vel alia, vel aliter, quam Apostoli; in simplicitate Christianæ pietatis non acquiescentes: à quorum studiis & moribus, tanquam causis meritoriis hujus castigationis, Rationes sex affert.
units.tr: Precept 2. Concerning the avoiding of perverse teachers, that is, that they are to be kept from the ministry, or removed from it, or excommunicated from the Church. Many such men there were at that time, heterodidaskaloi [ἑτεροδιδασκαλοι], who departed either from the Apostolic truth in the matter of their teaching, or from Apostolic simplicity in the manner of teaching, teaching either other things or otherwise than the Apostles did, and not resting in the simplicity of Christian godliness. Paul gives six reasons for the rebuke of these men, taking their pursuits and manners as the meritorious causes of it.

units.la: Non accedit Ratio prima, Obstinati sunt, qui se non subjiciunt sanis CHRISTI sermonibus, seu doctrinæ sanæ, quæ in materia & modo docendi est secundùm pietatem.
units.tr: Does not consent: the first reason is that they are obstinate, since they do not submit themselves to the sound words of Christ, or to sound doctrine, which in its matter and manner of teaching is according to godliness.

units.la: Vers. 4. Is turget, nihil sciens sed insaniens circa quæstiones ac verborum pugnas: ex quibus nascitur invidia, lis, maledicentia, suspiciones malæ,
units.tr: Vers. 4. He is puffed up, knowing nothing, but doting about questions and strifes of words, from which come envy, strife, railings, evil suspicions,

units.la: Ratio 1. Quia superbi sunt & inflati vanâ opinione scientiæ suæ, cum nihil solidè sciant in mysterio Euangelii.
units.tr: Reason 1. Because they are proud and inflated with the vain opinion of their own learning, while they know nothing solidly about the mystery of the Gospel.

units.la: Insaniens Ratio 3. Quia adeo sunt eristico ingenio, ut insaniant circa ineptas quæstiones & λογομαχίας.
units.tr: Doting: Reason 3. Because they have such a contentious disposition that they go mad over trifling questions and logomachiai [λογομαχίαι].

units.la: Ex quibus Ratio 4. Quia suis cavillationibus invidiam, contentionem, maledicentiam, & suspiciones pravas excitant.
units.tr: From which: Reason 4. Because by their cavils they stir up envy, contention, slander, and wicked suspicions.

units.la: Verf. 5. Perversæ exercitationes hominum mente corruptorum, & qui privati sunt veritate, & quæstui habent pietatem, secede ab iis qui ejusmodi sunt.
units.tr: Vers. 5. Perverse disputings of men of corrupt minds, and who are destitute of the truth, and suppose that gain is godliness: from such withdraw thyself.

units.la: Ratio 5. Quia suis perversis exercitationibus produnt se perversa esse & corrupta mente, destitutos veritate, & studiosiores quæstus quam pietatis, imo eos qui pietatem quæstu vendunt. Unde infert censuram se-cessionis ab iis, quod consequens est excommunicationis.
units.tr: Reason 5. Because by their perverse disputings they show that they have perverse and corrupt minds, destitute of the truth, and more eager for gain than for godliness; indeed they sell godliness for gain. Hence he infers the censure of withdrawal from them, which follows from excommunication.

units.la: Ver. 6. Est autem quæstus magnus, pietas cum animo suasor-te contento,
units.tr: Vers. 6. But godliness with contentment is great gain.

units.la: Præceptum 3. De sectanda pietate, tanquam quæstu maximo & vitanda avaritia,
units.tr: Precept 3. Concerning pursuing godliness as the greatest gain, and avoiding covetousness.

units.la: Rationes præcepti sunt octo: Ratio prima, Quia pietas est ejusmodi quæstus, qui sibi quasi sufficiens, animum in omni conditione contentum reddit, vel quæstus est qui secum affert sufficientiam veram.
units.tr: There are eight reasons for the precept. The first reason: godliness is a kind of gain which, being in a way sufficient for itself, makes the mind content in every condition; or it is a gain which brings true sufficiency with it.

units.la: Vers. 7. Nihil enim intulimus in mundum, videlicet nec effer- re quicquam possumus.
units.tr: Vers. 7. For we brought nothing into this world, and it is certain we can carry nothing out.

units.la: Ratio 2. Quia divitiæ in hac vita tantum, & non post mortem usum habent: Idcirco non inhiandum opibus.
units.tr: Reason 2. Because riches have their use only in this life and not after death; therefore we should not gasp after wealth.

units.la: Verf. 8. Sed habentes alimenta, & quibus tegamur, his contenti simus.
units.tr: Vers. 8. But having food and raiment, let us be therewith content.

units.la: Ratio 3. Quia divitiis etiam in hac vita carere possumus, & victu & amictu quali quali contenti esse debemus.
units.tr: Reason 3. Because even in this life we can do without riches, and we ought to be content with food and clothing, of whatever sort.

units.la: Verf. 9, Qui autem volunt ditescere, incidunt in tentationem & laqueum, & cupiditates multas amentes, & damnosas, quæ demergunt homines in exitium & interitum.
units.tr: Vers. 9. But those who desire to be rich fall into temptation and a snare, and many foolish and harmful lusts, which drown men in destruction and perdition.

units.la: Ratio 4. Quia qui divitiis congerendis maximè intenti sunt & destinato consilio iis inhiant, peccatis maximis, animi cruciatibus, amentiæ, & miseriæ in hoc mundo, & perditioni æternæ, proximi sunt.
units.tr: Reason 4. Because those who are wholly intent on heaping up riches, and set their minds on them with settled purpose, are close to the greatest sins, mental torments, folly and misery in this world, and to eternal ruin.

units.la: Verf. 10. Siquidem radix omnium malorum est amor pecuniæ: quam quidam dum appetunt, aberrarunt à fide, & seipsos transfixerunt doloribus multis.
units.tr: Vers. 10. For the love of money is the root of all evil, which some coveting after have erred from the faith, and pierced themselves through with many sorrows.

units.la: Ratio 5. Quia amor pecuniæ est radix omnium malorum, ut impietatis, mendaciorum, perjurii, crudelitatis, &c.
units.tr: Reason 5. Because the love of money is the root of all evils, such as impiety, lying, perjury, cruelty, and so on.

units.la: Quam quidam ] Ratio 6. Ab experientia aliquorum, qui pecuniæ aviditate defecerunt à religione Christiana, & se miserrimos reddiderunt.
units.tr: Which some: Reason 6. From the experience of certain people who, through greed for money, fell away from the Christian religion and made themselves most wretched.

units.la: Verf. 11.
units.tr: Vers. 11.

units.la: Tu vero, homo Dei, ista fuge: sectare autem justitiam, pietatem, fidem, charitatem, tolerantiam, lenitatem.
units.tr: But you, O man of God, flee these things; and follow after righteousness, godliness, faith, love, patience, gentleness.

units.la: cum applicatione speciali, Quia indignum est hoc vitium Ministro, qui est homo Dei, & ad Dei negotia coelestia separatus, qui idcirco debet fugere avaritiam & mundanas cupiditates.
units.tr: With a special application: this vice is unworthy of a minister, who is a man of God and set apart for the heavenly business of God, and who for that reason ought to flee covetousness and worldly desires.

units.la: Ratio 8. Quia decet Dei hominem, seu Ministrum Evangelii divitias virtutum affectare, & ex his alias aliis cumulare, quales enumerat sex.
units.tr: Reason 8. Because it becomes a man of God, that is, a minister of the Gospel, to aim at the riches of virtues, and to heap up one after another, such as Paul lists, six in number.

units.la: Decerta praeclarum certamen fidei: apprehende vitam aeternam, cujus causa & vocatus es, & professus praeclaram prosessionem coram multis testibus.
units.tr: Fight the good fight of faith; lay hold on eternal life, to which you were also called, and have professed a good profession before many witnesses.

units.la: Praeceptum 4. Ut omnibus legitimis mediis adhibitis, pro Evangelio propagando, & veritate doctrinae defendenda, fortiter & constanter contra omnes adversarios & impedimenta quaecunque decertet.
units.tr: Precept 4. That, by employing all lawful means for spreading the Gospel and defending the truth of doctrine, he should fight bravely and constantly against all adversaries and every hindrance.

units.la: Praeclarum ] Rationes hortationis, seu praecepti sunt quatuor: 1. Quia hoc certamen bonum, laudabile & utile est.
units.tr: Good: there are four reasons for the exhortation, or precept: 1. Because this fight is good, praiseworthy and useful.

units.la: Vitam ] Ratio 2. Quia sic vitam aeternam apprehensurus es.
units.tr: Lay hold: Reason 2. Because by this you will lay hold on eternal life.

units.la: Ad quam ] Ratio 3. Quia ad defensionem Evangelii, & participationem vitae, seu fidei, vocatus es. Professus ] Ratio 4. Jam praeclaram fidei confessionem coram multis testibus ediditi: Perge ergo praeclarum illud certamen fidei decertare.
units.tr: To which: Reason 3. Because you have been called to the defence of the Gospel and to participation in life, or faith. Have professed: Reason 4. You have already made a good confession of faith before many witnesses; continue, therefore, to fight that good fight of faith.

units.la: Denuntio tibi coram Deo qui vivificat omnia, & Iesu Christo, qui testatam fecit coram Pontio Pilato bonam illam professionem.
units.tr: I charge you in the sight of God, who quickens all things, and of Jesus Christ, who before Pontius Pilate witnessed that good confession.

units.la: Ut serves haec mandata, macula & culpa omni experts, usque ad illustrem illum adventum Domini nostri Jesu Christi.
units.tr: That you keep this commandment without spot, unrebukable, until the appearing of our Lord Jesus Christ.

units.la: Praeceptum 5. Cum gravissima & vehementissima obtestatione coram Deo & Christo Mediatore, ut Timotheus, & omnes post eum Pastores, aliique omnes quibus Ecclesiae cura incumbet, quos in ejus persona alloquitur, usque ad Christi adventum, haec mandata illibata conservent, seu ut munus sibi commissum ita exequantur, & has de Ecclesia regenda regulas fideliter observent, ut in doctrina & moribus inculpati, & irreprehensibiles comperiantur; & quia difficile erat id ad quod hortatur opus, Argumenta obtestationis, seu praecepti addit sex, quae omnia probant superiora mandata summa fide servanda.
units.tr: Precept 5. With the most grave and urgent adjuration, before God and Christ the Mediator, that Timothy, and all the ministers after him, and all others to whom the care of the Church is committed, whom he addresses in his person, should keep these commandments unblemished until the coming of Christ; or that they should so carry out the office committed to them, and faithfully observe these rules for governing the Church, that they may be found blameless and irreproachable in doctrine and in conduct. And because the work to which he exhorts is difficult, he adds six arguments for the adjuration, or precept, all of which prove that the above commandments are to be kept with the utmost faithfulness.

units.la: Vivificat ]
units.tr: Who quickens

units.la: Argumentum primum, Et ad sustinendam infirmitatem tuam,& ad te contra pericula ab hostibus tuis defendendum, satis est sub-sidii in Deo vivificante omnia : Ergo nihil obstat quominus fidelíter observés hæc omnia.
units.tr: The first argument: to sustain your weakness, and to defend you against the dangers from your enemies, there is sufficient help in God, who quickens all things. Therefore nothing stands in the way of your faithfully observing all these things.

units.la: Arg. 2. Christus exemplo suo tibi præivit, qui doctrinam suam fideliter exposuit in salutem Ecclesiæ, & tandem eam coram tribunali Pilati assertam, obeundo mortem voluntariam obsignavit : Ergo simi-liter tibi & Ecclesiæ Ministris observanda sunt superiora mandata.
units.tr: Argument 2. Christ has gone before you by his example, who faithfully set forth his doctrine for the salvation of the Church, and at last, when it was asserted before the tribunal of Pilate, sealed it by undergoing a voluntary death. Therefore the above commandments are likewise to be observed by you and by the ministers of the Church.

units.la: Arg. 3. Christus venturus est Judex viventium & mortuorum, ut unicuique secundum opera retribuat. Fideliter ergo observanda superiora mandata omnia.
units.tr: Third argument: Christ is to come as Judge of the living and the dead, to repay each one according to his works. Therefore all the above commandments are to be faithfully observed.

units.la: Vers. 15. Quem temporibus suis ostendet ille beatus, & solus Princeps, Rex regum, & Dominus dominorum:
units.tr: Verse 15: Which in his own times the blessed and only Potentate will show, the King of kings and Lord of lords:

units.la: Commoratur in hoc proximo argumento, & ne quis festinaret, aut moram adventus Christi ægrius ferret, ostendit eum constituto & maxime idoneo tempore venturum.
units.tr: He dwells on this next argument, and so that no one might hurry on or bear the delay of Christ's coming with impatience, he shows that Christ will come at the appointed and most fitting time.

units.la: Arg 4. Christus, seu Deus Pater, Filius, & Spiritus sanctus, cujus Ministerium agitur, solus est in se beatus, & potens, qui suos beare, & hostes perdere potest, ita ut omnium regum amicitiæ vel inimicitiæ ad ejus gratiam aut iram comparatæ, nihil sint; quia omnes Reges & Imperatores imperium mutuantur ab eo, pendent & reguntur ab eo, ejusque nutu stant vel cadunt : Ergo hæc ipsius mandata observanda sunt.
units.tr: Fourth argument: Christ, or God the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, whose ministry is being carried out, alone is blessed and powerful in himself, able to bless his own and destroy his enemies, so that the friendships or enmities of all kings, won by their favour or anger, count for nothing. For all kings and emperors borrow their power from him, depend on him and are governed by him, and at his nod they stand or fall. Therefore his commandments are to be observed.

units.la: Vers. 16. Qui solus habet immortalitatem, lucem habitans inaccessum, quem vidit nemo hominum, neque videre potest: cui honor & robur in æternum. Amen.
units.tr: Verse 16: Who alone has immortality, dwelling in unapproachable light, whom no man has seen or can see: to whom be honour and power everlasting. Amen.

units.la: Arg. 5. Quia vita æterna est in Christi manu, qui unus est cum Patre & Spiritu Sancto Deus, quippe qui solus à se immortalis est, & solus immortalitatem habet in sua potestate, ut communicet quibus vult : Ergo superiora mandata fideliter servanda sunt.
units.tr: Fifth argument: eternal life is in the hand of Christ, who is one God with the Father and the Holy Spirit, since he alone is immortal of himself, and alone has immortality in his power to communicate to whomever he wills. Therefore the above commandments are to be faithfully kept.

units.la: Arg. 6. Etiamsi rationes mandatorum ipsius nobis non constarent, ad obedientiam & fidem nostram tamen sufficit scire, quod in se Deus sit inaccefla lux, & secreta majestas, essentiam suam propriam ac peculiarem habens, quam capere non potest noster intellectus, nec beatificâ visione in hac vita mortali cernere : Ergo ejus voluntatem adorare, observare, & la-
units.tr: Sixth argument: even if the reasons for his commandments were not known to us, it is nevertheless enough for our obedience and faith to know that God in himself is unapproachable light and hidden majesty, having his own peculiar essence, which our intellect cannot grasp, nor discern by the blessed vision in this mortal life. Therefore it becomes us to adore, observe and

units.la: Xxx dare potius quam in eam scrutari nos decet, ipsi sit honor & potentia in æternum.
units.tr: praise his will rather than to pry into it; to him be honour and power for ever.

units.la: Vers. 17. Iis qui divites sunt in hoc seculo, denuntia ne efferantur animo, neque spem ponant in divitiis incertis, sed in Deo vivo, qui præbet nobis omnia copiosè ad fruendum:
units.tr: Verse 17: To those who are rich in this world, charge them not to be haughty in mind, nor to set their hope on uncertain riches, but on the living God, who richly provides us with all things to enjoy:

units.la: Præceptum 6. De admonendis ditioribus de officio suo duplici: Primum est, ut quod ad interiorem hominem attinet, ne animo elati propter divitias, præ se contemnant pauperes, neque opibus suis sed Deo viventi confidant. Hujus officii rationes reddit tres: 1. Quia divitiæ incertæ sunt: 2. Quia non sopulentia, sed Deus vitæ Autor est iis, qui in eum sperant: 3. Quia Deus dat & aufert pro arbitrio suo divitias, & reliqua omnia.
units.tr: Precept 6: on admonishing the rich about their twofold duty. The first is that, as far as the inner man is concerned, they should not, puffed up on account of their riches, despise the poor in comparison with themselves, nor trust in their wealth, but in the living God. He gives three reasons for this duty: (1) because riches are uncertain; (2) because it is not wealth but God who is the author of life to those who hope in him; (3) because God gives and takes away riches and all other things at his own pleasure.

units.la: Vers. 18. Ut alii benefaciant, ut divites sint operibus bonis, faciles ad impertiendum, facilis convivus:
units.tr: Verse 18: That they do good, that they be rich in good works, ready to give, willing to share:

units.la: Alterum officium divitum, ut quod ad externa opera attinet, beneficentiam erga egenos exerceant, adeoque generatim bonis operibus abundare studeant, faciles ad usum suarum facultatum cum aliis communicandum.
units.tr: The second duty of the rich, as far as outward works are concerned, is that they exercise beneficence towards the needy, and so strive to abound generally in good works, being ready to share the use of their means with others.

units.la: Vers. 19. Recondentes sibi ipsis fundamentum bonum in posterum, ut apprehendant æternam vitam.
units.tr: Verse 19: Laying up for themselves a good foundation for the time to come, that they may lay hold on eternal life.

units.la: Argumentum ad officium est, mercedis gratuitæ promissio, quia largiendo de bonis instabilibus, thesaurum durabilem & solidum reposituri sunt sibi in cœlo, & incedendo in via bonorum operum vitam æternam apprehensuri.
units.tr: The argument for this duty is the promise of a free reward: by giving away unstable goods, they will lay up for themselves a durable and solid treasure in heaven, and by walking in the way of good works they will lay hold on eternal life.

units.la: Vers. 20. Timothee, depositum serva, & aversare profanos de rebus inanibus clamores, & oppositiones falso nominatæ scientiæ:
units.tr: Verse 20: Timothy, keep that which is committed to you, and avoid the profane babblings and oppositions of what is falsely called knowledge:

units.la: Præceptum 7. & ultimum: Quo serio commendat Timotheo doctrinam Evangelii hactenus traditam, ut eam velut depositum quoddam ejus fidei commissum, fideliter custodiat, & ut profanas Sophistarum declamationes & rixas de rebus Divinis compescat, Rationes reddit tres: 1. Quia doctrinæ veritas est pretiosa instar thesauri: 2. Quia rixosæ disputationes vanæ sunt, & indignæ nomine Philosophiæ vel Scientiæ.
units.tr: Precept 7, and the last: he earnestly commends to Timothy the doctrine of the Gospel delivered so far, that he should guard it faithfully as a deposit, a trust committed to him, and that he should restrain the profane declamations and quarrels of the Sophists about divine things. He gives reasons: (1) because the truth of the doctrine is precious, like a treasure; (2) because contentious disputations are vain and unworthy of the name of philosophy or knowledge.

units.la: Vers. 21. Quam nonnulli pro se ferentes, circa fidem aberrarunt à scopo. Gratia sit tecum. Amen. Ratio 3. Quia experientia compertum est nonnullos professores scientiarum Philosophicarum, dum veritatis & simplicitatis Euangelii pertaesi ostentarent suam peritiam, aberrasse à scopo Euangelii, imò defecisse à fide. Tandem Apostolico voto Epistolam concludit, optans Timotheo Christi gratiam, absque qua nullum spirituale opus inchoari vel perfici, nulla tentatio diaboli vel mundi superari potest.
units.tr: Verse 21: Which some professing have erred concerning the faith, missing the mark. Grace be with you. Amen. Reason 3: because experience has shown that some professors of the philosophical sciences, while displaying their skill and weary of the truth and simplicity of the Gospel, have strayed from the aim of the Gospel, and indeed have fallen from the faith. Finally, with an apostolic wish, he concludes the Epistle, wishing Timothy the grace of Christ, without which no spiritual work can be begun or completed, and no temptation of the devil or the world can be overcome.

units.la: EXPOSITIO ANALYTICA EPISTOLAE SECUNDAE, AD TIMOTHEVM.
units.tr: EXPOSITION ANALYTICAL OF THE SECOND EPISTLE TO TIMOTHY.

units.la: Summarium.
units.tr: Summary.

units.la: Dem huius Epistolae scopus qui prioris, non solum ut instruatur & confirmetur Timotheus in praedicatione Euangelii, sed etiam ut in ejus persona Pastores omnes discant, quomodo Euangelii Ministerio rite defungi debeant. In quem finem, confirmatâ sua erga Timotheum voluntate, admonitiones subjicit quatuor. Capite primo, & totidem Capite secundo. Deinde confirmat, & consolatur Temotheum adversus falsos fratres, & adversus afflictiones, quae ipsi in defensione Euangelii tolerandae erant, Capite tertio. Denique condito quasi testamento gravissime obtestatur, ut muneris sui partes fideliter exequatur, variis in hunc finem propositis rationibus. Capite quarto.
units.tr: The aim of this Epistle is the same as that of the first: not only that Timothy may be instructed and confirmed in the preaching of the Gospel, but also that in his person all ministers may learn how they ought to discharge the ministry of the Gospel duly. To this end, having confirmed his own goodwill towards Timothy, he sets down four admonitions in the first chapter, and as many in the second. Then in the third chapter he confirms and comforts Timothy against false brethren and against the afflictions which he had to endure in defence of the Gospel. Finally, in the fourth chapter, having as it were drawn up a testament, he earnestly charges him to carry out faithfully the parts of his office, setting forth various reasons to this end.

units.la: Caput Primum.
units.tr: Chapter 1.

units.la: Post praefationem, quae tota ad persuadendum Timotheo de Apostoli in eum optima voluntate comparata est, verf. 6. Subjicit quatuor admonitiones, quibus ad fidelem Ministerii ipsius executionem animetur.
units.tr: After the preface, which is wholly devoted to persuading Timothy of the Apostle's excellent goodwill towards him, verse 6, he sets down four admonitions by which Timothy is to be stirred to the faithful performance of his ministry.

units.la: Verf. 1. PAulus Apostolus Iesu Christi per voluntatem DEI, secundum promissionem vitæ, quæ est in Christo Iesu.
units.tr: Verse 1. Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ by the will of God, according to the promise of life which is in Christ Jesus.

units.la: Ut doctrinæ huic sua constaret apud omnes autoritas, Apostolus Epistolæ suæ præmittit nomen, suum, officium, vocationem, & autoritatem sibi datam à Deo immediate: & denique summam doctrinæ Euangelii quam prædicabat, quæ est, promissio vitæ æternæ, credentibus in Iesum Christum secundum promissiones Prophetarum, in veteri Scriptura.
units.tr: So that his teaching might carry authority with all, the Apostle prefixes to his letter his name, his office, his calling, and the authority given him directly by God. Finally, he states the sum of the gospel doctrine he preached, namely the promise of eternal life to those who believe in Jesus Christ, according to the promises of the prophets in the Old Scripture.

units.la: Vers. 2. Timotheo dilecto filio, gratia, misericordia, pax à Deo Patre, & Christo Iesu Domino nostro.
units.tr: Verse 2. To Timothy, my dearly beloved son: grace, mercy, and peace from God the Father and Christ Jesus our Lord.

units.la: Ut Timotheum ad quem scribit Paulus omnibus Ecclesiis commendaret, Vocat eum dilectum filium suum potissimum, quia doctrinam quam à Paulo didicerat, fideliter instar Pauli prædicabat, Paulumque ut patrem in tota conversatione sua referebat; ideoque à Paulo diligebatur, & in æstimatione habebatur ut filius, cui omnia optima à Deo optat sicut in superiori Epistola.
units.tr: So that he might commend Timothy, to whom Paul writes, to all the churches, he calls him especially his dear son, because Timothy faithfully preached the doctrine he had learned from Paul, following Paul's example, and in the whole of his conduct he regarded Paul as a father. For this reason he was loved by Paul and held in esteem as a son, for whom Paul wishes every good thing from God, as in the earlier letter.

units.la: Vers. 3. Gratiam habeo Deo, cui servio à majoribus cum pura conscientia, ut assiduam tui memoriam teneo in precibus meis nocte ac die.
units.tr: Verse 3. I thank God, whom I serve from my forefathers with a pure conscience, that without ceasing I remember you in my prayers night and day.

units.la: Aliis tribus argumentis persuadere nititur Timotheo de suo in eum affectu.
units.tr: He seeks to convince Timothy of his affection towards him by three further arguments.

units.la: Memoriam] Argumentum primum, Quia assiduam recolit Timothei memoriam in precibus suis. Gratiam] Arg. 2. Quia meminisse Timothei æstimat pro beneficio sibiipsi à Deo dato, pro quo Deo agendas gratias agnoscit, & gratias agit: beneficium enim eximium est, & solis Sanctis datum, diligere Sanctos, seu quos Deus diligit. Hæc duo argumenta explicat & confirmat ex eo, quod sincero & non fucato animo, & precetur pro Timotheo, & gratias Deo agat pro eo: sinceritatem autem probat ex eo, quod non tantum in tota antea sta vita sua, semper studuerit conscientiam inviolatam conservare, ne quid ea reluctante faceret, sed etiam quod post conversionem suam ad fidem, in pura conscientia, id est, illuminata à Spiritu Sancto, & sanguine Christi purgata, studuerit servire Deo vero, Deo Israelis, seu Abrahami, Isaaci, Iacobi, reliquorumque fidelium majorum suorum Deo: nam qui Christum colit sincera mente, etiam Sanctum Israelis colit; Patrem, & Spiritum Sanctum colit, Triunum verum
units.tr: Remember] The first argument: because he keeps Timothy's memory constantly in his prayers. I thank] Second argument: because he counts the remembrance of Timothy a benefit given him by God, for which he acknowledges that thanks are due to God and gives them. For it is an remarkable benefit, and given only to the saints, to love the saints, or those whom God loves. He explains and confirms these two arguments from the fact that he prays for Timothy and gives thanks to God for him with a sincere and unfeigned heart. He proves his sincerity from the fact that not only throughout his former life has he always striven to keep his conscience inviolate, so as never to do anything against its prompting, but also that since his conversion to the faith he has striven, with a pure conscience, that is, one enlightened by the Holy Spirit and cleansed by the blood of Christ, to serve the true God, the God of Israel, or of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, and the God of the other faithful forefathers. For whoever worships Christ with a sincere mind also worships the Holy One of Israel; he worships the Father and the Holy Spirit, the true triune

units.la: Memoriam] Argumentum primum: Gratiam] Arg. 2. verum DEUM colit, & eandem veram religionem cum omnibus Sanctis Patribus tenet.
units.tr: Remember] First argument. I thank] Second argument. God, and holds the same true religion as all the holy fathers.

units.la: Vers. 4. Desiderans te videre, memor tuarum lacrhymarum, ut gaudeo replear:
units.tr: Verse 4. Longing to see you, mindful of your tears, that I may be filled with joy.

units.la: Aug. 3. Quod desiderio Timotheum videndi coram teneretur, ut ejus consortio frui posset. Hoc argumentum illustrat a tribus causis desiderii sui: quarum prima est memoria lachrymarum Timothei, seu tenerrimi ejus affectus, cum erga Deum, tum erga se propter Deum, a quo discedente Timotheus non potuit divelli, nisi cum lachrymis: altera erat spes gaudii non mediocris obtinendi ex ejus aspectu.
units.tr: Third argument: that Paul was held by a desire to see Timothy in person, so that he might enjoy his company. He illustrates this argument by three causes of his longing. The first is the memory of Timothy's tears, that is, of his very tender affection, both towards God and towards Paul for God's sake, from whom Timothy could not be parted except with tears. The second was the hope of obtaining no small joy from seeing him.

units.la: Vers. 5. Revocans in memoriam meam quae in te est, non simulatam fidem, quae habitavit prius in avia tua Loide, & matre tua Eunica: persuasus sum autem quod in te quoque.
units.tr: Verse 5. Calling to remembrance the unfeigned faith that is in you, which dwelt first in your grandmother Lois and your mother Eunice; and I am persuaded that it is in you also.

units.la: Causa 3. Desiderii, erat memoria sincerae fidei ipsius, qualis erat in ipsius avia & matre, quae in fide Mediatoris obierunt (utrum prius quam revelatus est iis Christus, Deus in carne manifestatus, incertum est, sed in Christum venturum secundum promissiones credidisse eas, certum est) in qua spe Timotheus a puero educatus erat per matrem, & in Scripturis ab ea institutus.
units.tr: The third cause of his longing was the remembrance of Timothy's sincere faith, such as was in his grandmother and mother, who died in faith in the Mediator. (Whether they believed before Christ, God manifest in the flesh, was revealed to them is uncertain, but that they believed in the coming of Christ according to the promises is certain.) In this hope Timothy had been brought up from boyhood by his mother, and instructed by her in the Scriptures.

units.la: Vers. 6. Quam ob causam suggero tibi, ut excitates donum Dei quod est in te per impositionem manuum mearum.
units.tr: Verse 6. For this reason I remind you to stir up the gift of God that is in you through the laying on of my hands.

units.la: Post praefationem sequuntur admonitiones quatuor. Prima est, tanquam consectarium, ex superioribus illata, ut igniculos facultatis Evangelii praedicandi, & donorum in eum collatorum, in hunc finem, per preces Ecclesiae, quando nomine Presbyterii Paulus eum in praedicatorem ordinabat, jam excitaret in se, & vim donorum sibi concessorum fortiter, & prudenter in Ministerii sui executione explicaret, contra omnia impedimenta, quae caro, mundus, & Diabolus opponerent.
units.tr: After the preface follow four admonitions. The first is drawn, as a corollary, from what has been said above: that Timothy should now rekindle in himself the sparks of his gift for preaching the gospel and of the gifts bestowed on him, for this purpose, through the prayers of the Church, when Paul, on behalf of the presbytery, ordained him as a preacher. He is to exercise the power of the gifts given him strongly and wisely in the discharge of his ministry, against all the hindrances which the flesh, the world and the Devil might set in his way.

units.la: Vers. 7. Non enim dedit nobis Deus Spiritum timiditatis, sed roboris, & charitatis, & sanitatis animi.
units.tr: Verse 7. For God has not given us a spirit of fear, but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind.

units.la: Admonitionis rationes sunt duae: 1. Quia Spiritus timiditatis (per quem quis non audet dicere & facere id quod debet, & quod dicturus vel facturus esset in Ministerio suo, nisi timor subesset) non est a Deo, nec decet Ministrum Dei.
units.tr: The admonition has two grounds. 1. Because the spirit of fear (by which a man does not dare to say and do what he ought, and what he would say or do in his ministry if fear did not hold him back) is not from God, and does not befit a minister of God.

units.la: Roboris ] Ratio 2. Quia Spiritus donum, quod Deus suis genuinis Ministris dat, est, 1. Spiritus potentiæ & efficaciæ, qui omni altitudini adversum Christum insurgenti, audeat, & valeat sese opponere, & 2. Spiritus charitatis, qui zelo non abripiatur à verâ dilectione hominum, & 3. Spiritus sanitatis animi, qui nec præpostero zelo, nec charitate stolida seu carnali transversum rapiatur à sanæ doctrinæ veritate, sed qui animum sanum in doctrina fidei, & cor charitate refertum reddat, & zelum rerum pro Christo fortiter gerendarum in corde accendat, & omnia hæc dona suâ conjunctione sacrâ, inter se colligata contineat.
units.tr: Of power] Second ground. The gift of the Spirit that God gives to his genuine ministers is: (1) a spirit of strength and effectiveness, which dares and is able to set itself against everything that rises up against Christ; (2) a spirit of love, which is not swept aside by zeal from true love of mankind; and (3) a spirit of a sound mind, which is not carried off course by a perverse zeal or by a foolish or carnal love away from the truth of sound doctrine, but which makes the mind sound in the doctrine of faith and the heart full of love, and kindles in the heart the zeal to carry out bravely the affairs of Christ, and holds all these gifts together in their holy bond.

units.la: Vers. 8. Ne igitur te pudeat testimonii Domini nostri, neque te pudeat mei, qui sum captivus ipsius: sed esto particeps afflictionum Euangelii ex potentia Dei:
units.tr: Verse 8. Be not ashamed therefore of the testimony of our Lord, nor of me his prisoner; but be a partaker of the afflictions of the gospel according to the power of God.

units.la: Admonitio 2. Ut Timotheus nec erubescat simplicitatem veritatis Euangelii, nec crucem Christi in servo suo Paulo, sed cruci & afflictionibus pro Christo ferendis se accingat, & serentibus crucem se associet.
units.tr: Second admonition: that Timothy should not be ashamed of the simplicity of the truth of the gospel, nor of the cross of Christ in his servant Paul, but should prepare himself for the cross and the afflictions to be borne for Christ, and join himself to those who bear the cross.

units.la: Ex potentia Dei Rationes admonitionis sunt octo: 1. Quia si quid sit ferendum supra vires nostras pro Christo, Dei potentia aderit adjutrix & liberatrix, cujus virtute freti, & auxilio fulti audere, & eniti supra vires nostras tenemur.
units.tr: According to the power of God. There are eight grounds for the admonition. 1. If anything must be borne for Christ beyond our strength, the power of God will be at hand as helper and deliverer; relying on his strength and supported by his help, we are bound to dare and to strive beyond our own powers.

units.la: Vers. 9. Qui servavit nos, & vocavit vocatione sancta: non ex operibus nostris, sed ex suo proposito & gratia, quæ data quidem est nobis in Christo Jesu ante tempora secularia:
units.tr: Verse 9. Who has saved us and called us with a holy calling, not according to our works, but according to his own purpose and grace, which was given to us in Christ Jesus before the world began.

units.la: Ratio 2. confirmans priorem, Quia salutem æternam concessit nobis Deus & sanctâ vocatione seperavit nos à mundo in hunc ipsum finem, ut Christum confiteamur. Ergo erubescere ob ejus testimonium aut crucem non debemus.
