units.tr: Second ground, confirming the first: because God has granted us eternal salvation and by a holy calling has set us apart from the world for this very purpose, that we should confess Christ. Therefore we ought not to be ashamed of his testimony or of the cross.

units.la: Non ex Ratio 3. Quia Deus gratis hæc omnia facit, non respiciens opera nostra, sed gratiam suam & gratuitum propositum suum, Ergo non æquum est ut nos pudeat testimonii Christi, aut crucis, seu afflictionum pro eo.
units.tr: Not according to Third ground: because God does all these things freely, not regarding our works but his own grace and his free purpose. Therefore it is not right that we should be ashamed of the testimony of Christ, or of the cross, or of afflictions for his sake.

units.la: Ante Ratio 4. confirmans priorem, Gratia data est nobis in Christo, ante tempora seculauia, antequam nos vel nostra opera exsistere possent, id est, antequam tempora fluere inciperent: Ergo non æquum est ut nos pudeat testimonii vel crucis Christi. Dicitur in Christo gratia nobis data, quia licet nos nondum exsisteremus, Christus tamen designatus Mediator, secunda persona Trinitatis, ab æterno subsistebat, qui pro nobis in fœdere redemptionis ante tempora sæcularia cum Patre inito, pro electis suis pactus est illud quod postea in tempore persolvit pretium redemptionis, & nostro nomine accepit assignatam nobis gratiam, per quam in tempore nos vocaremur, justificaremur, & singuli salvaremur gratis, temporibus idoneis.
units.tr: Before Fourth ground, confirming the first: grace was given us in Christ before the world began, before we or our works could exist, that is, before time began to flow. Therefore it is not right that we should be ashamed of the testimony or the cross of Christ. It is said that grace was given us in Christ because, although we did not yet exist, Christ, appointed as Mediator and the second person of the Trinity, subsisted from eternity; in the covenant of redemption made with the Father before the world began, he undertook for his elect to pay in time the price of redemption, and in our name he received the grace assigned to us, by which we are called in time, justified, and each of us saved freely, at fitting times.

units.la: Vers. 10. Sed patefacta nunc est per illustrem illum adventum Servatoris nostri Iesu Christi, qui & mortem abolevit, & vitam in lucem produxit ac immortalitatem, per Euangelium:
units.tr: Ver. 10. But now it has been made manifest through the glorious appearing of our Saviour Jesus Christ, who both abolished death and brought life and immortality to light through the Gospel.

units.la: Ratio 5. Thesin probans, & simul etiam beneficia omnia nobis data ostendens esse gratuita, Quia mortis abolitio, vita, & immortalitas, & reliqua quæ salutem spectant, incognita erant nobis, donec à Christo sunt revelata, in lucem producta, acta, & peracta omnia. Ergo vel ob gratiam hanc nobis factam, erubescere non decet nos ob Euangelium ejus.
units.tr: Argument 5, proving the thesis and at the same time showing that all the benefits given to us are gratuitous. The abolition of death, life, immortality, and the rest that concern salvation were unknown to us until they were revealed by Christ, brought to light, and all things done and accomplished. Therefore, on account of this grace bestowed upon us, it is not fitting for us to be ashamed of his Gospel.

units.la: Vers. 11. Cujus constitutus sum ego Præco & Apostolus, ac Doctor Gentium.
units.tr: Ver. 11. Of which I was appointed herald and apostle, and teacher of the Gentiles.

units.la: Ratio 6. Deus tanti æstimat Testimonium Euangelii, ut ad ipsum toti orbi, & Gentibus speciatim annunciandum, constituerit Paulum Apostolum. Ne ergo pudeat Timotheum, vel quenquam alium Euangelii hujus, vel Pauli Ministri ejus, licet afflicti pro Testimonio Euangelii.
units.tr: Argument 6. God so values the testimony of the Gospel that he appointed Paul as apostle to proclaim it to the whole world, and to the Gentiles in particular. Let neither Timothy nor anyone else therefore be ashamed of this Gospel, or of Paul his minister, even if they are afflicted for the testimony of the Gospel.

units.la: Vers. 12. Quam ob causam & hæc patior: neque erubesco, novi enim cui crediderim, & mihi persuasum est eum posse depositum, meum in illum diem servare.
units.tr: Ver. 12. For this reason I also suffer these things, yet I am not ashamed, for I know whom I have believed, and I am persuaded that he is able to keep my deposit until that day.

units.la: Ratio 7. ab exemplo Apostoli, Ego ipse patior vincula pro Euangelio, nec pudeo tamen: Ergo similiter decet fortem esse Timotheum, nec pudefieri in causa Euangelii.
units.tr: Argument 7, from the example of the Apostle. I myself suffer chains for the Gospel, yet I am not ashamed. Therefore Timothy likewise ought to be brave, and not be put to shame in the cause of the Gospel.

units.la: Novi. Ratio 8. Etiam ab exemplo Pauli, confirmans priorem, Ego Paulus, animam pariter & corpus, Deo fideli & potenti commili, ut servet mihi depositum hoc in diem Judicii: & persuasum habeo me ab eo servatum iri: Ergo neque pudefieri debeo ego, neque tu Timothee, quacunque nobis acciderint, propter Testimonium Euangelii.
units.tr: Novi. Argument 8, also from Paul's example, confirming the former. I, Paul, commit my soul and body alike to God, who is faithful and powerful, that he may keep this deposit for me until the day of judgment; and I am persuaded that I shall be kept by him. Therefore neither ought I to be put to shame, nor you, Timothy, whatever befalls us on account of the testimony of the Gospel.

units.la: Vers. 13. Exemplar teneto sanorum sermonum, quos à me audisti cum fide & charitate quæ est in Christo Iesu. Admonitio 3. Ut retineat & sequatur eam rationem docendi, (& quoad dogmata, & quoad docendi modum,) quam à Paulo didicerat, & eam quam proxime posset ad vivum exprimeret, addit in fide & charitate quæ est in Christo, ut summam doctrinæ ostendat, quæ tota ad fidem & charitatem, ex Christi cognitione profluentem, revocari potest.
units.tr: Ver. 13. Hold fast the pattern of sound words which you heard from me, with the faith and love which are in Christ Jesus. Admonition 3. That he may retain and follow that method of teaching, both as to doctrines and as to the manner of teaching, which he had learned from Paul, and express it as closely to the life as he can, he adds in faith and love which is in Christ, to show the sum of doctrine, which can all be traced back to faith and love flowing from the knowledge of Christ.

units.la: Verf. 14. Præclarum depositum serva, per Spiritum sanctum qui inhabitat in nobis.
units.tr: Ver. 14. Keep the noble deposit through the Holy Spirit who dwells in us.

units.la: Admonitio 4. Generalior, ut Ministerium & dona Spiritus, & integritatem doctrinæ Christianæ fideliter conservet, ne inertia sua, vel timiditate quicquam de ea periret, sed adversus insidias, & vim hostium Euangelii conservaretur.
units.tr: Admonition 4, more general: that he faithfully preserve the ministry, the gifts of the Spirit, and the integrity of Christian doctrine, so that nothing of it perishes through his sloth or timidity, but that it be kept safe against the snares and force of the enemies of the Gospel.

units.la: Argumenta hortationis sunt quinque, Quæ omnia probant formam sanæ doctrinæ tenendam esse: Argumentum primum, Forma hæc, depositum illud est, quod Deus tuæ fidei commisit, aliquando rationem depositi à te exacturus. Tenenda est ergo.
units.tr: There are five arguments of the exhortation, and all of them prove that the form of sound doctrine is to be held. First argument: this form is the deposit which God has committed to your faith, and one day he will demand from you an account of the deposit. It is therefore to be held.

units.la: Præclarum Arg. 2. Præclarum hoc depositum sanæ doctrinæ omnibus rebus mundanis, & ipsa etiam vita hac mortali excellentius est: Tenenda est ergo hæc doctrinæ forma.
units.tr: Noble. Argument 2. This noble deposit of sound doctrine is more excellent than all worldly things, and even than this mortal life itself. Therefore this form of doctrine is to be held.

units.la: Per Spiritum Arg. 3. Etiamsi vires propriæ in defensione doctrinæ, te deficerent, paratum tamen erit tibi auxilium Spiritus Dei habitantis in te, sincero ipsius servo, si ejus auxilium imploraveris: Tenenda ergo hæc sanæ doctrinæ forma.
units.tr: Through the Spirit. Argument 3. Even if your own powers failed you in defending doctrine, help would nonetheless be ready for you from the Spirit of God dwelling in you, if you implore his help, as his sincere servant. Therefore this form of sound doctrine is to be held.

units.la: Verf. 15. Nosti, hoc aversatos me fuisse omnes qui sunt in Asia: ex quibus est Phygellus & Hermogenes.
units.tr: Ver. 15. You know that all who are in Asia turned away from me, of whom are Phygellus and Hermogenes.

units.la: Arg. 4. Ex altera parte paratæ sunt tentationes, quibus incautus abripi potes ab Euangelii defensione & professione, sicut in exemplo fratrum Asianorum didicisti, nominatim Phygelli & Hermogenis; quorum exemplo monitum te, & omnes reliquos Euangelii Ministros, vigilare oportet. Ergo.
units.tr: Argument 4. On the other hand, temptations are at hand by which you, if unwary, may be carried away from the defence and profession of the Gospel, as you have learned from the example of the Asian brethren, namely Phygellus and Hermogenes. Warned by their example, you and all the other ministers of the Gospel ought to be watchful. Therefore.

units.la: Verf. 16. Præstet misericordiam Dominus Onesiphori familiæ, quoniam sæpe me recreavit, & catenam meam non erubuit.
units.tr: Ver. 16. May the Lord show mercy to the household of Onesiphorus, because he often refreshed me and was not ashamed of my chain.

units.la: Arg. 5. Ex altera parte in te & fidelibus aliis, adeo prævalet Dei Spiritus & gratia, ad constantiam, in probationibus, ut si vigiletis, non fit quod metuatis, ne sanam doctrinam amittatis: Sanæ igitur doctrinæ formulæ retinendæ invigilandum est. Verf. 17. Imò quum esset Roma, studiosissimè quæsivit me, & invenit.
units.tr: Argument 5. On the other hand, the Spirit and grace of God so prevail in you and other faithful people for constancy in trials that, if you are watchful, what you fear will not happen, namely that you lose sound doctrine. Therefore vigilance must be exercised in keeping the forms of sound doctrine. Ver. 17. Indeed, when he was in Rome, he sought me out very diligently, and found me.

units.la: Verf. 18. Det ei Dominus ut inveniat misericordiam apud Dominum in die illo: quàm multa etiam Ephesi subministrarit, tu optimè nosti.
units.tr: Ver. 18. May the Lord grant him to find mercy from the Lord in that day; and how many things he ministered at Ephesus, you know very well.

units.la: Hoc argumentum proponit & confirmat in exemplo Onesiphori, qui, inquit, fortiter professus est fidem, neque erubuit vincula mea, nec metuit sua, sed Ephesi, & Romæ se præstitit in professione Euangelii; pro quo DEUM oro, ut misericordiam inveniat, & ipse, & tota ejus familia in die DOMINI: Hujus exemplo animari vult Timotheum, & omnes Pastores ad Constantiam in Fidei professione, & conservatione præclari illius depositi,& Euangelicæ doctrinæ defensione: id quod etiam hinc deducit Apostolus initio sequentis Capitis.
units.tr: He proposes and confirms this argument in the example of Onesiphorus, who, he says, professed the faith boldly, was not ashamed of my chain, nor feared his own, but showed himself at Ephesus and at Rome in the profession of the Gospel. For him I pray to God that he and his whole household may find mercy in the day of the Lord. By his example he wishes to encourage Timothy and all ministers to constancy in professing the faith, in keeping that noble deposit, and in defending evangelical doctrine. This the Apostle also draws out at the beginning of the following chapter.

units.la: Caput Secundum.
units.tr: Chapter Two.

units.la: HOC Capite propositis aliis quatuor admonitionibus, pergit Timotheum ad ministerium recte obeundum instruere.
units.tr: In this chapter, after setting out four other admonitions, he goes on to instruct Timothy to discharge the ministry rightly.

units.la: Verf. 1. Tu igitur, fili mei, corroborare per gratiam quæ est in Christo Iesu:
units.tr: Verse 1. You therefore, my son, be strong in the grace that is in Christ Jesus:

units.la: Admonitio prima, Ut studeat propagando Euangelio, non solùm per se, sed etiam per alios qui successuri erant in Ministerio, nihili faciens labores ullos, qui ad hoc præstandum requirebantur. Admonitionis hujus tria sunt membra. Primum, Ut ad opus Ministerii armet se robore, induat animi fortitudinem, & accingat se subinde ad res præclarè gerendas, Argumenta subinnuit duo.
units.tr: The first admonition: that he should strive to spread the Gospel, not only himself but also through others who would succeed him in the ministry, counting as nothing any labours required for this task. This admonition has three parts. First, that he should arm himself with strength for the work of the ministry, put on courage of spirit, and gird himself from time to time to accomplish great things. He hints at two arguments.

units.la: Fili ] Arg. 1. Quia filium Pauli decet robur induere, & fortem esse.
units.tr: Son] Argument 1: because it befits the son of Paul to put on strength and be brave.

units.la: Per gratiam ] Arg. 2. Quia gratia quæ est in CHRISTO IESU solo, non est tibi accingenti te ipsum ad opus, defutura.
units.tr: Through grace] Argument 2: because the grace that is in Christ Jesus alone will not fail you when you gird yourself for the work.

units.la: Verf. 2. Et quæ audisti à me inter multos testes, hæc committe fidelibus hominibus, qui sunt idonei ad alios quoque docendos.
units.tr: Verse 2. And the things you have heard from me among many witnesses, commit these to faithful men, who will be able to teach others also.

units.la: Membrum 2. Ut non tantùm pro concione doceat populum, sed etiam ut am ut scholastice instituat candidatos Theologiæ, seu ut ad sacri ministerii functionem designatos instruat, doctrinam Apostolicam eis patefaciendo, & committendo, tanquam fidis depositariis, qui eandem doctrinam alios etiam docere possent, ut sic Euangelii doctrina de manu in manum traderetur & propagaretur. Argumentum addit ab exemplo suo, qui Timotheum, & multos alios ejus condiscipulos in hac doctrina instituerat non tantum una cum populo publice eos docendo, sed etiam secretim à populo scholastice instruendo.
units.tr: Second part: that he should not only teach the people in preaching, but also instruct candidates for theology in the schools, or those destined for the function of the sacred ministry, laying open the apostolic doctrine to them and committing it to them as to faithful depositaries, who could also teach the same doctrine to others, so that the doctrine of the Gospel might be handed on and spread from hand to hand. He adds an argument from his own example: he had instructed Timothy and many other fellow-disciples in this doctrine, not only by teaching them publicly along with the people, but also by instructing them privately in the schools, apart from the people.

units.la: Verf. 3 Tu igitur feras laborem, ut bonus miles Iesu Christi.
units.tr: Verse 3. You therefore endure hardship, as a good soldier of Jesus Christ.

units.la: Membrum 3. Ut neque laborem qui ad duplex hoc opus requirebatur, neque afflictiones seu persecutiones quæ hunc laborem sequuntur, metuat seu refugiat, sed fortiter excipiat & toleret.
units.tr: Third part: that he should not fear or shrink from the labour required for this twofold work, nor from the afflictions or persecutions that follow such labour, but should receive and bear them bravely.

units.la: Ut miles] Argumenta admonitionis seu hortationis sunt undecim, quæ omnia probant fortiter militandum in Ministerio Euangelii.
units.tr: As a soldier] The arguments of this admonition or exhortation are eleven, all of which prove that one must fight bravely in the ministry of the Gospel.

units.la: Argumentum primum, Quia miles es Iesu Christi, cui te ut imperatori quasi militari sacramento obstrinxisti, decet autem militem Christianum ad exemplum Christi cum adversariis non ferocia certare, sed patienter cruci assuescendo, & in opere suo peragendo contra difficultates luctantem pergere: Ergo tibi fortiter militandum est in Euangelii Ministerio.
units.tr: First argument: because you are a soldier of Jesus Christ, to whom you have bound yourself as to a commander, by a kind of military oath. A Christian soldier ought to follow the example of Christ, who did not contend with his adversaries by savagery, but patiently accustomed himself to the cross and pressed on in his work, struggling against difficulties. Therefore you must fight bravely in the ministry of the Gospel.

units.la: Verf. 4. Nemo qui militat implicatur vitæ negotiis ut ei placeat, à quo delectus est miles.
units.tr: Verse 4. No one who serves as a soldier entangles himself in the affairs of life, so that he may please the one who enlisted him.

units.la: Arg. 2. in comparatione propositum, Quia aliter non poteris imperatori tuo Christo placere, nisi posthabitis omnibus tuis negotiis quæ possent te avocare à Christi negotiis, te totum Christi servitio addicas: Ergo fortiter tibi militandum est.
units.tr: Argument 2, set out by comparison: because otherwise you cannot please your commander Christ, unless, setting aside all your affairs which could draw you away from Christ's business, you devote yourself wholly to Christ's service. Therefore you must fight bravely.

units.la: Verf. 5. Quod si certet etiam aliquis, non coronatur nisi legitimè certaverit.
units.tr: Verse 5. And if anyone also competes, he is not crowned unless he has competed lawfully.

units.la: Arg. 3. In comparatione ludorum, & certaminum inter Ethnicos nobilium propositum, Quia non poteris coronari, si primo conflictu fatigatus ex campo te ad quietem subduxeris, sed oportet te legitimè certare, & prosequi certamen, quousque lex præscribit, id est, perseverare quandiu vivis in hac militia Christiana, ut tandem victor coroneris: Ergo fortiter tibi militandum est.
units.tr: Argument 3, set out in comparison with the games and contests of the noble pagans: because you cannot be crowned if, wearied at the first clash, you withdraw from the field to rest. You must compete lawfully and carry the contest through as long as the rule prescribes, that is, persevere as long as you live in this Christian warfare, so that at last you may be crowned as victor. Therefore you must fight bravely.

units.la: Verl. 6. Agricolam oportet prius laborando fructus percipere.
units.tr: Verse 6. The farmer must first labour before he receives the fruits.

units.la: Arg 4. In similitudine etiam ut priora propositum, Quia, ut prius labores, necesse est, si fructus percipere velis, quos ut Agricola haud dubio percepturus es, si strenuè labori tuo incubueris. Ergo.
units.tr: Argument 4, likewise in a simile, as before: because, as you must labour first if you wish to receive fruits, so as a farmer you will undoubtedly receive them if you apply yourself vigorously to your labour. Therefore...

units.la: Vers. 7. Considera quæ dico; det igitur tibi Dominus intelligentiam in omnibus.
units.tr: Verse 7. Consider what I say; and may the Lord give you understanding in all things.

units.la: Ut plus colligat seu concipiat Timotheus ex his similitudinibus quam facile describi, vel poterat, vel explicare opus erat, colligendas relinquit Timotheo similitudinum harum apodoses, & insuper orat Deum, ut aperiat ei oculos ad videndum quæ hinc, & aliunde, edisci poterant de ipsius officio præstando documenta: nam infirmiores erant hæ comparationes, quam ut ad militiæ Christianæ præstantiam, & laborum in Ministerio mercedem satis ostendendam, sufficerent.
units.tr: So that Timothy may gather and grasp more from these similitudes than could easily be described or explained, Paul leaves him to draw out the applications of these similitudes himself. Moreover, he prays that God will open his eyes to see what lessons, both from these and from elsewhere, could be learned about discharging his office. For these comparisons were too weak to show sufficiently the excellence of the Christian warfare and the reward of labours in the ministry.

units.la: Vers. 8. Memento Iesum Christum resurrexisse ex mortuis, factum ex semine David, secundum Euangelium meum:
units.tr: Verse 8. Remember that Jesus Christ was raised from the dead, descended from the seed of David, according to my gospel:

units.la: Arg. 5. Quia Christus Imperator & Dux exercitus omnem adversam potestatem, & ipsam etiam mortem pertulit, & superavit virtute deitatis suæ, pro nobis resurgens à mortuis, in eadem carne, quam ex semine Davidis factam assumpserat, prout ego prædicavi. Idcirco sperare poteris, O Timothee, emersurum te etiam ex omnibus malis, & ex ipsa morte per virtutem Christi, verè Dei & verè hominis. In quem etiam finem memorem & tenacem Timotheum esse jubet, hujus doctrinæ, quæ hoc est fidei, spei, & consolationis Christianæ primum fundamentum.
units.tr: Argument 5: because Christ, the Commander and Leader of the army, endured and overcame every adverse power, and death itself, by the virtue of his deity, rising again from the dead for us in the same flesh which he had assumed, made from the seed of David, as I have preached. Hence, O Timothy, you may hope that you too will emerge from all evils, even from death itself, through the power of Christ, truly God and truly man. To this end also he bids Timothy be mindful and steadfast, since this doctrine is the first foundation of faith, hope and Christian consolation.

units.la: Vers. 9. In quo, ut facinorosus, affligor usque ad vincula: sed sermo Dei non est vinctus.
units.tr: Verse 9. In which I suffer hardship, even to chains, as a malefactor; but the word of God is not bound.

units.la: Arg. 6. Ab exemplo ipsius Pauli, Ego vincula & dedecus lubens patior in labore ministerii. Ergo & tu ad idem patiendum te compara.
units.tr: Argument 6: from the example of Paul himself: I gladly suffer chains and disgrace in the labour of the ministry. Therefore prepare yourself to suffer likewise.

units.la: Sed sermo ] Arg. 7. Omnes conatus adversariorum Euangelii, dum persequuntur nos Christi servos, etiam ad vincula, irritus plane est; quia licet vinciant nos Euangelii Confessores, non vincunt tamen, nec ipsum Euangelium vincire, nec cursum ejus impedire possunt. Ergo militandum est nobis confidenter.
units.tr: But the word] Argument 7: All the attempts of the adversaries of the Gospel, while they persecute us, the servants of Christ, even to chains, are utterly futile. For although the confessors of the Gospel are bound, the adversaries do not bind the Gospel itself, nor can they impede its course. Therefore we must fight with confidence.

units.la: Vers. 10. Ideo omnia sustineo propter electos, ut & ipsi salutem consequantur quæ est in Christo Jesu, cum gloria æterna.
units.tr: Verse 10. Therefore I endure all things for the sake of the elect, that they also may obtain the salvation which is in Christ Jesus, with eternal glory.

units.la: Arg. 8. Electi Dei digni sunt, pro quorum ædificatione & confirmatione in fide, ad salutem æternam per Christum partam omnis generis mala tolerare debemus omnes nos, qui fideles Ministri CHRISTI sumus: Ergo fortiter militandum est nobis.
units.tr: Argument 8: The elect of God are worthy that, for their building up and confirmation in faith, we who are faithful ministers of Christ should all endure evils of every kind, in view of the eternal salvation obtained through Christ. Therefore we must fight bravely.

units.la: Verf. 11. Fidus est hic sermo: nam si cum eo mortui sumus, cum eo etiam vivemus:
units.tr: Verse 11. This saying is faithful: for if we have died with him, we shall also live with him:

units.la: Verf. 12. Si toleramus, etiam cum eo regnabimus; si abnegamus, & ille abnegabit nos:
units.tr: Verse 12. If we endure, we shall also reign with him; if we deny him, he also will deny us:

units.la: Arg. 9. Etiamsi difficulter admittatur à carnis sensu hic sermo, certum tamen est, Communionem cum CHRISTI morte in tolerantia crucis, connexam esse cum communione vitæ CHRISTI, & certum est regnaturos esse eos cum CHRISTO, qui pro, vel cum ipso patiuntur. Ergo fortiter militandum, ut vivamus & regnemus cum CHRISTO.
units.tr: Argument 9: Even if this saying is hard for the sense of the flesh to accept, it is nevertheless certain that communion with Christ's death, in enduring the cross, is joined with communion in Christ's life, and certain that those who suffer for him or with him will reign with Christ. Therefore we must fight bravely, that we may live and reign with Christ.

units.la: Si autem ] Arg. 10. Quicunque persequutionis terrore, vel mundi illecebris decepti, confessionem nominis CHRISTI abjiciunt, etiam à CHRISTO abjicientur, ut pereant. Fortiter ergo militandum tibi est in Ministerio Evangelii.
units.tr: But if] Argument 10: whoever, deceived by the terror of persecution or the allurements of the world, casts off the confession of Christ's name, will also be cast off by Christ, so as to perish. Therefore you must fight bravely in the ministry of the Gospel.

units.la: Verf. 13. Si infidi sumus, ille tamen fidus manet; negare seipsum non potest.
units.tr: Verse 13. If we are faithless, he remains faithful; he cannot deny himself.

units.la: Arg. 11. Qui infidi sunt, afferant licet sibi exitium, nihil tamen detrahent veritati vel gloriæ CHRISTI, qui tutabitur suam veritatem contra adversariorum vim, & Apostatarum perfidiam, & rata faciet omnia quæ dixit, pro servis suis, & contra proditores. Ergo Ministerii officiis tibi gnaviter incumbendum est.
units.tr: Argument 11: Those who are faithless may bring ruin upon themselves, yet they will detract nothing from the truth or glory of Christ, who will defend his truth against the force of adversaries and the perfidy of apostates, and will make good all that he has said, for his servants and against traitors. Therefore you must apply yourself diligently to the duties of the ministry.

units.la: Verf. 14. Hæc suggere, obtestans coram Domino ne verborum pugnas sequantur; quod nullam adfert utilitatem, imo auditores subvertit.
units.tr: Verse 14. Charge them before the Lord to avoid contentions about words, which are of no use and subvert the hearers.

units.la: Secunda admonitio. Ut Timotheus non solum urgeat quæ dicta sunt, sed etiam curet prudenter tractandum Dei verbum, cum ab aliis, tum à seipso in aliorum exemplum. Hujus admonitionis tria sunt membra: Primum ut in nomine & autoritate CHRISTI compescat λογομαχίας, seu contentiones inutiles: Quales solent esse disputationes eorum qui venantur acuminis laudem in Sophistica sua.
units.tr: Second admonition: that Timothy should not only press what has been said, but also take care to handle the word of God prudently, both with others and with himself as an example to them. This admonition has three parts. First, that in the name and authority of Christ he should restrain logomachies [λογομαχίας], that is, useless contentions, such as the disputations usually are of those who hunt for a reputation for cleverness in their sophistry.

units.la: Inutilibus ] Rationes hujus membri sunt duæ: Ratio prima, Quia ejusmodi contentiones nullam afferunt utilitatem.
units.tr: Unprofitable] The reasons for this part are two. The first reason: such contentions bring no benefit at all.

units.la: Subversionem ] Altera ratio, Quia subvertitur aliquorum fides, qui altercando vel altercationibus spinosis aurem præbendo, amittunt veritatem.
units.tr: Subverting] The second reason: the faith of some is subverted, since those who engage in wrangling, or who lend an ear to thorny disputes, lose the truth.

units.la: Vers. 15. Stude teipsum probatum sistere DEO, operarium qui non erubescat, & qui recte sermonem veritatis secet.
units.tr: Ver. 15. Study to present yourself approved to God, a workman who has no need to be ashamed, rightly dividing the word of truth.

units.la: Membrum 2. Ut se exemplum præbeat in prudente Verbi Divini administratione, Studendo Deo seipsum approbare, cum alii plausum theatri captant: ostendendo se probum operarium, cum alii se ostentant otiosos disputatores, Operam semper dando, ne quid indecori faciat vel dicat, cujus ipsum pudeat postea coram Deo, dum alii certant inter se acriter, tantum quia pudet eos vinci, vel non haberi pro doctis: Denique seipsum occupando inter prædicandum non in verborum cortice secando, dum medulla intacta relinquitur, sed in sensus plane redditi prudenti distributione, & applicatione ad auditorum profectum in fide & obedientia veritatis.
units.tr: Second part: that he should set himself forth as an example in the prudent handling of the Word of God, by striving to approve himself to God, while others seek the applause of the theatre; by showing himself an upright workman, while others display themselves as idle disputers; by always taking care that he neither does nor says anything of which he would later be ashamed before God, while others contend fiercely with one another, only because they are ashamed to be beaten or to be thought learned. Finally, when preaching, he should occupy himself not with cutting the bark of words while the marrow is left untouched, but with the wise distribution of the sense, made plain, and with its application to the advancement of the hearers in the faith and in obedience to the truth.

units.la: Vers. 16. Profanos autem de rebus inanibus clamores cohibe: ad majorem enim procedent impietatem.
units.tr: Ver. 16. But shun profane and empty chatter, for it will lead on to more ungodliness.

units.la: Tertium membrum, Ut inflatum & sophisticum loquendi modum, phrases novas, inusitatas & prophanas compescat: Rationes hujus membri subnectit tres. Profanos ] Ratio prima, Quia sicut insolentes istiusmodi sermones proficiscuntur à mentis profanitate & impietate, ita impietatem in aliis fovent & augent.
units.tr: The third part: that he should restrain inflated and sophistical ways of speaking, and new, unusual and profane phrases. For this part he adds three reasons. Profane] The first reason: just as such insolent words spring from profanity and impiety of mind, so they foster and increase impiety in others.

units.la: Vers. 17. Et sermo eorum depascet ut gangræna: ex quibus est Hymæneus & Philetus;
units.tr: Ver. 17. And their talk will spread like a gangrene; of whom are Hymenaeus and Philetus;

units.la: Ratio 2. Quia docendi modus & doctrina sophistarum depascet Ecclesiam, sicut corpus exedit gangræna, quæ (ut docent Medici) nisi quam ocissimè curetur ad contiguas partes serpit, ofla ipsa occupat, nec grassandi finem, nisi homine extincto facit.
units.tr: Reason 2. Because the manner of teaching and the doctrine of the sophists will eat into the Church as gangrene eats into the body. This (as physicians teach) unless it is cured as quickly as possible, creeps into the neighbouring parts, seizes even the bones, and does not stop its spreading until it has killed the man.

units.la: Vers. 18. Qui circa veritatem aberrarunt à scopo, dicentes resurrectionem jam esse factam: & subvertunt quorundam fidem.
units.tr: Ver. 18. Who have gone astray concerning the truth, saying that the resurrection is already past; and they subvert the faith of some.

units.la: Ratio 3. Quia experientia jam compertum est hoc malum, in persona duorum hæreticorum: (quos infamiæ causa, & ut scopulos vitandos nominat) qui allegoricam resurrectionem tantum agnoscentes, abberrarunt ipsi à veritate doctrinæ, & fidem aliquorum subverterunt, & dum perversum suum dogma persuadebant aliis, in causa erant cur aliqui in fidei professione non radicati professioni Christianæ religionis renunciarint,
units.tr: Reason 3. Because this evil has already been proved by experience in the persons of two heretics, whom he names for the sake of infamy and as rocks to be avoided. Acknowledging only an allegorical resurrection, they strayed themselves from the truth of doctrine and subverted the faith of some. And while they pressed their perverse dogma upon others, they were the cause why some, not rooted in the profession of faith, renounced the profession of the Christian religion.

units.la: Verf. 19, Solidum tamen fundamentum Dei stat, habens sigillum hoc, Novit Dominus qui sint sui, & Discedat ab injustitia omnis qui nominat nomen Christi.
units.tr: Ver. 19. Yet the firm foundation of God stands, having this seal: The Lord knows those who are his; and let everyone who names the name of Christ depart from iniquity.

units.la: Admonitio 3. De retinenda doctrina perseverantiæ verè fidelium, etiamsi aliquorum fides subversa sit: quæ admonitio per modum consolationis & confirmationis fidei, adversus scandalum Apostatarum præcipuè doctorum nobilium proponitur: quorum levitas & perfidia debet quidem omnes ad vigilantiam excitare, sed non debet fidei Sanctorum certitudinem labefactare, Doctrina tenenda Timotheo hæc est, Etiamsi fides aliquorum subversa sit, firmum tamen manet ædificium salutis Electorum, seu verè fidelium, Seu Certa est perseverantia Sanctorum; Hoc probat sex argumentis. Solidum Argumentum primum, A comparatione ædificii, Ædificium fidei, & salutis electorum solidum habet fundamentum à Deo positum quod immobile constat, hoc autem est, gratuita Dei electio, cujus constantiam & stabilitatem comparat ædificii fundamento super vetram posito: Ergo Sanctorum perseverantia certa est.
units.tr: Third admonition: concerning the retention of doctrine of the perseverance of the truly faithful, even if the faith of some has been overthrown. This admonition is put forward by way of consolation and confirmation of faith, against the scandal of apostates, especially of noble teachers, whose levity and faithlessness ought indeed to rouse everyone to vigilance, but ought not to shake the certainty of the faith of the saints. The doctrine Timothy is to hold is this: Even if the faith of some is overthrown, the building of the salvation of the elect, that is, of the truly faithful, nonetheless remains firm; or, The perseverance of the saints is certain. He proves this by six arguments. Firm] The first argument, from a comparison with a building: the building of faith and of the salvation of the elect has a firm foundation laid by God, which stands immovable. This foundation is God's free election, whose constancy and stability he compares to a building's foundation laid upon a rock. Therefore the perseverance of the saints is certain.

units.la: Sigillum Arg. 2. A comparatione sigilli, In hunc sensum; Sub arcana Dei custodia, tanquam signatorio annulo, continetur salus Electorum, ita ut etiamsi mundo non patefiat qui sint illi omnes qui electi sunt, certum tamen est ex nobis, seu numero verè fidelium, non fuisse eos, qui à nobis verè fidelibus exierunt seu à nostra societate defecerunt. Ergo perseverantia Sanctorum certa est.
units.tr: Seal] Argument 2, from a comparison with a seal, to this effect: under the secret custody of God, as under a signet ring, the salvation of the elect is kept, so that, even though it is not made manifest to the world who all those are that are elect, it is nonetheless certain that those who have gone out from us, that is, from the number of the truly faithful, or who have departed from our fellowship, were never of us. Therefore the perseverance of the saints is certain.

units.la: Novit Arg. 3. Novit Deus eos, qui specialiter sui sunt, seu ad se pertinent, ut proprium suum peculium, novit ipsos, & eorum nomina & numerum, eosque speciali favore suo complexus est, ita ut à se divelli ipsos non sinat: Nosse enim ut suos, est speciali dilectione acquiescere in ipsis, ut in peculio suo: Ergo Sanctorum perseverantia certa est.
units.tr: Knows] Argument 3. God knows those who are specially his, or who belong to him, as his own peculiar possession; he knows them, and their names and number, and he embraces them with his special favour, so that he does not allow them to be torn from him. For to know them as his own is to rest in them with special love, as in his own possession. Therefore the perseverance of the saints is certain.

units.la: Sigillum Arg. 4. Tanquam sigillum alterum, legendum ab hominibus dedit Deus hoc præceptum, quod efficax reddit in omnibus Electis. Quicunque nominat nomen Domini discedat ab iniquitate, hoc est, simul retineat fidem & professionem Iesu Christi, simul etiam recedat per respicientiam, & vitæ sanctitatem à viis peccati: Ergo Sancti quos Deus, hoc quasi sigillo obsignavit pro suis, & in quibus efficaciter præcepti hujus obedientiam operatur, non peribunt in Apostasia, sed perseverabunt, & vitam finient in fide & obedientia Christi.
units.tr: Seal] Argument 4. As a second seal, to be read by men, God has given this precept, which makes itself effective in all the elect: Let everyone who names the name of the Lord depart from iniquity; that is, let him at the same time hold fast the faith and profession of Jesus Christ, and at the same time withdraw from the ways of sin by repentance and by holiness of life. Therefore the saints, whom God has sealed with this as his own, and in whom he effectually works obedience to this precept, will not perish in apostasy, but will persevere and end their lives in the faith and obedience of Christ.

units.la: Verf. 20. Caterum in magna domo non tantum sunt vasa aurea & argentea, sed etiam lignea ac testacea: & alia quidem ad decus, alia vero ad dedecus.
units.tr: Ver. 20. But in a great house there are not only vessels of gold and silver, but also of wood and earth; and some indeed to honour, but others to dishonour.

units.la: Arg. 5. Quemadmodum in magna, & bene instructa domo sunt alia vasa pretiosiora ad usus honestos; alia viliora ad usus inhonestos, seu ad dedecus: Ita in Ecclesia alii sunt reprobi, qui soli cum sordibus, quibus inquinari poterat Ecclesia, ex Ecclesia discedent per Apostasiam: Alii vero electi sunt & sanctificati a Deo, qui ad Dei gloriam, & suum ipsorum decus perseverabunt in fide & obedientia Christi: Perseverantia ergo Sanctorum est certa.
units.tr: Argument 5. Just as in a great and well-furnished house there are some more precious vessels for honourable uses, and others of less value for dishonourable or base uses, so in the Church some are reprobate, who alone, with the filth by which the Church could be defiled, will depart from the Church through apostasy. But others are elect and sanctified by God, who will persevere in the faith and obedience of Christ to the glory of God and to their own honour. Therefore the perseverance of the saints is certain.

units.la: Verf. 21. Siquis igitur seipsum ab his expurgaverit, erit vas ad decus, sanctificatum, & accommodum usibus Domini, & ad omne opus bonum comparatum.
units.tr: Ver. 21. If anyone therefore purges himself from these, he will be a vessel to honour, sanctified, and fit for the Lord's use, and prepared for every good work.

units.la: Arg. 6. Non solum certum est perseveraturos Electos, sed etiam pro vero tenendum est, certos eos esse posse de sua electione & perseverantia: Nam si quis per Dei gratiam seipsum a moribus hypocritarum, & inquinamentis peccatorum, (quibus vasa ad dedecus destinata replentur) seipsum studuerit purgare, manifestum faciet & ibi & aliis, quod ipse sit ex numero vasorum pretiosorum ad sanctitatem & gloriam, praeparatorum. Ergo perseverantia Sanctorum certa est.
units.tr: Argument 6. It is not only certain that the elect will persevere, but it must also be held as true that they can be certain of their election and perseverance. For if anyone, by the grace of God, has striven to purge himself from the ways of hypocrites and from the defilements of sins (with which the vessels destined to dishonour are filled), he will make it manifest both to himself and to others that he is of the number of the precious vessels prepared for holiness and glory. Therefore the perseverance of the saints is certain.

units.la: Verf. 22. Juveniles autem cupiditates fuge: sed sectare justitiam, fidem, charitatem, pacem cum iis qui invocant Dominum ex puro corde.
units.tr: Ver. 22. But flee youthful lusts; and pursue righteousness, faith, love, peace, with those who call on the Lord out of a pure heart.

units.la: Admonitio 4. Ad moderationem animi, & ad vitandum omnes juveniles motus, & quacunque possent contentiones excitare, aut aliorum animos irritare. Admonitionis tria sunt membra; Primum, Ut vitaret omnes cupiditates, seu motus animi juveniles, quales sunt non solum voluptates, sed etiam temeritas, contentio superbia, inanis gloriae cupido, & similes pravi affectus, quibus laborare solent juvenes, qui vel docendi, vel disputandi munus susceperunt.
units.tr: Admonition 4. For the moderation of the mind, and for the avoiding of all youthful passions, and of whatever could stir up contentions or irritate the minds of others. This admonition has three parts. First, that he should avoid all youthful desires or passions of the mind, such as not only pleasures, but also rashness, contentiousness, pride, the desire for empty glory, and similar wicked affections, with which young men who have undertaken the office of teaching or of disputing are wont to be troubled.

units.la: Sectare] Membrum 2. Ut contra sectetur. i. justitiam, quae neminem laedit: 2. Fidem quae sine disceptatione hilariter recipit mysteria a Deo revelata: 3. Charitatem, quae non aemulatur, non inflatur, non est ambitiosa, nec quæ sua sunt, quærit ; sed ea quæ etiam in bonum aliorum tendunt: 4. Pacem cum iis, qui invocant Dominum de corde puro, id est, cum veris Dei cultoribus.
units.tr: Pursue] Second part: that he should pursue the opposite: 1. righteousness, which harms no one; 2. faith, which receives cheerfully, without dispute, the mysteries revealed by God; 3. love, which does not envy, is not puffed up, is not ambitious, does not seek its own, but aims at the good of others also; 4. peace with those who call on the Lord from a pure heart, that is, with the true worshippers of God.

units.la: Vers. 23. Stultas autem & ineruditas quæstiones rejice, sciens eas gignere pugnas.
units.tr: Ver. 23. But refuse foolish and unlearned questions, knowing that they breed strife.

units.la: Membrum 3. Ut devitet quæstiones, ex quibus ad veram sapientiam & Christianam ædificationem nulla fit accessio. Rationes admonitionis sunt tres. Ratio prima, Quia rixas & contentiones pariunt, non sine dispendio pacis & charitatis Christianæ.
units.tr: Third part: that he should avoid questions from which no increase comes to true wisdom or to Christian edification. The reasons for the admonition are three. The first reason: they produce quarrels and contentions, not without loss of peace and of Christian charity.

units.la: Vers. 24. Servum autem Domini non oportet pugnare, sed placidum esse erga omnes, aptum ad docendum tolerantem malos.
units.tr: Verse 24. And the servant of the Lord must not strive, but be gentle toward all, apt to teach, patient toward the evil,

units.la: Ratio 2. Quia litigatio non decet Ministrum Christi, qui ipse modestissimus fuit, & Dominus pacis.
units.tr: Reason 2. Because contentiousness does not befit a minister of Christ, who was himself most gentle, and is the Lord of peace.

units.la: Ratio 3. Quia decent Ministrum contrariæ virtutes, quales enumerat quatuor: 1. Est mansuetudo erga omnis generis homines, quæ comitatem & affabilitatem continet: 2. Aptitudo ad docendum, seu animus pronus ad docendum potius quam ad cogendum:
units.tr: Reason 3. Because contrary virtues befit a minister, which he enumerates as four: (1) gentleness toward men of every kind, which includes courtesy and affability; (2) aptitude for teaching, or a mind inclined to teach rather than to compel;

units.la: 3. Patientia erga malos, ut à veritate aversos ac protervos, mansuetudine vincat, si qua spes sit salutis eorum.
units.tr: (3) patience toward the evil, so that, when they have turned away from the truth and are stubborn, he may overcome them by gentleness, if there is any hope of their salvation.

units.la: Vers. 25. Cum lenitate erudientem eos qui contrario animo sunt affecti, ecquando det eis Deus ut resipiscentes agnoscant veritatem:
units.tr: Verse 25. Instructing with gentleness those who are opposed in mind, if perhaps God may give them repentance so that they acknowledge the truth,

units.la: 4. Modestia In corripiendis diversa sentientibus, ne eos statim asperioribus verbis excipiat, sed cum mansuetudine doctrinam iis proponat salutarem, & sic corripiat, ut intelligant suam emendationem & salutem quæri. Rationes cur studere debeat huic ultimæ virtuti, seu modestiæ in contentionibus, reddit tres: Ratio prima, Quia possibilis est obstinatorum conversio, nec de ea temere desperandum. Ratio 2. Quia Dei donum est resipiscentia & agnitio veritatis & omnis fidei actus.
units.tr: (4) Moderation in correcting those who think differently, so that he does not at once receive them with harsher words, but sets before them the wholesome teaching with mildness, and corrects them in such a way that they understand that their amendment and salvation are being sought. He gives three reasons why he ought to strive for this last virtue, that is, moderation in disputes: the first reason is that the conversion of the obstinate is possible, and one should not despair of it rashly; the second reason is that repentance, the knowledge of the truth and every act of faith are the gift of God.

units.la: Vers. 26. Et elapsi ex Diaboli laqueo, à quo captivi tenentur mentis sanitatem recipiant ad prestandum illius voluntatem.
units.tr: Verse 26. And that, freed from the snare of the devil, by whom they are held captive, they may recover their sanity to do his will.

units.la: Ratio 3. Quia miseratione digna est eorum conditio, nam in laqueis diaboli jacent captivi secundum diaboli voluntatem acti, quam diu visum fuerit Deo, illud permittere.
units.tr: Reason 3. Because their condition is worthy of pity: for they lie captive in the snares of the devil, driven according to his will, for as long as it has seemed good to God to permit this.

units.la: Caput Tertium.
units.tr: Chapter 3.

units.la: HOC Capite præmunit, & confirmat Timotheum, & in eo omnes pastores, adversus falsos fratres, schismaticos & hæreticos, & adversus molestias, quas illi creaturi essent sinceris Dei servis:
units.tr: In this chapter he forewarns and strengthens Timothy, and in him all ministers, against false brothers, schismatics and heretics, and against the troubles that these would cause for the sincere servants of God:

units.la: 1. Describendo ipsorum ingenia & mores, ad vers. 8. 2. Consolando & armando eum adversus falsorum doctorum impetus & artes, ad finem, quæ duæ sunt capitis partes.
units.tr: 1. By describing their characters and morals, down to verse 8. 2. By comforting and arming him against the attacks and arts of false teachers, to the end. These are the two parts of the chapter.

units.la: Vers. 1. Illud autem scio, fore ut extremis diebus instent tempora molesta.
units.tr: Verse 1. But know this: in the last days hard times will press upon you.

units.la: Prima pars Capitis, & primus modus præmuniendi, est præmonitio de falsis fratribus exorituris, & jam tum exorientibus: & de molestiis quas illi daturi erant, ut minus læderent prævisæ; Extremi dies sunt tempus quod restabat post Christi ascensum ad ejus secundum adventum: Præmonitionis summa est, Tempora difficilia & molesta sunt, in quibus difficile sit consilium capere quomodo te grerere debeas adversus iltiusmodi monstra, quæ ex medio Ecclesiæ sinu prodibunt, & cum quibus conflictari, est molestissimum: opus igitur est ut te armes.
units.tr: The first part of the chapter, and the first way of forewarning, is a warning about false brothers who will arise, and who already are arising, and about the troubles they were going to bring, so that the foreseen troubles might do less harm. "The last days" is the time that remained after Christ's ascension until his second coming. The sum of the warning is this: the times will be difficult and troubled, so that it will be hard to know how you should conduct yourself against such monsters, who will come out from the very bosom of the Church, and to struggle with whom is most grievous. Therefore you must arm yourself.

units.la: Vers. 2. Erunt enim homines sui amantes, avari, gloriosi, superbi, maledici, parentibus immorigeri, ingrati, impuri,
units.tr: Verse 2. For men will be lovers of themselves, covetous, boastful, proud, abusive, disobedient to parents, ungrateful, unholy,

units.la: Vitia quibus dediti sunt plerunque, falsi fratres enumerat 19. Primum sunt amantes sui, id est, privatis student commodis posthabita salute & utilitate aliorum: 2. Avari sunt, seu amantes pecuniarum: 3. Insolentes, fastuosi, seu gloriosi, qui internam animi superbiam fastu produnt: 4. Superbi præferentes se aliis, eosque præ se contemnentes: 5. Maledici, qui bonorum famam non morantur lædere: 6. Parentibus non obedientes, id est, despicientes legitimam autoritatem eorum qui parentum loco ab illis debent honorari: 7. Ingrati quos ne beneficiis quidem demereri poteris, ut vicem dilectionis tibi rependant: 8. Trofani, seu destituti vero sanctitatis studio.
units.tr: Paul lists, for the most part, the vices to which these false brothers were given over, nineteen in all. The first are lovers of themselves, that is, they pursue private advantage and set aside the welfare and profit of others. 2. Covetous, that is, lovers of money. 3. Arrogant, showy, or boastful, who reveal inward pride by their ostentation. 4. Proud, who put themselves before others and despise them to their faces. 5. Abusive, who do not hesitate to injure the good name of others. 6. Disobedient to parents, that is, who despise the lawful authority of those who ought to be honoured in place of parents. 7. Ungrateful, whom you cannot even win over by kindness, so that they repay your love in return. 8. Unholy, that is, lacking any true zeal for holiness.

units.la: Vers. 3. Charitatis expertes, nescii fœderis, calumniatores, intemperantes, immites, minimè amantes bonorum,
units.tr: Verse 3. Without love, not keeping covenants, slanderers, intemperate, fierce, not lovers of the good,

units.la: 9. Adeo etiam alieni à charitate ut ne naturæ vincula respiciant: 10. Perfidi, qui pactorum & fœderum non habent rationem, sed ea violant: 11, Calumniatores, qui confictis criminibus aliorum innocentiam onerant: 12. Intemperantes, qui in quodvis genus carnalium voluptatum sese effundunt: 13. Immites, qui ingenio sunt feroci, & inhumano: 14. A bonis viris alieni, qui ob morum discrepantiam abhorrent ab amicitia bonorum, eosque oderunt.
units.tr: 9. So far estranged from love that they do not even respect the bonds of nature. 10. Treacherous, who take no account of pacts and covenants but violate them. 11. Slanderers, who burden the innocence of others with invented charges. 12. Intemperate, who abandon themselves to every kind of carnal pleasure. 13. Fierce, who are wild and inhuman by disposition. 14. Estranged from good men, who, because of differences in morals, shrink from friendship with good people and hate them.

units.la: Verf. 4. Proditores, præcipites, inflati, voluptatum amantes potius quam amantes Dei:
units.tr: Verse 4. Traitors, headstrong, puffed up, lovers of pleasures rather than lovers of God:

units.la: 15. Proditores, qui amicos bene meritos periculis vitæ objiciunt:
units.tr: 15. Traitors, who expose friends who have deserved well of them to danger of life.

units.la: 16. Protervi seu præcipites, qui feruntur quocunque rapit impetus cupiditatum: 17. Inflati, qui sibi placent maxime ex vana opinione suæ excellentiæ: 18. Qui suis voluptatibus Dei voluntatem & præcepta postponunt.
units.tr: 16. Headstrong or rash, who are carried wherever the impulse of their desires sweeps them. 17. Puffed up, who take pleasure above all in a vain opinion of their own excellence. 18. Who put their own pleasures before the will and precepts of God.

units.la: Verf. 5. Habentes formam pietatis, sed qui vim ejus abnegarint. Etiam istos aversare.
units.tr: Verse 5. Having a form of godliness, but denying its power. Avoid these too.

units.la: 19. Habentes speciem pietatis, quam verbis & cultu præ se ferunt: cujus virtutem seu veritatem in operibus adeo non curant, ut abjurasse eam videantur: Hos jubet devitare, hoc est, post admonitiones & correptiones per censuras Ecclesiasticas leviores, tandem per excommunicationem exclusos ab Ecclesia, cavere & coercere, & qua posset alia quavis prudenti ratione reprimere, ne quid detrimenti ab iis caperet Ecclesia.
units.tr: 19. Having an appearance of godliness, which they display in words and outward worship, but whose power or truth they care so little for in their works that they seem to have renounced it. He orders these to be avoided, that is, after admonitions and milder rebukes through ecclesiastical censures, and finally, when they have been excluded from the Church by excommunication, to be watched and restrained, and to be checked by any other prudent means, so that the Church suffers no harm from them.

units.la: Verf. 6. Ex his enim sunt isti qui irrepunt in familias, & captivas ducunt mulierculas, onustas peccatis, actas cupiditatibus variis:
units.tr: Verse 6. For of this sort are those who creep into households and lead captive silly women, laden with sins, led away by various lusts:

units.la: Pergit falsos fratres depingere, & in exemplo aliquorum sui temporis nebulonum, quasi in tabella ante oculos eos proponere, qui ventris sui causa, callide se insinuabant in alienas familias, & leviores in genere mulierum captivas ducebant, & eas onustas jam peccatis, adeo non exonerabant, aut liberabant, sicut promittebant, ut etiam majori servitute gravarent, & peccata peccatis accumularent, Causas deceptionum harum mulierculanum aperit duas: 1. Quia fœminæ istæ variis affectibus & desideriis, quæ moderari non poterant, ferebantur.
units.tr: He goes on to paint the false brothers, and sets before their eyes, as if on a panel, some scoundrels of his own time, who for the sake of their bellies cunningly insinuated themselves into other people's households and led away weak women. These women were already laden with sins, and the men did not unburden them or set them free as they promised, but rather burdened them with still greater slavery and heaped sins upon sins. He gives two causes of the deception of these silly women. 1. Because these women were carried away by various passions and desires that they could not control.

units.la: Verf. 7. Semper discentes, sed quæ nunquam ad cognitionem veritatis venire possint. Altera, quia non contentæ doctrinâ ab Apostolis acceptâ, præ curiositate & instabilitate animi semper nova & desideriis suis accommodata quærebant, ideoque quamvis discere velle videbantur, impossibile erat eas ad scientiam salutiferæ veritatis pervenire.
units.tr: Verse 7. Always learning, yet never able to come to the knowledge of the truth. The second cause is that, not content with the doctrine received from the Apostles, out of curiosity and restlessness of mind they always sought new things suited to their desires. So although they seemed to want to learn, it was impossible for them to attain to knowledge of the saving truth.

units.la: Secunda pars Capitis.
units.tr: Second part of the chapter.

units.la: Verf. 8. Quemadmodum autem Iannes & Iambres restiterunt Mosi, ita & hi resistunt veritati, homines mente corrupti, reprobi circa fidem.
units.tr: Verse 8. Now as Jannes and Jambres withstood Moses, so do these also resist the truth: men of corrupt minds, reprobate concerning the faith.

units.la: Secunda pars Capitis, in qua consolatur Timotheum, seu fidelem Pastorem adversus mali hujus efficaciam: idque argumentis 10. Quæ omnia probant consolationem ab eo admittendam esse in mediis certaminibus. Quemadmodum] Argumentum primum, Quia idem patiuntur veri Pastores ab his impostoribus, quod olim Moses & Aaron passi sunt à Magis Egyptiis sub Pharaone: Quorum nomina, Apostolus ex Spiritus Sancti inspiratione edoctus describit in ipsorum ignominiam perpetuam, & aliorum terrorem. Veritati] Arg. 2. Quia istiusmodi homines veritatis sunt adversarii, & pastorum verorum etiam propter veritatem hostes. Corrupti] Arg. 3. Quia cum sint mente corrupti, qui mentis Judicium vitiosis affectibus habent depravatum, & reprobi circa fidem, qui animi sui obstinatione, & corrupto Judicio viam sibi ad sanam fidei doctrinam præcluserunt, minus debent veri pastores eorum Judicium & sententias morari.
units.tr: The second part of the chapter, in which he comforts Timothy, that is, the faithful minister, against the power of this evil, and does so with ten arguments, all of which show that this comfort must be accepted by him in the midst of struggles. As: the first argument: because true ministers suffer the same from these impostors as Moses and Aaron once suffered from the Egyptian magicians under Pharaoh. Paul, taught by the inspiration of the Holy Spirit, records their names for their lasting shame and for the terror of others. Truth: argument 2: because such men are opponents of the truth, and enemies of true ministers even on account of the truth. Corrupt: argument 3: because, being corrupt in mind, that is, having their judgement of the mind depraved by sinful affections, and being reprobate concerning the faith, having by their obstinacy and corrupt judgement shut themselves off from the way to sound doctrine, true ministers ought all the less to give weight to their judgement and opinions.

units.la: Verf. 9. Sed non procedent amplius: nam amentia illorum evidens erit omnibus ut & illorum fuit.
units.tr: Verse 9. But they will not proceed further, for their folly will be plain to all, as theirs also was.

units.la: Arg. 4. Specialiter spectans eos impostores de quibus exempli causa loquitur, quia amplius non ferent res suas clam Ecclesiâ, nec sic proficient ut hypocrisi sua imponant omnibus, (quasi orthodoxi essent) sicut prius fecerant. Statuerat enim Apostolus excommunicationis notâ ipsos insigniendo, amentiam eorum omnibus manifestare.
units.tr: Argument 4: this refers specifically to those impostors of whom he speaks by way of example, because they will no longer carry on their affairs secretly from the Church, nor make such progress as to deceive everyone with their hypocrisy (as though they were orthodox), as they had done before. For the Apostle had determined to brand them with the mark of excommunication, and so to make their folly known to all.

units.la: Verf. 10. Tu verò assequutus es doctrinam meam, vitæ meæ rationem, propositum, fidem, lenitatem, charitatem, tolerantiam.
units.tr: Verse 10. But you have followed my teaching, my conduct, my purpose, my faith, my patience, my love, my endurance.

units.la: Verf. 11. Persecutiones, afflictiones quæ mihi acciderunt Antiochia, ochia, Iconii, Lystris: quas persequutiones sustinuerim: sed ex omnibus eripuit me Dominus.
units.tr: Verse 11. The persecutions and afflictions that came upon me at Antioch, at Iconium, at Lystra: what persecutions I endured. Yet out of them all the Lord delivered me.

units.la: Arg. 5. Consolationis & confirmationis Timothei adversus hos impostores, Quia Paulum habebat vivum & familiare exemplum, Primo virtutum quæ requiruntur in pastore, in doctrina, vita, & specialibus virtutibus illis quatuor, quas enumerat.
units.tr: Argument 5: a comfort and confirmation to Timothy against these impostors, because he had before him a living and familiar example of Paul. First, of the virtues required in a minister, in doctrine, in life, and in those special virtues which he lists.

units.la: Secundo in persecutionibus, quas nominatim in tribus oppidis sustinuit pro Euangelii defensione. Tertio, in lœto exitu, & liberatione ab omnibus illis molestiis, per Domini gratiam.
units.tr: Second, in the persecutions which he endured, named particularly in three towns, for the defence of the Gospel. Third, in the happy outcome and deliverance from all those troubles, by the grace of the Lord.

units.la: Verf. 12. Sed & omnes qui volunt pie vivere in Christo Iesu, persequutionem patientur.
units.tr: Verse 12. Indeed all who want to live godly in Christ Jesus will suffer persecution.

units.la: Arg. 6. Quia est communis sors non solum pastorum, sed & omnium Christianorum, ut propter Euangelium molestias, & persequutiones patiantur.
units.tr: Argument 6: because it is the common lot not only of ministers but of all Christians to suffer troubles and persecutions for the sake of the Gospel.

units.la: Verf. 13. Improbi autem homines & impostores procedent in pejus, tum seducentes alios, tum seducti ipsi.
units.tr: Verse 13. But evil men and impostors will go on from bad to worse, deceiving others and being deceived themselves.

units.la: Arg. 7. Quia caveri non potest, quin obstinati impostores, & falsi fratres proficiant in pejus, seque ipsos & alios erroribus suis in perditionem ducant; quod Timotheum scire & considerare referebat, ne se nimium torqueret, sed alta Dei Judicia revereretur, & seipsum consolaretur.
units.tr: Argument 7: because it cannot be prevented that obstinate impostors and false brothers will go on from bad to worse, and lead themselves and others into destruction by their errors. He told Timothy to know and consider this, so that he would not torment himself too much, but would revere the deep judgements of God and console himself.

units.la: Verf. 14. At tu permane in iis quæ didicisti, & quæ tibi credita sunt, sciens a quo didiceris:
units.tr: Verse 14. But you, continue in what you have learned and what has been entrusted to you, knowing from whom you learned it.

units.la: Arg. 8. Per hortationem propositum, Quia curandum erat ipsi tantum ut fideliter fungeretur officio suo, & depositum Euangelicæ doctrinæ pro virili custodiret.
units.tr: Argument 8. The exhortation proposes the matter: that Timothy need be concerned only that he discharge his office faithfully, and guard the deposit of the Gospel doctrine as far as in him lies.

units.la: Sciens Arg. 9. Confirmans superius, quia de veritate doctrinæ Cœlestis satis edoctus erat per Apostolum Christi, quem pro Apostolo probatum & compertum habebat.
units.tr: Knowing Argument 9. Confirming what was said above: he was sufficiently taught in the truth of the heavenly doctrine by the Apostle of Christ, whom he had found and proved to be an Apostle.

units.la: Verf. 15. Teque a puero sacras literas novisse, quæ te possunt sapientem reddere in salute, per fidem quæ est in Christo Iesu.
units.tr: Verse 15. And that from a child you have known the holy Scriptures, which are able to make you wise unto salvation through faith which is in Christ Jesus.

units.la: Arg. 10. Confirmans hortationem propositam versu superiori, & simul etiam thesin probans, Doctrina quam didicisti a me, & defendendam jam habes tibi commissam. Scripturæ sacræ & Prophetarum doctrinæ consentanea est. Ergo tu maneto in iis: Confirmator in veritate & consolationem habeto. Quæ te possunt ] Hoc Argumentum dilatat ex quinq; his considerationibus: 1. Scio te institutum, & familiariter versatum in Scripturis à puero: 2. Scriptura potest tibi sapientiam salutarem ministrare, quæ in cognitione & fide IESU CHRISTI consistit.
units.tr: Argument 10. Confirming the exhortation proposed in the preceding verse, and at the same time proving the thesis: The doctrine which you have learned from me, and which you now have committed to you to defend, agrees with the holy Scriptures and the doctrine of the Prophets. Therefore continue in those things, be confirmed in the truth, and have comfort. Which are able: this argument is expanded by five considerations: (1) I know that you were instructed and familiarly versed in the Scriptures from childhood; (2) Scripture can supply you with saving wisdom, which consists in the knowledge and faith of Jesus Christ.

units.la: Vers. 16. Tota scriptura divinitus est inspirata, & utilis ad doctrinam, ad redargutionem, ad correctionem, ad institutionem, quæ est in justitia.
units.tr: Verse 16. All Scripture is given by inspiration of God, and is profitable for doctrine, for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righteousness.

units.la: 3. Scriptura tota est divinitus inspirata, ideoque divinam plane autoritatem habet. 4. Scriptura tota facit ad vera docenda, & falsa redarguenda in iis quæ ad fidem pertinent, & ad malorum morum correctionem, & in bonis moribus institutionem.
units.tr: (3) All Scripture is divinely inspired, and therefore plainly has divine authority. (4) All Scripture serves to teach what is true and to refute what is false in matters pertaining to faith, to correct evil morals, and to instruct in good morals.

units.la: Vers. 17. Ut perfectus sit homo Dei, ad omne opus bonum perfectè instructus.
units.tr: Verse 17. That the man of God may be perfect, thoroughly furnished unto all good works.

units.la: 5. Denique Scriptura hominem Dei, seu Pastorem Ecclesiæ perfectè instructum reddere potest, ad omnes muneris sui partes, & ad omne bonum opus, quod ab ipso requirit DEUS, sive ad suam, sive ad aliorum salutem vel DEI gloriam. Ergo maneto in his quæ didicilti secundum Scripturas à me, cum Scripturam habeas ad manum, ut promptuarium, unde desumas quæcunque te perfectum, & perfectè instructum ad omne opus bonum reddant.
units.tr: (5) Finally, Scripture can render the man of God, that is, the minister of the Church, thoroughly furnished for all the parts of his office and for every good work which God requires of him, whether for his own salvation or that of others, or for the glory of God. Therefore continue in what you have learned from me according to the Scriptures, since you have Scripture at hand as a storehouse from which you may draw whatever makes you perfect and thoroughly furnished for every good work.

units.la: Caput Quartum.
units.tr: Chapter 4.

units.la: Duæ sunt Capitis partes, In prima quasi Testamento condito gravissimè hortatur Timotheum, ut muneris sui partes fideliter obeat, ad vers. 9. In secunda postquam de rebus privatis egit, quæ ipsum & Timotheum spectabant, concludit Epistolam.
units.tr: The chapter has two parts. In the first, as if making a will, he earnestly urges Timothy to discharge the duties of his office faithfully, up to verse 9. In the second, after dealing with private matters that concerned himself and Timothy, he concludes the Epistle.

units.la: Vers. 1. Obtestor igitur ego coram Deo & Domino Iesu Christo, qui judicaturus est vivos & mortuos, in illustri illo suo adventu & regno suo.
units.tr: Verse 1. I charge you therefore before God and the Lord Jesus Christ, who shall judge the living and the dead, at his glorious appearing and his kingdom.

units.la: Hortationi ad muneris sui partes obeundas præmittit obtestationem gravem in qua Timotheo ponit ante oculos: Primò, DEI majestatem jestatem: 2. DOMINUM IESUM CHRISTUM: 3. Tribunal CHRISTI, coram quo redditurus erat rationem Ministerii sui, una cum reliquis in novissimo illo die judicandis: 4. Gloriam illam CHRISTI, quam in illustri suo adventu, & regni sui plena manifestatione omnibus ostensurus erat.
units.tr: Before the exhortation to discharge the duties of his office, he sets down a solemn charge, placing before Timothy's eyes: first, the majesty of God; second, the Lord Jesus Christ; third, the tribunal of Christ, before which Timothy was to render account of his ministry, together with the others who are to be judged on that last day; fourth, the glory of Christ, which he was to display to all at his glorious appearing and the full manifestation of his kingdom.

units.la: Versf. 2. Pradica sermonem insta tempestive, intempestive: argue, objurga, exhortare cum omni lenitate & doctrina.
units.tr: Verse 2. Preach the word; be instant in season, out of season; reprove, rebuke, exhort with all longsuffering and teaching.

units.la: Ipsa hortatio in qua quinque requirit officia: 1. Assiduitatem in prædicando: 2. Ut strenuè contendat contra omnia obstacula: 3. Ut sequatur non tantum occasiones prædicandi, quæ cum ipsius commoditate, vel cum torpentis populi otio consistant, sed ut nullis parcens laboribus exstimulet seipsum: & populum ad vanas mundi occupationes nimium properantem quasi manu injecta, sistat, omnes solicitans ad unicum illud quod necessarium est, quærendum: 4. Ut omnem lapidem moveat pro concione, ad populo persuadendum, ut proficiant in fide & obedientia CHRISTI, non solum veram doctrinam prædicando, & falsam doctrinam redarguendo, sed etiam malos mores increpando & corrigendo, & hortando seu obsecrando ut pie, juste & sobrie vivant: 5. Ut zelum & fervorem in reprehensionibus temperet, & condiat lenitate: refutationes vero errorum muniat & fulciat solida doctrina, nelabor fit irritus.
units.tr: The exhortation itself requires five duties: (1) constancy in preaching; (2) that he strenuously contend against all obstacles; (3) that he pursue not only the opportunities for preaching which suit his own convenience or the idleness of a sluggish people, but that, sparing no labour, he stir up himself and, as it were laying hands on the people who rush too eagerly into the vain occupations of the world, hold them back, urging all to seek that one thing which is needful; (4) that he move every stone for the sermon, so as to persuade the people to grow in faith and obedience to Christ, not only by preaching sound doctrine and refuting false doctrine, but also by rebuking and correcting evil morals, and by exhorting and entreating them to live godly, righteously and soberly; (5) that he temper zeal and fervour in rebukes with gentleness, and season them with mildness, but fortify and strengthen the refutations of errors with solid doctrine, lest his labour become fruitless.

units.la: Versf. 3. Nam erit tempus quum sanam doctrinam non tolerabunt, sed auribus prurientes, ipsi sibi pro suis cupiditatibus coacervabunt doctores.
units.tr: Verse 3. For the time will come when they will not endure sound doctrine, but having itching ears they will heap up for themselves teachers after their own lusts.

units.la: Rationes subjungit exhortationi quatuor: prima, Quia instabat tempus, quo multi defecturi erant a doctrinæ sinceritate, idcirco necesse erat ut Timotheus diligentius incumberet officio suo: Defectionem autem hanc a suis quinque partibus, seu gradibus describit. Gradus primus, Sanam doctrinam non sustinebunt CHRISTI professores, non ferent vitiorum suorum reprehensiones, aut ad virtutem hortationes, nec quicquid salubre & salutiferum ipsis esse posset: Gradus 2 Desideriis seu cupiditatibus carnalibus mordicus adhærebunt: Gradus 3. In cordibus suis odio habebunt veros Pastores, tanquam communes hostes, & ut ipsos coerceant multos coacervabunt sibi doctores, qui populi cupiditatibus adblandiantur: Gradus 4. Non sapiet ipsis antiqua DEI veritas ad pietatem, & vitæ novitatem faciens, sed excuriositate ofitate semper aliquid novi audiendi, quærent sibi palponés, qui prurientes aures ipsorum suaviter scalpant, ac demulceant, præ se interim ferentes Christianæ doctrinæ,& religionis studium non mediocre.
units.tr: He adds four reasons to the exhortation. The first: because the time was at hand when many would fall away from the purity of doctrine, therefore it was necessary that Timothy apply himself more diligently to his office. He describes this defection by its five parts, or stages. The first stage: the professors of Christ will not endure sound doctrine, they will not bear the rebukes of their vices or exhortations to virtue, nor anything wholesome and salutary for them. The second stage: they will cling stubbornly to their carnal desires and lusts. The third stage: they will hate true ministers in their hearts, as common enemies, and in order to restrain them they will heap up many teachers for themselves, who flatter the lusts of the people. The fourth stage: the ancient truth of God, making for piety and newness of life, will no longer be savoury to them; instead, through a restless curiosity to hear something new always, they will seek for themselves flatterers who will softly scratch and soothe their itching ears, meanwhile displaying a not small zeal for Christian doctrine and religion.

units.la: Vers. 4. Et à veritate quidem aures avertent, ad fabulas vero convertentur.
units.tr: Verse 4. And they will turn their ears away from the truth, and will be turned unto fables.

units.la: Gradus 5. defectionis; Aperte profitebuntur se impatientes esse audiendi severos doctores veritatis, qui ipsis nihil canant præterquam quod ex sacra Scriptura didicerunt, & convertent se ad audiendum eos qui commenta hominum, somnia sua, historias, hominum sententias & flosculos, sigmenta, fabulas & legenda, pro concione proferent.
units.tr: The fifth stage of defection: they will openly profess that they are impatient of hearing severe teachers of the truth, who sing to them nothing but what they have learned from holy Scripture; and they will turn to hear those who in the sermon bring forward the inventions of men, their own dreams, stories, the opinions of men and flowers of rhetoric, fictions, fables and legends.

units.la: Vers. 5. At tu vigila in omnibus, perfer, opus perage Euangelistæ, ministerii tui plenam fidem facito.
units.tr: Verse 5. But watch thou in all things, endure afflictions, do the work of an evangelist, make full proof of thy ministry.

units.la: Hinc infert & repetit hortationem, ut Timotheus tanto magis invigilet, & omnes partes officii faciat, in laboribus & afflictionibus se obdurans, nec adversariis, nec periculis ullis cedens.
units.tr: From this he draws the conclusion and repeats the exhortation, that Timothy should all the more watch and perform all parts of his office, hardening himself in labours and afflictions, yielding neither to adversaries nor to any dangers.

units.la: Euangelistæ Hortationi repetitæ miscet alteram rationem, Quia decebat eum Euangelistam agere, hoc est, plus quam ordinarium doctorem, & nihil omittere eorum quæ à fideli Euangelista jure exigi possent.
units.tr: To the repeated exhortation he joins another reason: because it became him to act as an evangelist, that is, more than an ordinary teacher, and to omit nothing of those things which could rightly be required of a faithful evangelist.

units.la: Vers. 6. Nam ego jam libor, & tempus meæ resolutionis instat.
units.tr: Verse 6. For I am now ready to be offered, and the time of my departure is at hand.

units.la: Tertia hortationis ratio, Quia hæc est quasi testamentaria hortatio Pauli senioris, cujus consortio Timotheus non erat diu slurus, (nam hæc profert quasi jam mortem pro Christi Euangelio obiturus, & brevi solvendus ex mundi & corpusculi carcere, ut liber ad Deum evolaret;) ideoque hortatio hæc tanto altius imprimenda erat Timothei animo.
units.tr: The third reason for the exhortation: because this is, as it were, the testamentary exhortation of Paul the elder, whose company Timothy was not to enjoy for long (for he speaks as one about to die already for the gospel of Christ, and soon to be released from the prison of the world and the body, so that he might fly free to God); therefore this exhortation was to be impressed all the more deeply on Timothy's mind.

units.la: Vers. 7. Certamen illud præclarum decertavi, cursum consummavi, fidem servavi.
units.tr: Verse 7. I have fought a good fight, I have finished my course, I have kept the faith.

units.la: Ratio 4. Ab experientia Pauli hortantis, qui Ministerii sui cursum jam ferè absolverat, & certamen in eo decurrendo non modo non molestum, sed etiam consolationis & bonæ spei plenum expertus erat, & quod supererat decurrendum, in hoc stadio considebat gloriosum su-turum. Hoc argumentum quinque ipsius membris propositis, explicat.
units.tr: The fourth reason: from the experience of Paul, who exhorts, and who had now nearly completed the course of his ministry, and had found the contest in running it not only not troublesome but full of consolation and good hope, and who sat in this stadium expecting that what remained to be run would be glorious. He sets out this argument by means of five members, which he explains.

units.la: Membrum primum, Certamen susceptum in Apostolatu & jam pene absolutum, vocat bonum certamen, ut Timotheus sciret se non erubescere labores, afflictiones & persequutiones quas sustinuerat.
units.tr: The first member: he calls the contest undertaken in the apostleship, and now almost finished, a good fight, so that Timothy might know that he did not blush at the labours, afflictions and persecutions which he had endured.

units.la: Membrum 2. Gratulatur sibi de cursu consummato, quasi voti compos jam factus, & metam jam prope assequutus esset: Membrum 3. Lætatur quod duci suo Christo fidelem militem, per Dei gratiam sese præstiterit in doctrinâ, & vitâ, jusiurandum militiæ suæ observando.
units.tr: The second member: he rejoices over the course completed, as one who has already obtained his vow and has nearly reached the goal. The third member: he rejoices that, by the grace of God, he has shown himself a faithful soldier to his leader Christ, in doctrine and in life, keeping the oath of his service.

units.la: Versf. 8. Quod superest, repositâ est mihi justitiæ corona, quam reddet mihi Dominus in illo die, justus ille judex: non solum autem mihi, sed & omnibus qui expetiverint illustrem illum ipsius adventum.
units.tr: Verse 8. Henceforth there is laid up for me the crown of righteousness, which the Lord, the righteous judge, shall give me at that day: and not to me only, but to all also who have loved his appearing.

units.la: Membrum 4. Quoàd tempus futurum profitetur fiduciam suam de gratuita mercede, quam Deus gratis promisit omnibus fidelibus, & ut justus judex, juste simul & ex gratia rependet, non ex merito ullo nostro, sed priora dona sua gratuita posterioribus gratuito cumulando.
units.tr: The fourth member: as to the future he professes his confidence in the free reward which God has freely promised to all the faithful; and as a righteous judge he will repay justly and at the same time by grace, not on account of any merit of ours, but by heaping his free gifts upon his later gifts, as he has given the earlier ones freely.

units.la: Membrum 5. In quo Apostolus exemplum ad usum Timothei,& omnium fidelium accomodat, quod corona justitiæ non esset reddenda sibi soli, sed omnibus etiam qui studendo ea facere quæ placent Domino, declarant se expectare, & diligere Domini adventum.
units.tr: The fifth member: in which the Apostle applies the example to the use of Timothy and of all the faithful, that the crown of righteousness is not to be given to himself alone, but to all who, by striving to do those things which please the Lord, show that they look for and love the Lord's coming.

units.la: Secunda pars Capitis,
units.tr: The second part of the chapter,

units.la: Versf. 9. Stude venire ad me citò.
units.tr: Verse 9. Make haste to come to me quickly.

units.la: Secunda pars Capitis, In qua de rebus suis privatis, quæ inter Timotheum & ipsum intercedebant, & quæ Timotheum scire de ipsius negotiis referebat, agit.
units.tr: The second part of the chapter, in which he deals with his own private affairs, which lay between Timothy and himself, and with what Timothy was to learn about his circumstances.
