units.tr: Verse 11. Who was once useless to you, but now is useful to you and to me, whom I have sent back:

units.la: Arg. 5. Licet olim ante conversionem, inutilis tibi fuerit Onesimus, posthac tamen fidus & sedulus servus, in officiis servitutis præstandis, Futurus est: Ergo,
units.tr: Argument 5. Although Onesimus was once useless to you, before his conversion, yet hereafter he will be a faithful and diligent servant in performing the duties of service. Therefore,

units.la: Verf. 12. Tu autem eum, id est, viscera mea, excipe.
units.tr: Verse 12. But you receive him, that is, my own heart.

units.la: Arg. 6. Humaniter recipiendo Onesimum mea viscera refocillaturus es, sin minus, in mea viscera sæviturus es. Ergo.
units.tr: Argument 6. By receiving Onesimus kindly you will refresh my heart; if not, you will be inflicting cruelty on my heart. Therefore,

units.la: Verf. 13. Quem ego cupiebam apud me retinere, ut pro te ministraret mihi in vinculis Euangelii:
units.tr: Verse 13. Whom I wished to keep with me, that he might minister to me in your place in the chains of the gospel:

units.la: Verf. 14. Sed absque tua sententia nihil voluit facere: ne velut ex necessitate sit beneficium tuum, sed spontaneum.
units.tr: Verse 14. But without your consent he wished to do nothing, so that your kindness might be not as of necessity, but of your own free will.

units.la: Arg 7. Tanti facio Onesimi fidem in ministrando, ut ejus fidelitati commissurus essem me, & negotia mea, & usurus opera ipsius, nisi malem beneficium illud a te oblatum, quam per me extortum necessitate aliquâ consequi: Ergo. Ut pro te ] Arg. 8. Tu ipse Philemon teneris mihi in vinculis inservire, nedum meo rogatu servum tuum, in beneficium tuum proprium, recipere: Ergo.
units.tr: Argument 7. I value Onesimus's faithfulness in serving so highly that I would have entrusted myself and my affairs to his fidelity and made use of his services, were it not that I preferred to obtain that kindness offered by you rather than to extort it from you by some necessity. Therefore. For you. Argument 8. You yourself, Philemon, owe me service in my chains; much less should you receive your slave back at my request, as a benefit to yourself. Therefore.

units.la: Verf. 15. Nam mirum ni fecesset ad tempus, ut perpetuum eum reciperes:
units.tr: Verse 15. For perhaps he was parted from you for a time, that you might receive him for ever:

units.la: Arg. 9. Per Dei providentiam, Onesimi fuga ad tempus, convertenda est in bonum tuum, per Onesimi in posterum constantem permanssionem apud te. Ergo.
units.tr: Argument 9. By God's providence, Onesimus's flight for a time is to be turned to your good, through Onesimus's steadfast remaining with you in the future. Therefore.

units.la: Verf. 16. Non jam ut servum, sed amplius quam servum, fratrem dilectum, maxime mihi, quanto autem magis tibi & in carne & in Domino?
units.tr: Verse 16. No longer as a slave, but more than a slave, a beloved brother, especially to me, but how much more to you, both in the flesh and in the Lord?

units.la: Arg 10 Onesimus non est rediturus ad te servus tantum, sed etiam frater in Christo fidelis, & idcirco diligendus tibi, tum in carne, quia domesticus tuus est; tum in DOMINO, quia Christianus est: nam cum diligatur a me, qui ejus operâ non sum usurus, quantò magis diligi debet à te, qui utilitatem fidei ejus es percepturus. Ergo.
units.tr: Argument 10. Onesimus is going back to you not only as a slave but also as a faithful brother in Christ, and therefore is to be loved by you, both in the flesh, because he is your household servant, and in the Lord, because he is a Christian. For since he is loved by me, who am not going to make use of his service, how much more ought he to be loved by you, who are going to receive the benefit of his faith. Therefore.

units.la: Verf. 17 Itaque si putas nostra esse communia, excipe eum tanquam me.
units.tr: Verse 17. If then you count me a partner, receive him as you would me.

units.la: Arg. 11. In hoc probaturus sum quanti facias meam societatem, consortium & amicitiam. Ergo.
units.tr: Argument 11. In this I shall prove how highly you value my fellowship, partnership and friendship. Therefore.

units.la: Verf. 18 Quod siquid laesit te, aut debet, hoc mihi imputato.
units.tr: Verse 18. But if he has wronged you at all, or owes you anything, put that to my account.

units.la: Arg. 12. Per solutionem objectionis, Damnum furti per quod debitor aris alieni constitutus est Onesimus, Ego Paulus praestare paratus sum, in cujus rei testimonium, volo ut damnum tibi ab Onesimo illatum in meas rationes referatur, in eumque finem pro syngrapho hanc Epistolam propriâ manu exaratam haberi volo: Ergo recipiendus est.
units.tr: Argument 12. By answering an objection. Although Onesimus, through whom the debtor of another's money was made liable, has caused the loss of theft, I, Paul, am ready to make it good. In witness of this, I want the loss inflicted on you by Onesimus to be entered in my accounts, and to this end I want this letter, written in my own hand, to be held as a bond. Therefore he is to be received.

units.la: Verf. 19 Ego Paulus scripsi mea manu, ego dependam: ut ne dicam tibi te etiam teipsum mihi insuper debere.
units.tr: Verse 19. I, Paul, have written with my own hand; I will pay it, not to mention that you also owe me yourself besides.

units.la: Arg. 13. Teipsum debes mihi, quippe qui meo Ministerio conversus es, & mihi serviendo te tuaque teneris impendere; multo magis tam aequis conditionibus servum fugitivum recipere: Ergo.
units.tr: Argument 13. You owe yourself to me, since you were converted through my ministry, and by serving me you are bound to devote yourself and your own to me; much more, then, should you receive a runaway slave on such fair terms. Therefore.

units.la: Verf. 20. Et jam, frater, hunc ego fructum abs te consequar in Domino: refocilla mea viscera in Domino.
units.tr: Verse 20. Yes, brother, let me gain this benefit from you in the Lord; refresh my bowels in the Lord.

units.la: Arg. 14. Fructum tuae fidei perceptuus sum in Domino, si mihi annuendo, Onesimi viscera & mea refocillaveris propter CHRISTUM. Ergo recipiendus in gratiam est Onesimus.
units.tr: Argument 14. I shall receive the fruit of your faith in the Lord if, by agreeing to me, you refresh the bowels of Onesimus and my own for Christ's sake. Therefore Onesimus is to be received back into favour.

units.la: Verf. 21. Scripsi tibi, confisus fore ut audultes, ut qui norim te etiam amplius quàm dico facturum esse.
units.tr: Verse 21. I have written to you, confident that you will obey, knowing that you will do even more than I say.

units.la: Tertia Epistolae pars, Epilogus, in quo quatuor sunt Articuli: In primo profitetur Apostolus spem suam de impetratione veniae Onesimo dandae; imò & amplioris gratiae Onesimo concedendae, quam postulata fuit.
units.tr: The third part of the letter, the epilogue, in which there are four articles. In the first, the Apostle expresses his hope of obtaining pardon for Onesimus; indeed, of granting Onesimus a greater favour than was asked.

units.la: Verf. 22. Simul autem etiam para mihi hospitium: spero enim me per preces vestras donandum vobis.
units.tr: Verse 22. At the same time, also prepare a lodging for me; for I hope that through your prayers I shall be given back to you.

units.la: Articulus 2. In quo parari sibi hospitium rogat, ut Philemon sciret Apostolum venturum, in majorem ipsius consolationem, si obtemperaret huic Epistolae. Interim liberationis suae ex vinculis, causas interfecit duas, quae sunt donum vel gratia DEI, & fratrum preces. Verf. 23. Salutant te, Epaphras, (meus in captivitate propter Iesum Christum socius:)
units.tr: Article 2. In which he asks that a lodging be prepared for him, so that Philemon may know the Apostle is coming, for his greater comfort, if he complies with this letter. Meanwhile he names two causes of his release from his chains, which are the gift or grace of God and the prayers of the brothers. Verse 23. Epaphras, my fellow prisoner in Christ Jesus, greets you.

units.la: Verf. 24. Marcus, Aristarchus, Demas, Lucas, adjutores mei.
units.tr: Verse 24. Mark, Aristarchus, Demas, Luke, my fellow workers.

units.la: Articulus 3. In quo salutatio mittitur ad Philemonem, ab iis qui in Pauli consortio erant, quae omnia faciunt ad propositum Epistolae scopum, sicut & quae in praefatione posita sunt, nempe ad permovendum Philemonis animum, ut in Gratiam reciperet Onesimum.
units.tr: Article 3. In which greeting is sent to Philemon from those who were in Paul's company; all of which serve the purpose of the letter's aim stated in the preface, namely to move Philemon's mind to receive Onesimus back into favour.

units.la: Verf. 25. Gratia Domini nostri Iesu Christi sit cum Spiritu vestro, Amen.
units.tr: Verse 25. The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit. Amen.

units.la: Articulus 4. In quo benedictione Apostolica completens Philemonem & Appiam, claudit Epistolam.
units.tr: Article 4. In which, by completing the blessing of Philemon and Apphia with an apostolic benediction, he closes the letter.

units.la: EXPOSITIO ANALYTICA EPISTOLAE PAULI, AD HEBRAEOS.
units.tr: THE ANALYTICAL EXPOSITION OF THE EPISTLE OF PAUL TO THE HEBREWS.

units.la: Summarium.
units.tr: Summary.

units.la: Tiamsi Paulus, cum sciret se omnibus Hebraeis nondum conversis exosum, & fidelibus etiam multis infirmioribus, legalium rituum observationi nimium addictis suspectum, maluerit nomen suum in Epistolae initio supprimere, ut sine praejudicio veritatem possent facilius admittere; extra controversiam tamen est cum praecipuis aliquot Ecclesiis, & primariis aliquot fratribus, in quorum manus Epistola haec primum perventura erat, nomen suum per tabellarios significasse, & cognitum fuisse, ut ex fine Epistolae patet; Sed nobis post ejusdem Spiritus, in hac reliquisque Epistolis Paulinis demonstrationem satisfacere potest Petri Apostoli auctoritas, qui singuluri Dei providentia, Capite tertio secundae Epistolae sua, ad eosdem dispersos Hebraeos, Testatur de Epistola Pauli ad eosdem scripta, quæ tâm in manibus ipsorum terebatur, & Paulina palam agnoscebatur; quam Epistolam commendat ibi Petrus, unà cum reliquis Pauli Epistolis, ut divinitus ab eodem SPIRITU sapientiæ inspiratam, ut in canonem Scripturæ jam relatam, & ab Ecclesia unanimiter cum aliis ejus Epistolis agnitam & receptam. Hunc igitur ipsissimam esse necesse est agnoscamus, nisi minùs honorificè de Ecclesiæ fide, & providentia Dei, in custodiendo Scripturæ canone, & oraculis Ecclesiæ traditis, sentiremus.
units.tr: Although Paul, knowing that he was hated by all the Hebrews who had not yet been converted, and suspected also by many weaker believers who were too devoted to the observance of the legal rites, preferred to suppress his name at the beginning of the Epistle, so that they might more easily admit the truth without prejudice, it is nonetheless beyond dispute that he made his name known through couriers to some of the chief Churches and to some leading brethren, into whose hands this Epistle was first to come, and that it was recognised, as is clear from the end of the Epistle. But for us the authority of the Apostle Peter can supply proof of the Spirit's work in this Epistle and the other Pauline Epistles. By God's singular providence, in the third chapter of his second Epistle, he bears witness to the Epistle that Paul had written to the same scattered Hebrews, which was then in their hands and was openly acknowledged as Paul's. Peter there commends this Epistle, together with the rest of Paul's Epistles, as inspired by the same divine Spirit of wisdom, as already placed in the canon of Scripture, and as unanimously acknowledged and received by the Church along with his other Epistles. We must therefore acknowledge this to be truly his, unless we judged less honourably of the Church's faith and of God's providence in guarding the canon of Scripture and the oracles handed down to the Church.

units.la: Scopus Epistolæ est, ut Hebræos infirmos in fide, & magna ex parte ritPuum Legalium nimium tenaces, nec satis de Christi excellentia instructos; Præterea etiam ab infidelibus passim persecutionibus exagitatos, confirmaret; & ad perseverantiam in fide & obedientia Evangelii, contra omnem metum, animaret.
units.tr: The aim of the Epistle is to confirm the Hebrews, who were weak in faith and for the most part too tenacious of the legal rites, and not sufficiently instructed in the excellence of Christ. Moreover, it is to confirm those who were everywhere harassed by persecutions from unbelievers, and to encourage them to perseverance in faith and in obedience to the Gospel, against all fear.

units.la: Partes Epistolæ (ut & aliarum Epistolarum Pauli) duæ sunt. Altera ad fidem formandam & confirmandam, ad Cap. 12. Altera ad sanctimoniam, seu fructus fidei in vitæ conversatione proferendos spectans, Cap. 12, & 13.
units.tr: The parts of the Epistle (as also of Paul's other Epistles) are two. The one is concerned with forming and confirming faith, to Cap. 12. The other concerns holiness, or the bearing of the fruits of faith in the conduct of life, Cap. 12, & 13.

units.la: Quod ad fidei doctrinam attinet, docet Hebræos quanta sit excellentia Jesu Christi, in munere ipsius Prophetico & Sacerdotali.
units.tr: As regards the doctrine of faith, it teaches the Hebrews how great is the excellence of Jesus Christ in his prophetic and priestly office.

units.la: Quod ad excellentiam Prophetiæ Christi, incomparabilem eam esse, & supra omnes, & homines & Angelos longè eminere docetur, Capite primo.
units.tr: As regards the excellence of Christ's prophetic office, it is taught that this is incomparable, that it stands far above all, and that it rises high above both men and angels, Chapter 1.

units.la: Tribus proximè sequentibus Capitibus usus quadruplex hujus doctrinæ in quadruplici exhortatione deducitur. Prima hortatio est, Ne deficiant à fide Christiana. Secunda, Ne quid detrahant existimationi Christi, propter ipsius in carne passiones, Capite secundo. Tertia, Ut constanter retineant professionem fidei Christianæ, Capite tertio. Quarta, Ut festinent ingredi per fidem in promissam DEI requiem, dum audiunt vocem CHRISTI, Capite quarto.
units.tr: By the three chapters that immediately follow, the fourfold use of this doctrine is drawn out in a fourfold exhortation. The first exhortation is that they should not fall away from the Christian faith. The second is that they should detract nothing from the esteem of Christ on account of his sufferings in the flesh, Chapter 2. The third is that they should steadfastly hold fast the profession of the Christian faith, Chapter 3. The fourth is that they should hasten to enter by faith into the promised rest of God, while they hear the voice of Christ, Chapter 4.

units.la: Quod ad excellentiam Sacerdotii Domini nostri Jesu Christi, Ne Judæi nimium tribuerent Levitico Sacerdotio, & in ejus ceremoniis pertinaces hærerent. Probat Christum esse summum Sacerdotem, omni typico Pontifice excellentiorem, utpote verum illum Melchisedecum, correptâ interim Hebræorum ignorantiâ, qui ne capere quidem poterant quæ de Christi excellentia dicenda habebat, Capite quinto. Unde deducitur hortatio ad progressus faciendum in cognitione, & fide Evangelii, Capite sexto.
units.tr: As regards the excellence of the priesthood of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Jews should not attribute too much to the Levitical priesthood or cling obstinately to its ceremonies. The Epistle proves that Christ is the supreme priest, more excellent than every typical high priest, as being the true Melchizedek. Meanwhile it rebukes the ignorance of the Hebrews, who could not even grasp what he had to say about the excellence of Christ, Chapter 5. From this is drawn an exhortation to make progress in the knowledge and faith of the Gospel, Chapter 6.

units.la: Christi eminentiam supra Levitieos Sacerdotes pergit demonstrare, cum respectu Personæ, tum respectu officii Sacerdotalis, Capitibus 7, 8, 9. & partis priori Capitis 10. Doctrinam hanc in usum deducis, hortandes, ut in vera Religionis studio & professione constanter & patienter pergant, imitantes fideles Confessores & Martyres, qui ante Christum natum in fide decesserunt, posteriori parte Capitis 10. & Capite 11. In secunda Epistolae parte variae habentur hortationes ad officia Christianì, quae etiam inter superioris doctrinae usus communiores numerari possunt, Capite 12, 13.
units.tr: He goes on to demonstrate Christ's eminence above the Levitical priests, both with respect to his person and with respect to his priestly office, Chapters 7, 8, 9, and the earlier part of Chapter 10. He applies this doctrine to use, exhorting them to persevere constantly and patiently in the zealous study and profession of true religion, imitating the faithful confessors and martyrs who died in faith before Christ's birth, in the latter part of Chapter 10 and in Chapter 11. In the second part of the Epistle there are various exhortations to Christian duties, which may also be counted among the more general uses of the above doctrine, Chapters 12, 13.

units.la: Caput Primum.
units.tr: Chapter 1.

units.la: HOC Capite Prophetia Christi excellentiam incomparabilem, praecipue propter ipsum Deitatem, probat novem argumentis, quorum ultimum octo rationibus confirmatur.
units.tr: In this chapter he proves the incomparable excellence of Christ's prophecy, chiefly on account of his deity itself, by nine arguments, the last of which is confirmed by eight reasons.

units.la: Verf. 1. DEUS multis vicibus, multisque modis olim loquutus Patribus per Prophetas, ultimis diebus hisce loquutus est nobis per Filium.
units.tr: Verse 1. God, who at many times and in many ways spoke in former days to the fathers by the prophets, in these last days has spoken to us by the Son.

units.la: Argumentum primum, CHRISTUS DEI FILIUS praestantior est omnibus Prophetis, per quos Deus veteri Ecclesiae, seu Patribus loquutus est; praestantiorem namque reddidit conditionem nostram sub Evangelio, quam erat illa Patrum sub lege: Nam, primo, illi Prophetae per inspirationem erant, non quum volebant, sed tantum prout acti erant a Christi Spiritu; & ut Dei Ministri loquebantur: Christus vero filius est Dei, & Princeps Prophetarum, qui sua ipsius auctoritate, non minus quam Patris nomine loquutus est: 2. Prophetae illi multi erant, per quos olim multis vicibus, variis revelandi modis, per partes, gradatim, salutaris doctrinae claritatem Deus Ecclesiae manifestavit; filius vero unus est, per quem Pater semel plene, plane, & ultimo totam suam voluntatem novissimis mundi temporibus uniformiter enarravit nobis, qui sub Evangelio vivimus. Ergo Prophetiae ipsius excellentia incomparabilis est.
units.tr: First argument: Christ, the Son of God, is superior to all the prophets through whom God spoke to the old Church, or to the fathers. For he has made our condition under the Gospel better than the condition of the fathers under the law. First, those prophets were inspired not at their own will, but only as they were moved by the Spirit of Christ, and they spoke as ministers of God. Christ, however, is the Son of God and the Prince of the prophets, and he spoke by his own authority no less than in the name of the Father. Second, those prophets were many, and through them God once revealed the clarity of saving doctrine to the Church in many portions, in various ways of revelation, and gradually. But the Son is one, and through him the Father has once for all, fully, plainly, and finally, in the last times of the world, uniformly declared his whole will to us, who live under the Gospel. Therefore his prophecy is of incomparable excellence.

units.la: Verf. 2. Quem constituit haeredem omnium, per quem etiam mundum condidit.
units.tr: Verse 2. Whom he appointed heir of all things, through whom also he made the world.

units.la: Arg. 2. CHRISTUS sicut per naturam est haeres genitus: sic etiam aeterna Dei ordinatione ad officium Mediatoris, & ex pactione speciali constitutus est haeres, seu Dominus proprietarius omnium creaturarum, in coelo & terra. Idcirco ejus excellentia incomparabilis est. Per quem] Arg. 3. Per cum jam ab æterno existentem Pater mūndum, & omnia quæ in eo sunt, non ut per instrumentum, sed ut per verbum, & sapientiam suam condidit. Ergo ejus excellentia incomparabilis est.
units.tr: Argument 2: Christ, as he is by nature the begotten heir, so also by the eternal ordination of God and by a special covenant he is appointed to the office of Mediator, and is heir, or proprietary Lord, of all creatures in heaven and on earth. Therefore his excellence is incomparable. Through whom] Argument 3: Through him, who already existed from eternity, the Father made the world and all that is in it, not as through an instrument but as through his Word and wisdom. Therefore his excellence is incomparable.

units.la: Vers. 3. Qui quum sit splendor Glorĭæ, & character personæ il-lius, sustineatque omnia Verbo illo suo potente, purgatione peccātorum nostrorum per seipsum factâ, sedit ad dextram Majestatis il-lius excelsissima.
units.tr: Verse 3. Who, being the brightness of his glory and the express image of his person, upholds all things by the word of his power, when he had by himself purged our sins, sat down on the right hand of the Majesty on high.

units.la: Arg. 4. Christus, quantum imperfecta similitudo aperire potest, est ἀπαύγασμα splendor ille gloriæ Patris, seu gloriosæ ejus naturæ in luce inaccessa, refulgentis, effulgentia: In, & à Patre, ex Patris substantia ὑπόστασις genitus est, qui licet sine eo Pater nunquam fuerit, nec esse potuerit, à Patre tamen est distinctus, & in æternum indivulsus, per quem Pater revelat, & gloriam suam communicat, ut Sol per splendorem suum nobis fit conspicuus: Ergo incomparabilis est ejus excellentia.
units.tr: Argument 4: Christ, as far as an imperfect likeness can show, is the radiance [ἀπαύγασμα], that splendour of the Father's glory, that is, of his glorious nature shining in unapproachable light, the brightness. He was begotten in and from the Father, from the substance of the Father, as the substance [ὑπόστασις]. Although the Father never was, nor could be, without him, yet he is distinct from the Father, and inseparable for ever. Through him the Father reveals himself and communicates his glory, just as the sun becomes visible to us through its light. Therefore his excellence is incomparable.

units.la: Character] Arg. 5. Christus est character, seu expressa imago Personæ Patris, id est, (quantum de eo imperfecta similitudo docere nos potest,) distincta est à Patre persona, Patrem in omnibus referens, unius ejusdemque formæ seu essentiæ, qui Patrem nobis ad vivum repræsentat, ut qualis est Filius, talem & Patrem esse agnoscamus: Ergo incomparabilis est ejus excellentia.
units.tr: Express image] Argument 5: Christ is the express image, or exact likeness, of the person of the Father. That is, so far as an imperfect likeness can teach us about him, he is a person distinct from the Father, representing the Father in all things, of one and the same form or essence. He presents the Father to us to the life, so that, as the Son is, we may acknowledge the Father to be such also. Therefore his excellence is incomparable.

units.la: Sustineatque] Arg. 6 Christus omnes creaturas in Cœlo & terra sustentat, tuetur, conservat, nutu seu verbo divino suæ potentiæ, seu virrute Deitatis suæ: Ergo excellentia ejus incomparabilis est.
units.tr: Upholding] Argument 6: Christ upholds, protects, and preserves all creatures in heaven and on earth, by the nod or divine word of his power, that is, by the virtue of his deity. Therefore his excellence is incomparable.

units.la: Purificatione ] Arg. 7. Purgationem omnium peccatorum nostrorum plenissimè impetravit, acquisivit, & fecit, quatenus pontifex, & Θεανθρωπος est, non adjutus à quoquam, non per victimam ullam legalem, sed per semetipsum in cruce semel oblatum: Ergo excellentia ejus incomparabilis est.
units.tr: Purification] Argument 7: He has most fully obtained, acquired, and made the purification of all our sins, insofar as he is the high priest and God-man [Θεανθρωπος]. He was helped by no one, and not by any legal sacrifice, but by himself, offered once on the cross. Therefore his excellence is incomparable.

units.la: Sedit ] Arg. 8. Post expiationem peccatorum nostrorum per se solum semel factam, consedit Θεανθρωπος ut Rex Ecclesiæ ad dextram Majestatis in excelsis, æquali honore & potentia cum Deo Patre regnans, & gubernans omnia: Ergo incomparabilis est ejus excellentia.
units.tr: Sat down] Argument 8: After the expiation of our sins, which he made once by himself alone, the God-man [Θεανθρωπος] sat down as King of the Church at the right hand of the Majesty on high, reigning and governing all things with equal honour and power together with God the Father. Therefore his excellence is incomparable.

units.la: Verf. 4. Tanto præstantior factus Angelis, quanto excellentius præ illis sortitus est nomen.
units.tr: Verse 4. Being made so much better than the angels, as he has by inheritance obtained a more excellent name than they.

units.la: Arg. 9. CHRISTUS tanto praestantior est Angelis, quanto nomen filii Dei praestantius est nomine Angeli, seu nuntii. Nomen autem filii DEI Christo competit, & secundum divinitatem, ex aeterna generatione, communicata ipsi tota essentia divina; & insuper secundum humanitatem, non per adoptionem, sed per unionem datum est ei hoc nomen, siquidem eadem persona, quae fuit filius Dei incarnandus, est jam filius Dei incarnatus, humana natura in unionem & unitatem personae secundae, assumpta & vectâ.
units.tr: Argument 9: Christ is so much better than the angels as the name Son of God is better than the name angel, that is, messenger. Now the name Son of God belongs to Christ both according to his deity, by eternal generation, the whole divine essence being communicated to him, and also, according to his humanity, this name has been given to him not by adoption but by union. For the same person who was to be incarnated as Son of God is now the incarnate Son of God, the human nature having been assumed into the union and unity of the second person.

units.la: Verf. 5. Nam cui dixit unquam Angelorum, Filium meum es tu, ego hodie genui te? Ac rursum, Ego ero ei Pater, & ipse erit mihi Filius?
units.tr: Verse 5. For to which of the angels did he ever say, "You are my Son, today I have begotten you"? And again, "I will be to him a Father, and he shall be to me a Son"?

units.la: Hoc argumentum ultimum Apostolus confirmat octo rationibus, quarum septem priores ex totidem testimoniis Scripturae petuntur.
units.tr: The Apostle confirms this last argument with eight reasons, of which the first seven are taken from as many testimonies of Scripture.

units.la: Ratio prima, ex Psal. 2. 7. De Christo dicit Deus Pater: Filius meus es, ego hodie genui te. Ex quo loco probatur Christi Deitas, eo quod alio, & altiori modo sit Filius, quam Angelorum quisquam, Filius nempe per aeternam generationem: id quod confirmatur ex Act. 13. 33. & Rom. 1. 4. Ubi hic locus applicatur ad manifestationem Deitatis Christi, quam habebat ab aeterno, ante manifestationem factam per resurrectionem a mortuis. Nam nisi Christus in se fuisset Filius, non potuisset declarari mundo Filius. Et licet in Scriptura aliquid dicatur tum fieri cum patefit, Et sic Hodie genui te, erit Mundo hodie Unigenitum meum declaravi te; debet tamen (hodie) non tantum notare tempus declarationis Christi ὡς υἱοῦ ut filii, sed etiam aeternam & constanter immutabilem ejus generationem significare. Nam aeternitas optimè denotatur adverbio, hodie, quo praesens dies significatur; quia aeternitas quasi unus dies est, idemque totus semper praesens, in quo non est successivum quidquam, seu aliud post aliud, sicut in nostro tempore, sed una constans immutabilis permanentia. Et hic etiam utitur verbo praeteriti temporis, ut licet praesentem audias, persectam tamen intelligas generationem, sicut splendor Solis perfectus est, & tamen continuo emanat ex sole: Ergo Christus Angelis tanto est excellentior, quanto est Filius nuntio praestantior.
units.tr: First reason, from Psalm 2:7. Of Christ God the Father says: You are my Son, today I have begotten you. From this passage it is proved that Christ is God, because he is Son in another and higher way than any of the angels, namely the Son by eternal generation. This is confirmed from Acts 13:33 and Romans 1:4, where this passage is applied to the manifestation of the deity of Christ, which he had from eternity, before the manifestation made by the resurrection from the dead. For unless Christ had been Son in himself, he could not have been declared to the world as Son. And although in Scripture something is said to happen when it is made manifest, and so Today I have begotten you will mean Today I have declared my Only-begotten to the world, yet the word today ought not only to denote the time of Christ's declaration as Son [ὡς υἱοῦ], but also to signify his eternal and constantly unchangeable generation. For eternity is very well denoted by the adverb today, by which the present day is signified, because eternity is as one day, and that day is always wholly present, in which there is nothing successive, nor one thing after another, as in our time, but one constant and unchanging permanence. Here also the verb of the past tense is used, so that although you hear the present, you may understand a perfect generation, just as the brightness of the sun is perfect and yet constantly flows from the sun. Therefore Christ is as much more excellent than the angels as the Son is more excellent than a messenger.

units.la: Ego ero ] Ratio 2. Ex 2 Sam. 7. 19. Ubi in typo Salomonis promittit Deus missionem Messiae, quem Filium suum palam aspiraturus, & mundo declaraturus esset.
units.tr: I will be to him] Reason 2: From 2 Samuel 7:19. There, in the type of Solomon, God promises the sending of the Messiah, whom he was to make manifest as his Son and declare to the world.

units.la: Verf. 6. Rursum autem quum inducit primogenitum in orbem terrarum, dicit, Et adorent eum omnes Angeli Dei
units.tr: Verse 6. And again, when he brings the firstborn into the world, he says, "And let all the angels of God worship him."

units.la: Ratio 3. Ex Pfal. 97. 7. Cum Deus quasi jam introducturus esset Filium in mundum per incarnationem (ut Primogenitum suum, seu Hæredem omnium, propter ipsius nativum jus in omnia) communicat cum eo, sicut essentiam, sic gloriam suam soli Deo propriam, imperando, ut etiam Angeli omnes eum adorent. Ergo Christus Angelis excellentior.
units.tr: Reason 3: From Psalm 97:7. When God was, as it were, about now to bring his Son into the world through the incarnation, as his firstborn, or heir of all things, by his native right over all things, he shares with him his glory, which is proper to God alone, just as he shares his essence, by commanding that all the angels worship him. Therefore Christ is more excellent than the angels.

units.la: Verf. 7. Et de angelis quidem dicit, Qui Angelos suos facit Spiritus, & ministros suos, ignis flammam.
units.tr: Verse 7. And of the angels he says, "He who makes his angels spirits, and his ministers a flame of fire."

units.la: Ratio 4. ex Pfal. 104. 5. Angelos seclusit Deus à Divinæ gloriæ, seu adorationis & cultus communione, & constituit eos Ministros suos, qui ipsi (sicut venti vel flammæ) ad nutum serviant. Ergo Christus Angelis excellentior est.
units.tr: Reason 4: From Psalm 104:5. God set the angels apart from the communion of the divine glory, that is, from adoration and worship, and appointed them as his ministers, who serve at his nod, like the winds or flames. Therefore Christ is more excellent than the angels.

units.la: Verf. 8. Ad Filium autem, Thronus tuus, Deus, in seculum seculi: virga recta, virga regni tui.
units.tr: Verse 8. But to the Son, "Your throne, O God, is for ever and ever; the sceptre of your kingdom is a sceptre of righteousness."

units.la: Verf. 9. Dilexisti justitiam, & odisti iniquitatem, propterea unxit te Deus, Deus tuus, oleo exultationis, ultra consortes tuos.
units.tr: Verse 9: "You have loved righteousness and hated iniquity; therefore God, your God, has anointed you with the oil of gladness above your fellows."

units.la: Ratio 5. Ex Pfal. 45. 7, 8. Deus per os Prophetæ testatur de Filio: 1. Quod sit Deus: 2. Quod thronum seu regnum habeat in Electos, æternum: 3. Quod omnipotenti gratiâ Spiritus sit, in justitia per-ficiat subditos; per fidem justificatos in via rectitudinis dirigens ad vi‐tam æternam: 4. Quod Filius Deus Christus sicut est Deus, sic etiam homo futurus fuerit, cum hæc prædicebantur: 5. Quod fœderis Gratiæ cum Patre initi, altera pars fœderata fuerit, qua homo & princeps fœderatorum, Patrem suum, Deum suum habiturus: 6. Quod oleo Spi‐ritus Sancti (per quem omnis lætitia & felicitas communicatur ejus sub‐ditis) absque mensura perfundendus fuerit, ut de ejus plenitudine omnes confortes, fœderati & electi Dei, quantum satis elt, sortiantur: Ergo Christus Angelis est excellentior.
units.tr: Reason 5, from Ps. 45:7-8. God testifies through the prophet concerning the Son: (1) that he is God; (2) that he has a throne or kingdom over the elect, which is eternal; (3) that by the omnipotent grace of the Spirit he perfects his subjects in righteousness, directing those justified by faith in the way of uprightness to eternal life; (4) that the Son of God, Christ, was to be man as well as God, as these things were foretold; (5) that one party to the covenant of grace entered with the Father was the covenanted man and prince of the covenanted, who would have the Father as his God; (6) that he was to be anointed without measure with the oil of the Holy Spirit, through whom all joy and happiness are communicated to his subjects, so that all his fellows, the covenanted and elect of God, may receive as much as is enough from his fullness. Therefore Christ is more excellent than the angels.

units.la: Verf. 10. Et, Tu in initia Domine, terram fundasti; & opera manuum tuarum sunt cœli:
units.tr: Verse 10: "And, You, Lord, in the beginning laid the foundation of the earth, and the heavens are the work of your hands."

units.la: Verf. 11. Ipsi peribunt, tu autem permanes, & omnes ut vestimentum veterascent; Verf. 12. Ac velut amictum circumvolves eos, & mutabuntur: tu autem idem es, & anni tui non deficient.
units.tr: Verses 11-12: "They will perish, but you remain; and they will all grow old like a garment; and like a cloak you will fold them up, and they will be changed; but you are the same, and your years will not fail."

units.la: Ratio 6. ex Pfal. 102. 25. 26. Filius est Jehova, essentiâ Deus, unus cum Patre & Spiritu Sancto: 2. Et Creator omnium creaturarum in Coelo & Terra: 3. Et in se immutabilis in aeternum, semper sibi constans: Ergo Angelis excellentior est.
units.tr: Reason 6, from Ps. 102:25-26. (1) The Son is Jehovah, God in essence, one with the Father and the Holy Spirit; (2) and he is the Creator of all creatures in heaven and earth; (3) and in himself he is unchangeable for ever, always constant to himself. Therefore he is more excellent than the angels.

units.la: Verf. 13. Ad quem autem Angelorum dixit unquam, Sede ad dextram meam, usquedum posuero inimicos tuos scabellum pedum tuorum?
units.tr: Verse 13: "But to which of the angels has he ever said, Sit at my right hand, until I make your enemies a footstool for your feet?"

units.la: Ratio 7. ex Pfal. 110. Nulli unquam Angelorum communicavit Pater eam quam Christo, Messiae, Filio suo, Mediatori, & Ecclesiae Capiti, concessit aequalitatem Honoris & Potentiae, & Victoriam in omnes communes hostes Patris & Filii: Ergo Christus excellentior est Angelis.
units.tr: Reason 7, from Ps. 110. The Father has never granted to any of the angels the equality of honour and power that he granted to Christ, the Messiah, his Son, the Mediator and Head of the Church, together with victory over all the common enemies of the Father and the Son. Therefore Christ is more excellent than the angels.

units.la: Verf. 14. Nonne omnes sunt ministratores Spiritus, qui ministerii causa mittuntur propter eos qui haeredes erunt salutis?
units.tr: Verse 14: "Are they not all ministering spirits, sent to serve for the sake of those who are to inherit salvation?"

units.la: Ratio 8. Omnes Angeli sunt spiritus ministratores, qui non tantum servire tenentur Christo, sed etiam omnibus Electis, seu Fidelibus, qui haeredes vitae aeternae designantur a Deo: Ergo Christus tanto illis excellentior, quanto nomen Filii Dei excellentius est nomine ministrantium Spirituum.
units.tr: Reason 8. All the angels are ministering spirits, who are bound not only to serve Christ but also all the elect, or faithful, who are appointed by God as heirs of eternal life. Therefore Christ is as much more excellent than them as the name of the Son of God is more excellent than the name of ministering spirits.

units.la: Caput Secundum.
units.tr: Chapter 2.

units.la: Superioris doctrinae (de Prophetia, & persona Christi excellentia) sequitur usus duplex. Primus, ne deficiant a veritate doctrinae ipsius, ad verf. 6. Alter, ne quid detrahant existimationi CHRISTI, propter ipsius passiones in carne, ad finem.
units.tr: From the preceding doctrine (on the prophecy and the excellence of Christ's person) there follow two uses. The first is that they not fall away from the truth of this doctrine, at verse 6. The other is that they not detract from the esteem of CHRIST on account of his sufferings in the flesh, to the end.

units.la: Verf. 1. Propterea oportet nos eo magis attendere iis quae audivimus, ne quando perfluamus.
units.tr: Verse 1. Therefore we ought to give all the more heed to what we have heard, lest at any time we drift away.

units.la: Primi usus propositio haec est, Oportet nos attentius auscultare (id est credere & obedire) doctrinae Christi, seu ejus Evangelio. Argumenta ad probandam hanc propositionem sunt sex: Argumentum primum in verbo Propterea continetur, Quia scilicet jam demonstrata est, Capite superiori, Prophetiæ Christi excellentia. Idcirco attentius oportet auscultare ejus doctrinæ.
units.tr: The proposition of the first use is this: we ought to listen more attentively (that is, to believe and obey) to the doctrine of Christ, or to his Gospel. There are six arguments for proving this proposition. The first argument is contained in the word Therefore, namely because the excellence of Christ's prophecy has already been demonstrated in the preceding chapter. Hence we ought to listen more attentively to his doctrine.

units.la: Arg. 2. Nisi sedulò attendamus ejus doctrinæ, periculum est ne aliquando perfluamus, ne elabatur nobis ejus veritas & ne nos deficientes ab eo, pereamus: Ergo attentius auscultare nos oportet ejus doctrinæ.
units.tr: Arg. 2. Unless we attend diligently to his doctrine, there is danger that we may at some time drift away, that its truth slip from us and that, falling away from it, we perish. Therefore we ought to listen more attentively to his doctrine.

units.la: Verl. 2 Etenim si per Angelos dictus sermo fuit firmus, omnisque transgressio & contumacia justam mercedem retributionem retulit:
units.tr: Verse 2. For if the word spoken by angels was steadfast, and every transgression and disobedience received a just recompense of reward;

units.la: Hoc confirmat à comparatione Legis & Euangelii, in qua varia alia Argumenta continentur.
units.tr: He confirms this from a comparison of Law and Gospel, in which various other arguments are contained.

units.la: Arg. 3. Si sermo legis pronunciatus per ministerium Angelorum, seu nunciorum, quorum ministerio Deus usus est, firmus, ratus, authenticus, divinus, & inviolabilis habitus est, multò magis sermo Euangelii per Filium Christum prolatus, talis haberi debet: Ergo auscultandum est doctrinæ Christi Filio Dei.
units.tr: Arg. 3. If the word of the law, proclaimed through the ministry of angels, or messengers, by whom God acted, has been held firm, valid, authentic, divine and inviolable, much more must the word of the Gospel, spoken through the Son Christ, be held to be so. Therefore we must listen to the doctrine of Christ the Son of God.

units.la: Arg. 4. Si omnis transgressio & contumacia adversus legem (quæ doctrina est mortis meritæ) justam mercedem, seu retributionem capitalis supplicii retulit; Non poterimus nos effugere perditionem, si Euangelium salutis gratuitæ neglexerimus. Ergo auscultandum attentius Christi Euangelio.
units.tr: Arg. 4. If every transgression and disobedience against the law (which is a doctrine of deserved death) received a just recompense, that is, the reward of capital punishment, we shall not be able to escape destruction if we neglect the Gospel of free salvation. Therefore we must listen more attentively to the Gospel of Christ.

units.la: Verl. 2 Quomodo nos effugiemus, si tantam neglexerimus salutem? quæ quum primùm enarrari cœperit per ipsum Dominum, ab iis qui ipsum audiverant, fuit nobis confirmata:
units.tr: Verse 3. How shall we escape, if we neglect so great a salvation? which, having at the first begun to be spoken by the Lord himself, was confirmed unto us by them that heard him;

units.la: Verl. 4. Testimonium illis præbente Deo & signis & prodigiis, variisque virtutibus, & Spiritus sancti distributionibus, pro sua voluntate.
units.tr: Verse 4. God also bearing them witness, both with signs and wonders, and with divers miracles and gifts of the Holy Spirit, according to his own will.

units.la: Arg. 5. confirmans superius, Verbum Euangelii immediatè publicatum est ab ipso Iesu Christo Domino, in terris agente, & cum autoritate prædicatum est Ecclesiæ per Apostolos, qui oculati & auriti erant Testes doctrinæ ejus: Et denique, omnis generis donis Spiritus, & variis miraculis prædicationem Apostolorum comitantibus, quasi divinitus addito sigilli Divini testimonio confirmatum est. Ergo nisi attentius auscultemus ejus doctrinæ, impunè ferre non poterimus tantæ salutis nobis ita confirmatæ, neglectum.
units.tr: Arg. 5, confirming what was said above: the word of the Gospel was published immediately by the Lord Jesus Christ himself while he was living on earth, and was preached with authority to the Church through the Apostles, who were eyewitnesses and earwitnesses of his doctrine. And finally, the preaching of the Apostles was accompanied by gifts of the Spirit of every kind and by various miracles, and was confirmed, as it were, by a divine seal added from heaven. Therefore, unless we listen more attentively to his doctrine, we cannot escape punishment for neglecting so great a salvation thus confirmed to us.

units.la: Verf. 5. Non enim Angelis subjecit mundum illum futurum, de quo loquimur.
units.tr: Verse 5. For he hath not put in subjection to the angels the world to come, whereof we speak.

units.la: Mundi nova conditio futura sub Messia, seu mundus restaurandus, in gratiam Messiae, de quo loquebamur, à versu sexto superioris Capitis, non subjicitur Angelis, sed Christo Dei Filio. Ergo si Angelis (qui servi sunt,) non attente auscultare nefas fuit, quanto magis capitale erit potentissimum mundi instaurati regem aspernari Ecclesia. Quasi novus mundus, per Evangelium colligenda, seu nova creaturae conditio sub Messia, vocatur Mundus, Quia tota gloria quae in ornatu universi jam apparet, gloriosius splendet quando in noltrum usum convertitur per Christum. Dicitur futurus mundus, propter renovationis perfectionem, non nisi in futuro seculo perfecte futuram: Incepit jam quidem Christus nova omnia facere in suis, & propter suos, sed quod incepit, non nisi in die novissimo completum dabit, quando creatura asseretur à servitute corruptionis in libertatem gloriae filiorum Dei.
units.tr: The new condition of the world to come under the Messiah, or the world to be restored for the sake of the Messiah of whom we have been speaking since verse 6 of the preceding chapter, is not subjected to angels but to Christ the Son of God. Therefore, if it was wrong not to listen attentively to the angels (who are servants), how much more grave will it be for the Church to spurn the most powerful King of the restored world. The new world to be gathered through the Gospel, or the new condition of creation under the Messiah, is called world because all the glory which already appears in the adornment of the universe shines more gloriously when it is turned to our use through Christ. It is called the future world on account of the perfection of its renewal, which will be perfectly realized only in the future age. Christ has indeed already begun to make all things new in his own people and for his own people, but what he has begun he will bring to completion only on the last day, when creation will be set free from the bondage of corruption into the liberty of the glory of the children of God.

units.la: Secunda pars. Verf. 6. Testatus est autem quidem alicubi: dicens, Quid est homo, ut memor sis ejus? aut filius hominis, ut eum respicias?
units.tr: Second part. Verse 6. But one in a certain place testified, saying, What is man, that thou art mindful of him? or the son of man, that thou visitest him?

units.la: Hoc argumentum confirmans ad secundam partem Capitis dilabitur, ut probet nihil decedere de Christi excellentiâ vel æstimatione, per incarnationem, vel passiones ejus in carne: quod erat scandalum Hebraeorum. Argumenta in hunc finem sunt quatuordecim, ex quibus infert conclusionem probandam, versu primo sequentis Capitis, per admonitionem ad considerandum, quis nam sit Christus, id est, quam excellens sit in officiis Apostolatus, seu Prophetiae & Sacerdotii sui, in quibus humiliatus & passus est.
units.tr: Confirming this argument, he passes to the second part of the chapter, in order to prove that nothing is taken from Christ's excellence or esteem through his incarnation or his sufferings in the flesh, which was a stumbling block to the Hebrews. To this end there are fourteen arguments, from which he draws the conclusion to be proved in the first verse of the following chapter, by way of an exhortation to consider who Christ is, that is, how excellent he is in the offices of his Apostleship, namely his Prophecy and Priesthood, in which he was humbled and suffered.

units.la: Argumentum primum, ex Psal. 8. vers. 5. In hunc sensum; Apud Deum in pretio & honore admirabili habetur homo Christus, & alii homines ejus subditi propter Eum, si Dei Majestas, & operum ejus magnificentia, cum humanae naturae vilitate comparentur, vel si quantus Deus sit,& quam eximia ejus alia opera, & quantulus homo sit, consideretur: Ergo non debet Christi qua homo est, æstimatio apud nos deminui propter humanae naturae quam assumpsit, infirmitates & passiones.
units.tr: Argument 1, from Psalm 8:5. In this sense: before God, Christ as man is held in price and admirable honor, and other men are subject to him on his account. This holds if the majesty of God and the magnificence of his works are compared with the baseness of human nature, or if one considers how great God is, how excellent his other works are, and how small man is. Therefore the esteem of Christ, as he is man, ought not to be diminished among us on account of the infirmities and sufferings of the human nature he assumed.

units.la: Verf. 7. Fecisti eum paulisper inferiorem Angelis: gloria & honore coronasti eum, & constituisti eum super opera manuum tuarum.
units.tr: Verse 7. Thou madest him a little lower than the angels; thou crownedst him with glory and honour, and didst set him over the works of thy hands:

units.la: Arg. 2. ex Psal. 8. verf. 6. Etiamsi Christus tempore humiliationis, inferior factus fuerit Angelis, respectu passionum in carne; Non tamen fuit illa humiliatio perpetua, sed ad breve tempus, & ex parte tantum, humanae naturae patientis respectu; Quia pretio redemptionis persoluto, resuscitatus est a mortuis, evectus ad Dei dextram, & gloria & honore coronatus, Dominus & Rex declaratus super opera Dei omnia: Ergo nihil detrahi debet de ejus aestimatione, propter passiones in carne.
units.tr: Arg. 2, from Psalm 8:6. Even if Christ, in the time of his humiliation, was made lower than the angels with respect to his sufferings in the flesh, that humiliation was not perpetual but for a short time, and only in part, with respect to the suffering human nature. For when the price of redemption had been paid, he was raised from the dead, exalted to God's right hand, crowned with glory and honor, and declared Lord and King over all the works of God. Therefore nothing should be taken from his esteem on account of his sufferings in the flesh.

units.la: Verf. 8. Omnia subjecisti sub pedibus ejus. Enimvero per hoc quod ei subjecit omnia, nihil omisit quod non sit ei subjectum; at nunc nondum videmus ei omnia esse subjecta.
units.tr: Verse 8. Thou hast put all things in subjection under his feet. For in that he put all in subjection under him, he left nothing that is not put under him. But now we see not yet all things put under him.

units.la: Verf. 9. Sed Iesum illum cernimus gloria & honore coronatum, qui paulisper fuit inferior Angelis factus, propter mortis perpessionem, ut beneficio Dei pro omnibus mortem gustaret:
units.tr: Verse 9. But we see Jesus, who was made a little lower than the angels for the suffering of death, crowned with glory and honour; that by the grace of God he should taste death for every man.

units.la: Arg. 3. Ex Psal. 8. verf. 7. Angelorum Dominus est Christus, etiam qua homo; Deus enim subjecit ei omnia opera manuum suarum, sine exceptione, & sic inter alia Angelos. Ergo nihil detrahendum Christi aestimationi, propter humanae naturae assumptae infirmitates.
units.tr: Arg. 3, from Psalm 8:7. Christ is Lord of the angels, even as man; for God put all the works of his hands under him, without exception, and so among them the angels. Therefore nothing is to be taken from Christ's esteem on account of the infirmities of the human nature he assumed.

units.la: At nunc Arg. 4. Per solutionem objectionis propositum, Etiamsi nondum cernamus omnia subjici Christo, respectu membrorum suorum, quibus quotidie se opponunt hostes quam plurimi; Videmus tamen non oculis Fidei tantum, sed etiam rationis lumine per indicia multa, & miraculorum multitudinem convicti, Christum post humiliationem infra conditionem Angelorum, jam gloria & honore coronatum, in sua persona in Coelo, & sedentem ad dextram Patris, donec omnes hostes ponantur in scabellum pedum ipsius, atque ita videmus victoriam Christi inchoatam. Ergo nihil detrahendum aestimationi Christi propter ejus passiones, sive in persona propria, sive in membris ipsius.
units.tr: But now Arg. 4. By resolving the objection proposed: even though we do not yet see all things subjected to Christ, with respect to his members, against whom very many enemies daily set themselves, nevertheless we see, convinced not only by the eyes of faith but also by the light of reason, through many indications and the multitude of miracles, that Christ, after his humiliation below the condition of the angels, is now crowned with glory and honor in his own person in heaven, and sitting at the right hand of the Father, until all enemies are placed as a footstool under his feet; and thus we see the victory of Christ begun. Therefore nothing is to be taken from the esteem of Christ on account of his sufferings, whether in his own person or in his members.

units.la: Paulisper Arg. 5. Ex praedictione humiliationis, Psal. 8. v. 6. Ex decreto Dei, & ad complementum Prophetiarum de Christo, oportuit eum humiliari, & mortem pati, & in hunc finem, inferiorem aliqua ex parte Angelis reddi, ut mortem gustaret. Ergo non detrahendum ejus aestimationi propter ipsius passiones. Gustaret ] Arg. 6. Non temere nec necessitate coactus, passus est Christus sed ex gratia, seu gratuita voluntate Dei erga nos, mortem ad breve tempus degustavit, non pro se, sed pro omnibus nobis filiis adducendis ad salutem scilicet, ut versu sequenti exponitur. Ergo non minuenda ejus existimatio, propter carnis assumptæ passiones.
units.tr: Paulisper Arg. 5. From the prediction of the humiliation, Psalm 8:6. By the decree of God, and to complete the prophecies concerning Christ, it was necessary that he be humbled and suffer death, and to this end be made in some respect lower than the angels, so that he might taste death. Therefore his esteem is not to be diminished on account of his sufferings. Tasted] Arg. 6. Christ suffered not rashly, nor compelled by necessity, but from grace, that is, from God's gratuitous will toward us. He tasted death for a short time, not for himself but for all of us, to bring many sons to salvation, as is explained in the following verse. Therefore his esteem must not be lessened on account of the sufferings of the flesh he assumed.

units.la: Vers. 10, Decebat enim ut ipse propter quem sunt hæc omnia, & per quem sunt hæc omnia, multos filios in gloriam adducendo, principem salutis ipsorum per afflictiones consecraret.
units.tr: Verse 10. For it was fitting that he, for whom and by whom are all things, in bringing many sons to glory, should make perfect through afflictions the prince of their salvation.

units.la: Arg. 7. Conveniebat gloriæ Dei, qui Autor & Finis est rerum omnium, cum per Christi passiones maxime manifestari potuerint, ejus justitia, misericordia, sapientia, potentia, reliquaque attributa, ut Christum Principem salutis nostræ, per afflictiones consecraret, inauguraret, consummaret, & omni ratione idoneum redderet, quo decentius multos filios ad vitam electos in gloriam per afflictiones adduceret, non doctrina sua tantum, nec exemplo vitæ tantum, sed etiam merito ignominiosæ suæ mortis pro ipsis redimendis, obeundæ. Ergo non minuenda ejus existimatio, propter carnis assumptæ passiones.
units.tr: Argument 7. It befitted the glory of God, who is the author and end of all things, that his justice, mercy, wisdom, power and other attributes, which could be most clearly shown through the sufferings of Christ, should consecrate, inaugurate and perfect Christ as the Prince of our salvation through afflictions, and render him in every way fit to lead many sons chosen to life into glory more fittingly through afflictions. He was to do this not only by his teaching or the example of his life, but also by the merit of his ignominious death, which he underwent to redeem them. Therefore the estimation of him is not to be diminished on account of the sufferings of the flesh he assumed.

units.la: Vers. 11. Nam & qui sanctificat, & qui sanctificantur, ex uno sunt omnes: quam ob causam non erubescit fratres ipsos vocare,
units.tr: Verse 11. For both he who sanctifies and those who are sanctified are all of one; for which cause he is not ashamed to call them brethren,

units.la: Arg. 8. Redemptor & Redempti, Sanctificator & sanctificati, non tantum ex Dei decreto, & Scripturæ prædictionibus, sed etiam ex ipsa justitia, unius ejusdemque sunt naturæ, ejusdem naturalis massæ, ab eodem Adamo derivati: Justitia enim & Sapientia Dei requirebat, ut in natura humana quæ peccaverat, plecteretur peccatum: Et idcirco exigebat ut Redemptor hominum verè Homo esset. Ergo propter humanæ naturæ infirmitates assumptas, Christi Filii Dei existimatio non est minuenda
units.tr: Argument 8. The Redeemer and the redeemed, the Sanctifier and the sanctified, are of one and the same nature, of one and the same natural mass, derived from the same Adam, not only by the decree of God and the predictions of Scripture, but also by justice itself. For the justice and wisdom of God required that sin be punished in human nature, which had sinned; and therefore it required that the Redeemer of men be truly man. Therefore, on account of the infirmities of human nature which he assumed, the estimation of Christ the Son of God is not to be diminished.

units.la: Quam ob ] Arg. 9. Confirmans superius, Messias voluit incarnari, ut posset nos fratres habere, & nobis se fratrem exhibere; & licet sit Dei Filius, non erubescit tamen Redemptos seu Electos vocare Fratres suos. Ergo non minuenda est ejus existimatio, propter passiones ipsius in carne humana, sed gloriari nos decet potius in ejus consanguinitate, & ipsum, passionum pro nobis nomine, tanto magis glorificare.
units.tr: For which cause] Argument 9. Confirming what was said above: the Messiah willed to be incarnate so that he might have us as brethren and show himself to us as a brother. And although he is the Son of God, he is not ashamed to call the redeemed or elect his brethren. Therefore his estimation is not to be diminished on account of his sufferings in human flesh; rather we ought to glory in his kinship with us, and so much the more to glorify him for the sake of the sufferings he endured for us.

units.la: Vers. 12. Dicens, Annuntiabo nomen tuum fratribus meis, in medio Ecclesiæ tibi hymnos canam.
units.tr: Verse 12. Saying, I will declare thy name unto my brethren; in the midst of the church will I sing praise unto thee.

units.la: Hoc argumentum probat tribus Scripturæ testimoniis. Primum petitur ex Psal. 22. verf. 22. In quo Christus & suscipit in se λυτρ* persolutionem, & pollicetur se justitiam partam per suam obedientiam, prædicaturum fratribus suis Electis, seu Ecclesiæ Fidelium, in quorum coetibus, etiam post ascensionem, Spiritu suo præsens est, fidem, gaudium, & gratiarum actionem in cordibus Fidelium per prædicationem Justitiæ, excitans.
units.tr: This argument is proved by three testimonies of Scripture. The first is taken from Psalm 22:22, where Christ takes upon himself the payment of a ransom [λύτρων] and promises that he will proclaim to his brethren, the elect, that is, the faithful of the Church, the righteousness obtained by his obedience. Even after his ascension he is present with them by his Spirit in their assemblies, stirring up in the hearts of believers faith, joy and thanksgiving through the preaching of righteousness.

units.la: Verf. 13. Et rursum, Ego fretus ero ipso, Et iterum, Ecce ego & pueri quos mihi dedit Deus.
units.tr: Verse 13. And again, I will put my trust in him. And again, Behold I, and the children whom God hath given me.

units.la: Testimonium 2. ex Psal. 18. 3. Unde Christus probatur homo esse, quia in numero fœderatorum, à Deo per fidem pendentium, ponitur.
units.tr: The second testimony is from Psalm 18:3. By it Christ is shown to be man, because he is placed among the number of those who are covenanted to God and depend on him by faith.

units.la: Et iterum ] Testimonium 3. ex Isa. 8. 18. Ubi Christus inducitur à Propheta, associans se pueris, ut fratribus suis; quos Deus elegerat, & ei redimendos, seu salvandos dederat, quos unà secum sistit Patri, in servos tandem glorificandos.
units.tr: And again] The third testimony is from Isaiah 8:18. There the prophet introduces Christ as associating himself with the children as his brethren, whom God had chosen and given to him to be redeemed or saved; he presents them together with himself to the Father, to be finally glorified as his servants.

units.la: Verf. 14. Quoniam igitur pueri participes sunt carnis & sanguinis, ipse quoque consimiliter particeps factus est eorundem, ut per mortem aboleret eum qui mortis imperium habet, hoc est, Diabolum:
units.tr: Verse 14. Forasmuch then as the children are partakers of flesh and blood, he also himself likewise took part of the same; that through death he might destroy him that had the power of death, that is, the devil;

units.la: Arg. 10. Christus ex dilectione Electorum Dei Filiorum, ejusdem humanæ naturæ cum ipsis particeps esse voluit, ut posset pro iis moriendo satisfacere, & ita Diaboli potentiam in eos abolere, quam ille, ut lictor vel carnifex habet per legem, in omnes peccatores: Ergo non est minuenda existimatio Christi propter assumptæ car-nis passiones.
units.tr: Argument 10. Christ, from love for the elect children of God, willed to share in the same human nature with them, so that by dying for them he might make satisfaction and thus abolish in them the power of the devil, which the devil holds over all sinners as an executioner or hangman holds power by law. Therefore the estimation of Christ is not to be diminished on account of the sufferings of the flesh he assumed.

units.la: Verf. 15. Et liberos redderet quotquot metu mortis, per omnem vitam obnoxii erant servituti.
units.tr: Verse 15. And deliver them who through fear of death were all their lifetime subject to bondage.

units.la: Arg. 11. Inter mortis Christi fructus & fines hic est, ut Christus liberaret suos à metu mortis, & temporariæ & æternæ: cui metui obnoxii tota vitâ suâ tenentur omnes peccatores, donec apertis oculis per fidem in Christum, videant se manumissos à peccato & morte, propter morientis pro ipsis Christi meritum: Ergo non est minuenda existimatio Christi propter assumptæ carnis passiones.
units.tr: Argument 11. Among the fruits and ends of Christ's death is this: that Christ should free his people from the fear of death, both temporal and eternal. All sinners are held subject to this fear throughout their whole lives, until, with eyes opened by faith in Christ, they see themselves set free from sin and death through the merit of Christ who died for them. Therefore the estimation of Christ is not to be diminished on account of the sufferings of the flesh he assumed.

units.la: Verf. 16. Non enim utique Angelos assumpsit, sed semen Abrahæ assumpsit.
units.tr: Verse 16. For verily he took not on him the nature of angels; but he took on him the seed of Abraham.

units.la: Arg. 12. CHRISTUS assumendo semen Abrahæ, seu humanam naturam in unitatem Personæ suæ, in qua ab æterno subsistebat, naturam humanam respectu Privilegiorum, dignitatis, & honoris, evexit supra naturam Angelicam, quam non assumpsit. Ergo propter assumptæ carnis passiones non est deminuenda CHRISTI existimatio.
units.tr: Argument 12. Christ, by assuming the seed of Abraham, that is, human nature, into the unity of his person, in which he subsisted from eternity, raised human nature, in respect of privileges, dignity and honour, above the angelic nature, which he did not assume. Therefore on account of the sufferings of the flesh he assumed, the estimation of Christ is not to be lessened.

units.la: Vers. 17. Unde debuit per omnia fratribus similis fieri, ut misericors esset & fidelis pontifex, in iis quæ apud Deum agenda sunt, ad expiandum peccata populi.
units.tr: Verse 17. Wherefore in all things it behoved him to be made like unto his brethren, that he might be a merciful and faithful high priest in things pertaining to God, to make reconciliation for the sins of the people.

units.la: Arg. 13. Debuit CHRISTUS electis fratribus similis fieri natura, proprietatibus, affectibus, & infirmitatibus omnibus, excepto peccato, ut possent ejus fratres de fidelitate & misericordia ipsius, in sacerdotii exercitio, & perpetua intercessione apud DEUM pro ipsis, certiores & confidentiores esse. Ergo propter assumptæ carnis passiones nihil deminui debet de excellentiæ CHRISTI existimatione.
units.tr: Argument 13. Christ ought to have been made like his elect brethren in nature, properties, affections and all infirmities, except sin, so that his brethren might be more certain and more confident of his faithfulness and mercy in the exercise of his priesthood and his perpetual intercession with God for them. Therefore nothing of the excellence of Christ ought to be diminished on account of the sufferings of the flesh he assumed.

units.la: Vers. 18. Nam ex eo quod perpessus fuit, quum tentatus est, potest & iis qui tentantur succurrere.
units.tr: Verse 18. For in that he himself hath suffered being tempted, he is able also to succour them that are tempted.

units.la: Arg. 14. confirmans superius, CHRISTUS ex eo quod perpessus sit afflictiones, & tentationes in natura humana, idoneus per malorum experientiam factus est, cui confidamus, quod nobis similia patientibus succurrere & possit & velit. Ergo non minuenda est ejus existimatio propter assumptæ carnis passiones: Atque ita sicut superiori Capite demonstravit CHRISTUM esse vere DEI Filium, sic hoc Capite demonstravit vere esse Filium hominis; Unum, verum ΘεάνθρωποΣ; Simulque infirmitatum & passionum CHRISTI in carne scandalum, ad quod impingebant Hebraei omnes infideles, è medio sustulit.
units.tr: Argument 14, confirming what was said above: Christ, because he suffered afflictions and temptations in human nature, has been made fit, through his experience of evils, for us to trust that he both can and will succour us when we suffer similar things. Therefore his estimation is not to be diminished on account of the sufferings of the flesh he assumed. And so, as in the previous chapter he showed Christ to be truly the Son of God, so in this chapter he has shown him to be truly the Son of man; one true God-man. At the same time he has removed from the way the stumbling block of the infirmities and sufferings of Christ in the flesh, against which all unbelieving Hebrews stumbled.

units.la: Caput Tertium.
units.tr: Chapter 3.

units.la: Indicatâ Prophetiæ & personæ Christi excellentiâ, etiam sub omnibus assumptæ carnis passionibus, Capite superiori, digito quasi intento ad hujus Excellentiæ considerationem, hortatur, ut firmiter retineant professionem fidei Christianæ, nec ab ea deficiant, adductis in hunc finem Argumentis quindecim.
units.tr: Having shown the excellence of the Prophet and the person of Christ, even under all the sufferings of the assumed flesh, in the previous chapter, as if pointing a finger at the consideration of this excellence, he exhorts them to hold firmly to the profession of the Christian faith and not to fall away from it, adducing fifteen arguments to this end.

units.la: Vers. 1. Unde, fratres sancti, vocationis caelestis participes, consideráte Apostolum & Pontificem professionis nostrae Christum Iesum:
units.tr: Verse 1. Therefore, holy brethren, partakers of the heavenly calling, consider the Apostle and High Priest of our profession, Christ Jesus.

units.la: Propositio de firmiter retinenda professione fidei continetur in hortatione ad seriam considerationem Christi, Apostoli & Pontificis professionis nostrae. Arg. 1. Sanctificati estis & efficacis ad coelestia vocationis, coelitus participes per fidem facti estis. Ergo firmiter retinenda vobis est professio hujus fidei.
units.tr: The proposition, that the profession of faith must be held firmly, is contained in the exhortation to a serious consideration of Christ, the Apostle and High Priest of our profession. Argument 1. You have been sanctified and made partakers of the heavenly calling through faith. Therefore the profession of this faith must be held firmly by you.

units.la: Apostolum ] Arg 2. Habetis Iesum Christum Filium Dei Apostolum, seu Doctorem vestrae hujus fidei a Deo missum, & Pontificem nostrum, qui sanguine suo expiavit peccata nostra: Habetis (inquam) hunc Autorem hujus professionis. Ergo ea firmiter est retinenda.
units.tr: Apostle] Argument 2. You have Jesus Christ, the Son of God, the Apostle, that is, the Teacher of this your faith, sent from God, and our High Priest, who expiated our sins with his own blood. You have (I say) this Author of the profession. Therefore it must be held firmly.

units.la: Vers. 2 Fidelem ei qui ipsum constituit; ut & Moses fidelis fuit in tota domo ipsius.
units.tr: Verse 2. Faithful to him who appointed him, as also Moses was faithful in all his house.

units.la: Arg. 3. Christus in administratione Apostolatus & Pontificatus, seu Sacerdotii sibi commissi, non minus fidelis est quam Moses, qui testimonium obtinuit a Deo, quod fidelis fuerit in tota domo ejus. Ergo Christianae fidei professio firmiter vobis tenenda est. Quia Mosi ministro plus quam satis erat, tribuebant Hebraei, & a ceremoniis Mosaicis aegre divelli poterant, ut ad Christum transirent, Idcirco hic dedita opera comparat Christum cum Mose.
units.tr: Argument 3. Christ, in the administration of the Apostleship and High Priesthood, or priesthood committed to him, is no less faithful than Moses, who obtained testimony from God that he was faithful in all his house. Therefore the profession of the Christian faith must be held firmly by you. The Hebrews attributed more than enough to Moses the minister, and could hardly be torn away from the Mosaic ceremonies so as to pass over to Christ; for this reason the author deliberately compares Christ with Moses.

units.la: Vers. 3. Tanto namque ampliore gloria prae Mose hic dignus est habitus, quanto majorem habet honorem is qui construxit domum, quam domus ipsa.
units.tr: Verse 3. For he has been counted worthy of more glory than Moses, by as much as the one who built the house has more honour than the house itself.

units.la: Arg 4. Christus tanto excellentior est Mose, & totâ etiam Ecclesiâ, quanto conditor domus excellentior est ipsa domo, vel aliquâ ejus parte: Christus autem Ecclesiae totius, quae domus est Dei, conditor est. Moses vero membrum tantum est illius Ecclesiae, & pars illius domus tantum: Ergo professio fidei Christianae firmiter retinenda est.
units.tr: Argument 4. Christ is more excellent than Moses, and than the whole Church, by as much as the builder of a house is more excellent than the house itself, or any part of it. But Christ is the builder of the whole Church, which is the house of God. Moses, however, is only a member of that Church, and only a part of that house. Therefore the profession of the Christian faith must be held firmly.

units.la: Vers. 4. Omnis enim domus constituitur ab aliquo: porro qui condidit omnia hac, Deus est.
units.tr: Verse 4. For every house is built by someone; but he who built all things is God.

units.la: Arg. 5. confirmans superius sub eadem comparatione, Sicut nulla domus, neque pars domus conditur a se ipsa, sed ab alio, ita neque Ecclesia clesia, neque Moses, qui membrum est Ecclesiae, conditur à se, sed debet architecto superiori sui aedificationem. Christus verò qui Deus jam probatus est, Conditor est Ecclesiae, & singulorum ejus membrorum, & rerum insuper omnium. Ergo & excellentior est Mose, & doctrinae ipsius fides & professio firmiter retinenda est.
units.tr: Argument 5, confirming what was said above under the same comparison. As no house, nor part of a house, is built by itself but by another, so neither the Church nor Moses, who is a member of the Church, is built by himself, but owes his building to a higher architect. Christ, however, who has already been proved to be God, is the builder of the Church, and of each of its members, and indeed of all things. Therefore he is more excellent than Moses, and the faith and profession of his teaching must be held firmly.

units.la: Verf. 5. Et Moses quidem fidelis fuit in tota domo ipsius, ut ut famulus, ad testificanda quae post dicenda erant:
units.tr: Verse 5. And Moses indeed was faithful in all his house, as a servant, to testify those things which were to be spoken afterwards;

units.la: Verl. 6. At Christus, ut Filius domui suae praeest: cujus domus sumus nos, si fiduciam & spem illam de qua gloriamur, ad finem usque firmam tenuerimus.
units.tr: Verse 6. But Christ, as a Son, is over his own house; whose house we are, if we hold fast the confidence and the hope of which we glory, firm to the end.

units.la: Arg. 6. Moses fidelis fuit, ut servus in familia aliena ad testificandum, & id quidem obscurè, quod posteà plenius & apertius dicendum erat de Christo, ipsiusque dominio. At Christus est fidelis, ut Filius & Haeres, qui praeest domui suae, & loquitur ex autoritate sua. Ergo Christus Mose excellentior est, doctrinaeque ejus professio firmiter retinenda est.
units.tr: Argument 6. Moses was faithful as a servant in another's household, to testify, and that indeed obscurely, to what was afterwards to be said more fully and plainly about Christ and his dominion. But Christ is faithful as the Son and Heir, who is over his own house and speaks with his own authority. Therefore Christ is more excellent than Moses, and the profession of his teaching must be held firmly.

units.la: Cujus domus ] Arg. 7. Si firmiter retineamus fiduciam & spem vitae aeternae, per Christum nobis partae & communicandae, (in qua spe nunc gloriamur) declarabimus nos esse domum ejus, seu veram ejus Ecclesiam, in qua Dominus habitaturus est. Ergo professio fidei Christianae firmiter retinenda est.
units.tr: Whose house] Argument 7. If we firmly hold the confidence and hope of eternal life, obtained and to be shared through Christ (in which hope we now glory), we shall show ourselves to be his house, that is, his true Church, in which the Lord is to dwell. Therefore the profession of the Christian faith must be held firmly.

units.la: Verl. 7. Quapropter sicut dicit Spiritus ille Sanctus, Hodie si vocem ejus audieritis,
units.tr: Verse 7. Wherefore, as the Holy Spirit says, Today if you hear his voice,

units.la: Verl. 8. Ne obdurate corda vestra, sicut in exacerbatione in die tentationis illius in deserto:
units.tr: Verse 8. Do not harden your hearts, as in the provocation, in the day of temptation in the wilderness:

units.la: Verf. 9. Ubi tentaverunt me patres vestri, probaverunt me, & viderunt opera mea quadraginta annis.
units.tr: Verse 9. Where your fathers tempted me, proved me, and saw my works for forty years.

units.la: Arg. 8. ex Psal. 95. 8, 9, &c. Nisi firmiter retineatis fidem Christi, futuri estis inobedientes Spiritui Sancto, qui in Scriptura vetat obdurare corda, cum auditis Dei verbum, seu ne loquentem Deum rejiciatis, vel ne verbo ejus vos subjicere recusetis. Ergo firmiter retinenda est fidei Christianae professio.
units.tr: Argument 8, from Psalm 95:8, 9, etc. Unless you hold the faith of Christ firmly, you will be disobedient to the Holy Spirit, who in Scripture forbids us to harden our hearts when we hear the word of God, or to reject God speaking, or to refuse to submit ourselves to his word. Therefore the profession of the Christian faith must be held firmly.

units.la: Sicut in] Arg. 9 ex 17. Exodi, Cavendum vobis est pravum exemplum Patrum vestrorum, qui ex infidelitate in deserto tentarunt Deum, qui potentiam & bonitatem suam, operum suorum testimonio totos quadragin-
units.tr: As in] Argument 9, from Exodus 17. You must beware of the wicked example of your fathers, who in unbelief tempted God in the wilderness, who had shown his power and goodness, by the testimony of his works, for forty-

units.la: Cujus domus] Arg. 7. (marginal note, left) quadraginta annos, in ipsorum conspectu probatam dederat. Firmiter ergo vobis Christiana fides retinenda est.
units.tr: Whose house] Argument 7. (marginal note, left) years, in their sight. Therefore the Christian faith must be held firmly by you.

units.la: Vers. 10. Quapropter infensus fui nationi isti: & dixi, Semper errant corde: neque cognoverunt vias meas.
units.tr: Verse 10. Wherefore I was grieved with that generation, and said, They always err in heart; and they have not known my ways.

units.la: Arg. 10. ex verbis Psal. 95. nisi in fide firmi perstiteritis, Haeredes futuri estis irae Dei, in Gentem incredulam denunciatae, & condemnandi estis ejusdem pravitatis cum Patribus vestris, qui in cordibus suis affectarunt errorem, nec voluerunt Dei vias cognoscere. Ergo in fide vobis firmiter perseverandum est.
units.tr: Argument 10, from the words of Psalm 95. Unless you persevere firmly in the faith, you will be heirs of the wrath of God, which was threatened against the unbelieving nation, and you will be condemned to the same wickedness as your fathers, who in their hearts aimed at error and would not know God's ways. Therefore you must persevere constantly in the faith.

units.la: Vers. 11. Itaque juravi in ira mea, Si introibunt in requiem meam.
units.tr: Verse 11. So I swore in my wrath, They shall not enter into my rest.

units.la: Arg. 11. ex eodem Psalmo, Nisi firmi in fide permanseritis, periculum est ne juramento irati Dei excludamini a regno Coelorum, seu a requie Dei. Ergo in fide constanter vobis est permanendum.
units.tr: Argument 11, from the same Psalm. Unless you remain firm in the faith, there is danger that by the oath of an angry God you will be shut out from the kingdom of heaven, or from the rest of God. Therefore you must persevere constantly in the faith.

units.la: Vers. 12. Videte, fratres, ne quando sit in ullo vestrum cor malum & infidele, deficiendo a Deo vivo.
units.tr: Verse 12. Take heed, brethren, lest there be in any of you an evil and unbelieving heart, in departing from the living God.

units.la: Arg. 12. Ex applicatione citati exempli, per hortationem propositum, Nisi singuli caveatis vobis assiduo, a nativa cordis pravitate & incredulitate, defecturi estis procul dubio a Deo vivente. Ergo in fide vigilanter perseverandum est.
units.tr: Argument 12. From the application of the example cited, through the exhortation proposed: unless each of you takes constant care against the innate wickedness and unbelief of the heart, you will undoubtedly depart from the living God. Therefore you must persevere vigilantly in the faith.

units.la: Vers. 13. Sed exhortamini alii alios quotidie, quoad appellatur dies hodiernus: nequis ex vobis induretur fraude peccati.
units.tr: Verse 13. But exhort one another daily, while it is called today, lest any of you be hardened through the deceitfulness of sin.

units.la: Arg. 13. Singulis incumbit, non vobisipsis solum cavere ne deficiatis, sed etiam per mutuas hortationes, quamdiu occasio datur, curare, & operam dare, ne quis ex vestro numero per seductionem peccati obfirmet animum in quovis vitio, ne defectio in religionis negotio sequatur, ex corruptela morum: Ergo ut omnes & singuli in fide perstent, laborandum est.
units.tr: Argument 13. It falls to each of you not only to take care that you yourselves do not fall away, but also, by mutual exhortations, as long as opportunity is given, to see to it and take pains that none of your number hardens his mind in any vice through the seduction of sin, so that apostasy in the matter of religion does not follow from corruption of morals. Therefore, that all and each persevere in the faith, we must labour.

units.la: Vers. 14. Christi enim participes facti sumus, si modo principium illud quo sustentamur, firmum tenuerimus ad fidem usque:
units.tr: Verse 14. For we have become partakers of Christ, if only we hold fast the beginning of our confidence firm to the end:

units.la: Arg. 14. Nemo vere particeps est Iesu Christi in praesenti, qui non firmiter ad finem usque retinuerit principium illud per quod sustentamur, id est, fidem per quam subsistimus in vita nostra spirituali. Ergo in fide firmiter permanendum est.
units.tr: Argument 14. No one is truly a partaker of Jesus Christ in the present who does not hold firmly to the end that beginning by which we are sustained, that is, the faith through which we subsist in our spiritual life. Therefore we must remain firm in the faith.

units.la: Vers. 15. Interim dum dicitur, Hodie si vocem ejus audieritis, ne obdurate corda vestra, ut in exacerbationem.
units.tr: Verse 15. Meanwhile, while it is said, Today if you hear his voice, do not harden your hearts, as in the provocation.

units.la: Vers. 16. Nam quidam quum audissent, exacerbarunt Dominum, non omnes tamen ii qui exierant ex Ægypto per Mosen.
units.tr: Verse 16. For some, when they had heard, provoked him; yet not all who had come out of Egypt by Moses.

units.la: Vers. 17. Quibus autem infensus fuit quadraginta annis? nonne iis qui peccaverant, quorum corpora ceciderunt in deserto?
