units.tr: Verse 17. But with whom was he grieved for forty years? Was it not with those who had sinned, whose bodies fell in the wilderness?

units.la: Vers. 18. Quibus autem juravit non ingressuros in requiem suam, nisi iis qui non obedierant?
units.tr: Vers. 18. But to whom did he swear that they would not enter into his rest, except to those who did not obey?

units.la: Vers. 19. Et videmus non potuisse ingredi propter incredulitatem.
units.tr: Vers. 19. And we see that they could not enter because of unbelief.

units.la: Arg. 15. Ex consideratione circumstantiarum textus Psalmi citati, in hunc sensum, Ex verbis Psalmi citati, vers. 15. colligere licet non omnes, sed aliquos tantum Deum exacerbasse, (aliqui enim in fide promissionum perseveraverunt, vers. 16.) qui autem Deum exacerbarunt, soli erant illi qui ab exitu Egypti ad vitae suae finem permanserunt incredduli: quique ita Deum provocarunt, ut in ira Deus eos occiderit in deserto, vers. 17. & incredulitatis jam damnatos juramento exclusepit à requie sua, vers 18. Quos cum ex historia videamus non potuisse ingredi in Dei requiem propter incredulitatem, vers. 19. Sequitur necessario vos quotquot cum fidelibus (qui ab ira & exclusione à Dei requie excipiuntur) servari cupitis, & cum incredulis, à Dei requie seclusis, arceri non vultis, in fide Christi firmiter perstare oportere.
units.tr: Arg. 15. From a consideration of the circumstances of the text of the Psalm cited, the argument runs thus: from the words of the cited Psalm, verse 15, it may be gathered that not all, but only some, provoked God (for some persevered in faith in the promises, verse 16); and those who provoked God were only those who remained unbelieving from the going out of Egypt to the end of their lives; and who so provoked God that, in wrath, God struck them down in the wilderness, verse 17, and, having already condemned them for unbelief, by oath excluded them from his rest, verse 18. Since we see from the history that these could not enter into God's rest because of unbelief, verse 19, it follows necessarily that all of you who wish to be saved along with the faithful (who are spared from the wrath and from exclusion from God's rest), and who do not wish to be shut out along with the unbelievers, shut off from God's rest, must persevere firmly in faith in Christ.

units.la: Caput Quartum.
units.tr: Chapter 4.

units.la: Verf. I. Metuamus igitur nequando derelicta promissione introeundi in requiem ejus, videatur aliquis ex vobis fuisse frustratus.
units.tr: Verse 1. Let us fear, therefore, lest, while the promise of entering into his rest still stands, any of you should seem to have come short of it.

units.la: INsistens in loci ex Psal. 95. citati, expositione & applicatione, hortatur ut teneant, per fiduciam in Christum, ingredi in requiem Dei. Per requiem Dei, intelligit spiritualem illam & coelestem requiem, qua cessamus à peccato, & tranquillitatem habemus in conscientiâ, ex pace erga Deum, & tuti habitamus sub umbra Dei, cujus initium est in hac vita, & complementum in vita futura: in hanc requiem per fidem magis magisque ingredimur. gredimur, donec tandem consequamur plenum, refrigerium in adventu Domini. Argumenta hortationis sunt undecim.
units.tr: Insisting on the exposition and application of the passage cited from Psalm 95, he urges them to hold fast, through trust in Christ, to entering into God's rest. By God's rest he means that spiritual and heavenly rest in which we cease from sin and have tranquillity of conscience from peace with God, and dwell safely under the shadow of God. Its beginning is in this life and its completion in the life to come. We enter into this rest more and more through faith, and progress until at last we obtain full refreshment at the coming of the Lord. There are eleven arguments of exhortation.

units.la: Argumentum primum, In gremio comminationis, versu ultimo Psal. 95. relinquitur nobis fidelibus promissio introeundi in requiem Dei. Ergo festinandum vobis ut per fidem in requiem illam ingrediamini.
units.tr: The first argument: in the midst of the threatening, in the last verse of Psalm 95, the promise of entering into God's rest is left to us believers. Therefore you must hasten to enter that rest through faith.

units.la: Arg. 1. Nisi festinetis in cursu fidei, ingredi in promissam requiem, periculum est, ne nimium tardando excludi videamini, vel exclusi inveniamini: Segnis enim & otiosa fides merito suspecta est. Ergo cum timore qui acuat diligentiam, vobis festinandum est, ut ingrediamini in requiem.
units.tr: Argument 1. Unless you hasten in the course of faith to enter the promised rest, there is a danger that by delaying too long you may seem to be shut out, or be found shut out. For a slack and idle faith is rightly suspect. Therefore, with a fear that sharpens diligence, you must hasten to enter the rest.

units.la: Vers. 2. Etenim nobis evangelizatum est sicut & illis; at non profuit illis auditus sermo, ut qui fidei mixtus non fuerit ipsis qui audierant.
units.tr: Verse 2. For we have had the gospel preached to us just as they did; but the word preached did not profit them, because it was not mixed with faith in those who heard it.

units.la: Arg. 3. confirmans utrumque praecedens, Cum eadem illa Evangelica promissio, eadem conditione praedicetur tam nobis quam illis, & non profuerit sermo auditus illis, qui fide admistum non susceperunt, sed solum iis qui per fidem eum amplexi sunt; Sequetur neque nobis profuturam hanc promissionem introeundi in requiem, nisi fide amplectentes promissiones studeamus in requiem ingredi: & contra, sequetur promissionem nobis profuturam, si per fidem ingredi curae sit: Studendum ergo ut ingrediamini.
units.tr: Argument 3, confirming both of the preceding: since the same evangelical promise, on the same condition, is preached to us as to them, and the word heard did not profit those who did not receive it mixed with faith, but only those who embraced it through faith, it follows that this promise of entering the rest will profit us only if we strive to enter the rest by embracing the promises in faith. And conversely, it follows that the promise will profit us if we take care to enter through faith. Therefore you must strive to enter.

units.la: Vers. 3. Introimus enim in requiem nos qui credimus, sicut dixit, Itaque juravi in ira mea si ingressuri sint in requiem meam: licet operibus a jactis fundamentis mundi perfectis.
units.tr: Verse 3. For we who believe enter into rest, as he said: "So I swore in my wrath, They shall not enter into my rest," although the works were finished from the foundation of the world.

units.la: Vers. 4. Ita enim dixit quondam in loco de septimo die, Et quievit Deus die septimo ab omnibus operibus suis.
units.tr: Verse 4. For he said somewhere concerning the seventh day, "And God rested on the seventh day from all his works."

units.la: Vers. 5. Et hic rursum, Si introibunt in requiem meam.
units.tr: Verse 5. And here again, "They shall not enter into my rest."

units.la: Arg. 4. Nos qui credimus in Christum aditum in requiem habemus apertum nobis per fidem: Ergo festinemus per fidem progredi, donec plenam requiem consequamur.
units.tr: Argument 4. We who believe in Christ have an open entrance into rest through faith. Therefore let us hasten to advance through faith until we obtain full rest.

units.la: Arg. 5. confirmans superius, Dominus in ira jurans excludendos infideles a requie, a contrario jurat admittendos esse fideles in requiem ejus: Ergo juranti Deo fidem habentes, festinemus magis magisque ingredi in ejus requiem.
units.tr: Argument 5, confirming what was said above: since the Lord, swearing in his wrath, excludes unbelievers from rest, he conversely swears that believers are to be admitted into his rest. Therefore, trusting God who swears, let us hasten more and more to enter his rest.

units.la: Operibus ] Explicat hujus argumenti vim, ad verf. 10. Tribus modis: primo ostendendo requiem Dei in juramento expreßam, Psal. 95. 11. Non esse requiem De i die septimo, quo Deus requievit ab operibus no‑vis creandis, Quia operibus illis jam initio mundi finitis, verf. 3. cele‑brata est septimi diei requies, ut patet ex Gen. 2. atque ita illa requies Dei praeterit, verf 4. in Psalmo autem 95. 11. David de alia requie mentio‑nem facit: Ergo non hic intelligitur illa prima Dei requies, per Sabbatismum septimi Diei clebrata, verf. 5.
units.tr: Works] He explains the force of this argument at verse 10 in three ways. First, by showing that the rest of God expressed in the oath, Psalm 95:11, is not the rest of God on the seventh day, when God rested from the works he had created. For those works were already finished at the beginning of the world, and the rest of the seventh day was celebrated, as is clear from Gen. 2, and so that rest of God has passed by (verse 4). But in Psalm 95:11 David makes mention of another rest. Therefore the first rest of God, celebrated by the sabbatism of the seventh day, is not meant here (verse 5).

units.la: Verf 6. Quia igitur reliquum est ut aliqui introeant in eam, & quibus prius annuntiatum fuit, non introierunt propter incredulitatem.
units.tr: Verse 6. Since therefore it remains that some should enter into it, and those to whom it was first announced did not enter because of unbelief.

units.la: Secundo, Argumentum explicat declarando consequens, quod sequi‑tur ex eo, quod excludantur infideles propter infidelitatem, ne intro‑irent in requiem; necessario relinquitur (inquit) colligendum fore, ut aliqui, id est, fideles introeant in eam. Nam aut fideles introibunt in regnum Dei, aut infideles: At infideles non introibunt, sed exclu‑ duntur Dei juramento. Reliquum est igitur ut aliqui, id est, fideles introeant.
units.tr: Second, he explains the argument by stating the consequence that follows from the exclusion of unbelievers because of their unbelief from entering into rest. It necessarily remains (he says) to be concluded that some, that is, believers, enter into it. For either believers will enter into the kingdom of God, or unbelievers. But unbelievers will not enter, since they are shut out by God's oath. It remains, therefore, that some, that is, believers, enter.

units.la: Verl. 7. Rursum quendam praefinit diem, Hodie, apud Davi-dem dicens, tanto post tempore (prout dictum est) Hodie si vocem ejus audieritis, ne obdurate corda vestra.
units.tr: Verse 7. Again he fixes a certain day, "Today," saying through David, after so long a time (as has been said), "Today, if you hear his voice, do not harden your hearts."

units.la: Tertio, oltendendo requiem Dei in juramento expressam Psal. 95: 11. non esse requiem typicam in terra Canaan, Quod probat, Quia David Psal. 95. verf. 7. 8. quendam praefinit diem hodie tanto tem-pore post requiem septimi diei, & post populi ingressum in terram Ca-naan, nempe diem patientiae Dei: quandiu, viz. audimus vocem Dei: quandiu admonemur ne induremus corda, quandiu Deus ,hominibus ipsius vocem audientibus offert ingressum in requiem suam, nisi per infidelitatem induraverint corda sua, Ergo per requiem Dei non intelligitur à Propheta Davide requies in terra Canaan typica.
units.tr: Third, by showing that the rest of God expressed in the oath, Psalm 95:11, is not the typical rest in the land of Canaan. This he proves because David, in Psalm 95, verses 7 and 8, fixes a certain day, "today," after so long a time following the rest of the seventh day and after the people's entrance into the land of Canaan. This is the day of God's patience: as long as we hear his voice, as long as we are admonished not to harden our hearts, as long as God offers to men who hear his voice entrance into his rest, unless they have hardened their hearts through unbelief. Therefore by the rest of God the prophet David did not mean the typical rest in the land of Canaan.

units.la: Verf. 8. Nam si eos Iesus in requie collocasset, nequaquam de alio post hac die loquutus fuisset:
units.tr: Verse 8. For if Jesus had placed them in rest, he would never have spoken afterwards of another day.

units.la: Verl. 9 Itaque reliquis est aliquis sabatismus populo Dei.
units.tr: Verse 9. So there remains a sabbatism for the people of God.

units.la: Cujus rationem reddit, Quia si Iosua, seu Iesus typicus collocasset populum in requie illa Dei, quam David promittit, tum David nequaquam de alio post hac die loquutus fuisset in Psalmo, At loquutus est vers. 8. Ergo reliquus est aliquis Sabbatismus, seu alia requies populo Dei promissa à Davide, quam typica requies in terra Canaan, vers. 9.
units.tr: He gives the reason for this: if Joshua, or Jesus the type, had placed the people in that rest of God which David promises, then David would never have spoken afterwards of another day in the Psalm. But he did speak of it (verse 8). Therefore there remains a sabbatism, or another rest promised to the people of God by David, other than the typical rest in the land of Canaan (verse 9).

units.la: Vers. 10. Nam qui ingressus est in requiem ipsius, requievit, & ipse ab operibus suis, quemadmodum à suis DEVS.
units.tr: Verse 10. For he who has entered into his rest has himself also rested from his works, as God did from his.

units.la: Vers. 11. Studeamus igitur ingredi in illam requiem, ne quis in idem incidat contumaciae exemplum.
units.tr: Verse 11. Let us therefore strive to enter that rest, lest anyone fall into the same example of disobedience.

units.la: Arg. 6. Requies DEI est cessatio ab operibus nostris, sicut Deus cessavit ab operibus suis, seu est cessatio à peccatis, à molestiis, à curis discruciantibus, seu anxietatibus, & miseriis omnibus nostris: Ergo festinemus per fidem ingredi in illam requiem, ne quis nostrum ex requie Dei, cum contumacibus Israelitis excludatur.
units.tr: Argument 6. The rest of God is a cessation from our works, as God ceased from his works; or it is a cessation from sins, from troubles, from tormenting cares or anxieties, and from all our miseries. Therefore let us hasten to enter that rest through faith, lest any of us, like the stubborn Israelites, be shut out of God's rest.

units.la: Vers. 12. Vivus est enim sermo Dei & efficax, & penetrantior quovis gladio anceps, ac pertingit usque ad divisionem animae simul ac Spiritus, compagumque & medullarum, & judicat cogitationes & conceptiones cordis.
units.tr: Verse 12. For the word of God is living and effective, and sharper than any two-edged sword, and reaches even to the division of soul and spirit, of joints and marrow, and judges the thoughts and intents of the heart.

units.la: Arg. 7. confirmans superius in hunc sensum, Sermo ille Dei, qui vocat nos ad requiem ejus, cum interminatione irae nisi obtemperemus, non minus efficaciae jam habet & ad servandum fideles, & ad perdendum infideles quam olim habebat; Festinemus ergo per sinceram fidem ingredi in illam requiem, ne pereamus sicut olim infideles.
units.tr: Argument 7, confirming what was said above in this sense: that word of God, which calls us to his rest, with the threat of wrath if we do not obey, has no less efficacy now, both to save believers and to destroy unbelievers, than it had formerly. Let us therefore hasten to enter that rest by sincere faith, lest we perish as the unbelievers did of old.

units.la: Epitheta autem verbi tria sunt: 1. est vivum, Quia vim suam non amittit cum mortalibus prophetis, qui illud praedicant, neque cum illis mortalibus, quibus primum dicitur, sed perpetuam vim virtutemque retinet per omnes aetates, Zach. 1. 56. 2. Efficax est, Quia est potentia & brachium Dei ad operandum quod pronunciat, sive in consolationem, sive in terrorem. 3. Est penetrantius quovis gladio ancipiti: Quia sicut gladius anceps penetrat in intimas, abditissimas, & durissimas corporis partes, sic verbum Dei penetrat perfecta lucis manifestatione in intimos cordis recessus, qui per medullas in ossibus & per ossium commissuras intelliguntur, & in intimas animae facultates omnes, ut discernat quid moliatur pars animae sensitiva, quid pars intellectiva, quid intendat, quid praetendat quid cupiat, unusquisque, & quibus mediis ac rationibus studeat quod intendit ailequi: Pervadit, inquam, Dei Verbum, omnes humanæ Animæ facultaes, ut palam faciat unicuique, si qua hypocrisis, si qua radix amaritudinis aut infidelitatis in ipso lateat, utque discernendum, unicuique proponat secundum normam, non solum quid intus ipse cogitet in corde suo, verumetiam quâ intentione cogitet ac vult; ita ut qui intus meditantur apostasiam, vel apostasiæ in se semina tovent, Verbi Divini vim, nullis suis artibus, aut sophistica possint eludere, vel ictum ipsius declinare.
units.tr: There are three epithets of the word. (1) It is living, because it does not lose its power with the mortal prophets who preach it, nor with the mortal men to whom it was first spoken, but retains its power and virtue through all ages (Zach. 1, 56). (2) It is effective, because it is the power and arm of God for doing what it declares, whether for consolation or for terror. (3) It is sharper than any two-edged sword: just as a two-edged sword penetrates the innermost, most hidden and hardest parts of the body, so the word of God, by the full manifestation of light, penetrates into the innermost recesses of the heart, which are understood by the marrow in the bones and by the joints of the bones, and into all the inner faculties of the soul. It thus discerns what the sensitive part of the soul and what the intellectual part plots, what each intends, what each puts forward, what each desires, and by what means and reasons each strives for what it intends. I say the Word of God pervades all the faculties of the human soul, so that it makes plain to each person whatever hypocrisy, whatever root of bitterness or unbelief lies hidden within him, and so that it sets before each one, according to the rule, not only what he himself thinks within his heart, but also with what intention he thinks and wills it. Thus those who inwardly meditate apostasy, or harbour the seeds of apostasy within themselves, can by no arts or sophistries of their own elude the force of the divine Word or turn aside its blow.

units.la: Verf. 13. Nec est ulla res creata quæ non conspicua sit: coram ipso imò omnia sunt nuda & patentia oculis ejus qui eum nobis est negotium.
units.tr: Verse 13. Nor is there any created thing that is not manifest: indeed, all things are naked and open to the eyes of him with whom we have to do.

units.la: Arg. 8. confirmans superius, Deus quibuscum nobis res est, quando cum verbo ejus nobis res est, omnia perspicit, si quid intus infidelitatis lateat sub larva professionis externæ, quia omnia, etiam intima cordis penetralia, nuda & aperta sunt in ejus conspectu, licut cum animal per cervicem & spinam dorsi ita dividitur, ut viscera omnia pateant. Ergo studendum ut per sinceram fidem ingrediamini in ejus quietem, nec putetis eludi posse vim comminationum ejus si secus feceritis.
units.tr: Argument 8, confirming what was said above: God, with whom we have to do when we have to do with his word, sees all things, so that if any unbelief lies hidden inside under the mask of outward profession, it cannot escape him, because all things, even the innermost recesses of the heart, are naked and open in his sight, just as when an animal is cut through the neck and the backbone so that all its entrails lie exposed. Therefore we must take care to enter into his rest by sincere faith, and not think that the force of his threats can be evaded if you act otherwise.

units.la: Verf. 14. Habentes igitur Pontificem magnum, qui penetravit cœlos, Iesum Filium Dei, teneamus hanc professionem.
units.tr: Verse 14. Having therefore a great high priest, who has passed into the heavens, Jesus the Son of God, let us hold fast this profession.

units.la: Arg. 9. Habemus Iesum Christum Filium Dei, Pontificem, seu Sacerdotem magnum, qui jam penetravit Cœlos & ingressus est regnum, ut aperiat nobis aditum. Ergo retinendo professionem fidei studeamus introire.
units.tr: Argument 9. We have Jesus Christ the Son of God, the high priest, or great priest, who has already passed into the heavens and entered the kingdom, so that he may open the way to us. Therefore, by holding fast the profession of faith, let us strive to enter in.

units.la: Verf. 15. Non enim habemus Pontificem, qui non possit affici sensu infirmitatum nostrarum, sed tentatum in omnibus similiter, absque peccato.
units.tr: Verse 15. For we do not have a high priest who cannot be touched with the feeling of our infirmities, but one tempted in all things in like manner, yet without sin.

units.la: Arg. 10. per occupationem objectionis, Etiamsi Christi Majestas terrere nos posst, ne audeamus nos indigni peccatores aspirare ad requiem illam cœlestem, ubi ejus sanctitas habitat, misericors tamen est Pontifex noster, & aliquando expertus in sua carne eandem tentationes quas nos experimur, sed sine peccato. Ergo possumus, & audere debemus per fidem ad eum contendere, & studere, ut ingrediamur in illam requiem.
units.tr: Argument 10, by anticipating an objection: even if the majesty of Christ may terrify us, so that we unworthy sinners dare not aspire to that heavenly rest where his holiness dwells, nevertheless our high priest is merciful, and having himself in his flesh experienced the same temptations that we experience, but without sin. Therefore we can, and ought to dare, to press toward him through faith, and to strive to enter into that rest.

units.la: Verf. 16. Accedamus igitur cum fiducia ad thronum gratiæ, ut consequamur misericordiam, & gratiam inveniamus ad opportunum auxilium. Arg. II. In hunc sensum, Non sedet Deus in throno justitiæ accedentibus ad Christum per fidem, sed in throno gratiæ, ut in omnibus necessitatibus auxilium nobis ferat opportuno tempore. Ergo accedendum cum fiducia ad thronum gratiæ, ut sub alis propitiatorii quiescamus: quod idem est ac in requiem Dei per fidem ingredi.
units.tr: Verse 16. Let us therefore come with confidence to the throne of grace, that we may obtain mercy and find grace for timely help. Argument 11. To this effect: God does not sit on a throne of justice for those who come to Christ through faith, but on a throne of grace, so that he may bring us help in all our needs at the opportune time. Therefore we must come with confidence to the throne of grace, so that we may rest under the wings of the mercy seat; which is the same as entering into God's rest through faith.

units.la: Caput Quintum.
units.tr: Chapter Five.

units.la: Vit excellentia Prophetiæ Iesu Christi, & necessitas adhærendi ipsi, doctrinæque ejus qui est Apostolus & magnus Propheta professionis nostræ. Sequitur excellentia Sacerdotii ipsius. Capitis duæ sunt partes, In prima probat Christum esse Pontificem, seu summum Sacerdotem, omni typico Pontifice excellentiorem, ut Hebræos doceat moderatè sentire de Levitico Sacerdotio, quod illi in præjudicium adversus Christum, nimis magni faciebant, ad vers. II. In secunda est objurgatio segnitiei Hebræorum, ut attentiores reddat ad sequentem doctrinam. Excellentiam autem Pontificatus Christi supra Leviticum, probat Argumentis novem.
units.tr: Here the excellence of the prophecy of Jesus Christ is set out, and the necessity of adhering to him and to his teaching, who is the Apostle and the great Prophet of our profession. Next follows the excellence of his priesthood. The chapter has two parts. In the first, he proves that Christ is the High Priest, or chief Priest, more excellent than every typical priest, so as to teach the Hebrews to think moderately of the Levitical priesthood, which they overvalued to the prejudice of Christ. This runs to verse 11. In the second, he rebukes the sluggishness of the Hebrews, to make them more attentive to the doctrine that follows. He proves the excellence of Christ's priesthood above the Levitical one by nine arguments.

units.la: Vers. I. Nam omnis Pontifex ex hominibus assumitur, & pro hominibus constituitur in iis quæ apud Deum agenda sunt: ut offerat donaria & victimas pro peccatis.
units.tr: Verse 1. For every high priest taken from among men is ordained for men in things pertaining to God, that he may offer both gifts and sacrifices for sins.

units.la: Vers. 2. Qui quantum satis est, possit miserari vicem ignorantium & aberrantium: quod & ipse circumdatus sit infirmitate;
units.tr: Verse 2. Who can have compassion on the ignorant, and on those who are out of the way, since he himself also is compassed with infirmity.

units.la: Vers. 3. Et propter hanc debeat, sicut pro populo, ita & pro seipso offerre victimam pro peccatis.
units.tr: Verse 3. And by reason hereof he ought, as for the people, so also for himself, to offer for sins.

units.la: Argumentum primum, Perfectiones quæ requirebantur in Leviticis Sacerdotibus, vers. 1. 2. conjunctæ erant cum notis imperfectionis, & cum peccatis Sacerdotum, vers 2. 3. Ergo Christus, qui Pontifex absque peccato declaratus est, in fine superioris Capitis, excellentior est Sacerdotibus Leviticis.
units.tr: First argument: the perfections required in the Levitical priests (verses 1-2) were joined with marks of imperfection and with the priests' own sins (verses 2-3). Therefore Christ, who is declared to be a priest without sin at the end of the previous chapter, is more excellent than the Levitical priests.

units.la: Ex hominibus ] Levitici Pontificis perfectiones sunt quatuor: 1. Leviticus Pontifex ex hominibus assumebatur, unus ex multis eligebatur: 2. Constitutus erat pro hominibus in iis quæ apud Deum agenda erant, id est, ut populi vice & nomine administraret cultum Dei, Deum orando pro populo, populum Dei nomine docendo, & ut omni qua poslet ratione honorem Dei, populiq; salutem procuraret. 3. Offerebat donaria re-rum inanimatarum, & sacrificia animalium: nunc holocausta pro peccatis generatim, nunc pacifica pro impetrandis beneficiis, nunc Eucharistica pro beneficiis acceptis, nunc sacrificia pro peccatis specialibus, Quibus omnibus virtutes sacrificii Iesu Christi leviter adumbrabantur.
units.tr: From among men. The Levitical high priest had four perfections. (1) He was taken from among men; he was chosen from among many. (2) He was appointed for men in the things to be done before God, that is, to perform the worship of God on behalf of the people, praying to God for the people, teaching the people in God's name, and by every means in his power securing the honour of God and the people's salvation. (3) He offered gifts of inanimate things and sacrifices of animals: now burnt offerings for sins in general, now peace offerings to obtain benefits, now thank offerings for benefits received, now sacrifices for particular sins. In all of these the virtues of the sacrifice of Jesus Christ were faintly foreshadowed.

units.la: Miserari ] 4. Perfectio in officio sacerdotali requisita, est sympathia proportionata ad miseriae populi magnitudinem, qua tangi oportebat eos erga peccantes, sive ex ignorantia sive ex errore voluntario & consilio deliberato delinquentes.
units.tr: To have compassion. (4) The fourth perfection required in the priestly office is a sympathy proportionate to the greatness of the people's misery, with which they ought to be moved towards those who sin, whether through ignorance or through wilful error and deliberate wrongdoing.

units.la: Quid ipse ] Notae imperfectionis sunt duae: 1. Quid ipsi obnoxii fuerint infirmitatibus iisdem, hoc est, ignorantiae, & erroribus, miseriisque, quae peccata consequuntur.
units.tr: Since he himself. There are two marks of imperfection. (1) That they themselves were subject to the same infirmities, that is, ignorance and error, and the miseries that follow from sin.

units.la: Ita & pro ] Secunda nota imperfectionis, demonstrans priorem, quod ex officio obligati sint non minus pro suis ipsorum peccatis offerre victimas, quam pro peccatis populi. Hoc primum argumentum est.
units.tr: So also for. The second mark of imperfection, which shows the first, is that they were bound by their office to offer sacrifices for their own sins no less than for the sins of the people. This is the first argument.

units.la: Verf. 4. Neque sibi ipsi quisquam sumit hunc honorem, sed qui vocatur a Deo, sicut & Aaron.
units.tr: Verse 4. And no man taketh this honour unto himself, but he that is called of God, as was Aaron.

units.la: Verf. 5. Ita & Christus non sibi hunc honorem tribuit, ut fieret Pontifex, sed is qui dixerat ei: Filius meus es tu, ego hodie genui te.
units.tr: Verse 5. So also Christ glorified not himself to be made an high priest; but he that said unto him, Thou art my Son, to day have I begotten thee.

units.la: Arg. 2. Sicut legitimi sacerdotes vocati sunt ad hujus muneris honorem, Sic Christus non tantum legitime vocatus est a Patre, ut Aaron, sed etiam insuper Filius Dei unigenitus, agnitus, & declaratus est, in hoc munere sacerdotali: Ergo Leviticis sacerdotibus multo est excellentior. Probatur autem antecedens ex Psal. 2. ubi Pater Filium alloquens, verf. 7. vocat eum Filium suum quem genuit, prius quam jubeat eum, verf. 8. petere ab eo fines terrae, seu intercedere pro hominum salute, quod est sacerdotis partes exercere. Ergo ex hoc Psalmo non tantum vocatur ad officium sacerdotale a Patre, sed etiam Filius agnoscitur, & sic excellentior est Leviticis Sacerdotibus.
units.tr: Second argument: just as lawful priests were called to the honour of this office, so Christ was not only lawfully called by the Father, as Aaron was, but was also acknowledged and declared, in this priestly office, to be the only-begotten Son of God. Therefore he is far more excellent than the Levitical priests. The antecedent is proved from Psalm 2, where the Father, addressing his Son, in verse 7 calls him his Son whom he has begotten, before, in verse 8, bidding him ask of him the ends of the earth, that is, intercede for the salvation of men, which is the part of a priest. Therefore from this Psalm he is not only called to the priestly office by the Father, but the Son is also acknowledged, and so he is more excellent than the Levitical priests.

units.la: Verf. 6. Sicut & alibi dicit, Tu es Sacerdos in aeternum, secundum ordinem Melchisedec.
units.tr: Verse 6. As he saith also in another place, Thou art a priest for ever after the order of Melchisedec.

units.la: Arg. 3. ex Psal. 110. Christus a Patre constituitur Sacerdos in aeternum, cujus sacerdotii non est finis, secundum ordinem typi Melchisedeci. Ergo est excellentior Leviticis pontificibus.
units.tr: Third argument, from Psalm 110: Christ is appointed by the Father a Priest for ever, whose priesthood has no end, after the order of the type Melchizedek. Therefore he is more excellent than the Levitical priests.

units.la: Verf. 7. Qui in diebus carnis suæ, quum deprecationes & supplicationes apud eum qui poterat ipsum servare à morte, cum clamore valido, & lachrymis obtulisset, & exauditus esset ex metu,
units.tr: Verse 7. Who in the days of his flesh, when he had offered up prayers and supplications, with strong crying and tears, unto him that was able to save him from death, and was heard in that he feared;

units.la: Arg. 4 Quinque membris constans, quæ totidem possent esse Argumenta: 1. Christus hic est Filius Dei, ut etiam sit homo, seu filius in carne nostra, cujus infirmitates sine peccato ille aliquando expertus est, & sic excellentior homo est quam ullus ex Leviticis Sacerdotibus: 2. Obtulit deprecationes & supplicationes, seque ipsum ad mortem usque, pro populo suo: atque ita excellentius sacrificium obtulit quam Levitici: 3. Majori cum sensu miseriæ nostræ, & reatus nostri intercessit, cum Clamore valido & lachrymis; & sic in sympathia sua erga suos excellebat supra Levitcos: 4. Majori cum fiducia causam egit nostram, quam quivis ex typicis posset, etiam tum cum in angustiis mortis, & sensu iræ seu maledictionis divinæ, peccatis nostris debitæ, sancta humana natura ipsius cum terroribus mortis conflictabatur: 5. Majori cum efficacia & fructu, quam ullus typicus Sacerdos oravit: nam liberatus est secundum precationem à metu, quem sensui, & sanctæ rationi injiciebat irati Dei aspectus, quia jam persoluto pretio sufficienti pro nobis, iræ, metuque causa sublata est. Ergo Christus est Leviticis Pontificibus, Sacerdos longè excellentior.
units.tr: Fourth argument, consisting of five members, each of which could be a separate argument. (1) Christ here is the Son of God who also became man, a son in our flesh, whose infirmities he once experienced without sin; and so he is a more excellent man than any of the Levitical priests. (2) He offered prayers and supplications, and gave himself even to death, for his people; and so he offered a more excellent sacrifice than the Levitical priests. (3) He interceded for our misery and guilt with a greater sense of them, with strong crying and tears; and so in his sympathy towards his own he excelled the Levites. (4) He pleaded our cause with greater confidence than any of the typical priests could have done, even when, in the anguish of death and in the sense of divine wrath or curse due to our sins, his holy human nature was struggling with the terrors of death. (5) He prayed with greater efficacy and fruit than any typical priest; for he was delivered from the fear that the sight of an angry God brought upon his feeling and holy reason, because, the price being fully paid for us, the cause of wrath and fear was now removed. Therefore Christ is a priest far more excellent than the Levitical high priests.

units.la: Verf. 8 Quamvis Filius esset, tamen ex iis quæ passus est didicit obedientiam:
units.tr: Verse 8. Though he were a Son, yet learned he obedience by the things which he suffered;

units.la: Arg. 5. ex prioribus deductum, Quod simul removet scandalum crucis, simul excellentiam Sacerdotii Christi ostendit. Christus non occupabatur in spectandis victimarum occisionibus, ipse interim immunis ab omni passione, ut Levitici Sacerdotes in victimis cædendis, sed etiamsi Filius Dei fuerit, reipsa tamen in corporis & animæ suæ sanctæ passionibus expertus est, quam arduæ res fuerit peccata nostra expiare, experientiâ edoctus quam fuerit difficile expiatoriam obedientiam usque ad mortem crucis, ad Patris iram placandam, & justitiæ satisfaciendum præstare: Est ergo Christus Leviticis sacerdotibus multò excellentior.
units.tr: Fifth argument, drawn from what precedes, which at once removes the scandal of the cross and shows the excellence of Christ's priesthood. Christ was not occupied in watching the slaughter of victims while himself free from all suffering, as the Levitical priests were in killing the victims; but although he was the Son of God, he nevertheless truly experienced in the holy sufferings of his body and soul how arduous a thing it was to expiate our sins. Taught by experience, he learned how difficult it was to render expiatory obedience, even to the death of the cross, in order to appease the Father's wrath and satisfy justice. Therefore Christ is far more excellent than the Levitical priests.

units.la: Verf 9 Et consecratus, factus est autor salutis æternæ omnibus qui ipsi auscultant:
units.tr: Verse 9. And being made perfect, he became the author of eternal salvation unto all them that obey him;

units.la: Arg. 6. Christus summus Sacerdos, fuit omnibus numeris completus plenus & perfectus, in quo nec minimum quidem desiderari potest, quod in Sacerdote requiritur; postquam enim jam sanctificatus, seu in sacrificium propitiatorium Patri oblatus est, totum pretium redemptionis complevit, seu quod restabat, in ultimis suis passionibus persolvit; cujus pretii nulla pars à Leviticis persoluta est: Ergo Leviticis & umbratilibus illis Sacerdotibus. multo est excellentior.
units.tr: Sixth argument: Christ, the High Priest, was complete and perfect in every respect, so that nothing at all can be lacking in him of what is required in a priest. For once he had been sanctified, that is, offered to the Father as a propitiatory sacrifice, he had fully completed the whole price of redemption, paying in his last sufferings what remained to be paid; and no part of that price was paid by the Levites. Therefore he is far more excellent than the Levitical and shadowy priests.

units.la: Autor ] Arg. 7 CHRISTUS jam pretio redemptionis plenè persoluto, merito & efficacia, evasit & declaratus est Author, Dominus, Dator & Consummator vitæ æternæ omnibus in ipsum credentibus, & seipsi in disciplinam tradentibus: Ergo CHRISTUS Leviticis Sacerdotibus multo excellentior est.
units.tr: Author. Seventh argument: Christ, the price of redemption having been fully paid by his merit and efficacy, has become and been declared the Author, Lord, Giver and Consummator of eternal life to all who believe in him and surrender themselves to his discipline. Therefore Christ is far more excellent than the Levitical priests.

units.la: Verf. 10. Cognominatus à Deo Pontifex secundum ordinem Melchesidec.
units.tr: Verse 10. Called of God an high priest after the order of Melchisedec.

units.la: Arg 8. Confirmans superius, CHRISTUS à DEO cujus dictum efficax est; cognominatus est Sacerdos secundum ordinem Melchisedeci, qui ordo excellentior est multo ordine Levitico: Ergo CHRISTUS est summus Pontifex, Leviticis omnibus multo excellentior.
units.tr: Eighth argument, confirming what was said above: Christ, by God, whose word is effective, has been named a priest after the order of Melchizedek, which order is far more excellent than the Levitical order. Therefore Christ is the chief High Priest, far more excellent than all the Levites.

units.la: Verf. 11. De quo nobis multa sunt dicenda, eaque difficilia explicatu; quandoquidem segnes facti estis auribus.
units.tr: Verse 11. Of this we have many things to say, and they are difficult to explain, since you have become sluggish in hearing.

units.la: Arg 9. Doctrina de Sacerdotii CHRISTI excellentiâ, præsertim prout in typo Melchisedeci repræsentatur, copiosior & altior est quam ab Apostolo possit ad ipsorum captum facile explicari: Ergo Leviticis Sacerdotibus multo est excellentior.
units.tr: Argument 9. The doctrine of the excellence of Christ's priesthood, especially as it is represented in the type of Melchizedek, is too extensive and too lofty to be easily explained to their understanding by the Apostle. Therefore it is far more excellent than the Levitical priests.

units.la: Secunda pars.
units.tr: The second part.

units.la: Secunda pars Capitis, in qua infert ex doctrinæ de CHRISTI sacerdotii excellentiâ, reprehensionem ignorantiæ & tarditatis ingenii Hebræorum, ad mysteria Evangelii discenda. Propositio reprehensoria hæc est, Vos Hebraei reprehendendi estis ob segnitiem ad capiendum mysteria Evangelii, quale est, CHRISTI Sacerdotium.
units.tr: The second part of the chapter, in which he infers from the doctrine of the excellence of Christ's priesthood a rebuke of the ignorance and dullness of mind of the Hebrews in learning the mysteries of the Gospel. The reproving proposition is this: You Hebrews are to be rebuked for sluggishness in grasping the mysteries of the Gospel, such as the priesthood of Christ.

units.la: Verf. 12. Vos enim quos oportuit pro temporis ratione doctores esse, rursum opus est doceri quæ sint elementa initii eloquiorum Dei: factique estis ii quibus lacte sit opus, & non solido cibo.
units.tr: Verse 12. For you who ought by now to be teachers, given the time, again have need that someone teach you what are the elements of the beginning of the oracles of God; and you have become such as need milk and not solid food.

units.la: Rationes reprehensionis reddit quatuor: prima est, Quia opus habetis elementario, catechetico & puerili genere doctrinæ, etiam jam postquam pro temporis in luce Euangelii perac̈ti ratione, multa ipsi didicisse, & alios instituere potuissetis.
units.tr: He gives four reasons for the rebuke. The first is this: you still need the elementary, catechetical and childish kind of teaching, even though, given the time that has passed in the light of the Gospel, you ought to have learned a great deal yourselves and be able to instruct others.

units.la: Factique] Ratio 2. Confirmans superiorem, Quia pueri & infantes estis in cognitione Euangelii, qui lacte, seu qui in rudimentis doctri-næ institui opus habeatis, potius quam cibo solido, seu doctrinæ perfectione.
units.tr: "And have become": the second reason, confirming the previous one: you are children and infants in the knowledge of the Gospel, so that you need to be instructed in the rudiments of doctrine, which is milk, rather than in solid food, that is, the perfection of doctrine.

units.la: Vers. 13, Enimverò cui cum lacte res est, is rudis est sermonis justitiæ: ( infans enim est )
units.tr: Verse 13. For everyone who partakes of milk is unskilled in the word of righteousness, for he is an infant.

units.la: Ratio 3. Probans superiorem, Quia rudes estis sermonis justitiæ, seu non bene intelligitis doctrinam justificationis per fidem Christi; sed parati estis ceremonias legis cum fide Christi conjungere. Idcirco & infantes estis, & ob ignorantiam reprehendendi.
units.tr: The third reason, proving the previous one: you are unskilled in the word of righteousness, that is, you do not rightly understand the doctrine of justification through faith in Christ, but you are ready to join the ceremonies of the law with faith in Christ. Therefore you are both infants and, through ignorance, deserving of rebuke.

units.la: Vers 14. Sed adultorum est solidus cibus, eorum videlicet qui propter habitum sensus habent exercitatos ad discretionem boni ac mali.
units.tr: Verse 14. But solid food belongs to adults, namely to those who, because of practice, have their senses trained to discern good and evil.

units.la: Ratio 4. Explicans postremam partem rationis secundæ, Quia destituti estis proprietatibus adultorum: Adulti enim gaudent cibo solido, seu affectant perfectiorem doctrinam: 2. Gaudent crebra exercitatione. 3. Per crebram exercitationem sui in doctrina Euangelii habitum contraxerunt cognitionis salutaris non facile mutabilem, & sensus seu facultates animi expeditiores habent ad judicandum de veritate & falsitate doctrinæ propositæ; de utilitate veritatis, & de errorum periculo, ut possint bonum prosequi, & malum evitare. Tales non estis vos Hebræi, licet per tempus post vestram fidei professionem tales esse potuissetis. Ergo reprehendendi estis.
units.tr: The fourth reason, explaining the last part of the second reason: you lack the properties of adults. For adults delight in solid food, that is, they desire more perfect doctrine; second, they delight in frequent practice; third, through frequent exercise of themselves in the doctrine of the Gospel they have acquired a habit of saving knowledge not easily changed, and their senses or faculties of mind are more ready to judge the truth and falsity of the doctrine proposed, the usefulness of the truth, and the danger of errors, so that they may pursue the good and avoid the evil. You Hebrews are not such, although through the time since your profession of faith you could have been such. Therefore you deserve rebuke.

units.la: Caput Sextum.
units.tr: Chapter Six.

units.la: Equitur ex priori reprehensione segnitiei deducta hortatio ad perseverandum, & progressus faciendum in fide Euangelii.
units.tr: There follows from the previous rebuke, drawn from their sloth, an exhortation to persevere and to make progress in the faith of the Gospel.

units.la: Vers. 1. QVapropter omisso qui in Christo rudes incheat, sermone, ad perfectionem feramur: non jacientes rursum fundamentum resipiscentiæ ab operibus mortuis, & fidei in Deum. Propositio primis verbis continetur, Debetis perseverare, & progressus facere in fide Euangelii. Nam omittere sermonem catecheticum, qui rudes in Christo inchoat, est praesupponere, & pro confesso habere, quod ea rudimenta jam teneant, Aliquo modo, idcirco non opus esse scribenti ad eos, his immorari, sed catecheticis omissis, ad perfectionem, id est, ad perseverandum, & progressus in fide faciendum, eos promovere.
units.tr: Verse 1. Therefore, leaving aside the word of the beginning of Christ, let us be carried on to perfection, not laying again the foundation of repentance from dead works, and of faith in God. The proposition is contained in the first words: you must persevere and make progress in the faith of the Gospel. For to leave aside the catechetical word, which begins the untrained in Christ, is to presuppose and take for granted that they already hold those rudiments to some extent. Therefore there is no need for the writer to dwell on them with the Hebrews; with the catechetical matters set aside, he advances them to perfection, that is, to persevering and making progress in the faith.

units.la: Argumenta hortationis sunt quindecim. Argumentum primum, Sicut fundamentum domus, sic fundamentum religionis non est bis ponendum, sed fundamento semel posito pergendum in aedificio extruendo. Ergo vobis perseverandum & progrediendum est in fide Euangelii; Fundamentales autem seu catecheticas doctrinas enumerat sex: prima, Est de resipiscentia ab operibus mortuis, seu a peccatis: Hoc fundamentum continet initialem doctrinam de lege Dei, de agnitione peccati, & meritae damnationis consequentis, de dolore ob peccata, & desiderio liberationis a peccato & a morte. 2, Fundamentalis doctrina est de fide in DEUM, quae doctrinam continet redemptionis per Christum, & de justitia & vita per eum partâ, deque fide in eum ad salutem.
units.tr: There are fifteen arguments for the exhortation. The first argument: just as the foundation of a house is not laid twice, but once the foundation is laid one proceeds to erect the building, so the foundation of religion is not to be laid twice. Therefore you must persevere and progress in the faith of the Gospel. He lists six fundamental or catechetical doctrines. The first is of repentance from dead works, that is, from sins. This foundation contains the initial teaching about the law of God, the recognition of sin and the damnation it deservedly brings, grief over sins, and desire to be freed from sin and death. The second fundamental doctrine is of faith in God, which contains the teaching of redemption through Christ, of the righteousness and life obtained through him, and of faith in him unto salvation.

units.la: Verf. 2 Baptismatum doctrina, ac manuum impositionis, & resurrectionis mortuorum, & judicii aeterni.
units.tr: Verse 2. The doctrine of baptisms, and of the laying on of hands, and of the resurrection of the dead, and of eternal judgment.

units.la: 3 Est doctrina baptismatum, continens rationem confirmandi fidem per Sacramentum Baptismi, & doctrinam sanctificationis, & afflictionis, seu crucis ferendae pro Euangelii defensione, quae doctrina per Baptismum significatur: 4. Est doctrina impositionis manuum, quae in collatione donorum Spiritus sancti, ad confirmationem divinae veritatis Euangelii olim facta est, modo extraordinario in primitiva Ecclesia: nunc vero modo ordinario fit in ordinatione Ministrorum Ecclesiae, de quorum autoritate & officio, sicut ad omnes catechumenos olim spectabat, sic jam ad omnes spectat fideles recte institui, ut Dei ordinationi le alacrius subjiciant in Ecclesiasticae disciplinae obedientia.
units.tr: 3. The third is the doctrine of baptisms, containing the account of confirming faith through the sacrament of Baptism, and the doctrine of sanctification and of affliction, that is, of bearing the cross in defence of the Gospel, which doctrine is signified by Baptism. 4. The fourth is the doctrine of the laying on of hands, which was formerly done in the primitive Church, in an extraordinary manner, in the conferring of the gifts of the Holy Spirit for the confirmation of the divine truth of the Gospel. Now, however, it is done in the ordinary manner in the ordination of ministers of the Church. Just as formerly it pertained to all catechumens to be rightly instructed concerning the authority and office of these men, so now it pertains to all the faithful, that they may more readily submit to God's ordinance in obedience to church discipline.

units.la: 5. Doctrina est de resurrectione mortuorum in die novissimo: 6. Est de judicio extremo, quo per Christum fidelibus vita aeterna, impiis vero mors aeterna adjudicanda est.
units.tr: 5. The doctrine concerning the resurrection of the dead at the last day. 6. The doctrine of the final judgment, by which, through Christ, eternal life is to be adjudged to the faithful and eternal death to the impious.

units.la: Verf 3. Atque id faciemus, siquidem permiserit Deus.
units.tr: Verse 3. And this we shall do, if God permits.

units.la: Arg. 2. ad perseverantiam & profectum in fide Euangelii, Ego Apostolus per Dei gratiam, ut in cognitione Euangelii promovea-tis operam tis operam daturus sum pro virili, quantum Deo videbitur meis in ministerio laboribus benedicere: Ergo vobis opera danda, ut perseveretis, & progrediamini in fide Euangelii.
units.tr: Argument 2, for perseverance and progress in the faith of the Gospel: I, the Apostle, by the grace of God, will labour as far as I can, so that you may advance in knowledge of the Gospel, insofar as God sees fit to bless my labours in the ministry. Therefore you must take pains to persevere and progress in the faith of the Gospel.

units.la: Vers. 4 Nam fieri non potest, ut qui semel fuerint illuminati, gustaverintque donum cœleste, & participes facti fuerint SPIRITVS Sancti,
units.tr: Verse 4. For it is impossible that those who were once enlightened, and have tasted the heavenly gift, and have been made partakers of the Holy Spirit,

units.la: Vers. 5. Gustaverintque bonum Dei verbum, ac virtutes futuri seculi.
units.tr: Verse 5. And have tasted the good word of God, and the powers of the age to come,

units.la: Vers. 6 Si prolabuntur, ut denuo renoveнтur per resipiscentiam, ut qui rursum crucifigant sibimetipsis Filium Dei, & ad ignominiam exponant.
units.tr: Verse 6. If they fall away, it is impossible to renew them again through repentance, since they crucify again the Son of God to themselves, and expose him to shame.

units.la: Arg. 3. Quicunque post talem animi convictionem de veritate Euangelii, qualem hic descriptam habetis, non perseverant, sed à rudimentis fidei resiliunt, & prolabuntur in peccatum illud irremissibile in Spiritum Sanctum, non possunt resipiscere nec servari: Ergo ne in hoc peccatum incidatis, perseverandum & progrediendum vobis in fide Euangelii.
units.tr: Argument 3: whoever, after such a conviction of the truth of the Gospel as is described here, does not persevere but recoils from the rudiments of faith and lapses into that sin against the Holy Spirit which is unforgivable, cannot repent nor be saved. Therefore, lest you fall into this sin, you must persevere and progress in the faith of the Gospel.

units.la: Describuntur autem illi adversus quos stringitur hæc comminatio ex his sex notis: 1. Illuminati sunt per cognitionem Euangelii; per cujus lumen misera conditio hominis, & ratio redemptionis per Christum potest etiam irregenitis aperiri: 2. Gustaverunt donum cœleste, quod fieri potest per contemplationem Christi, & rerum cœlestium in Euangelio revelatarum, omnis enim veritatis vel levissima delibatio sensum aliquem excitat lui, licet non semper solidum & permanentem: 3. Participes facti sunt Spiritus Sancti, quod fieri potest per dona aliqua regenitis & irregenitis communia: 4. Gustaverunt bonum Dei verbum, quod fieri potest per fidem historicam Euangelii, & per apprehensionem possibilis suæ ipsorum salutis, quam ut actu adipiscantur non prosequuntur: 5. Gustarunt virtutes futuri seculi in leviusculo gaudio de futura vita, quod fieri potest per fidem temporariam in iis qui recipiunt verbum in terra petrosa cum gaudio, Math. 13. 20. ex apprehensione non possibilis tantum, sed etiam probabilis, & apparenter futuræ suæ salutis: quam ut lubenter cum Balaamo optare, & cum fatuis virginibus sperare possunt, etiamsi mundo, & pravis suis cupiditatibus non renunciaverint: 6. Potest omnes hos gradus convictionis de veritate religionis Christianæ à Spiritu Dei productos, prolabuntur, seu laplu totali, voluntario, & malitioso, ut postea apparebit, defectionem faciunt à Christo.
units.tr: Those against whom this threat is aimed are described by six marks. 1. They are Enlightened through knowledge of the Gospel, by whose light the wretched condition of man and the way of redemption through Christ can be disclosed even to the unregenerate. 2. They have tasted the heavenly gift, which can happen through contemplation of Christ and of the heavenly things revealed in the Gospel; for even the slightest taste of any truth stirs up some feeling, though not always a solid and lasting one. 3. They have been made partakers of the Holy Spirit, which can happen through certain gifts common to the regenerate and the unregenerate. 4. They have tasted the good word of God, which can happen through the historical faith of the Gospel and through the apprehension of the possibility of their own salvation, which they do not pursue so as actually to obtain it. 5. They have tasted the powers of the age to come in a rather slight joy about the future life, which can happen through temporary faith in those who receive the word on stony ground with joy (Matt. 13:20), from an apprehension of their future salvation that is not merely possible but also probable and apparent. They can gladly desire it with Balaam and hope for it with the foolish virgins, even if they have not renounced the world and their wicked lusts. 6. All these degrees of conviction concerning the truth of the Christian religion are produced by the Spirit of God; yet if they fall away, that is, lapse totally, voluntarily and maliciously, as will appear later, they make defection from Christ.

units.la: Denuo ] Poena quam minatur hujusmodi apostatis, est quod ipsorum resipiscentia, & per consequens salus, sit impossibilis; quia post peccatum hoc, nunquam sequitur resipiscentia. Cujus rationes redduntur dua: 1. A malitia ipsorum adversus Christum, quia Filium Dei semel crucifixum malitiose abnegando, nolunt salvari per ejus mortem, abhorrent ab ea ratione salutis consequendæ, ex qua sola dependet resipiscentia & salus, imo vero quantum in se est Christum de solio cœlestis gloriæ deturbatum, si fieri posset, & denuo crucifixum vellent.
units.tr: Again. The punishment threatened to such apostates is that their repentance, and consequently their salvation, is impossible, because after this sin repentance never follows. Two reasons are given. 1. The first is their malice against Christ: since by maliciously renouncing the Son of God once crucified they are unwilling to be saved by his death, they shrink from that way of obtaining salvation on which alone repentance and salvation depend. Indeed, so far as lies in them, they would, if it were possible, thrust Christ down from the throne of heavenly glory and crucify him again.

units.la: Exponunt ] Altera ratio à scandalo dato, Quia Christum ignominiæ, ludibrio & sannis infidelium ultro exponunt, atque atrociori scelere, quam illi qui primo Christum ignorantes in crucem egerunt.
units.tr: They expose. The second reason is the scandal given: they willingly expose Christ to the shame, mockery and jeers of unbelievers, with a more atrocious crime than those who, not yet knowing Christ, drove him to the cross.

units.la: Vers. 7. Nam terra quæ imbrem sæpius in se venientem combiberit, & progenuerit herbam accomodam eis per quos excoluntur, recipit ben dictionem à Deo:
units.tr: Verse 7. For the earth which has often drunk in the rain that comes upon it, and brings forth herbage fit for those by whom it is tilled, receives blessing from God.

units.la: Arg. 4. ad perseverandum, Sicut terra frugifera recipit benedictionem à Deo, sic perseverantes, & progressum facientes in fide & obedientia Evangelii benedictionem à Deo recipiunt: Ergo vobis perseverandum est.
units.tr: Argument 4, for perseverance: just as fruitful earth receives blessing from God, so those who persevere and make progress in the faith and obedience of the Gospel receive blessing from God. Therefore you must persevere.

units.la: Vers 8. At quæ profert spinas & tribulos, reproba est, & maledictioni affinis: cujus exitus tendit ad exustionem.
units.tr: Verse 8. But that which bears thorns and thistles is worthless, and near to being cursed; its end is to be burned.

units.la: Arg. 5 Sicut terra culta, & sæpius irrigata, quæ nihil profert præter spinas & tribulos, rejectanea, maledictioni proxima, & tandem exurenda est: Sic Apostatæ qui jam sæpius imbrem verbi Divini in se venientem combiberunt, & tamen nullum bonum fructum proferunt, sed prolabuntur, omninoque deficiunt, reprobi sunt & maledictioni proximi, prorsus perituri, ut quorum couversio & salus est desperata.
units.tr: Argument 5: just as cultivated and often watered land which produces nothing but thorns and thistles is rejected, near to a curse, and finally to be burned, so apostates who have often drunk in the rain of the divine word coming upon them, and yet bring forth no good fruit, but fall away and altogether fail, are reprobate and near to a curse, utterly destined to perish, since their conversion and salvation is despaired of.

units.la: Vers 9. Sed persuasimus nobis de vobis, dilecti, istis meliora, & cum salute conjuncti, etiamsi ita loquamur.
units.tr: Verse 9. But we are persuaded of better things concerning you, beloved, and things connected with salvation, even though we speak thus.

units.la: Consolatur Hebræos fideles adversus asperitatem dictorum, & ipsorum apostasiæ futuræ suspicionem, quam intus de iis fovere videri potuisset Apostolus, nisi se purgasset, & addit Arg. 6. Etiamsi periculum apostasiæ propoluerim vobis, persuasimus tamen nobis meliora de veltra fide vera, & obedientia sincera, & perseverantia, aliisque gratiis, quæ cum salute æterna necessariam habent connexionem. Ergo vobis perseverandum est animosius.
units.tr: He comforts the faithful Hebrews against the harshness of his words, and against the suspicion of their future apostasy, which the Apostle might seem to have harboured inwardly had he not cleared himself. He adds argument 6: even if I have set before you the danger of apostasy, we are nevertheless persuaded of better things concerning your true faith, sincere obedience, perseverance, and other graces, which have a necessary connection with eternal salvation. Therefore you must persevere the more boldly.

units.la: Vers. 10, Non enim injustus est Deus, ut obliviscatur operis vestri, & laboriosæ charitatis quam exhibuistis ipsius nomini, ut qui ministraveritis sanctis & ministretis.
units.tr: Verse 10. For God is not unjust, so as to forget your work and the laborious love which you have shown toward his name, in that you ministered, and still minister, to the saints.

units.la: Arg. 7. confirmans superius, Justitia & Veritas Dei non patientur ut gratia Dei salvifica vobis jam data, & in efficaci conjtantique charitate vestra erga verè Fideles, seu Sanctos, opere demonstrata, oblivioni tradatur, sed gratiam pro gratia tribuens perseverantiam & vitam æternam promissam etiam vobis dabit. Ergo vobis animosè perseverandum
units.tr: Seventh argument, confirming what came before: the justice and truth of God will not allow the saving grace of God, already given to you, and the effective and steadfast love you have shown toward the truly faithful, or saints, by your deeds, to be forgotten; rather, repaying grace for grace, he will also give you the perseverance and the eternal life promised. Therefore you must persevere bravely.

units.la: Vers. 11, Cupimus autem, ut unusquisque vestrum idem ostendat studium ad plenam spei persuasionem, ad finem usque:
units.tr: Verse 11: "And we desire that each of you show the same diligence unto the full assurance of hope until the end:"

units.la: Arg. 8. Perseverantiæ studendo magis magisque certam reddetis vestræ ipsorum spei persuasionem: Ergo unicuique vestrum danda opera ut perseveretis. Atque hic ipsa hortatio ad perseverantiam expresse ponitur.
units.tr: Eighth argument: by applying yourselves to perseverance more and more, you will make the assurance of your hope more certain. Therefore each of you must take pains to persevere. Here exhortation to perseverance is expressly set down.

units.la: Vers. 12. Ut ne sitis segnes, sed imitatores eorum qui per fidem ac patientiam obtinent promissam hæreditatem.
units.tr: Verse 12: "That you be not slothful, but followers of them who through faith and patience inherit the promises."

units.la: Arg 9 Excutiendo segnitiem in comparanda altiori cognitione Evangelii, & pergendo in studio charitatis, debetis imitari sanctos Patres, qui in fide & patientia perseverantes, promissam hæreditatem obtinuerunt: Studete igitur perseverantiæ.
units.tr: Ninth argument: by shaking off sluggishness in gaining a higher knowledge of the Gospel, and by continuing in the pursuit of love, you ought to imitate the holy Fathers, who, persevering in faith and patience, obtained the promised inheritance. Therefore strive for perseverance.

units.la: Vers. 13. Deus enim pollicitus Abrahæ, quum non posset per quemquam majorem jurare, juravit per seipsum,
units.tr: Verse 13: "For when God made promise to Abraham, because he could swear by no greater, he sware by himself,"

units.la: Vers. 14 Dicens, Certè benedicens benedicam tibi, & multiplicans multiplicabo te.
units.tr: Verse 14: "Saying, Surely blessing I will bless thee, and multiplying I will multiply thee."

units.la: Vers. 15 Atque ita quum patienter expectasset, assecutus est promissum
units.tr: Verse 15: "And so, after he had patiently endured, he obtained the promise."

units.la: Arg. 10. Promissio benedictionis factæ fidelibus, in persona Abrahami, Patris Fidelium, & per juramentum Dei optimi maximi confirmata, experimento speciali comprobata est Abrahamo, patienter in fide & spe perseveranti. Ergo in fide promissionis, & spe benedictionis similiter vobis est patienter perseverandum. Hujus argumenti vis, ut appareat, meminisse oportet hanc promissionem factam Abrahæ, de hæ, de benedictione, intelligendam esse non de nascituro Isaaco tantum, sed de Christo, ex Isaaco oriundo, & de justitia gratuita & vita æterna in Christo danda, non Abrahæ tantum, sed etiam ut credentium Patri, & credentibus omnibus in ejus persona repræsentatis, id est, veris hæredibus istius promissæ benedictionis, sicut Apostolus hoc loco, & alibi pro concesso habet, & nominatim Gal. 3. 9, 10, 13, &c. expresse docet.
units.tr: Tenth argument: the promise of blessing made to the faithful in the person of Abraham, the father of the faithful, and confirmed by the oath of God, most good and most great, was proved by a special experience in Abraham, who persevered patiently in faith and hope. Therefore in faith in the promise and hope of the blessing you likewise must persevere patiently. For the force of this argument to appear, it must be remembered that this promise made to Abraham, concerning the blessing, is to be understood not only of the son Isaac about to be born, but of Christ, descended from Isaac, and of the gratuitous justice and eternal life to be given in Christ; not to Abraham alone, but also as to the father of believers, and to all believers represented in his person, that is, the true heirs of this promised blessing. So the Apostle holds here, and elsewhere, as granted, and expressly teaches it by name in Gal. 3:9, 10, 13, etc.

units.la: Verf. 16. Nam homines quidem per eum jurant qui sit major, atque iisdem omnis controversiæ finis, est jusjurandum ad confirmationem adhibitum.
units.tr: Verse 16: "For men verily swear by the greater, and an oath for confirmation is to them an end of all strife."

units.la: Arg. 11. ex superiori deductum, Sicut cum homines jurant per majorem, & jusjurandum ad confirmationem adhibitum, est finis controversiæ inter eos; Sic promissio benedictionis, seu justitiæ & vitæ gratuito in Christo dandæ, per juramentum supremi Dei confirmata omnibus fidelibus in Abrahamo, finis debet esse controversiæ inter Deum & fideles, ne titubent in fide promissionis: Ergo vos Hebræi fideles sic confirmati, confidenter perseverate in fide.
units.tr: Eleventh argument, drawn from what precedes: just as, when men swear by a greater, and an oath is applied for confirmation, it is the end of strife between them, so the promise of blessing, or of justice and life to be given freely in Christ, confirmed by the oath of the supreme God to all the faithful in Abraham, ought to be an end of strife between God and the faithful, lest they waver in faith in the promise. Therefore you Hebrews, thus confirmed, persevere confidently in the faith.

units.la: Verf. 17. Qua in re Deus volens ex abundanti hæredibus promissionis ostendere immutabilitatem consilii sui, fidejussit jurejurando:
units.tr: Verse 17: "Wherein God, willing more abundantly to shew unto the heirs of promise the immutability of his counsel, confirmed it by an oath:"

units.la: Arg. 12. Etiamsi sufficiens fuisset nuda promissio benedictionis, Deus tamen ex abundanti interposuit juramentum (quasi vadimonium) ut Isacidas, filios & hæredes promissionis, id est, fideles omnes, certiores redderet de immutabilitate consilii sui, de ipsis benedicendis. Ergo vos fideles Hebræi ex abundanti confirmati, perseverare debetis in fide Euangelii.
units.tr: Twelfth argument: even if the bare promise of blessing had been sufficient, God nevertheless added an oath, as a surety (as it were a pledge), so that the sons of Isaac and heirs of the promise, that is, all the faithful, might be more certain of the immutability of his counsel concerning their blessing. Therefore you Hebrew believers, more abundantly confirmed, ought to persevere in the faith of the Gospel.

units.la: Verf. 18. Ut per duas res immutabiles, in quibus fieri non potest ut mentitus sit Deus, validam consolationem habeamus nos, qui cursum eo corripuimus, ut spem propositam obtineamus:
units.tr: Verse 18: "That by two immutable things, in which it was impossible for God to lie, we might have a strong consolation, who have fled for refuge to lay hold upon the hope set before us:"

units.la: Arg. 13. in hunc sensum, Deus eo ipso fine juravit, ut fideles qui perseverare studient, ex duabus rebus immutabilibus hauriant consolationem & fiduciam validam, & gaudium in Deo solidum, adversus omnem metum & miseriam: Ergo vos fideles Hebræi, hac consolatione animati, perseverare debetis confidenter. Describit fideles hæredes promissionis, qui perseverare student, ex ipsorum proprietate, quod ex conscientia peccatorum, & itæ meritæ, confugiant ad Christum, ut speratam vitam æternam in eo propositam obtineant. Duas res immutabiles intelligit: 1. Promissionem Dei: 2. Juramentum Dei, per quæ certi reddantur fideles de tertio immutabili, id est, de consilio seu decreto Dei de ipsis salvandis.
units.tr: Thirteenth argument, to this sense: God swore for this very end, that the faithful who study to persevere might draw from two immutable things a strong consolation and confidence, and a solid joy in God, against every fear and misery. Therefore you Hebrew believers, animated by this consolation, ought to persevere confidently. He describes the faithful heirs of the promise who study to persevere by their own characteristic, that, from the awareness of sins and of their demerit, they flee to Christ, to obtain the hoped-for eternal life set before them in him. By the two immutable things he understands: (1) the promise of God; (2) the oath of God, through which the faithful are made certain of a third immutable thing, that is, of the counsel or decree of God concerning their salvation.

units.la: Fieri non potest ] Ratio nem reddit immutabilitatis illius duplicis, quia impossibile est ut Deus mentiatur, hoc est, ut non præstet quod promisit simul & juravit.
units.tr: "It is impossible": he gives the reason for that double immutability, because it is impossible for God to lie, that is, not to perform what he promised and at the same time swore.

units.la: Vers. 19. Quam velut animæ ancoram habemus tutam ac firmam, & ingredientem usque in ea quæ sunt intra velum
units.tr: Verse 19: "Which hope we have as an anchor of the soul, both sure and steadfast, and which entereth into that within the veil;"

units.la: Arg. 14. Nos fideles habemus spem vivam, velut tutam & firmam anchoram animæ fluctuantis, jactam intra Cœlum, quod per velum Templi figurabatur. Ergo ad portum salutis constanter cum fiducia vobis est contendendum.
units.tr: Fourteenth argument: we the faithful have a living hope, as a sure and steadfast anchor of a tossed soul, cast within heaven, which was figured by the veil of the Temple. Therefore you must strive constantly, with confidence, toward the harbour of salvation.

units.la: Tuta vocatur anchora Spes, quia tutos conservat sperantes: nam spes nunquam pudefacit: Firma vocatur, & quia nunquam diffrumpitur penitus, & quia firmiter defixa & fundata est in rupe, nitens omnipotentia, veritate, & bonitate Dei, & merito Christi.
units.tr: Hope is called an "anchor" that is "sure" because it keeps safe those who hope; for hope never puts to shame. It is called "steadfast" both because it is never utterly broken, and because it is firmly fixed and founded on the rock, resting on the omnipotence, truth, and goodness of God, and on the merit of Christ.

units.la: Vers. 20 Quo prævcursor pro nobis ingressus est Iesus, secundum ordinem Melchisedec, Pontifex factus in æternum
units.tr: Verse 20: "Whither the forerunner is for us entered, even Jesus, made an high priest for ever after the order of Melchisedec."

units.la: Arg. 15. Iesus Christus pro nobis fidelibus ingressus est cœlum, quod figurabatur per Pontificis ingressum intra velum in Sanctum Sanctorum, Præcursor pro nobis paratarus locum, & pro nobis intercessurus, ne in curlu deficiamus, constitutus à Patre in æternum Sacerdos, secundum ordinem Melchisedeci. Ergo vos fideles Hebræi debetis cum fiducia perseverare in fide Evangelii.
units.tr: Fifteenth argument: Jesus Christ has entered heaven for us the faithful, which was figured by the entry of the high priest within the veil into the Holy of Holies; as forerunner he has been prepared a place for us, and is to intercede for us, lest we fail in the course, appointed by the Father a priest for ever, after the order of Melchizedek. Therefore you Hebrew believers ought to persevere with confidence in the faith of the Gospel.

units.la: Caput Septimum.
units.tr: Chapter 7.

units.la: Prosequitur institutum sermonem de Melchisedeco hoc Capite, & simul etiam doctrinam de excellentia Christi 1. Capitis duæ sunt partes: In prima probat excellentiam Christi supra Levitticos Sacerdotes respectu personæ, ad vers. 11. In secunda excellentiam Christi supra eosdem respectu officii Sacerdotalis, ad finem. Proponitur dignitas personæ Christi, partim in descriptione typica Melchisedeci, partim in Argumentis inde deductis. Omnes autem partes descriptionis de Melchisedeco typicè accipiendæ sunt, de Christo autem verè & propriè intelligendæ, ut ex fine versus tertii apparet. Notæ excellentiæ personæ Christi typicè propositæ, sunt tresdecim.
units.tr: In this chapter he pursues the argument he began about Melchizedek, and at the same time the teaching about the excellence of Christ from chapter 1. The chapter has two parts. In the first, up to verse 11, he proves that Christ is superior to the Levitical priests with respect to his person. In the second, from there to the end, he proves that Christ is superior to them with respect to the priestly office. The dignity of Christ's person is set forth partly in the typical description of Melchizedek and partly in the arguments drawn from it. All parts of the description must be taken typically, but they are to be understood truly and properly of Christ, as the end of verse 3 shows. There are thirteen notes of the excellence of Christ's person set forth typically.

units.la: Vers 1. NAM hic Melchisedec rex erat Salem, Pontifex Dei altissimi, qui occurrit Abrahæ revertenti à cæde regum, & benedixit ei:
units.tr: Verse 1. For this Melchizedek, king of Salem, priest of the most high God, met Abraham as he returned from the slaughter of the kings, and blessed him.

units.la: Nota prima, Ut Melchisedecus Rex erat in typo, sic Christus rex est proprie. Sacerdos ] Nota 2. Ut Melchisedecus Sacerdos Dei altissimi erat typicè, Sic Christus Sacerdos Dei altissimi, proprie & Deus ipse altissimus est.
units.tr: First note: as Melchizedek was king in the type, so Christ is king in the proper sense. Priest: Second note: as Melchizedek was typically the priest of the most high God, so Christ is the priest of the most high God, properly, and is himself the most high God.

units.la: Occurrit ] Nota 3. Ut revertenti Abrahamo à cæde regum occurrit Melchisedecus, & benedixit ei, ut typus Christi: Sic Christus is est qui solus potest efficaciter benedicere credentibus in eum.
units.tr: Met: Third note: as Melchizedek met Abraham returning from the slaughter of the kings and blessed him, as a type of Christ, so Christ is the one who alone can effectively bless those who believe in him.

units.la: Vers. 2. Cui & decimas ex omnibus impartitus est Abraham qui primum quidem ex interpretatione dicitur rex justitiæ, deinde verò etiam rex Salem: quod est rex pacis.
units.tr: Verse 2. To him also Abraham gave a tenth of all, he who is first, by interpretation, king of righteousness, and then also king of Salem, which is king of peace.

units.la: Nota 4. Sicut Abrahamus Melchisedecum agnovit per oblationem decimæ unius, quæ Deo proprie debentur, Sacerdotem & Christi venturi typum fuisse: Sic etiam in eo agnovit Christum Sacerdotem Dei esse, & Deum in typo repræsentatum.
units.tr: Fourth note: just as Abraham recognised Melchizedek, through the offering of a tenth, which is properly owed to God, as a priest and a type of the coming Christ, so also in him he recognised Christ as the priest of God, and God represented in a type.

units.la: Primum ] Nota 5. Sicut Melchisedecus in typo, sic Christus in veritate, est primum Rex Justitiæ, donans justitiam (nam id significat Melchisedec Rex) deinde Rex Salem, id est, pacis, seu donans pacem, quæ sequitur justitiam per fidem imputatam.
units.tr: First: Fifth note: as Melchizedek in the type, so Christ in truth is first king of righteousness, bestowing righteousness (for this is what the name Melchizedek, king, means), and then king of Salem, that is, of peace, or bestowing peace, which follows righteousness imputed through faith.

units.la: Vers. 3. Sine Patre, sine Matre, sine genere: nec initium dierum, neque vitæ finem habens: sed assimilatus Filio Dei, manet Sacerdos in perpetuum.
units.tr: Verse 3. Without father, without mother, without genealogy, having neither beginning of days nor end of life, but made like to the Son of God, he remains a priest for ever.

units.la: Nota 6. Sicut Melchisedecus in statu typico, & in esse historico, est sine Patre: Sic Christus qua homo ex virgine natus vere est sine Patre.
units.tr: Sixth note: as Melchizedek, in his typical state and in his historical existence, is without father, so Christ, as man born of a virgin, is truly without father.

units.la: Matre ] Nota 7. Sicut Melchisedecus in typo, sic Christus in rei veritate ut DEVS, est sine matre.
units.tr: Mother: Seventh note: as Melchizedek is in the type, so Christ in the reality of the matter, as God, is without mother.

units.la: Genere ] Nota 8. Ut Melchisedecus in esse suo historico & typico: sic Christus ut Deus in rei veritate, est sine genere seu genealogia, expers omnis cognationis, & consanguinitatis naturalis, seu terrenæ. Nec in
units.tr: Genealogy: Eighth note: as Melchizedek in his historical and typical existence, so Christ as God in the reality of the matter is without genealogy, that is, without ancestry, free of all natural or earthly kinship and blood relation. Nor in

units.la: Nec in
units.tr: Nor in

units.la: Nota 9. Sicut Melchizedecus in statu historico & typico: Sic Christus verè æternus est, sine principio dierum. & sine vitæ termino. Quamobrem nimis curiosè & audacter agere videntur, qui genealogiam Melchizedeci à Deo de industria cœlitam, scrutari & definire audent, etiam ex Scripturâ.
units.tr: Ninth note: as Melchizedek in his historical and typical state, so Christ is truly eternal, without beginning of days and without end of life. Therefore those seem to act too curiously and boldly who venture to search out and define, even from Scripture, the genealogy of Melchizedek, which God deliberately passed over in silence.

units.la: Ut comparatio hæc solida agnoscatur, Apostolus has omnes descriptionis partes, typicè, & in assimilatione illa quâ repræsentabat Filium Dei Sacerdotem æternum ostendit esse concipiendas.
units.tr: So that this comparison may be recognised as sound, the Apostle shows that all these parts of the description are to be understood typically, and in that likeness by which he represented the Son of God as an eternal priest.

units.la: Verf. 4 Spectate verò quantus hic fuerit, cui etiam Decimas spoliorum dederit Abraham patriarcha.
units.tr: Verse 4. But consider how great this man was, to whom even Abraham the patriarch gave a tenth of the spoils.

units.la: Sicut Abraham, licet victor in prælio adversùs tot Reges, & Patriarcha, seu princeps Patrum nobilissimus, in spoliorum decimis persolvendis, agnovit tamen Melchizedecum superiorem se esse, nempe quia Melchizedecus typus erat Christi. Sic Christum typo ito repræsentatum multò se superiorem agnovit necessariò.
units.tr: Although Abraham, victor in battle against so many kings, and a patriarch, or the most noble prince of the fathers, nevertheless, in paying the tenth of the spoils, acknowledged Melchizedek to be superior to himself, namely because Melchizedek was a type of Christ. So Abraham necessarily acknowledged that Christ, represented in that type, was far superior to himself.

units.la: Verf. 5. Et ii quidem qui sunt ex filiis Levi, sacerdotio fungentes, præceptum habent decimarum accipiendarum à populo secundum Legem, hoc est, à fratribus suis, licet egressis ex lumbis Abrahæ.
units.tr: Verse 5. Indeed those of the sons of Levi who hold the priesthood have a commandment to take tithes from the people according to the Law, that is, from their brothers, although these have come out of the loins of Abraham.

units.la: Hanc notam esse excellentiæ, probat Apostolus ex eo, quod Levi hoc ipso nomine superior fit fratribus suis, quia secundum Dei mandatum, acceperat decimas à fratribus: Ergo propter eandem rationem superior est Melchizedec Abrahamo, qui ultro decimas offerendo se inferiorem agnovit Melchizedeco.
units.tr: The Apostle proves that this is a mark of excellence from the fact that Levi, by this very name, is superior to his brothers, because by God's command he received tithes from his brothers. Therefore, for the same reason, Melchizedek is superior to Abraham, who, by offering tithes of his own accord, acknowledged himself inferior to Melchizedek.

units.la: Verf. 6 Is vero cuius genus ad illos non refertur, decimas accepit ab Abraham, & habenti promissiones, benedixit.
units.tr: Verse 6. But he whose lineage is not reckoned among them received tithes from Abraham, and blessed the one who had the promises.
