units.la: Melchizedecus qui in Levitarum genere non est censendus, non tantum accepit decimas ab Abrahamo, sed etiam ut superior, Abrahamo benedixit, ipsi (inquam) Abrahamo, qui omnium Fideliun nomine, primus accepit promissiones: Ergo Christus (cujus ille typus & umbra tantum fuit) multò est excellentior & Abrahamo, & Leviticis omnibus Sacerdotibus ab ipso oriundis.
units.tr: Melchizedek, who is not to be counted in the lineage of the Levites, not only received tithes from Abraham but also, as the superior, blessed Abraham himself, I say, Abraham, who, in the name of all the faithful, was first to receive the promises. Therefore Christ, of whom Melchizedek was only a type and shadow, is far more excellent than Abraham and than all the Levitical priests descended from him.

units.la: Verf. 7. Porrò sine ulla controversia, id quod minus est, ab eo quod majus est, benedicitur.
units.tr: Verse 7. Moreover, beyond all dispute, the lesser is blessed by the greater.

units.la: Hanc esse notam excellentiæ probat, ex eo quod extra controversiam fit, benedici minorem à majori. Quod non intelligendum est de benedictione one laudis quâ benedicimus Deo, nec de benedictione charitatis, quâ alii aliis bona precamur, sed de benedictione potestatis, quâ Deus efficaciter suis benedicit, vel autoritatis sive ordinariæ, qua Pastores & parentes ex officio communiter, sive extraordinariæ, quâ Dei legati extra ordinem, ex speciali legatione specialiter precando applicant Dei benedictionem alicui: In hoc genere benedicens quâ talis, major est eo cui benedicitur.
units.tr: He proves that this is a mark of excellence from the fact that it is beyond controversy that the lesser is blessed by the greater. This must not be understood of the blessing of praise, by which we bless God, nor of the blessing of charity, by which we wish good things to one another, but of the blessing of power, by which God effectively blesses his own, or of authority, whether ordinary, as when ministers and parents bless in the ordinary course of their office, or extraordinary, as when the ambassadors of God, by special commission, specifically apply God's blessing to someone by praying. In this kind, one who blesses, as such, is greater than the one who is blessed.

units.la: Vers. 8. Atque hic quidem homines qui moriuntur, decimas accipiunt: illic autem is de quo testatum est quòd vivat.
units.tr: Verse 8. And here indeed mortal men receive tithes, but there he of whom it is witnessed that he lives.

units.la: Nota 12. Melchizedecus, licet nec in statu physico, nec in statu civili, in statu tamen typico & scripturali, decimas accipit, ut semper vivens, ut Dei immortalis imago: Levitæ vero decimas recipiunt, ut homines mortales. Ergo Christus per Melchizedecum repræsentatus, qui natura est Deus verè immortalis, cum Levitis comparatus, multo iis excellentior est.
units.tr: Twelfth note: Melchizedek, although he is not in the physical state nor in the civil state, nevertheless in the typical and scriptural state receives tithes as ever living, as the image of the immortal God. The Levites, however, receive tithes as mortal men. Therefore Christ, represented through Melchizedek, who by nature is truly immortal God, when compared with the Levites, is far more excellent than they.

units.la: Vers. 9. Et (ut ita loquar) in Abraham decimatus est etiam ipse Levi, qui decimas solet accipere. Vers. 10. Nam is adhuc in lumbis patris erat, quum occurreret Abrahæ Melchisedec.
units.tr: Verse 9. And, so to speak, Levi himself, who is accustomed to receive tithes, paid tithes through Abraham. Verse 10. For he was still in the loins of his father when Melchizedek met Abraham.

units.la: Nota 13. Melchizedecus qua typus Christi, & per consequens ipse Christus qui veritas, erat in Melchizedeco repræsentata, accepit decimas non tantùm ab ipso Abrahamo, sed etiam à Levi, qui fuit in lumbis Abrahæ, secundùm rationem naturalis generationis, quando decimas obtulit Abraham Melchizedeco, & Christo per ipsum repræsentato: Ergo verus Melchizedecus, Christus, & in se, & cum Levitis comparatus, multò est illis excellentior. Verum quidem est Christum etiam ex semine Abrahami oriundum fuisse, quando Abraham decimas obtulit Melchizedeco, sed non erat ab eo oriundus secundum rationem æterni Sacerdotii Mediatoris, de quo hic agitur, nec secundùm rationem naturalis generationis, neque secundum rationem personæ simpliciter, sed tantùm secundum humanam naturam, secundum materiam carnis, in qua licet Christus Sacerdotium administraturus erat, non tamen ut homo merus, instar Levitarum, sed ut Θεὸς ἀνθρώπῳ Abrahami Deus, & Mediator inter Deum & Abrahamum, quo respectu Christus non continetur in Abrahamo, sed opponitur in typo Melchizedeci, & Abrahamo, & omnibus aliis ab eo oriundis, ut superior illis & excellentior. Tenet ergo Argumentum firmiter.
units.tr: Thirteenth note: Melchizedek, as a type of Christ, and consequently Christ himself, who is the truth, was represented in Melchizedek, and received tithes not only from Abraham himself but also from Levi, who was in the loins of Abraham, according to the reasoning of natural generation, when Abraham offered tithes to Melchizedek, and to Christ represented through him. Therefore the true Melchizedek, Christ, both in himself and when compared with the Levites, is far more excellent than they. It is true that Christ too was descended from the seed of Abraham when Abraham offered tithes to Melchizedek, but he was not descended from him according to the reasoning of the eternal priesthood of the Mediator, which is what is discussed here, nor according to the reasoning of natural generation, nor according to the reasoning of the person simply, but only according to human nature, according to the matter of the flesh. In that flesh, although Christ was to administer the priesthood, he was not to do so as a mere man, like the Levites, but as God-man [Θεὸς ἀνθρώπῳ], the God of Abraham, and Mediator between God and Abraham. In this respect Christ is not contained in Abraham but is set over against Abraham, and against all others descended from him, in the type of Melchizedek, as superior and more excellent than they. The argument therefore holds firmly.

units.la: Vers. 11. Porrò si consummatio per Leviticum Sacerdotium erat, (nam sub hoc sancita Lex est populo) quid amplius erat opus alium exoriri Sacerdotem secundum ordinem Melchisedec, nec secundum ordinem Aaronis dici?
units.tr: Verse 11. Moreover, if perfection came through the Levitical priesthood (for the law was sanctioned to the people under it), what further need was there for another priest to arise according to the order of Melchizedek, and not to be called according to the order of Aaron?

units.la: Fuit excellentia personæ Christi, Sequitur altera pars Capitis, in qua probatur excellentia Sacerdotii Christi supra Leviticum, idque Argumentis septemdecim. Arg. 1. Perfectio, seu efficax consummatio cultorum Dei, quoad peccati expiationem, justificationem, sanctificationem, & vitam æternam, non potuit obtineri per Leviticum Sacerdotium. Ergo imperfectum est Leviticum Sacerdotium; neque tam excellens quam Christi Sacerdotium.
units.tr: That was the excellence of Christ's person. The second part of the chapter follows, in which the excellence of Christ's priesthood above the Levitical is proved, and this by seventeen arguments. Argument 1. Perfection, or the effective fulfilment of God's worshippers as regards the expiation of sin, justification, sanctification and eternal life, could not be obtained through the Levitical priesthood. Therefore the Levitical priesthood is imperfect and not as excellent as Christ's priesthood.

units.la: Quid amplius ] Arg. 2 confirmans superius, Si perfectio obtineri potuisset per Sacerdotium Leviticum, non opus fuisset alium præstantiorem Sacerdotem oriri, nempe Christum secundum ordinem Melchizedeci, & non secundum ordinem Aaronis. Assumptionem nobis relinquit colligendam, quæ hæc est, At opus fuit ut oriretur præstantior Sacerdos, ut patet ex Psalmo 110: Ergo perfectio per Sacerdotium Leviticum obtineri non potuit, sed per Sacerdotium Christi, quod idcirco excellentius est.
units.tr: Quid amplius] Argument 2, confirming what was said above. If perfection could have been obtained through the Levitical priesthood, there would have been no need for another, more excellent priest to arise, namely Christ according to the order of Melchizedek and not according to the order of Aaron. He leaves us to gather the assumption for ourselves, which is this: but there was need for a more excellent priest to arise, as is evident from Psalm 110. Therefore perfection could not be obtained through the Levitical priesthood, but through Christ's priesthood, which is for this reason more excellent.

units.la: Populus enim ] Ratio confirmans majorem connexam, Sub hoc Sacerdotio Lex data est & populus in eius disciplina exercitatus est: & quicquid virium Lex, seu legalis Fœdus habebat, huc totum collatum est à Legis zelotis, ut cultores per hoc Sacerdotium perficerentur, sed frustra. Ergo si per hoc Sacerdotium, vel per Legem, seu legale Fœdus cum eo junctum obtineri potuisset perfectio cultorum, non opus fuisset Sacerdotio præstantiori, & Lege alia: cum vero perfectio per hoc Sacerdotium obtineri non potuerit, opus fuit alio præstantiori necessario.
units.tr: Populus enim] A reason confirming the connected major premise. Under this priesthood the law was given, and the people were trained in its discipline. Whatever strength the Law, or the legal covenant, had was all brought to bear by the zealots of the Law, so that worshippers might be perfected through this priesthood, but in vain. Therefore, if the perfection of worshippers could have been obtained through this priesthood, or through the Law, or the legal covenant joined with it, there would have been no need for a more excellent priesthood and another Law. But since perfection could not be obtained through this priesthood, a more excellent one was necessarily needed.

units.la: Vers. 12. Mutato igitur Sacerdotio, necesse quoque est ut fiat mutatio legis.
units.tr: Verse 12. Therefore, the priesthood being changed, it is necessary also that there be a change of the law.

units.la: Arg. 3 Simul etiam probans Christum exoriturum Sacerdotem, secundum ordinem Melchizedec, non denominandum secundum ordinem Aaronis, nec legi Leviticæ obnoxium. Sacerdotii Levitici mutabilitas & mutatio, secum traxit legis Leviticæ, seu fœderis legalis cum eo conjuncti, mutabilitatem & mutationem, ut succederet aliud Sacerdotium, & alia lex, seu aliud foedus immutabile. Ergo Leviticum Sacerdotium mutabile non tam excellens est quam Melchisedeci, seu Christi Sacerdotium immutabile.
units.tr: Argument 3, at the same time proving that Christ is to arise as a priest according to the order of Melchizedek, not to be named according to the order of Aaron, nor subject to the Levitical law. The mutability and change of the Levitical priesthood brought with it the mutability and change of the Levitical law, or of the legal covenant joined with it, so that another priesthood and another law, or another, unchangeable covenant, might succeed. Therefore the Levitical priesthood, being mutable, is not as excellent as the priesthood of Melchizedek, or of Christ, which is immutable.

units.la: Vers. 13. Nam is de quo haec dicuntur, ad aliam tribum pertinet, de qua nullus attendit altari.
units.tr: Verse 13. For he of whom these things are said belongs to another tribe, from which no one has attended at the altar.

units.la: Vers. 14. Talam est enim e tribu Juda exortum esse Dominum nostrum: cujus tribus respectu nihil de Sacerdotio loquutus est Moses.
units.tr: Verse 14. For it is evident that our Lord arose from the tribe of Judah, concerning which tribe Moses said nothing about priesthood.

units.la: Arg. 4 Simul probans mutato Sacerdotio Levitico mutandam etiam esse legem Leviticam. CHRISTUS de quo haec dicuntur in Psalmo 110. Pertinet ad aliam tribum, eamque principem & dignissimam, nempe Judah, (unde constat Dominum nostrum ortum esse) ex qua nullus attendit altari, nullus praeceptum habet a Mose de exercendo Sacerdotio Levitico. Ergo introducto CHRISTI Sacerdotio abolendum est Sacerdotium Leviticum, cum Lege Ceremoniali Levitica, & per consequens Sacerdotium CHRISTI, de principe tribu oriundi, praestantius est Levitico.
units.tr: Argument 4, at the same time proving that when the Levitical priesthood is changed, the Levitical law must also be changed. CHRIST, of whom these things are said in Psalm 110, belongs to another tribe, and that a principal and most worthy one, namely Judah (from which it is established that our Lord arose), from which no one has attended at the altar, and no one has a command from Moses to exercise the Levitical priesthood. Therefore, with the introduction of Christ's priesthood, the Levitical priesthood must be abolished, along with the Levitical Ceremonial Law; and consequently Christ's priesthood, being of the principal tribe, is more excellent than the Levitical.

units.la: Vers. 15. Itaque etiam magis patet ex eo quod ad instar Melchisedec exoritur Sacerdos alius.
units.tr: Verse 15. And it is yet more evident from the fact that after the likeness of Melchizedek another priest arises.

units.la: Arg. 5. Ex verbis, Psal. 110. idem probans quod prius, CHRISTUS est alius Sacerdos a Leviticis, inter quem & Melchisedecum ipsius typum est similitudo. Sequitur ergo & non pendere CHRISTI Sacerdotium a lege Levitica, & simul etiam quia Melchizedecianum est, Sacerdotio Levitico longe praestantius esse.
units.tr: Argument 5, from the words of Psalm 110, proving the same as before: Christ is a priest other than the Levitical ones, and between him and Melchizedek, Melchizedek being his type, there is a likeness. It follows that Christ's priesthood does not depend on the Levitical law, and at the same time, because it is Melchizedekian, it is far more excellent than the Levitical priesthood.

units.la: Vers. 16. Qui non ex lege, cujus mandatum sit carnale, factus est Sacerdos sed ex vi indissolubilis vita.
units.tr: Verse 16. Who has become priest not by a law whose commandment is carnal, but by the power of an indissoluble life.

units.la: Arg. 6. CHRISTUS factus est Sacerdos, non secundum legem quae dabat mandata infirma & carnalia, de corporalibus Ceremoniis, sicut Levitici Sacerdotes, sed secundum virtutem & potentiam vitae immortalis seu indissolubilis, qua CHRISTUS in aeternum ipse vivens, & vitae autor poslet suis vitam aeternam efficaciter conferre: Ergo CHRISTI Sacerdotium excellentius est Levitico.
units.tr: Argument 6. Christ became priest not according to the law, which gave weak and carnal commandments about bodily ceremonies, as the Levitical priests did, but according to the virtue and power of an immortal or indissoluble life, by which Christ, living for ever and the author of life, is able to confer eternal life effectively on his own. Therefore Christ's priesthood is more excellent than the Levitical.

units.la: Vers. 17. Testificatur enim ad hunc modum, Tu es Sacerdos in aeternum, secundum ordinem Melchisedec. Hoc argumentum confirmat, ex Pfal. 110. In quo Pater pronunciat Filium suum Sacerdotem in aeternum secundum ordinem Melchizedeci, & per consequens declarat vim Sacerdotii Christi, ad aeternam vitam cultoribus ipsius sufficere.
units.tr: Verse 17. For it is testified in this way: You are a priest for ever, according to the order of Melchizedek. This argument is confirmed from Psalm 110, in which the Father declares his Son to be a priest for ever according to the order of Melchizedek, and consequently declares that the power of Christ's priesthood is sufficient for eternal life for its worshippers.

units.la: Verf. 18. Nam mandatum praecedens abrogatur, quod nullis viribus sit praditum, & inutile.
units.tr: Verse 18. For the preceding commandment is abrogated, because it was endowed with no strength and was useless.

units.la: Arg. 7. ex eodem Psalmo deductum. Lex seu foedus legale, (cum mandatis ceremonialibus, totoque Sacerdotio Levitico foederi isti conjunctis,) propter infirmitatem & inutilitatem ipsius in se, ad peccatorum expiationem, ad justificationem hominum, & vitam aeternam conferendam, aboletur per introductionem Sacerdotii aeterni, Christi videlicet. Ergo Christi Sacerdotium praestantius est illo Levitico.
units.tr: Argument 7, drawn from the same Psalm. The Law or legal covenant (with the ceremonial commandments and the whole Levitical priesthood joined to that covenant), because of its own weakness and uselessness in conferring the expiation of sins, the justification of men and eternal life, is abolished by the introduction of the eternal priesthood, namely Christ's. Therefore Christ's priesthood is more excellent than that Levitical one.

units.la: Verf. 19. Nihil enim sanctificavit Lex, sed adscita spes melior, per quam appropinquamus Deo.
units.tr: Verse 19. For the law made nothing perfect, but a better hope is introduced, through which we draw near to God.

units.la: Arg, 8. confirmans priorem. Lex seu foedus legale, sub Sacerdotio Levitico, licet paedagogus fuerit quidem ad Christum; per se tamen nihil perficiebat, nullum justificabat sanctificabat, vel servabat. Sed Sacerdotium Christi, spes illa melior, seu Evangelium, bonum illud praefiguratum, & speratum a fidelibus sub lege, in locum Sacerdotii Levitici, seu legalis foederis, jam introductum: Hoc, inquam, perfectionem affert Dei populo & bonam spem vitae nobis facit. Ergo Christi Sacerdotium est excellentius Levitico.
units.tr: Argument 8, confirming the former. The Law or legal covenant under the Levitical priesthood, although it was indeed a schoolmaster to Christ, nevertheless of itself perfected nothing, and justified, sanctified or preserved no one. But Christ's priesthood, that better hope, or the Gospel, the good thing prefigured and hoped for by the faithful under the law, now introduced in place of the Levitical priesthood or legal covenant: this, I say, brings perfection to God's people and gives us a good hope of life. Therefore Christ's priesthood is more excellent than the Levitical.

units.la: Per quam ] Arg. 9. Per Sacerdotium Christi, (seu per spem illam lege & Sacerdotio Levitico meliorem,) nos qui per naturam longe distamus a Deo, prope accedimus omnes ad Deum, ad Thronum gratiae ejus; quod privilegium erat Sacerdotum tantum, vel summi Sacerdotis potius, sub legalibus typis, Ergo excellentius est Christi sacerdotium Legali seu Levitico.
units.tr: Through which] Argument 9. Through Christ's priesthood (or through that hope better than the law and the Levitical priesthood) we, who by nature are far from God, all draw near to God, to the throne of his grace. This privilege belonged only to the priests, or rather to the high priest, under the legal types. Therefore Christ's priesthood is more excellent than the legal or Levitical.

units.la: Verf. 20. Et jam quatenus non absque jurejurando.
units.tr: Verse 20. And inasmuch as it was not without an oath.

units.la: Verf. 21. Nam illi quidem, citra jusjurandum Sacerdotes facti sunt; (hic vero cum jurejurando, per eum qui dixit ei, Jurav t Dominus, & non poenitebit eum, Tu es Sacerdos in aeternum secundum ordinem Melchizedec.)
units.tr: Verse 21. For those indeed were made priests without an oath; but this one with an oath, by him who said to him: The Lord has sworn, and will not repent, You are a priest for ever according to the order of Melchizedek.

units.la: Arg. 10. Sacerdotes Levitici, citra jusjurandum per legem ex voluntate legislatoris mutabilem, facti sunt Sacerdotes: Christus vero ut ex Pfal. 110. Psal. 110. constat, pronunciatur Sacerdos æternus ex juramento Dei Patris: Ergo Sacerdotium Christi excellentius est Levitico.
units.tr: Argument 10. The Levitical priests were made priests without an oath, by law, which was changeable at the will of the lawgiver. But Christ, as is established from Psalm 110, Psalm 110, is pronounced an eternal priest by the oath of God the Father. Therefore Christ's priesthood is more excellent than the Levitical.

units.la: Vers. 22. Tanto potioris fœderis sponsor factus est Jesus.
units.tr: Verse 22. By so much better a covenant has Jesus become surety.

units.la: Arg. 11. Christus in Sacerdotio suo tanto præstantioris fœderis sponsor est, quantò Sacerdotium juramento confirmatum, præstantius est Sacerdotio imperato ad tempus, & mutabili, Ergo ejus Sacerdotium est præstantius. Nam ubi Sacerdos, ibi est fœdus, cujus fœderis sponsor est Sacerdos; fœdus legale & umbratile, sponsorem habebat Sacerdotem typicum & umbratilem, qui præfigurabat verum Sacerdotem Christum venturum: Fœdus vero gratiæ habet Christum verum Sacerdotem sponsorem, qui primo se obligavit ad satisfactionem divinæ justitiæ præstandam pro debito nostro, deinde fore ut tanquam Dei amici in fœdere gratiæ ambularemus, ad vitam æternam. Aliæ etiam sunt sponsionis partes, sed hæ sufficiunt ad præsens argumentum explicandum.
units.tr: Argument 11. Christ in his priesthood is surety of a covenant so much better, as a priesthood confirmed by oath is more excellent than a priesthood imposed for a time and changeable. Therefore his priesthood is more excellent. For where there is a priest, there is a covenant, of which the priest is surety. The legal and shadowy covenant had as its surety a typical and shadowy priest, who prefigured the true priest Christ who was to come; but the covenant of grace has Christ, the true priest, as surety. He first bound himself to render satisfaction to divine justice for our debt, and then that we should walk in the covenant of grace as God's friends unto eternal life. There are other parts of this suretyship too, but these suffice for explaining the present argument.

units.la: Vers. 23. Et illi quidem, plures facti sunt Sacerdotes, quod mors prohiberet eos permanere:
units.tr: Verse 23. And indeed those were made priests in greater number, because death prevented them from remaining.

units.la: Vers. 24. At iste propterea quod in æternum maneat, perpetuum habet Sacerdotium.
units.tr: Verse 24. But this one, because he remains for ever, has a perpetual priesthood.

units.la: Arg. 12. Sacerdotes Levitici simul plures erant, & successivè alii aliis morte sublatis succedebant: nam unus omnia subire solus non poterat, & mors prohibebat, ne diu ullus in officio permaneret. Sed Christus solus Sacerdotio suo præest in æternum, nullo Collega vel Successore vel substituto indigens: Ergo Sacerdotium ejus præstantius est Levitico.
units.tr: Argument 12. The Levitical priests were many at the same time, and when one died others succeeded him one after another. A single man could not perform all the duties alone, and death prevented anyone from remaining long in office. But Christ alone presides over his priesthood forever, needing no colleague, successor or substitute. Therefore his priesthood is more excellent than the Levitical.

units.la: Vers. 25. Unde & servare prorsus potest eos qui per ipsum accedunt ad Deum, semper vivens ut interpellet pro eis.
units.tr: Verse 25. Wherefore he is able also to save them to the uttermost that come unto God by him, seeing he ever liveth to make intercession for them.

units.la: Arg. 13. ex priori tanquam consectarium deductum, Noster Sacerdos Christus, semper vivendo, & odore perpetuo sui sacrificii intercedendo pro suis, prorsus servare & perficere potest, seu omnibus numeris absolutam dare, sanctificationem, & salutem omnium Fidelium, seu accedentium ad Deum per eum. At Levitici Sacerdotes id non potuerunt. Ergo Sacerdotium ejus præstantius est Levitico.
units.tr: Argument 13, deduced as a consequence of the previous one: our priest Christ, by living forever and by interceding for his people with the continual fragrance of his sacrifice, is able to save and to perfect completely, that is, to give complete sanctification and salvation in every respect to all the faithful, or to all who come to God through him. But the Levitical priests could not do this. Therefore his priesthood is more excellent than the Levitical.

units.la: Vers. 26. Talis enim nos decebat Pontifex, pius, innocens, impollutus, segregatus à peccatoribus, & sublimior Cœlis factus:
units.tr: Verse 26. For such an high priest became us, who is holy, harmless, undefiled, separate from sinners, and made higher than the heavens;

units.la: Arg. 14. Christus Sacerdos, sicut decebat unicum nostrum Redemptorem personæ suæ qualitates excellentiores, & statum seu conditionem excellentiorem habet, quam ullus ex Leviticis. Ergo ejus Sacerdotium est excellentius: Quod ad qualitatem personæ: 1. Sanctus est, & natura sua, & voto suo, in Dei Patris honorem totus consecratus: 2. Innocens est qui nulli homini nec ulli creaturæ faciat injuriam: 3. Impollutus est, Primo à pollutione seu labe omnis peccati, & sui & alieni immunis: 4. Segregatus à peccatoribus, id est, nullo modo obnoxius peccato, vel adeo remotus à peccato, ut peccator esse non possit.
units.tr: Argument 14. Christ the priest: as it befitted our only Redeemer, he has qualities of person more excellent, and a status or condition more excellent, than any of the Levitical priests. Therefore his priesthood is more excellent. As to the qualities of his person: (1) he is holy, both by his nature and by his will, wholly consecrated to the honour of God the Father; (2) he is harmless, who does no injury to any man or any creature; (3) he is undefiled, first, free from the pollution or stain of every sin, both his own and that of others; (4) he is separate from sinners, that is, in no way liable to sin, or so far removed from sin that he cannot be a sinner.

units.la: Quod ad statum seu conditionem personæ attinet, sublimior est cœlis omnibusque in cœlo creaturis, nam etiam corpore suo evectus supra Cœlos aspectabiles, ad societatem Throni cum Patre exaltatus est.
units.tr: As to the status or condition of his person, he is higher than the heavens and all the creatures in heaven, for even in his body he has been carried above the visible heavens and exalted to share the throne with the Father.

units.la: Verf. 27. Cui non sit quotidie necesse, quemadmodum illi pontificibus, prius pro peccatis propriis victimas offerre, deinde pro peccatis populi: id enim fecit semel quum semetipsum obtulit.
units.tr: Verse 27. Who needeth not daily, as those high priests, to offer up sacrifice, first for his own sins, and then for the people's: for this he did once, when he offered up himself.

units.la: Arg. 15. ex priori consequens, Non est Christo imposita necessitas offerendi victimam pro peccatis suis, quæ nulla habuit, nec offerendi victimam sæpius pro peccatis populi; nam semel obtulisse seipsum sufficit: Sacerdotibus vero Leviticis necesse erat & pro suis peccatis, & peccatis populi quotidie offerre. Ergo ejus Sacerdotium præstantius est Levitico.
units.tr: Argument 15, following from the previous one: Christ was not under any necessity of offering a victim for his own sins, for he had none, nor of offering a victim often for the sins of the people, since it is enough that he offered himself once. But the Levitical priests were obliged to offer daily both for their own sins and for the sins of the people. Therefore his priesthood is more excellent than the Levitical.

units.la: Seipsum obtulit ] Arg. 16. Sacrificium Christi non erat pecudis vel animalis bruti alicujus, sed ipse obtulit seipsum & ad hoc sacrificium offerendum, nullus idoneus & dignus sacerdos esse potuit præter ipsum, ipse solus seipsum obtulit; Levitici vero Sacerdotes offerebant pecudes, quibus offerendis sufficiebant homines. Ergo Christi Sacerdotium Levitico excellentius est.
units.tr: He offered up himself: Argument 16. Christ's sacrifice was not that of a sheep or of some other brute animal, but he offered himself. No one else could be a fit and worthy priest to offer this sacrifice; he alone offered himself. The Levitical priests, however, offered sheep, and men were sufficient to offer them. Therefore the priesthood of Christ is more excellent than the Levitical.

units.la: Verf. 28. Lex enim homines constituit Pontifices infirmos: at sermo jurisjurandi post Legem concepti, Filium constituit qui in æternum est sanctificatus
units.tr: Verse 28. For the law maketh men high priests which have infirmity; but the word of the oath, which was since the law, maketh the Son, who is consecrated for evermore.

units.la: Arg. 17. A sextuplici differentia Levitici seu legalis Sacerdotii, & Euangelici seu Christi: Differentia prima, Constitutio Sacerdotis Levitici fluit à lege, quæ mutari potest: Constitutio vero Sacerdotis Euangelici seu Christi fluit à sermone jurisjurandi, qui mutari non potest, propter teft, propter jusjurandum Dei immutabile: Differentia 2. Lex Levitica admittit homines in plurali: Euangelium unum tantum CHRISTUM: Differentia 3. Lex admittit ut alius post alium succedor sit. Euangelium vero admittit, unicum tantum sine successore, nempe CHRISTUM Filium Dei: Differentia 4. Levitica lex admittit Sacerdotes homines, infirmitate laborantes, id est, peccato obnoxios, qui sacrificium suum non possunt efficax reddere ad Deum placandum, vel benedictionem quam pronunciant, reapse conferre in eos quibus benedicunt: Euangelicus vero sermo constituit Christum, qui Filius est Dei omnipotens, qui Sacerdotium suum in omnibus efficax poterit reddere: Differentia 5. Lex constituit Sacerdotes temporarios, qui consecrantur tantum in breve tempus vitæ suæ. Euangelium vero habet unicum filium qui in æternum consecratus est: Differentia 6. Lex Levitica præcessit, nec fuit lex, sententia Dei ultima, de Sacerdotibus: At Euangelium seu sermo juris-jurandi post legem successit, ut Dei sententia ultima: Ergo Sacerdotium CHRISTI excellentius est Levitico. Huc omnia tendunt ut Hebraei fideles, perspecta Sacerdotii Levitici infirmitate, & abolitione, & CHRISTI Sacerdotii excellentia, legalibus ritibus renunciarent, & Christo firmius adhærerent.
units.tr: Argument 17, from a sixfold difference between the Levitical or legal priesthood and the Gospel or Christ's priesthood. The first difference: the appointment of the Levitical priest flows from the law, which can be changed; but the appointment of the Gospel priest, that is Christ, flows from the word of the oath, which cannot be changed, being God's immutable oath. The second: the Levitical law admits men in the plural, while the Gospel admits only one, CHRIST. The third: the law admits that one should succeed another, but the Gospel admits only one, without a successor, namely CHRIST the Son of God. The fourth: the Levitical law admits priests who are men burdened with infirmity, that is, liable to sin, who cannot make their sacrifice effective in appeasing God, or make the blessing they pronounce really benefit those whom they bless; but the Gospel word appoints Christ, who is the almighty Son of God, who will be able to make his priesthood effective in all things. The fifth: the law appoints temporary priests, who are consecrated only for the brief time of their lives; but the Gospel has one Son, who is consecrated forever. The sixth: the Levitical law came first, and was not the last word of God concerning priests; but the Gospel, or the word of the oath, came after the law, as God's final word. Therefore the priesthood of CHRIST is more excellent than the Levitical. All of this aims to make the faithful Hebrews, having clearly seen the infirmity and abolition of the Levitical priesthood and the excellence of Christ's priesthood, renounce the legal rites and cling more firmly to Christ.

units.la: Caput Octavum.
units.tr: Chapter 8.

units.la: Eem argumentum prosequitur. Capitis dua sunt partes: In prima probat excellentiam Sacerdotii Christi supra Levitticum; Argumentis quatuor, ad versl. 7. In secunda probat novum fœdus præstantius esse veteri. De tota autem capite præfatur, quod in eo summa totius comparationis inter Leviticum, & Christi Sacerdotium continetur.
units.tr: He pursues the same argument. The chapter has two parts: in the first he proves the excellence of Christ's priesthood above the Levitical, by four arguments, up to verse 7; in the second he proves that the new covenant is more excellent than the old. Concerning the whole chapter he states in advance that the sum of the whole comparison between the Levitical priesthood and Christ's priesthood is contained in it.

units.la: Cæterum eorum quæ dicimus hæc summa est, Talem nos habere Pontificem, qui consedit ad dextram throni Majestatis illius in Cœlis,
units.tr: Moreover, the sum of what we say is this: we have such a High Priest, who has sat down at the right hand of the throne of the Majesty in the heavens,

units.la: Argumentum primum, CHRISTUS noster Pontifex talis, & tantæ dignitatis est, ut consideat rex ad dextram Throni Majestatis Dei Patris in cœlis, pari cum Patre potestate & gloria: Relinquit nobis alteram comparationis partem, ut satis perspicuam, de Pontifice Levitico, quod non sit talis: Ergo præstantius est Christi Sacerdotium Levitico.
units.tr: First argument: Our Lord Christ is such a High Priest, of such dignity, that he sits as king at the right hand of the throne of the Majesty of God the Father in the heavens, with equal power and glory with the Father. The other part of the comparison remains, which is plain enough: that the Levitical high priest is not such. Therefore Christ's priesthood is more excellent than the Levitical.

units.la: Verf. 2. Sanctuarii minister, ac veri illius tabernaculi quod fixit Dominus, & non homo.
units.tr: Verse 2. A minister of the sanctuary and of the true tabernacle, which the Lord pitched, and not man.

units.la: Arg. 2. Christus Minister est illius Sanctuari in Cœlis, ubi sedet Rex in Throno, & rerum sanctarum omnium quæ ad cultum Dei, & salutem hominis pertinent, non otiosus Sacerdos, sed Sacerdotis partes strenuè agens in cœlis, licet pontifex regalis propter personæ dignitatem, & modum administrationis, ut Minister tamen propter officium Mediatoris. Tales non sunt Levitici Sacerdotes in terra, sed tantum Ministri: Ergo Christi Sacerdotium est excellentius Levitico.
units.tr: Second argument. Christ is the minister of that sanctuary in the heavens, where the King sits on the throne, and of all holy things which pertain to the worship of God and the salvation of man; he is not an idle priest, but acts the part of a priest vigorously in the heavens, though he is a royal high priest by reason of the dignity of his person and the manner of his administration, yet a minister by reason of the office of Mediator. Such are not the Levitical priests on earth, but only ministers. Therefore Christ's priesthood is more excellent than the Levitical.

units.la: Veri tabernaculi ] Arg. 3. Christus in cœlis est Minister veri illius tabernaculi, quod fixit Dominus & non homo, nempe corporis sui (quod ipse Christus comparavit tabernaculo) & quod per typicum figuratum est: quod Tabernaculum verum corporis sui, formavit & aptavit illi per miraculum Spiritus Sanctus in utero Virginis: Christus autem jam in cœlis ministrans repræsentat Patri corpus illud, & humanitatem suam, in qua passus est: eique offert continuo in illo corpore pro nobis intercedens. Sacerdotes vero Levitici Ministri sunt tantum typici Tabernaculi, quod homo ædificavit. Ergo Christi Sacerdotium excellentius est Levitico.
units.tr: The true tabernacle] Third argument. Christ in the heavens is the minister of the true tabernacle, which the Lord pitched and not man: namely of his own body (which Christ himself compared to a tabernacle), and which was foreshadowed by the typical tabernacle. This true tabernacle of his body the Holy Spirit formed and fitted for him by a miracle in the womb of the Virgin. But Christ, now ministering in the heavens, presents that body and his humanity, in which he suffered, to the Father, and continually offers it to him for us, interceding in that body. But the Levitical priests are ministers only of the typical tabernacle, which man built. Therefore Christ's priesthood is more excellent than the Levitical.

units.la: Verf. 3. Omnis enim Pontifex ad offerenda dona & victimas constituitur: unde necesse fuit hunc quoque habere quod offerret.
units.tr: Verse 3. For every high priest is appointed to offer gifts and sacrifices; hence it was necessary that this one also should have something to offer.

units.la: Probat Christum constanter offerre tabernaculum verum corporis sui Deo Patri, rationibus tribus: 1. Quia cum omnis Pontifex ad offerenda dona & victimas constituatur, necesse est etiam ut Christus habeat quod offerat, At præter intercessionem, & corporis sui sacrificati exhibitionem Patri, in Cœlo nihil habet Christus quod propitium reddat Deum. Ergo verum illud tabernaculum corporis sui solum est, quod Christus in Cœlesti Sanctuario Deo offert.
units.tr: He proves that Christ constantly offers the true tabernacle of his body to God the Father, by three reasons: (1) Since every high priest is appointed to offer gifts and sacrifices, it is necessary that Christ also have something to offer. But apart from his intercession and the presentation of his sacrificed body to the Father, Christ has in heaven nothing with which to render God propitious. Therefore that true tabernacle of his body is the only thing that Christ offers to God in the heavenly sanctuary.

units.la: Verf. 4. Nam si esset in terra, ne Sacerdos quidem esset, manentibus illis Sacerdotibus, qui secundum Legem offerunt dona.
units.tr: Verse 4. For if he were on earth, he would not even be a priest, since there are those who offer gifts according to the Law.

units.la: Ratio 2. Quia si esset in terra, non posset per legem esse Sacerdos ad offerendum scilicet quæ lex offerenda præscribit Sacerdotibus, dona nempe & sacrificia typica. Ergo verum illud tabernaculum corporis poris sui solum restat, quod CHRISTUS in Coelesti Sanctuario DEO offert.
units.tr: Reason 2. Because if he were on earth, he could not be a priest by the law, namely to offer what the law prescribes to the priests to offer, that is, the typical gifts and sacrifices. Therefore that true tabernacle of his body is the only thing left, which Christ offers to God in the heavenly sanctuary.

units.la: - Vers. 5. Ut qui exemplari & umbrę deserviunt rerum cælestium, sicut divinitus dictum est Mosi, quum esset absoluturus tabernaculum. Vide enim, inquit, ut facias omnia ad exemplar quod ostensum est tibi in monte.
units.tr: Verse 5. Who serve the copy and shadow of heavenly things, as Moses was divinely instructed when he was about to finish the tabernacle. For see, he says, that you make all things according to the pattern that was shown you on the mountain.

units.la: Ratio 3. confirmans etiam priorem. Quia Sacerdotes secundum legem, in terra deserviunt tantum exemplari, & umbrae rerum cœlestium; nam eorum Ministerium alligatur Tabernaculo, vel Templo Hierosolymitano, & exercetur in figuris & ceremoniis typicis administrandis, sicut probatur ex lege Levitica. Ergo CHRISTUS cum per legem non posset typica ulla sacrificia offerre, si esset in terra, neque posset esse Sacerdos per legem, & nunc in coelo cum sit, in eoque Sacerdotium suum exerceat, necesse est ut rem illam cœlestem per umbras illas legales figuratam, nempe Ceremoniarum omnium corpus, & substantiam administret. Id quod facit verum Tabernaculum corporis sui constanter DEO repræsentando, & beneficia spiritualia per corporis sui oblationem acquisita nobis dispensando. Testimonium ad probandum antecedens est Exod. 25. 40. ex quo sub nomine Tabernaculi, Deus vult non Tabernaculum tantum, sed etiam omnia quæ ad Leviticum sacerdotium pertinebant, repræsentationes esse rerum cœlestium, nimirum sacerdotii CHRISTI, & beneficiorum ejus.
units.tr: Reason 3, confirming also the former. Because the priests according to the law serve on earth only the copy and shadow of heavenly things; for their ministry is bound to the tabernacle or the Jerusalem temple, and is exercised in administering the typical figures and ceremonies, as is proved from the Levitical law. Therefore Christ, since by the law he could offer no typical sacrifices if he were on earth, nor could be a priest by the law, and now, since he is in heaven and exercises his priesthood there, it is necessary that he administer that heavenly reality, figured by those legal shadows, namely the whole body and substance of all the ceremonies. This he does by his true tabernacle, constantly representing it to God and dispensing to us the spiritual benefits acquired by the offering of his body. The testimony to prove the antecedent is Exod. 25. 40., from which, under the name of the tabernacle, God wills that not only the tabernacle but also all things which pertained to the Levitical priesthood are representations of heavenly things, namely of the priesthood of Christ and of his benefits.

units.la: Vers. 6. At nunc noster ille Pontifex eo excellentius ministerium sortitus est, quo præstantioris est fœderis intercessor, quod præstantioribus promissis sancitum est.
units.tr: Verse 6. But now that High Priest of ours has obtained a ministry as much more excellent as he is the mediator of a better covenant, which was established on better promises.

units.la: Arg. 4 Ad probandam excellentiam Sacerdotii CHRISTI supra Leviticum, à præstantia Fœderis novi, præ veteri. Quia CHRISTUS tanto excellentius Ministerium sortitus est præ Leviticis, quanto fœdus cujus CHRISTUS est Mediator præstantius est, & præstantioribus promissis sancitum, quam fuit fœdus sub Sacerdotio Levitico: Nam fœdus sub Sacerdotio Levitico, quoad externam ejus formam, erat fœdus operum, promissis conditionalibus rerum externarum sancitum: fœdus vero sub CHRISTI Sacerdotio partum, est fœdus gratiæ fidelibus, seu fœderatis, CHRISTUM cum omnibus beneficiis, gratis promittens. Sacerdotis autem officium est intercedere inter Deum & homines, & pacta inter eos conventa oblato sacrificio confirmare, tum operam dare, ut divinis promissis homines mines potiantur. Quare quanto pacta meliora fuerint, tanto Sacerdotium ipsum majoris censeri dignitatis, consentaneum est.
units.tr: Fourth argument. To prove the excellence of Christ's priesthood above the Levitical, from the excellence of the new covenant over the old. Christ has obtained a ministry as much more excellent than the Levitical as the covenant of which Christ is Mediator is more excellent, and established on better promises, than the covenant under the Levitical priesthood. For the covenant under the Levitical priesthood, as to its external form, was a covenant of works, established by conditional promises of external things; but the covenant brought forth under Christ's priesthood is a covenant of grace, freely promising Christ with all benefits to the faithful, that is, to those in covenant. Now the office of a priest is to intercede between God and men, and by the offering of a sacrifice to confirm the agreements made between them, and also to labour that men may obtain the divine promises. Hence it is fitting that the better the agreements, the greater the dignity of the priesthood itself is judged to be.

units.la: Secunda pars.
units.tr: The second part.

units.la: Verf. 7. Nam si prius illud tale fuisset, ut nihil in eo posset requiri, haud quaquam fuisset secundo quaesitum locus.
units.tr: Verse 7. For if that first covenant had been such that nothing could be found fault with in it, there would never have been occasion to seek a second.

units.la: Secunda pars Capitis, in qua hoc argumentum confirmat per partes & primum probat praestantius esse novum foedus Euangelicum veteri illo legali abolito, sex rationibus.
units.tr: The second part of the chapter, in which he confirms this argument by parts, and first proves that the new Evangelical covenant is more excellent than that old legal covenant, now abolished, by six reasons.

units.la: Nam si Ratio prima praesuppositta in connexa propositione, Prius foedus sub Sacerdotio Levitico fuit imperfectum, in quo aliquid desiderari vel reprehendi potuit, non respectu sui quidem, sed respectu efficaciae & virtutis, idque vitio non foederis, sed foederatorum impotentium: Ergo minus excellens erat prius foedus, quam novum hoc scilicet.
units.tr: For if The first reason, presupposed in the connected proposition: the earlier covenant under the Levitical priesthood was imperfect, and something in it could be wanting or found fault with, not indeed in respect of itself, but in respect of efficacy and power; and this fault lay not in the covenant but in the covenanters, who were unable to keep it. Therefore the earlier covenant was less excellent than this new one.

units.la: Haud quaquam Ratio 2. confirmans priorem, Quia abolendum erat vetus foedus, & novum foedus ejus loco surrogandum, quod non contigisset nisi imperfectum fuisset: Ergo illud prius est imperfectius, hoc novum vero excellentius.
units.tr: Certainly not The second reason, confirming the first: the old covenant had to be abolished and a new covenant put in its place, which would not have happened unless the old one had been imperfect. Therefore the former is more imperfect, and the new one more excellent.

units.la: Verf. 8. Nam incusans eos, inquit, Ecce, dies venient, dicit Dominus, quum pangam cum domo Israel & cum domo Juda foedus novum:
units.tr: Verse 8. For finding fault with them, he says: Behold, the days come, saith the Lord, when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah.

units.la: Ratio 3. confirmans priores, Quia prius foedus propter infirmitatem foederatorum ad praestationem legis, quae erat sederis conditio, non potuit reddere foederatos irreprehensibiles, vel ab accusatione Dei eos liberare, sed oportebat melius foedus & efficacius a Deo excogitari ad populum Dei justificandum, sanctificandum, & salvandum. Ergo prius foedus minus excellens est, novum vero excellentius.
units.tr: Reason 3, confirming the former: because the earlier covenant, on account of the weakness of the covenanters, could not, by their performance of the law which was the condition of the covenant, make them blameless or free them from the accusation of God; but a better and more effective covenant had to be devised by God to justify, sanctify and save his people. Therefore the earlier covenant is less excellent, and the new one more excellent.

units.la: Verf. 9. Non secundum foedus quod feci cum patribus ipsorum, quo die prehendi manum ipsorum, ut educerem eos ex Ægypto: nam ipsi non perstiterunt in illo meo foedere, & ego despexi eos, dicit DOMINUS.
units.tr: Verse 9. Not according to the covenant that I made with their fathers, on the day when I took them by the hand to lead them out of Egypt; for they did not continue in my covenant, and I regarded them not, saith the Lord.

units.la: Ratio 4. Quia novum foedus non est simile foederi, quod Deus pepigit cum populo in monte Sinai, cum eduxit eos ex Egypto, de quo, Jer. 31. 31. Nam illud etiamsi non carebat aliqua obscura significatione gratiae obtinendae in Christo, per sacrificia repraesentato, externam tamen formam habebat Fœderis legalis, & conditionem expressam plenæ obedientiæ omnibus Dei mandatis præstandæ, ut patet ex ejus formula, Exod. cap. 19. & 20. & Jer. 17. 23. 31, 32, &c. Novum vero (ut statim patebit) absolutum à conditione operum, & respectu ejus qui fœdus initurus est, & respectu ejus qui jam pepigit fœdus.
units.tr: Reason 4. Because the new covenant is not like the covenant which God made with the people at Mount Sinai when he brought them out of Egypt, concerning which see Jer. 31. 31. For although that covenant did not lack some obscure signification of grace to be obtained in Christ, represented through sacrifices, it nevertheless had the external form of a legal covenant and an express condition of full obedience to be rendered to all God's commands, as is clear from its formula, Exod. chapters 19 and 20, and Jer. 17. 23, 31, 32, etc. But the new covenant (as will presently be clear) is free from the condition of works, both with respect to him who is to enter the covenant and with respect to him who has already made it.

units.la: Nam ipsi ] Ratio 5. Fœderati secundum vetus fœdus deficere possunt, & defecerunt, & irritum sibi reddere possunt illud fœdus, & reddiderunt. Novum vero ut statim patebit, est perpetuæ gratiæ, secundum quod vere fœderati, seu fideles nunquam defecerunt, nec deficere propter Dei gratiam, nec irritum sibi reddere possunt novum fœdus, propter timorem quem Deus indit ipsorum cordibus, ne discedant ab eo, Jerem. 32. 40. Ergo fœdus novum præstantius est.
units.tr: For they] Reason 5. Covenanters under the old covenant can fall away, and did fall away, and can render that covenant void for themselves, and did so. But the new covenant, as will presently be clear, is of perpetual grace, so that those who are truly covenanted, that is the faithful, never fell away, nor can they fall away, on account of God's grace, nor render the new covenant void for themselves, on account of the fear which God puts into their hearts, that they should not depart from him (Jer. 32. 40). Therefore the new covenant is more excellent.

units.la: Despexi ] Ratio 6. Fœderati secundum vetus fœdus abutentes maritali Dei clementia, & adulterium cum alienis diis in idololatria sua perpetrantes, secundum Dei maritalem, & Dominicam in eos potestatem, despici, rejici, & condemnari possunt à Deo: Non sic fœderati secundum novum fœdus. Ergo novum fœdus præstantius est, cujus Christus & Mediator & Sponsor est.
units.tr: Regarded not] Reason 6. Covenanters under the old covenant, abusing the marital clemency of God and committing adultery with strange gods in their idolatry, can, according to God's marital and lordly power over them, be despised, rejected and condemned by God. It is not so with covenanters under the new covenant. Therefore the new covenant is more excellent, of which Christ is both Mediator and Bridegroom.

units.la: Vers. 10. Quamobrem hoc est fœdus quod pacisçar domui Israel post dies illos, dicit Dominus. Indam Leges meas mente eorum, & corde eorum inscribam: & ero ipsis DEVS, & ipsi erunt mihi populus.
units.tr: Verse 10. Wherefore this is the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel after those days, saith the Lord: I will put my laws into their mind, and write them on their hearts; and I will be their God, and they shall be my people.

units.la: Jam probat alteram partem argumenti, Quod scilicet fœdus novum sancitum sit melioribus promissionibus, idque quatuor promissiones absolutas, Electis seu Fidelibus factas, enumerando. Indam ] Promissio prima est regenerationis; Quæ nihil aliud est quam Legis Dei inscriptio primum in mente, consistens in animi renovatione ad imaginem Dei, in sapientia & cognitione. Deinde in corde, quæ fit cum cor renovatur ad imaginem Dei, secundum justitiam & sanctimoniam veram. Et ero ipsis DEVS ] Promissio 2. est perpetuæ cum Deo communionis, & juris matrimonialis ex confœderatione orti, quo populus fœderatus cedit Deo in possessionem dilectionis peculiaris, Deus vero cedit populo suo in possessionem beatificantem, & utrumque hic omittit Deus: Ego me iis præstabo Deum, (inquit) eoque præstabo populum meum, & habebo pro populo meo.
units.tr: He now proves the other part of the argument, namely that the new covenant has been ratified with better promises, by enumerating four absolute promises made to the elect or faithful. I will put] The first promise is that of regeneration, which is nothing other than the inscription of God's law first in the mind, consisting in the renewal of the soul to the image of God, in wisdom and knowledge. Then on the heart, which takes place when the heart is renewed to the image of God, in true righteousness and holiness. And I will be their God] The second promise is of perpetual communion with God, and of the marital right arising from the covenant, by which the covenanted people yield to God the possession of special love, and God yields to his people the possession that makes blessed; and God here leaves out both: I will show myself to them as God, he says, and thereby will show myself to my people, and will hold them as my people.

units.la: Verf. 11. Neque docebunt singuli proximum suum, & singuli fratrem suum, dicentes, Cognosce Dominum: nam omnes cognoscent me, ab eo qui pusillus fuerit inter eos.
units.tr: Verse 11. And they shall not teach every man his neighbour, and every man his brother, saying, Know the Lord; for all shall know me, from the least of them to the greatest.

units.la: Promissio 3. est, Institutionis continuæ à Spiritu Sancto, ita ut non hausturi sint cognitionem Dei ex decretis & placitis hominum, nec suspensuri fidem suam ex autoritate hominum docentium, nec hæsuri in nudâ contemplatione illorum quæ prædicata audient, (sicut iis contingit qui extra novum fœdus degunt irregeniti,) Sed per docendi media divinitus instituta, imbuendi sint omnes (minimi pariter & maximi) viva, affectuosâ, efficaci & salvifica cognitione Dei, amore & observantiâ Dei, ita ut neque in se, neque in æstimatione credentium, is qui plantat, vel is qui rigat (ut aliquid futurus, in comparatione cum Deo scilicet: sed Deus futurus solus doctor, qui docet efficaciter & dat incrementum.
units.tr: The third promise is of continual instruction by the Holy Spirit, so that they shall not draw the knowledge of God from the decrees and opinions of men, nor rest their faith on the authority of men who teach, nor cling to the bare contemplation of those things which they hear preached (as happens to those who live outside the new covenant, unregenerate). But, by the means of teaching divinely instituted, all (the least as well as the greatest) are to be imbued with a living, affectionate, effective and saving knowledge of God, the love and observance of God; so that neither in himself nor in the estimation of believers is he who plants, or he who waters (as if he were to be something), in comparison with God; but God alone is to be the teacher, who teaches effectively and gives the increase.

units.la: Verf. 12. Ero enim propitius iniquitatibus eorum, & peccatorum ipsorum & iniquitatum ipsorum non recordabor amplius.
units.tr: Verse 12. For I will be merciful to their iniquities, and their sins and their iniquities I will remember no more.

units.la: Promissio 4. Est perpetuæ remissionis peccatorum, quâ Deus propter obedientiam Christi propitium se semper fidelibus confœderatis ostendit.
units.tr: The fourth promise is of perpetual remission of sins, by which God, for the obedience of Christ, shows himself always propitious to the faithful covenanted to him.

units.la: Verf. 13. Dum novum dicit, antiquavit prius: porrò quod antiquatur ac senescit, prope est ut evanescat.
units.tr: Verse 13. In saying new, he has made the first old; and that which decays and grows old is near to vanishing.

units.la: Ex verbis Jeremiæ citatis infert consectarium duplex. Primum est, fœdus legale seu Leviticum, propterea quod vetus esse declaretur à Propheta, in Epitheto Novi, consenuit & antiquatum est.
units.tr: From the words of Jeremiah cited he draws a twofold consequence. The first is that the legal or Levitical covenant, because it is declared by the Prophet to be old in contrast with the new, has grown old and been antiquated.

units.la: Porro Alterum consectarium hinc derivatum, Temporibus Jeremiæ Prophetæ, prope erat ut moreretur, & evanesceret fœdus legale seu Leviticum, & per consequens post adventum Christi, sub quo nova facta sunt omnia, expiravit. Quo nihil efficacius dici potuit ad movendum Hebræos, ut renunciantes Ceremoniis Leviticis, soli Christo se totos consecrarent.
units.tr: Moreover The second consequence drawn from this: in the time of the prophet Jeremiah the legal or Levitical covenant was near to dying and vanishing, and consequently after the coming of Christ, under whom all things were made new, it expired. Nothing more effective could be said to move the Hebrews to renounce the Levitical ceremonies and devote themselves wholly to Christ alone.

units.la: Caput Nonum.
units.tr: Chapter Nine.

units.la: Resequitur comparationem Sacerdotii Levitici cum Sacerdotio Christi, & Sacerdotii Christi excellentiam porro oftendit. Capitis duae sunt partes, In prima Sacerdotium Christi excellentius esse Levitico, probat Argumentis quindecim, ad versum 16. In secunda tollit scandalum Crucis, seu Mortis Christi, necessitatem & sufficientiam ejus ostendendo, ad finem.
units.tr: It goes on to compare the Levitical priesthood with the priesthood of Christ, and further shows the excellence of Christ's priesthood. The chapter has two parts. In the first, the author proves by fifteen arguments, up to verse 16, that the priesthood of Christ is more excellent than the Levitical. In the second, he removes the stumbling-block of the Cross, that is, the death of Christ, by showing its necessity and sufficiency, to the end.

units.la: Verf. 1. Igitur habebat quidem etiam prius foedus constitutos religionis ritus, & sanctuarium mundanum.
units.tr: Verse 1. Then indeed the first covenant also had ordinances of divine worship and a worldly sanctuary.

units.la: Quod ad primam partem attinet, septem priora Argumenta sunt totidem imperfectionis Levitici Sacerdotii indicia, ex quibus commendatur excellentia Sacerdotii CHRISTI.
units.tr: As for the first part, the first seven arguments are so many signs of the imperfection of the Levitical priesthood, from which the excellence of CHRIST's priesthood is commended.

units.la: Argumentum primum, Primum Foedus ad Leviticum Sacerdotium pertinens, habebat umbratiles justificationis ritus, & Sanctuarium terrenum tantum. Sequitur ergo CHRISTI Sacerdotium, (quod habet veram justificationem secundum novum foedus, & coeleste Sanctuarium, ut prius ostensum est,) esse multò excellentius.
units.tr: Argument 1. The first covenant, which pertained to the Levitical priesthood, had shadowy rites of justification and only an earthly sanctuary. It follows, therefore, that CHRIST's priesthood, which has true justification under the new covenant and a heavenly sanctuary, as was shown before, is far more excellent.

units.la: Verf. 2. Tabernaculum enim construtum fuit: prius quidem in quo erat candelabrum, & mensa, & propositi panes quod sancta vocant.
units.tr: Verse 2. For there was a tabernacle made: the first, wherein was the candlestick, and the table, and the shewbread, which is called the sanctuary.

units.la: Hoc Argumentum explicat, Primo describendo Sanctuarii partes, & quae in illis erant sacra; deinde justificationis ritus typicos. Tabernaculum quod erexit Moses, habebat duas partes; Anterior pars vocabatur Sanctum, interior pars Sanctum Sanctorum. In prima parte seu anteriori, fuit candelabrum: in parte domus meridionali ingredienti ad sinistram positum. Ex opposito, in parte domus septentrionali erat mensa cum panibus propositionis, sic dictis, quia coram Deo proponebantur: quibus significabatur accedentibus ad Deum, lucem, & vitam ministrari. Erat etiam in hac parte, altare suffitus ante aditum interioris partis collocatum, quo precum oblatio significabatur.
units.tr: This argument is explained, first by describing the parts of the sanctuary and the sacred things in them, and then the typical rites of justification. The tabernacle that Moses set up had two parts. The front part was called the Holy place, and the inner part the Holy of Holies. In the first, or front, part stood the candlestick, on the south side of the house, to the left as one enters. Opposite it, on the north side of the house, was the table with the bread of the presentation, so called because it was set out before God. By these things it was signified that light and life are supplied to those who approach God. In this part there was also the altar of incense, placed before the entrance to the inner part, by which the offering of prayer was signified.

units.la: Verf. 3. Post medium autem velum erat Tabernaculum quod vocant Sancta Sanctorum:
units.tr: Verse 3. And after the second veil, the tabernacle which is called the Holiest of all;

units.la: Velum quod pendebat in aditu hujus partis, hic intelligitur esse primum mum Velum: Alterum velum quod dividebat partem anteriorem à Sancto Sanctorum, vocatur hic medium velum: & interius domicilium quod post illud erat, Sanctum Sanctorum dicitur: prior pars figurabat Ecclesiam in terris, posterior figurabat cælum, seu locum in quo Deus triumphanti Ecclesiæ se manifestat.
units.tr: The veil that hung at the entrance to this part is understood here to be the first veil. The other veil, which divided the front part from the Holy of Holies, is here called the middle veil. The inner dwelling that lay behind it is called the Holy of Holies. The former part figured the Church on earth; the latter figured heaven, or the place in which God manifests himself to the triumphant Church.

units.la: Verf. 4. Aureum habens thuribulum, & arcam Fœderis undique circumtectam auro in qua urna aurea habens manna, & virga Aaron quæ germinavit, & Tabulæ fœderis.
units.tr: Verse 4. Which had the golden censer, and the ark of the covenant overlaid round about with gold, wherein was the golden pot that had manna, and Aaron's rod that budded, and the tables of the covenant.

units.la: In Sancto Sanctorum, 1. erat aureum thuribulum, quod in usum Pontificis ingredientis semel quotannis intervire potuit, aptum ad significandum intercessionem Christi precantis pro nobis, & nostras preces acceptas Deo reddentis: 2. Erat Arca fœderis undique tecta auro, unde Deus vocem edebat. Idonea figura Verbi incarnati, & consilium Dei nobis aperientis: 3. Erat urna habens Manna, abditum illud Manna (quod Deus vere fidelibus in Christo ad vitam æternam vescendum dat) commodè figurans: 4. Erat virga Aaronis, quæ germinavit, apta ad figurandam benedictionem efficacem, quam Christus ministrorum suorum laboribus concedit: 5. Tabulæ fœderis in arca positæ, quæ Legis impletionem non nisi in Christo nobis quærendam docebant. Verf. 5. Supra hanc autem Cherubim gloriosi, obumbrantes propitiatorium: de quibus non est nunc dicendum singulatim.
units.tr: In the Holy of Holies there were: (1) the golden censer, which could be carried in by the high priest once a year when he entered, fitting to signify the intercession of Christ praying for us and rendering our prayers acceptable to God; (2) the ark of the covenant, covered on every side with gold, from which God gave his voice, a fitting figure of the incarnate Word and of God's counsel revealed to us; (3) the pot holding the manna, which suitably figured that hidden manna (which God truly gives to believers in Christ to feed on for eternal life); (4) Aaron's rod that budded, apt to figure the effective blessing which Christ grants through the labours of his ministers; (5) the tables of the covenant placed in the ark, which taught that the fulfilment of the Law is to be sought in Christ alone. Verse 5. And over it the cherubims of glory shadowing the mercyseat, of which we cannot now speak particularly.

units.la: 6. Erant Angeli Cherubini, alis ad se invicem conversis, operculum Arcæ obumbrantes; inter quas alas Deus quasi sedebat, & consulentibus responsa dabat; quo ministerium Angelorum Christo (magno pietatis mysterio, & in luce inaccessa habitanti) inservientium in typo proponebatur. Et quia latis hic dictum de gloria externi Tabernaculi, seu de loco terreno, Apostolus abrumpit ampliorem de loco terreno disputationem.
units.tr: (6) There were the angelic cherubim, with their wings turned towards one another, overshadowing the cover of the ark; between their wings God seemed to sit and gave answers to those who consulted him. In this the ministry of the angels serving Christ, who dwells in unapproachable light and is the great mystery of godliness, was set forth in type. And since the author has said enough here about the glory of the outward tabernacle, that is, about the earthly place, the Apostle breaks off a fuller discussion of the earthly place.

units.la: Verf. 6 His autem ita ordinatis, in prius quidem Tabernaculum quovis tempore ingrediuntur Sacerdotes qui ritus obeunt:
units.tr: Verse 6. Now when these things were thus ordained, the priests went always into the first tabernacle, accomplishing the service of God.

units.la: Fuit locus; proxime describit umbratilis justificationis ritus, & primo quotidianos, quos quilibet sacerdotes quotidie exercebant in anteriori parte Tabernaculi, suffitum adolentes, panes ad mensam instruendam, oleum ad candelabrum, reliquaque secundum legem cuiantes.
units.tr: This is the place. Next he describes the shadowy rites of justification, and first the daily ones, which every priest performed each day in the front part of the tabernacle: burning incense, setting out the bread on the table, supplying oil for the candlestick, and the other things done according to the law.

units.la: Verf. 7. In secundum autem semel quotannis solus Pontifex, non sine sanguine quem offert pro seipso, & pro populi erratu.
units.tr: Verse 7. But into the second went the high priest alone once every year, not without blood, which he offered for himself, and for the errors of the people.

units.la: Deinde describit ritus anniversarios, qui hujusmodi erant: 1. Pontifex solus sine comite: 2. Semel quotannis, non laepius: 3. Nunquam sine oblatione sanguinis vituli, & hirci in pelvim excepti: 4. Sanguinem hunc efferebat pro suis peccatis, maximis & minimis, & pro peccatis populi. Haec autem omnia externa, mundana & umbratilia, & in se minime efficacia erant. Praefigurabant enim CHRISTI ingressum in coelum per sanguinem suum vere propitiatorium. Hoc primum est argumentum, terrenae imperfectionis in Sacerdotio Levitico.
units.tr: Then he describes the annual rites, which were of this kind: (1) the high priest alone, without a companion; (2) once a year, and not more often; (3) never without the offering of the blood of a calf and a goat, received into a basin; (4) he carried this blood in for his own sins, both great and small, and for the sins of the people. All these things were outward, worldly and shadowy, and in themselves of no real efficacy. For they foreshadowed Christ's entry into heaven through his own blood, the true mercy seat. This is the first argument: the earthly imperfection of the Levitical priesthood.

units.la: Verf. 8. Hoc declarante Spiritu sancto, nondum patefactam fuisse viam ad Sanctuarium, priore Tabernaculo adhuc consistente.
units.tr: Verse 8. The Holy Ghost this signifying, that the way into the holiest of all was not yet made manifest, while as the first tabernacle was yet standing.

units.la: Arg. 2. per expositionem mysterii proximi propositum, Tempore Levitici Sacerdotii, dum statum obineret Tabernaculum, & cultus ille ceremonialis circa Sanctuarium, via ad Coelum, seu ad verum Sanctuarium non erat manifeste declarata, sicut jam manifesta facta est sub CHRISTI Sacerdotio. Id quod SPIRITUS Sanctus docebat per exclusionem Sacerdotum ex Sanctuario intimo: per admissionem Pontificis semel in anno clauso manente Sanctuario, reliquo toto anno: Ergo excellentius est CHRISTI Sacerdotium Levitico.
units.tr: Argument 2. By the explanation of the mystery set forth in the nearer sense, in the time of the Levitical priesthood, while the tabernacle and that ceremonial worship about the sanctuary stood, the way to heaven, or to the true sanctuary, was not clearly declared, as it has now been made plain under the priesthood of Christ. The Holy Spirit taught this by excluding the priests from the innermost sanctuary, and by admitting only the high priest, once a year, while the sanctuary remained closed for the rest of the year. Therefore the priesthood of Christ is more excellent than the Levitical.

units.la: Verf. 9 Quod erat exemplar pro tempore illo praesenti quo dona sacrificiaque offeruntur, quae non possunt in conscientia sanctifica- re cultorem,
units.tr: Verse 9. Which was a figure for the time then present, in which were offered both gifts and sacrifices, that could not make him that did the service perfect, as pertaining to the conscience;

units.la: Arg. 3. Ritus expiatorii prædicti, & reliqua istius generis exercitis Pontificis Levitici, erant typica, parabolica, & merum exemplar eorum quæ per Christum præstanda erant: Ergo in excellentia cum Christi Sacerdotio minimè æquiparandum est Leviticum.
units.tr: Argument 3. The aforesaid rites of atonement, and the other things of this kind performed by the Levitical high priest, were typical and parabolic, and a mere figure of those things which were to be accomplished through Christ. Therefore the Levitical priesthood is by no means to be compared with the priesthood of Christ in excellence.

units.la: Tempore ] Arg. 4. Quæ hebant à Pontifice & Sacerdotibus Leviticis inserviebant tantùm pro tempore legalis pædagogiæ, scilicet in Ecclesiæ ruditate & infantiâ, quo dona & sacrificia typica offerebantur; Ergo Leviticum Sacerdotium longè est inferius Sacerdotio Christi.
units.tr: For the time. Argument 4. The things done by the high priest and the Levitical priests served only for the time of the legal schooling, namely, while the Church was in its rudeness and infancy, when typical gifts and sacrifices were offered. Therefore the Levitical priesthood is far inferior to the priesthood of Christ.

units.la: Non possunt ] Arg. 5. Dona & sacrificia quæ offerebantur à Levitieis Sacerdotibus, non poterant in conscientia sanctificare cultorem, vel malam conscientiam peccatorum admissorum tollere: Ergo Sacerdotium Leviticum cum Christi Sacerdotio non est comparandum.
units.tr: Cannot. Argument 5. The gifts and sacrifices offered by the Levitical priests could not sanctify the worshipper in conscience, or take away an evil conscience of sins committed. Therefore the Levitical priesthood cannot be compared with the priesthood of Christ.

units.la: Verf. 10. In cibis duntaxat & potionibus, & diversis ablutionibus ac ritibus carnalibus, usque ad tempus correctionis imposita. ;
units.tr: Verse 10. Which stood only in meats and drinks, and divers washings, and carnal ordinances, imposed on them until the time of reformation.

units.la: Arg. 6. confirmans superius, Quae donabantur & offerebantur à Levitico Sacerdote, tantùm in cibis & potionibus, & diversis lotionibus, & carnalibus ritibus consistebant, quae non commendabant hominem DEO, 1 Cor. 8. 2. sed tantùm ut in carne sanctificati ceremonialiter mundi haberentur cultores, faciebant: Ergo nihil est Sacerdotium Leviticum ad excellentiam Sacerdotii CHRISTI comparatum.
units.tr: Argument 6, confirming what was said above. The gifts and offerings made by the Levitical priest consisted only in meats and drinks, various washings and carnal rites, which did not commend a man to God (1 Cor. 8:2), but only made the worshippers ceremonially clean in the flesh. Therefore the Levitical priesthood, compared with the excellence of the priesthood of Christ, is nothing.

units.la: Arg. 7. Imposita erant dona & sacrificia, reliquaque Sacerdotum Leviticorum officia, ut jugum & onus, usque ad tempus correctionis tantùm, id est, ad CHRISTI adventum, qui correcturus erat veteris Sacerdotii sacrificia & dona imperfecta, iisque abolitis donum & sacrificium perfectius introducturus: Ergo perfectius est CHRISTI Sacerdotium Levitico.
units.tr: Argument 7. The gifts and sacrifices, and the other duties of the Levitical priests, were imposed like a yoke and a burden only until the time of reformation, that is, until the coming of Christ, who was to correct the sacrifices and imperfect gifts of the old priesthood, and, with these abolished, was to introduce a more perfect gift and sacrifice. Therefore the priesthood of Christ is more perfect than the Levitical.

units.la: Verf. 11. Adveniens autem Christus Pontifex futurorum bonorum, per majus & perfectius Tabernaculum non manufactum, id est, non hujus structurae,
units.tr: Verse 11. But Christ being come an high priest of good things to come, by a greater and more perfect tabernacle, not made with hands, that is to say, not of this building;

units.la: Arg. 8. CHRISTUS est Pontifex non typorum, sed bonorum spiritualium, ut justificationis, sanctificationis & salutis, quae per typos figurabantur: Ergo CHRISTI Sacerdotium est longe excellentius.
units.tr: Argument 8. Christ is the high priest not of types, but of spiritual good things, such as justification, sanctification and salvation, which were figured by the types. Therefore the priesthood of Christ is far more excellent.

units.la: Arg. 9. CHRISTUS majus & perfectius tabernaculum habebat, non manufactum, non communis structurae, nempe tabernaculum corporis sui, quod à SPIRITO Sancto speciali modo fabricatum est in utero virginis, sine peccati originalis labe: in quo tabernaculo plenitudo Deitatis inhabitat: Ergo ejus Sacerdotium longe excellentius est Levitico.
units.tr: Arg. 9. Christ had a greater and more perfect tabernacle, not made by hands and not of ordinary construction, namely the tabernacle of his own body, which was formed in a special way by the Holy Spirit in the womb of the virgin, without the stain of original sin. In this tabernacle the fullness of the Godhead dwells. Therefore his priesthood is far more excellent than the Levitical.

units.la: Verf. 12. Neque per sanguinem hircorum & vitulorum, sed per proprium sanguinem ingressus est semel in Sacrarium, aeternam redemptionem nactus.
units.tr: Verse 12. Neither by the blood of goats and calves, but by his own blood, he entered once into the Sanctuary, having obtained eternal redemption.

units.la: Arg. 10. CHRISTUS obtulit non sanguinem taurorum, seu hircorum, ut Levitici Pontifices, sed sanguinem proprium, factusque est idem & Sacerdos & Sacrificium: Ergo ejus Sacerdotium est excellentius Levitico.
units.tr: Arg. 10. Christ offered not the blood of bulls or goats, as the Levitical priests did, but his own blood, and he was both the priest and the sacrifice. Therefore his priesthood is more excellent than the Levitical.

units.la: Arg. 11: CHRISTUS ingressus est semel in Sacrarium verum, id est, in coelum, ibique manet, non saepius ut Levitici Pontifices in typicum: Ergo excellentius est ejus sacerdotium Levitico.
units.tr: Arg. 11. Christ entered once into the true Sanctuary, that is, into heaven, and there he remains, not repeatedly as the Levitical priests did into the typical sanctuary. Therefore his priesthood is more excellent than the Levitical.

units.la: Æternum ] Arg. 12. CHRISTUS æternam redemptionem suo sacrificio comparavit, quod Leviticis erat impollibile. Ergo ejus Sacerdotium longè excellentius est Levitico.
units.tr: Eternal] Arg. 12. Christ obtained eternal redemption by his sacrifice, which was impossible under the Levitical law. Therefore his priesthood is far more excellent than the Levitical.

units.la: Verf. 13: Nam si sanguis taurorum & hircorum, & cinis juvencæ aspergens inquinatos sanctificat ad carnis puritatem,
units.tr: Verse 13. For if the blood of bulls and goats, and the ashes of a heifer sprinkling the unclean, sanctifies to the purity of the flesh,

units.la: Verf. 14. Quanto magis sanguis Christi qui per Spiritum æternum semetipsum obtulit inculpatum DEO purgabit conscientiam vestram a mortuis operibus ad serviendum Deo vivo?
units.tr: Verse 14. How much more shall the blood of Christ, who through the eternal Spirit offered himself without blemish to God, purge your conscience from dead works to serve the living God?

units.la: Emundabit ] Arg. 13 confirmans superius, CHRISTI sanguis purgat conscientiam, partim quatenus conscientia videns plenam pro se justitiæ divinæ satisfactionem factam in CHRISTI passione, absolutionem suam perfectam amplectitur, & in ea conquiescit: partim quatenus vis sanctificans cor ad DEO serviendum, ab eo profluit.
units.tr: Will purge] Arg. 13, confirming what was said above: the blood of Christ purges the conscience, partly insofar as the conscience, seeing that full satisfaction of divine justice has been made for it in the passion of Christ, embraces its perfect absolution and rests in it; partly insofar as the power that sanctifies the heart to serve God flows from that blood.

units.la: Nam si ] Hoc argumentum confirmat à minori. Sanguis taurorum reliquique typi præstiterunt id ad quod erant instituti, nempe purificationem externi hominis Ecclesiasticam, ut sanctus haberi posset ad opera cultus externi; Quanto magis præstabit sanguis CHRISTI antitypus id, quod per typos est significatum, nempe purificationem conscientiæ, à peccatis, ad DEO serviendum. Peccata vocantur opera mortua, quia mortem merentur, & mortis reos reddunt peccatores.
units.tr: For if] This argument proceeds from the lesser to the greater. The blood of bulls and the other types accomplished what they were instituted for, namely the ecclesiastical purification of the outward man, so that a person could be regarded as holy for the works of outward worship. How much more will the blood of Christ, the antitype, accomplish what was signified by the types, namely the purification of the conscience from sins, so that it may serve God. Sins are called dead works because they deserve death and make sinners liable to death.

units.la: Per Spiritum ] Arg. 14. In oblatione CHRISTI, SPIRITUS æternus, seu CHRISTUS quâ DEUS, præcipuas Sacerdotis partes agebat, & seipsum ut hominem immaculatum pro sacrificio offerebat: Ergo ejus Sacerdotium Levitico tantò excellentius est, quantò Deus homine, & sancta ejus humanitas, pecude præstantior est.
units.tr: Through the Spirit] Arg. 14. In the offering of Christ, the eternal Spirit, that is, Christ as God, played the chief part of the priest, and he offered himself as a spotless man for a sacrifice. Therefore his priesthood is as much more excellent than the Levitical as God is greater than man, and his holy humanity is more excellent than a beast.

units.la: Verf. 15 Itaque ob id novi Fœderis Mediator est, ut morte intercedente, ad redemptionem earum prævaricationum quæ fuerant sub priore Testamento, vocati promissionem accipiant æterna hereditatis.
units.tr: Verse 15. And therefore he is the Mediator of the new covenant, so that, by means of his death, for the redemption of the transgressions that were under the former testament, those who are called may receive the promise of eternal inheritance.

units.la: Arg. 15. Sub veteri fœdere nec remissio peccatorum, nec vitæ æternæ hæreditas data est vocatis, nisi propter CHRISTI mortem intercedentem sub novo fœdere, in quem finem ille jam Mediator novi fœderis constitutus est in gratiam omnium Vocatorum. Ergo præstantius est illius Sacerdotium Levitico illo sub veteri fœdere.
units.tr: Arg. 15. Under the old covenant neither forgiveness of sins nor the inheritance of eternal life was given to those who were called, except on account of the death of Christ, who intervenes under the new covenant. To this end he has now been appointed Mediator of the new covenant for the grace of all who are called. Therefore his priesthood is more excellent than the Levitical priesthood under the old covenant.

units.la: Secunda pars.
units.tr: Second part.

units.la: Verf. 16. Nam ubi testamentum est, mors intercedat, necesse est testatoris.
units.tr: Verse 16. For where there is a testament, the death of the testator must necessarily intervene.

units.la: Secunda pars Capitis, in qua ad tollendum scandalum crucis, probat primo necessitatem mortis Christi, Argumentis sex, ad vers. 25. Deinde sufficientiam oblationis semel factæ in cruce, Argumentis quinque, probat ad finem.
