units.tr: The second part of the chapter, in which, to remove the offense of the cross, he first proves the necessity of the death of Christ by six arguments, up to verse 25. Then he proves by five arguments, to the end, the sufficiency of the offering made once on the cross.

units.la: Argumentum primum, Novum fœdus Christi, est novum Testamentum Christi: Ergo intercedere mortem Testatoris Christi necesse erat.
units.tr: The first argument: the new covenant of Christ is the new testament of Christ. Therefore it was necessary for the death of Christ as testator to intervene.

units.la: Vers. 17. Testamentum enim in mortuis ratum est, quandoquidem nondum valet quum vivit testator.
units.tr: Verse 17. For a testament is valid over the dead, since it has no force while the testator is alive.

units.la: Arg. 2. confirmans superius, Nisi mortuus fuisset Christus, fœdus seu testamentum non fuisset ratum: nam etiam inter homines non valet testamentum, dum testator vivit, sed tantùm postquam mortuus est: mutari enim potest viventis testamentum, sed non demortui: Ergo necesse erat ut moreretur Christus.
units.tr: Arg. 2, confirming what was said above: unless Christ had died, the covenant or testament would not have been valid. For even among men a testament is not valid while the testator lives, but only after he has died; for the will of a living man can be changed, but not that of a dead man. Therefore it was necessary for Christ to die.

units.la: Vers. 18. Unde ne prius quidem illud absque sanguine dedicatum fuit.
units.tr: Verse 18. Hence not even the first was dedicated without blood.

units.la: Arg. 3. Sicut vetus testamentum non fuit Deo dedicatum, fine sanguine typico: Sic neque novum testamentum, fine veri Mediatoris Christi vero antitypo sanguine dedicari potest, seu offerri in satisfactionem pro hominibus peccatoribus: Ergo Christum mo-ri necessarium fuit.
units.tr: Arg. 3. Just as the old testament was not dedicated to God without the typical blood, so neither can the new testament be dedicated, that is, offered in satisfaction for sinful men, without the true antitypical blood of Christ the true Mediator. Therefore it was necessary for Christ to die.

units.la: Vers. 19. Quum enim Moses omnia mandata secundum Legem recitasset toti populo, sumpto sanguine vitulorum & hircorum, cum aqua & lana coccinea & hyssopo, simul & ipsum librum & totum populum aspersit:
units.tr: Verse 19. For when Moses had recited all the commandments according to the Law to the whole people, he took the blood of calves and goats, with water and scarlet wool and hyssop, and sprinkled both the book itself and the whole people,

units.la: Vers. 20 Dicens, Hic est sanguis testamenti quod mandavit vobis DEVS.
units.tr: Verse 20. Saying, This is the blood of the testament which God has commanded you.

units.la: Argumentum hoc explicat & probat ex historia, Exod. 24. de dedicatione primi tabernaculi per sanguinem; ubi librum fœderis & populum aspersit Moses sanguine Vitulorum & Hircorum; simul significationem & usum ceremoniæ exponens, quod sanguis ille esset sanguis fœderis, deris, seu symbolum foederis typice iti in illis ceremoniis, & vere complendi in Christi sanguine.
units.tr: This argument is explained and proved from history, Exod. 24, concerning the dedication of the first tabernacle by blood, where Moses sprinkled the book of the covenant and the people with the blood of calves and goats. At the same time he explains the meaning and use of the ceremony: that this blood was the blood of the covenant, a symbol of the covenant, present typically in those ceremonies and to be truly fulfilled in the blood of Christ.

units.la: Verf. 21. Insuper autem & Tabernaculum, & omnia vasa sacrorum, sanguine similiter aspersit.
units.tr: Verse 21. Moreover, both the tabernacle and all the vessels of the sacred service he likewise sprinkled with blood.

units.la: Verf. 22. Et omnia fere secundum Legem sanguine purificantur, & absque sanguinis effusione non fit remissio.
units.tr: Verse 22. And almost all things are purified with blood according to the Law, and without shedding of blood there is no remission.

units.la: Arg. 4: Sicut sub lege omnia purgabantur vel sanguine, vel lotionibus ex sacrificiis vim purgandi trahentibus, adeo ut absque sanguinis effusione typica nulla fieret remissio peccatorum. Sic in novo foedere nulla poslet esse remissio peccatorum, nisi ex sanguinis Christi vera effusione: Ergo Christi mors fuit necessaria. Dicuntur sanguine aspergi tabernaculum, & vasa sacra quae in se impolluta erant, quia respectu nostri nisi per Christi sanguinem nos purificemur, omnia cedunt nobis in pollutionem. Idcirco sanctificari oportet nobis rerum sanctissimarum usum per Christum: alioqui immundis omnia sunt immunda; quatenus in omnibus, & per omnia, se polluunt infideles.
units.tr: Arg. 4. Just as under the law all things were purified either by blood or by washings which drew their power of cleansing from sacrifices, so that without the typical shedding of blood there was no remission of sins, so in the new covenant there could be no remission of sins except from the true shedding of Christ's blood. Therefore the death of Christ was necessary. The tabernacle and the sacred vessels are said to be sprinkled with blood, though in themselves they were unpolluted, because, with respect to us, unless we are purified by the blood of Christ, all things turn to pollution for us. Hence we must be sanctified in our use of the most holy things through Christ; otherwise to the unclean all things are unclean, since unbelievers are defiled in all things and through all things.

units.la: Verf. 23. Itaque necesse fuit exemplaria quidem eorum quae sunt in Coelis, hisce rebus purificari, ipsa vero coelestia potioribus quam haec sint victimis.
units.tr: Verse 23. Therefore it was necessary that the copies of the things in the heavens be purified with these, but the heavenly things themselves with better sacrifices than these.

units.la: Arg. 5. Si typos oportuit purgare sanguine typico, res coelestes spirituales significatas per typos oportuit consecrari melioribus victimis, hoc est, sanguine ipsius Mediatoris, qui virtute sua omnium victimarum vim continet, & per consequens Christi mors necessaria erat.
units.tr: Arg. 5. If the types had to be purified with typical blood, then the spiritual heavenly realities signified by the types had to be consecrated with better sacrifices, that is, with the blood of the Mediator himself, who by his power contains the efficacy of all sacrifices. Consequently the death of Christ was necessary.

units.la: Verf. 24. Non enim in manufactum sacrarium ingressus est Christus, quod sit exemplar, vero sacrario respondens: sed in ipsum coelum, ut appareat nunc in conspectu Dei pro nobis.
units.tr: Verse 24. For Christ has not entered into a sanctuary made with hands, which is a copy of the true sanctuary, but into heaven itself, to appear now in the presence of God for us.

units.la: Arg. 6. confirmans superius. Christus non est ingressus in manufactum Sacrarium typycum, sed in coelum per Sacrarium significatum, ut constanter pro nobis apparens intercederet. Ergo tanto digniorem victimam (id est, Seipsum oportebat offerre) quanto coelum superat terrestre sacrarium. Et per consequens mors ejus necessaria fuit.
units.tr: Arg. 6, confirming what was said above. Christ did not enter a typical sanctuary made with hands, but heaven, which the sanctuary signified, so that he might intercede by constantly appearing for us. Therefore the victim had to be far more worthy (that is, he had to offer himself) by as much as heaven surpasses the earthly sanctuary. And consequently his death was necessary.

units.la: Verf. 25. Neque ut saepe offerat semetipsum, sicut Pontifex intrat in sacrarium quotannis cum sanguine alieno:
units.tr: Verse 25. Nor that he should offer himself often, as the high priest enters into the sanctuary every year with the blood of another:

units.la: Jam probat sufficientiam unicae oblationis Christi in cruce, Argumentis quinque. Argumentum primum, CHRISTUS non est ingressus Sanctuarium terrestre saepius, ut saepe offerret seipsum, sicut Pontifex Leviticus, qui non suum sed alienum sanguinem quotannis offerebat. Sed coelum ingressus est semel. Ergo sufficiebat unica illa oblatio sui in cruce, per quam in coelum admissus est.
units.tr: Now he proves the sufficiency of the single offering of Christ on the cross, by five arguments. The first argument: Christ did not enter an earthly sanctuary often, so as to offer himself often, as the Levitical high priest did, who every year offered not his own blood but another's. But he entered heaven once. Therefore that single offering of himself on the cross was sufficient, by which he was admitted into heaven.

units.la: Verf. 26. Alioquin oportuisset eum saepe passum fuisse à condito mundo (sed nunc semel in consummatione saeculorum ad abolendum peccatum per immolationem sui ipsius patefactus est.
units.tr: Verse 26. Otherwise he would have had to suffer often since the foundation of the world; but now once, at the consummation of the ages, he has been manifested to put away sin by the sacrifice of himself.

units.la: Arg. 2. Nisi sufficeret unica CHRISTI oblatio in cruce, oportuisset eum saepius se offerendo, saepius mori ab initio mundi: nam si saepe deberet fieri oblatio corporis CHRISTI pro peccato, certe necesse fuit ut incipiset oblatio, quo tempore primum peccatum coepit & commissum est, hoc est, initio mundi, & ab eo tempore oportuisset eandem oblationem toties repeti, quoties peccata nova post oblationem commissa sunt, repetitis vicibus absque numero: At hoc absurdum est. Ergo sufficit unica oblatio ejus in cruce facta.
units.tr: Argument 2. Unless the single offering of Christ on the cross were sufficient, he would have had to offer himself again and again, and to die again and again from the beginning of the world. For if the offering of Christ's body for sin had to be made often, then certainly the offering must have begun at the time when the first sin began and was committed, that is, at the beginning of the world; and from that time the same offering would have had to be repeated as often as new sins were committed after the offering, in an endless succession of repetitions. But this is absurd. Therefore his single offering made on the cross is sufficient.

units.la: Nunc semel Arg. 3. CHRISTUS in plenitudine temporis apparuit eo fine, ut unica sui oblatione aboleret peccata suorum in praesenti, praeterito, & futuro tempore; nam ad impetrandam & applicandam remissionem peccatorum, ad mortificationem & abolitionem peccatorum, omnium Redemptorum seu Electorum, satis est valoris in morte CHRISTI. Ergo sufficit unica oblatio.
units.tr: Now once Argument 3. Christ appeared in the fullness of time for this purpose, that by his one offering he might abolish the sins of his people in the present, the past, and the future. For to obtain and apply the forgiveness of sins, and to mortify and abolish the sins of all the redeemed, that is, the elect, the death of Christ has value enough. Therefore the single offering is sufficient.

units.la: Verf. 27. Et sicut illud statutum est hominibus ut semel moriantur, post hoc vero judicium.
units.tr: Heb. 9:27. And as it is appointed unto men once to die, but after this the judgment.

units.la: Verf. 28. Ita & Christus semel oblatus, ut multorum peccata tolleret, altera vice absque peccato conspicietur iis qui ipsum expectant ad salutem.
units.tr: Heb. 9:28. So Christ also, having been offered once to bear the sins of many, will appear a second time, apart from sin, to those who eagerly await him for salvation.

units.la: Arg. 4. Sicut a DEO statutum est, ut omnes moriantur semel, & ut post mortem fiat judicium. Sic statutum est a DEO, ut CHRISTUS semel tantum se offerret ad expiandum peccata multorum, id est, Electorum, & ut secundo veniret Judex Vivorum & Mortuorum. Ergo sufficit unica ejus oblatio in cruce.
units.tr: Argument 4. As it has been appointed by God that all men die once, and that after death judgment follows, so it has been appointed by God that Christ should offer himself only once to expiate the sins of many, that is, of the elect, and that he should come a second time as Judge of the living and the dead. Therefore his single offering on the cross is sufficient.

units.la: Secundo Arg 5. CHRISTUS secunda vice veniens in die judicii manifestum faciet toti mundo, se unica oblatione sui plenissime satisfecisse pro peccato, peccatique imputationem, & poenas seu miseriam, & quaecunque cunque alia sunt vestigia peccati, & à se ut Sponsore, & à suis pro quibus spopondit removisse, & salutem impetrasse Fidelibus, qui adventum ejus expectant. Ergo sufficit unica illa oblutio in cruce ad redemptionem nostri plenam. Dicitur Christus in secundo adventu apparituros, sine peccato, respectu primi adventus, in quo licet à peccati pollutione inhaerente liberrimus fuerit, non tamen liber fuit à peccato alieno, seu nostro, quod ei imputatum est: Et propter quod infirmitati & miseriae obnoxius factus est, donec pro peccatis nostris satisfecit. In die autem judicii apparebit in gloria, quae peccati abolitionem omnimodam testificabitur: & per consequens demonstrabit unicam illam oblationem in cruce ad peccata tollendum abundè sufficientem esse.
units.tr: Secondly, Argument 5. Christ, coming a second time on the day of judgment, will make it manifest to the whole world that by his single offering he has fully satisfied for sin, and has removed from himself, as Surety, and from those for whom he stood surety, the imputation of sin, its punishments or misery, and whatever other traces of sin there are, and has obtained salvation for the faithful who await his coming. Therefore that single offering on the cross is fully sufficient for our redemption. It is said that Christ will appear at his second coming without sin, with respect to his first coming; in which, although he was most free from the pollution of inherent sin, he was not free from the sin of another, or of ours, which was imputed to him, and on account of which he was made subject to infirmity and misery until he had made satisfaction for our sins. But on the day of judgment he will appear in glory, which will testify to the complete abolition of sin; and consequently it will demonstrate that the single offering on the cross is abundantly sufficient to take away sin.

units.la: Caput Decimum.
units.tr: Chapter 10.

units.la: CHRISTI Sacerdotium pergit supra Leviticum extollere. Capitis duae sunt partes, In priori probat praestantius esse sacrificium Christi unicum, omnibus victimis legalibus, ad verl. 19. In posteriori doctrinam hanc deducit in usum, hortatione adhibita ad fiduciam & constantiam in fidei professione, & vitae sanctitate, cum patientia, ad finem.
units.tr: The priesthood of Christ goes on to exalt itself above the Levitical priesthood. The chapter has two parts. In the first, he proves that the sacrifice of Christ, the single sacrifice, is more excellent than all the legal victims, up to verse 19. In the second, he draws this doctrine into practice, by way of exhortation to confidence and steadfastness in the profession of faith, and to holiness of life with patience, to the end.

units.la: Verf. 1. LEX enim umbram obtinens futurorum bonorum, non expressam formam rerum, iis hostiis quas singulis annis eadem continenter offerunt, nunquam potest accedentes sanctificare.
units.tr: Verse 1. For the law, having a shadow of good things to come, and not the very image of the things, can never with those sacrifices, which they offer continually year by year, make the comers thereunto perfect.

units.la: Argumenta excellentiae sacrificii CHRISTI supra Leviticas victimas sunt duodecim. Argumentum primum, Praescriptae in Lege Ceremoniali Leviticae victimae, umbram tantum sacrificii CHRISTI, & beneficiorum ejus continebant, non vivam rerum ipsarum repraesentationem, qualis redditur in speculo Euangelii à rebus ipsis, prout jam exhibitae in seipsis considerantur: Ergo longè inferiores erant CHRISTI sacrificio illo repraesentato.
units.tr: There are twelve arguments for the excellence of the sacrifice of Christ above the Levitical victims. The first argument: the victims prescribed in the Levitical ceremonial law contained only the shadow of the sacrifice of Christ and of its benefits, not the living representation of the things themselves, such as is given in the mirror of the Gospel, where the things are considered in themselves as now actually exhibited. Therefore those victims were far inferior to the sacrifice of Christ, which they represented.

units.la: Arg. 2. Etiam praestantissimae hostiae Leviticae quotannis repetitae, per Pontificem, non poterant justificare vel sanctificare eos pro quibus, vel à quibus offerebantur. Ergo deteriores erant Christi sacrificio.
units.tr: Arg. 2. Even the most excellent Levitical victims, repeated every year by the high priest, could not justify or sanctify those for whom, or by whom, they were offered. Therefore they were inferior to the sacrifice of Christ.

units.la: Verf. 2. Alioqui desissent offerri, propterea quòd qui sacrifi-cassent, ac semel purgati essent, nullorum peccatorum amplius essent sibi conscii:
units.tr: Verse 2. Otherwise they would have ceased to be offered, because the worshippers, once purged, would no longer have had any consciousness of sins.

units.la: Arg. 3. confirmans superius, Victimæ Leviticæ, ipsâ sui repetitâ oblatione, præ se ferebant imperfectionem suam & impotentiam ad justi-ficandum peccatores, pro quibus offerebantur. Ergo deteriores erant Sacrificio Christi.
units.tr: Arg. 3. Confirming what was said above: the Levitical victims, by the very fact that they were offered repeatedly, showed their own imperfection and their inability to justify the sinners for whom they were offered. Therefore they were inferior to the sacrifice of Christ.

units.la: Alioqui ] Ratio redditur antecedentis, Si victimæ illæ justificassent cultores, sæpius offerri desiissent, quia cultores purgati à peccatorum reatu & quieti in conscientiis redditi, per unicam oblationem, non opus habuissent repetitâ oblatione. At victimæ illæ Leviticæ non desierunt sæpius offerri, quia lex repetitionem mandabat. Ergo non justificarunt cultores suos, illæ victimæ.
units.tr: Otherwise: a reason is given for the preceding statement. If those victims had justified the worshippers, they would have ceased to be offered more often, because the worshippers, cleansed from the guilt of sins and made quiet in their consciences by one offering, would have had no need of a repeated offering. But those Levitical victims did not cease to be offered often, because the law commanded repetition. Therefore those victims did not justify their worshippers.

units.la: Verf. 3. Atqui in illis repetita fi-mentio peccatorum quotannis.
units.tr: Verse 3. But in those sacrifices there is a yearly remembrance of sins.

units.la: Arg. 4. confirmans idem, Etiam nobilissimæ ex iis nempe anniversariæ victimæ quotannis secum ferebant omnium præteritorum peccatorum repetitam mentionem; quod frustra fuisset, si per priora sacrificia abolita fuissent: Ergo longè deteriora erant hæc sacrificia Christi sacrificio.
units.tr: Arg. 4. Confirming the same point: even the most noble of them, namely the yearly victims, brought with them each year a repeated remembrance of all past sins. This would have been pointless if the earlier sacrifices had been abolished by those that followed. Therefore these sacrifices were far worse than the sacrifice of Christ.

units.la: Verf. 4. Non enim potest sanguis taurorum & hircorum auferre peccata.
units.tr: Verse 4. For it is not possible that the blood of bulls and goats should take away sins.

units.la: Arg. 5. confirmans etiam secundum; Viliora erant hæc sacrificia (ut pote bestiarum) quam ut auferre possent peccata. Ergo Christi sacrificio longè erant inferiora.
units.tr: Arg. 5. Confirming also the second argument: these sacrifices, being the blood of beasts, were too base to be able to take away sins. Therefore they were far inferior to the sacrifice of Christ.

units.la: Verf. 5. Quapropter ingrediens mundum, dicit, Sacrificium & oblationem noluisti, corpus autem aptasti mihi.
units.tr: Verse 5. Wherefore, when he cometh into the world, he saith, Sacrifice and offering thou wouldest not, but a body hast thou prepared me.

units.la: Verf. 6 Holocautomata & hostium pro peccato non approbasti.
units.tr: Verse 6. In burnt offerings and sacrifices for sin thou hast had no pleasure.

units.la: Verf. 7. Tunc dixi, Ecce adsum (in capite libri scriptum est de me) ut faciam, Deus, voluntatem tuam.
units.tr: Verse 7. Then said I, Lo, I come (in the volume of the book it is written of me) to do thy will, O God.

units.la: Verf. 8. Quum superius dixisset, Sacrificium & oblationem, & holocautomata & hostiam pro peccato noluisti, neque approbasti (quae juxta Legem offeruntur)
units.tr: Verse 8. When he said above, Sacrifice and offering, and burnt offerings and sacrifices for sin thou wouldest not, neither hadst pleasure therein (which are offered according to the law),

units.la: Verf. 9. Tunc dixit, Ecce adsum ut faciam, Deus, voluntatem tuam, Tollit prius, ut posterius statuat.
units.tr: Verse 9. Then said he, Lo, I come to do thy will, O God. He taketh away the first, that he may establish the second.

units.la: Hoc argumentum probat ex Psal. 40. In quo introducitur CHRISTUS à Propheta, quo tempore homo factus est, & in carne apparuit, pronuncians sublata esse à Patre sacrificia legalia, & statutam esse ipsorum loco suam in corpore obedientiam, ad mortem usque crucis, in eo quod dicit, aures sibi perforatas, vel corpus sibi aptatum à Deo, qua utraque phrasi intelligitur Filium Dei incarnatum, formatum fuisse ad obsequium, & obedientiam Patris. Nam cum repudiata videt sacrificia legalia, ut indigna quæ expiarent peccata, offert ipsum ad moriendum ex Patris voluntate, secundum Prophetias, quæ de ipso in volumine Bibliorum continentur; Atque ita tollit sacrificia Levitica, ut stabiliat sacrificium CHRISTI.
units.tr: This argument is proved from Psalm 40, in which Christ is introduced by the Prophet, at the time when he was made man and appeared in the flesh, declaring that the legal sacrifices had been taken away by the Father, and that in their place his own obedience in the body, even to the death of the cross, had been established. This is shown in the words "ears pierced for me" or "a body prepared for me by God", phrases by which it is understood that the incarnate Son of God was fashioned for the obedience and submission of the Father. For when he sees that the legal sacrifices have been rejected as unworthy to expiate sins, he offers himself to die by the will of the Father, according to the prophecies which are contained concerning him in the volume of the Bible. And so he removes the Levitical sacrifices in order to establish the sacrifice of Christ.

units.la: Verf. 10. Qua voluntate sanctificati sumus, per oblationem corporis Iesu Christi semel factam.
units.tr: Verse 10. By which will we are sanctified, through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all.

units.la: Arg 7. Per oblationem corporis CHRISTI ex voluntate Dei justificamur & sanctificamur nos, qui per sacrificia legalia sanctificari non poteramus. Ergo CHRISTI sacrificium etiam ex institutione divina, est præstantius Leviticis.
units.tr: Arg. 7. Through the offering of the body of Christ, by the will of God, we are justified and sanctified, we who could not be sanctified by the legal sacrifices. Therefore the sacrifice of Christ, instituted also by divine appointment, is more excellent than the Levitical ones.

units.la: Vers. 11. Omnis igitur Sacerdos adstat quotidie operans, & eandem sæpius offerens hostias quæ nunquam possunt auferre peccata:
units.tr: Verse 11. And every priest standeth daily ministering and offering oftentimes the same sacrifices, which can never take away sins.

units.la: Vers. 12 Hic verò una pro peccatis oblata victima, in perpetuum sedet ad dextram Dei:
units.tr: Verse 12. But this man, after he had offered one sacrifice for sins for ever, sat down on the right hand of God;

units.la: Arg. 8 Sacerdotes juge sacrificium offerentes quotidie stabant, ut ministri, laborantes & offerentes eandem hostias, ad peccata auferenda inefficaces: Christus vero unâ victima semel oblatâ, ut Dominus cœli & terræ, in perpetuum consedit in consortio gloriæ cum Patre regnans. Ergo ejus sacrificium præstantius est Leviticis.
units.tr: Arg. 8. The priests, who offered sacrifice continually, stood daily as ministers, labouring and offering the same victims, which were ineffective for taking away sins. But Christ, having offered one victim once, sat down for ever, as Lord of heaven and earth, in fellowship of glory, reigning with the Father. Therefore his sacrifice is more excellent than the Levitical ones.

units.la: Vers. 13 Id quod superest, expectans, donec inimici ipsius scabellum pedum ejus fiant
units.tr: Verse 13. From henceforth expecting till his enemies be made his footstool.

units.la: Arg. 9 Post sacrificium Christi nihil faciendum restat pro expiatione peccatorum impetrandâ fidelibus seu electis, sed sola superest debellatio Diaboli, mundi, peccati inhabitantis, mortis, & reliquorum nostrorum & Christi inimicorum plena subjectio ut redempti potiantur plenâ felicitate, ab hostibus omnibus liberati. Ergo excellentius est ejus sacrificium Leviticis.
units.tr: Arg. 9. After the sacrifice of Christ nothing remains to be done to obtain expiation of sins for the faithful or elect; there remains only the overthrow of the Devil, the world, indwelling sin, death, and the full subjection of the rest of our enemies and Christ's enemies, so that the redeemed may enjoy full happiness, freed from all enemies. Therefore his sacrifice is more excellent than the Levitical ones.

units.la: Verf. 14. Unica enim oblatione consecravit in perpetuum eos qui sanctificantur.
units.tr: Verse 14. For by one offering he hath perfected for ever them that are sanctified.

units.la: Arg. 10. confirmans superius, Oblatio CHRISTI semel facta, vim habet infinitam, non tantum satisfaciendi pro peccatis Electorum seu Fidelium, qui in sanctitatis voto seipsos dedicarunt DEO, sed etiam efficaciter conferendi in eos omnes, qui fuerunt, sunt, & erunt, sanctitatem, & salutem, per gradus perficiendam, & in perpetuum duraturam. Ergo & excellentior est haec oblatio Leviticis, & ea jam oblata nihil restat praeter abolitionem hostium, & applicationem beneficiorum per illam oblationem partorum, in Electorum bonum.
units.tr: Arg. 10. Confirming what was said above: the offering of Christ, once made, has infinite power, not only to satisfy for the sins of the elect or faithful, who have dedicated themselves to God in a vow of holiness, but also to bestow effectually upon all those who have been, are, and will be, holiness and salvation, to be brought to completion by degrees and to endure for ever. Therefore this offering is also more excellent than the Levitical ones, and since it has already been offered, nothing remains but the abolition of the enemies and the application of the benefits obtained by that offering, for the good of the elect.

units.la: Verf. 15. Testificatur autem nobis & ipse Spiritus sanctus: nam postquam praedixit,
units.tr: Verse 15. Whereof the Holy Ghost also is a witness to us: for after that he had said before,

units.la: Verf. 16. Hoc est foedus quod pacisdar cum iis post dies illos, dicit Dominus, Indam leges meas cordibus eorum, & eorum mentibus eas inscribam:
units.tr: Verse 16. This is the covenant that I will make with them after those days, saith the Lord; I will put my laws into their hearts, and in their minds will I write them;

units.la: Verf. 17. Et peccatorum atque iniquitatum ipsorum non recordabor amplius.
units.tr: Verse 17. And their sins and iniquities will I remember no more.

units.la: Arg. 11. Foedus novum fundatum in Sacrificio CHRISTI, absolute, nulla posita conditione promittit electis omnibus plenam sanctificationem. Indam legem meam, &c; & remissionem peccatorum eorum non recordabor amplius, ut testatur Spiritus Sanctus: Jer. 31, 31. &c. Ergo CHRISTI sacrificium quo sancitur hoc foedus est praestantius Levitico.
units.tr: Arg. 11. The new covenant, founded on the sacrifice of Christ, promises absolutely, with no condition attached, full sanctification to all the elect: "I will put my laws..."; and the forgiveness of sins: "I will remember their sins no more", as the Holy Spirit testifies (Jer. 31:31, etc.). Therefore the sacrifice of Christ, by which this covenant is ratified, is more excellent than the Levitical.

units.la: Verf. 18. Porro ubi est horum remissio, non est amplius oblatio pro peccato.
units.tr: Verse 18. Now where remission of these is, there is no more offering for sin.

units.la: Arg. 12. Unica illa oblatio CHRISTI a DEO plenam remissionem peccatorum impetrat fidelibus sub novo foedere, ut neque relinquat locum suae ipsius repetitioni; neque ulli alii pro peccato oblationi. Ergo praestantior est oblationibus Leviticis.
units.tr: Arg. 12. That single offering of Christ obtains from God, for the faithful under the new covenant, full remission of sins, so that it leaves no place either for its own repetition or for any other offering for sin. Therefore it is more excellent than the Levitical offerings.

units.la: Secunda pars Capitis,
units.tr: The second part of the chapter,

units.la: Verf. 19. Quum igitur, fratres, habeamus libertatem ingrediendi Sacrarium per sanguinem Iesu,
units.tr: Verse 19. Since therefore, brethren, we have liberty to enter the sanctuary by the blood of Jesus,

units.la: Secunda pars Capitis, in qua doctrinam praecedentem deducit in usum, per hortationem ex variis membris constantem, ut cum fiducia in DEO, ad verf. 23. Sanctitatis studium in seipsis singillatim, & in omnibus bus Ecclesiæ membris promoventes, ad verf. 26. confidenter & patienter perseverent in fide, ad finem. Brevitatis autem causa, hortatio tota, hac propositione comprehendi poterit, Debetis cum fiducia in sanctitatis studio, confidenter & patienter perseverare. Argumenta hortationis quæ propositionem hanc probant & urgent, sunt novemdecim: Quorum aliqua, allusione facta ad typos ita proponit, ut interim ad rei significatæ excellentiam animum Hebræorum attollat.
units.tr: The second part of the chapter, in which he applies the preceding doctrine to practice by an exhortation made up of several parts, that with confidence in God, ministering to the holiness of themselves individually and of all the members of the Church, they may persevere confidently and patiently in the faith to the end (verse 23 to verse 26). For the sake of brevity, the whole exhortation can be summed up in this proposition: You ought, with confidence, in the pursuit of holiness, to persevere confidently and patiently. There are nineteen arguments which prove and press this exhortation. Some of them he sets out with an allusion to the types, so that in the meantime he raises the minds of the Hebrews to the excellence of the thing signified.

units.la: Habeamus ] Argumentum primum, Habetis unà nobiscum libertatem per fidem in precibus vestris in hac vita, & plenam potestionem post hanc vitam ingrediendi in cœlum, & ad Deum ipsum accedendi. Ergo debetis cum fiducia perseverare in fide.
units.tr: Habeamus] First argument: You have liberty along with us, through faith, in your prayers in this life, and the full power, after this life, of entering heaven and of approaching God himself. Therefore you ought to persevere in faith with confidence.

units.la: Per sanguinem ] Arg. 2. Per sanguinem seu mortem Iesu, tanquam per plenissimum pretium redemptionis & reconciliationis nostræ, paratur vobis hoc privilegium, ut in omnibus necessitatibus vestris, liberè sensa animi Deo proponatis. Ergo confidenter vobis est perseverandum.
units.tr: Per sanguinem] Argument 2. Through the blood or death of Jesus, as through the most full price of our redemption and reconciliation, this privilege is prepared for you, that in all your needs you may freely lay the feelings of your heart before God. Therefore you ought to persevere with confidence.

units.la: Verf. 20. Ea via quam dedicavit nobis recentem & vivam, per velum, hoc est per carnem suam:
units.tr: Verse 20. By the way which he has dedicated for us, new and living, through the veil, that is, through his flesh:

units.la: Arg. 3. in hunc sensum, Christus homo factus, & communione naturæ se nobiscum uniens, carnem suam seu humanitatem dedicavit in hunc usum, ut vos nobiscum hoc communionis vinculo adjuti (per ejus mediationem, tanquam per viam recentem, planam, tutam, & viventem, quæ ambulantes in ea vivificet, & delassatos refocillet) ad Deum accederetis, sicut Leviticus Pontifex per velum ingressus est in Sanctuarium. Ergo cum fiducia in Deum vobis perseverandum est.
units.tr: Argument 3, to this effect: Christ, made man, and uniting himself with us by a communion of nature, dedicated his flesh, or humanity, to this use, so that you, aided by this bond of communion with us (through his mediation, as through a new, plain, safe and living way, which will give life to those who walk in it and refresh the weary), might draw near to God, just as the high priest under the Law entered the sanctuary through the veil. Therefore you ought to persevere in God with confidence.

units.la: Verl. 21. Quumque habeamus Sacerdotem magnum, præfectum domui Dei:
units.tr: Verse 21. And since we have a great priest, set over the house of God:

units.la: Arg. 4. Habemus Christum Pontificem nostrum seu Sacerdotem magnum, qui præeat nobis in via, gerens iniquitatem inferiorum Sacerdotum, ne quæ à nobis perperam fiunt in nostro imperfecto colendi modo, aditum nobis ad Deum præcludant. Cum fiducia ergo in Deum vobis est perseverandum.
units.tr: Argument 4. We have Christ as our High Priest, or great Priest, who goes before us on the way, bearing the iniquity of the lesser priests, so that whatever is done amiss by us in our imperfect manner of worship may not shut off our access to God. Therefore you ought to persevere in God with confidence.

units.la: Præfectum ] Arg. fiduciæ 5. Habemus Christum nostri amantissimum, præfectum domui Dei, qui potestatem habet intromittendi in cœlum quos vult, locumque assignandi ingressis, quem vult, & ex thesauro gratiæ tribuendi ipsis quantum optari potest. Ergo cum fiducia vobis, unà nobiscum perseverandum est.
units.tr: Set over] Argument 5 of confidence. We have Christ, most loving of us, set over the house of God, who has the power of bringing into heaven whom he wills, and of assigning to those who enter the place he wishes, and of bestowing upon them out of the treasury of grace as much as can be desired. Therefore you ought to persevere along with us, with confidence.

units.la: Verf. 22. Accedamus cum vero corde, & certa persuasione, fidei, puris cordibus à conscientia mala:
units.tr: Verse 22. Let us draw near with a true heart, in full assurance of faith, with hearts sprinkled from an evil conscience:

units.la: Vers. 23. Et abluto corpore aqua pura, teneamus confessionem spei non vacillantem: (fidelis enim est qui promisit)
units.tr: Verse 23. And having our bodies washed with pure water, let us hold fast the confession of our hope without wavering (for he is faithful who has promised):

units.la: Arg. 6. Fidelibus datum est jus ad novum & sincerum cor, ad ple-nam persuasionem fidei, & ad quietam in Christo conscientiam, & ad vitæ sanctitatem, quæ per lotiones legales significabatur: Vos ergo per fidem nobiscum apprehendentes jus vestrum & aspergentes, seu applicantes vobis vim sanguinis Christi, per fidem certiorati in vitæ sanctitate debetis unâ nobiscum ad Deum accedere propius, & adhærescere Deo, ut confidentius perseveretis.
units.tr: Argument 6. The right to a new and sincere heart, to a full persuasion of faith, to a quiet conscience in Christ, and to the holiness of life, which was signified by the legal washings, has been given to believers. You, therefore, laying hold of your right along with us through faith, and sprinkling yourselves, or applying to yourselves, the power of Christ's blood, and being assured by faith, ought, in holiness of life, to draw nearer to God together with us, and cleave to God, so that you may persevere more confidently.

units.la: Fidelis] Arg. 7. Deus qui promisit omnem gratiam sperantibus in ipsum, ut in sanctitate perseverent ad salutem, fidelis est. Ergo cum fiducia vobis perseverandum est.
units.tr: Faithful] Argument 7. God, who has promised all grace to those who hope in him, so that they may persevere in holiness unto salvation, is faithful. Therefore you ought to persevere with confidence.

units.la: Vers. 24. Et observemus alii alios, ut nos acuamus ad charitatem & bona opera:
units.tr: Verse 24. And let us consider one another, to stir up one another to love and good works:

units.la: Vers. 25. Non deserentes aggregationem nostri mutuam, sicuti mos est quibusdam, sed adhortantes alii alios; idque eo magis quod videtis diem illum appropinquare.
units.tr: Verse 25. Not forsaking the assembling of ourselves together, as the manner of some is, but exhorting one another; and so much the more as you see the day approaching.

units.la: Arg. 8. Nisi diligentiam adhibeatis ut omnibus modis & mediis quæ vel ad propriam singulorum, vel ad Ecclesiæ in communi perseverantiam in fide & obedientia Euangelii faciant, (nempe alii alios observando, & exacuendo ad charitatem & bona opera, cœtus publicos observando; & unitatem Ecclesiæ conservando, &c.) periculum est ne separatio vel schisma sequatur, & tandem apostasia à fide, sicut in aliquorum exemplo experientia testatur. Ergo in fide perseverandum est.
units.tr: Argument 8. Unless you apply diligence, by all the means and methods which contribute to the perseverance in faith and obedience to the Gospel, both of each individual and of the Church in common (namely, by observing one another and stirring one another up to love and good works, by observing public assemblies, and by preserving the unity of the Church, etc.), there is danger that separation or schism will follow, and finally apostasy from the faith, as the experience of some examples bears witness. Therefore one must persevere in the faith.

units.la: Eo magis] Arg. 9. Dies judicii appropinquat, in quo perseverantibus, & à fide deficientibus, retributio secundum opera est danda. Ergo vobis studiose perseverandum est.
units.tr: So much the more] Argument 9. The day of judgment is drawing near, on which a reward according to works is to be given to those who persevere and to those who fall away from the faith. Therefore you ought to persevere diligently.

units.la: Vers. 26. Nam si ultrò peccaverimus post acceptam cognitionem veritatis, non adhuc pro peccatis reliqua est hostia.
units.tr: Verse 26. For if we sin willfully after we have received the knowledge of the truth, there remains no more sacrifice for sins.

units.la: Arg. 10. Nisi perstiteritis in fide, vel si post agnitam Euangelii veritatem, sponte, ultro, seu destinato animi proposito, defectionem feceritis ab Euangelio (quod est peccatum admittere in Spiritum Sanctum) non restat pro peccatis aliqua hostia, neque per consequens peccati remissio, siquidem malitiosè rejecto Christo, & ejus sacrificio, reliquum est nullum sacrificium pro peccato. Ergo ne incidatis in hanc abyssum studiosè perseverandum est.
units.tr: Argument 10. Unless you persist in the faith, or if after the truth of the Gospel has been acknowledged you make defection from the Gospel of your own accord, willingly, or with a deliberate purpose of mind (which is to sin against the Holy Spirit), no sacrifice remains for sins, and consequently no remission of sin, since, when Christ and his sacrifice have been maliciously rejected, no sacrifice for sin is left. Therefore, lest you fall into this abyss, you ought to persevere diligently.

units.la: Vers. 27. Sed horrenda quaedam expectatio judicii, & ignis fervor, qui devoraturus est adversarios.
units.tr: Verse 27. But a certain fearful expectation of judgment, and a fury of fire, which will devour the adversaries.

units.la: Arg. II. Apostatas, qui Christum agnitum ultro abiiciunt, & in adversaria castra malitiosè transeunt, manet metus horrendi judicii Dei, & ignis æterni certò devoraturi omnes Christi hostes, & inter primos, apostatas. Ergo perseverandum in fide.
units.tr: Argument 11. For apostates, who willingly cast off the recognised Christ and maliciously pass over into the hostile camp, there remains the dread of the horrible judgment of God and of eternal fire, certain to devour all the enemies of Christ, and first among them the apostates. Therefore one must persevere in the faith.

units.la: Vers. 28. Qui violarit Mosis legem, absque misericordia, ex duorum aut trium testimonio moritur.
units.tr: Verse 28. He who has violated the law of Moses dies without mercy, on the testimony of two or three witnesses.

units.la: Vers. 29. Quanto (putatis) acerbiore supplicio dignus censebitur, qui Filium Dei conculcarit, & sanguinem fœderis per quem fuerat Sanctificatus, profanum duxerit, & Spiritum gratiæ contumelia afficerit?
units.tr: Verse 29. Of how much sorer punishment, think you, will he be judged worthy, who has trodden under foot the Son of God, and has counted the blood of the covenant, by which he was sanctified, an unholy thing, and has insulted the Spirit of grace?

units.la: Hoc Argumentum confirmat sex rationibus: 1. Quia contemptor legis Mosaicæ legitimè convictus, capitale luebat supplicium, sine misericordia. Ergo multò magis apostata perdendus est.
units.tr: This argument he confirms with six reasons: 1. Because a despiser of the Mosaic law, lawfully convicted, paid the capital penalty without mercy. Therefore the apostate must much more certainly perish.

units.la: Conculcavit ] Ratio 2. Quia apostata non minori contumelia Christum afficit, quantùm in ipso est, quam si pedibus conculcaret ipsum de Throno detractum. Sanguinis ] Ratio 3. Quia sanctissimum sanguinem Christi, (per quem semel quoad externum hominem, seu carnis externam sanctificationem Ecclesiasticam, separati sunt à mundo, & Deo consecrati in Baptismo,) quasi de vulgo hominis cujuspiam sanguinem æstimant. Spiritum ] Ratio 4. Quia Spiritum Sanctum qui ipsos convicit de Christi Deitate, & Divinâ virtute, contumelia assiciunt quasi mendacem.
units.tr: Has trodden under foot] Reason 2. Because the apostate insults Christ with no less contempt, so far as in him lies, than if he trampled him under foot after casting him down from the throne. Blood] Reason 3. Because they esteem the most holy blood of Christ (through which they were once set apart from the world, as to the outward man, or the external ecclesiastical sanctification of the flesh, and consecrated to God in baptism) as the blood of some common man. Spirit] Reason 4. Because they insult the Holy Spirit, who has convinced them of Christ's deity and divine power, as a liar.

units.la: Vers. 30. Novimus enim eum qui dixit, Meum est ulcisci, ego repensam, dicit Dominus. Et rursum, Dominus judicabit populum suum.
units.tr: Verse 30. For we know him who said, Vengeance is mine, I will repay, says the Lord. And again, The Lord will judge his people.

units.la: Ratio 5. Quia Deus profitetur se Ultorem omnium peccatorum, & Vindicatorem injuriarum populo suo factarum, Deuter. 32. 35, 36. Et multò magis tam atrocis peccati adversùs Filium suum, simul & Ecclesiam totam, admissi.
units.tr: Reason 5. Because God professes himself the avenger of all sins and the vindicator of the injuries done to his people (Deut. 32:35, 36), and much more so of such an atrocious sin committed against his Son and at the same time against the whole Church.

units.la: Vers. 31. Horrendum est, incidere in manus Dei vivi. Ratio 6. Quia apostatis negotium est non cum miseris mortalibus, sed cum DEO vivo, hoc est, Omnipotente, & ad ultionem semper paratο, in cujus manus, ut in Judicis irati, incidere horrendum est. Ergo apostatis nihil expectandum praeter horrendum DEI judicium.
units.tr: Verse 31. It is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God. Reason 6. Because the apostates have to do not with wretched mortals but with the living God, that is, the Almighty, always ready for vengeance, into whose hands it is a dreadful thing to fall, as into those of an angry judge. Therefore nothing is to be expected by apostates except the dreadful judgment of God.

units.la: Simul hic habetur Argumentum 12. ad perseverandum in fide. Ultronea apostasia à fide, conjuncta est cum tot atrocibus in CHRISTUM & SPIRITUM Sanctum contumeliis. Ergo ab apostasia cavendum, & constanter in fide perseverandum est.
units.tr: At the same point there is also contained Argument 12 for perseverance in the faith. Voluntary apostasy from the faith is joined with so many atrocious insults against Christ and the Holy Spirit. Therefore one must beware of apostasy and persevere constantly in the faith.

units.la: Verf. 32. Revocate vero in memoriam superiores dies, quibus postquam illuminati fuistis, ingens certamen afflictionum sustinuistis:
units.tr: Verse 32. But call to remembrance the former days, in which, after you were enlightened, you endured a great fight of afflictions:

units.la: Verf. 33. Partim quidem, dum & cum probris, & cum oppressionibus in theatrum ejus producti: partim vero, dum socii facti ejus eorum qui eo statu versantur;
units.tr: Verse 33. Partly indeed, while you were both made a gazingstock with reproaches and afflictions, and partly while you became partners with those who were in such a state:

units.la: Verf. 34 Nam & de vinculis meis mecum doluistis; & direptionem facultatum vestrarum cum gaudio accepistis, ut qui sciretis vos habere apud vos potiorem substantiam in Cœlis, & quae permanent.
units.tr: Verse 34. For you both suffered with me in my bonds, and accepted with joy the plundering of your goods, knowing that you have in yourselves a better possession in heaven, which endures.

units.la: Arg. 13. Persequutionem patiendo pro Evangelio, edidistis jampridem constantiae vestrae in fide praeclarum specimen, in spe mercedis vobis in coelis repositae. Ergo in fide constanter vobis jam postea est perseverandum. Hoc Argumentum declarat, revocando illis in memoriam quomodo statim post receptam fidem CHRISTI, ex illuminatione Verbi & SPIRITUS DEI commissi sint quasi in certamen cum afflictionibus ingentibus, verf. 32. Partim dum ipsi publicè ignominia afficerentur ab Evangelii hostibus, & opprimerentur omnis generis injustitia & violentia. Partim denique dum se ex Christiana sympathia socios adjungebant afflictis & oppressis pro Evangelio, verf. 33. Id quod experientia manifestum facit, quia dum Apostolus vinciretur pro Evangelio, Hebraei fideles condoluerunt, & facultatum suarum direptionem cum gaudio acceperunt, nihil curantes terrenas divitias prae coelesti & aeterna haereditate in coelis sibi repositá, verf. 34.
units.tr: Argument 13. By suffering persecution for the Gospel, you have already given a notable proof of your constancy in the faith, in hope of the reward laid up for you in heaven. Therefore you must now persevere constantly in the faith. This argument is drawn from reminding them how, immediately after receiving the faith of Christ, through the enlightening of the Word and the Spirit of God, they were sent, as it were, into a contest with great afflictions (verse 32). Partly this happened when they themselves were publicly disgraced by the enemies of the Gospel and oppressed with every kind of injustice and violence; partly when they joined themselves, out of Christian sympathy, to those afflicted and oppressed for the Gospel (verse 33). Experience makes this plain, since when the Apostle was in bonds for the Gospel, the Hebrew believers grieved with him and accepted the plundering of their goods with joy, caring nothing for earthly riches in comparison with the heavenly and eternal inheritance laid up for them in heaven (verse 34).

units.la: Verf. 35. Ne igitur abjicite fiduciam vestram, quae magnam habet praemii retributionem.
units.tr: Verse 35. Therefore do not cast away your confidence, which has a great reward of recompense.

units.la: Arg. 14. Constans perseverantia in fide magnam habet praemii retributionem. Ergo non abjicienda, sed retinenda est vobis constanter fidei professio.
units.tr: Argument 14. Steadfast perseverance in the faith has a great reward of recompense. Therefore your profession of the faith is not to be cast away, but must be held fast constantly.

units.la: Verf. 36. Nam patientia vobis opus est: ut ubi voluntatem Dei praestiteritis, reportetis promissionem.
units.tr: Verse 36. For you have need of patience, that when you have done the will of God, you may receive the promise.

units.la: Arg. 15. Si patienter perseveraveritis, vitam aeternam vobis promissam reportabitis, alioqui non. Ergo constanter & patienter perseverandum est vobis.
units.tr: Argument 15. If you persevere patiently, you will obtain the eternal life promised to you; otherwise you will not. Therefore you must persevere constantly and patiently.

units.la: Verf. 37. Adhuc enim tantillum, tantillum inquam, & qui venturus est veniet, neque tardabit.
units.tr: Verse 37. For yet a very little while, a very little while, I say, and he who is coming will come and will not delay.

units.la: Arg. 16. Laborum statim finis erit, & modicum tantum restat ad victoriam: statim aderit Deus vos liberaturus ab omni molestia: (ut Propheta admonet, Habbak. 2. 4.) Ergo constanter perseverandum.
units.tr: Argument 16. The end of your labours will come at once, and only a little remains until victory: God will at once be present to deliver you from every trouble (as the Prophet admonishes, Habbak. 2. 4). Therefore you must persevere constantly.

units.la: Verf. 38. Justus autem ex fide vivet: at si quis se subduxerit, non probat eum animus meus.
units.tr: Verse 38. But the just shall live by faith: but if anyone draws back, my soul has no pleasure in him.

units.la: Arg. 17. Justus non praesenti spei suae possessione, sed fide vivet: justitiam simul & vitam, non nisi fide apprehendens. Ergo in fide vobis perseverandum est, ut justitiam & vitam consequamini.
units.tr: Argument 17. The just man lives not by the present possession of his hope but by faith, laying hold of righteousness and life together only through faith. Therefore you must persevere in faith, that you may obtain righteousness and life.

units.la: Siquis] Arg. 18. Qui abiecta fide superbit in fiducia carnali virium suarum, vel ullius creaturae virtuti innititur, odiosus est, & Deo & Sanctis ipsius: Ergo vobis in fide perseverandum est.
units.tr: If anyone] Argument 18. Whoever, having cast off faith, takes pride in a carnal confidence in his own strength, or leans on the power of some creature, is hateful both to God and to his saints. Therefore you must persevere in faith.

units.la: Verf. 39. At nos non ii sumus qui nos subducamus ad exitium, sed qui credamus ad animae salutem.
units.tr: Verse 39. But we are not of those who draw back to destruction, but of those who believe to the saving of the soul.

units.la: Arg. 19. Persuasum habeo nos qui vere fideles sumus, non esse de numero hypocritarum rejectitiorum, qui in die tentationis solent deficere ad sui perditionem, sed de numero Electorum, ex quibus nullus non perseverat ad animae suae salutem. Ergo vobis confidenter perseverandum est in fide.
units.tr: Argument 19. I am persuaded that we who are truly faithful are not of the number of reprobate hypocrites, who are wont to fall away in the day of temptation to their own perdition, but of the number of the elect, none of whom fails to persevere to the saving of his soul. Therefore you must persevere confidently in the faith.

units.la: Caput Undecimum.
units.tr: Chapter 11.

units.la: Ergit confirmare superiorem hortationem ad perseverandum in fide, variis argumentis deductis a fidei proprietatibus & effectis, multiplici experientia Sanctorum, illustratis. Argumenta hortationis sunt viginti quatuor, Quae omnia probant fovendam esse fidem, seu perseverandum in fide, seu vivendum ex fide in mediis afflictionibus.
units.tr: He goes on to confirm the previous exhortation to persevere in faith, using various arguments drawn from the properties and effects of faith and illustrated by the manifold experience of the saints. There are twenty-four arguments of this exhortation, all of which prove that faith must be cherished, that is, that we must persevere in faith and live by faith amid the greatest afflictions.

units.la: Verf. I. EST autem fides, illud quod facit ut extent quæ sperantur, & quod demonstrat quæ non videntur.
units.tr: Verse 1. Now faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen.

units.la: Argumentum primum, Fides amplexa promissionem de rebus sperandis, eas nobis sistit tanquam præsentes, isque quasi subsistentiam quandam tribuit, quatenus veritatem & potentiam Dei promittentis, (in cujus virtute res promissæ continentur) nobis applicat, & in gremium injicit, nosque tam certos reddit de eventu, quam si promissa jam præstita essent: Ergo in fide perseverandum & vivendum est.
units.tr: The first argument: faith, embracing the promise concerning things to be hoped for, sets them before us as if they were present. It gives them a kind of subsistence, inasmuch as it applies to us and places in our lap the truth and power of God who promises, in whose power the promised things are contained, and it makes us as certain of the outcome as if the promised things had already been given. Therefore we must persevere in faith and live by it.

units.la: Et quod] Arg 2. Fides amplexa Dei verbum est demonstratio convincens de veritate rerum præteritarum, præsentium, & futurarum quæ non videntur, vel nobis apparent, & tamen pro certissimis jure à nobis habentur, propter indubitatam autoritatem verbi Divini, Ergo in fide perseverandum & vivendum est.
units.tr: And that] Argument 2. Faith, embracing the Word of God, is a convincing demonstration of the truth of things past, present and future, which are not seen or which appear to us only dimly, yet which rightly count with us as most certain, on account of the indubitable authority of the divine Word. Therefore we must persevere in faith and live by it.

units.la: Verf. 2. Ob eam enim testimonio sunt ornati majores.
units.tr: Verse 2. For by it the elders obtained a good report.

units.la: Arg. 3 Per fidem, à Deo testimonio ornantur, laudantur, justificantur, & beati prædicantur fideles, ut in antiquorum exemplis in Scriptura positis appareat. Ergo in fide perseverandum est, & in mediis afflictionibus vivendum.
units.tr: Argument 3. Through faith, believers are honoured by God with testimony, praised, justified and pronounced blessed, as appears from the examples of the ancients set down in Scripture. Therefore we must persevere in faith and live by it amid afflictions.

units.la: Vers. 3. Per fidem intelligimus constructum sisse mundum verbo DEI, ut quæ cernimus non sint ex apparentibus facta.
units.tr: Verse 3. Through faith we understand that the worlds were framed by the word of God, so that things which are seen were not made of things which do appear.

units.la: Arg. 4. Fides sibi satisfacit in Verbo Dei omnipotentis, de constructione mundi ex nihilo, seu de creatione omnium quæ cernimus, ex nulla apparenti, vel præexistenti materia. Ergo ex fide vivendum est, in eâque perseverandum, etiamsi nihil cernamus eorum quæ in verbo Dei nobis promittuntur: Siquidem potest Deus non minus verbo suo promissam nobis salutem ex non apparentibus producere, quam potuit mundum ex nihilo creare.
units.tr: Argument 4. Faith rests satisfied in the Word of the almighty God concerning the framing of the world out of nothing, that is, concerning the creation of all that we see out of no visible or pre-existing matter. Therefore we must live by faith and persevere in it, even if we see nothing of the things promised to us in the Word of God; for God can bring forth from things not seen the salvation promised us by his word no less than he could create the world out of nothing.

units.la: Vers. 4. Abel per fidem majoris pretii sacrificium obtulit Deo quàm Caïn: per quam testimonium obtinuit quòd esset justus testimonium perhibente Deo de donis ejus: & per hanc mortuus adhuc loquitur.
units.tr: Verse 4. By faith Abel offered unto God a more excellent sacrifice than Cain, by which he obtained witness that he was righteous, God testifying of his gifts; and by it he being dead yet speaketh.

units.la: Sequuntur proprietates fidei, quæ illustrantur speciali experientiâ Sanctorum, quos in quatuor quasi classes ordinis cautâ dispescit. Prima classis est eorum qui vixerunt ante diluvium, ad versum 8. Secunda est eorum qui à diluvio ad descensum Israelis in Egyptum vixerunt, ad verf. 23. Tertia elt eorum qui sub exitum ex Egypto vixerunt, ad verf. 32. Quarta est eorum qui reliquo polt teinpore vixerunt, ad finem.
units.tr: There follow the properties of faith, which are illustrated by the special experience of the saints, whom the author carefully arranges in four classes. The first class consists of those who lived before the flood, to verse 8. The second consists of those who lived from the flood to the descent of Israel into Egypt, to verse 23. The third consists of those who lived near the exodus from Egypt, to verse 32. The fourth consists of those who lived in the remaining time, to the end.

units.la: In prima clafle primus elt Abel, qui dicitur praestantius sacrificium obtulisse per fidem quam Cain, non solum quia fides efficit ut delectum faceret praestantissimi sacrificii, quod per Dei mandatum licuit ipsi offerre, sed maxime quia per fidem in rem significatam, id est, in Messiam, immaculatum illum Agnum Dei promissum, qui sublaturus erat peccata mundi, conjecit oculos, & in Spiritu Deum coluit; cum Cain in nuda ceremonia superficiali tantummodo haereret. Atque ita declaratus est Abel justificatus per fidem, Deo testimonium perhibente de praestantia sacrificii ab ipso oblati: Per quam etiam fidem licet mortuus sit, loquitur hucusque tamen, exemplo suo docens omnes in Ecclesia, in Christum credere, fidemque suam sanguinis Martyrio, si Deus voluerit, obsignare. Hinc Arg. 5. Per fidem declarantur fideles justi, acceptantur ipsorum munera, cultus Deo oblatus probatur, & postea aedificantur fidelium exemplo, ut Abelis experientia manifestum est, ergo in fide perseverandum est.
units.tr: In the first class the first is Abel, who is said to have offered a more excellent sacrifice through faith than Cain. This was not only because faith led him to choose the most excellent sacrifice, which by God's command he was permitted to offer, but chiefly because through faith he fixed his eyes on the thing signified, that is, on the Messiah, the spotless Lamb of God promised, who was to take away the sins of the world, and worshipped God in spirit, whereas Cain clung only to the bare superficial ceremony. And so Abel was declared justified through faith, God bearing witness to the excellence of the sacrifice offered by him. Through that same faith, although he is dead, he still speaks, teaching by his example all in the Church to believe in Christ and, if God should will it, to seal their faith with the martyrdom of blood. Hence Argument 5: through faith the righteous believers are declared just, their gifts are accepted, the worship offered to God is approved, and afterwards they are built up by the example of the faithful, as the experience of Abel makes plain. Therefore we must persevere in faith.

units.la: Verf. 5.
units.tr: Verse 5.

units.la: Per fidem Enoch fuit translatus, ne videret mortem; nec fuit inventus, propterea quod translulerat eum DEVS: priusquam enim transferretur, testimonium obtinuerat quod placuisset DEO.
units.tr: By faith Enoch was translated that he should not see death; and was not found, because God had translated him: for before his translation he had this testimony, that he pleased God.

units.la: Verf. 6.
units.tr: Verse 6.

units.la: Atque fieri non potest, ut sine fide quisquam ei placeat; nam qui accedit ad Deum, hunc credere oportet esse Deum, & praemia largiri iis qui ipsum requirunt.
units.tr: But without faith it is impossible to please him: for he that cometh to God must believe that he is, and that he is a rewarder of them that diligently seek him.

units.la: Sequitur secundo loco Enoch, qui per Fidem dicitur translatus in vitam immortalem, non interveniente morte seu separatione animae a corpore, sed mutatione tantum facta a qualitatibus mortalibus ad immortales. Probat autem quod haec translatio fuerit fructus Fidei, quia Enoch Deo placuit, seu approbatus est ante translationem sui. Placere autem Deo impossibile est, nisi per fidem: cujus ratio redditur, quia nemo ad Deum accedit, seu in societatem cum Deo admittitur, nisi Dei omnisufficientiae & bonitati per fidem subscribat, ita ut etiam sibiipsi oblatam Dei bonitatem applicet, & accedat ad Deum, communionemque cum Deo colat. Sola enim fides est quae hominem omni dignitate propria exuit, Deoque misericordi & benigno agglutinat. Hinc Per fidem obtinemus æternam vitam, sicut Deus testatum nobis fecit per translationem Enochi, qui nisi fide præditus fuisset, non placuisset Deo, neque ad Deum accessisset, neque in Cœlum admissus suisset. Ergo in Fide perseverandum est.
units.tr: In the second place follows Enoch, who is said to have been translated through faith into immortal life, without death or the separation of soul from body intervening, but only by a change from mortal to immortal qualities. The author shows that this translation was the fruit of faith, because Enoch pleased God, that is, was approved, before his translation. Now it is impossible to please God except through faith. The reason is given: no one comes to God, or is admitted into fellowship with God, unless he subscribes to God's all-sufficiency and goodness through faith, so that he also applies to himself the goodness of God offered to him, and draws near to God and cultivates communion with him. For faith alone strips a man of all his own dignity and joins him to the merciful and kind God. Hence through faith we obtain eternal life, as God has shown us by the translation of Enoch, who, unless he had been endowed with faith, would not have pleased God, nor have come to God, nor have been admitted into heaven. Therefore we must persevere in faith.

units.la: Vers. 7. Per fidem divinitus admonitus Noe de iis quæ nondum videbantur, veritus apparavit arcam ad servandam domum suam, per quam arcam condemnavit mundum, & ejus quæ ex Fide est justitiæ factus est hæres.
units.tr: Verse 7. By faith Noah, being warned of God of things not seen as yet, moved with fear, prepared an ark to the saving of his house; by the which he condemned the world, and became heir of the righteousness which is by faith.

units.la: Tertius est Noach, qui divinitus admonitus de deluvio post multos annos venturo, credidit, & metuit, arcamque paravit ex Dei mandato ad familiæ suæ conservationem. Quo facto convicit incredulitatis reliquos in mundo secum tum viventes, & declaratus est hæres illius justitiæ, quæ est per fidem in Christum, qui per arcam repræsentatus est: Hinc Arg. 7. Per fidem cavemus nobis à Dei ira, mediisque ad salutem institutis diligenter utimur, per quam diligentiam mundum arguimus infidelitatis & socordiæ, & veritatem testamur fidei nostræ, per quam credimus in Christum, hæreditatemque justitiæ in illo consequimur, ut in experientia Noachi manifestum elt. Ergo in fide perseverandum est.
units.tr: The third is Noah, who, warned by God of a flood to come after many years, believed and feared, and prepared an ark by God's command for the preservation of his family. By doing this he convicted the rest of the unbelieving world who lived with him at that time, and he was declared heir of that righteousness which is through faith in Christ, who was represented by the ark. Hence Argument 7: through faith we guard ourselves from the wrath of God and diligently use the means instituted for salvation; by this diligence we accuse the world of unbelief and carelessness, and we attest the truth of our faith, by which we believe in Christ and obtain in him the inheritance of righteousness, as is evident from the experience of Noah. Therefore we must persevere in faith.

units.la: Vers. 8. Per Fidem, vocatus Abraham auscultavit Deo, ut abiret in locum quem accepturus erat in hæreditatem: & exivit, nesciens quo esset venturus:
units.tr: Verse 8. By faith Abraham, when he was called to go out into a place which he should after receive for an inheritance, obeyed; and he went out, not knowing whither he went.

units.la: Vers. 9. Per Fidem commoratus est in terra promissa ut aliena, commoratus est in tabernaculis cum Isaac & Jacob coharedibus ejusdem promissionis.
units.tr: Verse 9. By faith he sojourned in the land of promise, as in a strange country, dwelling in tabernacles with Isaac and Jacob, the heirs with him of the same promise.

units.la: Vers. 10. Expectabat enim urbem habentem fundamenta, cujus artifex & conditor est Deus.
units.tr: Verse 10. For he looked for a city which hath foundations, whose builder and maker is God.

units.la: Secunda classis Fidelium, qui à diluvio ad tempora descensus Israelitarum in Egyptum, vixerunt. In quo ordine primus est Abraham, qui per fidem renunciavit patriæ suæ, & Deum sequutus est in terram alienam, nixus Dei promissione de hæreditate sibi danda, incertus interim ubi terrarum ipse commoraturus esset, vers. 8. Per fidem etiam in terra promissa agebat in tabernaculis, ut Advena & peregrinus aliquis, sicut etiam Isaac & Jacob ejus posteri fecerunt, quibus eadem promissio hæreditatis facta est, vers. 9. Typicam enim illam terram Canaan, non tam respexit, 'quam repræsentatum per illam terram promissionis cœlum, quod est simile munitæ & firmissimæ fundatæ civitati, à Deo & non ab hominibus conditæ: Hinc Arg. 8. Per fidem vocati à Deo renunciamus rebus terrenis omnibus, & forte pro Dei beneplacito qualicunque in hoc mundo contenti peregrinamur, sub spe hæreditatis firmissimæ in cœlo à nobis possidendæ, ut in exemplo Abrahæ perspicuum est, Ergo in fide perseverandum est.
units.tr: The second class of believers, who lived from the flood to the time of the descent of the Israelites into Egypt. In this order the first is Abraham, who through faith renounced his homeland and followed God into a foreign land, relying on God's promise of an inheritance to be given him, uncertain meanwhile where on earth he himself would dwell (verse 8). Through faith he also lived in tabernacles in the promised land as a sojourner and stranger, as Isaac and Jacob his descendants did, to whom the same promise of inheritance was made (verse 9). For he regarded not so much that typical land of Canaan as the heaven represented by that land of promise, which is like a strongly fortified and firmly founded city, built by God and not by men. Hence Argument 8: through faith we, called by God, renounce all earthly things, and perhaps, content with whatever small portion pleases God in this world, we live as strangers, under the hope of a most firm inheritance to be possessed by us in heaven, as is plain from the example of Abraham. Therefore we must persevere in faith.

units.la: Vers. 11. Per Fidem & ipsa Sara vim ad concipiendum semen accepit, ac præter ætatis rationem peperit, quod Fidelem judicaverit eum qui promiserat.
units.tr: Ver. 11. By faith Sarah herself also received strength to conceive seed, and bore a child beyond the time of her age, because she judged him faithful who had promised.

units.la: Vers. 12. Quapropter & ex uno, eoque jam emortuo, nati sunt posteri, quanta est astrorum Cœli multitudo, & quasi arena illa innumerabilis, quæ est ad oram maris.
units.tr: Ver. 12. Therefore there were born from one man, and he already as good as dead, descendants as numerous as the stars of heaven, and as the innumerable sand which is by the seashore.

units.la: Antequam absolvat quæ dicturus erat de Abrahamo, mentionem facit fidei uxoris ipsius Saræ, cujus fides concurrebat cum Abrahami fide ad apprehendendam promissionem de numerosa sobole ab ipsis oriunda. Sarah per fidem nixa veritate promissionis Dei fidelis & omnipotentis, sterilis licet & vetula, supra naturæ vires idonea reddita est ad semen concipiendum, & filium Isaacum pariendum ex Abrahamo jam effœto, & respectu prolificationis quasi emortuo, atque ita Dei promissio de sobole innumerabilitate effectum sortita est. Hinc Argumentum 9: Per fidem idonei reddimur ad ea præstandum, quæ longè superant humanas vires, & ad promissionum, ratione carnali incredibilium, complementum recipiendum, sicut experientiâ Saræ comprobatum est. Ergo in fide perseverandum est.
units.tr: Before he finishes what he was going to say about Abraham, he mentions the faith of Abraham's wife Sarah, whose faith agreed with Abraham's in laying hold of the promise of a numerous offspring springing from them. Sarah, resting by faith on the truth of God's promise, faithful and almighty, was made fit, though barren and advanced in years, beyond the powers of nature to conceive seed and to bear the son Isaac from Abraham, who was already worn out and, as regards begetting, as good as dead. Thus God's promise of an innumerable offspring obtained its effect. Hence Argument 9: By faith we are made fit to do things that far exceed human powers, and to receive the fulfilment of promises that are incredible by carnal reasoning, as the experience of Sarah has proved. Therefore we must persevere in faith.

units.la: Verf. 13. Secundum fidem mortui sunt isti omnes, non adepti promissa, sed eminus ea conspicati, postquam credidissent, & amplexi essent, ac professi fuissent se hospites & advenas esse in terra.
units.tr: Ver. 13. These all died in faith, not having received the promises, but having seen them afar off, and having believed and embraced them, and having confessed that they were strangers and pilgrims on the earth.

units.la: Arg. 10. Omnes hi proximè recitati, nempe Abraham cum uxore Sara, & Isaacus, & Jacobus, perseveraverunt in fide, usque ad mortem, neque potiti sunt bonis à Deo promissis in hac vita: Tantùm per fidem cernebant rerum promissarum certitudinem, deque eâ persuasi eminus salutarunt promissa bona, extenuisque quasi fidei ulnis ea amplexi sunt, satis habentes quod essent iis post hanc vitam potituri profitentes. sitentes interim dum viverent, hospites se & advenas esse in terra. Ergo etiam & vobis in fide perseverandum, & ex fide vivendum est.
units.tr: Argument 10. All these just mentioned, namely Abraham with his wife Sarah, and Isaac, and Jacob, persevered in faith unto death, and did not obtain the good things promised by God in this life. They discerned the certainty of the promised things only by faith, and being persuaded of it, they greeted the promised good things from afar, and embraced them as it were with the arms of faith, being content to obtain them after this life, and confessing that while they lived they were strangers and pilgrims on the earth. Therefore we too must persevere in faith and live by faith.

units.la: Vers. 14. Nam qui haec dicunt, palam ostendunt se patriam quaerere:
units.tr: Ver. 14. For those who say these things plainly show that they seek a country.

units.la: Vers. 15. Quod si illius memores fuissent ex qua exierant, habuissent tempus ad revertendum:
units.tr: Ver. 15. And if they had been mindful of that country from which they had come out, they would have had opportunity to return.

units.la: Vers. 16. Nunc autem meliorem expetunt, hoc est, coelestem: quapropter non erubescit ipse DEUS, vocari DEUS eorum, paravERAT enim eis urbem.
units.tr: Ver. 16. But now they desire a better country, that is, a heavenly one; therefore God is not ashamed to be called their God, for he has prepared for them a city.

units.la: Probat eos quandiu in terris agebant non adeptos fuisse bona promissa, duabus rationibus. Ratio 1. Quia profitendo se hospites in terra esse, palam ostendebant se patriam quaerere, verf. 14. non autem terrenam patriam quaerebant, quia tempus habebant revertendi ad eam si illam quaesivissent, vers. 15. Ergo coelestem patriam a Deo promissam quaerebant.
units.tr: He proves in two ways that, as long as they lived on earth, they had not obtained the promised good things. Reason 1: by professing that they were strangers on the earth, they plainly showed that they sought a country (v. 14); but they did not seek an earthly country, since they had opportunity to return to it had they sought it (v. 15). Therefore they sought the heavenly country promised by God.

units.la: Quapropter] Ratio 2. Deus non erubuit Deus ipsorum vocari, unde significavit, & se urbem paratam, id est, coelum iis paratum habere, & statuisse eos a mortuis suscitare, ut tam corpore quam anima patriam illam desideratam possiderent, nam ut Deus ipsorum urbem illam paraverat eis, sic denominari se ab illis voluit Deus ipsorum, ut sciant omnes non separandos fuisse sanctos hos a Dei societate quam quaerebant.
units.tr: Therefore: Reason 2: God was not ashamed to be called their God. Thereby he signified both that he had a city prepared for them, that is, that he had heaven ready for them, and that he had determined to raise them from the dead, so that they might possess that desired country both in body and in soul. For just as God had prepared that city for them, so he wished to be called their God, so that all may know that these saints were not to be separated from the fellowship with God which they sought.

units.la: Vers. 17. Abraham quum tentaretur, obtulit Isaac per fidem, unigenitum, inquam, illum obtulit is qui promissiones exceperat.
units.tr: Ver. 17. By faith Abraham, when he was tested, offered up Isaac; yes, he offered up his only begotten son, he who had received the promises.

units.la: Vers. 18. Ad quem dictum fuerat, In Isaac vocabitur tibi semen.
units.tr: Ver. 18. To whom it had been said, In Isaac shall your seed be called.

units.la: Vers. 19. Quum illud secum perpendisset, Deum vel a mortuis excitare posse: unde etiam illum similitudine quadam recepit.
units.tr: Ver. 19. Reckoning that God was able to raise him even from the dead; from which also he received him back in a kind of parable.

units.la: Fuerunt argumenta ex communi effecto fidei patriarcharum. Sequuntur argumenta ex fidei effectis singulorum propriis. Primum commendat fidem Abrahami, quod cum Deus probaret ipsum, an fidem habiturus esset promissionibus, adeoque an in omnibus obediturus esset, nihil reliqui fecit ad offerendum Isaacum in holocaustum, licet unigenitum Filium suum, licet immediate accepisset Abraham promissiones de multiplicando semine in hoc ipso Isaaco, verf. 17. Licet diserte dictum fuerit ipsi de hoc ipso Isaaco, quod semen benedictum, (in quo omnes Gentes benedicendæ erant) ex eo oriturum esset, verf. 18. Per fidem enim Abraham ratiocinatus est Deum, qui ex effœtis parentibus Isaacum produxerat, potentiâ etiam præditum esse ad excitandum eum ex cineribus. Atque ita è faucibus mortis Isaacum ereptum recepit in similitudine quadam quasi à mortuis suscitatum, verf. 19. Hinc Arg. 11. Per fidem in tentationibus superantur omnia impedimenta, quæ obedientiam Deo præstandam ullo modo possent remorari, idque felicissimo cum successu, ut Abrahami experientia manifestum facit. Ergo in fide perseverandum est.
units.tr: These were arguments drawn from the common effect of the patriarchs' faith. Now follow arguments drawn from the particular effects of the faith of individuals. The first commends Abraham's faith: when God tested him, whether he would have faith in the promises and so whether he would obey in all things, he held nothing back from offering Isaac as a burnt offering, although Isaac was his only begotten son, and although Abraham had immediately received the promise of a multiplied seed in this very Isaac (v. 17). Indeed it had been plainly said to him about this very Isaac that the blessed seed, in whom all nations were to be blessed, would come from him (v. 18). For by faith Abraham reasoned that God, who had brought forth Isaac from parents who were as good as dead, was also endowed with power to raise him from the ashes. And so he received Isaac back, snatched from the jaws of death, as it were raised from the dead in a kind of parable (v. 19). Hence Argument 11: By faith all hindrances that could in any way delay the obedience to be rendered to God are overcome in temptations, and that with the happiest success, as the experience of Abraham makes plain. Therefore we must persevere in faith.

units.la: Verf. 20 Per fidem defuncto benedixit Isaac filio Jacob & Esau.
units.tr: Ver. 20. By faith Isaac, when he was about to die, blessed his sons Jacob and Esau.

units.la: Proximè nominat Isaacum, qui per fidem pronunciavit de futuris benedictionibus, ac si eas præsens conspexisset: Unde Arg 12. Per fidem futuræ benedictiones quasi præsentes statuuntur, deque iis certitudo non minor habetur, quam si coram tenfu aspicerentur. Ergo in fide perseverandum est.
units.tr: Next he names Isaac, who by faith pronounced concerning future blessings, as if he had seen them present before him. Hence Argument 12: By faith future blessings are held as if they were present, and certainty about them is had no less than if they were seen with the eyes. Therefore we must persevere in faith.

units.la: Verf. 21. Per fidem, Jacob moriens singulis filiis Joseph benedixit: & adoravit baculo innixus.
units.tr: Ver. 21. By faith Jacob, when dying, blessed each of the sons of Joseph, and worshipped, leaning on the top of his staff.

units.la: Sequitur Iacobi exemplum, qui moriens, & se, & filios suos consolatus est per fidem, de benedictionibus secundum Dei promissionem venturis in nepotes suos, & eorum posteros, idque tantâ cum persuasione, ut præ gaudio adoraverit Deum, baculo innitens præ corporis infirmitate: Hinc Arg. 13. Per fidem morientes consolationem capere possunt, & non seipsos solùm, sed etiam alios de benedictionibus promissis confirmare, Ut in exemplo morientis Iacobi videre est: Ergo in fide perseverandum est.
units.tr: There follows the example of Jacob, who, dying, comforted both himself and his sons by faith, concerning the blessings to come according to God's promise upon his grandchildren and their posterity. He did so with such persuasion that, for joy, he worshipped God, leaning on his staff because of the weakness of his body. Hence Argument 13: By faith dying men can receive comfort, and can confirm not only themselves but also others concerning the promised blessings, as is seen in the example of dying Jacob. Therefore we must persevere in faith.

units.la: Verf. 22. Per fidem, Joseph moriens de egressione filiorum Israel meminit, deque ossibus suis mandavit.
units.tr: Ver. 22. By faith Joseph, when dying, made mention of the departure of the children of Israel, and gave commandment concerning his bones.

units.la: Patriarcharum ultimus nominatur Joseph, cujus animo neque potestas, neque bonorum affluentia qua potiebatur in Egypto, oblivionem, aut neglectum inducere potuit promissionum Dei, quin persuasus de egressione filiorum Israel ex Egypto, deque introductione eorum (licet post multos annos) in terram Patribus promissam, mandaret ossa sua simul asportari, in testimonium quod rem significatam per terram promissam omnibus rebus terrenis prætulerit. Unde Arg. 14.
