Fides superat temporis diuturnitatem, ante promissionis complementum intercedentis, unâque cum vitæ hujus commodis mortis & sepulchri putredinem, & mala, & futuram resurrectionem cum Sanctis constanter expectat, ut in Josephi morientis exemplo videmus. Ergo in fide perseverandum est.
units.tr: The last of the patriarchs named is Joseph, whose mind neither the power nor the abundance of goods which he enjoyed in Egypt could bring to forget or neglect God's promises. Rather, persuaded of the departure of the children of Israel from Egypt, and of their introduction (though after many years) into the land promised to the fathers, he commanded that his bones be carried away along with them, as a testimony that he preferred the thing signified by the promised land to all earthly things. Hence Argument 14: Faith overcomes the long lapse of time that intervenes before the fulfilment of the promise, and, together with the comforts of this life, constantly awaits the putrefaction of death and of the grave, and the evils, and the future resurrection with the saints, as we see in the example of dying Joseph. Therefore we must persevere in faith.

units.la: Vers. 23. Per fidem, Moses quum natus esset, occultatus est mensies tres à parentibus suis, quod viderent venustum esse puerulum; & non timuerunt edictum regis,
units.tr: Ver. 23. By faith Moses, when he was born, was hidden for three months by his parents, because they saw that the child was beautiful; and they did not fear the king's edict,

units.la: Sequitur tertia classis exemplorum, à temporibus prope egressum Israelis ex Egypto, ad tempora Judicum. Primum exemplum est Parentum Moisis, qui colligentes ex pueri Moisis pulchritudine, Deum designasse ipsum ad singulare aliquod opus, per fidem occultarunt ipsum tres menses, toto illo tempore non passi, ut metus edicti Regii obstaret, quo minus vivum conservarent eum, quem Rex ut masculum in profluentem abjicii edixerat: Unde Arg. 15. Per fidem superatur metus, quem tyranni injustis edictis suis, fidelibus injiciunt, ut in exemplo parentum Moisis manifestum est. Ergo in fide perseverandum est.
units.tr: There follows the third class of examples, from the times near the departure of Israel from Egypt to the times of the Judges. The first example is that of Moses' parents. Gathering from the beauty of the boy Moses that God had designated him for some singular work, they by faith hid him for three months, and throughout that whole time did not allow the fear of the king's edict, by which the king had ordered male children to be cast into the flowing river, to stand in the way, so that they would not keep alive the one whom the king had ordered to be thrown out as a male. Hence Argument 15: By faith fear, which tyrants instil into the faithful by their unjust edicts, is overcome, as is manifest in the example of Moses' parents. Therefore we must persevere in faith.

units.la: Vers. 24. Per fidem, Moses jam grandis renuit vocari Filius Filiae Pharaonis.
units.tr: Ver. 24. By faith Moses, when he was grown, refused to be called the son of Pharaoh's daughter.

units.la: Vers. 25. Potius eligens simul malis affici cum populo DEI, quam temporariis commodis peccati frui.
units.tr: Verse 25. Choosing rather to suffer affliction together with the people of God than to enjoy the temporary pleasures of sin.

units.la: Vers. 26. Majores arbitratus divitias probrum Christi, quam Aegyptiorum thesauros. Intuebatur enim in praemii largitionem.
units.tr: Verse 26. Esteeming the reproach of Christ greater riches than the treasures of the Egyptians. For he looked to the bestowal of the reward.

units.la: Secundum exemplum est Moisis, cujus fidei actus plures numerantur, qui plurium Exemplorum & Argumentorum vim habent. Primus actus fidei Moisis est, quod jam adultus, rationis & consilii potens, per fidem contempserit cognationem regis n, maluitque Hebraeus vocari, quam nepos Pharaonis: quod fecit non tam verbis quam facto, quando relictâ aulâ regiâ egressus est ad fratres suos Hebraeos in afflictione visitandos, nec ad aulae delicias ultra est reversus, verf. 24. actum hunc Apostolus commendat triplici nomine; Primo, quod elegerit potius afflictiones omnes in exilio, & servitute dura pati, ut populo Dei tandem aliquando prodesset, quam deesse officio suo, & momentaneis deliciis aulicis cum peccato, seu officii neglectu, frui, verf. 25. Secundo; quod contemni, unà cum populo Dei, propter fidem in Christum venturum, atque ita gestare crucem, seu probrum Christi (in quem ut caput, injuriae factae ipsius membris, reflectuntur) majores divitias aestimaverit, quam thesauros Egyptiorum in aula Pharaonis possidere. Tertio, quod le sustinuerit spe liberationis populi Dei, & expectatione gratuiti præmii, quod Deus promisit servis suis se redditurum: Unde probatur totum quod de Mose dixit, fidei esse effectum, vers. 26. Hinc Arg. 16. Per fi-dem vilescunt honores & divitiæ, aliæque illecebræ mundanæ, quibus capiuntur incauti homines ad suam perditionem, & splendescunt afflictiones, Christi nomine toleratæ, propter Communionem cum Sanctis, & Christo ipso, in persecutionibus obsignatam, & expectationem præmii afflictis Dei servis promissi, ut in exemplo Mosis perspicuè apparet. Ergo in fide perseverandum est.
units.tr: The second example is that of Moses, whose acts of faith are many, and which have the force of many examples and arguments. The first act of faith of Moses is that, being already a grown man, able to reason and to judge, he by faith rejected the kinship of the king's daughter and preferred to be called a Hebrew rather than the grandson of Pharaoh. He did this not so much in words as in deed, when he left the royal court to visit his brethren the Hebrews in their affliction, and afterwards did not return to the court's luxuries. The Apostle commends this act under three heads, in verse 24. First, that he chose rather to suffer all afflictions in exile and harsh servitude, so that at last he might be of use to the people of God, than to fail in his duty and enjoy the momentary pleasures of the court, with sin or with neglect of duty (verse 25). Second, that he judged the reproach of Christ, that is, the scorn he bore together with the people of God for the sake of faith in the Christ who was to come, and so bearing the cross (the injuries done to his members being reflected upon Christ as the head), to be greater riches than to possess the treasures of the Egyptians in Pharaoh's court. Third, that he endured this in hope of the deliverance of the people of God and in expectation of the free reward which God promised to repay to his servants. Hence it is shown that all that is said of Moses was the effect of faith (verse 26). Hence the argument 16: through faith, honours and riches and other worldly allurements, by which unwary men are caught to their own destruction, grow worthless; and the afflictions borne for the name of Christ shine forth, because of fellowship with the saints and with Christ himself, sealed in persecutions, and because of the expectation of the reward promised to God's afflicted servants, as is plainly seen in the example of Moses. Therefore one must persevere in faith.

units.la: Vers. 27 Per Fidem reliquit Ægyptum, nihil timens iram regis: nam ut qui videret eum qui est invisibilis, ita forti animo fuit.
units.tr: Verse 27. By faith he left Egypt, not fearing the wrath of the king; for as one who saw him who is invisible, so he was of strong courage.

units.la: Secundus Actus fidei Mosis est, quod fretus promissione Dei, Pharaoni denunciaverit, se vel invito ipso, populum Israeliticum ex Ægypto educaturum, & facto reliquerit Ægyptum, unà cum universo populo, cui ad discedendum Author & Dvctor fuit. Hic actus duplici nomine commendatur: Primò, quod non metuerit iram regis, qui timidum & imbellem populum abeuntem, collectis copiis armatâ vi, vel occidere, vel in graviorem servitutem retrahere potuisset, nisi Deus se opposuisset. Secundò, quod fide intuitus sit Dei invisibilis veritatem & potentiam, seque in difficultatibus omnibus hoc aspectu se sustinuerit, unde probat actum hunc, fidei effectum fuisse. Hinc Arg. 17. Per fidem promissam liberationem populi Dei ex regno tenebrarum prosequimur, & superamus omnem metum, quem tyrannorum ira, & armata potentia contendentibus ad promissam hæreditatem injicere possent, oculis semper in Dei invisibilis promissum auxilium, intentis, ut in Mosis exemplo probatum est. Ergo in side perseverandum est.
units.tr: The second act of faith of Moses is that, trusting in the promise of God, he declared to Pharaoh that he would lead the Israelite people out of Egypt even if the king were unwilling, and in fact he left Egypt together with the whole people, of whom he was the author and leader of their departure. This act is commended under two heads. First, that he did not fear the wrath of the king, who, if he had gathered his forces and used armed might, could have either slain the timid and unwarlike people as they departed or dragged them back into harsher servitude, had God not opposed him. Second, that by faith he looked upon the truth and power of the invisible God, and sustained himself in all difficulties by this gaze; hence the Apostle proves that this act was the effect of faith. Hence the argument 17: through faith we pursue the promised deliverance of God's people out of the kingdom of darkness, and we overcome all fear which the anger of tyrants and armed power could strike into those who strive for the promised inheritance, our eyes always fixed upon the promised help of the invisible God, as has been proved in the example of Moses. Therefore one must persevere in faith.

units.la: Vers. 28. Per fidem peregit Pascha, & effusionem illam sanguinis: ne, qui perimebat primogenita ipsos tangeret.
units.tr: Verse 28. By faith he kept the Passover and the sprinkling of blood, lest he who destroyed the firstborn should touch them.

units.la: Tertius Actus fidei Mosis est, quod ex Dei promissione certioratus & persuasus, celebraverit in Ægypto festum Paschatis, effusoque Agni Paschalis sanguine, aspergenda curaverit ostia Israelitarum omnium: Dei nomine omnibus promittens fore ut liberarentur à plaga Angeli, (illâ nocte interempturi Primogenitos Ægyptiorum) quicunque ædes haberent agni immolati sanguine insignitas. Hinc Arg. 18. Per hdem, Sacramenta in Ecclesia, publicumque Dei cultum celebramus, in testimonium spei nostræ de liberatione ab interitu, quo involvendus est reliquus mundus, ut apparet in Mosis exemplo. Ergo in fide perseverandum est.
units.tr: The third act of faith of Moses is that, being made certain and persuaded by the promise of God, he celebrated the feast of the Passover in Egypt, and, the blood of the paschal lamb having been poured out, he saw to it that the doorposts of all the Israelites were sprinkled, promising to all in God's name that they would be delivered from the plague of the Angel (who was to slay the firstborn of the Egyptians that night) whoever had houses marked with the blood of the slain lamb. Hence the argument 18: through faith we celebrate the sacraments in the Church and the public worship of God, as a testimony of our hope of deliverance from the destruction in which the rest of the world is to be involved, as appears in the example of Moses. Therefore one must persevere in faith.

units.la: Vers. 29. Per Fidem transierunt rubrum mare, veluti per siccam terram: cujus facto periculo Ægyptii obsorpti sunt.
units.tr: Verse 29. By faith they passed through the Red Sea as through dry land, which, when the Egyptians attempted it, they were swallowed up.

units.la: Tertium Exemplum est credentium Israelitarum, unà cum ductore ipsorum Mose, qui per fidem, sicut aliì sunt divisarum aquarum apertas fauces ingredi, & iter per umbram mortis satis longum capellere, sic incolumes transierunt rubrum mare, veluti per aridam terram: Ægyptii verò absque Dei promissione periculum facientes, an possent eos sequi, absorpti sunt. Hinc Arg. 19. Per fidem res humanæ rationi impossibiles aggredimur, & pericula in quibus pereunt infideles, pervadimus, ut in populi transitu per mare rubrum manifestum est, Ergo in fide perseverandum est.
units.tr: The third example is that of the believing Israelites, together with their leader Moses, who by faith, as others entered the open jaws of the divided waters and undertook a road long enough through the shadow of death, so they passed unharmed through the Red Sea as through dry land; but the Egyptians, attempting it without any promise of God, to see whether they could follow them, were swallowed up. Hence the argument 19: through faith we undertake things impossible to human reason, and we pass through the dangers in which unbelievers perish, as is clear in the passage of the people through the Red Sea. Therefore one must persevere in faith.

units.la: Vers. 30. Per Fidem Mœnia Jericho conciderunt quum ea circumvissent ad dies septem.
units.tr: Verse 30. By faith the walls of Jericho fell down, after they had been encircled for seven days.

units.la: Exemplum 4. Est Josuæ & Israelitarum credentium, qui pet fidem expectantes ruinam murorum Jerichuntis, ad septem dies mœnia circumierunt cum arcâ fœderis, & tubis Sacerdotalibus, nec ípe frustrati sunt. Hinc Arg. 20. Per fidem, Credentes precibus suis absque ope omni humanâ munitissimas arces & urbes hostium suorum dejiciunt, & expugnant; ut in exemplo Israelitarum ingredientium in terram promissam probatum est. Ergo in fide perseverandum est.
units.tr: The fourth example is that of Joshua and the believing Israelites, who, by faith awaiting the fall of the walls of Jericho, went around the walls for seven days with the ark of the covenant and the priestly trumpets, and were not disappointed. Hence the argument 20: through faith, believers, by their prayers and without any human help, cast down and conquer the most strongly fortified citadels and cities of their enemies, as was proved in the example of the Israelites entering the promised land. Therefore one must persevere in faith.

units.la: Vers. 31. Per Fidem, Rahab meretrix illa non periit unà cum iis qui non obedierant, quum pacificè excepisset hospitio exploratores.
units.tr: Verse 31. By faith Rahab the harlot did not perish with those who did not obey, when she had received the spies peaceably into her house.

units.la: Exemplum 5. Est fidei Rachab meretricis, & alienigenæ, in qua studium servandi exploratores respicit Deus ut effectum fidei, mendacium vero ab humana infirmitate profectum abluit, & præteriit sed non probat; nam qui fidem habent non agunt omnia ex fide. Muliercula hæc per fidem in Deum Israelis, pacificè excepit, & clam dimisit exploratores Israeliticos, & servata est, ne periret cum incredulis concivibus suis Jerichuntinis. Hinc Arg. 21. Nulla peccata præcedentia impedire possunt, quo minus qui per fidem confugiunt ad Deum & consortium veræ Ecclesiæ, servantur, ne pereant cum infidelibus, ut exemplo meretricis Rachab conversæ ad fidem apparet. Ergo in fide perseverandum est.
units.tr: The fifth example is the faith of Rahab, the harlot and foreigner, in whom God regards her zeal in saving the spies as an effect of faith, while her lie, which proceeded from human weakness, he washes away and passes over, but does not approve; for those who have faith do not do everything from faith. This little woman, by faith in the God of Israel, received the spies peaceably and secretly sent away the Israelite spies, and she was preserved so that she would not perish with her unbelieving fellow citizens of Jericho. Hence the argument 21: no preceding sins can prevent those who flee by faith to God and to the fellowship of the true Church from being saved and not perishing with unbelievers, as appears in the example of the harlot Rahab converted to the faith. Therefore one must persevere in faith.

units.la: Verf. 32. Et quid praterea loquor? deficiet enim me tempus commemorantem de Gideone, de Barac, & Samsone, & Jephthe, & Davide, & Samuele, ac Prophetis:
units.tr: Verse 32. And what more shall I say? For time would fail me to tell of Gideon, Barak, Samson, Jephthah, David, Samuel, and the Prophets:

units.la: Verf. 33. Qui per fidem debellarunt regna, exercuerunt justitiam, assecuti sunt promissiones, obluserunt ora leonum:
units.tr: Verse 33. Who through faith subdued kingdoms, wrought righteousness, obtained promises, stopped the mouths of lions:

units.la: Verf. 34. Extinxerunt vim ignis, effugerunt acies gladii, validi facti sunt ex imbecillis, effecti sunt robusti in bello, exercitus exterorum in fugam verterunt:
units.tr: Verse 34. Quenched the violence of fire, escaped the edge of the sword, out of weakness were made strong, waxed valiant in fight, turned to flight the armies of the aliens:

units.la: Verf. 35. — Mulieres acceperunt ex resurrectione mortuos suos:
units.tr: Verse 35. Women received their dead raised to life again:

units.la: Sequitur 4. Classis exemplorum, nempe fidei eorum qui reliquo post Josuam tempore vixerunt, quorum nomina recitat aliquot, numero sex, & his adjungit in cumulo, Prophetas aliosque sanctos, qui ante Christum vixerunt: ex quibus alii, Quid non valuerunt per fidem efficere? Alii vero quid non valuerunt per fidem pati? Factorum autem genera enumerat decem: 1. Alii per fidem debellarunt regna, ut Judices nominati & David rex: 2. Alii exercuerunt justitiam in casibus difficillimis probati, ut cum David bis pepercit Sauli hostiliter ipsum persequenti: 3. Alii superatis difficultatibus constanter perdurarunt, donec speciales ipsis factae promissiones praestitae sunt, ut David promissum regnum per fidem adeptus est: 4. Alii occluserunt per fidem ora Leonum, ut Sampson, David, Daniel, verf. 33: 5. Alii per fidem extinxerunt vim ignis, ut tres socii Danielis: 6. Alii effugerunt acies gladii, seu praesentissimam mortem, ut Elias fugiens minas Jezabelis: 7. Alii corroborati sunt in infirmitate & convaluerunt ex morbis lethalibus, ut Ezechias: 8. Alii effecti sunt robusti in bello, ut Samson & David: 9. Alii exercitus exterorum in fugam verterunt, ut Gideon verf. 34: 10. Alii acceperunt ex resurrectione mortuos suos, ut Vidua Sareptana hospita Eliae. Et Shunamita hospita Elizaei verf. 35.
units.tr: There follows the fourth class of examples, namely the faith of those who lived in the time after Joshua, whose names he recites, six in number, and to these he adds in a heap the Prophets and other saints who lived before Christ. Of these some, (1) what they could not effect through faith; others (2) what they could not suffer through faith. He lists ten kinds of deeds: (1) some by faith subdued kingdoms, as the named Judges and King David; (2) some practised righteousness, proved in the most difficult cases, as when David twice spared Saul, who was hostilely pursuing him; (3) some, having overcome difficulties, persevered constantly until the special promises made to them were fulfilled, as David obtained by faith the kingdom promised to him; (4) some by faith stopped the mouths of lions, as Samson, David, and Daniel (verse 33); (5) some by faith quenched the violence of fire, as the three companions of Daniel; (6) some escaped the edge of the sword, that is, the most imminent death, as Elijah fleeing the threats of Jezebel; (7) some were strengthened in weakness and recovered from deadly diseases, as Hezekiah; (8) some were made strong in war, as Samson and David; (9) some turned to flight the armies of aliens, as Gideon (verse 34); (10) some received their dead raised to life again, as the widow of Zarephath, the hostess of Elijah, and the Shunammite, the hostess of Elisha (verse 35).

units.la: Verf. — 35 Alii vero distenti sunt, neglecta liberatione, ut potiorem resurrectionem nancisccrentur.
units.tr: Verse 35. But others were tortured, refusing deliverance, so that they might obtain a better resurrection.

units.la: Atque haec sunt genera actionum illustrium, in quibus excelluerunt sancti per fidem, Sequuntur etiam decem genera passionum, in quibus fortiter ferendis, superiores per fidem evaserunt alii Sancti Dei tervi, quorum nomina non recitat, sed an ejusmodi fuerint dubitare nefas, cum autorem habeamus Spiritum Sanctum, qui amanuensem suum Paulum de veritate dictorum certissimum reddidit, ut nullus restet nobis dubitandi locus, imo nec locus quaerendi curiose, ex qua historia desumpserit illa, cum sciamus hanc ipsam narrationem omni exceptione majorem esse. Primum genus passionum, alii distenti sunt per tortores suos, quemadmodum corium in tympano distenditur, & fustibus percussi ut tympana, donec intumescerent & morerentur, quibus oblata est liberatio si fidem abnegarent; sed liberationem ea conditione promissam contempserunt, sub spe resurrectionis ad vitam meliorem.
units.tr: These are the kinds of illustrious deeds in which the saints excelled through faith. There follow also ten kinds of sufferings, in enduring which bravely, other servants of God, whose names he does not recite, prevailed through faith. But to doubt that they were of this sort is wrong, since we have as author the Holy Spirit, who made his amanuensis Paul most certain of the truth of what was said, so that no ground for doubt remains for us, nor even ground for inquiring curiously from what history he took those things, since we know that this very narration is greater than any exception. The first kind of suffering: some were stretched by their torturers, as hide is stretched on a drum, and beaten with clubs like drums, until they swelled up and died; and deliverance was offered to them if they would renounce their faith; but they despised the deliverance promised on that condition, looking to the hope of resurrection to a better life.

units.la: Verf. 36. Alii rursus ludibria & flagella sunt experti, insuper & vincula & carcerem.
units.tr: Verse 36. Others again experienced mockings and scourgings, besides chains and prison.

units.la: Secundum genus passionum, Alii passi sunt ludibria: 3. Alii verberibus affecti: 4. Alii insuper vinculis astricti: 5. Et alii etiam carceribus inclusi.
units.tr: The second kind of suffering: some suffered mockings; (3) some were subjected to beatings; (4) some were moreover bound with chains; (5) and some also were shut up in prisons.

units.la: Verf. 37. Lapidati sunt, dissecti sunt, tentati sunt, gladio caesi occubuerunt: oberraverunt cum ovillis & caprinis pellibus: destituti, oppressi, male habiti: Verf. 38 (Quorum indignum erat mundus) in deserti errantes, & montibus ac speluncis, & cavernis terrae.
units.tr: Verse 37. They were stoned, they were sawn asunder, they were tempted, they died by the sword; they wandered about in sheepskins and goatskins, destitute, oppressed, ill-treated; Verse 38 (of whom the world was not worthy), wandering in deserts, and on mountains, and in dens and caves of the earth.

units.la: Genus 6. Alii lapidati sunt: 7. Alii terra dissecti sunt: 8. Alii tentati, nunc illecebris allecti, nunc minis territi, nunc importunitate amicorum solicitati; nunc disputationibus & sophismatis ad oppugnandam Fidem comparatis, vexati: Quod genus tormenti morte ipsa acerbius est, imbecillitatis suae conscii, & metuentibus ne succumbant in tentationibus: 9. Alii gladio caesi occubuerunt: 10. Alii qui necem effugerunt, oberrarunt, certas sedes non habentes, ob persequutorum saevitiam loca subinde mutare coacti; prae inopia vestimentorum amicti ovillis & caprinis pellibus ad nuditatem tegendam, destituti ope & auxilio hominum, ad varias angustias redacti, & a mundo male tractati quocunque venirent, adeo ut elegerint in montibus, in desertis, in speluncis & cavernis terrae, inter feras potius quam inter homines agere. Qui ne a Deo deserti in his malis videri possent, pronunciat Apostolus genus humanum, (quod ipsos tam misere tractabat) indignum fuisse ejusmodi perticiorum Dei servorum consortio. Ex his omnibus brevitatis causa unicum tantum Argumentum ducemus, quod memoriae causa statuimus. Arg. 22. Quid est quod per fidem non valebimus efficere eorum quæ à nobis Deus requirit efficienda? Quid est quod per fidem non valebimus pati, seu sufferre eorum quæ Deus nobis imponit ferenda, sicut Deus Fidelium Sanctorum experientiâ nobis comprobatum reddidit: Ergo fovenda fides, ex eâ vivendum, & in eâ perseverandum est.
units.tr: The sixth kind: some were stoned; (7) some were sawn asunder; (8) some were tempted, at one time enticed by allurements, at another terrified by threats, at another harassed by the importunity of friends, at another assailed by disputations and sophisms devised to attack the faith; a kind of torment more bitter than death itself, for those who are aware of their own weakness and fear lest they succumb to temptations; (9) some died by the sword; (10) some who escaped death wandered about, having no fixed abode, compelled by the savagery of their persecutors to change places from time to time; clothed in sheepskins and goatskins to cover their nakedness for want of garments, destitute of help and assistance from men, reduced to various straits, and ill-treated by the world wherever they came, so that they chose to live in mountains, in deserts, in caves and dens of the earth, among wild beasts rather than among men. Lest these men should seem to be forsaken by God in these evils, the Apostle declares that the human race (which treated them so wretchedly) was unworthy of the fellowship of such excellent servants of God. From all these, for the sake of brevity, we will draw only one argument, which we set down for the sake of memory. Argument 22. What is there that through faith we shall not be able to accomplish of those things which God requires us to accomplish? What is there that through faith we shall not be able to endure, or bear, of those things which God lays upon us to be borne, as God has shown us by the experience of his faithful saints? Therefore faith is to be cherished, we must live by it, and persevere in it.

units.la: Verf. 39. Atque hi omnes testimonium adepti per fidem, non obtinuerunt promissum:
units.tr: Verse 39. And all these, having obtained a good report through faith, did not receive the promise:

units.la: Arg. 23. Omnes (de quibus diximus) sancti per fidem à Deo approbati, justificati, seu testimonio Dei ornati sunt, quod Deo placuerint; nec tamen magnum promissum illud de incarnando Messia, seu de semine illo mulieris venturo (in quo omnes promissiones sunt Etiam & Amen,) completum habuerunt, dum in vivis agerent: Cum igitur illi qui in obscuriore luce vivebant, perseverarunt in omnibus persecutionibus, constantes in Fide Christi venturi, quanto magis debemus nos, qui promissionem illam completam videmus in Fide Christi jam exhibiti, perseverare.
units.tr: Argument 23. All those (of whom we have spoken) saints, approved by God through faith, justified, or adorned with the testimony of God, that they pleased God; yet they did not have that great promise concerning the incarnation of the Messiah, or concerning that seed of the woman who was to come (in whom all the promises are Yea and Amen) fulfilled while they were living. Since therefore those who lived in the dimmer light persevered in all persecutions, steadfast in faith in Christ who was to come, how much more ought we, who see that promise fulfilled in faith in Christ already exhibited, to persevere.

units.la: Verf. 40. Quod Deus de nobis melius quiddam providerat, ne absque nobis consecrarentur.
units.tr: Verse 40. Because God had provided something better concerning us, that they should not be made perfect apart from us.

units.la: Solvit quæstionem, Quæreret aliquis cur Deus distulerit Christi adventum? Aut quare non sit editus priscorum Patrum temporibus: Respondet, & addit Arg. 24. Visum est Deo hanc nobis beatitudinem concedere, ut oculis cerneremus omnium oraculorum & typorum complementum; honorem videndi diem Christi, & Evangelium audiendi, Patribus non concessit, sed reservavit nobis: Ergo tanto magis tenemur perseverare in Fide Christi, & constanti professione fidei, Christum honorare.
units.tr: He resolves the question: someone might ask why God deferred the coming of Christ, or why he was not published in the times of the ancient Fathers. He answers, and adds Argument 24. It seemed good to God to grant us this blessedness, that with our eyes we should behold the fulfilment of all oracles and types, the honour of seeing the day of Christ and hearing the Gospel, which he did not grant to the Fathers but reserved for us. Therefore we are bound all the more to persevere in faith in Christ, and to honour Christ by a steadfast profession of faith.

units.la: Ne absque nobis ] Aperit consilium Dei, de reservato honore Christum exhibitum videndi, ad nostra tempora, & addit Arg. 25. Noluit Deus infantilem conditionem Ecclesiæ ante Christum exhibitum perfici, absque adultâ conditione Ecclesiæ post Christum exhibitum; ut tota Ecclesia, ante, & post Christum esset unus quasi perfectus homo in Christo; nec voluit Deus fideles sub typis legalibus viventes aliter perfici, quam unà nobiscum intuendo ad rem significatam, quæ nostris temporibus exhibetur. Cum igitur illi in conditione Ecclesiæ infantili, perfectam justitiam & salutem consequuti sint, per fidem intuendo nobiscum in rem significatam per typos legales, id est in CHRISTUM exhibendum tanquam exhibitum, iisque ea fide patienter per omnia adversa perseveraverunt: Turpe erit nisi & nos in fide CHRISTI exhibiti constanter perseveremus.
units.tr: That they should not be made perfect apart from us. He sets out the counsel of God, concerning the honour, reserved to our times, of seeing Christ exhibited; and adds Argument 25. God was unwilling that the childlike condition of the Church before Christ was exhibited should be perfected apart from the adult condition of the Church after Christ was exhibited, so that the whole Church, before and after Christ, might be one, as it were, perfect man in Christ. Nor was God willing that the faithful living under the legal types should be perfected otherwise than by looking together with us to the thing signified, which is exhibited in our times. Since therefore those in the childlike condition of the Church obtained perfect righteousness and salvation, looking through faith together with us to the thing signified by the legal types, that is, to Christ to be exhibited as already exhibited, and with that faith persevered patiently through all adversities: it would be shameful unless we too persevered constantly in faith in Christ exhibited.

units.la: Caput Duodecimum.
units.tr: Chapter 12.

units.la: Ltera pars Epistolæ, in qua varie continentur hortationes ad officia Christiana. Hoc capite habentur tres: Prima hortatio consolatoria est, ad patientiam & fidei constantiam in adversis, ad vers. 14. Secunda est ad pacem sanctam, vers. 14. Tertia est, ut retineant Gratiæ doctrinam, nec eâ abutantur, ad finem. Propositio prima hortatoria, in qua Apostolus seipsum, & alios fideles involvit, hæc est, Debetis afflictiones, & maximè eas quæ fidei causâ vobis obveniunt, patienter tolerare. Argumenta quæ confirmat hanc propositionem, sunt undecim.
units.tr: The second part of the Epistle, in which various exhortations to Christian duties are contained. Three are found in this chapter. The first exhortation is consolatory, to patience and constancy of faith in adversities, up to verse 14. The second is to holy peace, verse 14. The third is that they should hold to the doctrine of grace and not abuse it, to the end. The first hortatory proposition, in which the Apostle includes himself and other faithful people, is this: You ought to bear afflictions patiently, and especially those which come upon you for the sake of faith. There are eleven arguments which confirm this proposition.

units.la: Vers. 1.
units.tr: Verse 1.

units.la: PRoinde nos quoque, quum tanta nos circumstet testium nubes, abjecto omni pondere & peccato ad nos circumcingendos proclivi, constanter propositum nobis stadium decurramus:
units.tr: Therefore we also, since so great a cloud of witnesses surrounds us, laying aside every weight and the sin that so easily entangles us, let us run with perseverance the race set before us.

units.la: Infertur autem hæc propositio ex præcedente Fidelium catalogo, similitudine athletarum in stadio currentium vestitâ, Debemus omnibus impedimentis abjectis, propositum nobis stadium constanter decurrere.
units.tr: This proposition is drawn from the preceding catalogue of the faithful, and is illustrated by the likeness of athletes running in a stadium: we ought, with every hindrance laid aside, to run constantly the race set before us.

units.la: Quum tanta ] Argumentum primum, Habemus exempla Fidelium omnium, ante CHRISTUM exhibitum defunctorum, qui nos in stadio currentes copiosâ multitudine instar nubis condensatæ circum stant, testimonium dicentes quisque suum, de promissionum Divinarum certitudine, de Fidei excellentia, & DEI bonitate, qui etiam testes adversus nos futuri sunt, nisi constanter per prospera & adversa omnia perrexerimus in cursu Christiano. Ergo constanter per adversa omnia pergere debemus.
units.tr: Since so great] The first argument: we have examples of all the faithful who died before Christ was revealed. They stand around us, who run in the stadium, in a great crowd like a dense cloud, each bearing witness concerning the certainty of the divine promises, the excellence of faith and the goodness of God. They will also be witnesses against us if we do not persevere constantly through all prosperity and adversity in the Christian course. Therefore we ought to press on constantly through all adversity.

units.la: Abjecto ] Ut hortationem faciliorem, & eos ad cursum hunc expeditiores redderet Apostolus, de duobus impedimentis, altero externo, altero interno, vitandis admonet. Externum impedimentum est, quod à rebus externis, divitiis, honoribus, rebusque aliis mundanis objicitur, quæ non debent tanti à nobis æstimari, quin parati simus iis renunciare, quando & quatenus retardant cursum nostrum in obedientia Fidei: tunc enim pondera fiunt, quæ abjici jubet. Internum impedimentum est ab innato peccato, seu concupiscentia in carne habitante, quæ natura nobis adhæret, facillimeque incautos irretiat, nisi caveamus. Dicimur autem hoc peccatum abjicere, cum carnis curam non habemus ad explendas cupiditates ejus, neque vitæ hujus mortalis studio tanto tenemur, quin cum Deus nos vocat, parati simus ad vitam deponendam, sic enim abjicitur peccatum innatum, ne nos in fidei probationibus irretiat, alioqui enim nullis conatibus omnino reprimi potest, quandiu in carne vivimus.
units.tr: Laying aside] So that he might make the exhortation easier and make them more ready for this course, the Apostle warns them to avoid two hindrances, one external and one internal. The external hindrance is what is put before us by external things: riches, honours and other worldly matters. These ought not to be valued by us so highly that we are not ready to renounce them, whenever and insofar as they slow our course in obedience to faith. For then they become weights, which he bids us lay aside. The internal hindrance is the innate sin, or the concupiscence dwelling in the flesh, which clings to our nature and very easily ensnares the unwary unless we take care. We are said to lay this sin aside when we do not take care of the flesh so as to satisfy its desires, nor are we so bound by concern for this mortal life that, when God calls us, we are not ready to lay that life down. In this way innate sin is laid aside, so that it does not entangle us in the trials of faith. Otherwise, as long as we live in the flesh, it can by no efforts at all be wholly restrained.

units.la: Vers. 2. Intuentes in Fidei ducem ac perfectorem Iesum, qui pro sibi proposito gaudii pertulit crucem, ignominia contempta, & ad dextram throni Dei consedit.
units.tr: Verse 2. Looking unto Jesus, the author and perfecter of faith, who for the joy set before him endured the cross, despising the shame, and has sat down at the right hand of the throne of God.

units.la: Arg. 2. Habemus non pro exemplo tantùm, sed etiam pro adjumento maximo, Christum Iesum fidei nostræ Ducem, qui ut Autor est, sic & Persector fidei nostræ, in quem oculis fidei intuentes stadium percurrere valebimus: Ergo constanter per adversa omnia nobis pergendum est.
units.tr: Argument 2. We have, not only as an example but also as a very great help, Jesus Christ, the leader of our faith, who as he is its author, so too is its perfecter. Looking to him with the eyes of faith, we shall be able to run through the stadium. Therefore we must press on constantly through all adversity.

units.la: Hoc Argumentum confirmat tribus rationibus: Prima ratio, Dux noster præ desiderio salutis nostræ, per Crucem pervenit ad Gloriam, patienter pertulit Crucem, & contempsit contemptum, pro nihilo habuit ignominiam pati, ut nos redimeret, Victorque rediret ad Gloriæ suæ possessionem, & nos eâdem viâ posse se ad Gloriæ suæ consortium duceret: Ergo (Duce Christo) per Crucem, & Mundi contemptum nobis pergendum est.
units.tr: This argument is confirmed by three reasons. The first reason: our leader, from desire for our salvation, came through the cross to glory. He patiently endured the cross, despised the contempt, and counted it nothing to suffer shame, in order to redeem us, and returned as victor to the possession of his glory. He would lead us by the same way to the fellowship of his glory. Therefore, with Christ as our leader, we must press on through the cross and the contempt of the world.

units.la: Vers. 3. Reputate igitur quis ille sit qui talem sustinuit à peccatoribus adversus sese contradictionem, ne animis deficientes, fatisfatis.
units.tr: Verse 3. Consider him who endured such hostility from sinners against himself, so that you may not grow weary and faint in your minds.

units.la: Ratio 2. Tanta est Christi excellentia supra nos, tantæ ejus passiones, quas pro nobis sustinuit ab adversariis indignissimis, ut nostræ passiones in militia nostra Christiana, (feriâ comparatione factâ nostri cum Christo) evanescant. Ergo ejus exemplum intuendum nobis, & per adversa omnia pergendum est. Ratio 3. Nihil à Christo lucem, animos, virésque per fidem subinde mutuetis in cursu vestro, periculum est ne in medio certamine animum deserat. spondeatis, & peccatis. Ergo constanter oportet intueri Christum Ducem, & per fidem in ipsum, in cursu pergere.
units.tr: Reason 2. Christ's excellence is so great above us, and his sufferings, which he bore for us from most unworthy adversaries, so great, that our sufferings in our Christian warfare (when we compare them with Christ) vanish away. Therefore we must look to his example and press on through all adversity. Reason 3. Since you draw light, courage and strength from Christ by faith from time to time in your course, there is danger that you may lose heart in the middle of the contest.

units.la: Vers. 4 Nondum ad sanguinem usque restitistis, adversus peccatum decertantes:
units.tr: Verse 4. You have not yet resisted to the point of shedding blood, striving against sin.

units.la: Arg. 3. In certamine contra peccatum (ad quod vos cogere conantur persequutores) nondum vitam & sanguinem profudistis pro Christo, sicut tenemini, si ita ejus gloria postulaverit: Ergo constanter pergite per omnia adversa parati etiam vitam ponere potius, quam peccato manus detis.
units.tr: Argument 3. In the struggle against sin (to which your persecutors try to force you), you have not yet poured out your life and blood for Christ, as you are bound to do if his glory should demand it. Therefore press on constantly through all adversities, ready even to lay down your life rather than surrender to sin.

units.la: Vers. 5. Et obliti estis exhortationis, quae vobis tanquam filiis loquitur, Fili mi, ne negligito castigationem Domini, neque deficias animo quum ab eo argueris.
units.tr: Verse 5. And you have forgotten the exhortation which speaks to you as to sons: My son, do not despise the chastening of the Lord, nor faint when you are rebuked by him.

units.la: Arg. 4. cum reprehensione conjunctum, Amica Dei hortatio, in Scriptura, vos, ut filios compellans, exigit a vobis, ut neque contemnatis Dei ferulam in cordis veltri duritie, neque animo deficiatis castigati prae cordis mollitie, id quod nunc facere videmini, obliti hortationis divinae: Ergo patienter & constanter tolerandae vobis sunt afflictiones.
units.tr: Argument 4. The friendly exhortation of God in Scripture, joined with reproof, addresses you as sons and requires of you that you neither despise God's rod through the hardness of your heart, nor lose heart when chastened because of softness of heart. This is what you now seem to be doing, having forgotten the divine exhortation. Therefore you must bear afflictions patiently and constantly.

units.la: Vers. 6. Quem enim diligit Dominus, castigat: & flagellat quemcunque filium recipit.
units.tr: Verse 6. For whom the Lord loves he chastens, and he scourges every son whom he receives.

units.la: Vers 7. Si castigationem sustinetis, Deus sese vobis offert ut filiis: quis enim est filius quem non castiget pater?
units.tr: Verse 7. If you endure chastening, God offers himself to you as to sons. For what son is there whom a father does not chasten?

units.la: Arg 5. confirmans superius, Castigatio est effectum dilectionis divinae erga eum quem Deus castigat: siquidem castigatio pertinet ad emendationem ejus qui castigatur: Ergo patienter tolerandae vobis sunt afflictiones.
units.tr: Argument 5, confirming what was said above. Chastisement is the effect of God's love toward the one whom God chastens, since chastisement serves the amendment of the one who is chastened. Therefore you must bear afflictions patiently.

units.la: Flagellit Arg. 6. Afflictiones patienter tolerare, signum est adoptionis; neminem agnoscit Deus pro filio adoptivo, quem non exerceat etiam asperioribus afflictionibus, nec quisquam est qui excipitur: Ergo ut adoptionis tesseram gestare comperiamini, vosque Dei filios probetis, afflictiones patienter tolerare debetis.
units.tr: Scourges] Argument 6. To bear afflictions patiently is a sign of adoption. God does not acknowledge anyone as an adopted son whom he does not also train with harsher afflictions, and there is no one who is not so received. Therefore, that you may be found to bear the token of adoption and prove yourselves God's sons, you must bear afflictions patiently.

units.la: Vers. 8 Quod si estis absque castigatione, cujus participes sunt omnes, nempe spurii estis, & non filii.
units.tr: Verse 8. But if you are without chastisement, of which all have been partakers, then you are illegitimate and not sons.

units.la: Arg. 7. Qui immunes sunt a castigatione, vel qui paternam Dei castigationem non ferunt, non sunt genuini Dei Filii; externam & visibilem Ecclesiam unà cum hypocritis, matrem habere poterint; Deum vero, patrem habere non possunt. Ergo nisi hypocritæ & filii supposititii haberi vultis, afflictiones patienter tolerare debetis.'
units.tr: Argument 7. Those who are free from chastisement, or who do not bear God's fatherly chastisement, are not genuine sons of God. They may have the external and visible Church as their mother, together with hypocrites, but they cannot have God as their Father. Therefore, unless you wish to be counted hypocrites and spurious sons, you must bear afflictions patiently.

units.la: Verl. 9. 'Deinde corporum nostrorum patres habuimus castiga> tores, & eos reveriti sumus: annon multo magis subjiciemur Patri spirituum: & vivemus :
units.tr: Verse 9. Furthermore, we have had earthly fathers as chastisers of our bodies, and we have revered them. Shall we not much more be subject to the Father of spirits, and live?

units.la: Arg. 8. Patres corporum nostrorum jus habent castigandi nos filios suos, eorumque castigationes ferre æquum est, imo eas cum reverentia toleravimus. Quanto magis jus castigandi nos habet Pater spirituum nostrorum Deus, nosque hujus castigationes æquo animo ferre tenemur.
units.tr: Argument 8. Our bodily fathers have the right to chastise us as their sons, and it is right to bear their chastisements; indeed we have borne them with reverence. How much more does God, our Father of spirits, have the right to chastise us, and we are bound to bear his chastisements with an even mind.

units.la: Vivemus ] Arg. 9. Vitam æternam consequemur, si Paternas Dei castigationes patienter tulerimus. Ergo eas patienter tolerare debemus.
units.tr: And live] Argument 9. We shall obtain eternal life if we have borne the fatherly chastisements of God patiently. Therefore we ought to bear them patiently.

units.la: Vers. 10. Nam illi ad paucos dies, prout ipsis videbatur, nos castigabant; hic autem ad commodum nostrum, ut participes simus sanctimoniæ ipsius.
units.tr: Verse 10. For they chastened us for a few days as seemed good to them, but he does so for our profit, that we may be partakers of his holiness.

units.la: Arg. 10. Si toleravimus castigationes parentum nostrorum, qui ad breve tempus intuitu commodi nostri temporalis pro arbitrio suo, sæpè non satis justè nos castigarunt, multò magis tolerare debemus castigationes Dei, qui nos castigat ad breve tempus prudentissimè & justissimè in commodum nostrum spirituale, ut nos sanctitatis suæ participes faciat, seu ad vitam æternam sanctificet.
units.tr: Argument 10. If we have borne the chastisements of our parents, who for a short time, with a view to our temporal good, often chastened us at their own discretion and not always justly, how much more ought we to bear the chastisements of God. He chastens us for a short time, most wisely and most justly, for our spiritual good, so as to make us partakers of his holiness, that is, to sanctify us to eternal life.

units.la: Vers. 11. Omnis autem castigatio in præsens quidem non videtur esse gaudii, sed tristitiæ: at posteà fructum tranquillum justitiæ reddit iis qui per eam fuerint excercitati.
units.tr: Verse 11. Now all chastening for the present seems not to be joyful but grievous; yet afterward it yields the peaceful fruit of righteousness to those who have been trained by it.

units.la: Vers. 12. Quapropter manus remissas, & genua soluta surrigite.
units.tr: Verse 12. Therefore lift up the hands that hang down, and the feeble knees.

units.la: Arg. 11. cum solutione objectionis, Licet in præsens ex carnis judicio nulla castigatio videatur esse materia gaudii, sed tristitiæ tantum; postea tamen iis qui per eam exercitati, probati, & subacti fuerint, sedatis & tranquillis ipsorum animis hæc disciplina profuisse comperietur, & sanctimoniam, seu fructum justitiæ promovïsse demonstrabitur. Ergo afflictiones tolerare debetis, & insuper animos & robur colligere, volque ad constanter progrediendum in viis Domini componere, Quod per erectionem manuum remissarum, & solutorum genuum, significatur.
units.tr: Argument 11, with the answer to an objection. Although, judging by the flesh, no chastening seems at present to be a matter of joy but only of sorrow, yet afterwards it will be found to have profited those who have been trained, tested and subdued by it, and it will be shown to have advanced their holiness, or the fruit of righteousness, once their minds have been calmed and quieted. Therefore you must bear afflictions, gather courage and strength, and prepare yourselves to press on steadily in the ways of the Lord. This is signified by "lifting up the hands that hang down and the feeble knees."

units.la: Vers. 13. Et rectas orbitas facite pedibus vestris; ne quid claudum est abducatur à via, sed ut sanetur potius.
units.tr: Verse 13. And make straight paths for your feet, lest what is lame be turned out of the way, but rather be healed.

units.la: Arg. 12. Nisi afflictiones Euangelii causâ obvenientes patienter toleretis, & infracto animo pergatis in fidei professione, in viis Domini seu orbitis rectis, periculum est ne claudicantes, & ad defectionem inclinantes propter afflictiones, quas fidei causa patimini, statim plane deficiatis, & omnino deflectatis de via, seu ne fidei renuncietis. Ergo sanationem per medicamenta fidei & consolationis Christianæ admittite, patienter afflictiones tolerate, animosè in viis Domini, rectisque orbitis ejus, pedes vestros firmate, & pergite.
units.tr: Argument 12. Unless you bear patiently the afflictions that come upon you for the sake of the gospel, and press on with an unbroken spirit in the profession of faith, in the ways of the Lord, that is, in straight paths, there is danger that you who limp and are inclined to defection because of the afflictions you suffer for the faith will altogether fail and wholly turn aside from the way, or renounce the faith. Therefore accept healing through the remedies of faith and Christian consolation, bear afflictions patiently, firm your feet courageously in the ways of the Lord and his straight paths, and press on.

units.la: Verf. 14. Pacem sectamini cum omnibus & sanctimoniam, sine qua nemo videbit DOMINVM;
units.tr: Verse 14. Follow peace with all men, and holiness, without which no man shall see the Lord;

units.la: Hortatio 2. Ut studeant paci cum omnibus colendæ, cum iis qui intra Ecclesiam sunt, tum iis qui extranei sunt, quantum in ipsis est, simul etiam studeant sanctimoniæ, ita ut dum paci student, sanctimoniam non negligant, seu ne in gratiam pravorum hominum peccent, malum faciendo, aut bonum omittendo.
units.tr: Exhortation 2. That they should strive to cultivate peace with all, both with those within the Church and with those who are outside it, as far as lies in them; and at the same time they should strive for holiness, so that while they labour for peace they do not neglect holiness, that is, they must not sin to win favour with wicked men, by doing evil or omitting good.

units.la: Sine qua Rationem conjungendi studii sanctimoniæ cum studio pacis reddit: quia absque pace erga homines, salutem æternam consequi possent, verum absque sanctimonia, servari non possent, seu videre Dominum, in cujus aspectu, societate & fruitione in cœlis consistit vita æterna.
units.tr: "Without which" gives the reason for joining the pursuit of holiness with the pursuit of peace: men might obtain eternal salvation without peace toward other men, but they could not obtain it without holiness, that is, they could not see the Lord, in whose sight, fellowship and enjoyment in heaven eternal life consists.

units.la: Verf. 15. Prospicientes nequis deficiat à gratia Dei, neque radix amara suppullulans obturbet, & per hanc inquinentur multi.
units.tr: Verse 15. Looking carefully lest any man fail of the grace of God; lest any root of bitterness springing up trouble you, and thereby many be defiled.

units.la: Hortatio 3. Ne quis deficiat à gratia, vel eâ abutatur ad profanitatem, quæ ad singulos spectat, potissimum ad Episcopos seu Gubernatores Ecclesiæ, sicut res & verba insinuant, quia sicut omnium, sic horum præcipue officium est studere purgandæ Ecclesiæ à corruptelis doctrinæ & morum, per hortationem ad mutua charitatis officia, & per disciplinam Ecclesiasticam. Quod ad corruptelas doctrinæ, prospicere jubet ne quis deficiat à doctrina Euangelii, seu à sanâ doctrina gratiæ: seu ne quis minus ascribat gratiæ quam æquum est (atque ita deficiens à veritate, a tergo relictus ab aliis in fide progredientibus, quibus assentiri in doctrina gratiæ vel non potuit, vel non voluit) fiultretur gratiâ, atque ita pereat.
units.tr: Exhortation 3. Lest anyone fall short of grace, or abuse it for profanity. This applies to each individual, but especially to the bishops or governors of the Church, as both the matter and the words suggest, since the duty of all, and of these above all, is to labour to cleanse the Church of corruptions in doctrine and morals, by exhorting to mutual offices of love and by ecclesiastical discipline. As regards corruptions of doctrine, he bids them take care lest anyone fall away from the doctrine of the gospel, that is, from the sound doctrine of grace, or lest anyone ascribe less to grace than is just, and so, failing in the truth and left behind by others who advance in faith, whom he could not or would not assent to in the doctrine of grace, be defrauded of grace and so perish.

units.la: Ne quis radix Rationes hortationis sunt sex: Ratio prima spectans ad membrum primum, Qua a defectio à gratiâ, seu doctrinâ gratiæ per infidelitatem in aliquo membro Ecclesiæ, est instar amaississimæ radicis suppullulantis lulintis in Dei Ecclesia (quae est vinea seu hortus DOMINI) qua multi in Ecclesia turbari & infici poterint.
units.tr: "Lest any root" The reasons for the exhortation are six. The first reason, concerning the first member: defection from grace, or from the doctrine of grace, through unbelief in some member of the Church, is like a most bitter root springing up in God's Church (which is the vineyard or garden of the Lord), by which many may be troubled and infected in the Church.

units.la: Verf. 16. Nequis sit scortator, aut profanus, velut Esau, qui unico edulio vendidit suum jus primogeniti.
units.tr: Verse 16. Lest there be any fornicator, or profane person, like Esau, who for one morsel of meat sold his birthright.

units.la: Quod ad corruptelas morum attinet, (aquibus etiam ad defectionem a fide proclivis est via) vetat, ne quis sit inter eos scortator, hoc est, ne tolerarent, sed ex Ecclesia ejicerent scortatores & profanos, qui coelestia privilegia, & bona fidelibus & sanctis promissa contemnentes, gulae, ventri, & vitiosis voluptatibus se dedunt, instar Esau qui jus primogenituræ uno vendidit edulio: Atque ita ostendit pluris se fecisse gulam suam, quam primogenituram: quæ æternæ haereditatis, ex gratuita Dei promissione consequendæ credentibus, pignus erat, & spem ipsius fovebat in Patriarcharum familiis.
units.tr: As regards corruptions of morals, which also make the way to defection from the faith easy, he forbids anyone to be among them as a fornicator; that is, they should not tolerate such men but cast out of the Church fornicators and profane persons, who despise the heavenly privileges and goods promised to believers and saints and give themselves over to gluttony, appetite and vicious pleasures. They are like Esau, who sold his birthright for a single meal, and so showed that he valued his belly more than his firstborn's rights, which were a pledge of the eternal inheritance to be obtained by believers from God's gratuitous promise, and which kept their hope alive in the families of the patriarchs.

units.la: Verf. 17. Scitis enim cum etiam postea quum vellet haereditario jure benedictionem assequi, reprobatum fuisse; non enim repperit poenitentiæ locum, quamvis cum lachrymis benedictionem illam exquisisset.
units.tr: Verse 17. For you know that afterwards, when he wished to obtain the blessing by hereditary right, he was rejected; for he found no place for repentance, though he sought the blessing with tears.

units.la: Ratio 2. hortationis, membrum secundum spectans, Quia sicut ex historia sacra notum est Esavum (cum poenitentia ductus postea lachrymans, solicitasset Patrem suum, ut haereditario jure benedictionem asequeretur) repulsam passum esse, & repudiatum a primogenituræ benedictione; Sic metuendum est profanis, gratiæ Dei, & sanctimoniæ contemptoribus, (qui dum audiunt Dei Vocem, obdurant corda, nec resipiscunt, cum offertur occasio) ne excludantur a Dei misericordia, nec resipiscentiæ locum inveniant jam exclusi: Purganda ergo est Ecclesia ab ejusmodi corruptelis.
units.tr: Reason 2 of the exhortation, concerning the second member. As is known from sacred history, Esau, when afterwards moved by repentance he entreated his father with tears to obtain the blessing by hereditary right, suffered rejection and was refused the blessing of the firstborn. So profane men, despisers of God's grace and holiness, who harden their hearts when they hear God's voice and do not repent when the opportunity is offered, must fear that they will be shut out from God's mercy and, once shut out, will find no place for repentance. The Church must therefore be purged of such corruptions.

units.la: Verf. 18 Non enim accessistis ad contrectabilem montem, & Incensum ignem, ac turbinem, & caliginem & procellam:
units.tr: Verse 18. For you have not come to the mount that might be touched, and that burned with fire, nor to blackness, and darkness, and tempest,

units.la: Verf. 19 Tubaeque sonitum & vocem verborum; quam qui audierant, deprecati sunt ne amplius sibi fieret sermo.
units.tr: Verse 19. And the sound of a trumpet, and the voice of words; which voice they that heard entreated that no word more should be spoken to them.

units.la: Verf. 20 (Non enim ferebant quod imperabatur, Si vel bestia tetigerit montem, lapidabitur, aut jaculo configetur.
units.tr: Verse 20. (For they could not bear what was commanded: If even a beast touch the mountain, it shall be stoned or pierced with a dart.)

units.la: Verf. 21: Et Moses, adeo terribile erat visum quod apparebat, dixit, Expavefactus sum ac tremebundus) Ratio 3. in hunc sensum, Non vocati estis ad fœdus legale, ejusque terrores, ad verf. 22. sed ad fœdus gratiæ, & societatem suavissimam CHRISTI, & Sanctorum ipsius, ad versum 25. Ergo prospiciendum ne quis deficiat à gratia, vel ne quis profanus sit, id est, ne quis infidelitate suâ detrahat DEI gratiæ, vel profanitate sua gratiam convertat in profanam licentiam. Quod idem est cum Apostoli conclusione, quam infert versu 25. Videte ne recusetis eum, id est, CHRISTUM, qui loquitur, &c. Vis Argumenti hæc est, Si jam (cum non Timor sed Amor, non Justitia sed Gratia, non Lex sed Euangelium, Ducem se vobis offert ad Cœlum proficiscentibus) defeceritis à gratia, vel eâ ad profanitatem abusi fueritis, futurum est ut CHRISTUM loquentem de Cœlo, & vos ad communionem suam, & Sanctorum placidissimè, invitantem recusare, & repudiare comperiamini, quod vobis cavendum est.
units.tr: Verse 21. And so terrible was the sight that Moses said, I am exceedingly afraid and tremble.) Reason 3, to this effect: you have not been called to the legal covenant and its terrors (verse 22), but to the covenant of grace and the most sweet fellowship of Christ and his saints (verse 25). Therefore we must take care lest anyone fall away from grace, or lest anyone become profane, that is, lest anyone by his unbelief detract from the grace of God, or by his profanity turn grace into profane licence. This is the same as the Apostle's conclusion, which he draws in verse 25: See that you do not refuse him, that is, Christ, who speaks, and so on. The force of the argument is this: if now (since it is not fear but love, not justice but grace, not law but gospel, that offers itself as your guide as you set out for heaven) you have fallen away from grace, or abused it to profanity, you will find that you refuse and reject Christ speaking from heaven and most gently inviting you to his fellowship and that of the saints, and this is what you must guard against.

units.la: Pro Fœdere Operum seu Legè, ponit descriptionem terribilis modi quo tradita est Lex; cujus descriptionis membra sunt octo: 1. In fœdere operum seu legali pangendo mons erat contrectabilis (cui opponitur Cœlum, seu cœlestis mons Zion, thronus Gratiæ) quasi diceret, Postquam credidistis in CHRISTUM, non accessistis ad montem illum contrectabilem & terrenum, cujus ipse aspectus terrorem incutiebat, & per quem repræsentabatur thronus Justitiæ, in quo sedet DEUS, cum ei res est cum homine irregenito, confidenti in suis viribus, & operum suorum merito nitenti: 2. In illo fœdere pangendo, mons igne incendebatur, quo repræsentabatur ira Judicis armati, & parati ad consumendum peccatores, suis meritis, seu operibus confidentes, & ex fœdere operum cum ipso agentes: 3. In illo fœdere pangendo erat turbo, caligo, & procella, quibus repræsentabatur animi conditio perplexa, consternatio, & horror, quibus constringitur peccatoris anima, quando Judex ex lege seu fœdere operum, justitiam, iramque suam, secundum conditionem violati fœderis ipsi demonstrat: 4. In lege tradenda erat Tubæ sonitus, quo significabatur citandos & sistendos esse necessario omnes violati fœderis operum reos, ad DEI Judicis supremi Tribunal, nec evadendi locum relictum iri cuiquam. 5. In illo fœdere pangendo erat Vox verborum, per quam repræsentabatur litera Legis, officia debita recitantis, vires vero ad præstandum imperata minimè conferentis: 6. In illo fœdere pangendo, Illi qui vocem verborum audierant, deprecati sunt, ne amplius sibi fieret sermo, Quo significabatur intolerabile pondus multiplicati reatus, ex violatione legis contracti, simul etiam desperationem de lege in posterum præstandâ conscientiæ iucumbere, quando ex fœdere operum Deus cum peccatore agit; Id quod Apostolus hic insinuat, cum dicit, Non enim ferebant quod imperabatur: 7. In illo fœdere pangendo, Si vel bestia tetigisset montem, lapidanda, aut jaculo configenda erat. Quo significabatur, Primò, Excludi à Deo peccatorem ab omni accessu, nec licere cuiquam peccatori ad Deum appropinquare, ex hujus fœderis conditione: Secundò, Abominationi esse Deo, & peccatorem ipsum, & omnia quæ ad ipsum pertinent, jumenta & pecudes: Tertiò, Miserrimè perdendum esse peccatorem, ex hoc fœdere, id est, cum contemptu & ignominiâ, quasi lapidibus & jaculis eminùs contortis in ejus dirum & abominandum Caput. 8. In illo fœdere pangendo adeò terribile erat visum quod apparebat, ut Moses expavefactus totus contremuerit, & horrorem suum confessus fuerit; Quo significabatur etiam justissimos seu sanctissimos mortalium non posse consistere coram Deo, si secundum fœdus operum cum ipso agatur, ut Psal. 143. 2. dicitur, In conspectu tuo nulla caro justificabitur: Hæc prior est pars argumenti, cujus hæc est summa, Liberavit vos Deus à fœdere operum, & ipsius terroribus.
units.tr: In place of the covenant of works or the law, he sets out a description of the terrible manner in which the law was delivered. The parts of this description are eight. (1) In making the covenant of works or of the law there was a mount that could be touched (set over against heaven, or the heavenly mount Zion, the throne of grace), as if he said: after you have believed in Christ, you have not come to that earthly mount that might be touched, whose very sight struck terror, and through which the throne of justice was represented, on which God sits when he deals with the unregenerate man who trusts in his own strength and relies on the merit of his works. (2) In making that covenant the mount was burning with fire, by which the wrath of the Judge, armed and ready to consume sinners who trust in their merits or works and deal with him on the footing of the covenant of works, was represented. (3) In making that covenant there was blackness, darkness and tempest, by which was represented the perplexed condition of mind, the consternation and horror with which the soul of the sinner is constrained, when the Judge, according to the law or covenant of works, shows him his justice and wrath in accordance with the state of the broken covenant. (4) In delivering the law there was the sound of a trumpet, by which was signified that all guilty of breaking the covenant of works must necessarily be summoned and brought before the supreme tribunal of God the Judge, and that no place of escape would be left to anyone. (5) In making that covenant there was the voice of words, by which was represented the letter of the law, reciting the duties owed but not giving strength to perform what is commanded. (6) In making that covenant, those who heard the voice of words entreated that no word more should be spoken to them. By this was signified the intolerable weight of the multiplied guilt incurred by violating the law, and also the despair that the conscience will have of fulfilling the law in future, when God deals with the sinner on the footing of the covenant of works. This is what the Apostle hints at here when he says: For they could not bear what was commanded. (7) In making that covenant, if even a beast touched the mountain it was to be stoned or pierced with a dart. By this was signified: first, that the sinner is shut out by God from every approach, and that under the conditions of this covenant it is lawful for no sinner to draw near to God; second, that both the sinner himself and all that pertains to him, beasts of burden and cattle, are an abomination to God; third, that the sinner is to be destroyed most wretchedly under this covenant, that is, with contempt and ignominy, as though with stones and darts hurled from afar upon his dreadful and abominable head. (8) In making that covenant the sight was so terrible that Moses was utterly terrified, trembled all over and confessed his dread. By this was signified also that the most righteous or holiest of mortals cannot stand before God, if he deals with them according to the covenant of works, as it is said in Psalm 143:2: In thy sight shall no flesh be justified. This is the first part of the argument, whose sum is this: God has delivered you from the covenant of works and from its terrors.

units.la: Vers. 22. Sed accessistis ad montem Sion, & civitatem DEI vivi, Hierusalem Cælestem, & myriadas angelorum,
units.tr: Verse 22. But you have come to Mount Sion, and to the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem, and to myriads of angels,

units.la: Vers. 23 Conventum & concionem primogenitorum qui conscripti sunt in Cœlis, & Judicem universorum Deum, & Spiritus justorum consecratorum,
units.tr: Verse 23. To the assembly and gathering of the firstborn who are enrolled in heaven, and to God the Judge of all, and to the spirits of the just made perfect,

units.la: Vers. 24. Et ad novi testamenti mediatorem Iesum, & sanguinem aspersionis præstantiora loquentem quàm loqueretur sanguis Abel.
units.tr: Verse 24. And to Jesus the mediator of the new covenant, and to the sprinkling of blood that speaks better things than the blood of Abel.

units.la: Sequitur secunda Argumenti pars, de Fœdere gratiæ, quod pepigit Deus cum fidelibus in Christum credentibus; Conditio autem & felicitas hominis credentis in Christum, & sub fœdere gratiæ, describitur partibus quasi suis: 1. Postquam credidistis in Christum, liberati à monte Sinai, & à throno justitiæ accessistis ad montem Sion, quo repræsentabatur thronus gratiæ, in quo Deus propitium se ostendit omnibus ad Christum accedentibus: 2. Postquam credidistis in Christum, postliminio revocati ab exilio & erroribus in deserto hujus mundi, recolligimini ad caput vestrum Christum, & ad civitatem perfugii, ad latum quietum, possidendum in Christo; liberati ab ira & morte, & Deo reconciliati, donati estis civitate Dei viventis; liberati à terroribus justi Judicis, admittimini in Hierosolymam, id est, DEI Ecclesiam in qua visiones pacis videatis: liberati ab inferno, etiam liberati estis a ceremoniis Leviticis, quibus inferior & terrestris Jerusalem jam servit cum liberis suis, & admittimini ad privilegia coelestis Hierusalem Ecclesiae Fidelium, & regni coelorum: 3. Postquam credidistis in CHRISTUM, liberati a societate Daemoniorum, peccato & cruciatibus obnoxiorum, admittimini in societatem innumerabilium Myriadum Angelorum beatorum: 4. Postquam credidistis in CHRISTUM, evocati & segregati a societate reproborum, impiorum & proscriptorum hominum, seu ab haereditate vitae aeternae seclusorum, accessistis & admissi estis in societatem catholicae Ecclesiae, ad Conventum universalem, ad coetum, concionemque Electorum, qui ad Primogeniturae jus & privilegia restituuntur, ut sitis DEO sacerdotes, & portio DEI selecta, ex hominibus: 5. Qui agebatis olim inter mundanos, quorum portio est in hoc mundo, & quorum nomina scripta sunt in terra, nunc comperti estis ex Electorum numero esse, & ex iis qui olim scripti sunt in Coelis, in Libro Vitae, inter Electos, & Praedestinatos ad gratiam, & gloriam obtinendam: 6. Qui in mundo eratis sine DEO, hostes DEI, DELMQUE infensum Judicem habuistis olim, nunc DEO reconciliati, judicem habetis propitium, qui vos absolvat, hostesque vestros potenter perdat: 7. Qui olim in catalogo damnatorum, & censu perditorum numerabamini, confortes cum spiritibus impiorum, qui jam sunt in carcere; ex foedere gratiae per CHRISTUM fratres facti estis eorum qui jam Coelum possident, spiritusque suos consummatos habent in coelo, i. qui liberati a peccato & miseria in spiritu suo sanctificantur plene & glorificantur: 8. Liberati a foedere operum, quod Mediatorem non admisit, & insuper a jugo Ceremoniarum, admissi estis ad IESUM Servatorem, qui novi foederis Mediator & Sponsor est, qui pro vobis spopondit se effecturum, ut praestetis quod ex foedere a vobis exigitur, idque proculdubio efficiet. 9. Vos qui in vobis justitia & sanctitate destituti, & omni genere peccatorum polluti eratis, nunc virtute novi Foederis admissi estis ad conspersionem sanguinis Jesu Christi, Agni immaculati, (quo justificemini, & sanctificemini, & ab Angelo interemptore conservemini) cujus sanguis licet, per nos nostraque peccata fusus sit, non clamat tamen adversus nos, sicut sanguis Abel clamavit adversus Cainum interfectorem, sed pro nobis intercedit apud DEUM, ut ipse propitius erga nos omnia nobis concedat, quae pretio sanguinis ipsius empta sunt.
units.tr: Now follows the second part of the argument, concerning the covenant of grace, which God made with the faithful who believe in Christ. The condition and happiness of the man who believes in Christ, and who lives under the covenant of grace, is described in its parts: (1) After you believed in Christ, you were freed from Mount Sinai and from the throne of justice, and you have come to Mount Sion, which represents the throne of grace, where God shows himself propitious to all who come to Christ. (2) After you believed in Christ, you were restored by right of return from exile and from the errors of the wilderness of this world; you are gathered to your head, Christ, and to the city of refuge, to the quiet abode to be possessed in Christ. Freed from wrath and death and reconciled to God, you have been given the city of the living God; freed from the terrors of the just Judge, you are admitted into Jerusalem, that is, the Church of God, in which you shall see visions of peace. Freed from hell, you are also freed from the Levitical ceremonies, under which the lower and earthly Jerusalem still serves with her children, and you are admitted to the privileges of the heavenly Jerusalem, the Church of the faithful, and of the kingdom of heaven. (3) After you believed in Christ, you were freed from fellowship with the demons, who are liable to sin and torments, and you are admitted into fellowship with the countless myriads of blessed angels. (4) After you believed in Christ, you were called out and separated from the fellowship of the reprobate, the impious, and the outlawed, or shut out from the inheritance of eternal life; you have come and been admitted into the fellowship of the catholic Church, to the universal assembly, to the gathering and congregation of the elect, who are restored to the right and privileges of the firstborn, so that you may be priests to God and a chosen portion of God from among men. (5) You who once lived among worldly people, whose portion is in this world, and whose names are written on earth, have now been found to be of the number of the elect, and of those who were once written in heaven, in the Book of Life, among the elect and predestined to obtain grace and glory. (6) You who were in the world without God, enemies of God, and once had God as an angry Judge, now that you are reconciled to God have a propitious Judge, who absolves you and powerfully destroys your enemies. (7) You who were once numbered in the catalogue of the damned and the census of the lost, companions of the spirits of the impious who are now in prison, by the covenant of grace through Christ have become brothers of those who already possess heaven and have their spirits perfected in heaven, that is, who, freed from sin and misery, are fully sanctified in their spirit and glorified. (8) Freed from the covenant of works, which did not admit a Mediator, and moreover from the yoke of the ceremonies, you are admitted to Jesus the Saviour, who is the Mediator and Surety of the new covenant, who promised for you that he would bring it about that you perform what is required of you by the covenant, and without doubt he will accomplish it. (9) You who were destitute of righteousness and holiness in yourselves, and polluted with every kind of sin, are now by the power of the new covenant admitted to the sprinkling of the blood of Jesus Christ, the spotless Lamb, (by which you are justified and sanctified, and preserved from the destroying Angel), whose blood, although it was shed through us and our sins, does not cry out against us as the blood of Abel cried out against Cain the murderer, but intercedes for us before God, so that he himself, being propitious towards us, may grant us all those things which were purchased by the price of his blood.

units.la: Verf. 25. Videte ne aspernemini eum qui loquitur: nam si illi non effugerunt qui aversabantur eum qui loquebatur Dei nomine in terra, multo magis nos, si eum qui de Cœlis est, aversemur:
units.tr: Verse 25. See that you do not refuse him who speaks; for if those did not escape who refused him who spoke on earth in the name of God, much more shall we not escape if we turn away from him who speaks from heaven:

units.la: Sequitur conclulio Argumenti hortatoria, Ne sub prætextu excusationis cujusvis recusent obedire Christo, ipsos alloquenti in Euangelio, & invitanti ad Gratiam & Sanctitatem.
units.tr: Now follows the hortatory conclusion of the argument: that under the pretext of any excuse they should not refuse to obey Christ, who addresses them in the Gospel and invites them to grace and holiness.

units.la: Hortationis ratio 4. Si Israelitæ contemptores Mosis loquentis in terra, pœnas non effugerunt; Multò minùs effugietis pœnas, si contemptoritis Christum Mediatorem loquentem de Cœlo. Idcirco cavendum est vobis, ne deficiatis ab ejus gratia, & ne gratiâ ad prosanitatem abutamini.
units.tr: The reason for the exhortation is the fourth: If the Israelites who despised Moses speaking on earth did not escape punishment, much less will you escape punishment if you despise Christ the Mediator, who speaks from heaven. Therefore you must take care not to fall away from his grace, and not to abuse grace into profanity.

units.la: Verl. 26. Cujus vox tunc concussit terram: nunc autem denunciavit, dicens, Adhuc semel ego concutiam non solùm terram, sed etiam Cœlum.
units.tr: Verse 26. Whose voice then shook the earth; but now he has promised, saying, Yet once more I will shake not only the earth, but also the heaven.

units.la: Hanc rationem confirmat à potentia Christi, qui olim voce suâ concussit terram, seu montem Sinai, & in die Judicii semel concutiet & Cœlum & terram, sicut prædixit per Prophetam Haggæum, 2. 6. quod fiet quando Cœlum & Terra igne conflagrabunt, & quicquid instabile vel corruptibile habent abolebitur, ut Cœlum novum, & Terra nova successant, in quibus habitet justitia, id est, Sancti immortales redditi, perpetuò maneant.
units.tr: He confirms this reason from the power of Christ, who once shook the earth, or Mount Sinai, with his voice, and on the day of Judgment will once shake both heaven and earth, as he foretold through the Prophet Haggai, 2.6. This will happen when heaven and earth are consumed by fire, and whatever is unstable or corruptible in them will be abolished, so that a new heaven and a new earth may succeed, in which righteousness dwells, that is, the saints, made immortal, may remain forever.

units.la: Verl. 27. Porro illud Adhuc semel declarat instabilium rerum, ut putà factitiarum, amotionem, ut maneant quæ sunt stabilia.
units.tr: Verse 27. Moreover, that "Yet once" declares the removal of unstable things, such as things made by hands, so that those which are stable may remain.

units.la: Ut hunc sensum admittamus, exponit verba Prophetæ sic intelligenda esse, propterea quod, qui dicitur semel concuslurus Cœlum & Terram & non læpiùs, dicitur eo ipso amoturus res omnes instabiles & factitias, seu creatas, quoàd mutabilem ipsorum conditionem, seu qualitates mutabiles, ut stabilia & immutabilia succedant, qualia futura sunt omnia in regno Christi glorioso.
units.tr: To admit this sense, he explains that the words of the Prophet are to be understood thus: because he who is said to shake heaven and earth once, and not more often, is by that very fact said to remove all things that are unstable and made, or created, as to their changeable condition or changeable qualities, so that stable and immutable things may succeed, such as all things will be in the glorious kingdom of Christ.

units.la: Verl. 28. Quapropter regnum assumentes quod concuti non potest, teneamus gratiam, per quam ita serviamus DEO, ut ei placeamus, cum reverentia & religione.
units.tr: Verse 28. Wherefore, receiving a kingdom that cannot be shaken, let us hold fast to grace, by which we may so serve God that we please him, with reverence and godly fear.

units.la: Hinc deducit hortationis rationem quintam, Jus datum nobis est ad regnum gloriosum, quod concuti non potest, & fide jam à nobis acceptum est. Ergo firmiter tenenda est doctrina Gratiæ & Sanctitatis studium,seu quod idem est, teneamus gratiam per quam ita serviamus Deo, ut ei placeamus, cum verecundia & reverentia.
units.tr: From this he draws the fifth reason for the exhortation: a right has been given to us to the glorious kingdom, which cannot be shaken, and it has already been received by us through faith. Therefore the doctrine of grace must be firmly held, and zeal for holiness pursued; or, which is the same thing, let us hold grace, by which we may so serve God that we please him, with modesty and reverence.

units.la: Verf. 29. Etenim Deus noster, consumens ignis est.
units.tr: Verse 29. For our God is a consuming fire.

units.la: Ratio hortationis sexta, Adversus eos qui gratiam Dei vel non tenent, vel eâ abutuntur ad profanitatem, Deus noster est ignis consumens: Ergo teneamus Gratiam cum studio Sanctitatis. Qui licet se Deum Fidelium profiteatur; non feret tamen inultos eos, qui fidem mentiuntur quam non habent, vel qui doctrinâ gratiæ ad licentiam profanam, cum Esavo abutuntur.
units.tr: The sixth reason for the exhortation: against those who either do not hold fast to the grace of God, or abuse it for profanity, our God is a consuming fire. Therefore let us hold grace with zeal for holiness. Although he professes himself the God of the faithful, he will not allow those unpunished who falsely claim a faith they do not have, or who abuse the doctrine of grace for profane licence, like Esau.

units.la: Caput Decimumtertium.
units.tr: Chapter 13.

units.la: Aptitis duæ sunt partes. In priori continentur hortationes septem, ad verf. 18. In altera est Epilogus Epistolæ.
units.tr: The chapter has two parts. The first contains seven exhortations, up to verse 18. The second contains the Epilogue of the Epistle.

units.la: Verf. 1. Fraterna charitas maneat.
units.tr: Verse 1. Let brotherly love remain.

units.la: Hortatio prima ad Constantiam in Charitate erga fratres: In qua tacitè eos commendat, quod hactenus quidem, fideles seu fratres fide & religione sincerâ conjunctos, complexi sint, & sublevarint propter Christum, & apertè rogat, ut constantes, & indefatigati pergant in virtute ista. Maneat, inquit, fraterna charitas.
units.tr: The first exhortation concerns constancy in love towards the brothers.
