In it he tacitly commends them, because until now they have embraced the faithful, that is, the brothers joined to them by faith and sincere religion, and have sustained them for Christ's sake. He openly asks them to continue steadfast and untiring in this virtue. Let brotherly love remain, he says.

units.la: Verf. 2. Hospitalitatis ne sitis immemores: per hanc enim quidam insciì exceperunt Angelos hospitio.
units.tr: Verse 2. Do not forget hospitality, for through it some unknowingly entertained angels as guests.

units.la: Hortatio 2. specialior, Ut colant hospitalitatem, & beneficentiam erga peregrinos, advenas hospites, qui subsidio & consolatione egent imprimis.
units.tr: The second exhortation is more specific: that they cultivate hospitality and kindness towards foreigners, sojourners and guests, who above all need help and comfort.

units.la: Per hanc ] Argumentum ad hortationis obedientiam unicum est, Quia nonnulli hospitalitatem colentes, Angelos receperunt, cum putarent homines à se receptos, ut Abraham & Lot, Genef. 18. & 19. Vis argumenti est, Quia plus boni in hoc genere praestatur, quam putaret aliquis facile: nam & ipse Dominus acceptum sibi fert quicquid ipsius nomine egenis Fidelibus, Prophetis vel Discipulis praestatur.
units.tr: For through it: the argument for obeying this exhortation is single. Some who practised hospitality received angels, supposing they were receiving men, as Abraham and Lot did (Gen. 18 and 19). The force of the argument is that more good is done in this kind of work than one would easily think. For the Lord himself counts as done to himself whatever is done in his name for needy faithful, prophets or disciples.

units.la: Verf. 3. Memores estote vinctorum, tanquam una cum illis vincti: eorum qui malis premuntur, ac si ipsi quoque corpore affliti essetis.
units.tr: Verse 3. Remember those in bonds, as if bound with them, and those who are oppressed by evils, as if you yourselves were also afflicted in body.

units.la: Hortatur
units.tr: He exhorts

units.la: Ut erga fratres qui sunt in vinculis potissimum religionis nomine captivi, sic afficiantur eisque ita subveniant, ac si ipsi pariter vincti essent, & in eodem carcere, eisdemque cum iis vinculis jacerent. Nec id solum, sed etiam hortatur ut tanquam membra ejusdem corporis mystici, fratrum quovis modo afflictorum malis ita afficiantur, sicut affici vellent alios, si res ipsorum ageretur; siquidem quandiu in vivis agebant, gerebant corpus mortale iisdem malis obnoxium: Quod enim cuiquam accidit, cuivis etiam accidere potest, & commiserationem movere debet communis infirmitas.
units.tr: That they should be so disposed towards brothers who are captives in chains, chiefly for the sake of religion, and should so help them, as if they themselves were equally bound, lying in the same prison and with the same chains. And not only this: he also exhorts them, as members of the same mystical body, to be affected by the evils of brothers afflicted in any way, just as they would wish others to be affected if their own case were being considered. For while they lived in this world they bore a mortal body liable to the same evils. What happens to one person can happen to anyone, and common frailty ought to move compassion.

units.la: Honorabile est inter quosvis conjugium, & cubile impollutum; fornicatores autem & adulteros damnabit Deus.
units.tr: Marriage is honourable among all, and the bed undefiled; but God will judge fornicators and adulterers.

units.la: ad castitatem tuendam, duobus argumentis, praeceptum hoc confirmantibus, involuta: Argumentum primum, In hunc sensum, Si quis donum continentiae non habeat, paravit Deus remedium & subsidium, conjugium scilicet, pronunciavitque hanc vitae conditionem honorabilem in omni genere hominum, & torum seu lectum conjugalem, secundum Dei institutum usurpatum, sanctum esse & immaculatum. Colenda ergo est castitas.
units.tr: This is a call to preserve chastity, wrapped in two arguments that confirm the precept. The first argument runs thus: if anyone lacks the gift of continence, God has provided a remedy and help, namely marriage. He has declared this condition of life honourable among all kinds of men, and the marriage bed, used according to God's institution, holy and undefiled. Chastity is therefore to be cultivated.

units.la: ] Arg. 2. Si quis neglexerit conjugium, quod est incontinentiae remedium, & se polluerit, vel fornicatione, caelebs vel adulterio conjugatus, sciat (ille quisquis fuerit) Deum fornicatores & adulteros damnaturum, Colenda ergo est castitas.
units.tr: The second argument: if anyone neglects marriage, which is the remedy for incontinence, and defiles himself, either by fornication while unmarried or by adultery while married, let him know, whoever he is, that God will condemn fornicators and adulterers. Chastity is therefore to be cultivated.

units.la: Sint mores alieni ab avaritia: sitis contenti praesentibus, dixit enim ipse, Non te deseram, neque te derelinquam.
units.tr: Let your manners be free from avarice, and be content with what you have, for he himself has said, I will not leave you nor forsake you.

units.la: Adeo ut confidenti animo dicamus, Dominus mihi auxiliator, nec timebo quid faciat mihi homo.
units.tr: So that with a confident mind we may say, The Lord is my helper, I will not fear what man may do to me.

units.la: Ad vitandam avaritiam, ne vitium hoc ipsorum mores corrumpat. Rationes hortationis sunt tres: 1. Sub forma praecepti proponitur. Sufficere vobis debent quae habetis, seu quae vobis in vocatione aliqua honesta occupatis, divina benedictione obveniunt, iisque contentos vos esse decet, nec plus habendi cupidine turbari: Ergo avaritia cavenda.
units.tr: This is to avoid avarice, lest this vice corrupt their manners. There are three reasons for the exhortation: (1) It is set forth in the form of a precept. What you have, or what comes to you by divine blessing in some honest calling in which you are engaged, ought to suffice you, and you should be content with it and not troubled by the desire to have more. Therefore avarice is to be avoided.

units.la: Dixit enim ] Ratio 2. ex Josua, versu 5. In illa promissione quam Deus fecit Josuae in vocatione ipsius, propositi Deus generalem consolationem omnibus servis suis in vocationibus ipsorum: Nempe quod non sit in ulla re necessaria suppeditanda, ipsis defuturus, seu ipsos deserturus. Avaritia ergo cavenda.
units.tr: For he has said: the second reason is taken from Joshua 1:5. In the promise God made to Joshua at his calling, God set forth a general consolation to all his servants in their callings: namely, that he will not fail them or forsake them in any necessary supply. Therefore avarice is to be avoided.

units.la: Ratio 3. Non minus cuivis fideli quam Davidi, in Psal. 118. verf. 6. Licet cum fiducia sibi polliceri, non tantum subsidia necessaria ad vitam præsentem, sed etiam auxilium Dei paratum adversus omnes malorum hominum impugnationes, qui una cum facultatibus vitam etiam Dei servis auferre moliuntur. Ergo vitanda avaritia.
units.tr: The third reason is no less for any faithful person than for David (Ps. 118:6). One may with confidence promise oneself not only the necessary support for the present life, but also God's help, prepared against all the assaults of wicked men, who strive to take life away from God's servants along with their possessions. Therefore avarice is to be avoided.

units.la: Verf. 7. Memores estote ducum vestrorum, qui loquuti sunt vobis sermonem Dei: quorum imitamini fidem, considerantes qui fuerit exitus conversationis ipsorum.
units.tr: Verse 7. Remember your leaders, who spoke the word of God to you; imitate their faith, considering the outcome of their conduct.

units.la: Hortatio 6. Ad custodiendam puritatem Euangelii absque fermento doctrinæ Judaizantium. Rationes hortationis sunt sex.
units.tr: The sixth exhortation is to guard the purity of the Gospel, without the leaven of the doctrine of the Judaizers. There are six reasons for the exhortation.

units.la: Ratio prima, Doctores vestri Apostoli, aliique fideles CHRISTI Ministri nihil prædicarunt vobis, præter Dei verbum, nullumque sibi in conversatione sua finem proposuerunt, præter eum qui fidis doctoribus proponi debet, gloriam Dei scilicet, & vestram salutem: Ergo imitantes ipsorum fidem, & intuentes finem conversationis ipsorum custodite Euangelii seu doctrinæ fidei puritatem.
units.tr: The first reason: your teachers, the Apostles and other faithful ministers of Christ, preached nothing to you but the word of God, and in their conduct they set themselves no end except the one faithful teachers ought to set before them, namely the glory of God and your salvation. Therefore, imitating their faith and considering the end of their conduct, keep the purity of the Gospel, or of the doctrine of faith.

units.la: Verf. 8 Iesus Christus heri & hodie idem est, & in secula. Ratio 2. IESUS CHRISTUS, cujus doctrina vobis ab ipsius ministris prædicata est, non est varius, sed unus, idemque semper sibi constans ab æterno in æternum. Ergo custodite puritatem doctrinæ ipsius, & unitatem fidei cum doctoribus illis vestris, qui vobis prædicarunt verbum Dei.
units.tr: Verse 8. Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever. The second reason: Jesus Christ, whose doctrine was preached to you by his ministers, is not changeable but one and the same, always constant from eternity to eternity. Therefore keep the purity of his doctrine, and unity of faith with those teachers of yours who preached the word of God to you.

units.la: Verf. 9. Doctrinis variis & peregrinis ne circumferimini, bonum enim est gratia confirmari cor, non cibis, quibus non sunt adjuti qui in ipsis versati sunt.
units.tr: Verse 9. Do not be carried about by various and strange doctrines. For it is good that the heart be strengthened by grace, not by foods, by which those occupied with them have not been helped.

units.la: Ratio 3. sub forma præcepti proposita. Variæ & peregrinæ doctrinæ, Apostolis ignotæ, & quæ CHRISTUM non habent autorem, si iis auscultaveritis, sicut ventus paleam in terra, vel fluctuantes in mari naves agitat, sic vos circumferent huc illuc, ne quicquam fixum teneatis. Stabiles igitur estote in doctrinæ puritate confervanda.
units.tr: The third reason, set forth in the form of a precept. Various and strange doctrines, unknown to the Apostles, and which have no Christ as their author, if you listen to them, will carry you hither and thither, as the wind drives chaff over the earth or tosses ships on the sea, so that you hold nothing fixed. Be steadfast, therefore, in keeping the purity of doctrine.

units.la: Ratio 4. Præstat (Immo simpliciter bonum & salutare est) ut cordis seu conscientiæ tranquillitatem, & stabilimentum quæratis in CHRISTI gratia, quam solam ipsius Euangelium vobis commendat, & non in Legalibus cæremoniis, non in observatione ciborum, dierum, {ä}trum, & similibus: in quibus justitia minime consistit. Puritatem ergo fidei sine fermento doctorum Judaizantium custodire.
units.tr: The fourth reason. It is better (indeed it is simply good and salutary) that you seek the tranquillity and stability of heart or conscience in the grace of Christ, which alone his Gospel commends to you, and not in legal ceremonies, nor in the observance of foods, days, months and the like, in which righteousness does not at all consist. Therefore keep the purity of faith, without the leaven of the Judaizing teachers.

units.la: Unde nullam ] Ratio 5, confirmans superiorem ab experientia Judaizantium, Legales illæ observationes nihil profuerunt ad justitiam vel salutem, iis qui in talibus multum versati sunt, iniisque conlenuerunt. Ergo fidem Euangelii puram custodite ab omni istiusmodi fermento.
units.tr: The fifth reason, confirming the previous one from the experience of the Judaizers: those legal observances profited nothing for righteousness or salvation to those who had long been immersed in such things and had grown old in them. Therefore keep the purity of the Gospel faith free from every such leaven.

units.la: Verf. 10 Habemus altare ex quo non habent jus edendi qui tabernaculo deserviunt.
units.tr: Verse 10. We have an altar, from which those who serve the tabernacle have no right to eat.

units.la: Ratio 6. Qui tabernaculo Judaico deserviunt post CHRISTUM jam exhibitum, seu qui Leviticis Ceremoniis pertinaciter adhærent, non possunt participes esse CHRISTI, qui nobis est res illa significata per altare & sacrificia, & reliquas umbras Leviticas, & verum umbrarum omnium corpus: Ergo custodienda doctrina fidei à fermento judaizantium doctorum, qui harum ceremoniarum observationem cum Euangelio jungendam putabant. In quem sensum dicit idem Apololus, Galat. 5. 2. Si circumcidamini CHRISTUS vobis nihil prodest. Cujus rei ratio est hæc, Ceremoniarum legalium observatores, seu umbrarum jam abolitarum renovatores, in præscriptâ ciborum distinctione, altarium, festorum, jubileorum, aquæ lustralis, vestimentorum Sacerdotalium & similium Ceremoniarum observatione, reipsa prædicant nondum ortum esse solem justitiæ, nondum venisse CHRISTUM, nondum antiquatam esse paedagogiam Ceremonialem: sed hucusque durare tempus umbrarum & signorum, quæ tantum ad CHRISTUM præfigurandum, usque ad tempus correctionis, instituebantur.
units.tr: The sixth reason. Those who serve the Jewish tabernacle after Christ has been revealed, or who obstinately cling to the Levitical ceremonies, cannot be partakers of Christ, who is for us the thing signified by the altar and the sacrifices and the other Levitical shadows, and the true body of all those shadows. Therefore the doctrine of faith is to be guarded from the leaven of the Judaizing teachers, who thought the observance of these ceremonies should be joined with the Gospel. To this effect the same Apostle says, Gal. 5:2: If you are circumcised, Christ profits you nothing. The reason is this: the observers of legal ceremonies, or the renewers of shadows already abolished, by observing the prescribed distinction of foods, altars, feasts, jubilees, lustral water, priestly garments and similar ceremonies, in fact proclaim that the sun of righteousness has not yet risen, that Christ has not yet come, and that the ceremonial schoolmaster has not yet been abolished. They hold that until now the time of shadows and signs continues, which were instituted only to prefigure Christ until the time of correction.

units.la: Verf. 11. Quorum enim animalium sanguis infertur pro peccato in Sacrarium per Pontificem, horum corpora exuruntur extra castra.
units.tr: Verse 11. For the bodies of those animals whose blood is carried into the sanctuary for sin by the high priest are burned outside the camp.

units.la: Verf. 12. Quapropter & Iesus, ut sanctificaret populum per proprium sanguinem, passus est extra portam.
units.tr: Heb. 13. 12. Therefore Jesus also, that he might sanctify the people through his own blood, suffered outside the gate.

units.la: Probat excludendos esse à CHRISTO omnes qui justitiam, vel justitiæ partem quærunt in legis umbris vel operibus, Quia Deus hoc præfiguravit in typo victimæ piacularis. Nam, Levit. 23. 27. victimæ piacula is sanguis à Pontifice inferebatur in sacrarium, ejus vero carnes integræ exurebantur igni, nec quicquam inde cedebat Sacerdotibus, sicut ex aliis victimis dandum erat iis. Apostolus asserit hoc significasse neminem ex iis qui operum fœderi adhærent CHRISTUM ęderepossę, sed ab ejus communio ne excludi omnes, quotquot non in solidum CHRISTO adhærent, sed justitiæ vel ullam particulam in Leviticis umbris, vel operibus quærunt.
units.tr: He proves that all who seek justice, or a part of justice, in the shadows or works of the law are to be excluded from Christ, because God foreshadowed this in the type of the sin offering. For at Lev. 16. 27 the blood of the sin offering was carried by the High Priest into the sanctuary, but its flesh was burnt whole in the fire, and nothing from it fell to the priests, as was to be given to them from the other sacrifices. The Apostle asserts that this signified that none who cling to the covenant of works can eat of Christ, but that all who do not cling wholly to Christ, but seek justice, or any particle of it, in the Levitical shadows or in works, are excluded from his fellowship.

units.la: Extra castra | Per hoc significari voluit Deus, Primò, CHRISTUM passurum extra portas Hierosolymæ, id quod reipsa factum est: Nam CHRISTUS extra portam crucifixus est. Secundò, Quærendam esse expiationem veram in sanguine Messiæ, extra Hierosolymam (seu locum consecratum Levitico cultui) passuri. Et hoc etiam intendisse ipsum CHRISTUM docet Apostolus, (quando in sua providentia ita de re tota disposuit, ut extra urbem pateretur) nimirum CHRISTUM exeuntem extra portas ad se offerendum, ipso facto significare voluisse, non quærendam esse justificationis aut sanctificationis virtutem ullam in ullis ritibus legalibus, sed in proprio suo sanguine tantum, seclusis illis legalibus ritibus omnibus.
units.tr: Outside the camp. By this God meant to signify, first, that Christ would suffer outside the gates of Jerusalem, which in fact came to pass: for Christ was crucified outside the gate. Second, that true expiation is to be sought in the blood of the Messiah, who would suffer outside Jerusalem (or the place consecrated to the Levitical worship). The Apostle teaches that Christ himself also intended this (when in his providence he so arranged the whole matter that he should suffer outside the city), namely, that Christ, by going out beyond the gates to offer himself, meant to signify by the very fact that the power of justification or sanctification is not to be sought in any legal rites whatever, but in his own blood alone, all those legal rites being set aside.

units.la: Verf. 13. Exeamus igitur ad eum extra castra, opprobrium ejus portantes.
units.tr: Verse 13. Let us therefore go forth to him outside the camp, bearing his reproach.

units.la: Verf. 14. Non enim habemus hic sitam civitatem, sed futuram inquirimus.
units.tr: Verse 14. For here we have no continuing city, but we seek one to come.

units.la: Verf. 15. Per ipsum igitur assidue offeramus DEO sacrificium laudis, id est, fructum labiorum confitentium nomini ejus.
units.tr: Verse 15. By him therefore let us offer continually to God the sacrifice of praise, that is, the fruit of lips confessing his name.

units.la: Verf. 16. Beneficentiæ vero & communicationis ne obliviscimini: talibus enim victimis delectatur Deus.
units.tr: Verse 16. But do not forget beneficence and fellowship, for with such sacrifices God is pleased.

units.la: Hinc deducitur hortatio sexta, ad prudentem imitationem CHRISTI extra urbem cuntis, & se Patri offerentis. Imitatio autem hæc in tribus consistit: 1. Sicut CHRISTUS extra urbem proficiscens mundo renunciavit, ut Patris voluntatem faceret, Sic nos ejus causa rebus mundanis omnibus renunciare debemus, parati patrem, matrem, familiam, & facultates nostras relinquere, nisi indigni ejus consortio haberi vellemus.
units.tr: From this is drawn the sixth exhortation, to a wise imitation of Christ, who went out of the city and offered himself to the Father. This imitation consists of three things. 1. Just as Christ, going forth outside the city, renounced the world in order to do the Father's will, so we ought to renounce all worldly things for his sake, being ready to leave father, mother, family and our possessions, unless we wish to be counted unworthy of his fellowship.

units.la: 2. Sicut CHRISTUS crucem suam portavit, exiens in locum probrosum, Golgotha: sic nos oportet opprobrium CHRISTI seu crucem nostram post eum portare, id est, ad exilia, persecutiones, contumelias, & id genus aerumnas, ejus causa ferendas nos comparare, & paratos esse.
units.tr: 2. Just as Christ bore his cross, going out to the place of reproach, Golgotha, so we ought to bear Christ's reproach, or our cross, after him, that is, to prepare ourselves and be ready to endure for his sake exiles, persecutions, insults, and hardships of that kind.

units.la: Non enim Hujus membri rationem reddit, quia nos fideles novimus momentanea omnia esse haec terrena, nec nobis commorandi locum esse in terra, sed quærendam esse civitatem, coelestem illam hæreditatem: ad quam obtinendam, prompto animo decet nos ex mundo exire, & rebus mundanis renuntiare.
units.tr: For he gives the reason for this part: because we believers know that all these earthly things are momentary, and that we have no abiding place on earth, but must seek the city, that heavenly inheritance; to obtain which it is fitting that we go out of the world with a ready mind and renounce worldly things.

units.la: Per ipsum
units.tr: Through him.

units.la: Tertium in quo imitari debemus Christum patientem, est; ut nitentes intercessione, merito, & dignitate ejus, offeramus Deo hostias spirituales & acceptas, hoc est, Sicut Christus, ut passione sua typos Leviticos omnes impleret & aboleret, seipsum Deo obtulit: sic nos (quos unico suo sacrificio consummavit, quod ad justificationem attinet, & ut Sacerdotes Deo consecratos sanctificavit, ut abolitis legalibus sacrificiis spiritualia sacrificia offerremus) offerre debemus nos ipsos ut hostias vivas, ad Deo serviendum: & simul etiam offerre sacrificia laudis, precationis, & gratiarum actionis, quae sunt nostrae frugum primitiae, nostri vituli & spiritualia illa sacrificia, quae assiduè debemus offerre Deo per Christum, cujus merito nos Deo grati sumus, & per quem accepta redditur obedientia nostra.
units.tr: The third thing in which we ought to imitate Christ suffering is that, leaning on his intercession, merit and dignity, we offer to God spiritual and acceptable sacrifices. That is, just as Christ offered himself to God, so that by his passion he might fulfil and abolish all the Levitical types, so we (whom he has perfected by his one sacrifice, as far as justification is concerned, and whom he has sanctified as priests consecrated to God, so that, the legal sacrifices being abolished, we might offer spiritual sacrifices) ought to offer ourselves as living sacrifices to serve God; and at the same time also to offer sacrifices of praise, prayer and thanksgiving, which are the first fruits of our produce, our calves, and those spiritual sacrifices which we ought continually to offer to God through Christ, by whose merit we are pleasing to God, and through whom our obedience is rendered acceptable.

units.la: Praeter vitulos labiorum, jubet etiam beneficentiam exercere, hoc est, omnia charitatis officia erga omnes, potissimum vero erga fideles seu domesticos, fidei praestare.
units.tr: Besides the calves of the lips, he also bids us to exercise beneficence, that is, to render all offices of charity towards all, but especially towards believers or those of our household.

units.la: Hanc partem hortationis urget ratione validâ, quia hujus generis sacrificia Deo placent, seu accepta sunt, ut suavissimus fructus fidei nostrae in Christum, & evidentissimum testimonium sincerae dilectionis nostrae erga Deum & proximum.
units.tr: He urges this part of the exhortation with a strong reason: because sacrifices of this kind are pleasing to God, or acceptable, as the sweetest fruit of our faith in Christ and the most evident testimony of our sincere love towards God and our neighbour.

units.la: Vers. 17. Obedite ducibus vestris, & obsecundate, vigilant enim ipsi pro animabus vestris, tanquam rationem reddituri: ut cum gaudio hoc faciant, & non gementes, id enim est vobis inutile.
units.tr: Verse 17. Obey your leaders and submit to them, for they watch over your souls, as those who must give account, so that they may do this with joy and not with groaning, for that is unprofitable for you.

units.la: Hortatio 7. Ut officia erga Pastores, & Gubernatores debita, sedulò praestent: ut Dei ministros reverenter eos excipientes, amore, propter opus Dei in ipsorum manibus, proficuentes, iis obtemperantes in omnibus quae Dei nomine pro officii sui ratione, credenda & facienda, ex Dei verbo praescribunt, labores ipsorum & curas, quâ possent gratitudine compensare studentes.
units.tr: The seventh exhortation: that they diligently render the duties owed to pastors and governors, so that, receiving them reverently as ministers of God, they may be eager to repay their labours and cares with gratitude, out of love, on account of the work of God in their hands, obeying them in all things which, in the name of God and according to the nature of their office, they prescribe from the Word of God to be believed and done.

units.la: Hortationis argumenta sunt quatuor: 1. Ministri Ecclesiastici ductores vestri excubant pro vobis precantes, studentes, disputantes pro vobis, praedicantes Euangelium, & disciplinam Ecclesiasticam exercentes vestro bono inter vos, Ergo obedite iis.
units.tr: The arguments of the exhortation are four. 1. Your ecclesiastical ministers, your leaders, keep watch for you, praying, studying, disputing on your behalf, preaching the Gospel and exercising church discipline among you for your good. Therefore obey them.

units.la: Arg. 2. Exiget Deus rationem ab iis animarum vestrarum, si vel unica earum, ipsorum culpâ perierit. Obedite ergo iis qui in tam periculosâ & durâ provinciâ inter vos laborant.
units.tr: Argument 2. God will require an account from them of your souls, if even one of them perishes through their fault. Therefore obey those who labour among you in so dangerous and hard a charge.

units.la: Arg. 3. Si obedieritis, ut decet, gaudebunt Pastores vestri, alacriusque incumbent operi suo: Sin minus, facient quidem officium suum, sed ægre & cum gemitibus, atque ita vos qui grati esse debuissetis, tortores Pastorum vestrorum, & crudeles in eos evadetis. Ergo obedite ipsis.
units.tr: Argument 3. If you obey as is fitting, your pastors will rejoice and apply themselves more cheerfully to their work; but if not, they will indeed do their duty, but with difficulty and with groans, and so you, who ought to have been grateful, will turn out to be tormentors of your pastors and cruel towards them. Therefore obey them.

units.la: Id enim ] Arg. 4. cum occupatione objectionis (si forte quis inter eos Pastorum molestias, dolorem, & gemitus non curaret) Vestro malo cedet, si vestra culpa Dei ministri ingemiscere cogantur, Exaudiet Deus gemitus eorum, & contemptum suorum Legatorum severiter vindicabit. Ergo iis obedite.
units.tr: For this] Argument 4, with the anticipation of an objection (in case someone among them might not care about the troubles, grief and groans of the pastors): it will turn to your harm if the ministers of God are compelled to groan because of your fault; God will hear their groans and will severely avenge the contempt shown to his messengers. Therefore obey them.

units.la: Secunda pars.
units.tr: Second part.

units.la: Vers. 18. Orate pro nobis: confidimus enim nos bonam conscientiam habere, ut qui in omnibus cupiamus honeste conversari:
units.tr: Verse 18. Pray for us: for we trust that we have a good conscience, desiring in all things to live honestly:

units.la: Altera pars Capitis, in qua est Epilogus Epistolæ, cujus articuli sunt sex; in primo, quia officium est omnium commilitonum in exercitu Ecclesiæ militantis, pro se mutuò precari, Apostolus more suo sub finem Epistolæ commendat se precibus fidelium Hebræorum, quos orare vult, ut Deus ipsi benedicat in omnibus, speciatim vero, ut liberè, & cum fructu Euangelium prædicare posset. Loquitur autem de se in plurali numero, ut liquet ex sequentibus, quæ ad ipsius personam pertinent, ex quibus perspicuum est non latuisse fideles Hebræos, Paulum Epistolæ Scriptorem fuisse, id quod etiam Petrus nobis confirmat, licet propter infideles Hebræos quos lucrifacere studebat, Epistolæ huic nomen suum illis exosum non præfixerit: Rationes cur Paulus orare eos velit pro se ipso, sunt duæ.
units.tr: This is the second part of the chapter, which contains the epilogue of the Epistle. It has six articles. In the first, since it is the duty of all fellow soldiers in the army of the militant Church to pray for one another, the Apostle, in his customary manner near the end of the Epistle, commends himself to the prayers of the faithful Hebrews, whom he asks to pray that God would bless him in all things, and especially that he might preach the Gospel freely and with fruit. He speaks of himself in the plural, as is clear from what follows, which pertain to his own person. From this it is evident that the faithful Hebrews did not fail to know that Paul was the writer of the Epistle, as Peter also confirms for us. Yet, because of the unbelieving Hebrews whom he was eager to win, he did not prefix his name to it, since that would have been hateful to them. There are two reasons why Paul wants them to pray for him.

units.la: Confidimus ] Ratio prima, cum occupatione objectionis, Quia etiamsi læsdatur fama mea per calumniatores, qui hostes sunt Euangelii, nec me prædicantem de Christi gratia, & liberatione à fœdere operum, & ceremoniarum Leviticarum ferunt, mihi tamen conscius sum officii bene administrati, & vitæ adeo innocenter actæ, ut de nemine malè meritus sim. Modestissimè autem hic loquitur de se, ne cavillandi occasionem daret ullam.
units.tr: We trust] The first reason, with an anticipated objection: even if my reputation is harmed by slanderers, who are enemies of the Gospel and who say that I do not preach the grace of Christ and deliverance from the covenant of works and the Levitical ceremonies, I am nonetheless conscious that I have administered my office well and have lived so blamelessly that I have done harm to no one. He speaks very modestly here about himself, so as not to give any occasion for slander.

units.la: Amplius ] Ratio 2. Quia si pro me oraveritis, futurum est ut citius quam expectatis & quam causæ secundæ permissuræ videntur, copia mei vobis concedatur, & restituar Ecclesiis vestris, à quibus diutius quam vellem variis impedimentis implicitus, distineor, Verf. 19. Amplius autem obsecro vos, ut id faciatis, ut celerius restituar vobis,
units.tr: Moreover] The second reason: if you pray for me, it will come about that I shall be granted to you sooner than you expect and sooner than secondary causes seem to allow, and I shall be restored to your churches, from which I am kept away longer than I would like, entangled in various hindrances. Verse 19. Moreover I beg you to do this, so that I may be restored to you more quickly,

units.la: Verf. 20. Deus vero pacis author, qui magnum illum ovium per sanguinem foederis aeterni Pastorem, Dominum nostrum Iesum, à mortuis reduxit,
units.tr: Verse 20. Now the God of peace, who brought again from the dead the great Shepherd of the sheep, through the blood of the everlasting covenant, our Lord Jesus,

units.la: Verf. 21 Perficiat vos in omni opere bono, ad praestandum ipsius voluntatem: efficiens in vobis quod acceptum sit in conspectu suo, per Iesum Christum: cui sit Gloria in saecula saeculorum. Amen.
units.tr: Verse 21. Make you perfect in every good work to do his will, working in you what is well pleasing in his sight, through Jesus Christ: to whom be glory for ever and ever. Amen.

units.la: Articulus 1.
units.tr: Article 1.

units.la: In quo praemissis argumentis fiduciae de exauditione, precatur Apostolus pro Hebraeis, ut eos Deus plenè sanctificet, id est, aptet coagmentet, perficiat, tanquam unius corporis membra componat, & absolutos reddat in omni opere bono, ad praestandam ipsius voluntatem. Quo insinuat ineptos nos esse ad omne opus bonum, quippe qui ut luxata membra, neque possumus, quod nostrum est, facere, neque cum aliis concurrere ad praestandum vel promovendum ullum bonum, donec Deus nos ad se trahat propius, & nos sibi conjungat, nisi voluntatem nostram moveat, & incitet ad bonum volendum; efficiens, ut velimus & perficiamus, seu ut praestemus bonum, quod ipse voluntate praeceptiva faciendum imperat. Id quod Apostolus plenius explicat, addendo modum quo Deus perficiat eos, Efficiens, inquit, in vobis quod acceptum sit in conspectu suo, per Iesum Christum, hoc est per gratiam suam efficaciter operantem in vobis, & per vos, opera sibi placentia, & efficiens omne bonum in quo ei placeatis: sub quo bono, principia actionum bonarum necessario continentur, & nominatim ipse afflatus voluntatis ejusque cooperatio. Addit autem per Iesum. 1. Quia merito mortis Christi omnia illa bona nobis emuntur: 2. Per eum ut per canalem derivantur ad nos:
units.tr: In this article, having set out the arguments for confidence that he will be heard, the Apostle prays for the Hebrews that God would fully sanctify them, that is, fit, join together and perfect them, and so put them together as members of one body, and make them complete in every good work, to do his will. By this he implies that we are unfit for every good work: like dislocated limbs, we cannot do what is our part, nor join with others to perform or advance any good, until God draws us nearer to himself and joins us to himself, unless he moves and stirs our will to will the good, working in us both to will and to perform, that is, to carry out the good which he commands by his preceptive will. The Apostle explains this more fully by adding the means by which God perfects them: working in you what is well pleasing in his sight, through Jesus Christ, that is, through his grace efficaciously working in you and through you, producing works pleasing to him and every good in which he is pleased with you. Under this good the principles of good actions are necessarily contained, and especially the inspiration of the will itself and its cooperation. He adds through Jesus for these reasons: (1) because all those good things are purchased for us by the merit of Christ's death; (2) because they flow down to us through him as through a channel;

units.la: 3. Per eum efficiuntur illa bona opera: 4. Per eum purgantur, & accepta redduntur: Idcirco Deo & Christo Gloria tribuitur in aeternum, Amen. Fiduciae suae in precando Argumenta habet quatuor, verf. 20.
units.tr: (3) because those good works are made effective through him; (4) because through him they are cleansed and made acceptable. For this reason glory is ascribed to God and Christ for ever, Amen. He has four arguments for his confidence in praying: verse 20.

units.la: Deus pacis ] Arg. 1. cum relatione ad Ecclesiae concordiam, Deus est Deus pacis. Ergo confidenter petendum est à Deo, ut det vobis studium pacis inter vos & erga Deum, in sanctitate celebranda.
units.tr: The God of peace] Argument 1, with reference to the concord of the Church: God is the God of peace. Therefore we must confidently ask God to give you a zeal for peace among yourselves and toward God, in the pursuit of holiness.

units.la: Qui reduxit ] Arg. 2 Reduxit Deus Christum à mortuis. Ergo & potest & vult vos oves ipsius, & membra corporis ipsius perficere in omni opere bono, propter quae CHRISTUS & mortuus, & suscitatus est.
units.tr: Who brought again] Argument 2: God raised Christ from the dead. Therefore he both can and will perfect you, his sheep and the members of his body, in every good work, for which Christ both died and was raised.

units.la: Aug. 3. CHRISTUS est bonus ille, & summus Pastor ovium: Ergo expectandum ab eo ut sanctificet, & plene perficiat vos oves suas.
units.tr: Aug. 3. Christ is that good and chief Shepherd of the sheep. Therefore we must expect from him that he will sanctify you and fully perfect you, his sheep.

units.la: Arg. 4. Aeternum foedus ictum est de ovium redemptione, id est, de sanctitate & salute earum perficienda, idque sanguine CHRISTI sancitum est: Ergo vos ex foedere perficiemini in omni opere bono.
units.tr: Argument 4. The everlasting covenant was struck concerning the redemption of the sheep, that is, concerning the perfecting of their holiness and salvation, and this was sealed by the blood of Christ. Therefore you will be perfected in every good work by virtue of the covenant.

units.la: Verf. 22. Praetor autem vos, fratres, sufferte sermonem consolationis: etenim brevibus scripsi vobis.
units.tr: Verse 22. Yet I beseech you, brethren, suffer the word of exhortation: for I have written to you in few words.

units.la: Articulus 3.
units.tr: Article 3.

units.la: In quo Hebraeos orat, ut non tantum boni consulant, quicquid in hac hortatoria Epistola acrius aut aculeatum videri posset, sed etiam ut exhortationis sermonem, quo ista specialius dilaturi, & ipsis applicaturi erant ipsorum Pastores ordinarii, sufferant, & in optimam partem accipiant.
units.tr: In which he asks the Hebrews to take in good part, and to bear with, not only whatever in this hortatory epistle might seem sharp or stinging, but also the words of exhortation, by which their ordinary ministers were going to treat these matters more specifically and apply them to them; and to take them in the best sense.

units.la: Ratio petitionis est, Quia brevius ista conscripta sunt ab Apostolo, absque ullis condimentis, quae reprehensiones lentire potuissent, & opus habent explicatione, oratione copiosa, applicatione ampliori & magis aculeata, ab ordinariis Pastoribus.
units.tr: The reason for the request is this: these things were written by the Apostle more briefly, without any seasoning that might have softened the rebukes, and they need explanation, a fuller discourse, and a wider and more pointed application from the ordinary ministers.

units.la: Verf. 23. Scitote fratrem nostrum Timotheum solutum esse, cum quo (si celerius venerit) visam vos.
units.tr: Verse 23. Know that our brother Timothy has been set free, with whom (if he comes more quickly) I shall see you.

units.la: Articulus 4.
units.tr: Article 4.

units.la: Est laetum nuncium de Timothei comitis sui assidui, quem ipsis gratum fuisse noverat, liberatione: ut quem captivum detineri audiverant & dolebant, scirent nunc liberatum esse, & recreantur. In eundem finem spem facit adventus sui ad eos, una cum Timotheo.
units.tr: This is a joyful announcement of the release of Timothy, his constant companion, whom he knew to be dear to them: so that those who had heard he was held captive and grieved for him might now know that he was freed, and be refreshed. To the same end he gives hope of his own coming to them together with Timothy.

units.la: Verf. 24. Salutate omnes duces vestros, & omnes sanctos. Salutant vos Itali.
units.tr: Verse 24. Greet all your leaders, and all the saints. The Italians greet you.

units.la: Articulus 5.
units.tr: Article 5.

units.la: In quo salutationes continentur: Nam primo salutem mittit omnibus Pastoribus & Gubernatoribus Ecclesiarum in Judaea: Deinde reliquis Fidelibus, ut omnes a se pariter amari sciant. Tertio loco Sanctorum in Italia nomine salutatos vult fideles Hebraeos.
units.tr: In this the greetings are contained: for first he sends greetings to all the ministers and governors of the churches in Judaea; then to the rest of the faithful, so that they may all know they are equally loved by him; and third, he wishes the Hebrew believers to be greeted in the name of the saints in Italy.

units.la: Verf. 25 Gratia sit cum omnibus vobis.
units.tr: Verse 25. Grace be with you all.

units.la: Articulus 6.
units.tr: Article 6.

units.la: In quo Paulus, consueto suo signaculo, 2. Thess. 2. 17, claudit Epistolam, omnibus gratiam optans, id est, omnia dona salutaria, seu quaecunque ad ipsos perficiendos ex fonte gratuitae beneficentiae DEI necessario requiruntur.
units.tr: In this, Paul, with his customary sign-off (2 Thess. 2:17), closes the epistle, wishing grace to all, that is, all the saving gifts, or whatever is necessarily required for their perfection from the fountain of God's free goodness.

units.la: Quod ad ὑπογραφὴν; quæ post Epistolam adjicitur, non est quod ei fidem habeamus: Nam ex hujus Capitis verf. 23. constat Timotheum abfuisse cum scripta fuit hæc epistola: A librario igitur aliquo imperito adjectæ videntur subscriptiones. Ideoque eas missas facimus omnes.
units.tr: As for the subscription (ὑπογραφή) which is added after the epistle, there is no reason for us to put faith in it: for from verse 23 of this chapter it is clear that Timothy was absent when this epistle was written. The subscriptions therefore seem to have been added by some unskilled scribe. For that reason we set them all aside.

units.la: EXPOSITIO ANALYTICA EPISTOLÆ IACOBI.
units.tr: Expository analysis of the Epistle of James.

units.la: Summarium.
units.tr: Summary.

units.la: Acobus Apostolus, cognomento Alphæi, ex ossicio Apostolatus sui, Hæbreos fideles graviter commone‑facit de variis officiis Christianis, quibus ornari posse fidem Christianam, & promoveri ipsorum salutem prospi‑ciebat: eas virtutes quibus opus habere videbantur, ma‑ximè in eum finem ipsis prudenter proponens; & vitia ad quæ proclivíores erant, vel quibus jam laborabant a‑criter corripiens. Singula capita suum habent numerum ad‑monitionum, prout in singulis explicandis specialius ostenditur. Quæ omnes ad‑ moniciones, etiamsi in Ecclesiæ Catholicæ usum scriptæ sunt, apparet tamen Apo‑stolum voluisse eas legi præcipuè ab omnibus dispersis Israelitis & conversis ad Fidem, & non conversis cujus consilii Indicia sunt tria, primum, generalis Epi‑stolæ inscriptio ad omnes duodecim tribus. Secundum est, communis & civilis salutandi formula: & tertium est, docendi genus quod ad excutiendum torporem conscientiarum, & resipiscentiam excitandam maximè ex parte comparatur, si forte ex errantibus aliquis hac doctrinâ in viam revocari potuisset, id quod versu ultimo Capitis ultimi non obscurè ab Apostolo intendi significatur.
units.tr: James the Apostle, surnamed the son of Alphaeus, in the discharge of his apostolic office, earnestly admonishes the faithful Hebrews concerning various Christian duties, by which he saw that the Christian faith could be adorned and their salvation advanced. He wisely sets before them those virtues which they seemed to need, chiefly with that end in view, and sharply rebukes the vices to which they were more prone, or with which they were already afflicted. Each chapter has its own number of admonitions, as is shown more particularly in the explanation of each. Although all these admonitions were written for the use of the Catholic Church, it nevertheless appears that the Apostle intended them to be read chiefly by the dispersed Israelites, both those converted to the faith and those not converted. There are three indications of this purpose: first, the general inscription of the letter to all twelve tribes; second, the common and civil form of greeting; and third, the manner of teaching, which is designed chiefly to shake off the torpor of consciences and to stir up repentance, if perhaps some of the erring might be called back to the way by this teaching, an aim which the Apostle does not obscurely indicate in the last verse of the last chapter.

units.la: Caput Primum.
units.tr: Chapter One.

units.la: POst inscriptionem Epistolæ, vers. 1, hoc capite, loci communes seu admo‑nitiones, habentur tres: Prima admonitio de rectè ferendis persequutioni‑bus, seu tentationibus externis, ad verl 13. Secunda, de recta æstimatio‑ne tentatiore tentationum internarum, ad verf. 2i. Tertia, de religione solide exercenda, ad finem.
units.tr: After the inscription of the Epistle (v. 1), this chapter contains three topics, or lines of exhortation. The first is on how to bear persecutions, or external temptations, rightly, down to verse 13. The second is on rightly judging internal temptations, at verse 2 and following. The third is on practising religion soundly, to the end.

units.la: Verf. 1. IACOBVS Dei ac Domini Iesu Christi servus, duodecim tribubus dispersis, salutem:
units.tr: Verse 1. James, a servant of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ, to the twelve tribes scattered abroad, greeting:

units.la: In Epistolæ inscriptione describitur Scriptor, Iacobus servus Dei, & Domini Iesu Christi, scilicet in Apostolatus munere, quo posset omnes tribus Israelis cum autoritate docere, & de officiis suis monere, Dei servum se vocat, ut oltendat se Patrio Deo servire, serviendo filio ejus Iesu Christo, & speciali autoritate Dei, & Christi, se hæc scribere. Illi ad quos Epistola scribitur, sunt Israelitæ, præcipuè fideles ejecti ex Terra Sancta, & per regiones dispersi, sed (quod ad spem cœli, per sanctam terram repræsentati) ad servatorem Iesum collecti. Hos jubet solidè (& ut Christianis est concessum) salvere vel gaudere, mutuata salutationis formâ, ex communi Ethnicorum usu, sed in Christianum sensum conversa.
units.tr: In the inscription of the Epistle the writer is described as James, a servant of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ, namely in the office of apostleship, by which he could teach all the tribes of Israel with authority and admonish them about their duties. He calls himself a servant of God to show that he serves the Father by serving his Son Jesus Christ, and that he writes these things by the special authority of God and Christ. Those to whom the Epistle is written are Israelites, chiefly believers driven out of the Holy Land and scattered through the regions, but gathered to the Saviour Jesus (as far as the hope of heaven is concerned, they are represented by the holy land). He bids them to greet, or rejoice, heartily (and as Christians are permitted to do), using the form of greeting borrowed from the common custom of the heathen, but turned to a Christian sense.

units.la: Verf. 2. Tro summo gaudio ducite, fratres mei, quoties in tentationes varias inciderritis:
units.tr: Verse 2. Count it all joy, my brethren, when you fall into various temptations:

units.la: Prima admonitio, Ne ægrius & impatientius ferrent afflictiones externas, & persequutiones pro Euangelio, sed ut corrigerent carnis judicium de externis illis exercitiis, quibus Deus tentabat, seu probabat ipsorum fidem & sinceritatem. In hunc finem thesis statuitur carnis judicio contraria, nempe, Omnis, seu summi gaudii materia æstimanda est, cum Dei providentia incidthey in varias persequutiones vel afflictiones, quibus probemini an velitis etiam in rebus adversis Deo adhærere, hanc Thesin confirmat argumentis septem.
units.tr: The first admonition is that they should not bear external afflictions and persecutions for the Gospel too grievously or impatiently, but should correct the judgement of the flesh about those external trials by which God tests, or proves, their faith and sincerity. To this end a thesis is laid down, contrary to the judgement of the flesh, namely: every matter of supreme joy is to be judged such when, by the providence of God, they fall into various persecutions or afflictions, by which you are proved whether you are willing to cleave to God even in adversity. He confirms this thesis with seven arguments.

units.la: Verf. 3. Illud scientes, probationem fidei vestræ parere patientiam:
units.tr: Verse 3. Knowing this, that the trying of your faith works patience:

units.la: Argumentum primum, Illæ tentationes sunt fidei vestræ exploratio, expolitio, & productio in apertum. Ergo summo gaudio ducere debetis, cum in varias tentationes inciderits.
units.tr: First argument: those temptations are the testing, refining, and bringing into the open of your faith. Therefore you ought to count it supreme joy when you fall into various temptations.

units.la: Parere Arg. 1. Quia hoc exercitium pariet vobis patientiam, quæ majoris est pretii, quam ut afflictiones pollint in comparationem cum ea venire: Ergo, &c.
units.tr: Works Argument 1: because this exercise will work patience in you, which is of greater worth than that afflictions could be weighed against it. Therefore, etc.

units.la: Verf. 4. Caterum patientia opus perfectum habeat, ut sitis perfecti & integri, ita ut nihil desit.
units.tr: Verse 4. But let patience have its perfect work, that you may be perfect and entire, lacking nothing.

units.la: Arg. 3. cum hortatione conjunctum, Opus est variis afflictionibus, & ut cum aliqua mora incumbant vobis, (nempe quandiu Deo visum fuerit) ut tolerantiæ opus perficiatur, & ut vos qui habetis alias dotes, habeatis etiam patientiæ donum, atque ita compleatur imago CHRI-STI in vobis, ut ad integritatem seu perfectionem Partium sanctitatis nihil vobis deest. Ergo afflictiones summo gaudio ducere debetis.
units.tr: Argument 3, joined to the exhortation: there is need of various afflictions, and that they should press upon you for some time (namely as long as God sees fit), so that the work of endurance may be completed, and that you who have other gifts may also have the gift of patience, and so the image of Christ may be complete in you, so that you lack nothing for the wholeness or perfection of the parts of holiness. Therefore you ought to count afflictions a matter of supreme joy.

units.la: Verf. 5. Quòd si cui vestrum deest sapientia, postulet à Deo qui dat cam omnibus benignè, nec exprobrat, & dabitur ei.
units.tr: Verse 5. But if any of you lacks wisdom, let him ask of God, who gives to all liberally and without reproach, and it shall be given him.

units.la: Arg. 4. per occupationem objectionis propositum, Parata est, & in promptu posita sapientia, quæ & gaudii & patientiæ rationes in his exercitiis efficaciter suppeditet omnibus afflictis, donum hoc à Deo petentibus. Ergo gaudendum in afflictionibus.
units.tr: Argument 4, introduced by way of an objection: wisdom is ready and at hand, and it will effectively supply reasons for joy and patience in these trials to all the afflicted who ask God for this gift. Therefore one must rejoice in afflictions.

units.la: Qui dat ] Hoc Argumentum confirmat ab abundanti gratia Dei, qui petentibus omnibus gratis, abundanter, & sine exprobratione indignitatis vel ingratitudinis in precante, resipiscenti dat quodcunque petitur spirituale donum, quantum ad salutem sufficit.
units.tr: Who gives: this argument is confirmed from the abundant grace of God, who gives freely and abundantly to all who ask, and without reproaching the suppliant for unworthiness or ingratitude, gives to the penitent whatever spiritual gift is asked, as much as is sufficient for salvation.

units.la: Verf. 6. Sed postulet cum fide nihil disceptans: nam qui disceptat, similis est fluctui maris, qui ventis agitatur & jactatur.
units.tr: Verse 6. But let him ask in faith, nothing wavering. For he who wavers is like a wave of the sea, driven and tossed by the wind.

units.la: Idem Argumentum explicat à parte precantis, requirens ut oret in fide, seu fiducia fundata in promissione Dei, de dono dando, sine disceptatione, & ne admittat dubitationem, an Deus sit illud necessarium donum sibi promissum concessurus; Cujus requisitæ fiduciæ, & prohibitæ disceptationis rationes reddit tres.
units.tr: The same argument is explained from the side of the one who asks: he requires that he pray in faith, that is, in confidence grounded in God's promise to give, without wavering, and not to admit doubt whether God will grant the necessary gift promised to him. He gives three reasons for the required confidence and the forbidden wavering.

units.la: Nam qui ] Ratio prima, Quia disceptans qui huc illuc jactatur in precibus, dubius an Deum veracem & misericordem sit experturus, similis est fluctibus marinis, qui à vento huc illuc sine fructu agitantur, & evanescunt.
units.tr: For he who: the first reason: the one who wavers in prayer, uncertain whether he will find God truthful and merciful, is like the waves of the sea, which are driven hither and thither by the wind without profit and vanish away.

units.la: Verf. 7 Ne igitur existimet homo ille se quicquam acceptu.um à Domino.
units.tr: Verse 7. Let not that man suppose that he will receive anything from the Lord.

units.la: Ratio 2 Quia disceptatio ista, quæ non definit in conclusionem fidei, preces reddit irritas, quibus Deus non annuit.
units.tr: Reason 2: because such wavering, which does not end in a conclusion of faith, makes prayers void, and God does not grant them.

units.la: Verf. 8 Vir animo duplici, inconstans est in omnibus viis suis.
units.tr: Verse 8. A double-minded man is unstable in all his ways.

units.la: Ratio 3. Quia istiusmodi disceptator infidelis, vel dubius quid statuat, instabilis est & inconstans in consiliis & actionibus suis, & non minus paratus ad discedendum à Deo, quam ad manendum cum eo, liquidem nihil fixi vel firmi tenet in præsenti religionis negotio, quod præ manibus habet:
units.tr: Reason 3: because such a doubter, unbelieving or uncertain what to resolve, is unstable and inconstant in his plans and actions, and is no less ready to depart from God than to remain with him, since he holds nothing fixed or firm in the present matter of religion that is before him.

units.la: Verf. 9. Porrò frater qui est abjectus, gloriet ur in sublimitate sua: Redit ad institutum, & addit Argumentum quintum ad probandum, quod in exercitio Crucis materia sit gaudii, Qui per Crucem seu afflictiones est humiliatus à Domino, gloriari potest in exercitio suo, tanquam nota adoptionis, & exaltationis suæ ad dignitatem filii Dei adoptivi, & ad privilegia Sanctorum; quæ sublimitas opulentorum divitias, & regum thronos longe superat. Ergo in probationibus per Crucem factis, vobis gaudendum est.
units.tr: Verse 9. But let the brother of humble circumstances glory in his exaltation. He returns to his subject and adds a fifth argument to prove that matter for joy lies in the exercise of the cross. The one who has been humbled by the Lord through the cross or afflictions can glory in his exercise, as a mark of his adoption and of his exaltation to the dignity of an adopted son of God and to the privileges of the saints. This exaltation far surpasses the riches of the wealthy and the thrones of kings. Therefore in the trials that come through the cross you ought to rejoice.

units.la: Verf. 10. Contra, qui dives est, in abjectione sui, quoniam veluti flos herbæ præteribit.
units.tr: Verse 10. But the rich, in his humiliation, because as the flower of the grass he will pass away.

units.la: Verf. 11. Nam velut exorto sole cum æstu, exaruit herba, & flos illius decidit, & speciosus decor ipsius periit: ita & dives in vitis suis marcescet.
units.tr: Verse 11. For the sun rises with its burning heat and withers the grass; its flower falls, and the beauty of its appearance perishes. So also the rich man will fade away in his pursuits.

units.la: Arg. 6. Qui dives est & intactus adhuc à persequutoribus & afflictionibus, nullam habet gloriandi materiam in prosperitate sua, sed in dimissione animi sui, seu in præparatione ad Crucem & afflictiones serendas, cum reliquis afflictis.
units.tr: Argument 6: the rich man, who is still untouched by persecutors and afflictions, has no matter for glorying in his prosperity, but in the humbling of his spirit, that is, in readiness to bear the cross and afflictions along with the rest of the afflicted.

units.la: Quoniam ] Ratio redditur, Quia qui non sic sapit, sed confidit in divitiis suis, est vanus, & evanescet, sicut flos herbæ arescet & peribit cum omnibus suis consiliis.
units.tr: Because: a reason is given: because he who does not think thus, but trusts in his riches, is vain and will vanish away, just as the flower of the grass withers and perishes with all his plans.

units.la: Verf. 12. Beatus vir qui tolerat tentationem: quoniam quum probatus erit accipiet coronam vitæ, quam promisit Dominus iis à quibus diligitur.
units.tr: Verse 12. Blessed is the man who endures temptation; for when he has been approved he will receive the crown of life, which the Lord has promised to those who love him.

units.la: Arg. 7. Qui patienter fert afflictiones, & probatus in fide compertus est, jam beatus est, & promissam coronam vitæ æternæ tandem consequetur, ad quam per exercitium Crucis jam paratur: Ergo materia gaudii æstimanda est exercitatio per Crucem.
units.tr: Argument 7: he who patiently bears afflictions, and is found approved in faith, is already blessed, and will at last obtain the promised crown of eternal life, for which he is already being prepared through the exercise of the cross. Therefore the exercise through the cross is to be judged a matter of joy.

units.la: Verf. 13. Nemo quum tentatur, dicat se à Deo tentari: nam Deus tentari malus non potest, nec quenquam tentat.
units.tr: Verse 13. Let no one say when he is tempted, "I am tempted by God"; for God cannot be tempted with evil, and he himself tempts no one.

units.la: Admonitio 2. De rectè æstimandis tentationibus internis, ne quis violet Dei sanctitatem, ne quidem vel cogitationum suarum senten- tiis, quasi Deus solicitaret quemvis ad peccandum, id quod Adami fi- liis est familiare, nempe ut culpam rejiciant in Deum quasi autorem.
units.tr: Admonition 2. On rightly judging inward temptations, so that no one violates God's holiness, not even in the judgments of his own thoughts, as though God stirred up anyone to sin. This is familiar to the sons of Adam, namely to throw the blame on God as the author.

units.la: Argumenta admonitionis seu dehortationis sunt octo, quæ omnia probant tentationes ad malum non ascribendas Deo.
units.tr: There are eight arguments of this admonition or dissuasion, all of which prove that temptations are not to be ascribed to God.

units.la: Nam Deus ] Argumentum primum, Deus non potest solicitari vel permoveri ad peccandum: Ergo nec solicitare potest alium quenquam ad peccandum: & per consequens tentatio ad peccatum non ascribenda est Deo.
units.tr: For God] The first argument: God cannot be stirred or moved to sin. Therefore neither can he stir up anyone else to sin, and consequently temptation to sin is not to be ascribed to God.

units.la: Verf. 14. Sed unusquisque tentatur, dum a propria cupiditate abstrahitur & illectatur.
units.tr: Verse 14. But each one is tempted when he is drawn away and enticed by his own lust.

units.la: Arg. 2. Propria uniuscujusque concupiscentia est vera tentationis causa. Ergo non ascribenda est Deo. Antecedens probat, methodum seductionis ad peccandum quinque suis gradibus explicando. Nam primò per concupiscentiam depravatam abstrahitur homo a bono vero, ne in eo conquiescat: Deinde illicitur a falsa specie boni, ad prosequendum malum.
units.tr: Argument 2. Each person's own concupiscence is the true cause of temptation. Therefore it is not to be ascribed to God. The antecedent is proved by explaining the method of seduction to sin in five stages. First, through depraved concupiscence a man is drawn away from the true good, so that he does not rest in it. Then he is enticed by a false appearance of good to pursue evil.

units.la: Verf. 15. Deinde cupiditas, postquam concepit, parit peccatum: peccatum vero perfectum gignit mortem.
units.tr: Verse 15. Then lust, after it has conceived, gives birth to sin; and sin, when it is full grown, brings forth death.

units.la: Tertiò, Voluntate & corde concipit propositum ad peccatum actu perpetrandum. Quartò, Peccatum actu perpetrat, Et quintò, Peccatum perpetratum merito suo quali parit & procurat mortem. Atque ita originalis pravitas gignit actuale peccatum, & per gradus ad summum incrementum perducit.
units.tr: Third, by the will and the heart he conceives a purpose to commit sin in deed. Fourth, he actually commits the sin. Fifth, the committed sin, by its own merit, brings forth and procures death. And so original depravity begets actual sin and, step by step, brings it to its highest growth.

units.la: Verf. 16. Ne erratis, fratres mei dilecti.
units.tr: Verse 16. Do not err, my beloved brethren.

units.la: Arg. 3. Errabitis, & falsum blasphemumque dogma tenebitis, si causam veltræ ad peccandum impulsionis Deo ascripseritis.
units.tr: Argument 3. You will err and hold a false and blasphemous doctrine if you ascribe to God the cause of your being impelled to sin.

units.la: Verf. 17. Omne munus bonum, & omne donum est perfectum, supernè descendens est à Patre luminum, apud quem non transmutatio, aut conversionis obumbratio.
units.tr: Verse 17. Every good gift and every perfect gift is from above, coming down from the Father of lights, with whom there is no variation or shadow of turning.

units.la: Arg. 4. Deus est Fons & Autor solus omnis boni (quod in nobis est, vel quod nobis conceditur, sive in statu naturæ sive gratiæ) & boni tantum, quippe à quo descendit omne bonum, & omne donum quod ad nostri perfectionem ullo modo conducit: Non ergo dicendum quod Deus sit causa peccati, vel mali in nobis.
units.tr: Argument 4. God is the sole Fount and Author of all good, whether what is in us or what is granted to us, whether in the state of nature or of grace, and he is the author of good alone, since from him descends every good and every gift that contributes in any way to our perfection. Therefore it must not be said that God is the cause of sin or of evil in us.

units.la: Arg. 5. Deus est Pater luminum, cognitionis, intelligentiæ, sanctitatis, & felicitatis: Ergo non est Pater tenebrarum oppositarum, seu peccati.
units.tr: Argument 5. God is the Father of lights, of knowledge, understanding, holiness and happiness. Therefore he is not the Father of the opposite darkness, that is, of sin.

units.la: Arg. 6. Deus est immutabilis, naturâ suâ expers omnis variationis in melius vel deterius: ab omni æternitate sui semper in omnibus similis ita, ut non sit ipsius à seipso discrepantiæ fundamentum ullum; nec motus, seu mutationis ejus, vel levissima obumbratio: Ergo est impossibile ut Deus sit Autor peccati.
units.tr: Argument 6. God is immutable. By his nature he is free from all variation for better or for worse. From all eternity he is always the same in all things, so that there is no ground in him for any discord with himself, nor any movement or change, nor even the slightest shadow of it. Therefore it is impossible that God should be the author of sin.

units.la: Vers. 18. Is quia voluit, progenuit nos sermone veritatis, ut essemus, primitiæ quarum creaturarum.
units.tr: Verse 18. Of his own will he brought us forth by the word of truth, that we should be a kind of firstfruits of his creatures.

units.la: Arg. 7. Deus voluntate suâ solâ permotus, per verbum Euangelii regenuit, & convertit nos à statu peccati ad sanctitatis suæ imaginem: Ergo non est ullius peccati in nobis autor.
units.tr: Argument 7. Moved by his will alone, God regenerated us through the word of the Gospel and turned us from the state of sin to the image of his holiness. Therefore he is not the author of any sin in us.

units.la: Ut essemus Arg. 8. Finis regenerationis nostræ intentus à Deo est, ut simus sancti, & toti consecrati instar primitiarum sub lege, in ipsius gloriam. Ergo non debemus blasphemias ullas cogitationes de eo admittere, quasi permoveremur ab eo ad malum seu peccatum.
units.tr: That we should be Argument 8. The end of our regeneration intended by God is that we should be holy and wholly consecrated, like firstfruits under the law, to his glory. Therefore we ought not to entertain any blasphemous thoughts about him, as though he moved us to evil or sin.

units.la: Vers. 19. Itaque, fratres mei dilecti, sit omnis homo velox ad audiendum, tardus ad loquendum, tardus ad iram.
units.tr: Verse 19. So then, my beloved brethren, let every man be swift to hear, slow to speak, slow to anger.

units.la: Tertia admonitio ex commemoratione regenerationis ipsorum per verbum Veritatis illata, ut solidam rationem ineant, qua reipsa & factis, religiosos se & verè regenitos demonstrent. Trimembris autem hæc admonitio est: In primo, docet modum audiendi & recipiendi sermonem Dei, quo præparentur ad praxin, ad vers. 22. In secundo jubet in genere, ut verbum ad praxin referant, ad vers. 26. In tertio jubet in specie, ut sermonis sanctitate, & charitatis operibus manifestam faciant religionis suæ virtutem.
units.tr: The third admonition is drawn from the mention of their regeneration through the word of truth, so that they may take up a solid line of reasoning by which they show, in deed and in works, that they are religious and truly regenerate. This admonition has three parts. In the first, it teaches the manner of hearing and receiving God's word, by which they are prepared for practice (to verse 22). In the second, it commands in general that they bring the word into practice (to verse 26). In the third, it commands in particular that they show the manifest power of their religion by the holiness of their speech and by works of love.

units.la: In primo membro admonitionis de sermone audiendo requirit quinque:
units.tr: In the first part of the admonition, on hearing the word, it requires five things:

units.la: 1. Ut dociles sint, & doctrinæ avidi: 2. Ne temere præcipitent judicium suum, seu ne subito sententiam ferant de rebus potissimum fidei. 3. Nec iracunde excipiant eos, qui primâ facie ab iis dissentire videntur.
units.tr: (1) That they be teachable and eager for doctrine. (2) That they not rashly hasten their judgment, that is, not pass a sudden verdict, especially on matters of faith. (3) That they not receive angrily those who at first sight seem to dissent from them.

units.la: Vers. 20. Nam ira viri justitiam Dei non exquitur.
units.tr: Verse 20. For the anger of man does not work the righteousness of God.

units.la: Rationem reddit hujus partis, Quia passionibus & perturbationibus nostris, vel carnali nostro zelo & fervore, non promovetur Dei opus, seu justitia illa quam ille requirit.
units.tr: He gives the reason for this part: the work of God, or that righteousness which he requires, is not advanced by our passions and disturbances, or by our carnal zeal and fervour.

units.la: Vers. 21. Quapropter abjectis omnibus sordibus & excremento malitiæ, cum lenitate recipite insitum sermonem, qui potest servare animas vestras,
units.tr: Verse 21. Therefore, putting away all filthiness and overflow of wickedness, receive with meekness the implanted word, which is able to save your souls,

units.la: 4. In verbo audiendo requirit, ut abjiciant sordidas voluptates carnis, & pravitatem illam naturalem quâ omnes abundamus, resipiscentiæ mortificationi studentes, ne impediatur sermonis Divini in ipsis femi-natio vel plantatio: 5 Ut in lenitate recipiant verbum, id est, animo humili & religioso in cordis sinum admittant termonem insititium, qui inleritur, & radices per fidem agit in corde, & cum eo quasi coalescit; Cujus ratio redditur, Quia sic receptus Dei sermo, salvas potest reddere ipsorum animas.
units.tr: (4) In hearing the word he requires that they put away the filthy pleasures of the flesh and that natural depravity in which we all abound, striving for the mortification of repentance, so that the seed or planting of the divine word in them is not hindered. (5) That they receive the word in meekness, that is, with a humble and reverent mind admit into the bosom of the heart the implanted word, which takes root and by faith strikes roots in the heart and, as it were, grows together with it. The reason is given: the word of God so received is able to save their souls.

units.la: Vers. 22. Reipsa verò præstate sermonem: nec sitù auditores solum, fallentes vosmetipsos.
units.tr: Verse 22. But be doers of the word, and not hearers only, deceiving yourselves.

units.la: In secundo membro admonitionis requirit in genere, ut non sint auditores Verbi tantùm, sed etiam factores, hoc est, in praxin redigant quod præcipit Dei Verbum: Cujus rationes reddit tres: Prima, Quia alioqui deciperent seipsos, putantes satis esle ad veritatem fidei probandam, audire Dei Verbum, licet ei obedire non studeant.
units.tr: In the second part of the admonition he requires, in general, that they be not only hearers of the Word but also doers, that is, that they bring into practice what the Word of God commands. He gives three reasons. First, otherwise they would deceive themselves, thinking it enough to prove the truth of faith to hear God's Word, even if they take no pains to obey it.

units.la: Vers. 23. Nam siquis audit sermonem, & eum non præstat, is similis est viro consideranti faciem suam nativam in speculo.
units.tr: Verse 23. For if anyone is a hearer of the word and not a doer, he is like a man who looks at his natural face in a mirror.

units.la: Vers. 24. Consideravit enim seipsum, & abiit, & statim oblitus qualis esset.
units.tr: Verse 24. For he looks at himself and goes away, and immediately forgets what manner of man he was.

units.la: Ratio 2. confirmans priorem, Quia non magis prodest audire Dei Verbum sine studio in praxin illud redigendi, quam si quis natívam faciem in speculo otiosè intueretur, sine ulu vel fructu aliquo.
units.tr: Reason 2, confirming the former: hearing God's Word without zeal to bring it into practice profits no more than if someone idly gazed at his natural face in a mirror, with no use or fruit at all.

units.la: Vers. 25. At qui intro spexerit in perfectam illam Legem libertatis, & in ea permanserit, quia non fuerit auditor obliviosus, sed efsector operis, beatus erit in opere suo,
units.tr: Verse 25. But whoever looks intently into the perfect law of liberty, and continues in it, not being a forgetful hearer but a doer of the work, will be blessed in his doing.

units.la: Ratio 3. Quia contra, qui quatuor hæc facit: 1. Qui accurate introspicit in Verbum Dei, studiose inquirens in omnem Dei voluntatem revelatam, quæ dicitur Lex, seu doctrina Libertatis: quia docet veram rationem liberationis à peccato & ira, & veram rationem ingenuè serviendi Deo, ut decet Dei libertos, qui dilectione & gratitudine constringuntur, ad Deo placendum: 2. Qui perseverat in studio sanctæ doctrinæ permanens: 3. Qui cavet ne oblivioni tradantur quæ dicit: 4. Denique, Qui opere studet in praxin redigere, quod jubet Dei sermo: Næ ille in operatione sua beatus erit, quia licet impossibile sit, ut operibus mereatur felicitatem, operibus tamen declarabitur coram omnibus esse beatus, & in operum bonorum exercitio, tanquam in via ad cælum ambulando, beatitudinem Sanctis promissam certò consequetur; & sic beatus erit in operatione sua.
units.tr: Reason 3. On the contrary, he who does these four things: (1) He looks carefully into the Word of God, diligently inquiring into all of God's revealed will, which is called the law or doctrine of liberty, because it teaches the true way of liberation from sin and wrath, and the true way of serving God freely, as befits the free men of God, who are bound to please God by love and gratitude. (2) He perseveres, remaining in the study of holy doctrine. (3) He takes care that what it says is not forgotten. (4) Finally, he strives to bring into practice what God's word commands. Such a one will indeed be blessed in his doing. For although it is impossible to merit happiness by works, yet by works he will be shown to be blessed before all, and walking in the exercise of good works, as on the way to heaven, he will certainly attain the blessedness promised to the saints. And so he will be blessed in his doing.

units.la: Verf. 26. Siquis videtur religiosus esse inter vos, non frænans linguam suam, sed suum ipsius cor seducens, hujus vana est religio.
units.tr: Verse 26. If anyone among you seems to be religious, and does not bridle his tongue but deceives his own heart, this man's religion is vain.

units.la: In tertio membro admonitionis requirit duo: Primum, Ut qui religiosi esse velint, & verè haberi, frænent linguam suam, & attendant, ut quod loquuntur sit præceptis Dei consentaneum, & Deo probatum. Rationes hujus requisiti reddit duas: 1. Qui contrà facit, & se religiosum putat, decipit cor suum: 2. Hypocrita est cui religio istiusmodi nihil erit profutura; siquidem cum ex abundantia cordis os loquatur, cor minimè curare censendus est, qui linguam non frænat.
units.tr: In the third part of the admonition he requires two things. First, that those who wish to be religious, and truly considered so, should bridle their tongue and take care that what they say agrees with the precepts of God and is approved by him. He gives two reasons for this requirement: (1) whoever acts otherwise and thinks himself religious deceives his own heart; (2) the one whose religion is of this kind will gain nothing from it, since the mouth speaks out of the abundance of the heart, so that a man who does not bridle his tongue must be judged to take no care of his heart at all.

units.la: Verf. 27. Religio pura & immaculata apud Deum & Patrem, hæc est, invisere orphanos & viduas in afflictione ipsorum, & immaculatum seipsum servare à mundo.
units.tr: Ver. 27. Pure and undefiled religion before God and the Father is this: to visit orphans and widows in their affliction, and to keep oneself unspotted from the world.

units.la: Secundum quod requirit, est, Ut operibus charitatis, & sanctâ conversatione manifestum faciant, se verè religiosos esse, seu suam professionem fidei Christianæ puram, sinceram, & immaculatam esse, vel quæ non dehonestet fidem illam quam profitentur, & quam Deus noster, & Pater noster approbet.
units.tr: The second thing he requires is that they show by works of charity and holy conduct that they are truly religious, that is, that their profession of the Christian faith is pure, sincere and undefiled, or at least does not dishonour the faith they profess, and that our God and Father may approve it.

units.la: Quod ad opera charitatis exempli causâ, nominat misericordiam erga orphanos & egenos in afflictione: nam visitare est miseriam & necessitatem benefice sublevare, sub quo officio synecdochicè comprehendit reliqua ergà proximum officia.
units.tr: As an example of works of charity, he names mercy towards orphans and the needy in affliction; for to visit means to relieve misery and want by help, and under this duty he comprehends, by synecdoche, the other duties towards our neighbour.

units.la: Quod ad sanctam conversationem attinet, eam comprehendit sub studio conservandi, per Dei gratiam, nos ipsos immaculatos à mundo, seu ab inquinamentis, quæ in mundo grassantur, & à contagione alienorum peccatorum, ita ut nec ipsi nos polluamus sceleribus, nec polluentibus se in cœno peccatorum communicemus.
units.tr: As for holy conduct, he includes under it the care, by the grace of God, of keeping ourselves unspotted from the world, that is, from the defilements that rage in the world and from contact with other people's sins, so that we neither pollute ourselves with wickedness nor take part in the mire of sin with those who defile themselves.

units.la: Caput Secundum.
units.tr: Chapter Two.

units.la: HOC Capite continentur duæ admonitiones: Prima de vitandâ profopolepsiâ, potissimum in rebus Ecclesiasticis, ad verf. 14. Altera de vitanda inani jactantia Fidei, ubi desunt bona opera.
units.tr: This chapter contains two admonitions: the first, against partiality (prosopolepsia), chiefly in ecclesiastical matters, at verse 14. The second, against the empty boasting of faith where good works are lacking.

units.la: Verf. 1. FRatres mei, ne cum respectu personarum habete fidem Domini nostri Iesu Christi gloriosi.
units.tr: Verse 1. My brethren, have not the faith of our glorious Lord Jesus Christ with respect of persons.

units.la: Primum vitium de quo vitando admonet, est Prosopolepsia, quæ committitur, cum in eadem causa plùs vel minùs tribuitur alicui quam æquum est, propter aliquid in ipsius personâ, quod ad causam illam nihil pertinet. Sic peccabant inter Hebræos, qui fidem in CHRISTUM magnificiebant in ditioribus: in pauperioribus verò eandem fidem nihili faciebant, usque adeo ut etiam divites infideles in pretio magno haberent, pauperes vero fideles in nullo numero æstimarent, sed contemnerent. Ab hoc vitio dehortatur, Argumentis adhibitis decem.
units.tr: The first vice he warns against is prosopolepsia, which is committed when, in the same cause, someone is given more or less than is fair, on account of something in that person which has nothing to do with the cause. This was the sin among the Hebrews, who honoured the faith in Christ in the rich, but made nothing of the same faith in the poorer. So far did they go that they esteemed unbelieving rich men highly, while they counted poor believers as nothing and despised them. He dissuades them from this vice with ten arguments.

units.la: Argumentum primum, IESUS CHRISTUS est gloriosus, & fides in ipsum in omnibus æquè gloriosa est. Ergo à personarum acceptione cavendum.
units.tr: First argument: Jesus Christ is glorious, and faith in him is equally glorious in all. Therefore the acceptance of persons must be avoided.

units.la: Verf. 2. Nam siquis in cœtum vestrum ingrediatur, aureum gestans annulum, veste splendida, ingrediatur autem & pauper cum sordida veste,
units.tr: Verse 2. For if there come into your assembly a man with a gold ring, in goodly apparel, and there come in also a poor man in vile raiment;

units.la: Verf. 3. Et respexeritis ad eum qui vestem gestat splendidam, & dixeritis ei, Tu sede hic pulchrè, & pauperi dicatis, Tu sta illic, aut sede hic subter scabellum meum:
units.tr: Verse 3. And ye have respect to him that weareth the gay clothing, and say unto him, Sit thou here in a good place; and say to the poor, Stand thou there, or sit here under my footstool:

units.la: Verf. 4. Nonne discrimen fecistis apud vos, & facti estis judices perversè deliberantes?
units.tr: Verse 4. Are ye not then partial in yourselves, and are become judges of evil thoughts?

units.la: Arg. 2. Hæc personarum acceptio etiam à conscientia vestra condemnatur, (Quod in exemplo facti ipsorum manifestum facit) nam divites infideles in Ecclesias vestras, curiositatis forte gratiâ tantum venientes, ita publicè honoratis solo divitiarum respectu, ut interim pauperes fratres neglectui habeatis, verf. 2. 3. Hoc conscientiæ testimonium interrogatione urget.
units.tr: Second argument: This acceptance of persons is also condemned by your own conscience, which the practice of your own actions makes plain. For you publicly honour unbelieving rich men who perhaps come to your churches only out of curiosity, solely out of respect for their riches, while meanwhile you neglect your poor brethren (verses 2 and 3). He presses this testimony of conscience with a question.

units.la: Et falsi] Arg. 3. Qui personas acceptant, sunt perversi Judices, quorum cogitationes perversæ sunt, non quod honorare Divites vel magis honorare Divitem quam pauperem iniquum sit, sed quod honorare Divites, etiam impios, propter Divitias cum contemptu fidelium, & piorum pauperum, quia pauperes sunt, iniquum sit. Sic enim Divitiæ habentur sola causa æstimationis; pietas verò sine divitiis contemnitur. Ergo personarum acceptatio vitanda est.
units.tr: And have become] Third argument: Those who accept persons are wicked judges, whose thoughts are wicked. It is not unjust to honour the rich, or to honour a rich man more than a poor one; but it is unjust to honour the rich, even impious ones, on account of their riches, with contempt for believers and for poor pious people, simply because they are poor. For riches are thus held to be the sole ground of esteem, while piety without riches is despised. Therefore the acceptance of persons is to be avoided.

units.la: Vers. 5. Audite, fratres mei dilecti, nonne Deus elegit pauperes mundi res mundi hujus ut fierent divites fide, & haredes regni quod promisit iis a quibus diligitur?
units.tr: Verse 5. Hearken, my beloved brethren, Hath not God chosen the poor of this world, rich in faith, and heirs of the kingdom which he hath promised to them that love him?

units.la: Verf. 6. At vos contumelia affecistis pauperem. Nonne divites per tyrannidem opprimunt vos, & trahunt vos ad tribunalia?
units.tr: Verse 6. But ye have dishonoured the poor man. Do not rich men oppress you by tyranny, and draw you before the judgment seats?
