units.la: Verf. 15. Et oratio fidei servabit laborantem, erigetque eum Dominus: quòd si peccata commiserit, remittentur ei.
units.tr: Verse 15. And the prayer of faith shall save the one who is labouring, and the Lord shall raise him up; and if he has committed sins, they shall be forgiven him.

units.la: Hujus unctionis & orationis, duplicem effectum sequuturum docet: 1. Si is qui donum sanationis miraculosæ, speciali revelatione fidem habens de successu, oraverit, oratio hæc à fide hujusmodi proveniens, servabit ægrotum à corporali morbo: Nam Dominus, inquit, restituet ei sanitatem, & eriget eum: Alter effectus, Si Ipecialia aliqua peccata ægroti morbum attraxerunt, Deus rogatus ab ægroto, & Presbyteris ea remissurus est.
units.tr: He teaches that this anointing and prayer will have a twofold effect: (1) If the one who has the gift of miraculous healing, having faith in the outcome through a special revelation, prays, this prayer, arising from such faith, will save the sick person from bodily disease; for the Lord, he says, will restore him to health and raise him up. (2) The other effect: if certain particular sins have brought on the sickness, God, asked by the sick person and the elders, will forgive them.

units.la: Verf. 16. Confitemini alii aliis offensas, & orate alii pro aliis, ut sanemini, multum enim valet deprecatio justi efficax.
units.tr: Verse 16. Confess your offences to one another, and pray for one another, that you may be healed; for the effective prayer of a righteous man avails much.

units.la: Quartum membrum admonitionis, de mutuo se juvandis in conscientiæ vulneribus & oneribus, ut sive admoniti à fratribus de peccatis, sive intus onere peccati vexati, confiterentur alii aliis peccata,& orarent alii pro aliis, mutuò alii alios sublevantes & consilio & oratione apud Deum, ut sanarentur. Rationes hujus membri sunt quatuor.
units.tr: The fourth member of the admonition concerns mutual help in the wounds and burdens of conscience: that, whether admonished by brethren about their sins or troubled inwardly by the burden of sin, they should confess their sins to one another and pray for one another, mutually raising one another up by counsel and by prayer before God, so that they may be healed. There are four reasons for this member.

units.la: Ut sanemini Ratio prima, Quia sic sanari poterant vulnera conscientiæ, & errores vitæ, quibus tanquam morbis laborabant.
units.tr: "That you may be healed." The first reason: because in this way the wounds of conscience and the errors of life, by which they were labouring as if by diseases, could be healed.

units.la: Magna Ratio 2. Quia oratio ardens, seu excitata ex fide & dilectione justi, seu hominis vere fidelis, multum conducit, ut speciale medium à Deo sanctificatum, ad obtinenda bona quæ nobis sunt necessaria.
units.tr: "Much." The second reason: because fervent prayer, or prayer stirred up by the faith and love of a righteous man, that is, of a truly faithful person, greatly avails, as a special means sanctified by God for obtaining the goods that are necessary for us.

units.la: Verf. 17. Elias homo erat iisdem quibus nos obnoxius, & precibus precatus est ne plueret: & non pluit super terram annos tres & sex menses:
units.tr: Verse 17. Elijah was a man subject to the same things as we are, and he prayed earnestly that it might not rain; and it did not rain upon the earth for three years and six months.

units.la: Verf. 18 Et rursum precatus est, & Cælum dedit pluviam, & terra protulit fructum suum.
units.tr: Verse 18. And again he prayed, and heaven gave rain, and the earth brought forth its fruit.

units.la: Ratio 3. confirmans priorem, Quia Eliæ precatio efficax fuit, non idcirco quod alienus fuerit ab infirmitatibus & passionibus, quibus alii fideles obnoxii sunt, nam etiam ille fuit ὁμοιοπαθης, sed quia ardenter, ex fide, secundum Dei voluntatem sibi revelatam, precatus est, ut clauderentur Coeli & aperirentur. Ergo si vos oraveritis alius pro alio ardenter, valiturae erunt, inquit, & vestrae preces.
units.tr: The third reason, confirming the former: Elijah's prayer was effective not because he was free from the infirmities and sufferings to which other believers are subject (for he too was ὁμοιοπαθὴς [of like passions]), but because he prayed fervently, in faith, according to the will of God revealed to him, that the heavens might be shut and opened. Therefore, he says, if you pray for one another fervently, your prayers too will avail.

units.la: Vers. 19. Fratres, si quis inter vos aberrarit à veritate, & converterit eum quispiam,
units.tr: Verse 19. Brethren, if anyone among you has strayed from the truth, and someone converts him,

units.la: Vers. 20. Sciat eum qui averterit peccatorem ab errore viae suae, servaturum animam à morte, & obtecturum multitudinem peccatorum.
units.tr: Verse 20. let him know that whoever turns a sinner from the error of his way will save a soul from death and cover a multitude of sins.

units.la: Ratio. 4. Quia si alii alios admonerent, & alii aliis peccata confiterentur, & precibus alius pro alio apud Deum insisterent, & instrumenta Dei se praeberent, ad cujuslibet errantis peccatoris conversionem: tum instrumenta etiam futuri essent servandi animam proximi sui à morte, ad quam errans properabat, & simul instrumenta futuri operiendi, & obtegendi multitudinem peccatorum fratris errantis: qui nisi resipuisset, peccata ipsius fuissent producenda in judicio Dei, ad condemnationem & mortem: quae jam post admonitionem errantis, & resipiscentiam admoniti, obteguntur.
units.tr: The fourth reason: because if they admonished one another, and confessed their sins to one another, and persevered in prayer for one another before God, and made themselves instruments of God for the conversion of any erring sinner, then they would also be instruments for saving the soul of their neighbour from death, towards which the wanderer was hastening, and at the same time instruments for covering and hiding the multitude of sins of the erring brother; which, unless he had repented, would have been brought forward in the judgment of God to condemnation and death, but which, after the admonition of the wanderer and the repentance of the admonished, are covered.

units.la: EXPOSITIO ANALYTICA PRIORIS EPISTOLAE PETRI.
units.tr: EXPOSITION OF THE FIRST EPISTLE OF PETER.

units.la: Summarium.
units.tr: Summary.

units.la: Epistolae scopus est ut Hebraeos per Gentes dispersos, & ad Christum conversos confirmaret in fide Christi, eosque excitaret ad perseverandum, & progressus faciendum in fide & vitae sanctitate, secundum uniuscujusque vocationem, ut apparet ex fine Epistolae Cap 5. vers. 12. In quem finem Gratiis actis Deo de ipsorum conversione, hortatur in genere ad sanctam conversationem, & charitatem mutuam exercendam. Capite primo, & priori parte Capitis secundi. Deinde descendit in specie ad officia, subditorum erga Magistratum; Servorum erga Dominos: ad mutua officia Conjugum, & Fratrum in Christo; cum inter se, tum erga persequutores, reliquo Capite secundo, & Capite tertio, & Capite quarto. Eandemque doctrinam prosequitur, Capite quinto. Presbyteros in Ecclesia, Juniores aetate, & cujusvis ordinis homines in officiis suis instruendo.
units.tr: The aim of the epistle is to strengthen the Hebrews scattered among the Gentiles who had been converted to Christ, to confirm them in faith in Christ, and to stir them to persevere and to make progress in faith and in holiness of life, according to each one's calling, as appears from the end of the epistle, chap. 5, vers. 12. To this end, having given thanks to God for their conversion, he exhorts them in general to holy conduct and to the exercise of mutual love. This is done in the first chapter and the first part of the second chapter. Then he descends in particular to the duties of subjects toward the magistrate and of servants toward their masters, and to the mutual duties of spouses and of brothers in Christ, both among themselves and toward their persecutors, in the rest of the second chapter, and in the third and fourth chapters. He pursues the same teaching in the fifth chapter, instructing the elders in the Church, the younger in age, and people of every rank in their duties.

units.la: Caput Primum.
units.tr: Chapter 1.

units.la: Capitis dua sunt partes, praeter inscriptionem Epistolae. In prima per modum gratiarum actionis de ipsorum conversione ad fidem, commendat veritatem doctrinae Euangelii, seu gratiae in qua stabant, & excellentiam conditionis ad quam evecti sunt per fidem, ut sic eos in fide confirmaret, ad versl 13. In secunda ex commemoratione spiritualium beneficiorum in Hebraeos fideles collatorum, deducit hortationem ad studium pietatis in genere, & φιλαδελφίαν in specie.
units.tr: The chapter has two parts, apart from the inscription of the letter. In the first, by way of thanksgiving for their conversion to the faith, he commends the truth of the doctrine of the Gospel, or the grace in which they stood, and the excellence of the condition to which they have been raised through faith, so as to confirm them in the faith, up to verse 13. In the second, from the recollection of the spiritual benefits bestowed upon the faithful Hebrews, he draws an exhortation to the pursuit of piety in general and to brotherly love [φιλαδελφίαν] in particular.

units.la: Verf. 1. Petrus Apostolus Iesu Christi, advenis dispersis per Pontum, Galatiam, Cappadociam, Asiam & Bithyniam:
units.tr: Verse 1. Peter, an apostle of Jesus Christ, to the strangers scattered throughout Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia and Bithynia:

units.la: Verf. 2. Dilectis ex praenotione Dei Patris ad sanctificationem Spiritus per obedientiam & aspersionem sanguinis Iesu Christi; gratia vobis & pax multiplicetur.
units.tr: Verse 2. Elect according to the foreknowledge of God the Father, through the sanctification of the Spirit, unto obedience and the sprinkling of the blood of Jesus Christ: grace and peace be multiplied unto you.

units.la: In inscriptione primo describitur Petrus scriptor Epistolae, ab officio Apostolatus, ut Epistolae huic sua constaret auctoritas: Deinde describuntur Hebraei ad quos scribitur, Primo ab externa conditione humili, quod peregrini fuerint dispersi per regiones nominatas, non exclusis reliquis qui alibi degebant. Secundo, ab interno (spirituali & excellenti) statu, quod nimirum fuerint electi, praecogniti, sanctificati, participes obedientiae, & aspersionis sanguinis Iesu Christi. Nam eligi per sanctificationem Spiritus ad obedientiam, & aspersionem Iesu Christi, est eligi ut per viam sanctificationis perveniamus ad plenam participationem fructuum obedientiae Christi, & aspersionis sanguinis eius, seu imputatae robis justitiae Christi, Patri suo pro nobis obedientis facti, usque ad mortem crucis: Atque ita excellentis conditionis fidelium Hebraeorum, seu status nostri spiritualis, causae ponuntur quatuor: Prima est electio Dei Patris, complectens et electionem illam aeternam, qua Deus ab aeterno illos prae aliis segregatos voluit ad salutem obtinendam in Christo: & illam temporalem, qua per efficacem vocationem Deus nem Deus actu illos segregavit ab aliis. Altera causa est Prænotio Dei, per quam intelligit actum Divinæ prædilectionis, quo in se statuit, seu voluit ex mero suo beneplacito omnibus suis ovibus, & illis nominatim, benefacere. Causa tertia est sanctificatio Spiritus, per quam intelligitur totus progressus commutationis spiritualis status nostri à conversionis initio ad perfectam usque sanctitatem, & gloriam. Quarta causa est obedientia Christi, & afflictio languinis ipsius: per quas intelligitur justitia Christi activa & passiva (ut nonnulli distinguunt) imò totum opus Redemptionis una cum ejus applicatione ad justificationem ipsorum & reconciliationem erga Deum: quæ causæ salutis illustrantur, nominando tres personas Divinas, quibus distinctè quidem, sed absque divisione, seu separatione personarum, causæ illæ ascribuntur eo ordine, quo personarum distinctionem, gratiam, virtutem, & operandi ordinem pollemus facillime percipere: Nam Deo Patri ascribitur Præunotio & Electio, ut fonti felicitatis nostræ. Christo, Reconciliatio ut Mediatori promerenti, & mercanti felicitatem illam: & Spiritui Sancto, ut executori applicanti eam nobis. Atque ita justitiæ & salutis nostræ causæ, Scaturigo, Impetratio, & Applicato in solidum ponuntur in solo beneplacito unius Dei, ex gratia mera nos eligentis. Unde fluit efficax vocatio nostri, & vera sanctificatio, ut certus fructus electionis: Medium vero illud unicum quo electionis vis & efficacia ad sanctificationem & salutem nostram derivatur ad nos, ponitur mediatio Christi, seu reconciliatio nostri facta in Christo. In benedictione seu voto salutatorio optat incrementum, & multiplicationem effectorum Divini favoris erga eos in omnibus, quæ ipsorum sanctificationem & salutem complere possent.
units.tr: In the inscription, first Peter, the writer of the letter, is described from his office of apostleship, so that his authority might stand behind this letter. Then the Hebrews to whom it is written are described: first from their external humble condition, that they were strangers scattered through the named regions, not excluding the others who lived elsewhere; second, from their internal (spiritual and excellent) state, namely that they were chosen, foreknown, sanctified, and partakers of the obedience and sprinkling of the blood of Jesus Christ. For to be chosen through the sanctification of the Spirit unto obedience and the sprinkling of Jesus Christ is to be chosen so that, by the way of sanctification, we may come to full participation in the fruits of Christ's obedience and of the sprinkling of his blood, that is, in the righteousness of Christ imputed to us, who was made obedient to his Father for us, even unto the death of the cross. And so four causes of the excellent condition of the faithful Hebrews, or of our spiritual state, are set down. The first is the election of God the Father, embracing both that eternal election by which God from eternity willed to set those people apart from others to obtain salvation in Christ, and that temporal election by which God, through effectual calling, actually separated them from others. The second cause is the foreknowledge of God, by which we understand the act of divine favour by which he resolved, or willed of his mere good pleasure, to do good to all his sheep, and to these by name. The third cause is the sanctification of the Spirit, by which is understood the whole progress of the change of our spiritual state, from the beginning of conversion to perfect holiness and glory. The fourth cause is the obedience of Christ and the shedding of his blood, by which is understood the active and passive righteousness of Christ (as some distinguish them), indeed the whole work of redemption together with its application to their justification and reconciliation with God. These causes of salvation are illustrated by naming the three divine persons, to whom the causes are ascribed distinctly, yet without division or separation of the persons, in the order by which we can most easily perceive the distinction of the persons, the grace, the power, and the order of operation. For foreknowledge and election are ascribed to God the Father, as the fountain of our happiness; reconciliation to Christ, as the Mediator who merited and procured that happiness; and the Holy Spirit is the executor who applies it to us. And so the causes of our righteousness and salvation, the fountain, the procuring, and the application, are set wholly in the sole good pleasure of the one God, who chooses us from mere grace. From this flows our effectual calling and true sanctification, as the certain fruit of election. But the one middle means by which the force and efficacy of election is conveyed to us for our sanctification and salvation is set down as the mediation of Christ, or our reconciliation made in Christ. In the salutation, or wish of blessing, he prays for the increase and multiplication of the effects of divine favour towards them in all things that could complete their sanctification and salvation.

units.la: Vers. 3. Benedictus Deus & Pater, Domini nostri Iesu Christi, qui ex multa sua misericordia regenuit nos in spem vivam, per resurrectionem Iesu Christi ex mortuis.
units.tr: Verse 3. Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who according to his abundant mercy hath begotten us again unto a lively hope by the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead.

units.la: Prima pars Capitis, in qua ut confirmet eos in fide & gratia Christi in qua stabant, gratias agit Deo ut Patri Iesu Christi, pro spiritualibus beneficiis concessis in Christo, illis in hoc statu gratiæ collocatis. Rationes gratiarum actionis, & simul fidei confirmationis sunt sedecim, quæ omnes probant debere eos Deo benedicere, & in fide confirmari.
units.tr: The first part of the chapter, in which, in order to confirm them in the faith and grace of Christ in which they stood, he gives thanks to God as the Father of Jesus Christ for the spiritual benefits granted in Christ, placing them in this state of grace. The reasons for the thanksgiving, and at the same time for the confirmation of their faith, are sixteen, all of which prove that they ought to bless God and be confirmed in the faith.

units.la: Nos] Ratio prima, Deus non minus vos quam reliquos Sanctos, imò non minus quam ipsos etiam Apostolos, regeneravit. Ergo debetis Deo benedicere, & in fide corroborari. Ratio 2. Regeneravit vos ut Deus, & Pater Domini nostri Iesu Christi, id est, regenerando ascivit vos in societatem foederis Christi, & in societatem filiationis Christi per adoptionem recepit. Ergo debetis, &c.
units.tr: "Us." First reason: God regenerated you no less than the rest of the saints, indeed no less than the apostles themselves. Therefore you ought to bless God and be strengthened in the faith. Second reason: he regenerated you as the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, that is, by regenerating he admitted you into the fellowship of Christ's covenant, and received you by adoption into the sonship of Christ. Therefore you ought, etc.

units.la: Ratio 3. Ex multa sua misericordia regeneravit vos, id est, non modo nullis meritis inductus, sed etiam nulla vestra indignitate, nullis malis vestris meritis impeditus, regenerationis beneficium vobis concessit. Ergo debetis Deo benedicere, & in fide corroborari.
units.tr: Third reason: he regenerated you out of his abundant mercy, that is, moved not only by no merits of yours, but also with no unworthiness of yours hindering him, with none of your evil deserts standing in the way, he granted you the benefit of regeneration. Therefore you ought to bless God and be strengthened in the faith.

units.la: Ratio 4. Deus ad vitae aeternae spem certam, vivificam, operibus vitae spiritualis se exerentem regeneravit vos. Ergo, &c.
units.tr: Fourth reason: God regenerated you to a certain and living hope of eternal life, showing itself in the works of spiritual life. Therefore, etc.

units.la: Ratio 5. Deus vestrae spei vivacem certitudinem fundavit solide in Christi resurrectione ex mortuis, quae est & causa & pignus vestrae resurrectionis ex mortuis. Ergo debetis, &c.
units.tr: Fifth reason: God firmly founded the living certainty of your hope in the resurrection of Christ from the dead, which is both the cause and the pledge of your resurrection from the dead. Therefore you ought, etc.

units.la: Verf. 4. In haereditatem quae nec perire potest, nec contaminari, nec marcescere, nobis in Coelis servatam.
units.tr: Verse 4. Unto an inheritance incorruptible, and undefiled, and that fadeth not away, reserved in heaven for you.

units.la: Ratio 6. Deus regeneravit vos ad vitam aeternam, quae gratis vobis concedenda est, ex testamento Patris vestri, ut haereditas nullis vestris meritis parta, & quae non terrena, sed coelestis, incorruptibilis, incontaminabilis, immarcescibilis est, omnes possessiones mundanas, & ipsam etiam conditionem vitae quam habuit Adam innocens, antecellens: utpote quae nulli mutationi obnoxia est, & cui nihil ad summam perfectionem deest. Ergo debetis Deo benedicere, & in fide corroborari.
units.tr: Sixth reason: God regenerated you to eternal life, which is to be freely bestowed upon you by the testament of your Father, as an inheritance obtained by none of your merits, and which is not earthly but heavenly, incorruptible, undefiled, and unfading; it surpasses all worldly possessions, and even the very condition of life which Adam had in innocence, since it is subject to no change and lacks nothing of the highest perfection. Therefore you ought to bless God and be strengthened in the faith.

units.la: Verf. 5 Qui virtute Dei custodimur per fidem, ad salutem quae parata est patefieri tempore ultimo.
units.tr: Verse 5. Who are kept by the power of God through faith unto salvation ready to be revealed in the last time.

units.la: Ratio 7. Deus regenitos perseverantia donavit, donumque stabilivit, tanquam praesidio armato vos custodiens ad salutem, & fidem vestram sustinens, ne deficiatis a via salutis, idque firmissimo decreto suo, quo & salutem istam vobis praeparavit, & certum etiam tempus constituit ad eam communicandam, nempe diem judicii. Ergo debetis Deo benedicere, & in fide corroborari.
units.tr: Seventh reason: God endowed the regenerate with perseverance, and established that gift, keeping you as an armed garrison unto salvation, and sustaining your faith, lest you fall away from the way of salvation; and this by his most firm decree, by which he has prepared that salvation for you, and has also appointed a certain time for its communication, namely the day of judgment. Therefore you ought to bless God and be strengthened in the faith.

units.la: Verf. 6. Qua in re exultatis, tristitia paululum nunc (si opus est) in variis tentationibus affecti:
units.tr: Verse 6. Wherein ye greatly rejoice, though now for a season, if need be, ye are in heaviness through manifold temptations:

units.la: Verf. 7. Ut exploratio fidei vestrae multo pretiosior auri, quod perit, & tamen per ignem exploratur, comperiatur vobis esse Laudi & Gloriæ & Honoris, quum patefiet IESVS CHRISTVS,
units.tr: Verse 7. That the trial of your faith, being much more precious than of gold that perisheth, though it be tried with fire, might be found unto praise and honour and glory at the appearing of Jesus Christ:

units.la: Ratio 8. Conditio fidei & gratiæ Christi in qua statis, solida est vobis materia gaudii & exultationis.
units.tr: Eighth reason: the condition of faith and of the grace of Christ in which you stand is a solid matter for your joy and exultation.

units.la: Ratio 9. Gratia in qua statis vobis ministrat gaudium, etiam cum variis afflictionibus agitati, aliquando ad tristitiam gravamini, solida consolationis argumenta suppeditans vobis: qualia sunt haec quatuor; 1. Brevitas afflictionum: 2. Intermissio afflictionum: 3. Et necessitas earum, Nam Tristitia effecti ejus ad exiguum tempus, nunc fi oportet. 4. Utilitas afflictionum, quæ est exploratio & purgatio fidei ut purior evadat, tanquam aurum probatum ad laudem, honorem, & gloriam vestram, quibus Christus vos omnes probatæ fidei sanctos, in adventu suo ornabit. Ergo debetis, &c.
units.tr: Ninth reason: the grace in which you stand supplies you with joy even when you are troubled by various afflictions, sometimes grievous to sadness, furnishing you with solid grounds of consolation, such as these four: (1) the brevity of afflictions; (2) the intermission of afflictions; (3) their necessity, for the sadness is for a little time, "now if need be"; (4) the usefulness of afflictions, which is the trial and purging of faith, that it may come forth purer, like gold proved, to your praise, honour and glory, with which Christ at his coming will adorn all of you who are saints of proven faith. Therefore you ought, etc.

units.la: Verl. 8. Quem quum non videritis, diligitis: quem quum nunc non cernatis, ei tamen credentes, exultatis gaudio & ineffabili & glorioso:
units.tr: Verse 8. Whom, though you have not seen, you love; though you do not now see him, yet believing in him, you rejoice with joy that is unspeakable and full of glory.

units.la: Ratio 10. Gratia in qua statis supra sensum tollit vestros animos, ad spiritualem contemplationem, & dilectionem Christi suavissimam: Ergo. Ratio 11. Etiamsi nec prius videritis Christum, nec jam cernatis, fides tamen in qua statis, efficit ut exultetis gaudio ineffabili & glorioso, quod superat omnem explicationem verborum nostrorum, & captum etiam nostrum, & de quo si jam gloriamini, posteà vos nunquam pudebit. Ergo.
units.tr: Reason 10. The grace in which you stand lifts your minds above the senses, to spiritual contemplation and to the most sweet love of Christ. Therefore... Reason 11. Even though you have neither seen Christ before nor see him now, the faith in which you stand makes you rejoice with joy unspeakable and full of glory, which surpasses all the explanation of our words and even our understanding. If you already glory in it, you will never be ashamed of it afterwards. Therefore...

units.la: Verl. 9. Reportantes mercedem fidei vestræ salutem animarum.
units.tr: Verse 9. Receiving as the reward of your faith the salvation of your souls.

units.la: Ratio 12. confirmans priorem, Per fidem in quâ statis, etiam in hac vitâ percipitis fructum, mercedem, & finem fidei veltræ, inchoatam ic licet felicitatem animarum veltrarum, in mediis corporum vestrorum afflictionibus. Ergo debetis, &c.
units.tr: Reason 12, confirming the previous one. Through the faith in which you stand, you already receive in this life the fruit, the reward and the end of your faith, namely the beginning of the happiness of your souls, even amid the afflictions of your bodies. Therefore you ought to...

units.la: Verl. 10. De qua salute inquisierunt, & quam scrutati sunt Prophetæ, qui venturam in vos gratiam prædixerunt:
units.tr: Verse 10. Concerning this salvation the prophets inquired and searched diligently, those who foretold the grace that would come to you.

units.la: Ratio 13. à Testimonio prophetarum, Hæc gratia in qua statis, est illa ipsa salus de qua Prophetæ omnes olim prophetarunt, nostris his temporibus ventura. Ergo debetis, &c.
units.tr: Reason 13, from the testimony of the prophets. This grace in which you stand is that very salvation of which all the prophets prophesied long ago, which was to come in our times. Therefore you ought to...

units.la: Verl. 11. Scrutantes in quem aut cujusmodi temporis articulum prænuntius ille qui in ipsis erat Spiritus Christi, declararet eventuras Christo perpessiones, & gloriam illas consequuturam.
units.tr: Verse 11. Searching what, or what manner of time, the Spirit of Christ that was in them, when it testified beforehand, signified would come, the sufferings of Christ, and the glory that would follow them.

units.la: Confirmat certitudinem hujus testimonii, ex his quatuor, Primum, Quod non solum Prophetæ prædixerint de salute hac ventura, sed etiam in hanc gratiam & salutem diligentissimè inquisiverint, eamque scrutati sunt, ut prædicerent nobis: Secundum, Quod non solum scrutati sint de gratia Euangelii revelanda, sed etiam de articulo temporis, quo esset revelanda. Tertium, Quod non pependerint ex incertis conjecturis in hoc scrutinio, sed Spiritum Christi, omnium rerum præscium & prænuntium, (qui in ipsis fuit modo extraordinario præsens) consuluerint. Quartum, Quia doctrina salutis Prophetarum temporibus & nostris eadem fuit, & summatim comprehenditur humiliatione seu perpessionibus Christi: & exaltatione seu gloriâ consequuturâ in effectis perpessionum Christi: Ergo debetis hoc nomine Deo benedicere, & in sanctâ fide vestrâ corroborari.
units.tr: He confirms the certainty of this testimony from four points. First, the prophets not only foretold this coming salvation, but also inquired most diligently into this grace and salvation and searched into it, so that they might proclaim it to us. Second, they searched not only into the gospel grace to be revealed, but also into the time of its revelation. Third, they did not rely on uncertain conjectures in this search, but consulted the Spirit of Christ, who knows and foretells all things (and who was present in them in an extraordinary way). Fourth, the saving doctrine of the prophets was the same in their times as in ours, and it is summed up briefly in the humiliation, or sufferings, of Christ, and in the exaltation, or the glory to follow, as the outcome of Christ's sufferings. Therefore you ought to bless God for this and be strengthened in your holy faith.

units.la: Vers. 12 Quibus patefactum est eos non sibi sed nobis ea administrare, quæ nunc annunciata sunt vobis per eos qui vobis prædicarunt Euangelium per emissum è Cælo Spiritum sanctum, in quæ desiderant angeli introspicere.
units.tr: Verse 12. To whom it was revealed that they did not minister these things to themselves but to you, which now have been announced to you through those who preached the gospel to you by the Holy Spirit sent down from heaven, things into which the angels desire to look.

units.la: Ipsum testimonium proponitur in responsione Spiritus: quæ responsio exhibet Rationem 14, à Prærogativâ Fidelium post Christum exhibitum supra sortem Prophetarum, quibus patefactum est, Quod etiamsi fructum fidei nobilcum essent percepturi, complementum tamen & finem Prophetiarum suarum non essent ipsi visuri, sed nos qui post Christum exhibitum nati sumus; quibus Prophetiæ pronunciatæ sunt in eum finem, ut conferentes prædicationem cum complemento, confirmaremur in fide. Ergo debetis Deo benedicere, & in fide corroborari.
units.tr: The testimony itself is set forth in the response of the Spirit. This response gives Reason 14, from the privilege of believers after Christ was manifested, above the lot of the prophets, to whom it was revealed that, although they would receive the fruit of faith along with you, they would not themselves see the completion and end of their prophecies, but we, who were born after Christ was manifested, would see them; to us the prophecies were uttered for this end, that by comparing the preaching with its fulfilment we might be confirmed in faith. Therefore you ought to bless God and be strengthened in faith.

units.la: Per eos Ratio 15. Quæ Prophetæ prophetabant per prænuncium Christi Spiritum in ipsis loquentem, Apostoli enunciarunt vobis per emissum è Cælo Spiritum Sanctum. Ergo certi esse poteritis quod hæc sit vera gratia in qua statis, eoque nomine Deo debetis benedicere.
units.tr: Through them Reason 15. What the prophets prophesied through the Spirit of Christ speaking in them, the apostles have declared to you through the Holy Spirit sent down from heaven. Therefore you can be sure that this is the true grace in which you stand, and for this you ought to bless God.

units.la: Angeli Ratio 16. Fidei & gratiæ in qua statis tanta est præstantia, ut Angeli etiam ipsi cœlestes in eam cupiant introspicere; partim ut in eam porro inquirant, partim ut in eâ perspectâ le magis oblectent admirantes gloriam Dei in gratiâ fidelibus datâ. Ergo in fide corroborari debetis & Deo benedicere: Hic autem alludit ad typum duorum Cherubim, qui arcæ fœderis insistentes, facies suas versus operculum illius convertebant vertebant, tanquam introspicere desiderantes. Quo praeter alia significabatur dignum esse Mysterium Incarnationis Filii Dei & Redemptionis hominum, in quo contemplando cum admiratione occupari possunt ipsi Angeli.
units.tr: Angels Reason 16. The faith and grace in which you stand is of such excellence that even the heavenly angels desire to look into it: partly to search further into it, and partly so that, having looked into it, they may take greater delight, wondering at the glory of God in the grace given to believers. Therefore you ought to be strengthened in faith and bless God. Here he alludes to the type of the two cherubim, who stood upon the ark of the covenant and turned their faces toward its lid, as though desiring to look into it. This signified, among other things, that the mystery of the incarnation of the Son of God and the redemption of mankind is worthy to occupy the angels themselves in contemplating it with wonder.

units.la: Secunda pars Capitis,
units.tr: The second part of the chapter,

units.la: Verf. 13. Quapropter succincti lumbis mentis vestrae, sobrii, integre sperate in eam quae ad vos defertur gratiam in patefactione Iesu Christi.
units.tr: Verse 13. Therefore, girding up the loins of your mind, be sober, and hope perfectly for the grace that is brought to you at the revelation of Jesus Christ.

units.la: Altera pars Capitis, In qua ex commemoratione Spiritualium beneficiorum, & demonstratione veritatis gratiae in qua stabant, deducit hortationem ad studium pietatis, & ad pergendum in gratia Dei. Hortationis membra sunt tria: Primum, ut sicut illi qui vel iter facturi, vel operis aliquid aggrediri sunt, quo expeditiores sint, lumbos succingunt: Ita illi succingant lumbos mentis, id est, refrenent ac restringant mentes suas ab omni cupiditate, qua impediri possent, ne expedite & libere Deo servirent: Membrum 2. Ut sint sobrii, non solum caventes intemperantiam cibi & potus, sed etiam omnem immoderatum rerum delectabilum usum: Membrum 3. Ut firmiter & constanter sperent, & expectent illam gratiam, quae jam revelatur, & porro plene revelabitur in adventu Christi. In qua hortatione totus fidei & sanctitatis cursus comprehenditur. Argumenta hortationis sunt tredecim, quae omnia probant in pietate & fide doctrinae de gratia pergendum esse.
units.tr: The second part of the chapter. From the recollection of spiritual benefits, and from the demonstration of the truth of the grace in which they stood, he draws an exhortation to the pursuit of godliness and to persevering in the grace of God. The members of the exhortation are three. First, that just as those who are about to travel, or to undertake some work, gird up their loins so as to be more free in their movements, so they should gird up the loins of their mind, that is, restrain and bind their minds from every desire by which they might be hindered from serving God freely and unencumbered. Second, that they should be sober, not only avoiding intemperance in food and drink, but also every immoderate use of pleasant things. Third, that they should hope and wait firmly and steadfastly for that grace which is now revealed and will be fully revealed at the coming of Christ. In this exhortation the whole course of faith and holiness is comprehended. There are thirteen arguments for the exhortation, all of which prove that one must persevere in godliness and in faith in the doctrine of grace.

units.la: Quapropter Argumentum primum, Ex connexione hortationis cum praecedente doctrina, expressa in voce quapropter. Ex consideratione gratiae in qua statis & beneficiorum spiritualium per fidem Christi concessorum vobis, excitari debetis ad omne studium pietatis. Ergo in pietate & gratia in qua statis constanti professione pergendum est.
units.tr: Therefore The first argument, from the connection of the exhortation with the preceding doctrine, expressed in the word therefore. From the consideration of the grace in which you stand, and of the spiritual benefits granted to you through faith in Christ, you ought to be roused to every effort after godliness. Therefore one must persevere in godliness and in the grace in which you stand, by a steadfast profession.

units.la: Revelabitur Arg. 2 Gratia jam manifestata, & quae tandem plene manifestanda est in appropinquante Christi adventu, vos excitare debet ad pietatem colendam & Dei gratiam retinendam. Ergo, &c.
units.tr: Will be revealed Argument 2. The grace already manifested, and which is finally to be fully manifested at the approaching coming of Christ, ought to stir you up to cultivate godliness and to hold fast the grace of God. Therefore, etc.

units.la: Verf. 14. Ut filii obedientes, qui vos non conformetis prioribus quae in ignorantia vestra viguerunt cupiditatibus:
units.tr: Verse 14. As obedient children, not conforming yourselves to the former desires you had in your ignorance:

units.la: Arg. 3. Jure adoptionis ut filii obedientes, pietatis studium & gratiae professionem prosequi tenemini. Ergo.
units.tr: Argument 3. By the right of adoption, as obedient children, you are bound to pursue the study of godliness and the profession of grace. Therefore.

units.la: Non configuretis Arg 4. Cum filiorum obedientia consistere non poteat, ut test, ut pristinis cupiditatibus, quæ in vobis ante conversionem regnabant, vos conformetis: Ergo pietati & Dei gratiæ retinendæ oportet studere.
units.tr: Do not conform Argument 4. Since obedience of children cannot stand with conforming oneself to the former desires that reigned in you before your conversion, one ought to study godliness and holding fast to the grace of God. Therefore.

units.la: Vers. 15. Sed sicut is qui vos vocavit sanctus est, ipsi queque sancti in omni conversatione reddamini.
units.tr: Verse 15. But as he who called you is holy, so be you also holy in all your conduct.

units.la: Vers. 16. Propterea scriptum est sancti estote: nam ego sanctus sum.
units.tr: Verse 16. For it is written: Be holy, for I am holy.

units.la: Arg. 5. Sanctæ vocationi respondere debetis in omnis generis conversatione sanctâ: Pergendum ergo.
units.tr: Argument 5. You ought to answer to your holy calling with holy conduct in every kind of life. Therefore one must persevere.

units.la: Sicut ] Arg. 6. confirmans superius, Similitudinem in sanctitate intercedere decet inter vos, & Deum sanctum qui vos vocavit. Conformitati ergo huic studendum est. Hoc argumentum confirmat testimonio Scripturæ, Levit. 11. 44. Math 5. 17.
units.tr: As Argument 6, confirming what was said above: it is fitting that there should be a likeness in holiness between you and the holy God who called you. Therefore one must strive after this conformity. He confirms this argument with the testimony of Scripture, Lev. 11. 44; Matt. 5. 17.

units.la: Vers. 17. Itaque si patrem cognominatis eum qui citra personarum respectum judicat ex cujusque opere, cum timore versamini commorationis vestræ tempore:
units.tr: Verse 17. And if you call on him as Father, who without respect of persons judges according to each one's work, pass the time of your sojourning in fear:

units.la: Arg. 7. Deus est judex operum uniuscujusque, & severius exigit sanctitatem ab iis qui appropinquant ad eum, & cognominant ipsum Patrem suum. Ergo in Dei timore transigendum est tempus commorationis vestræ in hac vita. Verf. 18 Ut qui sciatis vos non caducis rebus, argento vel auro, fuisse redemptos ex vana vestra conversatione, ex patrum traditionibus acceptâ:
units.tr: Argument 7. God is the judge of every one's works, and he requires holiness more strictly from those who draw near to him and call him their Father. Therefore the time of your sojourning in this life must be spent in the fear of God. Verse 18. Knowing that you were redeemed not with corruptible things, silver or gold, from your vain conduct received by tradition from your fathers:

units.la: Arg. 8. Redempti estis ab omni vana conversatione in legalibus purificationibus illis à re significata separatis, & in traditionibus humanis positâ, quæ nullius est pretii, quamvis Patrum nostrorum exemplo, & traditione vobis commendetur: Ergo nisi redemptionem frustraneam reddere velletis, pietati veræ studendum, & vanæ conversationi renunciandum vobis est.
units.tr: Argument 8. You have been redeemed from every vain conduct, from those legal purifications separated from the thing signified, and consisting in human traditions, which are of no worth, though they are commended to you by the example and tradition of our fathers. Therefore, unless you wish to render your redemption fruitless, you must pursue true godliness and renounce vain conduct.

units.la: Redempti ] Arg. 9. Per redemptionem emptitii servi Dei estis, ut non ex vestra vel mundi, vel diaboli voluntate amplius vivatis, sed ex arbitrio redemptoris: Ergo in fide & obedientia Christi vivendum est.
units.tr: Redempti] Argument 9. You are bought servants of God through redemption, so that you no longer live by your own will, or the will of the world or the devil, but by the decision of your Redeemer. Therefore we must live in the faith and obedience of Christ.

units.la: Verf. 19. Sed pretiosò sanguine, utpote agni immaculati & incontaminati, nempe Christi:
units.tr: Verse 19. But with precious blood, as of a lamb unblemished and undefiled, namely of Christ:

units.la: Arg. 10. Sanguis morientis Christi filii Dei, per agnum typicum repræsentati, tantæ est præstantiæ, ut pretiosissima, quæque in hoc mundo longè do longe superet: Ergo in Gratia CHRISTI standum, & sanctitati studendum est, nisi vellētis hoc pretium vilipendere.
units.tr: Argument 10. The blood of Christ, the Son of God, dying and represented by the typical lamb, is of such excellence that it far surpasses all the most precious things in this world. Therefore we must stand in the grace of Christ and strive for holiness, unless you wish to hold this price in contempt.

units.la: Verf. 20. Prædestinati quidem ante jacta mundi fundamenta, patefacti verò ultimis temporibus propter vos,
units.tr: Verse 20. Indeed foreordained before the foundation of the world, but made manifest in the last times for your sake,

units.la: Arg. 11. Quamvis CHRISTUS ab æterno præordinatus fuerit ad opus redemptionis, non tamen nisi ultimis his temporibus manifestatus est, idque præcipuè vestrâ causâ, qui veluti perditæ oves Israelis estis. Ergo vos maximè tenemini per Sanctitatis studium DEUM glorificare.
units.tr: Argument 11. Although Christ was foreordained from eternity for the work of redemption, he was not made manifest until these last times, and that chiefly for your sake, who are as the lost sheep of Israel. Therefore you above all are bound to glorify God through the pursuit of holiness.

units.la: Verf. 21. Qui per eum creditis DEO, qui excitavit eum à mortuis, & gloriam ei dedit, ut fides ac spes vestra in Deo esset.
units.tr: Verse 21. You who through him believe in God, who raised him from the dead and gave him glory, so that your faith and hope might be in God.

units.la: Arg. 12. Non tantum in bonum vestrum, qui fideles estis, manifestatus est CHRISTUS, sed etiam per CHRISTUM, seu CHRISTI meritum, & operationem, fides ipsa quâ creditis in DEUM impetrata, & producta est in vobis. Ergo æquum est ut Deo in sanctitate vivatis.
units.tr: Argument 12. Christ was manifested not only for your good, who are faithful, but also through Christ, or the merit and working of Christ, the faith itself by which you believe in God was obtained and produced in you. Therefore it is fitting that you live in holiness before God.

units.la: Suscitavit ] Deus suscitando CHRISTUM Redemptorem à mortuis, & glorificando eum eâ gloriâ quam habebat apud DEUM, ab æterno, demonstravit vobis & toti mundo CHRISTUM verè Filium DEI, seu verè DEUM esse. Ut fides vestra quâ creditis in CHRISTUM, comperiretur esse fides in Deum; atque ita soliditas vestræ fidei innotescERET vobis, in vestram majorem consolationem & gloriam. Ergo vos fideles Hebræi, qui polt CHRISTUM relucitatum vivitis: Tenemini tanto magis in fidei & sanctitatis studio, ut DEO placeatis studere.
units.tr: Raised] By God raising Christ the Redeemer from the dead, and glorifying him with that glory which he had with God from eternity, he showed you and the whole world that Christ is truly the Son of God, that is, truly God. So that your faith, by which you believe in Christ, might be found to be faith in God; and thus the steadfastness of your faith might be made known to you, to your greater comfort and glory. Therefore you faithful Hebrews, who live after Christ has risen again, are bound all the more to strive in the pursuit of faith and holiness, so as to be pleasing to God.

units.la: Verf. 22. Animabus vestris purificatis, auscultando veritati per Spiritum, cum charitate fraterna, simulationis experte ex puro corde alii alios diligite impense.
units.tr: Verse 22. Having purified your souls by obeying the truth through the Spirit, unto unfeigned brotherly love, love one another earnestly from a pure heart.

units.la: Secunda hortatio specialior ad charitatem fraternam inter se colendam, ut se mutuo diligant. Hujus hortationis membra sunt tria. Membrum primum, ut impense diligant non frigidè, non remisse, quasi parati essent, etiam exiguam ob causam odisse: 2. Ut puro corde diligant, alii aliorum bono studentes, non privatis commodis tantum inhiantes. 3. Ut sine hypocrisi φιλαδελφίας sequantur, diligentes non verbo & lingua tantum, sed opere dilectionem ostendentes, sine fuco, sine dolo.
units.tr: A second, more specific exhortation to cultivate brotherly love among themselves, that they should love one another. This exhortation has three parts. The first part: that they love earnestly, not coldly or half-heartedly, as if they were ready to hate even for a slight cause. Second: that they love with a pure heart, each seeking the good of the others, not merely aiming at private advantage. Third: that they follow brotherly love without hypocrisy, showing their love not only in word and tongue but in deed, without pretence and without guile.

units.la: Animas ] Argumenta hortationis sunt tria. Arg. 1. Præsupponendum est quod justificati per fidem, voto, proposito, & inchoato studio, per SPIRITUS Sancti virtutem, purificaveritis animas vestras ad sinceram fratrum dilectionem, in obedientia doctrinæ Euangelii. Ergo diligere alii alios debetis impensè.
units.tr: Souls] There are three arguments for the exhortation. Argument 1: It must be presupposed that you, justified through faith, by vow, purpose and an inchoate endeavour, through the power of the Spirit of God, have purified your souls to sincere love of the brethren, in obedience to the doctrine of the Gospel. Therefore you ought to love one another earnestly.

units.la: Verf. 23. Renati non ex semine corruptibili, sed ex incorruptibili, per sermonem Dei vivi, & manentis in æternum.
units.tr: Verse 23. Born again not of corruptible seed, but of incorruptible, through the word of the living God, which abides for ever.

units.la: Arg. 2. Fraternitas hæc Fidelium præstantior est carnali illa, utpote quæ non ex naturali generatione, sed ex spirituali regeneratione orta sit, quæque dilectionem mutuam firmiorem & præstantiorem requirit: Ergo alii alios impensè diligere debetis.
units.tr: Argument 2: This brotherhood of believers is more excellent than that carnal one, inasmuch as it arises not from natural generation but from spiritual regeneration, and it requires a mutual love that is firmer and more excellent. Therefore you ought to love one another earnestly.

units.la: Sermonem ] Arg. 3: confirmans superius, Fraternitas hæc Fidelium, sicut oritur ab incorruptibili principio, ita nunquam interitura est. Siquidem sermo Dei qui semen est regenerationis nostræ, non est corruptibilis instar seminis naturalis generationis. Ergo impensè & constanter alii alios diligere debetis.
units.tr: The word] Argument 3, confirming what was said above: this brotherhood of believers, as it arises from an incorruptible principle, so it will never perish. For the word of God, which is the seed of our regeneration, is not corruptible like the seed of natural generation. Therefore you ought to love one another earnestly and constantly.

units.la: Verf. 24. Nam omnis caro est ut gramen, & omnis gloria hominis ut flos graminis: exaruit gramen, & flos ejus decidit.
units.tr: Verse 24. For all flesh is as grass, and all the glory of man as the flower of grass: the grass withers, and its flower falls.

units.la: Utramque partem comparationis confirmat testimonio Scripturæ; & primò corruptibilitatem seminis naturalis probat, ex Isa. 40. 6. qui pronunciat gloriam omnis carnis, & per consequens omnem relationem fraternitatis in carne fundatam, esse in genere corruptibilium.
units.tr: He confirms each part of the comparison by a testimony of Scripture; and first he proves the corruptibility of natural seed from Isaiah 40:6, which declares that the glory of all flesh, and consequently every relationship of brotherhood founded in the flesh, belongs to the class of corruptible things.

units.la: Verf. 25. Sed verbum Domini manet in æternum: hoc autem est verbum illud quod euangelizatum est vobis.
units.tr: Verse 25. But the word of the Lord abides for ever: and this is the word which was preached to you as the gospel.

units.la: Quod semen regenerationis sit incorruptibile, probat ejusdem Isaiæ testimonio, Quia Verbum Domini manet in æternum. Hoc autem de Verbo Euangelii dictum esse affirmat, uti res est, quia prædicatio veritatis de salute per Christum fidelibus concedenda, efficax est ad vitam æternam fidelibus tribuendam & conservandam. Ergo est incorruptibile.
units.tr: That the seed of regeneration is incorruptible he proves by the same testimony of Isaiah, because the word of the Lord abides for ever. He affirms that this was said of the word of the Gospel, as the fact is, because the preaching of the truth about salvation through Christ, to be given to believers, is effective for bestowing and preserving eternal life for believers. Therefore it is incorruptible.

units.la: Caput Secundum.
units.tr: Chapter 2.

units.la: Ergit hortari ad officia pietatis & sanctitatis. Hortationes hoc Capite habentur quatuor.
units.tr: Next he exhorts them to the duties of piety and holiness. There are four exhortations in this chapter.

units.la: Verf. 1. Proinde deposita omni malitia, & omni dolo, & simulationibus & invidentiis, & omnibus obtrectationibus.
units.tr: Verse 1. Wherefore laying aside all malice, and all guile, and hypocrisies, and envies, and all evil speakings.

units.la: Hortatio prima est ad amorem & appetitionem Verbi Divini, quod nuper commendaverat. Hortationis membra sunt duo: Primum de cavendis & deponendis naturæ corruptæ familiaribus vitiis, quæ desiderium Verbi Divini possent vel extinguere, vel diminuere, qualia enumerat quinque, Quorum primum est malitia, quâ quis data opera nocet alteri: 2. Dolus, quo artificiosè quis proximum decipit in ipsius detrimentum: 3. Simulationes seu mendacia in facto, cum quis benevolentiam vultu præ se fert, quam non habet in animo: 4. Invidentia, quibus de aliorum bono dolemus: 5. Obtrectationes, quibus proximi fama læditur.
units.tr: The first exhortation urges love for, and desire after, the Word of God, which he had recently commended. It has two parts. The first concerns avoiding and putting away the familiar vices of corrupt nature, which could either extinguish or diminish the desire for the Word of God. He lists five: (1) malice, by which someone deliberately harms another; (2) guile, by which someone cunningly deceives a neighbour to his harm; (3) hypocrisies, or lies in deed, when someone shows goodwill in his face that he does not have in his heart; (4) envies, by which we grieve at another's good; (5) evil speakings, by which a neighbour's reputation is injured.

units.la: Vers. 2. Ut modo nati infantes, lac illud sermonis sincerum expetite, ut per illud adolescatis:
units.tr: Verse 2. As newborn babes, desire the sincere milk of the word, that ye may grow thereby.

units.la: Hortationis secundum membrum, Ut sanam Euangelii doctrinam cupidè imbibat, ut lac sincerum.
units.tr: The second part of the exhortation urges them to drink in eagerly the sound doctrine of the gospel, as sincere milk.

units.la: Argumenta hortationis sunt undecim. Argumentum primum, Sicut lac maternum est aptum nutrimentum alendis infantibus naturaliter genitis: Sic doctrina Euangelii est idoneum nutrimentum alendis spiritualiter regenitis. Ergo expetendum & imbibendum est.
units.tr: There are eleven arguments for the exhortation. The first argument: just as a mother's milk is the fitting nourishment for infants naturally born, so the doctrine of the gospel is the fitting nourishment for those spiritually born again. Therefore it is to be desired and drunk in.

units.la: Per illud Arg. 2. Sicut per lac infantes augescunt, sic per doctrinam Euangelii, & ampliorem cognitionem Verbi Divini fideles adolescere possunt, id est, magis ac magis in vitæ novitate progressus facere. Verbum ergo DEI vobis expetendum est.
units.tr: That ye may grow thereby. Second argument: just as infants grow by milk, so believers can grow up by the doctrine of the gospel and a fuller knowledge of the Word of God, that is, make ever greater progress in newness of life. Therefore the Word of God is to be desired by you.

units.la: Lac Arg. 3. Verbum DEI est quasi lac spirituale, rationale, sincerum, purum, & ab omni errore alienum, quod nemine decipere poterit, ad placendum animam accommodatissimum. Ergo Verbum DEI vobis expetendum est.
units.tr: Milk. Third argument: the Word of God is like spiritual milk, rational, sincere, pure, and free from all error, which can never deceive anyone, and most suited to nourish the soul. Therefore the Word of God is to be desired by you.

units.la: Vers. 3. Si quidem gustastis quod benignus sit Dominus.
units.tr: Verse 3. If so be ye have tasted that the Lord is gracious.

units.la: Arg. 4. Verbum DEI nihil continet præter bonitatem DEI, & Servatoris nostri IESU CHRISTI erga credentes, cujus dulcedinem qui gustarunt, non poterunt illud non expetere. Ergo si gustastis quod Deus sit bonus, expetendum vobis est DEI Verbum.
units.tr: Fourth argument: the Word of God contains nothing but the goodness of God and of our Saviour Jesus Christ towards believers, and those who have tasted its sweetness cannot fail to desire it. Therefore, if you have tasted that God is good, you ought to desire the Word of God.

units.la: Vers. 4. Ad quem accedentes, qui est lapis vivus, ab hominibus quidem reprobatus, apud Deum verò electus ac pretiosus.
units.tr: Verse 4. To whom coming, as unto a living stone, disallowed indeed of men, but chosen of God, and precious.

units.la: Arg. 5. Imbibentes sanam Euangelii doctrinam, ut lac sincerum, propius indies accedit ad CHRISTUM, & sanctam cum ipso communionem arctiorem consequimini. Ergo Verbum Euangelii expetendum vobis &
units.tr: Fifth argument: those who drink in the sound doctrine of the gospel, as sincere milk, draw nearer to Christ day by day and attain a closer holy communion with him. Therefore the word of the gospel is to be desired by you, and to be drunk in eagerly and

units.la: † & avidè & avide imbibendum est. Hoc argumentum variis similitudinibus illu‐strat, & in iis alia argumenta hortationis superaddit.
units.tr: † and eagerly drunk in. He illustrates this argument with various similes, and adds further arguments for the exhortation within them.

units.la: Imbibentibus vobis lac veritatis, & fecundum Dei verbum accedentibus vobis ad Christum, Christus prœstiturus est seipsum firmum, & vitale fundamentum salutis, summæ æstimationis & pretii apud Deum, (qui aliud fundamentum salutis non admittit) etiamsi reprobi homines eum contemnant & rejiciant. Ergo expetendum & imbibendum lac veritatis Euangelicæ.
units.tr: As you drink in the milk of truth, and according to the word of God draw near to Christ, Christ will show himself to you as a firm and living foundation of salvation, of the highest esteem and value before God (who admits no other foundation of salvation), even though reprobate men despise and reject him. Therefore the milk of evangelical truth is to be desired and drunk in.

units.la: Ipsi quoque velut vivi lapides, ædificemini domus spiritualis sacerdotium sanctum, ad offerendum spirituales hostias, acceptas Deo per Iesum Christum.
units.tr: Ye also, as lively stones, are built up a spiritual house, an holy priesthood, to offer up spiritual sacrifices, acceptable to God by Jesus Christ.

units.la: Accedentes secundum Euangelii sermonem, non tantùm comperturi estis Christum solidum fundamentum, sed etiam vos ipsi virtute Christi magis, magisque superaedificandi estis Christo, in unum corpus mysticum, cum reliquis fidelibus, ut sitis spiritualè templum in quo Deus habitet: Ergo lac verbi vobis expetendum est.
units.tr: By coming to Christ according to the word of the gospel, you will not only find Christ to be a solid foundation, but you yourselves, by the power of Christ, are to be built ever more and more upon Christ, into one mystical body with the other believers, so that you may be a spiritual temple in which God dwells. Therefore the milk of the word is to be desired by you.

units.la: Arg. 8. Accedentes ad Christum secundùm Evangelii sermonem, non tantùm consecramini & dedicamini Deo, ut ejus Templum, sed etiam sanctum Sacerdotium nanciscimini, ut meliores hostias quam illas typicas, spiritualis obedientiæ fructus scilicet quotidie offeratis, qui cultus Deo placiturus est, & gratus acceptuque futurus Deo per Christi intercessionem: Atque ita majorem gloriam consequimini, quam umbratile templum per se spectatum habebat: Lac ergo sermonis Euangelii expetendum vobis est.
units.tr: Argument 8. By coming to Christ according to the word of the gospel, you are not only consecrated and dedicated to God as his temple, but you also obtain a holy priesthood, so that you may offer better sacrifices than those typical ones, namely the fruits of spiritual obedience, every day. This worship will be pleasing to God and acceptable and welcome to God through the intercession of Christ. And so you attain greater glory than the shadowy temple had when viewed in itself. Therefore the milk of the word of the gospel is to be desired by you.

units.la: Quapropter etiam continetur in Scriptura, Ecce pono in Sion lapidem in imo angulo, electum, pretiosum: cui qui credit, non pudefiet.
units.tr: Wherefore also it is contained in the scripture, Behold, I lay in Sion a chief corner stone, elect, precious: and he that believeth on him shall not be confounded.

units.la: Hæc argumenta confirmat testimoniis Scripturæ variis, eaque testimonia in usum præsentem accommodat, ad acuendum studium Hebræorum erga doctrinam Euangelii. Primum testimonium, Isa. 28. 16. probans argumentum sextum per partes: 1. Quod scilicet Christus positus sit à Deo in fundamentum Ecclesiæ, in lapidem angularem, qui & ædificium contineat & ornet, qui honoris & præstantiæ sit plenus, electus, & pretiosus in æstimatione Dei, & qui primò in Sione seu Ecclesiâ Judæorum manifestandus esset, ut è Zion exiret Lex & Verbum Domini ex Hierusalem. Et quod credentibus se præstiturus sit solidum fundamentum, probat ex eo quod credentes in illum non pudefient.
units.tr: He confirms these arguments with various testimonies of Scripture, and applies those testimonies to the present purpose, to sharpen the Hebrews' zeal for the doctrine of the gospel. The first testimony is Isa. 28. 16., which proves the sixth argument in parts: (1) that Christ has been placed by God as the foundation of the Church, as the corner stone, which both holds the building together and adorns it, which is full of honour and excellence, chosen and precious in the esteem of God, and which was first to be made manifest in Zion, or the Church of the Jews, so that the law and the word of the Lord might go out from Zion and from Jerusalem. And from the fact that he will provide a solid foundation for believers, he proves that believers in him will not be confounded.

units.la: Vers. 7. Vobis igitur est honor qui creditis: Immorigeris vero lapis quem reprobaverunt aedificantes, hic factus est caput anguli, & lapis offendiculi, & petra offensionis:
units.tr: Verse 7. Unto you therefore which believe he is precious: but unto them which be disobedient, the stone which the builders disallowed, the same is made the head of the corner,

units.la: Vers. 8. Nempe iis qui offendunt ad sermonem, immorigeri, ad quod etiam conditi fuerunt.
units.tr: Verse 8. And a stone of stumbling, and a rock of offence, even to them which stumble at the word, being disobedient: whereunto also they were appointed.

units.la: Confirmat postremum membrum sexti argumenti, quod scilicet non debeant moveri per scandalum positum ab impiis, qui Christum rejecerunt; partim, quia satis est quod fidelibus Christus sit pretiosus; partim, quia increduli non possunt honorem Christo a Patre datum auferre, In eam rem citat secundum testimonium Scripturae, ex Psal. 118. vers. 22. Unde probatur: 1. Oportuisse Christum rejici ab iis, qui regimen in Ecclesia obtinebant. Secundo inanes fore ipsorum conatus. Tertio futurum, ut qui non crederent in Christum, seu qui impingerent ad hunc lapidem, ruerent & perirent. Et hic citat tertium Testimonium scripturae, ex Isa. 8. 14. Quarto nullos esse qui repudiaturi sunt Christum praeter reprobos, quos Deus destinavit, per & propter suam ipsorum obstinatam incredulitatem ad exitium meritum perventuros. Et hic continetur Argumentum 8. hortationis ad studium doctrinae Evangelicae; & ad fugiendum ab veritatis de Christo: Quia incredulitas & impactio in sermonem veritatis de Christo, indicium est reproborum & perditorum hominum, seu ad perditionem destinatorum. Ergo nisi rejectitii haberi velletis, Sermonem Evangelii expetite.
units.tr: He confirms the last part of the sixth argument, namely that they ought not to be moved by the stumbling-block placed by the impious, who have rejected Christ. This is partly because it is enough that Christ is precious to believers, and partly because unbelievers cannot take away the honour given to Christ by the Father. For this purpose he cites a second testimony of Scripture, from Psalm 118, verse 22. From this it is proved: (1) that Christ had to be rejected by those who held rule in the Church; (2) that their attempts would be in vain; (3) that those who did not believe in Christ, or who stumbled against this stone, would fall and perish. Here he cites a third testimony of Scripture, from Isa. 8. 14. (4) Fourth, that none will reject Christ except the reprobate, whom God has destined, and who through their own obstinate unbelief will deservedly come to destruction. Here is contained the eighth argument for the exhortation to zeal for evangelical doctrine, and for avoiding turning away from the truth about Christ: because unbelief and stumbling at the word of truth about Christ is a sign of reprobate and lost men, or of those destined to perdition. Therefore, unless you wish to be counted as rejected, seek the word of the gospel.

units.la: Vers. 9. Vos autem genus electum, regale sacerdotium, gens sancta, populus quem sibi Deus ut proprium vindicat: ut virtutes praedicetis illius qui vos vocavit e tenebris in admirabilem suam lucem.
units.tr: Verse 9. But ye are a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, an holy nation, a peculiar people; that ye should shew forth the praises of him who hath called you out of darkness into his marvellous light.

units.la: Arg. 9. Honor Gentis Hebraeorum, quem Patribus vestris concessit Deus, Exod. 19. & alibi, conservatur in vobis fidelibus Hebraeis, qui creditis in Christum: Ergo tenemini doctrinam fidei Christianae studiose appetere & imbibere. Vocantur autem regale Sacerdotium, quia sunt & regni Christi & Sacerdotii participes, imo per Christum Sacerdotes, & reges constituti. Vocantur, Genus electum, quia Deus eos prae aliis populis sibi adoptaverat. Gens sancta, quia eos sibi dicaverat Deus in vitæ puritatem. Populus in acquisitionem, quia Deus eos redemerat, & sibi in thesaurum & hæreditatem asciverat.
units.tr: Ninth argument: the honour of the Hebrew nation, which God granted to your fathers (Exod. 19 and elsewhere), is preserved in you Hebrews who believe in Christ. Therefore you are bound to desire eagerly and to drink in the doctrine of the Christian faith. They are called a royal priesthood because they share in both the kingdom and the priesthood of Christ, indeed they are made priests and kings through Christ. They are called a chosen generation because God had adopted them for himself above other peoples. They are called a holy nation because God had dedicated them to himself in purity of life. A people for a possession, because God had redeemed them and claimed them for himself as his treasure and inheritance.

units.la: Vocavit ] Arg. 10. Deus vos vocavit ex tenebris peccati, miseriæ, & incredulitatis ad cognitionem veritatis Evangelicæ, & participationem luminis gloriosæ illius veritatis, ut Dei sapientia, bonitas, justitia, reliquaeque ipsius virtutes, in vobis, ut in imagine, splenderent. Ergo decet vos Evangelicæ doctrinæ lac expetere, & avidè imbibere, ut id valeatis præstare.
units.tr: Called. Tenth argument: God has called you out of the darkness of sin, misery and unbelief into the knowledge of evangelical truth and a share in the light of that glorious truth, so that God's wisdom, goodness, justice, and his other virtues might shine in you as in an image. Therefore it becomes you to desire the milk of evangelical doctrine and to drink it in eagerly, so that you may be able to show these things forth.

units.la: Verf. 10 Qui quondam eratis non populus, nunc estis populus DEI: qui non consecuti misericordiam, nunc estis misericordiam consecuti.
units.tr: Verse 10: Who once were not a people, are now the people of God; who had not obtained mercy, have now obtained mercy.

units.la: Arg. 11. confirmans superius, Repudiatæ Gentis Hebrææ recollectio, & reconciliatio prædicta per Hoseam, Cap. 2. verf. 23. impleri cæpit in vobis Hebræis fidelibus, & illa quidem ex mera Dei in vos gratia. Ergo hortationi prædictæ tenemini studiose obedire.
units.tr: Argument 11, confirming what was said above: the recollection and reconciliation of the rejected Hebrew nation, foretold by Hosea, chapter 2, verse 23, has begun to be fulfilled in you Hebrew believers, and that from the pure grace of God toward you. Therefore you are bound to obey the aforesaid exhortation diligently.

units.la: Verf. 11 Dilecti, precor ut tanquam advenæ ac peregrini, abstineatis à carnis cupiditatibus, quæ militant adversus animam.
units.tr: Verse 11: Beloved, I beg you, as sojourners and strangers, abstain from the desires of the flesh, which war against the soul.

units.la: Secunda hortatio ad sanctitatem bimembris est: Memb. 1. Ut abstineant ab omnibus carnis seu corruptæ naturæ cupiditatibus, sive in mente, sive in corpore se exerant: Memb. 2. Ut honestè, id est, sanctè, innocenter & juste se gerant coram hominibus.
units.tr: The second exhortation to holiness has two parts. Part 1: that they abstain from all desires of the flesh, that is, of corrupt nature, whether these work in the mind or in the body. Part 2: that they conduct themselves honourably, that is, holily, blamelessly and justly, before men.

units.la: Inquilini ] Rationes hortationis sunt quinque, quæ probant à carnalibus cupiditatibus abstinendum illis esse: Ratio prima, Advenæ seu inquilini estis, non tantum quod à Patria exuletis, sed etiam quia filii Dei ubicunque terrarum agant mundi sunt hospites: Ergo vobis abstinendum à carnalibus cupiditatibus.
units.tr: Sojourners: There are five reasons for the exhortation, which prove that they must abstain from fleshly desires. The first reason: you are sojourners or strangers, not only because you have been exiled from your homeland, but also because the sons of God are strangers in the world, wherever on earth they live. Therefore you must abstain from fleshly desires.

units.la: Militant ] Ratio 2 Non potestis carnis cupiditatibus morem gerere, nisi in vestram perniciem, siquidem veteris hominis corrupti assectus salutì æternæ adversantur, & adversus animæ salutem militant. Ergo ab iis vobis abstinendum est.
units.tr: War: The second reason: you cannot indulge the desires of the flesh except to your own ruin, since the affections of the corrupt old man oppose eternal salvation and war against the salvation of the soul. Therefore you must abstain from them.

units.la: Verf. 12. Et conversationem vestram habeatis honestam inter Gentes, ut pro eo quod loquuntur adversus vos, velut malefactos, ex bonis operibus quæ perspexerint, glorificent Deum in die visitationis.
units.tr: Verse 12: And have your conduct honest among the Gentiles, so that, whereas they speak against you as evildoers, they may glorify God in the day of visitation, because of the good works they observe.

units.la: Ratio 3. Nisi obtemperaveritis hortationi, infidelibus Evangelii hostibus, qui captabant occasiones vobis obloquendi, ut facinorosis, anilam daturi estis. Ergo hortationi obtemperandum est. Ratio 4. Non satis est ut vestrā innocentiā ansam maledicendi hostibus praecipiatis; sed etiam bonis operibus convincendi à vobis sunt adversarii, & obturanda eorum ora, ne possint obloqui cum vellent maximè. Obtemperandum ergo huic hortationi.
units.tr: The third reason: unless you obey the exhortation, you will give the unbelieving enemies of the Gospel, who seek occasion to speak against you, grounds to regard you as criminals. Therefore the exhortation must be obeyed. The fourth reason: it is not enough to deprive your enemies of a handle for slander by your innocence; the adversaries must also be convinced by your good works, and their mouths stopped, so that they cannot speak against you when they most wish to. Therefore obey this exhortation.

units.la: Ratio 5. Idoneum & accommodatum hoc medium erit ad conversionem infidelium, & ad gloriam per eos Deo dandam, quo tempore Deo visum fuerit ex gratia ipsos visitare, & ad fidem Christi permovere. Ergo hortationi obtemperandum est.
units.tr: The fifth reason: this will be a suitable and fitting means for the conversion of unbelievers, and for giving glory to God through them, at the time God sees fit to visit them by grace and move them to faith in Christ. Therefore the exhortation must be obeyed.

units.la: Verf. 13. Proinde subjecti estote cuivis humanae ordinationi propter Dominum: sive regi ut qui superemineat:
units.tr: Verse 13: Therefore submit yourselves to every human ordinance for the Lord's sake, whether to the king, as the one who is supreme,

units.la: Tertia hortatio, specialiter deducta ex superiori, ad obedientiam erga Magistratum, Quem vocat ordinationem humanam, quia licet omnis potestas in genere sit ordinatio Dei, singularis tamen modus gubernationis potius per Monarchiam quam ullam aliam rationem, aut Aristocratiam, aut Democratiam, aut aliquam ex his mittam rationem, non est à Deo determinatus, sed unicuique reipublicae relinquitur determinandus, qui cum determinatur, vocatur ordinatio humana, quae rata habetur à Deo, quasi ipsius ordinatio. Etiamsi enim in Ecclesiasticis & spiritualibus, Christus solus dominium & potestatem dominicam habeat, & sibi retineat: nec dominium ullum, sed merum Ministerium sibi subordinatum in spirituali regno patiatur. In civilibus tamen dominium subordinatum constituit, & homines vocavit Dâ€‘os, licet non absolutè. Quaecunque ergo fuerit gubernandi forma, in quam consenserit regnum, sive respublica, jubet hic Apostolus Hebraeos fideles subditos se praebere, & regi ut supereminenti, & praesidibus, qui ab ipso mittuntur.
units.tr: The third exhortation, drawn specially from the previous one, is to obedience toward the magistrate, whom he calls a human ordinance. For although all power in general is an ordinance of God, the particular manner of government, whether by monarchy rather than any other form, or by aristocracy, or democracy, or some mixture of these, has not been fixed by God, but is left to each commonwealth to determine. When it is determined, it is called a human ordinance, which is held to be ratified by God as if it were his own ordinance. For although in ecclesiastical and spiritual matters Christ alone has lordship and dominion and keeps it to himself, and suffers no dominion but only a mere ministry subordinate to himself in the spiritual kingdom, yet in civil matters he has established a subordinate lordship, and has called men gods, though not absolutely. Therefore, whatever form of government a kingdom or commonwealth has agreed upon, the Apostle here orders the faithful Hebrews to show themselves subjects, and to obey the king as supreme and the governors sent by him.

units.la: Rationes hortationis sunt quinque: 1. Dominus hanc subjectionem requirit, nempe quatenus non advertus Dominum praecipiunt quicquam: nam propter se, non contra se potestatem imperandi dedit hominibus Deus: Subjecti ergo estote.
units.tr: The reasons for the exhortation are five. 1. The Lord requires this subjection, namely insofar as they command nothing against the Lord; for God gave men the power to command for his own sake, not against himself. Therefore: submit yourselves.

units.la: Verf. 14 Sive praesidibus ut qui per eum mittantur, tum ad ultionem maleficorum, tum ad laudem recte a eum:
units.tr: Verse 14: Or to governors, as those sent by him, both for the punishment of evildoers and for the praise of those who do well:

units.la: Ratio 2. Finis ordinationis est ad reprimendos malos, & bonos conservandos seu fovendos: Ergo hujus finis gratiâ & intuitu subjecti esse debetis.
units.tr: The second reason: the purpose of the ordinance is to restrain the wicked and to preserve and cherish the good. Therefore you ought to submit for the sake of, and with regard to, this purpose.

units.la: Verf. 15. Quoniam ita est voluntas Dei, ut bene agendo, capistro frænetis amentium hominum ignorantiam:
units.tr: Verse 15: For so is the will of God, that by doing well you may put to silence the ignorance of foolish men:

units.la: Ratio 3. Deus vult per subjectionem Fidelium Magistratibus præstitam, quasi capistro frænare ora brutorum hominum, qui sine ratione insaniunt adversus Dei populum, quasi Magistratibus adversarium. Ergo subjecti estote.
units.tr: The third reason: God wills that, through the subjection rendered by the faithful to the magistrates, the mouths of brutish men be restrained as with a bridle, men who rage without reason against the people of God as if they were adversaries of the magistrates. Therefore submit yourselves.

units.la: Verf. 16. Ut liberi, ac non veluti malitiæ velamen habentes veritatem, sed ut servi Dei.
units.tr: Verse 16: As free, yet not using your liberty as a cover for wickedness, but as servants of God.

units.la: Ratio 4. per occupationem objectionis, Deus non permittit ut quisquam libertatem Christianam prætendat suæ malitiæ, seu rebellioni suæ, quasi libertas Christiana eximeret quenquam à subjectionis civilis officio, sed mandat, ut liberi à peccato liberè serviatis justitiæ Dei promovendæ, cujus Minister est magistratus. Ergo Magistratibus subjici, & politicum ordinem observare debetis.
units.tr: The fourth reason, by anticipating an objection: God does not permit anyone to pretend Christian liberty as a cover for his malice or his rebellion, as if Christian liberty freed anyone from the duty of civil subjection. Rather, he commands you, free from sin, to serve freely the justice of God, which the magistrate is appointed to promote. Therefore you must be subject to the magistrates and observe the political order.

units.la: Verf. 17. Omnes honorate: fraternitatem diligite, Deum timete: Regem honorate.
units.tr: Verse 17: Honour all men; love the brotherhood; fear God; honour the king.

units.la: Ratio 5. Conjuncta sunt quatuor hæc officia Christianorum: 1. Neminem despicere, sed omnium rationem habere secundùm stationem in qua eos locavit Deus: 2. Eos qui sunt de familia fidei intime diligere: 3. Deum timere, & 4. Magistratui debitum honorem & obedientiam præstare, ita ut qui postremum ex his officium non præstiterit, nec reliqua sincere præstare censendus sit: Ergo subjecti estote Magistratui.
units.tr: The fifth reason: these four duties of Christians are joined together: 1. to despise no one, but to have regard for all according to the station in which God has placed them; 2. to love intimately those who belong to the household of faith; 3. to fear God; and 4. to render due honour and obedience to the magistrate. Whoever fails to perform the last of these duties is not to be thought to perform the rest sincerely. Therefore submit yourselves to the magistrate.

units.la: Verf. 18. Famuli, subditi estote cum omni timore dominis, non solum bonis & æquis, sed etiam pravis.
units.tr: Verse 18: Servants, be subject to your masters with all fear, not only to the good and gentle, but also to the froward.

units.la: Quarta hortatio ad servos Christianos, Ut suis Heris non tantùm æquioribus & humanis, sed etiam asperis & iniquis, cum omni reverentia pareant:
units.tr: The fourth exhortation, to Christian servants: that they obey their masters with all reverence, not only the more gentle and kind, but also the harsh and unjust.

units.la: Verf. 19. Hoc enim gratum est, si quis propter conscientiam Dei sustinet molestias injustè afflictas.
units.tr: Verse 19: For this is acceptable, if someone, for conscience toward God, endures grief, suffering unjustly.

units.la: Argumenta hortationis sunt duodecim, quæ probant servis tolerandas esse injurias à Dominis suis illatas.
units.tr: There are twelve arguments for the exhortation, which prove that servants must bear the injuries inflicted on them by their masters.

units.la: Argumentum primum, Hæc est gratia seu gloriosum opus specialis gratiæ Dei, supra naturæ vires in homine operantis, si quis eo consilio ut Deo placeat, patienter toleret injurias sibi factas. Ergo servis tolerandæ sunt injuriæ à Dominis.
units.tr: The first argument: this is grace, or the glorious work of God's special grace, operating in a man above the powers of nature, if someone, with the intention of pleasing God, patiently bears injuries done to him. Therefore servants must bear injuries from their masters.

units.la: Verf. 20 Quae enim est laus si quum peccantes colaphis caedimini toleratis? Sed si quum benefacitis, tamen afflicti toleratis, hoc est gratum apud Deum.
units.tr: Verse 20: For what glory is there, if, when you sin and are beaten with blows, you endure it? But if, when you do good and yet suffer, you endure it, this is acceptable with God.

units.la: Arg. 2. confirmans superius à contrario, Quia nulla est gloria, sed opus commune malefactoribus verbera pati ob malefacta: injurias vero pati ob benefacta, est gloriosa in opus gratiae, Deo acceptum & approbatum. Ergo servis tolerandae sunt, &c.
units.tr: The second argument, confirming the previous by the contrary: there is no glory in malefactors suffering blows for their misdeeds, which is a common thing; but to suffer injuries for well-doing is a glorious work of grace, acceptable and approved by God. Therefore servants must endure, etc.

units.la: Verf. 21. Nam ad hoc vocati estis, quoniam & Christus passus est pro vobis, relinquens vobis exemplar, ut insequeremini vestigia ipsius:
units.tr: Verse 21: For to this you were called, because Christ also suffered for you, leaving you an example, that you should follow in his steps:

units.la: Arg. 3. Vocati estis ad crucem gestandam, & injurias propter Dei gloriam ferendas. Ergo tolerate &c. Christus ] Arg. 4. Christus passus est pro nobis ab hostibus suis multo graviora mala. Ergo tenemini vos pro Dei gloria injurias à Dominis vestris illatas patienter ferre.
units.tr: The third argument: you are called to bear the cross and to endure injuries for the glory of God. Therefore endure, etc. Christ: The fourth argument: Christ suffered for us from his enemies far greater evils. Therefore you are bound to bear patiently, for the glory of God, the injuries inflicted on you by your masters.
