units.la: Relinquens ] Arg. 5. Christus in passionibus suis reliquit nobis exemplar patiendi injurias, & vult omnes fideles sibi conformes esse, & suum exemplum imitari. Ergo vobis tolerandae sunt injuriae à Dominis vestris illatae.
units.tr: Leaving: The fifth argument: in his sufferings Christ left us an example of enduring injuries, and wills all the faithful to be conformed to him and to imitate his example. Therefore the injuries inflicted on you by your masters must be borne by you.

units.la: Verf. 22. Qui peccatum non fecerat, nec inventus est dolus in ore ipsius.
units.tr: Verse 22: Who did no sin, neither was guile found in his mouth.

units.la: Arg. 6. confirmans superius, In Christo nullum omnino peccatum fuit; Vos vero servi etiamsi alieni à culpa litis in eo, ob quod affligimini à Dominis, non tamen alieni estis ab omni peccato, ab omni dolo in labiis vestris. Ideoque tenemini eo patientius ferre injurias vobis ab hominibus illatas.
units.tr: The sixth argument, confirming the previous: in Christ there was no sin at all. You servants, though free from the cause of the quarrel for which you are afflicted by your masters, are not, however, free from all sin, from all guile on your lips. Therefore you are bound to bear the injuries inflicted on you by men all the more patiently.

units.la: Verf. 23 Qui convitiis affectus, non vicissim convitabatur: quum malis afficeretur, non minabatur: sed committebat vindictam ei qui iuste iudicat.
units.tr: Verse 23: Who, when he was reviled, did not revile in return; when he suffered, he did not threaten, but committed the matter to him who judges justly.

units.la: Arg. 7. Christus ab omni talione abstinuit, nec convicia nec minas conviciantibus, & vim ipsi inferentibus regerebat. Ergo vobis servos frenandi sunt animi vestri, ne malum pro malo reddere appetatis, & tolerandae injuriae à Dominis.
units.tr: Argument 7. Christ abstained from every kind of retaliation: he returned neither reproach nor threats to those who reviled him or laid violent hands on him. Therefore your own minds must be restrained, so that you do not seek to repay evil with evil, and you must endure the injuries inflicted by your masters.

units.la: Committebat ] Arg. 8. Si exemplo Christi patienter ferentes injurias caulam vestram iusto Iudici commiseritis, habituri estis Deum vindicem injuriarum vobis illatarum. Tolerate ergo.
units.tr: Committebat] Argument 8. If, following Christ's example, you bear injuries patiently and commit your cause to the just Judge, you will have God as the avenger of the injuries done to you. Endure, then.

units.la: Verf. 24. Qui peccata nostra pertulit in corpore suo super lignum ut peccatis mortui, justitiæ viveremus, cujus vibicibus sanati estis.
units.tr: Verse 24: Who himself bore our sins in his body on the tree, so that we, dead to sins, might live to righteousness, by whose wounds you have been healed.

units.la: Cum Christus & reatum & pœnas peccatorum nostrorum, in Cruce pendens, sustinuerit realiter in corpore suo, & sultulerit, non est vobis su-spicandum, quod Deus, dum per manus dominorum injustorum vos affligit, vindictam de vestris præteritis peccatis, ut iratus Judex exigat. Ergo de expiatione peccatorum vestrorum certiorati, debetis æquiori animo afflictionum exercitia perferre.
units.tr: Since Christ, hanging on the Cross, truly bore in his body both the guilt and the punishments of our sins, and carried them away, you must not suspect that God, when he afflicts you through the hands of unjust masters, is exacting vengeance for your past sins as an angry Judge would. Therefore, assured that your sins have been expiated, you ought to bear the trials of your afflictions with a more equable mind.

units.la: Vt peccatis ] Arg 10. Eo fine Christus abstulit peccatorum nostrorum reatum & pœnas, ut mortificatio peccati in nobis, & vera justitia per ipsius mortem pasta, promoveatur omnibus modis, & per consequens ut temperantes vobis à vindicta, studeatis patientiæ: Ergo tolerandæ vobis injuriæ, &c.
units.tr: That we, dead to sins] Argument 10. Christ took away the guilt and punishments of our sins for this purpose: that the mortification of sin in us, and true righteousness nourished by his death, might be advanced in every way; and consequently, that, restraining yourselves from revenge, you may strive for patience. Therefore injuries must be endured by you, etc.

units.la: Cujus ] Arg. 11. In plagis, verberibus, & vulneribus Christi parata est consolatio & sanitas, adversus omnem animi ægritudinem spiritualem, & omnes plagas, seu vulnera corporis, quæ vel inflixerunt, vel inflisturi sunt vobis servis fidelibus injusti vestri Domini: quod verbis Isaiæ, Capit 53. confirmat: Ergo tolerandæ patienter vobis sunt injuriæ à Dominis.
units.tr: By whose] Argument 11. In the wounds, stripes and bruises of Christ there is ready consolation and healing against every spiritual sickness of the mind and all the blows or wounds of the body which your unjust masters have inflicted or will inflict upon you, faithful servants. Isaiah confirms this in the words of Isaiah, chapter 53. Therefore injuries must be patiently endured by you from your masters.

units.la: Vers. 25. Nam eratis velut oves errantes, sed conversi nunc estis ad pastorem & curatorem animarum vestrarum.
units.tr: Verse 25: For you were like sheep going astray, but you have now returned to the Shepherd and Overseer of your souls.

units.la: Arg. 12. Alia nunc vitæ ratio vobis ineunda est ab eâ, quam olim te-nebatis. Nam olim in ignorantia & peccatis, ut pecudes errabatis in vestram ipsorum perniciem, nunc recolleƈti ad Episcopum & Pastorem animarum vestrarum Iesum Christum, debetis Ducem vestrum sequi, & vos, vestraque omnia, animasque imprimis, ipsius committere curæ & custodiæ: Ergo patienter vobis servis, tolerandæ sunt à Dominis vestris injuriæ.
units.tr: Argument 12. You must now adopt a way of life different from the one you formerly followed. For formerly, in ignorance and sin, you went astray like sheep to your own destruction; now that you have turned back to Jesus Christ, the Bishop and Shepherd of your souls, you ought to follow your Leader, and to commit yourselves and all that is yours, and above all your souls, to his care and keeping. Therefore, you servants must patiently endure the injuries inflicted by your masters.

units.la: Caput Tertium.
units.tr: Chapter Three.

units.la: Apitus duae sunt partes: Prima de Vxoris & Mariti ossiciu; Altera de communibus virtutibus quae ad omnis generis homines spectant.
units.tr: This chapter has two parts. The first concerns the duty of wife and husband; the second concerns the common virtues that apply to all kinds of people.

units.la: Verf. 1. Similiter uxores subjectae sint suis viris, ut etiam, si qui non obediunt sermoni, per uxorum conversationem absque sermone lucrifiant:
units.tr: Verse 1. Likewise, wives, be subject to your own husbands, so that even if some do not obey the word, they may be won over without a word through the conduct of their wives:

units.la: Prima pars Capitis, In qua primum praecepta dat Uxoribus de officiis suis erga Maritos suos, licet infideles. Primum Praeceptum, Ut subjiciantur suis viris, & obediant iis, non vero refragentur, imperium detrectantes.
units.tr: The first part of the chapter, in which he first gives precepts to wives about their duties toward their husbands, even unbelieving ones. The first precept: that they should be subject to their husbands and obey them, not oppose them or refuse their authority.

units.la: Rationes praecepti sunt tres: Ratio prima, Quia similiter ex Legis obligatione, tenentur Uxores ad subjectionem erga maritos praestandam, sicut tenentur servi ad dominis suis se subjiciendum, licet non ad eundem gradum subjectionis, seu ad eadem officia in subjectione. Ratio 2. Quia infideles mariti ex sancta conversatione uxorum fidelium praeparari poterint ad sermonem fidei audiendum, & ad amplexandam Christi fidem lucrifieri eatenus, ut antequam audiant Dei Verbum, diligant ipsam propter ipsius effecta, quae in uxoribus suis observant.
units.tr: There are three reasons for this precept. The first reason: wives are bound by the obligation of the Law to render subjection to their husbands, just as servants are bound to submit to their masters, though not to the same degree of subjection or in the same duties of submission. The second reason: unbelieving husbands can be prepared by the holy conduct of believing wives to hear the word of the faith, and can be won to embrace the faith of Christ, so that before they hear the Word of God, they come to love it for the effects they see in their wives.

units.la: Verf. 2. Vbi spectarint cum reverentia conjunctam castam conversationem vestram.
units.tr: Verse 2. When they behold your chaste conversation coupled with fear.

units.la: Ratio 3. confirmans priorem, Quia pura & casta conversatio fidelium uxorum, infideles maritos permovere poterat, ad considerationem excellentiae Christianismi, per quem ad puritatem & timorem discipuli ipsius instituuntur.
units.tr: The third reason, confirming the first: the pure and chaste conduct of believing wives could move unbelieving husbands to consider the excellence of Christianity, through which its disciples are trained to purity and the fear of God.

units.la: Verf. 3. Quarum ornatus non sit externus ille in nodis capillorum, & circumposito auro, vel palliorum amictu;
units.tr: Verse 3. Whose adorning let it not be that outward adorning of plaiting the hair, and of wearing of gold, or of putting on of apparel;

units.la: Praeceptum 2. De uxorum cultu seu ornatu, ne sint nimis curiosae in externo corporis ornatu nimium sibi indulgentes, in nimiae elegantiae & superflui splendoris affectatione. Vers. 4. Sed occultus ille cordis homo situs in incorruptione lenis ac quieti Spiritus, qui est coram Deo pretiosus.
units.tr: The second precept concerns the wives' dress or adornment: they should not be overly fastidious about outward adornment of the body, indulging themselves excessively in an affectation of great elegance and showy display. Verse 4. But let it be the hidden man of the heart, in the incorruptible [adornment] of a meek and quiet spirit, which is of great price before God.

units.la: Præceptum 3. ex antithesi propositum, Ut ornent interiorem hominem, id est, animam suam jam renovari coeptam, ornatu virtutum, nominatim mansueti & quieti spiritus, qui efficiat, ut modeste se gerant in omnibus.
units.tr: The third precept, set forth by way of contrast: that they should adorn the inner man, that is, their soul, which has already begun to be renewed, with the adornment of virtues, namely a meek and quiet spirit, which makes them conduct themselves modestly in all things.

units.la: Rationes præcepti sunt quinque: Ratio prima, Quia hic ornatus est incorruptibilis, respectu animæ immortalis, & respectu virtutis non perituræ. Ratio 2. Quia ornatus hic est pretiosus in conspectu Dei, gratus, acceptusque in oculis ejus, cujus rationem decet fœminas habere, potius quam oculorum vanorum hominum inspectantium.
units.tr: There are five reasons for this precept. The first reason: this adornment is incorruptible, with respect to the immortal soul, and with respect to a virtue that will not perish. The second reason: this adornment is precious in the sight of God, pleasing and acceptable in his eyes, and it befits women to have regard to his judgment rather than to the eyes of vain men who look on.

units.la: Vers. 5. Ita enim olim & sanctæ illæ mulieres sperantes in Deo, et nabant se, subjectæ suis viris.
units.tr: Verse 5. For after this manner in the old time the holy women also, who trusted in God, adorned themselves, being in subjection to their own husbands.

units.la: Ratio 3. Ab exemplo sanctarum mulierum in veteri Testamento, quæ laudem habent in Scriptura, non ex ornatu corporis externo, sed ex fide in Deum, & subjectione præstitâ maritis suis.
units.tr: The third reason: from the example of the holy women in the Old Testament, who are praised in Scripture, not for outward bodily adornment, but for faith in God and for the subjection they rendered to their husbands.

units.la: Vers. 6. Sicut Sara obedivit Abrahæ, dominum eum vocans: cujus factæ estis filiæ, dum bene facitis, etiam quum non terremini ullo pavore.
units.tr: Verse 6. Even as Sarah obeyed Abraham, calling him lord, whose daughters ye are, as long as ye do well and are not afraid with any amazement.

units.la: Ratio 4. Ab exemplo Saræ, quæ Abrahamo mansuete obedivit, & dominum suum agnovit eum, etiam de eo loquens.
units.tr: The fourth reason: from the example of Sarah, who obeyed Abraham meekly and acknowledged him as her lord, even when speaking of him.

units.la: Ratio 5. Quia si pietatem & modestiam Saræ moribus suis exprimerent, neque ullo metu mundano se a studio pietatis abduci paterentur, sanctæ hujus matronæ filias se esse declararent.
units.tr: The fifth reason: if they express the piety and modesty of Sarah in their conduct, and do not allow themselves to be drawn away from the pursuit of piety by any worldly fear, they will show themselves to be daughters of this holy matron.

units.la: Vers. 7. Viri similiter, una versentur ut scientes decet, vasi muliebri ut infirmiori tribuentes honorem, utpote quum una etiam heredes sitis gratiæ vitæ, ne interrumpantur preces vestræ.
units.tr: Verse 7. Likewise, ye husbands, dwell with them according to knowledge, giving honour unto the wife, as unto the weaker vessel, and as being heirs together of the grace of life; that your prayers be not hindered.

units.la: Ex altera parte præcipit viris, ut cohabitent cum uxoribus suis, id est, humaniter eas alant, & foveant secundum notitiam, id est, ut sapientes decet, prudenter uxores suas regant.
units.tr: On the other side, he instructs husbands to live with their wives, that is, to support them kindly and cherish them according to knowledge, that is, to govern their wives prudently, as wise men should.

units.la: Rationes præcepti sunt quatuor: Ratio prima, Quia similiter ex obligatione Legis Divinæ tenentur viri erga uxores mutua officia præstare, non minus quam uxores erga viros.
units.tr: There are four reasons for this precept. The first reason: husbands, likewise, are bound by the obligation of the Divine Law to render mutual duties to their wives, no less than wives to their husbands.

units.la: Ratio 2. Quia prudentia requirit ut sexus fœminei tanquam quam fragilioris tantò major ratio habeatur, quantò fœmina infirmior est, & suspicari alioqui potest se despici a viro. Ratio 3. Quia Uxores non tantum participes sunt honoris & bonorum terrenorum, quæ ad maritos suos spectant, sed etiam cohæredes sunt cum suis maritis fidelibus, gratiæ salutaris. Ratio 4. Quia alioqui orituræ essent rixæ & jurgia, quibus preces, & domesticæ & secretæ, cum mariti tum uxoris, interrumpi possent, vel turbari.
units.tr: The second reason: prudence requires that the female sex, as the weaker, be shown all the more consideration the weaker she is, and otherwise she may suspect that she is being despised by her husband. The third reason: wives are not only sharers in the honour and earthly goods that belong to their husbands, but are also co-heirs with their believing husbands of saving grace. The fourth reason: otherwise quarrels and strife would arise, by which the prayers, both private and domestic, of husband and wife could be interrupted or disturbed.

units.la: Secunda pars.
units.tr: Second part.

units.la: Verf. 8. Denique omnes estote concordes, mutuo molestiarum sensu affecti, fraterna præditi charitate, misericordes, comes:
units.tr: Verse 8. Finally, be ye all of one mind, having compassion one of another, love as brethren, be pitiful, be courteous:

units.la: Secunda pars Capitis, In qua hortatur ad studium sanctitatis, licet cum Cruce conjunctum, seu ad communia sanctitatis officia, & virtutes quæ ad cujuslibet generis homines spectant, quales enumerat sex: Quarum prima est Concordia, sine qua omnis vita perpetuis turbis ac rixis inquietatur. Secunda est Sympathia, quæ facit ut proximorum & molestiis & bonis, sicut decet afficiamur, dolentes cum dolentibus, & gaudentes cum gaudentibus. Tertia est Fraterna Charitas, qua Christianos utpote fratres in DOMINO arctè complectimur. Quarta est Misericordia, qua egenis & peregrinis sive exulibus succurrimus. Quinta est Comitas, quâ affabiles & humanos nos præstamus erga alios, ad bonum publicum, & aliorum ædificationem.
units.tr: The second part of the chapter, in which he exhorts to zeal for holiness, although joined with the cross, or to the common duties of holiness and the virtues that apply to men of every kind. He lists six of them. The first is concord, without which all life is disturbed by constant tumults and quarrels. The second is sympathy, which makes us be affected by the troubles and the blessings of our neighbours as we should, weeping with those who weep and rejoicing with those who rejoice. The third is brotherly love, by which we embrace Christians closely as brothers in the Lord. The fourth is mercy, by which we help the needy, strangers and exiles. The fifth is courtesy, by which we show ourselves affable and humane toward others, for the public good and for their edification.

units.la: Vers 9 Non reddentes malum pro malo, aut convitium pro convitio, sed contrà, benedicentes: ut qui sciatis vos ad hoc vocatos esse, ut benedictionis hereditatem possideatis.
units.tr: Verse 9. Not rendering evil for evil, or railing for railing, but contrariwise blessing; knowing that ye are thereunto called, that ye should inherit a blessing.

units.la: Sexta est Patientia, quâ injurias ab aliis acceptas, sive facto, sive verbo æquo animo toleramus, imò quâ pro maleficiis beneficia rependimus.
units.tr: The sixth is patience, by which we bear with an equal mind the injuries received from others, whether by deed or by word, and indeed by which we repay good for evil.

units.la: Argumenta hortationis ad studium harum virtutum potissimum patientiæ, sunt septemdecim, Quæ omnia probant his virtutibus studendum esse, etiamsi tolerandæ propterea essent afflictiones.
units.tr: The arguments for exhorting to the pursuit of these virtues, especially patience, are seventeen. All of them prove that these virtues must be pursued, even if afflictions must for that reason be endured.

units.la: Ut qui Argumentum primum, Quia ad hanc conditionem à DEO sumus vocati, ut constanter bene agendo, ac mala fortiter perferendo vitam æternam, velut hæreditario jure concessam adeamus. Ergo studendum his virtutibus, & nominatim patientiæ. Verf 10, Itaque qui vult vitam diligere, & videre dies bonos, coerceat linguam suam a malo, & labia sua, ne loquantur dolum.
units.tr: So that you who. The first argument: because we have been called by God to this condition, that by constantly doing good and bravely enduring evils we may attain eternal life, as if granted by hereditary right. Therefore these virtues, and especially patience, must be pursued. Verse 10. For he that will love life, and see good days, let him refrain his tongue from evil, and his lips that they speak no guile.

units.la: Verf. 11. Declinet a malo, & faciat bonum: quærat pacem, & persequatur eam.
units.tr: Verse 11. Let him eschew evil, and do good; let him seek peace, and ensue it.

units.la: Verf. 12. Nam oculi Domini sunt intenti in justos, & aures ejus in deprecationem eorum: vultus vero Domini adversum eos qui faciunt mala.
units.tr: Verse 12. For the eyes of the Lord are over the righteous, and his ears are open unto their prayers: but the face of the Lord is against them that do evil.

units.la: Arg. 2. A testimonio Scripturæ, ex Psal. 34. verf. 12, 13, 14, 15, 16. Ubi docetur viam proximam ad felicitatem esse, ut Dei filii studeant bonis operibus, & temperent sibi ab impatientia & omni maleficiorum genere: utque ex altera parte ipse benedictionis divinæ, ex altera vero metu divinæ iræ, hinc atque hinc septi pergant in cursu sanctitatis. Ergo his virtutibus & præcipuè patientiæ studendum est.
units.tr: The second argument, from the testimony of Scripture, Psalm 34, verses 12, 13, 14, 15, 16. There it is taught that the nearest way to happiness is for the sons of God to strive after good works and to refrain from impatience and every kind of wrongdoing; and that, on the one hand, the blessing of the divine favour, and on the other, the fear of divine wrath, hem them in on either side as they press on in the course of holiness. Therefore these virtues, and above all patience, must be pursued.

units.la: Verf. 13. Et quis est qui affligat vos, si bonitatis æmulatores fueritis?
units.tr: Verse 13. And who is he that will harm you, if ye be followers of that which is good?

units.la: Arg. 3. Quia hæc ratio optima est, quâ studiosi harum virtutum liberentur ab incommodis multis, quorum inferendorum occasionem captant impii: adeo ut monstro simili sit, qui innocentes, & omnis bonitatis studiosos lædere velit. Ergo studendum his virtutibus & nominatim patientiæ.
units.tr: The third argument: this is an excellent reason, by which those who pursue these virtues are freed from many troubles, for the infliction of which the wicked seek an occasion; so much so that it would be like a monstrous thing for someone to wish to harm the innocent and those who devote themselves to all goodness. Therefore these virtues, and especially patience, must be pursued.

units.la: Verf. 14. Sed & si quid perpetiamini propter justitiam, beati tamen eritis. Cæterum timorem eorum ne timete, neque turbamini.
units.tr: Verse 14. But and if ye suffer for righteousness' sake, happy are ye: and be not afraid of their terror, neither be troubled.

units.la: Arg. 4: Quia si dum his virtutibus studetis, justitiæ causâ mala patiamini, beati tamen manseri eritis coram Deo, utcunque fortuna vestra misera videri poterit in mundo. Ergo his virtutibus studendum est.
units.tr: Argument 4: For if, while you devote yourselves to these virtues, you suffer evil for the sake of righteousness, you will nevertheless remain blessed before God, however wretched your lot may seem in the world. Therefore these virtues must be pursued.

units.la: Verf. 15. Sed Dominum Deum sanctificate in cordibus vestris: Estote autem semper parati ad respondendum cuilibet petenti rationem ejus spei, quæ in vobis est, cum lenitate & reverentia:
units.tr: Verse 15. But sanctify the Lord God in your hearts. Always be ready to answer anyone who asks you for a reason for the hope that is in you, with gentleness and reverence.

units.la: Arg. 5. Non debetis vos Christiani à studio harum virtutum deterreri impiorum minis & terrore, imo ne vel animo quidem turbari, sed contrà, debetis Deum in corde vestro sanctificare; hoc est, Dei terrorem & benevolentiam, Dei mandata, minas, promissiones, potentiam, auxilium, consolationes, liberationes & exitus, quos ille dare & potest & præ labit, tanti æstimare, ut flocci facatis, & despiciatis quicquid homines facere contra vos poterint.
units.tr: Argument 5. You Christians ought not to be deterred from the pursuit of these virtues by the threats and terror of the wicked, nor even be troubled in mind. Rather, you ought to sanctify God in your heart; that is, to esteem so highly the fear and goodwill of God, his commands, threats, promises, power, help, consolations, deliverances and outcomes, which he both can and will give, that you count everything men can do against you as nothing (flocci facere) and despise it.

units.la: Parati ] Arg. 6. Tantò abest ut à studio virtutum deterreri debeatis metu hominum, ut contrà præ fiducia in Dei bonitate & omnipotentia parati debeatis esse ad sanctificandum Deum in aperta confessione fidei Christianæ, nihil erubescentes verbum Dei, pro ratione & fundamento fidei vestræ proferre, quotiescunque petitur ratio fidei à vobis, ita, ut ad Dei gloriam, seu sanctificationem nominis ipsius tendere possit responsio, quæ exigitur. Interim jubet hanc confessionem edicu n mansuetudine erga hominęs, & timore, seu reverentiâ erga Deum, ne nostris assectibus ullo modo contaminetur Dei veritas.
units.tr: Ready: Argument 6. You ought to be so far from being deterred from the pursuit of virtue by fear of men that, on the contrary, trusting in the goodness and omnipotence of God, you should be ready to sanctify God by an open confession of the Christian faith, blushing at nothing, and to set forth the Word of God as the reason and foundation of your faith whenever a reason for your faith is demanded of you. In this way the answer that is required may tend to the glory of God, or the sanctification of his name. Meanwhile he commands that this confession be made with gentleness towards men, and with fear, or reverence, towards God, so that the truth of God is in no way polluted by our passions.

units.la: Vers. 16 Conscientiam bonam habentes: ut proeo quod loquuntur adversum vos, tanquam maleficos, pudefiant qui incessunt vestram bonam in Christo conversationem.
units.tr: Verse 16. Having a good conscience, so that those who speak against you as evildoers may be put to shame, those who revile your good conduct in Christ.

units.la: Arg. 7. Conscientiam bonam ex studio harum virtutum habituri estis, quæ in omni conditione poterit vobis bonum testimonium intus præbere. Ergo his virtutibus studendum.
units.tr: Argument 7. From the pursuit of these virtues you will have a good conscience, which in every condition can give you good testimony within. Therefore these virtues must be pursued.

units.la: Pudesiunt ] Arg. 8 Per studium harum virtutum obturaturi estis ora hostium Euangelii, qui vestræ famæ insidiantur, vobisque tanquam maleficis obloquuntur.
units.tr: May be put to shame: Argument 8. Through the pursuit of these virtues you will stop the mouths of the enemies of the Gospel, who lie in wait for your reputation and speak against you as evildoers.

units.la: Vers. 17 Melius enim est ut bene agentes, si ita velit Dei voluntas, malè afficiantur, quam male agentes:
units.tr: Verse 17. For it is better, if the will of God should so wish, to suffer for doing good than for doing evil.

units.la: Arg. 9 Quia longè præstat ut studentes his virtutibus ob benefacta affligamini, si ita ferat Dei voluntas, quam ob malefacta: illic enim est gratia & laus; hic verò judicium & dedecus. Ergo his virtutibus studendum.
units.tr: Argument 9. It is far better that you be afflicted for good deeds, while pursuing these virtues, if the will of God so bears it, than for evil deeds. For in the former case there is grace and praise; in the latter, judgment and disgrace. Therefore these virtues must be pursued.

units.la: Vers. 18. Nam & Christus semel pro peccatis passus fuit, justus pro injustis: ut nos ad Deum adduceret, mortificatus quidem carne, vivificatus autem Spiritu:
units.tr: Verse 18. For Christ also suffered once for sins, the just for the unjust, that he might bring us to God, put to death indeed in the flesh but made alive in the Spirit.

units.la: Arg. 10. CHRISTUS semel pro peccatis expiandis passus est. Ergo vos fideles exempti à pœna peccatorum, tenemini, si Deus ità vult, pati molestias ob studium harum virtutum.
units.tr: Argument 10. Christ suffered once to expiate sins. Therefore you faithful, exempt from the punishment of sins, are bound, if God so wills, to endure troubles for the sake of pursuing these virtues.

units.la: Justus ] Arg. 11. CHRISTUS passus est prorsus justus, & innocens pro nobis injustis. Ergo nos fideles, qui non prorsus innocentes sumus tenemur ob studium justitiæ non renuere pati quæ Deus vult.
units.tr: Just: Argument 11. Christ suffered, being wholly just and innocent, for us who are unjust. Therefore we faithful, who are not wholly innocent, are bound, for the sake of righteousness, not to refuse to suffer what God wills.

units.la: Ut nos ] Arg. 12. CHRISTUS justus passus est, ut justificatos nos, & patientes mala, sibi conformaret, & ad Deum adduceret. Ergo in studio virtutum & patientia afflictionum ob benefacta sequi eum tenentur fideles. Vivificatus ] Arg. 13. Cum felix fuerit exitus passionum CHRI-STI (quippe qui licet propter carnis nostræ quam gestabat, infirmitatem, mortuus sit, resurrexit tamen à morte, per virtutem & potentiam Spiritus seu Deitatis suæ) vos etiam fideles nala patientes pro CHRISTO & ejus justitiâ, proculdubio lætum etiam exitum ex passionibus vestris, & ex morte ipla consequuturi estis. Ergo studendum his virtutibus etiamsi propterea affligamini.
units.tr: That he might bring us: Argument 12. Christ, being just, suffered so that he might conform us, justified and enduring evil, to himself and bring us to God. Therefore the faithful are bound to follow him in the pursuit of virtue and in patiently enduring afflictions for good deeds. Made alive: Argument 13. Since the outcome of Christ's sufferings was happy (for although he died on account of the weakness of the flesh he bore, he nevertheless rose from death through the power and might of the Spirit, that is, of his Deity), you also, faithful, enduring evil for Christ and his righteousness, will undoubtedly reach a happy outcome from your sufferings, and from death itself. Therefore these virtues must be pursued even if on that account you are afflicted.

units.la: Verf. 19. Per quem etiam spiritibus qui sunt in carcere profectus prædicavit.
units.tr: Verse 19. In which also he went and preached to the spirits that are in prison.

units.la: Verf. 20. Olim immorigeris, quum semel expectabat Dei patientia in diebus Noe, quum appararetur arca; in qua pauca (id est octo) anima servatæ sunt in aqua.
units.tr: Verse 20. Who formerly were disobedient, when the patience of God once waited in the days of Noah, while the ark was being prepared; in which few, that is eight, souls were saved through water.

units.la: Verf. 21. Cui rei correspondens exemplar Baptismi, nos quoque servat (non quo carnis sordes abjiciuntur, sed quo fit ut bona conscientia DEUM interroget) per resurrectionem Jesu Christi.
units.tr: Verse 21. Corresponding to which, the pattern of baptism now saves us also (not by putting away the filth of the flesh, but by the answer of a good conscience towards God) through the resurrection of Jesus Christ.

units.la: Arg. 14. Jam sunt in carcere seu inferno, spiritus seu animæ incredulorum istorum & inobedientium hominum, quibus CHRISTUS per SPIRITUM suum olim in Noacho Præcone justitiæ, proficiscens prædicavit resipiscentiam, & studium justitiæ, eo quod olim nempe temporibus Noachi immorigeri fuerint, abutentes DEI erga eos lenitate, dum pararetur arca. Ergo huic hortationi ad virtutum studium obedire expedit vobis Hebræis, ne eádem pœnâ involvamini.
units.tr: Argument 14. Now there are in prison, that is, in hell, the spirits or souls of those unbelieving and disobedient men to whom Christ, going forth through his Spirit, once preached repentance and the pursuit of righteousness through Noah, a herald of righteousness; for in the days of Noah they were disobedient, abusing God's forbearance towards them while the ark was being prepared. Therefore it is expedient for you Hebrews to obey this exhortation to the pursuit of virtue, lest you be involved in the same punishment.

units.la: Pauca ] Arg. 15. Sicut paucæ illæ animæ quæ erant in arca servatæ sunt in aquis diluvii per arcam; Sic omnes fideles baptizati servantur, ne pereant uliis afflictionibus, per baptisma quod typo arcæ correlponder. Ergo nihil metuendum vobis justitiæ studiosis, etiamsi ob justitiam patiamini.
units.tr: Few: Argument 15. Just as those few souls who were in the ark were saved through the waters of the flood by the ark, so all the faithful who are baptized are preserved, lest they perish under other afflictions, through baptism, which corresponds to the type of the ark. Therefore you who pursue righteousness have nothing to fear, even if you suffer for righteousness.

units.la: Non quo carnis sordes ] Explicat hoc argumentum, ostendens se non intelligere Baptismum externum, qui consistit in ablutione sordium corporis, sed baptismum internum, qui consistit in ablutione peccatorum, seu lordium animæ, cujus signum & effectum proprium, est stipulatio bonæ conscientiæ apud DEUM seu illa confidentia, quam bona conscientia per fidem purgata, habet apud DEUM, per & propter resurrectionem CHRISTI. Simul addit Arg. 16. Jam ellis imbuti illâ confidentiâ, quam bona conscientia per fidem purgata habet apud DEUM, perum, per & propter resurrectionem CHRISTI. Ergo non est quod in studio virtutum harum afflictiones metuatis. Addit per resurrectionem Christi, partim, Quia in resurrectione CHRISTI ipso facto declarata fuit sententia DEI absolventis nos in CHRISTO à peccato & morte : partim, quia CHRISTUS resuscitatus à mortuis perficit ea potenter in, & pro fidelibus, quæ morte suâ illis meritus est, & impetravit.
units.tr: Not by putting away the filth of the flesh: He explains this argument, showing that he does not mean external baptism, which consists in the washing away of bodily filth, but internal baptism, which consists in the cleansing of sins, or the filth of the soul. Its sign and proper effect is the answer of a good conscience towards God, that is, the confidence which a conscience cleansed through faith has before God, through the resurrection of Christ. At the same time he adds Argument 16: Since you are already imbued with that confidence which a good conscience cleansed through faith has before God, through and on account of the resurrection of Christ, there is no reason for you to fear afflictions in the pursuit of these virtues. He adds through the resurrection of Christ partly because in the resurrection of Christ the sentence of God, absolving us in Christ from sin and death, was declared by the very fact; and partly because Christ, raised from the dead, powerfully brings to completion in and for the faithful those things which he merited and obtained for them by his death.

units.la: Vers. 22. Qui est ad dextram Dei, profectus in Cœlum, subjectis ipsi angelis & potestatibus ac virtutibus.
units.tr: Verse 22. Who is at the right hand of God, gone into heaven, with angels and authorities and powers made subject to him.

units.la: Arg. 17. Confirmans superius, & simul etiam hortationem ad studium virtutum, licet ferendæ essent afflictiones ob eam causam, CHRISTUS salutis nostræ Autor evectus est in Cœlo, ad summam regnandi in omnia gloriam; supremamque, & sempiternam potestatem obtinet in omnes creaturas, ne Angelis quidem ullis exceptis. Ergo vos fideles debetis studium virtutum prosequi fortiter adversus omnia pericula & terrores, certi de salute vestra, quia talem habetis in Cœlis Salvatorem.
units.tr: Argument 17. Confirming what was said above, and at the same time the exhortation to pursue virtue even though afflictions must be borne for its sake: Christ, the author of our salvation, has been exalted in heaven to the highest glory of reigning over all things, and holds supreme and everlasting power over all creatures, not even angels excepted. Therefore you faithful ought to pursue the virtues bravely against all dangers and terrors, certain of your salvation, because you have such a Saviour in heaven.

units.la: CAPUT QUARTUM.
units.tr: CHAPTER FOUR.

units.la: Idem Argumentum quod superiori Capite tractatur hic prosequitur. Capitis duæ sunt partes; In prima habentur hortationes ad sanctimoniam ad vers. 12. Altera consolatoria est, adversus persecutiones, ad finem. Hortationes ad Sanctimoniam sunt sex; Prima generaliter est, ad vers. 7. reliquæ specialiores.
units.tr: This chapter pursues the same subject as the previous one. It has two parts. The first contains exhortations to holiness, down to verse 12. The second is consolatory, against persecutions, to the end. There are six exhortations to holiness. The first is general, up to verse 7; the rest are more specific.

units.la: Vers. 1. Quum igitur Christus passus sit pro nobis carne, vos quoque eadem cogitatione armamini; nempe quod qui passus est in carne, desitit à peccato.
units.tr: Verse 1. Since therefore Christ suffered for us in the flesh, arm yourselves also with the same mindset; namely, that he who has suffered in the flesh has ceased from sin.

units.la: Argumenta ad sanctimoniam in genere sunt septem, quæ ut melius concipiantur, tenendum est CHRISTUM in cruce pendentem, quatuor modis rem nostram egisse: Primò enim ut nos repræsentans judicialiter, seu personam sustinens nostram, reatum peccatorum nostrorum, & pœnam peccatis nostris debitam portabat & auferebat: 2. Ut Sponfor pro nobis suscipiebat in fe mortificationem, seu crucifixionem veteris nostri hominis, futuram virtute crucifixonis suæ: 3. Seipsum exemplar effi<ax proponebat nobis, cui nolmet conformaremus in noltri abnegatione, & renunciatione omnium quæ nobis ad cœlum tendentibus possent esse impedimento: 4. Ut Sponsor, Advocatus, Patronus, Pater, Maritus, Caput, & Persona communis nos multiplicibus vinculis juris constringebat, & obligabat ad moriendum peccato, & ad utendum omnibus mediis, quibus id fieri posset: His præsuppositis Argumenta quæ sequuntur constringunt fortius.
units.tr: There are seven general arguments for holiness. To grasp them better, we must hold that Christ, hanging on the cross, dealt with our cause in four ways. First, representing us judicially, or bearing our person, he carried and removed the guilt of our sins and the punishment due to them. Second, as our Surety he took upon himself the mortification, or crucifixion, of our old man, to be effected by the power of his own crucifixion. Third, he set himself before us as an effective example, to which we should conform ourselves by denying and renouncing everything that could hinder us as we make for heaven. Fourth, as Surety, Advocate, Patron, Father, Husband, Head, and common Person, he bound and obliged us by many bonds of law to die to sin and to use all the means by which this could be done. With these things presupposed, the arguments that follow press more strongly.

units.la: Argumentum primum, CHRISTUS passus est in carne pro nobis, & rem nostram egit publicè modis supra dictis. Ergo vos fideles Hebræi debetis vos armare hac meditatione fidei contra omnes tentationes, ut carnis corruptæ desideriis moriamini.
units.tr: First argument: Christ suffered in the flesh for us, and dealt with our cause publicly in the ways mentioned above. Therefore you faithful Hebrews ought to arm yourselves with this meditation of faith against all temptations, so that you may die to the desires of the corrupt flesh.

units.la: Qui passus est ] Arg. 2. Confirmans superius à judiciali nexu fidelium cum CHRISTO moriente, in quo passo in carne fideles, censentur tanquam passi etiam in carne: Sicut ergo qui passi sunt in carne, vel mortui sunt, deliterunt à peccato pro quo passi sunt & justificantur, tum à peccato, tum à pœnâ peccati, quâ jam defuncti sunt: Sic vos fideles Hebræi quos habeo pro judicialiter passis in carne, seu pro mortuis, desistere debetis à peccato, & nihil amplius cum eo negotii habere.
units.tr: Who suffered] Second argument. It confirms what was said above from the judicial union of believers with Christ dying, in whose suffering in the flesh the faithful are reckoned as having also suffered in the flesh. Just as those who have suffered in the flesh, or died, cease from sin, for which they suffered and are justified, both from sin and from the punishment of sin, by which they are already released; so you faithful Hebrews, whom I regard as judicially suffered in the flesh, or as dead, ought to cease from sin and have nothing more to do with it.

units.la: Verf. 2.
units.tr: Verse 2.

units.la: Ut non amplius cupiditatibus hominum, sed voluntati Dei, quod reliquum est temporis in carne vivat.
units.tr: So as no longer to live for the lusts of men, but for the will of God, the rest of the time in the flesh.

units.la: Arg. 3. Judicialis liberatio Fidelium à peccato, facta in morte CHRISTI, in eum finem fit, ut quandiu vivimus in hac mortali vita, tempus impendamus, non sectandis cupiditatibus carnalibus secundum voluntatem hominum, sed implendæ Dei voluntati. Ergo ut voluntati Dei conformes sitis vobis laborandum est.
units.tr: Third argument. The judicial deliverance of the faithful from sin, effected in the death of Christ, has this end: that as long as we live in this mortal life we should spend our time not in pursuing carnal lusts according to the will of men, but in fulfilling the will of God. Therefore you must labour to be conformed to the will of God.

units.la: Verf. 3 Satis enim est nobis quod anteacto vitæ tempore libidinem Gentium patraverimus, quum ingederemus in protervitis, cupiditatibus vinolentiis, comessationibus, compotationibus, & nefariis simulacrorum cultibus.
units.tr: Verse 3. For it is enough for us that in the past time of our life we have carried out the will of the Gentiles, when we walked in lewdness, lusts, drunkenness, revelries, carousings, and abominable worship of idols.

units.la: Arg. 4. Satis & plus nimium peccatum est adversus DEUM tempore vitæ præteritæ, cum vitia quæ in Gentibus regnant contra secundam & primam tabulam in ignorantia & incredulitate sectabamini: Tempus Lucis Evangelicæ jam alios poltulat mores: Ergo Sanctitati studendum est.
units.tr: Fourth argument. Enough, and more than enough, sin was committed against God in the time of your past life, when you pursued in ignorance and unbelief the vices that reign among the Gentiles, against the second and first tables of the law. The time of the Gospel light now demands other manners. Therefore holiness must be pursued.

units.la: Verf. 4. Quamobrem illi non concurrentibus vobis ad eandem luxus profusionem, peregrinari sibi videntes, blasphemant:
units.tr: Verse 4. Wherefore, since you do not join them in the same excess of riot, they are surprised and blaspheme,

units.la: Verf. 5. Qui reddituri sunt rationem ei qui paratus est ad judicandum vivos & mortuos.
units.tr: Verse 5. Who shall give account to him who is ready to judge the living and the dead.

units.la: Arg. 5. Per occupationem objectionis, Etiamsi infideles offendantur veltra abstinentia a pristinis vitiis, & blasphemient vestram religionem, blasphemiarum poenas daturi in die judicii, non tamen oportet vos propterea moveri, quia si non in hac vita, saltem in die judicii Deus exactissimus est rationem contumeliarum ejusmodi. Pergendum ergo in studio sanctimoniae.
units.tr: Fifth argument, by anticipating an objection. Even if unbelievers are offended at your abstinence from former vices, and blaspheme your religion, they will pay the penalties of their blasphemies on the day of judgment. Nevertheless you ought not on that account to be moved, because if not in this life, at least on the day of judgment, God is most exact in reckoning such insults. Therefore one must go on in the pursuit of holiness.

units.la: Verf. 6. Nam idcirco mortuis quoque praedicatum est Evangelium, ut damnarentur quidem secundum homines, id est, carne: viverent autem secundum Deum, id est, Spiritu:
units.tr: Verse 6. For this reason the Gospel was also preached to the dead, that they might indeed be judged according to men in the flesh, but live according to God in the Spirit.

units.la: Arg. 6 Faciens etiam ad tollendum scandalum positum ab infidelibus, qui blasphemabant & condemnabant Christianos ob morum dissimilitudinem: Fidelibus qui jam mortui sunt, sive non ita pridem, sive prioribus saeculis, Evangelium praedicatum est eodem fine quoad sanctitatem urgendam, & eodem successu quoad judicium mundanorum hominum, & denique eadem fructus seu utilitatis ipse, ut scilicet condemnati ab hominibus, & castigati a Deo, secundum carnem seu externum hominem, vitam spiritualem in animabus suis, seu interiori homine, imo & vitam aeternam apud Deum consequerentur. Ergo aequum est ut vos Hebraei fideles similem vivendi rationem, & conditionem non recusetis amplecti, sed ut eadem conditione sanctimoniae studeatis.
units.tr: Sixth argument, which also serves to remove the stumbling-block placed by unbelievers, who blasphemed and condemned Christians for their dissimilar manners. The Gospel was preached to believers who are now dead, whether not long ago or in earlier ages, with the same end of urging holiness, and with the same success as regards the judgment of worldly men. Finally, the same fruit or benefit was intended: that, condemned by men and chastened by God according to the flesh or the outward man, they might obtain spiritual life in their souls, that is, in the inner man, and even eternal life with God. Therefore it is fair that you Hebrew believers should not refuse to embrace a similar manner and condition of living, but should strive for holiness under the same condition.

units.la: Verf. 7. Omnium autem finis imminet. Estote igitur sobrii & vigilantes ad orandum.
units.tr: Verse 7. But the end of all things is at hand. Be therefore sober and watchful unto prayer.

units.la: Arg. 7. Instat judicium ultimum, quod commodis & incommodis hujus vitae omnibus impositurum est finem. Ergo nihil morantes vitae hujus commoda vel incommoda, sanctimoniae vobis est studendum.
units.tr: Seventh argument. The last judgment is at hand, which will put an end to all the advantages and disadvantages of this life. Therefore, not delaying over the advantages or disadvantages of this life, you must pursue holiness.

units.la: Estote igitur Ex his argumentis & potissimum ex ultimo infert hortationem ad sanctitatem, & specialiter ad sex virtutes Christianas.
units.tr: Be therefore] From these arguments, and especially from the last, he draws the exhortation to holiness, and specifically to six Christian virtues.

units.la: Ad preces Pun a speciali hortatio est ad sedulo precandum, & in eum finem, ut sobrii & vigilantes sint, quo aptiores essent ad precandum, observantes omnem occasionem precandi, & ut in omnibus suis negotiis ita se gerant, ut ad precandum non inepti redderentur.
units.tr: Unto prayer] Here is a specific exhortation to pray diligently, and to this end: that they may be sober and watchful, so as to be better fitted for prayer, seizing every occasion to pray, and so conducting themselves in all their affairs that they would not be rendered unfit for prayer.

units.la: Verf. 8. Ante omnia vero charitatem alii in alios propensam habentes: nam charitas operiet multitudinem peccatorum.
units.tr: Verse 8. Above all things, having fervent charity among yourselves; for charity shall cover a multitude of sins.

units.la: Hortatio 2. Specialis ad charitatem; quam primo singulari cura prosequendam ante omnia vult, deinde ut fervida & intensa sit, requirit.
units.tr: Second exhortation, specific to charity, which he wills to be pursued above all things with singular care, and then requires that it be fervent and intense.

units.la: Charitas ] Hujus rationem specialem reddit, Quia charitas praevenit, & praeveniendo operit iras, rixas, opprobria, contentiones & odia, ne excitentur inter homines, & in apertum prorumpant, & ne serpant, erumpentia haec mala reprimit, condonat, & tegit, ideoque ei imprimis studendum est.
units.tr: Charity] He gives a special reason for this: charity goes before, and by going before it covers angers, quarrels, reproaches, contentions and hatreds, so that they are not stirred up among men and do not break out into the open or creep along. Charity restrains, forgives, and hides these evils as they erupt; therefore it is above all to be pursued.

units.la: Verf. 9. Hospitales esse ote alii erga alios, sine murmurationibus.
units.tr: Verse 9. Be hospitable to one another without murmuring.

units.la: Hortatio 3. Ad hospitalitatem, quam voluntariam & non coactam jubet esse: nam quae cum murmuratione conjungitur beneficentia charitate destituitur.
units.tr: Third exhortation, to hospitality, which he commands to be voluntary and not forced. For beneficence that is joined with murmuring lacks charity.

units.la: Verf. 10. Ut quisque accepit donum, ita alium in alium illud subministrantes, ut boni dispensatores variae Dei gratiae.
units.tr: Verse 10. As each has received a gift, so minister it to one another, as good stewards of the manifold grace of God.

units.la: Hortatio 4. Ad mutuam communionem omnium donorum Dei, Rationes hortationis includuntur duae. Prima, Quia dona sunt ex gratia, & a Deo in usum communem conceduntur.
units.tr: Fourth exhortation, to the mutual sharing of all the gifts of God. Two reasons for the exhortation are included. The first: because the gifts are from grace, and are granted by God for common use.

units.la: Ut Boni ] Ratio 2. Quia qui donum habet non est ejus doni Dominus, sed dispensator.
units.tr: As good] Second reason: because he who has a gift is not its lord, but its steward.

units.la: Verf. 11. Si quis loquitur, loquitur ut eloquia Dei; si quis ministrat, ministret tanquam ex viribus quas suppeditat Deus: ut in omnibus glorificetur Deus per Iesum Christum, cui est gloria & imperium in saecula saeculorum. Amen.
units.tr: Verse 11. If anyone speaks, let him speak as the oracles of God; if anyone ministers, let him minister as of the strength which God supplies; that in all things God may be glorified through Jesus Christ, to whom belong glory and dominion for ever and ever. Amen.

units.la: Hortatio 5. specialior, Ut qui loquitur verbum Dei (sive ex officio speciali, ut Pastor vel Doctor, sive ex officio communi, ut alii Christiani, in mutua sui aedificatione) loquatur cum ea reverentia & fide, quae decet Dei Verbum, hoc est, ut loquens recte conceptum Verbi Divini sensum ex fide, cum reverentia quam Dei veritas requirit, profetat, ne Dei nomen sumatur in vanum.
units.tr: Fifth and more specific exhortation: that whoever speaks the word of God (whether by a special office, as a minister or teacher, or by the common office of other Christians in their mutual edification) should speak with that reverence and faith which befit the Word of God. That is, the speaker should declare with faith, and with the reverence which the truth of God requires, the rightly conceived sense of the divine Word, so that the name of God is not taken in vain.

units.la: Ministrat Hortatio 6. Ut qui vel ope, vel facultatibus suis, aliorum necessitatibus ministrat, illud praestet prompte & hilariter pro viribus, quas ei Deus suppeditavit. Rationes hortationis sunt duae.
units.tr: He ministers Exhortation 6. Whoever serves others, whether by his help or by his means, should do so promptly and cheerfully, according to the strength that God has given him. There are two reasons for this exhortation.

units.la: Ut in ] Ratio prima, Ut Deo cedat gloria, & ex opere nostro & ex agendi modo.
units.tr: That in] The first reason: that glory may accrue to God both from our work and from the manner in which we perform it.

units.la: Per Iesum ] Ratio 2. Ut Deo cedat gloria per Christum, cujus solius gratia & virtute officium praestatur. Has hortationes claudit Doxologia, ad quam ex consideratione dignitatis Dei, rapitur.
units.tr: Through Jesus] The second reason: that glory may accrue to God through Christ, by whose grace and power alone the duty is performed. These exhortations are closed by the doxology, to which the mind is carried by consideration of God's dignity.

units.la: Secunda pars.
units.tr: Second part.

units.la: Vers. 12. Charissimi, ne tanquam hospites, exploratione illa per ignem quae fit in vobis ad veStri experimentum, percellimini, ut si peregrinum aliquid vobis accideret.
units.tr: 1 Peter 4:12. Beloved, do not think it strange concerning the fiery trial which is among you to try you, as though some strange thing happened to you.

units.la: Altera pars Capitis, In qua adversus persequutiones animat fideles & hortatur ne offendantur, aut perturbentur persequutionibus tanquam re nova. Argumenta hortationis sunt tredecim, quae omnia probant non metuendam persequutionem ob Euangelii professionem.
units.tr: The second part of the chapter, in which the apostle encourages the faithful against persecutions and exhorts them not to be offended or disturbed by persecutions as if they were something new. There are thirteen arguments for this exhortation, all of which prove that persecution for the profession of the Gospel is not to be feared.

units.la: Argumentum primum, Persequutio non est vos laesura, sed exploratura & purgatura, quemadmodum ignis explorat & purgat aurum & argentum. Ergo non metuenda est vobis persequutio.
units.tr: First argument: persecution is not going to harm you but to test and purify you, just as fire tests and purifies gold and silver. Therefore persecution is not to be feared by you.

units.la: Vers. 13. Imo in eo quod consortes estis afflictionum Christi, gaudete ut & quum patefiet ejus gloria, gaudeatis, exultantes.
units.tr: 1 Peter 4:13. But rejoice, inasmuch as you are partakers of Christ's sufferings; that when his glory shall be revealed, you may also be glad with exceeding joy.

units.la: Arg. 2. Gaudendum potius & laetandum in afflictionibus ob Euangelium. Ergo non metuenda persequutio. Arg. 3. confirmans superius, Persequutionem patientes participes estis afflictionum, Christi membris destinatarum, & conformes reddimini Christo, qui similia passus est ob confessionem veritatis. Non metuenda ergo persequutio. Arg. 4. Quia communionem gloriae & gaudii cum Christo habituri estis in ejus adventu. Ergo.
units.tr: Second argument: one should rather rejoice and be glad in afflictions for the Gospel. Therefore persecution is not to be feared. Third argument, confirming what was said above: by suffering persecution you are partakers of Christ's afflictions, which are appointed for Christ's members, and you are made conformable to Christ, who suffered similar things for the confession of the truth. Therefore persecution is not to be feared. Fourth argument: because you will have fellowship with Christ in his glory and joy at his coming. Therefore, etc.

units.la: Vers. 14. Si probris afficimini in nomine Christi: beati estis: quoniam & ille gloriae & ille Dei Spiritus super vos requiescit, qui quod ad illos quidem attinet blasphematur, quod ad vos autem: glorificatur.
units.tr: 1 Peter 4:14. If you are reproached for the name of Christ, you are blessed; for the Spirit of glory and of God rests upon you: on their part he is blasphemed, but on your part he is glorified.

units.la: Arg. 5. Qui vel probris afficiuntur propter nomen Christi, beatitudinis suae habent & medium, & indicium; multo magis illi qui graviora patiuntur: Ergo vobis metuenda non est persequutio.
units.tr: Fifth argument: those who are reviled for the name of Christ have both the means and the sign of their blessedness; much more so those who suffer heavier things. Therefore persecution is not to be feared by you.

units.la: Arg. 6. Tolerantia crucis Christi est indicium Spiritus Christi gloriosi quiescentis super vos, & nunquam a vobis discessuri: Ergo persequutio vobis non est metuenda. Quod ad] Arg. 7. confirmans superius, D e i Spiritus licet à parte perlequentium blalphemetur; à fidelibus tamen perfequutionem patientibus glorificatur. Ergo vobis non elt metuenda perlequutio.
units.tr: Sixth argument: the endurance of Christ's cross is a sign of the glorious Spirit of Christ resting upon you, and who will never depart from you. Therefore persecution is not to be feared by you. As to what] Seventh argument, confirming what was said above: though the Spirit of God is blasphemed on the part of the persecutors, yet he is glorified by the faithful who suffer persecution. Therefore persecution is not to be feared by you.

units.la: Verf. 15. Nequis igitur vestûn affligatur ut homicida, aut fur, aut maleficus, aut alienarum rerum inspestor:
units.tr: 1 Peter 4:15. Let none of you therefore suffer as a murderer, or a thief, or an evildoer, or as a meddler in other men's matters.

units.la: Ve f. 16 Sed si ut Christianus, ne pudesiat, imo glorificet Deum hac in parte.
units.tr: 1 Peter 4:16. But if as a Christian, let him not be ashamed; but let him glorify God on this behalf.

units.la: Arg. 8. Etiamsi omnis afflistio, & nominatim ob maleficia, non fit gloriola, cum tamen quis non suo merito afficitur malo (sed Christi nomine seu quia & quatenus est Christianus) afflistio gloriola elt, nec debet ita pertuibari) afflictus,quasi puderet ipsum nominis Christi, sed Deum potius glorificare tenetur, qui martyrii quolibet gradu ipsum honoravit. Non ergo vobis metuenda persequutio.
units.tr: Eighth argument: even if every affliction, especially one inflicted for wrongdoing, is not a matter of glory, yet when someone is afflicted not for his own evil deserts but for the name of Christ, that is, because and insofar as he is a Christian, the affliction is glorious, and the one afflicted ought not to be troubled as if ashamed of the name of Christ, but is bound rather to glorify God, who has honoured him in whatever degree of martyrdom. Therefore persecution is not to be feared by you.

units.la: Verf. 17. Nam tempus est quo incipiat judicium à domo Dei, quòd si primum incipit à nobis, quis erit finis eorum qui non parent Dei Euangelio?
units.tr: 1 Peter 4:17. For the time is come that judgment must begin at the house of God; and if it first begin at us, what shall the end be of them that obey not the gospel of God?

units.la: Arg. 9. Judicium quod Deus exercitypus est in hominum peccata, inchoatur in Ecclesia, ut in familia Dei, in domesticos suos: quorum peccata castigat Deus, & crucifigit per crucem Christi. Ergo vo-bis non est metuenda persequutio.
units.tr: Ninth argument: the judgment which God exercises upon the sins of men begins in the Church, as in the family of God, upon his own household, whose sins God chastises and crucifies through the cross of Christ. Therefore persecution is not to be feared by you.

units.la: Quis erit] Arg. 10. Afflictiones quas patiuntur fideles, argumento sunt fore ut infideles & persequutores tandem gravissimè puniantur: Ergo non metuenda vobis est persequutio.
units.tr: What shall the end be] Tenth argument: the afflictions which the faithful suffer are an argument that the unbelievers and persecutors will at last be most severely punished. Therefore persecution is not to be feared by you.

units.la: Verf. 18, Et, si justus vix servatur, impius & peccator ubi comparebit?
units.tr: 1 Peter 4:18. And if the righteous is scarcely saved, where shall the ungodly and the sinner appear?

units.la: Arg. 11. superius argumentum declarans, Cum fidelium conditio adeo fit dura, ut non sine difficultate & per afflictiones servantur, intolerabilis proculdubio erit conditio impiorum. Ergo nec à fide deficiendum, ne pereatis, neque à persequutoribus metuendum, quia illi periturí sunt.
units.tr: Eleventh argument, declaring the above argument more fully: since the condition of the faithful is so hard that they are saved not without difficulty and through afflictions, the condition of the wicked will undoubtedly be intolerable. Therefore one must neither fall away from the faith, lest you perish, nor fear the persecutors, because they are destined to perish.

units.la: Verf. 19 Itaque qui affliguntur ex voluntate DEI, tanquam fideli Conditiori commendent animas suas bene faciendo.
units.tr: 1 Peter 4:19. Wherefore let them that suffer according to the will of God commit their souls to him in well doing, as to a faithful Creator.

units.la: Hinc infert hortationem confirmandam unà cum argumentis duobus aliis. Arg. 12 est. Qui malis afficiuntur nomine Christi, proprie affliguntur non ex voluntate hominum, sed ex voluntate Dei; qui per afflictiones opus suum in suis perficere statuit. Ergo non est vobis metuenda persecutio.
units.tr: From this he draws an exhortation, to be confirmed together with two other arguments. The twelfth argument is this: those who are afflicted for the name of Christ are properly afflicted not by the will of men but by the will of God, who has determined to complete his work in his own people through afflictions. Therefore persecution is not to be feared by you.

units.la: Fideli ] Arg. 13. Qui patiuntur in carne aliquid pro Christo, & cui in sanctimonia pergere statuerunt, quod bonum est facientes, certi & securi esse poterunt de salute animarum suarum, & quia Deus omnipotens est, & quia fidelis est ad praestandum omnia quae suis promisit. Ergo vobis non est metuenda persecutio.
units.tr: Faithful] Thirteenth argument: those who suffer something in the flesh for Christ, and who have resolved to persevere in holiness, doing what is good, can be certain and secure concerning the salvation of their souls, both because God is almighty and because he is faithful to perform all that he has promised to his people. Therefore persecution is not to be feared by you.

units.la: Caput Quintum.
units.tr: Chapter Five.

units.la: Estant hortationes tres, cum Epilogo, Prima ad Presbyteros, altera ad juniores. Tertia communis, ad omnes. PResbyteros qui inter vos sunt, precor ego unà presbyter, ac testis afflictionum Christi, atque idem gloriæ patefaciendæ consors.
units.tr: There are three exhortations, with an epilogue: the first to the elders, the second to the younger members, and the third common to all. Presbyters who are among you I exhort, I who am a fellow-elder with you, and a witness of the sufferings of Christ, and also a partaker of the glory that is to be revealed.

units.la: Verf. 2 Pascite Dei gregem qui penes vos est, curam illius agentes non coactè, sed libenter; non turpiter affectantes lucrum, sed prompto animo:
units.tr: Verse 2: Feed the flock of God which is among you, taking the oversight thereof, not by constraint, but willingly; not for filthy lucre, but of a ready mind.

units.la: Hortatio 1. ad presbyteros primo in genere. Ut munus suum exequantur, pascendo gregem sibi commissum. Rationes hortationis à persona hortantis præmittuntur quatuor. Precor ] Ratio prima, Quia Apostolus id precatur & submisse flagitat ab iis. Una presbyter ] Ratio 2. Quia ut consors, & socius in munere Presbyteratus, hortatur.
units.tr: The first exhortation, to the elders, is that they should discharge their office by feeding the flock committed to them. Four reasons for the exhortation are set out first, from the person of the one exhorting. I exhort: the first reason is that the Apostle entreats and humbly asks them. A fellow-elder: the second reason is that he exhorts them as a partner and companion in the office of the eldership.

units.la: Testis ] Ratio 3. Quia testis erat afflictionum CHRISTI, quas Christus in muneris sui executione passus est, & particeps afflictionum pro CHRISTO cum aliis martyribus. Gloriæ ] Ratio 4. Quia per fidem particeps erat gloriæ veris pastoribus olim communicandæ in adventu Domini. Pascite ] Ipsa hortatio modum pascendi gregem præscribens speciatim in quatuor officiis.
units.tr: A witness: the third reason is that he was a witness of the sufferings of Christ, which Christ endured in the execution of his office, and a partaker with other martyrs in sufferings for Christ. Of the glory: the fourth reason is that through faith he was a partaker of the glory that was to be communicated to true ministers at the coming of the Lord. Feed: the exhortation itself prescribes the manner of feeding the flock, particularly in four duties.

units.la: Inspectioni ] Primum, Ut vacent diligenter inspectioni gregis, non leviter & perfunctoriè rem agentes: 2. Ut officium faciant, non coactè sed libenter: 3. Non turpis lucri gratia, sed animo prompto, & liberali officio fungantur. Verf. 3. Neque ut dominantes cleris, sed ut qui situ exem-plaria gregu.
units.tr: Oversight: first, that they should devote themselves diligently to the oversight of the flock, not performing the task carelessly or perfunctorily; second, that they should do the work not by constraint but willingly; third, that they should carry out the office not for the sake of base gain, but with a ready and generous mind. Verse 3: Neither as being lords over God's heritage, but being ensamples to the flock.

units.la: Quarto, ut fine usurpatione dominii in Ecclesiam, doctrinâ, & exemplo præirent Ecclesiæ in omnibus virtutibus.
units.tr: Fourth, that without usurping dominion over the Church, they should go before the Church by teaching and example in all virtues.

units.la: Verf. 4 Et yuum apparuerit ille Pastorum princeps, reportabitis immarceffibilem illam gloriæ coronam.
units.tr: Verse 4: And when the chief Shepherd shall appear, ye shall receive a crown of glory that fadeth not away.

units.la: Subjungit hortationi rationes alias tres. Princeps] Ratio prima, Quia Iesus Christus ut Pastorum princeps aliquando manifestandus est, qui à subjectis sibi pastoribus rationem exactui us est administrati officii.
units.tr: He adds three further reasons to the exhortation. The chief: the first reason is that Jesus Christ, as the chief Shepherd, is to be made manifest at some time, and he will require an account of the office faithfully administered from the shepherds subject to him.

units.la: Reportabitis] Ratio 2. Quia pro præmio daturus est coronam gloriæ fidelibus Pastoribus Amarantinum] Ratio 3. Quia corona illa futura est florida & quæ nunquam marcescet, nedum peribit.
units.tr: Ye shall receive: the second reason is that he will give a crown of glory as a reward to faithful shepherds. Unfading: the third reason is that the crown to come will be flourishing and will never wither, much less perish.

units.la: Verf. 5. Similiter juniores subjecti estote senioribus; & omnes vicissim subjicimini Modesti estote intus ornati; nam DEVS superbis resistit, humilibus autem dat gratiam.
units.tr: Verse 5: Likewise, ye younger, submit yourselves unto the elder. Yea, all of you be subject one to another, and be clothed with humility: for God resisteth the proud, and giveth grace to the humble.

units.la: Secunda hortatio ad gregem seu populum, qui nomine juniorum insignitur, quia sicut ordinarió Presbyteri maxima ex parte electi erant ex senioribus ætate, sic maxima pars greges constabat ex junioribus.
units.tr: This is the second exhortation, to the flock or people, who are designated by the name of the younger, because just as the elders were ordinarily for the most part chosen from those older in age, so the greater part of the flock consisted of the younger.

units.la: Subjecti] Hortationis membra sunt tria. Primum ad subjectionem speciali erga Presbyteros, ut sicut Episcopatum injunxerat Deus Presbyteris, sic sim liter subjectionem injunxerat gregi, seu junioribus, ut Presbyteris officium facientibus, & nomine Dei recta jubentibus, obedirent.
units.tr: Submit: the exhortation has three parts. The first is to a special submission toward the elders: just as God had enjoined the episcopate upon the elders, so likewise he had enjoined submission upon the flock, or the younger, that they should obey the elders while they perform their office and command what is right in the name of God.

units.la: Et omnes] Secundum membrum hortationis est ad subjectionem communem seu mutuam, ut vicissim subjiciantur, nempe ad officia charitatis humillima mutuò præstanda, E. g. ad privatas admonitiones vicissim recipiendas, & ad infirmitates mutuas tolerandas.
units.tr: And all: the second part of the exhortation is to a common or mutual submission, that they should submit to one another in turn, namely by mutually rendering the most humble offices of love, for example by receiving private admonitions in turn and by bearing with one another's infirmities.

units.la: Submissione] Tertium membrum hortationis, ut studeant animi submissioni, seu humilitati Christianæ, absque qua, nec possent Pastoribus, nec sibi invicem rite subjici. Rationes hortationis sunt septem.
units.tr: Submission: the third part of the exhortation is that they should strive for a submissiveness of mind, or Christian humility, without which they could not rightly be subject either to the ministers or to one another. There are seven reasons for the exhortation.

units.la: Ornati] Ratio prima, Quia humilitas seu submissio ornamentum est speciale. Deus] Ratio 2. Quia Deus superbis resistit. Submissis] Ratio 3. Quia humilibus Deus dat gratiam.
units.tr: Clothed: the first reason is that humility or submissiveness is a special ornament. God: the second reason is that God resists the proud. The humble: the third reason is that God gives grace to the humble.

units.la: Verf. 6. Submittite igitur vosipsos potenti manui Dei, ut vos in tempore extollat;
units.tr: Verse 6: Humble yourselves therefore under the mighty hand of God, that he may exalt you in due time.

units.la: Ratio 4. Quia submissio illa mutuò requisita, non tam homines quam Deum respicit, qui illam submissionem praecipit. Quia robur & potestas Dei ad subjectionem movere vos debet:
units.tr: Fourth reason: that mutual submission required of them looks not so much to men as to God, who commands that submission. Fifth reason: the strength and power of God ought to move you to submission.

units.la: Ratio 6. Quia submissos & humiles Deus opportuno tempore exaltaturus est ad gloriam.
units.tr: Sixth reason: God will exalt the submissive and humble to glory at the proper time.

units.la: Vers. 7. Omnem curam vestram in eum conjecta: nam illi cura est de vobis.
units.tr: Verse 7: Casting all your care upon him; for he careth for you.

units.la: Ratio 7 per occupationem objectionis, Quia non debetis moveri incommodis illis quae dissuadere possent ab hac submissione animi, sed solicitudinem de eventu obedientiae, huic mandato praestandae, & omnem insuper curam vestram, quae hanc vitam spectat in Deum conjicere debetis. Hujus ratio redditur, quia Deus res servorum suorum, & quae vobis in obedientia ipsius ambulantibus accidere possunt, curat diligenter, ne quid detrimenti vobis accidat, & ne quid boni necessarii vobis desit.
units.tr: Seventh reason, by anticipating an objection: you ought not to be moved by those inconveniences which might dissuade you from this submissiveness of mind, but you must cast all anxiety about the outcome of obedience to this command, and indeed all your care that concerns this life, upon God. The reason for this is given: God diligently cares for the affairs of his servants, and for whatever can happen to you while you walk in obedience to him, so that no harm befalls you and no necessary good is lacking to you.

units.la: Vers. 8. Sobrii estote: vigilate, nam adversarius vester Diabolus tanquam leo rugiens obambulat, quaerens quem devoret.
units.tr: Verse 8: Be sober, be vigilant; because your adversary the devil, as a roaring lion, walketh about, seeking whom he may devour.

units.la: Tertia hortatio generalis seu communis omnibus, Ne carnis securitati indulgeant, sed ut compositi ad vigilantiam in omni sobrietate, contra omnem tentationem pergant in gratia quam acceperunt.
units.tr: The third exhortation, general or common to all: that they should not indulge in the security of the flesh, but, being disposed to watchfulness in all sobriety, should persevere in the grace they have received against every temptation.

units.la: Rationes hortationis ad Christianam hanc militiam sunt novem.
units.tr: There are nine reasons for this exhortation to Christian warfare.

units.la: Adversarius ] Ratio prima, Quia res est vobis cum adversario. Diabolus ] Ratio 2. Quia vobis res est, cum Diabolo hostium pessimo. Ut Leo ] Ratio 3. Quia Diabolus crudeliter ut Leo rugiens praedae inhiat. Obambulat ] Ratio 4 Quia, ut vulpes circumspicit & captat obambulans omnes occasiones nocendi, ut incautos vos opprimat & absorbeat.
units.tr: Adversary: the first reason is that you have to do with an adversary. Devil: the second reason is that you have to do with the Devil, the most wicked of enemies. As a lion: the third reason is that the Devil, roaring like a lion, cruelly gapes for prey. Walketh about: the fourth reason is that, like a fox, he goes about watching and lying in wait for every opportunity to harm, so that he may overwhelm and swallow you while you are unwary.

units.la: Vers. 9. Cui resistite firmi per fidem, scientes eandem afflictiones à vestra quae in mundo est fraternitate implere.
units.tr: Verse 9: Whom resist stedfast in the faith, knowing that the same afflictions are accomplished in your brethren that are in the world.

units.la: Ratio 5, Quia de fuga ab adversario non est cogitandum, sed de ei resistendo tantum, idque per fidem firmam.
units.tr: Fifth reason: one must not think of flight from the adversary, but only of resisting him, and that with a firm faith.

units.la: Ut qui ] Ratio 7. Quia non soli certatis in hoc certamine afflictionum contra Diabolum, sed omnes ubique fratres fideles in Ecclesia militante habent commilitones, & una vobiscum patientes, quorum conditionem non debetis aversari, aut aliqua meliori quam illorum conditione frui velle.
units.tr: As those who: seventh reason: you are not the only ones contending in this struggle of afflictions against the Devil, but all faithful brethren everywhere in the militant Church have fellow soldiers, who suffer along with you, and whose condition you ought not to shun, or wish to enjoy any better condition than theirs.

units.la: Vers. 10. Caeterum Deus omnis gratiae autor, qui vocavit nos ad aeternam ad æternam suam gloriam in Christo Iesu, paulisper afflictos, is, inquam, absolutos vos reddat, stabiliat, roboret, fundet-.
units.tr: Verse 10: But the God of all grace, who hath called us unto his eternal glory by Christ Jesus, after that ye have suffered a while, make you perfect, stablish, strengthen, settle you.

units.la: Ratio 8, Quia me Apostolum vestrum habituri estis unà vobiscum, certantem in precibus, ut constanter pergatis in via cæpta. Precatur autem pro iis hæc quatuor: Primo, Ut Deus perficiat quod inchoatum, & nondum perfectum est opus gratiæ: 2. Ut stabiliat quod rectum est: 3. Ut roboret quod infirmum est: 4. Ut fundet, seu ut cohærere faciat firmiter cum Christo quod ædificatum est. Argumenta fiduciæ duo sunt. Arg. 1. Omnisufficientia gratiæ in Deo: 2. Vocatio fidelium ad æternam gloriam per Christum.
units.tr: Eighth reason: you will have me, your Apostle, together with you, striving in prayers that you may persevere steadfastly on the way you have begun. He prays for them in these four things: first, that God would perfect the work of grace which is begun but not yet complete; second, that he would stablish what is right; third, that he would strengthen what is weak; fourth, that he would settle, that is, make firmly cohere with Christ what has been built up. There are two arguments for confidence. First argument: the all-sufficiency of grace in God. Second: the calling of believers to eternal glory through Christ.

units.la: Paulisper] Interim limitat orationem suam, ut Deus ista præstet ipsis paululum afflictis, & sic addit Rationem nonam hortationis ad Christianam militiam: Quia tempus certaminis vestri non est futurum longum, sed breve; & afflictiones non intolerabiles, sed in comparatione ad gloriam, leves.
units.tr: A while: he now limits his prayer, so that God would grant these things to them, who are a little afflicted; and so he adds the ninth reason for Christian warfare: the time of your struggle will not be long but short, and the afflictions are not intolerable but, in comparison with the glory, light.

units.la: Verf. 11. Ipsi gloria & robur in secula seculorum. Amen.
units.tr: Verse 11: To him be glory and dominion for ever and ever. Amen.

units.la: Hanc & reliquas hortationes claudit insigni doxologia, adscribendo Deo gloriam omnis gratiæ & roboris, quo opus gratiæ prosequatur & perficiat.
units.tr: He concludes this and the remaining exhortations with a remarkable doxology, ascribing to God the glory of all grace and strength, by which he may carry forward and perfect the work of grace.

units.la: Verf. 12. Per Sylvanum vobis (ut opinor) fidelem fratrem paucis scripsi, adhortans vos, & testificans hanc esse veram gratiam Dei in qua statis.
units.tr: Verse 12: By Silvanus, a faithful brother unto you, as I suppose, I have written briefly, exhorting you, and testifying that this is the true grace of God wherein ye stand.

units.la: Epilogus Epistolæ cujus tres sunt articuli.
units.tr: The epilogue of the Epistle, which has three articles.

units.la: Articulus primus tria continet, Primum Tabellarii nomen & commendationem ab ipsius fidelitate: 2. Epistolæ commendationem à brevitate: 3. Scopum & summam totius Epistolæ, nempe ut confirmentur Hebræi de veritate doctrinæ Evangelii, seu gratia Christi quam profitebantur, & ut animentur ad constanter pergendum in ejus fide & obedientiâ.
units.tr: The first article contains three things: first, the name of the bearer and his commendation from his faithfulness; second, the commendation of the Epistle from its brevity; third, the aim and sum of the whole Epistle, namely that the Hebrews may be confirmed in the truth of the doctrine of the Gospel, that is, in the grace of Christ which they profess, and be encouraged to persevere steadfastly in its faith and obedience.

units.la: Verf. 13. Salutat vos ea quæ est Babylone vobiscum electa Ecclesia, & Marcus Filius meus.
units.tr: Ver. 13. The chosen Church that is in Babylon, along with you, salutes you, and Mark my son.

units.la: Art. 2. Continet salutationem nunciatam ab Ecclesia Babylonica & Marco Evangelista, (qui propter fidei, morumque similitudinem filius dicitur Petri, sicut Timotheus Pauli) ad reliquos Hebræos ejusdem gratiæ, & electionis in Christo participes. Babylonem hic intelligimus proprie dictam quæ in Chaldæa erat, ubi post exactos 70. Captivitatis annos mansere multi Judæi qui domum non sunt reversi, & in qua synagogas habebant, sicut in aliis civitatibus, quorum gratiâ Petrus ex pacto cum Paulo, ut Apostolus Hebræorum profectus est Babylonem, ubi frequentia Judæorum major erat: unde hanc epistolam ad reliquos dispersos scripsit.
units.tr: Art. 2. It contains a greeting sent by the Church at Babylon and by Mark the Evangelist (who, on account of the likeness of faith and manners, is called the son of Peter, just as Timothy is called the son of Paul) to the rest of the Hebrews who share in the same grace and election in Christ. Here we understand Babylon properly so called, which was in Chaldea, where after the seventy years of captivity many Jews remained who did not return home, and where they had synagogues, as in other cities. Peter, by agreement with Paul that he would be apostle to the Hebrews, went to Babylon for their sake, since the number of Jews there was greater; hence he wrote this epistle to the rest who were scattered.

units.la: Vers. 14. Salutate alii alios charitatis osculo. Pax vobis omnibus qui estis in Christo Iesu. Amen.
units.tr: Ver. 14. Greet one another with a kiss of charity. Peace be with you all who are in Christ Jesus. Amen.

units.la: Articulus 3. Continet, 1. Salutationem præceptam ab Apostolo, qua jubet Fideles osculo, seu ordinariis signis charitatis, sine simulatione se invicem salutare: 2. Votum Apostolicum, quo sub nomine Pacis salutem fidelibus omnibus, omniaque quæ ad sanctitatem, & felicitatem faciunt, ex gratuiti favoris fonte exoptat, comprecatur, applicat, & obsignat.
units.tr: Article 3. It contains: (1) the greeting commanded by the Apostle, by which he bids the faithful to greet one another with a kiss, that is, with the customary signs of love, without pretence; (2) the apostolic wish, by which, under the name of peace, he prays for, applies and seals salvation to all the faithful, and all things that contribute to holiness and happiness, desiring them from the fountain of free favour.

units.la: EXPOSITIO ANALYTICA POSTERIORIS EPISTOLAE PETRI. Summarium.
units.tr: EXPOSITION ANALYTICAL OF THE SECOND EPISTLE OF PETER. Summary.
