units.la: Orti jam vicinus Apostolus extremum hoc voluntatis suae testimonium, (ut apparet ex Capite primo. verf. 12, 13, &c.) in usum omnium ubique Fidelium, maximè Hebraeorum, quorum doctor fuerat, quasi testamentum condens in hac Epistola consignat. Partes Epistolae praecipuae sunt tres, pro numero Capitum: In prima hortatur ad Studium proficiendi in vera fide & pietate Christiana, Capite primo: In secunda dehortatur ab audiendis Pseudoprophetis, quos in Ecclesia exorituros praedicit, Capite secundo. In Tertia profanos irrisores, qui adventum CHRISTI ad judicium pro fabula habent, serio cavendos esse monet, Capite tertio.
units.tr: The Apostle, now close to his death, (as appears from Chapter 1, verses 12, 13, etc.) sets this last testimony of his will in writing in this Epistle, as though drawing up a testament, for the use of all the faithful everywhere, especially the Hebrews, whose teacher he had been. The principal parts of the Epistle are three, according to the number of the Chapters: In the first he exhorts them to strive to advance in true faith and Christian piety, Chapter 1; in the second he dissuades them from listening to the false prophets whom he foretells will arise in the Church, Chapter 2; in the third he warns them earnestly to beware of the profane scoffers who regard the coming of CHRIST to judgment as a fable, Chapter 3.

units.la: Caput Primum.
units.tr: Chapter 1.

units.la: Capitis tres sunt partes: In prima est Epistolæ exordium, ad verf. 5. In secundâ, hortatio ad proficiendum in fide & pietate, ad verf. 19 In tertiâ, digreditur in commendationem Scripturæ Propheticæ, ad finem.
units.tr: The chapter has three parts: the first is the introduction to the Epistle, down to verse 5; the second is the exhortation to advance in faith and piety, to verse 19; the third turns to the commendation of prophetic Scripture, to the end.

units.la: Verf. 1. Simeon Petrus servus & Apostolus Iesu Christi, iis qui æquè pretiosam fidem nobiscum sortiti sunt per justitiam Dei nostri, & servatoris Iesu Christi:
units.tr: Verse 1. Simeon Peter, a servant and apostle of Jesus Christ, to those who have obtained a faith equally precious with ours, through the righteousness of our God and Saviour Jesus Christ:

units.la: Inscriptio Epistolæ tria continet: 1. est descriptio Scriptoris à nomine communi Simeon, & cognomine à Christo ei impositio, Petrus, unà cum officio in Ecclesia generali Servus: Et speciali, unde autoritas ad scribendum data, Apostolus Iesu Christi. Secundum est, descriptio Fidelium ad quos scribitur à fidei quâ donati sunt, præstantia: cujus excellentia ad distinctionem fidei historicæ proponitur: 1. Quod pretiosa sit: 2. Quod sit Electorum propria, non hypocritica: 3. Quod æquè pretiosa sit, atque erat fides Apostolorum; gradum & quantitatem non comparat, sed qualitatem, & naturam doni, quia ab eodem Spiritu Sancto, ab iisdem Christi meritis, & ad eadem bona, Christum scilicet & ejus beneficia apprehendendum, erat data: 4. Quod profluat à Dei justitia, seu fidelitate, gratuitas promissiones Patribus factas fideliter præstante, & per Justitiam Iesu Christi Dei nostri, unà cum omnibus aliis bonis ad nos derivetur.
units.tr: The address of the Epistle contains three things. 1. There is a description of the writer, from his common name Simeon and his surname Peter, given him by Christ, together with his office: in the Church at large, a servant; and in particular, the source of his authority to write, an apostle of Jesus Christ. Second, there is a description of the faithful to whom he writes, from the excellence of the faith by which they were endowed. Its excellence is set against historical faith, and is shown in four ways: 1. that it is precious; 2. that it belongs to the elect, not to hypocrites; 3. that it is equally precious with the faith of the apostles. He does not compare degree or quantity but the quality and nature of the gift, since it was given by the same Holy Spirit, through the same merits of Christ, and for the same blessings, namely to apprehend Christ and his benefits; 4. that it flows from the justice of God, that is, his faithfulness in fulfilling the free promises made to the fathers, and that through the righteousness of Jesus Christ our God it is conveyed to us together with all other blessings.

units.la: Verf. 2. Gratia vobis & pax multiplicetur per agnitionem Dei, & Iesu Domini nostri.
units.tr: Verse 2. Grace and peace be multiplied to you through the knowledge of God and of Jesus our Lord.

units.la: Tertium in Epistolæ inscriptione est Salutatio, in quâ votum & voti confirmatio. In voto optat omnibus Hebræis fidelibus ampliorem manifestationem, multiplicationem, & incrementum omnium salutarium donorum Spiritus Sancti, & multiplicationem Pacis, seu omnium bonorum, quæ ad felicitatem præsentem, & futuram promovendam & perficiendam faciunt, idque per incrementum fidei salvificæ, seu agnitionis Dei & Christi, prout in Evangelio revelantur.
units.tr: The third element in the address of the Epistle is the greeting, in which there is a wish and a confirmation of the wish. In the wish he prays that for all the faithful Hebrews there may be a fuller manifestation, multiplication and increase of all the saving gifts of the Holy Spirit, and a multiplication of peace, that is, of all the good things that promote and perfect present and future happiness; and this through the growth of saving faith, that is, of the knowledge of God and Christ as they are revealed in the Gospel.

units.la: Verf. 3. Utpote quum divina vis ipsum omnia nobis donarit, quæ ad vitam & pietatem pertinent, per agnitionem illius qui vocavit nos ad gloriam ac virtutem. Spem voti confirmat fore nempe ut gratiam & pacem multiplicet iis Deus, per fidem, quinque Argumentis. Divina vis ] Argumentum primum, Potentia, seu efficax gratia potenter operans, omnia impedimenta quae ad pietatem seu gratiam, & ad vitam seu pacem pertinent, vobis largita est, per agnitionem seu fidem ipsius, & quoad jus, & quoad inchoatam possessionem: Ergo dona illa augebit, & multiplicabit Deus, donec perfectionem vitae & pietatis adipiscamini: Par enim est ratio initii & progressus, quod ad Dei favorem attinet. Vocavit ] Arg. 2. Deus vocavit vos ad virtutem seu gratiam, & ad gloriam seu pacem. Ergo perficiet ea, ad quae vos vocavit.
units.tr: Verse 3. Since his divine power has given us all things that pertain to life and godliness, through the knowledge of him who called us to glory and virtue. He confirms the hope of the wish, namely that God will multiply grace and peace to them through faith, by five arguments. Divine power: the first argument. The power, or effectual grace working mightily, has bestowed on you all things that pertain to godliness, that is, grace, and to life, that is, peace, which were impeding, through the knowledge or faith of him, both as to right and as to the inchoate possession. Therefore God will increase and multiply those gifts until you attain the perfection of life and godliness, for the reasoning of beginning and progress is the same as far as God's favour is concerned. Called: the second argument. God has called you to virtue or grace, and to glory or peace. Therefore he will bring to completion those things to which he has called you.

units.la: Vers. 4. Ex eo quod maxima nobis ac pretiosa promissa donata sint, ut per haec efficeremini divinae consortes naturae, elapsi ex corruptione quae est in mundo per concupiscentiam.
units.tr: Verse 4. Since very great and precious promises have been given to us, so that through them you might become partakers of the divine nature, having escaped the corruption that is in the world through lust.

units.la: Arg. 3. confirmans superius, Deus donavit vobis promissiones Evangelii, quae ut maximae sunt, (quia rerum maximarum justitiae, scilicet & vitae aeternae) sic etiam sunt pretiosae & vobis ad vitam consequendam summe necessariae. Ergo promissiones illas praestabit, multiplicando ad perfectionem usque, illa quae promisit.
units.tr: The third argument, confirming what was said above: God has given you the promises of the Gospel, which are as great as the greatest things, since they concern righteousness and eternal life, and they are also precious and most necessary for you to obtain life. Therefore he will fulfil those promises, multiplying what he has promised until they are perfected.

units.la: Ut per haec ] Arg. 4. Eo fine & promissiones, & initia rerum promissarum dedit vobis, ut efficeremini consortes divinae naturae, non quoad Essentiam, sed quoad Virtutes & Perfectiones, quae naturam Dei in coelesti sapientia, sanctitate & felicitate, tanquam in viva imagine, repraesentant. Ergo multiplicabit vobis gratiam & pacem, ut fine suo in vobis perficiendis potiatur.
units.tr: So that through them: the fourth argument. God gave both the promises and the first fruits of the promised things for this end, that you might become partakers of the divine nature, not in essence but in virtues and perfections, which represent the nature of God in heavenly wisdom, holiness and blessedness, as in a living image. Therefore he will multiply grace and peace to you, so that he may attain his end in perfecting you.

units.la: Elapsi ] Arg. 5. Jam elapsi estis ex regno mortis & peccati ex foedere liberati ab interitu, in quo jacet mundus per cupiditatem seu concupiscentiam. Idcirco gratiam, quae opponitur peccato, & pacem, quae opponitur interitui, vobis multiplicabit eadem Dei gratiosa voluntas.
units.tr: Having escaped: the fifth argument. You have already escaped from the kingdom of death and sin, and by the covenant have been delivered from the ruin in which the world lies through cupidity or lust. Therefore the same gracious will of God will multiply to you grace, which is opposed to sin, and peace, which is opposed to ruin.

units.la: Vers. 5. Ad hoc ipsum vero vos omni praeterea collato studio, adjicite fidei vestrae virtutem, virtuti vero scientiam.
units.tr: Verse 5. For this very reason, adding all diligence, supply in your faith virtue, and in virtue knowledge.

units.la: Post praefationem hortatur ad serium studium proficiendi in fide, & pietate, virtutes Christianas praecipuas per gradationem enumerans. Quarum prima est fides, quae nobis primum ad Deum aperit aditum: Huic adjungenda virtus, seu studium justitiae generalis, quippe sine qua fides est mortua & ineffica x. Sequitur scientia vel prudentia in pleniori coelestium mysteriorum cognitione. & ad praxin applicatione.
units.tr: After the preface he urges earnest zeal to advance in faith and piety, listing the principal Christian virtues in a graded sequence. The first of these is faith, which first opens the way to God. To this must be joined virtue, or zeal for general righteousness, since without it faith is dead and ineffective. Next comes knowledge, or prudence, in a fuller understanding of the heavenly mysteries and their application to practice.

units.la: Verf 6. Scientiæ vero temperantiam, temperantiæ verò tolerantiam, tolerantiæ verò pietatem,
units.tr: Verse 6. And to knowledge self-control, and to self-control perseverance, and to perseverance godliness,

units.la: Post hanc requirit Temperantiam, quâ quis continet se ab illis illecebris, quibus avocari posset ab officio. Temperantiæ annexi vult Patientiam, seu fortitudinem, quæ consistit in sustinendis rebus adversis, & non cessando ab officio propter mala quæ insequuntur, & hæ virtutes quatuor sunt, quæ vulgò dicuntur cardinales. His adjungi vult tres alias: 1. Pietatem, quæ in ipso Dei cultu potissimum consistit.
units.tr: After this he requires self-control, by which a person restrains himself from those allurements by which he might be drawn away from his duty. Joined to self-control he wishes patience, or fortitude, which consists in bearing adversity and not ceasing from duty because of the evils that follow; these four virtues are commonly called cardinal. To them he wishes to add three others: 1. godliness, which consists chiefly in the worship of God itself.

units.la: Verf. 7. Pietati vero, animum in fratres propensum, animo vero in fratres propensō, charitatem.
units.tr: Verse 7. And to godliness brotherly kindness, and to brotherly kindness love.

units.la: Alia virtus, quam addi vult est φιλαδελφία, quâ fratres seu domesticos fidei complectimur. Ultima virtus est Charitas, seu dilectio communis, quæ ad omnes hominès etiam inimicos extendenda est.
units.tr: The other virtue he wishes to add is brotherly love [φιλαδελφία], by which we embrace the brethren, that is, those of the household of faith. The last virtue is love, or common affection, which is to be extended to all people, even enemies.

units.la: Verf. 8. Hæc enim si vobis adsunt & exuberant, non inertes nec infructuosos vos efficient ad Domini nostri Iesu CHRISTI cognitionem.
units.tr: Verse 8. For if these things are yours and abound, they will not make you idle or unfruitful in the knowledge of our Lord Jesus Christ.

units.la: Argumenta hortationis sunt quatuordecim, Quæ omnia probant his virtutibus conjunctim sumptis studendum.
units.tr: There are fourteen arguments for the exhortation, all of which prove that one must strive for these virtues taken together.

units.la: Argumentum primum, Si obedieritis hortationi, studentes ut & habeatis has virtutes, & ut in iis abundetis, probabitis fidem vestram, seu agnitionem CHRISTI in vobis non esse otiosam vel infructuosam, sed efficacem, quæ ad bene agendum agiles vos reddit. Obediendum ergo.
units.tr: The first argument: if you obey the exhortation, striving both to have these virtues and to abound in them, you will prove that your faith, or your knowledge of Christ, in you is not idle or unfruitful, but effective, making you nimble for doing good. Therefore one must obey.

units.la: Verf. 9. Nam cui hæc non adsunt, is cæcus est, nihil procul cernens, oblitus Iese à veteribus peccatis suis fuisse purgatum.
units.tr: Verse 9. For he who lacks these things is blind, seeing nothing afar off, having forgotten that he was cleansed from his former sins.

units.la: Arg. 2. Si destituti fueritis his virtutibus, declarabitis vos nihil eminùs cernere, sed rebus hujus mundi tantum intentos esse, cæcos verò esse in rebus divinis, seu spiritualibus, & ingratos erga Deum, à quo vetera peccata condonata vobis esse profitemini. Studendum ergo his virtutibus.
units.tr: Second argument: if you lack these virtues, you will show that you see nothing from afar, but are intent only on the things of this world, and are blind in divine or spiritual things, and ungrateful towards God, from whom you profess that your former sins have been forgiven. Therefore one must strive for these virtues.

units.la: Verf. 10. Quapropter, fratres, potius studete vocationem & electionem vestram firmam efficere: hæc enim si feceritis, nunquam impingetis.
units.tr: Verse 10. Therefore, brethren, be all the more diligent to make your calling and election sure; for if you do these things, you will never fall.

units.la: Arg. 3. cum repetita hortatione, Per studium harum virtutum, probabitis vos esse efficaciter vocatos, & electos, & vosmet ipsos in hac persuasione solidè confirmabitis. Studete ergo his virtutibus.
units.tr: Third argument, with the exhortation repeated: by the zeal for these virtues you will prove that you have been effectually called and elected, and you will firmly confirm yourselves in this assurance. Therefore strive for these virtues.

units.la: Hoc enim] Hæc enim ] Arg. 4. Si studueritis his virtutibus, conservabimini ab apostasia seu defectione, nec succumbetis in tentationibus. Ergo his studendum.
units.tr: For if you do these things: the fourth argument. If you strive for these virtues, you will be kept from apostasy or defection, and will not succumb in temptations. Therefore one must strive for them.

units.la: Vers. 11. Ita enim copiosè subministrabitur vobis introitus in æternum regnum Domini nostri, & Servatoris Iesu Christi.
units.tr: Verse 11. For thus an entrance into the eternal kingdom of our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ will be richly supplied to you.

units.la: Arg. 5. Sic ministrabitur vobis amplior introitus in regnum æternum Christi, id est, felicitas & vita illa æterna amplius pandet & explicabit see vobis, ut liberius & copiosius penetrare possitis in regni hujus partes interiores, & frui vitæ illius sensu in ampliori mensura: Studendum ergo his virtutibus.
units.tr: Fifth argument: in this way a fuller entrance into the eternal kingdom of Christ will be granted to you; that is, that eternal happiness and life will open up and unfold more fully to you, so that you may penetrate more freely and abundantly into the inner parts of this kingdom and enjoy the sense of that life in greater measure. Therefore one must strive for these virtues.

units.la: Vers. 12. Quapropter non negligam vos de iis semper commonefacere, tametsi periti & confirmati sitis in præsenti veritate.
units.tr: Ver. 12. Wherefore I will not be negligent to put you always in remembrance of these things, though ye know them and are established in the present truth.

units.la: Arg. 6 cum occupatione objectionis, Etiamsi stabiliti sitis in præsenti veritate: Ego Apostolus tamen pro studio veritas utilitatis jam censui hortationem necessariam, & minimè negligendam: Studete ergo his virtutibus.
units.tr: Arg. 6, with the objection anticipated: Even though you are established in the present truth, I the Apostle nevertheless, for the sake of the usefulness of the truth, have judged an exhortation necessary and by no means to be neglected. Be zealous therefore in these virtues.

units.la: Vers. 13. Justum enim arbitror, quamdiu sum in hoc tabernaculo, excitare vos per commonefactionem.
units.tr: Ver. 13. Yea, I think it meet, as long as I am in this tabernacle, to stir you up by putting you in remembrance.

units.la: Arg 7. Ipsa justitia ex ratione officii mei Apostolici exigit à me, ut per hortationes & commonefactiones hujusmodi, quamdiu in vivis agam, vos excitem ad sanctimoniam. Obedite ergo.
units.tr: Arg. 7. Justice itself, from the nature of my apostolic office, requires of me that, by such exhortations and reminders, as long as I live, I stir you up to holiness. Obey therefore.

units.la: Vers. 14. Quum sciam brevi futurum, ut deponam hoc tabernaculum meum, sicut Dominus noster Iesus Christus declaravit mihi.
units.tr: Ver. 14. Knowing that shortly I must put off this my tabernacle, even as our Lord Jesus Christ hath shewed me.

units.la: Arg. 8. Sicut prædixit Dominus, expecto fore, ut brevi glorioso martyrio vitam finiam. Ergo ut mihi incumbit vos hortari ad virtutes has: sic vobis, hortationi auscultare, incumbit.
units.tr: Arg. 8. As the Lord foretold, I expect that I shall end my life shortly by a glorious martyrdom. Therefore, as it falls to me to exhort you to these virtues, so it falls to you to listen to the exhortation.

units.la: Vers. 15. Sed & studebo, ut vos jubinde post exitum meum possitis horum mentionem facere.
units.tr: Ver. 15. Moreover I will endeavour that ye may be able after my decease to have these things always in remembrance.

units.la: Arg 9. Hortatio hæc, scripto commissa utilis vobis futura est ad memoriam officiorum vestrorum, etiam post meum obitum: Auscultate monitis igitur.
units.tr: Arg. 9. This exhortation, committed to writing, will be useful to you for remembering your duties even after my death. Listen therefore to these admonitions.

units.la: Vers. 16. Non enim arte compositas fabulas secuti, notam vobis fecimus Domini nostri Iesu Christi potentiam & adventum: sed ut qui oculis nostris aspeximus illius majestatem.
units.tr: Ver. 16. For we have not followed cunningly devised fables, when we made known unto you the power and coming of our Lord Jesus Christ, but were eyewitnesses of his majesty.

units.la: Arg. 10. Quæ ego docui vos de Christi incarnatione, seu primo adventu ad officium Redemptoris exequendum, deque ejus Divina natura, potentia, sufficientia, & efficacia ad salvandum Dei populum; non sunt fabulæ artificiose confictæ, quæ despici, vel negligenter sine usu & fructu præteriri possunt: Sed res seriæ & certæ. His admonitionibus igitur meis auscultandum est vobis.
units.tr: Arg. 10. What I have taught you about Christ's incarnation, or first coming, to perform the office of Redeemer, and about his divine nature, power, sufficiency and efficacy to save God's people, are not artfully devised fables, which may be despised or passed over carelessly without use or profit, but serious and certain realities. You must therefore listen to these my admonitions.

units.la: Sed ut qui ] Arg. 11. Per nos Apostolos Christi oculatos & auritos testes veritatis jam demonstratæ edocti estis, adeò ut certitudo hujus Euangelii, etiam humanitus tanta fuerit, quanta possibilis est de rebus gestis & præteritis. Nos enim Apostoli tantam Christi Majestatem sensibus percepimus, ut non potuerimus prohibere, quin ex aspectu raperemur in extasin, prout habetur in Historia Math. 17. de Christi transfiguratione: Obedite igitur meis hortationibus.
units.tr: But were eyewitnesses] Arg. 11. You have been taught through us Apostles, who were eyewitnesses and earwitnesses of a truth already demonstrated, so that the certainty of this Gospel, even humanly speaking, is as great as is possible for things done and past. For we Apostles perceived Christ's majesty with our senses so greatly that we could not help being caught up from the sight into ecstasy, as is recorded in the history of Christ's transfiguration, Matt. 17. Obey therefore my exhortations.

units.la: Verf. 17. Acceperat enim à Deo Patre honorem & gloriam, voce ad cum delata hujusmodi à magnifica gloria, Hic est ille Filius meus dilectus, in quo acquiesco.
units.tr: Ver. 17. For he received from God the Father honour and glory, when there came such a voice to him from the excellent glory: This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.

units.la: Arg. 12. Christus in cujus fide & obedientiâ ut proficiatis hortamur, audibili voce Patris de cœlo loquentis, testimonium gloriosum accepit à magnifica Patris gloriâ, quod sit Filius Dei, in quo ut in Mediatore & Sponsore pro populo redempto, Deus acquiescit in ipsius mediatione & λυτρω abunde sibi satisfaciens. Diligentius igitur obedite huic hortationi.
units.tr: Arg. 12. Christ, in whose faith and obedience we exhort you to make progress, received from the audible voice of the Father speaking from heaven a glorious testimony, from the magnificent glory of the Father, that he is the Son of God, in whom, as Mediator and surety for the redeemed people, God is well pleased in his mediation and, fully satisfied with his ransom [λυτρω], is reconciled. Attend therefore more diligently to this exhortation.

units.la: Verf. 18 Et hanc vocem nos audivimus è Cœlo delatam, quum essemus una cum eo in monte sancto.
units.tr: Ver. 18. And this voice which came from heaven we heard, when we were with him in the holy mount.

units.la: Arg. 13. Adeo sancta sunt ista quæ pertinent ad Christi regnum, ut locus ipse in quo declarabantur ea quæ à nobis prædicata sunt, aliquo modo sanctus factus fuerit, nempe propter extraordinariam Dei vocem, & Divinam Christi gloriam ibi manifestatam: Majori ergo reverentia hortationibus nostris auscultandum est.
units.tr: Arg. 13. So holy are these things that pertain to Christ's kingdom that the very place in which the things we have preached were declared has in some way been made holy, namely on account of the extraordinary voice of God and the divine glory of Christ manifested there. Therefore our exhortations ought to be heeded all the more reverently.

units.la: Verf. 19. Et habemus firmissimum sermonem propheticum: cui recte facitis quod attendatis, velut lucernæ splendenti in obscuro loco, usquedum dies illucescat, & lucifer exoriatur in cordibus vestris:
units.tr: Ver. 19. We have also a more sure word of prophecy, whereunto ye do well that ye take heed, as unto a light that shineth in a dark place, until the day dawn and the day star arise in your hearts:

units.la: Arg. 14. Doctrina de Christo, in cujus fide & obedientia ut proficiatis hortamur, confirmatur Testimonio Scripturæ, seu sermonis Prophetici firmissimi: Ergo hortationi meæ studiosè obediendum est. In hoc argumento pedem figit, certitudinem Scripturæ Propheticæ confirmans septem rationibus.
units.tr: Arg. 14. The doctrine of Christ, in whose faith and obedience we exhort you to make progress, is confirmed by the testimony of Scripture, or the most sure prophetic word. Therefore my exhortation must be obeyed diligently. In this argument he plants his foot, confirming the certainty of prophetic Scripture by seven reasons.

units.la: Firmissimum ] Ratio prima, Quia Scriptura comparata cum aliis revelationis modis, medium est firmissimum longissimè positum extrà & supra exceptiones, quibus alia media revelationis, non minùs vera & clara, obnoxia sunt: potissimum autem valebat hæc ratio apud Hebræos, qui visiones & revelationes Apostolis factas examinaturi erant per Scripturam veteris Testamenti. Nam in ipsorum animis ab aliquot retrò seculis divina veteris Scripturæ autoritas erat confirmata.
units.tr: More sure] First reason: because Scripture, compared with other modes of revelation, is the most sure means, placed far off and above those exceptions to which other means of revelation, no less true and clear, are liable. This reason especially held good among the Hebrews, who were about to examine the visions and revelations made to the Apostles by the Scripture of the Old Testament. For in their minds the divine authority of the ancient Scripture had been confirmed for some centuries.

units.la: Propheticum ] Ratio 2. Quod testimonium prævidentis veritatem suturam, majorem habeat in se Divinæ operationis evidentiam, quam testimonium ejus qui testatur, quod præsens vidit vel audivit: nam prævidere veritatem hanc non potuit ullus præter Prophetam, videre veritatem completam poterat quilibet fidelis.
units.tr: Prophetic] Second reason: the testimony of one who foresees that the truth will come has in itself a greater evidence of divine working than the testimony of one who bears witness to what he saw or heard present. For no one except a prophet could foresee this truth, whereas any believer could see the truth fulfilled.

units.la: Quem ] Ratio 3. Quia dignus est sermo Propheticus, cui fideles attenderent, in cujus sensum inquirerent, cujus veritati & autoritati conscientias subjicerent, & quem applicarent, ad fines & usus quibus inservit.
units.tr: Which] Third reason: because the prophetic word is worthy of the attention of believers, who should inquire into its sense, subject their consciences to its truth and authority, and apply it to the ends and uses which it serves.

units.la: Velut ] Ratio 4. Quia in caligine & tenebris versaturi erant, nisi attenderent Scripturis, quæ sunt in se, & fidelibus, ut Lucerna splendens in obscuro loco, ad dirigendum in omnibus, quid & quomodo agendum.
units.tr: As] Fourth reason: because they would be in darkness and gloom unless they attended to the Scriptures, which in themselves, and for believers, are like a lamp shining in a dark place, directing in all things what and how to act.

units.la: Vsque dum ] Ratio 5. Quia religiosè attendentibus Scripturæ, tandem apparituros est Ipse Sol Justitiæ, IESUS CHRISTUS, in gloria vitæ futuræ plenum diei lumen, sine occasu secum allaturus; & Lux SPIRITUS Sancti, tanquam Stella matutina oritura est in cordibus ipsorum, nunc patefaciens unum fidei articulum, eumque quasi sigillo suo in interioribus sensibus confirmans; nunc alium articulum confirmans, atque itaque gradatim fideles discipulos Scripturæ illuminatura; quæ illuminatio SPIRITUS, quia perfici non potest in hac vita, & quia dies plenæ præsentiæ CHRISTI solis nostri, non nisi in futura vita futurus est: ideo in tota vita nostra Scripturæ attendendum est in omnibus.
units.tr: Until] Fifth reason: because to those who attend to Scripture with reverence, at last the Sun of Righteousness himself, Jesus Christ, will appear, bringing with him the full daylight of the glory of the future life, without setting; and the Light of the Holy Spirit, like the morning star, is going to rise in their hearts, now disclosing one article of faith and sealing it, as it were, upon their inner senses, now confirming another article, and so gradually illuminating the faithful disciples of Scripture. This illumination of the Spirit cannot be perfected in this life, and the day of the full presence of Christ our Sun is to come only in the future life. Therefore in our whole life we must attend to Scripture in all things.

units.la: Vers. 20. Si illud primum noveritis, nullam Prophetiam Scripturæ esse propriæ explicationis.
units.tr: Ver. 20. Knowing this first, that no prophecy of the scripture is of any private interpretation.

units.la: Ratio 6, Quia pro principio credendi, & primò credibili firmiter tenendum est, Scripturas non esse humanæ inventionis, sed Divinæ revelationis; non ex propria Scriptoris mente, sensu seu explicatione, sed ex mente, sensu, & explicatione Dei, profectas esse, quæ idcirco non ex explicatione quam homines sive pauci, sive multi confingunt, sed ex explicatione cujus ipse Dei Spiritus auctor est, intelligendæ sunt.
units.tr: Sixth reason: because, as the principle of believing and the first credible thing, it must be firmly held that the Scriptures are not of human invention but of divine revelation; that they proceeded not from the writer's own mind, sense or explanation, but from the mind, sense and explanation of God. They are therefore to be understood not by the explanation which men, whether few or many, devise, but by that explanation of which the Spirit of God himself is the author.

units.la: Verf. 21. Non enim libidine hominis allata est olim Prophetia, sed acti à Spiritu sancto, loquuti sunt sancti Dei homines.
units.tr: Ver. 21. For the prophecy came not in old time by the will of man, but holy men of God spake as they were moved by the Holy Ghost.

units.la: Ratio 7. confirmans priorem. Quia in Scriptura sunt Prophetiæ quæ ex libitu hominis seu ex humano Prophetæ sensu vel affectu edi non poterant: sed necesse est ut Spiritus Sancti instinctu loquuti sint Sancti illi viri, qui divina oracula Scriptis consignata nobis reliquerunt. Æquum igitur est, ut Spiritus Sanctus suorum verborum per alia Scripturæ suæ loca interpres sit: & ut fideles attendant Scripturis, eaque inter se comparent, ut sensum Spiritus Sancti percipiant.
units.tr: Seventh reason, confirming the former: because there are in Scripture prophecies which could not have been produced by the will of man or by the prophet's own sense or feeling; but those holy men who left us the divine oracles committed to writing must have spoken under the impulse of the Holy Spirit. It is therefore fitting that the Holy Spirit should be the interpreter of his own words through other passages of his Scripture, and that believers should attend to the Scriptures and compare them with one another, so that they may perceive the sense of the Holy Spirit.

units.la: Caput Secundum.
units.tr: Chapter Two.

units.la: VO melius morem gererent superiori hortationi, monet, ut sibi caveant à Doctoribus falsis in Ecclesia exorituris, & jam tum exorientibus, simulque mores & vitia ipsorum describit & redarguit, unde veluti ex notis quibusdam dignosci possent & caveri.
units.tr: Now that they might better comply with the previous exhortation, he warns them to beware of false teachers who will arise in the Church and who are already arising. At the same time he describes and refutes their manners and vices, so that they might be recognised and guarded against by certain marks.

units.la: Verf. 1. FUerunt autem & pseudaprophetæ in populo, ut etiam inter vos erunt falsi doctores, qui subintroducent hæreses exitiales, etiam Dominum qui illos mercatus est abnegantes, accersentes sibi ipsis velox exitium.
units.tr: Verse 1. But there were also false prophets among the people, as there will also be false teachers among you, who will secretly bring in destructive heresies, even denying the Lord who bought them, bringing swift destruction upon themselves.

units.la: Notæ falsorum doctorum, quæ simul rationes continent, propter quas caveri debent, sunt novem: Non quod omnes in uno aliquo hæretico vi-lendæ sint, sed quod aliæ, aliis atque aliis hæreticis conveniant.
units.tr: The marks of false teachers, which at the same time contain the reasons why they must be guarded against, are nine: not that all of them are to be found in any one heretic, but that different ones belong to different heretics.

units.la: Fuerunt etiam ] Nota prima, Quales erant olim Pseudoprophetæ in populo Dei, tales erunt falsi doctores in Ecclesia, nimirum eximii hypocritæ, simulantes se veros esse Prophetas, & in populi gratiam se insinuantes. Subintroducent ] Nota 2. Callidè subintroducturi sunt hæreses exitiales, & licet non expresse, per consequens tamen, seu reipsa, CHRISTUM in aliquo saltem articulo fidei abnegaturi, id est, erunt CHRISTI proditores.
units.tr: Fuerunt etiam: Mark 1. Just as the false prophets were once among God's people, so the false teachers in the Church will be: namely, outstanding hypocrites, pretending to be true prophets and insinuating themselves into the favour of the people. Subintroducent: Mark 2. They will cunningly bring in destructive heresies, and though not expressly, yet by consequence or in fact, they will deny Christ in at least some article of faith; that is, they will be traitors to Christ.

units.la: ] Crimen amplificat quatuor modis: 1. Ex eo quod abnegaturi sint Dominum seu Herum qui ipsos mercatus est, Quod dicitur in ltylo Ecclesiae visibilis, in qua veritatis sunt, & se pro redemptis venditaturi, & quos Ecclesia pro redemptis habitura erat, id quod in stylo etiam judiciali, seu forensi, verum est; per quem, quicunque CHRISTUM, Redemptorem suum esse ore profitetur, & interea facto ipsum abnegat, ex ore suo judicatus, dicitur abnegare Dominum, qui ipsum mercatus erat; quia ad meritum criminis perinde est ac si reipsa emptus fuisset, si putat & profitetur se emptum,& agnitum emptorem sui abnegat.
units.tr: He amplifies the crime in four ways. 1. From the fact that they will deny the Lord or Master who bought them. This is said in the language of the visible Church, in which they are, and they will sell themselves as redeemed, and as those whom the Church would have regarded as redeemed. This is also true in the judicial or forensic idiom: whoever professes with his mouth that Christ is his Redeemer, yet denies him by his deeds, is judged out of his own mouth to deny the Lord who bought him. For as far as the merit of the crime goes, it is just as if he had really been bought, if he thinks and professes that he has been bought, and yet denies the buyer whom he has acknowledged.

units.la: ] Secundo amplificat crimen, ex eo quod per has haereses sibi ipsis merito accersituri sint subitum exitium.
units.tr: Secondly, he amplifies the crime from the fact that through these heresies they will deservedly bring upon themselves sudden destruction.

units.la: Verf. 2. Et multi sequentur eorum exitia, per quos via veritatis blasphemabitur.
units.tr: Verse 2. And many will follow their destructions, through whom the way of truth will be blasphemed.

units.la: Tertio amplificat crimen, ex eo quod multos discipulos seducturi, & in exitium secum ducturi sint. Per quos ] Quarto, Ex eo quod ipsi & iplorum allectae, & blasphematuri sint viam veritatis, seu sanam Evangelii doctrinam, & autores futuri, ut alii contumeliose de ea loquantur.
units.tr: Thirdly, he amplifies the crime from the fact that they will seduce many disciples and lead them with themselves to destruction. Per quos: Fourthly, from the fact that they and their followers will blaspheme the way of truth, that is, the sound doctrine of the Gospel, and will be the authors of others speaking contemptuously of it.

units.la: Verf. 3. Et per avaritiam fictis sermonibus vos negotiabuntur: quibus damnatio jam olim non otiatur, & quorum exitium non dormitat.
units.tr: Verse 3. And through covetousness they will make merchandise of you with feigned words: for whom judgment has long been not idle, and whose destruction does not slumber.

units.la: Nota 3. est Avaritia, quae radix multorum malorum, & haeresium plerumque comes, & mater est. Fictis ] Nota 4. Est termo falsus & fictus, artificiose compositus ad seducendum: fucata eloquentia errores obducens & persuadens. Negotiabuntur ] Nota 5. Nundinatio animarum, & foeda mercatura, qua modo quaestum suum promovere poterint haeretici de dispendio animarum nihil erunt soliciti. Quibus ] Crimen redarguit ex damnatione & exitio celeriter inlequuturis, sicut olim praeparatum erat.
units.tr: Mark 3. Covetousness is the root of many evils, and for the most part the companion and mother of heresies. Fictis: Mark 4. It is a false and feigned word, artfully composed for seduction: painted eloquence that veils errors and persuades men of them. Negotiabuntur: Mark 5. It is the trafficking in souls and a foul trade, by which heretics, in order to advance their own gain, will be unconcerned about the loss of souls. Quibus: He refutes the crime by the condemnation and destruction that will swiftly follow, as was prepared of old.

units.la: Verf. 4. Nam si Deus Angelis qui peccarant non pepercit, sed in tartarum detrusos catenis caliginis traditit damnationi servatos:
units.tr: Verse 4. For if God did not spare the angels who sinned, but cast them down into hell and delivered them into chains of darkness, reserved for damnation:

units.la: Poenam probat sequuturam triplici exemplo: Primum est, Angelorum lapsorum, quibus si Deus non pepercit, sed deturbatos a luce supremi Coeli, ad loca inferiora tenebrosa detrusit, detrusosque potenti manu vinctos in miseria detinet ad ultimum aeternae damnationis supplicium asservandos: Certe Deus fallis illis Doctoribus non parcet.
units.tr: He proves that the punishment will follow by a threefold example. The first is that of the fallen angels: if God did not spare them, but cast them down from the light of the highest heaven into the lower dark places, and, having thrust them down, holds them bound in misery with a mighty hand, keeping them to be reserved for the final torment of eternal damnation, then certainly God will not spare those false teachers.

units.la: Verf. 5. Et prisco mundo non pepercit, sed octavum Noe justitiæ prædconem servavit, diluvio in mundum impiorum inducto:
units.tr: Verse 5. And did not spare the ancient world, but preserved Noah, the eighth, a preacher of righteousness, when he brought the flood upon the world of the ungodly.

units.la: Secundum exemplum est prisci mundi, qui fi juste totus periit (exceptis septem illis, & Noe octavo Præcone Justitiæ, quem præcipuè & cujus causa reliquos servavit Deus) diluvio in mundum impiorum induKto: Certè peribunt etiam falsi illi Doctores.
units.tr: The second example is that of the ancient world, which entirely perished by the flood, except for those seven, and Noah the eighth, the preacher of righteousness, whom God preserved chiefly and for whose sake he saved the rest. Certainly those false teachers too will perish.

units.la: Verf. 6. Et civitates Sodomorum ac Gomorrhæ in cinerem redactas subversione damnavit, fecitque ut essent exemplar impiè viduris.
units.tr: Verse 6. And the cities of Sodom and Gomorrah, reduced to ashes, he condemned with an overthrow, and made them an example to those who would afterwards live ungodly.

units.la: Verf. 7. Et justum Lot, libidinosa nefariorum conversatione fatigatum eripuit,
units.tr: Verse 7. And rescued righteous Lot, wearied by the lustful conduct of the lawless,

units.la: Verf. 8. (Justus enim ille quum habitaret inter eos indies animam justam iniquis illorum factis, & videndo & audiendo excruciabat)
units.tr: Verse 8. (For that righteous man, dwelling among them, daily tormented his righteous soul by seeing and hearing their lawless deeds.)

units.la: Tertium exemplum, Si Deus Sodomam & Gomorrham perdidit in exemplar impiè victuris, & justum Lot eripuit vexatum & excruciatum, videndo & audiendo nefariorum lcelefte facta & dicta. Nonnè Deus confervatis fervis suis, puniet impios Doctores, qui Euangelio jam clarè patefacto tam protervè adhuc lascivisunt.
units.tr: The third example: if God destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah as an example to those who would live ungodly, and rescued just Lot, vexed and tormented by seeing and hearing the wicked deeds and words of the lawless, will not God, who keeps his servants safe, punish the ungodly teachers, who still act so shamelessly now that the Gospel has been clearly revealed?

units.la: Verf. 9. Novit Dominus pios è tentatione eripere, injustos autem in diem judicii fervare ipsos puniendos:
units.tr: Verse 9. The Lord knows how to rescue the godly out of temptation, but to keep the unrighteous for the day of judgment, to be punished.

units.la: Confirmat hujus Argumenti vim à sapientia & potentia Dei, qua potest Deus utrumque facere, nempe tum pios eripere ex tentationibus & afflictionibus, tum impios ad diem ultimi judicii reservare supplicis æternis puniendos.
units.tr: He confirms the force of this argument from the wisdom and power of God, by which God is able to do both: to rescue the godly from temptations and afflictions, and to reserve the ungodly for the day of final judgment, to be punished with eternal torments.

units.la: Verf. 10. Maxime verò eos qui carnem sequentes, in impura cupiditate incedunt, & dominatum despiciunt: qui, inquam, ut sunt audaces & sibi placentes, non horrent dignitates conviciis incessere:
units.tr: Verse 10. But chiefly those who walk after the flesh in impure lust and despise dominion: who, I say, being bold and self-pleasing, do not shudder to revile dignities.

units.la: Nota hæreticorum sexta, Est luxuriosa & libidinosa vita, propter quam rectè colligit exempla Justitiæ Dei prædicta, minari illis æternum exitium, maxime, quia carnem seu corruptam naturam ducem sequuntur & pergunt in impuritate, vitæ suæ cursum producentes in cupiditatibus fœdis, & voluptatibus carnis indulgentes. Dominatum ] Nota 7. Est contemptus dominatus, seu legitimæ autoritatis, quam sublatam è mundo vellent, ne essent qui ipsorum vitia punirent. Hoc vitium depingit & amplificat sex rationibus.
units.tr: The sixth mark of the heretics: they lead a licentious and lustful life, on account of which he rightly infers that the threatened examples of God's justice will befall them, that eternal destruction awaits them, especially because they follow the flesh, that is, corrupt nature, as their guide, and persist in impurity, carrying on the course of their life in foul desires and indulging the pleasures of the flesh. Dominatum: Mark 7. It is contempt of dominion, that is, of lawful authority, which they would wish removed from the world, so that there would be no one left to punish their vices. He depicts and amplifies this vice by six reasons.

units.la: Ratio prima, Quod non sit nuda inobedientia mandatorum illicitorum Gubernatoris errantis, sed Contemptus Magistratus officium praestantis, contemptus ipsius potestatis & ordinationis DEI.
units.tr: The first reason: it is not mere disobedience to the unlawful commands of an erring governor, but contempt for the magistrate performing his office, contempt of the power itself and of God's ordinance.

units.la: Ratio 2. Quod sit Audacia cum contemptu conjuncta.
units.tr: Reason 2: that it is audacity joined with contempt.

units.la: Ratio 3. Quod sit audacia in contemptu cum Complacentia in peccato illo conjuncta. Ratio 4. Quod sit Audacia, in contemptu, ad maledicentiam, convitia, & probra in Magistratum jacienda, prorumpens.
units.tr: Reason 3: that it is audacity in contempt joined with complacency in that sin. Reason 4: that it is audacity which, breaking out in contempt, bursts into slander, abuse, and reproaches to be cast at the magistrate.

units.la: Vers. 11. Quum ipsi Angeli qui sunt robore ac potestate majores, non ferant adversus eas apud Dominum judicium maledicum.
units.tr: Verse 11. Whereas the angels themselves, who are greater in strength and power, do not bring a railing judgment against them before the Lord.

units.la: Ratio 5. Quod cum sint viles hominiones audeant maledicere Magistratibus, quibus Angeli qui eminent supra Magistratus, maledicere non audent: nam etiamsi adhibeantur ad puniendos aliquando Principes, semper tamen Principatum, Magistratum, & Potestates, earumque æstimationem custodire iatagunt Angeli; Contra quam Haeretici quidam faciunt, & factum vellent.
units.tr: Reason 5: that, since they are vile men, they dare to speak evil of magistrates, whereas the angels, who excel above magistrates, do not dare to speak evil. For even when the angels are sometimes employed to punish princes, they always strive to guard principality, magistracy, and powers, and their esteem; contrary to what some heretics do, and would wish to do.

units.la: Vers. 12. At isti, veluti animantia rationis expertia quæ naturali impetu feruntur, facta ad eum finem ut capta intereant, ea vim superantes quæ ignorant, sua ipsorum corruptela interibunt:
units.tr: Verse 12. But these, like irrational animals, born by natural impulse to be caught and destroyed, blaspheming what they do not know, shall perish in their own corruption.

units.la: Ratio 6. Quod Haeretici sint brutis feris in hoc vitio similes: Nam sicut ferae, 1. Rationis expertes sunt: 2. Feruntur impetu, non consilio: 3 Captæ intereunt. Sic Haeretici illi, qui Magistratum inter homines, vel in Ecclesia non ferunt: Sed huic ordinationi maledicunt, 1. Judicii expertes, DEI ordinationem ignorant: 2. Pravo impetu feruntur ad blasphemandum, seu vituperandum quod ignorant: 3. Sicut ferae sibi interitum accersunt, & sua ipsorum corruptela perennt.
units.tr: Reason 6: that heretics are like brute beasts in this vice. For as beasts 1. are without reason; 2. are carried by impulse, not counsel; 3. perish when taken. So those heretics who do not endure magistracy among men or in the Church, but curse this ordinance: 1. lacking judgment, they are ignorant of God's ordinance; 2. are carried by depraved impulse to blaspheme or revile what they do not know; 3. like beasts they bring destruction upon themselves and perish in their own corruption.

units.la: Vers. 13. Reportaturi mercedem injustitia, ut qui pro voluptate ducant quotidianas delicias, labes ac maculæ, qui fraudibus suis se obleCtant, vobiscum epulando.
units.tr: Verse 13. Receiving back a reward of injustice, as those who count daily pleasures a delight; stains and blemishes, who delight themselves in their deceits while feasting with you.

units.la: Vers. 14 Oculos habentes plenos adulterii, & qui a peccando cessare nesciant: inescantes animas instabiles, cor habentes ad avaritiam exercitatum, execrandi homines:
units.tr: Verse 14. Having eyes full of adultery, and who cannot cease from sin; enticing unstable souls, having hearts trained in covetousness, accursed people:

units.la: Repetit comminationem meritæ ipsorum condemnationis, & addit notam octavam in tribus impudentiæ ipsorum demonstrationibus. Prima est in aperto luxu, quia etiam tempore diurno, nec Euangelii, nec Solis lucem metuentes animos suos luxui ded.tos oltendent in conviviis deliciantes. Secunda impudentiæ demonstratio, in aperta impudicitia, quam celare minime ītudebunt, sed adulteria cordis sui, oculis prodent, suamque in libidine impotentiam præ se ferent; atque ita non se polluent tantum, sed etiam animas inltabiles destitutas solidâ & salvificâ fide, decipient & inescabunt. Tertia impudentia consistit in Avaritia, cujus artes & methodos ita meditatas habebunt, & cor vitioso habitu adeo exercitatum, ut non dissimulaturi sint suam habendi cupiditatem: Quæ vitia in summa complectens, execrandos vocat homines illos nequam.
units.tr: He repeats the threat of their deserved condemnation and adds the eighth mark, shown in three ways of their shamelessness. The first is open luxury: even in the daytime, fearing neither the Gospel nor the light of the sun, they indulge their minds given over to luxury, delighting themselves at feasts. The second is open impurity, which they will not be ashamed to conceal: their adulteries of heart will show in their eyes, and they will display their helplessness in lust. Thus they not only defile themselves but also entice and deceive unstable souls, who lack a firm and saving faith. The third shameless act consists in covetousness. They will have devised its arts and methods, and their hearts will be so practised in the wicked habit that they will not hide their desire for gain. Summing up these vices, he calls those worthless men accursed.

units.la: Verl. 15. Qui relicta recta via, aberrarunt, sequuti viam Balaam Filii Bosor, qui mercedem iniquitatis amavit;
units.tr: Verse 15. Who, having left the straight way, have gone astray, following the way of Balaam the son of Bosor, who loved the wages of iniquity;

units.la: Verf. 16. Sed redargutionem suæ transgressionis sustinuit: nam subjugis asina muta, humana voce loquuta prohibuit prophetæ dementiam.
units.tr: Verse 16. But he was rebuked for his transgression: for a dumb donkey, speaking with a human voice, restrained the prophet's madness.

units.la: Impudentem horum hominum avaritiam comparat avaritiæ Baalam, cujus historiam ex Num. 22. breviter repetit, qui cupiditate mercedis, de via quam profellus est se sequuturum, aberravit, & impietati apertæ se tandem dedidit: in qua tam stupidus fuit, ut ab alina sua subjugi meritus fuerit reprehendi & castigari; id quod similiter merentur falsi doctores, turpis lucri causa, falsa docentes.
units.tr: He compares the shameless greed of these men with the greed of Balaam, whose story he briefly recalls from Numbers 22. Driven by the lure of wages, Balaam strayed from the way he had professed he would follow, and at last gave himself over to open impiety. He was so foolish that he deserved to be rebuked and corrected by his own donkey. False teachers deserve the same, teaching falsehoods for the sake of shameful gain.

units.la: Verf 17. Isti sunt fontes aqua carentes nebula a turbine agitae: quibus caligo tenebrarum in æternum servata est.
units.tr: Verse 17. These are wells without water, clouds driven by a whirlwind, for whom the darkness of gloom is reserved forever.

units.la: Nota 9. Est vaniloquentia cum saltu & hypocrisi conjuncta: cujus respectu comparat eos fontibus aquâ carentibus, & nubibus a turbine agitatis & dissipatis, ita ut pluviam quam promittere videbantur, non dent. Tales sunt falsi Doctores, qui debent esse Stellæ lucentes, & Lux Mundi, & nihil habent interim præter tenebras, & errorum caliginem: Quapropter ad judicandos eos æternis in inferno tenebris pronunciat Apostolus.
units.tr: Mark 9. There is empty talk joined with boasting and hypocrisy. With regard to this he compares them to wells without water and to clouds driven and scattered by the wind, so that they do not give the rain they seemed to promise. Such are the false teachers, who ought to be shining stars and the light of the world, yet have nothing but darkness and the gloom of error. Therefore the Apostle pronounces them to be judged to the eternal darkness of hell.

units.la: Verl. 18. Nam pratumidam vanitatem loquendo per carnis cupiditates lascivas, eos inescant qui verè effugerant eos qui in errore versantur;
units.tr: Verse 18. For speaking proud, empty words, they entice by fleshly lusts and wantonness those who have truly escaped from those who live in error;

units.la: Vaniloquentiam eorum proponit perspiciendam in tribus: Primò in prætumido docendi stylo, & inflato orationis genere; in quo verbo-rum ampullis perstringunt simplicium oculos, & incautos in admirationem rapiunt: quod genus dicendi tegendis ambagibus valde elt appolitum. Secundo, in eo quod doctrina sua patrocinentur carnalibus hominum concupiscentiis, quasi non effet opus contra eas dicere; atque ita ineicant aliquos carnis laicivis, qui prius convicti de erro-ribus, in quibus versabantur dum inter mundanos eilent, id est, extra Ecclesiam, renunciaverant eorum societati, & vere seu destinato confi-lio ab iis aufugerant (quod vi naturalis luminis conscientiæ, fieri po-telt) feque contulerant ad consortium Ecclesiæ Christianæ, quod etiam fine spiritVali regeneratione fieri potelt.
units.tr: He sets out their empty talk to be seen in three respects. First, in a bombastic style of teaching and an inflated manner of speech, by which they dazzle the eyes of simple people with the bubbles of words and carry the unwary into admiration. This kind of speech is very well suited to hiding behind circumlocutions. Second, in that they defend their teaching by appealing to people's carnal desires, as though there were no need to speak against them. Thus they entice some who, having first been convicted of the errors in which they lived while among worldly people, that is, outside the Church, had renounced that fellowship and had truly, or with a settled purpose, fled from them (which can happen by the power of the natural light of conscience), and had joined the fellowship of the Christian Church, which can also happen without spiritual regeneration.

units.la: Verl. 19. Libertatem eis pollicendo, quum ipsi fervi sint corru-ptionis siquidem à quo quis superatus est, huic etiam in fervitu-tem ast addictus.
units.tr: Verse 19. Promising them liberty, while they themselves are slaves of corruption; for by whom a man is overcome, to this one he is also enslaved.

units.la: Tertio, in dissimilitudine inter ipsos & ipsorum promissa. Promitte-bant enim libertatem aliis, cum illos in servitutem peccati trahebant, & ipsimet eflent fervi corruptelæ, & fecundùm præxin suam, & fecun-dum Doctrinæ suæ principia. Nam non est alia libertas Christiana, quam quæ manumissos à peccato, & servili jugo tederis operun, in liberum justitiæ obsequium ipsos adducat.
units.tr: Third, in the unlikeness between them and their promises. For they promised liberty to others while they drew them into the slavery of sin, and they themselves were slaves of corruption, both by their own practice and by the principles of their teaching. For there is no other Christian liberty than that which leads those freed from sin and from the servile yoke of corruption into the free obedience of righteousness.

units.la: Siquidem ] Probat libertinos hos cum suis discipulis mancipia esse peccati abjectissima & miserrima, quatuor rationibus. Superatus ] Ratio prima, Quia devicti sunt & superati à peccato; cujus fervituti fe addicunt, deceptionibus falsæ Doctrinæ inducti. Ergo verè fervi sunt.
units.tr: For: he proves that these libertines, with their disciples, are the most abject and wretched slaves of sin, by four reasons. Overcome: the first reason is that they have been conquered and overcome by sin, to whose slavery they surrender themselves, led on by the deceptions of false doctrine. Therefore they are truly slaves.

units.la: Verl. 20. Itaque fi postquam inquinamenta mundi, per agni-tionem Domini & Servatoris IESU CHRISTI effugerint, his rursum implicati superentur fatta est ultima eorum conditio deterior priore.
units.tr: Verse 20. For if, after they have escaped the defilements of the world through the knowledge of the Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ, they are again entangled in them and overcome, their last state has become worse than the first.

units.la: Ratio 2. Quia ipsi & discipuli ipsorum per apostasiam à sancta conversatione incidunt in deteriorem conditionem, quam erat ea in qua degebant priusquam nomen dederunt Christo; nam postquam in Baptismo renunciaverunt inquinamentis mundi, & per agnitionem Christi, qualem qualem, aufugerunt ab iis recipientes fe in gremium alicujus Ecclesiæ Christi, fi denuò implicati fuerint illis inquinamentis, & victi dederint manus, facta est ultima conditio deterior priore.
units.tr: Second reason: they and their disciples, through apostasy from holy conduct, fall into a worse condition than the one they were in before they gave their name to Christ. For after they renounced the defilements of the world in Baptism, and through the knowledge of Christ, however imperfect, fled from them, receiving themselves into the bosom of some Church of Christ, if they are again entangled in those defilements and yield, their last state is worse than the first.

units.la: Satius enim fuisset eis non cognovisse viam justitiae, quam cognita illa, regredi à sancta doctrina ipsis traditae.
units.tr: For it would have been better for them not to have known the way of righteousness, than, having known it, to turn back from the holy doctrine delivered to them.

units.la: Ratio 3. probans priorem, Quia scientes, volentes à cognita via justitiae, & sancto mandato semel illis tradito ut transfugae in adversaria castra retrocedunt; quod multo gravius est peccatum & durior servitus, quam si nunquam cognovissent viam justitiae; melior enim futura fuisset ipsorum conditio in ignorantia quam in apostasia.
units.tr: Third reason, proving the former: because, knowing and willingly, they turn back from the known way of righteousness and the holy command once delivered to them, like deserters going back into the enemy's camp. This is a much graver sin and a harsher slavery than if they had never known the way of righteousness. Their condition would have been better in ignorance than in apostasy.

units.la: Sed accidit eis quod vero proverbio dici solet, Canis reversus est ad suum ipsius vomitum: & Sus lota, ad volutabrum caeni.
units.tr: But it has happened to them as the true proverb is wont to say: The dog has returned to its own vomit, and the washed sow to the wallowing in mud.

units.la: Ratio 4. Faciens ad tollendum scandalum quod ab eorum apostasia oriri potuit; Quia ex apostasia sua testantur se nunquam fuisse ex veris ovibus Christi, sed in Baptismo & apparenti vitae sanctitate, qua se aliquando pro sanctis venditabant, demonstrant se fuisse sues & canes, sine spirituali & interna naturae renovatione, semperque sues & canes mansisse: Ideoque non mirandum si eis accidat quod vero proverbio dici solet, Sicut Canis licet purgatus per vomitum, resorbet tamen quod vomuerat, & Sus lota licet, revertitur tamen ad volutabrum caeni: Sic Apostatae, licet resipiscentiam à peccatis, & fidem in Christum, & obedientiam mandatorum ejus profiteantur, data occasione tamen revertuntur ad pristinos mores.
units.tr: Fourth reason, serving to remove the scandal that could arise from their apostasy. By their apostasy they bear witness that they were never true sheep of Christ, but in Baptism and in the outward appearance of holiness by which they once boasted themselves to be saints, they show that they were swine and dogs, without spiritual and inward renewal of nature, and always remained swine and dogs. Therefore it is no wonder if what the true proverb is wont to say happens to them: As a dog, though cleansed by vomiting, nevertheless takes back what it had vomited, and a washed sow, though washed, returns to the wallowing in mud. So apostates, though they profess repentance from sins, faith in Christ, and obedience to his commands, nevertheless, when occasion arises, return to their former ways.

units.la: Caput Tertium.
units.tr: Chapter 3.

units.la: Ranfit ad aliam commonefactionem de cavendis irrisoribus, qui adventum Christi negabant, quorum blasphemiam refutat, ad verf. 11. In secunda ostendit usum & fructum suae doctrinae de adventu CHRISTI potissimum, ad finem.
units.tr: He passes on to another warning, about being on guard against scoffers who denied the coming of Christ, whose blasphemy he refutes at verse 11. In the second part he shows the use and fruit of his teaching about the coming of Christ, chiefly, to the end.

units.la: HAsce jam alteras vobis literas scribo, dilecti, quibus sinceram mentem vestram per commonefactionem excito:
units.tr: Beloved, I now write to you this second letter, in which I stir up your sincere mind by way of reminder,

units.la: Verl. 2, Ut memores sitü verborum quæ prædicta sunt à sanctis Prophetis, & doctrinæ nostræ qui sumus Apostoli, Domini & Servatoris.
units.tr: Verse 2: That you may be mindful of the words which were spoken before by the holy Prophets, and of our teaching, we who are Apostles of the Lord and Saviour.

units.la: Ut sibi viam paret ad ea quæ sequuntur, scopum utriusque Epistolæ proponit, nempe ut mentes vere fidelium commonefaciendo excitaret ad constantiam in fide & obedientiâ doctrinæ Euangelicæ, quam ex Scriptura Prophetarum, & institutione Apostolorum didicerant.
units.tr: In order to prepare the way for what follows, he sets out the aim of both letters: namely, by reminding the minds of true believers, to rouse them to steadfastness in faith and obedience to the Gospel teaching, which they had learned from the Scripture of the Prophets and the instruction of the Apostles.

units.la: Verf. 3. Illud primum scientes, venturos extremis diebus irrisores, ut qui in suis ipsorum cupiditatibus incedant:
units.tr: Verse 3: Knowing this first, that in the last days there shall come scoffers, walking after their own lusts,

units.la: Ut caverent sibi ab Atheis & illusoribus pietatis, describit istiusmodi monstra quatuor modis: Primò, Ab antecedenti prædictione SPIRITUS Sancti, admonentis de adventu & frequentia impiorum irrisorum sub finem mundi tanquam hostium Euangelii capitalium, qui temporibus Euangelii omnem pietatem ludibrio erant habituri: 2. A vitiosâ ipsorum vitâ, quod vitam acturi essent secundùm cupiditates suas.
units.tr: So that they might guard themselves against atheists and mockers of godliness, he describes such monsters in four ways. First, by the prior prediction of the Holy Spirit, warning of the coming and multiplication of impious scoffers at the end of the world, as chief enemies of the Gospel, who would hold all godliness in derision in the times of the Gospel. Second, by their sinful way of life: that they would live according to their own lusts.

units.la: Verf. 4. Et dicant, Ubi est pollicitatio adventus ejus? nam ex quo die Patres obdormierunt, omnia ita permanent ab initio creationis.
units.tr: Verse 4: And they shall say, Where is the promise of his coming? For since the Fathers fell asleep, all things continue as they were from the beginning of the creation.

units.la: Tertio, à blasphemis dictis, quod ausuri essent etiam Domini adventum ad judicium impudenter negare, & promissiones Dei fallitatis aperte insimulare: 4. A pertinaci defensione blasphemiæ suæ, quod auderent disputare contra adventum Domini, quasi non venturus esset omninò, sed mundus in æternum duraturus esset, idcirco quia tot retrò seculis nondum venit Judex, & quia res omnes ita se habent nostris temporibus, sicut se habebant ab initio creationis; sensum suum carnalem, mensuram fidei suæ facientes, & verbum Dei post tergum abjicientes.
units.tr: Third, by the blasphemous words they would speak: that they would dare shamelessly to deny even the Lord's coming to judgment, and openly accuse the promises of God of falsehood. Fourth, by their stubborn defence of their blasphemy: that they would dare to dispute against the Lord's coming, as if he were never going to come at all but the world would endure for ever, because the Judge has not come in so many ages past, and because all things in our times are as they were from the beginning of creation. They make their carnal sense the measure of their faith and cast the Word of God behind their backs.

units.la: Verl. 5. Illud enim sponte ipsos latet, Cœlos jam elim extitisse per Dei termonem, & terram ex aqua & in aqua consistentem:
units.tr: Verse 5: For this they willingly forget, that the heavens were of old, and the earth standing out of the water and in the water, by the word of God.

units.la: Refutat hos blasphemos canes quinque Argumentis, Arg. primum, Quia respuunt oblatam sibi cognitionem ex verbo Dei, & sponte ignorant quod creatus sit mundus per Dei termonem; nam si creationem agnoscerent per Dei verbum fuisse: finem mundi prædictum in Dei verbo oporteret etiam agnoscere.
units.tr: He refutes these blaspheming dogs with five arguments. The first argument: because they reject the knowledge offered to them from the Word of God, and willingly ignore that the world was created by the word of God. For if they acknowledged that creation came about through God's word, they would also have to acknowledge the end of the world foretold in God's word.

units.la: Et terram ] Arg. 2, Sponte ignorant & claudunt oculos ad constans miraculum terræ emergentis ex aqua, & consistentis per aquam, per quam solida redditur ne diffluat in pulverem, cum terra natura sua infimum elementum subsideret tota, & aquis tegeretur, & absorberetur. In quo miraculo perspicere possent naturam regi & firmari solius Dei voluntate, ut sic vel secus se habeat prout Deo placuerit.
units.tr: And the earth] Second argument: they willingly ignore and close their eyes to the plain miracle of the earth rising out of the water and standing through the water, by which the solid ground is kept from dissolving into dust, since by its nature the earth, the lowest element, would sink down entirely and be covered and swallowed up by the waters. In this miracle they could see that nature is governed and sustained by the will of God alone, so that it is or is not as God pleases.

units.la: Versf. 6. Quamobrem is qui tum erat mundus aqua inundatus periit:
units.tr: Verse 6: Whereby the world that then was, being overflowed with water, perished.

units.la: Arg. 3. Quod terra praeter naturam emineat ex aquis, & quod omnia non maneant in eodem tempore statu, evidens est ex historia Diluvii, quo priori ordine mutato, mundus seu humanum genus, quod tunc erat, aquis inundantibus periit. Non est ergo incredibile mundum decurrentem eam mutationem passurum, quam Dei verbum praedixit.
units.tr: Third argument: that the earth rises above the waters contrary to nature, and that all things do not remain in the same state at all times, is evident from the history of the Flood, when the former order was changed and the world, or the human race which then existed, perished under the rising waters. It is therefore not incredible that the world, running its course, will undergo the change which the Word of God has foretold.

units.la: Verf. 7. Qui vero nunc sunt Coeli ac terra, eodem sermone repositi, servantur igni in diem damnationis, & exitii impiorum hominum.
units.tr: Verse 7: But the heavens and the earth which are now, by the same word are stored up, reserved unto fire against the day of judgment and perdition of ungodly men.

units.la: Arg. 4. Coeli, qui nunc sunt, & terra quae nunc est, per idem Dei verbum & efficacem ejus voluntatem conservantur ad ignem judicii extremi, quando condemnabuntur, & peribunt impii & irrisores adventus Domini maxime.
units.tr: Fourth argument: the heavens which now are, and the earth which now is, are kept by the same Word of God and his effective will for the fire of the last judgment, when the ungodly and especially the scoffers at the Lord's coming will be condemned and perish.

units.la: Vers. 8. Unum autem hoc ne vos lateat, dilecti, Unum diem apud Dominum perinde est ut mille annos, & mille annos ut diem unum.
units.tr: Verse 8: But, beloved, be not ignorant of this one thing, that one day is with the Lord as a thousand years, and a thousand years as one day.

units.la: Diluit objectionem, Dicerent impii, Cur differt adventum? Responsio triplex est, Prima, Etiamsi differre adventum videatur Dominus, dilatio haec tamen non debet esse offendiculo cuiquam, quia non ora non debet aestimari ex nostro sensu, sed ex aeternitate Dei, cui illud spatium temporis, quod nobis videtur admodum longum, est instar unius diei, & apud quem unus dies & mille anni non differunt, quod ad proportionem attinet mensurae.
units.tr: He answers an objection: the ungodly might say, Why does he delay his coming? The answer is threefold. First, even if the Lord seems to delay his coming, this delay ought not to be a stumbling block to anyone, because it must not be judged by our feeling but by the eternity of God, to whom that span of time, which seems to us very long, is like a single day, and with whom one day and a thousand years do not differ as far as the measure of proportion goes.

units.la: Vers 9. Non tardat Dominus qui promisit, (ut nonnulli tarditatem hanc esse ducunt,) sed patiens est erga nos, nolens ullos perire, sed omnes ad resipiscentiam tendere
units.tr: Verse 9: The Lord is not slack concerning his promise, as some men count slackness; but is longsuffering to us-ward, not willing that any should perish, but that all should come to repentance.

units.la: Responsio 2. Haec dilatio non provenit ex tarditate, ut judicant nonnulli, sed ex patientia Dei erga nos electos scilicet, quorum multi nondum convertuntur, & quorum nullos vult Deus perire, sed omnes suo tempore ad resipiscentiam pervenire, quod fieri non potest nisi in tempus maturum differretur Christi adventus. Nam si Deus anticiparet judicii tempus à se decretum, aliqui eorum perirent quos ab æterno elegit ad salutem.
units.tr: Second answer: this delay does not arise from slackness, as some judge, but from the patience of God towards us, namely the elect, many of whom are not yet converted, and of whom God wills that none should perish, but that all should come to repentance in their own time. This could not happen unless the coming of Christ were deferred until the time was ripe. For if God were to anticipate the time of judgment he had decreed, some of those whom he chose from eternity for salvation would perish.

units.la: Verf. 10 Veniet autem, sicut fur in nocte dies ille Domini, quo Cœli cum stridore præteribunt, elementa vero âstuantia solventur, terràque & quæ in ea sunt opera exurentur.
units.tr: Verse 10: But the day of the Lord will come as a thief in the night, in which the heavens shall pass away with a great noise, and the elements shall melt with fervent heat, and the earth and the works that are therein shall be burned up.

units.la: Responsio 3. & Arg. 5. refutationis irrisorum à modo adventus Domini, qui describitur in tribus: 1. Erit hominibus improvisus, quomodo fures venire solent, quo tempore sciunt se minime expectari:
units.tr: Third answer, and fifth argument against the scoffers, from the manner of the Lord's coming, which is described in three points: 1. It will be unforeseen by men, as thieves usually come, at a time when they know they are least expected;

units.la: 2. Erit cum universi totius maxima mutatione, & 3. Cum abolitione omnium, in quibus athei felicitatem suam in hoc mundo quærere solent, siquidem cœli cum stridore præteribunt, elementa æstuantia solventur, terraque & quæ in ea sunt opera exurentur: adeo ut solicit debeant omnes esse ad semetipsos parandos, potius quam quicquam cuiole de modo vel tempore adventus scilicet ari, vel de tarditate conqueri.
units.tr: 2. It will bring the greatest change of the whole universe; and 3. it will bring the abolition of all those things in which atheists are wont to seek their happiness in this world, since the heavens will pass away with a great noise, the elements will melt with fervent heat, and the earth and the works that are in it will be burned up. So all should be anxious to prepare themselves, rather than to inquire about the manner or time of the coming, or to complain of its delay.

units.la: Secunda pars.
units.tr: The second part.

units.la: Verf. 11. Quum igitur hæc omnia solvantur quales oportet esse vos in sanctis conversationibus & pietatis officiis:
units.tr: Verse 11. Since therefore all these things are to be dissolved, what manner of persons ought you to be in holy conversation and the duties of godliness?

units.la: Secunda pars Capitis, in qua doctrinam hanc trahit in usum per hortationem ad sanctitatis studium, & ad perseverantiam in eo. Argumenta hortationis sunt octo: Argumentum primum, Per postulationem testimonii à conscientiis ipsorum: Hæc omnia visibilia præsertim opera quæ in terra sunt, dissolvenda sunt. Ergo sanctitati studendum est.
units.tr: The second part of the chapter, in which he draws this doctrine into use by exhortation to the pursuit of holiness and to perseverance in it. The arguments of the exhortation are eight. The first argument, from the demand of testimony from their own consciences: all these visible things, especially the works that are on the earth, are to be dissolved. Therefore we must strive after holiness.

units.la: Verf. 12. Expectantes & properantes ad adventum diei Dei, in quo Cœli conflagrantes solventur, & elementa æstuantia liquescent?
units.tr: Verse 12. Waiting for and hastening unto the coming of the day of God, in which the heavens, being set on fire, shall be dissolved, and the elements shall melt with fervent heat?

units.la: Arg. 2. Quia sic decet vos, qui spe expectatis, & desiderio properatis in occursum Domini adventantis, id est, oportet vos spe adventus Christi patienter laborare in vocatione vestra, & sanctitati studere.
units.tr: Argument 2. Because it becomes you, who wait in hope and hasten with desire to meet the coming Lord, that is, you ought to labour patiently in your calling by the hope of Christ's coming, and to strive after holiness.

units.la: In quo Arg. 3. Quia Domini adventus ad judicium adeo terribilis futurus est, ut cœli conflagrantes solvendi sint, & elementa æstuantia liquefacienda sint.
units.tr: Argument 3. Because the coming of the Lord to judgment will be so terrible that the heavens, being set on fire, are to be dissolved, and the elements that glow with heat are to be melted.

units.la: Verf. 13 Sed Cœlos novos ac terram novam secundum promissum expectamus, in quibus justitia inhabitat.
units.tr: Verse 13. But we look for new heavens and a new earth according to his promise, in which righteousness dwells.

units.la: Verf. 14. Quapropter, dilecti, haec expectantes, studete ut immaculati & incontaminati ab eo reperiamini cum pace.
units.tr: Verse 14. Wherefore, beloved, since you look for these things, be diligent that you may be found by him without spot and blameless, in peace.

units.la: Arg. 4. Quia iecundum Dei promissa Isa. 65. 17, & 66. 22. Expectamus novos coelos, & novam terram, in quibus soli justi habitabunt: Ergo sanctitati & justitiae studere debemus, qui hanc spem habemus. Nominat autem & coelos & terram habitaculum justorum, quia totus mundus erit possessio & Palatium, & regnum electorum; qui comitabuntur CHRISTUM quocunque proficiscetur.
units.tr: Argument 4. Because according to God's promises, Isa. 65. 17 and 66. 22, we look for new heavens and a new earth, in which only the righteous will dwell. Therefore we ought to strive after holiness and righteousness, we who have this hope. Moreover he calls both heavens and earth the habitation of the righteous, because the whole world will be the possession, palace and kingdom of the elect, who will accompany Christ wherever he goes.

units.la: Studete ] Cum repetita hortatione ad sanctitatem, addit Arg. 5 Studentes ut sitis immaculati, & irreprehensibiles inveniemini à CHRISTO in pace, id est, reconciliati Deo & pro amicis CHRISTI, ab eo ubi ad judicium venerit, habebimini.
units.tr: "Be diligent": with the exhortation to holiness repeated, he adds Argument 5: be diligent that you may be found by Christ unspotted and irreproachable, in peace, that is, reconciled to God and counted as friends of Christ, when he comes to judgment, you will be held by him.

units.la: Verf. 15. Dominique nostri patientiam, salutem arbitremini; sicut & charus frater noster Paulus pro sibi data sapientia scripsit vobis:
units.tr: Verse 15. Count the patience of our Lord as salvation, as also our dear brother Paul wrote to you according to the wisdom given to him:

units.la: Arg 6. Cum occupatione objectionis, Tantum abest ut tædio frangi debeatis, quia CHRISTUS differre videtur adventum, ut contra prosigno salutis dandae omnibus vobis existimare debeatis, hanc moram, sed tolerantiam potius Domini & tarditatem ad iram.
units.tr: Argument 6, with the objection anticipated: far from your being broken by weariness because Christ seems to delay his coming, you ought rather to think that this delay is the salvation offered to all of you, and the patience and slowness of the Lord toward wrath.

units.la: Sicut ] Arg. 7. Paulus in sua Epistola ad vos Hebraeos scripta, (pro non exigua sapientiae sibi datae mensura) diligenter hortatus est ad studium sanctitatis, & ad patientiam sub ipse adventus Domini, ut multis locis, sic praecipue in fine Cap. 10. verf. 36, Ergo sanctitati & patientiae studendum est.
units.tr: "As also": Argument 7. Paul, in his Epistle written to you Hebrews (according to no small measure of the wisdom given to him), diligently exhorted to the pursuit of holiness and to patience under the very coming of the Lord, as in many places, so especially at the end of chapter 10, verse 36. Therefore we must strive after holiness and patience.

units.la: Verf. 16. Ut qui in omnibus fere epistolis loquatur de iis: inter quae sunt nonnulla difficilia intellectu, quae indocti parumque, stabiles detorquent, ut & reliquas Scripturas, suo ipsorum exitio.
units.tr: Verse 16. As also in almost all his epistles he speaks of these things, among which are some things hard to understand, which the untaught and unstable twist, as they do the rest of the Scriptures, to their own destruction.

units.la: Ex mentione facta Epistolae Pauli ad Hebraeos captat occasionem commendandi reliquas Pauli Epistolas pro Canonicis, & tollit scandalum difficultatis quorundam locorum in ipsius Epistolis, ex eo, Quod non detorqueantur nec Pauli dicta, nec aliae Scripturae ullae nisi ab indoctis vel instabilibus, vel perversis hominibus, idque in perniciem suam ipsorum, qui pervertunt eas.
units.tr: From the mention made of Paul's Epistle to the Hebrews he seizes the occasion of commending the remaining Epistles of Paul as canonical, and removes the stumbling-block of the difficulty of certain passages in his Epistles, on the ground that neither Paul's sayings nor any other Scriptures are twisted except by the untaught or unstable or perverse men, and that to their own ruin, since they who pervert them do so to their own destruction.

units.la: Verf 17. Vos igitur, dilecti, qui haec praescitis cavete ne illorum nefariorum errore abducti, excidatis a propria stabilitate: Vers. 18 Sed crescite in gratia & agnitione Domini nostri & Servatoris Iesu Christi: cui gloria & nunc & ad tempus sempiternum. Amen.
units.tr: Verse 17. You therefore, beloved, who know these things beforehand, take heed lest, being led away by the error of those wicked men, you fall from your own steadfastness. Verse 18. But grow in grace and in the knowledge of our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ, to whom be glory both now and for ever. Amen.

units.la: Arg. 8. Hortationis modo propositum, ad carnis ignaviam excutiendam. Praemoniti de falsorum Doctorum erroribus, quibus discipulos suos seducunt à via veritatis & sanctitatis, non tantum cavere vobis tanto magis debetis, ne excidatis à propria stabilitate, (id est, à fide & obedientia doctrinae Christi, in qua fixo animi proposito jam stătis) sed etiam studere debetis ut proficiatis & crescatis in gratia seu sanctitate, & in notitia seu fide Domini nostri Iesu Christi.
units.tr: Argument 8, set forth in the manner of exhortation, to shake off the sluggishness of the flesh.
