Having been forewarned about the errors of false teachers, by which they seduce their disciples from the way of truth and holiness, you ought all the more to take heed that you do not fall from your own steadfastness (that is, from the faith and obedience of the doctrine of Christ, in which you now stand with a mind fixed in purpose), but you ought also to strive to advance and grow in grace or holiness, and in the knowledge or faith of our Lord Jesus Christ.

units.la: Cui gloria] Claudit Epistolam doxologia insigni, qua Christum verum Deum agnoscit: nam Deo soli debetur gloria; Christum autem & nunc, dum in hac mundi militia versamur, glorificandum proponit, & etiam in futuro seculo, quod vocat diem aeternitatis, quia tota aeternitas una dies est. Ipsi sit gloria, AMEN.
units.tr: "To whom be glory": the Epistle closes with a notable doxology, by which he acknowledges Christ as true God; for glory is due to God alone. He sets forth that Christ is to be glorified both now, while we are engaged in this warfare of the world, and also in the future age, which he calls the day of eternity, because all eternity is one day. To him be glory, AMEN.

units.la: EXPOSITIO ANALYTICA PRIMAE EPISTOLAE IOANNIS. Summarium.
units.tr: Analytical Exposition of the First Epistle of John. Summary.

units.la: Ioannis Apostoli (qui & Evangelium scripsit, & Apocalypsin) tres extant Epistolae. Hujus quae primi est scopus est docere qua ratione habeamus communionem cum Deo, & quo pacto de ea communione certi esse possumus, ad plenam consolationem in vita & in morte. In quem finem proponit summam doctrinae Evangelicae, Capite primo. Usum huius doctrinae ostendit in variis hortationibus, nempe ad studium sanctitatis, ad dilectionem fratrum, ad odium mundi, & constantiam in fide, Capite secundo. Prosequitur hortationem ad studium justitiae & fraternae dilectionis, Capite tertio Similiter, post hortationem ad cavendum à seductoribus, pergit in hortatione ad diligendum fratres, Capite quarto. Denique, Ut credentes sciant se vitam habere, & scientes magis magisque credant in Iesum Christum, notas Fidelium, & Argumenta ad credendum abundè cumulat, Capite quinto.
units.tr: Three Epistles of the Apostle John survive (he also wrote the Gospel and the Apocalypse). The aim of the first is to teach by what reasoning we may have communion with God, and by what means we can be certain of that communion, for full consolation in life and in death. To this end he sets out the sum of evangelical doctrine in chapter 1. He shows the use of this doctrine in various exhortations, namely to the pursuit of holiness, to love of the brothers, to hatred of the world, and to constancy in the faith, in chapter 2. He continues the exhortation to the pursuit of righteousness and brotherly love in chapter 3. Similarly, after the exhortation to beware of seducers, he goes on to exhort us to love the brothers, in chapter 4. Finally, that believers may know that they have life, and knowing it may believe more and more in Jesus Christ, he heaps up in abundance the marks of the faithful and the arguments for believing, in chapter 5.

units.la: Artificiosa valde est huius Epistolæ Methodus, Nam ad modum catenæ, Christiana Fidei mysteria, & axiomata connectuntur. Semper enim ex fine præcedentis doctrinæ sequentem tractationem orditur.
units.tr: The method of this Epistle is very skilful. For the Christian mysteries and axioms are linked together as in a chain, and always from the end of the preceding doctrine the following discussion takes its start.

units.la: Caput Primum.
units.tr: Chapter One.

units.la: HOC Capite summam Doctrinæ Euangelicæ à se & reliquis Apostolis prædicatæ, proponit. Capitis duæ sunt partes, In prima confirmat præstantiam suæ prædicationis, & objectum fidei salvificæ ostendit, ad versum textum. In altera notas dat hominis verè fidelis, ad quem gratia Euangelii prædicati vere pertinet, ad finem.
units.tr: In this chapter he sets out the sum of the Evangelical doctrine that he and the other apostles preached. The chapter has two parts. In the first he confirms the excellence of his preaching and shows the object of saving faith, in the verse below. In the second he gives the marks of the man who is truly faithful, and to whom the grace of the preached Gospel truly belongs, at the end.

units.la: Verf. 1. Quod erat à principio, quod audivimus, quod vidimus oculis nostris, quod spectavimus, & manus nostræ contrectarunt de Sermone vitæ.
units.tr: Verse 1. That which was from the beginning, which we have heard, which we have seen with our eyes, which we have looked upon, and our hands have handled, concerning the Word of life.

units.la: Præstantiam Euangelii à se prædicati confirmat octo rationibus: Ratio prima continetur ultimis huius versiculi verbis, scilicet, quod ipsius Euangelium tractet de præstantissimo objecto, nempe de Verbo, seu Sermone Vitæ, id est, de Filio Dei Iesu Christo, qui dicitur Λόγος Sermo, ut distinctionem Personæ Filii à Patre, & ordinem operandi concipiamus, cum Sermo sit alicujus, nempe Patris Sermo: Et ut doceat generationis Filii modum spiritualem, & immanentem, & inseparabilem esse ejus subsistentiam à Patre, & ut ejus officium præcipuè respiciamus, quod est Deum & Dei consilium de nostra salute declarare. Deinde dicitur Sermo Vitæ: 1. Quia vitam habet in seipso, & Ipse Vita est: 2. Quia comparavit vitam nobis, eamque ostendit; Et denique, quia eam applicat nobis, efficitque ut vitam æternam vivamus.
units.tr: He confirms the excellence of the Gospel he preached by eight reasons. The first reason is contained in the last words of this verse, namely that the Gospel deals with the most excellent object, that is, the Word or Speech of life, that is, the Son of God Jesus Christ, who is called the Word [Λόγος]. We are to grasp this so that we understand the distinction of the Person of the Son from the Father and the order of their working, since a word belongs to someone, namely the Word of the Father. It also teaches the spiritual and indwelling mode of the Son's generation, and that his subsistence is inseparable from the Father. And we should chiefly regard his office, which is to declare God and God's counsel concerning our salvation. Next, he is called the Word of life: (1) because he has life in himself and is himself life; (2) because he has obtained life for us and shown it to us; and finally, (3) because he applies it to us and makes us live the eternal life.

units.la: Quod erat Ratio 2. Præstantiæ prædicationis suæ, Quod veritas prædicata antiqua sit, nempe quæ erat ab initio: partim, quatenus nulla unquam erat alia ratio salutis præter unicam hanc in Christo solo, qui est Agnus occisus ab initio mundi. Partim quia Christus prædicatus ab Apostolo, quoad divinitatem, ante incarnationem subsistebat ab initio mundi, idem Dei Filius & Mediator salutis nostrae: & mundi initio erat, cum res creatae nondum subsisterent, sed inciperent esse, seu qui ab aeterno idem in aeternum est. Subjectum ergo Euangelii nostri excellentissimum est.
units.tr: That which was. The second reason for the excellence of his preaching is that the truth preached is ancient, namely that which was from the beginning. This is partly because no other way of salvation has ever existed apart from this one in Christ alone, who is the Lamb slain from the beginning of the world. It is partly because Christ, preached by the apostle, as to his divinity, subsisted from the beginning of the world before the incarnation, being the same Son of God and Mediator of our salvation. He was at the beginning of the world, when created things did not yet exist but were only beginning to be; he is the one who from eternity is the same to eternity. Therefore the subject of our Gospel is most excellent.

units.la: Quod vidimus ] Ratio 3. Quia veritas praedicata est certa & comperta Apostolis, quippe qui infallibili sensuum testimonio, CHRISTUM ipsum suis temporibus manifestatum in carne, seu incarnatum, oculati & auriti testes observaverant. Partim auribus de die in diem doctrinam CHRISTI, sanctam & audibili voce prolatam, hauriendo: partim ejus facta & ordinaria & miraculosa, & passiones in carne, & glorificationem in transfiguratione, & resurrectionem a mortuis, oculis videndo; & post penitissimam inquisitionem in rei veritatem, clarissime perspiciendo: Partim denique ejus carnem, seu humanam naturam assumptam manibus palpando & contrectando. Unde certitudo testimonii ipsorum de CHRISTO exhibito ita constat, ut in dubium vocari non poterit. Excellentissima igitur est veritas a nobis praedicata.
units.tr: That which we have seen. The third reason is that the truth preached is certain and established for the apostles, who as eyewitnesses and earwitnesses observed Christ himself, manifested in the flesh, that is, incarnate, in their own times, by the infallible testimony of the senses. Partly they took in with their ears, day by day, the doctrine of Christ, holy and uttered in an audible voice; partly with their eyes they saw his deeds, both ordinary and miraculous, his sufferings in the flesh, his glorification in the transfiguration, and his resurrection from the dead, and they perceived these most clearly after the most careful inquiry into the truth of the matter; and partly they touched and handled with their hands his flesh, that is, the human nature he had assumed. Hence the certainty of their testimony concerning Christ manifested is so firmly established that it cannot be called into doubt. The truth we preach is therefore most excellent.

units.la: Vers. 2. ( Nam vita patefacta est, & vidimus & testamur, & annuntiamus vobis vitam illam aeternam, quae erat apud Patrem, & patefacta est nobis )
units.tr: Verse 2. (For the life was manifested, and we have seen and bear witness, and show to you that eternal life which was with the Father, and was manifested to us.)

units.la: Ratio 4. in parenthesi interjecta confirmans priorem, De CHRISTO novimus, 1. Quod sit vita illa, verus JEHOVAH, qui in se vita est essentialiter, & respectu nostri causaliter: quippe Autor vitae nostrae, non naturalis tantum, sed etiam spiritualis & aeternae, Autor lucis & illuminationis, Autor gratiae & omnis pii, seu laudabilis motus: 2. Quod divinitus talis manifestatus sit, & nobis patefactus & per patefactionem visus & agnitus a nobis esse vita illa: 3. Quem esse vitam revelatam vidimus & agnovimus, eum testamur esse vitam, & praedicamus vobis, nempe eum esse, & aeternum DEUM, & aeternae vitae nobis communicandae Procuratorem, Datorem, & Conservatorem: 4. Novimus FILIUM DEI, secundam Trinitatis personam distinctam, quae ab aeterno erat apud Patrem, & a mundo condito agebat rem nostram apud Patrem, & jam revelata est nobis post incarnationem per divinam patefactionem: Idcirco & praestantissima & certissima est haec nostra veritatis & vitae praedicatio.
units.tr: The fourth reason, set in the parenthesis, confirms the former. Concerning Christ we know: (1) that he is that life, the true Jehovah, who is life in himself essentially and to us causally, being the author of our life, not only natural but also spiritual and eternal, the author of light and illumination, the author of grace and of every godly or praiseworthy motion; (2) that he was thus manifested by God, and made known to us, and by that manifestation was seen and recognised by us to be that life; (3) that we bear witness to him whom we have seen and recognised as the revealed life, and we proclaim to you that he is the eternal God and the Procurer, Giver and Preserver of the eternal life to be communicated to us; (4) we know the Son of God, the distinct second person of the Trinity, who from eternity was with the Father, and from the foundation of the world carried on our cause with the Father, and who has now been revealed to us after the incarnation by divine manifestation. Therefore this our preaching of truth and life is both most excellent and most certain.

units.la: Vers. 3. Quod, inquam, vidimus & audivimus, id annuntiamus vobis, ut & vos communionem habeatis nobiscum: & communio nostra sit cum Patre & cum Filio Iesu Christo.
units.tr: Verse 3. That which we have seen and heard, I say, we declare to you, so that you also may have fellowship with us; and our fellowship is with the Father and with his Son Jesus Christ.

units.la: Ratio 5. Per veritatem prædicatam à nobis Apostolis oculatis & auri- tis testibus, fideles ejusdem felicitatis, & eorundem bonorum nobiscum efficientur participes. Excellentissima est igitur veritas à nobis prædicata.
units.tr: The fifth reason: through the truth preached by us apostles, who were eyewitnesses and earwitnesses, the faithful become partakers with us of the same happiness and the same good things. Therefore the truth preached by us is most excellent.

units.la: Et communio ] Ratio 6. Qui nobiscum uniuntur in fide prædicatæ à nobis veritatis, etiam cum PATRE & FILIO IESU CHRISTO per Spiritus Sancti virtutem unientur. Ergo.
units.tr: And fellowship. The sixth reason: those who are united with us in faith in the truth preached by us will also be united with the Father and with the Son Jesus Christ through the power of the Holy Spirit. Therefore...

units.la: Versi. 4. Et hæc scribimus vobis, ut gaudium vestrum sit plenum.
units.tr: Verse 4. And we write these things to you, so that your joy may be full.

units.la: Ratio 7. Prædicationis nostræ summa ad vos scripta pro fine habet, ut gaudeatis gaudium verum ac spirituale, certi redditi de electione & glorificatione, utque gaudium illud veltrum constet & perficiatur: Me- rito ergo excellentissima habenda est.
units.tr: The seventh reason: the sum of our preaching, written to you, has as its end that you may rejoice in a true and spiritual joy, made certain of election and glorification, and that this your joy may be established and brought to completion. Rightly, then, it must be regarded as most excellent.

units.la: Versi. 5. Hoc est igitur nuntium quod audivimus ex ipso, & renuntiamus vobis, Deum lucem esse, & tenebras in eo esse nullas.
units.tr: This is the message. Verse 5. This, then, is the message which we have heard from him and declare to you, that God is light, and in him there is no darkness at all.

units.la: Ratio 8. Summa prædicationis nostræ est, quod Deus sit Lux, seu adversus mala ignorantiæ, errorum, falsitatis, vitiorum & miseriæ, quæ sunt in nobis, præsentissimum & perfectissimum remedium: & quod in se Deus sit ab his malis alienissimus, adeo ut impossibile sit accedentes ad ipsum decipi, non illuminari & dirigi: à peccatis & miseriâ non liberari, & æternam salutem non consequi: Ergo excellentem esse prædicationem meam, & reliquorum Apostolorum necesse est.
units.tr: The eighth reason: the sum of our preaching is that God is Light, that is, the most present and most perfect remedy against the evils of ignorance, error, falsehood, vice and wretchedness that are in us; and that God in himself is most remote from these evils, so that it is impossible for those who approach him to be deceived, not enlightened and directed, not freed from sin and misery, and not to obtain eternal salvation. Therefore it is necessary that my preaching, and that of the other apostles, be excellent.

units.la: Secunda pars Capitis.
units.tr: The second part of the chapter.

units.la: Versi. 6. Si dixerimus nos societatem habere cum eo, & in tenebris incedimus, mentimur, nec sincere agimus.
units.tr: Verse 6. If we say that we have fellowship with him, and walk in darkness, we lie, and do not act sincerely.

units.la: Altera pars Capitis, in qua proponit partim negative, partim affirma- tive notas seu indicia vere fidelis, qui particeps futurus est bonorum in Evangelio promissorum. Notæ autem sunt quinque.
units.tr: The other part of the chapter, in which he sets out, partly negatively and partly affirmatively, the marks or signs of the truly faithful man, who will be a partaker of the good things promised in the Gospel. There are five marks.

units.la: Nota prima, negative proponitur cum sui confirmatione, Vere fide- lis non ambulat in tenebris, non est deditus peccato, vitam agens secun- dum cupiditates carnales; quia si quis profitetur se cum Deo, qui lux & sanctitas est communionem habere, & interim ambulat in peccato- rum suorum tenebris, hypocrita & mendax est, utpote qui non facit quod rectum est, sed quod ore profitetur, operibus negat.
units.tr: The first mark is set out negatively, with its confirmation: the truly faithful man does not walk in darkness, is not given over to sin, and does not live according to carnal desires. For if anyone professes that he has communion with God, who is light and holiness, and yet meanwhile walks in the darkness of his sins, he is a hypocrite and a liar, since he does not do what is right but denies by his works what he professes with his mouth.

units.la: Versi. 7. Quod si in luce incedimus, sicut ipse est in luce, communionem habemus cum eo mutuam, & sanguis Iesu Christi Fi- lii ejus purgat nos ab omni peccato. Nota . Affirmativè propônitur, Qui ambulat in luce, seu qui sanctitati studet, ut conformis sit Deo, qui lux seu perfecta sanctitas est, is est vere fidelis, verè communionem habens cum Deo & sanctis, & ad quem fructus mortis Christi ad peccatorum remissionem solidè pertinet.
units.tr: Verse 7. But if we walk in the light, as he is in the light, we have fellowship one with another, and the blood of Jesus Christ his Son cleanseth us from all sin. Note. It is set out affirmatively: whoever walks in the light, that is, who strives after holiness so as to be conformed to God, who is light or perfect holiness, is truly faithful, truly has communion with God and with the saints, and to him the fruit of Christ's death for the remission of sins belongs firmly.

units.la: Vers. 8. Si dixerimus nos peccatum non habere, nosmetipsos fallimus, & veritas in nobis non est.
units.tr: Verse 8. If we say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves, and the truth is not in us.

units.la: Nota 3 negativa. Verè fidelis, non ita est justus in oculis suis, ut vel verbo vel facto neget se peccare posse, vel peccasse post justificationem, vel qui (quasi non egeret quotidiana Christi intercessione, meritique ipsius applicatione quotidianâ ad conscientiæ à novo reatu liberationem) non tangatur peccati sensu, ita ut ad Christum liberatorem subinde confugiat. Quisquis enim sive verbo, sive opere, & reipsâ sic negat se peccatum habere in præsenti, seipsum decipit, & hypocrita est, in quo non est sinceritas.
units.tr: Mark 3, negative. The truly faithful man is not so righteous in his own eyes that he denies, either by word or by deed, that he can sin, or that he has sinned after justification; nor is he one who (as if he did not need Christ's daily intercession and the daily application of his merit to free his conscience from new guilt) is not touched by a sense of sin, so that he flees at times to Christ the deliverer. For whoever denies that he has sin at present, whether by word or by work, and in fact, deceives himself and is a hypocrite, in whom there is no sincerity.

units.la: Vers. 9. Si confiteamur peccata nostra, fidelis est & justus, ut remittat nobis peccata nostra, & purget nos ab omni iniquitate.
units.tr: Verse 9. If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.

units.la: Nota 4. Verè fidelis tali sensu peccatorum suorum subinde afficitur, ut ea agnoscat coram Deo, & confiteatur ex animo, mortem se mereri æternam, nec posse expiari reatum suum aliter, quam merito sanguinis Filii Dei nec nisi divina Spiritus Christi virtute, posse se sanctificari, seu à peccati immunditie liberari.
units.tr: Mark 4. The truly faithful man is at times so affected by a sense of his sins that he acknowledges them before God and confesses from his heart that he deserves eternal death, and that his guilt cannot be expiated otherwise than by the merit of the blood of the Son of God, and that he cannot be sanctified, that is, freed from the uncleanness of sin, except by the divine power of the Spirit of Christ.

units.la: Fidelis ] Ei qui sic confitetur peccata Apostolus promittit ex fidelitate & justitia Dei fore, ut absolvatur à peccati reatu, & purgetur, seu sanctificetur à peccati labe: fidelis enim est Deus, qui illa promisit, & justus est Deus, qui satisfactionem nactus a Christo Sponsore, non exigat debitum ab eo, pro quo satisfecit Christus, sed contrà præstet fideli omnia bona, quæ in ipsius salutem Christus emit.
units.tr: Faithful. To one who thus confesses his sins, the Apostle promises that, from the faithfulness and justice of God, it will come about that he is absolved from the guilt of sin and cleansed, or sanctified from the stain of sin. For God is faithful, who made those promises, and God is just, who, having received satisfaction from Christ the Surety, does not exact the debt from him for whom Christ made satisfaction, but on the contrary bestows on the believer all the good things which Christ purchased for his salvation.

units.la: Vers. 10. Si dixerimus nos non peccasse, mendacem facimus eum & sermo ejus non est in nobis.
units.tr: Verse 10. If we say that we have not sinned, we make him a liar, and his word is not in us.

units.la: Nota 5. negativa. Qui verè fidelis est, nec negat, nec extenuat peccata præterita, quasi vel cum Pharisæo illo omnia Dei mandata præstitisset à juventute; vel quasi originale peccatum vel nullum esset, vel morte minimè dignum: Nec impænitens est, quasi quæ admiserit, leviora peccata sint, seu venialia, quæ expiatione sanguinis Christi non opus habeant, vel quasi in natura ipsius non esset tanta corruptio, quin libero suo arbitrio se ad gratiam disponere & gratiam mereri, vel saltem consequi se posse, suis viribus confidat. Nam qui vel sic, vel ullo alio modo directè vel indirectè negat se peccasse, & per consequens negat mortis adeo reum se esse vel fuisse, ut opus fuerit tanta expiatione, quanta est mors filii Dei, blasphemus est in Deum, (eum arguens mendacii qui in verbo suo peccatores, & mortis reos omnes peregit, nec ullam esse remissionem peccatorum nisi per sanguinem Filii sui affirmavit) nec sermo Dei per fidem unquam receptus est in ejus corde: id est, nunquam fidem habuit doctrinae legis, nedum Euangelii.
units.tr: Mark 5, negative. He who is truly faithful neither denies nor extenuates past sins, as if he had fulfilled all God's commandments from his youth, like that Pharisee, or as if original sin were either non-existent or not deserving of death. Nor is he unrepentant, as if the sins he has committed were lighter, or venial, needing no expiation by the blood of Christ, or as if there were not in his nature such corruption that he trusts in his own powers to dispose himself to grace by his free will, and to merit grace, or at least to obtain it. For whoever denies, either in this way or in any other way, directly or indirectly, that he has sinned, and consequently denies that he is, or has been, so much a debtor to death that an expiation as great as the death of the Son of God was needed, is a blasphemer against God (accusing of lying him who in his word has condemned all men as sinners and debtors to death, and has affirmed that there is no remission of sins except through the blood of his Son), and the word of God has never been received by faith in his heart: that is, he has never had faith in the doctrine of the law, much less in the Gospel.

units.la: Caput Secundum.
units.tr: Chapter 2.

units.la: Rget usum superioris doctrinae tota reliqua Epistola, in quem finem proponuntur hortationes quinque hoc capite. Prima, ad verf. 9. Secunda, ad verf. 15. Tertia ad verf. 18. Quarta ad verf. 29. Quinta, versu ultimo.
units.tr: The whole remaining Epistle draws on the teaching above, and to this end five exhortations are set out in this chapter. The first runs to verse 9, the second to verse 15, the third to verse 18, the fourth to verse 29, and the fifth is in the last verse.

units.la: Filioli mei, haec scribo vobis, ne peccetis. Quod si quis peccarit, advocatum apud Patrem habemus, Iesum Christum justum.
units.tr: My little children, I write these things to you so that you may not sin. And if anyone sins, we have an advocate with the Father, Jesus Christ the righteous.

units.la: Hortatio prima est ad studium sanctitatis ne peccarent. Rationes hortationis praeter amicam compellationem sunt undecim.
units.tr: The first exhortation is to the pursuit of holiness, that they should not sin. Apart from the friendly form of address, there are eleven reasons for this exhortation.

units.la: Ratio prima, Quia hic finis & usus est doctrinae Euangelicae & scriptionis Apostoli. Haec scribo ne peccetis, inquit, Ergo studete sanctimoniae.
units.tr: The first reason: this is the aim and purpose of the Gospel teaching and of the Apostle's writing. "I write these things," he says, "so that you may not sin." Therefore, strive for holiness.

units.la: Quod si] Ratio 2. Si studueritis sanctimoniae, peccata in quae forte incidetis, per intercessionem Iesu Christi Advocati, & Domini nostri, auferentur. Ergo sanctimoniae operam date. Cum unum Advocatum nominat, alios omnes excludit, alioqui enim Christus esset non simpliciter Advocatus noster, sed ex Advocatis unus.
units.tr: "And if"... The second reason: if you strive for holiness, the sins into which you may perhaps fall will be taken away through the intercession of Jesus Christ, our Advocate and Lord. Therefore, devote your effort to holiness. In naming one Advocate he excludes all others; otherwise Christ would not be simply our Advocate, but one of several advocates.

units.la: Justum] Ratio 3. confirmans etiam priorem; Christus Advocatus justus est, id est, non tantum idoneus qui intercedat pro peccatoribus, propter justitiam personae suae, sed etiam justus in officio suo, qui nihil postulet a Patre nomine nostro, nisi quod ex pacto & mortis merito, intercedenti pro nobis juste debetur. Justus etiam est ut nos justitia sua imputata tegat. Et justus denique, qui ex pacto Redemptionis nos injustitiae justitiæ studio promoveat, à lapsibus resuscitet, & plenè tandem justos seu sanctos reddat. Ergo & debent fideles sanctitati studere, & si forte labantur in peccatum, virtutem intercessionis Christi sperare.
units.tr: "The righteous": the third reason, which also confirms the first. Christ is the righteous Advocate, that is, not merely fit to intercede for sinners because of the righteousness of his person, but also righteous in his office. He asks nothing of the Father in our name except what is justly owed to the intercessor by the covenant and by the merit of his death. He is also righteous in covering us with his imputed righteousness. And finally he is righteous in that, by the covenant of redemption, he advances us in the pursuit of righteousness, raises us up from our falls, and at last makes us fully righteous, or holy. Therefore believers ought to pursue holiness, and if perhaps they slip into sin, they should hope for the power of Christ's intercession. Christ

units.la: Versf. 2. Et ipse est propitiatio pro peccatis nostris: nec pro nostris solùm sed etiam pro totius mundi peccatis.
units.tr: Verse 2. And he is the propitiation for our sins; and not for ours only, but also for the sins of the whole world.

units.la: Ratio 4. confirmans etiam rationem secundam, Mors Christi victima expiatoria, fuit oblata, non tantum pro nobis ex Judæis electis scilicet, & ad fidem Christi conversis, sed etiam pro peccatis omnium Electorum, seu redemptorum in mundo. Ergo cavere debetis à peccati malo, quod non nisi Christi morte expiari potuit: & si peccetis, expiationis adeo divitis & intercessionis Christi virtutem confidenter expectare.
units.tr: The fourth reason, which also confirms the second: the death of Christ, as an expiatory sacrifice, was offered not only for us who are elect Jews and converted to faith in Christ, but also for the sins of all the elect, or redeemed, in the world. Therefore you must beware of the evil of sin, which could be expiated only by the death of Christ. And if you do sin, you should confidently look for the power of so rich an expiation and of Christ's intercession.

units.la: Verf. 3. Et per hoc scimus nos eum nosse, si mandata ipsius observamus.
units.tr: Verse 3. And hereby we do know that we know him, if we keep his commandments.

units.la: Ratio hortationis ad studium sanctitatis, quinta. Per studium sincerè observandi Dei præcepta, tanquam per firmum indicium, cognoscere poteritis fidei vestræ veritatem, seu quod verè credatis in Deum, eumque sincerè diligatis. Ergo studete sanctimoniæ, seu ne peccetis.
units.tr: The fifth reason for the exhortation to the pursuit of holiness: by sincerely striving to observe God's precepts, as by a firm sign, you can come to know the truth of your faith, that is, that you truly believe in God and sincerely love him. Therefore, strive for holiness, that is, that you may not sin.

units.la: Verf. 4 Qui dicit, Novi eum, & mandata ejus non servat, mendax est, & in eo veritas non est:
units.tr: Verse 4. He that saith, I know him, and keepeth not his commandments, is a liar, and the truth is not in him.

units.la: Ratio 6. Qui profitetur se nósse Deum, id est, credere in Eum, Eumque diligere, & sanctitati non studet (nam secundum Euangelii stylum, sincerè operam dare sanctitati, est mandata servare) hypocrita est, in quo non est sinceritas, seu fidei veritas: Ergo Sanctimoniæ studete.
units.tr: The sixth reason: whoever professes to know God, that is, to believe in him and love him, and does not strive for holiness (for in the language of the Gospel, to devote sincere effort to holiness is to keep the commandments), is a hypocrite in whom there is no sincerity, that is, no truth of faith. Therefore, strive for holiness.

units.la: Verf. 5. Qui autem servat sermonem ejus, verè in hoc charitas Dei expleta est: per hoc scimus nos in ipso esse.
units.tr: Verse 5. But whoso keepeth his word, in him verily is the love of God perfected: hereby know we that we are in him.

units.la: Ratio 7. Qui studet sanctitati, probat sinceritatem dilectionis suæ erga Deum, quæ dilectio impletur, seu sincera esse declaratur, ex studio custodiendi sermonem Dei, eiquæ obediendi. Studendum igitur Sanctitati. Per hoc Ratio 8. Qui studet sanctitati, seu non peccare, seu sermonem Dei custodire, indicium habet suæ cum Deo communionis, & scit se in Christo per fidem habitare, Ergo, &c.
units.tr: The seventh reason: whoever strives for holiness proves the sincerity of his love towards God, and that love is fulfilled, or is shown to be sincere, by the effort to keep God's word and obey it. Holiness is therefore to be pursued. Hereby The eighth reason: whoever strives for holiness, that is, not to sin, or to keep God's word, has a sign of his communion with God, and knows that he dwells in Christ through faith. Therefore, etc.

units.la: Verf. 6 Qui dicit se in eo habitare, debet, sicut ille ambulavit, ita & ipse ambulare.
units.tr: Verse 6. He that saith he abideth in him ought himself also so to walk, even as he walked.

units.la: Ratio 9. confirmans priorem. Quicunque profitetur communionem le habere cum Christo, debet sanctitati studere, seu in vita & conversatione Christum imitari. Ergo Sanctimoniae studendum est.
units.tr: The ninth reason, which confirms the previous one: whoever professes to have communion with Christ ought to strive for holiness, that is, to imitate Christ in life and conduct. Therefore holiness must be pursued.

units.la: Verf. 7. Fratres, novam doctrinam non scribo vobis, sed doctrinam veterem, quam videlicet habuistis jam inde a principio: vetus haec doctrina, sermo ille est quem audistis jam inde a principio.
units.tr: Verse 7. Brethren, I write no new commandment unto you, but an old commandment which ye had from the beginning. The old commandment is the word which ye have heard from the beginning.

units.la: Ratio 10. Nullum novum officium a vobis exigo, cum urgeo sanctitatis studium, seu mandatorum Dei observationem, sed vetus mandatum repeto, quod non solum a Christo & ejus ministris, ab initio audivistis, sed etiam ex Lege & Prophetis vobis commendatum habuistis. Ergo Sanctitati studete.
units.tr: The tenth reason: when I press the pursuit of holiness, that is, the observance of God's commandments, I impose no new duty on you, but repeat an old command, which you have heard not only from Christ and his ministers from the beginning, but also had commended to you in the Law and the Prophets. Therefore, strive for holiness.

units.la: Verf. 8. E contrario doctrinam novam scribo vobis, quod verum est in ipso, & in vobis: quia tenebrae praeterunt, & vera illa lux jam lucet.
units.tr: Verse 8. Again, a new commandment I write unto you, which thing is true in him and in you: because the darkness is past, and the true light now shineth.

units.la: Ratio 11. Mandatum hoc non est vetus in vetustate literae, quale olim erat quandiu sub foedere operum irregeniti degebatis, quando lex jubebat, & vires nullas ad praestandum conferebat, sed novum est in novitate spiritus: ad quod praestandum Christus gratiam subinde novam suppeditaturus est vobis. Ergo sanctitati studendum est.
units.tr: The eleventh reason: this commandment is not old in the oldness of the letter, as it was once, when you lived under the covenant of works in your unregenerate state, when the Law commanded but gave no strength to perform it. It is new in the newness of the Spirit, and for performing it Christ will from time to time supply you with fresh grace. Therefore, holiness must be pursued.

units.la: Id quod ] Quid sit novum mandatum ipse exponit proximis verbis, affirmans mandatum novum, esse & respectu Christi, qui scilicet mandatum vivificat, & respectu ipsorum, qui novae creaturae jam facti erant per regenerationem, id est, quibus gratia suppeditata & porro suppeditanda erat ad obedientiam.
units.tr: Which thing He himself explains in the words that follow, affirming that the commandment is new both with respect to Christ, who quickens the commandment, and with respect to those who had already been made new creatures through regeneration, that is, to whom grace had been and was to be supplied for obedience.

units.la: Quia tenebrae ] Ratio redditur in hunc sensum, Quia non estis sub lege, sed sub gratia; non estis in statu irregenerationis, sed renovati. Nam tenebrae nempe foederis legalis, & status irregenerationis, transierunt, & jam Christus qui vitam & gratiam affert secum, & vera est lux, vobis fidelibus ut Sol justitiae ortus est, & lucem simul & calorem vitae, vobis communicavit. Ergo praeceptum vobis novum est, ut animari debeatis ad studium sanctitatis alacrius prosequendum.
units.tr: Because the darkness The reason is given in this sense: because you are not under the Law but under grace; you are not in the state of unregeneration but renewed. For the darkness, namely of the legal covenant and of the state of unregeneration, has passed away, and now Christ, who brings life and grace with him, is the true light, risen for you believers as the Sun of righteousness, and has imparted to you light and at the same time the warmth of life. Therefore the command is new to you, so that you may be roused to pursue the pursuit of holiness more eagerly.

units.la: Verf. 9. Qui dicit se in luce esse, & fratrem suum odit, in tenebris est usque adhuc.
units.tr: Verse 9. He that saith he is in the light, and hateth his brother, is in darkness even until now.

units.la: Secunda hortatio contrahens superiorem ad dilectionem Fratrum: Argumenta hortationis sunt decem, praeter illa duo quae proxime recitata sunt, & huc etiam referri possunt. Argumentum primum, Quicunque profitetur se in luce esse, seu regeneratum, & odit fratrem, ad- huc in tenebris ignorantiæ & peccati jacet irregenitus. Studendum ergo dilectioni fraternæ.
units.tr: The second exhortation, which draws the former one towards love of the brethren. There are ten arguments for this exhortation, besides the two just recited, and these too may be referred here. The first argument: whoever professes to be in the light, that is, regenerate, and hates his brother, still lies in the darkness of ignorance and sin, unregenerate. Therefore, brotherly love must be pursued.

units.la: Vers. 10 Qui diligit fratrem suum, in luce manet, & offendiculum in eo non est.
units.tr: Verse 10. He that loveth his brother abideth in the light, and there is none occasion of stumbling in him.

units.la: Arg. 2. Qui diligit fratrem suum, manet in luce, & perseverat in via veritatis, sortem & conditionem Sanctorum aliqua ex parte possidens: Ergo studendum, &c.
units.tr: The second argument: whoever loves his brother abides in the light and persists in the way of truth, possessing in some measure the lot and condition of the saints. Therefore, it must be pursued, etc.

units.la: Et offendiculum ] Arg. 3. Qui diligit fratrem, nec ipse impingit in via sanctitatis (semper videns quo vadat, nempe ad Deum ex fide per viam obedientiæ) nec aliis offendiculum præbet, quo vel inducantur in peccatum, vel indurentur in peccato. Studendum ergo dilectioni fraternæ.
units.tr: And there is none occasion of stumbling The third argument: whoever loves his brother neither stumbles himself in the way of holiness (always seeing where he is going, namely to God, by faith, through the way of obedience), nor gives occasion of stumbling to others, by which they might be led into sin or hardened in it. Therefore, brotherly love must be pursued.

units.la: Vers. 11. Qui autem odit fratrem suum, in tenebris est, & in tenebris ambulat: & nescit quo eat, quia tenebræ oculos ipsius obcæcaverunt.
units.tr: Verse 11. But he that hateth his brother is in darkness, and walketh in darkness, and knoweth not whither he goeth, because that darkness hath blinded his eyes.

units.la: Arg. 4. Qui odit fratrem, totus in peccato jacet & perseverat, & deflectens de via recta, quæ ad salutem ducit, fertur in præcipitium, ignorans quo tendat, quia peccato occæcatur ejus mens: Ergo dilectioni fraternæ studendum.
units.tr: The fourth argument: whoever hates his brother lies wholly in sin and persists in it, and turning aside from the straight way that leads to salvation, is carried towards destruction, not knowing where he is heading, because his mind is blinded by sin. Therefore brotherly love must be pursued.

units.la: Vers. 12 Scribo vobis filioli, quoniam remissa sunt vobis peccata, propter nomen ejus.
units.tr: Verse 12: I write to you, little children, because your sins are forgiven you for his name's sake.

units.la: Arg. 5. O Fideles filioli & De I, & mei, gratis remissa sunt vobis peccata veltra propter nomen Christi, id est, propter Christi meritum, quod vobis prædicatum est, & fide apprehensum à vobis: Scriptâ ergo hâc hortatione ad sanctimoniam & fraternam dilectionem obstricti tenemini ad obediendum ei.
units.tr: Argument 5. O faithful little children, your sins are forgiven you freely for Christ's name, that is, for the merit of Christ, which has been preached to you and grasped by you through faith. Therefore, having been bound by this written exhortation to holiness and brotherly love, you are obliged to obey it.

units.la: Vers. 13. Scribo vobis, patres, quoniam noflis eum qui àprincipio est. Scribo vobis, adolescentes, quoniam Malum illum vicistis. Scribo vobis, pueruli, quoniam noflis Patrem.
units.tr: Verse 13: I write to you, fathers, because you know him who is from the beginning. I write to you, young men, because you have overcome the evil one. I write to you, little children, because you know the Father.

units.la: Arg. 6. Ab omnis ætatis & ordinis fidelibus sine exceptione, requiritur studium sanctitatis, & fraternæ dilectionis: nominatim à senioribus, qui propterea tenemini obedire, quia admissi estis ad cognitionem Antiqui dierum, seu æterni Filii De I; cujus cognitio vos beatiores reddidit, quam omnis illa veltra ex usu & experientia multorum annorum hausta rerum cognitio. Ergo studendum, &c. Adolescentes ] Arg. 7. Quia sicut omnes, sic adolescentes tenentur obedire, propterea quod victoria data sit illis contra diabolum in CHRISTO. In quo etiam vires ad quotidie vincendum suppeditantur, quae victoria bellicas omnes laudes superat.
units.tr: Argument 6. From the faithful of every age and rank, without exception, the pursuit of holiness and brotherly love is required, and especially from the elders, who are for this reason obliged to obey, because you have been admitted to the knowledge of the Ancient of Days, that is, of the eternal Son of God. This knowledge has made you more blessed than all that worldly knowledge of things which you have drawn from practice and experience over many years. Therefore the duty stands, etc. Young men: Argument 7. Because, just as all others, young men are bound to obey, since victory over the devil has been given to them in Christ. In Christ also the strength to conquer daily is supplied, and this victory surpasses all military glory.

units.la: Pueruli ] Arg. 8. Quia sicut omnes, sic Pueri fideles tenentur obedire his hortationibus, quia quamvis rerum mundanarum nondum periti sint, DEUS seipsis Patrem in CHRISTO demonstravit, & dedit ipsis ut DEUM Patrem suum agnoscerent: Ergo.
units.tr: Little children: Argument 8. Because, just as all others, faithful children are bound to obey these exhortations, since, although they are not yet skilled in worldly affairs, God has shown himself to them as Father in Christ, and has given them to acknowledge God as their Father. Therefore...

units.la: Verf. 14. Scripsi vobis, patres, quoniam noscitis eum qui est a principio. Scripsi vobis, Adolescentes, quia fortes estis, & verbum Dei habitat in vobis, & illum Malum vicistis.
units.tr: Verse 14: I have written to you, fathers, because you know him who is from the beginning. I have written to you, young men, because you are strong, and the word of God dwells in you, and you have overcome the evil one.

units.la: Patres ] Arg. 9 Nova vi repetens sextum Argumentum, Quia sicut omnes, sic imprimis seniores fideles tenentur obedire hortationi, quod ipsis potius quam aliis datum sit cognoscere aeternum DEI Filium, quod beneficium etiam atque etiam in considerationem venire debet.
units.tr: Fathers: Argument 9. Repeating the sixth argument with new force: just as all others, the faithful elders above all are bound to obey this exhortation, since it has been given to them, rather than to others, to know the eternal Son of God, a benefit which ought to be considered again and again.

units.la: Adolescentes ] Arg. 10. Nova vi repetens Argumentum septimum, Qua sicut omnes, sic etiam Adolescentes fideles tenentur obedire hortationi, quandoquidem DEUS ipsos in CHRISTO, primo, ex alto induerit robore spirituali, quod naturali longe praestantius est. Secundo, Et sermonem suum ipsorum animis per SPIRITUM indiderit, ut per fidem constanter in iis maneret: Tertio, Et dedit ipsis etiam ut per CHRISTUM vincerent diabolum; Faciunt etiam haec Argumenta ad sequentem hortationem.
units.tr: Young men: Argument 10. Repeating the seventh argument with new force: just as all others, the faithful young men too are bound to obey this exhortation, since God has first clothed them in Christ with spiritual strength from on high, which is far more excellent than natural strength; secondly, he has placed his word in their minds through the Spirit, so that it might abide constantly in them through faith; thirdly, he has given them also to overcome the devil through Christ. These arguments also bear on the exhortation that follows.

units.la: Verf. 15
units.tr: Verse 15

units.la: Ne diligite mundum, neque ea quae in mundo sunt, si quis diligit mundum, non est charitas Patris in eo.
units.tr: Do not love the world, nor the things that are in the world. If anyone loves the world, the love of the Father is not in him.

units.la: Hortatio 3. Ad cavendum amorem mundi, & eorum quae in mundo sunt. Per mundum intelligit conditionem hominum irregenitorum, in qua sibi placent, felicesque sibi videntur. Per ea quae in mundo sunt, intelligit illecebras, seu ejusmodi bona quibus homines irregeniti capiuntur, quales sunt voluptates, divitiae, honores. Diligere, est in pretio habere, affectare. Argumenta hortationis sunt quatuor.
units.tr: Exhortation 3. To beware of the love of the world and of the things that are in the world. By the world he means the condition of unregenerate men, in which they please themselves and seem happy to themselves. By the things that are in the world he means allurements, or such goods by which unregenerate men are caught, such as pleasures, riches, and honours. To love is to hold in esteem, to aspire after. There are four arguments of the exhortation.

units.la: Si quis ] Argumentum primum, Dilectio mundi ad res mundanas cor alligat, & excludit dilectionem Dei, seu PATRIS, siquidem cor non potest ferri ad contraria studia, vel oppositis dominis servire: Ergo cavenda dilectio mundi.
units.tr: If anyone: The first argument: love of the world binds the heart to worldly things and excludes the love of God, that is, of the Father, since the heart cannot be directed to opposite pursuits or serve opposing masters. Therefore the love of the world is to be avoided.

units.la: · Verf. 16. Quoniam quicquid est in mundo, cupiditas carnis & libido oculorum, & fastus vitæ, non est ex Patre, sed ex mundo est.
units.tr: Verse 16: For all that is in the world, the lust of the flesh, the lust of the eyes, and the pride of life, is not of the Father, but is of the world.

units.la: Arg. 2 confirmans superius, Studia mundanorum hominum ad quæ feruntur homines pleнo impetu, quales sunt Cupiditas carnis, seu voluptas sensualis, gulæ & libidinis; Cupiditas oculorum, seu avaritia inordinatè appetens utilia; & fastus vitæ, seu cupiditas honorum inordinata, in vivendi genere; hæc, inquit, studia non sunt à Deo, sed à corruptelis hominum irregenitorum. Ergo cavenda.
units.tr: Argument 2, confirming what was said above: the pursuits of worldly men, to which people are carried with full force, such as the lust of the flesh, that is, sensual pleasure of gluttony and lust; the lust of the eyes, that is, avarice inordinately desiring useful things; and the pride of life, that is, inordinate desire for honours in the manner of living. These pursuits, he says, are not from God, but from the corruptions of unregenerate men. Therefore they are to be avoided.

units.la: Verf. 17 Porrò mundus præterit, & cupiditas ipsius, Qui verò præstat voluntatem Dei, manet in æternum.
units.tr: Verse 17: And the world passes away, and its lust; but whoever does the will of God abides for ever.

units.la: Arg. 3. Conditio mundanorum hominum, & quæ in hac conditione delectabilia videntur, varia sunt & mox transitura. Ergo non sunt diligenda. Qui verò ] Arg. 4. Qui renunciat voluntati suæ perversæ, & voluntati hominum pravorum, & studet Dei voluntatem facere, vivet in æternum. Cavenda ergo dilectio mundi. Faciunt & hæc ad ea quæ sequuntur.
units.tr: Argument 3. The condition of worldly men, and what in this condition seems delightful, is varied and soon to pass away. Therefore it is not to be loved. But whoever: Argument 4. Whoever renounces his own perverse will and the will of wicked men, and strives to do the will of God, will live for ever. Therefore the love of the world is to be avoided. These arguments also bear on what follows.

units.la: Verf. 18. Tueruli, ultimum tempus adest: & sicut audistis antichristum venturum, etiam nunc antichristi multi cæperunt esse, unde scimus ultimum tempus adesse.
units.tr: Verse 18: Little children, it is the last time; and as you have heard that antichrist is coming, even now many antichrists have appeared; whence we know that it is the last time.

units.la: Hortatio 4. Ut caveant sibi à seductoribus, & ne deficiant à vera fide, sed ut constantes maneant in fide & obedienta veritatis.
units.tr: Exhortation 4. That they should beware of seducers, and not fall away from the true faith, but remain steadfast in the faith and in obedience to the truth.

units.la: Pueruli | Ratiocnes hortationis sunt quindecim: Ratio prima, Ut pueruli opus habetis cautione. Idcirco cavere tenemini. Tempus] Ratio 2. Nunc tempus est, quo periculum est à seductoribus, ultima scilicet hora, & ultimum mundi tempus, in quo Diabolus maximè insanit, sciens quod tempus breve sit, & in quo vigilare, & se parare debent omnes ad judicium in secundo Christi adventu futurum. Ergo.
units.tr: Little children: There are fifteen grounds of this exhortation. The first ground: you little children need caution; therefore you are bound to beware. The time: The second ground: now is the time when there is danger from seducers, namely the last hour, and the last time of the world, in which the devil rages most, knowing that his time is short, and in which all ought to watch and prepare themselves for the judgment to come at Christ's second coming. Therefore...

units.la: Et sicut ] Ratio 3 confirmans priorem, Secundum prænionitionem à Christo & Apostolis factam, de venturo illo Antichristo insigni, venerunt multi præcursores Antichristi, qui sub specie Doctorum, seducunt homines à Christo, & Christi adversarii sunt. Ergo tempus est ultimum, in quo periculum est à seductoribus, à quibus vobis sedulò cavendum est.
units.tr: And as: The third ground, confirming the first: according to the prediction made by Christ and the Apostles concerning that coming notable Antichrist, many forerunners of Antichrist have come, who, under the appearance of teachers, seduce men from Christ and are adversaries of Christ. Therefore this is the last time, in which there is danger from seducers, against whom you must diligently beware.

units.la: Verf. 19. E nobis egressi sunt, sed non erant ex nobis; nam si fuissent ex nobis, permansissent utique nobiscum; sed hoc factum est, ut paterent non omnes esse ex nobis.
units.tr: Verse 19: They went out from us, but they were not of us; for if they had been of us, they would no doubt have remained with us; but it happened so that it might be made plain that not all are of us.

units.la: Ratio 4. Apostatæ discedentes ab externa communione vere Fidelium, non sunt de numero verè Credentium: Ergo ab Apostasia & Seducctoribus cavendum vobis est.
units.tr: The fourth ground: apostates who depart from the outward communion of true believers are not of the number of those who truly believe. Therefore you must beware of apostasy and of seducers.

units.la: Nam si fuissent ex nobis ] Ratio 5. confirmans priorem, Qui sunt ex numero verè Fidelium seu Electorum, manent in societate veræ Ecclesiæ, & in communione doctrinæ Apostolicæ: Et sic se declarant esse verè Fideles: qui verò deficiunt, Illi (quatenus Dei consilium respicitur) discedunt à doctrina Apostolorum, eo fine ut manifestetur ipsorum hypocrisis, & ut declarentur non esse ex numero verè Fidelium. Ergo si velletis censeri à Deo, vel hominibus verè Fideles, seu non ex numero hypocritarum, ab apostasia & seductoribus, vobis cavendum est.
units.tr: For if they had been of us: The fifth ground, confirming the first: those who are of the number of true believers, or the elect, remain in the fellowship of the true Church and in communion with the apostolic doctrine, and so they show themselves to be truly faithful; but those who fall away, as far as God's counsel is concerned, depart from the doctrine of the Apostles, to the end that their hypocrisy may be made manifest and they may be shown not to be of the number of true believers. Therefore, if you wish to be counted by God or by men as truly faithful, and not of the number of hypocrites, you must beware of apostasy and of seducers.

units.la: Verf. 20. At vos unctionem habetis à Sancto illo profectam, & nostis omnia.
units.tr: Verse 20: But you have an anointing from the Holy One, and you know all things.

units.la: Ratio 6. Donis necessariis & auxilio Spiritus Sancti instructi estis, ut salutaria dogmata omnia cognoscatis, atque ita evitetis seductionem Apostatarum. Cavendum vobis igitur.
units.tr: The sixth ground: you have been furnished with the gifts necessary and with the help of the Holy Spirit, so that you may know all saving doctrines, and thus avoid the seduction of apostates. Therefore you must beware.

units.la: Verf. 21. Non scripsi vobis idcirco quod veritatem ignoretis; sed quia eam nostis, & nullum mendacium ex veritate esse.
units.tr: Verse 21: I have not written to you because you do not know the truth, but because you know it, and that no lie is of the truth.

units.la: Ratio 7. Occurrens objectioni, Hortando, seu scribendo ad vos, non arguo vos ignorantiæ, sed ideo hortor ad constantiam, quod sciam vos veritatem nosse, & ea delectari. Hortationi ergo vobis auscultandum est.
units.tr: The seventh ground, meeting an objection: in exhorting, or writing, to you, I do not charge you with ignorance, but I exhort you to steadfastness for this reason, that I know you know the truth and delight in it. Therefore you ought to heed the exhortation.

units.la: Et nullum mendacium ] Ratio 8. Admoniti de veritate, satis poteritis mendacium discernere, quod scilicet ad veritatis regulam examinatum, cum veritate minimè congruat. Ergo hortationi meæ eo fine ut examinetis & rejiciatis mendacia, auscultandum est.
units.tr: And that no lie: The eighth ground: once you are reminded of the truth, you will be able to distinguish a lie, namely that which, when examined by the rule of truth, does not agree with the truth at all. Therefore you ought to heed my exhortation, to the end that you may examine and reject lies.

units.la: Verf 22. Quis est mendax nisi qui negat Iesum esse Christum? hic est antichristus negans Patrem & Filium.
units.tr: Vers. 22. Who is the liar but he who denies that Jesus is the Christ? This is the antichrist, who denies the Father and the Son.

units.la: Ratio 9. Seductores à vera doctrina Euangelii sunt, suo quisque ordine, hominum mendacissimi (sicut interrogatio insinuat) quippè qui aliquo modo negant Iesum esse Christum; talem enim Christum non agnoscunt, qualem eum Pater in Euangelio nobis offert: nam vel ejus personam vel naturas, vel proprietates naturarum, vel officia, vel virtutem, seu efficaciam, vel gratiam, vel veritatem, vel gloriam, aperte, vel actis cuniculis oppugnant: Ergo cavendum est vobis à seductoribus. Hic est ] Ratio 10. Seductores singuli, qui auditores abducunt à CHRISTO in quovis articulo, sunt Antichristi, negantes & Patrem & Filium; & sic religionem veram, & religionis fundamenta, mendaciis suis evertentes, quippe cum extra CHRISTUM nullus sit verus DEUS: nam in Eo habitat tota plenitudo Deitatis: Cavendum ergo à seductoribus.
units.tr: Argument 9. Seducers from the true doctrine of the gospel are, each in his own way, the most lying of men (as the question suggests), since in some manner they deny that Jesus is the Christ. For they do not acknowledge the Christ whom the Father offers us in the gospel. They attack either his person or his natures, or the properties of his natures, or his offices, or his power and efficacy, or his grace, or his truth, or his glory, whether openly or by secret mines. Therefore you must beware of seducers. This is ] Argument 10. Each seducer who draws hearers away from Christ in any article of faith is an Antichrist, denying both the Father and the Son. By his lies he overthrows the true religion and its foundations, since apart from Christ there is no true God: for in him dwells all the fullness of the Godhead. Beware, therefore, of seducers.

units.la: Vers. 23. Quisquis negat Filium, is ne Patrem quidem habet. Confirmat hanc rationem, ex inseparabilitate PATRIS & FILII, ut non possit quis habere Patrem pro Deo suo, qui negat Filium quovis modo, quia DEUS se totum nobis in CHRISTO fruendum dedit, & frustra alibi quaeritur, aut alio modo, quam quo DEUS se manifestavit nobis in CHRISTO: qui nobis ut Patris imago repraesentat, & exhibet quicquid de Patre ad salutem cognitu est necessarium vel utile: & contrà, Quicunque CHRISTO ut Filio Dei debitum honorem exhibent, agnoscentes eum, qualem se in Scripturis patefecit, etiam Patrem agnoscunt, & pro Deo suo habent.
units.tr: Vers. 23. Whoever denies the Son, the same does not have the Father either. He confirms this argument from the inseparability of the Father and the Son: no one who denies the Son in any way can have the Father as his God. For God has given himself wholly to us to be enjoyed in Christ, and it is vain to seek him elsewhere, or in any way other than that in which God has revealed himself to us in Christ. Christ, as the image of the Father, sets him before us and presents whatever about the Father is necessary or useful to know for salvation. And conversely, those who give Christ the honour due to him as the Son of God, acknowledging him as he has revealed himself in the Scriptures, also acknowledge the Father and hold him as their God.

units.la: Vers. 24. Quod igitur audistis à principio, in vobis maneat. Si in vobis manserit quod audistis à principio, et vos quoque in Filio & patre manebitis.
units.tr: Vers. 24. Let therefore that abide in you which you have heard from the beginning. If what you have heard from the beginning abides in you, you also shall abide in the Son and in the Father.

units.la: Ratio 11. Verè antiqua & una sibi semper constans veritas Dei, est haec, quam ut teneatis vos hortor; quam scilicet audivistis ab initio Evangelii, non tantum praedicati per CHRISTUM, sed etiam promissi, & declarati in Scripturis per Prophetas. Ergo retinenda vobis est ea veritas: & hic scopum seu hortationem profert in apertum.
units.tr: Argument 11. The truth of God is truly ancient and always consistent with itself. This is the truth which I urge you to hold: the truth which you have heard from the beginning of the gospel, not only preached by Christ but also promised and declared in the Scriptures through the prophets. Therefore you must retain this truth. Here he openly states his aim and exhortation.

units.la: Si in vobis manserit ] Ratio 12. Si doctrinam à CHRISTO & Apostolis secundum Scripturas vobis traditam retinueritis, permanebitis in societate & amicitia Dei Filii, & Patris: Ergo cavendum vobis à seductoribus.
units.tr: If what you have heard abides in you ] Argument 12. If you retain the doctrine delivered to you by Christ and the apostles according to the Scriptures, you will remain in fellowship and friendship with the Son of God and the Father. Therefore you must beware of seducers.

units.la: Vers. 25. Haec autem illa est promissio quam ipse pollicitus est nobis, nempe vita illa aeterna.
units.tr: Vers. 25. And this is the promise that he himself has made to us, namely that eternal life.

units.la: Vers. 26. Haec scripsi vobis de iis qui seducunt vos.
units.tr: Vers. 26. I have written these things to you concerning those who seek to deceive you.

units.la: Ratio 13. Hac conditione nobis promisit Deus vitam aeternam, si retinuerimus doctrinam CHRISTI constanter: Ergo constanter permanendum in fide, & obedientia doctrinae CHRISTI, & cavendum à seductoribus, qui operam dant ut vos a veritate seducant: & hic rursum scopum horum Argumentorum aperte profitetur Apostolus.
units.tr: Argument 13. God has promised us eternal life on this condition, that we hold fast the doctrine of Christ constantly. Therefore we must persevere constantly in the faith and in obedience to the doctrine of Christ, and beware of seducers, who labour to lead you away from the truth. Here again the apostle openly declares the aim of these arguments.

units.la: Verf. 27. Sed unctio quam vos accepistis ab eo, manet in vobis, nec necesse habetis ut quisquam doceat vos: verum sicut eadem unctio docet vos de omnibus, quae & verax est, & non mendax: & sicut docuit vos, manebitis in eo.
units.tr: Vers. 27. But the anointing which you have received from him abides in you, and you do not need that anyone should teach you; but as the same anointing teaches you about all things, and is true and not a lie, and as it has taught you, you shall abide in him.

units.la: Ratio 14. Ut custodiamini à seductoribus multiplici praesidio muniti estis: Primò enim ad externam doctrinam, etiam unctionem, seu Spiritum Sanctum, qui vos intus doceat & confirmet in doctrinae Christi veritate, accepistis à Christo, in sua quisque mensura. Secundò, Spiritus ille manet in vobis qui fideles estis, & non aufertur à credentibus. Tertio, Non habetis opus aliquo, qui doceat vos aliud quicquam praeter id quod Christi Spiritus in Scriptura docuit, & in cordibus vestris confirmavit, tantum opus habetis hortatione, ut maneatis in Christo, sicut Spiritus seu Unctio in Scripturis loquens, & id quod in Scripturis est, in cordibus vestris confirmans, & porro instituens ex Scripturis in omnibus ad salutem necessariis vos docet: qui Spiritus Veritas est, id est, ipsissima Scripturae; quae veritas est, confirmatio, & non mendacium, sed mendaciorum refutator & olor: Ergo constanter vobis manendum est in Christo: sicut Spiritus secundum veritatem Scripturae vos docuit, & cavendum vobis à seductoribus.
units.tr: Argument 14. To guard you against seducers, you have been armed with a manifold protection. First, you have received from Christ, in each one's measure, the outward doctrine together with the anointing, that is, the Holy Spirit, who teaches and confirms you inwardly in the truth of Christ's doctrine. Second, that Spirit abides in you who are faithful, and is not taken away from believers. Third, you have no need of anyone to teach you anything beyond what the Spirit of Christ has taught in the Scriptures and confirmed in your hearts; you need only exhortation to abide in Christ. The anointing, speaking in the Scriptures and confirming in your hearts what is in the Scriptures, further instructs you from the Scriptures in all things necessary to salvation. This Spirit is truth, that is, the very truth of Scripture; which is truth, a confirmation, and not a lie, but the refuter and the overthrower of lies. Therefore you must constantly abide in Christ, as the Spirit has taught you according to the truth of Scripture, and beware of seducers.

units.la: Verl. 28 Nunc igitur, Filioli, manete in eo: ut quum patefactus fuerit, habeamus fiduciam, neque pudefiamus coram eo in ipsius adventu.
units.tr: Vers. 28. Now therefore, little children, abide in him, so that when he appears we may have confidence and not be ashamed before him at his coming.

units.la: Ratio 15. Quicunque non perseverant in fide Christi, nec in ejus communione manent, quicunque demum fuerint in hominum aestimatione, pudefacti discedent à Christo in ejus judicio: Contra vero, Perseverantes in fide, confidenter consistent coram eo. Ergo constanter vobis est permanendum in Christi fide, & cavendum a seductoribus.
units.tr: Argument 15. Whoever does not persevere in the faith of Christ, nor remain in communion with him, however highly esteemed they may be in the opinion of men, will depart from Christ in his judgment, put to shame. On the contrary, those who persevere in the faith will stand before him with confidence. Therefore you must constantly remain in the faith of Christ and beware of seducers.

units.la: Verf. 29. Si scitis eum justum esse, nostis, quicunque exercet justitiam, ex ipso natum esse.
units.tr: Vers. 29. If you know that he is righteous, you know that everyone who practises righteousness is born of him.

units.la: Hortatio 5. quam prosequetur in priori parte sequentis Capitis, nempe ut operam dent Justitiae, seu ut studeant Sanctitati. Argumenta hortationis sunt quindecim. Arg. 1. A testimonio conscientiae ipsorum confirmatum, Qui operam dat justitiae, natus ex Deo est, qui ipse justus est, & testimonium habet suae adoptionis & regenerationis. Ergo operam date Justitiae
units.tr: Exhortation 5, which he pursues in the first part of the following chapter: that they should labour after righteousness, that is, strive for holiness. There are fifteen arguments for this exhortation. Argument 1: confirmed by the testimony of their own conscience. Whoever labours for righteousness is born of God, who himself is righteous, and he has the testimony of his own adoption and regeneration. Therefore labour after righteousness.

units.la: Caput Tertium.
units.tr: Chapter 3.

units.la: Artes Capitis sunt duae, In prima prosequitur hor-tationis Argumenta reliqua, ad verf 11. In secunda subnectit aliam hortationem ad dilectionem Fratrum, ad finem.
units.tr: The chapter has two parts. In the first he pursues the remaining arguments of exhortation, up to verse 11. In the second he adds another exhortation, to love of the brethren, to the end.

units.la: Verf. 1. Videte qualem charitatem dedit nobis Pater, nempe, ut Filii Dei vocemur: propterea mundus non novit nos, quoniam non novit eum.
units.tr: Verse 1. See what manner of love the Father has bestowed on us, that we should be called the sons of God. For this reason the world does not know us, because it did not know him.

units.la: Arg. 2. Hortationis ad studium Justitiæ, Ex mera seu gratuita dilectione Deus vos fideles honore adoptionis in filios ornavit. Tenemini ergo Patrem veltrum Justitiæ studio referre.
units.tr: Argument 2. From an exhortation to the study of righteousness: out of pure, or gratuitous, love God has adorned you believers with the honour of adoption as sons. You are bound therefore to repay your Father with zeal for righteousness.

units.la: ] Arg. 3. per occupationem objectionis, Impedire non debet studium Justitiæ in vobis, quod mundus non agnoscat vos pro Filius Dei, quandoquidem hic contemptus communis est vobis cum Deo Patre vestro, quem etiam contemnit mundus; sed potiùs ad unionem & conformitatem cum Deo in justitiæ studio colendam, vos incitare debet: Ergo.
units.tr: Argument 3, by answering an objection: the study of righteousness ought not to be hindered in you by the fact that the world does not acknowledge you as sons of God, since this contempt is common to you and to God your Father, whom the world also despises. Rather it ought to spur you on to cultivate, in the study of righteousness, union and conformity with God. Therefore...

units.la: Vers. 2. Charissimi, nunc filii Dei sumus, sed nondum patefactum est quid erimus. Scimus autem fore ut quum ipse patefactus fuerit, similes ei simus: quoniam videbimus eum sicuti est:
units.tr: Verse 2. Beloved, now we are the sons of God, but it has not yet been revealed what we shall be. We know that when he shall be revealed we shall be like him, for we shall see him as he is.

units.la: Arg. 4 Per occupationem alius similis objectionis, Non debet impedire studium justitiæ in vobis, quod nondum appareat gloria vestra, satis est, quod sciamus jus Filiorum Dei jam nobis datum esse, nosque adityros possessionem, quando CHRISTUS manifestabitur, similesque ei in gloria & felicitate futuros, & beatifica visione ipsius in æternum fruituros: Debetis ergo justitiæ operam dare.
units.tr: Argument 4, by answering another similar objection: the study of righteousness ought not to be hindered in you by the fact that your glory does not yet appear. It is enough that we know the right of the sons of God has already been given to us, and that we are heirs entering into possession, and that when Christ is made manifest we shall be like him in glory and happiness, and shall enjoy his blessed vision for ever. You must therefore labour at righteousness.

units.la: Vers. 3. Et quisquis habet hanc spem in eo sitam, purificat se, sicut & ille purus est.
units.tr: Verse 3. And everyone who has this hope set in him purifies himself, as he also is pure.

units.la: Arg. 5. Quicunque habet spem vivam conformitatis cum CHRISTO in gloria, purificat seipsum, ut CHRISTO in hac vita, in puritatis & justitiæ studio conformis sit. Ergo justitiæ studendum.
units.tr: Argument 5. Whoever has the living hope of conformity with Christ in glory purifies himself, so that in this life he may be conformed to Christ in the study of purity and righteousness. Therefore righteousness is to be pursued.

units.la: Vers. 4. Quisquis committit peccatum, etiam Legem transgreditur: nam peccatum est Legis transgressio.
units.tr: Verse 4. Whoever commits sin also transgresses the law, for sin is the transgression of the law.

units.la: DDDDD
units.tr: DDDDD

units.la: Arg. 6. Quicunque non studet justitiæ, sed operam dat peccato, etiam Legis transgressioni operam dat, quia peccatum nihil aliud est quam Legis transgressio, cui si quis operam dat, Deo bellum indicit: Ergo studendum justitiæ.
units.tr: Argument 6. Whoever does not study righteousness but labours at sin also labours at the transgression of the law, because sin is nothing other than the transgression of the law; and whoever labours at this declares war on God. Therefore righteousness is to be pursued.

units.la: Verf. 5 Et scitis illum patefactum esse, ut peccata nostra tolleret, & peccatum in eo non esse.
units.tr: Verse 5. And you know that he was made manifest to take away our sins, and that in him there is no sin.

units.la: Arg. 7. Eo fine manifestatus est Christus, ut reatum peccati lueret, & tolleret à suis (quod confirmat ex eo, quod Christus nullum in se habuerit peccatum pro quo lueret) unde fit, ut qui peccato operam dat, eo ipso contrarium Christo faciat, pretiumque redemptionis vilipendat: Ergo nisi Christo contrarii videri vultis, studendum est Justitiæ.
units.tr: Argument 7. Christ was made manifest for this end: to atone for the guilt of sin and take it away from his own. (He confirms this from the fact that Christ had no sin of his own for which he would have to atone.) Hence it follows that whoever labours at sin by that very act works against Christ and makes light of the price of redemption. Therefore, unless you wish to appear opposed to Christ, you must pursue righteousness.

units.la: Verf. 6 Quisquis in eo manet, non peccat; quisquis peccat, non vidit eum, neque novit eum.
units.tr: Verse 6. Whoever abides in him does not sin; whoever sins has not seen him, nor known him.

units.la: Arg. 8. Proprietas est omnis fidelis, seu manentis in Christo, non dare operam peccato, sed Justitiæ. Ergo Justitiæ studendum est.
units.tr: Argument 8. It is the property of every faithful man, that is, of everyone who abides in Christ, not to labour at sin but at righteousness. Therefore righteousness is to be pursued.

units.la: Quisquis Arg. 9. Quicunque peccato studet aut indulget, fallo prætendit Christi hdem, seu notitiam, quæ sine studio novitatis vitæ esse non potest. Studendum ergo Justitiæ.
units.tr: Whoever Argument 9. Whoever is devoted to sin or indulges it falsely pretends to faith in Christ, or knowledge of him, which cannot exist without the study of newness of life. Therefore righteousness is to be pursued.

units.la: Verf. 7. Filioli, nemo vos seducat: qui exercet justitiam, justus est, sicut ille justus est.
units.tr: Verse 7. Little children, let no one deceive you: he who does righteousness is righteous, as he is righteous.

units.la: Arg. 10. Quicunque non ita studet justitiæ, ut operibus & actionibus suis testetur novitatis vitæ studium, seipsum decipit, vel decipi se patitur. Frustra enim persuadent sibi homines se habere sepultam in cordibus justitiam, dum pedes, manus, linguam, & oculos palam occupat iniquitas. Studendum igitur est Justitiæ.
units.tr: Argument 10. Whoever does not pursue righteousness in such a way that his works and actions bear witness to a zeal for newness of life deceives himself, or allows himself to be deceived. For men vainly persuade themselves that they have righteousness buried in their hearts, while iniquity openly occupies their feet, hands, tongue and eyes. Therefore righteousness is to be pursued.

units.la: Qui exercet Hoc Argumentum confirmat, describendo Justum seu Justificatum ex fide, à proprietate ipsius inseparabili, nempe praxi Justitiæ, & conformitate cum Deo cui studet justificatus, ut justitiam suam opere manifestet; Nemo justificatus est, qui non ita et justo Deo conformis esse, seu qui opere justitiam non exercet: Decipit ergo se quisquis aliter existimat.
units.tr: He who does This argument confirms the point by describing the righteous, or justified by faith, from his inseparable property, namely the practice of righteousness and conformity with God, to which the justified man is devoted, so that he shows his righteousness by his work. No one is justified who is not in this way conformed to the just God, or who does not practise righteousness in his work. Therefore whoever thinks otherwise deceives himself.

units.la: Verf. 8. Qui committit peccatum, ex Diabolo est: quoniam à principio Diabolus peccat. Ad hoc patefactus est Filius Dei, ut dissolvat opera Diaboli.
units.tr: Verse 8. He who commits sin is of the devil, for the devil has sinned from the beginning. To this end the Son of God was made manifest, that he might destroy the works of the devil.

units.la: Arg. II.
units.tr: Argument 11.

units.la: Arg. 11. Quicunque operam dat peccato, diaboli filius est, patrem suum itudiis suis referens: Hoc confirmat à Diaboli in peccando vetustate, qui itatim post creationem peccavit, & ab eo tempore peccandi autor fuit hominibus: Ergo nisi Diaboli filii haberi vultis, Justitiæ itudendum est. Arg. 12. Eo fine Christus manifestatus est, ut opera Diaboli solveret, id est, dominium peccati destrueret in suis, & peccati inhabitationem aboleret gradatim, per sanctificationem. Hinc fit ut qui operam peccato dat, ædificet id ad quod destruendum Christus manifestatus est. Studendum igitur.
units.tr: Argument 11. Whoever labours at sin is a son of the devil, reflecting his father in his pursuits. This is confirmed from the devil's ancient habit of sinning: he sinned immediately after creation and from that time has been the author of sin to men. Therefore, unless you wish to be counted sons of the devil, you must pursue righteousness. Argument 12. For this end Christ was made manifest, that he might dissolve the works of the devil, that is, destroy the dominion of sin in his people and gradually abolish the indwelling of sin through sanctification. Hence whoever labours at sin builds up what Christ was made manifest to destroy. Therefore one must pursue righteousness.

units.la: Verf. 9. Quisquis natus est ex Deo, peccatum non committit, quoniam semen ipsius in eo manet: nec potest peccare, eo quod ex Deo natus est.
units.tr: Verse 9. Whoever is born of God does not commit sin, because his seed remains in him; nor can he sin, because he is born of God.

units.la: Arg. 13 Licet regenitus præoccupari possit à peccato, operam tamen dare peccato non potest, propter regenerationis naturam, seu propter Dei semen manens in ipso (id est, quia Dei Verbum & Spiritus, vel talis Dei gratia in regeneratione communicata est in illorum donorum numero, quorum Deum non pœnitet) cujus vi regenitus perpetuo retrahitur à peccatis, & impellitur ad justitiam sectandam; nec potest peccare, seu peccato indulgere. Ergo nisi vos irregenitos probare velletis, studendum vobis est Justitiæ.
units.tr: Argument 13. Although the regenerate may be overtaken by sin, yet he cannot labour at sin, on account of the nature of regeneration, or because God's seed abides in him (that is, because the Word and Spirit of God, or such grace of God, is communicated in regeneration, among those gifts which God does not repent of). By its power the regenerate is constantly drawn back from sins and impelled to pursue righteousness, and he cannot sin, or indulge sin. Therefore, unless you wish to prove yourselves unregenerate, you must pursue righteousness.

units.la: Arg. 14. Regenitus non potest operam dare peccato, quia genitus est ex Deo, qui natum ex se non deserit, sed ita gubernat & movet sui nati cor, ut constanter militet adversus peccatum, & ductum Spiritus sequatur: Ergo si à Deo natos vos probare vultis, Justitiæ itudendum est.
units.tr: Argument 14. The regenerate cannot labour at sin, because he is begotten of God, who does not forsake what he has begotten, but so governs and moves the heart of his child that he constantly fights against sin and follows the leading of the Spirit. Therefore, if you wish to prove that you are born of God, you must pursue righteousness.

units.la: Verl. 10. Ter hoc manifesti sunt filii Dei & filii Diaboli, quisquis non exercet justitiam, non est ex Deo, & qui non diligit fratrem suum.
units.tr: Verse 10. In this the children of God and the children of the devil are made manifest: whoever does not practise righteousness is not of God, nor is he who does not love his brother.

units.la: Arg. 15. In hoc differunt regeniti & irregeniti; Filii Dei & filii Diaboli, quod ii qui sunt ex Deo, studeant justitiæ: illi vero, qui non student justitiæ exercendæ, & nominatim fratrum dilectioni, non sunt ex Deo, sed ex diabolo. Justitiæ ergo, & imprimis fraternæ dilectioni studendum vobis est.
units.tr: Argument 15. In this the regenerate and the unregenerate, the children of God and the children of the devil, differ: those who are of God pursue righteousness, whereas those who do not pursue the practice of righteousness, and in particular love of the brethren, are not of God but of the devil. Therefore you must pursue righteousness, and above all brotherly love.

units.la: Secunda pars
units.tr: The second part

units.la: Verf. 11. Quoniam hoc est nuntium quod audistis à principio, ut diligamus alii alios. Hinc ad alteram hortationem dilabitur, scilicet ad diligendos fratres: hortationis argumenta sunt quindecim. Argumentum primum, Praeceptum de dilectione fratrum ab initio vocationis vestrae datum est vobis à Christo. Ergo fratres diligite.
units.tr: Verse 11. "For this is the message that you heard from the beginning, that we should love one another." Hence he passes to the second exhortation, namely to love the brethren. The arguments of the exhortation are fifteen. The first argument: the command to love the brethren was given to you by Christ from the beginning of your calling. Therefore love the brethren.

units.la: Vers. 12 Non sicut Cain, qui ex illo Malo erat, & occidit fratrem suum. Cujus autem rei gratia occidit eum? quia opera ejus mala erant, fratris autem ejus justa.
units.tr: Verse 12. "Not as Cain, who was of that Evil one, and slew his brother. And why did he slay him? Because his works were evil, but his brother's just."

units.la: Arg 2. Dissimiles debent esse fideles Caino, diaboli filio & fratricidae. Ergo Cujus ] Arg. 3. confirmans & illustrans superius, Qui fratres non diligunt, sed odio habent, odisse Dei gratiam in fratribus comperientur, & in hoc similes esse Caino, qui imaginem Dei in fratre suo odio persequebatur ex invidia. Dilectioni fratrum ergo studendum est.
units.tr: Argument 2. The faithful ought to be unlike Cain, the son of the devil and a fratricide. Therefore... "Whose" [is the] third argument, confirming and illustrating what was said above: those who do not love the brethren but hold them in hatred are found to hate the grace of God in the brethren, and in this they are like Cain, who in envy persecuted with hatred the image of God in his brother. Therefore love of the brethren is to be pursued.

units.la: Vers. 13. Ne miremini, fratres mei, si odit vos mundus.
units.tr: Verse 13. "Do not be surprised, my brethren, if the world hates you."

units.la: Arg. 4. Per occupationem, & retorsionem objectionis. Tantum abest ut frigescere debeat charitas inter fideles, propterea quod exosos se videant à mundo, ut contrà tanto impensius debeant se mutuò diligere. Ergo.
