units.tr: Argument 4. By occupation and retorsion of the objection. Charity among the faithful ought not to grow cold because they see themselves hated by the world; rather, on the contrary, they ought all the more earnestly to love one another. Therefore.

units.la: Vers. 14. Nos scimus nos translatos esse ex morte ad vitam, quia diligimus fratres: qui non diligit fratrem, manet in morte.
units.tr: Verse 14. "We know that we have passed from death to life, because we love the brethren; he who does not love his brother remains in death."

units.la: Arg. 5. Ex dilectione fratrum, seu dilectione imaginis Dei in illis certiores reddimur tanquam ex indicio certo, quod nos ipsi regeniti sumus, & translati à morte in vitam.
units.tr: Argument 5. From love of the brethren, or love of the image of God in them, we are made certain, as by a sure sign, that we ourselves are regenerate and have passed from death into life.

units.la: Qui non ] Arg. 6. Qui non diligit fratrem, manet in statu peccati & mortis irregenitus, Ergo ut regenitos vos probetis, diligite fratres.
units.tr: "He who does not" [is] argument 6. He who does not love his brother remains unregenerate, in the state of sin and death. Therefore, that you may prove yourselves regenerate, love the brethren.

units.la: Vers. 15. Quisquis odit fratrem suum, homicida est: & nostis nullum homicidam habere vitam aeternam in se manentem.
units.tr: Verse 15. "Whoever hates his brother is a murderer, and you know that no murderer has eternal life abiding in him."

units.la: Arg. 7. confirmans superius, Qui non diligit fratrem odio habet eum, & ideo homicida est, & per consequens, nec habet initia vitae aeternae in se, nec jus ad vitam aeternam, sed manet obnoxius morti aeternae. Ergo nisi tales haberi velletis, dilectioni fratrum incumbendum est.
units.tr: Argument 7, confirming what was said above: he who does not love his brother hates him, and therefore is a murderer, and consequently has neither the beginnings of eternal life in himself nor a right to eternal life, but remains liable to eternal death. Therefore, unless you wish to be held such, you must devote yourselves to love of the brethren.

units.la: Vers. 16. Ter hoc cognovimus charitatem, quod ille animam suam pro nobis posuit: nos igitur debemus pro Fratribus animas ponere. Arg. 8. CHRISTUS nos impensè dilexit, cum vitam suam pro nobis posuit, nos igitur debemus alii alios diligere, exemplum ejus imitantes.
units.tr: Verse 16. "By this we have known love, that he laid down his life for us; we therefore ought to lay down our lives for the brethren." Argument 8. Christ loved us exceedingly when he laid down his life for us; we therefore ought to love one another, imitating his example.

units.la: Nos igitur ] Arg. 9. Gratitudinem hanc debemus CHRISTO, qui pro nobis & fratribus posuit vitam, ut parati simus vitam nostram profundere in bonum Ecclesiæ, seu fratrum nostrorum: Ergo multo magis affectu sincerò debemus ipsos prosequi, & inferiora officia dilectionis erga eos præstare.
units.tr: "We therefore" [is] argument 9. We owe this gratitude to Christ, who laid down his life for us and for the brethren, so that we are ready to pour out our life for the good of the Church, or of our brethren. Therefore, much more, we ought to pursue them with sincere affection and render to them the lesser duties of love.

units.la: Vers. 17. Qui verò habuerit mundanas facultates, & viderit fratrem suum egentem, & clauserit viscera sua coram eo, quomodo charitas Dei manet in eo?
units.tr: Verse 17. "But whoever has worldly goods, and sees his brother in need, and shuts up his bowels of compassion against him, how does the love of God abide in him?"

units.la: Arg. 10. confirmans superius, Qui non sic diligunt fratres, ut egentibus, communicent de facultatibus suis, idque ex misericordiæ visceribus permoti, hypocritæ sunt, & longè absunt ab illa dilectione quæ vitam impendere pro fratribus parata est. Verf. 18. Filioli mei, ne diligamus verbo, neque lingua solùm, sed opere & veritate.
units.tr: Argument 10, confirming what was said above: those who do not love the brethren so as to share their goods with the needy, moved by the bowels of mercy, are hypocrites and are far from that love which is ready to lay down its life for the brethren. Verse 18. "My little children, let us not love in word, nor in tongue only, but in deed and truth."

units.la: Hinc infertur ipsa hortatio: ut opere & veritate, mutuam dilectionem testentur, & non verbis, seu linguâ tantùm.
units.tr: Hence the exhortation itself follows: that they should attest mutual love by deed and truth, and not merely by words or tongue.

units.la: Verf. 19. Et per hoc cognoscimus nos ex veritate esse, & coram ipso secura reddemus corda nostra.
units.tr: Verse 19. "And by this we know that we are of the truth, and shall reassure our hearts before him."

units.la: Arg. 11. Per dilectionem fratrum, tanquam per fructum fidei sincerae cognoscimus nos sinceros esse, seu verè fideles, & ex Deo genitos: Ergo dilectioni fratrum studendum est. Coram ipso] Arg. 12. Per dilectionem confirmabimus fiduciam nostram apud Deum, & conscientiam in lucta fidei juvabimus ex hoc effectu fidei, ad dandum nobis testimonium absolutionis, seu justificationis per fidem. Ergo.
units.tr: Argument 11. Through love of the brethren, as through the fruit of sincere faith, we know that we are sincere, that is, truly faithful and born of God. Therefore love of the brethren is to be pursued. "Before him": argument 12. Through love we shall confirm our confidence before God, and from this effect of faith we shall help our conscience in the struggle of faith, so that it may give us the testimony of absolution, or justification, through faith. Therefore.

units.la: Verf. 20. Nam si nos condemnet cor nostrum, potentior est Deus corde nostro, & novit omnia.
units.tr: Verse 20. "For if our heart condemns us, God is greater than our heart, and knows all things."

units.la: Verf. 21. Charissimi, si cor nostrum nos non condemnet, fiduciam habemus apud Deum:
units.tr: Verse 21. "Beloved, if our heart does not condemn us, we have confidence before God."

units.la: Hoc Argumentum confirmat per collationem vigilantis, & malae conscientiae, hoc versu, in effectis condemnationis; cum conscientia bona, versu sequenti, in effectu absolutionis: Sicut quando mala conscientia condemnat eum qui plane vacuus est fraternae dilectionis, sententia condemnationis à Deo supremo Judice omnisicio rata manet, donec ad CHRISTUM confugiant. Sic ex altera parte, quando bona conscientia (quæ ut ut imperfectionis nos arguat) nos non condemnat, quasi plane destitutos hoc fructu, vel studio proficiendi in dilectione fraterna; fiduciam retinemus adeundi Deum, ut Patrem nostrum in Christo. Idcirco ex studio fraternæ dilectionis secura reddemus corda nostra coram Deo, ut verf. 19. habetur.
units.tr: By this argument he confirms, through a comparison of a watchful and an evil conscience, in the effects of condemnation in this verse, and a good conscience in the following verse, in the effect of absolution. Just as when an evil conscience condemns one who is wholly empty of brotherly love, the sentence of condemnation, pronounced by God the supreme and all-knowing Judge, remains valid until such a person flees to Christ. So on the other side, when a good conscience (which, although it reproves us for imperfection) does not condemn us, as if we were wholly lacking this fruit or the zeal of advancing in brotherly love, we retain confidence of approaching God as our Father in Christ. Therefore, from zeal for brotherly love we shall make our hearts secure before God, as is stated in verse 19.

units.la: Verf. 22. Et quicquid petierimus, accipimus ab eo, quoniam præcepta ejus custodimus, & ea quæ ipsi placent facimus.
units.tr: Verse 22. "And whatever we ask, we receive from him, because we keep his commandments and do the things that please him."

units.la: Arg. 13. Facit conscientia dilectionis fraternæ ad fiduciam impetrandi ea, quæ secundum Dei voluntatem petimus ab eo bona: quia ratiocinari possumus ex studio custodiendi mandata Dei & faciendi ea, quæ ei placent, nos esse ex numero verè Fidelium, qui per fidem in Christum, sunt in gratia apud Deum, & quorum preces Deus non rejicit, sicut hypocritarum & impiorum preces aversatur. Ergo dilectioni fraternæ studendum est.
units.tr: Argument 13. The consciousness of brotherly love contributes to confidence in obtaining those good things which we ask of God according to his will: for we may reason, from the zeal of keeping God's commandments and doing what pleases him, that we are of the number of the truly faithful, who through faith in Christ are in grace before God, and whose prayers God does not reject, as he turns away the prayers of hypocrites and the impious. Therefore brotherly love is to be pursued.

units.la: Verf. 23. Hæc est igitur ejus doctrina, ut credamus nomini Filii ejus Iesu Christi, & diligamus alii alios, sicut mandavit nobis
units.tr: Verse 23. "This then is his teaching: that we should believe in the name of his Son Jesus Christ, and love one another, as he commanded us."

units.la: Arg. 14. confirmans superius, & objectioni occurrens, nequis supradictis abateretur ad merita operum, aut justificationem ex operibus tuendum. Præceptum de dilectione fraternâ includitur per consequens in præcepto de fide salvifica, in Christum collocandâ. Nam cum Deus præcipit fidem in Christum, quæ operetur per charitatem, simul præcipit ut alii alios diligamus, Ergo si quis præcepti de fide in Filium Dei rationem habet, rationem etiam mandati de dilectione mutua habeat necesse est, ut ei obedire studeat. Studendum ergo dilectioni fraternæ.
units.tr: Argument 14, confirming what was said above and meeting an objection, lest anyone be diverted from the foregoing to the merits of works, or to defending justification by works. The command of brotherly love is consequently included in the command concerning saving faith, placed in Christ. For when God commands faith in Christ, which works through love, he at the same time commands that we love one another. Therefore, if anyone takes account of the command concerning faith in the Son of God, he must necessarily also take account of the command of mutual love, so as to strive to obey it. Therefore brotherly love is to be pursued.

units.la: Verf. 24. Nam qui servat ejus mandata, in eo habitat, & ipse in eo, & per hoc novimus eum habitare in nobis, nempe ex Spiritu quem nobis dedit.
units.tr: Verse 24. "For he who keeps his commandments abides in him, and he in him; and by this we know that he abides in us, namely by the Spirit whom he has given us."

units.la: Arg. 15. In quo elt studium obediendi præceptis Dei, & nominatim præcepto de fide in Christum quæ per dilectionem fratrum efficaciter operatur, is communionem habet cum Deo, & communionem se habere novit per Spiritus Sancti gratuitam præsentiam: quam Spiritus præsentiam dignoscere poterit ex ipsius effectu, nempe ex studio obediendi Dei mandato, de viva fide in Christum per charitatem operante: Ergo dilectioni fratrum studendum est.
units.tr: Argument 15. He in whom there is zeal to obey the precepts of God, and especially the precept concerning faith in Christ which works effectually through love of the brethren, has communion with God, and knows that he has this communion through the gratuitous presence of the Holy Spirit. This presence of the Spirit he will be able to recognise from its effect, namely from zeal to obey God's command concerning living faith in Christ working through love. Therefore love of the brethren is to be pursued.

units.la: Caput
units.tr: Chapter

units.la: Caput Quartum.
units.tr: Chapter 4.

units.la: HOC capite Apostolus totus est in stabilienda ipsorum fide, & in dilectione erga fratres excitandâ. Capitis duæ sunt partes: In prima hortatur ad discernendos Spiritus, ut cavent sibi ab impostoribus ad versf. 7. In altera urget denuò fraternam dilectionem, ad finem.
units.tr: In this chapter the Apostle is wholly concerned with establishing their faith and stirring up love towards the brothers. The chapter has two parts: in the first he urges them to test the spirits, so that they may guard themselves against impostors, up to verse 7; in the second he again presses brotherly love, to the end.

units.la: Verf. 1. DIlecti, ne cuivis Spiritui credite, sed probate Spiritus an ex Deo sint, nam multi Pseudoprophetæ venerunt in mundum.
units.tr: Verse 1. Beloved, do not believe every spirit, but test the spirits whether they are from God, for many false prophets have gone out into the world.

units.la: Ex occasione mentionis factæ, de Dei Spiritu versu ultimo capitis superioris, hortatur ut nulli spiritui, seu doctrinæ à quovis spiritu profisiscenti prius habeant fidem, quam examinaverint & probaverint an à Deo sit. Argumenta hortationis sunt sex: Argumentum primum, Multi Pseudoprophetæ seu hæretici exorti sunt, & in mundum aperte jam prodierunt. Ergo non nisi habito examine, ulli doctrinæ, fidem habere debetis.
units.tr: Taking occasion from the mention made, in the last verse of the previous chapter, of the Spirit of God, he urges that they should not give credence to any spirit, or to any teaching proceeding from any spirit, before they have examined and tested whether it is from God. There are six arguments of the exhortation. The first argument: many false prophets, that is heretics, have arisen and have already openly come forth into the world. Therefore you ought to give credence to no teaching without first examining it.

units.la: Verf. 2. Ex hoc cognoscite Dei Spiritum: Quicunque spiritus confitetur Iesum Christum in carnem venisse, ex Deo est:
units.tr: Verse 2. By this know the Spirit of God: every spirit that confesses that Jesus Christ has come in the flesh is from God.

units.la: Arg. 2. Paratam habetis regulam, ad quam tanquam ad lapidem lydium examinare potestis omnem spiritum, seu spiritus cujusvis doctrinam, an ex Deo sit. Regulæ prima pars hæc est, Quicunque Spiritus CHRISTI personam secundùm Deitatem in qua existebat ab æterno, & secundùm humanitatem, quam verè assumpsit in incarnatione serió & reipsâ confitetur, & serió etiam agnoscit Eum esse CHRISTUM illum, secundùm omnia ejus officia, Eique soli plenam gloriam perfecti Salvatoris tribuit, Is spiritus, seu hæc doctrina, à Deo est.
units.tr: Argument 2. You have a ready rule by which, as by a touchstone, you can examine every spirit, or the teaching of any spirit, whether it is from God. The first part of the rule is this: every spirit which sincerely and in truth confesses the person of Christ, according to the Deity in which he existed from eternity, and according to the humanity which he truly assumed in the incarnation, and which also sincerely acknowledges that he is that Christ according to all his offices, and ascribes to him alone the full glory of the perfect Saviour, that spirit, or that teaching, is from God.

units.la: Verf. 3 At quicunque spiritus non confitetur Iesum Christum, in carnem venisse, ex Deo non est: sed hic est ille spiritus Antichristi, de quo audistis eum venturum fuisse, & jam nunc in mundo esse.
units.tr: Verse 3. But every spirit that does not confess that Jesus Christ has come in the flesh is not from God; but this is the spirit of Antichrist, of whom you have heard that he would come, and who is now already in the world.

units.la: Altera regulæ pars negativa hæc est, Quicunque Spiritus, seu quæcunque doctrina non confitetur reipsa & solidè CHRISTUM IESUM, ad eum modum scilicet qui jam dictus est, sed detrahit quicquam ejus personæ, vel officiis, vel virtuti & efficaciæ ad salutem inchoandam&, plenissimè consummandam; is non est à Deo, sed Spiritus est Antichristi, qui Spiritus jam nunc est in mundo, licet nondum invaluerit ita, ut Thronum sibi apertè in Ecclesia erexerit: Ergo cum hanc habeatis regulam, non debetis ullam doctrinam admittere, nisi præmisso examine.
units.tr: The other, negative part of the rule is this: every spirit, or every teaching, which does not confess in deed and solidly Christ Jesus, in the manner just stated, but takes away anything from his person, or his offices, or his power and efficacy for beginning and most fully completing salvation, that is not from God, but is the spirit of Antichrist, which spirit is already now in the world, although it has not yet so prevailed as to have openly erected its throne in the Church. Therefore, since you have this rule, you ought to admit no teaching without a prior examination.

units.la: Verf. 4, Vos ex Deo estis, filioli, & vicistis eos, quoniam potentior est qui est in vobis, quàm qui in mundo est.
units.tr: Verse 4. You are of God, little children, and have overcome them, because greater is he who is in you than he who is in the world.

units.la: Arg. 3. Parata est vobis victoria de seductoribus non minus certò, quam si res transacta fuisset. Ne igitur metuatis habito examine, cum iis contendere. Ex Deo] Hoc argumentum confirmat tribus rationibus ex Deo: Ratio prima, Electi & regeniti estis à Deo: Ergo certò vincetis seductores. In vobis] Ratio 2. Habetis Spiritum Dei habitantem in vobis, per quem discernatis impostoras, & caveatis: Ergo certò vincetis seductores. Major] Ratio 3. Spiritus Dei habitans in vobis potentior est diabolo, seductore illo Spiritu qui in mundo est, seu in improbis impostoribus: Ergo certò vincetis seductores.
units.tr: Argument 3. Victory over the seducers is ready for you no less certainly than if the matter had already been accomplished. Therefore do not fear, after examination, to contend with them. Of God: this argument is confirmed by three reasons. The first reason: you are elect and regenerate by God; therefore you will certainly overcome the seducers. In you: the second reason: you have the Spirit of God dwelling in you, through whom you may discern and guard against impostors; therefore you will certainly overcome the seducers. Greater: the third reason: the Spirit of God dwelling in you is more powerful than the devil, that seducing spirit who is in the world, or in wicked impostors; therefore you will certainly overcome the seducers.

units.la: Verf 5. Ipsi è mundo sunt, ideo mundana loquuntur, & mundus eos audit.
units.tr: Verse 5. They are of the world, therefore they speak worldly things, and the world hears them.

units.la: Arg. 4 per occupationem objectionis, Non debetis perturbari, quod mendacius seductorum mundus mendax auscultet; siquidem illi seductores de mundo sunt, & mendacia quæ mundo placeant, docent: sed contra tanto studiosius cavere, & aversari debetis seductores, quanto mundus illis est addictus magis: Ergo probandi vobis sunt Spiritus an à Deo sint, nec ulla doctrina nisi habito examine, admittenda est à vobis.
units.tr: Argument 4, by way of anticipating an objection. You ought not to be troubled that the world, which is false, listens to the lies of the seducers; for those seducers are of the world, and they teach lies which please the world. But you ought all the more carefully to beware of and turn away from the seducers, in proportion as the world is more devoted to them. Therefore the spirits are to be tested by you, whether they are from God, and no teaching is to be admitted by you without a prior examination.

units.la: Verf. 6. Nos ex Deo sumus: qui novit Deum, audit nos: qui non est ex Deo, non audit nos: ex hoc cognoscimus Spiritum veritatis, & Spiritum erroris.
units.tr: Verse 6. We are of God: he who knows God hears us; he who is not of God does not hear us. By this we know the spirit of truth and the spirit of error.

units.la: Arg. 5. per occupationem etiam objectionis, Cum nos Apostoli & sinceri Doctores à Deo habeamus doctrinam nostram, efficacemque vocationem, & ad fidem Christi, & ad fidei prædicationem, satis est quod Electi Dei, & instituti à Deo audiant nostram doctrinam, ut ut forsan exiguus fuerit ipsorum numerus Ergo audite nos, & Spiritus erroris, facto examine rejicite. Is qui non est] Arg 6. Proprietas est non renovati hominis, & cui cum Deo nondum ulla est communio, Non adhærere doctrinæ nostræ Apostolicæ, sed seductoribus fidem habere.
units.tr: Argument 5, also by way of anticipating an objection. Since we apostles and sincere teachers have our doctrine and our effectual calling from God, both for faith in Christ and for the preaching of the faith, it is enough that the elect of God, and those appointed by God, hear our teaching, however small their number may perhaps be. Therefore hear us, and after examination reject the spirit of error. He who is not: Argument 6. It is the property of a man not yet renewed, who as yet has no fellowship with God, not to cleave to our apostolic teaching but to give credence to seducers.

units.la: Et hoc indicium est, unde discernatur aliquis utrum Spiritu erroris, an veritatis ducatur: Nam si Apostolorum doctrinæ non auscultaverit quis, erroris spiritu ducitur: si vero quis errores aversetur, & Apostolorum doctrinæ constanter adhæserit, Spiritu veritatis ducitur: Ergo probandi & discernendi vobis sunt Spiritus, ut caveatis seductores.
units.tr: And this is the sign by which one may discern whether someone is led by the spirit of error or of truth. For if anyone has not listened to the teaching of the apostles, he is led by the spirit of error; but if anyone turns away from errors and steadfastly cleaves to the teaching of the apostles, he is led by the Spirit of truth. Therefore you must test and discern the spirits, so that you may guard against seducers.

units.la: Secunda pars Capitis
units.tr: The second part of the chapter

units.la: Verf. 7, Dilecti, diligamus alii alios: nam charitas ex Deo est, quisquis diligit, ex Deo natus est, & novit Deum.
units.tr: Verse 7. Beloved, let us love one another: for love is of God; and every one that loveth is born of God, and knoweth God.

units.la: Altera pars Capitis, In qua hortatur ad fraternam dilectionem. Argumenta hortationis sunt viginti. Argumentum primum, Dilectio erga Fratres est à Deo, nempe, ut speciale donum, quod Electis solum datum est. Ergo ei studendum. Quisquis ] Arg. 2. confirmans superius, Qui charitate præditus est erga fratres, quia fratres, è numero regenitorum est. Ergo charitati studendum. Novit ] Arg. 3. Qui dilectionem exercet novit Deum, id est, credit in Eum, Eumque diligit. Ergo dilectioni fratrum studendum est.
units.tr: The other part of the chapter, in which he urges brotherly love. There are twenty arguments for the exhortation. The first argument: love towards the brethren is from God, namely as a special gift, which is given to the elect alone. Therefore it is to be pursued. Every one that loveth: the second argument, confirming what went before: he who is endowed with love towards the brethren is of the number of the regenerate, because the brethren are so. Therefore love is to be pursued. Knoweth: the third argument: he who practises love knows God, that is, believes in Him and loves Him. Therefore brotherly love is to be pursued.

units.la: Verf. 8. Qui non diligit, non novit DEVM: nam DEVS est charitas.
units.tr: Verse 8. He that loveth not knoweth not God; for God is love.

units.la: Arg. 4. Qui plane destitutus est charitate; erga Fratres nec credit in Deum, nec Deum diligit. Hujus ratio redditur, quia Deus est Charitas, totus amor quoad essentiam, totus amabilis in Se, & in Imagine quaque sua. Totus amans nostri, & omnis charitatis Autor seu Effector in omnibus Filiis suis: adeo ut qui destitutus est charitate, Deum non poterit novisse. Studendum ergo charitati.
units.tr: Argument 4: He who is plainly destitute of love towards the brethren neither believes in God nor loves God. The reason for this is given: God is love, wholly love in essence, wholly lovable in Himself and in each of His images; wholly loving us, and the author or effector of all love in all His sons. So he who is destitute of love cannot have known God. Therefore love is to be pursued.

units.la: Verf. 9 Per hoc patefacta est charitas Dei in nobis, quod Filium illum suum unigenitum misit DEVS in mundum, ut vivamus per eum.
units.tr: Verse 9. In this was manifested the love of God toward us, because that God sent his only begotten Son into the world, that we might live through him.

units.la: Arg. 5. confirmans etiam præcedentem rationem, Deus ita dilexit nos, qui ejus populus nunc sumus, ut Filium suum unigenitum misérit in Mundum, ut nos per ipsius passiones liberati à morte, vitam æternam consequeremur: Ergo nos debemus ejus Filios adoptivos, seu Fratres nostros diligere.
units.tr: Argument 5, also confirming the preceding reason: God so loved us, who are now his people, that he sent his only begotten Son into the world, so that we, freed from death through his sufferings, might obtain eternal life. Therefore we ought to love his adopted sons, that is, our brethren.

units.la: Verf. 10. In hoc est charitas, non quòd nos dilexerimus Deum, sed quòd ipse dilexerit nos, & misérit Filium suum ut esset propitiatio pro peccatis nostris, Verf. 11, Dilecti, si Deus nos ita dilexit, debemus & nos alii alios diligere.
units.tr: Verse 10. Herein is love, not that we loved God, but that he loved us, and sent his Son to be the propitiation for our sins. Verse 11. Beloved, if God so loved us, we ought also to love one another.

units.la: Arg. 6. confirmans & illustrans superius, Deus gratis dilexit nos indignos, & immerentes, etiam & hostes, qui amorem ejus non tantum non meriti sumus, sed ne quidem amorem ejus prius desideravimus, sed Deus nos prior dilexit, & impensissime dilexit, mittendo Filium suum, qui se in victimam offerret pro expiandis peccatis nostris, & impetrandis omnibus donis, quae praeparandis nobis ad vitam aeternam possidendam, necessaria sunt. Unde sequitur nos debere fraternam dilectionem mutuam colere, verf. 11.
units.tr: Argument 6, confirming and illustrating the above: God loved us freely, though we were unworthy and undeserving, even enemies. We not only did not deserve his love, we did not even desire it beforehand; but God loved us first and most lavishly, by sending his Son, who offered himself as a victim to expiate our sins and to obtain all the gifts necessary for preparing us to possess eternal life. Whence it follows that we ought to cultivate mutual brotherly love, verse 11.

units.la: Verf. 12. Deum nemo spectavit unquam: si diligamus alii alios, Deus in nobis habitat, & charitas ejus expleta est in nobis.
units.tr: Verse 12. No man hath seen God at any time. If we love one another, God dwelleth in us, and his love is perfected in us.

units.la: Arg. 7. Etiamsi Deus sit invisibilis, qui sensibus corporeis a nemine unquam conspici potuerit in essentia sua, si tamen nos alii alios diligamus, communionem habemus cum eo, & ipse habitare in nobis comperitur: Ergo dilectioni studendum est. Ádimpleta] Arg. 8. Ex dilectione Fratrum, dilectio nostra erga Deum perfecta, seu sincera esse demonstratur, qualem Deus acceptat & probat. Ergo.
units.tr: Argument 7: Even though God is invisible, and no one has ever been able to see him in his essence with bodily senses, yet if we love one another, we have communion with him, and he is found to dwell in us. Therefore love is to be pursued. Perfected: argument 8: from love of the brethren our love towards God is shown to be perfect, or sincere, such as God accepts and approves. Therefore...

units.la: Verf. 13. Per hoc cognoscimus nos in eo habitare, & ipsum in nobis, quod de Spiritu suo dedit nobis.
units.tr: Verse 13. Hereby know we that we dwell in him, and he in us, because he hath given us of his Spirit.

units.la: Arg. 9. Nos non tantum habemus communionem cum Deo, sed etiam in cognitionem certam, & persuasionem ducimur de communione nostra cum Deo, & mutua quasi inhabitatione, ex eo quod Spiritum suum, seu Spiritum dilectionis nobis dederit: a quo Spiritu Ipse separari non poterit. Ergo.
units.tr: Argument 9: We not only have communion with God, but are also led to a certain knowledge and persuasion of our communion with God, and of a mutual, as it were, indwelling, from the fact that he has given us his Spirit, or the Spirit of love, from which Spirit he himself cannot be separated. Therefore...

units.la: Verf. 14 Nos vero spectavimus, & testamur Patrem misisse Filium qui esset servator mundi.
units.tr: Verse 14. And we have seen and do testify that the Father sent the Son to be the Saviour of the world.

units.la: Arg. 10. Ab experientia Apostolorum, in hunc sensum, Etiamsi Deum nemo spectavit unquam, nos tamen Apostoli spectavimus effectum summae dilectionis in Eo, nempe, quod Pater misit Filium suum, ut esset Salvator mundi, seu Universitatis Electorum suorum Filiorum, per totum Mundum dispersorum, nec possumus celare homines tantum bonum, sed ex dilectione Fratrum electorum quae in nobis est, testamur intrepide de dilectione illa Dei erga homines: Ergo omnes Fideles idem pro suo quisque modulo debet facere.
units.tr: Argument 10: From the experience of the Apostles, to this sense: even though no one has ever seen God, we Apostles have seen the effect of his highest love in him, namely that the Father sent his Son to be Saviour of the world, that is, of the whole body of his elect sons scattered throughout the world. Nor can we conceal such a good from men; from the love of the elect brethren which is in us, we testify fearlessly of that love of God towards men. Therefore all the faithful ought each, according to his measure, to do the same.

units.la: Verf. 15. Quisquis confessus fuerit Iesum esse Filium Dei, Deus in eo habitat, & ipse in Deo.
units.tr: Verse 15. Whosoever shall confess that Jesus is the Son of God, God dwelleth in him, and he in God.

units.la: Arg. 11. Ex superiori illatum, & superius confirmans; Quia non Apostoli tantùm, sed etiam quicunque fuerit qui ex dilectione Dei & Fratrum, Verbo & Opere confessus fuerit excellentiam & virtutem Iesu CHRISTI Filii Dei, sicut nos facimus, ipsi non minùs quam nobis communio cum Deo, ex mutuâ inhabitatione intercedit. Ergo dilectioni fraternæ studendum est.
units.tr: Argument 11: Inferred from the above, and confirming it: not only the Apostles, but whoever, from love of God and of the brethren, shall have confessed by word and deed the excellence and power of Jesus Christ the Son of God, as we do, has communion with God and mutual indwelling no less than we. Therefore brotherly love is to be pursued.

units.la: Verf. 16. Et nos cognovimus & credidimus charitatem quam habet Deus in nobis. Deus charitas est: & qui manet in charitate, in Deo manet; & Deus in eo.
units.tr: Verse 16. And we have known and believed the love that God hath to us. God is love; and he that dwelleth in love dwelleth in God, and God in him.

units.la: Arg. 12. Ab experientia etiam Apostolorum, in hunc sensum, Nos Apostoli experientia & fide persuasi de Dei charitate erga nos, cogimur, & testimonium ei dare, (quod sit ipsa Charitas, & in Se, & erga suos) eumque & ejus liberos amare: Ergo omnes Fideles qui idem credunt, & experti sunt, similiter facere debent.
units.tr: Argument 12: From the experience of the Apostles also, to this sense: we Apostles, persuaded by experience and faith of God's love towards us, are compelled also to bear witness to it (that he is love itself, both in himself and towards his own), and to love him and his children. Therefore all the faithful who believe and have experienced the same ought to do likewise.

units.la: DEVS Charitas Arg. 13. Cum Deus sit Charitas ipsa, quicunque in fide charitatis Divinæ erga se, & studio charitatis exercendæ erga Deum, & Fratres, constanter permanet, constantem habet communionem cum Deo, & Deus cum ipso. Ergo ut fixa maneat hæc communio, dilectioni fraternæ studendum est.
units.tr: God is love. Argument 13: Since God is love itself, whoever constantly remains in faith in the divine love towards himself, and in the zeal of exercising love towards God and the brethren, has constant communion with God, and God with him. Therefore, that this communion may remain fixed, brotherly love is to be pursued.

units.la: Verf. 17. Per hoc expleta est charitas in nobis, ut fiduciam habeamus in die judicii; quòd qualis ille est, tales & nos sumus in hoc mundo.
units.tr: Verse 17. Herein is our love made perfect, that we may have boldness in the day of judgment: because as he is, so are we in this world.

units.la: Arg. 14. Et illa Dei erga nos Charitas quæ credenda est, & illa Dei Charitas, quæ nobis exercenda proponitur erga Deum & fratres, completa & sincerâ esse cognoscitur, & implenda urgetur à nobis eo fine, ut in die Judicii coram Deo, intrepidè stemus: utque nunc de eo die cogitantes confidamus, quasi jam ad Dei Tribunal sisteremur: Ergo Charitati studendum est. Qualis Arg. 15. Rationem reddens superioris, Ex charitate Dei in nobis compertâ colligimus solidè nos in hac vita à Deo dilectos, & in hoc mundo esse factos conformes Deo, qui Charitas est: ideoque persuasi esse poterimus, tanquam ex certissimo signo, nos fore in numero eorum quibus non est condemnatio in vita futura. Ergo studendum fraternæ dilectioni.
units.tr: Argument 14: That love of God towards us which is to be believed, and that love of God which is set before us to be exercised towards God and the brethren, is known to be complete and sincere, and is urged upon us to be fulfilled to this end: that in the day of judgment we may stand fearlessly before God, and that, thinking now of that day, we may be confident, as though we were already set before the tribunal of God. Therefore love is to be pursued. As he is: argument 15, giving the reason for the preceding. From the love of God found in us we solidly gather that we are loved by God in this life, and have been made conformed to God, who is love, in this world. Therefore we may be persuaded, as from a most certain sign, that we shall be among those for whom there is no condemnation in the future life. Therefore brotherly love is to be pursued.

units.la: Verf. 18. Metus non est in charitate: expleta charitas foras ejicit metum: quoniam metus cruciatum habet: qui autem metuit, non est perfectus in charitate.
units.tr: Verse 18. There is no fear in love; but perfect love casteth out fear: because fear hath torment. He that feareth is not made perfect in love.

units.la: Arg. 16. confirmans superius, Charitas Dei per fidem apprehensa, & charitatem accendens erga Deum & fratres, persuasionem de salute nostra ita confirmat, ut non metuamus nobis ab ira & judicio. & quanto persuasio de Dei erga nos charitate ardentius in nobis studium excitat diligendi Deum & proximum, tanto fortius ejicitur metus condemnationis, saltem ille qui cum cruciatu jungitur. Ergo Charitati Fratrum, ex persuasione Charitatis Dei in nos, studendum est.
units.tr: Argument 16, confirming the above: the love of God, grasped by faith and kindling love towards God and the brethren, so confirms our persuasion of salvation that we do not fear wrath and judgment for ourselves. The more ardently the persuasion of God's love towards us stirs in us the zeal of loving God and neighbour, the more strongly is the fear of condemnation cast out, at least that fear which is joined with torment. Therefore zeal for brotherly love, from the persuasion of God's love towards us, is to be pursued.

units.la: Metuit ] Arg. 17. Tanquam aliud consectarium ex superiori Argumento deductum, Quisquis metu condemnationis agitatur, non est satis solide confirmatus in fide Charitatis Dei, & in exercitio Charitatis erga Deum & Fratres, sed eget incremento & hortationibus, ut proficiat in Charitate ad solidam certitudinem: Ergo omnes qui imperfectionem hanc sentiunt in se, dilectioni fratrum ex persuasione Charitatis Dei erga se studere debent.
units.tr: Metuit ] Argument 17. As another corollary drawn from the previous argument: whoever is driven by fear of condemnation is not solidly enough confirmed in the faith of God's love, nor in the exercise of love towards God and the brethren, but needs growth and exhortations so that he may advance in love to a firm certainty. Therefore all who feel this imperfection in themselves ought to strive for brotherly love from the persuasion of God's love towards them.

units.la: Verl. 19: Nos diligimus eum, quoniam ipse prior dilexit nos.
units.tr: Verse 19: We love him, because he first loved us.

units.la: Arg. 18. Dilectio qua nos diligimus Deum, non est causa dilectionis qua Deus nos diligit, sed effectus posterior. Ergo studeamus ex persuasione dilectionis Dei erga nos, Deum magis magisque diligere, & quanto impensius studebimus Deum diligere in Se, & in Filiis suis se nobis diligendum offerentem, tanto confirmatiores erimus de ejus dilectione erga nos. Studendum ergo charitati.
units.tr: Argument 18. The love by which we love God is not the cause of the love by which God loves us, but its later effect. Therefore let us strive, from the persuasion of God's love towards us, to love God more and more; and the more earnestly we strive to love God, who in himself and in his sons offers himself to us to be loved, the more confirmed we shall be in his love towards us. Therefore we must strive for love.

units.la: Verf. 20. Siquis dixerit, Diligo Deum, & fratrem suum oderit, mendax est. Qui enim non diligit fratrem suum quem vidit, Deum quem non vidit quomodo potest diligere?
units.tr: Verse 20: If anyone says, I love God, and hates his brother, he is a liar. For he who does not love his brother whom he has seen, how can he love God whom he has not seen?

units.la: Arg 19. Vana est dilectionis jactantia erga Deum, ubi non est dilectio fratrum, quia gratia Dei non operatur dilectionem Dei sine dilectione fratrum. Ergo, &c. Qui enim ] Hoc argumentum confirmat hac ratione, quia cum magis moveamur ad amandum aspectu, quam auditu: is qui fratrem quem videt, & Dei in eo imaginem non diligit, Deum quem non videt non potest diligere. Vana est igitur dilectionis erga Deum jactantia, ubi non est dilectio fratrum.
units.tr: Argument 19. Boasting of love towards God is empty where there is no love of the brethren, because the grace of God does not work love for God without love for the brethren. Therefore, etc. For he who ] This argument is confirmed by this reasoning: since we are moved to love more by sight than by hearing, he who does not love the brother whom he sees, and in whom is God's image, cannot love God whom he does not see. Therefore boasting of love towards God is empty where there is no love of the brethren.

units.la: Verl. 21. Et hoc mandatum habemus ab eo, ut qui diligit Deum, diligat & fratrem suum. Arg 20. Eadem autoritas Dei simul utrumque mandatum conjunxit, requirens ab omnibus qui Deum diligunt, ut fratres etiam suos diligant. Ergo fratrum dilectioni studendum est.
units.tr: Verse 21: And this commandment we have from him, that he who loves God should love his brother also. Argument 20. The same authority of God has joined both commandments together, requiring of all who love God that they love their brethren also. Therefore we must strive for love of the brethren.

units.la: Caput Quintum.
units.tr: Chapter 5.

units.la: Scopus principalis totius Epistolæ, & hujus potissimum Capitis, verf. 13. proponitur, scilicet, ut credentes in Christum sciant se habere vitam æternam, & ut scientes se habere vitam, credant in Christum magis magisque. Capitis duæ sunt partes: In prima describit notas veræ Fidelium seu Renatorum, quibus jus datur ad vitam æternam, cum inchoata possessione, ad verf. 6. In secundâ argumenta proponit, quæ moveant ut credamus in Christum.
units.tr: The principal aim of the whole Epistle, and especially of this chapter, is set out in verse 13: namely, that believers in Christ may know that they have eternal life, and that, knowing they have life, they may believe in Christ more and more. The chapter has two parts. In the first he describes the marks of true believers, that is, of the regenerate, by which they are given a right to eternal life, with its beginning already possessed, down to verse 6. In the second he sets out the arguments that move us to believe in Christ.

units.la: Verf. 1. Quisquis credit Iesum esse Christum, ex Deo natus est: & quisquis diligit genitorem, diligit etiam eum qui ex eo genitus est.
units.tr: Verse 1. Whoever believes that Jesus is the Christ is born of God, and whoever loves the one who begets loves also the one who is begotten by him.

units.la: Notæ verè Fidelium seu Renatorum, & sincerè Agentium, sunt sex. Nota prima hæc est, Verè Fidelis, seu ex Deo genitus seriò credit Iesum esse Christum promissum, scilicet Redemptorem mundi; nam quicunque hanc veritatem solidè imbibit, & corde agnoscit sibi illam applicans, sicut Scriptura requirit, ex Deo natus est: Et quisquis Nota 2. verè Fidelis. Sic diligit Deum, ut etiam fratres seu genitos ex Deo, diligat.
units.tr: The marks of true believers, that is, of the regenerate, who act sincerely, are six. The first mark is this: the true believer, or the one born of God, earnestly believes that Jesus is the promised Christ, namely the Redeemer of the world. For whoever takes this truth in fully and acknowledges it in his heart, applying it to himself as Scripture requires, is born of God. And whoever (Mark 2) is a true believer. In this way he loves God, and so also loves the brethren, that is, those begotten of God.

units.la: Verf. 2. Per hoc cognoscimus nos diligere filios Dei, quum nos Deum diligimus, & mandata ejus servamus.
units.tr: Verse 2. By this we know that we love the children of God, when we love God and keep his commandments.

units.la: Nota 3. Verè fideles sic diligunt fratres, ut simul diligant Deum, & ex dilectione Dei studeant ejus mandata servare.
units.tr: Mark 3. True believers love the brethren in such a way that they love God at the same time, and from their love of God they strive to keep his commandments.

units.la: Verf. 3. Hæc est enim charitas Dei, ut mandata ejus servemus: & mandata ejus gravia non sunt.
units.tr: Verse 3. For this is the love of God, that we keep his commandments, and his commandments are not grievous.

units.la: Nota 4. explicans priorem, Verè Fideles demonstrant charitatis sinceritatem, in studio observandi mandata ex dilectione Dei, adeò ut ejus mandata quantumcunque difficilia, & carni ingrata, illis tamen non sunt gravia, sed quæ lubentissimè cupiant præstare.
units.tr: Mark 4, explaining the former: true believers show the sincerity of their love by their eagerness to observe the commandments out of love for God. So his commandments, however difficult and unwelcome to the flesh, are not grievous to them, but things they most gladly desire to perform.

units.la: Verf. 4. Quoniam quicquid natum est ex Deo, vincit mundum & hæc est victoria quæ vicit mundum, nempe fides nostra,
units.tr: Verse 4. For whatever is born of God overcomes the world, and this is the victory that has overcome the world, namely our faith.

units.la: Nota 5. rationem reddens prioris, Vere Fideles seu Renati vincunt mundum, id est, superant quicquid se opponit Dei Spiritui, nempe, fallacias, illecebras, & terrores mundi, & omnia obstacula, quæ possent eos à studio mandatorum Dei impedire, adeò ut etiamsi conflictus sit quotidianus, non cedant tamen sed certi de triumpho, ut victores opponant se & persequantur hostes. Et hæc ] Nota 6. explicans priorem, Vere Fideles, non nituntur suis viribus in bello adversus mundum; sed per fidem innituntur Christo, qui mundum superavit ipsorum nomine, quique vires suppeditat ad vincendum mundum, Quod est vincendi genus certissimum, præclarissimum & plenissimum.
units.tr: Mark 5, giving the reason for the former: true believers, or the regenerate, overcome the world, that is, they master whatever sets itself against the Spirit of God: deceits, allurements and the terrors of the world, and all the obstacles that could hinder them from zeal for God's commandments. So even though the conflict is daily, they do not give way but, sure of triumph, stand against and pursue their enemies as victors. And this (Mark 6, explaining the former): true believers do not rely on their own strength in the war against the world, but through faith they rest on Christ, who overcame the world on their behalf, and who supplies the strength to overcome the world. This is the surest, most glorious and most complete kind of victory.

units.la: Verf. 5. Quis est qui vincit mundum, nisi qui credit Iesum esse Filium Dei?
units.tr: Verse 5. Who is he that overcomes the world, but he who believes that Jesus is the Son of God?

units.la: Ratio redditur victoriæ reportatæ de mundo per fidem, Quia impossibile est ut quisquam vincat mundum, nisi qui sibi diffidens recumbit per fidem in solam veritatem, & virtutem Iesu Christi, ut Omnipotentis Filii Dei, qui non solum vicit mundum pro suis, sed victores reddit etiam omnes inos.
units.tr: The reason is given for the victory won over the world through faith: because no one can overcome the world unless he, distrusting himself, rests by faith on the sole truth and power of Jesus Christ, as the Almighty Son of God, who not only overcame the world for his own people but also makes all of them victors.

units.la: Secunda pars
units.tr: The second part

units.la: Verf. 6. Hic ille est qui venit per aquam & sanguinem, nempe Iesus Christus: non per aquam solum, sed per aquam & sanguinem: & spiritus is est qui testificatur spiritum veritatem esse.
units.tr: Verse 6. This is he who came by water and blood, namely Jesus Christ: not by water only, but by water and blood. And it is the Spirit who bears witness, because the Spirit is truth.

units.la: Altera pars Capitis, In qua probat credendum esse in Christum, ut Filium Dei. Argumenta sunt quatuordecim.
units.tr: The second part of the chapter, in which he proves that we must believe in Christ as the Son of God. There are fourteen arguments.

units.la: Argumentum primum, Quia Iesus Christus est ille, qui veniens, secum attulit solidam legalium ceremoniarum substantiam, quod ad peccati abolitionem attinet præsertim: nam venit cum aqua, seu cum ea sanctitate in Se, & virtute ad sanctificandum suos, quæ per aquam & ablutiones in veteri lege significabatur futura in Messia cum veniret. Et venit cum sanguine, seu cum plena expiatione peccati suorum, per propitiatorium sacrificium sanguinis sui, ad tollendum peccata populi sui, in Cruce oblatum. Non per aquam ] Id confirmat, Quia venit Christus, non cum una proprietate Mediatoris, quæ est sanctitas personæ suæ, & sanctificandi suos virtus per aquam, seu ablutiones legales, significata; Sed venit etiam cum altera proprietate, quæ est expiatio & plena reconciliatio, per sanguinis aspersionem seu mactatas pecudes significata. Cujus conjunctionis admirandum symbolum erat fluxus aquæ simul & sanguinis ex latere ejus in cruce, sicut Apostolus noster studiosè observavit in Euangelio suo, Cap. 19 34 Ut omnes sciamus Christum quos justificat eosdem etiam sanctificare, & contra, quoscunque sanctificat, eosdem etiam justificare. Ergo in Christum credendum est.
units.tr: The first argument: Jesus Christ is he who, coming, brought with him the solid substance of the legal ceremonies, especially as regards the abolition of sin. For he came with water, that is, with that holiness in himself and that power to sanctify his people, which was signified in the Old Law by water and washings, to be found in the Messiah when he should come. And he came with blood, that is, with the full expiation of the sins of his own people, through the propitiatory sacrifice of his blood, offered on the Cross, to take away the sins of his people. Not by water only: this confirms the point, because Christ came not with one property of the Mediator, which is the holiness of his person and the power of sanctifying his own, signified by water, that is, the legal washings; but he came also with the other property, which is atonement and full reconciliation, signified by the sprinkling of blood or the slain beasts. A wonderful symbol of this union was the flow of water and blood together from his side on the cross, as our Apostle carefully noted in his Gospel, chap. 19:34. So that we may all know that those whom Christ justifies he also sanctifies, and conversely, whomever he sanctifies, these he also justifies. Therefore we must believe in Christ.

units.la: Spiritus ] Arg. 2. Spiritus idem testatur, id est, Spiritus manifestatio in variis suis donis super Christi discipulos, effusis, testatur & obsignat Christum esse Filium Dei, suoque dictamine hoc in verè fidelium cordibus fixum reddit. Ergo in Christum est credendum.
units.tr: The Spirit: the second argument. The Spirit bears witness, that is, the manifestation of the Spirit in his various gifts poured out upon the disciples of Christ bears witness and seals that Christ is the Son of God, and by his own dictate fixes this in the hearts of true believers. Therefore we must believe in Christ.

units.la: Veritatem ] Hoc argumentum confirmat ex eo, quod Spiritus in his operationibus suis verax sit & ab omni impostura alienissimus, quippè qui nihil præter verbum Dei, seu ipsissimam veritatem nobis commendat.
units.tr: Truth: this argument confirms the point from the fact that the Spirit in these operations is true and wholly free from all deceit, since he commends to us nothing but the Word of God, that is, the very truth.

units.la: Vers. 7. Nam tres sunt qui testificantur in Cœlo, Pater Sermo & Spiritus Sanctus: & hi tres unum sunt.
units.tr: Verse 7. For there are three who bear witness in heaven: the Father, the Word and the Holy Spirit; and these three are one.

units.la: Arg. 3. Quia tres personæ Deitatis, Pater, Sermo & Spiritus Sanctus, sicut unum sunt Essentia, sic etiam consensu testandi conspirant ad hoc unum confirmandum; Quod Iesus Christus sit Filius Dei. Nam Pater de eo testatus est: Primo, voce audibili in Christi Baptismo, & in transfiguratione pronuncians eum esse filium suum dilectum, in quo acquiescit. Secundo operibus, quæ dedit Christo, ut ea perficeret, Joh. 5, 19. 36. Deinde, Sermo, seu Verbum testatur de Christo, hoc est, Christus (qua Deus est) testatur de seipso incarnato, quod sit Filius Dei, partim viva voce affirmans id sæpissimè, partim in tota doctrinâ manifestum faciens, quod is ipse sit qui è sinu Patris prodiit, & ejus consilium de hominum salute patefecit. Qui superne venit, qui è Cœlo venit supra omnes est, Joh. 4. 31. Tertio, Spiritus Sanctus testatur Iesum Christum esse Filium Dei, partim descensu super eum in Baptismo ipsius: Partim descensu super ejus Apostolos & Discipulos in die Pentecostes; partim doctrinam Christi, Scripturæ Amanuensibus inspirando, eamque mundo commendando, ut homines doceat, iis persuadeat, & eos confirmet de illa veritate, ut verè divinâ: per eam colligat Ecclesiam, quam in omni veritate ducat ad vitam æternam. Dicuntur hi tres testari in Cœlo Primùm, quia ex Cælo tanquam ex solio pro imperio immediatè testimonium dicunt. Deinde, quia majestas horum testium præcipuè in Cœlo splendet. Tertium, quia non nisi ab animis in Cœlum sublatis auditur, observatur, agnoscitur hoc testimonium. Denique, quia hoc testimonium in Cœlo maximâ ex parte perficitur, etiamsi in terra omnino non reciperetur: Ergo in CHRISTUM propter hoc testimonium est credendum.
units.tr: Argument 3: because the three persons of the Godhead, the Father, the Word and the Holy Spirit, are one in essence, so also in the agreement of their witness they join together to confirm this one thing, that Jesus Christ is the Son of God. For the Father has borne witness concerning him: first, by an audible voice at the Baptism of Christ and at the transfiguration, declaring him to be his beloved Son, in whom he is well pleased; second, by the works he gave Christ to perform, John 5:19, 36. Then the Word, that is, the Word bears witness concerning Christ; in other words, Christ (as God) bears witness about himself incarnate, that he is the Son of God, partly by affirming it very often with his living voice, partly by making plain in all his teaching that he is the one who came forth from the bosom of the Father and revealed his counsel concerning the salvation of men. He who comes from above, who comes from heaven, is above all (John 3:31). Third, the Holy Spirit bears witness that Jesus Christ is the Son of God: partly by descending upon him at his Baptism; partly by descending upon his Apostles and disciples on the day of Pentecost; partly by inspiring the writers of Scripture with the doctrine of Christ, and commending it to the world, so that he may teach men, persuade them and confirm them in that truth as truly divine, and through it gather the Church, which he leads into all truth to eternal life. These three are said to testify in heaven: first, because they bear witness immediately from heaven as from a throne, with authority. Second, because the majesty of these witnesses shines chiefly in heaven. Third, because this testimony is heard, observed and acknowledged only by minds lifted up to heaven. Last, because this testimony is for the most part accomplished in heaven, even if on earth it is not received at all. Therefore we must believe in Christ on account of this testimony.

units.la: Verf. 8. Et tres sunt qui testificantur in terra, Spiritus & Aqua, & Sanguis: & hi tres in unum consentiunt.
units.tr: Verse 8. And there are three who bear witness on earth: the Spirit, and the water, and the blood; and these three agree in one.

units.la: Arg. 4. Quia tres testes in terra conspirant in hoc unum, ut probent CHRISTUM esse Filium DEI, Spiritus, Aqua, & Sanguis: qui testes dicuntur in terra; Primò, quia testimonium hoc mediatum est, & ex operibus in terra spectandis profertur. Secundò, quia in hominibus, qui in terra sunt, hujus testimonii dictio scribitur & agnoscitur in Ecclesia visibili scilicet. Denique, quia non tantùm in Ecclesia sonat hoc testimonium, sed etiam vocem edit inter mundanos, & auditur ab iis, ad ipsorum convictionem: Nam primò Spiritus, seu Spiritus manifestatio partim in donis miraculosis, quæ in Ecclesiam effusa sunt usque ad mundi stuporem, ad satis multos annos post CHRISTI ascensionem: Partim in donis ordinariis, quæ & in Ecclesia etiamnum vigent, sufficit & ad testandum, quod CHRISTUS qui inter nos est prædicatus, DEUS sit; & ad extorquendam confessionem ab iis, qui extra Ecclesiam sunt, quod DEUS sit in nobis, qui in CHRISTUM credimus, 1 Cor. 14. Deinde Spiritus operatio in cordibus fidelium ita vivificat verba CHRISTI, & per ea instruit, consolatur, & confirmat electos, ut nullum relinquat dubium de CHRISTI Divinate.
units.tr: Arg. 4. Since three witnesses on earth agree in this one thing, to prove that CHRIST is the Son of GOD: the Spirit, the Water, and the Blood, which are said to be witnesses on earth. First, because this testimony is mediated and is brought forward from works to be observed on earth. Second, because the utterance of this testimony is written down and acknowledged in men who are on earth, namely in the visible Church. Finally, because this testimony not only sounds in the Church but also gives forth its voice among worldly people and is heard by them, for their conviction. For first, the Spirit, or the manifestation of the Spirit, partly in the miraculous gifts poured out upon the Church, to the astonishment of the world, for quite many years after the ascension of CHRIST; and partly in the ordinary gifts, which still flourish in the Church, suffice also to testify that CHRIST, who is preached among us, is God, and to extort a confession from those outside the Church that God is in us who believe in CHRIST, 1 Cor. 14. Then the operation of the Spirit in the hearts of the faithful so quickens the words of CHRIST, and through them instructs, comforts and confirms the elect, that it leaves no doubt about CHRIST's divinity.

units.la: Quod ad aquam attinet, quæ est CHRISTI virtus sanctificans suos, expresse adeo de CHRISTO loquitur, ut cogantur etiam, qui extra Ecclesiam sunt, videntes in Christianis lucem bonorum operum, glorificare Patrem nostrum, & Patrem CHRISTI, qui in cœlo est, ita ut etiam in fœminis perspecta, maritos infideles, qui verbum DEI initio non agnoverunt, ad DEUM adduxerit, 1 Pet. 3. 1.
units.tr: As for the water, which is the sanctifying power of CHRIST over his own, it speaks so expressly of CHRIST that even those outside the Church are compelled, seeing in Christians the light of good works, to glorify our Father and the Father of CHRIST who is in heaven; so much so that, observed even in women, it has brought unbelieving husbands, who at first did not acknowledge the word of God, to God, 1 Pet. 3. 1.

units.la: Denique quod ad sanguinem attinet, qui est pretium redemptionis, & CHRISTI virtus expians peccata, & reconcilians homines DEO; loquitur ille sanguis meliora quam sanguis Abelis, ut conscientias Fidelium tranquillas & pacatas reddat, aditum ad DEI Thronum aperiat, & corda ipsorum adversus mundum, omniaque quæ in eo sunt adversa ita confirmet, ut audeant & valeant, etiam sanguine suo testimonii hujus dictionem stionem ipsis etiam audientibus hostibus in mediis tormentis cum gaudio, resonare, Apoc. 12. 11. Ergo debemus in CHRISTUM ut Filium DEI credere.
units.tr: Finally, as for the blood, which is the price of redemption and the power of CHRIST atoning for sins and reconciling men to God, that blood speaks better things than the blood of Abel: it makes the consciences of the faithful tranquil and at peace, opens access to the throne of God, and so strengthens their hearts against the world and all the adversities in it, that they dare and are able, even by their own blood, to let this testimony resound with joy, even while the enemies who hear it stand by amid the torments, Rev. 12. 11. Therefore we ought to believe in CHRIST as the Son of God.

units.la: Vers. 9. Si testimonium hominum accipimus, testimonium Dei, majus est: nam hoc est testimonium DEI, quod testificatus est de Filio suo,
units.tr: Verse 9. If we receive the testimony of men, the testimony of God is greater: for this is the testimony of God, which he has testified concerning his Son.

units.la: Arg. 5. Propter testimonium verorum hominum credimus eorum assertionibus: Ergo propter majus testimonium DEI, de Filio suo testantis credere debemus in CHRISTUM, ut Filium DEI.
units.tr: Arg. 5. On account of the testimony of true men we believe their assertions. Therefore, on account of the greater testimony of God, who testifies concerning his Son, we ought to believe in CHRIST as the Son of God.

units.la: Vers. 10. Qui credit in Filium Dei, habet testimonium in seipso; qui non credit Deo, mendacem eum fecit, quia non credidit testimonio quod testificatus est Deus de Filio suo.
units.tr: Verse 10. He who believes in the Son of God has the testimony in himself; he who does not believe God has made him a liar, because he has not believed the testimony which God has testified concerning his Son.

units.la: Arg. 6. Qui credit in CHRISTUM ut Filium DEI, tantam comperit certitudinem sibi factam, ut in testimonio Spiritus, veritatem hanc verbi divini intus confirmantis acquiescat, Ergo, &c.
units.tr: Arg. 6. He who believes in CHRIST as the Son of God has found such certainty made for him that he rests in the testimony of the Spirit, who inwardly confirms this truth of the divine word. Therefore, etc.

units.la: Qui non credit ] Arg. 7. Qui non credit in CHRISTUM ut Filium DEI, reipsa Deum accusat mendacii, quia ejus testimonium de Filio suo rejicit, quasi falsum esset. Ergo credendum in CHRISTUM ut DEI FILIUM.
units.tr: He who does not believe ] Arg. 7. He who does not believe in CHRIST as the Son of God in fact accuses God of lying, since he rejects God's testimony concerning his Son, as if it were false. Therefore one must believe in CHRIST as the Son of God.

units.la: Vers. 11. Est autem hoc testimonium, nempe, quod vitam æternam dedit nobis Deus: & hæc vita in Filio ejus est.
units.tr: Verse 11. And this is the testimony, namely, that God has given us eternal life, and this life is in his Son.

units.la: Arg. 8. Credentes in Filium habent jus ad vitam æternam, quæ est in Filio, ut in Fonte, Procuratore, Datore, Conservatore, sibi datum ex gratia, & confirmatum per testimonii DEI constantiam. Ergo, &c.
units.tr: Arg. 8. Those who believe in the Son have a right to eternal life, which is in the Son as in its Fountain, Procurer, Giver and Preserver, given to them from grace and confirmed by the constancy of God's testimony. Therefore, etc.

units.la: Vers. 12. Qui habet Filium, habet vitam; qui non habet Filium Dei, vitam non habet.
units.tr: Verse 12. He who has the Son has life; he who does not have the Son of God does not have life.

units.la: Arg. 9 Qui in amplexibus verè fidei habet FILIUM, habet etiam vitam æternam, non tantùm quoàd jus, sed etiam quoàd inchoatam possessionem, & qui non habet FILIUM per fidem, vel quærit in alio quam in Eo vitam, destituitur & secluditur ab omni vitâ spirituali. Ergo credendum in CHRISTUM ut Filium DEI.
units.tr: Arg. 9. He who in the embrace of true faith has the SON also has eternal life, not only as to right but also as to a begun possession; and he who does not have the SON through faith, or seeks life in anyone other than in Him, is deprived and shut off from all spiritual life. Therefore one must believe in CHRIST as the Son of God.

units.la: Vers. 13. Hæc scripsi vobis, qui creditis in nomen Filii DEI: ut sciatis vos vitam æternam habere, & ut credatis in nomen Filii DEI.
units.tr: Verse 13. These things I have written to you who believe in the name of the Son of God, that you may know that you have eternal life, and that you may believe in the name of the Son of God.

units.la: Arg. 10. In hunc finem scripta sunt ad Fideles omnia hæc à Spiritu Sancto per Amanuensem Apostolum, ut certi sint se jam habere vitam æternam, & magis magisque credant in nomen Filii Dei. Ergo in Christum credendum est.
units.tr: Arg. 10. To this end all these things were written to the faithful by the Holy Spirit, through the Apostle as amanuensis, that they may be certain that they already have eternal life, and believe more and more in the name of the Son of God. Therefore one must believe in CHRIST.

units.la: Verf. 14 Et hæc est fiducia quam apud Deum habemus ipsum, siquid petierimus secundum voluntatem ejus, nos audire.
units.tr: Verse 14. And this is the confidence which we have toward him, that if we ask anything according to his will, he hears us.

units.la: Arg. 11. Qui credit in Christum, fiduciam habet accedendi ad Deum in precibus, & quod benevolam Dei aurem sit experturus in omni petitione, quæ secundum Dei voluntatem proponitur. Ergo.
units.tr: Arg. 11. He who believes in CHRIST has confidence in approaching God in prayer, and that he will find God's kindly ear in every petition put forward according to God's will. Therefore.

units.la: Verf. 15. Quòd si scimus eum audire nos, quicquid petierimus, scimus nos habere petitiones quas ab eo petiimus.
units.tr: Verse 15. And if we know that he hears us, whatever we ask, we know that we have the petitions which we have asked of him.

units.la: Arg. 12. explicans & confirmans superius, Qui credit in Christum, cognoscendo se propitium habere Deum in legitimis suis, seu recte ordinatis petitionibus, statuere etiam & potest petitiones suas, quas secundum Dei promissiones propulsuit, concessas jam esse à Deo, antequam perficiantur; Atque ita securus esse potest de successu precum suarum. Ergo credendum vel hanc ob causam in Christum.
units.tr: Arg. 12. Explaining and confirming the above: he who believes in CHRIST, knowing that he has God propitious toward his lawful, or rightly ordered, petitions, can also be assured that his petitions, which he has put forward according to God's promises, are already granted by God before they are fulfilled; and so he can be secure about the outcome of his prayers. Therefore one must believe in CHRIST, for this reason too.

units.la: Verf. 16. Si quis viderit fratrem suum peccare peccato quod non est ad mortem, petet & dabit ei vitam, peccantibus dico, non ad mortem. Est peccatum ad mortem; non pro illo dico ut roget.
units.tr: Verse 16. If anyone sees his brother sinning a sin which is not unto death, he shall ask, and God shall give him life, for those sinning, I say, not unto death. There is a sin unto death; I do not say that he should pray for it.

units.la: Arg. 13. Qui credit in Christum, non tantùm pro seipso, sed etiam pro fratribus suis delinquentibus ex charitate orans, exaudietur, quibus per peccati meritum, ad interitum vergentibus, & pereuntibus Deus restituet vitam rogatus à Fideli: Ergo, &c.
units.tr: Arg. 13. He who believes in CHRIST, praying out of love not only for himself but also for his brothers who offend, will be heard; for God, when asked by the faithful, will restore life to those brothers who, through the merit of sin, are tending toward ruin and perishing. Therefore, etc.

units.la: Excipit in casu peccati in Spiritum Sanctum, Quando professor fidei, seu frater, quoad externam communionem Ecclesiæ incidit in apertam apostasiam à fide Christi, & hostile odium suscipit adversus Euangelium & Fideles, contrà illuminationem conscientiæ semel factam à Spiritu Sancto; pro eo qui hoc peccatum admiserit, cum poterit discerni, non jubet precari. Dicitur autem peccatum ad mortem, quia mors æterna peccatum illud consequitur, & qui in ipsum cadit, manet in eo sine resipiscentia, donec detrudatur in infernum.
units.tr: He excepts the case of the sin against the Holy Spirit, when a professor of the faith, or a brother as far as external communion with the Church goes, falls into open apostasy from the faith of CHRIST and takes up hostile hatred against the Gospel and the faithful, against the enlightenment of conscience once wrought by the Holy Spirit. For one who has committed this sin, when it can be discerned, he does not bid us pray. It is called a sin unto death because eternal death follows that sin, and whoever falls into it remains in it without repentance until he is thrust down into hell.

units.la: Verf. 17. Omnis iniquitas peccatum est: [sed est peccatum quod non est ad mortem.] Explicat dictum, ostendens, quod licet omnis transgressio Legis sit peccatum, cujus propterea stipendium meritum est mors, non tamen omne peccatum consequitur mors; quia alicui remittitur quodvis genus peccati, excepto hoc peccato, quod blasphemia dicitur adversus Spiritum Sanctum, quæ nulli unquam remissa est, nec ulli unquam remittetur.
units.tr: Verse 17. All unrighteousness is sin: [but there is a sin which is not unto death.] He explains the saying, showing that although every transgression of the Law is sin, whose wages therefore is death, yet not every sin is followed by death; for every kind of sin is forgiven to someone, except this sin, which is called blasphemy against the Holy Spirit, and which has never been forgiven to anyone, nor ever will be.

units.la: Vers. 18. Scimus quod quisquis natus est ex Deo, non peccat: sed qui genitus est ex Deo, conservat seipsum, & Malus ille non tangit eum.
units.tr: Verse 18. We know that whoever is born of God does not sin; but he who has been begotten of God keeps himself, and the Evil One does not touch him.

units.la: Arg. 14. Regenitus, seu qui verè credit in Filium Dei, conservatur, ne peccet hoc peccatum: imo, nec in ullo peccato jacet perpetuò implicitus, sed per Dei gratiam, seminisque Dei in eo permanentis virtutem, servat se ipsum, ne diabolus hoc peccato ad mortem tangat eum. Ergo in Christum credendum est.
units.tr: Arg. 14. The one who is born again, or who truly believes in the Son of God, is kept from committing this sin. Indeed, he does not lie perpetually entangled in any sin; but through the grace of God and the power of the seed of God remaining in him, he keeps himself, lest the devil touch him with the sin unto death. Therefore one must believe in CHRIST as the Son of God.

units.la: Vers. 19. Scimus nos ex DEO esse, & mundum totum in malo jacere.
units.tr: Verse 19. We know that we are of God, and that the whole world lies in wickedness.

units.la: Hoc argumentum per modum assumptionis ex thesi applicat in consolationem suam, & Fidelium ad quos scribit, & confirmat quinque rationibus, nempe, quod Fideles, ad quos scribit, confervandi sint una cum seipso, & perseveraturi in fide & obedientia Evangelii.
units.tr: By way of an assumption drawn from the thesis, he applies this argument for the comfort of himself and of the faithful to whom he writes, and confirms it with five reasons, namely, that the faithful to whom he writes are to be preserved together with himself, and will persevere in faith and in obedience to the Gospel.

units.la: Scimus ] Ratio prima, Persuasi certò sumus de nostra regeneratione: Ergo persuasum habemus nos non peccaturos illud peccatum irremissibile, nec servituros peccato, sed liberatum iri à Diabolo, plenè per Christum. Mundum ] Ratio 2. Soli mundani positi sunt in Diaboli maligni istius potestate, ut eos ex scelere in scelus præcipitet. Ergo nos qui ex mundo translati sumus in regnum Dei, non sumus in maligni istius potestate, sed ut liberi Dei perseveraturi sumus.
units.tr: We know: the first reason. We are certainly persuaded of our regeneration; therefore we are persuaded that we shall not commit that unforgivable sin, nor be enslaved to sin, but shall be fully freed from the Devil through Christ. The world: the second reason. Worldly men alone are placed under the power of that evil Devil, so that he may hurl them from crime to crime. Therefore we, who have been transferred out of the world into the kingdom of God, are not in the power of that evil one, but, as free men of God, we shall persevere.

units.la: Vers. 20. Sed scimus Filium Dei venisse, & dedisse nobis mentem, ut cognoscamus illum qui verax est, & sumus in verace illo, in Filio ejus Christo: hic est verus Deus & vita aeterna.
units.tr: Verse 20. But we know that the Son of God has come, and has given us a mind to know him who is true, and we are in him who is true, in his Son Jesus Christ: this is the true God and eternal life.

units.la: Ratio 3. Nos certi sumus de Christi Liberatoris adventu in mundum, qui mentes nostras illuminavit suâ gratiâ, & fide in Deum verâ donavit: Ergo non peccabimus ad mortem, sed perseverabimus.
units.tr: The third reason: we are certain of the coming of Christ the Liberator into the world, who has illuminated our minds by his grace and has bestowed upon us true faith in God. Therefore we shall not sin unto death, but shall persevere.

units.la: Et sumus ] Ratio 4. Nos communionem habemus cum Deo & Christo, in quo sumus & habitamus per fidem: Ergo intacti ab illo peccato perseverabimus.
units.tr: And we are: the fourth reason. We have communion with God and Christ, in whom we are and dwell through faith. Therefore, untouched by that sin, we shall persevere.

units.la: Hic est ] Ratio 5. Christus est ipsissimus verus Deus, & Vita æterna, qui na, qui in Seipso vita est; Vitæque communicandæ fidelibus Fons, Procurator, Dator, & Conservator est. Ergo certò sumus persuasi de perseverantia nostrâ, & salute æternâ.
units.tr: This is: the fifth reason. Christ is the very true God and eternal life, who is life in himself, and is the fountain, procurer, giver and preserver of the life to be communicated to the faithful. Therefore we are certainly persuaded of our perseverance and eternal salvation.

units.la: Vers. 21. Filioli, cavete vobis ab idolis. Amen.
units.tr: Verse 21. Little children, keep yourselves from idols. Amen.

units.la: Pro conclusione Epistolæ subjicit brevem admonitionem, ut caveant sibi, seu custodiant se ab idolis, in plurali numero, idque ab omnigenere idolorum, quæ quovis modo se ingererent loco veritatis, vel veri Dei, ad abducendum eos à fide veræ doctrinæ, vel à vero cultu, seu obedientia Dei, sub quovifcunque prætextu: eoque magis quia à Diabolo, & ejus asseclis obtrudenda erant hæc idola fidelibus, & omni quâ fieri posset arte ipsis insinuanda. Propterea jubet studiosius invigilare, & se custodire ab iis, ne quovis modo ab iis polluerentur, nominatim verò ut caverent sibi à simulachris, in quibus Antichristus gloriaturus erat, & per ea mundum decepturus.
units.tr: As a conclusion to the Epistle, he adds a brief admonition that they should take heed to themselves, that is, guard themselves from idols, in the plural, and from every kind of idol which might thrust itself in any way in place of the truth or the true God, to draw them away from faith in the true doctrine or from the true worship, or obedience to God, under whatever pretext; and this all the more because these idols were to be pressed upon the faithful by the Devil and his followers, and insinuated to them by every art possible. Therefore he bids them watch more diligently and guard themselves from these, lest they be polluted by them in any way, and specifically that they should beware of the images in which Antichrist was going to glory, and by which he would deceive the world.

units.la: EXPOSITIO ANALYTICA SECVNDÆ EPISTOLÆ IO- ANNIS. Summarium.
units.tr: Analytical Exposition of the Second Epistle of John. Summary.

units.la: Sicut Lucas librum Euangelii, & Actorum Apostolicorum inscripsit Nobili cuidam Theophilo, in usum omnium Fidelium; Sic Ioannes familiarem hanc Epistolam Nobili cuidam, & sanctæ Matronæ, ejusq; liberis scripsit, non solùm ut doctrinam, quam superiori Epistola universæ Ecclesiæ Fidelium commendaverat, privatæ huic familiæ breviter applicaret, sed etiam ut doceret Pastores quomodo ipsis publicè & per singulas domos docendum sit, Apostolorum exemplo, Act: 20 20. Partes Epistolæ sunt tres, Præfatio continens directionem Epistolæ, & salutationem, ad vers. 4. Hortatio ad perseverantiam in obedientia Euangelii, seu in constanti exercitio Fiaei, per charitatem efficacis, ad vers. 12. Tertia est conclusio.
units.tr: Just as Luke dedicated the book of the Gospel and the Acts of the Apostles to a certain noble man, Theophilus, for the use of all the faithful, so John wrote this familiar Epistle to a certain noble and holy matron and her children. He did this not only so that he might briefly apply to this private household the teaching which he had commended to the whole Church of the faithful in the earlier Epistle, but also so that he might teach ministers how they ought to teach publicly and from house to house, after the example of the Apostles, Acts 20.20. The parts of the Epistle are three: a preface containing the address of the Epistle and the greeting, to verse 4; an exhortation to perseverance in obedience to the Gospel, that is, in the constant exercise of faith made effective through love, to verse 12; and third, the conclusion.

units.la: Verf. 1. Presbyter electa Domina, & liberis ejus quos ego vere diligo, nec ego solus, sed & omnes qui norunt veritatem:
units.tr: Verse 1. The elder to the chosen lady and to her children, whom I truly love, and not I alone, but also all who know the truth:

units.la: Directio Epistolæ ostendit, quis, quibus, & quo animo Epistolam hanc scripserit. Scriptor est Ioannes Apostolus, qui de autoritate sua in hac familia nihil dubitans, ordinarii & communis Ministerii titulo contentus, se Presbyterum vocat, quo nomine ætatem etiam suam jam grandævus notat, quo altius iusigeretur ipsius non diu per ætatem victuri, admonitio. Persona ad quam præcipuè scribitur, est Domina electa, ad significationem civilis & debiti honoris, Dominam vocat; ad agnitionem felicioris conditionis spiritualis in Domino, Electam vocat, siquidem quod hæc matrona ex fidei suæ sinceritate se electam declaraverit elogium præstantius est, quam quod Domina in civili conditione ab hominibus habita fuerit: Adjunguntur ejus liberi, quia gratiæ Dei in agnitione Christi cum matre participes erant.
units.tr: The address of the Epistle shows who wrote it, to whom, and with what intention. The writer is John the Apostle, who, not doubting his own authority over this household, is content with the title of the ordinary and common ministry and calls himself elder. By this name he also notes his own advanced age, so that the warning might be pressed more deeply, since he would not live long because of his years. The person chiefly addressed is the chosen lady. He calls her lady to signify the civil and due honour, and chosen to acknowledge her happier spiritual condition in the Lord. For the fact that this matron has shown herself chosen by the sincerity of her faith is a more excellent commendation than that she was regarded as lady by men in her civil station. Her children are added because they shared with their mother in the grace of God in the knowledge of Christ.

units.la: Quod ad animum scribentis erga eos ad quos scribit, attinet, profitetur, & suam dilectionem, & dilectionis suæ sinceritatem, simulque testatur de dilectione omnium aliorum fidelium, qui Evangelii veritatem amplexi erant, & de hac familia audiverant.
units.tr: As to the writer's feeling towards those he addresses, he professes both his love and the sincerity of that love, and at the same time bears witness to the love of all the other faithful who had embraced the truth of the Gospel and had heard of this household.

units.la: Verf. 2. Propter veritatem quæ permanet in nobis, & nobiscum erit in aeternum.
units.tr: Verse 2. On account of the truth which abides in us and will be with us for ever.

units.la: Utque de sinceritate suæ dilectionis constaret, causam ejus asserit communem fidem veritatis Evangelii, in qua fide perseveraturam confidit Dominam hanc, & liberos ipsius una cum seipso, reliquisque fidelibus, virtute fructuque veritatis Evangelii in æternum potituros. Tota ergo Præfatio ad confirmationem fidei hujus piæ familiæ comparata est: 1. Quod electa Mater: 2. Quod liberi fideles: 3. Quod dilecti ab Apostolo: 4. Quod dilecti ab omnibus fidelibus: 5. Quod propter veritatem potius quam nobilitatem generis, dilecti: 6. Quod veritas Evangelii in illis, & quoad fidem esset permansura, & quoad fructum in æternum duratura.
units.tr: So that the sincerity of his love might be established, he asserts its cause: the common faith in the truth of the Gospel. He trusts that this lady and her children, together with himself and the rest of the faithful, will enjoy for ever the power and fruit of the truth of the Gospel, in which faith they will persevere. The whole preface is therefore designed to confirm the faith of this pious household: (1) because the mother is chosen; (2) because the children are faithful; (3) because they are loved by the Apostle; (4) because they are loved by all the faithful; (5) because they are loved on account of the truth rather than the nobility of their birth; (6) because the truth of the Gospel would remain in them as to faith, and would last for ever as to its fruit.

units.la: Verf. 3. Sit vobiscum gratia, misericordia, pax à Deo Patre, & à Domino Iesu Christo Filio Patris, cum veritate & charitate.
units.tr: Verse 3. Grace, mercy and peace be with you from God the Father, and from the Lord Jesus Christ, the Son of the Father, in truth and love.

units.la: In salutatione seu benedictione Apostolica (in qua non nudum votum, sed etiam applicatio quædam optati boni continetur) confirmat eos, primo De Dei erga ipsos gratia, seu benevolentia gratuita, qua nos gratis sibi efficit gratos, omniaque largitur nobis, quæ Dei imaginem in nobis reparent: Deinde de Dei misericordia quæ si distinguatur à gratia, miseriæ & peccatorum ablutionem significat.
