Tertiò, de Dei pace, quæ reconciliationem, conscientiæ tranquillitatem, omnesque gradus felicitatis inchoatæ, & perficiendæ comprehendit: Et quia fructu expectatur benedictio nisi à vero Fonte, ducit eos ad Deum Patrem ( à quo tota Divina Essentia communicatur Filio & Spiritui Sancto) & ad Mediatorem Christum ( secundam Deitatis Personam incarnatam, & officio nobis salutari, vestitam ) quem vocat Filium Patris in veritate & in charitate: Primò, quia plenus est veritate & gratia unà cum Patre ejusdem Naturæ seu Essentiæ, quippe Filius verissimus & dilectissimus, Joh. I. 14. Deinde, quia non alius est animus Patris, non alia erga nos voluntas, quam est illius, idem utriusque de nobis firmum consilium, eadem erga nos dilectio. Tertio, quia ille veritatem consilii, ac propositi Patris nobis revelat, & dilectionem quâ nos diligit Pater, ille in apertum profert, & ad nos derivat, seu communicat nobis, omnique modo se Patris esse Filium ostendit, in doctrinæ veritate & efficaci amore erga nos, expressam ejus exhibens imaginem.
units.tr: In the apostolic salutation or blessing (which contains not a bare wish but also a certain application of the good desired), he strengthens them. First, by God's grace towards them, that is, his free goodwill, by which he makes us freely acceptable to himself and bestows on us everything that restores the image of God in us. Next, by God's mercy, which, if it is distinguished from grace, signifies the cleansing of misery and sins. Thirdly, by God's peace, which embraces reconciliation, tranquillity of conscience, and all the degrees of happiness begun and yet to be perfected. And since a blessing is to be expected in fruit only from the true Fountain, he leads them to God the Father (from whom the whole divine essence is communicated to the Son and the Holy Spirit) and to the Mediator Christ (the second Person of the Godhead, incarnate and clothed with the office of saving us), whom he calls the Son of the Father in truth and in love. First, because he is full of truth and grace together with the Father, being of the same nature or essence, as the most true and most beloved Son, John 1.14. Next, because the mind of the Father, and his will towards us, is no other than his; the same firm purpose of both concerning us, the same love towards us. Thirdly, because he reveals to us the truth of the Father's counsel and purpose, and brings forth into the open the love with which the Father loves us, and conveys it to us, or communicates it to us; and in every way he shows himself to be the Son of the Father, both in the truth of his doctrine and in his effective love towards us, exhibiting the express image of him.

units.la: Vers. 4. Gavisus sum valde quòd invenerim ex filiis tuis qui integrè incedant, sicut mandatum accepimus à Patre.
units.tr: Verse 4. I rejoiced greatly that I have found some of your children walking in truth, as we received commandment from the Father.

units.la: Sequitur corpus Epistolæ, in qua hortatur Matronam hanc cum liberis suis, ut perseverent in obedientia Euangelii, id est, in fide per charitatem in Deum & fratres, efficaci. Argumenta hortationis sunt novem: Primum præmittitur hoc versu, in quo gaudium suum professus, quod hactenus hæc familia in obedientia Euangelii perstitisset, confirmat eam quod ad præteritum attinet, ita ut simul excitet ad perseverandum in futuro. Vestra constantia in obedientia Euangelii mihi & fidelibus omnibus qui de vobis audiunt, gaudii spiritualis, & per consequens gratias Deo agendi amplam materiam est suppeditatura. Ergo in fide perseverate.
units.tr: There follows the body of the Epistle, in which he exhorts this matron, with her children, to persevere in obedience to the Gospel, that is, in an effective faith expressed through love towards God and the brethren. There are nine arguments for the exhortation. The first is set forth in this verse, in which he professes his joy that this household has hitherto persisted in obedience to the Gospel. He confirms them as to the past, so that at the same time he may stir them to persevere in the future. Your constancy in obedience to the Gospel will furnish me and all the faithful who hear of you with ample matter for spiritual joy, and consequently for giving thanks to God. Therefore persevere in faith.

units.la: Vers. 5. Et nunc rogo te, Domina, non ut mandatum novum scribens tibi, sed quod habuimus à principio, ut diligamus alii alios
units.tr: Verse 5. And now I ask you, lady, not as writing a new commandment to you, but that which we had from the beginning, that we love one another.

units.la: Hinc infert hortationem ad matrem familias præcipuè, sub cujus regimine liberi continebantur, unà cum secundo argumento. Mandatum ad efficaciam fidei demonstrandam in dilectione fratrum, nihil novi in se continet, præter id quod ab initio vocationis vestræ ex Dei dono didicitis, cuique assuevistis; nempè, ut ex fide & dilectione Iesu Christi, Christianam fraternitatem etiam diligatis: Pergite igitur in obedientia fidei per dilectionem efficacis.
units.tr: From this he draws the exhortation, addressed chiefly to the mother of the household, under whose government the children were, together with the second argument. The commandment that faith should be shown effective in love of the brethren contains nothing new in itself, except what you have learned from the beginning of your calling by the gift of God, and to which you have been accustomed: namely, that out of faith and love towards Jesus Christ you should also love Christian brotherhood. Press on, therefore, in obedience to faith, which works through love.

units.la: Verf. 6. Hæc autem est charitas, ut incedamus secundum doctrinam ejus. Hæc est doctrina, ut sicut audistis à principio, ita in eo ambuletis.
units.tr: Verse 6. And this is love, that we walk according to his commandments. This is the commandment, that as you have heard from the beginning, so you should walk in it.

units.la: Arg. 3. Nulla alia est vera dilectio vel proximi, vel Dei præter eam, quæ in constanti studio observandi omnia mandata Dei consistit & ambulandi seu proficiendi in illa obedientia. Ergo. Vel sic. Mandatum seu summa doctrinæ nobis in Euangelio traditæ est, ut custodiamus fidem & bonam conscientiam, ut credamus in Iesum Christum & diligamus proximum. Ergo in fidei seu mandati hujus obedientia perseverate.
units.tr: Argument 3. There is no other true love, either of neighbour or of God, than that which consists in the constant endeavour to observe all the commandments of God, and in walking, that is, advancing, in that obedience. Therefore. Or thus: the commandment, or the sum of the doctrine delivered to us in the Gospel, is that we keep the faith and a good conscience, that we believe in Jesus Christ and love our neighbour. Therefore persevere in obedience to this faith and commandment.

units.la: Verf. 7. Nam multi impostores ingressi sunt in mundum qui non confitentur Iesum Christum venisse in carne. Qui est ejusmodi impostor, est & antichristus.
units.tr: Verse 7. For many deceivers have entered into the world, who do not confess that Jesus Christ has come in the flesh. Whoever is such a deceiver is also the antichrist.

units.la: Arg. 4. Periculum non leve est, ne decipiamini propter seductorum multitudinem, qui per mundum grassantur & se impudenter ostentant. Diligentius igitur studendum ut perseveretis. Seductores autem vocat, non solum eos, qui Christi personam, officia & virtutem aperte oppugnabant; sed etiam eos qui non confitebantur Christum nec ei gloriam ascribebant totam, quam ipsi Spiritus Dei in sacra Scriptura ascribendam docet. Quicunque enim is fuerit, eatenus Antichristus est, quatenus Christum non agnoscit & confitetur, qualem se nobis exhibuit in doctrina sua sancta.
units.tr: Argument 4. There is no slight danger that you may be deceived because of the multitude of seducers who roam through the world and boldly display themselves. Therefore greater diligence must be given to persevering. He calls them seducers not only those who openly attacked the person, offices and power of Christ, but also those who did not confess Christ nor ascribed to him the whole glory which the Spirit of God teaches should be ascribed to him in holy Scripture. For whoever he may be, he is so far antichrist as he does not acknowledge and confess Christ as he has shown himself to us in his holy doctrine.

units.la: Verf. 8 Attendite vobismetipsis ne perdamus quæ operati sumus, sed ut mercedem plenam recipiamus.
units.tr: Verse 8. Look to yourselves, that we lose not what we have wrought, but that we receive a full reward.

units.la: Arg. 5. Nisi perseveretis constanter in fide vera Euangelii ejusque obedientia, amissuri eritis omnem fructum fidei, quam hactenus professi estis, & afflictionum etiam quas perpessi estis, & operum quæ prius præstitistis; siquidem per defectionem prodetis fidem vestram nunquam fuisse sincerum sed sine veritate, inanem professionem. Ergo studendum ut promissam mercedem omnibus qui fideliter Deo adhærent, plenam & copiosam per perseverantiam consequamini.
units.tr: Argument 5. Unless you persevere constantly in the true faith of the Gospel and in its obedience, you will lose all the fruit of the faith you have professed until now, and also of the afflictions you have suffered and the works you have performed before; for by defection you would betray that your faith was never sincere but an empty profession without truth. Therefore care must be taken that you obtain the promised reward, full and abundant, through perseverance, by all who cleave faithfully to God.

units.la: Verf. 9 Quisquis transgreditur, nec manet in doctrina Christi, Deum non habet: qui manet in doctrina Christi, hic & Patrem & Filium habet.
units.tr: Verse 9 Whoever goes beyond and does not abide in the teaching of Christ does not have God; he who abides in the teaching of Christ has both the Father and the Son.

units.la: Arg. 6. Quicunque transgreditur doctrinam CHRISTI & non permanet in ea constanter, id est, qui diversam doctrinam vel docet vel recipit, vel in doctrinæ CHRISTI obedientia non permanet, communionem nullam habet cum DEO, sed DEI expers est in mundo.
units.tr: Argument 6. Whoever goes beyond the teaching of Christ and does not remain constant in it, that is, whoever either teaches or receives a different doctrine, or does not remain in obedience to the teaching of Christ, has no fellowship with God, but is destitute of God in the world.

units.la: Arg. 7. Qui constanter permanet in fide & obedientia doctrinæ CHRISTI, cum DEO & CHRISTO communionem habet & habiturus est, & pro mercede habet Patrem & filium per Spiritum ipsorum in seipso habitantes.
units.tr: Argument 7. He who constantly remains in the faith and obedience of the teaching of Christ has and will have fellowship with God and Christ, and as his reward he has the Father and the Son dwelling in himself through their Spirit.

units.la: Vers. 10 Si quis venit ad vos, & hanc doctrinam non adfert, ne recipite eum domum, nec ave ei dicite.
units.tr: Verse 10 If anyone comes to you and does not bring this teaching, do not receive him into your house, nor say "Greetings" to him.

units.la: Arg. 8. per modum præcepti propositum, Usque adeo perseverantiæ in fide studendum est, ut quicunque detectus fuerit seductor hominum à doctrina CHRISTI, vel qui aliam doctrinam docet, quam CHRISTUS docuit, non debeat hospitio accipi, imo ne vel familiariter salutari, ita scilicet, ut ratio nulla habeatur, aut haberi videatur erroris ejus aut ipsius propter errorem, sed potius omni ratione ita tractari, ut intelligi possit (& ab ipso Pseudopropheta, & ab omnibus) odio haberi errorem, quem docet.
units.tr: Argument 8. Set down in the manner of a precept: so much care must be taken in perseverance in the faith that whoever is discovered to be a seducer of men from the teaching of Christ, or who teaches another doctrine than Christ taught, ought not to be received into hospitality, nor even be greeted in a friendly way; so that no account is taken, or is seen to be taken, of his error or of himself on account of his error, but rather he is to be treated in every way so that it may be understood (both by the false prophet himself and by all) that the error he teaches is held in hatred.

units.la: Vers. 11. Qui enim dicit illi, Ave, communicat operibus ejus malis.
units.tr: Verse 11. For whoever says to him, "Greetings," shares in his evil works.

units.la: Ratio hujus præcepti seu argumenti redditur, quia, qui in gratiam seductoris facit vel minimum, ex quo colligi potest errorem ipsius in aliquo pretio haberi apud salutantem, vel hospitio excipientem, communicat ipsius malis operibus.
units.tr: The reason for this precept or argument is given: because whoever does even the least thing out of goodwill toward a seducer, from which it can be inferred that his error is held in some esteem by the one greeting or receiving him in hospitality, shares in his evil works.

units.la: Vers. 12. Quum multa haberem vobis scribenda, nolui charta & atramento: sed spero me venturum ad vos, & præsentem præsentibus loquuturum, ut gaudium nostrum sit completum.
units.tr: Verse 12. Although I had many things to write to you, I did not wish to do so with paper and ink; but I hope to come to you and speak face to face, so that our joy may be complete.

units.la: Restat conclusio, In qua duo sunt articuli: In primo excusat brevitatem, spe facta adventus sui ad hanc familiam, & coram plenius ipsam instituendi & confirmandi in doctrina fidei, ut ex doctrina uberiori plenius gaudium spirituale perciperent omnes in ea fideles.
units.tr: There remains the conclusion, in which there are two parts: in the first he excuses his brevity, with the hope of his coming to this family and of instructing and strengthening them more fully in person in the doctrine of the faith, so that from the fuller teaching all the faithful in it might receive a fuller spiritual joy.

units.la: Vers. 13. Salutant te filii sororis tuæ electæ AMEN.
units.tr: Verse 13. The children of your elect sister greet you. AMEN.

units.la: In secundo articulo dicit salutem huic Matronæ à filiis sororis, quæ etiam fidelis erat, & signa dabat suæ electionis: Epistolæ totius doctrinam obsignans, AMEN.
units.tr: In the second part he says that the children of the sister greet this matron, who was also faithful and gave signs of her election, sealing the doctrine of the whole epistle: AMEN.

units.la: EXPOSITIO
units.tr: EXPOSITION

units.la: EXPOSITIO ANALYTICA EPISTOLÆ IOANNIS TERTIÆ.
units.tr: Analytical Exposition of the Third Epistle of John.

units.la: GAtum ad quem scribit Apostolus, Judæum natione, religione Christianum, lautioris fortunæ homo & abundè in Sanctos liberalis, In gratia apud Ecclesiam in qua vivebat, & in honore apud Pastorem suum ambitiosum Diotrephen, sicut ex ipsa Epistola hæc colligitur. Hinc hortatur Apostolus, ut Ministros aliquos Evangelii, qui hæc quasi litteras commendatitias ad eum perferebant, liberali exciperet hospitio, & discedentes viatico honoraret. Partes Epistolæ sunt tres: In prima est præfatio, ad vers. 3. In secunda est excitatio Gaii, ad perseverandum in exercitio charitatis & liberalitatis in Sanctos, ad vers. 13. In Tertia est conclusio.
units.tr: Gaius, to whom the Apostle writes, was a Jew by nation and a Christian by religion. He was a man of comfortable means, generous abundantly toward the saints, held in favour by the Church in which he lived, and held in honour by his minister, the ambitious Diotrephes, as this letter itself makes clear. Hence the Apostle urges him to receive generously into his hospitality certain ministers of the Gospel, who carried this letter to him like a letter of commendation, and to honour them with provision for their journey when they departed. The Epistle has three parts. The first is the preface, to verse 3. The second is the exhortation to Gaius to persevere in the exercise of love and liberality toward the saints, to verse 13. The third is the conclusion.

units.la: Vers. 1. Senior Gaio dilecto, quem ego verè diligo.
units.tr: Verse 1. The elder to the beloved Gaius, whom I truly love.

units.la: Vers. 2. Dilecte, in primis opto ut prospere agas & valeas, sicut prospere agit anima tua.
units.tr: Verse 2. Beloved, above all I pray that you may prosper and be in health, even as your soul prospers.

units.la: In directione Epistolæ à se ad Gaium, studium suum erga ipsum declarat, repetita compellatione amicâ: 2. Speciali professione sinceri sui erga ipsum amoris: 3. Precando pro eo, ut prosperum rerum statum Deus ipsi continuaret, potissimùm, ut sanitatem animæ, quam hactenus in fidei & charitatis exercitio ostenderat, ipsi conservaret.
units.tr: In the opening of the letter, he declares his affection toward Gaius by addressing him again in friendly terms; (2) by a special avowal of his sincere love for him; (3) by praying that God would continue to grant him a prosperous state of affairs, and above all that God would preserve in him the health of soul which he had hitherto shown in the exercise of faith and love.

units.la: Vers. 3. Gavisus sum enim valdè quàm venissent fratres, & testimonio suo commendassent integritatem tuam, prout tu integrè incedis.
units.tr: Verse 3. For I rejoiced greatly when the brethren came and bore witness to your integrity, even as you walk in truth.

units.la: Secunda pars Epistolæ in qua hortatur ut perseveret in demonstratione charitatis suæ erga Sanctos, & nominatim erga aliquot Dei servos, qui Epistolam hanc perferebant ad ipsum. Argumenta sunt undecim: Quæ probant pergendum esse Gaio, in charitatis officiis.
units.tr: The second part of the Epistle, in which he urges Gaius to persevere in showing his love toward the saints, and especially toward certain servants of God who carried this letter to him. There are eleven arguments, which prove that Gaius must go on in works of love.

units.la: Argumentum primum, Ex anteacta sinceræ suæ fidei per charitatem efficacis demonstratione. Sinceritatis tuæ testimonium à fratribus venientibus à bus à te, beneficentiam tuam expertis, & laudem amplissimam consecutus es, & mihi gaudendi pro te, gratias agendi Deo, & gratulandi tibi materiam exhibuisti. Ergo tibi quod superest pergendum est in ossiciis charitatis.
units.tr: The first argument is drawn from his past demonstration of a sincere faith made effective through love. You have obtained a testimony to your sincerity from the brethren who came from you and had experienced your kindness, and they have given you the highest praise. You have also given me cause to rejoice over you, to give thanks to God, and to congratulate you. Therefore, what remains is that you should go on in the duties of love.

units.la: Verf. 4. Majus isti gaudium non habeo, quum videlicet audio filios meos integre incedere.
units.tr: Verse 4. I have no greater joy than this, namely to hear that my children walk in truth.

units.la: Arg. 2. confirmans & explicans superius, Nullum majus gaudium mihi accidere potest, quam si mei discipuli, quos per Euangelium Deo genui, indies proficiant in verae fidei & charitatis exercitiis, Pergendum ergo tibi in illis est.
units.tr: Argument 2, confirming and explaining what was said above: no greater joy can come to me than to see my disciples, whom I have begotten to God through the Gospel, make daily progress in the exercise of true faith and love. You must therefore go on in these things.

units.la: Verf. 5. Dilecte, fideliter agis quicquid facis erga fratres, & erga peregrinos,
units.tr: Verse 5. Beloved, you act faithfully in whatever you do for the brethren and for strangers,

units.la: Arg. 3. Quae exerces opera misericordiae & charitatis erga Sanctos Dei servos & peregrinos, hominem te vere fidelem demonstrant. Ergo in iis perge.
units.tr: Argument 3. The works of mercy and love which you perform toward the saints, the servants of God, and toward strangers, show you to be truly a faithful man. Therefore persevere in them.

units.la: Verf. 6. Qui testimonio suo commendarunt charitatem tuam in conspectu Ecclesiae: quos recte facies si prosequutus fueris ut Deo dignum est.
units.tr: Verse 6. who have borne witness to your love before the Church; whom you will do well to send forward on their way, as is worthy of God.

units.la: Arg. 4. Hi fratres, qui has literas ad te perferunt, testimonium publicum perhibuerunt charitatis tuae in conventu Ecclesiae publico. Ergo perge de iis & aliis bene mereri.
units.tr: Argument 4. These brethren, who bring you this letter, have given public testimony to your love in the public assembly of the Church. Therefore go on to deserve well of them and of others.

units.la: Recte facies] Arg. 5. Si jam venientes ad te exceperis sicut prius excepisti, & discedentes, viatico instruxeris, & comitatus fueris, eos aliquousque in via proficiscentes alio, sicut decet & dignum est deducere ministros Dei, rem praeclaram facturus es, & opus dignum pietate tua erga Deum: Vide ut facias ergo.
units.tr: You will do well] Argument 5. If you receive them when they come to you as you received them before, and when they depart you furnish them with provision for the journey and accompany them for some distance on their way, as it becomes and is fitting to send forward the ministers of God, you will be doing a noble thing and a work worthy of your godliness toward God. See that you do so.

units.la: Verf. 7. Nam pro nomine ejus profecti sunt, nihil accipientes à Gentibus.
units.tr: Verse 7. For they went forth for the sake of his name, taking nothing from the Gentiles.

units.la: Arg. 6. Ad praedicandum nomen Dei, seu Euangelium Christi, qui Deus est, ipsonte profecti sunt, nihil à Gentibus, neque à conversis, neque à non conversis accipientes, ne occasionem darent cuiquam dicendi, quod emolumenti causa praedicarent Euangelium Gentibus. Ergo tu liberalius cum iis agito.
units.tr: Argument 6. They set out to proclaim the name of God, that is, the Gospel of Christ, who is God, taking nothing from the Gentiles, neither from the converted nor from the unconverted, so that they would give no one occasion to say that they preached the Gospel for the sake of gain. Therefore you should treat them more generously.

units.la: Verf. 8. Nos ergo debemus recipere hujusmodi, ut administri simus veritati.
units.tr: Verse 8. We therefore ought to receive such men, that we may be fellow-workers with the truth.

units.la: Arg. 7. Tenentur omnes qui favent Euangelii prædicationi pro facultatibus suis istiusmodi hominum conatus promovere, ut partem habeant in opere Euangelii, prædicatores ipsius sultentando, vel quovis modo adjuvando. Ergo tu hic ne desis.
units.tr: Argument 7. All who favour the preaching of the Gospel are bound, according to their means, to promote the efforts of such men, so that they may share in the work of the Gospel, by supporting its preachers or helping them in any way. Therefore do not be lacking here.

units.la: Vers. 9. Scripsi Ecclesiæ; sed qui primatum inter eos ambit Diotrephes, non recipit nos.
units.tr: Verse 9. I wrote to the Church; but Diotrephes, who loves to have the first place among them, does not receive us.

units.la: Arg. 8. In eum finem scripsi ad Ecclesiam in quâ tu versaris, ut ex publicis sumptibus viaticum illis daretur, sed metuo de successu, propterea quod ambitiosus Diotrephes, qui præ reliquis consortibus eminere studet parvi faciat, & me, & meas literas commendatitias.
units.tr: Argument 8. To this end I wrote to the Church in which you live, so that provision for the journey might be given to them from public funds. But I fear for the outcome, because the ambitious Diotrephes, who strives to stand out above his fellows, makes little of me and of my letter of commendation.

units.la: Vers. 10. Propterea si venero, suggeram ipsius facinora quæ facit, verbis improbis garriens in nos; quique etiam his non contentus, neque ipse recipit fratres, & qui volunt recipere prohibet, & ex Ecclesia ejicit.
units.tr: Verse 10. Therefore, if I come, I will bring to mind the deeds which he does, prating against us with wicked words; and not content with these, he himself does not receive the brethren, and forbids those who wish to receive them, and casts them out of the Church.

units.la: In ambitiosum hunc primatus amatorem præmonet Apostolus se animadversurum coram Ecclesia cum venerit, & rationes propositi sui reddit quinque. Ratio prima, Quia Diotrephes mala opera faciebat:
units.tr: The Apostle warns this lover of primacy, the ambitious man, that he will call him to account before the Church when he comes, and he gives five reasons for his purpose. The first reason: because Diotrephes was doing evil works.

units.la: 2. Quia verbis malignis deblaterabat in Apostolos, & nominatim in Ioannem, quem ambitioni & humano episcopatui (per istiusmodi hominum ambitionem & artes) irrepenti in Ecclesiam, inimicum noverat:
units.tr: 2. Because he spoke against the Apostles with malicious words, and by name against John, whom he knew to be an enemy of his ambition and of the human episcopate that was creeping into the Church (through the ambition and arts of such men).

units.la: 3. Quia neque hospitio excipiebat, neque ullo alio genere beneficentiæ afficiebat veros Christianos, Apostolicæ doctrinæ in omnibus tenaces: 4. Quia eos, qui excipiebant hospitio, & officiis Christianis prosequebantur illos prædicatores, qui ab Apostolis mittebantur: Editis & constitutionibus suis tyrannicis prohibebat, cum interminatione excommunicationis, seu ejectionis ex Ecclesia, si contra facerent: 5. Quia transgredientes ipsius mandata, & fratres hujusmodi excipientes hospitio excommunicabat pro imperio.
units.tr: 3. Because he neither received into his hospitality nor showed any other kind of kindness to true Christians, who held firmly to the apostolic doctrine in all things. 4. Because by his tyrannical edicts and decrees he forbade those who received into their hospitality and showed Christian kindness to those preachers who were sent out by the Apostles, under threat of excommunication, that is, expulsion from the Church, if they acted contrary to this. 5. Because he excommunicated, at his own pleasure, those who transgressed his commands and received such brethren into their hospitality.

units.la: Vers. 11. Dilecte, ne imitare quod malum est, sed quod bonum est, qui bene facit, ex DEO est; qui autem male facit, non vidit DEVM.
units.tr: Verse 11. Beloved, do not imitate what is evil, but what is good. He who does good is of God; but he who does evil has not seen God.

units.la: Arg. 9. Non debes imitari malos mores tui Pastoris Diotrephis, vel obtemperare ejus edictis nefariis, quia hoc malum esset, & veræ in Deum fidei & charitati repugnans; sed debes imitari id solum quod bonum est, & doctrinæ sanæ conveniens. Perge ergo in charitatis officiis exercendis. Qui bene] Arg. 10. confirmans superius, Qui studet benefacere ex DEO genitus est; qui vero studet malefacere, expers est veræ & salvificæ cognitionis DEI, seu fidei in eum. Perge ergo tu bene agere, ut te genitum ex DEO probes.
units.tr: Argument 9. You ought not to imitate the evil ways of your minister Diotrephes, nor obey his wicked edicts, because this would be evil and opposed to true faith and love toward God. You ought to imitate only what is good and agrees with sound doctrine. Therefore go on in performing the duties of love. Whoever does good] Argument 10, confirming what was said above: whoever strives to do good is born of God; but whoever strives to do evil lacks the true and saving knowledge of God, or faith in him. Therefore go on doing good, so that you may prove yourself born of God.

units.la: Verf. 12. Demetrio testimonium redditum est ab omnibus, & ab ipsa veritate: sed & nos testimonium perhibemus, & nostrum testimonium nostrum verum esse.
units.tr: Verse 12. Demetrius has the testimony of all, and of the truth itself; and we also bear witness, and you know that our testimony is true.

units.la: Arg. 11. Debes potius Demetrii beneficentiam in sanctos & peregrinos pauperes imitari, de quo omnes, & ipsa rei veritas factis se ostendens testatur, & ipse ego, qui non nisi vera & comperta affirmare soleo, testimonium dico in ejus laudem. Imitare eum ergo, & perge in charitatis officiis.
units.tr: Argument 11. You ought rather to imitate the kindness of Demetrius toward the saints and poor strangers, of whom all bear witness, and the truth of the matter itself, showing itself by his deeds; and I myself, who am accustomed to affirm only what is true and well established, bear witness in his praise. Therefore imitate him, and go on in the duties of love.

units.la: Verf 13. Multa possem scribere, sed nolo atramento & calamo tibi scribere:
units.tr: Verse 13. I have many things to write to you, but I am unwilling to write them to you with ink and pen;

units.la: Verf. 14. Spero autem fore ut statim te videam, & ut coram loquamur.
units.tr: Verse 14. But I hope to see you soon, and we shall speak face to face.

units.la: Restat conclusio, in qua duo sunt articuli. In primo brevitatem excusat Epistolæ, spe facta de adventu suo, & colloquio.
units.tr: There remains the conclusion, which has two parts. In the first, he excuses the brevity of the Epistle, having held out the hope of his coming and of a conversation with him.

units.la: Verf. 15. Pax tibi: Salutant te amici. Saluta amicos nominatim.
units.tr: Verse 15. Peace be to you. The friends salute you. Greet the friends by name.

units.la: In articulo secundo, 1. Salutat Gaium, optando ei pacem, id est, in omnibus, DEI benedictionem: 2. Salutem Gaio nunciat ab amicis sanctis scilicet, qui veri erant amici. 3. Salutare suo nomine jubet, sigillatim & nominatim omnes amicos, id est, sanctos, qui ipsum diligebant.
units.tr: In the second part: (1) he greets Gaius, wishing him peace, that is, God's blessing in all things; (2) he conveys to Gaius a greeting from the friends, namely the saints, who were true friends. (3) He bids him greet all the friends, that is, the saints who loved him, one by one and by name.

units.la: EXPOSITIO
units.tr: EXPOSITION

units.la: EXPOSITIO ANALYTICA EPISTOLAE JUDÆ Apostoli.
units.tr: Analytical Exposition of the Epistle of Jude, the Apostle.

units.la: Onnulli orti erant Hæresiarchæ, qui gratia Dei abutebantur ad licentiam carnis, & sub prætextu Evangelii, vitiis omnibus laxabant fræ",nos, & sanctam veræ Fidelium conversationem, quasi fatuorum Idiotarum, qui veram libertatem Christianam ignorarent, aperte irridebant. Adversus has pestes excitavit Deus Petrum Apostolum, & hunc Judam, qui Iacobi minoris cognomento Alphæi, frater dicitur hic, & Act: 1. Cognatus Domini nostri, Math: 13. 55. qui etiam cognomento Lebbæus, & Thaddæus dicebatur, Math: 10. 3. Judas hic noster: Fideles ad quos scribit, hortatur, ut constanter tenerentur veram Evangelii doctrinam adversus falsos doctores, de quibus Petrus eos commonuerat, 2 Epist: Cap: 2. idem prorsus tractans argumentum. Epistolæ partes sunt tres: Præfatio, vers. 1 & 2. Hortatio ad certandum de vera fide retinenda adversus impostores, ad vers. 24. & conclusio, versibus duobus ultimis.
units.tr: Some heresiarchs had arisen who abused the grace of God as a licence for the flesh, and under the pretext of the Gospel loosened every restraint on vice, openly mocking the holy conduct of true believers as the foolishness of simple laymen who did not understand Christian liberty. Against these plagues God raised up the Apostle Peter and this Jude, who is here called the brother of James the Less, the son of Alphaeus (Acts 1), the kinsman of our Lord (Matt. 13:55), who was also surnamed Lebbaeus and Thaddaeus (Matt. 10:3). This Jude addresses the faithful, urging them to hold steadfastly to the true doctrine of the Gospel against false teachers, about whom Peter had warned them (2 Pet. 2), treating entirely the same subject. The epistle has three parts: the preface, verses 1 and 2; an exhortation to contend for the true faith against impostors, to verse 24; and a conclusion in the last two verses.

units.la: Vers. 1. Judas Iesu Christi servus, frater autem Iacobi, vocatus à Deo Patre sanctificatus, & Iesu Christo servatus:
units.tr: Verse 1. Jude, servant of Jesus Christ, and brother of James, called, sanctified by God the Father, and preserved in Jesus Christ:

units.la: Præfatio inscriptionem continet & salutationem. Inscriptio Epistolæ directionem ostendit, à quo, & ad quos. Describitur Scriptor Epistolæ, primò à nomine: Secundò, ab officio Apostolatus, sub nomine servi, (quo magis gloriatur, quam cognatione naturali, quæ inter ipsum & Christum Dominum intercedebat) 3. A distinctione ipsius à Juda proditore, à quo non moribus tantum, sed etiam nominis descriptione discerni cupiebat. Illi, ad quos scribit, describuntur à quatuor proprietatibus Electorum, 1. Sunt in Deo Patre, id est, per Christum reconciliati, habent cum Deo communionem, seu sanctam societatem: 2. Sanctificati sunt per Spiritus Sancti speciale operationem & inhabitationem: 3. Conservati per donum perseverantiæ à Christo Redemptore, qui nullum ex suis patitur sibi eripi: 4 Vocati scilicet non externa tantum, sed interna & efficaci vocatione.
units.tr: The preface contains the inscription and the greeting. The inscription shows who the writer is and to whom he writes. The writer is described first by his name; secondly, by his office of apostle, under the name of servant, in which he takes more pride than in the natural kinship that existed between himself and the Lord Christ; thirdly, by a distinction between himself and Judas the traitor, from whom he wished to be distinguished not only by his conduct but also by the way his name is described. Those to whom he writes are described by four properties of the elect: 1. They are in God the Father, that is, reconciled through Christ, and have communion with God, or holy fellowship. 2. They are sanctified by the special operation and indwelling of the Holy Spirit. 3. They are preserved by the gift of perseverance from Christ the Redeemer, who suffers none of his own to be snatched from him. 4. They are called, namely, not only by an outward calling but by an inward and effectual one.

units.la: Vers. 2. Misericordia vobis & Pax, & Charitas multi- plicetur.
units.tr: Verse 2. Mercy to you, and peace, and love be multiplied.

units.la: In salutatione ex autoritate Apostolica, non optat solum, sed etiam applicat in ipsorum fidei confirmationem, 1. Dei misericordiam, quæ malis omnibus, id est, peccato & miseriæ medetur: 2. Pacem, quæ reconciliationem, & felicitatis partes continet: 3. Et dilectionem, quæ ut fons bonorum omnium comprehendit gratiam & effecta omnia, quæ ad sanctificationem & salutem perficiendam attinent. Hæc omnia multiplicanda illis pronunciat respectu graduum, incrementi, & manifestationis, in aliis atque aliis effectis, prout salus ipsorum, & Dei gloria postulatura erant.
units.tr: In the greeting, by apostolic authority, he does not merely wish these things but also applies them to the confirmation of their faith: 1. the mercy of God, which heals all evils, that is, sin and misery; 2. peace, which contains reconciliation and the parts of happiness; 3. and love, which, as the fountain of all good things, embraces grace and all the effects that pertain to the perfecting of sanctification and salvation. He declares that all these are to be multiplied in them, with respect to degrees, increase and manifestation, in one effect after another, as their salvation and the glory of God required.

units.la: Vers. 3. Dilecti, quum omne studium adhibeam, ut scribam ad vos de communi salute, necesse habui vobis scribere, ad vos hortandos, ut decertetis pro fide quæ semel tradita est sanctis.
units.tr: Verse 3. Beloved, although I was giving all diligence to write to you about our common salvation, I found it necessary to write to you, exhorting you to contend earnestly for the faith which was once delivered to the saints.

units.la: Sequitur corpus Epistolæ, In quo causas scribendi & scopum Epistolæ proponit, quem deinceps prosequitur. Scribendi causas affert duas, Prima est Studium & propensio pro officio suo, non solum prædicandi Euangelium, ubicunque daretur occasio, sed etiam scribendi de communi salute Electorum per Christum impetrata, & gradatim perficienda, quæ summa est Euangelii: Causa secunda, Accedebat necessitas Ecclesiarum à seductoribus periclitantium, quæ jam scripturientem impellebat, ut scriberet. His præmissis scopum Epistolæ proponit, qui est, hortari, ut doctrinam Apostolicam sartam tectam conservarent sibi & posteris à seductorum corruptelis. Sanam doctrinam vocat fidem credendam scilicet, quia omnia continet quæ ad salutem creditu sunt necessaria. Semel traditam Sanctis dicit, quia uno ore omnes Apostoli eandem veritatem secundum Scripturas veteres, de salute per fidem veram in Christum obtinendâ, plenè & perfectè tradiderunt Ecclesiæ Sanctorum tenendam, ut immutabilem vitæ æternæ consequendæ regulam, & fine additione aut diminutione in adventum DOMINI observandam: Pro hac fide contendendum dicit, quia Caro, Diabolus, Mundus, & qui in eo sunt Diaboli ministri nunquam cessaturi sunt ab oppugnatione hujus veritatis, ita ut necesse sit omnibus verè Fidelibus cum his bellum gerere ἀγωνίζεσθαι.
units.tr: There follows the body of the epistle, in which he sets out the reasons for writing and the aim of the epistle, which he then pursues. He gives two reasons for writing. The first is his eagerness and inclination, in keeping with his office, not only to preach the Gospel wherever an opportunity was given, but also to write about the common salvation of the elect, obtained through Christ and to be perfected step by step, which is the sum of the Gospel. The second reason: the churches were in danger from seducers, and this necessity already pressed him to write. With these things premised, he sets out the aim of the epistle, which is to exhort them to keep the apostolic doctrine whole and sound for themselves and for posterity against the corruptions of seducers. He calls the sound doctrine the faith to be believed, because it contains all that is necessary to be believed for salvation. He says it was delivered once for all to the saints, because all the apostles with one voice fully and perfectly handed down to the Church of the saints, to be held, the same truth, according to the ancient Scriptures, about obtaining salvation through true faith in Christ, as an unchangeable rule for attaining eternal life, and to be observed without addition or subtraction until the coming of the Lord. He says that one must contend for this faith, because the flesh, the devil, the world, and those in it who are ministers of the devil will never cease to assail this truth, so that it is necessary for all truly faithful people to wage war against them: agonizesthai [ἀγωνίζεσθαι].

units.la: Versf. 4. Nam subrepserunt quidam homines, prius jam olim descripti ad hanc damnationem impii, qui DEI nostri gratiam transferunt ad lasciviam, & solum illum verum Deum ac Dominum nostrum Iesum Christum negant.
units.tr: Verse 4. For certain men have crept in unnoticed, who were long ago marked out for this condemnation, ungodly men, who turn the grace of our God into licentiousness and deny the only true God and our Lord Jesus Christ.

units.la: Argumenta hortationis sunt novem, quorum pleraque sumuntur à seductorum peccatis & poenis.
units.tr: The arguments of the exhortation are nine, most of which are drawn from the sins and punishments of the seducers.

units.la: Argumentum primum, Probans diligenter conservandam esse fidem Apostolicam, semel Ecclesiæ datam, à seductorum corruptelis: Quia jam periculum erat à seductoribus, qui clam irrepserant, ut adversarii hujus doctrinæ; quos ita describit, ut singulæ descriptionis partes scopo inserviant. Nam, 1. Modus insinuandi errores suos fratribus, latens erat: clam enim, obliquis viis & modis, antequam observari potuerunt, errores suos aliquorum, mentibus instillaverunt: 2. Non sine consilio Divino permisit suum ipsorum ingenium sequi ad cribrandam & ventilandam Ecclesiam; nam in sancto DEI consilio ab æterno reprobi erant & destinati, ut ad damnationem hanc per sua peccata pervenirent, non minus certò quam si in libro scriptæ essent nomina ipsorum designata. 3. Impii erant, qui nullo Numinis Divini sensu, vel reverentia tangebantur, ut eum colerent, vel in eum crederent: 4. Gratiam DEI nostri IESU CHRISTI, seu doctrinam gratiæ, quæ in Evangelio proponitur, in hunc ipsum finem, ut homines, abnegata omni impietate sanctè viverent: illi in contrarium plane finem transferebant, vertebantque in occasionem omnis lasciviæ & carnalium voluptatum: 5. Relictâ, doctrinâ & factis abnegabant solum Dominum nostrum, & Herum nostrum, & DEUM nostrum IESUM CHRISTUM, quem solum nominat. DEUM nostrum non, ut excludat Patrem & SPIRITUM Sanctum, sed ut excludat creaturas & fictitia numina. Ergo adversus hujusmodi seductores custodienda est fidei puritas.
units.tr: The first argument, proving that the apostolic faith, once given to the Church, must be carefully preserved against the corruptions of seducers, since there was already danger from seducers who had crept in secretly as opponents of this doctrine. He describes them in such a way that each part of the description serves his purpose. For: 1. The manner of insinuating their errors to the brethren was hidden; they had secretly instilled their errors into the minds of some, by oblique ways and means, before they could be observed. 2. Not without the counsel of God, he permitted them to follow their own disposition, to sift and winnow the Church; for in God's holy counsel they had been reprobated and destined from eternity to come to this condemnation through their own sins, no less certainly than if their names had been written and designated in a book. 3. They were ungodly, moved by no sense or reverence of the divine majesty, either to worship him or to believe in him. 4. They turned the grace of our God and Lord Jesus Christ, or the doctrine of grace which is set forth in the Gospel, to the very opposite end, namely, that men, having renounced all impiety, might live holily; these men turned it into an occasion for all licentiousness and carnal pleasures. 5. By their doctrine and deeds they denied only our Lord, our Master, and our God Jesus Christ, whom alone he names. He says "our God" not to exclude the Father and the Holy Spirit, but to exclude creatures and fictitious deities. Therefore the purity of the faith must be guarded against seducers of this kind.

units.la: Versf. 5. Volo autem vos istorum commonefacere, ut qui semel hoc sciatis, hoc sciatis, Dominum, quum populum ex Ægypto liberasset, rur-sus eos, qui non credebant perdidisse.
units.tr: Verse 5. I wish therefore to remind you of these things, though you know them once for all, that the Lord, having brought the people out of Egypt, afterwards destroyed those who did not believe.

units.la: Arg. 2. Deus Israelitas eductos ex Egypto postea in deserto apostatas incredulos perdidit: Ergo horum exemplo moniti cavere debetis, ne seducti cum aliis pereatis.
units.tr: Argument 2. God, having led the Israelites out of Egypt, afterwards destroyed in the wilderness those who were apostate and unbelieving. Therefore, warned by their example, you ought to take care lest, being seduced, you perish together with others.

units.la: Verf. 6. Et Angelos qui non servata sua origine reliquerunt suum domicilium, judicio magni illius diei vinculis aeternis sub caligine reservasse.
units.tr: Verse 6. And the angels who did not keep their own origin but left their own dwelling, he has reserved in everlasting chains under darkness until the judgment of the great day.

units.la: Arg. 3. Deus Angelos apostatas de coelo deturbatos, aeterno exitio, decreto irrevocabili adjudicavit: Ergo fidelibus cavendum ab apostasia, ne similiter pereant.
units.tr: Argument 3. God condemned the apostate angels, cast down from heaven, to eternal ruin by an irrevocable decree. Therefore believers must beware of apostasy, lest they likewise perish.

units.la: Verf. 7. Sicut Sodoma & Gomorrha, & his finitimæ civitates, similí modo atque illæ scortatæ, & carnem alienam sectatæ, propositæ sunt exemplo, ignis æterni pœnam sustinentes.
units.tr: Verse 7. As Sodom and Gomorrah, and the cities around them, in like manner as those, having given themselves to fornication and gone after strange flesh, are set forth as an example, suffering the punishment of eternal fire.

units.la: Arg. 4. Deus Sodoma & Gomorrha, vicinaque civitates perdidit, postquam in scortationem & foedas libidines, quibus isti impostores se polluunt effusæ sunt, & in exemplum posteris in ignem aeternum conjecit. Cavendum ergo ab impostoribus illis, qui in ejusmodi peccata & poenas vos pertrahere possent.
units.tr: Argument 4. God destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah and the neighbouring cities, after they had poured themselves out in fornication and the foul lusts by which these impostors defile themselves, and he set them forth as an example to posterity, consigning them to eternal fire. Therefore beware of those impostors, who could draw you into such sins and punishments.

units.la: Verf. 8. Similiter tamen & isti sopiti, carnem quidem polluunt, dominatum vero rejiciunt, & dignitates conviciis incessunt.
units.tr: Verse 8. Likewise these dreamers also defile the flesh, reject dominion, and revile dignities.

units.la: Arg. 5. Quia seductores illi sunt similiter vasa irae coagmentata ad interitum, quos Deus aliquando similiter perditurus est: cujus rationem, reddit a novem vel pluribus vitiis, quae in illis regnabant, Ex quibus suis fructibus tanquam notis se dignoscendos, & dijudicandos exhibebant. Vitium 1. horum libertinorum erat. Quod somniis delusi carnem contaminabant, hoc est, libidini, aliisque flagitiis secure indulgebant, Diabolicis errorum incantamentis non aliter fascinati animis, & conscientiis suis quam si somno corriperentur: Vitium 2. Omnis politiae adversarii sunt, nullum genus Magistratus vel Dominationis ferentes, sed in honorandas illas Dei ordinationes maledicta & convitia congerentes, quales Anabaptistas fanaticos etiamnum aetas nostra videt.
units.tr: Argument 5. Those seducers are likewise vessels of wrath, fitted for destruction, whom God will in like manner at some time destroy. He gives the reason for this from nine or more vices that reigned in them, by which they showed themselves to be recognised and judged by their fruits as by their marks. Vice 1 of these libertines was that deluded by dreams they defiled the flesh, that is, they indulged securely in lust and other shameful acts, bewitched in their minds and consciences by the diabolical incantations of error no differently than if they were seized by sleep. Vice 2: they are enemies of every polity, bearing no kind of magistracy or lordship, but heaping curses and reproaches upon those ordinances of God which are to be honoured, such as our age still sees among the fanatical Anabaptists.

units.la: Verf. 9. At Michael archangelus, quum adversus Diabolum certans, disceptaret de corpore Moßis, non ausus est illi impingere rotam maledicti, sed dixit, Increpet te Dominus.
units.tr: Verse 9. But Michael the archangel, when contending with the Devil and disputing about the body of Moses, did not dare to hurl at him a wheel of reproach, but said, The Lord rebuke you.

units.la: Hoc vitium ex eo amplificat, quod Archangelus Michael disputans, & decertans contra Satanam, ne corpus Moßs à Deo sepultum Israelitis revelaretur, qui superstitiose reliquias coluisse illius, cujus verba dum viveret despiciebant. Non est ausus, seu non potuit à tua sanctitate impetrare, ut talia convicia in Satanam conjiceret, qualia haeretici illi in Magistratum deblaterant: nam satis habuit Archangelus dicere, Increpet te Dominus, seu coerceat tuos conatus. Unde hanc historiam didicerit Apostolus frustra quaeritur ab iis, qui omnem Scripturam divinitus inspiratam agnoscunt.
units.tr: He amplifies this vice from the fact that the archangel Michael, disputing and contending with Satan, did so lest the body of Moses, which God had buried, should be revealed to the Israelites, who superstitiously cultivated the relics of the man whose words they despised while he lived. He did not dare (nor could he obtain from your holiness) to hurl at Satan such insults as those heretics babble against the magistrate; for the archangel was content to say, "The Lord rebuke you," that is, restrain your attempts. By whom the apostle learned this history is asked in vain by those who acknowledge all Scripture to be divinely inspired.

units.la: Verf. 10. At isti, quae non noverunt, ea convitiis incessunt: quae vero naturaliter, ut animantia rationis expertia sciunt, in iis corrumpuntur.
units.tr: Verse 10. But these men revile what they do not know; and what they know naturally, as irrational animals do, they are corrupted by in these things.

units.la: Vitium 3. est, Quod cum ignari sint divinarum ordinationum, Christianorum officiorum, & rerum omnium spiritualium, non rudes tantum, sed & incapaces, impudenter tamen audent de iis rebus pronunciare, & blasphemias suas in eas evomere: Vitium 4. Quod quae naturaliter ut animalia sensitiva norunt, in iis, se infra bestias abjiciunt, & se ad omnem libidinem & intemperantiam instigant & impellunt.
units.tr: The third vice is that, although they are ignorant of the divine ordinances, of Christian duties, and of all spiritual matters, they are not only unskilled but incapable, yet they shamelessly dare to pronounce on those things and vomit their blasphemies against them. The fourth vice is that, in the things they know naturally, as sensitive animals do, they cast themselves below the beasts and goad and drive themselves on to every lust and intemperance.

units.la: Verf. 11. Vae ipsis: nam viam Cain ingressi sunt, & deceptione mercedis, qui deceptus fuit Balaam, effusi sunt, & contradictione Core perierunt.
units.tr: Verse 11. Woe to them! For they have gone the way of Cain, and have rushed headlong for the reward of error, as Balaam did, and have perished in the rebellion of Korah.

units.la: Vitium 5. Cum denunciatione maledictionis Dei in eos, Est odium adversus sanctos fratres, quale erat odium Caini fratricidae: Vitium 6. est Avaritia, qualis erat Balaami, qui sicut linguam venalem habebat, sic illi turpis lucri gratia doctrinam Dei adulterabant: Vitium 7. est Seditio, qualis erat Corhe, qua se veris Dei Ministris opponunt, & tumultibus suis bene constitutae Ecclesiae Pacem perturbant, perituri in sua seditione, sicut periit Corhe.
units.tr: The fifth vice, with the pronouncement of God's curse upon them, is hatred against the holy brethren, such as the hatred of Cain the murderer of his brother. The sixth vice is covetousness, such as that of Balaam, who, having a tongue for sale, so adulterated the teaching of God for the sake of shameful gain. The seventh vice is sedition, such as that of Korah, by which they set themselves against the true ministers of God and by their tumults disturb the peace of a well-ordered Church, perishing in their sedition as Korah perished.

units.la: Verf. 12. Hi sunt maculorum instar in agapis vestris, dum vobiscum convivantur, absque ullo metu seipsos pascentes: nubes aqua carentes, ventis circumactae, arbores, emarcidae, infrugiferae, bis emortuae, eradicatae: Vitium 8. Ingluvies, quâ corrumpebant, & pravo suo exemplo contaminabant, & se & alios in conviviis Christianis, quæ ad fovendam quidem charitatem erant destinata, sed per Epicuros hujusmodi in præsepia porcorum conversa erant: dum abjecto Dei timore securè indulgebant voluptati ventris & gulæ; Pascentes carnem suam, non vero animas auditorum: Vitium 9. Vel vitiorum congeries potius, varus similitudinibus adumbratur, quod ad opus Ministerii, & ad omne opus bonum fuerint ineptissimi & plane reprobi; nam sicut nubes steriles & leves à ventis circumactæ, quam specie externâ pollicebantur doctrinæ salutaris pluviam nullam reddunt ullibi locorum, sed avidos discendi auditores quocunque veniunt frustrantur: & licet speciem præ se ferant arborum bonarum, talesque se jactitent, sunt tamen arbores autumnales ac frugiferdæ, quia fructum, si quem ferre videantur, maturum & utilem reddere non possunt: imo verius prorsus infructuosi sunt, quia nullum salutarem fructum ferunt, neque in se, neque in sectatoribus suis: & sicut arbores excisæ, emarcidæ & eradicatæ, nullam relinquunt spem de fructu ferendo, sic illi permanent in peccatis, mortui per naturam, & suâ nequitia attrahentes in se judicialem cordis indurationem, quasi secundo mortui sunt, & jam in reprobum sensum traditi, spem omnem præciderunt conversionis & resipiscentiæ suæ.
units.tr: Verse 12. These are spots in your love feasts, while they feast with you, feeding themselves without any fear; clouds without water, carried about by the winds; trees, withered, unfruitful, twice dead, uprooted: The eighth vice is gluttony, by which they corrupted and, by their wicked example, polluted both themselves and others at Christian banquets, which were indeed designed to foster charity, but through such Epicureans had been turned into the troughs of swine, while, having cast off the fear of God, they indulged securely in the pleasures of belly and throat, feeding their own flesh and not the souls of their hearers. The ninth vice, or rather a heap of vices, is shadowed forth by various similitudes: that they were most unfit and altogether reprobate for the work of the ministry and for every good work. For like barren clouds, light and carried about by the winds, they yield no rain anywhere, though they promise by their outward show the rain of wholesome teaching, but they disappoint the eager hearers who come to them wherever they go. And although they display the appearance of good trees and boast themselves to be such, they are autumn trees, yet fruitless, since whatever fruit they seem to bear they cannot make ripe and useful; indeed, more truly, they are altogether unfruitful, since they bear no saving fruit, neither in themselves nor in their followers. And as trees cut down, withered and uprooted, leave no hope of bearing fruit, so they remain in their sins, dead by nature, and by their own wickedness drawing upon themselves a judicial hardening of heart; they are as it were twice dead, and, now given over to a reprobate mind, they have cut off all hope of their conversion and repentance.

units.la: Vers. 13. Undæ maris efferatæ, despumantes sua ipsorum dedecora: stellæ errantes, quibus caligo tenebrarum in æternum servata est.
units.tr: Verse 13. Raging waves of the sea, foaming out their own shames; wandering stars, for whom the blackness of darkness is reserved for ever.

units.la: Denique ejusmodi sunt, qui à nequitia desistere non possunt, sed instar undarum æstuantis maris, suam semper produnt turpitudinem, nec magis quam stellæ erraticæ in motu, sibi constant illi in doctrina sua. Quibus propterea, pro condigno supplicio, denunciat denuò tenebras infernales densissimas & profundissimas in æternum.
units.tr: Finally, such are those who cannot desist from wickedness, but like the waves of a seething sea always display their own filthiness, and no more than wandering stars in their motion do they keep to a fixed course in their teaching. For these, therefore, as a due punishment, He again threatens the most dense and profound infernal darkness for ever.

units.la: Vers. 14. Prophetavit autem etiam de istis septimus ab Adam Enoch, dicens, Ecce, venit Dominus cum sanctis millibus suis,
units.tr: Verse 14. And Enoch, the seventh from Adam, also prophesied of these men, saying, Behold, the Lord comes with his holy myriads,

units.la: Vers. 15. Ut ferat judicium adversus omnes, & redarguat quicunque ex ipsis sunt impii, de factis omnibus quæ impie patrarint, deque omnibus duris quæ loquuti fuerint adversus ipsum peccatores impii.
units.tr: Verse 15. To execute judgment upon all, and to convict all the ungodly among them, of all the ungodly deeds which they have done in an ungodly way, and of all the hard things which ungodly sinners have spoken against him.

units.la: Arg. 6. probans cavendum esse à seductoribus, &c. Quia Enoch septimus ab Adam inclusivè, spiritu Prophetico prædixit de iniquorum nebulonum peccatis, & condemnatione in die judicii; quando CHRISTUS Angelorum & Sanctorum myriadas secum adducens exequetur judicium adversus omnes impios, & supplicium sumet præcipuè de iis, qui linguis suis petulanter usi fuerant adversus DEUM, & ipsius doctrinam sanctissimam. De Prophetia Enoch, an scripta fuerit prius, an non, vel quomodo constiterit Apostolo de rei veritate, idem dicimus quod prius, SPIRITUM DEI, qui in Enocho loquebatur, etiam Apostolo per inspirationem dictasse, id quod ipse per Enochum olim prædixerat, & quid quantumque scripto committeret, Apostolo præscripsisse.
units.tr: Argument 6, proving that one must beware of seducers, etc. Because Enoch, the seventh from Adam inclusive, by the prophetic Spirit foretold the sins of the wicked scoundrels and their condemnation on the day of judgment, when Christ, bringing with him the myriads of angels and saints, will execute judgment upon all the ungodly and will exact punishment chiefly from those who had used their tongues wantonly against God and his most holy doctrine. Concerning the prophecy of Enoch, whether it was written earlier or not, or how it was established for the apostle as a matter of truth, we say the same as before: the Spirit of God, who spoke in Enoch, also dictated to the apostle by inspiration what he himself had formerly foretold through Enoch, and prescribed to the apostle what and how much he should commit to writing.

units.la: Vers. 16 Hi sunt murmuratores, queruli, in cupiditatibus suis incedentes - & quorum os loquitur pr̄tumida, admirantes personas utilitatis gratia.
units.tr: Verse 16. These are murmurers, complainers, walking according to their own lusts; and their mouth speaks proud words, admiring persons for the sake of advantage.

units.la: Ut sequatur Conclusio de perditione seductorum hujusmodi secundum Enochi prophetiam, & per consequens vitandos esse, quasi assumendo, ostendit tales fuisse seductores hos, quales descripserat Enoch, perdendos, ex indiciis quatuor. Indicium primum, Erant murmuratores, & queruli, qui forte suâ nunquam contenti erant, neque de justis DEI ordinationibus in Ecclesia, vel Republica satis unquam habentes, carpebant, vellicabant & vituperabant omnia, omnis fræni impatientes. Secundò, Sibiipsis pro regula statuebant, nec Leges Divinas in Divinis, seu Ecclesiasticis, nec Leges Humanas in Humanis, seu Politicis, sed desideria sua tantùm, & voluptates suas. Tertiò, Etiamsi vilissima essent libidinum suarum mancipia, ut haberentur tamen in aliquo pretio, inflato stylo, & ad populi admirationem comparato, verba tumentia, & magnifica loquebantur, ubi nemo erat qui eorum intolentiam reprimeret. Quartò, Contrà verò si qui essent, quos timerent, vel à quibus aliquid commodi sperarent, illis sordidè adblandiebantur, illos in pretio habebant, admirabantur, prædicabant, digni ne, an indigni essent non respicientes.
units.tr: So that the conclusion may follow concerning the destruction of such seducers according to the prophecy of Enoch, and consequently that they are to be avoided, he shows, as if assuming it, that these seducers were such as Enoch had described, doomed to destruction, by four signs. The first sign: they were murmurers and complainers, who perhaps were never content with their own lot, and who, never satisfied with the just ordinances of God in the Church or the commonwealth, carped at, nibbled at and disparaged everything, impatient of every restraint. (2) Second, they set up for themselves as a rule not the divine laws in divine or ecclesiastical matters, nor the human laws in human or political matters, but only their own desires and pleasures. (3) Third, although they were the most worthless slaves of their lusts, yet, that they might be held in some esteem, they spoke swelling words in an inflated style, designed to win the admiration of the people, where there was no one to restrain their insolence. (4) On the contrary, if there were any whom they feared, or from whom they hoped for some advantage, they fawned upon them basely, held them in high esteem, admired and praised them, without considering whether they were worthy or unworthy.

units.la: Vers. 17. Vos autem dilecti memores estote verborum quæ prædicta fuerint ab Apostolis Domini nostri Iesu Christi;
units.tr: Verse 17. But you, beloved, remember the words which were spoken before by the apostles of our Lord Jesus Christ;

units.la: Verf. 18. Quòd videlicet dixerunt vobis, In extremo tempore futuri irrisores, qui in impiis suis cupiditatibus incedant.
units.tr: Verse 18. How they told you that in the last time there would be scoffers, who walk after their own ungodly lusts.

units.la: Arg. 7. Probans cavendum à seductoribus, quia Apostoli reliqui prædixerant tales virtuos filios Belial in Ecclesia, quales prædixerat etiam Enoch.
units.tr: Argument 7, proving that one must beware of seducers, because the other apostles had foretold that such sons of Belial would appear in the Church, just as Enoch had foretold.

units.la: Verf. 19. Hi sunt qui seipsos segregant, animales, Spiritum non habentes.
units.tr: Verse 19. These are they who separate themselves, sensual, not having the Spirit.

units.la: Ut sequatur Conclusio de vitandis supra descriptis seductoribus, rursum assumit, & ostendit tales fuisse seductores quibuscum ipsis erat negotium, idque ex duabus notis. Nota prima, Quod à vera Dei Ecclesia, & sana Apostolorum doctrina, nulla necessitate vel auctoritate Dei, sed sua tantum voluntate separabant seipsos, ne sub jugo Domini, seu Disciplinæ ejus manerent. Nota 2. animales erant Spiritum non habentes, quia regenerationis expertes ea tantum sapiebant & sectabantur, ad quæ ducit natura, seu ratio humana divinitus non illuminata, destituti, quippe Dei Spiritu, seu gratia Dei sanctificante; Reliquum erat ut sensus & caro plena libertate dominaretur, eosque impelleret ad omnes & corporis & animæ pollutiones.
units.tr: So that the conclusion may follow concerning the seducers described above, to be avoided, he again assumes and shows that these were the seducers with whom they had to do, and this from two marks. The first mark: they separated themselves from the true Church of God and the sound doctrine of the apostles, not by any necessity or authority of God, but by their own will alone, so as not to remain under the yoke of the Lord or his discipline. The second mark: sensual, they were without the Spirit, because, lacking regeneration, they savoured and pursued only those things to which nature, or human reason not enlightened by God, leads, being destitute, of course, of the Spirit of God, or the sanctifying grace of God. What remained was that sense and flesh should rule with full liberty and drive them to every pollution both of body and of soul.

units.la: Verf. 20. Vos autem, dilecti, sanctissimæ vestræ fidei superstruentes vosipsos, per Spiritum sanctum orantes,
units.tr: Verse 20. But you, beloved, building yourselves up on your most holy faith, praying in the Holy Spirit,

units.la: Arg. 8. Probans perseverandum in fide, contra seductorum machinationes, per medum præcepti propositum, Quia Spiritus Sanctus præscripsit media, quibus & ipsi perseverent, & qui defecerunt revocari possint; & rationem proposuit, qua singuli Satanæ machinas despicere queant, nempe, primo si fidem seu doctrinam sanctissimam Apostolicam, quæ nihil humani admixtum habet, pro fundamento immobili sibi statuerent, à qua ne latum quidem unguem unquam discederent: 2. Si assiduo superædificationi suæ studerent, & ad profectum in cognitione & fide veritatis in verbo Dei revelatæ, contenderent; 3. Si assidui essent in precibus ex sensu necessitatum suarum, sequentes ductum Spiritus Sancti, qui Sanctorum infirmitates sublevat, & quid & quomodo orandum sit secundum Dei voluntatem ostendit.
units.tr: Argument 8. Proving that one must persevere in the faith against the schemes of seducers, by way of a proposed precept. For the Holy Spirit has prescribed the means by which both they themselves may persevere and those who have fallen away may be recalled; and he has set out the reason by which each of them may be able to despise the snares of Satan, namely: first, if they set the most holy Apostolic faith or doctrine, which has nothing of man mixed into it, as an immovable foundation for themselves, from which they would never depart by so much as a hair's breadth; second, if they strive by constant building up of themselves and by striving toward progress in the knowledge and faith of the truth revealed in the Word of God; third, if they are constant in prayer out of a sense of their needs, following the guidance of the Holy Spirit, who relieves the infirmities of the saints and shows what and how to pray according to the will of God.

units.la: Verf. 21. Alii alios in charitate Dei conservate, expectantes misericordiam Domini nostri Jesu Christi in vitam æternam.
units.tr: Verse 21. Keep yourselves in the love of God, one another, looking for the mercy of our Lord Jesus Christ unto eternal life.

units.la: 4. Si studerent ex fide dilectionis Dei erga se, charitatem in fratres & proximos conservare; 5. Si Domini adventum prae oculis haberent: 6. Si apprehenderent vitam aeternam: 7. Si contra omnem suam indignitatem, adhaerérent misericordiae Christi, qui ita judex nostro futuro sit, ut gratuitum redemptionis a le partae beneficium & suum Euangelium pro judicandi regula sit habiturus: Ex his sequitur perseverandum in fide, &c.
units.tr: Fourth, if they studied to keep love toward brethren and neighbours, from faith in God's love toward themselves; fifth, if they kept the coming of the Lord before their eyes; sixth, if they laid hold of eternal life; seventh, if, despite all their own unworthiness, they clung to the mercy of Christ, who will be our judge in such a way that he will hold the free benefit of the redemption obtained by him, and his own Gospel, as the rule of judging. From these things it follows that one must persevere in the faith, etc.

units.la: Vers. 22: Et alios quidem habito delectu commiseramini:
units.tr: Verse 22: And some indeed, having made a distinction, have mercy on them:

units.la: Vers. 23. Alios vero terrore servate, ex flamma rapientes: odio habentes, vel eam tunicam quae a carne contacta sit maculata.
units.tr: Verse 23. But others save with fear, snatching them out of the fire, hating even the garment that has been spotted by the flesh.

units.la: Arg. 9. Per modum praecepti propositum, quia ratio a Deo proposita est Ecclesiae, quâ non tantum ipsi perseverare possent, sed etiam errantes, & lapsos in viam revocare, & erigere valerent, nempè si unumquemque pro suo ingenio tractarent, id est, si posita differentia inter errantes, uterentur misericordia & mansuetudine erga alios, nempè, mites & tractabiles: si vero quis contumax fuerit, aut securius sibi in peccato indulserit, per timorem vel severiorem castigationem ituderent eum servare, nempe, per excommunicationem si aliter corrigi non posset. Hujus rationes redduntur duae.
units.tr: Argument 9. Proposed by way of precept, because the reason has been set before the Church by God, by which they might not only persevere themselves, but also be able to recall and raise up those who err and have fallen from the way; namely, if they should deal with each one according to his disposition, that is, if, having made a distinction between those who err, they should use mercy and gentleness toward others, namely, the meek and tractable; but if anyone should be stubborn, or should have indulged himself more securely in sin, they should seek to save him with fear or with more severe chastisement, namely, by excommunication if he could not otherwise be corrected. Two reasons for this are given.

units.la: Ratio prima, Sub idonea similitudine. Nam ubi est incendii periculum violenter rapere non dubitamus eum, quem cupimus incolumem: Sic etiam curanda est salus eorum, qui non nisi duriter tractati resipiscunt, qui censuris vel severissimis a perditione Gehennae servandi sunt.
units.tr: The first reason, under a suitable likeness. For where there is danger of fire, we do not hesitate to snatch violently the one whom we wish to be safe. So too the salvation of those must be cared for who do not repent unless they are harshly treated, who are to be saved from the perdition of Gehenna by the most severe censures.

units.la: Ratio 2. Per allusionem ad typum legalem, Levitic. 15. 4 17; Quia ubi periculum est infectionis & contagionis, ut in obstinatis & sceleFum exemplis, etiam consortium vitandum est, & abscedendum ab istiusmodi libertinis pollutioni carnali deditis: Sicut olim in lege à leprosis, vel peste infectis, & pollutis vestimentis recedendum erat, quod est consequens excommunicationis.
units.tr: The second reason, by allusion to the legal type, Leviticus 15 and 17: because where there is danger of infection and contagion, as in the examples of the obstinate and wicked, even fellowship must be avoided, and one must withdraw from such libertines given over to carnal pollution; just as formerly under the law one had to withdraw from lepers, or from those infected with plague, and from polluted garments, which is the consequence of excommunication.

units.la: Vers. 24 Caeterum, ei qui potest vos servare à peccato immunes & statuere in conspectu gloriae suae inculpates cum exultatione.
units.tr: Verse 24. Now to him who is able to keep you from stumbling, and to present you faultless before the presence of his glory with exceeding joy.

units.la: Restat tertia pars Epistolae nempe conclusio, in qua perseverantiae laudem totam Deo ascribendam docet, ne quis nimium tribuat hominum viribus ribus, quorum diligentia in mediis utendis tantopere in præceden-tibus urgetur. Laudem autem perseverantiæ ascribendam Christo, probant rationes sequentes quinque.
units.tr: There remains the third part of the Epistle, namely the conclusion, in which he teaches that the whole praise of perseverance is to be ascribed to God, lest anyone attribute too much to human powers, whose diligence in using the means is so strongly urged in what precedes. That the praise of perseverance is to be ascribed to Christ, the following five reasons prove.

units.la: Potest ] Ratio prima, Quia officium in illo solo residet potenter conservandi fideles, ne in hac vita concidant in curiu pietatis, vel-deneciant, Statuere ] Ratio 2. Quia in eo residet potentia, secundum officium suum sistendi omnes suos in die judicii, in conspectu Dei gloriosi inculpatos, cum omni exultatione.
units.tr: Is able: the first reason, because the office resides in him alone to keep the faithful powerfully, so that in this life they do not fall from the course of piety or despair. To present: the second reason, because in him resides the power, according to his office, of presenting all his own before the glorious God in the day of judgment, faultless, with all joy.

units.la: Vers. 25. Id est soli sapienti DEO, Servatori nostro gloria, & magnificentia, & robur, & potestas, & nunc & in omnia secula. Amen.
units.tr: Verse 25. That is, to the only wise God our Saviour, be glory and majesty, dominion and power, both now and for all ages. Amen.

units.la: Ratio tertia, Quia ille est Deus solus sapiens, ut modis viisque suis hoc negotium totum solus perficiat. Servatori ] Ratio quarta, Quia Servator est noster, merito, officio, & efficacia, ut necesse sit eum quod suscepit in se perficiendum, perficere. Gloria ] Ratio 5. Quia ut in omni opere suo gloriam suam manifestari vult: sic præcipue in hoc negotio gloriosam suam Majestatem patefieri immensam suam potentiam exeri, & supremam suam in omnes, & omnia autoritatem conspici, & agnosci, & nunc, & in æternum. Ergo & perseverabitis vos verè Fideles, & gloria tota Salutis nostræ Deo cedet: Cui ut in solidum debetur, sic in æternum pendatur: AMEN.
units.tr: The third reason: because he is the only wise God, so that by his own ways and means he alone may accomplish this whole business. Saviour: the fourth reason, because he is our Saviour by merit, office and efficacy, so that it is necessary that he complete what he has undertaken to complete. Glory: the fifth reason, because as he wills to have his glory made manifest in every work of his, so especially in this business he wills his glorious Majesty to be laid open, his immense power to be exercised, and his supreme authority over all and in all to be seen and acknowledged, both now and for eternity. Therefore you too will persevere as true faithful ones, and all the glory of our salvation will go to God, to whom it is owed in full, and to whom it is ascribed for eternity. AMEN.

units.la: FINIS.
units.tr: END.

units.la: ERRATA Typographica, In notis Arithmeticis vel Inon apponendis, vel non satis Latine nonnunqnam explicandis, vel male numerandis. In literarum permutatione, quae voces & sensum notat, ut ex Gr. pag. 8. lin. 20. correptus, pro corruptus: & pag. 12. lin. 3. sequi pro seque. & pag. 155. lin. 2. iuscitanda, pro suscitanda, & similibus nonnullis. Omissione, ut pag. 31. lin. 18. parem, pro patrem & pag. 50. 11. mortis, pro mortuis. Additione, ut pag. 35. lin. 23. contristentur, pro contristent. Transpositione, ut pag. 4. lin. 18. inrtoiit, pro introiit. pag. 493. lin. 19. irrelperat, pro irreplerat. In vocum transpositione, ut E. G. pag. 3. lin. 3. imputabatur: &, pro & imputabatur. Conjunctione, ut E. G. pag. 52. lin. 4. Infolutione, pro in solutione, pag. 382. lin 19. obligatita, pro obligat, ita. In accentuum in Graecis & Latinis vocibus omissione. In commutatum & distinctionum multiplicatione, transpositione, & defectu. Reliquaque quae observabis graviora aliquot, & leviora multa, ut tua peritia emendet, & humanitas condonet, oramus
units.tr: Typographical errata: in the arithmetical signs, either not inserted, or sometimes not explained well enough in Latin, or numbered wrongly. In the interchange of letters, which alters words and sense: for example, page 8, line 20, "correptus" for "corruptus"; page 12, line 3, "sequi" for "seque"; page 155, line 2, "iuscitanda" for "suscitanda"; and some similar cases. By omission, as page 31, line 18, "parem" for "patrem"; and page 50, line 11, "mortis" for "mortuis". By addition, as page 35, line 23, "contristentur" for "contristent". By transposition, as page 4, line 18, "inrtoiit" for "introiit"; page 493, line 19, "irrelperat" for "irreplerat". In the transposition of words, as for example page 3, line 3, "imputabatur: &" for "& imputabatur". By conjoining, as page 52, line 4, "Infolutione" for "in solutione"; page 382, line 19, "obligatita" for "obligat, ita". In the omission of accents in Greek and Latin words. In the multiplication, transposition and lack of stops and marks of punctuation. And the other more serious errors, and many lighter ones, which you may notice: we ask that your skill correct them and your kindness pardon them.
